6Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son. 7But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life. 8So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
9Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant. 10The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
11Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
12Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared. 13Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep. 14She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
15When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute 16and asked her to sleep with him. She asked, “What will you give me if I do?”
17“One of my young goats,” he answered.
“What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
18“What do you want?” he asked in return.
“The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
19After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
20Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there. 21Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?”
“There's never been one here,” they answered.
22Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
23“If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
24About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!”
“Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
25As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
26“Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
27-28Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
29At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez. 30When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_text:
Juda ni Taama wia
1A guŋ saŋa hiŋ, Juda lii u lulla hiŋ be di la ga so baal bɛl banna yir Hira be, bol bɛl banna yir Adulam. 2Denii u huuzi Keenan hina biihaaŋ n faa ɛɛ Sua biihaaŋ, di kpau. 3Sua kpogli hia di lul biibaal, Juda dau u sɔŋ Ɛr. 4U haaŋ hiŋ kaa kpogli hia di lul biibaal, u dau u ge sɔŋ Ɔnan. 5U kaa lul horohiŋ, u dau u ge sɔŋ Sɛla. A Sɛla lulaa saŋa, di ba jaa du bol la banna yir Kɛzib.
6Denii u nyiŋŋi haaŋ bɛl banna yir Taama, di tɛɛ u biinabɔma Ɛr, u kpa. 7Ka Ɛr faa ɛɛ biinikpola hiŋ werge maa Kɔraawiizi be. U kuu guŋ wia di kpuu.
8Denii Juda faa ŋɔ Ɛr niwee Ɔnan be, “Gil i ni i kpɛɛma haaŋ Taama chɔɔ, í ɛɛ gunla u jaari n dɛkkɛ u ɛɛ tɛu.” 9Ka Ɔnan faa zum lugɔ a biizi wàá ɛɛ u hora. Awia, di u ni Taama faa haŋ wa chɔɔ maa, waa ɔɔ sɛɛ u banni zuu u ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, waa nyiŋŋi Taama wa kpogli hia di lul biizi, bá ɛɛ u kpɛɛma hiŋ hora.
10Kɔraawiizi faa na lugɔ Ɔnan ɛɛ biinikpola hinnɛ werge maa. U kaa kpu u ge. 11Ɔnan n wa siuwɛ, Juda ŋɔ u naahaaŋ Taama be, “Filaŋkeŋ, kpogli i luhanni di ga du i mɛɛ dia guŋŋ n biibaal Sɛla wa hel haaŋ kpai.” U faa ŋɔ gunnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra ɔmuu lugɔ Sɛla ge gba daŋ siu alugɔ u kpɛɛnna la. Denii Taama bir la u mɛɛ dia di ga du de.
12Aŋ wa birgee tama, Juda haaŋ Sua la siu. Uŋ wa wii u lee tuŋ, Juda ni u dammu Adulam hinuu Hira la Timna, bɔr la banna fuŋ u peeza huna la. 13Denii nɛbɛl ga ŋɔ tɛɛ Taama lugɔ u jaari mɛɛ ra la Timnaa, ú ga fuŋ u peeza huna. 14Taama na lugɔ Sɛla helloo tuŋ, ka Juda waa u wia ra ŋɔ lugɔ ú kpau. Denii u wir u luhanni laala, ka kpa saata bɛl tɔ lugɔ bá gilɛɛ zumuu, ka jaa lii di ga so Ɛnam n du Timna ŋmɛnɛɛ dominua.
15Denii Juda wa nau, ka fɛ lugɔ sensɛnni bɛllɛ, dikuu uŋ kpa saata di tɔ u siwee la wia. 16U la u be a ŋmɛnikɛrii di ga ŋɔ ú nuu chɔɔ. Haali a guŋ saŋa maa di u haa waa zummɛ lugɔ u biibaal haannɛ.
Taama pɛɛzuu, “Aŋmɛnɛɛ í turginnei?”
17Juda ŋɔ, “N daŋ lau buuŋ di wa turgii.”
U kaa ŋɔ, “Beedee kunnɛ i kpa tɛŋ mɔɔ ń zum lugɔ i daŋ wa tɛŋ a buunnɛi?”
18Juda bir ŋɔ, “Too, beedee waarɛ i ra nyiŋŋei?”
Taama kaa ŋɔ, “N na nyiŋŋi kuŋ la hiŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra jag hɔna, ni u ŋmɛŋ ani i daŋkpala naa hiŋ kpoglee naa.” Denii Juda kpa kuna la maa uŋ baglɛɛ la di tɛu. U jaa sɛɛ u nuu chɔɔ. Ban chɔɔwɛ la u kpogli hia. 19Uŋ wa kaalɛɛ la, u ga lau u saata la wir, ka kpa u luhanni laala la di laali.
20Juda ge bir la ka ga gil u dammu Adulam hinuu la lau a buuŋ di la ú ga tɛu, ka lɛɛ u kuna la uŋ ŋɔ nua di kpa tɛɛ a haaŋ la wa tɛu. Ka wɔɔ ga nawɛɛ. 21Denii u pɛɛzi baala baŋhina n du de, “Lee sɛnsɛnni la n faa du a bol naa ŋmɛnikɛrii la duɛi?”
Ba bir ŋɔ u be, “Yaa waa sɛnsɛnni maa dɔɔwɛ bɔnnaa.”
22Hira jaa bir la ga ŋɔ Juda be lugɔ wɔɔ nawɛɛ. Haali de hina gba ŋɔ lugɔ ba waa sɛnsɛnni maa dɔɔwɛ de.
23Denii Juda ŋɔ, “Gil u kpogli a kuna. Yaa ɛɛ aniaa di lau a buuŋ ya vii ga tɛu, ka yaa wɔɔ nawɛɛ. Di yaa bittɔ la de, ba daŋ gaa mam yaa.”
24Aŋ wa ɛɛ baaguzi ahoro, ba tili Juda be lugɔ u biibaal haaŋ Taama sɛmmɔɔ di kpogli hia.
Denii Juda ŋɔ, “Aa! Ií lawuu ba di wa fuuuh.”
25Ka baŋ wa lawuu di ra la ba ga kpu la, u tili di ŋɔ Juda be, “Baal la maa kuŋ n ɛɛ hɔna jagrikuŋ ni u ŋmɛŋ ani daŋkpala naabuu duŋ a hia. I zum a hiŋaa?”
26Juda sɛɛ lugɔ u kunaa, ka ŋɔ, “U hor summɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, maa n nua la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ yuu Sɛla la hiŋŋɛ.” Ama, waa kaa sɛɛ u nuu chɔɔ maa.
27Taama lulaa n wa helle, biinɛɛrii du u hia, ba maa ɛɛ baala. 28Unna lul la, bɛl nonii feli lii, haaŋ la n lawuu la kpa gessiaahmu di u nonii hiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “Unniibuu felee lii.” 29Ka uŋ wa bittɛ di lau u nonii du, unla hiŋ bir feli di wa lii. 30Denii a haaŋ ŋɔ, “I fittɔɔ lii.” Ba faa dau u sɔŋ Pɛrɛz. Ba kaa dau unla ge gessi n vɔɔ u nonii la sɔŋ, Zɛra.

english_text:
Joseph and Potiphar's Wife
1The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard. 2-3 So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner.
Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did. 4Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property. 5Because of Joseph, the Lord began to bless Potiphar's family and fields. 6Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat.
Joseph was well-built and handsome, 7 and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her, 8but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns. 9No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.” 10She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
11One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there. 12Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
13When this happened, 14she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help. 15And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
16Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home. 17Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me! 18But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
19Potiphar became very angry 20and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept.
While Joseph was in prison, 21 the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that 22he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail. 23The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_text:
Joosɛf ni Pɔtifa haaŋ wia
1Ismɛl kɔkɔɔza la kpogli Joosɛf kaali Ijip. Pɔtifa la n ɛɛ Ijip koori kooridia binna nabɔma yawuu. 2Kɔraawiizi faa du Joosɛf be, u wia maa dɔɔ siwee u dɔɔri la dia. 3Denii u dɔɔri la n wa zummɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du Joosɛf benii, u wia maa dɔɔ siwee la, 4u wia paruu werge maa, u jaa kpau birgi u himmaa huŋhunni. U kpa Joosɛf di birgi nɛr la n na binni u diahina wiimaa ni, di faa kpa u kundɔɔlaa maa du u nonee. 5Di lii a hɔl la Pɔtifa n gillɛ Joosɛf ɛɛ u dia nabɔma la maanii, Kɔraawiizi faari di ra kissi Pɔtifa, dikuu Joosɛf wia. U dia wiimaa ge wia faa ra la see nɛnnɛ. Haali u pattikuna ɔɔ lɛɛ, u sela gba ra wazi. 6Denii Pɔtifa faa jaa kpa kunla maa un dɔɔwɛ fɔŋŋa di du Joosɛf nonee. Joosɛf n du u be la, wiimaa faa waa kaa tiruu, di diwee la unna di bɛŋ wia lɛi.
Joosɛf mai faa wesso nɛnnɛ, u kaa ɛɛ bunɔɔŋ, 7Denii Pɔtifa haaŋ faa bir di ra nyiŋŋuu, di ŋɔ ú nuu chɔɔ.
8Ka Joosɛf vɛɛ, di ŋɔ u be, “N dɔɔri yardimbuu, di gil n na binni kummaa n du dia naa biini. Awiarɛ waa kaa ra du a tau la. 9Nɛr maa waa a fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ di kaaliŋ. Kummaanii u kpa tɛŋ di i bɛŋ lɛi. U haannɛ hiŋ. Ɛrɛɛ ń wer ɛɛ keŋ widɔŋai? Guŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, Kɔraawiizi be.” 10Haali uŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ Joosɛf be guŋ hɔpizi bii maa gba, ka Joosɛf waa ɔɔ sɛɛ, u nuu chɔɔ gɛɛ u du u be gba.
11Denii a hɔl bɛl u zuu a dia ú hum u huma, di a dia balii bɛl maa waa hoo. 12A haaŋ la ga lau u tagtajaŋ di ŋɔ, “Gil n nii chɔɔ!” Joosɛf waa sɛɛwɛ, ka wir u tagtajaŋ hiŋ di du u nonee, ka chɔ lii bossee. 13A haaŋ n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Joosɛf wir u tagtaarɛ di du u nonii ka chɔ lii bossee la, 14u yir u diahina, di ŋɔ, “Ií na gunla Hibru hina yombaal naa n jaari n yauwɛ naa n ɔɔ hanna binni yaa pɛɛ, haali u wa zuu ŋɔ ú pumiŋ, ka n lɔ wile werge maa. 15Miŋ jaa lɔ a wile hiŋ, u wir u tagtajaŋ du n nonee, ka chɔ lii bossee.”
16U kpa a tagtajaŋ hiŋ di dau. U jaari n wa ballɛ, 17u kpa guŋ bagli tɛu, di ŋɔ, “Hibru hina yombaal naa hiŋ lauwɛ ba naa binnimbuu pɛɛ, haali di wa zuu n be, 18n lɔ wile u wir u tagtajaŋ du n nonee ka chɔ lii.” 19Pɔtifa n wa nuu gunla u haaŋ n ŋɔwɛɛ la, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa! 20U lau Joosɛf di tɔ dia, bɔr la u dɔɔri Ijip koori la n na tɔ nɛra la.
Joosɛf n du a nɛra tɔi dia hiŋ, 21Kɔraawiizi faa haa du u benii di ra hiinuu u wiɛɛlaa maa biini, u wia ra par nɛr la n na binni banla baŋ tɔ dia la ni. 22Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, u gil Joosɛf ɛɛ u dɔŋahina la baŋ tɔ dia la maa nabɔma, di ra du wii la maa n na ɛɛ a dia biini tau. 23A nɛra tɔi dia binni la faa waa kaa ra fɔŋ wia la maa uŋ kpawɛɛ du Joosɛf nonee ŋɔ ú ra binni wia, Kɔraawiizi faa du u benii, di gil u wiimaa ra vol nɛnnɛ.

english_text:
Joseph Tells the Meaning of the Prisoners' Dreams
1-3While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph. 4They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
5One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings. 6The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset, 7and he asked, “Why are you so worried today?”
8“We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.”
Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
9The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine 10with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe. 11I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
12Joseph said:
This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days, 13and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do. 14But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place. 15I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
16When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head. 17The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
18Joseph said:
This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days, 19 and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
20Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook. 21He put the personal servant back in his old job 22and had the cook put to death.
Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would, 23but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_text:
Libikpogli ni paanuɔɔzi wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, a Ijip koori huŋhunni la n ɛɛ u libikpogli ani u paanuɔɔza binni la, ɛɛ wia di zuu a koori ni. 2U baaŋ fuuh ba ni werge maa, 3u lau baa di tɔ dia, u dia binna nabɔma Pɔtifa dia, bɔr la baŋ tɔ Joosɛf la. 4Ban du a nɛra tɔi dia la, Pɔtifa gil Joosɛf ra du ba tau. Ban du de hiŋ, 5a hɔl bɛl hamuŋa ni, koori libikpogli ni u paanuɔɔzi chɔɔ deezi, bɛl maa deeza zɛɛ kur. 6Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Joosɛf ba ba be, u na lugɔ ba biine chɔkkɔɔ. 7U pɛɛzi baa, “Beedee n kpogli ia zinaa, ii nyɛm gunnɛi?”
8Denii ba ŋɔ, “Yaa dɛɛ deezoore, ka nɛr maa waa hoo ú bagli a zɛɛzi tɛɛ yaa.”
Joosɛf ŋɔ, “Deeza zɛɛzi baglaa lii Kɔraawiizi benii. Ií bagliŋ ii deeza hiŋ.”
9A koori libikpogli la ŋɔ, “N na grepu daa bɛllɛ n chigɛ n see, 10di dɔɔ kela ahoro. U ni waraa di u fiiwɔ, u ni u fii di u nɔnnɔ, u nɔna aah. 11N kaa na lugɔ miŋ kpogli Ijip koori libee. Denii n kpa nɔna la di hanzi a niiri di du a libee biini, di kpa tɛɛ Ijip koori.”
12Joosɛf ŋɔ, “N zum i deeza hiŋ zɛɛrɛ. Kela ahoro la ɛɛ hɔpizaa ahoroo.
13Hɔpizaa ahoro biini, a koori daŋ lizii lii nɛra tɔi dia naa biini, di gil i kaa ra kpogli u libee, ú ra nyɔɔ gunla hiŋ faa ɔɔ ra kpogluu di ra tɛu saŋa maa la. 14Awia, di i wa liwɔɔ, i wiimaa kuari nɛnnɛ, ɛɛ ra liizi n wia di ɛɛŋ nɛnnɛ, di gil Ijip koori zum n wia di liziŋ bɔnnaa. 15N kipar lɛi ba lii n ni Hibru hɛri di ba ɛŋ. Maa wii maa ɛɛwɛ di dɛg lugɔ bá tɔŋ dia gba.”
16Too, a paanuɔɔza nabɔma la n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ lugli hiŋ la deeza zɛɛ wessoo la, u ge bagli u deeza tɛɛ Joosɛf, di ŋɔ, “N deezoore di na alugɔ miŋ chigɛ paanuuzi kɛɛgɔɔzi ahoro. 17Unla n hɔŋ chiŋ la su paanuɔɔzaa irizi miŋ chigɛ di ra la ń ga tɛɛ Ijip koori. Ka zumbizi ba di waa dia.”
18Joosɛf kaa ŋɔ, “N daŋ bagli a ge zɛɛ tɛi. Kɛɛgɔzi ahoro la ɛɛ hɔpizaa ahoroo. 19Hɔpizaa ahoro biini, Ijip koori daŋ teŋ i nyuu, ka kpa i bɔrahɔŋ tɔɔh daa ni, zumbizi ba di waa di.”
20Hɔpizaa ahoro n wa bɛrɛɛ, Ijip koori lulaa hɔpizii hel, u daali diuzenaa di tɛɛ u huŋhunna ni ba nabɔnzi ani u diahina maa. Denii u hum dí ba ga lizi u libikpogli la ani paanuɔɔza nabɔma la, a nɛra tɔi dia biini di ba u ni u nabɔnzi la see. 21Baŋ wa ballɛ, u kaa kpa libikpogli la waa nabɔmuu la tɛu, 22ka ŋɔ bá kpu unla waa, di kpau tɔɔh daa ni, gunla himmaa Joosɛf n baglɛɛ la. 23Ka Ijip koori libikpogli la faa suuh Joosɛf wia kɔrai, waa kaa ra liizi u wia tama maa gba.

english_text:
Joseph Interprets the King's Dreams
1Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River. 2Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank. 3Then seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river and 4ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
5The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk. 6Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert. 7The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
8 The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
9The king's personal servant said:
Now I remember what I was supposed to do. 10When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard. 11One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning. 12A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant, 13and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
14The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
15The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
16“Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
17The king told Joseph:
I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River. 18I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass. 19Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt. 20The skinny cows ate the fat ones. 21But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
22I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe. 23Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert. 24These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
25Joseph replied:
Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do. 26The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain. 27The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
28It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do. 29For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain, 30but that will be followed by seven years when there won't be enough. The good years of plenty will be forgotten, and everywhere in Egypt people will be starving. 31The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty. 32God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
33Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt. 34Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty. 35Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities. 36It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food.
Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
37The king and his officials liked this plan. 38So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
39The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do. 40 I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me. 41You are now governor of all Egypt!”
42 Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck. 43He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
44The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.” 45He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
46Joseph was 30 when the king made him governor, and he went everywhere for the king. 47For seven years there were big harvests of grain. 48Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested. 49In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
50Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began. 51Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.” 52His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
53Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end, 54 and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty. 55 When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
56The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians. 57People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_text:
Ijip koori deeza wia
1Binni anɛɛ n wa bɛrɛɛ, a hɔl bɛl Ijip koori chɔɔ di deezi uŋ chigɔ Muu Naal baŋgia. 2U deeza hiŋ biini, u na nauna aniidaanɛɛ n pɔllɛ di du wer werge maa, a lii a nii biini di ra di kooree u baŋgia. 3Denii akɔgni werge aniidaanɛɛ ge kaa lii a nii biini, di ga chi anla n pɔllɛ la be. 4U ŋɔ u binni, di akɔgni la lauri a pɔllaa la di ligli. Ijip koori n na gunla, u hassi izi.
5Denii u kaa foozi chɔɔ dɔɔ di kaa deezi di na midaakpaŋ n dɔɔ nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ, a du bee nɛnnɛ di du wer. 6Denii minyuuni aniidaanɛɛ kaa wa lii di jaa anla ni. Ka aawaa, peu lii wiifurii di wa ta a ni, a hil, a bee maa war di chogli. 7A minyuchɔga hiŋ kpa a minyunanaa aniidaanɛɛ la di ligli. Ijip koori kaa hassi izi, di deeza biinii.
8Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Ijip koori haa ra liizaa, a tiruu werge maa. U chaali u ziŋgaabo hina ni nunzunna la maa n du Ijip hɛri, di bagli u deeza la tɛɛ baa. Ka bɛl maa waa wette u bagluu a zɛɛzi.
9Denii koori libikpogla nabɔma la ŋɔ u be, “Zinaa n liizi wii bɛl miŋ ɛɛwɛ di leu. 10Saŋa la i baaŋ n faa fuuh n ni i paanuɔɔza nabɔma ni, i kpa yaa tɛɛ i dia nɛbinna nabɔma u tɔ dia la, 11a hɔl bɛl hamuŋa ni yaa bɛl maa deezi, a deeza bɛl maa dɔɔ u zɛɛ. 12Denii yaa bagli yaa deeza la di tɛɛ Hibru hina biipɔllii la n ɛɛ i dia nɛbinna nabɔma Pɔtifa balii, di ge du a nɛra tɔi dia la, u bagli bɛl maa deeza zɛɛ tɛu. 13Gunla uŋ baglɛɛ la, guŋ himmaanii wa ɛɛwɛ. I bittɔɔ kpa n nabɔmuu tɛŋ, ka teŋ paanuɔɔza nabɔma la ge nyuu, gunla himmaa uŋ baglɛɛ la.”
14Denii Ijip koori hum dí ba ga lizi Joosɛf ba. Ba ɛɛ manaŋ di ga lizuu lii a nɛra tɔi dia, di gil u fuŋ u taŋhuna manaŋ, ka ba kpa laala tɛu u laali, ka kpogluu la Ijip koori be.
15Ijip koori ga ŋɔ, “Dɛɛla n deezoore ka n nɛra naa bɛl maa waa wette ú bagliŋ a zɛɛ. Ka n nuu lugɔ i wettoo di ra bagli deeza zɛɛzi.”
16Denii Joosɛf ŋɔ, “Miŋwaa wàá wer bagli a zɛɛ. Kɔraawiizii niŋ baglii a zɛɛ i bɔra wer sɔɔnii nɛnnɛ.”
17Denii Ijip koori ŋɔ, “N deeza hiŋ biini, n na miŋ chigɛ Muu Naal baŋgiarɛ. 18N ŋɔ n binni di nauna aniidaanɛɛ n pɔllɛ, di du wer werge maa lii a nii biini, di ra hee kooree u baŋgia. 19N kaa ŋɔ n binni di aniidaanɛɛ aŋhina n kɔkkɛzi werge ge lii a nii biini. A kɔkkɔɔ werge maa, haali n haa waa a dɔŋa nawɛɛ Ijip hɛri naa maa. 20Denii akɔgni werge la lauri anla n pɔllɛ di feli lii a nii biini la di ligli. 21Haali an liglaa la, ka a faa haa du a duulaa. Denii n hassi izi.
22N kaa chɔɔ deezi na midaakpaŋ n lul nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ, a ge maa du bee nɛnnɛ di du wer. 23N kaa ŋɔ n binni di nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ aŋhina ge lii a midaakpaŋ la ni. Peu lii wiifurii di wa ta a ni, a maa war di chogli. 24A minyuchɔgaa hiŋ ge kpa a minyunanaa la di ligli. Too, n bagli a deeza naabuu tɛɛ n ziŋgaabo hina ani n nunzunna maa, ka ba waa wette bá bagliŋ a zɛɛzi.”
25Denii Joosɛf ŋɔ Ijip koori be, “A deeza anɛɛ hiŋ maa zɛɛzi ɛɛ kpannɛ. Kɔraawiizi a bagliibuu wia la un niŋ wa ɛɛ. 26A nauna aniidaanɛɛ la n pɔllɛ werge ani a minyunanaa aniidaanɛɛ la maa chigɔɔ tɛɛ binni aniidaanɛɛ. 27A nakɔgni werge aniidaanɛɛ la ani a minyuchɔgaa aniidaanɛɛ la peu n lii wiifurii di ta a ni a war la maa ge ra bagli binni aniidaanɛɛ lɔchɔgii n niŋ wa chol labuu.
28Kennaa miŋ baglɛɛ naa himmaanii niŋ ɛɛ. Kɔraawiizi teŋ bagliibuu gunla un niŋ ɛɛ. 29Diwee daŋ su Ijip hɛri maa binni aniidaanɛɛ n niŋ ba la. 30Di a wa bɛrɔɔ, lɔzi ge daŋ chol binni aniidaanɛɛ, di dɔɔ tɔɔrɔɔ werge maa, haali nɛra suuh diwee werge la maa baŋ faa dɔɔwɛ binni la n bɛrɛɛ la biini wia. 31Ba wàá ka liizi diwee werge la wia, dikuu lɔchɔgii la n na ba ú wa chol ba ni wia. 32Hiŋ deezi wikpaŋ bunɛɛ la, gunna bagluu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi lau gunla un niŋ ɛɛu nɛnnɛ, a wàá birgi ka ú ɛɛ guŋ.”
33Denii Joosɛf kaa ŋɔ Ijip koori be, “Nyiŋŋi nɛr la n ɛɛ nunzunni, di dɔɔ nfɛrɛ nɛnnɛ, di kpa Ijip hɛri du u nonee u ra binni. 34I daŋ kaa lizi nabɔnzi di gil ba ra lɛɛ Ijip hɛri pattikuna. Di nɛr maa ɔɔ wa kpa u koo kuna, bá lɛɛ a bɔra anue bɔkpaŋ, guŋŋ a binni aniidaanɛɛ la diwee n niŋ du de werge maa la biini, 35di gil bá chaali a maa di du buugizenaa biine, di chiŋŋaa bolzenaa la maa biine, di ra gua, 36diwee wer du a bola maa biine, mɔɔ ka lɔzi wa chol Ijip hɛri, di lii a guŋ binni aniidaanɛɛ naa biini. Guŋ daŋ gil lɔzi wàá kpu nɛra, bá siuzi.”
37Joosɛf wiŋɔzi la faa ɛɛ wibii werge maa tɛɛ Ijip koori ani u hɛri nabɔnzi la maa. 38Ijip koori ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ wer na nɛr u hum a keŋ huma naa, di kaa kaali baal naa? Kɔraawiizi Duma du u benii.”
39Denii u jaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Kɔraawiizi n pilli a wia naa maa tɛi i zumaa kennaa, nɛr maa waa kaa dɔɔ nunzuma ni nfɛrɛ di kaalii. 40Awia, hinuu niŋ jaa ra binni n hɛri ni, n nɛra maa ra sɛɛ i dɔɔra. N bɛnnɛ niŋ ɛɛ nabɔma i ni.” 41Ijip koori kaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “N kpa Ijip hɛri maanii di du i nonee biini.” 42Denii a koori lizi u nonibisig la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, u kpa ra jag kuna ni la, di du Joosɛf nonibii. U kaa tɛu laalinanaa, di kpa saliŋ baŋaakuŋ di duu. 43Ijip koori faa gil u zuu torko bɛl zagu n na tɛrgi, u ra bagli lugɔ waabuu hiŋ koori la ni. Di u haŋ wa zuuu di ra la bɔr la maa, u balaa ɔɔ tɔ u seere, di ra ŋɔ kpegzi ni, “Ií ra tɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ oo!” Gunnɛ a faa ɛɛ, Joosɛf dɔɔ Ijip hɛri maa di ra binni.
44Ijip koori kaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Minuu Ijip hɛri maa koori, ka nɛr maa wàá wer izi di ɛɛ wiimaa Ijip hɛri naa biini, di hɔɔ tɛɛwɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ.” 45Ijip koori faa kaa bir dau u sɔŋ Zafɛnaf Pania, di kaa nyiŋŋi suŋguru bɛl banna yir Asɛnaf tɛu. A suŋguru mɛɛrɛ faa Pɔtifɛra. Waabuu faa Hɛliɔpɔlis vug Ɔɔn kizeehiŋ. Joosɛf faa jaa gaagi di ra binni Ijip hɛri maa.
46Uŋ faa zuu Ijip koori huma hiŋ biini la, di u binni du tokko ni kpɔrgɔ. Ka u faa lii u be di gaagi di ra binni Ijip hɛri maa. 47A binni aniidaanɛɛ la diwee n niŋ du de werge biini la, diwee wa pur, di su a hɛri maa werge. 48A binni biinii Joosɛf faa kpa pattikuna maa ni a dizi banna par Ijip hɛri yeŋa, di ra chiŋŋi ba bolzenaa biine. A bolzeŋ bɛl maa kooni diweere u faa kpa di ra chiŋŋi de. 49Ba buugazi maanii faa suugi diwee werge maa alugɔ muunua hɛɛhriichaa. A diwee faa kannɔɔ werge. Awia, Joosɛf faa gil a mɛgzaa.
50Mɔɔ ka lɔzi wa chol la, di Joosɛf ni u haaŋ Asɛnaf la lul biibaala banɛɛ. 51Joosɛf faa dau u biinabɔma sɔŋ Manasɛ. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi hiinimbuu n suuh tɔɔrɔɔzi ani n mɛɛ diahina maa wia.” 52Di dau nɛɛhiŋ la ge sɔŋ Ɛfram. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n lul biizi hɛri la miŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ la biini.”
53Denii a binni aniidaanɛɛ la diwee n du de werge la n wa tunnɛ, 54ka a binni aniidaanɛɛ a lɔchɔgii n niŋ chol la jaa faari, gunla himmaa Joosɛf n faa baglɛɛ la. Diwee faa waa hoo hɛssi la n dugli Ijip hɛri la. Ama, diwee faa su Ijip hɛriwaa maanii. 55Awia, lɔzi faa ra kpu nɛra werge maa Ijip hɛri. Denii ba ga suŋŋi Ijip koori dí u tɛɛ baa diwee. U ŋɔ ba be, “Ií la Joosɛf be, ú ga bagli ia gunla iin niŋ ɛɛ.” 56A lɔzi n faa chol a hɛri maa, di du kpeg wia, Joosɛf faa jaa pilli a buugazi hiŋ, di yoo a diwee ra tɛɛ a Ijip hina. 57Hɛssi la gba n dugli de la gba nɛra ɔɔ la Ijip hɛri di gaa yau diwee Joosɛf be, dikuubɛɛwiai, lɔzi faa chol durnya yemmaanii werge maa.

english_text:
Joseph's Brothers Go to Egypt To Buy Grain
1When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another? 2 I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
3Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain. 4But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him. 5So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
6Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground. 7-8They did not recognize Joseph, but at once he knew who they were, though he pretended not to know. Instead, he spoke harshly and asked, “Where do you come from?”
“From the land of Canaan,” they answered. “We've come here to buy grain.”
9 Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
10“No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain. 11We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
12“That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
13But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
14Joseph replied:
It's like I said. You're spies, 15and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here. 16Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
17Joseph kept them all under guard for three days, 18before saying to them:
Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives. 19If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families. 20But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death.
Joseph's brothers agreed 21and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
22 Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
23They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter. 24Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched.
Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
25Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done, 26they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
27When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag. 28“Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.”
They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
29When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
30The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies. 31But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies. 32We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
33Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families. 34But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
35When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob, 36who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
37Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
38But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_text:
Joosɛf kpɛɛnna n la Ijip wia
1Denii Jekɔb wa nuu lugɔ sɔgmia du Ijip hɛrii. U ŋɔ u biibaala be, “Ɛrɛɛ ii so di ra binni dɔŋa ninɛi? 2N nuuwɔ lugɔ sɔgmia du Ijip hɛrii ba ra yoo. Ií la ga yau aŋhina ba. Di guŋ lɛi, lɔzi daŋ kpu yaa maa ya siuzi.” 3Joosɛf kpɛɛnna fi la jaa la Ijip hɛri, bá ga yau a sɔgmia. 4Ama, Jekɔb faa waa sɛɛwɛ Joosɛf niwee Bɛnjamin lawaa la. U faa ra ɔmuu lugɔ wii bɛl daŋ ga ɛɛu.
5Denii Jekɔb biibaala la ani nɛkpila maa ga hel Ijip hɛri, bá yau a sɔgmia, dikuubɛɛwiai, Keenan hɛri maanii a lɔzi faa chol. 6Joosɛf n faa ɛɛ Ijip hɛri maa nabɔma, di kaa ra yoo a sɔgmia la wia, u benii u kpɛɛnna la faa la bá ga yau a sɔgmia. Baŋ ga hel u be, ba togni hɛri di jaamuu. 7Denii Joosɛf na baa, di zum baa manaŋ, ka ɛɛ lugɔ waa baa zummɛ. U jaa nyɛg ba ni, ka pɛɛzi baa, “Lee ii liiyɛi?”
Ba ŋɔ, “Keenan hɛrii yaa lii di ba ya wa yau sɔgmia.”
8Haali Joosɛf n zum u kpɛɛnna la, ka baawaa wɔɔ zummɛ. 9Denii u jaa ra liizi deezazi un deezee la, ka ŋɔ ba be, “Nɛchɔgaarɛ ia, ii ballɔɔ ii wa daani yaa di na, ka ba wa lɔ yaa laal.”
10U kpɛɛnna hiŋ ŋɔ, “Akai, nabɔma, i balaa ballɔɔ bá wa yau sɔgmia. 11Nɛkpaŋ biizii yaa maa. Yaa ɛɛ biinihuŋŋu hinaa. Yaa waa wichɔgii maa fɛwɛɛ ka ba.”
12Joosɛf haa vɛɛ ka ra ŋɔ, “Ií kara de! Ií ballɔɔ ii wa daani yaa di na yaa gɛrga.”
13Ba kaa ŋɔ, “Yaa nabɔma, yaa du biibaala fidibanɛɛrɛ yaa mɛɛ lul Keenan hɛri. Yaa kalugu du yaa mɛɛ be, ka yaa bɛlwaa siuwɔɔ.”
14Ka Joosɛf haa ŋɔ, “Ií kara de! Maa ŋɔ ii ballɔɔ ií wa daani yaa naa? 15Kenne ya ɛɛ di zum di gunla iinna ŋɔ naa ɛɛ wibiire. N hɛɛhzi Ijip koori lugɔ di ii kalugu la waa ɛŋ ballɛ, ii bɛl maa wàá lii Ijip hɛri naa biini. 16Ií bɛlhiŋ la ga kpogli ii niwee hiŋ ba. Ií banla n kawɛɛ daŋ du nɛra tɔi dia, ka ya ra kpaŋ baa. Gunnɛ ya ɛɛ di zum di ii wiŋɔzi naa ɛɛ wibiire gɛɛ di karaawɛi? Di karaa ii ra kanni, guŋwaa, n hɛɛhzi Ijip koori la n du de lugɔ ii ballɔɔ ii wa daani yaa di na.” 17Denii u lau baa tɔ dia hɔpizaa ahoro.
18A hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl la, Joosɛf ŋɔ ba be, “N na ɔm Kɔraawiizii. Awia, di ii daŋ ɛɛ wii naa min niŋ ŋɔ naa, ii daŋ na miibɔɔ. 19Di ii ɛɛ wibii hinaa, ii gil ii bɛl du nɛra tɔi dia naa, ka ii banla n kawɛɛ la kpa sɔgmia di la bol di ga tɛɛ ii nɛra, lɔzi n na kpu baa wia. 20Ama, di ii ga bittɔ di ra ba, ií kpogli ii niwee la ba. Di ii wa ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ zum lugɔ ii ɛɛ wibii hinaa, ɛnnɛ maa, màá ka kpu ia.” Denii ba sɛɛ, dí ba daŋ ɛɛ guŋ.
21Ba ra ŋɔ dɔŋa be, “Gunla yaa n ɛɛ Joosɛf la wiarɛ annii maa ra huuzi yaa la. U suŋŋi yaabuu siaahmu maa ni lugɔ ya ta u haahkɛ, ka yaa vɛɛ. Aabuu gillɛ a keŋ siaahmu naa huuzi yaa la.”
22Rubin pɛɛzi baa, “Maa ii be ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ya gilɛɛ ɛɛ yaa niwee wichɔgaa, ka ii vɛɛa? Too, u kpui labuu ra pɛɛzi yaa nua zinaa la.” 23Ba waa wette zum lugɔ Joosɛf ra nuuabuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɔɔ faa ŋɔ wiarɛ, nɛbɛl biraa di ra du ba mɔɔri biini di ra tɛɛ baa. 24Uŋ wa nuu gunla banna ŋɔ la, u lii bossee di ga nyiŋŋi bɔr la un niŋ wer suah di wii. Uŋ ga wiiwe tuŋ, u bir ba, di lizi Simɛɔn di lii ba biini, di gil ba vɔɔzuu ba maa sibɔɔ.
Joosɛf kpɛɛnna n bittɛ kaali Keenan hɛri wia
25Denii u gil u balaa ɛɛ sɔgmia di du banla n kawɛɛ la bɔɔtizi biine. Di kaa ŋɔ u balaa hiŋ be lugɔ ba suahzi bir bɛl maa kebee di du u bɔɔti biini, di kaa tɛɛ baa sɔgmia ban ninna di ŋmɛnɛɛ. Baŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ, 26ba jaa kpa ba bunni di chug ba kauzi di ra kaali ba bol.
27Baŋ wa hel bɔr la ban niŋ chɔɔ hɔpizi la, bɛl pilli u bɔɔti ú ɛɛ mia tɛɛ u kawee. Uŋ pillɛɛ la u na kebee n du a bɔɔti nua di ŋɔ, 28“Ií na, ba bir n kebee labuu tɛŋ. Aabuu du n bɔɔti biini la.”
Denii ɔnsii lau baa werge maa, ba ŋɔ, “Beedee Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ yaa kennei?”
29Baŋ ga hel ba mɛɛ Jekɔb be Keenan hɛri, ba bagli gunla maa n du de di tɛu, di ŋɔ, 30“A Ijip hina nabɔma hiŋ nyɛg yaa ninɛɛ werge maa, di ŋɔ yaa ɛɛ nɛchɔgaarɛ di ba ya wa daani baa, di zum ba hɛri wikpoglaa maa. 31Ka yaa ŋɔ yaa ɛɛ biinihuŋŋu hinaa. Yaa waa wichɔgii maa fɛwɛɛ ka ba. 32Denii yaa kaa ŋɔ u be lugɔ yaa du biizi fidibaanɛɛ yaa mɛɛ n lullɛ, bɛl siu, ka yaa kaluguwaa du yaa mɛɛ be, Keenan hɛri. 33Denii a hɛri nabɔma hiŋ ŋɔ dí mɔɔ ka ú zum yaa wibii, u daŋ lau yaa bɛl di tɔ dia, ka yaa banla n kawɛɛ la kpa sɔgmia di ba bol di wa tɛɛ yaa nɛra, lɔzi n na kpu baa wia. 34Ama, dí ya lau yaa niwee hiŋ di ra ba, ú jaa zum lugɔ yaa ɛɛ wibii hinaa ɛnɛ maa. Dí, di yaa ɛɛ guŋ, u daŋ lizi yaa kpɛɛma la tɛɛ yaa, ka ya ɔɔ ba u hɛri di waa yau sɔgmia u be.”
35Ka baŋ pilli ba bɔɔtizi la, bɛl maa na kebee la uŋ kpawɛɛ turgi a sɔgmia la. Ɔnsii lau ba ni ba mɛɛ werge maa. 36Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Ií gillɔɔ maa kaa dɔɔ bie maa! Joosɛf waa hoo, Simɛɔn waa hoo. Ii kaa ŋɔ ii lau Bɛnjamin ge di jaa, ka n haŋ so di ra di dɔgnyaa?”
37Denii Rubin ŋɔ u mɛɛ be, “Di maa bittɛ ba, kpu n biibaala banɛɛ la min dɔɔwɛ la. Kpau du n nonee biini. N daŋ bir kpogluu ba.”
38Ka Jekɔb bir ŋɔ u be, “N biibaal naawaa wàá ka hiŋ ia la de. Joosɛf n siuwɛ la, u bɛnnɛ jaa ka u maa biibaal. Di wiimaa kaa wa huuzi u ge, ii daŋ gil biinichɔg kpuŋ.”

english_text:
Joseph's Brothers Return to Egypt with Benjamin
1The famine in Canaan got worse, 2until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
3-5Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
6Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
7They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
8Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death. 9I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live. 10If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
11Their father said:
If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds. 12Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks. 13Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
14When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
15The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph, 16he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
17The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house. 18But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
19So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge, 20“Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain. 21But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back, 22together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
23“It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
24The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys. 25The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
26When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him. 27After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
28They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
29When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
30Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried. 31After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
32Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews. 33To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest. 34They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_text:
Joosɛf kpɛɛnna n kpogli Bɛnjamin la Ijip wia
1Denii lɔzi la faa haa ra nyaŋŋi werge maa, a hɛri biini. 2Sɔgmia la baŋ yauwɛ Ijip hɛri ba la n wa tunnɛ, Jekɔb kaa ŋɔ u biibaala la be, “Ií kaa la Ijip hɛri di ga yau sɔgmia di wa tɛɛ yaa.”
3Ka Juda ŋɔ, “Siaahmu maanii u faa ŋɔ lugɔ waa kaa ra nyiŋŋi u na yaa siwii ni, di yaa waa yaa niwee hiŋ kpoglee ba. 4Di i gillɔ yaa nuu maa la, yaa daŋ wer la ga na sɔgmia yau. 5Di hàá gil yaa nuu lawaa, guŋwaa, yaa gba n haŋ so bolle bɔ. A baal ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ wàá sɛɛ ya kaa nau, di yaa waa ya niwee kpoglee ba.”
6Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Ka bɛɛ n baani ii ŋɔ lugɔ ii dɔɔ niwee bɛllɛ bol, di ra nyiŋŋi ii kpa tɔɔrɔɔ duŋ kennei?”
7Ba kaa ŋɔ, “A baallɛ faa ra pɛɛzi yaa nɛnnɛ yaa diahina wia, di ra nyiŋŋi u zum di yaa mɛɛ haa du de gɛɛ, di kaa pɛɛzi lugɔ yaa dɔɔ niwee bɛllɛ di jaa? Ɛrɛɛ ya faa ɛɛ zum lugɔ u daŋ ŋɔ ya wa lawuu banɛi?”
8Juda ŋɔ u mɛɛ be, “Kpa a bie du n nonee ya kaali manaŋ. Di guŋ lɛi, lɔzi daŋ kpu yaa dia naa hina maa. 9N kpa n miibɔɔrɛ di ra char u siu. N danna binnuu, wiimaa wàá wer ɛɛu. Di maa wa bittɛ ba u ni di wa tɛi, minuu u haahkɛ chug saŋa maa, di ra la. 10Di i vii sɛɛwɔɔ yaa nuu la, keŋ yaa vii jaa la ga yau a sɔgmia naa bunɛɛ maa di ba.”
11A tuna maa, Jekɔb wa ŋɔ, di gunnɛ amɔ, ba nyiŋŋi ba ge hɛri kunnaanaa di ra la ga sunzi a baal. Denii ba nyiŋŋi nuuri aŋhina dizi, huuhnuu, dɔzi tiuzaa kuna ni kunsɔɔhrisuma ani daanɔna n summɛ, di ɛɛ sirya. 12Jekɔb kaa ŋɔ, “Bɛl maa kpa kebee la baŋ faa kpawɛɛ la guŋ bunɛɛ, di bir kpa anla un nawɛɛ u bɔɔti biini la ga tɛu. Aŋhinabe, nɛbɛl faa suuhwɔ ka ɛɛ guŋ. 13Ií lau ii niwee la di ɛɛ manaŋ kaali. 14Kɔ́raawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la hiini ia, di ga gil a baal suŋ ii ni, di lizi Simɛɔn a nɛra tɔi dia, di kaa gil Bɛnjamin ge gba bir ba n be. Gunla maa an niŋ du, di ba daŋ siuwuu gɛɛ di ba waa siu, ka ɛrɛɛ n kaa ɛɛi?”
15Awia, ba jaa lau Bɛnjamin di kpa ba kunsunzaa la ge ani ba kebee bɔra anɛɛ, di yali siwee di lii di ra la Ijip hɛri. Baŋ ga hel de, ba la Joosɛf be. 16Uŋ wa na Bɛnjamin ni baa n na ba la, u ŋɔ u diahiŋ be, “N ni nɛra naabuu niŋ di diwee wibaŋa naa. Awia, lau baa di zuu dia, ka lau sel kpu di daali a diwee.” 17A baal jaa ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, di lau baa la Joosɛf dia.
18Baŋ wa hel de la, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa. Ba ŋɔ, “Kebee la baŋ bittɛ kpa du yaa bɔɔtizi biine lugli la wiarɛ la. U ra nyiŋŋuu ú lauri yaa di birgi u yoma, ka foozi yaa kauzi.” 19Baŋ ga hel Joosɛf dia dominua, ba la a diibinni be, 20di ga ŋɔ, “Yaa nabɔma, yaa n felee ba ɛŋ di wa yau sɔgmia 21di ra la la, yaa ga hel yembɛl yaa n niŋ chɔɔ, di ŋɔ ya binni yaa bɔɔtizi biine, di kebee la yaa n kpawɛɛ ba di wa turgi a sɔgmia labuu du yaa bɔɔtizi biine. Aabuu keŋ yaa bir kpa ba ya wa tɛi. 22Ama, yaa dɔɔ kebee aŋhinaa yaa n niŋ kaa kpa yau sɔgmia. Yaa waa zum gunla maa a kebee n ɛɛwɛ zuu yaa bɔɔtizi biine.”
23A diibinni la ŋɔ, “Ií gilɛɛ gil a tir ia. Aŋhinabe, Kɔraawiizi la ii ni ii mɛɛ n na hum labuu kpaa di du ii bɔɔtizi biine. N faa lɛɛ ii kebee hinnɛ, wibii maa.” Denii u ga pilli Simɛɔn di kpogluu ba ba be.
24Ka u jaa kpogli baa di zuu dia, di ga ɛɛ nii tɛɛ baa ba sanzi ba naazi, di tɛɛ ba kauzi la diwee a di. 25Baŋ wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba daŋ di diwee de la, ba ɛɛ ba kunsunzaa la sirya di ra kpaŋ Joosɛf, ú ba ba di a wibandiwee. 26Joosɛf n wa ballɛ, ba kpa a kunsunzaa zuu dia, di ga togni u see di kpaa tɛu. 27U pɛɛzi baa gunla baŋ duwɛɛ, di kaa pɛɛzi baa, “Ɛrɛɛ ii bazɛŋa duɛi? U haa du de ni miibɔɔ, di dɔɔ alaanfiaa?”
28Ba ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh nabɔma, i balii, yaa mɛɛ dɔɔ alaanfiarɛ.” Ka kaa tognuu.
29Joosɛf binni di na u niwee Bɛnjamin la n ɛɛ u maabie himmaa la, ka ŋɔ, “Ii niwee la iiŋ ŋɔ u wia labuu keŋŋ? Kɔ́raawiizi hiinii, n biibaal.” 30Denii u hahzi di lii. U niwee la wia faa sɔɔni u bɔraa werge maa, haali u ra nyiŋŋi wiraa. Uŋ ga zuu u chɔɔribɔr, u jaa ra wii.
31Uŋ wiiwe la, u sam u siwee, ka kaa lii di ba ba be, di lau u hiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “Ií kpa diwee la ba.”
32Baŋ wa ba a ni, Joosɛf so u bɛŋ, u kpɛɛnna la ge so ba bɛnaa, a Ijip hina la ge n du de la ge gba so ba bɛnaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Ijip hina faa ɔɔ ra gbɛlli Hibru hinaa, ba waa ɔɔ sɛɛ ba ni baa ra so bɔkpaŋ di ra di. 33Denii Joosɛf gil u kpɛɛnna la so hiŋ nabɔmuu guŋŋ di ga chug bichalahiŋ, ba nuu chaŋ dɔŋa. A tir baa. 34Ka ba jaa ba bɛl maa diwee ni di wa tɛu, di lii bɔr la Joosɛf n soge la. Ka Bɛnjamin diwee kaali ba bɛl maa hora lugɔ naabunue. Denii ba nuu maa so di di, ka nyɔɔ.

english_text:
The Missing Cup
1-2Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
3Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys. 4But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup? 5Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
6When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say. 7But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that! 8We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house? 9If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
10“Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
11Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it. 12Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup. 13This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
14When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph, 15who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
16“Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
17Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.”
Judah Pleads for Benjamin
18Judah went over to Joseph and said:
Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak. 19You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers. 20So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
21You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself. 22We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him. 23But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us. 24So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
25Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain. 26But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
27Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons. 28One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal, 29and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
30That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much 31that he will die if Benjamin doesn't come back with me. 32I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
33Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers. 34How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_text:
Saliŋhuŋŋu libee wia
1Joosɛf ŋɔ u diibinni be lugɔ ú ɛɛ sɔgmia di du ba bɛl maa bɔɔti biini gunla maga un niŋ wer chi, ka suahzi kpa bɛl maa kebee la uŋ turgee la di bir du u bɔɔti biini, 2ka kpa u himmaa saliŋhuŋŋu libee la di du ba bichala hiŋ la bɔɔti biini di jaa kebee la ni. Denii a diibinni ɛɛ gunla maa Joosɛf n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la. 3Bɔr n waa chaani kɔlɔkɔlɔ, u ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ, ba ni ba kauzi hiŋ chi ba bunni di ra kaali. 4Ba faa haa waa yemmaa helle, ka Joosɛf ŋɔ u diibinni la be, “Duŋŋi baala la luge manaŋ. Di i ga huuzi baa, pɛɛzi baa, ‘Ɛrɛɛ ii kpa wichɔgaa di ra turgi winanaa kimɛi? 5Bɛɛ n baani ii ŋmɛɛ n dɔɔri saliŋhuŋŋu libee la uŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra nyɔɔ nii, di kaa kpau ra vug lai? Ií na gunla biinikpola huma iiŋ hummɛ!’ ”
6Joosɛf n bagluu gunla, u izi dau ba luge di ga huuzi baa, di kpa guŋ ŋɔ. 7Ba pɛɛzi a baal, “Beedee wiarɛ i ra ŋɔ gunnɛi? Kɔraawiizi la a ni bɔɔnɛɛ alugɔ ya ɛɛ a keŋ wichɔgaa naa dɔŋ. 8Kebee la yaa n nawɛɛ yaa bɔɔtizi biine la, yaa waa bittɛ kpaa di lii Keenan hɛri di bir baa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ya ŋmɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋu gɛɛ saliŋ himmaa i dɔɔri diai? 9Di i wa na a saliŋhuŋŋu libee yaa bɛl maa be, guŋwaa, kpu a hiŋ, ka yaa ge maa birgi i yoma di hanna la.”
10A baal ŋɔ, “N nuu gunla iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛrɛ. Unla n ŋmɛɛu la bɛnnɛ niŋ birgi yom. Ka ii banla waa maa n kawɛɛ daŋ wer di ra la.” 11Denii ba chug ba bɔɔtizi ba kauzi hiŋ ni manaŋ, bɛl maa lau u hor pilli. 12Joosɛf diibinni hiŋ faari di chi ba nabɔma hiŋ la be di pigzaa di ra la. Denii u ga na a kuŋ ba bichala hiŋ Bɛnjamin bɔɔti biini. 13Uŋ wa nau Bɛnjamin be la, u kpɛɛnna la lauri ba laala di piili ni biinichɔg, ka bir vɔɔzi ba bunni di chug ba kauzi, di bir ra la a bolzeŋ.
14Joosɛf haa du dia biinii, ka Juda ni u niuna la bir ba di wa togni u see. 15U pɛɛzi baa, “Ka bɛɛ ii faa ŋɔ ii ɛɛ gunnɛi? Ií waa zummɛ lugɔ miŋ du kennaa, n daŋ wer vug di zum nɛr la n ŋmɛɛu waa?”
16Denii Juda ŋɔ, “Oo, n dɔɔri, ɛrɛɛ ya kaa ŋɔi? Ɛrɛɛ ya suŋŋɛi? Ɛrɛɛ ya ŋɔ, í zum lugɔ yaa waa u wia zummɛi? Kɔraawiizii ra tɔɔri yaa dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wia. N dɔɔri, yaa maa bittɔɔ ba ya wa birgi i yoma. Yaa ni yaa niwee la baŋ na i libee la u bɔɔti biini la maa daŋ birgi i yoma.”
17Ka Joosɛf ŋɔ, “Akai, n ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá sɛɛ ɛɛ guŋ. Unla n ŋmɛɛ kunla bɛnnɛ niŋ ɛɛ n yom. Ií banla n kawɛɛ la, iawaa daŋ wer ra la bol ii mɛɛ be ani bɔsɔna.”
18Denii Juda tuzi hel u be, di ŋɔ, “Jaande maa, n dɔɔri, di kanyitti tɛŋ, ya ŋɔ wikpaŋ tɛi. Haali hiŋ du lugɔ Ijip koori gba, ka i gilɛɛ gil i baaŋ waa fuuh n ni. 19N dɔɔri, i faa pɛɛzi yaabuu, ‘Ii dɔɔ mɛɛ gɛɛ niweeaa?’ 20Yaa ŋɔ yaa dɔɔ mɛɛrɛ u jaa zɛŋ ani yaa kalugu uŋ zɛŋŋɛ ka lul. U kpɛɛma siuwɔɔ ka kau, u bɛŋ jaa ɛɛ u maa bie. Dikuu guŋ wia, u mɛɛ nɔŋŋuubuu werge maa. 21Denii i ŋɔ ya la ga lawuu ba, í himmaa nau. 22N dɔɔri, yaa ŋɔ i be lugɔ a bie wàá wer gil u mɛɛ. Di u liwɔɔ ka kau, u daŋ siu. 23I ŋɔ lugɔ haa kaa ra nyiŋŋi i na yaa ni siwii, di yaa waa yaa niwee hiŋ ni ballɛ. 24Denii yaa n bittɛ la, yaa ga ŋɔ yaa mɛɛ be guŋ.
25U kaa ŋɔ ya bir ba wa yau diwee tama ba. 26Ka yaa ŋɔ yaa wàá wer ba, di yaa ni yaa niwee la waa haŋ ba, nabɔma la ŋɔ waa kaa ra nyiŋŋi u na yaa ni siwii. 27Yaa mɛɛ la ŋɔ, ‘Ií zummɔ lugɔ n haaŋ hiŋ biizi du banɛɛ bɛŋ. 28Ka bɛl leu, maa kaa nau. N ɛɛ tamii lugɔ sechɔgii bɛllɛ lawuu. 29Di ii kaa lau u niwee naa ge lɛɛ, wii bɛl ga huuzi u ge, ii daŋ gil biinichɔg kpuŋ.’
30N nabɔma, filaŋkennaa, màá ka wer bir la n mɛɛ be, di n ni a bie lɛi. U miibɔɔrɛ a bie. 31Di yaa laŋŋɔ, di Bɛnjamin waa hoo yaa be, n mɛɛ daŋ siu. Yaabuu niŋ gil u siu ani biinichɔg la. 32Nabɔma, n kpa n miibɔɔrɛ di char u hor, di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ n mɛɛ lugɔ di maa haŋ wa bir ba a bie ni, minuu u haahkɛ chug saŋa maa di ra la. 33Awia, jaande, nabɔma, gil miŋwaa lɛɛ u bɔr di birgi i yom, ka ú ni n lulla naa waa bir kaali. 34Di guŋ lɛi, ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ di bir la n mɛɛ be, di Bɛnjamin waa n ni jaawɛi? Akai! Gilɛɛ gil n wàá na n mɛɛ biinichɔg.”

english_text:
Joseph Tells His Brothers Who He Is
1 Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.” 2Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
3Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer. 4Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said:
Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt. 5Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
6There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain. 7But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way. 8After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
9 Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can. 10You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own. 11I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
12All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph. 13Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
14Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying. 15Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
16When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy. 17So the king said to Joseph:
Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan. 18Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there. 19Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father. 20They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
21Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered. 22Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and 300 pieces of silver. 23To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip. 24Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
25Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan, 26they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them. 27Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better 28and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_text:
Joosɛf n kpa u hiŋ bagli u kpɛɛnna wia
1A guŋ saŋa, Joosɛf faa waa kaa wer ú lau u hiŋ. Denii u ŋɔ u balaa be kpegzi ni, “Ií maa lii bossee!” Nɛr maa faa waa hoo saŋa la Joosɛf n kpa u hiŋ bagli u kpɛɛnna la. 2U jaa ra wii werge maa. Ijip hina ra nuu u wiraa, haali ba la ga ŋɔ Ijip koori be gunla n ɛɛwɛ.
3U jaa ŋɔ u kpɛɛnna la be, “Minuu Joosɛf. N mɛɛ haa du de ni miibɔɔa?” Ka u kpɛɛnna la waa kaa wer ba ŋɔ wia gba. Baŋ wa zummɛ lugɔ Joosɛfuu chigɛ ba see di ra ŋɔ wia la, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa.
4Joosɛf ŋɔ, “Ií tuzi hel n be.” Ba tuzi di heluu, u kaa ŋɔ, “Minuu ii niwee Joosɛf la iiŋ yoowe tɛɛ Ijip hina la. 5Ama, ii gilɛɛ gil a tir ia, ii ra pag iihinaa ni, dikuu iiŋ ɛɛ guŋ wia. Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ guŋ. Waabuu gillɛ n tɔ ii see di ba bɔnnaa, ya wa wer lɛɛ nɛra, bá gilɛɛ siuzi. 6Lɔzi teŋ cholloo binni anɛɛ la, ka u daŋ haa du de di ra la binni anue biini. Nɛr maa wàá ka wer par, ba wàá ŋɔ kuna kumaa wia. 7Kɔraawiizii gillɛ n tɔ ii see di ba bɔnnaa, ń wer ɛɛ wizenaa naa, di lɛɛ ii ni ii naanna maa miibɔɔni. 8Wibii maa, ia lɛi ba n ni, Kɔraawiizii ba n ni bɔnnaa, haali di gil n birgi nɛr la n ɛɛ nabɔma, di ra hiŋ Ijip koori ni, di ra binni u dia kummaa ani Ijip hɛri maa ni.
9Ií la manaŋ di ga ŋɔ n mɛɛ be lugɔ kenne u biibaal Joosɛf ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n birgi Ijip hɛri maa nabɔma. Awia, ú ba manaŋ, u gilɛɛ waa birgi. 10U ni u biizi ni u naanna ni u kundɛɛzaa maa daŋ wa so Gɔsɛn di dugliŋ. 11N danna binni i ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, a lɔchɔgii daŋ haa di binni anue di jaa anɛɛ naa n bɛrɛɛ naa ni. Maa nyiŋŋi lɔzi ra kpu i diahina maa.’ ”
12Denii Joosɛf kaa ŋɔ, “Ii himmaa ani n niwee Bɛnjamin gba binniŋ na. Ií daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Joosɛf, wibii maa. 13Ií ga ŋɔ n mɛɛ be gunla miŋ ɛɛ nabɔma Ijip hɛri. Ií bagli wia la maa iin nawɛɛ tɛu, ka gil u ba n be manaŋ.”
14Denii u ga faami Bɛnjamin kpogli, di ra wii ni bɔsɔna, u ge gba faamuu ka ra wii. 15Gunnɛ u ra wii ka faami u kpɛɛnna la maa guŋŋ di wa kaali. Uŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ, u ni baa haa wer ra ŋɔ wia.
16Filaŋkeŋ maa, di a amaniye teŋ hel Ijip kooridia lugɔ Joosɛf kpɛɛnna ballɔɔ. Ijip koori ni u nabɔnzi bɔra faa sɔɔni guŋ wia werge maa. 17Denii Ijip koori ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Gil i kpɛɛnna kpa sɔgmia chug ba kauzi manaŋ, di bir la Keenan hɛri. 18Gil ba ga kpogli i mɛɛ ani u diahina maa, bá wa so Ijip hɛri bɔnnaa. Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ mìŋ́ Ijip koori daŋ tɛɛ baa Ijip hɛrnanii ba so, di ra di a hɛri suma.
19Kali i kpɛɛnna hiŋ, bá kpa zagra ni torkozi di lii Ijip hɛri bɔnnaa, di ga kpogli ba haana ni ba biizi ani i mɛɛ di ba. 20Ba daŋ wer gil ba kundɔɔlaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, apazi la maa n du Ijip hɛri la daŋ wa ɛɛ ba hora.”
21Denii Jekɔb biibaala la ɛɛ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. Joosɛf kpa a zagra torkozi di tɛɛ baa gunla Ijip koori n baglɛɛ la. Di kaa tɛɛ baa diwee la ban ninna di ŋmɛnɛɛ. 22Denii u kaa tɛɛ ba bɛl maa kunlaalifalaa. Di tɛɛ Bɛnjamin waa laala bɔra anue ani saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaahoro.
23U kaa vɔɔzi kunnanaa werge maa n du Ijip hɛri di chug kauzi fi. Kauzi fi ge kaa chi mia ni paanuu ani diuirizi maa, bá ga tɛɛ u mɛɛ, di ba wa lii ŋmɛnɛɛ di ra ba Ijip hɛri, ba kpa ra hiini ba hiŋ. 24Denii u jaa ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ, ka karfi baa, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ra dazi ii waa naa ŋmɛnɛɛ!”
25Ba jaa lii Ijip hɛri di kaali ba mɛɛ be Keenan hɛri. 26Baŋ ga helle, ba ŋɔ Jekɔb be, “Joosɛf haa du denii ni miibɔɔ, haali di ɛɛ nɛzeŋ di ra binni Ijip hɛri maa.” Jekɔb n wa nuu guŋ, u nua kpu, waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ wibiire.
27Ka baŋ wa baglɛɛ gunla maa Joosɛf n ŋɔwɛɛ, u ge kaa na torkozi la uŋ gillɛ ba kpa ba, bá wa hiinuu la Ijip hɛri la, u siwee jaa ba hɛri. 28Denii Jekɔb ŋɔ, “N jaa zumuu lugɔ wibii maa, Joosɛf haa du denii ni miibɔɔ. Guŋwaa n daŋ la ga nau mɔɔ ka siu.”

english_text:
Jacob and His Family Go to Egypt
1Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped. 2That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!”
“Here I am,” Jacob answered.
3God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation. 4I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
5-7 Jacob and his family set out from Beersheba and headed for Egypt. His sons put him in the wagon that the king had sent for him, and they put their small children and their wives in the other wagons. Jacob's whole family went to Egypt, including his sons, his grandsons, his daughters, and his granddaughters. They took along their animals and everything else they owned.
8-15When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families.
Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of 33 children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, but two of their grandchildren had died in Canaan.
Their oldest son Reuben took his sons Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Their son Simeon took his sons Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, whose mother was a Canaanite.
Their son Levi took his sons Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Their son Judah took his sons Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Judah's sons Er and Onan had died in Canaan. Judah's son Perez took his sons Hezron and Hamul.
Their son Issachar took his sons Tola, Puvah, Jashub, and Shimron.
Their son Zebulun took his sons Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
Their daughter Dinah also went.
16-18Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of 16 children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren.
Their son Gad took his sons Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
Their son Asher took his sons Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, who took his sons, Heber and Malchiel.
Serah, the daughter of Asher, also went.
19-22 Jacob and Rachel had 14 children and grandchildren.
Their son Joseph was already in Egypt, where he had married Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, the priest of Heliopolis. Joseph and Asenath had two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
Jacob and Rachel's son Benjamin took his sons Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
23-25Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren.
Their son Dan took his son Hushim.
Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
26Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law. 27 Jacob's two grandsons who were born there made it a total of 70 members of Jacob's family in Egypt.
28Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen. 29So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time. 30Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
31Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them:
I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan. 32I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own. 33The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living. 34When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen.
Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_text:
Jekɔb n la Ijip hɛri wia
1Jekɔb ɛɛ sirya manaŋ, di kpa kunla maa un dɔɔwɛ di ra la Ijip hɛri. Uŋ ga hel bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba, u kpu sela tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la u mɛɛ Aizik n faa ra hum la, di lizi mbusu.
2Kɔraawiizi ba u be lugɔ deeza biini hamuŋa ni, di wa yiruu, “Jekɔb! Jekɔb!”
Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Minuu keŋ.”
3Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Minuu Kɔraawiizi, minuu i mɛɛ Aizik faa ra hum la. Gilɛɛ ra ɔm Ijip hɛri laŋaa. N daŋ du i be, di ga hiinii de, í dee wazi di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa. 4N daŋ tɔ i see í ga zuu Ijip hɛri, di kaa wa bir lizi i nɛra lii Ijip hɛri, di bir ba ba ni Keenan hɛri naa. Joosɛf daŋ na i tuna.”
5Denii Jekɔb lii bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba. U biibaala kpa a zagra ni torkozi la Ijip koori n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ baa ba la, di paa ba mɛɛ ni ba haana ni ba biizi di du a biine. 6Ba sela ani kuna la maa baŋ faa dɔɔwɛ lii Keenan hɛri la maanii ba faa kpa di ra la Ijip hɛri. Gunnɛ a faa ɛɛ Jekɔb ni u dee maa faa la Ijip hɛri. 7U biizi ni u naanna, baala ni haana faa jaa u ni, ba maa la a hɛri.
8Jekɔb dee la n izee la Ijip hɛri la sɔnaa keŋ,
Rubinnɛ faa u biinabɔma.
9Rubin ge biibaalaa faa,
Hanɔk, Palu, Hɛzrɔn ani Kaami.
10Simɛɔn ge biibaalaa faa,
Jɛmuɛl, Jamin, Ɔhad, Jakin, Zɔha, di faa kpa Sual. Sual naawaa maa faa ɛɛ Keenan hinuurɛ.
11Levi ge biibaalaa faa,
Gɛsɔn, Kɔhaf ani Mɛrari.
12U biibaal Juda ge biibaalaa faa,
Ɛr, Ɔnan, Sɛla, Pɛrɛz ani Zɛra.
Ama, Ɛr la ni Ɔnan maanii faa siuwɛ Keenan hɛri.
Pɛrɛz ge biibaalaa faa,
Hɛzrɔn ani Hamul.
13Isaka ge biibaalaa faa,
Tola, Pua, Jasub ani Simrɔn.
14Zɛbulɔn ge biibaalaa faa,
Sɛrɛd, Ɛlɔn ani Jaliil.
15Biibaala la Jekɔb ni u haaŋ Lia n lullɛ Mɛsɔpɔtemia labuu faa la, di kpa ba niuhambie Daina jaa, ba ge faa du tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni bahoro.
16Gad biibaalaa faa,
Zɛfɔn, Hagi, Suni, Ɛzbɔn, Ɛri, Arɔd ani Arɛli.
17Asɛ ge biibaalaa faa,
Imna, Isva, Isvi
ani Bɛria.
Ba ra yir ba niuhambie Sɛra.
Bɛria ge biibaalaa faa,
Hɛba ani Malkiɛl.
18Ba nɛra fidibanumbɛl naa genii faa ɛɛ Jekɔb ni u haaŋ Zilpa biibaala. Zilpa naa faa ɛɛ balii la Lia mɛɛ Laban n faa kpawɛɛ tɛu labuu.
19Jekɔb ni u haaŋ Rachɛl ge biibaalaa faa,
Joosɛf ani Bɛnjamin. 20Joosɛf ge biibaala un lullɛ Ijip hɛrii faa Manasɛ ani Ɛfram. Ba maarɛ faa Hɛliɔpɔlis vug Ɔɔn kizeehiŋ Pɔtifɛra biihaaŋ Asɛnaf.
21Bɛnjamin ge biibaalaa faa
Bɛla, Bɛka, Asbɛl, Gɛra, Naaman, Ɛhi, di kaa kpa Rɔs, Mupim, Hupim ani Aad.
22A biibaala fidibanaazu naabuu Jekɔb ni u haaŋ Rachɛl faa lul.
23Dan ge biibaallɛ faa,
Husim.
24Naftali ge biibaalaa faa,
Jaziɛl, Guni, Jɛza
ani Silɛm.
25Jekɔb ani Bilha la Laban n faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ u biihaaŋ la biibaalaa faa la. Ba ge faa du nɛra baniidaanɛɛ.
26Jekɔb dee la n faa la Ijip hɛrii la. Ba faa du nɛra tokkoahoro ni banumbɛl. U biiziwaa haana faa waa jaawɛ. 27Biizi banɛɛrɛ Joosɛf ge faa lul Ijip hɛri di jaa. Ba maa kpau faa ɛɛ nɛra tokkoahoro ni fi, di ɛɛ Jekɔb diahina la n la Ijip hɛri.
28Denii Jekɔb hum Juda ú tɔ see di ga huuzi Joosɛf, ú bagluu Gɔsɛn bɔr. Baŋ wa hel de, 29Joosɛf zuu u zagra torko, di la ga chem u mɛɛ ni de. Baŋ wa chem dɔŋa ni, Joosɛf la ga faami u mɛɛ, ka jaa wii birgi.
30Denii Jekɔb ŋɔ u be, “N jaa ɛɛ siryaa ń siu filaŋkeŋ, dikuu n himmaa n nai ni siwii, di zum lugɔ i haa du denii ni miibɔɔ wia.”
31Joosɛf bir ŋɔ u kpɛɛnna ni ba nɛra la maa be, “N daŋ bir la ga kali Ijip koori be lugɔ ii jaa lii Keenan hɛrii di ba n be. 32N daŋ kaa ŋɔ u be lugɔ ii ɛɛ senɔɔnaa, di ra dɛɛzi sela. Awia, ii kpa ii peeza, buuna, nauna ani kunla maa iin dɔɔwɛɛ di ba. 33Awia, di Ijip koori haŋ wa yir ia, di pɛɛzi huma la iinna hum, 34ií kaluu lugɔ ii ni ii naabaala maa humaa sela dɛɛzaa, ii de dui maa. Di ii wa ŋɔ u be guŋ, guŋwaa, u daŋ gil ii so Gɔsɛn hɛri naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Ijip hina faa ra gbɛlli senɔɔnaa.”

english_text:
1-2Joseph took five of his brothers to the king and told him, “My father and my brothers have come from Canaan. They have brought their sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else they own to the region of Goshen.”
Then he introduced his brothers to the king, 3who asked them, “What do you do for a living?”
“Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep. 4But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
5The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived. 6I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
7Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing, 8and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
9Jacob answered, “I have lived only 130 years, and I have had to move from place to place. My parents and my grandparents also had to move from place to place. But they lived much longer, and their life was not as hard as mine.” 10Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left. 11Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses. 12Joseph also provided food for their families.
A Famine in Egypt
13The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly. 14So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury. 15But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
16“If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.” 17From then on, they brought him their horses and donkeys and their sheep and goats in exchange for grain.
Within a year Joseph had collected every animal in Egypt. 18Then the people came to him and said:
Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land. 19Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
20The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king 21and made everyone the king's slaves, 22except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land. 23Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant, 24but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
25“Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.” 26Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land.
Jacob Becomes an Old Man
27The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families. 28Jacob himself lived there for 17 years, before dying at the age of 147. 29 When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt. 30Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.”
“I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
31“Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked.
“Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_text:
1Denii Joosɛf la Ijip koori be di ga ŋɔ, “N mɛɛ ni n kpɛɛnna lii Keenan hɛrii di ba. Haali ba peeza ni ba nauna ni kuna la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛ maanii ballɛ, di wa du Gɔsɛn hɛri.” 2Joosɛf faa lau u kpɛɛnna banuere ga bagli Ijip koori.
3Ijip koori pɛɛzi baa, “Beedee humaa ii ra hummɛi?”
Ba ŋɔ, “Jara, yaa ɛɛ senɔɔnaa. 4Yaa ballɔɔ ya wa du Ijip hɛri, di wer na diwee ra di. Lɔzi la nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ Keenan hɛri, yaa sela ge waa kaa na diwee di ra di. Awia, yaa ra suŋŋiibuu í gil ya so Gɔsɛn hɛri.”
5Ijip koori jaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Filaŋkeŋ, i mɛɛ ni i kpɛɛnna ba i benii bɔnnaa. 6Hinuu dɔɔ a Ijip hɛri naa maa. Nyiŋŋi u bɔnanii tɛɛ baa ba so. Gɔsɛn hɛrii wesse. Gil ba ga so de. I daŋ kaa wer binni ba biini, di lizi banla n zum huma nɛnnɛ, di gil ba waa nɔɔni n gba sela ra tɛŋ.”
7Denii Joosɛf faa gil u mɛɛ Jekɔb ge ga jaami Ijip koori. Jekɔb faa kissuu. 8Ijip koori pɛɛzuu, “I binni du aŋmɛnɛi?”
9Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Binni kalfa ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔɔ n di hɛri naa. Ka n haa waa binnɛ hel gunla n naabaala n faa binnɛ la. N di dɔgnyaa a bintama naa maa biini.” 10Uŋ wa ŋɔ ú lii Ijip koori be, u kaa kissuu mɔɔ ka haa kaali.
11Awia, Joosɛf faa jaa binni Ijip hɛri bɔnanii n dugli bol bɛl banna yir Ramɛsis, di faa kpa de di tɛɛ u mɛɛ ni u kpɛɛnna ba so, gunla Ijip koori n ŋɔwɛɛ la. 12Ka faa jaa kpa diwee werge maa tɛɛ baa, gunla maga n niŋ wer hel ba ni ba biizi maa nɛnnɛ.
13Annii n na ɛɛ naa, di lɔzi faa haa ra nyaŋŋi werge Ijip ani Keenan hɛssi maa. Diwee faa waa hoo, lɔzi ra kpu nɛra, ba ra huahgi bɔr maa. 14Joosɛf lɛɛ diwee la ban faa yoowe la kebee maa di lii Ijip ni Keenan hɛssi, di faa kpaa la Ijip kooridia. 15Ka Ijip ani Keenan hina n waa kaa wa dɔɔ kebee ba yau diwee, Ijip hina ba Joosɛf be, di wa wii ra duu, di ŋɔ, “Tɛɛ yaa diwee ya di! Di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ siuzi. Yaa waa kaa dɔɔ kebee ya yau diwee di.”
16Denii Joosɛf ŋɔ ba be, “Iiŋ waa kebee dɔɔwɛ ii yau naa, amɔ, ii lauri ii sela di waa char a diwee.” 17Awia, ba lauri ba zagra, peeza, buuna, nauna ani ba kauzi di waa char a diwee Joosɛf be. Ama, a bina hiŋwaa biini, ba wettoo kpa ba kundɛɛzaa chɛr diwee di.
18Ka bina bɛl n kaa wa hel, ba kaa ba Joosɛf be di wa ŋɔ, “Wiimaa waa hoo yaa n niŋ wer kpa suah i ni, yaa nabɔma. Yaa kebee maanii tunnɛ, yaa sela la maa gba kaa birgi i hora. Awia, yaa waa kaa dɔɔ kummaa, di yaa bɔrahɔna ni yaa hɛssi naa bɛŋ lɛi. 19Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ í ra binni yaa ka ya siuzɛi? Awia, yau yaa ni yaa hɛri naa maa, yá ɛɛ Ijip koori yoma, ka í tɛɛ yaa diwee ya di. Tɛɛ yaa kundee ya kpa a yeŋ di, ka kpa a yeŋ ga duu yaa hɛssi, á gilɛɛ chɔɔ pɛɛ, ya ge gilɛɛ siuzi.”
20Denii Joosɛf faa yau Ijip hɛri maa u birgi Ijip koori hor. Ijip hina la maa faa yoo ba kooni tɛɛ Ijip koori, dikuu lɔzi n faa nyaŋŋi baa werge maa wia. Gunnɛ a ɛɛ a hɛri maa birgi Ijip koori hor. 21Joosɛf kaa gil a nɛra la maa n du a hɛri yemmaa la ge birgi u yoma. 22Hɛssi la bɛŋ uŋ faa waa yauwɛ Ijip hɛri biinii faa kizeehina hɛssi, dikuubɛɛwiai, Ijip koori faa ɔɔ ra tɛɛ baawaarɛ diwee. Gunnɛ baani ba waa ba hɛssi yoowe.
23Joosɛf ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Miŋ yau ii ni ii hɛri zinaa di tɛɛ Ijip koori filaŋkennaa, kundeere keŋ, ií kpa duu a hɛri. 24Di ii wa kpa ii diwee, ií lizi a bɔra anue bɔkpaŋ di tɛɛ Ijip koori, ka a bɔr la n kawɛɛ lawaa, a daŋ birgi ii kundee ni ii diwee.”
25Ba ŋɔ, “Ii lɛɛ yaa miibɔɔnii. Gil yaa wia parii, nabɔma. Yaa daŋ ɛɛ Ijip koori yoma.”
26Awia, Joosɛf dau guŋ, u ɛɛ gbɔg Ijip hɛri. Haali ni zinaa, pattikuna bɔra anue bɔkpaŋ haa ɛɛ Ijip koori hotte. Kizeehina hɛssi bɛnnɛ waa Ijip koori hor ɛɛwɛ.
27Denii Izrɛl hina la so Ijip hɛri, Gɔsɛn paga. Ba na kuna de, di ra lul di wazi.
28Jekɔb so Ijip hɛri binni fidaaniidaanɛɛ, u de dui binni faa du kalfa ni tokkoanɛɛ ni aniidaanɛɛ. 29U siu n waa dugli, u yir u biibaal Joosɛf, di ŋɔ u be, “Di n wia parii, kpa i nonii du n naapɔg zɛɛ, di ŋɔ nua tɛŋ lugɔ i daŋ ɛɛŋ winanaa, di gil i wia dɔɔ wibii. Gilɛɛ waa hugiŋ Ijip hɛri, 30ka di n wa siuwɔ, kpaŋ lii Ijip hɛri, di ga hugiŋ n mɛɛwaa hugribɔr.”
Joosɛf ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛ guŋ.”
31U mɛɛ ŋɔ, “Hɛɛhzi tɛŋ.” Denii Joosɛf hɛɛhzi tɛu. Jekɔb jaa pi u daŋkpala ni di jaami Kɔraawiizi.

english_text:
Jacob Blesses Joseph's Two Sons
1Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. 2When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
3 Jacob told Joseph:
God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing 4and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
5Then Jacob went on to say:
Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine. 6Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh. 7 Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
8-10Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?”
Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.”
“Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
