Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles. 2I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
3Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said:
How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me. 4Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts 5that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees. 6Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country.
After Moses left the palace, 7the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
8The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
9“Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
10The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good. 11Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
12The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
13Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts 14 were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many. 15The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
16At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. 17Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
18Moses left the palace and prayed. 19Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt, 20but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go.
Darkness
21 The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.” 22 Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days. 23During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
24The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
25“No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God, 26and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
27This time the Lord made the king so stubborn 28that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
29“Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_text:
Lotorozi wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “La Ijip koori be, n gillɔɔ u ni u nabɔnzi la digna du kpeg, ka ń wer ɛɛ wizenaa wia naa ba baaŋ, 2ii ŋmɛnɛ wa ŋɔ ii biizi ni ii naanna be, gunla miŋ faa tɔɔri Ijip hina ani gunla miŋ ɛɛ wizenaa ba baaŋ di ŋmaabi baa, ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”
3Awia, Moosis ni Aarɔn kpa la a koori be, di ga ŋɔ u be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Hibru hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ á birgi magɛi, ka i haa sɔɔni siwii tɛnnɛi? Tɛɛ n nɛra ŋmɛnɛɛ bá kaali di gaa jaamiŋ. 4Di i vɛɛwɔ lugɔ ba gilɛɛ kaali, n daŋ kɛrɛ gil lotorozi ba i hɛri. 5A daŋ tɔ i hɛri maa ni, hàá ka wer na u yemmaa. A daŋ di diutama la maa n kawɛɛ di lii dobee wiilchɔgii la har, haali daazi la maa n du kooni gba. 6A daŋ wa suugi i ni i nabɔnzi ni i nɛra maa diini. Wii la i mɛɛwaa gɛɛ i naabaala ŋmɛnɛ maa n haa waa nawɛɛ ba hɛri naa, ba de dui maa, di wa lii zinaa.’ ” Denii Moosis gil a koori ka kaali.
7A koori nabɔnzi la ŋɔ u be, “Ɛrɛɛ baal naa tɔɔri yaa birgi magɛi? Gil a nɛra kaali, di gaa jaami Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la. Haa zummɛ lugɔ Ijip hɛri chɔkkɔɔwaa?”
8Awia, ba bir yir Moosis ni Aarɔn, ba ba Ijip koori see, u ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ra la gaa jaami Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Ka ii babɛlaarɛ n niŋ lanɛi?”
9Moosis ŋɔ u be, “Yaa nabɔnzi ni bichalli maanii niŋ kaali, yaa biibambizi ni biihambizi ni yaa sela maanii niŋ kaali, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa daŋ ga di hɔpizizeŋ di tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi.”
10Ijip koori ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi la ii ni, ka màá tɛɛ ii ni ii haana ni ii biizi maa ŋmɛnɛɛ ií kaali, wibii maa, ii dɔɔ nfɛrchɔgaarɛ. 11Akai! Ií baala bɛŋ la ga jaami Kɔraawiizi, guŋ lɛi ii ra suŋŋiaa?” Denii ba jaa duŋŋi Moosis ni Aarɔn lii a koori be.
12Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Tɛr i nonii guali Ijip hɛri ni, lótorozi la lii tɔ a hɛri maa ni, di di ba pattikuna maa n du ba kooni ani kuna la maa a dobee n faa waa chɔkkɛ la.”
13Denii Moosis lalli u daŋkpala guali Ijip hɛri ni, Kɔraawiizi gil pezeŋ bɛl lii wiifurii di ba a hɛri, di chi chɔɔzi di ta guŋŋ hɔɔ kaa wa pizi. Hɔɔŋ wàá pizi, di u ba a lotorozi ni, 14a wa tɔ Ijip hɛri maa di su bɔr maa milmilmil. Lotorozi naa dɔŋ ŋmɛnɛ haa waa ballɛ gɛɛ a ŋmɛnɛ wàá ka ba. 15A tɔ a hɛri maa u jaa bir biri guŋ tuum, di di kuna la dobee la n faa waa chɔkkɛ la maa, kuna la maa n faa du de di ra hel ani daazi nɔna maa. Kummaa paŋhoo faa waa kaa ka, Ijip hɛri yemmaa.
16A koori ɛɛ manaŋ di gil ba yir Moosis ni Aarɔn ba ba, u ŋɔ ba be, “N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu ii ni Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la maa ni. 17Awia, annii waa be, ií gil n wichɔgaa tɛŋ ka suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, ú lizi wiilchɔgii naa n ni.” 18Moosis lii Ijip koori be di ga suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi. 19Denii Kɔraawiizi jaa gil peu la bir du kpeg di ta lii wiicholii di ra la wiifurii, di paa a lotorozi maa kaali ga du Muuzeŋaahmu la biini. A bɛl maa faa waa kaa ka Ijip hɛri. 20Ka Kɔraawiizi haa gil Ijip koori digna du kpeg, waa sɛɛwɛ ú tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛɛ bá kaali.
Bɔbiri wia
21Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Lalli i nonii tɛr chiŋ, bɔbiri werge ba wa tɔ Ijip hɛri maa, limpiriŋ.” 22Denii Moosis jaa lalli u nonii tɛr chiŋ, a bɔbiri ba wa tɔ a Ijip hɛri maa limpiriŋ, guŋŋ hɔpizaa ahoro. 23Nɛr maa waa kaa wer ú na u dɔŋhiŋ gɛɛ ú kaa wer lii u dia la yemmaa, a hɔpizaa ahoro hiŋ biini. Ka Izrɛl hina la waa duuribɔra la maa chaani.
24Ijip koori yir Moosis di ga ŋɔ ú be, “Ií la gaa jaami Kɔraawiizi. Ií kpogli ii haana ni biizi maa di ra la, ka gil ii sela waa maa.”
25Ka Moosis ŋɔ u be, “A dɛkkɔɔ yaa n dɔɔ sela ga lizi mbusuzi ani mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum. 26Yaa kundɛɛzaa la gba maa daŋ hiŋ yaa la, kpaŋkpaŋ maa wàá ka har, haali naafirii gba. Yaa daŋ ga lizi a sela aŋhina di jaami Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la, ka di de lɛi yaa hel, yaa wàá wer zum sela la dizi yaa n niŋ kpa jaamuu.”
27Ka Kɔraawiizi haa gil Ijip koori digna du kpeg, waa sɛɛwɛ ú tɛɛ baa ŋmɛnɛɛ bá kaali. 28Ijip koori ŋɔ Moosis be, “Leu n siwee! Gilɛɛ kaa gil n siwii waa nai maa! A hɔl la min niŋ kaa nai, n daŋ kpui!” 29Moosis ŋɔ u be, “Kennaa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa waa, n ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka ba i be.”

english_text:
Moses Warns the Egyptians That the Lord Will Kill Their First-Born Sons
1The Lord said to Moses:
I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out. 2Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
3So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
4Moses went to the king and said:
I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt, 5and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die. 6Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
7But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you. 8Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave.
Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
9What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.” 10So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_text:
Biibambilugla siu wia
1Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii, “N daŋ kaa tɛr Ijip hina ni ba koori digna kakpaŋ. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, u daŋ tɛɛ ia ŋmɛnɛɛ ii lii ɛŋ kaali. Wibii maa, ii maanii ú duŋŋi lii ɛŋ. 2Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ baal gɛɛ haaŋ maa suŋŋi saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋu kuna lii u dɔŋhiŋ Ijip hinuu be.” 3Kɔraawiizi jaa gil Izrɛl hina wia par Ijip hina. Moosis ge faa ɛɛ nɛtɔg Ijip koori nabɔnzi ni a nɛra maa be.
4Denii Moosis ŋɔ a koori be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Hɛhhɛɛhzi ni, n daŋ gaagi Ijip hɛri maa. 5Ijip hina biibambilugla maa daŋ siuzi, di lii koori biibambilugli la n niŋ ŋmɛnɛ wa di kora la ga hel yoŋhaaŋ la n na nam sau la biibambilugli. Ba sela lugli biibala ge maa daŋ siuzi. 6Chɛɛhgaa werge maa daŋ wa tɔ Ijip hɛri maa, di kaali gunla baŋ faa ra chɛɛhgi gɛɛ baŋ ŋmɛnɛ n haa waa chɛɛhgɛɛ. 7Ama, Izrɛl hinuu maa wàá wii gɛɛ nuahiŋ gba wozi baa.’ Gunnɛ hìŋ́ koori ni i nɛra chi di zum lugɔ Ijip ni Izrɛl hina wia kuttɔɔ Kɔraawiizi be. 8Ií nabɔnzi naa maa daŋ ba n be di wa togni suŋŋiŋ di ŋɔ, ‘Kpogli i nɛra maa lii kaali!’ A saŋaa n jaa lii ni n nɛra maa di kaali.” Denii Moosis baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u lii a koori be.
9Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii, “Ijip koori wàá nuu gunla hin niŋ ŋɔ u be la, guŋ gil ń wer ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia Ijip hɛri, di jaa.” 10Moosis ni Aarɔn faa ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia la maa, Ijip koori see, ka Kɔraawiizi faa gil a koori digna du kpeg, waa sɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la ŋmɛnɛɛ bá lii u hɛri kaali.

english_text:
The Passover
1 Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
2This month is to be the first month of the year for you. 3Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat. 4-5If any family is too small to eat the whole animal, they must share it with their next-door neighbors. Choose either a sheep or a goat, but it must be a one-year-old male that has nothing wrong with it. And it must be large enough for everyone to have some of the meat.
6Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed. 7Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten. 8That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast. 9Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted. 10Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left. 11When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
12That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt. 13The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
14 Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor. 15For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel. 16Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
17Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year. 18Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day. 19During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel. 20Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
21Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said:
Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover. 22Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
23 During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
24-25After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year. 26Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?” 27And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.”
After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord. 28Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do.
Death for the First-Born Sons
29 At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
30That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead.
The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
31During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked. 32Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
33The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.” 34So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
35 The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes. 36The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
37The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about 600,000 of them, not counting women and children. 38Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle. 39They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
40-41 The Lord's people left Egypt exactly 430 years after they had arrived. 42On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord.
Instructions for Passover
43The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover:
Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
44Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised, 45but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
46 The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration.
No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken. 47And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
48If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal! 49This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
50The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them. 51And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_text:
Gillikaali wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, Ijip hɛri, 2“Baagu naabuu niŋ ɛɛ ii bina maa lugli baagu. 3Kali Izrɛl hina maa be lugɔ baagu naa, u hɔpizaa fi hɔl, baal maa daŋ lau pepɔl gɛɛ bupɔl kpu tɛɛ u ni u diahina maa. 4Di dia bɛl maa nɛra waa kpil alugɔ bá wer hee sebir, a diahina ni dia la maa n dugli baa daŋ wer kpu sekpaŋ di bɔnni dɔŋa, a hel baa, gunla maga bɛl maa n niŋ wer hee. 5Sela la maa iin niŋ lizi la dɛkkɔɔ á du kpeg di di bina bir, a daŋ wer ɛɛ pebala gɛɛ bubala. 6Ií ra binni a ni nɛnnɛ di ra ba a baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ hɔl la. A duaninsɔnnɛ Izrɛl hina maa kpua. 7A diini la biine ban niŋ hee a ola la, bá ɛɛ a challi di fɔg a bossee dominuuzi gbessi kɛraa ni a chine daazi. 8A hɔl hamuŋa hiŋ, bɛl maa daŋ ɔɔzi a ol, di kpa tagkpola ani paanuu la baŋ waa yiisi duwɛɛ jaa a ni, di hee. 9Ií gilɛɛ waa hee a olhuu gɛɛ u daalii. Ka ii ɔɔzi u maa, haali u nyuu, u gballi ani u biini kuna maa jaa. 10Ií gilɛɛ waa gil a yemmaa wa ka hɔɔ wàá pizi, di a yeŋ wa kawɔɔ, ií fuuah. 11Kenne dɛkkɛ ii dia, ii kirsi ii tagtajaŋra, di du ii gawa, di kpa ii daŋkpalli kpogli alugɔ iinna la ŋmɛnɛɛ la, di ra dia manamanaŋ. Kɔraawiizi Gillikaali diweere.
12A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋaa ń wa gaagi Ijip hɛri biini, di kpuuzi ba biibambilugla ani ba sela ge biilugla. N daŋ tɛr Ijip hɛri vuga maa digna. Minuu Kɔraawiizi. 13Challi labuu niŋ bagli diini la biini iin duwɛɛ. Di n wa na a challi, n daŋ gilli ii ni kaali. Di n wàá tɛr Ijip hina digna, wichɔgii maa wàá huuzi ia.
14Ií ɔɔ ra di a hɔpizii naa di ra tɔgzuu, di gil ú ɛɛ hɔpizizeŋ tɛɛ ii naanna, ba ɔɔ ra diu di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi, ú ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ baa di hanna la. 15Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ biini, ií ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ. A lugli hɔpizii la, bɛ́l maa lizi yiisi maa lii u dia, dikuubɛɛwiai, di nɛr maa haŋ wa di diwii la maa n dɔɔ yiisi, di lii a lugli hɔpizii di ra la a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la, bá lizuu Izrɛl hina biini. 16Ií gil a lugli hɔpizii hiŋ ɛɛ hɔpizii la iin niŋ ɔɔ chaali jaamiŋ. Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la ge, ií kaa jaamiŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma a hɔpizaa naa bɛl maa biini. Ii wiɛɛlii maanii ií ɔɔ daali diwee tɛɛ nɛra maa, bá di.
17Ií ɔɔ ra di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizeŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɔpizii naabuu n lizi ii dizi maa lii Ijip hɛri. Awia, ii ɔɔ ra diu saŋa maa, di gil ú ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ii naanna di hanna la. 18A lugli baagu la biini, ii gilɛɛ waa hee paanuu la baŋ du yiisi, di lii a baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ la duana ni, di ra la u hɔpizaa tokko ni kpaŋ la ge duana ni. 19A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ, bɛ́l maa gilɛɛ waa gil yiisi ra du u dia. Di nɛr maa haŋ wa di kummaa n dɔɔ yiisi a ni, di hɔɔhrii gɛɛ di bol biere, ba daŋ lizuu Izrɛl hina biini. 20Ií gilɛɛ waa hee kummaa n dɔɔ yiisi. Bɔr la maa iin duwɛɛ, ií ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la baŋ waa yiisi duwɛɛ.”
21Denii Moosis chaali Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi maa, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií izi la manaŋ, di ga lizi ii sela la tɛɛ ii diini hina, bá kpu di di Gillikaali. 22Bɛ́l maa mɔŋ daa bɛl banna yir hisɔp, di kpa lii u sel chal n du tassazeŋ biini, di kpa fɔg u bossee dominua kɛraa ni u chiŋ daazi la maa. Ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ kaa wàá lii u dia a hɔl hiŋ di hɔɔ waa pizɛɛ lɛi. 23Di Kɔraawiizi wa gaagɔɔ di ra chɔgi Ijip hina la, u daŋ wa na challi la n fɔg ii dominuuzi chine ani kɛraa daazi la ni. Di u wa naa guŋ, u daŋ gilli ii ni kaali, wàá sɛɛ mɛlika la n na kpu la zuu a diini di kpu nɛr maa.
24Ií ni ii biizi ni ii naanna maa ra hiŋ Gillikaali wia la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa, di gil á ɛɛ widaulaa ií ra hiŋaa saŋa maa. 25Di ii wa zuu hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ia la, ii haa ra liizi a widaulaa naa di ra ɛɛa. 26Di ii biizi wa pɛɛzi ia, ‘A Hɔpizizeŋ naa dii zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ?’ 27Ií ŋɔ ba be lugɔ u ɛɛ Gillikaali mbusuzi yaa ra lizi di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Dikuu uŋ faa gilli yaa Izrɛl hina n faa du Ijip hɛri diini ni di kaali, ka waa yaa ɛɛwɛ wiimaa, ka kpuuzi Ijip hina la waa wia.” Denii a nɛra jaa giŋŋi jaami Kɔraawiizi. 28Izrɛl hina la sɛɛ, di ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be la.
29A hɔl hɛhhɛɛhzi ni, Kɔraawiizi ba di wa kpuuzi Ijip hina biibambilugla maa, di lii Ijip koori biibambilugli la n niŋ ŋmɛnɛ wa di kora la ga hel banla baŋ tɔ dia la gba biibambilugla ani ba sela biilugla maa. 30Ijip koori ni u hɛri nabɔnzi la maa ani Ijip hina maa izi a hamuŋa ni, ba chɛɛhgaa werge maa tɔ Ijip hɛri maa, dia maa waa hoo di nɛr waa siuwɛ.
Ijip hɛri lii wia
31A hɔl hamuŋa ni, Ijip koori yir Moosis ni Aarɔn, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ga kpogli Izrɛl hina maa lii n hɛri! Ií ra la gaa jaami Kɔraawiizi gunla iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. 32Ií kpa ii sela maa gunla iiŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ la di ra la. Ka ií suŋŋi wiizi ú kissiŋ.”
33Ijip hina la jaa ra fɔrgi a nɛra dí ba ɛɛ manaŋ di lii ba hɛri, di ŋɔ, “Di guŋ lɛi, yaa maa daŋ siuzi!” 34Awia, Izrɛl hina kpa ba saŋmittaa n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ di du hɛnni la banna ŋmiraa la biine, di kpa wɛjɛzi fɔɔzaa, di kpaa sagzi ba baŋaazi. 35Izrɛl hina la faa ɛɛ gunla Moosis n ŋɔ ba be la, di suŋŋi a Ijip hina kuna baŋ kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋu kuari ani laala. 36Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ Izrɛl hina wia ra par Ijip hina, ba tɛɛ baa kuna la maa baŋ faa suŋŋɛɛ ba be la, a guŋ gil Izrɛl hina chi Ijip hina daama kaali.
37Izrɛl hina faa lii bol la banna yir Ramɛsis di vol ga hel bol la banna yir Sukɔf. Baala la n faa ra vol naazi daŋ faa hel kagboŋa kalfaanumbɛl, ba waa haana ni biizi waa kutte. 38Nɛra la n faa waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ gba, faa jaa ba ni ba kundɛɛzaa ninɛɛ di ra la. 39Saŋmittaa la baŋ faa chigɛ di lii Ijip hɛri ba la, ba kpaa ɔɔzi paanuu la baŋ waa yiisi ra du a ni la. A saŋmittaa faa waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ a ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, Ijip hina la faa duŋŋi baabuu lii ba hɛri, ba waa kaa dɔɔ saŋa bá daali diwee.
40Izrɛl hina faa du Ijip hɛrii binni kalfaanaazu ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ. 41A hɔl la a binni kalfaanaazu ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ n wa su a maga, a hɔl himmaanii Kɔraawiizi nɛra dizi la maa faa lii Ijip hɛri. 42Dikuu Kɔraawiizi n faa du ba tau a hamuŋa maa guŋŋ di lizi baa lii Ijip hina nonee biini wia. Awia, bina maa biini, gunnɛ Izrɛl hina ge ɔɔ so di ra nyiŋ hamuŋa hiŋ ni guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi. Gunnɛ ba ni ba naanna ɔɔ ra ɛɛ, di ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi saŋaa saŋa maa.
Gillikaali widaulaa wia
43Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, “Gillikaali widaulaarɛ keŋ, hɔɔhri maa gilɛɛ waa diu. 44Ka yom la maa iiŋ yauwɛ, di ii teŋ u hɛŋ daŋ wer diu. 45Hɔɔhri la maa ge n du ii be di ra di paah, gilɛɛ waa diu.
46Ií ɔɔ so diikpaŋ biini di ra diu, di gilɛɛ waa kpa a ol yemmaa di ra lii bossee. Ií gilɛɛ waa ku u hog bɛl maa. 47Ií Izrɛl hina maa daŋ ɔɔ ra di a hɔpizii naa.
48Hɔɔhri la maa n du ii be ka ra nyiŋŋi ú di Kɔraawiizi Gillikaali naa, a hiŋ gil ba teŋri baala la maa n du u dia hɛna. Denii ú jaa wer jaa Gillikaali diire ni alugɔ nɛr la baŋ lullɛ a hɛri. Baal la maa hɛŋ n waa teŋŋe, ú gilɛɛ waa diu. 49A widaulii naa du denii tɛɛ nɛra la baŋ lullɛ a hɛri ni hɔɔhra la maa n du ba be.”
50Izrɛl hina la maa sɛɛ di hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa bagli Moosis ni Aarɔn la. 51A hɔpizii himmaanii Kɔraawiizi lizi Izrɛl hina dizi la maa lii Ijip hɛri.

english_text:
Dedication of the First-Born
1The Lord said to Moses, 2 “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.”
The Festival of Thin Bread
3-4Moses said to the people:
Remember this day in the month of Abib. It is the day when the Lord's mighty power rescued you from Egypt, where you were slaves. Do not eat anything made with yeast. 5The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey.
Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way: 6For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord. 7During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes. 8Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
9This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt. 10Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
11The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors. 12 From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him. 13You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
14In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt. 15The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
16This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt.
The Lord Leads His People
17After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.” 18So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea.
The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
19 Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
20The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert. 21-22 During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_text:
Biibambilugla kpai tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Kpa biibambilugla maa tɛŋ. Biibaal maa gɛɛ sebal maa baŋ luglɛɛ lul Izrɛl hina biini ɛɛ n hotte.”
3Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií ra liizi a hɔpizii naa dii nɛnnɛ. A hɔpiziirɛ ii lii Ijip hɛri, ii waa kaa ɛɛ yoma. Kɔraawiizi faa kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ labuu lizi ia lii de. Ií ɔɔ gilɛɛ waa di kummaa yiisi n du u ni. 4Lugli baagu la banna yir Abib baagu naabuu ii kpa ra lii. 5Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa Keenan, Hitti, Amɔri, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina hɛssi la n summɛ di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la tɛɛ ia, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ yaa naabaala la. Denii ii jaa gaa di a hɔpizizeŋ naa baagu naa biini, bina maa. 6Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ maa biini, ií ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la baŋ waa yiisi duwɛɛ la bɛŋ. A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la, ií ɔɔ di a hɔpizizeŋ di ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi. 7A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ maa biini, ií ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la yiisi n waa hoo a ni. Ií gilɛɛ gil yiisi wàá dugli gɛɛ di wàá du ii hɛri waa yemmaa. 8A hɔpizii hiŋ, bɛ́l maa ŋɔ u biibaal be, ‘N na ɛɛ kenne dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ tɛŋ, saŋa la miŋ lii Ijip hɛri la.’ 9Wia naa daŋ ɛɛ alugɔ kuŋ iiŋ kpawɛɛ vɔɔzi ii nonee ni ii hilli, di gil ii ra liizi lugɔ a dɛkkɔɔ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg n du ii nuuzi. U kpa u fɔŋŋazenne lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri. 10Ií ɔɔ ra liizi hɔpizizeŋ naa, di ra diu saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n dauwɛ la, bina maa.
Biibambilugli wia
11Di Kɔraawiizi wa ba ii ni Keenan hɛri, di wa kpau tɛɛ ia gunla uŋ faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii ni ii naabaala la, 12ii daŋ ɔɔ kpa ii biibambilugla tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Sel maa biibal un luglɛɛ lul ɛɛ u hotte. 13Kaweewaa hor, ií ɔɔ kpa pebii charuu, ka di ii wàá ɛɛ guŋ, ií ku u baŋaa. Ií ɔɔ bir yau ii biibambilugla waa, di lɛɛ baa. 14Di ii biibaala ŋmɛnɛ wa pɛɛzi ia lugɔ wii naa zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ? Ií ŋɔ ba be, ‘Kɔraawiizi kpa u fɔŋŋazenne lizi yaa lii Ijip hɛri, yaa waa kaa ɛɛ yoma. 15Saŋa la Ijip koori n dɔɔ dignikpega, di vɛɛ lugɔ ú tɛɛ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ ya kaali la, Kɔraawiizi faa kpuuzi Ijip hina biibambilugla maanii. Newea ni sela maa. Guŋ wiarɛ yaa ra lizi a biibambilugla di ra lizi mbusuzi, di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di bir turgi yaa biibambilugla maa kima di ra lɛɛ baa la.’ 16Wia naa daŋ ɛɛ alugɔ kuŋ iiŋ kpawɛɛ vɔɔzi ii nonee ni ii hilli, di gil ii ra liizi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ labuu lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri.”
Muuzeŋaahmu gii wia
17Saŋa la Ijip koori n wa gillɛ a nɛra lii di ra la la, Kɔraawiizi tɔ ba see ba ra la, ka u faa waa sɛɛwɛ ú kpogli baa ga Filisti hɛri. Haali de ŋmɛnɛɛ n faa duglɛɛ gba. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di nɛra naa haŋ wa chem laal maa ni, aŋhinabe, ba daŋ bir ba nfɛssi, di bir kaali Ijip hɛri.” 18Dikuu guŋ wia Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ ba bɛɛ kpa hɛribɔduma ŋmɛnɛɛ la n chɔɔwɛ di ra la Muuzeŋaahmu la. Izrɛl hina faa ɛɛ sirya ni ba laal kuna di lii ra la.
19Moosis faa paa Joosɛf hoga di jaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Joosɛf faa gillɔɔ Izrɛl hina naabaala hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua lugɔ ba daŋ ɛɛ guŋ. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi daŋ ŋmɛnɛ hiini ia ii lii bɔnnaa wibii maa. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, ií paa n hoga di jaa ra la.”
20Baŋ wa izi bol la banna yir Sukɔf la, ba ga baŋzi ba tantizi yembɛl banna yir Ɛtam n du hɛribɔduma kɛrii la, di chɔɔ de. 21Bɔchaaŋ, Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ du baama bɛl n du miriti di la chiŋ di tɔ ba see di ra bagli baa ŋmɛnɛɛ, hamuŋa ge, u kaa ɛɛ lugɔ niŋ di tɔ ba see, di ra chaani baa, bá wer di ra vol bɔchaaŋ ni hamuŋa maa. 22A baama la n du miriti la chiŋ labuu ɔɔ faa tɔ ba see bɔchaaŋ ni hamuŋa maa la, faa du ba benii saŋa maa.

english_text:
The Israelites Cross the Red Sea
1At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
2Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea. 3The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country. 4I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord.
The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
5When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
6The king got his war chariot and army ready. 7He commanded his officers in charge of his 600 best chariots and all his other chariots to start after the Israelites. 8The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way. 9But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
10When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help. 11They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway? 12While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
13But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again. 14The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
15The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward. 16Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground. 17I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry. 18The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
19All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them, 20but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
21 Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up, 22 and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
23The Egyptian chariots and cavalry went after them. 24But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic. 25Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
26The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.” 27Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea. 28The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive. 29But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
30On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them. 31Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_text:
Muuzeŋaahmu gii wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ ba bir har di ga chɔɔ dugli bol la banna yir Pi Hahirɔf n du Migdɔl ni muuzeŋ la baambaaŋ, a muuzeŋ kɛrii, di chaŋ Baal Zɛfɔn. 3Ijip koori danna fɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina leuwoo a hɛribɔduma biini, di ra juuri, dikuu a hɛribɔduma n tɔ baa ŋmɛnɛɛ wia. 4N daŋ gil Ijip koori digna du kpeg, ú duŋŋi ba luge, ń na girme tɛɛ n hiŋ di lii a koori ni u laallɔɔra maa be. Denii Ijip hina chi zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi himmaa la.” Awia, Izrɛl hina la faa ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.
5Saŋa la a koori n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ a nɛra chɔwɔɔrɛ kaali la, u ni u nabɔnzi la kaa bir ba nfɛssi a Izrɛl hina wia, di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ yaa ɛɛ gunnɛi? Yaa gillɔɔ ba maa kaali, ba wàá kaa du de di hum di ra tɛɛ yaa!” 6Denii u gil ba ɛɛ u laal torko sirya, di chaali u laallɔɔra jaa. 7U vɔɔ lii ni u laal torkozi maa, kalfaanumbɛl ɛɛ a kpega, laallɔɔra nabɔnzi zuua tɔ ba see. 8Kɔraawiizi kaa gil Ijip koori digna du kpeg, a guŋ gil u ra dau Izrɛl hina la luge, di Izrɛl hina la ta chɔŋ di ra kaali banni ni, a saŋa. 9A koori ni u laallɔɔra baŋhinaa zuu ba laal torkozi zagra n na tɛrgi, baŋhina ge tinni zagra, ba maa ra duŋŋi a Izrɛl hina, di ga dugli baa bɔr la baŋ faa baŋzi ba tantizi di chɔɔ, muuzeŋ la kɛrii la n dugli Pi Hahirɔf, di chaŋ Baal Zɛfɔn la.
10A koori ni u laallɔɔra n waa dugli, a Izrɛl hina kɛɛ binni, di na banna ba. Ɔnsii lau baa werge ba bɔra ra sa. Ba lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi lugɔ ú mɔgli baa. 11Ba ŋɔ Moosis be, “Amɔ, Ijip hɛri n waa ŋmama dɔɔwɛ, ba hug nɛra wiarɛ i ba yaa ni hɛribɔduma naa biini ya wa siuzaa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ɛɛ yaa gunnɛi? 12Yaa faa waa felee ŋɔ i be Ijip hɛri lugɔ i gil yaa, ya hum di ra tɛɛ Ijip hina laa? Yaa n faa ɛɛ yoma, di hum ra tɛɛ baa la, a guŋ faa bɔ yaa n niŋ siuzi hɛribɔduma naa biini.”
13Denii Moosis ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Ií chi chigigi ka na gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lɛɛ ia zinaa. Ijip hina naa iin nawɛɛ zinaa naa, ii wàá ka na baa maa. 14Kɔraawiizi daŋ yoo tɛɛ ia, ii wiimaanii ii chi bɔɔiih.”
15Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii wii ra duŋ gunnɛi? Ŋɔ a nɛra be dí ba izi ra vol. 16Lalli i daŋkpala, di tɛruu guali a muuzeŋ ni, ú chah bɔra anɛɛ, hɛrhilii chɔɔ, á Izrɛl hina wer ga de gi. 17N daŋ gil a Ijip hina digna du kpeg, ba duŋŋi ia zuu de. A koori ni u laallɔɔra ni ba laal torkozi ni baala la n tinni zagra la maanii niŋ duŋŋi ia zuu de. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, n daŋ na girme. 18Di n wa kpegli Ijip hina, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi himmaa.”
19Denii Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la n faa tɔ Izrɛl hina laallɔɔra la see la, bir kaali ba harbɔɔ. Baama la n du miriti di la chiŋ la ge lii ba see di kaali ba harbɔɔ. 20A wa chi Ijip hina ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra la baambaaŋ. A hamuŋa maa baama la ɔɔ gil bɔr biri Ijip hina la keŋkere, ka gil bɔr chaani Izrɛl hina la waa keŋkere. Gunnɛ a ɛɛ ba waa dɔŋa duglɛɛ, a hamuŋa maa.
21Denii Moosis lalli u daŋkpala di guali muuzeŋ la ni, Kɔraawiizi gil pekpeg bɛl lii wiifurii a hamuŋa maa, di wa lau a muuzeŋ nii chah bɔra anɛɛ, hɛrhilii chɔɔ. 22Izrɛl hina la ga a muuzeŋ biini hɛrhilii la di kaali, ka a muuzeŋ nii maa faa chi ba nodig ni nomɛɛl alugɔ koŋlaa.
23Ijip hina la haa ra duŋŋi baa di ge zuu a muuzeŋ biini. Zagra ni banla maa n faa tinnaa la ni banla n faa chigɛ laal torkozi la biine, maanii faa hiŋ baa zuu de. 24Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Kɔraawiizi faa du baama ni niŋ alugɔ dola la biini, ka liŋŋi na Ijip laallɔɔra, di gil ba bugmi. 25U gil ba laal torkozi la naazi nir, a jaa du kpol ban niŋ kaa wer la see. Denii a Ijip hina la ŋɔ, “Ií gil ya gil baa ka bir chɔ kpo! Kɔraawiizii yoowe di ra tɛɛ baa la.”
26Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kaa lalli i nonii guali a muuzeŋ ni, á nii wa tɔ a Ijip hina maa ni ba zagra ni ba laal torkozi ani banla maa n tinni zagra la ni.” 27Moosis lalli u nonii guali a muuzeŋ ni. Hɔɔ n waa pizi, di u maa bittɔ su gunla uŋ faa suwee la. Ijip hina la faa ra chɔ bá lii, ka Kɔraawiizi bir taa baa di du a muuzeŋ biini. 28Nii la ba wa tɔ Ijip laallɔɔra la n faa ra duŋŋi Izrɛl hina la n zuu muuzeŋ la biini maa ni, ba maa mag de.
29Ka Izrɛl hina la waa faa ga hɛrhilii a muuzeŋ biini, a niiri n faa chigɛ alugɔ koŋlaa ba nodig ni ba nomɛɛl keŋkerezi la di kaali. 30A hɔllɛ Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ Izrɛl hina di lii Ijip hina nonee biini, ba jaa na a Ijip hina n siuzɛɛ di chɔɔgi a muuzeŋ kɛraa maa. 31A saŋa Izrɛl hina n wa na gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagli u fɔŋŋazeŋ Ijip hina ni la, ba jaa ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi, di yardi u ni u balii Moosis maa.

english_text:
The Song of Moses
1 Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord:
I sing praises to the Lord
for his great victory!
He has thrown the horses
and their riders
into the sea.
2 The Lord is my strength,
the reason for my song,
because he has saved me.
I praise and honor the Lord—
he is my God and the God
of my ancestors.
3The Lord is his name,
and he is a warrior!
4He threw the chariots and army
of Egypt's king
into the Red Sea,
and he drowned the best
of the king's officers.
5They sank to the bottom
just like stones.
6With the tremendous force
of your right arm, our Lord,
you crushed your enemies.
7What a great victory was yours,
when you defeated everyone
who opposed you.
Your fiery anger wiped them out,
as though they were straw.
8You were so furious
that the sea piled up
like a wall,
and the ocean depths
curdled like cheese.
9Your enemies boasted
that they would
pursue and capture us,
divide up our possessions,
treat us as they wished,
then take out their swords
and kill us right there.
10But when you got furious,
they sank like lead,
swallowed by ocean waves.
11Our Lord, no other gods
compare with you—
Majestic and holy!
Fearsome and glorious!
Miracle worker!
12When you signaled
with your right hand,
your enemies were swallowed
deep into the earth.
13The people you rescued
were led by your powerful love
to your holy place.
14Nations learned of this
and trembled—
Philistines shook with horror.
15The leaders of Edom and of Moab
were terrified.
Everyone in Canaan fainted,
16struck down by fear.
Our Lord, your powerful arm
kept them still as a rock
until the people you rescued
to be your very own
had marched by.
17You will let your people settle
on your own mountain,
where you chose to live
and to be worshiped.
18Our Lord, you will rule forever!
The Song of Miriam
19The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground. 20Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance. 21Then she sang to them:
“Sing praises to the Lord
for his great victory!
He has thrown the horses
and their riders into the sea.”
Bitter Water at Marah
22After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water. 23They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name. 24The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
25 Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink.
At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings. 26Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
27Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and 70 palm trees. So they camped there.
translation_text:
Moosis ni Miriam yir
1Denii Moosis ni a Izrɛl hina yir yir naa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi,
“N daŋ yir yir tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi,
dikuu uŋ yoo laal lii,
di dɔɔ sɔŋ werge wia.
U vigzi zagra ni a tinna la maanii
ha muuzeŋ la biini.
2Kɔraawiizii n fɔŋŋa,
u wiarɛ n na yir yir naa,
waabuu ɛɛ n Lɛɛri.
Waabuu Kɔraawiizi la minna hum,
awia, n daŋ chɔluu,
Kɔraawiizi la n mɛɛ n na hum,
awia, n danna tɔgzuu werge.
3Kɔraawiizii u sɔŋ,
u ɛɛ lugɔ laallɔɔri.
4U vigzi Ijip koori laallɔɔra
ni ba laal torkozii
ha muuzeŋ la biini.
U laal nabɔmkpega la maanii
a Muuzeŋaahmu di.
5A niiluŋ la tɔ ba ni,
ba maa tuu zɛɛ alugɔ bia.
6N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i kpa i nodigre,
di bagli i fɔŋŋazeŋ.
I nodigre i kpa pinti,
yaa dɔma maa.
7I fɔŋŋa ni i zennii,
i kpa lɔ i dɔma ha.
I gillɔɔ i baaŋ haahri baa,
ba fuuh alugɔ zɔga.
8I heeza kpegzi wiarɛ
a nii chah di izi chi.
Di chi alugɔ koŋlii,
a niiluŋ la zɛɛ maa
jaa bir chɔɔ kpantalaŋ.
9Ba dɔm ta barabara di ŋɔ,
‘N daŋ duŋŋi ba luge
di ga lau baa.
N daŋ paagi ba daama di bɔnnaa,
n daŋ di di piŋ nɛnnɛ.
N daŋ pam n tokobi
di chɔgi ba maa.’
10Ka hinuu heuzi baa,
a muuzeŋ tɔ ba ni.
Ba tuu kaali a muuzeŋ zɛɛ
alugɔ kpana.
11Vug bɛliirɛ ge du de lugɔ hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizɛi?
Anɛɛ ba kpa di mɛgziinɛi?
I zenni ni i nanni waa dɔŋ dɔɔwɛ.
I zenni dɛg ɔmaarɛ,
hinuu kaa ra ɛɛ wizenaa.
12Hinuu tɛr i nodig,
a hɛri di yaa dɔma.
13Dikuu i nɔŋŋaa n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la wia,
i daŋ tɔ i nɛra la hiŋ lɛɛwɛ
lii ba dɔma nonee biini la see.
Dikuu i fɔŋŋa wia i daŋ kpogli baa
di la i duuribɔr
n ɛɛ bɔnaniinanii la.
14Durnya hɛssi nɛra maa
daŋ nuua ba bɔraa sa,
biinichɔg daŋ lau
Filisti hina werge maa.
15Ɔnsii daŋ lau Ɛdɔm hina koora werge maa,
bɔsai chol Moab hina sitɔɔra ni,
Keenan hɛri nɛra ge bɔra huah,
16ɔnsii werge ni banchullɔi
daŋ lau baa.
Kɔraawiizi, dikuu i banonii fɔŋŋa wia,
ba daŋ chi siriti alugɔ bii guŋŋ,
ka i nɛra la hiŋ lɛɛwɛ
di lii ba dɔma be la wa kaali.
17I daŋ kpogli i nɛra Izrɛl hina
di wa soŋŋi i bizeŋ la nyuu,
bɔr la hiŋ lizɛɛ di tɛɛ i hiŋ la,
bɔr la hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ
u ɛɛ i duuribɔr la.
I diinaniinanii la hiŋ mawɛɛ
i fɔŋŋa biini la.
18Hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ di i kora
di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.”
19Ijip koori zagra ni laal torkozi ani zagtinna la n waa zuu muuzeŋ la biini la, Kɔraawiizi gil muuzeŋ la nii bir ba, di wa tɔ ba ni, ka Izrɛl hina la waa vol di ga a muuzeŋ biini hɛrhilii di kaali. 20Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Miriam la n faa ɛɛ Aarɔn niuhambie la kpa kuŋyigzii bɛl, u dɔŋahina haana maa izi di ra hiŋuu, di ge kpogli ba kuŋyigzaa, di yigzi di ra sa. 21Denii Miriam yir yir tɛɛ baa, di ŋɔ,
“Ií yir yir di chɔli Kɔraawiizi,
waabuu dɔɔ sɔŋ werge maa.
U vigzi zagu maa ni u tinnii
ha muuzeŋ biini.”
Mara ni Ɛlim niiri wia
22Moosis tɔ Izrɛl hina see, di kpogli baa lii Muuzeŋaahmu la, di kaali Suur Hɛribɔduma la. Ba faa volloo hɔpizaa ahoroo a hɛribɔduma biini, di ba waa nii nawɛɛ bá nyɔɔ. 23Baŋ wa hel yembɛl banna yir Mara, ba faa waa wette bá nyɔɔ de nii, dikuu a nii n faa kpolle wia, guŋ wiarɛ ba ra yir de Mara. 24Awia, a nɛra ra nuumi di ra du Moosis ni, di ra ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ ya nyɔɔi?”
25Denii Moosis lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, u faa bagluu daa bɛl. Moosis faa kpa a daa vigzi nii la biini, a nii bir du sum.
Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ baa na de, di du Gbɔgni tɛɛ baa. 26U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di ii ɔɔ keŋŋi digna di ra nuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wiŋɔzi nɛnnɛ, di ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee n be, di ɔɔ sɛɛ ra nuu n widaulaa, di ra hiŋaa, màá gil wiila la miŋ faa kpawɛɛ ta Ijip hina ni la bɛl maa lau ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la n na chaa ia.”
27Denii ba lii de di yembɛl banna yir Ɛlim. De ge faa dɔɔ bulli fidaanɛɛ ani abɛ daazi tokkoahoro ni fii, ba jaa wa baŋzi ba tanti diini dugli a nii.

english_text:
The Lord Sends Food from Heaven
1On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai. 2There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron, 3“We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
4 The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me. 5But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
6Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt. 7And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
8Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
9Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
10Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud. 11The Lord said to Moses, 12“I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
13That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground. 14After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost. 15 The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?”
Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat. 16And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
17They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less. 18 Everyone had exactly what they needed, just the right amount.
19Moses told them not to keep any overnight. 20Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
21Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted. 22However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses, 23 he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
24The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms. 25“You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today. 26You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
27A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none. 28Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings? 29Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.” 30And so they rested on the Sabbath.
31 The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey. 32Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
33 Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
34Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping. 35-36 The Israelites ate manna for 40 years, before they came to the border of Canaan that was a settled land.
translation_text:
Maana ni zaahra wia
1Izrɛl hina ni ba dee maa kaa izi Ɛlim di la Sin Hɛribɔduma la n du Ɛlim ni Sinaai baambaaŋ. Baŋ lii Ijip hɛri la, a baagu anɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa fidaanuehiŋ hɔllɛ guŋ. 2A hɛribɔduma hiŋ biini, Izrɛl hina maa kaa ra nuumi werge maa di ra du Moosis ni Aarɔn ni. 3Izrɛl hina la ŋɔ ba be, “Di Kɔraawiizi faa kpuuzi yaa Ijip hɛri la, a vii bɔ. Yaa ɔɔ faa sou di bar viini ni ola, di ra di diwii la maa yaa n faa ra nyiŋŋi. Ka ii gil yaa lii de wa du hɛribɔduma naa biini lɔzi ra kpu, ya ni yaa dee maa siuzi.”
4Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “N daŋ ɔɔ gil diwii bɛl lii chiŋ chol lugɔ donii tɛɛ ia. A dɛkkɔɔ nɛr maa ɔɔ lii hɔpizi biimaa di paa gunla maga un niŋ ɔɔ wer di di piŋ, a hɔl hiŋ. Kenne ń ɛɛ baa di na, di ba daŋ sɛɛ di hiŋ n widaulaa gɛɛ ba wàá hiŋɛi. 5Hɔpizaa anumbɛl hɔl la, ba daŋ ɔɔ paa hɔpizaa anɛɛ diwee di daali.”
6Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn ŋɔ a Izrɛl hina maa be, “Duana naa ni, ii daŋ zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizii lizi ia di lii Ijip hɛri, 7chɔɔzi ge ni, ii daŋ na Kɔraawiizi girme, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nuu ii nuumaa labuu. Yaabuu babɛlaa ii nuumi ra du yaai?” 8Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií daŋ zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du ii benii, saŋa la un niŋ tɛɛ ia ola ii ra hee duana ni, di kaa tɛɛ ia diwii bɛl iri la maga iinna nyiŋŋi chɔɔzi ni ii di, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nuu ii nuumaazi la maa iiŋ faa nuumɛɛ di ra duu labuu. Yaabuu babɛlaai? Yaa lɛi ii nuumi ra du, Kɔraawiizii ii nuumi ra du.”
9Denii Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la maa be bá wa chi Kɔraawiizi see, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nuu ba nuumaa labuu.”
10Saŋa la Aarɔn n haa ra ŋɔ a wia Izrɛl hina maa be la, ba ŋɔ ba binni a hɛribɔduma hiŋ, di Kɔraawiizi girmee du baama biini di ra nyɛgzi. 11Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 12“N nuu Izrɛl hina nuumaarɛ. Awia, ŋɔ ba be, ‘Di bɔr waa lauri siwee, ii daŋ hee ol, chɔɔzi ni ge ii na diwii bɛl di. Denii ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.’ ”
13A hɔl duana ni zaahra ba di wa su bɔr la baŋ baŋzi ba tantizi la biini maa, chɔɔzi ge ni, ŋmɛnii chol di tɔ de baŋgia bar. 14A ŋmɛnii n wa tunnɛ, ba na kumpɛglɛgzi aŋhina alugɔ nyiŋ hɛga n tɔ a hɛribɔduma hiŋ maa. 15Izrɛl hina n wa naa, ba bir di ra pɛɛzi dɔŋa, “Bɛɛ kunaa gunnɛi?” Dikuu baŋ faa wàá zummɛ wia.
Denii Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “A kuna naa ɛɛ diwii bɛl irii Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ iabuu ŋɔ ií ra di. 16Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ii ɛɛ, ‘Ií bɛl maa la ga paa gunla maga n niŋ heluu, ú dia. Nɛra la n du tanti dia maa biini, a dɛkkɔɔ bɛl maa na kookoo tassa suul.’ ”
17Izrɛl hina la ɛɛ gunla maa baŋ bagli baa. Baŋhina paa werge, baŋhina ge paa tama. 18Baŋ wa kpa kookoo tassa mɛgzi bɛl maa hora, unla n paa diwee werge la waa diwee ka ka, unla ge n paa tama, waa diwee nyaawɛ. Bɛl maa horpaalaa heluubuu.
19Denii Moosis ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa chiŋŋi diwii naa yeŋ hɔɔ waa pizi.”
20Ka baŋhina faa vɛɛ Moosis nua la, ka gil a yeŋ chi hɔpizi. Hɔɔ n wa pizɛɛ, di a pɔɔhwɔ, di dɔɔ sandule di ra sɔɔhri. A guŋ gil Moosis baaŋ fuu ba ni.
21Chɔɔzi maa, bɛl maa ɔɔ la ga paa gunla maga un niŋ wer di, ka di wiizi wa nyaazɔɔ, anla n kawɛɛ la ɔɔ ŋmɛɛri di zuu hɛri.
22Hɔpizaa anumbɛl hɔl la, bɛl maa ɔɔ paa kookoo tassa suul bunɛɛ. Denii ba nabɔnzi wa ŋɔ a wia tɛɛ Moosis. 23Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi widauliirɛ keŋ, ‘Kɛrɛ daŋ ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpizii, di ɛɛ hɔpizinanii tɛu. Awia, a dɛkkɔɔ bɛl maa ɔɔzi gɛɛ daali kunla maa unna nyiŋŋi. Ka anla waa maa n kawɛɛ, ií gilaa chiŋŋi hɔpizi.’ ”
24Baŋ wa nuu guŋ, ba gil a diwee yeŋ chiŋŋi hɔɔ wa pizi gunla Moosis n faa ŋɔ ba be la, ka a faa waa sɔɔhri gɛɛ di ra lii sandule. 25Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií dia zinaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, zinaa ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Awia, ii wàá naa paa zinaa. 26Hɔpizaa anumbɛl biini, ii daŋ ɔɔ naa di ra paa, ka aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la n ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpizii la waa, ii waa ɔɔ na kummaa.”
27Ani a maa, ka baŋhina faa liwɔɔrɛ bá ga paagaa a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la. Baŋ laŋŋɛ ge, ba wàá nawɛɛ. 28Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi Moosis, “Ɛrɛɛ ii vɛɛ n widaulaa ni n baglaazi di birgi magɛi? 29Ií ra liizi lugɔ minuu tɛɛ ia Heezaa Hɔpizii naa. Awiarɛ n ɔɔ ra tɛɛ ia hɔpizaa anɛɛ diwee hɔpizaa anumbɛlhiŋ hɔl la. Bɛ́l maa ɔɔ du u dia, di gilɛɛ kaa wàá lii ra nyiŋŋi diwee a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la.” 30Awiarɛ a nɛra bɛl maa faa waa kaa ra hum huma a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl hiŋ.
31Izrɛl hina la faa ra yir a diwiire ‘maana’. A faa huuhzɔɔrɛ alugɔ zule. Di i diu, u ɔɔ du kpir ninɛɛ lugɔ baŋ kpa huuhnuu ɔɔzi kɛrɛkɛssizi. 32Denii Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ yaa benii dí ya nyiŋŋi a maana naa kookoo tassa chiŋŋi nɛnnɛ. Di yaa naanna wa izoo, ba wer na di zum diwii la iri Kɔraawiizi n faa tɛɛ yaa saŋa la un lizi yaa di lii Ijip hɛri yaa ga du hɛribɔduma la.” 33Moosis jaa ŋɔ Aarɔn be, dí u kpa vii jiga bɛl di mɛgzi maana kookoo tassa di du u biini. Di kpau chiŋŋi bɔr la yaa n na jaami Kɔraawiizi la biini, yaa naanna maa wer izi huuzaa.
34Moosis gil Aarɔn ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ u be la. U kpaa di chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, á wer du de di gilɛɛ waa leu. 35Izrɛl hina la faa di maana naabuu binni tokkoanɛɛ ka haa hel Keenan hɛri magbɔɔ, di so de.
36Kookoo tassa Izrɛl hina n na yir oma la, u bufii ba ra yir ɛfa.

english_text:
The Lord Gives Water from a Rock
1 The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
2The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!”
Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
3But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
4Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
5The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River. 6When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
7The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.”
Israel Defeats the Amalekites
8When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites. 9So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
10Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop. 11The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them. 12After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset. 13That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
14 Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
15Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.” 16Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_text:
Nii n lii bii ni wia
1Izrɛl hina la ni ba dee maa lii Sin Hɛribɔduma la, di vol di ra la bɔra gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ bá ra ɛɛ la. Ba faa wa baŋzi ba tantizi yembɛl banna yir Rɛfidim, ka nii faa waa hoo de bá nyɔɔ. 2Awia, ba ra naa Moosis wia, di ra ŋɔ, “Tɛɛ yaa nii yá nyɔɔ.” Denii Moosis bir ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra naannɛi? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra da Kɔraawiizi zɛɛi?”
3Ka niinyɔgzi n faa lau baa werge wia, ba haa vɛɛ ka nuumi ra du Moosis, di ra ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i kpogli yaa lii Ijip hɛri, í wa kpa niinyɔgzi kpu yaa ni yaa biizi ni yaa sela maa, yá siuzɛi?”
4Denii Moosis lɔ wile werge maa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ n ɛɛ nɛra naa wiai? A ka tama ka ba paagi bia lɔɔziŋ kpu.”
5Kɔraawiizi n wa nuu guŋ, u ŋɔ Moosis be, “Tɔ nɛra la see di ra la. Lizi Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi baŋhina jaa i hiŋ ni, di kpa daŋkpala la hiŋ faa kpawɛɛ lɔ Muu Naal nii la, di ra la. 6N daŋ chi ii see bii bɛl nyuu n du Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ. Di ii wa hel de, kpa i daŋkpala lɔu. Nii daŋ lii nɛra la maa nyɔɔ.” Denii Moosis ɛɛ guŋ Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi la maa see. 7U faa dau a bɔr sɔŋ Massa ni Mɛriba, dikuubɛɛwiai, denii Izrɛl hina nuumi di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi na, di ra ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi du yaa benii naa, gɛɛ waa kaa hoo yaa benei?”
Izrɛl hina n kpegli Amalɛk hina wia
8Nɛra baŋhina banna yir Amalɛk hina faa ba wa pig Izrɛl hina ni laal, Rɛfidim. 9Denii Moosis ŋɔ baal bɛl banna yir Josua be, “Lizi yaa nɛra baŋhina ií la ga lɔ Amalɛk hina laal. Kɛrɛ, n daŋ tinni giŋgimii naa nyuu chi, di kpa Kɔraawiizi daŋkpala la kpogli.”
10Denii Josua ni Amalɛk hina faa ra lɔ a laal gunla Moosis n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la. Ka Moosis ni Aarɔn ani baal bɛl banna yir Hur faa la ga tinni a giŋgimii nyuu. 11Di Moosis haŋ wa lalli u nonee chiŋ, Izrɛl hina ɔɔ ra kpegli ba dɔma labuu, ka di u wa gillɔ u nonee tuu zɛɛ, Amalɛk hina la ge ɔɔ ra kpegli baa. 12Moosis nonee n wa kuuhwɛ, ba kpa bii dau u so u ni. Aarɔn ni Hur lau u nonee lalli, bɛl chi u nodig bɛl ge chi u nomɛɛl, ú nonee wer chi guŋŋ wiizi wa chol. 13Gunnɛ Josua ɛɛ di wer kpegli Amalɛk hina laallɔɔra la maa.
14Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Sɛbi kennaa iiŋ wette kpegli ii dɔma naa di dau hɔŋ ni, ií wer di ra liizaa saŋa maa. Gil Josua nuu guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai n daŋ dim Amalɛk hina, nɛr maa wàá ka liizi ba wia maa.”
15Moosis kpa bia sagzi dɔŋa ni di kuari mbusu lizibɔr di dau u sɔŋ, “Kɔraawiizii n kpegzi dii tuuta.” 16Moosis faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií lalli Kɔraawiizi kpegzi dii tuuta chiŋ! U daŋ ɔɔ ra yoo Amalɛk hinaa laal saŋaa saŋa maa.”

english_text:
Jethro Visits Moses
1Jethro was the priest of Midian and the father-in-law of Moses. He heard what the Lord God had done for Moses and his people, after rescuing them from Egypt.
2-4 In the meantime, Moses had sent his wife Zipporah and her two sons to stay with Jethro, and he had welcomed them. Moses was still a foreigner in Midian when his first son was born, and so Moses said, “I'll name him Gershom.”
When his second son was born, Moses said, “I'll name him Eliezer, because the God my father worshiped has saved me from the king of Egypt.”
5-6While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
7When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent, 8where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
9Jethro was so pleased to hear this good news about what the Lord had done, 10that he shouted, “Praise the Lord! He rescued you and the Israelites from the Egyptians and their king. 11 Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.” 12Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship.
Judges Are Appointed
(Deuteronomy 1.9-18)
13The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening. 14Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
15Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do. 16They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
17Jethro replied:
That isn't the best way to do it. 18You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone. 19God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people, 20and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
21You will need to appoint some competent leaders who respect God and are trustworthy and honest. Then put them over groups of 10, 50, 100, and 1,000. 22These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier. 23This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
24Moses followed Jethro's advice. 25He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of 10, 50, 100, and 1,000. 26They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
27After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_text:
Jɛtro n la Moosis be wia
1Midian hina kizeehiŋ Jɛtro n ɛɛ Moosis hila nuu gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Moosis ni Izrɛl hina la, ni gunla Kɔraawiizi n lɛɛ u nɛra di lii Ijip hɛri.
2Awia Jɛtro kpogli Moosis haaŋ Zipɔra 3ani u biibaala banɛɛ Gɛsɔm ni Ɛliɛza uŋ gillɛ u be di ba. Moosis faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N faa ɛɛ hɔɔhrii di du hɛrduma.” Awiarɛ u faa dau bɛl sɔŋ Gɛsɔm. 4Bɛl ge sɔnnɛ faa Ɛliɛza. U kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la n mɛɛ n faa ra hum labuu ń hiini, u lɛɛmbuu lii Ijip koori nonee, u kpuŋ huhzi.”
5Jɛtro, Moosis haaŋ ani u biibaala faa la Moosis be a hɛribɔduma, bɔr la baŋ faa baŋzi ba tantizi dugli Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ Sinaai la. 6Jɛtro faa tiloore ŋɔ Moosis be, “Mìŋ́ i hila Jetro ni i haaŋ ni u biibaala banɛɛ la ra bau.”
7Denii Moosis lii ga chem u hila baal hiŋ ni, di togni ka izi faamuu di suuzuu, gunla banna jaami dɔŋa la. Ba maa jaami dɔŋa ka zuu Moosis tanti dia biini. 8Moosis jaa bagli gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n kuu Izrɛl hina wia di ɛɛ Ijip koori ni u nɛra. U kaa ŋɔ ba be tɔɔrɔɔ la maa baŋ faa diwee ŋmɛnɛɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi faa lizi baa a biini.
9Jɛtro n wa nuu winanaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, di lɛɛ baa lii Ijip hina nonee la, u bɔra sɔɔnuu werge maa. 10Denii u ŋɔ, “N na chɔli Kɔraawiizi la n lɛɛ i ni nɛra la maa, di lii Ijip koori ni Ijip hina noneere.” 11Jɛtro kaa ŋɔ, “Filaŋkeŋ n zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizii kaali vuga maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ gunnɛ tɔɔri banla n faa ra gbɛlli Izrɛl hina la.” 12Moosis hila Jɛtro n wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, u faa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ani mbusuzi lizaa kuna aŋhina tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Aarɔn ni Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi maa lii ba Moosis ni u hila la be, ba maa kpau di a diwee Kɔraawiizi see.
Izrɛl hina seriya diire lizaa wia
13Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Moosis so ra kuari a nɛra dɔŋa ni, ba maa chi baruu guŋŋ bɔr wa duani. 14U hila n wa na wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ ra tɛɛ a nɛra la, u pɛɛzuu, “Beedee wiarɛ i ɛɛ di ra tɛɛ nɛra naa, ba ra ba i be kennei? Ɛrɛɛ i bɛŋ ɔɔ so di ra kuari baa dɔŋa ni, ba chi barii lii chɔɔzi maa guŋŋ di wa hel duanai?”
15Moosis bir ŋɔ u be, “A nɛraa ɔɔ ba n be ŋɔ n bagli baa Kɔraawiizi kipar. 16Di banla maa wa naawɔ, n benii ba ɔɔ ba, n bagli unla hor n summɛ, di kaa bagli baa Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni u Gbɔgni.”
17Moosis hilabaal hiŋ ŋɔ u be, “Gunla hinna ɛɛ la waa wer. 18Di i ra ɛɛ guŋ, i ni a nɛra maa daŋ wa gɛrgi. Huma la siili i ninɛɛ. I bɛŋ huŋhunnaa lɛi. 19A nuu n be n birii liize. Di i nuuwɔ tɛŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ du i be. A dɛkkɔɔ i chi a nɛra naa, di kpa ba wia ra ba Kɔraawiizi be. 20A bagli baa Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni u Gbɔgni, ni ba de dui wia ani wia la ban ninna ɛɛ. 21Ka lizi baala baŋhina hiŋ zummɛ baŋ wer wiɛɛlaa, di kaa yardi Kɔraawiizi nɛnnɛ, ba wia dɔɔ wibii, ba waa wikara ra sɛɛ, di gil ba ɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa, kalfazi, tokkoanɛɛgaa ni fifi ani fizi sitɔɔra. 22Gil ba ɛɛ a nɛra sitɔɔra saŋa maa, ka gil ba ɔɔ kpa wia la n kpolle werge, baŋ wàá wer kuari waa ba i be, ka anla n waa kpol la waa, ba ɔɔ kuaraa. Guŋ daŋ gil i huma yɔɔ, dikuu i ni baa n bɔnnaa wia. 23Di i ɛɛ kennaa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ i ɛɛ naa, a wàá kaa ra nuui, ka a nɛra maa ɔɔ bir kaali diini ni bɔsɔna.”
24Moosis nuu gunla u hila n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu la. 25Denii u lizi baala la n wer wiɛɛlaa lii Izrɛl hina maa biini, bá ɛɛ ba nabɔnzi di ra binni nɛra kagboŋa, kalfazi, tokkoanɛɛgaa ni fifi ani fizi ni. 26Ba jaa ɛɛ a nɛra seriya diire saŋa maa. Ka anla waa n ɔɔ wa du kpol la, ba ɔɔ kpaa ra ba Moosis be, ka anlawaa n waa kpol, ba himmaa ɔɔ ra kuaraa.
27Denii Moosis jaa ta u hila Jɛtro ŋmɛnɛɛ, u bir kaali u hɛri.

english_text:
At Mount Sinai
1-2The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
3Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
4You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young. 5 Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine, 6 but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests.
Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
7After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said, 8and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
9The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
10Once more the Lord spoke to Moses:
Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes 11and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
12 Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death, 13either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
14After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God. 15He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime.
The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
16 On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear. 17Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
18Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook. 19The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
20The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there. 21Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die. 22Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
23Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
24Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
25After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_text:
Ban du Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ wia
1Izrɛl hina n lii Ijip hɛri, ba baaguzi ahorohiŋ lugli hɔpiziirɛ ba wa hel Sinaai Hɛribɔduma. 2Baŋ wa izi Rɛfɛdin labuu ba hel de, di baŋzi ba tantizi Bizeŋ Sinaai la zɛɛ.
3Moosis tinni a bizeŋ nyuu Kɔraawiizi be. Denii Kɔraawiizi yiruu di ŋɔ u be lugɔ u ŋɔ keŋ tɛɛ Jekɔb naanna Izrɛl hina, 4“Ií na gunla maa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n tɔɔri Ijip hina ka kpa n fɔŋŋazeŋ kpa ia alugɔ chig n ɔɔ kpa u biizi zaah la, di wa tɛɛ n hiŋ. 5Di ii daŋ sɛɛ di ra hiŋ n nua nɛnnɛ, di lau n ni ia nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la nɛnnɛ, ii daŋ ɛɛ n nɛnɔŋŋaa. Durnya nɛra maa n ɛɛ n horaa, ka iabuu n lizi. 6Iawaa daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehina di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa. Wia naabuu í ŋɔ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.”
7Denii Moosis lii a bizeŋ nyuu di tuu la ga chaali a nɛra nabɔnzi maa, di ŋɔ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu la di tɛɛ baa. 8Ba maa kpau sɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ hiŋ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ.” Denii Moosis bir kpa ba loobii hiŋ di ga tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.
9Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “N daŋ du baamatɔg biini ba i be, á nɛra ɔɔ nuu minna ŋɔ wia ra tɛi, bá yardii saŋaa saŋa maa.” Denii Moosis la ga ŋɔ a nɛra be gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.
10Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “La ga sɔ a nɛra di lizi ba doŋa ha, ka bá ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be, zinaa ni kɛrɛ. Gil ba chag ba kuna, 11di ɛɛ sirya ra kpaŋ hɔbil, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɔllɛ ń tuu Bizeŋ Sinaai la nyuu ba maa naŋ. 12Pii maga bar a bizeŋ tɛɛ a nɛra, ka ŋɔ ba be dí ba ra dazi di gilɛɛ waa tinnuu gɛɛ di waa gbɔgzuu. Di bɛl maa haŋ wa vɛɛ ka ɛɛ guŋ, bá kpuu. 13Biarɛ ii paa lɔɔzuu gɛɛ hobeere ii virguu kpu. Nɛr maa nonii gilɛɛ waa gbɔgzi a hindee. Di nɛruu gɛɛ selle, ií gilɛɛ giluu u du de di ra nyiŋ. Ka di ba wa nuu nyigaa wiraa guŋŋ, a guŋ saŋaa ba jaa wer tinni a bizeŋ nyuu.”
14Moosis n wa lii a bizeŋ nyuu tuu la a nɛra be la, u gil ba sɔ ba doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be. Ka ba jaa chag ba kuna. 15Denii u ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Bɛl maa ɛɛ sirya nɛnnɛ di ra kpaŋ a hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ la. Baal maa ni haaŋ gilɛɛ waa chɔɔ.”
16A hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ la chɔɔzi ni dooŋ ra pogzi di ra nyɛgzi werge maa. Denii baamatɔg wa guali a bizeŋ ni, ka ba nuu bensunoniina n wiiwe werge, ɔnsii lau baa, ba bɔra ra sa yogyogyog. 17Denii Moosis jaa tɔ ba see di lii ba chɔɔribɔr la, bá ga chem Kɔraawiizi ni, ba ga chi a bizeŋ zɛɛ. 18A bizeŋ nyuu maa faa tɔ nyɔɔzi guŋ kuull, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi du niŋ biinii di tuu u ni. A nyɔɔzi bir di ra tinni chiŋ kuull lugɔ ninzeŋ nyɔɔzi. A bizeŋ zigli werge maa guŋ gbigbigbi. 19Ba nuu a bensunoniina wiraa n kaa ra nyaŋŋi werge maa. Denii Moosis ŋɔ wia, Kɔraawiizi sɛɛ alugɔ dooŋ n pozee.
20Kɔraawiizi tuu ba a Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu di wa yir Moosis, dí u tinni ba, u tinni. 21Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Tuu la ga karfi a nɛra dí ba ra dazi, di gilɛɛ waa fir ba naŋ. Di ba wa vɛɛwɔ ka ɛɛ guŋ, ba kpila maa daŋ siuzi. 22Kizeehina la gba n na ba n be la, dɛkkɔɔ bá sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be, di guŋ lɛi, n daŋ tɛr ba digna.”
23Moosis bir ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Nɛr maa wàá wer tinni a bizeŋ nyuu, dikuu i himmaa n karfi yaa lugɔ ya pii maga bar a bizeŋ di gil u ɛɛ i bɛŋ hor, di ɛɛ naniinanii wia.”
24Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ u be, “Bir tuu la ga kpogli Aarɔn, i nuu maa tinni ba. Ka a kizeehina ni a nɛra waa gilɛɛ waa fir, bá tinni ba n be, di guŋ lɛi, n daŋ tɛr ba digna.”
25Denii Moosis tuu la ga ŋɔ a nɛra be gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

english_text:
The Ten Commandments
(Deuteronomy 5.1-21)
1God said to the people of Israel:
2I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
3Do not worship any god except me.
4 Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth. 5 Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me, I will punish your families for three or four generations. 6But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
7 Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
8 Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me. 9 You have six days when you can do your work, 10but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns. 11 In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
12 Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
13 Do not murder.
14 Be faithful in marriage.
15 Do not steal.
16 Do not tell lies about others.
17 Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else.
The People Are Afraid
(Deuteronomy 5.23-33)
18 The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off 19and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
20“Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.” 21But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off.
Idols and Altars
22The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel:
With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven. 23So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
24Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you. 25 If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship. 26And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_text:
Gbɔgni fi la wia
1Kenne Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ,
2“Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n lɛɛ ia lii Ijip hɛri, saŋa la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma de la.
3Ií gilɛɛ kaa wàá dɔɔ vuga maa di ra jaa n ni.
4Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa ú li kuŋ n du chiŋ gɛɛ hɛri gɛɛ nii biini di ra tɛɛ iihinaa. 5Ií gilɛɛ waa togni di ra jaamaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛ zoma hinnɛ, di ra tɛr banla maa n hahŋ biizi, ba naanna, ba naanatɛɛri ani ba ge biizi digna, dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia, 6ka nɔŋŋi jiminizi kagboŋa nɛra la maa n nɔŋŋiŋ, di ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni la.
7Ií gilɛɛ kpogli mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sɔŋ di ra dua. N daŋ tɛr nɛr la maa n niŋ ɛɛ guŋ digni.
8Ií ɔɔ ra di Heezaa Hɔpizii la, di gil ú ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinanii ii be. 9Ií ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛl di ra hum ii huma maa, 10ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ lawaa ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Awia, a waa dɛkkɛ ii ni ii biizi, ii balaa, ii sela ani hɔɔhra la maa n du ii bola ra hum huma a hɔl hiŋ. 11Mìŋ́ ii Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛllɛ ta chiŋ, hɛri, muuzeŋ ani kuna la maa n du a biine, ka heezi hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la, di kissuu, di gil u ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinanii.
12A kpa i mɛɛ ni i maa girme, gunnɛ í wer dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n na tɛɛ ia naa biini.
13Gilɛɛ waa kpu nɛr.
14Gilɛɛ wàá sɛm.
15Gilɛɛ wàá ŋmɛɛ.
16Gilɛɛ wàá kanni kara di ra chug i dɔŋhiŋ.
17Gilɛɛ wàá kɛlli i dɔŋhiŋ dia ni. Gilɛɛ wàá kɛlli i dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ gɛɛ u balii gɛɛ u sel gɛɛ u kuna maa ni.”
18A nɛra n wa nuu dooŋ la pogzaa, di na u nyɛgzaa, di nuu a bensunoniina la ge wiraa, di kaa na bizeŋ la maa n na lii nyɔɔzi la, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa ba bɔra ra sa. Ba chi bɔɔnɛɛ, 19ka ŋɔ Moosis be, “Í himmaa ŋɔ wia ra tɛɛ yaa, yá ra nuu. Gilɛɛ gil Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia ra tɛɛ yaa. Di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ siuzi.”
20Denii Moosis bir ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Kɔraawiizi ballɔɔ ú wa ɛɛ ia na, guŋ gil ii ra ɔmuu di ra hiŋuu nɛnnɛ, ka gilɛɛ ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa.”
21A nɛra faa haa chi a bɔɔnɛɛ, ka Moosis ga dugli bɔbiri limpiriŋ la biini Kɔraawiizi n faa duwɛɛ la.
22Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ u ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Ii himmaa nuuwɔɔ miŋ ŋɔ wia tɛɛ ia di lii chiŋ. 23Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa di ra jaa n ni. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa saliŋhuŋŋu ni saliŋ di kuari vuga tɛɛ iihinaa.
24Ií kpa hɛɛhraa di ma mbusu lizibɔr tɛŋ, di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa la de. Ií ɔɔ kpa ii peeza ni buuna ani nauna di ra ɛɛ guŋ. Bɔr la maa min niŋ lizi di ŋɔ ii ra tɔgzi n sɔŋ, n daŋ ba ii be di wa kissi ia de. 25Di ii wa ŋɔ ii kpa bia di sagzi dɔŋa ni di kuari mbusu lizibɔr tɛŋ, ií gilɛɛ waa sɛɛhzaa. Di ii vɛɛwɔ ka kpa kuŋ sɛɛhzaa, ii daŋ doŋuu. 26Ií gilɛɛ wàá ga keeriilɔŋa ni di tinni ra la n mbusu lizibɔr. Di ii ɛɛ guŋ ba daŋ na ii chakpalli.”

english_text:
Hebrew Slaves
(Deuteronomy 15.12-18)
1The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
2 If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him. 3If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom. 4If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
5But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them. 6Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
