7A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does. 8If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her. 9If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
10If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife. 11If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it.
Murder and Other Violent Crimes
The Lord said:
12 Death is the punishment for murder. 13 But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside. 14If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
15Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
16 Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
17 Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
18Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed, 19and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
20Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves. 21However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
22Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve. 23But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life, 24 eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, 25burn for burn, cut for cut, and bruise for bruise.
26If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free. 27The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
28A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
29Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning. 30However, you may save your own life by paying whatever fine is demanded. 31This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter. 32If the bull kills a slave, you must pay the slave owner 30 pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
33Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property. 34You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
35If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
36If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_text:
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kpa Gbɔgni naa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.”
Yoma Gbɔgni wia
2“Di i bɛl maa wa yau Hibru hinuu, u daŋ humii binni anumbɛl. Ka di aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la wa hello, gil u dɔɔ u hiŋ di lii, gilɛɛ gil u turgi kummaa tɛi. 3Di u bɛnnɛ ballɛ, u bɛnnɛ niŋ kaa kaali. Ka di u ni u haannɛ ballɛ, u nuubuu niŋ kaali. 4Di u dɔɔri tɛu haaŋ u lul biibaala gɛɛ biihaana, a baal bɛnnɛ niŋ kaali. U haaŋ ni u biizi la waa, ɛɛ u dɔɔri horaa.
5Ka di a yom wa ŋɔ lugɔ u nɔŋŋi u dɔɔri ni u haaŋ ni biizi hinnɛ di ra nyiŋŋi ú du ba be, 6a dɛkkɔɔ u dɔɔri hiŋ kpogluu la nabɔnzi see, di ga lau u digni pɛli gbera gɛɛ u daa ni di kpa hɛm furuu, ú jaa ɛɛ u yom di hanna la.
7Di baal yoo u biihaaŋ tɛɛ nɛr, waabuu wàá wer dɔɔ u hiŋ alugɔ yombaal. 8Ka di u wia waa u dɔɔri la n yawuu, ú kpa ɛɛ haaŋ la ra par, ú gil u mɛɛ bir yawuu. Ka ú gilɛɛ wa yoou di ra tɛɛ hɔɔhra, dikuu uŋ wɔɔ ɛɛwɛ nɛnnɛ wia. 9Di unla maa wa yau biihaaŋ di tɛɛ u biibaal u ɛɛ u haaŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ uŋ kpogluu lugɔ u himmaa biihaaŋ. 10Di u kaa wa kpa hahnɛɛhiŋ, u gilɛɛ waa kpolli u hahlugli la diwee ni laala gunla uŋ faa ra tɛu la, di gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u nuu chɔɔi. 11Di wɔɔ wàá tɛɛ kuna ahoro naa bɛl maa, amɔ, ú tau ŋmɛnɛɛ ú ra la, di gilɛɛ waa lɛɛu kummaa.”
Nɛr pira dui ni kpui Gbɔgni wia
12“Nɛr la maa n niŋ lɔ u dɔŋhiŋ kpu, a dɛkkɔɔ ba kpu u ge gba. 13Ka di waa kuttɛɛ lɛi ɛɛ guŋ, ú chɔ la ga zuu bɔr la min niŋ lizi ii ra lɛɛ iihinaa de la. 14Di nɛr kuttɔɔ kpu u dɔŋhiŋ, ií kpu u ge gba. Haali di u chɔwɔɔ ga lau Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la gba, ka ii lawuu lii de, di kpuu.
15Di nɛr la maa wa lɔ u maa gɛɛ u mɛɛ, bá kpuu.
16Di nɛr la maa wa fittɔ lau nɛr yoo, gɛɛ di ba wa nau u be, bá kpu a hiŋ.
17Nɛr la maa n na see u mɛɛ gɛɛ u maa nua, bá kpuu.
18Di nɛra banɛɛ ra naa, bɛl kpa bii gɛɛ noguruŋ di lɔ u dɔŋ di duu wiila ka waa siuwɛ, ka chɔɔ waa kaa wer ra lii baŋgia, 19di unla baŋ lɔwɛɛ la wa wetto kpa daŋkpala di ra lii bossee, ba wàá ɛɛ unla n lɔu la wiimaa. Ka a dɛkkɔɔ u turgi u saŋa la uŋ chɔkkɛ la maa kim tɛu, ka ra du u tau u wa nyaagi nɛnnɛ.
20Di nɛr wa kpa daa di lɔɔzi u yombaal gɛɛ u yoŋhaaŋ, u siu a biini, a dɛkkɔɔ ba tɛr u digni. 21Ka di u wa izoo hɔpizi kpaŋ gɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ biini, ba gilɛɛ waa tɛr u digni, dikuubɛɛwiai, u kundɔɔliirɛ.
22Di baala waa naa, di ga magzi haaŋ n kpogli hia ú lul, di u lulaa haa waa helle, ka waa piree werge, gunla n par u jaari ani gunla nabɔnzi n sɛɛwɛ, gunnɛ unla n piruu la turgi. 23Ka di a haaŋ piroo werge waa, di wa siu, bá kpu a baal ge, 24di u siwiire u chɔg, bá chɔg u hor, di u nyinnɛ u ku, bá ku u ge nyiŋ, di u noniire u ku, bá ku u hor, di u naapeere u ku, bá ɛɛ u ge guŋ. 25Di ninne u kpa baaruu u boŋŋi, gɛɛ u lɔubuu u yembɛl yigli chal, ba ɛɛ u ge gba guŋ.
26Di nɛr lɔ u yombaal gɛɛ u yoŋhaaŋ siwii chɔgi, a dɛkkɔɔ u gil u jaa dɔɔ u hiŋ, u siwii chɔgaa hiŋ turgi u kinnɛ. 27Di u nyiŋ genii u lɔ foŋ, u gil u jaa dɔɔ u hiŋ, a turgi u kim.
28Di nɛbɛl nabal wa gbuuri baal gɛɛ haaŋ u siu, a dɛkkɔɔ ba paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu, ka gilɛɛ waa hee a nau ol. Ka a waa dɛkkɛ baŋ tɛr a nau hiŋ digni. 29Ka di a nau hiŋ zummɔ lugɔ a nau ɛɛ nakpaaliirɛ, ba ŋɔ u be, ka wɔɔ tɔwɛɛ du lig, ka u kaa wa kpu baal gɛɛ haaŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ ba paagi bia lɔɔzi a nau ni u dɔɔri hiŋ maa kpu. 30Ka di ba wa tɛu kim maa ŋɔ u turgi, u daŋ wer turgi a kim ka dɔɔ u miibɔɔ. 31Di a sel wa kpu biibaal gɛɛ biihaaŋ guŋ himmaanii ba ɛɛu. 32Di a nau wa lau yombaal gɛɛ yoŋhaaŋ di kpu, a dɛkkɔɔ u dɔɔri turgi saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, di tɛɛ a yom dɔɔri. Ka ba paagi bia lɔɔzi a nau kpu.
33Di nɛr wa pilli bɔɔ gɛɛ di u ki bɔɔrɛ ka wɔɔ tɔwɛɛ, nabal gɛɛ kawee wa chol u biini di siu, 34u daŋ turgi a sel kim tɛɛ u hiŋ, ka kpa a sesiwii.
35Di nɛbɛl nabal boŋŋi u dɔŋhiŋ hor ú siu, ba yoo u nyinii la di bɔnni u kebee a mɛgzi, di kaa bɔnni u siwii la ge ol, ba maa di mɛgzi. 36Ka di a ɛɛwɔ lugɔ bɛl ɛɛ nagbuuriirɛ, nɛr maa zum, ka u dɔɔri wɔɔ tɔwɛɛ, ka guŋ wa ɛɛ, u daŋ nyiŋŋi u nyinii di turgi u siwii la kim tɛɛ u hiŋ, ka kpau.”

english_text:
Property Laws
The Lord said:
1If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep. 2-4But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double.
If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
5If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
6If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
7Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double. 8But if the thief isn't caught, some judges will decide if you are the guilty one.
9Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
10Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking. 11If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough. 12But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it. 13If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
14Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it. 15But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it.
Laws for Everyday Life
The Lord said:
16 Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her. 17But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
18 Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
19 Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
20 Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
21 Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
22Do not mistreat widows or orphans. 23If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue. 24In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
25 Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need. 26 Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan, 27because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
28 Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
29Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me.
Dedicate to me your first-born sons 30and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
31 You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_text:
Kundɔɔlaa Gbɔgni wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Di nɛr la maa wa ŋmɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ nabal gɛɛ peezi di kpu gɛɛ di yoo, ú turgi nauna anue di du a nabal bɔɔ, di turgi peeza anaazu di du a peezi ge bɔɔ.
2Di ŋmɛɛŋ wa suahwɔ zuu nɛr dia ba lɔu kpu, nɛr la n kpuu la waa chɔgri maa dɔɔwɛ. 3Ka di bɔchaaŋ magaa guŋ ɛɛ, a hiŋ dɔɔ chɔgrii.
Di nɛr ŋmɛɛwɔ ba lawuu, a dɛkkɔɔ ú turgi kim. Ka di waa wette, a dɛkkɔɔ ba yoou di turgi a kim.
4Di nɛbɛl wa ŋmɛɛ nabal gɛɛ kawee gɛɛ peezi, ba lawuu di u haa wɔɔ kpuwɛɛ gɛɛ di yoou, u daŋ nyiŋŋi a sedee anɛɛ di turgi a kim.
5Di nɛr maa wa nɔɔni u sela a gaa di u koo gɛɛ u grepu daazi koo, ka a sela leu di ga zuu nɛbɛl koo di di u kuna, a dɛkkɔɔ u kpa u koo kuna di turgi a kim.
6Di nɛr maa gaa fuuh u koo kɔlaa gɛɛ kooree, a niŋ loŋŋi ga fuuh u dɔŋhiŋ mia la uŋ kummɛ di chaalaa dau gɛɛ anla n haa chigɛ gɛɛ u koo maa, a dɛkkɔɔ unla n du a niŋ la turgi a kim.
7Di nɛr kpa kebee gɛɛ u kunnanaa tɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ u dau, nɛbɛl wa ŋmɛɛa ba lawuu, u daŋ turgi a kuna guŋ dɔŋ bunɛɛ. 8Ka di ba wɔɔ lauwɛ waa, ba lau unla n dawaa la di la nabɔnzi see. Ba ga na di waabuu ŋmɛɛa gɛɛ di waalɛiyɛi? 9Di nɛra waa gbirgi dɔŋa nuuzi dikuu kuna wia, di naballɛ gɛɛ kaweere gɛɛ peezii gɛɛ laalaa gɛɛ kunla maa n leuwene, ba maa kpa a wia la nabɔnzi see, bá ga ŋɔa. Di a wa chol unla maa ni, ú nyiŋŋi a kundee dɔŋ anɛɛ di turgi u dɔŋhiŋ la.
10Di nɛr wa kpa u kawee gɛɛ u nabal gɛɛ u peezi gɛɛ u sel maa di tɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ ŋɔ ú ra binni, u wa siu gɛɛ ba wa boŋŋuu gɛɛ ba wa ŋmɛɛu nɛra harbɔɔ, 11ba kpa a wia di ba Kɔraawiizi see. Unla n na binnaa la wa hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi see alugɔ waa lɛi ŋmɛɛu. A dɛkkɔɔ lugɔ a kuŋ hiŋ sɛɛ lugɔ wibiire di gilɛɛ gil ú turgi kummaa. 12Ka di ba ŋmɛɛ a selle di lii u be, a dɛkkɔɔ lugɔ unla n na binni a sel la turgi u kim tɛɛ u hiŋ. 13Di sechɔgii bɛllɛ lawuu di di ka ka, a dɛkkɔɔ u binni la paa u bɔr la n kawɛɛ la, di wa bagli lugɔ wibiire. Di u wetto ɛɛ guŋ, wàá kaa dɔɔ kim un niŋ turgi.
14Di nɛr kim u dɔŋhiŋ sel, ba wa boŋŋuu gɛɛ di u siuwɔɔ, di a sel hiŋ la himmaa waa hoo de, di na lugɔ wibiire, ú kinni la daŋ turgi u kim. 15Ka di a sel hiŋ du denii ka guŋ ɛɛ, nɛr la n kimuu la waa kim maa dɔɔwɛ un niŋ turgi. Di u faa dau kebeere ka lɛɛ a sel, aabuu u kpa turgi u kim.”
Gbɔgni la n kaa jaa wia
16“Di baal maa wa lau biihaaŋ la n haa waa baal la un niŋ yuu dɔɔwɛ di nyiŋŋi, ú kuari u wia ka u jaa ɛɛ u haaŋ. 17Di a biihaaŋ mɛɛ waa ba yuuri hiŋ sɛɛwɛ, ka a baal daŋ haa turgi kuna la maa n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú turgi dikuu uŋ chɔguu la wia.
18Haaŋ la maa n na vug, bá kpuu.
19Di nɛr maa wa lau sel nyiŋŋi, bá kpuu.
20Nɛr la maa n vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ka ra kuari vuga, bá kpuu.
21Ií gilɛɛ waa sunni hɔɔhra di ra ɛɛ baa wichɔgaa. Ií gba faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa Ijip hɛri.
22Ií gilɛɛ waa sunni luhaaŋ gɛɛ lalbie maa. 23Di ii ɛɛ guŋ, ba wii duŋ, n daŋ nuu ba wiraa. Wibii maa n daŋ hiini baa. 24N baaŋ daŋ fuuh ii ni werge maa, ń kpuuzi ia laal biini, ka ii haana ni biizi birgi luhaana ni lalbiizi.
25Di n nɛra la bɛl maa wa nyaawɔ di kim kebii u dɔŋ be, u gilɛɛ ɛɛ lugɔ kebikinni di wàá saguu nii. 26Di i lɛɛ i dɔŋhiŋ wɛjɛ dau talma, ɛɛ ania ka bir kpau ga tɛu ka wiizi chol, 27dikuubɛɛwiai, u bɛnnɛ u wɛjɛ. Bɛɛ u kaa dɔɔ ú kpa tɔ di chɔɔi. Di a waa nuu, u wii duŋ, n daŋ nuu u wiraa, dikuu minna suŋ nɛra ni wia.
28Gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi gɛɛ di ra see nɛr la n ɛɛ i hɛri nabɔma nua.
29Bɛl maa ɔɔ lizi mia, siŋ ani ɔlivi nuu di ra sunziŋ, di gilɛɛ waa kpolliŋ. A dɛkkɔɔ bɛl maa ɔɔ kpa u biibambilugli tɛŋ. 30Gunnɛ bɛ́l maa ɔɔ ɛɛ u nauna ni peeza biilugla. Ka u ɔɔ gil a du a maawaa be di wa hel hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ lawaa, ú kpau tɛŋ.
31Ii ɛɛ n nɛra la miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hinnɛ. Awia, ii gilɛɛ waa hee sel maa u dɔŋa n diwee ka ka. Ií ɔɔ kpaa tɛɛ nuuzihina.”

english_text:
Equal Justice for All
The Lord said:
1 Don't spread harmful rumors or help a criminal by giving false evidence.
2Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice. 3 And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
4 If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
5If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
6 Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court. 7Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
8Don't accept bribes. Judges are blinded and justice is twisted by bribes.
9 Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like.
Laws for the Sabbath
The Lord said:
10 Plant and harvest your crops for six years, 11but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
12 Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
13Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names.
Three Annual Festivals
(Exodus 34.18-26; Deuteronomy 16.1-17)
The Lord said:
14Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
15 Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
16 Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
17Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
18Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
19 Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
A Promise and a Warning
The Lord said:
20I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you. 21Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion. 22If you faithfully obey him, I will be a fierce enemy of your enemies. 23My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out. 24Don't worship their gods or follow their customs. Instead, destroy their idols and shatter their stone images.
25Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong. 26Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
27I will terrify those nations and make your enemies so confused that they will run from you. 28I will make the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites panic as you approach. 29But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere. 30Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
31I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land. 32But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods. 33Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
translation_text:
Wibii dii ni nɛsunaa Gbɔgni wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ wa kpa amaniye la n ɛɛ kara di ra yaari. Gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ wia di ra hiini biinikpola hiŋ.
2Gilɛɛ wàá hiŋ nɛkpila di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Di i waa ŋɔ wia seriya diiribɔr, gilɛɛ waa jaa nɛkpila ni di lau wia birgi, a chɔgi wibii dii. 3Di nyaari wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, gilɛɛ wa lɛɛ ra jaa u ni seriya diiri bɔr.
4Di i wa na i dɔm navarga gɛɛ kawee n leuwe, ɛɛ ania ka lawuu ga tɛu. 5Di i na i haahri kawee n chigɛ buntɔga a nyaŋŋuu u chol, gilɛɛ giluu de, aah siwii di hiinuu.
6Di nyaara wa la wia ni nabɔnzi see, gilɛɛ waa kpolli baa wibii. 7Gilɛɛ waa jaa karkanna ni. Gilɛɛ waa kpu nɛnanii la n waa wichɔgaa biini jaawɛ gɛɛ wibii hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ kpa bilchɔg tɛɛ a guŋ hiŋ.
8Gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ sunzaa la n niŋ gil i siwee tɔɔgi, i di wibii huhzi.
9Ií gilɛɛ waa sunni hɔɔhri. Ií zum gunla hɔɔhrinaa n duwɛɛnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ge gba faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa Ijip hɛri.”
Heezaa Hɔpizii Gbɔgni wia
10“Ií kpa binni anumbɛl di ra duu kuna ii kooni di ra kumaa bina maa. 11Ka aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biini, ii gilɛɛ waa par a hɛri gɛɛ di waa duu kummaa de. Di diutɛɛri wa lii a hɛri, a ɛɛ nyaara ge horaa. Di ba ge wa gil a yemmaa, pir sela genii dɔɔa a di. Guŋ himmaanii ií ɛɛ ii grepuzi ni ɔlivizi kooni.
12Ií ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛl di hum ii huma, ka aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la waa, ií ɔɔ heezi. Guŋ gil ii yoma baŋ lul ii diini ni hɔɔhra la n du ii be di ra hum ia, ni ii navargazi ni u kauzi maa gba wer heezi.
13Ií ra du tau di ra ɛɛ wia la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia la. Ií gilɛɛ waa yir vug maa sɔŋ di ra hɛɛhzuu, di gilɛɛ gil ba ra nuu a sɔna ii nuuzi gba.”
Hɔpizizenaa Ahoro Dii wia
14“Ií ɔɔ di hɔpizizenaa buhoro bina maa biini di ra chɔliŋ.
15Ií ɔɔ di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizenaa. Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛrɛ ií ɔɔ hee paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ gunla miŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ la. Ií ɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ baagu la banna yir Abib la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u biinii ii kpa di lii Ijip hɛri la.
Nɛ́r maa gilɛɛ waa ba n be ni u nodumazi.
16Ií ɔɔ di Kuna Kumaa Hɔpizizeŋ di ii waa faari a kumaa.
Ií ɔɔ di Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ bina maa tuna, di ii wa chaali ii kooni kuna di ba bol.
17Bina maa diuzenaa dii buhoro naa biini, a dɛkkɔɔ baal maa ɔɔ ba di wa jaami mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la.
18Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa kunla maa n dɔɔ yiisi di ra jaa sel maa ni, di lizi mbusu ra tɛŋ.
Ií gilɛɛ waa gil sel la iiŋ kpawɛɛ lizi mbusu tɛŋ la nuu wàá chi hɔɔ ra pizi.
19Bina maa, ií ɔɔ lizi ii pattikuna lugli horpazi di ba Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la Dia.
Ií ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ wa kpa buuŋ ilanii di ra daali u bie.”
Kɔraawiizi mɛlika n niŋ ɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ sirya wia
20“Ií ra nuu, n na hum mɛlikaa ú tɔ ii see di kpogli ia, di ga hel bɔr la miŋ kuarɛɛ dau ia la. 21Ií keŋŋi digna di ra nuu u be, di ra hiŋ gunla maa un niŋ bagli ia. Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u nua. Di ii wa vɛɛwɔ, wàá gil tɛɛ ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, n tɛubuu fɔŋŋa. 22Ka di ii ra nuu u be nɛnnɛ, di ra hiŋ gunla miŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ ia la, guŋwaa, ii dɔma daŋ ɛɛ n dɔma. Banla ge n niŋ kpa naari huuzi ia, n daŋ lɛɛ ii nua. 23N mɛlika daŋ tɔ ii see di hiini ia ii ga zuu nɛra la banna yir Amɔri, Hitti, Pɛriz, Keenan, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina la hɛssi. N daŋ dim ba maa. 24Ií gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ ba vuga dɔɔra gɛɛ di ra kuaraa gɛɛ di waa hiŋ ba wiɛɛlaa. Ií purgi ba vuga ni bia la baŋ baŋzɛɛ tɛɛa la burburbur. 25Ií ɔɔ ra jaami mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛŋ. Di ii ra ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ ɔɔ kissi ia, ii dɔɔ diwee ni nii, di lizi wiila maa ii ni. 26Ií haana hizi ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá lii gɛɛ bɛl maa ge wàá ɛɛ hahbara ii hɛri biini. N daŋ tɛɛ ia miibɔɔjaŋ ge jaa.
27N daŋ ɔɔ gil ɔnsii werge feli lau hɛri la maa hina ii ni baa n niŋ naa, ba bɔra ra sa, ba bugmi. N daŋ gil ii dɔma ɔɔ bir chɔ. 28N daŋ gil chirinchaazi tɔ ii see di ga duŋŋi Hivi, Keenan ani Hitti hina ii ŋmɛnɛɛ chaani. 29Ka màá duŋŋi baa biŋkpaŋ biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɛri daŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ, pir sela ge wazi werge tɛɛ ia. 30N danna duŋŋi baa tama tama guŋŋ, di ra la saŋa la iin niŋ wazi di wer dɔɔ a hɛri la.
31N daŋ gil ii hɛri magbɔɔni ga Muuzeŋaahmu la ga hel Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn, di kaa lii hɛribɔduma di ga chug Muu Yufretis la. N daŋ kpa nɛra la n du a hɛri du ii nonee ií duŋŋi baa. 32Ií gilɛɛ waa gil ii ni baa ni ba vuga dɔɔ nuukpaŋ. 33Ií gilɛɛ waa gil ba so ii hɛri, di guŋ lɛi ba daŋ gil ii ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu n ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba vuga kuaraa daŋ birgi lugɔ sidɛɛzi di lauri ia.”

english_text:
The People Agree To Obey God
1The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and 70 of Israel's leaders. They must worship me at a distance, 2but you are to come near. Don't let anyone else come up.”
3Moses gave the Lord's instructions to the people, and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded!” 4Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said.
The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel. 5He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord. 6Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar. 7Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
8 Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
9Moses and Aaron, together with Nadab and Abihu and the 70 leaders, went up the mountain 10and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
11Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank.
Moses on Mount Sinai
12The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.” 13Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
14Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
15When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it, 16and the bright glory of the Lord came down and stayed there. The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and on the seventh day the Lord told Moses to come into the cloud. 17-18 Moses did so and stayed there 40 days and nights. To the people, the Lord's glory looked like a blazing fire on top of the mountain.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi chigaa wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Í ni Aarɔn ni u biibaal Nada, Abihu ani Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi tokkoahoro ni fi tinni ba n be bizeŋ la nyuu. Di ii waa ba, ii chi bɔɔnɛɛ, ka jaamiŋ. 2Ka hìŋ́ Moosis bɛnnɛ niŋ hel n be. I dɔŋahina lawaa, gilɛɛ wàá dugliŋ. A nɛra waa gba gilɛɛ waa tinni a bizeŋ.”
3Moosis n ga ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii ni u Gbɔgni la maa wia tɛɛ a nɛra, ba maa kpau sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ ɛɛ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.” 4Moosis jaa sɛbi wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la di dau.
Denii u izi chɔɔzimpikke ni di kuari mbusu lizibɔr a bizeŋ zɛɛ, di kpa bia fidaanɛɛ ge baŋzi, bɛl maa chi tɛɛ Izrɛl dizi fidaanɛɛ la. 5Denii u gil Izrɛl hina biipɔllaa la ga lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa, di kpu naballi di lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 6Moosis bargi a challi bɔra anɛɛ, di kpa bɔkpaŋ du tassazi biini, ka kpa anla n kawɛɛ di mizi mbusu lizibɔr la. 7Denii u kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Hɔŋ la di karmuu tɛɛ a nɛra. Ba sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua di ɛɛ wii la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ.”
8Denii Moosis kpa a chal la n du a tassazi biini la di mizi baa ka ŋɔ, “Chal la n kuari ii ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋ labuu keŋ, dikuu u wiŋɔɔlaa la wia.” 9Moosis, Aarɔn, Nadab, Abihu ani Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi tokkoahoro ni fi la faa tinni a bizeŋ, 10di ga na Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la. Kumbɛl ɛɛ lugɔ binanii bɛl banna yir safaaya la du u naazi zɛɛ di chaani lugɔ chiŋ. 11Ka Kɔraawiizi faa waa a Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi hiŋ tɔɔrɛɛ. Ba faa na Kɔraawiizii ka piri. Awia, ba di ka nyɔɔ.
12Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Tinni ba n be a bizeŋ naa nyubaaŋ di wa du ɛŋ ń kpa n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa la miŋ sɛbɛɛ dau bipɛntɛnzi ni di tɛi, í gaa bagli a nɛra.”
13Denii Moosis ni u balii Josua ra la, Moosis waa ga tinni a Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ nyubaaŋ. 14Moosis faa ŋɔ a nabɔnzi be, “Ií du bɔnnaa di ra kpaŋ yaa, ya wa bir ba ii be. Aarɔn ni Hur du ii benii. Di bɛl maa wa dɔɔ wii, ú kpa ba ba be.”
15Moosis n wa tinni a bizeŋ la nyubaaŋ, baama wa tɔ de maa. 16Kɔraawiizi girme ba di wa tɔ Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu di ra chaani guŋŋ hɔpizaa anumbɛl. Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la, Kɔraawiizi yir Moosis di lii a baama biini. 17Izrɛl hina waa be, Kɔraawiizi girme la faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niŋ n na di a bizeŋ nyubaaŋ. 18Denii u tinni a bizeŋ nyubaaŋ di ga zuu a baama la biini, di du de hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ.

english_text:
The Sacred Tent
(Exodus 35.4-9)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Tell everyone in Israel who wants to give gifts that they must bring them to you. 3Here is a list of what you are to collect: Gold, silver, and bronze; 4blue, purple, and red wool; fine linen; goat hair; 5tanned ram skins; fine leather; acacia wood; 6olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices to mix with the incense and with the oil for dedicating the tent and ordaining the priests; 7and onyx stones and other gems for the sacred vest and the breastpiece. 8I also want them to build a special place where I can live among my people. 9Make it and its furnishings exactly like the pattern I will show you.
The Sacred Chest
(Exodus 37.1-9)
The Lord said to Moses:
10Tell the people to build a chest of acacia wood 110 centimeters long, 66 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 11Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid. 12Make four gold rings and attach one of them to each of the four legs of the chest. 13Make two poles of acacia wood. Cover them with gold 14and put them through the rings, so the chest can be carried by the poles. 15Don't ever remove the poles from the rings. 16When I give you the Ten Commandments written on two flat stones, put them inside the chest.
17 Make the lid of the chest out of pure gold. 18-19Then hammer out two winged creatures of pure gold and fasten them to the lid at the ends of the chest. 20The creatures must face each other with their wings spread over the chest. 21Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest. 22I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do.
The Table for the Sacred Bread
(Exodus 37.10-16)
The Lord said:
23Make a table of acacia wood 88 centimeters long, 44 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 24-25Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border 75 millimeters thick. 26Make four gold rings and attach one to each of the legs 27-28near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold. 29-30 The table is to be kept in the holy place, and the sacred loaves of bread must always be on it. All bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings are to be made of pure gold and set on this table.
The Lampstand
(Exodus 37.17-24)
The Lord said:
31Make a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold 32with three branches on each of its two sides. 33There are to be three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 34and four on the stem. 35There must also be a blossom where each pair of branches comes out from the stem. 36The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 37The lamp on the top and those at the end of each of its six branches must be made so as to shine toward the front of the lampstand. 38The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold. 39The lampstand and its equipment will require 35 kilograms of pure gold, 40 and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_text:
Kuna baŋ lizɛɛ bá kpa kuari Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ ba lizi kuna di wa tɛŋ. I daŋ lɛɛ kunla bɛl maa bampirii n tɛu lugɔ ú kpa ba wa tɛŋ. 3Kuna naabuu í lɛɛ di lii ba be. Saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa, danyɛ, 4gessihuŋŋunanaa, peezi huna baŋ liiwe burgu, a aahma lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, a aahma choihchoih, wɛjɛ la baŋ kpa buuŋ huna di suah, 5pebala hɔna la baŋ liiwe a aah, hɔŋbuglaa, akeesia daazi, 6fintina nuuri, kunsɔɔhrisuma ban niŋ kpa di kuari nuuwaarii, daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la banna fuuh, 7binanaa banna yir ɔnigs ani anla n kawɛɛ ba kpa margi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma tagtakpurii ni u bampirii pɛɛŋ la ni.
8Gil ba kuari Tanti Diinanii tɛŋ ń wa du ba be de. 9Ií kuari u ni kuna la maa n du u biini la a du gunla himmaa min niŋ baglii.
Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka wia
10Kpa akeesia daazi di kuari dakka, ú jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛ ni keza, ú wassi ɛɛ nogume ni keza, ú chiŋ laŋaa ge ɛɛ nogume ni keza. 11Ŋmɛɛri saliŋ himmaa di tɔ u biini ni u har maa di kpa saliŋ bar u nua. 12Luu saliŋ gbittizi anaazu di kpa bɛl maa, dí du u naazi anaazu la bɛl maa ni, anɛɛ du keŋkere bɛl, anɛɛ ge du keŋkere bɛl. 13Kpa akeesia daa di kuari daajaŋra di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a maa ni. 14Kpaa di suuzi gbittizi la bɔɔni, bá ɔɔ wer lawaa di ra kpa a dakka. 15Ií ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa lizi a daazi. 16Kpa Gbɔgni fi la miŋ sɛbɛɛ dau bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ ni min niŋ tɛi la du u biini.
17Kpa saliŋ himmaa di kuari a dakka tua la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih u nɛra ni de la, ú jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛ ni keza, ú wassi ge ɛɛ nogume ni keza. 18Kpa saliŋ di luu chɛrubzi anɛɛ di hɔŋ a dakka tua tunazi. 19Luu a chɛrub bɛl u chi a dakka tua kɛrii bɛl, di kaa luu bɛl ge ú chi u kɛrii bɛl ge. Kpa saliŋ luu a ni a tua la maa á ɛɛ kpaŋ. 20Gil a chɛrubzi siwee chaŋ dɔŋa di ra binni a tua, a keeri ge yaa di guali u ni. 21Kpa bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la, min niŋ wa kpa tɛi la di du a Dakka biini, di kpa u nua tua di tɔ. 22N daŋ chem i ni bɔr la chɛrubzi la n chigɛ n ni n nɛra Nuukpaŋ Daansɛɛ Dakka ni la baambaaŋ. Di kpa n Gbɔgni maa tɛi, í ga tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia Tɛɛbul la wia
23Kpa akeesia daa di kuari tɛɛbul, ú jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛ, ú wassi ge ɛɛ nogume, ú chiŋ laŋaa ge ɛɛ nogume ni keza. 24Ŋmɛɛri saliŋ himmaa dí tɔ u maa di kpa aŋhina dí bar u kɛraa lugɔ gir. 25Kaa kuari gir bar u kɛraa, ú ɛɛ nopaal wassi maga di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ sag u ni. 26Luu saliŋ gbittizi anaazu, di kpa bɛl maa mari ú siraa anaazu la, u naazi n duwɛɛ la ni. 27Gbittizi la ban niŋ ɔɔ kpa daazi suu di ra chi a tɛɛbul la daŋ dugli gir la n bar u kɛraa la. 28Gil a daajaŋra ge gba ɛɛ akeesia daazi, di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a maa ni. 29Kpa saliŋ himmaa di kuari u pɛrɛtuzi, libizi, golaa ani tassazi, bá kpa yiili siŋ di ta ra tɛŋ. 30I daŋ kpa paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ ra tɛŋ la di sag a tɛɛbul ni n see, saŋa maa.
Fintina daa la wia
31Kpa saliŋ himmaa luu fintina daa ni u zɛɛ, di kuari u nuuri duuribɔra la a du lugɔ fiiri n punzee, a ni a daa maa ɛɛ kpaŋ. 32Ú dɔɔ kela anumbɛl, ahoro du ú keŋkere maa. 33Kela anumbɛl la bɛl maa daŋ dɔɔ nuuri duuribɔra ahoro lugɔ daa bɛl banna yir almɔn fiiri ni a pume. 34Luu nuuri duuribɔra lugɔ almɔn fiiri ni a pume anaazu di du u daa la ni, 35di luu pumkpaŋkpaŋa di du a kela anɛɛgaa maa zɛɛ. 36Saliŋ himmaanii bá kpa di luu a fintina daa ni u kela ani fiiri la maa n du u ni la, á maa ɛɛ kpaŋ.
37Kuari katooljigzi aniidaanɛɛ di hɔŋzi u ni, á ra chaani bɔr la uŋ chigɛ la see. 38Kuna la ban niŋ kpa di ra mɔnni fintina yakɔssi ni a pɛrɛtujigzi daŋ ɛɛ saliŋ himmaa. 39Saliŋ himmaa tɔgzi ɛɛwɛ lugɔ mibɔɔti kezaa, bá kpa kuari a fintina daa ni u kummaa. 40A du tau nɛnnɛ ka kuari a kuna gunla himmaa miŋ faa baglii bizeŋ la nyuu la.”

english_text:
Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.8-19)
The Lord said to Moses:
1The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 2Make each piece twelve meters long and two meters wide 3and sew them together into two panels with five sections each. 4-6Put 50 loops of blue cloth along one of the wider sides of each panel, then fasten the two panels at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
7-8As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth 13 meters by 2 meters each. 9Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent. 10Put 50 loops along one of the wider sides of each panel 11and fasten the two panels at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 12-13The panel of goat hair will be a meter longer than the tent itself, so fold 50 centimeters of the material behind the tent and on each side as a protective covering. 14Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.20-34)
The Lord said:
15Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent. 16Make each frame 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 17with two wooden pegs near the bottom. 18-21Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put 20 of these frames along the south side and 20 more along the north. 22For the back wall along the west side use six frames 23-24with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom. 25Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
26-27Make five crossbars for each of the wooden frames, 28with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 29Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through. 30Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain.
The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.35-38)
The Lord said:
31-33 Make a curtain to separate the holy place from the most holy place. Use fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Cover four acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a silver stand. Then fasten gold hooks to the posts and hang the curtain there.
34Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid. 35Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
36For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 37Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Gil ba kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa la baŋ ŋmɛɛnɛɛ nɛnnɛ ni gessi la baŋ liiwe aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, zagbiiŋ nii ani u aahmu choihchoih, di suah patiisazi fi, di gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ, tɔɔhzi chɛrubzi di du a ni. 2Gil a patiisazi maa mɛgzi dɔŋa. Bɛl maa jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko ni ŋmantannaazi, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi anaazu. 3Gil ba kpa anue di nyɛr choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, di kaa kpa anue la ge n kawɛɛ di ɛɛ guŋ. 4Gil ba kpa pɛɛŋ burgu di gurgi lugɔ suzaa di nyɛr du a bɛl maa nua. 5Gil bá kuari suzaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi di du lugli patiisa la ni, di kaa kuari suzaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi di du nɛɛhiŋ la tuna, a chaŋ dɔŋa. 6Kpa saliŋ di luu kuna lugɔ kuŋgorgaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi di kpaa gorgi a patiisazi, a choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, á Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia maa ɛɛ kpaŋ.
7Kpa buuŋ huna di suah patiisazi fidikpaŋ di tɔ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia. 8A dɛkkɔɔ a maa mɛgzi, bɛl maa jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi anaazu. 9Kpa anue di nyɛr choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, di kpa anumbɛl ge nyɛr choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, di kpa anumbɛlhiŋ la kpɛu a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia see. 10Nyɛr suzaa tokkoanɛɛgaa ni fizi di du a bɛl maa tuna hor ni. 11Kpa danyɛ luu kuŋgorgaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, di du a suzaa la ni a lau a tanti dia ú ɛɛ kpaŋ. 12Gil ba kpa patiisa la yeŋ n kawɛɛ la, di sag a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia harbɔɔ. 13A patiisazi naa jaŋzi daŋ kaali a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la nogume maga, u keŋkerezi anɛɛ la maa. A bɔr la n kawɛɛ daŋ sag a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia harbɔɔ, di tɔ u ni nɛnnɛ. 14Kpa pebala hɔna baŋ liiwe a aah di kuari kuntɔɔrikuŋ di tɔ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia, di kaa kpa hɔŋbuglaa di kuari bɛl di tɔ sag a ni.
15Kpa akeesia daazi di kuari a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia. 16Á daazi la bɛl maa jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi fi, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogume ni keza. 17Mɔŋ a daa bɛl maa zɛɛ u dɔɔ naazi anɛɛ a mɛgzi dɔŋa. Kuari a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia daabaŋlaa la maa guŋ. 18Kuari daabaŋlaa tokko di du a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere 19di kpa saliŋhuŋŋa luu a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra tokkoanɛɛ, anɛɛgaa du a daabaŋlaa bɛl maa zɛɛ di lauraa chiŋŋi. 20Kuari daazi tokko di du u wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ge, 21di kaa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa luu a ge zɛɛ hɔŋribɔra tokkoanɛɛ, di kpa anɛɛgaa du bɛl maa zɛɛ. 22Kuari daabaŋlaa anumbɛl di du a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia harbɔɔ wiicholii tuna la, 23di kaa kuari daabaŋlaa anɛɛ di du a Dia siraa anɛɛ la n du tuna la. 24A siraa anɛɛ naa daabaŋlaa la daŋ ɛɛ anɛɛgaa guŋŋ di lii zɛɛ di la chiŋ di ga suu gbitti kpaŋ ni. Gunnɛ bá kuari a maa. 25Awia, a daabaŋlaa daŋ ɛɛ ŋmantannaazi ani a zɛɛzi saliŋhuŋŋa hɔŋribɔra ɛɛ fidaanumbɛl, anɛɛ du bɛl maa zɛɛ.
26Kaa kpa akeesia daazi kuari daakaŋlaa, anue kaŋli Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia keŋkere bɛl daabaŋlaa la ni, 27anue ge kaŋli anla n du u keŋkere la hiŋ ni, anue ge kaŋli u wiicholii hora la n du u tuna la ni. 28A baambaaŋ daakaŋlii la daŋ kaŋli keŋkere bɛl maa daabaŋlaa la baambaaŋ ni di wa kaali, di lii tuna bɛl di ga chug tuna bɛl. 29Ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a daabaŋlaa la bɛl maa ni. Di luu saliŋ gbittizi di du a ni, á lauri a daakaŋlaa kpogli, di kaa ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a daakaŋlaa ge ni.
30Gil ba kuari a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia gunla miŋ baglii bizeŋ la nyuu la.
31Gil ba kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa ni peezi huna baŋ liiwe aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina ge aah choihchoih di suah patiisa, di gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ tɔɔhzi chɛrubzi di du u ni. 32Luu saliŋ kuŋgorgaa du akeesia daabaŋlaa anaazu, saliŋ n tɔ a ni, a chi a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra la n ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa la ni, di gil a kuŋgorgaa lau a patiisa di sag. 33Gil a kuŋgorgaa lau a patiisa, ka kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la n du u biini la di chiŋŋi u har. A patiisa daŋ bargi Bɔnaniinanii la di lii Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la ni. 34Gil ba kpa N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la tua di tɔu. 35Gil ba kpa a tɛɛbul la di chiŋŋi a patiisa har wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, di gil ba kpa fintina daa la ge chiŋŋi de wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere, a chaŋ dɔŋa.
36Kpa gessi la n ɛɛ peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina ge aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa, di suah patiisazi, di gil ba tɔɔhzaa, di kpa tɔ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia dominua. 37Kpa akeesia daazi anue di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a ni, di luu saliŋ kuŋgorgaa du a ni, di kpa danyɛ luu a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra.”

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 38.1-7)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Use acacia wood to build an altar 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high, 2and make each of the four top corners stick up like the horn of a bull. Then cover the whole altar with bronze, including the four horns. 3All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4-5Halfway up the altar build a ledge around it, and cover the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. Then attach a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners of the altar. 6-7Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar. 8Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 38.9-20)
The Lord said:
9-15Surround the sacred tent with a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. Use 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods.
Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts. 16Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
17-18Make the curtains that surround the courtyard 2.25 meters high and hang them from the bronze posts with silver hooks and rods. 19Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard.
The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place
(Leviticus 24.1-4)
The Lord said to Moses:
20Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning 21in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_text:
Mbusu lizibɔr wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kpa akeesia daazi di kuari mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr, ú chiŋ laŋaa ɛɛ nogumzi ahoro, ú jaŋzi ni u wassi maa ɛɛ nogumzi anuezi. 2Sɛɛh u siraa anaazu la maa a baŋzi lugɔ nyigzi, a ni mbusu lizibɔr la maa ɛɛ kpaŋ. Ŋmɛɛri danyɛ tɔ u maa. 3Kpa danyɛ di luu mbusu lizibɔr kuna naa, viini la ban niŋ ɔɔ paa u hɔɔhri di ra du, sɔɔbulzi, hɛnni la ban ninna du chal di ra mizi, dunozi n dɔɔ nyina ba ɔɔ kpa di ra tɔɔhzi ola ani nimbuurikuna. 4Kpa danyɛ di luu nyagrinyagri ni gbittizi anaazu di du u siraa anaazu la ni. 5Kpa a nyagrinyagri di ga gir la zɛɛ di suu u biini u ga hel u baambaaŋ. 6Kpa akeesia daazi dí kuari daajaŋra, dí ŋmɛɛri danyɛ tɔa. 7Kpa a daajaŋra di suuzi a gbittizi la n du u keŋkerezi anɛɛ la bɔɔni, di ba waa chiu. 8Kpa daazi di kuari mbusu lizibɔr, di gil u dɔɔ bɔɔ gunla miŋ baglii a bizeŋ nyuu la.
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia diŋŋee wia
9Kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa patiisazi di teŋ diŋŋee bar n Tanti Dia hiŋ. U wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere jaŋzi daŋ ɛɛ nogumzi kalfa, 10ú dɔɔ daabaŋlaa ni a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra tokkozi, baŋ kpa danyɛ luu. Luu saliŋhuŋŋa kuŋgorgaa ni lugbidaazi la ban niŋ kpa sagzi a daabaŋlaa maa ni. 11Ɛɛ u wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ge guŋ.
12A diŋŋee wiicholii wassi daŋ ɛɛ nogumzi tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, di dɔɔ patiisazi, daabaŋlaa fi ni a zɛɛzi danyɛ hɔŋribɔra fi. 13U wiifurii paga la dominua n duwɛɛ la ge wassi daŋ ɛɛ nogumzi tokkoanɛɛ ni fi. 14Patiisazi la jaŋzi n ɛɛ nogumzi fidaanue daŋ tɔ a dominua keŋkere bɛl, di dɔɔ daabaŋlaa ahoro ani a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra, á lawaa kpogli. 15U keŋkere la hiŋ ge, du guŋ.
16Kpa peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina ge aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di suah patiisa, u jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko, di gil ba tɔɔhzuu di kpa tɔ a diŋŋee dominua. Daabaŋlaa anaazu daŋ hɔŋzi a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra anaazu ni di lawuu kpogli. 17Daabaŋlaa la maa n bar a diŋŋee la daŋ dɔɔ saliŋhuŋŋa kuŋgorgaa ni lugbidaazi ani a zɛɛzi danyɛ hɔŋribɔra. 18A diŋŋee jaŋzi daŋ ɛɛ nogumzi kalfa, u wassi ɛɛ tokkoanɛɛ ni fi di dɔɔ patiisazi baŋ kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa suah, a chiŋ laŋaa ɛɛ nogumzi anue, di dɔɔ danyɛ hɔŋribɔra. 19Kuna la n kawɛɛ ban niŋ kpa di ra hum n Tanti Dia la biini la, danyɛɛ bá kpa di luu a maa. Daasiraa ban niŋ kpa lauri a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni a diŋŋee daazi maa, danyɛɛ ba kpa lua.
Fintina daa nuu wia
20Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be bá tɛi ɔlivi nuu la n du yelemm, guŋ gil a fintinazi wer di ra lau saŋa maa. 21Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini, patiisa la n teŋ N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka see baŋgia la, Aarɔn ni u biibaalaa niŋ gil a fintinazi la nine ra lau Kɔraawiizi see, di lii duana di ra la hɔpizaa. Kenne niŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ni ba naanna, di hanna la.”

english_text:
The Clothes for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.1-7)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Send for your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They are the ones I have chosen from Israel to serve as my priests. 2Make Aaron some beautiful clothes that are worthy of a high priest. 3Aaron is to be dedicated as my high priest, and his clothes must be made only by persons who possess skills that I have given them. 4Here are the items that need to be made: a breastpiece, a priestly vest, a robe, an embroidered shirt, a turban, and a sash. These sacred clothes are to be made for your brother Aaron and his sons who will be my priests. 5Use only gold and fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool, for making these clothes.
The Vest for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.2-7)
The Lord said:
6-8Make the entire priestly vest of fine linen skillfully woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and decorate it with gold. It is to have two shoulder straps to support it and a sash that fastens around the waist.
9-12Put two onyx stones in gold settings, then attach one to each of the shoulder straps. On one of these stones engrave the names of Israel's first six sons in the order of their birth. And do the same with his remaining six sons on the other stone. In this way Aaron will always carry the names of the tribes of Israel when he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people.
13-14Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold.
The Breastpiece for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.8-21)
The Lord said:
15From the same costly material make a breastpiece for the high priest to use in finding out what I want my people to do. 16It is to be 22 centimeters square and folded double 17with four rows of three precious stones: In the first row put a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald; 18in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond; 19in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; 20and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount the stones in delicate gold settings 21and engrave on each of them the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
22-25Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps. 26Attach two other gold rings to the lower inside corners next to the vest 27and two more near the bottom of the shoulder straps right above the sash. 28Then take a blue cord and tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. This will keep the breastpiece in place.
29In this way Aaron will have the names of the twelve tribes of Israel written on his heart each time he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people. 30 He must also wear on his breastpiece the two small objects that he uses to receive answers from me.
The Other High-Priestly Clothes
(Exodus 39.22-26,30,31)
The Lord said:
31Under his vest Aaron must wear a robe of blue wool 32with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out. 33-34 Along the hem of the robe weave pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a gold bell between each of them. 35If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
36On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.” 37Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord, 38so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
39Make Aaron's robe and turban of fine linen and decorate his sash with fancy needlework.
The Clothes for the Other Priests
(Exodus 39.27-29)
40Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them. 41Then dress Aaron and his sons in these clothes, pour olive oil on their heads, and ordain them as my priests.
42Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves. 43Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina bɔmbɔga wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Yir i kpɛɛma Aarɔn ni u biibaala Nadab, Abihu, Ɛliaza, ani Itama, di lii Izrɛl hina biini, bá wa ɛɛ n kizeehina di ra humiŋ. 2Nyɛr kizeehiŋ bɔmbɔga tɛɛ i kpɛɛma Aarɔn, a guŋ gil u dɔɔ sɔŋ ni girme. 3Ŋɔ nɛra la maa miŋ tɛɛ nunzuma ba zum nonee huma nɛnnɛ la be lugɔ bá nyɛr bɔmbɔga la n wesse tɛɛ Aarɔn ú bɔg. A hɔl la ban niŋ sɔu di lizi u doŋa ha, ú ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii n be, di ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ di ra humiŋ la. 4Bɔmbɔga naabuu bá nyɛr. Bampirii pɛɛŋ, tagtakpurii, tagtajiga, tagtajaŋ, namu ani kirsɔɔ. Gil ba nyɛr a keŋ kizeehiŋ bɔmbɔga naa tɛɛ i kpɛɛma Aarɔn ani u biizi bá ɛɛ n kizeehina di hum ra tɛŋ. 5Kpa saliŋ gessi ni peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di nyɛraa.
Tagtakpurii la wia
6Gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ kpa gessizi, aŋhina ɛɛ saliŋ, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di nyɛr a tagtakpurii. 7Bá nyɛr vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa di mari u siraa, ú ɔɔ wer lawaa di vɔɔzi. 8Ba daŋ kpa saliŋ gessizi ni gessizi aŋhina n ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina aah choihchoih, ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di suah u chara kirsɔɔ la nɛnnɛ, ú du lugɔ pɛɛŋ la himmaa, a maa ɛɛ kpaŋ.
9Kpa binanaa anɛɛ banna yir ɔnigs, di sɛɛh ii naabaal Jekɔb biizi fidibanɛɛ la sɔna di dau a ni. 10Sɛɛhzaa gunla baŋ lul baa di hiŋ dɔŋa ni la, sɔna anumbɛl du bii maa ni. 11Gil nɛr la n zum binanaa sɛɛih, ú sɛɛh ba sɔna hiŋ du a binanaa anɛɛ hiŋ ni, di kpa saliŋ ŋmɛnni di baataa du u ni. 12Kpaa vɔɔzi margi a tagtakpurii vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa la ni. Á ɛɛ liize bia tɛɛ Izrɛl dizi fidaanɛɛ la. Aarɔn daŋ ɔɔ chi ba sɔnaa u vaampɛrɛzi ni a ɛɛ liize di tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 13Gil ba luu saliŋ wayananaa di baataa margi, 14di pɛr saliŋ himmaa yɔlɔzi anɛɛ lugɔ ŋmɛnni di kpaa lauri a bɔbaataa la.
Bampirii pɛɛŋ la wia
15Gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ nyɛr pɛɛŋ la n na tɔ bampirii maga bɛŋ la, di tɛɛ n Dia Kizeehina nabɔma, u ɔɔ kpa di ra zum Kɔraawiizi kipar. A pɛɛŋ daŋ du lugɔ tagtakpurii la pɛɛŋ himmaa. Gessizi la n ɛɛ saliŋ, burgu, zagbiiŋ nii, a aahma choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaarɛ ba kpa di suauh. 16Gil u jaŋzi ni u wassi maa ɛɛ nopaal wassi maga, í kpɛwuu bunɛɛ. 17Kpa binanaa la yoola n kpolle di margi u ni a hiŋzi dɔŋa lugɔ pichɔŋzi anaazu. A lugli pichɔŋa la daŋ dɔɔ binanaa banna yir rubi ni topaz ani bɛril, 18pichɔnnɛɛhiŋ la daŋ dɔɔ tɛkɔis, saafaya ani ɛmɛral, 19horohiŋ la dɔɔ jasint, aget ani amɛtis, 20naazuhiŋ la ge dɔɔ krisolait, ɔnigs ani jaspa. Kpa saliŋ ŋmɛnni di baataa du u ni. 21Gil a bia ɛɛ fidaanɛɛ, bɛl maa chi tɛɛ Jekɔb biibaala la sɔna, di gil ba sɛɛh Izrɛl dizi fidaanɛɛ la sɔna di du bɛl maa ni.
22Pɛr saliŋ himmaa yɔlɔzi di du a bampirii pɛɛŋ ni lugɔ ŋmɛŋ. 23Luu saliŋ gbittijigzi anɛɛ di kpaa margi a pɛɛŋ siraa anɛɛ ni, 24di kpa saliŋ yɔlɔzi la di vɔɔzi a gbittijigzi la n du bampirii pɛɛŋ siraa la ni. 25Lau a yɔlɔzi nuuzi anɛɛ la n kawɛɛ la, di vɔɔzi margi a bɔbaataa anɛɛ la n du a vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa la tagtakpurii la see. 26Luu saliŋ gbittijigzi anɛɛ, di du u siraa anɛɛ la n du a bampirii pɛɛŋ biini kɛrii, n dugli a tagtakpurii la. 27Kaa luu saliŋ gbittijigzi anɛɛ di du vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa la zɛɛ, n du tagtakpurii la see, di dugli bɔr la baŋ nyɛttɛ choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, u chara kirsɔɔ la chiŋ. 28Kpa ŋmɛmburgu di lau gbittijigzi la n du bampirii pɛɛŋ la ni, di vɔɔzi margi gbittijigzi la n du tagtakpurii la ni, di lawuu vɔɔ mari chara kirsɔɔ la, ú gilɛɛ waa lii a tagtakpurii ni.
29Saŋa maa di Aarɔn wa zuu Bɔnaniinanii la, u daŋ ɔɔ dɔɔ Izrɛl hina dizi sɔna u bampirii ni, dikuu un laali bampirii pɛɛŋ la n niŋ gil u zum mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi kipar, guŋ gil n ɔɔ ra liizi n nɛra wia. 30Gil ba kpa Urim ni Tumim la di du bampirii pɛɛŋ la biini, guŋ gil a du Aarɔn be di u wàá ba n see. Gunnɛ niŋ kaa gil ú zum n kipar di ŋɔ ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina bɔmbɔga aŋhina wia
31Kpa pɛɛmburgu di nyɛr tagtajaŋ ba ɔɔ laali tagtakpurii di sag u ni. 32Fur nyuu zuuribɔr u baambaaŋ. Di muuguu nɛnnɛ u gilɛɛ waa piili. 33Kaa kpa gessizi la baŋ kpa peezi huna di ta, di liaa, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii ani a aahma choihchoih, di tɔɔhzi kuna n du gulegule lugɔ daa bɛl nɔna n lugɔ pomegranet di du u nua bar, di kpa saliŋ bɛlinzi di du anɛɛ maa baambaaŋ. 34A saliŋ bɛlinzi ni a pomegranet nɔna daŋ hiŋzi dɔŋa ni a tagtajaŋ nua bɔmuugii la maa di bar. 35A dɛkkɔɔ Aarɔn ɔɔ laaluu saŋa maa di u waa hum kizeehiŋ huma. Di u waa zuu Bɔnaniinanii la biini n see gɛɛ di waa lii, a bɛlinzi daŋ ɔɔ ra gbɔgzi ba ra nuu, ú gilɛɛ waa siu.
36Luu saliŋ himmaa pɛrɛtu, di sɛbi wia naa dau u ni, ‘BA KPAUBUU TƐƐ KƆRAAWIIZI U ƐƐ KUNNANIINANII.’ 37Kpa ŋmɛmburgu di vɔɔ mari namu la see. 38Aarɔn daŋ ɔɔ kpau di vɔɔ mari u hile, guŋ gil ń lɛɛ mbusuzi lizaa kuna la Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ lizi di ra tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la. Haali di ba wa leuwo di ɛɛ wichɔgii maa, di lii a lizaa wia biini gba, ka Aarɔnnɛ niŋ lɛɛ a chɔgri. U daŋ ɔɔ mari u hilee saŋa maa di gil ba mbusuzi la banna lizi la, du wer di su mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi siwii.
39Kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa di suah pɛɛŋ di nyɛr tagtajaŋ ni namu la. Gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ, tɔɔhzi kunnanaa du kirsɔɔ la ni. 40Gil ba nyɛr tagtajaŋra, kirsɔɔzi ani kahurozi tɛɛ Aarɔn biizi, á gil ba dɔɔ sɔŋ ni girme. 41Kpa bɔmbɔga naa di bɔg i kpɛɛma Aarɔn ni u biibaala. Ka ɛɛ nuu waari ba nyuuni, di kpa nonee sagzi ba ni, di kpa baa tɛŋ ba birgi n kizeehina di ra humiŋ.
42Gil ba nyɛr gessihuŋŋunanaa galiŋkpuree ban niŋ du biini, a chi ba charazi di wa hel ba naapɔga. 43Aarɔn ni u biizi daŋ ɔɔ bɔg a bɔmbɔga naa saŋa maa, di ba waa zuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia gɛɛ di ra la mbusu lizibɔr la, ba ga hum ba huma Bɔnaniinanii la. Guŋ gil ba wàá ɛɛ wichɔgaa di dɔɔ chɔgri, di siu.
Keŋ daŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u naanna di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

english_text:
Instructions for Ordaining Priests
(Leviticus 8.1-36)
The Lord said to Moses:
1When you ordain Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests, choose a young bull and two rams that have nothing wrong with them. 2Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil. 3Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
4Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves. 5Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash. 6Put on his turban with its narrow strip of engraved gold 7and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
8Next, dress Aaron's sons in their special shirts, 9caps, and sashes, then ordain them, because they and their descendants will always be priests.
10Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head. 11Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent. 12Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar. 13Then take the fat from the animal's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and send them up as an offering to me in the smoke from the altar. 14But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
15Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head. 16Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar. 17Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head. 18 Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
19Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head. 20Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar. 21Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
22This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 23Take one loaf of each kind of bread from the basket, 24and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me. 25After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
26You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
27-28In the future, when anyone from Israel offers the ribs and a hind leg of a ram either to ordain a priest or to ask for my blessing, the meat belongs to me, but it may be eaten by the priests. This law will never change.
29-30After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
31Boil the meat of the ordination ram in a sacred place, 32then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent. 33At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it. 34If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
35Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you. 36Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy. 37Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy.
Daily Sacrifices
(Leviticus 6.8-13; Numbers 28.1-8)
The Lord said:
38Each day you must sacrifice two lambs a year old, 39one in the morning and one in the evening. 40-41With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me. 42-43You and your descendants must always offer this sacrifice on the altar at the entrance to the sacred tent.
People of Israel, I will meet and speak with you there, and my shining glory will make the place holy. 44Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests. 45I will live among you as your God, 46and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina doŋa lizaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kenne í ɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala, bá ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, guŋ gil ba ɛɛ kizeehina di ra humiŋ. Lau nabalee ani pebala anɛɛ la n kpekke, 2di kpa huuti sakɔla la baŋ waa yiisi duwɛɛ di ɔɔzi paanuu, di kaa ɛɛ nuu koozi a sau yeŋ ni di halli boforoti di ɔɔzi kɛrɛkɛssizi di ɛɛ nuu waari a ni. 3Kpaa du kɛɛgɔ biini di lau nabalee ni a pebala anɛɛ la jaa a ni di wa tɛŋ. 4Denii í kpogli Aarɔn ni u biibaala di ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua di wa sɔ baa nii. 5Kpa bɔmbɔga la di bɔg Aarɔn, aabuu tagtajaŋ, tagtajiga, tagtakpurii, tagtakpurii himmaa la ani bampirii pɛɛŋ la. Lau a tagtakpurii kirsɔɔ la baŋ suahwɛ nɛnnɛ di kirsuu. 6Di vɔɔu namu, ka kpa saliŋ kunla n ɛɛ naniinanii la di mari u ni. 7Yiili nuuwaarii la di waari u nyuu. 8Lau u biibaala la di wa kpa a tagtajaŋra laali baa, 9di kpa kahurozi hi baa, ka kpa kirsɔɔzi kirsi Aarɔn ni u biibaala la. Gunnɛ i ɛɛ di lizi baa bá ɛɛ n kizeehina di hanna la.
10Lau a nabal di ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see, di gil Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu, 11ka kɔrguu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, n see. 12Kpa i nonibii lii a nabal chal di faa mbusu lizibɔr la nyigzi la ka fug anla n kawɛɛ dau u zɛɛ. 13Lizi a nabal biini kuna nuu maa ani u hiah bɔnanii di jaa u siga ni a nuuri maa, di kpaa fuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni. 14Ka kpa a nabal ol, u hɔŋ ani u biini kuna maa ge, di lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di ga fuuah, á ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa.
15I daŋ lau pebal la bɛl di gil Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni. 16Kɔrguu, di kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi la maa. 17Mɔnni a pebal jigzijigzi, di yagli u biini kuna ni u naagballi, di kpaa jaa u nyuu ani u bɔr la n kawɛɛ ni. 18Denii í fuuh a pebal maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.
19Lau a pebal la n kawɛɛ la, di gil Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni. 20Kɔrgi u ge, di ɛɛ u chal di fɔg Aarɔn ni u biibaala nodige dignipaŋhoori, ba nodige nonibibala ani ba nodige naanibibala. Ka kpa a chal yeŋ la n kawɛɛ di mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi la maa. 21Kpa chal la n chɔɔ mbusu lizibɔr ni la yeŋ di koozi nuuwaarii la ni. Kpaa mizi Aarɔn ni u biibaala ni ba bɔmbɔga maa ni. U ni baa ani ba bɔmbɔga la maa jaa ɛɛ kunnanaananaa.
22Lizi a pebal dinzɛɛ, u biini kuna nuu, u hiah bɔnanii, u siga ni a nuuri ani u nodig hiih, di kpa a maa kpau dɔŋa ni, ba kizeehina kizee kpai peballɛ guŋ. 23Binni kɛɛgɔ la biini baŋ du paanuuzi di wa tɛŋ la, di ligzi a maa kpaŋkpaŋa, paanuu la baŋ kpa ɔlivi nuu ɔɔzi, unla n waa nuu dɔɔwɛ ani kɛrɛkɛsi. 24Kpa a kuna naa maa du Aarɔn ni u biibaala nonee, bá lallaa chiŋ dí viigi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa tɛŋ. 25Denii i jaa lɛɛa ba be di jaa mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la ni, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ. 26Kpa pebal naa bampirii di lalluu chiŋ viigi n see, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii, di ɛɛ i hor.
27Di ba waa lizi n kizeehiŋ, pebal la bampirii ni u hiih la baŋ ɔɔ lizi tɛŋ la, ɛɛa kunnanaananaa, á ɛɛ n kizeehina hora. 28Gunnɛ dɛkkɛ Izrɛl hina ɔɔ lizi ba mbusu lizaa kuna di ra tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala saŋa maa. Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi la, annii dɛkkɔɔ bá kpaa tɛŋ.
29Aarɔn bɔmbɔgnanaananaa la, u biibaalaa dɔɔa, di u wa siuwɔ. Ba ɔɔ bɔgaa saŋa la ban niŋ ɔɔ lizi bɛl ú kpa a kizee. 30Aarɔn biibaal la n niŋ ɔɔ kpa n kizee la waa zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia u hum Bɔnaniinanii la biini, u daŋ ɔɔ bɔgaa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.
31Daali Kɔraawiizi kizee kpai pebal ol la bɔnaniinanii la biini.
32Gil Aarɔn ni u biibaala hee a pebal ol ni paanuu la n du a kɛɛgɔ biini la, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua. 33Aarɔn ni u biibaalaa niŋ ɔɔ di a diwee naa baŋ kpawɛɛ lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu tɛŋ naa. Di ba bɛŋ lɛi, nɛr maa wàá wer dia dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛ diunanaananaarɛ n be. 34Di ba wa dia ka ka hɔɔ wa pizi, bá fuuah, dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛ diunanaananaarɛ n be.
35Ɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala gunla himmaa miŋ baglii la. Kpa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ di lizi baa, bá kpa n kizee. 36Ɛɛ kpu nabal hɔpizi biimaa, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa di lizi n baaŋ ba ni. Gunnɛ í ɛɛ di lizi mbusu lizibɔr ge doŋa ha, di lizi n baaŋ u ni. Kpa nuu di waari u ni, di lizi u doŋa. 37Kpa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ di lizi n baaŋ u ni. Gunnɛ niŋ gil mbusu lizibɔr ɛɛ kunnaniinanii werge maa, di kunla maa ge wa gbɔgzuu daŋ birgi kunnaniinanii.
38Kuna naabuu í ɔɔ kpa lizi mbusuzi hɔpizi biimaa, mbusu lizibɔr la ni, pebizi anɛɛ la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa. 39I daŋ ɔɔ kpu bɛl chɔɔzi, bɛl ge duana, di lizi mbusu. 40Lugli hor la, i daŋ ɛɛ huuti sakɔla kookoo tassa suul di koozi ɔlivi nuu pirintua ni keza ni, di buu, di kaa ɛɛ siŋ pirintua ni keza di ta, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa siŋ. 41Kpu pebii la n kawɛɛ la duaninsɔŋ ni, di kpa mbusu lizaa mia la ani sintaalii alugɔ chɔɔzinhor la, di jaa. Á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.
42Saŋaa saŋa maa, gunnɛ i naanna ɔɔ ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii naa di ra tɛŋ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua see. Denii ń ɔɔ chem n nɛra ni di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa. 43Denii ń ɔɔ chem Izrɛl hina ge gba ni, ń girme gil de ɛɛ bɔnaniinanii.
44Gunnɛ n wa ɛɛ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la ni mbusu lizibɔr la maa ɛɛ bɔnanaananaa, ka jaa ɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala ge nɛnanaananaa, bá ɛɛ n kizeehina di ra humiŋ. 45Denii ń jaa du Izrɛl hina be, di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum. 46Ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la n lizi baa lii Ijip hɛri la, ń wer du ba be. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la.”

english_text:
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 37.25-28)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Build an altar of acacia wood where you can burn incense. 2Make it 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high, and make each of its four corners stick up like the horn of a bull. 3Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 4Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar. 5These poles are also to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
6Put the altar in front of the inside curtain of the sacred tent. The chest with the place of mercy is kept behind that curtain, and I will talk with you there. 7-8From now on, when Aaron takes care of the lamps each morning and evening, he must burn sweet-smelling incense to me on the altar. 9Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings. 10 Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by smearing on its four corners the blood of an animal sacrificed for sin, and this practice must always be followed. The altar is sacred because it is dedicated to me.
The Money for the Sacred Tent
11The Lord said to Moses:
12Find out how many grown men there are in Israel and require each of them to pay me to keep him safe from danger while you are counting them. 13-15 Each man over 19, whether rich or poor, must pay me the same amount of money, weighed according to the official standards. 16This money is to be used for the upkeep of the sacred tent, and because of it, I will never forget my people.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 38.8)
17The Lord said to Moses:
18-21 Make a large bronze bowl and a bronze stand for it. Then put them between the altar for sacrifice and the sacred tent, so the priests can wash their hands and feet before entering the tent or offering a sacrifice on the altar. Each priest in every generation must wash himself in this way, or else he will die right there.
The Oil for Dedication and Ordination
(Exodus 37.29)
22 The Lord said to Moses:
23-25Mix four liters of olive oil with the following costly spices: six kilograms of myrrh, three kilograms of cinnamon, three kilograms of cane, and six kilograms of cassia. Measure these according to the official standards. Then use this sacred mixture 26for dedicating the tent and chest, 27the table with its equipment, the lampstand with its equipment, the incense altar with all its utensils, 28the altar for sacrifices, and the large bowl with its stand. 29By dedicating them in this way, you will make them so holy that anyone who even touches them will become holy.
30When you ordain Aaron and his sons as my priests, sprinkle them with some of this oil, 31and say to the people of Israel: “This oil must always be used in the ordination service of a priest. It is holy because it is dedicated to the Lord. 32So treat it as holy! Don't ever use it for everyday purposes or mix any for yourselves. 33If you do, you will no longer belong to the Lord's people.”
The Sweet-Smelling Incense
34-35Mix equal amounts of the costly spices stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, then add salt to make the mixture pure and holy. 36Pound some of it into powder and sprinkle it in front of the sacred chest, where I meet with you. Be sure to treat this incense as something very holy. 37It is truly holy because it is dedicated to me, so don't ever make any for yourselves. 38If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_text:
Daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kpa akeesia daazi di kuari daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr. 2Kuaruu ú jaŋzi ni u wassi maa ɛɛ kpaŋ. U jaŋzi daŋ ɛɛ nogume, u wassi ge ɛɛ guŋ, u chiŋ laŋaa ge ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛ. Gil u ni u siraa anaazu nyigzi maa ɛɛ kuŋkpaŋ. 3Ŋmɛɛri saliŋ himmaa di tɔ u nyuu ni u keŋkerezi ni u nyigzi maa, di kaa ŋmɛɛri saliŋ bar u nua lugɔ gir. 4Kpa saliŋ di luu gbittizi anaazu di du a nua gir la zɛɛ, anɛɛ du keŋkerezi la bɛl maa, di lauri daajaŋra la ban niŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra chiu la kpogli. 5Teŋri akeesia daajaŋra di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔa. 6Kpa a daahɛgsɔɔhsuma mbusu lizibɔr la di chiŋŋi patiisa la n teŋ N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see. Denii ń chem i ni.
7Chɔɔzi maa, di Aarɔn wa ballɔ, ú wa fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma mbusu lizibɔr ni tɛŋ, u daŋ ɔɔ du fintinazi la tau. 8A dɛkkɔɔ u ɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ duaninsɔŋ maa di u wa ballɔ u wa choŋŋi a fintinazi, u daŋ gil daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la ɔɔ ra fuuh mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. 9Ŋmɛnɛ maa, gilɛɛ waa kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la n waa dɛkkɛ gɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia gɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii maa, di ra fuuh u ni. Gilɛɛ waa fug siŋ di ra waari u ni. 10Bina maa, Aarɔn daŋ kpa chal di mizi a nyigzi ni kakpaŋ, di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ nɛra ni. A dɛkkɔɔ chal naa ɛɛ sel la baŋ ɔɔ kpu bina maa di lizi wichɔgaa ni Kɔraawiizi baaŋ u nɛra ni la chal. Gunnɛ ba ra ɛɛ di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. A mbusu lizibɔr ɛɛ kunnaniinaniirɛ werge maa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be.”
Miibɔɔ kim turgaa wia
11Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 12“Di i waa kur Izrɛl hina, bɛl maa daŋ turgi u miibɔɔ kim di tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. A guŋ daŋ gil wiilchɔgii maa wàá lau ba bɛl maa a kuraa saŋa. 13Nɛr la maa n laŋŋɛ di ga jaa banla baŋ teŋ kutte ni daŋ turgi gunla maga n dɛkkɛ, gunla banna mɛgzaa n Dia biini la. A saliŋhuŋŋu kebisaukeza naa ɛɛ sunzaarɛ di tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.
14Nɛr la maa n laŋŋɛ di ga jaa banla baŋ kutte la ni, di di binni tokko ka ra sag, daŋ turgi a kim naa di tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 15Dɔɔna ni nyaara maa dɛkkɔɔ ba turgi mɛgzi, di ba waa turgi ba miibɔɔni kim di ra tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, á ɛɛ sunzaa. 16Lɛɛ a kebee naa di lii Izrɛl hina be, di kpaa di ra hum mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia huma. A daŋ ɛɛ Izrɛl hina liize ni ba miibɔɔni kima turgaa wia.”
Danyɛ tassazeŋ wia
17Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 18“Kpa danyɛ di luu tassazeŋ ni u zɛɛ hɔŋribɔr, ba kpa di ra sanzi nonee ni naazi. Kpau chiŋŋi n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la ni mbusu lizibɔr la baambaaŋ di ɛɛ nii du u biini. 19U biini niirɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala ɔɔ ɛɛ di ra sanzi ba nonee ni naazi. 20Saŋa maa, di ba haŋ wa zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia, a niirɛ ba sam di gilɛɛ waa siu. Di ba wa la mbusu lizibɔr ba ga fuuh kuna di lizi mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, 21ba daŋ ɔɔ sanzi ba nonee ni naazii di gilɛɛ waa siu. Widaulii naa daŋ chɔɔ tɛɛ ba ni ba naanna maa di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.”
Nuuwaarii wia
22Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 23“Nyiŋŋi kunsɔɔhrisuma la n wesse. Mɛr la n ɛɛ nii, kilozi anumbɛl, ni daahɛga aŋhina banna yir sinamɔn la sɔɔh n summɛ werge, kilozi ahoro, di kpa kooriikpega aŋhina sɔɔh n summɛ werge, ba ra yiraa balsam kilozi ahoro. 24Kaa kpa daahɛga aŋhina banna yir kasia ge kilozi anumbɛl, a maa mɛg gunla banna mɛgzaa n Dia biini la, di kpa ɔlivi nuu pirintuani anumbɛl jaa. 25Annii maanii i kpa koozi dɔŋa ni, di kuari nuuwaarinaniinanii, u sɔɔh du sum alugɔ anla nɛr la n zum tulaale huma n kuarɛɛ. 26Kpa a nuu di waari n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia ani Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la, 27ni tɛɛbul la ni u kuna maa, ni fintina daa la ni u kuna maa ani daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr la, 28di kaa kpa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr ni u kuna maa, ni tassazeŋ ni u zɛɛ chignibɔr la. 29Gunnɛ í gil ba ɛɛa a ɛɛ kunnanaananaa werge, di kunla maa wa gbɔgzaa, u gba daŋ birgi kunnaniinanii.
30Denii í jaa waari Aarɔn ni u biibaala a nuu ba ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, di ɛɛ kizeehina di ra humiŋ. 31Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Nuuwaarii naa n ɛɛ naniinanii naabuu ba kpa di ra hum n huma jimini maa. 32Ií gilɛɛ wa ɛɛu di ra waari nɛduma maa, di gilɛɛ waa kpa kuna la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n baglɛɛ lugɔ ba kpa kuari a nuu naa, di wàá kuari nuu maa lugɔu. A dɛkkɔɔ ii zum lugɔ u ɛɛ nuunaniinaniirɛ, di kpogluu nɛnnɛ. 33Nɛr la maa n niŋ kuari tulaale alugɔu, di kpau waari nɛr la n waa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ ɛɛwɛ, ba duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.’ ”
Daahɛgsɔɔhsuma wia
34Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kpa daahɛga la sɔɔh n summɛ, kel ni onika ani galbanum di kpa fraŋkinsɛns himmaa jaa a ni a maa mɛgzi, 35di koozi dɔŋa aa sɔɔh du sum alugɔ nɛr la n zum tulaale huma n kuarɛɛ, ban niŋ ɔɔ ra fuuh. Du yazi a ni, á doŋa maa lii, a du wer di ɛɛ kunnanii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 36I daŋ nam aŋhina a ɛɛ kɔlɔlɔ di kpaa zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini di ga dau N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, bɔr la min niŋ chem i ni la. A daŋ ɛɛ kunnanaananaa werge maa tɛi. 37Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa keŋ kuna naa miŋ bagli ia naa, di ra kuari ii himmaa hora. Zum lugɔ u ɛɛ kunnaniinaniirɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 38Di nɛr la maa wa kuari ú dɔŋ dikuu u sɔɔh n summɛ u be wia, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.”

english_text:
The Lord Chooses Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 35.30—36.1)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2I have chosen Bezalel from the Judah tribe to make the sacred tent and its furnishings. 3-5Not only have I filled him with my Spirit, but I have given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 6I have appointed Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to work with him, and I have also given skills to those who will help them make everything exactly as I have commanded you: 7-11the sacred tent with its furnishings, the sacred chest with its place of mercy, the table with all that is on it, the lamp with its equipment, the incense altar, the altar for sacrifices with its equipment, the bronze bowl with its stand, the beautiful priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons, the oil for dedication and ordination services, and the sweet-smelling incense for the holy place.
Laws for the Sabbath
12-13Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had said:
The Sabbath belongs to me. Now I command you and your descendants to always obey the laws of the Sabbath. By doing this, you will know that I have chosen you as my own. 14-15 Keep the Sabbath holy. You have six days to do your work, but the Sabbath is mine, and it must remain a day of rest. If you work on the Sabbath, you will no longer be part of my people, and you will be put to death.
16Every generation of Israelites must respect the Sabbath. 17 This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
18When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_text:
Bɛzalɛl ni Ɔhɔliab wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“A nuu, n lizi Uri biibaal n ɛɛ Hur naannaa di lii Juda dee biini. U sɔnnɛ Bɛzalɛl. 3N Duma izi u ninɛɛ u dɔɔ kuŋkuaraa zumaa, di wer wia ɛɛi, di dɔɔ nunzuma werge maa, ú wer zum nonii huma maa iri nɛnnɛ. 4U daŋ wer kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa ani danyɛ di luu kuŋ maa iri u du wer, 5di zum binanaa sɛɛih ni a margaa kuna ni, di zum daazi sɛɛih ni nonii huma maa iri. 6N lizi Ahisamak biibaal Ɔhɔliab di lii Dan dee biini, ú hiinuu di hum a huma. N kaa tɛɛ a huŋhunna la maanii zumaa, bá wer kuari kunla maa miŋ ŋɔ i kuari la. 7Ba daŋ kuari n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia ani N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ni u tua ani kuna la maa n du a Tanti Dia biini la, 8tɛɛbul la ni u kuna, fintina daa la n ɛɛ saliŋ himmaa bɛŋ ni u kuna maa ani daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr la, 9di kaa wer kuari mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ani u kuna maa ni tassazeŋ la ani u zɛɛ hɔŋribɔr, 10ni bɔmbɔgnanaananaa la ban niŋ suah tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ Aarɔn ni u biibaal ban niŋ ɔɔ bɔg, di ba wàá hum n kizeehina huma, 11ni nuuwaarii, daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la ban ninna fuuh Bɔnaniinanii la biini. Ba daŋ kuaraabuu gunla himmaa miŋ baglii la.”
Heezaa Hɔpizii wia
12Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 13“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ ba ra tɔgzi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Heezaa Hɔpizaa la. Annii daŋ ɛɛ daansɛɛ di du n ni baa baaŋ jiminizi maa. Gunnɛ niŋ gil ba zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la n lizi baa, bá ɛɛ n nɛra.
