14A dɛkkɔɔ ba ra tɔgzi n Heezaa Hɔpizii la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinaniirɛ tɛɛ baa. Nɛr la maa n niŋ chɔguu, bá kpuu. Nɛr la maa n niŋ hum huma a hɔl, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. 15Hɔpizaa anumbɛllɛ ba ɔɔ kpa di hum ba huma. Ka aniidaanɛɛhiŋ lawaa, ba ɔɔ heezi, ú ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinaniirɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. Nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ ka hum huma a hɔl, bá kpuu. 16Izrɛl hina danna tɔgzi a Heezaa Hɔpizii naa di ra diu, ú ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra nuukpaŋ dɔɔi di hanna la. 17U daŋ ɛɛ daansɛɛ di du n ni Izrɛl hina baambaaŋ di ra la saŋa maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛllɛ di ta chiŋ ni hɛri ni kuna la maa n du a biine, ka kpa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la di heezi.”
18Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Moosis wa tuŋ a Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu, u jaa kpa bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la u himmaa n sɛbi Gbɔgni dau a ni la tɛu.

english_text:
The People Make an Idol To Worship
(Deuteronomy 9.6-29)
1 After the people saw that Moses had been on the mountain for a long time, they went to Aaron and said, “Make us an image of a god who will lead and protect us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but nobody knows what has happened to him.”
2Aaron told them, “Bring me the gold earrings that your wives and sons and daughters are wearing.” 3Everybody took off their earrings and brought them to Aaron, 4 then he melted them and made an idol in the shape of a young bull.
All the people said to one another, “This is the god who brought us out of Egypt!”
5When Aaron saw what was happening, he built an altar in front of the idol and said, “Tomorrow we will celebrate in honor of the Lord.” 6 The people got up early the next morning and killed some animals to be used for sacrifices and others to be eaten. Then everyone ate and drank so much that they began to carry on like wild people.
7The Lord said to Moses:
Hurry back down! Those people you led out of Egypt are acting like fools. 8They have already stopped obeying me and have made themselves an idol in the shape of a young bull. They have bowed down to it, offered sacrifices, and said that it is the god who brought them out of Egypt. 9Moses, I have seen how stubborn these people are, 10and I'm angry enough to destroy them, so don't try to stop me. But I will make your descendants into a great nation.
11 Moses tried to get the Lord God to change his mind:
Our Lord, you used your mighty power to bring these people out of Egypt. Now don't become angry and destroy them. 12If you do, the Egyptians will say that you brought your people out here into the mountains just to get rid of them. Please don't be angry with your people. Don't destroy them!
13 Remember the solemn promise you made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You promised that someday they would have as many descendants as there are stars in the sky and that you would give them land.
14So even though the Lord had threatened to destroy the people, he changed his mind and let them live.
15-16Moses went back down the mountain with the two flat stones on which God had written all of his laws with his own hand, using both sides of the stones.
17When Joshua heard the noisy shouts of the people, he said to Moses, “A battle must be going on down in the camp.”
18But Moses replied, “It doesn't sound like they are shouting because they have won or lost a battle. It sounds more like a wild party!”
19As Moses got closer to the camp, he saw the idol, and he also saw the people dancing around. This made him so angry that he threw down the stones and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain. 20He melted the idol the people had made, and he ground it into powder. He scattered it in their water and made them drink it. 21Moses asked Aaron, “What did these people do to harm you? Why did you make them sin in this terrible way?”
22Aaron answered:
Don't be angry with me. You know as well as I do that they are determined to do evil. 23They even told me, “That man Moses led us out of Egypt, but now we don't know what has happened to him. Make us a god to lead us.” 24Then I asked them to bring me their gold earrings. They took them off and gave them to me. I threw the gold into a fire, and out came this bull.
25Moses knew that the people were out of control and that it was Aaron's fault. And now they had made fools of themselves in front of their enemies. 26So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and shouted, “Everyone who is on the Lord's side come over here!”
Then the men of the Levi tribe gathered around Moses, 27and he said to them, “The Lord God of Israel commands you to strap on your swords and go through the camp, killing your relatives, your friends, and your neighbors.”
28The men of the Levi tribe followed his orders, and that day they killed about 3,000 men. 29Moses said to them, “You obeyed the Lord and did what was right, and so you will serve as his priests for the people of Israel. It was hard for you to kill your own sons and brothers, but the Lord has blessed you and made you his priests today.”
30The next day Moses told the people, “This is a terrible thing you have done. But I will go back to the Lord to see if I can do something to keep this sin from being held against you.”
31Moses returned to the Lord and said, “The people have committed a terrible sin. They have made a gold idol to be their god. 32 But I beg you to forgive them. If you don't, please wipe my name out of your book.”
33The Lord replied, “I will wipe out of my book the name of everyone who has sinned against me. 34Now take my people to the place I told you about, and my angel will lead you. But when the time comes, I will punish them for this sin.”
35So the Lord punished the people of Israel with a terrible disease for talking Aaron into making the gold idol.
translation_text:
Saliŋ nabalee wia
1Izrɛl hina la n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Moosis birgi a bizeŋ nyuurɛ werge la, ba chaali dɔŋa di ba Aarɔn be di wa ŋɔ, “Yaa waa zum wii la maa n kpogli Moosis, n kpogli yaa lii Ijip hɛri, u birgi keŋ. Awia, kuari vug tɛɛ yaa, ú tɔ yaa see.”
2Aarɔn ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gil ii haana ni biizi lizi ba saliŋ dignikuna di wa tɛŋ.” 3Awia, a nɛra maa lizaa wa tɛɛ Aarɔn. 4U kpaa di ŋmɛɛri kuari kumbɛl lugɔ nabalee. A nɛra ŋɔ, “Yaabalaa Izrɛl hina! Yaa vug la n kpogli yaa lii Ijip hɛrii keŋ!”
5Denii Aarɔn n wa na guŋ, u ma mbusu lizibɔr nabalee la baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari la see, ka ŋɔ kpegzi ni, “Kɛrɛ, hɔpizizeŋ dii daŋ du de tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.” 6Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzimpikke ni, ba lauri sela kpila maa di ba wa fuuh lizi mbusuzi. Aŋhina ge ɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa hora. Ba so di ra di, di ra nyɔɔ sinni di ra ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ wia.
7Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Bir tuu manaŋ di la nɛra la hiŋ lizɛɛ lii Ijip hɛri la, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa di vɛɛŋ. 8Ba teŋ ɛɛ manannɛ di vɛɛ n baglaa la ka kpa saliŋ di kuari kumbɛl lugɔ nabalee u ɛɛ ba vug, di ra kuaruu. Haali di lizi mbusuzi gba di ra tɛu, di ŋɔ lugɔ vug naabuu lizi baa di lii Ijip hɛri.”
9Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Nɛra naa kpoŋŋoo werge. 10Awia, giliŋ ń baaŋ fuuh ba ni, n dim baa. Ka gil i ni i dee wazi werge di ɛɛ hɛrzeŋ hina.”
11Ka Moosis suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi werge maa di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i baaŋ fuuh nɛra la hiŋ lizɛɛ lii Ijip hɛri ni i fɔŋŋazeŋ la ninɛi? 12Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ í gil Ijip hina wa ŋɔ lugɔ i dar i nɛraa di lii ba hɛri í wa kpuuzi bizenaa biini, di dim baa hɛri naa biinei? Awia, gilɛɛ gil i baaŋ na fuuh werge. Gil i baaŋ sɔɔni di gilɛɛ waa tɔɔri baa guŋ. 13A liizi gunla hiŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ di hɛɛhzi tɛɛ i balaa Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb la. I faa hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ di ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ gil ii naanna wazi di du kpil lugɔ chinchiŋwilaa. Di kaa dɔɔ hɛri la hiŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ i daŋ tɛɛ baa ú ɛɛ ba hor di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa la.’ ” 14Awia Kɔraawiizi nuu Moosis suŋŋaa la, di gil ba tɔɔraa.
15Moosis jaa bir lii a bizeŋ nyuu di tuu di kpogli bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la baŋ sɛbi Gbɔgni di dau a keŋkerezi ni la. 16Kɔraawiizi himmaanii faa kuari a bia di sɛbi a Gbɔgni dau a ni.
17Denii Josua nuu a nɛra n na kɔɔ, u ŋɔ Moosis be, “N nuu laal gbɔgaa yaa chɔɔribɔr la.”
18Moosis bir ŋɔ,
“A kɔɔi waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ
baŋ kpegli ba dɔma
gɛɛ ba dɔma n kpegli baa,
yiraa ba ra yir.”
19Moosis n wa tuuwe di ra dugli ba chɔɔribɔr la, u na a nabalee di ba ra sa werge maa. U baaŋ fuuh werge maa. U kpa bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la uŋ kpoglee, Gbɔgni fi la du a ni la, di viiri hɛri a bizeŋ zɛɛ, a maa purgi burburbur. 20U kpa a nabalee di fuuh. Di namuu u bii kɔlɔlɔ. U kpaa koozi nii ni di gil a Izrɛl hina maa nyɔɔu.
21U pɛɛzi Aarɔn, “Beedee wiirɛ nɛra naa ɛɛi i gil ba ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge kennei?”
22Denii Aarɔn ŋɔ u be, “N dɔɔri, gilɛɛ gil i baaŋ na fuuh. I himmaa zum gunla nɛra naa n dɔɔ wichɔgaa bilaa. 23Ba ballɔɔ di wa ŋɔ n be, ‘Yaa waa zum wii la maa n kpogli Moosis la n kpogli yaa di lii Ijip hɛri la, u birgi keŋ. Awia, kuari vug tɛɛ yaa, ú tɔ yaa see.’ 24N ŋɔ ba be, ‘Unla maa n dɔɔ saliŋ dignikuna ni baŋaakuna, ú kpaa ba.’ Ba kpaa ba, n kpaa di du niŋ biini, a birgi nabalee naa!”
25Moosis na lugɔ Aarɔn gillɔɔ ba kpoŋ di birgi gɛnaa ba dɔma see, ba ra mam baa. 26U lii ga chi ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ dominua ka ŋɔ, “Unla maa n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hor, u ra ba n be.” Levi dee la maa ba u be.
27Denii u ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la himmaa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ií kpa ii tokobizi zuu a chɔɔribɔr, di gaagi u biini, di kpuuzi ii niuna, ii kpɛɛnna ani ii dɔŋahina maa.’ ” 28Denii a Levi dee la ɛɛ gunla Moosis n ŋɔwɛɛ la. Di kpuuzi alugɔ nɛra kagboŋ buhoro a hɔl hiŋ. 29Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Ii lizi iihinaarɛ kizeehina di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi zinaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii chɔgi ii himmaa biizi ni lullaa. Awia, Kɔraawiizi kissi iabuu.”
30Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Moosis ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa. Ka filaŋkeŋ, n daŋ tinni Kɔraawiizi be, bizeŋ la nyuu di ga suŋŋuu, aŋhinabe, u daŋ gil ii wichɔgaa tɛɛ ia.”
31Moosis bir di la Kɔraawiizi be di ga ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, nɛra naa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa. Ba kpa salinnɛ di kuari vug tɛɛ bahinaa di sɛɛu dɔɔra. 32N Dɔɔri, gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa. Ka di haa guŋ wa sɛɛwɛ, guŋwaa, dinzi n sɔŋ lii hɔŋ la hiŋ sɛbi i nɛra sɔna u biini la.”
33Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Banla n zuu n ni labuu ń dinzi ba sɔna n hɔŋ biini. 34Awia, la ga kpogli n nɛra hiŋ di la bɔr la miŋ baglii la. N daŋ gil n mɛlika tɔ ii see. Ka di saŋa bɛl wa hello, n daŋ tɛr ba digna dikuu ba wichɔgaa naa wia.”
35Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ wiilchɔgii bɛl chol ba ni dikuu baŋ gillɛ Aarɔn kuari saliŋ nabalee la wia.

english_text:
The Lord Tells Israel To Leave Mount Sinai
1 The Lord said to Moses:
You led the people of Israel out of Egypt. Now get ready to lead them to the land I promised their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. 2-3It is a land rich with milk and honey, and I will send an angel to force out those people who live there—the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. But I will not go with my people. They are so rebellious that I would destroy them before they get there.
4-5Even before the Lord said these harsh things, he had told Moses, “These people really are rebellious, and I would kill them at once, if I went with them. But tell them to take off their fancy jewelry, then I'll decide what to do with them.” So the people started mourning, 6and after leaving Mount Sinai, they stopped wearing fancy jewelry.
The Lord Is with His People
7Moses used to set up a tent far from camp. He called it the “meeting tent,” and whoever needed some message from the Lord would go there. 8Each time Moses went out to this tent, everyone would stand at the entrance to their own tents and watch him enter. 9-11Then they would bow down because a thick cloud would come down in front of the tent, and the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, just like a friend. Afterwards, Moses would return to camp, but his young assistant Joshua would stay at the tent.
The Lord Promises To Be with His People
12Moses said to the Lord, “I know that you have told me to lead these people to the land you promised them. But you have not said who will go along to help me. You have said that you are my friend and that you are pleased with me. 13If this is true, let me know what your plans are, then I can obey and continue to please you. And don't forget that you have chosen this nation to be your own.”
14The Lord said, “I will go with you and give you peace.”
15Then Moses replied, “If you aren't going with us, please don't make us leave this place. 16But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
17So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”
18Then Moses said, “I pray that you will let me see you in all of your glory.”
19 The Lord answered:
All right. I am the Lord, and I show mercy and kindness to anyone I choose. I will let you see my glory and hear my holy name, 20but I won't let you see my face, because anyone who sees my face will die. 21There is a rock not far from me. Stand beside it, 22and before I pass by in all of my shining glory, I will put you in a large crack in the rock. I will cover your eyes with my hand until I have passed by. 23Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. You will not see my face.
translation_text:
1Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “I ni a nɛra la hiŋ kpoglee di lii Ijip hɛri la, lii bɔnnaa, di la hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ Abraham, Aizik, Jekɔb ani ba naanna la. 2N daŋ gil n mɛlika tɔ ii see di duŋŋi nɛra la maa n du a hɛri la, baabuu Keenan, Amɔri, Hitti, Pɛriz, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina. 3Ií la hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge maa la. Ka màá du ia di la, dikuu ii dignikpega wia, di guŋ lɛi n daŋ chɔgi ia.”
4A nɛra n wa nuu guŋ, ba biine chɔgi werge maa, ba ra wii. Ba bɛl maa waa kaa laali u saliŋ baŋaakuna gɛɛ di du u dignikuna, 5dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii, “Kali Izrɛl hina be lugɔ ba ɛɛ dignikpega hinaa. Di n faa ŋɔ ń hiŋ ia tama gba, aŋhinabe n daŋ faa chɔgi ia. Awia, ií lizi ii saliŋ baŋaakuna ni dignikuna la maa, ka ń zum gunla min niŋ dau ia.” 6Awia, Izrɛl hina ligzi ba saliŋ kuna maa Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ.
Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia wia
7Di Izrɛl hina la haŋ wa chɔɔ bɔr la maa, Moosis ɔɔ ga baŋ tanti diarɛ ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ baŋgia. Di ra yiruu, “Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia.” Di unla maa wàá nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi suŋŋaa, u ɔɔ la denii. 8Di Moosis haŋ wàá la de, Izrɛl hina la maa ɔɔ lii di chi ba tanti diini dominuuzii di ra binnuu guŋŋ ú ga zuu de. 9Di Moosis haŋ wa zuu a tanti dia la, baama la n du miriti di la chiŋ la ɔɔ tuu di wa tɔ de dominua, ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia ra tɛu. 10Di ba wa na baama la n du miriti di la chiŋ la n tɔ a tanti dia dominua, ba bɛl maa ɔɔ giŋŋi hɛrii ú tanti dia dominua di ra jaami Kɔraawiizi. 11Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ ŋɔ wiarɛ ra tɛɛ Moosis alugɔ nɛr ni u dammu n chigɛ di ra ŋɔ wia. Di ba wa ŋɔwɔɔ tuŋ, Moosis ɔɔ bir ba a nɛra be ka Nun biibaal Josua la n ɛɛ biipɔllii di ɛɛ u hiini la waa ɔɔ haa ka de.
Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi girme wia
12Moosis ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “I ɔɔ ra ŋɔ n benii lugɔ ń tɔ nɛra naa see, ka haŋ baglɛɛ nɛr la hin niŋ kpa jaa n ni. I ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N zum i sɔnnɛ, i wia ra pariŋ.’ 13Di n wia pariibuu, bagliŋ i ŋmɛnizi ń wer zumii, ń wia haa ra parii werge. A liizi lugɔ i lizi nɛra naabuu ba ɛɛ i hora.”
14Kɔraawiizi bir ŋɔ, “N daŋ du i be di ra la, di tɛi bampirsɔna.”
15Denii Moosis ŋɔ u be, “Di hàá du yaa be, gilɛɛ gil ya wàá lii bɔnnaa. 16Ɛrɛɛ nɛra wer zum lugɔ n ni i nɛra wia pariibuu, di haa yaa be duwɛɛi? Bɛɛ niŋ gil ya kur durnya naa hina ninɛi?”
17Kɔraawiizi jaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “N daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa hiŋ suŋŋɛɛ naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n zumiibuu nɛnnɛ, i wia pariŋ.”
18Moosis jaa suŋŋuu di ŋɔ, “Amɔ, í gil n na i girme.”
19Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Mìŋ́ ii Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil i na n nanni maa, di baglii n sɔŋ n sibɔɔ. N daŋ suŋ banla maa min niŋ suŋ ba ni, di kaa na banla maa miŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ la sinyɛna. 20Màá gil i na n siwee. Dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr maa wàá wer na n siwee ka haa dɔɔ miibɔɔ.”
21Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Bɔr du denii di dugliŋ i wer chi bital ni. 22Di n girme la wàá bɛri i ni, n daŋ kpai du a bii bɔɔ di kpa n nonii jaari i ni ka wa bɛri. 23Denii n jaa lalli n nonii, i na n harbɔɔ ka hàá na n siwee waa.”

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Deuteronomy 10.1-5)
1One day the Lord said to Moses, “Cut two flat stones like the first ones I made, and I will write on them the same commandments that were on the two you broke. 2Be ready tomorrow morning to come up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top. 3No one is to come with you or to be on the mountain at all. Don't even let the sheep and cattle graze at the foot of the mountain.” 4So Moses cut two flat stones like the first ones, and early the next morning he carried them to the top of Mount Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded.
5The Lord God came down in a cloud and stood beside Moses there on the mountain. God spoke his holy name, “the Lord.” 6 Then he passed in front of Moses and called out, “I am the Lord God. I am merciful and very patient with my people. I show great love, and I can be trusted. 7I keep my promises to my people forever, but I also punish anyone who sins. When people sin, I punish them and their children, and also their grandchildren and great-grandchildren.”
8Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped the Lord. 9He prayed, “Lord, if you really are pleased with me, I pray that you will go with us. It is true that these people are sinful and rebellious, but forgive our sin and let us be your people.”
A Promise and Its Demands
(Exodus 23.14-19; Deuteronomy 7.1-5; 16.1-17)
10The Lord said:
I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things. 11I will force out the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, but you must do what I command you today. 12Don't make treaties with any of those people. If you do, it will be like falling into a trap. 13 Instead, you must destroy their altars and tear down the sacred poles they use in the worship of the goddess Asherah. 14I demand your complete loyalty—you must not worship any other god! 15Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals. 16Your men will even marry their women and be influenced to worship their gods.
17 Don't make metal images of gods.
18 Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.
19 The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
20 You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son.
Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
21 Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting. 22 Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
23Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel. 24As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
25 When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
26 I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
27The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel. 28Moses stayed on the mountain with the Lord for 40 days and nights, without eating or drinking. And he wrote down the Ten Commandments, the most important part of God's agreement with his people.
Moses Comes Down from Mount Sinai
29 Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining. 30When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him. 31Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them. 32Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
33The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil. 34Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say. 35They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_text:
Bipɛntɛnfalaa wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Sɛɛh bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ alugɔ lugli hora la. N kaa sɛbi wia la n faa du lugli hora la hiŋ purgee la ni. 2Ɛɛ sirya chɔɔzi ni, di tinni Bizeŋ Sinaai di wa chem n ni u nyuu. 3Nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa jaa i ni di ra ba de. Maa nyiŋŋi n na nɛr maa a bizeŋ ni, haali sela gba gilɛɛ waa di u zɛɛ.”
4Denii Moosis sɛɛh a bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ alugɔ lugli hora la. Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzimpikke ni, u izi di kpaa tinni a bizeŋ nyuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la. 5Denii Kɔraawiizi ga baama biini di tuu wa chi u be, di yir u himmaa sɔnzeŋ, Minuu Kɔraawiizi. 6Kɔraawiizi ga Moosis see di ra ŋɔ, “Minuu Kɔraawiizi, Minuu Kɔraawiizi, di ra suŋ nɛra ni di ra na ba sinyɛna. N baaŋ waa fuuh manaŋ, di kaa dɔɔ nɔŋŋaa ni wibii werge. 7N nɔŋŋi nɛra kagboŋaa werge, di ɔɔ gil ba biinikpola, dignikpega ni ba wichɔgaa di ra tɛɛ baa. Ka maa gil wichɔgɛɛra digna tɛraa. N ɔɔ tɛrgi biizi ni naanna maa dignaa dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia, haali di ga hel jiminizi ahoro ni anaazu hina.”
8Moosis giŋŋi manaŋ di jaami Kɔraawiizi, 9ka ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, di n wia pariibuu, amɔ, i jaa yaa ni di ra la. Nɛra naa ɛɛ dignikpega hinaa, ka í gil yaa biinikpola ni wichɔgaa tɛɛ yaa, ka gil ya ɛɛ i nɛra.”
10Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “N ni ia ra ɛɛ nuukpannɛ filaŋkeŋ. N daŋ ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia miŋ haa waa ɛɛwɛ ŋmɛnɛ maa durnya hɛssi bɛl maa nɛra biini, i nɛra naa see. Ɔnsii werge daŋ lau nɛra la ii ni baa n duwɛɛ la, ba bɔra ra sa dikuu wia la Minuu Mìŋ́, n niŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ ia la wia. 11Ií ra hiŋ Gbɔgni naa maa miŋ tɛɛ ia zinaa naa. N daŋ duŋŋi Amɔri, Keenan, Hitti, Pɛriz, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina maa. 12Ií ra du tau di gilɛɛ waa gil ii ni nɛra la n soge hɛri la biini iinna la la wàá dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daŋ du ii biini lugɔ sidɛɛ di ra lauri ia. 13Ií purgi ba mbusu lizibɔra ni ba bia la baŋ baŋzɛɛ tɛɛ ba vuga di kuugi ba vughaaŋ Asɛra daazi. 14Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ n di Zoma la, ɛɛ zoma hinnɛ werge.
15Ií ra du tau di gilɛɛ waa gil ii ni nɛra la n soge a hɛri la wàá dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, di ba haŋ wàá kuari ba vuga di lizi mbusuzi di ra tɛɛa, ba daŋ wer yir ia, ii di a mbusuzi lizaa diwee. 16Di ii wa nyiŋŋi ba biihaana tɛɛ ii biibaala ba ɛɛ ba haana, ba daŋ gil ba janna wia nyaa wibii n be, di gil ba ra kuari ba vuga.
17Ií gilɛɛ waa luu vuga di ra kuaraa.
18Ií ɔɔ ra di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizeŋ la. Ií ɔɔ hee paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, gunla min ŋɔ ií ɔɔ ra ɛɛ la. Ií ra ɛɛ guŋ saŋa la min dauwɛ Abib baagu biini la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u biinii ii kpa lii Ijip hɛri la.
19Ií biibambilugla maa ɛɛ n horaa, ani ii sela ge gba biiballugla maa. 20Ií ɔɔ kpa pebii di bir yau kawee biiballugli maa. Di ii wàá ɛɛ guŋ, amɔ, ií ku a kawee baŋaa. A dɛkkɔɔ ii ɔɔ kpa pebii di bir yau biibambilugli ge maa.
Nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa ba n be ni nodumazi.
21Hɔpizaa anumbɛllɛ ií ɔɔ kpa di hum huma, ka kpa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la di heezi, haali di paraa gɛɛ kuna kpai saŋaa, ka ií ɔɔ heezi.
22Ií ɔɔ kpa ii huuti nyulugla di di ii Kuna Kummaa Hɔpizizeŋ di kaa di ii Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ, di ii wa tɔrgi ii daa nɔna, a bina tuna. 23Bina maa biini, Izrɛl hina baala dɛkkɔɔ ba ɔɔ ba mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa Izrɛl hina ra hum la see buhoro, di wa jaamiŋ. 24N daŋ tɔ ii see di duŋŋi hɛrkpila hina maa, di gil ii hɛri wazi. Di ii liwɔɔ buhoro bina maa ii wa jaami mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, nɛr maa waa ra kɛlli ii hɛri ni lugɔ u dɔɔu.
25Ii gilɛɛ waa kpa kunla maa n dɔɔ yiisi, di ra jaa sel maa chal ni, di lizi mbusu ra tɛŋ. Di ii ɔɔ wa lizi mbusu di tɛŋ Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la ge, a waa dɛkkɛ a yeŋ n chigɛ hɔɔ ra pizaa.
26Bina maa ií ɔɔ lizi ii pattikuna lugli horpazi di ba Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la Dia.
Ií ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ wa kpa buuŋ ilanii di ra daali u bie.”
27Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Sɛbi wia naa maa di dau, dikuubɛɛwiai, a ninɛɛ n chi, n nii ni Izrɛl hina ɛɛ nuukpaŋ.” 28Moosis du a bizeŋ la nyuu Kɔraawiizi be hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ, di waa kummaa diwee, waa kummaa nyɔɔwɛ. Denii u sɛbi Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra nuukpaŋ dɔɔi wia la di dau bipɛntɛnzi la ni. Gbɔgni Fi labuu guŋ.
Moosis siwee n na nyɛgzi wia
29Moosis n kpogli bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la Gbɔgni fi la du a ni, di lii Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu tuu la, u siwee ra nyɛgzi werge maa dikuu u ni Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ wia la wia, ka waa zummɛ. 30Aarɔn ni Izrɛl hina maa n wa na Moosis di u siwee ra nyɛgzi werge la, ɔnsii lau baa, ba waa nyiŋŋi ba dugluu. 31Ka Moosis yir baa. Denii Aarɔn ni Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi jaa sɛɛ ba u be, u ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa. 32Uŋ wa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa tuŋ, Izrɛl hina maa jaa tuzi heluu, u kpa Gbɔgni la maa Kɔraawiizi n tɛu Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu la di bagli baa.
33Moosis n wa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa tuŋ, u kpa saata tɔ u siwee. 34Ka saŋa maa, di u wa zuu Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Chemaa Tanti Dia la, ú ŋɔ wia tɛu, ɔɔ pilli a saataa di ga hel saŋa la un niŋ lii. Di u wa liwɔɔ ge di bagli gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ lugɔ ú ŋɔ tɛɛ baa la, 35ba ɔɔ na lugɔ u siwee ra nyɛgzuu werge maa. Denii Moosis ɔɔ bir lau a saata tɔ, di ra ba saŋa la un niŋ kaa zuu, u ni Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia la.

english_text:
Laws for the Sabbath
1Moses called together the people of Israel and told them that the Lord had said:
2 You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death. 3Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath.
Offerings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 25.1-9; 35.10-19)
4Moses told the people of Israel that the Lord had said:
5I will welcome an offering from anyone who wants to give something. You may bring gold, silver, or bronze; 6blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair; 7tanned ram skin or fine leather; acacia wood; 8olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or 9onyx stones or other gems for the sacred vest and breastpiece.
10If you have any skills, you should use them to help make what I have commanded: 11the sacred tent with its covering and hooks, its framework and crossbars, and its post and stands; 12the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it; 13the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 14the lamp with its equipment and oil; 15the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent; 16the altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 17the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance; 18the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard; 19and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
Gifts for the Lord
20Moses finished speaking, and everyone left. 21Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes. 22Men and women came willingly and gave all kinds of gold jewelry such as pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces. 23Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather. 24Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
25The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made. 26And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
27The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest. 28They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests. 29Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts.
Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 31.1-11)
30Moses said to the people of Israel:
The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe. 31-33Not only has the Lord filled him with his Spirit, but he has given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 34The Lord is urging him and Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to teach others. 35And he has given them all kinds of artistic skills, including the ability to design and embroider with blue, purple, and red wool and to weave fine linen.
translation_text:
Heezaa Hɔpizii widaulaa wia
1Denii Moosis chaali Izrɛl hina la maa di ŋɔ, “Wia naabuu Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ií ra ɛɛ. 2Ií daŋ ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛl di hum huma ka aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la daŋ ɛɛ hɔpizinanii tɛɛ ia. Ií kpau tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi di ɛɛu Heezaa Hɔpizii. Nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ ka hum huma a hɔpizii naa, bá kpuu. 3Ií gilɛɛ waa chem niŋ gba ii diini a Heezaa Hɔpizii hiŋ.”
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia kuaraa kuna wia
4Moosis kaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la maa be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ií ɛɛ. 5Kuna la maa iin dɔɔwɛ, ií lizi aŋhina di wa sunzi Kɔraawiizi. Di a par nɛr maa lugɔ u ba kuna aŋhina ni di wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, anniibuu dɛkkɛ u kpa ba. Saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa, danyɛ 6gessihuŋŋunanaa, peezi huna baŋ liiwe burgu, a aahma lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, a aahma choihchoih, wɛjɛ la baŋ kpa buuŋ huna suah, 7pebala hɔna la baŋ liiwe a aah, hɔŋbuglaa, akeesia daazi, 8fintina nuuri, kunsɔɔhrisuma ban niŋ kpa di kuari nuuwaarii, daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la banna fuuh, 9binanaa banna yir ɔnigs ani anla n kawɛɛ ba kpa margi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ tagtakpurii ni u bampirii pɛɛŋ la ni.
10Izrɛl hina la n zum nonii huma nɛnnɛ maanii niŋ chaali, di wa kuari kuna la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ yá kuari la. 11Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni u kuntɔɔrikuna, u kuŋgorgaa, daabaŋlaa kuna, u dominua daazi, daakaŋlaa, daabaŋlaa ani a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra, 12di kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ni u daajaŋra, u tua la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋ nɛra ni de, ani patiisa la n tɔ u ni la, 13tɛɛbul la ni u daajaŋra ni u kuna maa ani paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ kpa di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la. 14Fintina daa la n na chaani de ni u kuna maa ni u fintinazi ni nuu ba kpa di ra choŋŋaa. 15Daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr la ni u daajaŋra, nuuwaarii, a kunsɔɔhrisuma ani a Tanti Dia dominua patiisa, 16di kpa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni u danyɛ nyagrinyagri ni u daajaŋra ani u kuna. Danyɛ tassazeŋ ni u zɛɛ hɔŋribɔr, 17a diŋŋee patiisazi ni u daabaŋlaa ni a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra ani a diŋŋee dominua patiisa, 18Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni u diŋŋee daasiraa ni a ŋmɛnni, 19suahri bɔmbɔgnanaananaa la ban niŋ bɔg di ra hum Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia biini, di kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Aarɔn ni u biibaala bɔmbɔgnanaananaa ban niŋ bɔg di ba waa hum kizeehina huma.”
20Denii Izrɛl hina maa lii Moosis be di bir kaali ba diini, 21unla maa aŋ pattɛ, u bampirii tɛu guŋ, kpa u sunzaa di wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi bá kpa kuari Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia ni kuna la maa ban niŋ kpa di ra hum de huma, ani a bɔmbɔgnanaananaa la. 22Baala ni haana maa kpa kuna la maa baŋ kpa saliŋ luu di ba, dignikunaa, nonibisigaa ani baŋaakuna. Ba maa kpa ba saliŋ kuna di ba, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 23Nɛr la maa n dɔɔ gessizi naa, burguu, zagbiiŋ nii, a aahma choihchoih ni gessihuŋŋunanaa, buuŋ hunaa, pebala hɔna baŋ liiwe a aah, ani hɔŋbuglaa kpaa di ba. 24Banla maa n dɔɔ saliŋhuŋŋa ni danyɛ kpaa ba di wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Banla maa ge n dɔɔ akeesia daazi kpaa ba, ba hum a huma. 25Haana la maa n zum peezi huna tai nɛnnɛ kpa gessi burgu, zagbiiŋ nii ani a aahma choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa baŋ tawɛɛ di ba. 26Haana la maa n zum buuna huna tai nɛnnɛ, a par baa ge ta a gessi. 27Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi la maa ge kpa binanaa, ɔnigs ni anla n kawɛɛ di ba, ba margi Aarɔn tagtakpurii ni u bampirii pɛɛŋ la ni. 28Baŋhina ge ba kunsɔɔhrisuma, ɔlivi nuu ba kpa di ra du fintinazi, di kpa ra kuari nuuwaarii ani daahɛgsɔɔhsuma. 29Izrɛl hina baala ni haana la maa aŋ pattɛ, kpa ba sunzaazi di wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, bá wer hum huma la Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be di ŋɔ bá hum la.
Bizalɛl ni Ɔhɔliab wia
30Denii Moosis ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, “Ií ra nuu! Kɔraawiizi lizi Uri biibaal, Bɛzalɛl n ɛɛ Hur naannaa di lii Juda dee biini. 31Kɔraawiizi Duma izuubuu, u dɔɔ kuna kuaraa zumaa, di wer wia ɛɛi, di dɔɔ nunzuma werge maa, ú wer zum nonii huma maa iri nɛnnɛ. 32U daŋ wer kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa ani danyɛ di luu kuŋ maa iri u du wer, 33di zum binanaa sɛɛih ni a suuzaa kuna ni, di zum daazi sɛɛih ni nonii huma maa iri. 34Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ u ni Ahisamak biibaal Ɔhɔliab n lii Dan dee biinii nunzuma werge maa, bá wer di ra bagli nɛra. 35U faa tɛɛ baabuu zumaa ba ra hum huma maa ni a dizi alugɔ nonii huma, zɛuzaa, gessizi burgu, zagbiiŋ nii, a aahma ni gessihuŋŋunanaa suaih. Ba maa wettoo di ra hum nonii huma maa iri, di ra kuari kuna nɛnnɛ.”

english_text:
1The Lord has given to Bezalel, Oholiab, and others the skills needed for building a place of worship, and they will follow the Lord's instructions.
2Then Moses brought together these workers who were eager to work, 3and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning, 4that finally everyone stopped working 5and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.” 6So Moses sent word for the people to stop giving, and they did. 7But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done.
The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.1-14)
8-9The skilled workers got together to make the sacred tent and its linen curtains that were woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Each of the ten panels was twelve meters long and two meters wide, 10and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each. 11-13Then 50 loops of blue cloth were put along one of the wider sides of each curtain, and the two curtains were fastened together at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
14-15As the material for protecting the tent, goat hair was used to weave eleven sections 13 meters by 2 meters each. 16These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections. 17Fifty loops were put along one of the wider sides of each panel, 18and the two panels were fastened at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 19Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.15-30)
20Acacia wood was used to build the framework for the walls of the sacred tent. 21Each frame was 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 22-26with two wooden pegs near the bottom. Then two silver stands were placed under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so they could be joined together. Twenty of these frames were used along the south side and 20 more along the north. 27Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side 28-29with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom. 30Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
31-33Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 34The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through.
The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.31-37)
35They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 36They also made four acacia wood posts and covered them with gold. Then gold rings were fastened to the posts, which were set on silver stands.
37For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 38They made five posts, covered them completely with gold, and set each of them on a gold-covered bronze stand. Finally, they attached hooks for the curtain.
translation_text:
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ,“Awia, Bɛzalɛl, Ɔhɔliab ani huŋhunna la maa Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ nonii huma ni kuna kuraa zumaa, bá zum gunla ban niŋ kuari Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la, kuari kuna la maa gunla himmaa uŋ faa ŋɔ ba ɛɛ la.”
2Denii Moosis jaa yir Bɛzalɛl, Ɔhɔliab ani banla maa Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ baa kuna kuaraa zumaa ni wia ɛɛi la, a par baa lugɔ ba hum a huma la, bá ba wa hum a huma. 3Ba lɛɛ kuna la maa Izrɛl hina la n sunzɛɛ, bá kuari Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la di lii Moosis be. Ka Izrɛl hina haa kpa kuna di wàá sunzi Kɔraawiizi ani ba biine maa, hɔpizi bii maa. 4Denii huŋhunna la maa n dɔɔ kuŋkuaraa zumaa gil ba humazi, 5ka ba Moosis be di wa ŋɔ, “A nɛra haa ra ba kuna ninɛɛ werge maa, di kaali gunla maga Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ yá kpa di hum a huma. A kaali gunla maga yaa n na nyiŋŋuu.”
6Moosis n wa nuu guŋ, u gil ba ŋɔ nɛra la maa n du ba chɔɔribɔr la maa be, dí nɛr maa, baal gɛɛ haaŋ gilɛɛ kaa wàá kpa kummaa di wàá sunzi dikuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la wia. Denii a nɛra jaa gil, 7dikuubɛɛwiai, ba sunzaa teŋ kannɔɔ, a wer hum a huma maa tuŋ ka ka.
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia wia
8Banla n faa zum nonii huma nɛnnɛ a huŋhunna biini la maa faa nyɛr patiisazi fi di kuari Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la. Ba faa kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa la baŋ ŋmɛɛnɛɛ nɛnnɛ ni gessi la baŋ liiwe aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, zagbiiŋ nii ani u aahmu choihchoih, di suah patiisazi fi, di gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ, tɔɔhzi chɛrubzi di du a ni. 9A patiisazi maa faa mɛgzi dɔŋaa. Bɛl maa jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko ni ŋmantannaazi, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi anaazu. 10Ba faa kpa a patiisazi anue di nyɛr choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, di kaa kpa anue la ge n kawɛɛ di ɛɛ guŋ. 11Denii ba faa kpa pɛɛŋ burgu di gurgi lugɔ suzaa di nyɛr du a bɛl maa nua. 12Ba kaa kuari suzaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi di du lugli patiisa la ni, di kaa kuari suzaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi di du nɛɛhiŋ la tuna, a chaŋ dɔŋa. 13Denii ba kpa saliŋ di luu kuna lugɔ kuŋgorgaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi di kpaa gorgi a patiisazi anɛɛ hiŋ choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, á Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia maa ɛɛ kpaŋ.
14Ba kpa buuŋ huna di suah patiisazi fidikpaŋ di tɔ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia. 15A maanii faa mɛgzɛɛ, bɛl maa jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi anaazu. 16Ba kpa a anue di nyɛr choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, di kpa anumbɛl ge nyɛr di choŋŋi dɔŋa ni. 17Denii ba nyɛr suzaa tokkoanɛɛgaa ni fizi di du a bɛl maa tuna hor ni. 18Ba kpa danyɛ luu kuŋgorgaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, di lau a tanti dia, ú ɛɛ kpaŋ. 19Denii ba kpa pebala hɔna baŋ liiwe a aah di kuari kuntɔɔrikuŋ di tɔ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia, di kaa kpa hɔŋbuglaa di kuari bɛl di tɔ sag a ni.
20Ba kpa akeesia daazi di kuari Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la. 21Á daazi la bɛl maa jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi fi, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogume ni keza. 22Ba sɛɛh a daa bɛl maa zɛɛ, u dɔɔ naazi anɛɛ a mɛgzi dɔŋa. Ba kuari a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia daabaŋlaa la maa guŋ. 23Ba kuari daabaŋlaa tokko di du a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere, 24di kpa saliŋhuŋŋa luu a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra tokkoanɛɛ, anɛɛgaa du a daabaŋlaa bɛl maa zɛɛ di lauraa chiŋŋi. 25Ba kuari daazi tokko di du u wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ge 26ani a zɛɛ hɔŋribɔra la n ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa tokkoanɛɛ, di kpa anɛɛgaa du bɛl maa zɛɛ. 27Ba kuari daabaŋlaa anumbɛl di du a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia harbɔɔ wiicholii tuna la, 28di kaa kuari daabaŋlaa anɛɛ di du a Dia siraa anɛɛ la n du tuna la. 29A siraa anɛɛ naa, a daabaŋlaa faa ɛɛ anɛɛgaarɛ guŋŋ di lii zɛɛ di la chiŋ di ga suu gbitti kpaŋ ni. Gunnɛ ba kuari a maa. 30Awia, a daabaŋlaa faa du ŋmantannaazi ani a zɛɛzi saliŋhuŋŋa hɔŋribɔra ɛɛ fidaanumbɛl, anɛɛ du bɛl maa zɛɛ.
31Ba kaa kpa akeesia daazi kuari daakaŋlaa, anue kaŋli Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia keŋkere bɛl daabaŋlaa la ni, 32anue ge kaŋli anla n du u keŋkere la hiŋ ni, anue ge kaŋli u wiicholii hora la n du u tuna la ni. 33Ba kuari u baambaaŋ daakaŋlii la u kaŋli keŋkere bɛl maa daabaŋlaa la baambaaŋ ni di wa kaali, di lii tuna bɛl di ga chug tuna bɛl. 34Ba ŋmɛɛri saliŋ di tɔ a daabaŋlaa la bɛl maa ni, di luu saliŋ gbittizi di du a ni, a lauri a daakaŋlaa di kpogli, di kaa ŋmɛɛri saliŋ di tɔ a daakaŋlaa ge ni.
35Ba kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa ni peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina ge aah choihchoih di suah patiisa, di gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ, tɔɔhzi chɛrubzi di du u ni. 36Ba kuari akeesia daabaŋlaa anaazu di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ di tɔ a maa ni. Di luu saliŋ kuŋgorgaa di du a ni, di ŋmɛɛri saliŋhuŋŋa di luu a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra. 37Ba kpa gessi la n ɛɛ peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina ge aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa, di suah patiisazi, di gil ba tɔɔhzaa, di kpa tɔ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia dominua. 38Ba kpa akeesia daazi anue di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ, di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ di tɔ a chine ni lugbidaazi ni, di kpa danyɛ luu a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra.

english_text:
The Sacred Chest
(Exodus 25.10-22)
1Bezalel built a chest of acacia wood 110 centimeters long, 66 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 2He covered it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the top. 3He made four gold rings and attached one of them to each of the four legs of the chest. 4Then he made two poles of acacia wood, covered them with gold, 5and put them through the rings, so the chest could be carried by the poles.
6The entire lid of the chest, which was made of pure gold, was the place of mercy. 7-9On each of the two ends of the chest he made a winged creature of hammered gold. They faced each other, and their wings covered the place of mercy.
The Table for the Sacred Bread
(Exodus 25.23-30)
10Bezalel built a table of acacia wood 88 centimeters long, 44 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 11-12He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border 75 millimeters thick. 13He made four gold rings and attached one to each of the legs 14near the edging. The poles for carrying the table were placed through these rings 15and were made of acacia wood covered with gold. 16Everything that was to be set on the table was made of pure gold—the bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings.
The Lampstand
(Exodus 25.31-40)
17Bezalel made a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered gold, 18with three branches on each of its two sides. 19There were three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 20and four on the stem. 21There was also a blossom where each pair of branches came out from the stem. 22The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 23-24The lamp and its equipment, including the tongs and trays, were made of about 35 kilograms of pure gold.
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 30.1-5)
25For burning incense, Bezalel made an altar of acacia wood. It was 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull. 26He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 27Then below the edging on opposite sides he attached two gold rings through which he put the poles for carrying the altar. 28These poles were also made of acacia wood and covered with gold.
The Oil for Dedication and the Incense
(Exodus 30.22-38)
29 Bezalel mixed the sacred oil for dedication and the pure spices for the sweet-smelling incense.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka wia
1Bɛzalɛl kpa akeesia daazi di kuari dakka, u jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛ ni keza, u wassi ɛɛ nogume ni keza, u chiŋ laŋaa ge ɛɛ nogume ni keza. 2U ŋmɛɛri saliŋ himmaa di tɔ u biini ni u har maa di kpa saliŋ bar u nua. 3U kaa luu saliŋ gbittizi anaazu di kpa bɛl maa du u naazi anaazu la bɛl maa ni, anɛɛ du keŋkere bɛl, anɛɛ ge du keŋkere bɛl. 4Denii u kpa akeesia daa di kuari daajaŋra di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a maa ni. 5Di kpaa suuzi gbittizi la, bá ɔɔ wer lawaa di ra kpa a dakka.
6U kaa kpa saliŋ himmaa kuari a dakka tua la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih u nɛra ni de la, u jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛ ni keza, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogume ni keza. 7Denii u kpa saliŋ di luu chɛrubzi anɛɛ di hɔŋ a dakka tua tunazi. 8U kaa luu a chɛrub bɛl u chi a dakka tua kɛrii bɛl, di kaa luu bɛl ge u chi u kɛrii bɛl. U kpa saliŋ daa kpaŋ di luu a ni a tua la maa a ɛɛ kpaŋ. 9A chɛrubzi siwee chaŋ dɔŋa di ra binni a tua, a keeri ge yaa di guali u ni.
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia tɛɛbul
10Ba kpa akeesia daa di kuari tɛɛbul, u jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛ, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogume, u chiŋ laŋaa ge ɛɛ nogume ni keza. 11Denii u ŋmɛɛri saliŋ himmaa tɔ u maa, di kpa aŋhina bar u kɛraa lugɔ gir. 12U kaa kuari gir bar u kɛraa, u ɛɛ nopaal wassi maga di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ sag u ni. 13U kaa luu saliŋ gbittizi anaazu, di kpa bɛl maa mari u siraa anaazu la, u naazi n duwɛɛ la ni. 14Gbittizi la ban niŋ ɔɔ kpa daazi suu di ra chi a tɛɛbul la dugli gir la n bar u kɛraa la. 15Daajaŋra la ban niŋ kpa di ra chiu la ɛɛ akeesia daazi, ba ŋmɛɛri saliŋ di tɔ a maa ni. 16U kpa saliŋ himmaa di kuari u pɛrɛtuzi, libizi, tassazi ani tɔga, ba kpa yiili siŋ di ra ta Kɔraawiizi.
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia fintina daa wia
17Ba kpa saliŋ himmaa luu fintina daa ni u zɛɛ, di kuari u nuuri duuribɔra la a du lugɔ fiiri n punzee, a ni a daa maa ɛɛ kpaŋ. 18U dɔɔ kela anumbɛl, ahoro du u keŋkere maa. 19Kela anumbɛl la bɛl maa dɔɔ nuuri duuribɔra ahoro lugɔ daa bɛl banna yir almɔn fiiri ni a pume. 20Ba luu nuuri duuribɔra lugɔ almɔn fiiri ni a pume anaazu di du u daa la ni, 21di luu pumkpaŋkpaŋa di du a kela anɛɛgaa maa zɛɛ. 22Saliŋ himmaanii ba kpa luu a fintina daa ni u kela ani fiiri la maa n du u ni la, a maa ɛɛ kpaŋ.
23Ba kpa saliŋ himmaa di kuari katooljigzi aniidaanɛɛ ni kuna la ban niŋ kpa di ra mɔnni fintina yakɔssi ni pɛrɛtujigzi. 24Saliŋ himmaa kilozi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazuu ba kpa di kuari a fintina daa ni u kummaa.
Daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr wia
25Ba kpa akeesia daazi di kuari daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr. U jaŋzi ni u wassi maa ɛɛ kpaŋ. U jaŋzi ɛɛ nogume, u wassi ge guŋ, u chiŋ laŋaa ge ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛ, di gil u ni u siraa anaazu nyigzi maa ɛɛ kuŋkpaŋ. 26Ba ŋmɛɛri saliŋ himmaa di tɔ u nyuu ni u keŋkerezi ni u nyigzi maa, di kaa ŋmɛɛri saliŋ di bar u nua lugɔ gir. 27Ba kaa kpa saliŋ luu gbittizi anaazu di du a nua gir la zɛɛ, anɛɛ du keŋkerezi la bɛl maa, di lauri daajaŋra la ban niŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra chiu la di kpogli. 28Ba teŋri akeesia daajaŋra di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔa.
29Ba kaa kuari nuuwaarinaniinanii baŋ ɔɔ kpa ra waari Kɔraawiizi nɛra ni ani kunsɔɔhrisuma himmaa alugɔ nɛr la n zum tulaale huma n kuarɛɛ.

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 27.1-8)
1Bezalel built an altar of acacia wood for offering sacrifices. It was 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high 2with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull, and it was completely covered with bronze. 3The equipment for the altar was also made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4About halfway up the altar he built a ledge around it and covered the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. 5Then he attached a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners to put the poles through. 6He covered two acacia wood poles with bronze and 7put them through the rings for carrying the altar, which was shaped like an open box.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 30.18-21)
8 Bezalel made a large bowl and a stand out of bronze from the mirrors of the women who helped at the entrance to the sacred tent.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 27.9-19)
9-17Around the sacred tent Bezalel built a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. He used 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then he hung a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. He placed three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hung a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts.
18-19For the entrance to the courtyard, Bezalel made a curtain nine meters long, which he hung on four bronze posts that were set on bronze stands. This curtain was 2.25 meters high, the same height as the one for the rest of the courtyard, and was made of fine linen embroidered and woven with blue, purple, and red wool. He hung the curtain on the four posts, using silver hooks and rods. 20The pegs for the tent and for the curtain around the tent were made of bronze.
The Sacred Tent
21-23Bezalel had worked closely with Oholiab, who was an expert at designing and engraving, and at embroidering blue, purple, and red wool. The two of them completed the work that the Lord had commanded to be done.
Moses put Aaron's son Ithamar in charge of the Levites who kept record of the metals used for the sacred tent. 24According to the official weights, the amount of gold given was a ton, 25 and the silver that was collected when the people were counted came to 3.4 tons. 26 Everyone who was counted paid the required amount, and there was a total of 603,550 men who were 20 years old or older.
27Thirty-four kilograms of the silver were used to make each of the 100 stands for the sacred tent and the curtain. 28The remaining 30 kilograms of silver were used for the hooks and rods and for covering the tops of the posts.
29Two thousand four hundred and twenty-five kilograms of bronze were given. 30And it was used to make the stands for the entrance to the tent, the altar and its grating, the equipment for the altar, 31the stands for the posts that surrounded the courtyard, including those at the entrance to the courtyard, and the pegs for the tent and the courtyard.
translation_text:
Mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa bɔr wia
1Ba kpa akeesia daazi di kuari mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr, u chiŋ laŋaa ɛɛ nogumzi ahoro, u jaŋzi ni u wassi maa ɛɛ nogumzi anuezi. 2Ba sɛɛh u siraa anaazu la maa a baŋzi lugɔ nyigzi, a ni mbusu lizibɔr la maa ɛɛ kpaŋ, di ŋmɛɛri danyɛ di tɔ u maa. 3Ba kaa kpa danyɛ luu mbusu lizibɔr kuna naa, viini la ban niŋ ɔɔ paa u hɔɔhri di ra du, sɔɔbulzi, tassazi la ban ninna du chal di ra mizi, dunozi n dɔɔ nyina ba ɔɔ kpa di ra tɔɔhzi ola ani nimbuurikuna. 4Ba kaa kpa danyɛ luu nyagrinyagri, di kpau suu u biini u ga hel u galga. 5Ba kpa danyɛ luu gbittizi a lauri u siraa anaazu daajaŋra la n lau nyagrinyagri la di kpogli. 6Ba kpa akeesia daazi di kuari daajaŋra, di ŋmɛɛri danyɛ tɔa. 7Ba kpa a daajaŋra di suuzi a gbittizi la n du u keŋkerezi la bɔɔni ba wer lawaa di ra chiu. Taabɔɔzii ba kpa kuaruu u dɔɔ bɔɔ lugɔ dakka.
Nonee ni naazi sanzaa tassazeŋ wia
8Ba kpa danyɛ luu tassazeŋ ni u zɛɛ hɔŋribɔr, ba kpa di ra sanzi nonee ni naazi. Haana la n faa ra hum Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua la benii ba faa lɛɛ digee kuaraa.
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia diŋŋee wia
9Denii ba kaa kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa patiisazi di teŋ diŋŋee bar Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia. U wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere jaŋzi ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi kalfa, 10di dɔɔ daabaŋlaa ni a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra tokkozi, baŋ kpa danyɛ di luu. Di luu saliŋhuŋŋa kuŋgorgaa ni lugbidaazi la ban niŋ kpa sagzi a daabaŋlaa ni. 11U wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ge guŋ.
12A diŋŋee wiicholii wassi ɛɛ nogumzi tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, di dɔɔ patiisazi, daabaŋlaa fi ni a zɛɛzi danyɛ hɔŋribɔra fi, di kpa saliŋhuŋŋa kuŋgorgaa ani lugbidaazi jaa. 13U wiifurii paga la dominua n duwɛɛ la ge wassi ɛɛ nogumzi tokkoanɛɛ ni fi. 14Patiisazi la jaŋzi n ɛɛ nogumzi fidaanue tɔ a dominua keŋkere bɛl di dɔɔ daabaŋlaa ahoro ani a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra a lawaa kpogli. 15U keŋkere la hiŋ ge, guŋ himmaanii. 16Patiisazi la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ teŋ a diŋŋee ɛɛ gessihuŋŋunanaarɛ. 17Danyɛɛ ba faa kpa kuari a hɔŋribɔra. Di kpa saliŋhuŋŋa di ŋmɛɛri tɔ a daabaŋlaa nyuuni. A faa dɔɔ saliŋhuŋŋa kuŋgorgaa ni lugbidaazi. 18Ba kpa peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina ge aah choihchoih, di gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ tɔɔhzaa. U jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko, u chiŋ laŋaa ɛɛ nogumzi anue lugɔ diŋŋee hora la. 19U dɔɔ daabaŋlaa anaazu ni a zɛɛzi danyɛ hɔŋribɔra anaazu, di dɔɔ saliŋhuŋŋa kuŋgorgaa ni lugbidaazi. Ba kaa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa di ŋmɛɛri tɔ a daazi nyuuni. 20Danyɛɛ ba kpa di luu daasiraa di lauri Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni u diŋŋee la maa bar.
Kuna laa baŋ kpawɛɛ kuaruu wia
21Kuna la maa baŋ faa kpawɛɛ kuari Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia labuu keŋ. U biinii bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la baŋ sɛbi Gbɔgni fi du a ni la du. Moosis faa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Aarɔn biibaal Itama be lugɔ ú tɔ Levi dee see, bá sɛbi dawuu keŋ. 22Uri biibaal Bɛzalɛl n ɛɛ Hur naana di lii Juda dee biini, labuu faa kuari kuna la maa Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis kuari la, 23Ahisamak biibaal Ɔhɔliab n lii Dan dee biini, di faa ɛɛ nɛr la n zum nyɛraa ni tɔɔhzaa nɛnnɛ, di ɔɔ wer kpa peezi huna la baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina ɛɛ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di suah pɛɛna labuu faa jaa u ni. 24Saliŋ la maa baŋ faa lallɛɛ chiŋ di viigi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ba kpa hum u Tanti Dia huma la, tɔgzi faa ɛɛ kilozi kagbonne, gunla banna mɛgzaa Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la.
25Saliŋhuŋŋa la baŋ faa nawɛɛ lii nɛra la baŋ faa kutte, di lii nɛra kuraa saŋa la, faa du kilozi kagboŋa ahoro ni kalfaanaazu ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, gunla banna mɛgzaa Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia biini la. 26Kunla nɛr maa n faa turgee lii nɛra kuraa saŋa gunla an dɛkkɛ ú turgi, dikuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia kinturgaa wia biinii guŋ. Baala la n faa di binni tokko ni saga faa du kagboŋa kalfaanumbɛl ni ahoro ni kalfaanue ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi. 27Saliŋhuŋŋu tɔgzi n faa hel kilozi kagboŋa ahoro ni kalfaanaazuu ba faa kpa di kuari a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni u patiisazi zɛɛ kuŋhɔŋribɔra kalfa la. Kilozi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazuu ba faa kpa di kuari a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra la bɛl maa. 28A saliŋhuŋŋu la n kawɛɛ tɔgzi faa ɛɛ kilozi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, Bɛzalɛl faa kpa di kuari a daabaŋlaa kuŋgorgaa ni a chine ani a lugbidaazi.
29Danyɛ la baŋ faa lallɛɛ chiŋ di viigi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, tɔgzi du kilozi kagboŋa anɛɛ ni kalfaanaazu ni tokko ni anue. 30Aabuu ba faa kpa di luu a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua zɛɛ hɔŋribɔra ni mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kpa danyɛ kuari la ni u nyagrinyagri ani u kuna maa, 31di kpa a diŋŋee kɛraa ni u dominua zɛɛ hɔŋribɔra ani Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia daasiraa la maa n bar a diŋŋee la.

english_text:
Making the Priestly Clothes
(Exodus 28.1-14)
1Beautiful priestly clothes were made of blue, purple, and red wool for Aaron to wear when he performed his duties in the holy place. This was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
2-3The entire priestly vest was made of fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool. Thin sheets of gold were hammered out and cut into threads that were skillfully woven into the vest. 4-5It had two shoulder straps to support it and a sash that fastened around the waist. 6Onyx stones were placed in gold settings, and each one was engraved with the name of one of Israel's sons. 7Then these were attached to the shoulder straps of the vest, so the Lord would never forget his people. Everything was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Breastpiece
(Exodus 28.15-30)
8The breastpiece was made with the same materials and designs as the priestly vest. 9It was 22 centimeters square and folded double 10with four rows of three precious stones: A carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald were in the first row; 11a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond were in the second row; 12a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst were in the third row; 13and a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper were in the fourth row. They were mounted in a delicate gold setting, 14and on each of them was engraved the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
15-18Two gold rings were attached to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fastened with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps. 19Two other gold rings were attached to the lower inside corners next to the vest, 20and two more near the bottom of the shoulder straps right above the sash. 21To keep the breastpiece in place, a blue cord was used to tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Clothes for the Priests
(Exodus 28.31-43)
22The priestly robe was made of blue wool 23with an opening in the center for the head. The material around the collar was bound so as to keep it from wearing out. 24-26Along the hem of the robe were woven pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a bell of pure gold between each of them. This robe was to be worn by Aaron when he performed his duties.
27-29Everything that Aaron and his sons wore was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, including their robes and turbans, their fancy caps and underwear, and even their sashes that were embroidered with needlework.
30The words “Dedicated to the Lord” were engraved on a narrow strip of pure gold, 31which was fastened to Aaron's turban. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Work Is Completed
(Exodus 35.10-19)
32So the people of Israel finished making everything the Lord had told Moses to make. 33Then they brought it all to Moses: the sacred tent and its equipment, including the hooks, the framework and crossbars, and its posts and stands; 34the covering of tanned ram skins and fine leather; the inside curtain; 35the sacred chest with its carrying poles and the place of mercy; 36the table with all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 37the lampstand of pure gold, together with its equipment and oil; 38the gold-covered incense altar; the ordination oil and the sweet-smelling incense; the curtain for the entrance to the tent; 39the bronze altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 40the curtain with its posts and cords, and its pegs and stands that go around the courtyard; everything needed for the sacred tent; 41and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
42-43When Moses saw that the people had done everything exactly as the Lord had commanded, he gave them his blessing.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ bɔmbɔga wia
1Ba kpa gessizi la n ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina aah choihchoih, di suah pɛɛŋ nyɛr bɔmbɔga ba kpa di ra hum Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia biini. Di kaa nyɛr bɔmbɔgnanaananaa tɛɛ Aarɔn gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.
2Ba kpa saliŋ gessi ni peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina ɛɛ lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di nyɛr a tagtakpurii. 3Ba luu saliŋ pɛlɛpɛlɛ di mɔnnaa gininini lugɔ gessibee di kpa tɛɛ nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ, u kpa jaa gessizi la n ɛɛ burgu ni zagbiiŋ nii ni a aahma choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa ni. 4Ba nyɛr vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa di mari a tagtakpurii siraa, ú ɔɔ wer lawaa di vɔɔzi. 5Ba faa kpa saliŋ gessizi ni gessizi aŋhina n ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina aah choihchoih, ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di suah u chara kirsɔɔ la nɛnnɛ, u du lugɔ pɛɛŋ la himmaa, a maa ɛɛ kpaŋ, gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis be la.
6Ba kpa Binanaa anɛɛ banna yir ɔnigs di sɛɛh Jekɔb biizi fidibanɛɛ la sɔna di dau a ni, di kpa saliŋ ŋmɛnni di baataa du u ni. 7Denii ba kpaa vɔɔzi margi a tagtakpurii vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa la ni, á ɛɛ liize bia tɛɛ Izrɛl dizi fidaanɛɛ la, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.
Bampirii pɛɛŋ wia
8Ba gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ nyɛr pɛɛŋ n na tɔ bampirii maga bɛŋ, u du lugɔ tagtakpurii la pɛɛŋ himmaa. Gessizi la n ɛɛ saliŋ, burgu, zagbiiŋ nii, a aahma choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaarɛ ba kpa di suauh. 9U jaŋzi ni u wassi maa ɛɛ nopaal wassi maga, ba kpɛwuu bunɛɛ. 10Denii ba faa kpa binanaa la yoola n kpolle di margi u ni a hiŋzi dɔŋa pichɔŋzi anaazu. A lugli pichɔŋa la dɔɔ binanaa banna yir rubi ni topaz ani bɛril, 11pichɔnnɛɛhiŋ la dɔɔ tɛkɔis, saafaya ani ɛmɛral, 12horohiŋ la dɔɔ jasint, aget ani amɛtis, 13naazuhiŋ la ge dɔɔ krisolait, ɔnigs ani jaspa. Saliŋ ŋmɛnnii ba kpa baataa du u ni. 14A faa ɛɛ bia fidaanɛɛrɛ, bɛl maa chi tɛɛ Jekɔb biibaala la sɔna, di gil ba sɛɛh Izrɛl dizi fidaanɛɛ la sɔna di du bɛl maa ni.
15Ba kpa saliŋ himmaa yɔlɔzi di pɛr lugɔ ŋmɛŋ di du a bampirii pɛɛŋ ni. 16Ba kpa saliŋ waayananaa anɛɛ di baati saliŋ gbittijigzi anɛɛ, di margi a bampirii pɛɛŋ chiŋ kɛraa anɛɛ la ni, 17ba kpa saliŋ yɔlɔzi la di vɔɔzi a gbittijigzi la n du bampirii pɛɛŋ siraa la ni. 18Di lau a yɔlɔzi nuuzi anɛɛ la n kawɛɛ la di vɔɔzi margi a bɔbaataa anɛɛ la n du a vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa la tagtakpurii la see. 19Ba luu saliŋ gbittijigzi anɛɛ di du u siraa anɛɛ la n du a bampirii pɛɛŋ biini kɛrii n dugli a tagtakpurii la. 20Denii ba kaa luu saliŋ gbittijigzi anɛɛ di du vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa la zɛɛ n du tagtakpurii la see, di dugli bɔr la baŋ nyɛttɛ choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, u chara kirsɔɔ la chiŋ. 21Ba kpa ŋmɛmburgu di lau gbittijigzi la n du bampirii pɛɛŋ la ni di vɔɔzi margi gbittijigzi la n du tagtakpurii la ni, di lawuu vɔɔ mari chara kirsɔɔ la, u gilɛɛ waa lii a tagtakpurii ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina bɔmbɔga n kawɛɛ wia
22Ba kpa pɛɛmburgu di nyɛr tagtajaŋ la baŋ ɔɔ laali tagtakpurii sag u ni la. Suahrii faa suauh. 23Ba fur u baambaaŋ, di muugi u baŋaa hiŋ nɛnnɛ u gilɛɛ waa piili. 24Ba kpa gessizi la baŋ kpa peezi huna di ta, di liaa, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii ani a aahma choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di tɔɔhzi pomegranet du u nua bar, 25di kpa saliŋ himmaa bɛlinzi di du anɛɛ maa baambaaŋ. 26A saliŋ bɛlinzi ni a pomegranet hiŋzi dɔŋa di bar a tagtajaŋ nua bɔmuugii la, a kizeehina ɔɔ laaluu di ra hum, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.
27Suahri kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa di suah pɛɛŋ ba nyɛr tagtajaŋra di tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala, 28ni namu ni kahurozi ani pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii galiŋkpuree. 29Nɛr la n zum nonii huma nɛnnɛ kpa gessizi la n ɛɛ burgu ni zagbiiŋ nii ni a aahma choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di nyɛr kirsɔɔzi gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.
30Ba kaa luu saliŋ himmaa pɛrɛtu, di sɛbi wia naa dau u ni, ‘ba kpaubuu tɛɛ kɔraawiizi u ɛɛ kunnaniinanii.’ 31Denii ba kpa ŋmɛmburgu di vɔɔ mari namu la see ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis ɛɛ la.
32Denii a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia n ɛɛ U Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la huma jaa tuŋ. Izrɛl hina ɛɛ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis ɛɛ la. 33Denii ba kpa a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ba Moosis be. A Tanti Dia ni u kuŋgorgaa, daabaŋlaa kuna, u dominua daazi, daakaŋlaa, daabaŋlaa ani a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra. 34Pebala hɔna la baŋ liiwe a aah la, hɔŋbuglaa ani patiisa la n na tɔ de la, 35Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ni u daajaŋra ni u tua la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋ de la, 36tɛɛbul la ni u kuna maa ani paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, 37a saliŋ himmaa fintina daa la ni u fintinazi n hɔŋzɛɛ hiŋ dɔŋa ni u kuna maa, ani a fintina nuu, 38mbusu lizibɔr baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari la, nuuwaarii, a daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ani a Tanti Dia dominua patiisa, 39mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kpa danyɛ kuari ni u danyɛ nyagrinyagri, u daajaŋra ni u kuna, tassazeŋ la ni u zɛɛ hɔŋribɔr, 40a diŋŋee patiisazi ni u daabaŋlaa ni a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra ani a diŋŋee dominua patiisa, a diŋŋee ŋmɛnni ni a tanti daasiraa, a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia kuna maa, 41ani suahri bɔmbɔgnanaananaa la ban niŋ bɔg di ra hum Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia biini, di kpa Aarɔn ni u biibaala la n ɛɛ kizeehina la bɔmbɔga ban niŋ ɔɔ bɔg di ba wàá hum huma la.
42A Izrɛl hina hum huma la maa gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis ɛɛ la. 43Moosis binni a huma di na lugɔ ba humaabuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la. Awia, u kissi baa.

english_text:
The Lord's Tent Is Set Up
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Set up my tent on the first day of the year 3and put the chest with the Ten Commandments behind the inside curtain. 4Bring in the table and set on it those things that are made for it. Also bring in the lampstand and attach the lamps to it. 5Then place the gold altar of incense in front of the sacred chest and hang a curtain at the entrance to the tent. 6Set the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the entrance to my tent. 7Put the large bronze bowl between the tent and the altar and fill the bowl with water. 8Surround the tent and the altar with the wall of curtains and hang the curtain that was made for the entrance.
9Use the sacred olive oil to dedicate to me the tent and everything in it. 10Do the same thing with the altar for offering sacrifices and its equipment 11and with the bowl and its stand. 12Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent and tell them to wash themselves. 13Dress Aaron in the priestly clothes, then use the sacred olive oil to ordain him and dedicate him to me as my priest. 14Put the priestly robes on Aaron's sons 15and ordain them in the same way, so they and their descendants will always be my priests.
16Moses followed the Lord's instructions. 17And on the first day of the first month of the second year, the sacred tent was set up. 18The posts, stands, and framework were put in place, 19then the two layers of coverings were hung over them. 20The stones with the Ten Commandments written on them were stored in the sacred chest, the place of mercy was put on top of it, and the carrying poles were attached. 21The chest was brought into the tent and set behind the curtain in the most holy place. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
22The table for the sacred bread was put along the north wall of the holy place, 23after which the bread was set on the table. 24The lampstand was put along the south wall, 25then the lamps were attached to it there in the presence of the Lord. 26The gold incense altar was set up in front of the curtain, 27and sweet-smelling incense was burned on it. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
28The curtain was hung at the entrance to the sacred tent. 29Then the altar for offering sacrifices was put in front of the tent, and animal sacrifices and gifts of grain were offered there. 30The large bronze bowl was placed between the altar and the entrance to the tent. It was filled with water, 31then Moses and Aaron, together with Aaron's sons, washed their hands and feet. 32In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
33Finally, Moses had the curtains hung around the courtyard and at the entrance.
The Glory of the Lord
34 Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord. 35And so, Moses could not enter the tent. 36Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow; 37then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again. 38No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia baŋaa wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Baŋ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia hiŋ, lugli baagu lugli hɔpizii hɔl, 3di kpa N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di zuu chiŋŋi u biini, di kpa patiisa la teŋuu. 4Kpa tɛɛbul la ni u kuna maa di zuu chiŋŋi, di kpa fintina daa la ni u fintinazi la maa di zuu hɔŋzi u ni. 5Kpa mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di ga chiŋŋi N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, di vɔɔ a Tanti Dia dominua patiisa la.
6Di kaa kpa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la di chiŋŋi n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia hiŋ dominua see. 7Kpa tassazeŋ la chiŋŋi mbusu lizibɔr la ni n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia hiŋ baambaaŋ, di ɛɛ nii du u biini. 8Kuari diŋŋee baruu di kpa u dominua patiisa la di vɔɔ.
9Kpa nuuwaarii la di waari N Tanti Dia ani kuna la maa n du u biini, di lizi a doŋa ha, ka á ɛɛ kunnanaananaa n be. 10Di kaa ɛɛ a nuu waari mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni u kuna maa ni, di lizi u doŋa ha, ka ú ɛɛ kunnaniinanii himmaa n be. 11Waari tassazeŋ la ni u zɛɛ hɔŋribɔr la, di lizi a doŋa ha, ka á ɛɛ kunnanaananaa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be.
12Kpogli Aarɔn ni u biibaala di ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia hiŋ dominua, di wa sɔ baa nii. 13Di kpa bɔmbɔgnanaananaa la di bɔg Aarɔn, di waaruu a nuu, di sɔu lizi u doŋa ha, ú ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii, di ra hum n kizeehiŋ huma. 14Lau u biibaala di ba wa kpa a tagtajaŋra di bɔg baa. 15Waari baa a nuu alugɔ hiŋ ɛɛ ba mɛɛ la, ba ɛɛ n kizeehina. Guŋ daŋ gil ba ni ba naanna ɛɛ kizeehina di hanna la.” 16Moosis ɛɛ wia la maa gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.
17Awia, u baŋ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia labuu binni anɛɛhiŋ lugli baagu lugli hɔpizii hɔl. 18Moosis n wa baŋ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la, u kpa zɛɛzi kuŋhɔŋlaa la di du a bɔra, di baŋzi a ligee, di sagzi a dolli ni a saŋa. 19Denii u kpa kuntɔɔlii di yaa tɔ a Tanti Dia ni, di kaa kpa nɛɛhiŋ di yaa tɔ u ge ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la.
20U kaa kpa bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la di du Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la biini, di kpa a daajaŋra suuzi a gbittizi bɔɔni, di kpa u tua di tɔ. 21Denii u kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia biini, di kpa a patiisa vɔɔ teŋuu, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la.
22Moosis kpa tɛɛbul la di zuu ga chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag patiisa la baŋgia, 23di kpa a paanuu dau u ni, Kɔraawiizi see, gunla uŋ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.
24Denii u kpa fintina daa la di chiŋŋi chaŋ a tɛɛbul, Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini wiifurii nodig wiikakag, 25di choŋŋi u fintinazi Kɔraawiizi see, gunla uŋ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.
26Moosis kpa mbusu lizibɔr baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari la, di zuu chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini a patiisa see, 27di fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma u ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la. 28Denii u kpa patiisa vɔɔ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia dominua la.
29U kaa kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia n kaa ɛɛ U Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua la, di fuuh mbusuzi lizaa kuna ni mbusuzi lizaa mia u ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.
30U kpa tassazeŋ la di chiŋŋi mbusu lizibɔr ni a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia baambaaŋ di ɛɛ nii du u biini, bá ra sam. 31Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn ni u biibaala ɔɔ ra sanzi ba nonee ni naazi. 32Gunnɛ ba ɔɔ sanzi saŋa maa, di ba haŋ wàá zuu Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia gɛɛ di ba wàá ba mbusu lizibɔr la, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.
33Denii Moosis kuari a diŋŋee bar Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni mbusu lizibɔr la, di kpa u dominua patiisa la vɔɔ, di jaa tuŋ a huma.
Kɔraawiizi girme wia
34Denii baama la wa tɔ a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, Kɔraawiizi girme su de. 35Moosis faa waa kaa wer zuu de, dikuubɛɛwiai, a baama faa tɔ u ninɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi girme su de.
36Izrɛl hina volaa la maa biini, di a baama faa haŋ wa izi a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia nyuu, ba ge ɔɔ izuu di ra vol, 37ka di a baama waa haŋ wa izi, ba waa naa ra kpuzi, di a hɔl la uŋ izee lɛi. 38Awia, Kɔraawiizi baama la ɔɔ faa guali a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ninɛɛ bɔchaaŋ maga. Niŋ ge du u biini hamuŋa ni, Izrɛl hina maa ra na, ba volaa maa biini.

english_text:
1-3The Lord spoke to Moses from the sacred tent and gave him instructions for the community of Israel to follow when they offered sacrifices.
Sacrifices To Please the Lord
The Lord said:
Sacrifices to please me must be completely burned on the bronze altar.
Bulls or rams or goats are the animals to be used for these sacrifices. If the animal is a bull, it must not have anything wrong with it. Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, and I will let you know if it is acceptable to me. 4Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
5After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
6Skin the bull and cut it up, 7while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing. 8-9Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
10If you sacrifice a ram or a goat, it must not have anything wrong with it. 11Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
12-13Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
14If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon. 15A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar, 16remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar. 17Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_text:
Mbusu lizaa kuna fuuih wia
1Kɔraawiizi yir Moosis di ŋɔ wia tɛu di lii U Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini di ra ŋɔ, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ di ba bɛl maa waa lizi mbusu lizaa kuna ú wa tɛŋ, ú gil u lii u nauna gɛɛ u peeza gɛɛ u buuna biini.
3Di mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii lii u nauna biinii, a dɛkkɔɔ ú lizi u bal la n kpekke, di kpau ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, guŋ gil n lɛɛu. 4U daŋ kpa u nonee sag mbusu lizaa sel nyuu ni, ú ɛɛ u mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii, di ɛɛ u wichɔgaa kinturgaa. 5U daŋ kpu a nabalee n see, Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ kizeehina la kpa u chal tɛŋ, ka kpaa mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa n du n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua la. 6U daŋ sih a sel di mɔnnuu. 7Kizeehiŋ Aarɔn la biibaala daŋ paa daazi sag mbusu lizibɔr la ni di chem niŋ, 8ka jaa paagi a ola ni u nyuu ni u nuuri sag a niŋ ni. 9Nɛr la n na lizi mbusu la daŋ yagli u biini kuna ni u gballi, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la jaa fuuh u maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.
10Ka di u ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii di lii u peeza gɛɛ u buuna biini, u daŋ ɛɛ u bal la n kpekke. 11U daŋ kɔrguu mbusu lizibɔr la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere n see, Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ kizeehina la jaa kpa u chal mizi bar mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni. 12Nɛr la n na lizi mbusu la daŋ mɔnnuu di kpa u nyuu ni u nuuri jaa. Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ paagi a maa sag a niŋ ni mbusu lizibɔr la ni. 13Nɛr la n na lizi mbusu la, daŋ yagli u biini kuna ni u gballi, n kizeehiŋ la jaa kpa u maa fuuh, mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.
14Di u ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la n ɛɛ kunzaahri, guŋwaa, a dɛkkɔɔ u lizi koorikomma gɛɛ koŋaahmu. 15N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpau ba mbusu lizibɔr la, di wa lau u nyuu miŋŋi tɔri, di fuuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ka gil u chal toŋzi mbusu lizibɔr la kɛrii. 16U daŋ lizi u chigii la maa bir ha mbusu lizibɔr wiifurii la banna ta hɔɔhri la. 17Denii u jaa lau u keeri di tɛruu piili ka gilɛɛ waa tɔruu anɛɛ. Ka n kizeehiŋ la jaa fuuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni, u ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.”

english_text:
Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord
The Lord said:
1When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour, 2and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 3The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
4If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
5If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast. 6Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil. 7If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
8You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar. 9Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 10The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
11Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice. 12You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
13Salt is offered when you make an agreement with me, so sprinkle salt on these sacrifices.
14Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest. 15You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice. 16A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
translation_text:
Mbusu lizaa mia wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Di bɛl maa wa ba mbusu lizaa mia ni u wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, a daŋ ɛɛ sakɔla. U daŋ yiili ɔlivi nuu du a ni di kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma sag, 2di kpaa ga tɛɛ Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ n kizeehina la. N kizeehiŋ la daŋ muraa, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.
3A sau bɔr la n kawɛɛ daŋ jaa ɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala hor. Á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia bɔnaniinanii himmaanii, dikuu baŋ lizaa lii diwee la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛŋ la wia.
4Di bɛl maa wa kpa mbusu lizaa mia la baŋ ɔɔzɛɛ lugɔ paanuu n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ ba, a dɛkkɔɔ u ɛɛ paanuu tɔg baŋ kpa sakɔla ni ɔlivi nuu koozi dɔŋa ni, di kuari gɛɛ kɛrɛkɛssizi baŋ ɛɛ nuu waari a ni. 5Di mbusu lizaa mia ɛɛ paanuu la baŋ kpa maansa hɛna halli, a dɛkkɔɔ a ɛɛ sakɔla ni ɔlivi nuu n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ. 6I daŋ pussaa di fug nuu waari a ni, mbusu lizaa miarɛ guŋ. 7Di mbusu lizaa mia ɛɛ paanuu baŋ hallɛɛnɛ, a dɛkkɔ uŋ ɛɛ sakɔla ni ɔlivi nuu. 8Kpa mbusu hiŋ di tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la, waabuu niŋ kpaa la mbusu lizibɔr di ga tɛŋ. 9U daŋ lizi mbusu yeŋ á ɛɛ liize hor, di fuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni, a sɔɔh du sum tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 10Ka mbusu lizaa mia bɔr la n kawɛɛ la birgi Aarɔn ni u biibaala hotte. A ɛɛ mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa bɔnaniinanii himmaa la baŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii.
11Mbusu lizaa mia kuŋfuuhlii la maa hin niŋ kpa wa tɛŋ, gilɛɛ waa dua yiisi gɛɛ huuhnuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a waa dɛkkɛ hiŋ fuuh mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la maa n dɔɔ yiisi gɛɛ huuhnuu di ra tɛŋ. 12Kpa i lugli mia bina maa di wa lizi mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ka gilɛɛ waa fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni. 13Ɛɛ kpa yazi jaa mbusu lizaa mia kuna maa ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, yazi chigɔɔ tɛɛ n ni n nɛra nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la. A dɛkkɔɔ yazi ɔɔ du mbusu lizaa mia kuna maa ni.
14Di i wa kpa lugli mia í wa lizi mbusu n be, i daŋ hallaa di nyaaraa. 15Kpa nuu ni daahɛgsɔɔhsuma jaa a ni. Mbusu lizaa miarɛ guŋ. 16Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ fuuh a mihallaa ni nuu mbusu la á ɛɛ liize hor ani daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni tɛŋ.”

english_text:
Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing
The Lord said:
