1When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal. 2Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
3Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides, 4as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 5Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
6Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it. 7If you offer a sheep, you must present it to me at the entrance to the sacred tent. 8Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
9Offer the fat on the tail, the tailbone, and the insides, 10as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 11One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
12If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me 13at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
14Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides, 15as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 16One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me.
All fat belongs to me. 17So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
translation_text:
Dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Di nɛr maa wa lizi nabal gɛɛ naniina u nauna biini, ú lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ú lizi nau la n kpekke. 2A hiŋ daŋ kpa u nonee sag a sel nyuu ni mɔɔ ka kɔrguu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua. Denii Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ kizeehina la, kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni, 3a dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu sel bɔra naabuu bá lizi, á ɛɛ kuna la ban niŋ fuuh tɛŋ. U nuu la maa n tɔ u biini kuna ni, 4u siga ni a nuuri la maa n tɔ u fuuh ani u hiah bɔnanii. 5Denii Aarɔn biibaala kpa annii maa jaa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa la ni di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni a sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ.
6Di peezii gɛɛ buunnɛ u ŋɔ u kpa lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ ú ɛɛ u niina gɛɛ u bal la n kpekke, 7di peezii u kpa ba ú wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, 8u daŋ kpa u nonii sag u nyuu ni, ka kɔrguu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see. Denii Aarɔn biibaala kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr la keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni. 9U daŋ kpa a sel bɔra naa, u nuu, u dinzɛɛ ni de nuu la maa n dugli u fuuh hog, nuu la maa n tɔ u biini kuna ni, 10u siga ni a nuuri la maa ani u hiah bɔnanii la, di lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛŋ. 11N kizeehiŋ daŋ fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, á ɛɛ diwee mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.
12Di u mbusu sel la ɛɛ buunnɛ, ú kpau tɛŋ. 13U daŋ kpa u nonii sag a sel nyuu ni mɔɔ, ka kɔrguu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see. Denii Aarɔn biibaala kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr la keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni. 14U bɔra naabuu u lizi, á ɛɛ diwee mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛŋ, u nuu la maa n tɔ u biini kuna ni, 15u siga ni a nuuri la maa ani u hiah bɔnanii la. 16N kizeehiŋ daŋ fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, á ɛɛ diwee mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii sɔɔh n summɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. A nuu maa ɛɛ n hotte.
17A ɛɛ widaulii la n chɔɔwɛ saŋa maa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina naannaa keŋ. Di ii haŋ wa du bɔr maa, ka i ra kii sel nuu gɛɛ chal dii.”

english_text:
Sacrifices for Sin
(Leviticus 6.24-30)
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do.
When the High Priest Sins
The Lord said:
3When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it. 4The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there. 5He will take a bowl of the blood inside the tent, 6dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain. 7Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
8-10The priest will remove the fat from the bull, just as he does when he sacrifices a bull to ask my blessing. This includes the fat on the insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. He will then send it all up in smoke.
11-12The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap.
When the Whole Nation Sins
The Lord said:
13When the nation of Israel disobeys me without meaning to, the whole nation is still guilty. 14Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, 15where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
16The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent, 17dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain. 18Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent. 19-21After this, the priest will remove the fat from the bull and send it up in smoke on the altar. Finally, he will burn its remains outside the camp, just as he did with the other bull. By this sacrifice the sin of the whole nation will be forgiven.
When a Tribal Leader Sins
The Lord God said:
22Any tribal leader who disobeys me without knowing it is still guilty. 23As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it. 24This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar. 25The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 26Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven.
When Ordinary People Sin
The Lord said:
27 When any of you ordinary people disobey me without meaning to, you are still guilty. 28As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it. 29Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed. 30Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 31After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
32If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it. 33Lead the lamb to the altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed. 34The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 35After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_text:
Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Di unla maa waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ka ɛɛ wii la n waa deŋlee mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa biini, widaulaa naabuu ú hiŋzi.
3Di n Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, a buu a nɛra maa, a dɛkkɔ ú kpa nabalee la n kpekke tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ú ɛɛ bilchɔg mbusu, dikuu u wichɔgaa la wia. 4U daŋ kpa a nabalee ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, di kpa u nonii sag u nyuu ni, ka kɔrguu n see. 5Denii n Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la kpa a nabalee la chal yeŋ zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. 6U daŋ kpa u nonibii lii a chal di mizaa buniidaanɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia bɔnaniinanii patiisa la see. 7N kizeehiŋ daŋ jaa kpa a chal yeŋ fɔg nyigzi la n du daahɛgsɔɔhsuma mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ n see la, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Ka jaa fug a nabalee chal la n kawɛɛ la, dau mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la zɛɛ, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua la. 8U daŋ lizi a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa nau la nuu maa, anla maa n tɔ u biini kuna ni, 9u siga ni nuu la n tɔ a ni la, anla n du u fuuh ani u hiah bɔnanii la. Annii maanii ú lizi jaa u siga ni. 10N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa a nuu naa di fuuh mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni, gunla uŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa sel la. 11Ka u daŋ kpa a nau hɔŋ ni u ol maa di kpa u nyuu ni u naagballi ani u biini kuna maa, 12di kpa a maa lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia, bɔr la baŋ kuarɛɛ waa doŋŋe n be, ba ra ta hɔɔhri la, di chem niŋ fuuuh.
13Filaŋkennaa, di Izrɛl hina maa wa ɛɛ wii bɛl di chɔg mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa la bɛl maa, di ba waa kuttɛɛ gba, ka ba cholloo. 14Di ba wa zum wichɔgii la baŋ ɛɛwɛ la, guŋwaa, a dɛkkɔ a nɛra maa lizi nabalee, ú ɛɛ ba wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel di ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see. 15Denii a nɛra nabɔnzi kpa ba nonee sag a nabalee nyuu ni mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see mɔɔ, ka jaa kɔrguu de. 16N Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la daŋ kpa u chal yeŋ zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. 17U daŋ kpa ú nonibii lii a chal di mizi buniidaanɛɛ, a patiisa la see. 18U daŋ kpa a chal di faa mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ n see n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini la nyigzi ni, ka fug a chal la n kawɛɛ la maa dau mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la n chigɛ n Tanti Dia dominua la zɛɛ. 19U daŋ lizi u nuu maa u ni di fuuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni. 20Gunla himmaa uŋ haŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu nabalee la, gunnɛ ú ɛɛ a keŋ nabalee naa gba. Awia, n kizeehiŋ daŋ kpau lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛŋ, ń gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa. 21Denii u jaa kpa a nau lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di ga fuuuh gunla uŋ fuuh lugli hor la. A nɛra wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa la.
22Di ba nabɔma bɛl maa waa wa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di ɛɛ wii la n waa dɛkkɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, di lii n widaulaa la biini, ka u cholloo. 23Di u wichɔgaa la wa lii chaaŋ u zumaa, u daŋ lizi bubal la n kpekke. 24A hiŋ daŋ kpa ú nonii sag a bubal nyuu ni mɔɔ, ka kɔrguu bɔr la banna kpu mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa sela n see la. Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaarɛ la. 25Denii n kizeehiŋ kpa u nonibii lii a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel hiŋ chal yeŋ, di fɔg mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr nyigzi la, ka jaa keezi fug anla maa n kawɛɛ la ta u zɛɛ. 26U daŋ fuuh a nuu la maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni gunla uŋ fuuh dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu la. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a baal la n ɛɛ a wichɔgaa la, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi gil tɛu.
27Di unla maa waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ka ɛɛ wii la n waa dɛkkɛ, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa la biini, ka u cholloo. 28Di ba wa gillɔ u zum u wichɔgaa hiŋ wia, a dɛkkɔɔ u kpa buniina la n kpekke di wa lizi mbusu dikuu u wichɔgaa hiŋ wia. 29U daŋ kpa u nonii sag u wichɔgaa mbusu sel hiŋ nyuu ni mɔɔ, ka kɔrguu bɔr la banna kpu wichɔgaa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa sela la. 30Denii n kizeehiŋ kpa u nonibii lii u chal yeŋ di fɔg a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr nyigzi la, ka keezi fug anla n kawɛɛ la maa ta u zɛɛ. 31U daŋ lizi u nuu maa gunla baŋ ɔɔ lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa sel nuu la, n kizeehiŋ fuuah mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni, á sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a baal la n ɛɛ wichɔgaa la, ń gil tɛu.
32Di u wa ba pebii ni lugɔ u wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa selle, u daŋ ɛɛ ú lor la n kpekke. 33U daŋ kpa u nonii sag u ni mɔɔ, ka kɔrguu ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel, bɔr la banna kpu mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa la. 34Denii n kizeehiŋ kpa u nonibii lii u chal yeŋ di fɔg a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr nyigzi la, ka keezi fug anla n kawɛɛ la ta u zɛɛ. 35U daŋ lizi u nuu maa gunla baŋ ɔɔ lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa pebii nuu la, n kizeehiŋ kpaa di jaa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa la n chɔɔ mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni di fuuh a maa. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a baal, míŋ̀ Kɔraawiizi gil tɛu.’ ”

english_text:
The Lord said:
1If you refuse to testify in court about something you saw or know has happened, you have sinned and can be punished.
2You are guilty and unfit to worship me, if you accidentally touch the dead body of any kind of unclean animal.
3You are guilty if you find out that you have accidentally touched anything unclean that comes from a human body.
4You are guilty the moment you realize that you have made a hasty promise to do something good or bad.
5As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done. 6Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
7If you are poor and cannot afford to bring an animal, you may bring two doves or two pigeons. One of these will be a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, and the other will be a sacrifice to please me.
8Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head, 9splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar. 10Then he will follow the proper rules for offering the other bird as a sacrifice to please me.
You will be forgiven when the priest offers these sacrifices as the price for your sin.
11If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it. 12Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me. 13By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices.
Sacrifices To Make Things Right
(Leviticus 7.1-10)
14-15The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to:
If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests. 16In addition, you must pay what you owe plus a fine of 20 percent. Then the priest will offer the ram as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven.
17-19If you break any of my commands without meaning to, you are still guilty, and you can be punished. When you realize what you have done, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven.
translation_text:
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Di nɛr na wii gɛɛ di zum wii n ɛɛwɛ, ka vɛɛ ú di daansɛɛ seriya diiribɔr, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di dɛg dignitɛraa.
2Di nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi kunla maa n doŋŋe n be, alugɔ pir ni bol sesiwaa gɛɛ kuntuuzii, haali uŋ waa kuttɛɛ gba, ka u doŋŋoo n be.
3Gɛɛ di u gbɔgzi newee doŋa ka waa zummɛ, gɛɛ kunla n niŋ gil u doŋ, haali uŋ waa zummɛ gba, di u wa zumaa, u cholloo.
4Gɛɛ di nɛr waa nfɛrɛ fɛwɛɛ ka hɛɛhzi lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ winanaa gɛɛ wichɔgaa wiimaa biini, haali uŋ waa kuttɛɛ gba, ka di u wa zumaa, u cholloo.
5Di nɛr maa wa chollo lii annii bɛl maa biini, u daŋ sɛɛ a guŋ wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ la chɔgri n be, 6u wichɔgaa hiŋ kim daŋ ɛɛ pelor gɛɛ bulor di lii u sela biini, ú kpa wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. N kizeehiŋ jaa kpau lizi u wichɔgaa mbusu di sɛɛ chɔgri n be.
7Di wàá wer na pebii, u daŋ lizi koorikommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ wa tɛŋ, di turgi u wichɔgaa kim. Bɛl daŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor. 8U daŋ kpaa wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ, u feli kpa wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor la tɛŋ. U daŋ miŋŋi u baŋaa ku, ka gilɛɛ waa tɔri u nyuu, 9di kpa u chal yeŋ mizi mbusu lizibɔr la kɛrii, ka u chal la n kawɛɛ la, u daŋ kpaa chuuri mbusu lizibɔr la zɛɛ. Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaarɛ la. 10N kizeehiŋ daŋ kaa kpa unla, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor gunla baŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ la, di lizi u wichɔgaa mbusu tɛu, ú na giltɛɛi.
11Ka di waa koorikommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ la nawɛɛ, ú lizi sakɔla kookoo tassa suul wa tɛŋ, á ɛɛ u wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa. Ú gilɛɛ waa kpa nuu gɛɛ daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di ra sag a ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, á ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaarɛ. 12U daŋ kpaa wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ, ú muraa nonii suul, di kpaa sag mbusuzi lizaa kuna la n chɔɔ mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di fuuah tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, wichɔgaa mbusu lizaarɛ la. 13Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ, di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a baal, ú na giltɛɛi. A mbusu lizaa kuna la n kawɛɛ la daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ hor, gunla baŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia la.”
Bilchɔg mbusu lizaa wia
14Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 15“Di nɛr wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa la uŋ waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ, di suuh ú turgi kim la n ɛɛ kunnanaananaa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, u kim daŋ ɛɛ pebal la n kpekke, di lii u sela biini. U yoola hel gunla banna mɛgzi saliŋhuŋŋu kebisau n Tanti Dia biini la. Bilchɔg mbusu lizaarɛ la. 16A dɛkkɔɔ ú turgi a kim la maa uŋ waa wette turgi la, di kaa bɔnni a kim bɔra anue, di kpa bɔkpaŋ sag a ni, di kpaa ga tɛɛ a n kizeehiŋ, ú lizi u bilchɔg mbusu tɛu, u na giltɛɛi.
17Di nɛr maa waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa ka chɔg mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa, ka u cholloo, di dɛg a kim turgaa. 18U daŋ ba bilchɔg mbusu lizaa sel ni di wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la, ú ɛɛ pebal la n kpekke nɛnnɛ di lii u sela biini, u yoola mag n Tanti Dia biini yoola. N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpau lizi mbusu di sɛɛ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be tɛɛ a baal, dikuu u wichɔgaa la uŋ waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ la wia, ú na giltɛɛi. 19Bilchɔg mbusu lizaarɛ la. U faa cholloo dikuu uŋ ɛɛwɛ zuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ni wia.”

english_text:
Other Sins That Need Sacrifices or Payments
(Numbers 5.5-10)
1-3 The Lord told Moses what the people must do when they commit other sins against the Lord:
You have sinned if you rob or cheat someone, if you keep back money or valuables left in your care, or if you find something and claim not to have it.
4When this happens, you must return what doesn't belong to you 5and pay the owner a fine of 20 percent. 6-7In addition, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven for what you did wrong.
Daily Sacrifices
(Exodus 29.38-43; Numbers 28.1-8)
8-9The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord:
You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning. 10The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar. 11Change into your everyday clothes, take the ashes outside the camp, and pile them in the special place.
12The fire must never go out, so put wood on it each morning. After this, you are to lay an animal on the altar next to the fat that you sacrifice to ask my blessing. Then send it all up in smoke to me.
13The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out.
Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord
The Lord said:
14When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar, 15where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 16-17The rest of it is to be baked without yeast and eaten by the priests in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent. This bread is very holy, just like the sacrifices for sin or the sacrifices for making things right, and I have given this part to the priests from what is offered to me on the altar.
18Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change.
When Priests Are Ordained
19The Lord spoke to Moses 20and told him what sacrifices the priests must offer on the morning and evening of the day they are ordained:
It is the same as the regular morning and evening sacrifices—half a kilogram of flour 21mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 22-23Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten!
Sacrifices for Sin
(Leviticus 4.1,2)
24The Lord told Moses 25how the priests from Aaron's family were to offer the sacrifice for sin:
This sacrifice is very sacred, and the animal must be killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar. 26The priest who offers this sacrifice must eat it in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent, 27and anyone or anything that touches the meat will be holy. If any of the animal's blood is splattered on the clothes of the priest, they must be washed in a holy place. 28If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be destroyed, but if it was cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
29This sacrifice is very holy, and only the priests may have any part of it. 30None of the meat may be eaten from the sacrifices for sin that require blood to be brought into the sacred tent. These sacrifices must be completely burned.
translation_text:
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Di nɛr maa dar u dɔŋhiŋ dikuu kumbɛl uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛu u ra binni wia gɛɛ di ŋmɛɛu gɛɛ di finuu, u ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ zuu n ni. 3Di nɛr kugni kuŋ n leuwe ka kanni kara u wia gɛɛ di kanni kara di hɛɛhzi gɛɛ di ɛɛ guŋ dɔŋ wichɔgaa nɛra n niŋ wer ɛɛ, 4di u wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa chol, a dɛkkɔɔ u bir kunla uŋ ŋmɛɛwɛ gɛɛ di fini la ba gɛɛ kunla baŋ kpawɛɛ du u nonee biini gɛɛ kunla n leuwe u kugni la, 5gɛɛ wii la maa n ɛɛwɛ u kanni kara di hɛɛhzi dikuu u wia la. A dɛkkɔɔ u turgi a kim maa, di bir turgi, di kaa bɔnni a kim bɔra anue, di kpa bɔkpaŋ sag a ni, di tɛɛ a kuŋ hiŋ a hɔl la uŋ niŋ lizi u bilchɔg mbusu la. 6Aŋ ɛɛ kim la wia, firaarɛ lugɔ ú lizi pebal la n kpekke nɛnnɛ di lii u sela biini, u yoola hel gunla banna mɛgzi saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau n Tanti Dia biini la di wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ, ú kpa lizi u bilchɔg mbusu. 7Kenne n kizeehiŋ jaa kpaa di lizi u bilchɔg mbusu tɛɛ a baal n see, n gil tɛu dikuu wia la uŋ ɛɛwɛ chol la wia.”
Mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii wia
8Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 9“Kpa widaulaa naa tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biizi. Mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ŋmɛnizii keŋ, mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la daŋ ɔɔ sag mbusu lizibɔr la niŋ ni hamuŋa maa guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi. Niŋ la ge n du mbusu lizibɔr ni la, daŋ ɔɔ ra lawuu saŋa maa, di gilɛɛ waa dim ŋmɛnɛ maa. 10N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa u galiŋkpurii du, ka jaa kpa u tagtajaŋ huŋŋunanii la laali sag, di jaa paa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la n fuuhwe la hɔɔhri mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di dau mbusu lizibɔr kɛrii, 11ka wir a keŋ bɔmbɔga naa maa, ka kpa aŋhina laali, di paa a hɔɔhri lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia ga ha bɔr la n waa doŋŋe n be ba kuari la. 12Niŋ la n du mbusu lizibɔr ni la daŋ ɔɔ ra lawuu saŋa maa, di gilɛɛ waa dim ŋmɛnɛ maa. Chɔɔzi maa, n kizeehiŋ daŋ ɔɔ lizi daazi di jaa, di kuari mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii kuŋ la sag a niŋ ni di fuuh a dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu nuu la di jaa. 13A dɛkkɔɔ a niŋ ɔɔ ra lau saŋaa saŋa maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di gilɛɛ waa dim ŋmɛnɛ maa.”
Mbusu lizaa mia wia
14Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Mbusu lizaa mia ŋmɛnizii keŋ. Aarɔn biibaalaa niŋ ɔɔ kpa mbusu lizaa mia di ba n be, mbusu lizibɔr la see. 15N kizeehiŋ daŋ ɔɔ mur sakɔla la ni nuu di jaa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la maa n sag mbusu lizaa mia la ni, di fuuh liize mbusu lizaa hor la mbusu lizibɔr la ni, a sɔɔh du sum tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 16Ka Aarɔn ni u biibaala jaa kpa anla n kawɛɛ la, di gilɛɛ waa dua yiisi di dia bɔnaniinanii la biini, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la diŋŋee. 17Ba gilɛɛ waa kpa yiisi jaa a ni di ra ɔɔzi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii kpaa tɛɛ baa lugɔ ba hotte di lii mbusuzi lizaa kuna la baŋ ɔɔ lizi di ra fuuh di ra tɛŋ la biini. U ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ alugɔ wichɔgaa ni bilchɔg mbusuzi lizaa hora la. 18Saŋaa saŋa maa, Aarɔn dee biibaala maa daŋ wer dia. Ba hotte di lii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa la maa biini baŋ ɔɔ fuuh di ra tɛŋ la. Nɛr la maa gɛɛ kunla maa n niŋ gbɔgzi a mbusu lizaa mia naa, wia daŋ huuzuu.”
19Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 20“Mbusu naabuu Aarɔn ni u biibaala lizi wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, a hɔl la ban niŋ lizi bɛl maa n kizeehiŋ, di waari u nyuu nuu la. Kuna naabuu u lizi, sakɔla kookoo tassa suul á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia di ba waa lizi n kizeehiŋ maa. Ba ɔɔ kpa u keza chɔɔzi ni, di kaa kpa anla n kawɛɛ duana ni di lizi mbusu. 21Kpa nuu koozi a ni ka hallaa maansa hɛna biini, di pussaa di koozaa nɛnnɛ a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia, a sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ. 22U biibaal la maa n niŋ lɛɛ u bɔr di ɛɛ n Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma labuu niŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ. N hotte guŋ saŋaa saŋa maa, ba daŋ ɔɔ fuuh a maa nyaamm. 23N kizeehiŋ mbusu lizaa mia maa, fuuihre ba ɔɔ fuuah, ba gilɛɛ waa dia.”
Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa wia
24Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 25“Ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala be, ‘Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa ŋmɛnizii keŋ. Ba daŋ ɔɔ kpu wichɔgaa mbusu sel labuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, bɔr la baŋ ɔɔ kpu mbusu lizaa sel di fuuh la. A wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel, ɛɛ u naniinanii himmaanii. 26N kizeehiŋ la n lizi mbusu labuu niŋ diu, bɔnaniinanii la biini n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia diŋŋee la. 27Di nɛr la maa gɛɛ kunla maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi a ol, wia daŋ huuzuu, di u chal ge wa toŋzi u laala yemmaa ni, ú chaguu a bɔnaniinanii hiŋ biini. 28Vii la baŋ kpawɛɛ daali a ol, a dɛkkɔ ba purguu, ka di daansanii ba kpa daaluu, ba daŋ kuguu nɛnnɛ di yagluu ni nii. 29Biibambie la maa n lii n kizeehina dee biini ra diubuu, ú ɛɛ u naniinanii himmaanii. 30Ka di wichɔgaa mbusu sel chal la baŋ kpawɛɛ zuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini ba lizi wichɔgaa mbusu di sɛɛ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, a Bɔnaniinanii biini la, ba gilɛɛ waa dia, ka fuuah.’ ”

english_text:
Sacrifices To Make Things Right
(Leviticus 5.14-19)
The Lord said:
1The sacrifice to make things right is very sacred. 2The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar. 3Offer all of the animal's fat, including the fat on its tail and on its insides, 4as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 5One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me. 6This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
7The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
8In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal, 9just as he may eat the bread from a sacrifice to give thanks to me. 10All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family.
Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing
The Lord said:
11Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing: 12If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil. 13You must also make some bread with yeast. 14Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
15When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day. 16It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day, 17-18but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
19Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me. 20-21But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
22The Lord told Moses 23to say to the people:
Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats. 24If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it. 25If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 26 And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal, 27or you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
28The Lord also told Moses 29-30to say to the people of Israel:
If you want to offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, you must bring the part to be burned and lay it on the bronze altar. But you must first lift up the choice ribs with their fat to show that the offering is dedicated to me. 31A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests. 32-33The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal. 34I have decided that the people of Israel must always give the choice ribs and the upper joint of the right hind leg to Aaron's descendants 35who have been ordained as priests to serve me. 36This law will never change. I am the Lord!
37These are the ceremonies for sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessing or his forgiveness, as well as the ceremonies for those sacrifices that demand a payment and for the sacrifices that are offered when priests are ordained. 38While Moses and the people of Israel were in the desert at Mount Sinai, the Lord commanded them to start offering these sacrifices.
translation_text:
Bilchɔg mbusu lizaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Bilchɔg mbusu lizaa ŋmɛnizii keŋ, u ɛɛ u naniinanii himmaanii. 2Ba daŋ ɔɔ kpu a bilchɔg mbusu sel, bɔr la baŋ ɔɔ kpu mbusu lizaa sel di fuuh la, di kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr la keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni. 3U nuu maanii bá lizi tɛŋ, u dinzɛɛ nuu ani u nuu la n tɔ u biini kuna ni la, 4u siga anɛɛ la ni a nuuri la n tɔ a ni di dugli u fuuh la, ani u hiah bɔnanii la. 5N kizeehiŋ daŋ fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni tɛŋ, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii. Bilchɔg mbusu lizaarɛ la. 6Biibambie maa n lii n kizeehiŋ dee biini daŋ wer diu, ka a dɛkkɔɔ ba diu bɔnaniinanii la biini, u ɛɛ u naniinanii himmaanii.
7A keŋ widaulaa naa himmaanii ba ra hiŋ di ra lizi wichɔgaa ni bilchɔg mbusuzi. N kizeehiŋ la n lizi a wichɔgaa mbusu la horaa. 8N kizeehiŋ la maa haŋ wa lizi nɛr maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛu, daŋ wer kpa a sel hɔŋ. 9Mbusu lizaa mia la maa baŋ ɔɔzɛɛ gɛɛ di daali gɛɛ di halli ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la n niŋ kpaa tɛŋ la hotte, 10ani mbusu lizaa mia maa, di ba koozaabuu nuu gɛɛ a ɛɛ a hilaarɛ, a gba ɛɛ Aarɔn biibaala maa horaa, bá bɔnnaa mɛgzi.
Dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa wia
11Dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa la nɛr n niŋ lizi wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaarɛ keŋ. 12Di u lizuu lugɔ jaamaa mbusu, u daŋ kpa nuu di koozi paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ ni kɛrɛkɛssizi la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ ni di ɛɛ nuu waari a ni, di ŋmir boforoti sakɔla nɛnnɛ di dua nuu. 13Di kpa paanuu la baŋ du yiisi jaa u dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu ni di wa jaamiŋ. 14U daŋ lizi annii bɛl maa iri di wa lizi mbusu, ú ɛɛ u kɛɛi tɛŋ. U daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la n mizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi sela la chal hor. 15Ba daŋ hee u dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa ol la, a hɔl la maa baŋ lizuu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ la. Bá gilɛɛ wa gil u yemmaa ra chɔɔ hɔɔ ra pizi.
16Ka di u mbusu la ɛɛ nua lizaa gɛɛ u kipar mbusu lizaa, ba daŋ diu a hɔl la maa un lizuu la, ka keezi di u bɔr la n kawɛɛ, di hɔɔ wa pizɔɔ. 17A mbusu lizaa ol la maa n kawɛɛ, hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, bá kpa u maa fuuh. 18Awia, di dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa ol maa haŋ wa hel hɔpizaa ahoro ka nɛr maa heeu, màá lɛɛ u mbusu hiŋ, u daŋ ɛɛ kundoŋ. Nɛr la maa ge n niŋ heeu, wia daŋ huuzuu.
19Di a ol yemmaa wa gbɔgzi kunla maa n doŋŋe mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, ba gilɛɛ waa heeu, bá fuuuh. Ka nɛr la maa n waa doŋŋe n be, daŋ wer hee u bɔr la n kawɛɛ. 20Nɛr la maa n doŋŋe n be, ka di a dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa kuna la n ɛɛ n hor la, a dɛkkɔɔ ba duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. 21Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi kunla maa n doŋŋe n be, di u ɛɛ newee doŋaa gɛɛ sel doŋaa gɛɛ kundoŋ la maa miŋ kiiwee, ka hee dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa ol la n ɛɛ n hor la, ba duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.”
22Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 23“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be dí ba gilɛɛ waa hee nauna ni peeza gɛɛ buuna nuuri. 24Ba daŋ wer kpa sel la maa n siuwɛ gɛɛ pir sela n lauwɛ nuu di ɛɛ wiimaa, ka ba gilɛɛ waa hee a nuu. 25Nɛr la maa haŋ wa hee ol la baŋ kpawɛɛ lizi mbusu di fuuh ra tɛŋ la nuu, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. 26Bɔr la maa iin duwɛɛ, ií gilɛɛ waa hee sel maa gɛɛ kunzaahri maa chal. 27Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa hee chal, ba duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.”
Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ bɔdiilii wia
28Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 29“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, dí nɛr maa wa lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu, u yeŋ ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi hotte. 30U daŋ kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii du u himmaa nonee wa tɛŋ, a dɛkkɔ ú lizi u nuu ni u bampirii ba, di lalli u bampirii hiŋ chiŋ viigi n see, ú ɛɛ u mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii. 31N kizeehiŋ la daŋ fuuh u nuu la mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ka a bampirii la waa ɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala hotte. 32Ií dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa sela maa nodige hiiah ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ hotte. Ii kɛɛirɛ guŋ. 33Aarɔn biibaal la n kpa a dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa sel chal ni u nuu tɛŋ labuu dɔɔ u nodig hiih hiŋ. 34Di lii Izrɛl hina dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa biini, n kpa mbusu lizaa ol bampirii la baŋ lallɛɛ chiŋ di viigi ni u hiih la baŋ lizɛɛ labuu tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala, á ɛɛ ba bɔdiilaa saŋaa saŋa maa.”
35Anniibuu ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii bɔra la baŋ lizɛɛ tɛŋ. Aabuu ba lizi tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaalaa, a hɔl la baŋ lizi baa ba ra hum n kizeehina huma la. 36A hɔl la baŋ lizi baa di waari ba nyuuni nuu labuu n ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ ba ra lizi annii di ra tɛɛ ba ni ba naanna saŋaa saŋa maa.
37Anniibuu ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii, mia, wichɔgaa, bilchɔg, n kizeehina kpai ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa widaulaa, 38miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis, Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu, a hɔl la miŋ gillɛ Izrɛl hina lizi ba mbusuzi wa tɛŋ, Bizeŋ Sinaai Hɛribɔduma biini la.

english_text:
The Ceremony for Ordaining Priests
(Exodus 29.1-37)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Send for Aaron and his sons, as well as their priestly clothes, the oil for ordination, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and a basket of bread made without yeast. 3Then bring the whole community of Israel together at the entrance to the sacred tent.
4Moses obeyed the Lord, and when everyone had come together, 5he said, “We are here to follow the Lord's instructions.”
6After Moses told Aaron and his sons to step forward, he told them to wash themselves. 7He put the priestly shirt and robe on Aaron and wrapped the sash around his waist. Then he put the sacred vest on Aaron and fastened it with the finely woven belt. 8Next, he put on Aaron the sacred breastpiece that was used in finding out what the Lord wanted his people to do. 9He placed the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban was the narrow strip of thin gold as a sign of his dedication to the Lord.
10Moses then dedicated the sacred tent and everything in it to the Lord by sprinkling them with some of the oil for ordination. 11He sprinkled the bronze altar seven times, and he sprinkled its equipment, as well as the large bronze bowl and its base. 12He also poured some of the oil on Aaron's head to dedicate him to the Lord. 13Next, Moses dressed Aaron's sons in their shirts, then tied sashes around them and put special caps on them, just as the Lord had commanded.
14Moses led out the bull that was to be sacrificed for sin, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head. 15After it was killed, Moses dipped a finger in the blood and smeared some of it on each of the four corners of the bronze altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the altar. This purified the altar and made it a fit place for offering the sacrifice for sin. 16Moses then took the fat on the bull's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and sent them up in smoke on the altar fire. 17Finally, he took the skin and the flesh of the bull, together with the food still in its stomach, and burned them outside the camp, just as the Lord had commanded.
18Moses led out the ram for the sacrifice to please the Lord. After Aaron and his sons had laid their hands on its head, 19Moses killed the ram and splattered its blood against the four sides of the altar. 20-21Moses had the animal cut up, and he washed its insides and hind legs. Then he laid the head, the fat, and the rest of the ram on the altar and sent them up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. All this was done just as the Lord had commanded.
22Moses led out the ram for the ceremony of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head, 23and it was killed. Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot. 24Moses did the same thing for Aaron's sons, before splattering the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar. 25He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg. 26Then he took from a basket some of each of the three kinds of bread that had been made without yeast and had been dedicated to the Lord.
27Moses placed the bread on top of the meat and gave it all to Aaron and his sons, who lifted it up to show that it was dedicated to the Lord. 28After this, Moses placed it on the fires of the altar and sent it up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. This was part of the ordination ceremony. 29Moses lifted up the choice ribs of the ram to show that they were dedicated to the Lord. This was the part that the Lord had said Moses could have.
30Finally, Moses sprinkled the priestly clothes of Aaron and his sons with some of the oil for ordination and with some of the blood from the altar. So Aaron and his sons, together with their priestly clothes, were dedicated to the Lord.
31Moses said to Aaron and his sons:
The Lord told me that you must boil this meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it there with the bread. 32Burn what is left over 33and stay near the entrance to the sacred tent until the ordination ceremony ends seven days from now. 34We have obeyed the Lord in everything that has been done today, so that your sins may be forgiven. 35The Lord has told me that you must stay near the entrance to the tent for seven days and nights, or else you will die.
36Aaron and his sons obeyed everything that the Lord had told Moses they must do.
translation_text:
Aarɔn ni u biibaala Kɔraawiizi kizee kpai wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Kpogli Aarɔn ni u biibaala, di kpa ba bɔmbɔga, nuuwaarii la, wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa nabal ni pebala anɛɛ ani paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ kɛɛgɔ suul di ba, 3di chaali a nɛra maa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.” 4Moosis ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la, a nɛra maa jaa chaali Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.
5Moosis ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Wii naa miŋ ŋɔ n ɛɛ naa, waabuu Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ń ɛɛ.” 6Denii Moosis lau Aarɔn ni u biibaala lii ba see, di sɔ baa nii. 7Di kpa tagtajaŋ ni tagtajiga laali Aarɔn, di kpa kirsɔɔ kirsuu. Di kaa kpa tagtakpurii laaluu, ka lau u kirsɔɔ la baŋ suahwɛ nɛnnɛ, di kirsi u chara. 8Di kpa pɛɛnnanii bɛl di vɔɔ sag u bampirii, di kpa Urim ni Tumim du a bampirii pɛɛŋ hiŋ biini. 9Denii u vɔɔu namu, ka kpa saliŋ pɛrɛtunanii la di mari u see, di ra bagli lugɔ u ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hotte, gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la.
10Denii Moosis kpa nuuwaarii mizi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni kuna la maa n du u biini, di ra bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi horaa. 11Di ɛɛ a nuu yeŋ mizi mbusu lizibɔr ni u kuna maa, a tassazeŋ ni u zɛɛ hɔŋribɔr buniidaanɛɛ, di ra bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi horaa. 12Di yiili a nuu yeŋ waari Aarɔn nyuu di lizi u doŋa, ú ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛnaniinanii. 13Denii u lau Aarɔn biibaala ba see, di kpa tagtajaŋra laali baa, ka kpa kirsɔɔzi kirsi baa, di kpa kahurozi hi baa, gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.
14Denii u jaa lizi wichɔgaa mbusu nabal la, Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni. 15Moosis kɔrgi a nabal di kpa u chal di kpa u nonibii lii a yeŋ di faa mbusu lizibɔr la nyigzi maa ni di bagli lugɔ u ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hotte. Ka jaa fug a chal bɔr la n kawɛɛ dau mbusu lizibɔr hiŋ zɛɛ. Guŋ bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kunnaniinaniirɛ, di lizi wichɔgaa maa u ni. 16Moosis lizi a nabal biini kuna nuu maa ani u hiah bɔnanii di jaa u siga ni a nuuri maa ni, di kpaa fuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni. 17Ka kpa a nabal hɔŋ ni u ol ani u biini kuna maa ge lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di ga fuuh gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.
18Denii u jaa lau pebal la n ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sel la baŋ ɔɔ fuuh la, Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni 19Moosis kɔrgi a pebal di kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi la maa. 20U mɔnni a pebal jigzijigzi di kpa u nyuu ni a ol maa ani u nuu fuuh. 21Di kaa kpa u biini kuna ni u gballi di yaglaa di fuuh a pebal maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ, di ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, gunla uŋ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.
22Di kaa lizi a pebal la n kawɛɛ la, unla n ɛɛ u kizee kpai hor, Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni. 23Moosis kɔrgi a pebal di kpa u chal yeŋ fɔg Aarɔn nodig dignipaŋhoo ni u nodig nonibibal ani u nodig naanibibal. 24Moosis kaa lau Aarɔn biibaala ba see di kpa a chal yeŋ di fɔg ba nodige dignipaŋhoori ni ba nodige nonibibala ani ba nodige naanibibala. Denii u jaa kpa a chal di mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi la maa. 25Di kpa u nuu ni u dinzɛɛ nuu ni u nuu la maa n tɔ u biini kuna ni, ni u hiah bɔnanii ni u siga ni a nuu ani u nodig hiih. 26Lizi paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ lii kɛɛgɔ la biini baŋ du paanuuzi wa tɛŋ la, ani paanuukpaŋ baŋ kpa nuu kuari ni kɛrɛkɛsi kpaŋ, di kpaa sag peezi la nuu ni u nodig hiih ni. 27Denii u kpaa du Aarɔn ni u biibaala nonee, ba lallaa chiŋ di viigi, Kɔraawiizi see, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa. 28Denii Moosis lɛɛa ba be di jaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la n sag mbusu lizibɔr la ni di fuuah, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, kizee kpai mbusu lizaarɛ guŋ. 29Denii u kaa kpa u bampirii la n ɛɛ u diiribɔr la, di lalluu chiŋ viigi Kɔraawiizi see, gunla uŋ ŋɔ u ɛɛ la. 30Moosis kaa kpa nuuwaarii la yeŋ ani a chal yeŋ lii mbusu lizibɔr la, di mizi Aarɔn ni u biizi ni ba bɔmbɔga, ba ni ba bɔmbɔga maa ɛɛ kunnanaananaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.
31Denii Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala be, “Ií daali a ol Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua di hee u ni paanuu la n lii Kɔraawiizi kizee kpai mbusuzi lizaa kɛɛgɔ la biini, gunla Kɔraawiizi n baglɛɛ di ra ŋɔ, ‘Aarɔn ni u biibaala niŋ dia.’ 32Ií fuuh anla maa n kawɛɛ. 33Ií du Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua guŋŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ di ii waa chaaŋ liwɛɛ di ga hel a hɔl la ii Kɔraawiizi kizee kpai hɔpizaa maga n niŋ su. 34Wii la maa n ɛɛwɛ zinaa naa, Kɔraawiizii bagli guŋ, á ɛɛ u baaŋ lizaa ii ni. 35Ií daŋ du a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, wibaŋzi ni hamuŋzi di ɛɛ gunla maa miŋ baglɛɛ la, ka gilɛɛ waa siu. Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ ń ɛɛ guŋ.” 36Aarɔn ni u biibaala ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be ŋɔ bá ɛɛ la.

english_text:
The First Sacrifices Offered by Aaron and His Sons
1Eight days later Moses called together Aaron, his sons, and Israel's leaders. 2Then he said to Aaron:
Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
3Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them. 4Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
5After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord, 6Moses said:
The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory. 7 Aaron, step up to the altar and offer the sacrifice to please the Lord, then offer the sacrifices for the forgiveness of your sins and for the sins of the people, just as the Lord has commanded.
8Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins. 9His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot. 10But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. 11Then Aaron burned the skin and the flesh outside the camp.
12After Aaron had killed the ram that was sacrificed to please the Lord, Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against all four sides of the altar. 13They brought him each piece of the animal, including the head, and he burned them all on the altar. 14He washed the insides and the hind legs and also sent them up in smoke.
15Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins. 16And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way. 17He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
18 Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar. 19His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver 20on top of the choice ribs. 21Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
22 Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices. 23He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory. 24The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina huma faaraa wia
1A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ hɔl, Moosis yir Aarɔn ni u biibaala ani Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi. 2Denii u ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Lizi nabalee, ú ɛɛ ii wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel, di lizi pebal ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii, á du kpeg nɛnnɛ, di kpaa ba wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 3Kaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Ií lizi bubal ú ɛɛ ii wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, ni nabalee ani pebii, á maa di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ. Á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa. 4Di kaa lizi nabal ani pebal, a ɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa sela di wa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di kpa nuu koozi mbusu lizaa mia ni di jaa. Ií ɛɛ guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, zinaa Kɔraawiizi daŋ ba ii be.’ ”
5Ba kpa kuna la Moosis n baglɛɛ la ba Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see, a nɛra maa ba, di wa chi de ba jaami Kɔraawiizi. 6Denii Moosis ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi bagli lugɔ ii ɛɛ, guŋ gil u girme ba ii be.”
7Moosis kaa ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Tuzi ba mbusu lizibɔr la di wa kpa ii wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa ni ii mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la, di lizi i ni i nɛra maa wichɔgaa mbusu. Kpa unla n ɛɛ a nɛra hor la lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ baa, gunla Kɔraawiizi n baglɛɛ la.”
8Awia, Aarɔn ba mbusu lizibɔr di wa kɔrgi u himmaa wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa nabalee la. 9U biibaala kpa a chal wa tɛu, u kpa u nonibii liia di fɔg mbusu lizibɔr la nyigzi, ka fug a chal bɔr la n kawɛɛ dau mbusu lizibɔr hiŋ zɛɛ. 10Di kpa wichɔgaa mbusu sel la nuu, u siga ani u hiah bɔnanii, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagli Moosis la. 11Ka u ol ni u hɔŋ waa, ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgiarɛ u fuuah.
12Denii u kɔrgi mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la. U biibaala kpa a chal tɛu u mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni. 13Ba paagi ol la kpaŋkpaŋa di ra tɛu, di kpa u nyuu jaa, u fuuh a maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni. 14Ka jaa yagli u biini kuna ni u naagballi di kpaa sag anla ni mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di fuuah.
15A har, Aarɔn kpa a nɛra ge mbusu lizaa sel la ba. Di lau ba buuŋ la n ɛɛ ba wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel la, di kɔrguu, di lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu gunla uŋ felee ɛɛ unla.
16U kaa kpa mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la ge di lizi mbusu gunla banna ɛɛa la. 17Di kaa kpa mbusu lizaa mia la ge ba, di ɛɛa nokool suul, di jaa chɔɔzin mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la ni, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni.
18Di kɔrgi a nabal ni a pebal, a ɛɛ a nɛra dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu sela. U biibaala kpa a chal tɛu, u kpaa mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni. 19Ka u jaa kpa a nabal ni a pebal nuuri bɔra la waa, 20di sag a bampiree ni, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni. 21Denii Aarɔn lalli a bampiree ni u nodige hiiah la chiŋ di viigi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa, gunla Moosis n baglɛɛ la.
22Aarɔn lalli u nonee chaŋ a nɛra di kissi baa. Uŋ wa lizi a mbusuzi maa tuŋ, u jaa lii mbusu lizibɔr tuu.
23Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn jaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Baŋ wa liiwɛ, ba kissi a nɛra, Kɔraawiizi girme ba ba be. 24Kakpaŋ, niŋ lii Kɔraawiizi be di wa fuuh mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la maa ni a nuuri bɔra la, n sag mbusu lizibɔr la ni la. Nɛra la maa n wa na guŋ, ba chaasi ni bɔsɔna di chogli hɛri di pi.

english_text:
Nadab and Abihu
1Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to. 2Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death. 3Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said:
“I demand respect
from my priests,
and I will be praised
by everyone!”
Aaron was speechless.
4Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.” 5So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
6Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire. 7But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die.
Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
8The Lord said to Aaron:
9When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change. 10You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean. 11You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
12 Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar. 13The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place. 14-15 But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
16When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said, 17 “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt. 18Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
19Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
20Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_text:
Nadab ni Abihu siu wia
1Aarɔn biibaala Nadab ni Abihu kpa ba nimbuurikuna di buu niŋ, di kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di du a niŋ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di zuu u ni, dikuu uŋ waa ŋɔ bá ɛɛ guŋ wia. 2Awia, Kɔraawiizi gil niŋ lii chiŋ wa fuuh baa, ba siuzi u see. 3Moosis jaa ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
‘N daŋ gil banla maa n na ba n be,
zum lugɔ n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ.
N daŋ kpa n girme
bagli n nɛra.
A dɛkkɔɔ ba ra tɔgziŋ.’ ”
Ka Aarɔn siigi.
4Moosis yir Aarɔn naara biibaala Misɛl ni Ɛlzafan, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ba ɛŋ, di wa chi ii lulla naa n siuwɛ naa, lii Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la see, di la a nɛra chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia.” 5Awia, ba ba wa chi baa di ba haa laali ba tagtajaŋra la, di lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia gunla Moosis n baglɛɛ la. 6Denii Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala Ɛliaza ni Itama be, “Ií chaazi ii nyuuni di gilɛɛ waa piili ii laala, di guŋ lɛi, ii daŋ siuzi, ka Kɔraawiizi baaŋ kaa fuuh a nɛra maa ni. Ka ii diahina ni Izrɛl hina maa jaa ra wii banla Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ niŋ wa fuuh la lee. 7Ií gilɛɛ waa lii Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, di guŋ lɛi, ii daŋ siuzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waari iabuu Kɔraawiizi nuu.” Awia, ba ɛɛ gunla Moosis n baglɛɛ la.
8Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Aarɔn be, 9“I ni i biizi gilɛɛ waa nyɔɔ siŋ gɛɛ siŋkpega maa, di ii waa zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia naa biini, di guŋ lɛi, ii daŋ siuzi. Kennaa chɔɔwɔɔ di hanna la di tɛɛ i ni i naanna maa. 10A dɛkkɔɔ ii wer zum kuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora ani anla n ɛɛ nɛra maa hora, ni anla n doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be ani anla n waa doŋŋe u be. 11A ɛɛ firaarɛ lugɔ ií bagli Izrɛl hina widaulaa la maa miŋ tɛɛ baa di lii Moosis be la.”
12Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala Ɛliaza ni Itama la n kawɛɛ la be, “Ií kpa mbusu lizaa mia la baŋ wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi aŋhina ka la di ɔɔzi paanuu la baŋ wàá yiisi duwɛɛ la, di dia mbusu lizibɔr la kɛrii, dikuu aŋ ɛɛ a nanaananaa himmaa wia. 13Ií dia bɔnaniinanii la biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ni ii biibaala maa diiribɔttɛ de, di lii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la baŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la. Gunnɛ u ŋɔ n ɛɛ. 14Ií ni ii biibambizi ni biihambizi maa daŋ wer di a bampirii la baŋ lallɛɛ chiŋ di viigi ani hiih la baŋ lizɛɛ la. Ií dia bɔr la n waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be. Ba kpaabuu tɛɛ ii ni ii biizi, á ɛɛ ii diiribɔra di lii Izrɛl hina dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa biini. 15Hiih la baŋ lizɛɛ ni bampirii la baŋ ɔɔ lalli chiŋ di viigi la, a dɛkkɔɔ bá kpa nuuri bɔra la baŋ ɔɔ kpa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la ba, di wa lallaa chiŋ viigi Kɔraawiizi see, mbusu lizaa kuŋviigiire guŋ. Waabuu niŋ ɛɛ ii ni ii biizi bɔdiilii saŋa maa gunla Kɔraawiizi n baglɛɛ la.”
16Denii Moosis n wa pɛɛzi wichɔgaa mbusu buuŋ la wia, di wa na lugɔ ba fuuuhbuu, u baaŋ fuuh Ɛliaza ni Itama, Aarɔn biibaala la n kawɛɛ la ni, u ŋɔ, 17“Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii waa wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa kuna la diwee, bɔnaniinanii la biinei? A ɛɛ naniinanii himmaanii. Kɔraawiizi kpaubuu tɛɛ ia ii kpa ra lizi a nɛra wichɔgaa mbusu u see, ú gil di ra tɛɛ baa. 18Iiŋ waa u chal kpawɛɛ zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la biini wia, a dɛkkɔɔ ii faa di a mbusu lizaa kuna la de, gunla miŋ baglɛɛ la.”
19Aarɔn bir ŋɔ Moosis be, “A daŋ faa par Kɔraawiizi di n faa di a wichɔgaa mbusu naa zinaa? Zinaabuu ba lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu, di lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ka keŋ wikuna haa vɛɛ ba n be.” 20Moosis n wa nuu guŋ, a paruu.

english_text:
Clean and Unclean Animals
(Deuteronomy 14.3-21)
1 The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
You may eat 3any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud. 4-8But you must not eat animals such as camels, rock badgers, and rabbits that chew the cud but don't have divided hoofs. And you must not eat pigs—they have divided hoofs, but don't chew the cud. All of these animals are unclean, and you are forbidden even to touch their dead bodies.
9-12You may eat anything that lives in water and has fins and scales. But it would be disgusting for you to eat anything else that lives in water, and you must not even touch their dead bodies.
13-19Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
20-23The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
24-28Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
29-30Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean. 31Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening. 32If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening. 33If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean. 34If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
35If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed. 36A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean. 37If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean. 38But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
39If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening. 40If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
41-42Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground. 43If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are. 44 I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures. 45I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
46-47I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
translation_text:
Sela la n dɛg dii ni anla n waa dii dɛkkɛ wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, 2“Ií ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, dí sela la maa n du hɛri naa biini, anniibuu dɛg dii. 3Ií daŋ wer di sel la maa n dɔɔ naafiraa la n bargɛɛ nɛnnɛ, ka u ug di ra hee.
4Aŋhina du denii a naafiraa bargi, aŋhina ge ug di ra hee, ka ii gilɛɛ waa dia. Haali nyugma n ukke di ra hee gba, ka u naafiraa waa bargɛɛ. U ɛɛ kundonne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, waa dɛg ii dii. 5Haali aahri n ɔɔ ug di ra hee gba, ka u naafiraa waa bargɛɛ, u ɛɛ kundonne ii be, waa dɛg ii dii. 6Haali chooma gba n ukke di ra hee la, ka u naafiraa waa bargɛɛ, kundonne ii be, 7pereku gba naafiraa n bargɛɛ ka waa ukke di ra hee la wia, u ɛɛ kundonne ii be, waa dɛg ii dii. 8Ií gilɛɛ waa di a bɛl maa ol gɛɛ di wàá gbɔgzi u siwii, a doŋŋoo tɛɛ ia.
9Kunnyinee la maa n du nii biini di dɔɔ sɔɔhri ni hɛga waa, ii daŋ wer dia. 10Ka anla maa n du nii biini, a waa sɔɔhri ni hɛga dɔɔwɛ la, ii ra kia. 11Iin ninna kia la wia, ií ra kii a siwaa gba gbɔgzaa. 12Kunla maa n waa sɔɔhri ni hɛga dɔɔwɛ ka du nii biini, ií ra kiiu.
13Zumbizi naabuu ií ra kii di gilɛɛ ra dia, dikuubɛɛwiai, a doŋŋoo, aabuu, chig, duu iri maa, 14kɔlaahmu, kɔlbiŋŋu iri maa, 15dugli iri maa, 16kikiu ge iri maa, niilaaraa, kezaa iri maa, 17kikiujiga, niilaaraazeŋ, kikiuzeŋ 18kikiu iri maa, hɛribɔduma kikiu, duu, 19namɛŋŋu ge iri maa, lalaakpakpa ani ziŋ.
20Ií ra kii kunzaahrijigzi maa. 21Ka anla n dɔɔ naazi anaazu di dɔɔ kpuŋe, di wer ra jɔzi la, ii daŋ wer dia. 22Annii naa biini, ii daŋ wer di di lotoro waa iri maa, ni pom waa iri maa ani huuh ge iri maa. 23Ka anla maa n dɔɔ keeri di dɔɔ naazi anaazu, ií ra kia.
24Annii daŋ wer gil ii doŋ. Nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi a siwaa, u daŋ doŋ di ra ba duana. 25Nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi a siwaa, a dɛkkɔɔ u chag u laala ka u daŋ doŋ di ra ba duana.
26Sela la maa naazi n bargɛɛ ka a waa bargɛɛ nɛnnɛ la, gɛɛ a waa ukke di ra hee gba, a doŋŋoo. Nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi a siwaa, daŋ doŋ. 27Sela la maa n na vol naazi anaazu, ni anla n dɔɔ naanibifiiri doŋŋoo. Nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi a siwaa daŋ doŋ, di ra ba duana. 28Nɛr la maa n wa gbɔgzi a siwaa daŋ chag u laala ka doŋ di ra ba duana. A doŋŋoo tɛɛ ia.
29Sela naa iri doŋŋoo, ií ra kia. Aabuu, kacha, maree ani ger iri maa, 30jaza, bajagu, ger, saliŋgbalee ani kaliŋgboŋa. 31Anniibuu ií ra kii, di nɛr maa wa gbɔgzi a siwaa, u doŋŋoo di ra ba duana. 32Di bɛl maa wa siuwɔ chol kummaa ni, huma la maa baŋ kpau di ra hum, di daarɛ, hɔnnɛ, wɛjɛɛ gɛɛ gbɔglɔnnɛ, ka u doŋŋoo di tɛɛ ia. Ií kpau du nii biini, u daŋ doŋ di ra ba duana, ka jaa du wer. 33Di bɛl maa wa chol vii biini, a vii ni kuna la maa n du u biini doŋŋoo, a dɛkkɔɔ ií purguu. 34Diwii la maa iin niŋ di, di u dɔɔ nii u ni di lii a keŋ vii biini, u doŋŋoo. Kunnyɔɔlii la maa iin niŋ nyɔɔ lii u biini doŋŋoo. 35Di kunsiwii wa chol kummaa ni, u doŋŋoo, di dalaarɛ gɛɛ viire, ií purguu. 36Bule gɛɛ kɔlɔŋ waa maa nii waa doŋŋe, ka di nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi kunsiwaa naa bɛl maa doŋŋoo. 37Di kunsiwii wa gbɔgzi kundee la maa ban niŋ duu, a waa doŋŋe. 38Di ii ɛɛ nii siŋ kundee ka annii bɛl maa u siwii chol a ni, a doŋŋoo.
39Sel la maa iiŋ waa kii, di u siuwɔ ka nɛr maa gbɔgzuu, u doŋŋoo di ra ba duana. 40Nɛr la maa wa diu daŋ chag u kuna, ka doŋ di ra ba duana. Nɛr la maa wa kpa u siwii daŋ chag u kuna ka doŋ di ra ba duana.
41Kuna la maa n na tuuzi ani kunjigzi la maa n na vol hɛri, ii gilɛɛ waa di a bɛl maa. 42Ií gilɛɛ waa di kuntuuzii maa, di u ra tuuzi u hia ninɛɛ gɛɛ di u ra vol naazi anaazu ninɛɛ gɛɛ naakpila ninɛɛ u ra vol, ií ra kia. 43Ií gilɛɛ waa di annii bɛl maa, di wàá doŋ iihinaa n be. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpaa di ra doŋ iihinaa. 44Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum. Ií lizi ii doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa kuna la maa n na tuuzi hɛri di doŋ iihinaa. 45Minuu Kɔraawiizi la n lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri, ii ɛɛ nɛra la n na humiŋ. Awia, ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ.
46Sela, zumbizi, kunnyinee la maa n du nii biini ani anla maa n na vol hɛri, gbɔgnii keŋ. 47A dɛkkɔɔ ii ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di ra bargi anla n doŋŋe, di ra lii anla n waa doŋŋe ni, di kaa ra bargi sela la iin ninna di ani anla iiŋ wàá ra di.”

english_text:
What Women Must Do after Giving Birth
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period. 3 Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day, 4but her loss of blood keeps her from being completely clean for another 33 days. During this time she must not touch anything holy or go to the place of worship. 5Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another 66 days.
6When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin. 7After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl. 8 If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_text:
Hahsɔɔŋ doŋa lizaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ di haaŋ wa kpogli hia di wa lul biibaal, u daŋ doŋ n be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, gunla uŋ ɔɔ doŋ u baagu maa doŋa ɛɛi biini la. 3A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl, bá teŋ a bie hɛŋ. 4Ka a haaŋ haa kpaŋ guŋŋ hɔpizaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni ahoro hɔl, bá lizi u doŋa lii u doŋa ɛɛi biini. Ú gilɛɛ waa gbɔgzi kunla maa n ɛɛ kunnaniinanii di gilɛɛ wàá la n Tanti Dia la, di u doŋa lizaa saŋa la waa tunnɛ. 5Di biihaannɛ u lul, a haaŋ daŋ doŋ yauzi anɛɛ, gunla uŋ ɔɔ doŋ u baagu maa doŋa ɛɛi biini la. Denii u kaa kpaŋ guŋŋ hɔpizaa tokkoahoro ni anumbɛl mɔɔ, ka bá lizi u doŋa lii u doŋa ɛɛi biini.
6Di a biibaal gɛɛ di a biihaaŋ doŋa lizaa hɔpizaa wa bɛrɔɔ, a haaŋ daŋ lizi pepɔl la n di biŋkpaŋ, di wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, ú lizi mbusu di fuuuh. A haaŋ daŋ kpa koorikomma gɛɛ koŋaahmu jaa, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor. 7N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpaa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a haaŋ. Denii ú doŋa jaa tuŋ n be.
Anniibuu ɛɛ haaŋ lulaa widaulaa, di u wa lul biibaal gɛɛ biihaaŋ. 8Ka di wàá wer na pepɔl, u daŋ lizi koorikommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ, bɛl ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ di lizi u wichɔgaa ha, ú doŋa jaa tuŋ.”

english_text:
Skin Diseases
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
2If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests. 3If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
4But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 5If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 6Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
7However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest. 8If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
9Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest. 10If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white, 11he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.” 12-13But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.” 14-15If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
16-17However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
18-19If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest. 20If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 21But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
22If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.” 23But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
24If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white, 25a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.” 26But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 27On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 28However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
29If you have a sore on your head or chin, 30it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 31On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 32By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep, 33you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 34By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
35-36Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.” 37But if he thinks you are completely well, he will say, “You are clean.”
38If white spots break out on your skin, 39but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
40-41If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean. 42-43But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say, 44“This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
45If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!” 46As long as you have the disease, you are unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
47-50If a greenish or reddish spot appears anywhere on any of your clothing or on anything made of leather, you must let the priest examine the clothing or the leather. He will put it aside for seven days, 51and if the mildew has spread in that time, he will say, “This is unclean 52because the mildew has spread.” Then he will burn the clothing or the piece of leather.
53If the priest discovers that the mildew hasn't spread, 54he will tell you to wash the clothing or leather and put it aside for another seven days, 55after which he will examine it again. If the spot hasn't spread, but is still greenish or reddish, the clothing or leather is unclean and must be burned. 56But if the spot has faded after being washed, he will tear away the spot. 57Later, if the spot reappears elsewhere on the clothing or the leather, you must burn it. 58Even if the spot completely disappears after being washed, it must be washed again before it is clean.
59These are the rules for deciding if clothing is clean or unclean after a spot appears on it.
translation_text:
Bɔchɔgaa Gbɔgni wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, 2“Di nɛr maa bɔra wa dɔɔ ŋmɛra gɛɛ kunsɔna gɛɛ kisafa a ra buu, ba kpogluu ba Aarɔn la n ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ gɛɛ u biibaal bɛl maa be. 3N kizeehiŋ daŋ binni u ŋmɛr la na nɛnnɛ, di huna la n du a ŋmɛr biini la wa huuhzɔɔ, ka a ŋmɛr ge du luŋ di ɛɛ chofoo, u ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋ wiilbuuliire. Di n kizeehiŋ wa binnuu na nɛnnɛ tuŋ, u daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ a hiŋ doŋŋoo n be. 4Di a bɔr huuhzɔɔrɛ ka waa chofoo duwɛɛ, de ge huna waa bittɛ huuhzi, n kizeehiŋ daŋ gil a guŋ hiŋ ga du u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 5A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, n kizeehiŋ la kaa binnuu na, di u wa nawɔɔ lugɔ a ŋmɛr waa chɛttɛ, waa kaa lii u bɔra yemmaa, ka u haa gil ú gaa zuu u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ kaa. 6Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ híŋ, n kizeehiŋ kaa la ga binnuu na, di a ŋmɛr jaa waa hil, waa kaa lii u bɔra yemmaa ge, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ waa kaa doŋ, kisafa bɛnnɛ. A baal daŋ chag u laala, wàá ka doŋ n be. 7Di a kisafa kaa wa lii u bɔra maa, a dɛkkɔɔ u kaa kpa u hiŋ ga bagli n kizeehiŋ la. 8U daŋ kaa binnuu na, di a kisafa wa lii u bɔra maa, u daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo, u ɛɛ wiilbuuliire.
9Di nɛr la maa wa dɔɔ bɔchɔgaa la n na buu, bá kpogluu ba n kizeehiŋ la be. 10U daŋ binnuu nɛnnɛ, di u bɔra yemmaa wa ɔttɔ di huuhzi de huna ge bir huuhzi di du nii, 11u birgi zallaarɛ, u daŋ ŋɔ ú doŋŋoo, wiilbuuliire. U gilɛɛ waa gil ú gaa zuu u bɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u teŋ doŋŋoo. 12Di a wiila wa lii u bɔrahɔŋ maa, di lii u nyuu di ga tuu u naazi, 13n kizeehiŋ daŋ binnuu na nɛnnɛ, di a wiila wa lii u bɔra maa, u daŋ ŋɔ a hiŋ waa doŋŋe. Dikuu a maa n bittɛ huuhzi wia, waa doŋŋe. 14Ka ŋmɛnɛ maa di ŋmɛr wa du u ni, u doŋŋoo. 15Di n kizeehiŋ wa na a ŋmɛr, u daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo. A ŋmɛr doŋŋoo, u dɔɔ wiilbuuliire. 16Di a ŋmɛr wa hillɔ di bir huuhzi, ú la ga nau. 17Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ binnuu na, di u wa nawɔɔ lugɔ a ŋmɛr wa hillɔɔ di huuhzi, u daŋ ŋɔ a wiila hiŋ waa doŋŋe, denii u jaa ŋɔ u doŋa tunnɔɔ.
18Di nɛbɛl wa dɔɔ ŋmɛrbinaa, u wa tuŋ, 19di bɔhɔglii maa kaa wa lii bɔr la a ŋmɛrbinaa n faa duwɛɛ la di huuhzi gɛɛ di aah tama, ú kpa u hiŋ di ga bagli n kizeehiŋ. 20U daŋ binni de nɛnnɛ di na, di de du chofoo ka de huna bir huuhzi, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo. U ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋ wiilbuuliire di pozi lii bɔr la a ŋmɛrbinaa la n faa ɔttɛ la. 21Ka di n kizeehiŋ la wa binnuu nɛnnɛ di na lugɔ a de huna waa huuhzɛɛ waa kaa du chofoo, ka ra hil, guŋwaa, u daŋ gil ú gaa zuu u bɛŋ guŋŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 22Di u waa lii u bɔrahɔŋ maa, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo, wiilbuuliire. 23Ka di a bɔr waa chɛttɛ, waa kaa lii u yemmaa, guŋwaa, a ŋmɛrbinaa la pɛllɛ, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ waa doŋŋe.
24Di kuŋwema gɛɛ niŋ wa baari nɛr maa, de aah gɛɛ di huuhzi, 25n kizeehiŋ daŋ binni a bɔr nɛnnɛ, di a de huna wa bittɔ huuhzi a ŋmɛr ge du chofoo, u ɛɛ wiilbuulii la n pozee lii a bɔr la kuna n baareere. U daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ a hiŋ doŋŋoo. U ɛɛ wiilbuuliire. 26Ka di u wa binni de di na di de huna waa huuhzɛɛ, waa kaa du chofoo ka ra hil, guŋwaa, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ ú gaa zuu u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 27Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ binnuu na nɛnnɛ, di u wàá lii u bɔra maa, u ɛɛ wiilbuuliire, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo. 28Aŋhinabe di a bɔr waa chɛttɛ, waa kaa lii u bɔra yemmaa, ka hil, u ɛɛ kuŋwema gɛɛ niŋ baaraa ɔraarɛ, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ waa doŋŋe. U ɛɛ pɛl bɛnnɛ di lii a kuŋwema gɛɛ niŋ baaraa la biini.
29Di baal gɛɛ haaŋ wa dɔɔ ŋmɛr u nyuu gɛɛ u hama ni, 30n kizeehiŋ la daŋ binni a ŋmɛr na nɛnnɛ, di u wa du chofoo, de huna aah lugɔ susau ka du ginini, u daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ u doŋŋoo, u ɛɛ wiilbuuliire. 31Ka di u wa binni a ŋmɛr na, di waa chofoo duwɛɛ, di huŋbiŋŋe waa u biini duwɛɛ, guŋwaa, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ gil a hindee ga du u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 32Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, u daŋ binni a ŋmɛr, di a ŋmɛr waa u bɔra maa liwɛɛ, huŋaahma lugɔ susau waa u biini liwɛɛ, waa kaa du chofoo ge, 33a dɛkkɔɔ bá fuŋ a hiŋ ka ka a bɔr bɛŋ, n kizeehiŋ la gil ú bir gaa zuu u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 34N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kaa binni a ŋmɛr na hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, di waa u bɔra maa liwɛɛ, waa kaa du chofoo ge, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ waa doŋŋe. A wiila hiŋ daŋ chag u laala, denii u doŋa tuŋ. 35Ka di a ŋmɛr kaa wa lii u bɔra maa baŋ ŋɔ waa doŋŋe la har, 36n kizeehiŋ la daŋ binnuu di na, di a ŋmɛr wa lii u bɔra maa, ú gilɛɛ kaa wàá nyiŋŋi huŋsusau, a hiŋ doŋŋoo. 37Ka di u wa binnɔɔ di na lugɔ a ŋmɛr waa chɛttɛ, huŋbiŋŋe lii de, a de tunnɔɔ, waa doŋŋe. N kizeehiŋ daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ waa doŋŋe.
38Di baal gɛɛ haaŋ bɔra wa dɔɔ bɔhuŋŋa parapara, 39n kizeehiŋ daŋ binni baa di na, di a wa du fululu, a waa wiilchɔgii la n lii u bɔrahɔŋ ni ɛɛwɛ, a hiŋ waa doŋŋe.
40Di nɛr nyuu wa gbawɔɔ, waa doŋŋe. 41Di u hile magaa wa gbawɛɛ, waa doŋŋe. 42Ka di u dɔɔ ŋmɛr u aah ka huuhzi u nyugbaalii gɛɛ u hile ni, u ɛɛ wiilbuuliire. 43N kizeehiŋ daŋ binnuu nɛnnɛ, di a ŋmɛr ɔttɔɔ di du u nyuu gɛɛ u hile ni di aah ka huuhzi, di ɛɛ lugɔ wiilbuulii, 44a baal dɔɔ wiilaa, di doŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be. N kizeehiŋ daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ u doŋŋoo dikuu u nyuu ŋmɛr hiŋ wia.
45Nɛr la n dɔɔ a keŋ wiilbuulii daŋ laali kuŋkɔssi, di gilɛɛ waa chaazi u nyuu, ka kpa kuŋ fɔɔ u nua barii, ka ra wii di ra ŋɔ, ‘N doŋŋoo! N doŋŋoo!’ 46Saŋa la un niŋ dɔɔ a wiila di birgi mag, u doŋŋoo. A dɛkkɔɔ ú lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di ga du u bɛŋ.
Kuŋ n huh kɔɔla Gbɔgni wia
47Laala gɛɛ wɛjɛ maa baŋ kpa peezi huna gɛɛ gessihuŋŋunanaa suah, haŋ wa huh kɔɔla, 48kunla maa baŋ kpa peezi huna gɛɛ gessihuŋŋunanaa, suah gɛɛ di nyɛr gɛɛ hɔŋ gɛɛ kunla maa baŋ kpa hɔŋ kuari, 49di a kɔɔla wa du laala gɛɛ wɛjɛ maa ni gɛɛ hɔŋ gɛɛ pɛɛŋ la baŋ kpa gessihuŋŋunanii suah gɛɛ kunla maa baŋ kpa hɔŋ kuari, u biri lugɔ paŋhoo lɛɛ gɛɛ di aah, u ɛɛ kunla n huh kɔɔlaa di ra buu. A dɛkkɔɔ baŋ kpau ga bagli n kizeehiŋ. 50U daŋ binni a kɔɔla na nɛnnɛ, ka lizi a kuŋ dau u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 51A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, u daŋ kaa binnuu na nɛnnɛ, di a kɔɔla wa yaari u maa ni, u doŋŋoo. 52A dɛkkɔɔ u fuuuh, dikuubɛɛwiai, a kɔɔla ra yaaruu.
53Ka di n kizeehiŋ wa binnuu na di a kɔɔla waa u ni yaarɛɛ, 54u daŋ tɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ bá chag a kundee ka kaa gil bá kpau dau u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 55Di ba wa chag a kunla n faa huh a kɔɔla la tuŋ, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ binnuu na nɛnnɛ, di a kɔɔla waa chɛttɛ, haali aŋ waa wette yaari la gba, ka u doŋŋoo. U fuuuh, di a kɔɔla lau u keŋkere bɛl maa gba. 56Ka di ba wa chaguu, n kizeehiŋ la wa binnuu na di a kɔɔla waa liwɛɛ nɛnnɛ, ú lau de piili ha. 57Ka di a kaa kuari wa lii a kundee ni, a ra yaaruu, ú hiŋ fuuuh. 58Di u wa chag a laala gɛɛ a pɛɛndee gɛɛ a hɔŋ kuŋ a kɔɔla lii, ú kaa kuari chaguu, u jaa du wer.”
59Pɛɛŋ la maa baŋ kpa peezi huna gɛɛ gessihuŋŋunanaa suah, gɛɛ kunla maa baŋ kpa hɔŋ di kuari, di bɛl maa haŋ wa huh kɔɔla, a widaulaarɛ guŋ, bá ŋɔ lugɔ waa doŋŋe gɛɛ u doŋŋoo.

english_text:
The Ceremony for People Healed of Leprosy
1The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
2-3 After you think you are healed of leprosy, you must ask for a priest to come outside the camp and examine you. And if you are well, 4he will order someone to bring out two live birds that are acceptable for sacrifice, together with a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant. 5The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water. 6Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird. 7Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.
