8After this you must wash your clothes, shave your entire body, and take a bath before you are completely clean. You may move back into camp, but you must not enter your tent for seven days. 9Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
10On the eighth day you must bring to the priest two rams and a year-old female lamb that have nothing wrong with them; also bring 300 milliliters of olive oil and 3 kilograms of your finest flour mixed with oil. 11Then the priest will present you and your offerings to me at the entrance to my sacred tent. 12There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me. 13This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
14The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot. 15He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 16dip a finger of his right hand into the oil, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 17Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, 18-20and he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head. Then he will offer the other two animals—one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice. After this you will be completely clean.
21If you are poor and cannot afford to offer this much, you may offer a ram as a sacrifice to make things right, together with 300 milliliters of olive oil and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil as a grain sacrifice. The priest will then lift these up to dedicate them to me. 22Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. 23The priest will offer these to me in front of the sacred tent on the eighth day.
24-25The priest will kill this ram for the sacrifice to make things right, and he will lift it up with the olive oil in dedication to me. Then he will smear some of the blood on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
26The priest will pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 27then dip a finger of his right hand in the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 28He will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, just as he did with the blood of the sacrifice to make things right. 29-31And he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head.
Then, depending on what you can afford, he will offer either the doves or the pigeons together with the grain sacrifice. One of the birds is the sacrifice for sin, and the other is the sacrifice to please me. After this you will be completely clean.
32These are the things you must do if you have leprosy and cannot afford the usual sacrifices to make you clean.
When There Is Mildew in a House
33The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
34After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes. 35First, you must say to a priest, “I think there is mildew on the wall of my house.”
36The priest will reply, “Empty the house before I inspect it, or else everything in it will be unclean.”
37If the priest discovers greenish or reddish spots that go deeper than the surface of the walls, 38he will have the house closed for seven days. 39Then he will return and check to see if the mildew has spread. 40-41If so, he will order someone to scrape the plaster from the walls, remove the stones covered with mildew, then haul everything off and dump it in an unclean place outside the town. 42Afterwards the wall must be repaired with new stones and fresh plaster.
43If the mildew appears a second time, 44the priest will come and say, “This house is unclean. It's covered with mildew that can't be removed.” 45Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town. 46Meanwhile, if any of you entered the house while it was closed, you will be unclean until evening. 47And if you either slept or ate in the house, you must wash your clothes.
48On the other hand, if the priest discovers that mildew hasn't reappeared after the house was newly plastered, he will say, “This house is clean—the mildew has gone.” 49Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house. 50He will kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water 51-52and let its blood drain into the pot. Then he will dip the cedar, the hyssop, the yarn, and the other bird into the mixture of blood and water. Next, he will sprinkle the house seven times with the mixture, then the house will be completely clean. 53Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away, ending the ceremony for purifying the house.
54-57These are the things you must do if you discover that you are unclean because of an itch or a sore, or that your clothing or house is unclean because of mildew.
translation_text:
Bɔrahɔŋ wiilbuulaa doŋa lizaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Widaulaa la nɛr n niŋ hiŋ di bɔrahɔŋ wiila wa lawuu, ba kpau ba n kizeehiŋ be, u lizi u doŋa hau keŋ. 3N kizeehiŋ daŋ lii a nɛra chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di ga binnuu na nɛnnɛ, di u nyaagɔɔ, 4n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ bá lizi zumbizi anɛɛ la n waa doŋŋe ni hɛriŋkpol daa, gessiaahmu ani hisɔp daa di ba wa tɛɛ nɛr la ban niŋ sɔ la. 5Denii n kizeehiŋ la gil ba kpa a zumbee la bɛl di guali niinanii la n du vii biini la ni di kpu. 6U daŋ kpa zumbee la n kawɛɛ la, di kpa hɛriŋkpol daa ni hisɔp daa ani gessiaahmu la di jaa. Di kpa a maa kpau lii a zumbee la baŋ felee kpu la chal, 7di kpaa mizi nɛr la n nyaagɛɛ lii a bɔrahɔŋ wiila la biini buniidaanɛɛ, ka ŋɔ di waa kaa doŋ. Denii ú kpa a zumbinyinii la ha, ú zaah kaali.
8Nɛr la banna sɔ la daŋ chag u laala, di fuŋ u huna maa ha ka sɔ nii, denii u doŋa jaa lii. Di annii wa tunnɔ, u daŋ jaa wer zuu ba chɔɔribɔr la biini, ka u daŋ du u tanti dia baŋgia hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 9Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl, a dɛkkɔɔ á wiila hiŋ fuŋ u huna maa, u nyuu, u taŋhuna, u sikoŋa ani u huna la maa n kawɛɛ. U daŋ chag u laala di sɔ nii, ú doŋa jaa lii.
10A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl, a dɛkkɔɔ ú lizi peballi anɛɛ ani pelor la n di biŋkpaŋ, bɛl maa du kpeg. U daŋ nyiŋŋi sakɔla kookoo tassazi ahoro suul, di kpa ɔlivi nuu koozi a ni, di kaa kpa nuu pirintua keza jaa. A ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia. 11N kizeehiŋ la n siiwe lugɔ a hiŋ waa kaa doŋ labuu niŋ kpa a hiŋ ni u mbusu lizaa kuna la maa di wa tɛŋ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.
12Denii n kizeehiŋ kpa a pebalee la bɛl di lizi bilchɔg mbusu, di kpa nuu pirintua keza la jaa. U daŋ lallaa chiŋ di viigi n see, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa. 13U daŋ kpu a pebalee bɔnaniinanii la biini, bɔr la baŋ ɔɔ ra kpu wichɔgaa ni mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la. Gunla wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel la n ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ hor la, gunnɛ a bilchɔg mbusu lizaa sel gba ɛɛ u hor, waabuu ɛɛ u bɔnaniinanii himmaa. 14N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa a bilchɔg mbusu lizaa sel chal la yeŋ di faa nɛr la baŋ sɔwɛɛ la nodig dignipaŋhoo, u nodig nonibibal ani u nodig naanibibal. 15N kizeehiŋ daŋ jaa kpa ɔlivi nuu la yeŋ, di yiili du u himmaa nomɛɛl nopaal biini, 16di kpa u nodig nonibii di lii a nuu di mizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see buniidaanɛɛ. 17U daŋ kaa kpa a nuu bɔr la n kawɛɛ u nopaal biini la, di faa nɛr la ban niŋ sɔ la nodig dignipaŋhoo, u nodig nonibibal ani u nodig naanibibal di sag bilchɔg mbusu lizaa sel la chal ni. 18Ka a nuu la bɔr la n ka u nopaal biini la, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpaa di faa a nɛr la ban niŋ sɔ la nyuu di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih u ni.
19Denii n kizeehiŋ la lizi wichɔgaa mbusu di sɛɛ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, di tɛɛ nɛr la ban niŋ sɔ di lizi u doŋa ha la. A harbɔɔ, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpu mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii hiŋ, 20di kpa mbusu lizaa mia la di jaa u ni di sag mbusu lizibɔr la ni di sɛɛ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be tɛu, u doŋa jaa lii.
21Ka di u ɛɛ nyaari, wàá wer na annii, u daŋ kpa pebalee, ú ɛɛ bilchɔg mbusu, ba viiguu di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih u ni. U daŋ kpa sakɔla kookoo tassa suul, baŋ kpa ɔlivi nuu buu, nuu pirintuani anɛɛ di jaa, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia. 22U daŋ kaa lizi koorikommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ, bɛl ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa kuŋ, bɛl ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor.
23A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ hɔl, ú kpaa ba n kizeehiŋ be, ú sɔ u doŋa ha mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua n see. 24N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa bilchɔg mbusu lizaa pebalee la ni ɔlivi nuu pirintuani anɛɛ la, di lallaa chiŋ n see, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa. 25U daŋ kpu bilchɔg mbusu lizaa pebalee la, ú ɛɛ chɔgri sɛɛi mbusu lizaa sel n be, di ɛɛ u chal yeŋ faa nɛr la ban niŋ sɔ la nodig dignipaŋhoo, u nodig nonibibal ani u nodig naanibibal. 26N kizeehiŋ daŋ yiili nuu la yeŋ du u himmaa nomɛɛl nopaal biini, 27di kpa u nodig nonibii lii a nuu, di mizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see buniidaanɛɛ. 28Di kaa kpa a nuu la n du u nopaal biini la yeŋ di faa a hiŋ bɔra la himmaa uŋ kpa a bilchɔg mbusu sel chal faa la, u nodig dignipaŋhoo, u nodig nonibibal ani u nodig naanibibal ni. 29A nuu la n ka u nopaal biini la, n kizeehiŋ daŋ kpaa faa nɛr la baŋ ŋɔ bá sɔ la nyuu, di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih u ni. 30Denii ú jaa kpa a koorikommazi gɛɛ a koŋaahma la, anla a hiŋ n niŋ wer na la di lizi mbusu, 31bɛl ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor, di kpa mbusu lizaa mia la di jaa. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ, di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih nɛr la ban niŋ sɔ la ni.”
32Nɛr la maa n wa dɔɔ bɔrahɔŋ wiilbuulaa, ka wàá wer na kuna la ban niŋ kpa di sɔu widaulaarɛ guŋ.
Kɔɔla doŋa lizaa wia
33Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, 34“Di ii wa zuu Keenan hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia la, di kpa kɔɔla n na buu di du dia maa biini, 35a diahiŋ daŋ la ga ŋɔ n kizeehiŋ be, ‘N na kumbɛl lugɔ kɔɔla n dia.’ 36Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ gil bá bali a dia kummaa lii mɔɔ, ka ú zuu ga binni a kɔɔla, ba gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ lugɔ a dia kumbɛl doŋŋoo. A keŋ harbɔɔrɛ n kizeehiŋ la jaa zuu di binni a dia. 37U daŋ binni a dia koŋlaa kɔɔla hiŋ, di du jimejime lugɔ paŋhoolɛɛ gɛɛ di aah ka zuu biini di kaali a koŋlaa kɛraa, 38n kizeehiŋ lii a dia ka lawuu kar hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 39A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, n kizeehiŋ la bir ba di wa binni a dia na, di a kɔɔla wa lii a koŋlaa ni, 40ú gil bá lau bia la maa a kɔɔla n tɔ a ni la, ligzi, di paagaa lii a bolzeŋ kɛrii di ga ha bɔr la n doŋŋe. 41U daŋ gil bá haahzi a dia biini koŋlaa maa, dí kpa kuna la maa baŋ haahzɛɛ la lii a bolzeŋ kɛrii di ga ha bɔr la n doŋŋe. 42Denii ba jaa kpa bifalaa di kaa du anla bɔra, di kaa kpa vɔlfalaa saazi a koŋlaa.
43Di ba haŋ wa du bifalaa a koŋlaa ni, di bir kpa vɔlfalaa saazi, ka kɔɔla kaa bir wa lii a dia, 44N kizeehiŋ daŋ la ga pessi a dia nɛnnɛ, di a kɔɔla wa lii a dia maa, a ɛɛ kɔɔlchɔgaarɛ, a dia doŋŋoo. 45Bá purguu di paa u bia, u daazi ani u vɔlii maa lii a bolzeŋ kɛrii di ga ha bɔr la n doŋŋe.
46Nɛr la maa haŋ wa zuu a dia di ba haa tɔu, a hiŋ daŋ doŋ di ra ba duana. 47Nɛr la maa haŋ chɔɔ a dia gɛɛ di di diwee u biini, a dɛkkɔɔ ú chag u laala.
48Ka di ba wa saazi a dia vɔlii tuŋ, n kizeehiŋ ba wa binnuu na nɛnnɛ, di a kɔɔla waa yaarɛɛ, u daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ waa doŋŋe, dikuubɛɛwiai, a kɔɔla tunnɔɔ. 49Di u ŋɔ ú kuari a dia, ú nyiŋŋi zumbizi anɛɛ, hɛriŋkpol daa, ŋmɛŋaahmu ani hisɔp daa. 50U daŋ kpa a zumbee bɛl guali niinanii baŋ dɔɔwɛ wa du vii biini ni, ka kpuu. 51Denii u jaa kpa a hɛriŋkpol daa, hisɔp daa la, ŋmɛŋaahmu ani zumbee la n kawɛɛ la, di lii unla baŋ kɔrgɛɛ la chal n du niinanii la biini, di kpa mizi a dia buniidaanɛɛ. 52U daŋ kpa a zumbee chal ni niinanii la, zumbinyinii la n kawɛɛ la, hɛriŋkpol daa la, hisɔp daa la ani a ŋmɛŋaahmu la, di kuari a dia. 53Denii u jaa kpa a zumbinyinii la lii a bolzeŋ kɛrii bɔchaaŋ di kpau ha ú zaah kaali. Kenne ú ɛɛ di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih a dia ni, u doŋa jaa tuŋ.”
54Widaulaa la n chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ wiilbuulaa ni saŋgbana, 55kɔɔla n du laala gɛɛ dia ni, 56ŋmɛra, ŋmɛrbinni, kisafa ani bɔhɔglii, 57bá zum lugɔ kuŋ doŋŋo gɛɛ waa doŋŋee guŋ.
Widaulaa la n chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ bɔchɔgaa ni kɔɔlaa guŋ.

english_text:
Sexual Uncleanness
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
Any man with an infected penis is unclean, 3whether it is stopped up or keeps dripping. 4Anything that he rests on or sits on is also unclean, 5-7and if you touch either these or him, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
8If you are spit on by the man, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 9-10Any saddle or seat on which the man sits is unclean. And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 11If the man touches you without first washing his hands, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 12Any clay pot that he touches must be destroyed, and any wooden bowl that he touches must be washed.
13Seven days after the man gets well, he will be considered clean, if he washes his clothes and takes a bath in spring water. 14On the eighth day he must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 15The priest will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, then I will consider the man completely clean.
16Any man who has a flow of semen must take a bath, but he still remains unclean until evening. 17If the semen touches anything made of cloth or leather, these must be washed, but they still remain unclean until evening. 18After having sex, both the man and the woman must take a bath, but they still remain unclean until evening.
19When a woman has her monthly period, she remains unclean for seven days, and if you touch her, you must take a bath, but you remain unclean until evening. 20-23Anything that she rests on or sits on is also unclean, and if you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 24Any man who has sex with her during this time becomes unclean for seven days, and anything he rests on is also unclean.
25Any woman who has a flow of blood outside her regular monthly period is unclean until it stops, just as she is during her monthly period. 26Anything that she rests on or sits on during this time is also unclean, just as it would be during her period. 27If you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
28Seven days after the woman gets well, she will be considered clean. 29On the eighth day, she must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 30He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me; then I will consider the woman completely clean.
31When any of you are unclean, you must stay away from the rest of the community of Israel. Otherwise, my sacred tent will become unclean, and the whole nation will die.
32-33These are the things you men must do if you become unclean because of an infected penis or if you have a flow of semen. And these are the things you women must do when you become unclean either because of your monthly period or an unusual flow of blood. This is also what you men must do if you have sex with a woman who is unclean.
translation_text:
Nii la n niŋ lii nɛr bɔrahɔŋ di gil u doŋ wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Di baal maa hɛŋ waa lul, a hindee doŋŋoo dikuu guŋ wia. 3Di a hanna liiu, a waa teŋ gɛɛ di a teŋŋo gba, ka u doŋŋoo. 4Kunchɔɔrikuŋ la maa ni a baal n niŋ chɔɔ, birgi kundonne. Kunla maa ge un niŋ so u ni, birgi kundonne. 5Nɛr la maa haŋ gbɔgzi u kunchɔɔrikuŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ á hindee chag u laala dí sɔ nii, ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana. 6Nɛr la maa haŋ wa so kunla maa ni a baal n soge u ni la, a dɛkkɔɔ á hindee chag u laala dí sɔ nii, ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana.
7Nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi a baal, a dɛkkɔɔ á hindee chag u laala dí sɔ nii, ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana.
8Di nɛr la hɛŋ n na lul la wa pu nuuhaari du nɛr maa ni, a dɛkkɔɔ á hindee chag u laala dí sɔ nii, ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana.
9Di u wa tinni kawee di so kummaa ni, a kundee doŋŋoo, 10di nɛr maa ge wa gbɔgzi kunla maa uŋ soge u ni, a hindee daŋ doŋ di ra ba duana. Nɛr la maa ge wa paagi a kuna daŋ chag u laala di sɔ nii ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana.
11Di nɛr la hɛŋ n na lul la wa gbɔgzi nɛr maa, di waa felee sam u nonee, a dɛkkɔɔ a hindee chag u laala di sɔ nii ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana.
12Di a baal wa gbɔgzi vii maa, bá purguu gɛɛ kunla maa baŋ kpa daa kuari, a dɛkkɔɔ bá looruu.
13Di baal la hɛŋ n na lul la wa nyaagɔɔ, u daŋ di hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ ka chag u laala, di sɔ niinanii, ka u doŋa haa tuŋ Kɔraawiizi be. 14A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl, a dɛkkɔɔ ú nyiŋŋi koorikommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ dí kpaa ba n see n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, dí wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ. 15Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ kpaa lizi mbusu, bɛl ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor. Kenne ú ɛɛ di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih baa la hɛŋ n na lul la ni.
16Di baal maa banni wa liwɔɔ, a dɛkkɔɔ ú sɔ nii, ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana. 17Di laala maa gɛɛ hɔŋ maa, a banni n gbɔgzɛɛ, a dɛkkɔɔ bá chagaa ka a daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana. 18Di baal ni haaŋ wa chɔɔwɔ, u banni lii, a dɛkkɔɔ bá maa sɔ nii ka ba daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana.
19Di haaŋ waa ɛɛ u baagu doŋa, u daŋ doŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, di nɛr maa wa gbɔgzuu a hiŋ ge daŋ doŋ di ra ba duana.
20Kunla maa ni un niŋ chɔɔ gɛɛ di so u ni u doŋa ɛɛi hiŋ saŋa daŋ ɛɛ kundoŋ. 21Nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi u kunchɔɔrikuŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ ú chag u laala di sɔ nii, ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana. 22Nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi kunla maa ni uŋ soge, a dɛkkɔɔ ú chag u laala dí sɔ nii, ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana. 23Di u kunchɔɔrikuŋ gɛɛ kunla maa ni uŋ faa ra so ninɛɛ, di nɛr maa wa gbɔgzuu, a hiŋ daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana.
24Di baal nuu chɔɔwɔ u doŋa hiŋ gbɔgzuu, a baal daŋ doŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, di a baal chɔɔ kunchɔɔrikuŋ maa ni, a kunchɔɔrikuŋ doŋŋoo.
25Di haaŋ waa ɛɛ hahwia hɔpizikpila, ka a waa u baagu doŋa ɛɛwɛ gɛɛ a hɔpizaa bɛri u baagu doŋa ɛɛi hɔpizaa, u daŋ doŋ hɔpizaa la maga a doŋa n birgee mag la. 26Kunchɔɔrikuŋ la maa ni unna chɔɔ, ka a doŋa ra lii, daŋ doŋ alugɔ u kunchɔɔrikuŋ u baagu doŋ ɛɛi saŋa, ani kunla maa ni uŋ soge daŋ doŋ alugɔ u baagu doŋ ɛɛi saŋa. 27Nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi a keŋ kuna naa daŋ doŋ. A dɛkkɔɔ u chag u laala di sɔ nii, ka u daŋ haa doŋ di ra ba duana.
28Di u doŋa wa tunnɔ, u daŋ kur hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, di a guŋ wa hello, waa kaa doŋ Kɔraawiizi be. 29A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl, a dɛkkɔɔ ú nyiŋŋi koorikommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ di wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua. 30N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpaa lizi mbusu, bɛl ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor. Kenne ú ɛɛ di lizi a haaŋ doŋa tɛu, Kɔraawiizi see.
31Ií gil Izrɛl hina ni kuna la n doŋŋe bargi dɔŋa ni, bá gilɛɛ waa siu ni doŋa di wàá doŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la n du ii be la.’ ”
32Widaulaa la n chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ baal la hɛŋ n na lul gɛɛ banni n liwɛɛ, 33gɛɛ haaŋ la maa ge n na ɛɛ u hahwia, baal gɛɛ haaŋ la maa hɛŋ gɛɛ maŋ n na lul ani baal la maa ni haaŋ la maa n doŋŋe ka kpau chɔɔ.

english_text:
The Great Day of Forgiveness
1-2 Two of Aaron's sons had already lost their lives for disobeying the Lord, so the Lord told Moses to say to Aaron:
I, the Lord, appear in a cloud over the place of mercy on the sacred chest, which is behind the inside curtain of the sacred tent. And I warn you not to go there except at the proper time. Otherwise, you will die!
3 Before entering this most holy place, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for your sins and a ram as a sacrifice to please me. 4You will take a bath and put on the sacred linen clothes, including the underwear, the robe, the sash, and the turban. 5Then the community of Israel will bring you a ram and two goats, both of them males. The goats are to be used as sacrifices for sin, and the ram is to be used as a sacrifice to please me.
6Aaron, you must offer the bull as a sacrifice of forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 7Then you will lead the two goats into my presence at the front of the sacred tent, 8where I will show you which goat will be sacrificed to me and which one will be sent into the desert to the demon Azazel. 9After you offer the first goat as a sacrifice for sin, 10the other one must be presented to me alive, before you send it into the desert to take away the sins of the people.
11You must offer the bull as a sacrifice to ask forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 12Then you will take a fire pan of live coals from the bronze altar, together with two handfuls of finely ground incense, into the most holy place. 13There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there! 14Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
15 Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 16By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people. 17Only you are allowed in the sacred tent from the time you enter until the time you come out. 18After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat. 19Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
20After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent. 21 There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins. 22Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
23-24 Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people. 25The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
26The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp. 27 The remains of the bull and the goat whose blood was taken into the most holy place must be taken outside the camp and burned. 28And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp.
The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
29 On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work. 30This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence, 31and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath. 32The high priest must offer the sacrifices for cleansing from sin, while wearing the sacred linen clothes. 33He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community. 34You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel.
Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Baaŋfuuih Lizaa Hɔpizizeŋ wia
1Aarɔn biibaala banɛɛ la n faa ra lizi mbusu Kɔraawiizi see di siuzi la har, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ wiarɛ tɛɛ Moosis, 2“Ŋɔ i kpɛɛma Aarɔn be lugɔ ú ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa zuu Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la n du patiisazeŋ la harbɔɔ la n du N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka tua la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi n baaŋ nɛra ni la see, u kipar saŋa, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ siu, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɔɔ du baama la n guali mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih lizaa nɛra ni dakka la tɔa ninɛɛ.
3Kenne Aarɔn ɔɔ ɛɛ di zuu a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la. U daŋ ɔɔ kpa nabalee di wa lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, di kpa pebal ge ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii. 4U daŋ kpa u tagtajaŋnaniinanii la di laali, ka kpa u galŋa n ɔɔ ra chug u naahiine la di du. Di kpa u kirsɔɔ di kirsi, di vɔɔ namu. Annii ɛɛ bɔmbɔgnanaananaarɛ. Awia, ú ɔɔ sɔ nii mɔɔ ka laalaa. 5Izrɛl hina daŋ lau bubala anɛɛ tɛɛ Aarɔn, ú lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, di kaa lau pebal ge ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii.
6Aarɔn daŋ ɔɔ kpa nabal di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu di sɛɛ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be tɛɛ u ni u diahina maa. 7Denii ú kpa buuna anɛɛ la di tɛŋ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua. 8U daŋ ta kuna dikuu buuna anɛɛ la wia, dí zum unla un niŋ kpu tɛŋ ani unla ban niŋ pur ha, ú chi ba wichɔgaa kaali. 9Aarɔn daŋ kpa buuŋ la baŋ ta kuna lizi tɛŋ la, di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu. 10Ka kpa unla ban ta kuna lizi, u ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih lizaa hor la, di tɛŋ nyinii, ka puruu ha ú wer kpa a nɛra wichɔgaa di chɔ kaali hɛribɔduma biini.
11Di Aarɔn wa kpu nabal la di sɛɛ u ni u diahina chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be tuŋ, 12u daŋ buu niŋ di lii mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ n see la di su kunla baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la di ɛɛ daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la n ɛɛ kɔlɔlɔlɔ nonii suul bunɛɛ dí kpaa zuu Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la biini, patiisa la harbɔɔ. 13Denii ú jaa kpa a daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la di du niŋ la biini n see, a nyɔɔzi izi di tɔ N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la tua baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi n baaŋ nɛra ni la ni, ú gilɛɛ wa nau di siu. 14U daŋ kpa u nonibii di lii a nabal chal di mizi a tua la see, di kaa kpa a yeŋ di mizi N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see buniidaanɛɛ.
15Denii ú jaa kpu buuŋ la ge di lizi a nɛra wichɔgaa mbusu, dí kpa u chal di zuu a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa dí mizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la tua la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi n baaŋ u ni la see, gunla himmaa uŋ mizi nabal la chal la. 16Kenne ú ɛɛ di lizi a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la doŋa ha dikuu Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa ni ba dignikpega n chɔguu la wia. U daŋ ɛɛ guŋ himmaa di tɛɛ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u chigɔ a nɛra la doŋŋe chɔɔribɔr la baambaannɛ. 17Di haŋ chi saŋa la Aarɔn n niŋ zuu a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la ú ga lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih u himmaa, u diahina ani Izrɛl hina maa ni la, nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa du n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini di u haa waa liwɛɛ.
18Aarɔn daŋ jaa lii di ba mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, di wa kpa a nabal ni a buuŋ challi yeŋa di faa de nyigzi la di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih de gba ni. 19Ka kpa u nonibii di lii a chal di mizi mbusu lizibɔr hiŋ buniidaanɛɛ. Kenne ú ɛɛ di lizi de doŋa la Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa n gillɛ u doŋ la ha, ka ú kaa ɛɛ naniinanii. 20Denii Aarɔn n wa lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih, Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la ni n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la ani mbusu lizibɔr la ni di tuŋ, ú kpogli bunyinii la di ba, ba see. 21U daŋ kpa u nonee sag a buuŋ nyuu ni, di sɛɛ Izrɛl hina biinikpola ni dignikpega ani ba wichɔgaa maa chɔgri di du u ni. Denii ú lizi nɛbɛl ú duŋŋuu du hɛribɔduma biini, 22di ga giluu de, a buuŋ chi a nɛra wichɔgaa la di kaali bɔr la nɛra n waa duwɛɛ.
23Denii Aarɔn jaa zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini, di ga wir u tagtahuŋŋunanaa la uŋ bɔkkɛ mɔɔ, ka zuu Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la di gilaa de. 24U daŋ sɔ nii bɔnaniinanii biini, ka kpa ú hɔpizi biimaa laala di laali. Denii u jaa lii di wa lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa tɛɛ u hiŋ ni a nɛra maa, di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih ba ni. 25U daŋ fuuh wichɔgaa mbusu sel la nuu mbusu lizibɔr la ni.
26Baal la n duŋŋi buuŋ la di du hɛribɔduma la, a dɛkkɔɔ ú chag u laala di sɔ nii, ka jaa wer zuu chɔɔribɔr la biini. 27A dɛkkɔɔ ií kpa wichɔgaa mbusu nabal la ni buuŋ la challi baŋ kpawɛɛ zuu Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa biini la, di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih mbusu la, di lii chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia, di fuuah. A hɔna, a ola ani a biini kuna maa. 28A dɛkkɔɔ baal la n fuuah la, chag u laala di sɔ nii, ka jaa wer zuu chɔɔribɔr la biini.
29A kennaa daŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ia di hanna la. Baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa fihiŋ hɔl, a dɛkkɔɔ Izrɛl hinuu ni hɔɔhri maa n soge ii be vɔɔ nua, di gilɛɛ waa hum huma. 30A hɔl hinnɛ bá lizi ii wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ ia di lizi ii doŋa ha. Denii ii wichɔgaa doŋa jaa tuŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be. 31U ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ, a dɛg lugɔ ií vɔɔ nuuzi. U ɛɛ widauliirɛ di tɛɛ ia di hanna la. 32N kizeehiŋ la baŋ waari nuu ú kpa u mɛɛ gawa, di ɛɛ N Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la, daŋ lizi wichɔgaa mbusu di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih. U daŋ kpa bɔmbɔgnanaananaa la n huuhzɛɛ la di bɔg, 33di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia, mbusu lizibɔr la, N Dia kizeehina ani a nɛra maa ni.
34Kennaa daŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ia di hanna la. Bina maa, kakpannɛ ií ɔɔ lizi wichɔgaa mbusu di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih, dikuu Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa maa wia.”
Ba ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.

english_text:
Where To Offer Sacrifices
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell Aaron, his sons, and everyone else in Israel:
3-4Whenever you kill any of your cattle, sheep, or goats as sacrifices to me, you must do it at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you don't, you will be guilty of pouring out blood, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 5And so, when you sacrifice an animal to ask my blessing, it must not be done out in a field, 6but in front of the sacred tent. Then a priest can splatter its blood against the bronze altar and send its fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 7Don't ever turn from me again and offer sacrifices to goat-demons. This law will never change.
8Remember! No one in Israel, including foreigners, is to offer a sacrifice anywhere 9except at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you do, you will no longer belong to my people.
Do Not Eat Blood
The Lord said:
10 I will turn against any of my people who eat blood. This also includes any foreigners living among you. 11 Life is in the blood, and I have given you the blood of animals to sacrifice in place of your own. 12That's also why I have forbidden you to eat blood. 13Even if you should hunt and kill a bird or an animal, you must drain out the blood and cover it with soil.
14The life of every living creature is in its blood. That's why I have forbidden you to eat blood and why I have warned you that anyone who does will no longer belong to my people.
15If you happen to find a dead animal and eat it, you must take a bath and wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening. 16If you don't take a bath, you will suffer for what you did wrong.
translation_text:
Chal kii wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala ni Izrɛl hina maa be, 3‘Di Izrɛl hinuu maa wa kpu nau gɛɛ pebii gɛɛ buuŋ ba chɔɔribɔr la biini gɛɛ u baŋgia, 4di waa u ni ballɛ lɛi n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua ú wa lizi mbusu tɛŋ, a baal ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. U bizi challɛ, a dɛkkɔɔ bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. 5Gunna bagluu lugɔ filaŋkennaa, Izrɛl hina daŋ jaa gil ba mbusuzi lizaa baŋgia ka jaa kpaa di waa tɛŋ. Bá ɔɔ kpaa di waa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, ú kpaa tɛŋ. Á ɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa. 6N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa a challi di mizi mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua kɛraa, ka fuuh a nuu a ɛɛ sɔɔh la n summɛ tɛŋ. 7Izrɛl hina gilɛɛ kaa wàá bir ba hara di ra kpuŋ maa, di kaa wàá lizi ba mbusuzi maa di ra tɛɛ vuga la n li buuna. Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulaa di tɛɛ ba ni ba naanna maa, saŋaa saŋa maa.
8Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ hɔɔhri maa n soge ba be, wa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii gɛɛ mbusu maa, 9ka wɔɔ kpawɛɛ ba mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, di wa kpuu tɛŋ, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.
10Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ hɔɔhri bɛl maa n jaa ba ni di so gilɛɛ waa hee sel maa ni u chal, n daŋ bir har kpuu di duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. 11Dikuubɛɛwiai, sel maa miibɔɔ du u chal biinii, n kpaa tɛɛ ia, ii kpaa di ra lizi mbusu di ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih nɛra ni. Chal ɛɛ miibɔɔrɛ di ra lizi nɛra wichɔgaa ba ni. 12Awia, n na ŋɔ Izrɛl hina benii lugɔ bɛl maa gɛɛ hɔɔhri la maa n soge ii be, ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa hee chal.
13Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ hɔɔhri bɛl maa n soge ba be haŋ wa la kpaana, di ga kpu sel gɛɛ zumbee maa banna di, ú kɔrguu ú chal lii, ú ɛɛ hɛɛhraa tɔ a ni. 14Dikuubɛɛwiai, sel maa miibɔɔrɛ ú chal. Awiarɛ n na ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ bá ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa hee sel maa chal, dikuu sel maa miibɔɔ n ɛɛ u chal wia, di nɛr maa haŋ wa heea, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.
15Nɛr la maa n ɛɛ Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ hɔɔhri maa, haŋ wa di kunla maa n siuwɛ gɛɛ pir sela n kpuwɛɛ, daŋ chag u laala ka sɔ nii, ka doŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be di ra ba duana, denii ú doŋa jaa tuŋ. 16Ka di waa u kuna chakkɛ di sɔ nii, u daŋ di guŋ tɔɔrɔɔ.’ ”

english_text:
Forbidden Sex
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell the people of Israel:
I am the Lord your God! 3So don't follow the customs of Egypt where you used to live or those of Canaan where I am bringing you. 4I am the Lord your God, and you must obey my teachings. 5 Obey them and you will live. I am the Lord.
6Don't have sex with any of your close relatives, 7especially your own mother. This would disgrace your father. 8 And don't disgrace him by having sex with any of his other wives. 9 Don't have sex with your sister or stepsister, whether you grew up together or not. 10Don't disgrace yourself by having sex with your granddaughter 11or half sister 12-13 or a sister of your father or mother. 14Don't disgrace your uncle by having sex with his wife. 15 Don't have sex with your daughter-in-law 16 or sister-in-law. 17 And don't have sex with the daughter or granddaughter of any woman that you have earlier had sex with. You will be having sex with her closest relatives, and that would make you unclean. 18As long as your wife is alive, don't cause trouble for her by taking one of her sisters as a second wife.
19 When a woman is having her monthly period, she is unclean, so don't have sex with her.
20 Don't have sex with another man's wife—that would make you unclean.
21 Don't sacrifice your children on the altar fires to the god Molech. I am the Lord your God, and that would disgrace me.
22 It is disgusting for a man to have sex with another man.
23 Anyone who has sex with an animal is unclean.
24Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these disgusting practices of those nations that I am forcing out of the land for you. They made themselves 25and the land so unclean, that I punished the land because of their sins, and I made it vomit them up. 26-27Now don't do these sickening things that make the land filthy. Instead, obey my laws and teachings. 28Then the land won't become sick of you and vomit you up, just as it did them. 29-30If any of you do these vulgar, disgusting things, you will be unclean and no longer belong to my people. I am the Lord your God, and I forbid you to follow their sickening way of life.
translation_text:
Nyiŋŋaa la n waa dɛkkɛ wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, dí Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum. 3Ií gilɛɛ kaa wàá ɛɛ Ijip hina la iiŋ faa du ba be la wiɛɛlaa, di gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ Keenan la miŋ kpogli ia di ra la la hina wiɛɛlaa. 4Ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni widaulaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum. 5Ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa ni n Gbɔgni, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr la maa n wette di ra hiŋaa, waabuu niŋ na miibɔɔ a hiŋaa biini. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
6Nɛr maa ni u lulli himmaa gilɛɛ waa chɔɔ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
7Gilɛɛ wàá gbɛlli i mɛɛ di lau u haaŋ nyiŋŋi. I maarɛ, gilɛɛ wa lawuu ra nyiŋŋi.
8Gilɛɛ wa lau i mɛɛ haaŋ maa di ra nyiŋŋi, guŋ daŋ ɛɛ i mɛɛ gbɛllaa.
9Gilɛɛ wàá lau i niuhambie di ra nyiŋŋi, di i mɛɛ biere gɛɛ i maa biere, gɛɛ di ba luluubuu ii dia biini gɛɛ yembɛl gba.
10Gilɛɛ wàá lau i naana di ra nyiŋŋi, dikuubɛɛwiai, a guŋ daŋ gil ba ra gbɛllii.
11Gilɛɛ wàá lau i mɛɛ haaŋ biihaaŋ la u nuu n lullɛ di ra nyiŋŋi, dikuubɛɛwiai, i niuhambiere.
12Gilɛɛ wàá lau i nyaana di ra nyiŋŋi, dikuu uŋ ɛɛ i mɛɛ lulli himmaa wia.
13Gilɛɛ wàá lau i maazeŋ gɛɛ i maabie di ra nyiŋŋi, dikuu uŋ ɛɛ i maa lulli himmaa wia.
14Gilɛɛ wàá gbɛlli i mɛɛbee gɛɛ i mɛɛzeŋ di lau u haaŋ nyiŋŋi, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ i maarɛ.
15Gilɛɛ wàá lau i biibaal haaŋ di ra nyiŋŋi, dikuubɛɛwiai, i biibaal haannɛ.
16Gilɛɛ wàá lau i niwee gɛɛ i kpɛɛma haaŋ di ra nyiŋŋi, guŋ daŋ gil ba ra gbɛllii.
17Gilɛɛ wàá lau haaŋ ni u biihaaŋ maa di ra nyiŋŋi. Gilɛɛ waa nyiŋŋi u naanna. Dikuu baŋ ɛɛ u lulla himmaa wia. Guŋ ɛɛ biinikpolaa.
18Gilɛɛ wàá kpa i haaŋ kpɛɛma gɛɛ u niwee di ra ɛɛ haaŋ, di i haaŋ haa du de ni miibɔɔ.
19Gilɛɛ wàá lau haaŋ maa di ra nyiŋŋi, di u ra ɛɛ doŋa.
20Gilɛɛ wàá nyiŋŋi i dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ, guŋ daŋ chɔgii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be.
21Gilɛɛ wàá lau i bie maa di ra tɛɛ ba lizi mbusu ra tɛɛ vug Mɔlɛk, dikuubɛɛwiai, a waa dɛkkɛ hiŋ chɔg mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
22Ií gilɛɛ wàá nyiŋŋi baal gunla baal n ɔɔ nyiŋŋi haaŋ la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi hah gunnɛ werge.
23Ií gilɛɛ wàá lau sel maa di ra nyiŋŋi di wàá doŋ iihinaa n be. Haaŋ gilɛɛ waa kpa u hiŋ di ra tɛɛ sel ú nyiŋŋi. Guŋ waa dɛkkɛ maa.
24Ií gilɛɛ kpa annii bɛl maa di ra doŋ iihinaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, gunnɛ banla min niŋ duŋŋi ii sibɔɔ la ɛɛ di doŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be. 25Ba wiɛɛlaa faa gillɔɔ a hɛri doŋ, n vɛɛ baa. 26Ka a dɛkkɔɔ ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa. Ií biizi ni hɔɔhra la n soge ii be la maa gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wikuna naa bɛl maa, 27dikuubɛɛwiai, aabuu nɛra la n faa du a hɛri naa biini, mɔɔ ka ii haa ba la faa ra ɛɛ, a hɛri faa doŋ. 28Di ii haŋ wa doŋ a hɛri, u daŋ vɛɛ ia gunla uŋ faa vɛɛ banla n faa du de mɔɔ la.
29Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa ɛɛ wikuna naa bɛl maa, ii duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. 30Ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wikuna la nɛra la n faa du ɛŋ mɔɔ, ka ií ba la n faa ra ɛɛ la. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpaa di ra doŋ iihinaa. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.”

english_text:
Moral and Religious Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2 to say to the community of Israel:
I am the Lord your God. I am holy, and you must be holy too! 3-4 Respect your father and your mother, honor the Sabbath, and don't make idols or images. I am the Lord your God.
5When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, be sure to follow my instructions. 6You may eat the meat either on the day of the sacrifice or on the next day, but you must burn anything left over on the third day. 7If you eat any of it on the third day, the sacrifice will be disgusting to me, and I will reject it. 8In fact, you will be punished for not respecting what I say is holy, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
9 When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing along the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground. 10Don't strip your grapevines clean or gather the grapes that fall off the vines. Leave them for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God.
11 Do not steal or tell lies or cheat others.
12 Do not misuse my name by making promises you don't intend to keep. I am the Lord your God.
13 Do not steal anything or cheat anyone, and don't fail to pay your workers at the end of each day.
14 I am the Lord your God, and I command you not to make fun of the deaf or to cause a blind person to stumble.
15 Be fair, no matter who is on trial—don't favor either the poor or the rich.
16Don't be a gossip, but never hesitate to speak up in court, especially if your testimony can save someone's life.
17 Don't hold grudges. On the other hand, it's wrong not to correct someone who needs correcting. 18 Don't be angry or try to take revenge. I am the Lord, and I command you to love others as much as you love yourself.
19 Breed your livestock animals only with animals of the same kind, and don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field or wear clothes made of different kinds of material.
20If a man has sex with a slave woman who is promised in marriage to someone else, he must pay a fine, but they are not to be put to death. After all, she was still a slave at the time. 21-22The man must bring a ram to the entrance of the sacred tent and give it to a priest, who will then offer it as a sacrifice to me, so the man's sins will be forgiven.
23After you enter the land, you will plant fruit trees, but you are not to eat any fruit from them for the first three years. 24In the fourth year the fruit must be set apart, as an expression of thanks 25to me, the Lord God. Do this, and in the fifth year, those trees will produce an abundant harvest of fruit for you to eat.
26 Don't eat the blood of any animal.
Don't practice any kind of witchcraft.
27-28 I forbid you to shave any part of your head or beard or to cut and tattoo yourself as a way of worshiping the dead.
29 Don't let your daughters serve as temple prostitutes—this would bring disgrace both to them and the land.
30 I command you to respect the Sabbath and the place where I am worshiped.
31 Don't make yourselves disgusting to me by going to people who claim they can talk to the dead.
32I command you to show respect for older people and to obey me with fear and trembling.
33 Don't mistreat any foreigners who live in your land. 34Instead, treat them as well as you treat your own people and love them as much as you love yourself. Remember, you were once foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
35-36 Use honest scales and don't cheat when you weigh or measure anything.
I am the Lord your God. I rescued you from Egypt, 37and I command you to obey my laws.
translation_text:
Gbɔgni irizi wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina maa be, ‘Ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ.
3Ií bɛl maa ra tɔgzi u maa ni u mɛɛ, di ra tɔgzi Heezaa Hɔpizii la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.
4Ií gilɛɛ wàá vɛɛŋ ka bir di ra kuari vuga gɛɛ di wa kpa lugbia ŋmɛɛri kuari vuga, di ra sɛɛ a dɔɔra. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum. 5Di ii wa kpu sel di lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ií lizuu di hiŋ n widaulaa la miŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ ia la, guŋ gil n lɛɛu. 6Ií daŋ hee u maa a hɔl la maa iiŋ kpuu la gɛɛ u hɔpizaa anɛɛ hɔl di tuŋ. Ka di u yemmaa wa kawɔɔ ú hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, a dɛkkɔɔ ií fuuuh. 7Ka di ii wa hee u yemmaa a hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, u doŋŋoo, màá lɛɛ a mbusu lizaa. 8Nɛr la maa wa heeu daŋ di bilchɔg, dikuu uŋ kpa kunnaniinanii la baŋ tɛŋ di birgi kumpɛɛ wia. Ií duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.
9Di ii waa kum ii kooliŋkuna, ii gilɛɛ waa kumaa di ra hel ii kooni nuuzi gɛɛ di bir har di ra kugnaa. 10Ií gilɛɛ waa bir har di ra tɔrgi ii grepu kooni daazi nɔna bunɛɛ gɛɛ di wàá paagi anla n choglee. Ií gilaa tɛɛ nyaara ni hɔɔhra. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.
11Ií gilɛɛ ra ŋmɛɛ.
Ií gilɛɛ ra kanni kara.
Ií gilɛɛ ra dar dɔŋa.
12Ií gilɛɛ waa hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi, di ra kanni kara di ra chɔg Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum sɔŋ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
13Ií gilɛɛ wàá fini gɛɛ di ra ŋmɛɛ ii dɔŋahina.
Ií gilɛɛ wàá vɛɛ ii paahdiiri turgaa di ra ba hɔpizaa.
14Ií gilɛɛ wàá see gɛnii nua gɛɛ di wa kpa kuŋ di ra tɔ nyuŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛ ú wàá garguu. Minuu Kɔraawiizi, ií ra ɔmiŋ.
15Ií ra di wibii di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa. Ií gilɛɛ waa di nyaara seriya ni nɔŋŋaa gɛɛ di ra ɔm dɔɔna, ka ɔɔ ra di ii dɔŋahina seriya ni wibii.
16Ií gilɛɛ gaagi di ra kanni kara la n niŋ chɔg ii dɔŋahina nɛra biini.
Ií gilɛɛ wàá ɛɛ wii la maa n niŋ lizi ii dɔŋahina miibɔɔni. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
17Ií gilɛɛ hah ii dɔŋahina ii bampiree biine. Ka ii ɔɔ ra di baa wibii di gilɛɛ waa gil ba wichɔgaa ra buu ia.
18Ií gilɛɛ wa bir kpa wichɔgaa di ra turgi ii dɔŋahina wichɔgaa kim gɛɛ di hah ba, ka nɔŋŋi baa gunla iin nɔŋŋi ii hina la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
19Ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa.
Ií gilɛɛ gil sel maa wàá deezi ú duma maa.
Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa kundee irizi anɛɛ di ra duu koo kpaŋ.
Ií gilɛɛ waa laali sisaawa.
20Di baal lau yoŋhaaŋ baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ baal ka u haa waa u kim turgee, gɛɛ ba haa wɔɔ tawɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ u dɔɔ u hiŋ di nyiŋŋi. Ií tɔɔri baa ka gilɛɛ waa kpu baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u haa waa u hiŋ dɔɔwɛ. 21Ka a baal waa daŋ lizi pebal di ba mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, di wa lizi bilchɔg mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 22N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpa a pebal, di lizi bilchɔg mbusu di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih, ń gil a baal wichɔgaa tɛu.
23Di ii wa zuu Keenan hɛri di duu daa maa n na nɔŋ, ií ra kii u nɔna binni ahoro, dikuubɛɛwiai, a doŋŋoo n be. 24Ií daŋ kpa u binni anaazuhiŋ nɔna di wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, á ɛɛ a nanaananaa, di ɛɛ chɔlaa mbusu hora. 25Ka u binni anuehiŋ biini waa, ii daŋ jaa wer di u nɔna. Di ii ɛɛ annii naa maa, ii daazi daŋ ɔɔ nɔŋ werge. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.
26Ií gilɛɛ wàá hee ol la chal n haa du u ni.
Ií gilɛɛ wàá vug gɛɛ di ra di hiri.
27Ií gilɛɛ waa fuŋ ii nyukɛraa gɛɛ di wàá ŋmɛnni ii taŋhuna yeŋ.
28Ií gilɛɛ wa kuu lalii wia di ra mɔnni gɛɛ di ra zɛuzi ii bɔra. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
29Ií gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli ii biihaana di gil ba birgi sɛnsɛnna. Di ii haŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ, a hɛri maa daŋ su ni sɛnsɛŋ ni biinikpola.
30Ií ra di n Heezaa Hɔpizii la di ra tɔgzi n jaami bɔr la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
31Ií gilɛɛ ra la vugra gɛɛ ijɔzi be, ba ra bagli ia wia ŋmɛnizi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daŋ gil ii doŋ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.
32Ií ra ɔmiŋ, di ra tɔgzi nabɔnzi, di ra kpa baa girme. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
33Di hɔɔhri wa sogo ii hɛri, ií gilɛɛ ra diŋzuu. 34Ií ra ɛɛ hɔɔhri la maa n soge ii be lugɔ ii biilullii. Ií nɔŋŋuu alugɔ ii dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ge gba faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa Ijip hɛri. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.
35Ií gilɛɛ waa fini nɛr maa di ii ŋɔ ii mɛgzi kuŋ jaŋzi gɛɛ u tɔgzi gɛɛ u kanni di tɛu.
36Ií ɔɔ kpa mɛgzaa kuna la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ kookoo tassazi ni galɔnzi di ra mɛgzi kuna. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum, minuu kpogli ia di lii Ijip hɛri.
37Ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa maa. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”

english_text:
Penalties for Disobeying God's Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
Death by stoning is the penalty for any citizens or foreigners in the country who sacrifice their children to the god Molech. 3They have disgraced both the place where I am worshiped and my holy name, and so I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. 4Some of you may let them get away with human sacrifice, 5but not me. If any of you worship Molech, I will turn against you and your entire family, and I will no longer let you belong to my people.
6I will be your enemy if you go to someone who claims to speak with the dead, and I will destroy you from among my people. 7Dedicate yourselves to me and be holy because I am the Lord your God. 8I have chosen you as my people, and I expect you to obey my laws.
9 If you curse your father or mother, you will be put to death, and it will be your own fault.
10 If any of you men have sex with another man's wife, both you and the woman will be put to death.
11 Having sex with one of your father's wives disgraces him. So both you and the woman will be put to death, just as you deserve. 12 It isn't natural to have sex with your daughter-in-law, and both of you will be put to death, just as you deserve. 13 It's disgusting for men to have sex with one another, and those who do will be put to death, just as they deserve. 14 It isn't natural for a man to marry both a woman and her daughter, and so all three of them will be burned to death. 15-16 If any of you have sex with an animal, both you and the animal will be put to death, just as you deserve.
17 If you marry one of your sisters, you will be punished, and the two of you will be disgraced by being openly forced out of the community. 18 If you have sex with a woman during her monthly period, both you and the woman will be cut off from the people of Israel. 19 The sisters of your father and mother are your own relatives, and you will be punished for having sex with any of them. 20If you have sex with your uncle's wife, neither you nor she will ever have any children. 21 And if you marry your sister-in-law, neither of you will ever have any children.
22Obey my laws and teachings. Or else the land I am giving you will become sick of you and throw you out. 23The nations I am chasing out did these disgusting things, and I hated them for it, so don't follow their example. 24I am the Lord your God, and I have promised you their land that is rich with milk and honey. I have chosen you to be different from other people. 25That's why you must make a difference between animals and birds that I have said are clean and unclean—this will keep you from becoming disgusting to me. 26I am the Lord, the holy God. You have been chosen to be my people, and so you must be holy too.
27If you claim to receive messages from the dead, you will be put to death by stoning, just as you deserve.
translation_text:
Wichɔgaa dignitɛraa wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ di Izrɛl hinuu maa gɛɛ hɔɔhri maa n na zuu Izrɛl hɛri, haŋ wa kpa u bie lizi mbusu tɛɛ vug la banna yir Mɔlɛk la, ií paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu. 3N daŋ lizi siwii sag a guŋ hiŋ ni, di duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. Dikuu uŋ kpa u biizi tɛɛ vug Mɔlɛk wia, u doŋ N Tanti Diarɛ, di kaa chɔg n sɔnnanii. 4Di u ɛɛ guŋ, ka a nɛra siigi di giluu, ba wɔɔ kpuwɛɛ, 5n himmaa daŋ lizi siwii sag u ni u diahina ni, di duŋŋi banla maa n chigɛ u har, di nyaa wibii n be, di ra jaami vug Mɔlɛk la, di lii ba nɛra biine.
6N daŋ lizi siwii sag nɛr la maa n niŋ la vugra ni ijɔzi be, di nyaa wibii n be, n daŋ duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.
7Ií sɔ iihinaa di lizi ii doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be, dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum. 8Ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa nɛnnɛ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la n ɔɔ gil ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa.
9Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa see u mɛɛ gɛɛ u maa nua, ií kpuu, u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi u ni. 10Di baal maa nyiŋŋi u dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ, ií kpu ba maa.
11Di baal maa wa nyiŋŋi u mɛɛ haaŋ, u gbɛlli u mɛɛrɛ. Ií kpu a baal ni a haaŋ maa. Ba wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.
12Di baal maa nyiŋŋi u biibaal haaŋ, ií kpu ba maa. Ba ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, awia ba wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi ba ni.
13Di baal haŋ wa lau u dɔŋ baal di chɔɔ gunla baal n ɔɔ chɔɔ haaŋ la, ba maa banɛɛ la ɛɛ wikunaa. Ií kpu baa, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.
14Di baal haŋ wa kpa bie ni u màá maa kpau di ɛɛ u haana, guŋ ɛɛ biinikpolaa. Ií fuuh u ni a haana maa, guŋ gil biinikpola wàá du ii be.
15Di baal haŋ wa lau sel nyiŋŋi, ii kpu u ni a sel maa.
16Di haaŋ wa gillɔ sel nyiŋŋuu, ii kpu a haaŋ ni a sel maa, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.
17Di baal haŋ wa kpa u mɛɛ biihaaŋ gɛɛ u maa biihaaŋ, di nyiŋŋuu, a ɛɛ hiihzii werge maa. Ií duŋŋi baa di lii ii biini. U binni u niuhambie labuu pɛɛ, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.
18Di baal haŋ wa lau haaŋ la maa n na ɛɛ u baagu doŋa di nyiŋŋi, ií duŋŋi baa ii biini, dikuubɛɛwiai ba chɔg kuŋ doŋaa Gbɔgnii.
19Gilɛɛ wa lau i nyaana gɛɛ maazeŋ gɛɛ i maabie di ra nyiŋŋi, guŋ daŋ ɛɛ ii lulli gbɛllaa. Ii nɛra banɛɛ la maa daŋ turgi a kim.
20Di baal maa haŋ wa lau u naara haaŋ nyiŋŋi, u gbɛlli u naaraa. A baal ni a haaŋ daŋ turgi a kim. Ba daŋ wa siuzi di ba waa biizi lullɛ.
21Di baal haŋ wa kpa u kpɛɛma gɛɛ u niwee haaŋ, guŋ ɛɛ doŋaa di ɛɛ u kpɛɛma gɛɛ u niwee gbɛllaa. Ba daŋ wa siuzi di ba waa biizi lullɛ.”
22Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa, di wer du hɛri la minna la ii ni la biini. 23Ií gilɛɛ waa hiŋ hɛssi la hina minna duŋŋi ka ii zuu de la naana wia. Dikuubɛɛwiai, aabuu ba faa ra ɛɛ, n kii baa la. 24Ií ra nuu n be, ‘N daŋ kpau tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuŋ. U summɔɔ di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge.’ Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum, unla n lizi ia, ii kur hɛssi hina maa ni la.
25Awia, ií zum sela ni zumbizi la n waa doŋŋe ni anla n doŋŋe. Ií gilɛɛ waa di a sedoŋa gɛɛ zumbidoŋa gɛɛ kunla maa n na tuuzi hɛri di ra doŋ iihinaa. 26Ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa tɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ, di lizi ia ií kur hɛssi hina maa ni, dí ɛɛ n hora.
27Baal gɛɛ haaŋ la maa n ɛɛ vugri gɛɛ ijɔ di du ii biini, ií paagi bia lɔɔzi baa kpuuzi, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.”

english_text:
Instructions for Priests
1The Lord gave Moses these instructions for Aaron's sons, the priests:
Touching a dead body will make you unclean. So don't go near a dead relative, 2except your mother, father, son, daughter, brother, 3or an unmarried sister, who has no husband to take care of her. 4Don't make yourself unclean by attending the funeral of someone related to you by marriage. 5 Don't shave any part of your head or trim your beard or cut yourself to show that you are mourning. 6I am the Lord your God, and I have chosen you alone to offer sacrifices of food to me on the altar. That's why you must keep yourselves holy. 7Don't marry a divorced woman or a woman who has served as a temple prostitute. You are holy, 8because I am holy. And so, you must be treated with proper respect, since you offer food sacrifices to me, the God of holiness.
9If any of you priests has a daughter who disgraces you by serving as a temple prostitute, she must be burned to death.
10If you are the high priest, you must not mess up your hair or tear your clothes in order to mourn for the dead. 11Don't make yourself unclean by going near a dead body, not even that of your own father or mother. 12If you leave the sacred place to attend a funeral, both you and the sacred place become unclean, because you are the high priest.
13If you are the high priest, you must marry only a virgin 14from your own tribe. Don't marry a divorced woman or any other woman who has already had sex, including a temple prostitute. 15In this way, your descendants will be qualified to serve me. Remember—I am the Lord, and I have chosen you.
16The Lord told Moses 17-18to say to Aaron:
No descendant of yours can ever serve as my priest if he is blind or lame, if his face is disfigured, if one leg is shorter than the other, 19if either a foot or a hand is paralyzed, 20if he is a hunchback or a dwarf, if an eye or his skin is diseased, or if his testicles have been damaged. 21These men may not serve as my priests and burn sacrifices to me. 22They may eat the food offerings presented to me, 23but they may not enter the sacred place or serve me at the altar. Remember—I am the Lord, the one who makes a priest holy.
24Moses told all of this to Aaron, his sons, and the people of Israel.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina widaulaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ŋɔ Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ N Dia kizeehina la be, lugɔ bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa doŋ u hiŋ, u lulli lee wia biini. 2Di u lulli himaa, lugɔ u mɛɛ, u maa, u biibaal, u biihaaŋ, u niwee, u kpɛɛma, 3gɛɛ u niuhambie la n waa yuuwɛ ka du u be lɛi. 4Ú gilɛɛ waa doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be dikuu lula yuuri wia.
5A waa dɛkkɛ n kizeehiŋ maa n na fuŋ u nyuu ni u taŋhuna kɛraa gɛɛ di wàá mɔnni u bɔra. 6A dɛkkɔɔ ú ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii, di gilɛɛ waa chɔg n sɔŋ. Dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu ɔɔ ra kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa la n ɛɛ n diwee la di ra tɛŋ. A dɛkkɔɔ ú ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii.
7A waa dɛkkɛ n kizeehiŋ n kpa hahsɛnsɛnni gɛɛ suŋguru la n zum baal gɛɛ haaŋ la n yuuwɛ ka ka, di doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ nɛnaniinaniirɛ. 8Ií zum lugɔ u ɛɛ nɛnaniinaniirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu kpa míŋ̀ Kɔraawiizi diwee di ra tɛŋ. Ií ra tɔgzuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ, di gil n nɛra ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa.
9Di n kizeehiŋ biihaaŋ wa birgi sɛnsɛnni di doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, u kpa hiihzii kpu u mɛɛ. A dɛkkɔɔ ií fuuh a biihaaŋ.
10N Kizeehina Nabɔma la baŋ lizɛɛ u lulla biini di waaruu nuu u ra bɔg kizeehiŋ bɔmbɔga la, gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u nyuu chaazaa gɛɛ di wàá piili u bɔmbɔga, dikuu unna wii lee wia. 11A waa dɛkkɛ ú wàá zuu bɔr la lalii n chɔɔwɛ. A waa dɛkkɛ un doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, haali di u mɛɛrɛ gɛɛ u maarɛ gba, 12gɛɛ di waa lii N Tanti Dia la gɛɛ di waa doŋuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba lizuubuu di kpa n nuu waaruu. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
13A dɛkkɔɔ ú kpa haaŋ la n waa baal zummɛ. 14Ú gilɛɛ waa kpa luhaaŋ gɛɛ haaŋ la n yuuwɛ ka ka, gɛɛ haaŋ la n kpa sɛnsɛŋ di doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, see haaŋ la n waa baal zummɛ di lii u himmaa nɛra biini. 15Guŋ gilɛɛ gil ú wàá doŋ u biizi di lii u himmaa nɛra biini. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii gillɛ u ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii.”
16Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 17“Ŋɔ Aarɔn be, ‘Di i naana bɛl maa waa haŋ wa du kpeg, ú ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa kpa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizaa diwee di waa tɛŋ. 18Baal la maa n waa kpeg gilɛɛ waa dugliŋ, di u nyuŋŋɔɔrɛ gɛɛ u naa gɛɛ u nonii siuwɔɔ, 19gɛɛ baal la maa n dɔɔ naasiwii gɛɛ nosiwii 20gɛɛ gee hiŋ gɛɛ kirbii gɛɛ unla n dɔɔ siwiila gɛɛ di dɔɔ ŋmɛr la na wii nii gɛɛ nɛr la lurbee n chɔkkɛ. 21Aarɔn naana la maa n waa kpeg gilɛɛ waa kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa di ra tɛŋ. A waa dɛkkɛ un niŋ kpa n diwee di ra tɛŋ. 22U daŋ wer di n diunanaananaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tɛŋ gɛɛ anla n ɛɛ a nanaananaa himmaa la, 23ka uŋ waa kpeg la wia, a waa dɛkkɛ unna dugli n Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa patiisa la gɛɛ di wàá la mbusu lizibɔr la zɛɛ, di gilɛɛ waa doŋ n Tanti Dia la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi, minuu gillɛ ba ɛɛ kunnanaananaa.’ ”
24Denii Moosis ŋɔ annii naa maa tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala ni Izrɛl hina maa.

english_text:
The Offerings Are Holy
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to Aaron and his sons:
I am the Lord God, and I demand that you honor my holy name by showing proper respect for the offerings brought to me by the people of Israel. 3If any of you are unclean when you accept an offering for me, I will no longer let you serve as a priest. 4None of you may take part in the sacred meals while you have a skin disease or an infected penis, or after you have been near a dead body or have had a flow of semen, 5or if you have touched an unclean creature of any sort, including an unclean person. 6-7Once you are unclean, you must take a bath, but you still cannot eat any of the sacred food until evening. 8I command you not to eat anything that is killed by a wild animal or dies a natural death. This would make you unclean. 9Obey me, or you will die on duty for disgracing the place of worship. Remember—I am the Lord, the one who makes a priest holy.
10Only you priests and your families may eat the food offerings; these are too sacred for any of your servants. 11However, any slave that you own, including those born into your household, may eat this food. 12If your daughter marries someone who isn't a priest, she can no longer have any of this food. 13But if she returns to your home, either widowed or divorced, and has no children, she may join in the meal. Only members of a priestly family can eat this food, 14and anyone else who accidentally does so, must pay for the food plus a fine of 20 percent.
15I warn you not to treat lightly the offerings that are brought by the people of Israel. 16Don't let them become guilty of eating this sacred food. Remember—I am the Lord, the one who makes these offerings holy.
Acceptable Sacrifices
17The Lord told Moses 18to tell Aaron and his sons and everyone else the rules for offering sacrifices. He said:
The animals that are to be completely burned on the altar 19-20 must have nothing wrong with them, or else I won't accept them. Bulls or rams or goats are the animals to be used for these sacrifices.
21When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, there must be nothing wrong with the animal. This is true, whether the sacrifice is part of a promise or something you do voluntarily. 22Don't offer an animal that is blind or injured or that has an infection or a skin disease. 23If one of your cattle or lambs has a leg that is longer or shorter than the others, you may offer it voluntarily, but not as part of a promise. 24As long as you live in this land, don't offer an animal with injured testicles. 25And don't bring me animals you bought from a foreigner. I won't accept them, because they are no better than one that has something wrong with it.
26The Lord told Moses to say:
27Newborn cattle, sheep, or goats must remain with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day, you may send them up in smoke to me, and I will accept the offering. 28Don't sacrifice a newborn animal and its mother on the same day.
29When you offer a sacrifice to give thanks to me, you must do it in a way that is acceptable. 30Eat all of the meat that same day and don't save any for the next day. I am the Lord your God!
31Obey my laws and teachings—I am the Lord. 32-33I demand respect from the people of Israel, so don't disgrace my holy name. Remember—I am the one who chose you to be priests and rescued all of you from Egypt, so that I would be your Lord.
translation_text:
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Kali Aarɔn ni u biibaala lugɔ ba ra tɔgzi mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa la Izrɛl hina n kpawɛɛ waa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la, di gilɛɛ wàá chɔg n sɔnnaniinanii la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
3Ŋɔ ba be, ‘Di ii naana bɛl maa wa doŋŋo mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, ka ba di wa dugli mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa la Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ kpa ba di wa tɛŋ la, a dɛkkɔɔ ba duŋŋuu lii n be, wàá ka hum mbusu lizibɔr la maa. Guŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ di hanna la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
4Di Aarɔn naana maa wa dɔɔ bɔrahɔŋ wiilbuulaa gɛɛ u hɛŋ na lul, ú gilɛɛ waa di mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa di hanna la saŋa la ban niŋ lizi u doŋa ha. Di ba bɛl maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi kunla maa baŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ lalii gɛɛ nɛr la maa banni n liwɛɛ, u doŋŋoo 5gɛɛ di u wa gbɔgzi kuntuuzii maa gɛɛ nɛr la maa n doŋŋe. 6Di bɛl maa wa gbɔgzi annii bɛl maa, u daŋ doŋ di ra ba duana. Ú gilɛɛ waa di mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa la bɛl maa, see uŋ wa sɔ nii mɔɔ. 7Di wiizi wa chollo, wàá ka doŋ, u daŋ jaa wer di mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa dikuu aŋ ɛɛ u kundiilaa wia. 8Bɛl maa gilɛɛ wàá di sel la maa n siuwɛ u hiŋ ni gɛɛ pir sela n lauwɛ, di wàá doŋ u hiŋ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
9N Dia kizeehina la ra hiŋ n widaulaa la min dauwɛ tɛɛ baa la nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, di wàá siuzi, dikuu baŋ gbɛlliŋ la wia. Minuu Kɔraawiizi, minuu gillɛ ba ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa.
10Nɛr la maa n wàá n kizeehiŋ biilullii ɛɛwɛ, gilɛɛ wàá di mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa, haali di u ɛɛ u hɔɔhrii gɛɛ u balii gbaa, ka ú gilɛɛ waa dia. 11Ka di n kizeehiŋ kpa kebee yau yom, gɛɛ di ba lul yom u dia, a yom daŋ wer di u diwee. 12Di n kizeehiŋ biihaaŋ yuu nɛr la n wan kizeehiŋ la ɛɛwɛ, ú gilɛɛ waa di mbusu lizaa kunnaananaa bɛl maa. 13Ka di n kizeehiŋ biihaaŋ wa birgi luhaaŋ gɛɛ u jaari vɛɛu di wàá biizi dɔɔwɛ, u bir wa du u mɛɛ dia alugɔ u bichaluu saŋa la, u daŋ wer di u mɛɛ diwee. Nɛr la maa n waa dɛkkɛ, gilɛɛ waa dia.
14Di nɛr la maa wa foroo di mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa, u daŋ turgi n kizeehiŋ gunla un diwee la maga, di kaa bɔnni a diwee bɔra anue, di kpa bɔkpaŋ di sag a ni. 15N Dia kizeehina gilɛɛ waa doŋ mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa 16di wa gil ba ra dia, di wa kpa chɔgri ni dignitɛraa ra sag ba ni, a waa lɔ baa kim. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la n gillɛ a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa.’ ”
17Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 18“Ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala ni Izrɛl hina maa be, ‘Di ii bɛl maa, di Izrɛl hinuurɛ gɛɛ hɔɔhrii du Izrɛl hɛri, di wa kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ra tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, di ra lizi nua gɛɛ u kipar mbusu, 19ú lizi sebal la n kpekke di lii u nauna, peeza gɛɛ buuna biini, ń wer lɛɛu. 20Gilɛɛ waa lizi kunla maa n waa kpeg, dikuubɛɛwiai, màá lɛɛu. 21Di nɛr wa lizi nau gɛɛ peezi gɛɛ buuŋ di lii lig biini, ú wa lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, di u kipar mbusu lizaarɛ gɛɛ di nua mbusu lizaarɛ, ú lizi unla n kpekke, ń wer lɛɛu. 22Gilɛɛ waa lizi sel la n nyuŋŋɛɛ gɛɛ n boŋŋee gɛɛ n gbɛttɛ gɛɛ n dɔɔ wega gɛɛ n dɔɔ ŋmɛra la n na wii nii. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa annii naa bɛl maa di wàá sag mbusu lizibɔr la ni di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ra tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 23Ka ii daŋ wer lizi sel maa, di naurɛ gɛɛ peezi n zugmeere gɛɛ wàá kpeg, di ú ɛɛ ii kipar mbusu, ka màá lɛɛu di ii ra lizi nua waarɛ. 24Ií gilɛɛ wa lizi sel la maa lure n forgee, baŋ chanzɛɛ, baŋ mɔnnɛɛ gɛɛ baŋ chahwɛɛ di ra tɛŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ guŋ ii hɛri biini. 25Ií gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ a guŋ sela naa bɛl maa di ra lii hɔɔhri be di ra tɛŋ. Màá lɛɛa dikuu ii wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, a waa kpeg.’ ”
26Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 27“Di nau gɛɛ peezi gɛɛ buuŋ wa lullɔ, u biifula hiŋ daŋ du u maa be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Ka di jaa lii a hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl waa, ii daŋ wer kpau lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 28Gilɛɛ waa kpu nau gɛɛ peezi ni u bie maa hɔpizikpaŋ.
29Di ii haŋ wa kpu kummaa di ra jaami mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ií kpuu gunla n dɛkkɛ ń wer lɛɛu. 30Ií hee u maa a hɔl hiŋ, ií gilɛɛ waa gil u yemmaa hɔɔ ra pizi. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.”
31Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni. Minuu Kɔraawiizi. 32Gilɛɛ waa chɔg mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi sɔnnaniinanii la. A dɛkkɔɔ Izrɛl hina zum lugɔ n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la n gillɛ ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa. 33Minuu lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri la, ń ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iin ninna hum. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

english_text:
Religious Festivals
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
I have chosen certain times for you to come together and worship me.
3 You have six days when you can do your work, but the seventh day of each week is holy because it belongs to me. No matter where you live, you must rest on the Sabbath and come together for worship. This law will never change.
Passover and the Festival of Thin Bread
(Numbers 28.16-25)
The Lord said:
4-5 Passover is another time when you must come together to worship me, and it must be celebrated on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
6 The Festival of Thin Bread begins on the fifteenth day of that same month; it lasts seven days, and during this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast. 7On the first day of this festival you must rest from your work and come together for worship. 8Each day of this festival you must offer sacrifices. Then on the final day you must once again rest from your work and come together for worship.
Offering the First Part of the Harvest
9The Lord told Moses 10to say to the community of Israel:
After you enter the land I am giving you, the first bundle of wheat from each crop must be given to me. So bring it to a priest 11on the day after the Sabbath. He will lift it up in dedication to me, and I will accept you. 12You must also offer a sacrifice to please me. So bring the priest a one-year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it 13and two kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil. Then he will place these on the bronze altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. Together with these, you must bring a liter of wine as a drink offering. 14I am your God, and I forbid you to eat any new grain or anything made from it until you have brought these offerings. This law will never change.
The Harvest Festival
(Numbers 28.26-31)
The Lord said:
15 Seven weeks after you offer this bundle of grain, each family must bring another offering of new grain. 16Do this exactly 50 days later, which is the day following the seventh Sabbath. 17Bring two loaves of bread to be lifted up in dedication to me. Each loaf is to be made with yeast and with two kilograms of the finest flour from the first part of your harvest.
18At this same time, the entire community of Israel must bring seven lambs that are a year old, a young bull, and two rams. These animals must have nothing wrong with them, and they must be offered as a sacrifice to please me. You must also offer the proper grain and wine sacrifices with each animal. 19Offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and two rams a year old as a sacrifice to ask my blessing. 20The priest will lift up the rams together with the bread in dedication to me. These offerings are holy and are my gift to the priest. 21This is a day of celebration and worship, a time of rest from your work. You and your descendants must obey this law.
22 When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing around the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground. Leave it for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God!
The Festival of Trumpets
(Numbers 29.1-6)
23The Lord told Moses 24-25to say to the people of Israel:
The first day of the seventh month must be a day of complete rest. Then at the sound of the trumpets, you will come together to worship and to offer sacrifices on the altar.
The Great Day of Forgiveness
(Numbers 29.7-11)
26 The Lord God said to Moses:
27The tenth day of the seventh month is the Great Day of Forgiveness. It is a solemn day of worship; everyone must go without eating to show sorrow for their sins, and sacrifices must be burned. 28No one is to work on that day—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness, when sacrifices will be offered to me, so that I will forgive your sins. 29I will destroy anyone who refuses to go without eating. 30-31None of my people are ever to do any work on that day—not now or in the future. And I will wipe out those who do! 32This is a time of complete rest just like the Sabbath, and everyone must go without eating from the evening of the ninth to the evening of the tenth.
The Festival of Shelters
(Numbers 29.12-40)
33 The Lord told Moses 34to say to the community of Israel:
Beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, and continuing for seven days, everyone must celebrate the Festival of Shelters in honor of me. 35No one is to do any work on the first day of the festival—it is a time when everyone must come together for worship. 36For seven days, sacrifices must be offered on the altar. The eighth day is also to be a day of complete rest, as well as a time of offering sacrifices on the altar and of coming together for worship.
37I have chosen these festivals as times when my people must come together for worship and when animals, grain, and wine are to be offered on the proper days. 38These festivals must be celebrated in addition to the Sabbaths and the times when you offer special gifts or sacrifices to keep a promise or as a voluntary offering.
39Remember to begin the Festival of Shelters on the fifteenth day of the seventh month after you have harvested your crops. Celebrate this festival for seven days in honor of me and don't do any work on the first day or on the day following the festival. 40Pick the best fruit from your trees and cut leafy branches to use during the time of this joyous celebration in my honor. 41I command you and all of your descendants to celebrate this festival during the seventh month of each year. 42For seven days every Israelite must live in a shelter, 43so future generations will know that I made their ancestors live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
44This is how Moses instructed the people of Israel to celebrate the Lord's festivals.
translation_text:
Hɔpizizenaa la Kɔraawiizi n dauwɛ wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Hɔpizizenaa la iin niŋ ɔɔ chaali di ra di, di ra tɔgzi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii keŋ.
Heezaa Hɔpizii wia
3Hɔpizaa anumbɛllɛ ií ɔɔ kpa di hum huma, ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ iin niŋ ɔɔ kpa di chaali di jaami. Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa bɔr la maa iin niŋ du, u ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.
Gillikaali ni Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizenaa wia
4Anniibuu ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizizenaa, ií ɔɔ chaali di ra dia, saŋazi la miŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ ia la. 5Kɔraawiizi Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la daŋ ɔɔ faari lugli baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ hɔl duana wiizi aaih saŋa. 6A baagu hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔl ɔɔ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizeŋ dii faaraarɛ. Ií daŋ ɔɔ hee a paanuu hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 7A lugli hɔpizii, ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma. 8Ií ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ di lizi diwee mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. Ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa.’ ”
9Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 10“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Di ii wa zuu hɛri la minna nyiŋŋi n tɛɛ ia la, di wa kum ii pattikuna, ií lizi ii milugla la iiŋ kummɛ nyuuni di wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ. 11U daŋ kpaa di viigi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, n lɛɛa dikuu ii wia. N kizeehiŋ daŋ viigaabuu Heezaa Hɔpizichɔɔ hɔl. 12Hɔpizii la iiŋ viigi a minyuuni la, a dɛkkɔ iiŋ kpu pebii la n di biŋkpaŋ di du kpeg, di lizi mbusu fuuh tɛŋ, 13di kpa kookoo tassazi anɛɛ sau di ɛɛ ɔlivi nuu buua, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia di jaa u ni, di fuuh tɛŋ, a sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ. Ií daŋ kpa siŋ pirintua ni keza di jaa. 14Ií gilɛɛ waa di ii mifalaa maa, di a huurii gɛɛ a ɔɔzaarɛ gɛɛ baŋ kpaa ɔɔzi paanuu, see a hɔl la iiŋ kpa kuna naa di wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi mɔɔ. Guŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ, di tɛɛ ii naanna bɔr la maa ban niŋ du, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
Kuna Kumaa Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia
15Ií kur yauzi aniidaanɛ di lii baŋ di Heezaa Hɔpizii, ka hɔpizi la. A hɔllɛ ii ɔɔ kpa minyuuni, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa di wa tɛŋ la. 16Heezaa Hɔpizii aniidaanɛɛhiŋ har, ií kaa kur hɔpizaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, ka jaa lizi mifalaa di wa sunziŋ. 17Bɔr la maa iin duwɛɛ, ií ɔɔ kpa sakɔla kookoo tassazi anɛɛ ni yiisi di ɔɔzi paanuu anɛɛ, a ɛɛ diulugla mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa di wa tɛŋ. 18Ií ɔɔ lizi peballi aniidaanɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, nabalee, pebala anɛɛ la n kpekke ani mbusu lizaa mia ni siŋ mbusu, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ. 19Denii ií lizi bubal ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor ani pebizi anɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, á ɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa hor. 20N kizeehiŋ daŋ lalli a pebizi anɛɛ la ni diulugla paanuu la maa chiŋ n see, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa. A ɛɛ sunzinanaananaarɛ tɛŋ, di ɛɛ kizeehiŋ hor. 21Ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami a hɔl hiŋ ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa. Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ii naanna, bɔr la maa ban niŋ du di hanna la.
22Di ii ɔɔ waa kum ii kooliŋkuna, ií gilɛɛ waa kum ii kooni kɛraa gɛɛ di kaa bir har di ra kugni. Ií ɔɔ gilaa tɛɛ nyaara ni hɔɔhra. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.’ ”
Bensunoniinazi Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia
23Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 24“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ lugli hɔpizii, ií ɔɔ heezi, ka chaali dɔŋa di jaami di huuh bensunoniinazi werge. 25Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa ka ɔɔ lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.’ ”
Kɔraawiizi Baaŋfuuih Lizaa Hɔpizizeŋ wia
26Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 27“A baagu aniidaanɛɛhiŋ naa hɔpizaa fi hɔl daŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Baaŋfuuih Lizaa Hɔpizizeŋ. Ií ɔɔ chaali dɔŋa di jaami di vɔɔ nua ka lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛŋ. 28Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa a hɔl, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Baaŋfuuih Lizaa Nɛra Ni Hɔpizizenne, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia. 29Di nɛr maa waa haŋ wa vɔɔ nua a hɔl, ií duŋŋuu di lii u nɛra biini. 30N daŋ kpu nɛr la maa n niŋ hum huma a hɔl hiŋ di duŋŋuu u nɛra biini. 31Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa kɔrai. Guŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ tɛɛ ii naanna, bɔr la maa ban niŋ du di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. 32U ɛɛ heezaa ni nuuvɔɔi hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ ia. Di chi a baagu hɔpizaa kabɛl hɔl duana ni, di ga hel u hɔpizaa fi hɔl duana ninɛɛ, ii ɔɔ di a Heezaa Hɔpizii.”
Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia
33Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 34“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Baagu aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔllɛ Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ dii ra faari. Ii daŋ diu hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 35U lugli hɔpizii daŋ ɛɛ hɔpizii la iin niŋ ɔɔ chaali di jaami, ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa, a hɔl hiŋ. 36Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, ií ɔɔ ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ra tɛŋ hɔpizi biimaa, ka a hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl, ií kaa chaali jaami ka lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛŋ. Waabuu ii chaalaazi hɔpizaa maa tuna hiŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa.
37Anniibuu ɛɛ n Hɔpizizenaa la miŋ lizɛɛ, anla iin niŋ gil á ɛɛ ii chaalaazi hɔpizinanaa, ii ɔɔ ra ligzi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa di waa tɛŋ. Aabuu, mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, mbusu lizaa mia, siŋ ani mbusuzi la maa n dɛkkɛ hɔpizi biimaa. 38A mbusuzi naa lizaa daŋ jaa Kɔraawiizi Heezaa Hɔpizii mbusuzi lizaa, ii sunzaa mbusuzi lizaa, ii nuuzi lizaa ani ii kipar mbusuzi la iin ninna lizi ra tɛŋ la ni. 39Awia, di haŋ faari baagu aniidaanɛɛ hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔl, di ii wa chaali a hɛri pattikuna maa tuŋ, ií di a hɔpizizeŋ naa, hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. A lugli hɔpizii ni a hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ daŋ ɛɛ heezaa hɔpizaa. 40A lugli hɔpizii hɔl, ii daŋ kpa ii daazi nɔna la n wesse nɛnnɛ, di mɔnni abɛ paŋhoori ni daazi kela la, n dɔɔ paŋhoori nɛnnɛ di ra di iihinaa, di ra chɔliŋ ń see hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 41Ií ɔɔ ra di hɔpizizenaa naa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ binaa bina maa, di ra tɛŋ. Keŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ii ni ii naanna di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Ií ɔɔ ra diu baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ maa biini. 42Ií ɔɔ du ii pampannizi biine hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, di gilɛɛ waa lii chaaŋ. Izrɛl hina biilullaa maa ɔɔ du ba pampannizi biine, 43guŋ gil ii naanna zum lugɔ n faa gillɔɔ ii Izrɛl hina faa ra zuu pampannizi biine, saŋa la miŋ faa kpogli ia lii Ijip hɛri la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.’ ”
44Kennaabuu Moosis faa ɛɛ di dau hɔpizizenaa Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ba ra di, di ra tɔgzuu la.

english_text:
Caring for the Lamps
(Exodus 27.20,21)
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
You must supply the purest olive oil for the lamps in the sacred tent, so they will keep burning. 3-4Aaron will set up the gold lampstand in the holy place of the sacred tent. Then he will light the seven lamps that must be kept burning there in my presence, every night from now on. This law will never change.
The Sacred Bread
The Lord said:
5 Use your finest flour to bake twelve loaves of bread about two kilograms each, 6then take them into the sacred tent and lay them on the gold table in two rows of six loaves. 7Alongside each row put some pure incense that will be sent up by fire in place of the bread as an offering to me. 8Aaron must lay fresh loaves on the table each Sabbath, and priests in all generations must continue this practice as part of Israel's agreement with me. 9 This bread will always belong to Aaron and his family; it is very holy because it was offered to me, and it must be eaten in a holy place.
Punishment for Cursing the Lord
10-11Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri from the tribe of Dan, had married an Egyptian, and they had a son. One day their son got into a fight with an Israelite man in camp and cursed the name of the Lord. So the young man was dragged off to Moses, 12who had him guarded while everyone waited for the Lord to tell them what to do.
13Finally, the Lord said to Moses:
14This man has cursed me! Take him outside the camp and tell the witnesses to lay their hands on his head. Then command the whole community of Israel to stone him to death. 15-16And warn the others that everyone else who curses me will die in the same way, whether they are Israelites by birth or foreigners living among you.
17 Death is also the penalty for murder, 18but the killing of an animal that belongs to someone else requires only that the animal be replaced. 19Personal injuries to others must be dealt with in keeping with the crime— 20 a broken bone for a broken bone, an eye for an eye, or a tooth for a tooth. 21It's possible to pay the owner for an animal that has been killed, but death is the penalty for murder. 22 I am the Lord your God, and I demand equal justice both for you Israelites and for those foreigners who live among you.
23When Moses finished speaking, the people did what the Lord had told Moses, and they stoned to death the man who had cursed the Lord.
translation_text:
Fintinazi ni binnaa wia
