1When Moses had finished setting up the sacred tent, he dedicated it to the Lord, together with its furnishings, the altar, and its equipment. 2Then the twelve tribal leaders of Israel, the same men who had been in charge of counting the people, came to the tent 3with gifts for the Lord. They brought six strong carts and twelve oxen—one ox from each leader and a cart from every two.
4The Lord said to Moses, 5“Accept these gifts, so the Levites can use them here at the sacred tent for carrying the sacred things.”
6Then Moses took the carts and oxen and gave them to the Levites, 7-8who were under the leadership of Ithamar son of Aaron. Moses gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites for their work, and four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites for their work. 9But Moses did not give any to the Kohathites, because they were in charge of the sacred objects that had to be carried on their shoulders.
10On the day the altar was dedicated, the twelve leaders brought offerings for its dedication. 11The Lord said to Moses, “Each day one leader is to give his offering for the dedication.”
12-83So each leader brought the following gifts:
a silver bowl that weighed one and a half kilograms and a silver sprinkling bowl weighing almost a kilogram, both of them filled with flour and olive oil as grain sacrifices and weighed according to the official standards;
a small gold dish filled with incense;
a young bull, a full-grown ram, and a year-old ram as sacrifices to please the Lord;
a goat as a sacrifice for sin;
and two bulls, five full-grown rams, five goats, and five rams a year old as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing.
The tribal leaders brought their gifts and offerings in the following order:
On the first day
Nahshon from Judah,
on the second day
Nethanel from Issachar,
on the third day
Eliab from Zebulun,
on the fourth day
Elizur from Reuben,
on the fifth day
Shelumiel from Simeon,
on the sixth day
Eliasaph from Gad,
on the seventh day
Elishama from Ephraim,
on the eighth day
Gamaliel from Manasseh,
on the ninth day
Abidan from Benjamin,
on the tenth day
Ahiezer from Dan,
on the eleventh day
Pagiel from Asher,
on the twelfth day
Ahira from Naphtali.
84-88And so when the altar was dedicated to the Lord, these twelve leaders brought the following gifts:
12 silver bowls and 12 silver sprinkling bowls, weighing a total of almost 28 kilograms, according to the official standards;
12 gold dishes filled with incense and weighing over a kilogram;
12 bulls, 12 full-grown rams, and 12 rams a year old as sacrifices to please the Lord, along with the proper grain sacrifices;
12 goats as sacrifices for sin;
and 24 bulls, 60 full-grown rams, 60 goats, and 60 rams a year old as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing.
89Whenever Moses needed to talk with the Lord, he went into the sacred tent, where he heard the Lord's voice coming from between the two winged creatures above the lid of the sacred chest.
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi mbusu kuna lizaa wia
1Moosis n wa gillɛ ba baŋ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la tuŋ, u waaruubuu nuu, di lizi u ni u bɔmbɔga maa doŋa ha, a ɛɛ kunnanaananaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Guŋ himmaanii u ɛɛ mbusu lizibɔr la ni u kuna ani u tassazi maa. 2Denii Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi la n ɛɛ ba domeezi sitɔɔra, di kaa ɛɛ ba dizi sitɔɔra la, n kur baa la faa ba ba mbusuzi lizaa kuna ni. 3Torkozi anumbɛl baŋ tɔ kuna ani navargazi fidaanɛɛrɛ ba faa kpa ba. Aaron Puts the Gold Lamps in Place
1 The Lord said to Moses, 2“Tell Aaron to put the seven lamps on the lampstand so they shine toward the front.”
3Aaron obeyed and placed the lamps as he was told. 4The lampstand was made of hammered gold from its base to the decorative flowers on top, exactly like the pattern the Lord had described to Moses.
Instructions for Ordaining the Levites
5The Lord said to Moses:
6The Levites must be acceptable to me before they begin working at the sacred tent. So separate them from the rest of the Israelites 7and sprinkle them with the water that washes away their sins. Then have them shave their entire bodies and wash their clothes.
8They are to bring a bull and its proper grain sacrifice of flour mixed with olive oil. And they must bring a second bull as a sacrifice for sin.
9Then you, Moses, will call together all the people of Israel and send the Levites to my sacred tent, 10where the people will place their hands on them. 11Aaron will present the Levites to me as a gift from the people, so that the Levites will do my work.
12After this, the Levites are to place their hands on the heads of the bulls. Sacrifice one of the bulls for the forgiveness of sin, and the other to make sure that I am pleased. Then the Levites will be acceptable to me. 13They will stand at my altar in front of Aaron and his sons, who will dedicate the Levites to me.
14This ceremony will show that the Levites are different from the other Israelites and belong to me in a special way. 15After they have been made acceptable and have been dedicated, they will be allowed to work at my sacred tent. 16They are mine and will take the place of the first-born Israelite sons. 17 When I killed the oldest sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in each Israelite family would be mine, as well as every first-born male from their flocks and herds. 18But now I have chosen these Levites as substitutes for the first-born sons, 19and I have given them as gifts to Aaron and his sons to serve at the sacred tent. I will hold them responsible for what happens to anyone who gets too close to the sacred tent.
The Levites Are Dedicated to the Lord
20Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelites made sure that the Levites did everything the Lord had commanded. 21The Levites sprinkled themselves with the water of forgiveness and washed their clothes. Then Aaron brought them to the altar and offered sacrifices to forgive their sins and make them acceptable to the Lord. 22After this, the Levites worked at the sacred tent as assistants to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
23The Lord also told Moses, 24-25“Levites who are between the ages of 25 and 50 must work at my sacred tent. But once they turn 50, they must retire. 26They may help the other Levites in their duties, but they must no longer be responsible for any work themselves. Remember this when you assign their duties.”

1Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Kali Aarɔn lugɔ di u waa chiŋŋi fintinazi aniidaanɛɛ la, ú gil a ra chaani fintina daa la see.”
3Aarɔn chiŋŋaa gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis be la. 4Kenne ba faa kuari a fintina daa u du. Salinnɛ ba faa luu di kuari u zɛɛ di ga hel u kela nuuzi. Ba faa kuaruubuu gunla himmaa Kɔraawiizi n faa bagli Moosis la.
Levi dee kpai tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wia
5Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 6“Lizi Levi dee lii Izrɛl hina la biini, di lizi ba doŋa ha, bá ɛɛ nɛnanaa tɛŋ. 7Kenne í ɛɛ baa. Mizi baa nii la n na lizi doŋa, di gil ba fuŋ ba bɔra huna maa, di chag ba laala maa, guŋ gil ba ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be. 8Gil ba kpa nabalee ni sakɔla la baŋ koozi nuu, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia kuŋfuuhlii la n dɛkkɛ, di kaa kpa nabalee nɛɛhiŋ ge u ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor. 9Gil Izrɛl hina maa chaali n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see, di gil Levi dee chi u dominua. 10I daŋ gil Levi dee chi n see, di gil Izrɛl hina kpa ba nonee di sagzi ba ni. 11Aarɔn daŋ kpa Levi dee la tɛŋ alugɔ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa n lii Izrɛl hina be, di ɛɛ baa sirya, bá ra hum n huma.
12Di Levi dee la wa kpa ba nonee di sagzi nabala la nyuuni ni, kpa bɛl ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii, di lizi n baaŋfuuih ba ni, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia. 13Gil Levi dee la chi Aarɔn ni u biibaala see, í kpa baa tɛŋ alugɔ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii. 14Kenne í ɛɛ di bargi Levi dee la lii Izrɛl hina be di tɛŋ, bá ɛɛ n hora.
15Di i wa sɔ Levi dee la di lizi ba doŋa ha, ba ɛɛ nɛnanaa n be, di kpa baa tɛŋ lugɔ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii tuŋ, ba daŋ jaa ba, di waa hum ba huma n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. 16Baabuu Izrɛl hina la n niŋ kpa bahinaa tɛŋ, di ɛɛ n bɛŋ hora. N kpa baabuu di chɛr Izrɛl hina haaŋ maa biibambilugli. 17Biibambilugli maa n du Izrɛl, di neweere gɛɛ selle, u ɛɛ n hotte. Miŋ faa kpuuzi Ijip hina biibambilugla la, n faa lizi baabuu ba ɛɛ n hora. 18N jaa kpa Izrɛl hina biibambiluglaa di chɛr Levi dee la. 19Izrɛl hina la maa biini, Levi dee labuu n kpa sunzi Aarɔn ni u biibaala, bá ra hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini, di ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, di ra ligzi n baaŋfuuih ba ni dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, wiilchɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa lau baa di ba wa dugli n Tanti Dia Bɔnaniinanii la.”
20Moosis, Aarɔn ani Izrɛl hina maa faa ɛɛ Levi dee la gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la. 21Levi dee la faa sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, di chag ba laala. Denii Aarɔn jaa kpa baa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi alugɔ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii, di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih ba ni dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, ba jaa ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be. 22A guŋ harbɔɔ, Levi dee la jaa ba di wàá hum ba huma Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Aarɔn ni u biibaala ra binni ba ni. Ba faa kpa baabuu di ra hum gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.
23Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 24“Levi dee la maa n di binni tokko ni anue ani sagaa, niŋ ɔɔ ba di wàá hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. 25Di ba wa hel biini tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, a dɛkkɔɔ bá gil ba humazi. 26Ba daŋ wer hiini ba lulla di ra hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Ka ba gilɛɛ wa lɛɛ a huma di ra hum. Kenne í tɛɛ a Levi dee ba huma.”

english_text:
Regulations for Celebrating Passover
1 During the first month of Israel's second year in the Sinai Desert, the Lord had told Moses 2to say to the people, “Celebrate Passover 3in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.” 4-5Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
6Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron, 7“Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
8Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
9The Lord then told Moses 10to say to the community of Israel:
If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover. 11But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs, 12 and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
13But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
14Anyone, including foreigners who live among you, can celebrate Passover, if they follow all the regulations.
The Cloud over the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 40.34-38)
15-16As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it. 17-19The Lord used this cloud to tell the Israelites when to move their camp and where to set it up again. As long as the cloud covered the tent, the Israelites did not break camp. But when the cloud moved, they followed it, and wherever it stopped, they camped and stayed there, 20-22whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites. 23They obeyed the Lord's commands and went wherever he directed Moses.
translation_text:
Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia
1Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Moosis Sinaai Hɛribɔduma la biini. Ba Ijip hɛri lii binni anɛɛ lugli baagu biini, di ŋɔ, 2“Gil Izrɛl hina la ra di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la saŋa la miŋ dauwɛ la. 3Bá ra diu baagu naa hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl, di bɔr waa lauri siwee, di ra hiŋ u dii ŋmɛnizi ni u wiɛɛlaa maa gunla miŋ baglɛɛ la.”
4Awia, Moosis ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ bá di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la. 5Ba diu Sinaai Hɛribɔduma la biini, a baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl, di bɔr ra lauri siwee. A Izrɛl hina faa ɛɛ wiimaa gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.
6Ka baŋhina faa waa wette ba di a hɔpizii a hɔl, dikuu baŋ gbɔgzi lalii di doŋ wia. Awia, ba ba Moosis ni Aarɔn be a hɔl maa 7di wa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Yaa doŋŋoo dikuu yaa n gbɔgzi lalii wia, ka bɛɛ n baani yaa wàá wer jaa Izrɛl hina ni, di kpa yaa mbusu lizaa kuna di waa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi saŋa la baŋ dauwɛ lai?”
8Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ra kpaŋ ka n pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di zum gunla un niŋ ŋɔ ii wia.”
9Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 10“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, ‘Di ii bɛl maa gɛɛ ii naana bɛl maa wa doŋŋo dikuu uŋ gbɔgzi lalii wia gɛɛ di a hiŋ la ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ, ka u daŋ haa wer di a Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ hiŋ. 11Ba daŋ ɔɔ diubuu baagu nɛɛhiŋ la hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl, di bɔr waa lauri siwee la. Ba daŋ ɔɔ hee pebii la ol ni paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ ani tagkpola. 12A waa dɛkkɛ ban niŋ gil a ol yemmaa hɔɔ waa pizi gɛɛ di ku u hog bɛl maa. Di ba waa di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ, ba ra hiŋzi u widaulaa ni u wiɛɛlaa. 13Ka di baal maa waa doŋŋe mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, di waa ŋmɛnɛɛ ge laŋŋɛ, ka vɛɛ a hɔpizii dii, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini, dikuu uŋ waa u mbusu lizaa kuna kpawɛɛ wa tɛŋ saŋa la n dɛkkɛ la wia. A badee wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi u ni.
14Di hɔɔhri du ii biini ka ra nyiŋŋi ú di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ naa, u daŋ wer diu, ka a dɛkkɔɔ ú hiŋzi u dii ŋmɛnizi ni u widaulaa. Hɔɔhri ni bol bie maa danna hiŋ ŋmɛnikpannɛ.’ ”
Baama la n guali Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni wia
15A hɔl la baŋ kuari Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la, baama faa wa tɔ u ninɛɛ, di lii duana di ra ba chɔɔzi. 16Gunnɛ u faa haŋ du di ra la. Baama la ɔɔ faa ɛɛu lugɔ niŋ hamuŋa ni. 17Di baama la haŋ wa izi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni, Izrɛl hina ɔɔ bali ba kunaa di lii ra hiŋuu. Bɔr la maa uŋ wa chigɛ ba ɔɔ chɔɔ denii. 18Kɔraawiizii dɔɔ ba chɔɔi ni ba izaa fɔŋŋa. Saŋa la maa maga a baama n tɔ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni, guŋ magaa Izrɛl hina ge ɔɔ chɔɔ a bɔr. 19Di a baama wa guali u ni di birgi, Izrɛl hina ɔɔ sɛɛu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ra kpaŋuu. 20Saŋa bɛl ge, a baama ɔɔ guali u ninɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ, di Kɔraawiizi wa ŋɔ ba izi gɛɛ ba chɔɔ, gunnɛ ba ɔɔ ɛɛ. 21Saŋa bɛl ge a baama ɔɔ guali u ninɛɛ duana ni di ga hel chɔɔzi ka izi. Di u haŋ wa izi chɔɔzi ni, ba ge ɔɔ baluu lii di ra hiŋuu. Di a baama haŋ wa izi bɔchaaŋ gɛɛ hamuŋa, ba ge ɔɔ izuu di ra hiŋuu. 22Di a baama haŋ wa guali Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni hɔpizaa anɛɛ gɛɛ baagu kpaŋ gɛɛ biŋkpaŋ, Izrɛl hina ɔɔ du ba chɔɔri bɔttɛ. Ka di u haŋ wa izi, ba ge ɔɔ izuu. 23Di Kɔraawiizi haŋ wa ŋɔ bá chɔɔ gɛɛ bá izi, gunnɛ ba ɔɔ ɛɛ. Ba ɔɔ hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be di dau labuu.

english_text:
The Silver Trumpets
1The Lord told Moses:
2Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp. 3If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent. 4But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
5-6Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south. 7But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet. 8The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
9Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you. 10During the celebration of the New Moon Festival and other religious festivals, sound the trumpets while you offer sacrifices. This will be a reminder that I am the Lord your God.
The Israelites Begin Their Journey
11On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on. 12So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert. 13This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
14Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe, 15Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe, 16and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
17The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
18Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe, 19Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe, 20and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
21Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
22Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe, 23Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe, 24and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
25Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan, 26Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe, 27and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
28This was the order in which the Israelites marched each time they moved their camp.
29Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
30“No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
31“Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert. 32Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
33The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp. 34And the cloud always stayed with them.
35 Each day as the Israelites began their journey, Moses would pray, “Our Lord, defeat your enemies and make them run!” 36And when they stopped to set up camp, he would pray, “Our Lord, stay close to Israel's thousands and thousands of people.”
translation_text:
Saliŋhuŋŋu bensunozi wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Luu saliŋhuŋŋu di kuari bensunozi anɛɛ, di kpaa ra yir Izrɛl hina, ba ra chaali ani di ba waa nyiŋŋi izaa di la bɔfalii. 3Di ba haŋ wa kpau huuh anɛɛ hiŋ maa, Izrɛl hina la maa daŋ chaali i be n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua. 4Ka di kpaŋkpaŋ bɛnnɛ ba huuh, Izrɛl domeezi nabɔnzii niŋ chaali i see. 5Di ba haŋ wa huuh bensuno kakpaŋ, Izrɛl dizi la maa n chɔɔ wiifurii la daŋ izi di ra la. 6Di ba kaa wa huuh nɛɛhiŋ, banla n chɔɔ wiifurii nodig wiikakag la daŋ izi di ra la. A huuihrɛ ninna bagli lugɔ ba izaa helloo. 7Di i ɔɔ wa ŋɔ í chaali a nɛra maa, ɛɛ huuh a bensunozi anɛɛ hiŋ maa, ka a wiraazi kurgi.
8Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ n kizeehina labuu niŋ ɔɔ ra huuah. Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulaarɛ tɛɛ ii ni ii naanna maa. 9Di i ni i nɛra wàá lɔ ii dɔm la n na fir ia laal ii himmaa hɛri, ií huuh a bensunozi kakpaŋ. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum daŋ liizi ii wia di lɛɛ ia. 10Ií hinaa dii, ii hɔpizizenaa dii saŋazi ani Baagufalaa Dii Hɔpizaa la, ii daŋ ɔɔ huuah di du mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa kuna la ni, a ɛɛ wiliizaa ii be. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.”
Izrɛl hina n izee lii Sinaai Hɛribɔduma wia
11Binni anɛɛ, baagu nɛɛhiŋ la hɔpizaa tokko hɔl, Izrɛl hina n izee lii Ijip hɛri la, baama la izi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni. 12Denii Izrɛl hina izi Sinaai Hɛribɔduma di ra juuri, a baama jaa wa hel Paran Hɛribɔduma di chi. 13Ka ba lii de dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be di ŋɔ tɛɛ baa la wia.
14Juda dee ni sugezi la aŋhina ni ba tuutaa tɔ see. Aminadab biibaal Nasɔnnɛ faa ba nabɔma. 15Zuar biibaal Nɛtanɛl genii faa ra binni Isaka dee ni, 16Hɛlɔn biibaal Ɛliab ge ra binni Zɛbulɔn dee ni. 17Denii ba wil Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la, Gɛsɔn ni Mɛrari domeezi la n na chiu la, paaguu chi di lii ra vol.
18Rubin dee ni dizi la n ja ba ni, ni ba tuutaa kaa lii hiŋ. Sɛdur biibaal Ɛlizuruu faa ɛɛ ba nabɔma. 19Zurisadai biibaal Sɛlumiɛllɛ faa ɛɛ Simɛɔn dee la binni. 20Diwɛl biibaal Ɛliasaf ge faa ɛɛ Gad dee la nabɔma. 21Denii Kɔhaf domee la izi di kpa kunnanaananaa la chi di lii, di ra la. Gɛsɔn ni Mɛrari dizi labuu niŋ baŋzi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la mɔɔ ka Kɔhaf domee la haa ba.
22Ɛfram dee sugezi la ni ba tuuta ge kaa lii hiŋ. Amihud biibaal Ɛlisamaa faa ɛɛ ba nabɔma. 23Pɛdazur biibaal Gamaliɛllɛ faa ɛɛ Manasɛ dee nabɔma. 24Gidiɔni biibaal Abidannɛ faa ɛɛ Bɛnjamin dee nabɔma.
25Dan ni dizi la n chɔɔwɛ dugli baa la ge jaa lii ni ba tuuta. Amisadai biibaal Ahiɛzaa faa ɛɛ ba nabɔma. 26Ɔkran biibaal Pagiɛl genii faa ɛɛ Asɛ dee nabɔma. 27Ɛnan biibaal Ahira ge faa ɛɛ Naftali dee nabɔma. 28Gunnɛ Izrɛl sugezi la ɔɔ faa lii di hiŋzi dɔŋa di ra la.
29Denii Moosis ŋɔ u dakiah Hɔbab, n ɛɛ u hila baal Jɛtro n ɛɛ Midian hinuu biibaal be, “Yaa ra la bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ yaa labuu. A hiŋ yaa. Yaa daŋ ga kpoglii nɛnnɛ. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ nuarɛ lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina kunnanaa.”
30Hɔbab ŋɔ, “Akai, maa la. N daŋ bir kaali n himmaa hɛri ni n nɛra be.”
31Ka Moosis ŋɔ u be, “Gaafura, gilɛɛ waa gil yaa. Hinuu zum bɔr la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ya chɔɔ a hɛribɔduma biini. Hinuu yaa sitɔɔri. 32Di yaa nii laŋŋɔ, yaa nii daŋ bɔnni kunnanaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n niŋ tɛɛ yaa la.”
33Awia, ba izi lii Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ la zɛɛ. Levi dee la chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di tɔ ba see, ba vol hɔpizaa ahoro di ra nyiŋŋi bɔr, bá so di heezi. 34Kɔraawiizi baama la ɔɔ faa tɔ ba seere hɔpizaa saŋa di ba wa izi ba chɔɔribɔr.
35Di Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la haŋ waa lii, Moosis ɔɔ ŋɔu,
“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, izi chiŋ!
Gil i dɔma yaari,
di gil ba ra chɔ
di ba wa nai.”
36Di dakka la haŋ wa chi heezaa bɔr la, Moosis ɔɔ ŋɔ,
“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
bir ba Izrɛl hina la n kpillɛ werge maa,
ba wàá wer kur baa la be.”

english_text:
The Israelites Complain
1One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
2When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out. 3They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire.
The People Grumble about Being Hungry
4One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat! 5In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic. 6But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
7 The manna was like small whitish seeds 8-9 and tasted like something baked with sweet olive oil. It appeared at night with the dew. In the morning the people would collect the manna, grind or crush it into flour, then boil it and make it into thin wafers.
10The Israelites stood around their tents complaining. Moses heard them and was upset that they had made the Lord angry. 11He prayed:
I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people, 12but they're not my children. You told me to nurse them along and to carry them to the land you promised their ancestors. 13They keep whining for meat, but where can I get meat for them? 14This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself? 15If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life!
Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses
16The Lord said to Moses:
Choose 70 of Israel's respected leaders and go with them to the sacred tent. 17While I am talking with you there, I will give them some of your authority, so they can share responsibility for my people. You will no longer have to care for them by yourself.
18As for the Israelites, I have heard them complaining about not having meat and about being better off in Egypt. So tell them to make themselves acceptable to me, because tomorrow they will have meat. 19-20In fact, they will have meat day after day for a whole month—not just a few days, or even 10 or 20. They turned against me and wanted to go back to Egypt. Now they will eat meat until they get sick of it.
21Moses replied, “At least 600,000 grown men are here with me. How can you say there will be enough meat to feed them and their families for a whole month? 22Even if we butchered all our sheep and cattle, or caught every fish in the sea, we wouldn't have enough to feed them.”
23The Lord answered, “I can do anything! Watch and you'll see my words come true.”
24Moses told the people what the Lord had said. Then he chose 70 respected leaders and went with them to the sacred tent. While the leaders stood in a circle around the tent, Moses went inside, 25and the Lord spoke with him. Then the Lord took some authority from Moses and gave it to the 70 leaders. And when the Lord's Spirit took control of them, they started shouting like prophets. But they did it only this one time.
26Eldad and Medad were two leaders who had not gone to the tent. But when the Spirit took control of them, they began shouting like prophets right there in camp. 27A boy ran to Moses and told him about Eldad and Medad.
28Joshua was there helping Moses, as he had done since he was young. And he said to Moses, “Sir, you must stop them!”
29But Moses replied, “Are you concerned what this might do to me? I wish the Lord would give his Spirit to all his people so everyone could be a prophet.” 30Then Moses and the 70 leaders went back to camp.
The Lord Sends Quails
31Some time later the Lord sent a strong wind that blew quails in from the sea until Israel's camp was completely surrounded with birds, piled up about a meter high for many kilometers in every direction. 32The people picked up quails for two days—each person filled at least ten large baskets. Then they spread them out to dry. 33But before the meat could be eaten, the Lord became angry and sent a deadly disease through the camp.
34After they had buried the people who had been so greedy for meat, they called the place “Graves for the Greedy.”
35Israel then broke camp and traveled to Hazeroth.
translation_text:
Niŋ n lii Kɔraawiizi be wia
1A nɛra faa faari di ra nuumi dikuu ba anuula wia. Kɔraawiizi faa nuu, u baaŋ fuuh ba ni werge maa. Denii u gil niŋ wa zuu ba chɔɔribɔr la di di u kɛraa yeŋ. 2A nɛra n wa wiiwe tɛɛ Moosis, u suŋŋi wiizi, Kɔraawiizi nuu, di gil a niŋ dim. 3Awia, ba faa ra yir de Tabɛra, dikuubɛɛwiai, niŋ faa lii Kɔraawiizi benii di waa di ba baambaaŋ.
Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ Izrɛl hina zaahra wia
4Hɔɔhrijagazi la n du ba biini la faa faari di ra kɛlli diudumazi, guŋ gil Izrɛl hina gba faari di ra wii di ra ŋɔ, “Di yaa gba faa na ol, yaa daŋ hee! 5Yaa n faa du Ijip hɛri la, yaa faa na nyinnii di ra hee, di faa na kiime irizi, gaabu ani alibaasa iri bɛl banna yir galik di ra di. 6Ka filaŋkeŋwaa, lɔzi jaa ra kpu yaabuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa waa kaa na kummaa di ra di, di maana naa bɛŋ lɛi.”
7Maana la faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zule. 8A nɛra ɔɔ faa gaaguu chaalaa di namaa nam ni gɛɛ di chɔgaa tugree biini. Ba ɔɔ faa daalaabuu gɛɛ ba kpaa halli lugɔ maansa. A ɔɔ faa ɛɛu lugɔ baŋ kpa ɔlivi nuu di hallaa, di i daŋaa. 9Di sɔsɔŋ haŋ wa chol ba chɔɔribɔr hamuŋa, maana ge ɔɔ chogluu.
10Moosis faa nuu dia maa hina n na lɔɔgi wile ba tanti diini dominuuzi. Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh werge maa, Moosis lɔgɔ faa liiu. 11U pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, ɛrɛɛ mìŋ́ i balii ra di tɔɔrɔɔ kennei? Bɛɛ n ɛɛ di chɔgi i biini, i gil n na binni nɛra naa ninɛi? 12Minuu kpogli ba hizi di lul baa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ŋɔ ń kpogli baa lugɔ biifulli, di ra la hɛri la hiŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ, i daŋ kpa tɛɛ ba naabaala lai? 13Lee ń na ol tɛɛ nɛra naa maanɛi? Ba wiiwoo ra duŋ, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Tɛɛ yaa ol yá hee!’ 14N bɛŋ waa wer kpogli nɛra naa, ba tɔɔrɔɔ siili n ninɛɛ. 15Di kenne i ra ɛɛŋ, kpuŋ filaŋkennaa maa, di n wia kaa parii ge, gilɛɛ waa gil n na di tɔɔrɔɔ naa di wa siu.”
16Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Chaali Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi tokkoahoro ni fi, banla hiŋ zummɛ lugɔ ba ɛɛ nabɔnzi gɛɛ karchizenaa a nɛra biini. Gil bá ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, í ni baa wa chi de. 17N daŋ ba n nii ŋɔ wia de. N daŋ kpa n Duma la n du i ni la di du ba ni, bá hiinii di ra di nɛra naa tɔɔrɔɔ, í bɛŋ gilɛɛ kaa ra diu.
18Ŋɔ a nɛra be lugɔ bá sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be, di ra kpaŋ kɛrɛ, ii daŋ hee ol. N nuuwɔɔ baŋ wiiwe di ra ŋɔ lugɔ ba faa haŋ na ol ba daŋ hee, di kaa ŋɔ lugɔ, baŋ faa du Ijip la bɔ. Filaŋkeŋ, n daŋ tɛɛ baa ol bá hee. 19Hɔpizi kpaŋ gɛɛ anɛɛ gɛɛ anue gɛɛ fi gɛɛ tokko bɛŋ lɛi bá hee ol, 20ka baagu bitte bá heea, á jaa wàá sɔɔhri ba miibɔɔni di bazi baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba vɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n du ba be labuu, di wii ra ŋɔ, ‘Bɛɛ n baani yaa lii Ijip hɛri naanɛi?’ ”
21Ka Moosis ŋɔ, “Nɛra naa miŋ du ba be naa du kagboŋa bɔra kalfaanumbɛl, ka i ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ tɛɛ baa ol bá hee baagu bir.’ 22Ba daŋ wer na ol hee di piŋ, di yaa kpu yaa peeza, buuna ani nauna maa gɛɛ di yaa lauri muuzeŋ nyinni maa?”
23Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “N nyaa guŋ fɔŋŋaa waa? A binni, di wii la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la daŋ ɛɛ wibii gɛɛ di waa ɛɛ wibiiyei.”
24Awia, Moosis lii di kali a nɛra gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la. Di gil ba nabɔnzi tokkoahoro ni fi ba di wa chi bar Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la. 25Denii Kɔraawiizi tuu ba baama biini di wa ŋɔ wia, di kpa u Duma la n du Moosis ni la du ba ge ni. U Duma n wa zuu ba ni, ba faari di ra ŋɔ wia lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi, ka ba wàá ŋɔwɛɛ birgi.
26Ka baala banɛɛ naa, Ɛldad ni Mɛdad n faa dɛkkɛ ba jaa a nabɔnzi ni la, waa Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la laŋŋɛ, ka du ba chɔɔribɔra. Ka Kɔraawiizi Duma faa izi ba ge gba, ba faa ra ŋɔ wia lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi. 27Biipɔllii bɛl chɔ ba Moosis be, di wa ŋɔ lugɔ Ɛldad ni Mɛdad ra ŋɔ wiarɛ, lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi, ba chɔɔribɔra biini.
28Nun biibaal Josua la n na hiini Moosis di lii u pɔlaa saŋa maa la ŋɔ Moosis be, “N dɔɔri, ŋɔ ba be, bá gilɛɛ ra ɛɛ guŋ!”
29Ka Moosis bir ŋɔ, “I ra zomuu dikuu n wiaa? N kipattɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Duma izi u nɛra maa ni ba ɛɛ lugɔ dɔgtɛɛzi.” 30Denii Moosis ni a nabɔnzi bir la ba chɔɔribɔr la.
31Peu lii Kɔraawiizi be di duŋŋi zaahra lii muuzeŋ, a ba wa sagzi dɔŋa ni, di chɔɔ hɛri di la chiŋ lugɔ nogumzi anɛɛ, di du war lugɔ hɔpizikpaŋ volaa maga keŋkere maa hin niŋ ga. 32A hɔl hiŋ bɔchaaŋ ni hamuŋa ni hɔpizaa maa, a nɛra lii di ra paagaa. Bɛl maa hor paagaa tɔgzi ɛɛ lugɔ kookoo tassazi kagboŋ. Ba kpaa di wa pɛ a chɔɔribɔr maa. 33Ka baŋ wa faari a ola heei, di haa ra chaŋŋaa la, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh ba ni werge maa, u kpa wiilchɔgaa di ta ba ni. 34Dikuu guŋ wia, ba dau de sɔŋ Kibrɔf Hataava, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa hugzi nɛra la n na kɛlli diudumazi dii labuu de.
35A nɛra lii de di la Hazɛrɔf di ga du de.

english_text:
Miriam and Aaron Are Jealous of Moses
1-3 Although Moses was the most humble person in all the world, Miriam and Aaron started complaining, “Moses had no right to marry that woman from Ethiopia! Who does he think he is? The Lord has spoken to us, not just to him.”
The Lord heard their complaint 4and told Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to come to the entrance of the sacred tent. 5There the Lord appeared in a cloud and told Aaron and Miriam to come closer. 6Then after commanding them to listen carefully, he said:
“I, the Lord, speak to prophets
in visions and dreams.
7 But my servant Moses
is the leader of my people.
8He sees me face to face,
and everything I say to him
is perfectly clear.
You have no right to criticize
my servant Moses.”
9The Lord became angry with Aaron and Miriam. And after the Lord left 10and the cloud disappeared from over the sacred tent, Miriam's skin turned white with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her, 11he said to Moses, “Sir, please don't punish us for doing such a foolish thing. 12Don't let Miriam's flesh rot away like a child born dead!”
13Moses prayed, “Lord God, please heal her.”
14 But the Lord replied, “Miriam would be disgraced for seven days if her father had punished her by spitting in her face. So make her stay outside the camp for seven days, before coming back.”
15The people of Israel did not move their camp until Miriam returned seven days later. 16Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.
translation_text:
Miriam ni Aarɔn n na zɔɔzi Moosis wia
1Moosis haaŋ faa ɛɛ Itiopia hinuurɛ. Awia, Miriam ni Aarɔn faa ra zɔɔzi Moosis dikuu guŋ wia, 2di ra ŋɔ, “Moosis bɛmbɛŋ benii Kɔraawiizi faa ga di ra ŋɔ wiaa? U faa ga yaa gba benii di ra ŋɔ wia.” Kɔraawiizi faa nuu gunla banna ŋɔ la.
3Moosis faa ɛɛ sisɔna hinnɛ kaali nɛr maa durnya naa biini.
4Kakpaŋ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn ani Miriam be, “Ií nɛra bahoro naa maa lii ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la.” Awia, ba lii di ba de. 5Denii Kɔraawiizi du baama n du miriti di la chiŋ la biini, di tuu wa chi ba be u Tanti Dia dominua ka yir Miriam ni Aarɔn. Baŋ wa liwɛɛ chi, 6u ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu n wiŋɔzi.
Di n dɔgtɛɛ wa du ii biini,
aŋ kpa n hinnɛ
di ra bagluu
lugɔ deeza biini.
Aŋ ŋɔ wiarɛ di
ra tɛu deeza biini.
7Ka guŋ lɛi a du n balii Moosis waa be,
u wia dɔɔ wibiire n dia biini.
8N nuu ŋɔ wia di ra tɛɛ dɔŋa,
a chaani,
a waa ɔɔ ɛɛ wisuahlaa.
U ɔɔ na n duulaa.
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ɔnsii waa ia lauwɛi,
ii ra ŋɔ u wiai?”
9Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh ba ni, u lii ba be.
10Baama la n wa izi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni, ba ŋɔ ba binni di Miriam chigɔ, bɔchɔgaa lawuu, u huuhzi. Aarɔn bir u be di na lugɔ bɔchɔgaa lawuubuu. 11Aarɔn ŋɔ Moosis be, “N dɔɔri, gaafura, gil yaa gɛnni wichɔgaa naa yaa n ɛɛwɛ naa tɛɛ yaa. 12Gilɛɛ gil u ɛɛ lugɔ biifula la n siuwɛ di ra pɔɔh ka u maa luluu la!.”
13Awia, Moosis lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, jaande maa, chaau!”
14Kɔraawiizi bir ŋɔ Moosis be, “Di u mɛɛ faa pu nuuhaari du u siwee, u daŋ faa di hiihzi hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Gil ú du chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, a harbɔɔ í jaa gil ú bir zuu de.” 15Awia, ba faa gil Miriam du a chɔɔribɔr baŋgia hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. A nɛra faa waa de izee ka u saŋa wa hel, ba jaa izi.
16A harbɔɔ a nɛra lii Hazɛrɔf di ga chɔɔ Paran Hɛribɔduma.

Keenan hɛri daanaa na wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Hum baala baŋhina bá la ga gaagi di daani Keenan hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la di na. Lizi dee maa biini sitɔɔri kpaŋ.”
3Awia, Moosis faa hum a guŋ nɛra la lii Paran Hɛribɔduma biini gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u be la. Ba maa faa ɛɛ Izrɛl hina sitɔɔraa. 4Ba sɔnaa keŋ,
Rubin dee,
Zakur biibaal Samua.
5Simɛɔn dee
Hɔri biibaal Safat.
6Juda dee
Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb.
7Isaka dee,
Joosɛf biibaal Igal.
8Ɛfram dee,
Nun biibaal Hosia.
9Bɛnjamin dee,
Rafu biibaal Palti.
10Zɛbulɔn dee,
Gadiɛl biibaal Sodi.
11Manasɛ dee
Susi biibaal Gaddi.
12Dan dee,
Gɛmali biibaal Amiɛl.
13Asɛ dee,
Maikil biibaal Setur.
14Naftali dee,
Vɔfsi biibaal Nabi.
15Gad dee,
Maki biibaal Giwɛl.
16Banla Moosis n faa hummɛ bá ga gaagi dí daani a hɛri dí na sɔnaa guŋ. Denii Moosis faa bir dau Nun biibaal Hosia sɔŋ Josua.
17Moosis n faa hum baa di bá la ga gaagi di daani Keenan hɛri di na la, u faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií faari ɛŋ hɛribɔduma naa di ra la wiifurii nodig wiikakag Keenan hɛri giŋgimee bɔr. 18Ií pessi na gunla uŋ duwɛɛ, di kaa na di nɛra la n du de la kpekko gɛɛ ba waa kpegei, di ba kpillɔɔ gɛɛ ba waa kpilɛi? 19Bɛɛ hɛrdee biinii ba duɛi? U wessoo gɛɛ waa werei? Bolzeŋ bɛlaa dizi biinii ba duɛi? Ba ma koŋliikpegaa baraa gɛɛ a chɔɔ pɛɛrɛi? 20Ɛrɛɛ de hɛri duɛi? U summɔɔ gɛɛ waa summɛi? De dɔɔ daazii gɛɛ waa dɔɔwɛi? Ií ɛɛ ania maa ka tɔrgi a hɛri daazi nɔna aŋhina di ra ba.” A guŋ saŋaa ba ɔɔ faari di ra tɔrgi daazi la nɔna, banna yir grepuzi la.
21Denii ba faari Zin Hɛribɔduma di gaagi daani a hɛri guŋŋ, di ga lii Rɛhɔb di ra la Hamaf Ŋmɛnɛɛ barii. 22Ba ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di ga hel Hɛbrɔn la, Ahiman, Sɛsai ani Talmai domeezi la n faa ɛɛ Anak naanna, n duwɛɛ la. Ba faa tii bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn zɛɛrɛ, di mau so de guŋŋ binni aniidaanɛɛ mɔɔ, ka ba haa wa tii Zoan la n du Ijip hɛri la zɛɛ. 23Baŋ faa wa hel Ɛskɔl Waluu, ba ŋmɛŋ grepu daa kel kpaŋ la n dɔɔ nɔna nɛnnɛ. Ba kpa daa suu u baambaaŋ, ba nɛra banɛɛ kpau sag ba vaampɛrɛzi ni, di kpa nɔna aŋhina n lugɔ pomegranet ni figzi di jaa. 24Dikuu Izrɛl hina la n faa ŋmɛŋ a grepu daa kel nɔna de la wia, ba faa dau de sɔŋ Ɛskɔl Waluu. 25Ba faa gaagi di daani a hɛri guŋŋ hɔpizaa tokkoanɛɛ, ka bir ba.
26Ba la Moosis, Aarɔn ani Izrɛl hina la maa be, bɔr la banna yir Kadɛs n du Paran Hɛribɔduma biini la. Denii ba ŋɔ wii la maa baŋ ga nawɛɛ di tɛɛ baa, di kpa a hɛri daazi nɔna la di bagli baa. 27Kenne ba ŋɔ Moosis be, “Yaa zuu hɛri la hiŋ hum yaa la biinii, u summɔɔ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge! De daazi nɔnaa keŋ. 28Ka nɛra la n du de dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa werge maa, di ma koŋliikpega di bar ba bolzenaa. Haali yaa na Anak dee de. 29Amalɛk hina du de wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma. Hitti, Jɛbus ani Amɔri hina du u giŋgimee bɔr, ka Keenan hina ge du di dugli Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn ani Jɔɔdan muu la kɛraa.”
30Denii Kalɛb gil nɛra la maa siigi Moosis see, ka u ŋɔ, “Yá la ga foozi a hɛri dikuu yaa n niŋ wer ɛɛ guŋ wia.”
31Ka baala la u ni baa n la de la ŋɔ, “Yaa wàá lɔ a nɛra, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba kpekkoo kaali yaa.” 32Awia, ba lizi a hɛri wia amaniyekara di yaari Izrɛl hina la biini. Ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Hɛri la yaa n gaagɛɛ di daani na la hina ɛɛ lɔzimaa. Ba maa helloozi werge maa. 33Haali yaa na Anak naanna la n helle werge la de. Yaa na yaa hinaa di yaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ huuhni, di zum lugɔ gunnɛ ba gba na yaa n duwɛɛ.”

english_text:
The Israelites Rebel against Moses
1After the Israelites heard the report from the twelve men who had explored Canaan, the people cried all night 2and complained to Moses and Aaron, “We wish we had died in Egypt or somewhere out here in the desert! 3Is the Lord leading us into Canaan, just to have us killed and our women and children captured? We'd be better off in Egypt.” 4Then they said to one another, “Let's choose our own leader and go back.”
5Moses and Aaron bowed down to pray in front of the crowd. 6Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes in sorrow 7and said:
We saw the land ourselves, and it's very good. 8If we obey the Lord, he will surely give us that land rich with milk and honey. 9 So don't rebel. We have no reason to be afraid of the people who live there. The Lord is on our side, and they won't stand a chance against us!
10The crowd threatened to stone Moses and Aaron to death. But just then, the Lord appeared in a cloud at the sacred tent.
Moses Prays for the People
11The Lord said to Moses, “I have done great things for these people, and they still reject me by refusing to believe in my power. 12So they will no longer be my people. I will destroy them, but I will make you the ancestor of a nation even stronger than theirs.”
13-16 Moses replied:
With your mighty power you rescued your people from Egypt, so please don't destroy us here in the desert. If you do, the Egyptians will hear about it and tell the people of Canaan. Those Canaanites already know that we are your people, and that we see you face to face. And they have heard how you lead us with a thick cloud during the day and flaming fire at night. But if you kill us, they will claim it was because you weren't powerful enough to lead us into Canaan as you promised.
17Show us your great power, Lord. You promised 18 that you love to show mercy and kindness. And you said that you are very patient, but that you will punish everyone guilty of doing wrong—not only them but their children and grandchildren as well.
19You are merciful, and you treat people better than they deserve. So please forgive these people, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.
20Then the Lord said to Moses:
In answer to your prayer, I do forgive them. 21 But as surely as I live and my power has no limit, 22-23I swear that not one of these Israelites will enter the land I promised to give their ancestors. These people have seen my power in Egypt and in the desert, but they will never see Canaan. They have disobeyed and tested me too many times.
24 But my servant Caleb isn't like the others. So because he has faith in me, I will allow him to cross into Canaan, and his descendants will settle there.
25Now listen, Moses! The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valleys of Canaan. And tomorrow, you'll need to turn around and head back into the desert toward the Red Sea.
The Israelites Are Punished for Complaining
26The Lord told Moses and Aaron 27-28to give this message to the people of Israel:
You sinful people have complained against me too many times! Now I swear by my own life that I will give you exactly what you wanted. 29 You will die right here in the desert, and your dead bodies will cover the ground. You have insulted me, and none of you men who are over 20 years old 30will enter the land that I solemnly promised to give you as your own—only Caleb and Joshua will go in.
31You were worried that your own children would be captured. But I, the Lord, will let them enter the land you have rejected. 32You will die here in the desert! 33 Your children will wander around in this desert 40 years, suffering because of your sins, until all of you are dead. 34I will punish you severely every day for the next 40 years—one year for each day that the land was explored. 35You sinful people who ganged up against me will die here in the desert.
36Ten of the men sent to explore the land had brought back bad news and had made the people complain against the Lord. 37So he sent a deadly disease that killed those men, 38but he let Joshua and Caleb live.
The Israelites Fail To Enter Canaan
(Deuteronomy 1.41-45)
39The people of Israel were very sad after Moses gave them the Lord's message. 40So they got up early the next morning and got ready to head toward the hill country of Canaan. They said, “We were wrong to complain about the Lord. Let's go into the land that he promised us.”
41But Moses replied, “You're disobeying the Lord! Your plan won't work, 42-43so don't even try it. The Lord refuses to help you, because you turned your backs on him. The Amalekites and the Canaanites are your enemies, and they will attack and defeat you.”
44But the Israelites ignored Moses and marched toward the hill country, even though the sacred chest and Moses did not go with them. 45The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down from the hill country, defeated the Israelites, and chased them as far as the town of Hormah.
translation_text:
A nɛra nuumaa wia
1A nɛra maa chɛɛhgi werge guŋŋ a hamuŋa maa. 2Ba maa nuumi di ra du Moosis ni Aarɔn, di ŋɔ ba be, “Di yaa faa siuzi Ijip hɛri gɛɛ a hɛribɔduma biini faa bɔ! 3Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi ra ba yaa ni hɛri naa biini, ba wa kpu yaa laal biiniaa? Ba daŋ lauri yaa haana ni biizi. Yaa n bittɛ kaali Ijip hɛri waa bɔɔ?” 4Ba ŋɔ dɔŋa be, “Yá lizi sitɔɔri yaa biini, di bir kaali Ijip hɛri.”
5Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn giŋŋi Izrɛl hina la maa n chaalɛɛ la see. 6Nun biibaal Josua ani Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb la n faa jaa banla n gaagɛɛ di daani a hɛri la, piili ba laala dikuu biinichɔg wia. 7Ka ŋɔ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la maa n chaali de la be, “Hɛri la yaa n gaagi u biini di daanuu na la wessoo werge maa. 8Di yaa wia par Kɔraawiizi, u daŋ tɔ yaa see, di lɛɛ hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la tɛɛ yaa. 9Ií gilɛɛ ra di Kɔraawiizi mmɔri. Di gilɛɛ ra ɔm a hɛri nɛra, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa daŋ kpegli baa. Kuna la baŋ kpawɛɛ di guu bahinaa la maa kaalɔɔrɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi du yaa benii. Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm baa tama maa.”
10Ka a nɛra maa faa ra nyiŋŋi bá paagi bia lɔɔzi baa kpuuzi. Denii Kɔraawiizi girme tuu ba U Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la ni di ra nyɛgzi lugɔ dooŋ Izrɛl hina la maa be. 11Awia Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ɛrɛɛ nɛra naa gbɛlliŋ di birgi magɛi? Ɛrɛɛ ba vɛɛ n yardaa di birgi magɛi, haali miŋ ɛɛ wizenaa ba biinei? 12N daŋ kpa wiilchɔgii di ta ba ni di tuŋ baa, ka n daŋ gil i dee wazi werge maa di birgi hɛrzeŋ hina, dí dɔɔ fɔŋŋa kaali baa.”
13Moosis ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Ijip hɛri hina daŋ nuu guŋ wia! I kpa i fɔŋŋaa di lizi nɛra naa lii ba biini. 14Ba daŋ ŋɔa tɛɛ hɛri naa hina. Ba teŋ nuuwɔɔ alugɔ hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi du nɛra naa benii, i nii baa ra ŋɔ wia di lii baama la n du miriti di la chiŋ, di guali ba ni la biini. I ɔɔ gilluu a baama tɔ ba see bɔchaaŋ maga, di gil niŋ tɔ ba see hamuŋa. 15Di i gillɔ nɛra naa maa siu kakpaŋ, hɛssi la hina maa n niŋ nuu a keŋ wia naa daŋ ŋɔ, 16‘Kɔraawiizi waa wette kpogli nɛra naa, di ba hɛri la uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua, di tɛɛ baa la biini. Awiarɛ u kpu baa hɛribɔduma biini la.’
17Awia, n Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, bagli yaa i fɔŋŋa di ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔ nua saŋa la hiŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ, 18‘Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ waa fuuh manaŋ. N dɔɔ nɔŋŋaarɛ di gil nɛra wichɔgaa ni ba dignikpega di ra tɛɛ baa. Ka màá ɔɔ gil bilchɔg hina dignitɛraa. N ɔɔ tɛr biizi dignaa dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia di ga hel ba naanatɛɛri.’ 19Dikuu i nɔŋŋaa werge wia gil nɛra naa wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa, gunla hiŋ faa gillɛ di ra tɛɛ baa di lii saŋa la maa baŋ lii Ijip hɛri di wa lii ni zinaa la.”
20Kɔraawiizi bir ŋɔ, “N gillɔɔ tɛɛ baa gunla hiŋ suŋŋɛɛ la. 21Haali ani a maa, n lɔ bampiriire di hɛɛhzi lugɔ miŋ du de, n girme su durnya biini maa naa, 22nɛra naa na n de dui girme nyɛgzaa ni wizenaa la miŋ ɛɛwɛ Ijip hɛri ani hɛribɔduma biinii, ka ba ɛɛŋ di na bukpilakpila maa, di vɛɛ n tɔgzaa awia ba bɛl maa wàá du de ni miibɔɔ di zuu a hɛri. 23Ba bɛl maa wàá na hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ba naabaala la. Nɛr la maa n gbɛlliŋ wàá nau. 24Ka dikuu n balii Kalɛb manni n kuttɛ, u ra hiŋiŋ ni u biini maa wia, n daŋ kpogluu zuu hɛri la uŋ gaagɛɛ di daanuu na la biini. U naanna daŋ dɔɔu. 25Amalɛk ni Keenan hina n du a walli biini wia, ií bir har kɛrɛ di chaŋ a hɛribɔduma, di hiŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Muuzeŋaahmu la.”
26Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, 27“Ɛrɛɛ biinikpola hina naa nuumaa birgi magɛi? N nuu gunla Izrɛl hina naa n nuumɛɛ di ra dumbuu. 28Awia, ŋɔ ba be, ‘N lɔ bampiriire di hɛɛhzi lugɔ miŋ du de wia, n daŋ dau ia gunla himmaa miŋ nuuwɛ iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. 29Ií daŋ siuzi di yaari hɛribɔduma naa biini maa. Dikuu iiŋ nuumɛɛ di ra duŋ wia, di haŋ chi ii banla maa n di binni tokko ka ra sag, ba kur ia la maanii niŋ siuzi. 30Ií bɛl maa wàá zuu hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ lugɔ ń tɛɛ ia la, see Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb ani Nun biibaal Josua. 31Ka ii biizi la iiŋ ŋɔ ba daŋ lɔ baa laal di lauri la, n daŋ kpogli baa di ba a hɛri la iiŋ vɛɛwɛ la, ba wa di u suma. 32Ka iawaa daŋ siuzi hɛribɔduma naa biini. 33Ii biizi daŋ du ɛŋ di ra bar guŋŋ binni tokkoanɛɛ, di di tɔɔrɔɔ guŋŋ dikuu ii wibii nyaai wia, di ra ba saŋa la ii tuna hiŋ n niŋ siu hɛribɔduma naa biini. 34Ii daŋ di a guŋ tɔɔrɔɔ binni tokkoanɛɛ. Bina maa daŋ chi tɛɛ hɔpizaa tokkoanɛɛ la kpaŋkpaŋ maa iiŋ kpawɛɛ di gaagi di daani a hɛri la. Denii ii di ii wichɔgaa tɔɔrɔɔ di zum gunla n nɛtɔɔraa n duwɛɛ.’ 35Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ n daŋ kpa wia naa ɛɛ biinikpola hina naa, n chaalɛɛ di ra diŋ mmɔri naa wibii maa. Ba tunaa hɛribɔduma naa biini.”
36Nɛra la Moosis n faa hummɛ bá la ga gaagi di daani a hɛri di na la n bittɛ ba, di wa tɛɛ amaniyekara a hɛri wia, di gil a nɛra maa nuumi ra du Moosis la, 37Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ wiilchɔgii bɛl chol ba ni, ba siuzi. 38Banla maa n faa laŋŋɛ ga daani a hɛri na la, Nun biibaal Josua ni Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb bɛnnɛ faa kawɛɛ.
39Denii Moosis n wa bagli a wia naa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa, ba faa wiiwoo werge. 40Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzimpikke ni, ba izi di chaŋ de giŋgimee hɛri di ra ŋɔ, “Yaa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. Yaa daŋ la bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ nua u wia la.”
41Ka Moosis faa ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii waa Kɔraawiizi widaulii ra hiŋɛi? Ii wiɛɛlaa naa wàá wer na ɛɛi! 42Ií gilɛɛ waa la, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi waa ii be duwɛɛ. Ii dɔma daŋ kpegli ia. 43Di ii haŋ la, Amalɛk ni Keenan hina la daŋ lɔ ia laal di kpuuzi ia. Kɔraawiizi wàá du ii be, dikuu iiŋ bir har kpuu wia.”
44Ka ba faa haa di mmɔri di chaŋ de giŋgimee hɛri di ra la, haali Moosis gɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la n faa waa naa kpuzɛɛ lii ba chɔɔribɔr la biini gba. 45Denii Amalɛk ni Keenan hina la n faa du de la faa chem ba ni, di lɔ baa laal, di kpegli baa, haali di faa duŋŋi baa di ga hel bolzeŋ Hɔma la.

english_text:
Laws about Sacrifices
1The Lord told Moses 2to give the Israelites the following laws about offering sacrifices:
3Bulls or rams or goats are the animals that you may burn on the altar as sacrifices to please me. You may also offer sacrifices voluntarily or because you made a promise, or because they are part of your regular religious ceremonies. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices is pleasing to me.
4-5If you sacrifice a young ram or goat, you must also offer a kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil as a grain sacrifice. A liter of wine must also be poured on the altar.
6-7And if the animal is a full-grown ram, you must offer two kilograms of flour mixed with one and a half liters of olive oil. One and a half liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
8If a bull is offered as a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, 9you must offer three kilograms of flour mixed with two liters of olive oil. 10Two liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
11-13If you are a native Israelite, you must obey these rules each time you offer a bull, a ram, or a goat as a sacrifice. 14And the foreigners who live among you must also follow these rules. 15-16 This law will never change. I am the Lord, and I consider all people the same, whether they are Israelites or foreigners living among you.
17-19When you eat food in the land that I am giving you, remember to set aside some of it as an offering to me. 20From the first batch of bread dough that you make after each new grain harvest, make a loaf of bread and offer it to me, just as you offer grain. 21All your descendants must follow this law and offer part of the first batch of bread dough.
22-23The Lord also told Moses to tell the people what must be done if they ever disobey his laws:
24If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin. 25Then the priest will pray and ask me to forgive you. And since you did not mean to do wrong, and you offered sacrifices, 26the sin of everyone—both Israelites and foreigners among you—will be forgiven.
27 But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin. 28The priest will then ask me to forgive you, and your sin will be forgiven.
29The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
30-31But if one of you does wrong on purpose, whether Israelite or foreigner, you have sinned against me by disobeying my laws. You will no longer belong to my people.
A Man Put to Death for Gathering Firewood on the Sabbath
32Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath. 33He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community. 34But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
35Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!” 36So he was killed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Tassels on the People's Clothes
37The Lord told Moses 38 to say to the people of Israel, “Sew tassels onto the bottom edge of your clothes and tie a blue string to each tassel. 39-40These will remind you that you must obey my laws and teachings. And when you do, you will be dedicated to me and won't follow your own sinful desires. 41I am the Lord your God who led you out of Egypt.”
translation_text:
Mbusuzi lizaa Gbɔgni wia
1Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, ‘Di ii wa zuu hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tɛɛ ia ii so de la, 3di ii waa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa di ra lii ii nauna gɛɛ ii peeza gɛɛ ii buuna biine, di ra tɛŋ, a sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ la, di a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa gɛɛ mbusuzi lizaa gɛɛ nuuzi lizaa gɛɛ kipar gɛɛ hɔpizizenaa dii horaa, 4unla n na lizi a sel di waa tɛŋ la, daŋ kpa sakɔla kookoo tassa suul la baŋ kpa ɔlivi nuu pirintua ni keza di koozaa, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia. 5Ií ɔɔ kpa siŋ pirintua ni keza di jaa a peezi la n ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii gɛɛ a mbusu lizaa kuna ni, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa siŋ.
6Ií kpa sakɔla kookoo tassazi anɛɛ suul, di barguu bɔra fi, di kpa a bɔra anɛɛ di koozi nuu pirintuani anɛɛ ni di jaa pebal la ni, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia, 7ani siŋ pirintuani anɛɛ suul, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa siŋ di jaa. Fuuah, á sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ.
8Di ii wa kpa nabalee di ra lizi mbusu ii fuuh gɛɛ nua lizaa mbusu gɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa, di ra tɛŋ, 9ií ɔɔ kpa mbusu lizaa mia sakɔla kookoo tassazi ahoro suul, di barguu bɔra fi, di kpa a bɔra ahoro di koozi ɔlivi nuu pirintuani ahoro ni di jaa. 10Di kaa kpa siŋ pirintuani ahoro, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa siŋ. A daŋ ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ. 11Anniibuu ií ɔɔ kpa di jaa nabal gɛɛ pebal gɛɛ pebii gɛɛ bupɔl bɛl maa ni, gunnɛ ií ɔɔ ra ɛɛ. 12Di sela wa kpillɔ, gunnɛ ií ɔɔ kuari bɛl maa.
13Nɛr la maa n ɛɛ ii biilullii, a dɛkkɔɔ ú ɔɔ ra ɛɛ wia naa, di u waa ba mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ kuna ni ú wa tɛŋ. 14Saŋa maa, di hɔɔhri gɛɛ nɛr la maa n du ii be, ŋmɛnɛ maa waa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ di ra tɛŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ ú ɔɔ ɛɛ gunla himmaa iiŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ la. 15Widaulii naa chɔɔwɔɔ tɛɛ ii naanna di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Ii ni hɔɔhra maa daŋ ɛɛ kpaŋ n be. 16Ii ni hɔɔhra la maa n du ii be la maa danna hiŋ a Gbɔgni naa.’ ”
17Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 18“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Di ii wa zuu hɛri la miŋ kpogli ia di ra la la biini, 19di ra di a hɛri diwee, ií lizi a yeŋ, á ɛɛ n hor, ií kpa di wa tɛŋ. 20Ií ɔɔ kpa ii milugla di nam, di ɔɔzi paanuu, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa la n lii pila, di wa tɛŋ. 21Ii naanna maa daŋ ɔɔ ra lizi guŋ mbusu naa di waa tɛŋ.
22Aŋhinabe di nɛbɛl waa kuttɛɛ vɛɛ Gbɔgni naa bɛl maa miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis naa hiŋaa, 23di haŋ lii a hɔl la miŋ kpaa tɛu la, di hanna la ii naanna saŋa, 24di keŋ wa ɛɛwɔɔ ka a nɛra maa waa zummɛ, guŋwaa, a nɛra maa daŋ lizi nabalee, di lizi mbusu di fuuuh tɛŋ, ú sɔɔh du sum di ra pariŋ, di kpa mia ni siŋ di lizi mbusu la n dɛkkɛ ani bubal, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor di jaa. 25N kizeehiŋ daŋ lizi mbusu di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih Izrɛl hina ni, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, ń gil tɛɛ baa, dikuu baŋ waa kuttɛɛ, ka lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ani wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa la wia. 26N daŋ gil tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ni hɔɔhra la maa n du ba be la, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɛra maanii jaa a wichɔgaa la baŋ waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ hiŋ biini.
27Ka di nɛkpannɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa ka waa kuttɛɛ, ú kpa bulor la n di biŋkpaŋ di wa lizi u wichɔgaa mbusu. 28N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpau di lizi n baaŋfuuih dikuu u wichɔgaa la uŋ waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ la wia, di sɛɛ chɔgri tɛu. Di u wa lizi n baaŋfuuih nɛra ni mbusu la, n daŋ gil tɛu. 29A Gbɔg naa chɔɔwɔɔ tɛɛ nɛr la maa n niŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa la uŋ waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ, di u ɛɛ Izrɛl hinuurɛ gɛɛ di u ɛɛ hɔɔhrii.
30Ka nɛr la n kuttɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di Izrɛl hinuurɛ gɛɛ hɔɔhrii, u gbɛlli mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii, a dɛkkɔɔ bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. 31Dikuu uŋ gbɛlli n wiŋɔɔlii di chɔgi n widaulaa wia, a dɛkkɔɔ bá lizi a hindee u nɛra biini wibii maa. U wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi u ni.’ ”
Heezaa Hɔpizii chɔgri kpui wia
32Saŋa la Izrɛl hina n faa haa du hɛribɔduma biini la, denii ba na baal bɛl n faa ra nyiŋŋi daazi Heezaa Hɔpizii la. 33Banla n faa nau la kpogluu di ba Moosis ni Aarɔn ani Izrɛl hina la maa be, 34ba tɔu dia, dikuubɛɛwiai, gunla ban niŋ ɛɛu, faa haa waa chaanɛɛ nɛnnɛ ba be. 35Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis be, “A baal dɛkkɔɔ uŋ siuwɛ. Á nɛra lawuu lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu.” 36Awia, a nɛra faa lawuu lii ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ baŋgia, di paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa dauwɛ tɛɛ Moosis la.
Yɔɔza nyɛraa du bɔmbɔga ni wia
37Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 38“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, bá kuari yɔɔza di kpa gessiburgu di nyɛraa du ba bɔmbɔga nuuzi. Gunnɛ bá ɔɔ ra ɛɛ saŋaa saŋa maa. 39A yɔɔzaa niŋ ɔɔ ra bir ia liize, di ii ɔɔ wa naa saŋa maa, ii daŋ ɔɔ ra liizi n widaulaa di ra kpaa girme. Denii ii wàá bir har kpuŋ ka ra ɛɛ ii himmaa kipar. 40A yɔɔza daŋ ɔɔ ra bir ia liize, ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa maa, ií ɛɛ n bɛmbɛŋ hora. 41Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n kpogli ia lii Ijip hɛri, ii waa humiŋ la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

english_text:
Korah, Dathan, and Abiram Lead a Rebellion
1-2 Korah son of Izhar was a Levite from the Kohathite clan. One day he called together Dathan, Abiram, and On from the Reuben tribe, and the four of them decided to rebel against Moses. So they asked 250 respected Israelite leaders for their support, and together they went to Moses 3and Aaron and said, “Why do you think you're so much better than everyone else? We're part of the Lord's holy people, and he's with all of us. What makes you think you're the only ones in charge?”
4When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray. 5Then he said to Korah and his followers:
Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
6-7Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
8-9You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want? 10The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest. 11You and your followers have rebelled against the Lord, not against Aaron.
12Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come! 13It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around! 14You keep promising us rich farmlands with fertile fields and vineyards—but where are they? Stop trying to trick these people. No, we won't come to see you.”
15Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
16Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent. 17Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
18The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent. 19Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders.
When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory 20and said to Moses and Aaron, 21“Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
22But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
23The Lord answered Moses, 24“Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
25Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed. 26Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.” 27So everyone moved away from those tents, except Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and their families.
28Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know: 29If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me. 30But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
31As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up 32-33and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
34The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
35Suddenly the Lord sent a fire that burned up the 250 men who had offered incense to him.
36Then the Lord said to Moses, 37“Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred, 38because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
39Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar, 40just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers.
The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
41The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
42As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent. 43So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent, 44 where the Lord said to them, 45“Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.”
They immediately bowed down and prayed. 46Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
47-48Aaron did exactly what he had been told. He ran over to the crowd of people and stood between the dead bodies and the people who were still alive. He placed the incense on the pan, then offered it to the Lord and asked him to forgive the people's sin. The disease immediately stopped spreading, and no one else died from it. 49But 14,700 Israelites were dead, not counting those who had died with Korah and his followers.
50Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_text:
Kɔra, Datan ani Abiram wia
1Izhar biibaal Kɔra n ɛɛ Kɔhaf naanna di lii Levi dee biini ani Rubin dee nɛra baŋhina, Datan ani Abiram n ɛɛ Ɛliab biibaala ani Pɛlɛf biibaal Ɔɔn, faa izi di ra di Moosis hɔɔzi. 2Awia, ba ŋɔ Izrɛl hina domeezi nabɔnzi kalfaanɛɛ ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi jaa ba ni. Ba faa lizi baabuu bá tɔ Izrɛl hina see. 3Ba faa chaali ba, ba wa karsi Moosis ni Aarɔn di faa ŋɔ ba be, “Ii wiɛɛlaa nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ werge! Nɛra naa maa ɛɛ nɛnanaananaarɛ, ba bɛl maa waa kawɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi ge du ba be. Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii lizi iihinaa di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra nabɔnzɛi?”
4Moosis n wa nuu guŋ, u chol pi di suŋŋi wiizi, 5ka ŋɔ Kɔra ni u hiŋra maa be, “Kɛrɛ chɔɔzi, Kɔraawiizi daŋ bagli yaa unla n ɛɛ ú hor di ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii, di gil nɛr la un niŋ lizi tuzi heluu. 6Kenne hiŋ Kɔra ni i hiŋra maa ɛɛ. Ií kpa nimbuurikuna 7kɛrɛ chɔɔzi ni buu niŋ di kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma du a ni Kɔraawiizi see. Baal la maa Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lizi, waabuu nɛnaniinanii. Ii Levi dee ɛɛ wiarɛ nyaŋŋi!”
8Moosis faa kaa ŋɔ Kɔra be, “Ii Levi dee! Ií ra nuu! 9Amɔ, ii siwee waa suwee Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, n lizi ia lii a nɛra maa biini, di kpogli ia ba ii wa dugluu di ra hum u huma u Tanti Dia la biini, di ɔɔ chi a nɛra see di ra hum baa? 10U kpogli ii ni ii dɔŋahina Levi dee maanii ba, ií dugluu, ka filaŋkeŋ ii kaa ra nyiŋŋuu ií lɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina huma gba di jaa. 11Kɔraawiizii ii ni ii hiŋra ra naa dikuu iiŋ chaalɛɛ ɛɛ nuukpaŋ wia. Anɛɛ Aarɔn lugɔ ii ra nuumi di ra duuwɛi?”
12Denii Moosis yir Datan ni Abiram. Ka ba ŋɔ, “Yaa wàá ba! 13A wɛɛ kukkɛɛ hiŋ kpogli yaa lii Ijip hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la, di ba hɛribɔduma naa biini, í wa kpuuzia? Ka filaŋkeŋ i ra nyiŋŋi í dɔɔri yaaa? 14Di kaa kpa jaa, haa yaa ni ballɛ hɛri la n summɛ di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la biini gɛɛ di tɛɛ yaa patti hɛssi ni grepu daazi kooni. I ŋɔ í tɔ nɛra naa siweere gɛɛ? Akai, yaa wàá ba!”
15Denii Moosis baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Gilɛɛ wàá lɛɛ ba mbusu lizaa kuna. Maa kummaa lɛɛwɛ lii ba be lugɔ kawee gba, gɛɛ di ɛɛ wii bɛl di leu ba bɛl maa ni.”
16Moosis ŋɔ Kɔra be, “I ni i hiŋra ni Aarɔn maa ba Kɔraawiizi see kɛrɛ. 17Baal maa kpa u nimbuurikuŋ di ɛɛ daahɛgsɔɔhsuma du u biini, a maa daŋ ɛɛ nimbuurikuna kalfaanɛɛ ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, di wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. I ni Aarɔn gba maa daŋ wa tɛɛ ii hora.” 18Awia, baal maa kpa u nimbuurikuŋ, di buu niŋ di ɛɛ daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di du, di wa jaa Moosis ni Aarɔn ni, di chi Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua see. 19Denii Kɔra chaali u hiŋra la u ni baa ni Moosis n na tɛrgi dɔŋa la, a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, Kɔraawiizi girme ba Izrɛl hina maa be. 20Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, 21“Ií bargi iihinaa lii a nɛra naa maa be, ka ń tuŋ ba maa kakpaŋ.”
22Awia, Moosis ni Aarɔn chol pi hɛri, di lɔ wiile di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i benii miibɔɔ lii, i daŋ na baaŋ di du nɛra naa maa ni, dikuu nɛkpaŋ wichɔgaa wiaa?”
23Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 24“Ŋɔ a nɛra be, ‘Ií tuzi ka ka Kɔra, Datan ani Abiram tanti diini!’ ”
25Moosis izi di la Datan ni Abiram be, Izrɛl nabɔnzi hiŋuu. 26Moosis karfi a nɛra maa di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií tuzi ka ka biinikpola hina naa tanti diini! Ií gilɛɛ waa gbɔgzi ba kundɔɔlii maa, di guŋ lɛi, ii maanii niŋ tuŋ nyaamm dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia.” 27Awia, ba faa tuzi ka ka Kɔra, Datan ni Abiram ni ba haana tanti diini. Di Datan, Abiram, ba haana ani ba biizi maa faa liwɔɔ chi ba tanti diini dominuuzi.
28Denii Moosis ŋɔ, “Kenne ii chi di zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizii humiŋ lugɔ ń wa ɛɛ wia naa maa, n himmaa zumaa lɛi. 29Di baala naa daŋ siuzi ba saŋazi, guŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi lɛi humiŋ. 30Ka di Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ wii la ŋmɛnɛ n haa waa ɛɛwɛ maa, di gil hɛri peri, ba ni ba kundɔɔlaa maa zuu de, ba wia tuŋ, ii daŋ zum lugɔ baala naa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizii.”
31Uŋ wa ŋɔ annii maa di waa tuŋ, bɔr la Datan ni Abiram n chigɛ la peri, 32di di ba ni ba biizi, di kpa Kɔra ni u diahina ni u hiŋra ni ba kundɔɔlaa maa. 33Awia, ba ni ba kundɔɔlaa maa tuu kaali lalaa bol di ba haa ra nyiŋ, ka a hɛri bir wa tɔ, ba wia tuŋ. 34Dikuu ba chɛɛhgaa wia, Izrɛl hina la maa n faa chigɛ di bar baa la maa faa kɛɛhzi di ra chɛɛhgi di ra ŋɔ, “A hɛri daŋ lil yaa gbaoo!”
35Niŋ faa lii Kɔraawiizi be di wa di baala kalfaanɛɛ ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi la, n faa fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di faa ra tɛu la.
36Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 37“Ŋɔ n kizeehiŋ Aarɔn biibaal Ɛliaza be lugɔ, ú paagi nimbuurikuna la lii nɛra la n fuuhwe la be, di kpa a biine hɔla la di yaari yembɛl, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nimbuurikuna waa ɛɛ kunnanaananaarɛ. 38Baala la n ɛɛ wichɔgaa di siuzi la, luu ba nimbuurikuna, di tɔ mbusu lizibɔr la ni, dikuu baŋ faa kpaa tɛŋ wia, a birgi kunnanaananaarɛ. Gil guŋ ɛɛ liize tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.”
39Awia, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza faa paagaa di gil ba luua tɔ mbusu lizibɔr la ni, 40gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be di ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la. Keŋ faa ɛɛ di gil Izrɛl hina ra liizi lugɔ, di Aarɔn naanna bɛŋ lɛi, nɛr maa waa dɛg ú ba di wa fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, see Aarɔn naanna bɛŋ, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ birgi lugɔ Kɔra ni u hiŋra.
41Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Izrɛl hina maa nuumi ra du Moosis ni Aarɔn, di ra ŋɔ, “Ií kpu Kɔraawiizi nɛraa.”
42Ka ba maa n faa wa chaalɛɛ bá di Moosis ni Aarɔn mmɔri, di bir chaŋ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, ba na baama n wa guali de ni kakpaŋ, Kɔraawiizi girme tuu ba. 43Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn tuzi la a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia hiŋ see, 44denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 45“Ií chɔ lii a nɛra be ka ń tuŋ baa kakpaŋ.” Ba chol pi hɛri.
46Denii Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Kpa i nimbuurikuŋ di buu niŋ lii mbusu lizibɔr la, di ɛɛ daahɛgsɔɔhsuma du, di hahzi la a nɛra be di ga lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih ba ni dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, Kɔraawiizi gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa manaŋ. Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuihchɔgii la izoore, wiilchɔgii teŋ faarɔɔrɛ.” 47Awia, Aarɔn ɛɛ gunla Moosis n ŋɔwɛɛ la ka chɔ zuu a nɛra biini. Di a wiilchɔgii teŋ faarɔɔ di ra kpuuzi a nɛra, ka Aarɔn faa fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih ba ni, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia. 48U faa chi nyinee ni lalaa maa baambaaŋ, a wiilchɔgii faa tuŋ. 49Ka nɛra kagboŋa fidaanaazu ni kalfaaniidaanɛɛrɛ faa siuzɛɛ dikuu a wiilchɔgii wia, di kpa banla n faa siuzɛɛ dikuu Kɔra wia la di jaa. 50Denii Aarɔn faa bir ba Moosis be a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, dikuu a wiilchɔgii n jaa tuŋ wia.

english_text:
Aaron's Walking Stick Blooms and Produces Almonds
1The Lord told Moses:
2-3Call together the twelve tribes of Israel and tell the leader of each tribe to write his name on the walking stick he carries as a symbol of his authority. Make sure Aaron's name is written on the one from the Levi tribe, then collect all the sticks.
4Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you. 5I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
6Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe. 7Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
8 The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick. 9Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
10But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.” 11Moses did what he was told.
12The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for 13and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_text:
Aarɔn daŋkpala wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be bá nyiŋŋi daŋkpalli fidaanɛɛ di wa tɛi. Dee maa nabɔma daŋ nyiŋŋi kpaŋkpaŋ. Sɛbi bɛl maa sɔŋ di du u daŋkpala ni. 3Sɛbi Aarɔn sɔŋ di dau Levi dee hor ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, a dɛkkɔɔ dee maa nabɔma dɔɔ bɛl. 4Kpaa dau N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini, bɔr la n nii n ɔɔ ra chem la. 5Baal la min niŋ lizi la kpala daŋ fur paŋhoori, n himmaa gil Izrɛl hina saŋa maa nuumaa naa tuŋ.”
6Awia, Moosis ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, ba nabɔnzi tɛu daŋkpalli fidaanɛɛ, Aarɔn ge hor jaa a ni. 7Moosis kpaa di ga dau Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, u Tanti Dia la biini. 8Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzi ni, Moosis zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la, di ga na di Aarɔn hor la n chigɛ tɛɛ Levi dee la bɛnnɛ futtɛ, di fii di nɔŋ daa bɛl banna yir almɔn nɔna. 9Denii Moosis paa a daŋkpalli maa Kɔraawiizi see di lii ba Izrɛl hina la maa be. Ba binnaa, bɛl maa kpa u hor.
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kpa Aarɔn hor la dau n Ni Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, u chɔɔ de di ɛɛ liize kuŋ tɛɛ banla n na di mmɔri la. Gunnɛ niŋ tuŋ ba nuumaa la, guŋ gil ba gilɛɛ waa siuzi.” 11Moosis ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.
12A Izrɛl hina la faa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Yaa daŋ siuzi! Yaa wia tunnɔɔ! 13Nɛr la maa n niŋ dugli Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la gba daŋ siu. Yaa maanii niŋ siuzia?”

english_text:
The Duties of the Priests and Levites
1The Lord said to Aaron:
You, your sons, and the other Levites of the Kohath clan, are responsible for what happens at the sacred tent. And you and your sons will be responsible for what the priests do. 2The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent. 3You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die. 4No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it. 5Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
6I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers. 7But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death.
The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord
(Deuteronomy 18.1-8)
8-9The Lord said to Aaron:
I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar. 10Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
11You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things. 12For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts. 13And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
14 Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
15The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me. 16The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards. 17However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased. 18You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
19From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
20You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need.
What the Levites Receive
The Lord said to Aaron:
21 Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent. 22-23They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change.
Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own, 24they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me.
What the Levites Must Give
25The Lord told Moses 26to say to the Levites:
When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me. 27Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive 28as an offering to me. That amount must then be given to Aaron, 29so the best of what you receive will be mine.
30After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me. 31Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent. 32You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me.
The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee huma wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “I ni i biibaala ni Levi deere niŋ ɔɔ di tɔɔrɔɔ. Di ba wa gbɛlli n Tanti Dia la, ka i ni i biibaala bɛnnɛ niŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ, di ba wa gbɛlli n kizeehina huma. 2Kpogli i lulla Levi dee la n lii i naabaala dee biini la, di ba, bá wa hiini i ni i biibaala, di ii wàá hum huma n Tanti Dia la biini. 3Ba daŋ ɔɔ ra hum huma la maa hin niŋ ɔɔ tɛɛ baa, di ra hum n Tanti Dia biini huma maa, ka bá gilɛɛ wàá dugli kunnanaananaa la n du Bɔnaniinanii la ani mbusu lizibɔr la. Di ba haŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ kpuuzi i ni baa maa. 4Levi dee la daŋ hiinii di ra hum u biini huma, di ra du u tau nɛnnɛ, ka nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa dugli bɔr la hiŋ duwɛɛ la waa.
5I ni i biibaala bɛnnɛ ninna binni Bɔnaniinanii ani mbusu lizibɔr la ni, guŋ gil n baaŋfuuihchɔgii la gilɛɛ kaa wàá izi Izrɛl hina ni. 6N himmaanii lizi i lulla Levi dee la di lii Izrɛl hina biini di sunzii, bá ɛɛ n hora, di ra hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. 7Ka i ni i biibaala bɛnnɛ ninna hum n kizeehina huma mbusu lizibɔr la ani Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa patiisa la biini. N kpa n kizeehina humaa di ra sunzii. Nɛr la maa haŋ wa dugli kunnaananaa la n du u biini la, a dɛkkɔɔ bá kpuu.”
Mbusuzi lizaa kuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee hora wia
8Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi himmaanii kpa mbusu lizaa kuna la baŋ ɔɔ lizi di ra tɛŋ la, di ra tɛɛ ia. Mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa la Izrɛl hina ɔɔ lizi di wa tɛŋ la, n kpaabuu di ra tɛɛ i ni i biibaala, á ɛɛ i hora saŋa maa. 9Hinuu dɔɔ a mbusuzi lizaa kuna bɔnanaananaa himmaa la baŋ waa fuuh la. Di lii mbusuzi lizaa kuna la maa baŋ ɔɔ ra tɛŋ la, di miarɛ, wichɔgaa gɛɛ bilchɔg mbusu lizaa kunaa, á ɛɛ i ni i biibaala horaa. 10Ií ra dia alugɔ kuna la n ɛɛ nanaananaa himmaa la. Baal maanii niŋ na dia. Kpaa lugɔ kunnanaananaa.
11Annii gba ɛɛ i hora, kuna la maa baŋ lizɛɛ di lii Izrɛl hina mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa biini di dau a bɛŋ. N kpaabuu di ra tɛɛ i ni i biizi á ɛɛ ii hora di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Nɛr la maa n du i dia, di waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be, daŋ wer dia.
12N kpa ɔlivi nuunanaa ni siŋfalaa la n wesse ani mia la maa baŋ ɔɔ lizi di wàá tɛŋ, a ɛɛ ba lugli pattikuna labuu di ra tɛi. 13A hɛri diulugla maa baŋ ɔɔ kpa ba di waa tɛŋ la, ɛɛ i horaa. Nɛr la maa n du i dia, di waa doŋŋe n be daŋ wer dia.
14Kunla maa baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛŋ, ú ɛɛ n bɛmbɛŋ kuŋ di lii Izrɛl hɛri ɛɛ i horaa. 15Kummaa biilugli, di neweere gɛɛ di selle, baŋ kpawɛɛ di tɛŋ, ɛɛ i hotte. Ka i daŋ wer gil ba bir yau newea biibambilugla. Di kaa gil bá bir yau sel la maa n doŋŋe n be biiballugli gba. 16Di bie maa wa di baagu, ba daŋ yawuu saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau anue, gunla banna mɛgzaa n Tanti Dia biini la.
17Ka nau gɛɛ peezi gɛɛ buuŋ waa biilugla, á ɛɛ a nanaananaarɛ, ba wàá wer bir yawaa. Ɛɛ kpa a challi di mizi mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di fuuh a nuuri á ɛɛ mbusu sefuuhlaa la sɔɔh n summɛ di tɛŋ. 18A ola daŋ ɛɛ i hora gunla bampirii la baŋ ɔɔ viigi ani nodig hiih la, n ɛɛ i hora la. 19Mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa la maa Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ kpa ba di waa tɛŋ la, n kpaabuu di ra tɛɛ i ni i biizi. Guŋ ɛɛ n nii ni i naanna nuukpaŋ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ saŋa maa labuu.”
20Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Hàá dɔɔ kapɛttɛ kuŋ maa gɛɛ di dɔɔ a hɛri yemmaa. Minuu i kundɔɔlii Izrɛl hina biini.
