21N kpa Izrɛl hina kuna maa fi bɔkpaŋ la baŋ ɔɔ lizi tɛŋ labuu di ra tɛɛ Levi dee, á ɛɛ ba kinturgaa dikuu ba huma, baŋ ɔɔ ra hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini la wia. 22Haŋ lii filaŋkeŋ di hanna la, a waa dɛkkɛ Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ ra dugli n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, di guŋ lɛi, ba daŋ di a guŋ wichɔgaa tɔɔrɔɔ di siuzi. 23Levi dee labuu ninna hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia hiŋ huma, di ra di u gbɛllaa tɔɔrɔɔzi maa. Guŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ tɛɛ i naanna maa. Ba waa na kapɛttɛ maa di lii Izrɛl hina biini. 24Ka n kpa kuna fi bɔkpaŋ la maa Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ lizi di wàá turgiŋ labuu, di ra tɛɛ Levi dee, á ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuna. Guŋ wiarɛ n ŋɔ ba wia, lugɔ ba wàá na kapɛttɛ kuŋ maa, di lii Izrɛl hina biini la.”
25Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, 26“Ŋɔ Levi dee be, ‘Di ii wa lɛɛ kuna fi bɔkpaŋ la Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ lizi, n kpa tɛɛ ia la, á ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuna la, ií bɔnnaa bɔra fi, di lizi a bɔkpaŋ tɛŋ. 27N daŋ kpa mbusu lizaa naa ú ɛɛ lugɔ patti n ɔɔ lizi u mbusu lizaa mifalaa gɛɛ siŋfalii tɛŋ la. 28Gunnɛ ii ge ɔɔ ɛɛ di lizi mbusu di lii kuna la maa Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ lizi di wàá tɛɛ ia la biini di ra tɛŋ. Di lii kuna la maa Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ ra lizi la biini, ii daŋ ɔɔ ligzi n hora di ra tɛɛ Aarɔn la n ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la. 29A dɛkkɔɔ ií ɔɔ lizi a bɔra la n wesse nɛnnɛ di ɛɛ a nanaananaa himmaa la di ra tɛŋ.’
30Kaa ŋɔ Levi dee be, ‘Di ii wa lizi a bɔra la n wesse nɛnnɛ di tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ii daŋ kpogli anla n kawɛɛ gunla patti n ɔɔ kpogli u hora, di u wa lizi n hora di tɛŋ tuŋ la. 31Ii ni ii diini hina daŋ wer di a bɔr la n kawɛɛ yemmaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii huma la iinna hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini la kinturgaare guŋ. 32Ii wàá di bilchɔg, di ii ɔɔ lizi a bɔra la n wesse nɛnnɛ tɛŋ, ka ra di a bɔra la n kawɛɛ. Ka ii ra du tau di gilɛɛ waa dia, di ii haa waa a bɔra la n wesse nɛnnɛ la lizɛɛ tɛŋ, di ii ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ kpuuzi ia.’ ”

english_text:
The Ceremony To Wash Away Sin
1-2The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law:
The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing. 3Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches. 4He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent. 5Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned. 6A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
7After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening. 8The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
9 A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin. 10The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them.
What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body
The Lord said:
11If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days. 12But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean. 13Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
14If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean. 15Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
16If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
17-18Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water. 19If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
20If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel. 21These laws will never change.
The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening. 22When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_text:
Doŋa lizaa nii wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, 2“N Gbɔg widaulaarɛ keŋ. Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ bá lizi nalor aahmu la n kpekke, u haa waa huma maa hummɛ di wa tɛɛ ia. 3Ií kpau tɛɛ Ɛliaza la n ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la, ba daŋ lawuu lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di kɔrguu u see, 4Ɛliaza kpa u nonibii lii u chal di chaŋ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see di mizi buniidaanɛɛ. 5U danna binni ka ba fuuh a nau maa, u hɔŋ, u ol, u chal ani u biini kuna maa. 6N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa hɛriŋkpol ni hisɔp daa ani peezi huna n aahwɛ di ha a niŋ biini. 7Di guŋ wa tunnɔ, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ chag u laala di sɔ nii. U daŋ jaa wer zuu ba chɔɔribɔr la biini ka haa doŋ n be guŋŋ di ra ba duana. 8Baal la gba n fuuh a nau la daŋ chag u laala, di sɔ nii, ka ge doŋ n be guŋŋ di ra ba duana.
9Baal la n waa doŋŋe n be daŋ paa a nalor hɔɔhri di ga dau bɔr la n waa doŋŋe n be ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ baŋgia. A daŋ chɔɔ de tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, baa ɔɔ kpa di ra du doŋa lizaa nii biini. Aabuu ba kpa di ra lizi nɛra wichɔgaa doŋa. 10Baal la ge n paa a hɔɔhri la gba, daŋ chag u laala, ka doŋ n be guŋŋ di ra ba duana. Keŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulii la n chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ni hɔɔhra la maa n du ba be la, di hanna la.
11Nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi lalii maa daŋ doŋ n be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 12U daŋ ɛɛ a nii di sɔ lizi u doŋa, a hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ hɔl ani a aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl, denii u doŋa jaa tuŋ. Ka di waa u hiŋ sɔwɛɛ a hɔpizaa ahoro ni aniidaanɛɛ hɔla la, u doŋa wàá tuŋ. 13Nɛr la maa n gbɔgzi lalii maa ka waa u hiŋ sɔwɛɛ, doŋ n Tanti Diarɛ. A dɛkkɔɔ ba duŋŋi a hindee lii Izrɛl hina biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba wɔɔ mizɛɛ doŋa lizaa nii la. U doŋŋoo mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, u doŋa haa du u ninɛɛ.
14Di nɛr haŋ wa siu tanti dia biini, widaulii la n du denii keŋ. Nɛr la maa haŋ wa zuu a tanti dia biini ani unla maa n du u biini, daŋ doŋ n be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 15Kunla maa n waa tua dɔɔwɛ ge, daŋ doŋ.
16Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi nɛr la baŋ kpuwɛɛ gɛɛ u saŋa n helle u siu bossee, gɛɛ di nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi newee hog gɛɛ ŋmam, daŋ doŋ n be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.
17Di ba ŋɔ bá lizi a hindee doŋa, ba daŋ ɛɛ nalor aahmu la baŋ fuuhwe di lizi ba wiichɔgaa la hɔɔhri, di du vii biini di ɛɛ niinanii du. 18Denii baal la n waa doŋŋe n be kpa hisɔp daa, di lii a nii di mizi a tanti dia ni kuna la maa n du u biini ani nɛr la maa n gbɔgzi newee hog gɛɛ lalii gɛɛ ŋmam. 19Nɛr la n waa doŋŋe n bee niŋ mizi nɛr la n doŋŋe hɔpizaa ahoro ni aniidaanɛɛ hɔla la. A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, u jaa sɔu di lizi u doŋa. Nɛr la baŋ lizi u doŋa la daŋ chag u laala di sɔ nii, u doŋa tuŋ a duana ni. 20Ka di nɛr la n doŋŋe n be la waa u doŋa lizɛɛ, a dɛkkɔɔ ba duŋŋuu lii ba biini, dikuu uŋ doŋ n Tanti Dia la wia. Baŋ wɔɔ mizɛɛ doŋ lizaa nii la wia, u doŋŋoo n be. 21Keŋ ɛɛ widaulii la n chɔɔwɛɛ tɛɛ baa di hanna la.
Baal la gba n kpa a doŋa lizaa nii di mizuu la gba daŋ chag u laala. Nɛr la maa ge n gbɔgzi a nii gba daŋ doŋ n be guŋŋ di ra ba duana. 22Nɛr la n doŋŋe n be haŋ wa gbɔgzi kummaa, a kundee ge gba daŋ doŋ n be. Nɛr la maa ge wa gbɔgzuu u gba daŋ doŋ n be di ra ba duana.”

english_text:
Water from a Rock
1The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
2 The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron 3and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent. 4You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die! 5Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
6Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory 7-8and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
9Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent. 10After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!” 11 He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
12But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
13The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.”
Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
14Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom:
We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us. 15Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us, 16and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land.
Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh. 17Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
18But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
19Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
20But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!”
Then Edom sent out its strongest troops 21to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction.
Aaron Dies
22After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor 23on the Edomite border, the Lord said, 24“Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites. 25Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain. 26Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
27Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor. 28 Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there.
When Moses and Eleazar came down, 29the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for 30 days.
translation_text:
Nii n lii bii ni wia
1Lugli baagu hiŋ biini, Izrɛl hina maa wa hel Zin Hɛribɔduma biini, di chɔɔ Kadɛs. Denii Miriam siu, ba huguu.
2Nii faa waa hoo de, a nɛra faa chaali di wa bar Moosis ni Aarɔn di ra nuumi, 3di ŋɔ Moosis be, “Di yaa ni yaa balaa la maa faa siuzɔɔ Kɔraawiizi see, guŋ faa bɔ. 4Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i kpogli yaa di ba hɛribɔduma naa biini, ya ni yaa sela maa wa siuzɛi? 5Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i kpogli yaa lii Ijip hɛri di ba bɔkpol naa biinei? De waa mia ni fig daazi ni grepu daazi gɛɛ pomegranet dɔɔwɛ. Nii gba waa hoo yá nyɔɔ!”
6Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn lii a nɛra be di la Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua di ga chol pi hɛri, Kɔraawiizi girme chaani ba ni. 7Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 8“Kpa daŋkpala la n teli N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, í ni Aarɔn chaali a nɛra maa. Denii ii ŋɔ wia tɛɛ bital la, ba maa sibɔɔ. Nii daŋ pozi di lii u ni. Gunnɛ ii ɛɛ nii lii a bital ni tɛɛ a nɛra ni ba sela maa, bá nyɔɔ.”
9Awia, Moosis faa kpa a daa di lii a Tanti Dia biini, gunla uŋ ŋɔ u be la. 10U ni Aarɔn chaali a nɛra maa a bital zɛɛ. Denii Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Mmɔri diire, ií ra nuu! A dɛkkɔɔ yá gil nii lii bii naa ni tɛɛ iaa?” 11Denii Moosis lalli u daa la di lɔ a bital bunɛɛ. Nii pozi lii, a nɛra ni ba sela maa nyɔɔ.
12Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, “Dikuu iiŋ wan yardɛɛ nɛnnɛ di kpaŋ girme lugɔ n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ Izrɛl hina be wia, ii wàá kpogli baa zuu hɛri la minna tɛɛ baa la biini.”
13Mɛribaa wia naa faa ɛɛ, denii Izrɛl hina faa nuumi du Kɔraawiizi ni, u bagli baa gunla uŋ ɛɛ naniinanii la.
Ɛdɔm koori n tɔ Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛɛ wia
14Moosis faa hum u balaa Ɛdɔm hina Koori be di lii Kadɛs, bá ga ŋɔ,
“Kenne i lulla Izrɛl hina ŋɔ, ‘I zum tɔɔrɔɔ la n huuzi yaa, yaa di dɔgnyaa. 15Yaa naabaala la Ijip hɛrii, yaa du de binni kpilakpila maa. A Ijip hina sunni yaa ni yaa mɛɛwaa werge maa, 16ka yaa n wa wiiwe du Kɔraawiizi ni, u nuu yaa wiraare, di hum u mɛlika u wa lizi yaa di lii Ijip hɛri.
Filaŋkeŋ, bol la banna yir Kadɛs la n du i bol magbɔɔ nua labuu yaa so. 17Yaa ra ɛɛibuu jaande, gil ya ga i hɛri di kaali yaa laŋribɔr. Yaa waa zuu ii kooni gɛɛ ii grepu daazi kooni gɛɛ di wàá nyɔɔ ii kɔlɔŋzi niiri. I ŋmɛnizeŋ bɛnnɛ ya hiŋ guŋŋ di ga lii i hɛri, di yaa waa yemmaa bɛɛwɛ.’ ”
18Ka Ɛdɔm hina ŋɔ,
“Ií wàá ga yaa hɛri! Di ii haŋ kur, yaa daŋ lii lɔ ia laal.”
19Izrɛl hina la bir ŋɔ,
“Yaa daŋ hiŋ ŋmɛnizeŋ di ga lii, ka di yaa sela wa nyɔɔ ii nii maa, yaa daŋ turgi. Yaa hanna nyiŋŋuu yá vol di ga lii, wiimaa waa ka jaa.”
20Ba kaa kuari ŋɔ,
“Ií wàá ga de!”
Denii Ɛdɔm hina laallɔɔrakpila n kpekke werge faa vɔɔ laal bá ga chem ba ni. 21Dikuu Ɛdɔm hina n faa waa sɛɛwɛ bá ga ba hɛri biini wia, Izrɛl hina bir ga bɔduma.
Aarɔn siu wia
22Izrɛl hina la maa faa izi lii Kadɛs di ga hel Bizeŋ Hɔɔ, 23n dugli Ɛdɔm magbɔɔ la, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, 24“Aarɔn wàá zuu hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la, u daŋ ga chɔɔ ii naabaala be, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii nɛra banɛɛ maa faa waa n nua hiŋŋɛ Mɛriba niiri bɔr la. 25Kpogli Aarɔn ni u biibaal Ɛliaza, di tinni Bizeŋ Hɔɔ nyuu. 26Wir n kizeehiŋ Aarɔn bɔmbɔga di bɔg u biibaal Ɛliaza, dikuu Aarɔn n niŋ ga chɔɔ u naabaala be wia. Denii ú siu.”
27Moosis ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la. A nɛra maa ra binni ka ba tinni Bizeŋ Hɔɔ. 28Moosis wir Aarɔn bɔmbɔga di bɔg u biibaal Ɛliaza. Aarɔn jaa siu a bizeŋ nyuu. Denii Moosis ni Ɛliaza lii a bizeŋ nyuu di tuu. 29Izrɛl hina maa n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Aarɔn siuwɔɔ la, ba wii u lee hɔpizaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ.

english_text:
Israel Defeats the Canaanites at Hormah
1 The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, and when he heard that the Israelites were on their way to the village of Atharim, he attacked and took some of them hostage.
2The Israelites prayed, “Our Lord, if you will help us defeat these Canaanites, we will completely destroy their towns and everything in them, to show that they belong to you.”
3The Lord answered their prayer and helped them wipe out the Canaanite army and completely destroy their towns. That's why one of the towns is named Hormah, which means “Destroyed Place.”
Moses Makes a Bronze Snake
4 The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient 5 that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
6Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
7Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.”
Moses prayed, 8and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
9 Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes.
Israel's Journey to Moab
10As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth, 11then at Iye-Abarim in the desert east of Moab, 12and then in the Zered Gorge. 13After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites. 14A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River, 15with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
16From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
17That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song:
Let's celebrate!
The well has given us water.
18With their royal scepters,
our leaders pointed out
where to dig the well.
The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah, 19then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth. 20Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite
(Deuteronomy 2.26-37)
21The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
22Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
23But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz. 24Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
25The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages. 26King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge. 27That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon:
Come and rebuild Heshbon,
King Sihon's capital city!
28 His armies marched out
like fiery flames,
burning down the town of Ar
and destroying the hills
along the Arnon River.
29You Moabites are done for!
Your god Chemosh
deserted your people;
they were captured, taken away
by King Sihon the Amorite.
30We completely defeated Moab.
The towns of Heshbon and Dibon,
of Nophah and Medeba
are ruined and gone.
31After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory, 32Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there.
Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan
(Deuteronomy 3.1-11)
33The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
34The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
35So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_text:
Baŋ puri Arad wia
1Saŋa la Keenan hina koori bɛl n faa di kora di so bolzeŋ bɛl banna yir Arad, di du wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma banna yir Nɛgɛv, n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina ga ŋmɛnɛɛ la n ga Atarim labuu, u vɔɔ laal di ga lɔ baa, di lauri baŋhina. 2Denii Izrɛl hina faa lɛɛ nua naa Kɔraawiizi be, “Di i kpa nɛra naa du yaa nonee, yaa daŋ purgi ba bolzenaa, di chɔg ba ni ba sela maa nyaamm.” 3Kɔraawiizi nuu ba suŋŋaa la, di kpa Keenan hina du ba nonee, ba chɔgi ba ni ba bola maa nyaamm. Awia, ba faa dau de sɔŋ Hɔma.
Danyɛ hɛrikuŋ wia
4Ba vol lii Bizeŋ Hɔɔ di ga ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Muuzeŋaahmuu la, bá bar Ɛdɔm hɛri, ka Izrɛl hina faa di kanyitti huhzi ŋmɛnɛɛ, 5ka ra naa Kɔraawiizi ni Moosis wia, di ra ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii lizi yaa lii Ijip hɛri ya wa siuzi hɛribɔduma biinei? Diwee waa hoo ɛŋ! Nii gba waa hoo ɛŋ! Diubazaa naa jaa ra sɔɔhri yaa miizii!”
6Denii Kɔraawiizi faa gil duŋkpolli zuu Izrɛl hina biini, di dunzi bakpila, ba siuzi. 7A nɛra ba Moosis be di wa ŋɔ, “Yaa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ dikuu yaa n faa ŋɔ wia di zuu i ni Kɔraawiizi ni la wia. Suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ú lizi a hɛrikuna yaa be.” Awia, Moosis faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ baa.
8Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Gil luuri kpa danyɛ di luu hɛrikuŋ, í kpau sag daajaŋ ni. Di hɛrikuŋ wa dum bɛl maa, u binnuu, u daŋ nyaagi.” 9Awia, Moosis faa kpa a hɛrikuŋ di sag daajaŋ ni, di hɛrikuŋ wa dum nɛr maa u binnuu, u ɔɔ nyaaguu.
Baŋ volle la Moab wia
10Izrɛl hina izi di vol guŋŋ di ga chɔɔ Ɔbɔf, 11di kaa izi de di ga chɔɔ Iyɛ Abarim la n du hɛribɔduma biini Moab hɛri wiifurii paga la. 12Ba kaa lii de di ga chɔɔ Zɛrɛd Waluu, 13di izi de di ga chɔɔ Muu Aanɔn baŋgia la n du hɛribɔduma la n chɔɔwɛ di ra la Amɔri hina hɛri. A Muu Aanɔn faa ɛɛ Moab magbɔɔrɛ, di faa chɔɔ Moab ni Amɔri hina baambaaŋ. 14Guŋ wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi Laalzi Hɔŋ la ŋɔ,
“Bol bɛl banna yir Wahɛb la n du Sufa paga ani walli,
Muu Aanɔn
15ani walli bɔwillaa la
n na la bol bɛl banna yir Aa,
di chɔɔ ra la
Moab magbɔɔ la.”
16Ba lii de di kpa guŋŋ di ga hel Bɛɛ kɔlɔŋ la zɛɛ Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Chaali a nɛra ń tɛɛ baa nii.”
17Denii Izrɛl hina faa yir yir naa,
“Kɔlɔŋ, búl nii ya nyɔɔ!
Ya yir u yira di ra ŋɔ,
18kɔlɔŋ la sitɔɔra n kiiwe,
di kpa koori daŋkpala ani daŋkpalli ki la.”
Denii ba lii a hɛribɔduma di la Matana, 19di lii de di la Nahaliɛl, di kaa lii de ge di la Bamɔf, 20di lii de di la waluu la n du Moab, bɔr la Bizeŋ Pisga la baŋ ɔɔ chi u nyuu, di ra binni a hɛribɔduma zɛɛ la.
Baŋ kpegli Koora Sihɔn ni Ɔɔg wia
21Izrɛl hina hum nɛra, bá la ga ŋɔ Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn be,
22“Gil ya ga i hɛri kaali. Yaa wàá zuu ii kooni gɛɛ ii grepu daazi kooni gɛɛ di wàá nyɔɔ ii kɔlɔnzi niiri. I ŋmɛnizeŋ bɛnnɛ ya hiŋ di ga lii.”
23Ka Koori Sihɔn waa sɛɛwɛ Izrɛl hina ga u hɛri biini. U chaali u laallɔɔra maa ba lii di ga chem Izrɛl hina ni Jahaz, a hɛribɔduma biini, di lɔ baa laal. 24Ka Izrɛl hina kpegli baa di kpuuzi bakpila maa, di foozi ba hɛri di so de, di lii Muu Aanɔn guŋŋ di ga hel Muu Jabɔk wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, Ammɔn hina magbɔɔrɛ faa guŋ, dikuu baŋ faa kpekke de wia. 25Izrɛl hina faa kpegli Amɔri hina bolzenaa hina maa, di so a biine, di faa foozi Hɛsbɔn ani boljigzi la maa n faa soge baruu la. 26Hɛsbɔn faa ɛɛ Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn bolzenne, waabuu faa lɔ Moab hina kooribinii, di foozi u hɛri maa guŋŋ di ga hel Muu Aanɔn la.
27Awiarɛ yiryitta faa yir yira di ra ŋɔ,
“Ií ba ya bir di ma Hɛsbɔn,
ií gil yá bir ma Sihɔn bolzeŋ.
28Di lii Hɛsbɔn biini, Sihɔn laallɔɔra faa
liwɔɔrɛ alugɔ ninlau werge,
di chɔgi bolzeŋ Aa la n du Moab hɛri
ani banla n soge
Muu Aanɔn giŋgimee bɔra la.
29Moab hina, wia daŋ huuzi ia!
Ba chɔgi iabuu,
vug Kɛmɔs kuara!
Ií vug gillɔɔ ii biibaala chɔ yaari,
ii biihaana ge birgi yoma,
tɛɛ Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn.
30Ka yaa kpegli baabuu.
Hɛsbɔn puroore guŋŋ
di ga hel bolzeŋ Dibɔn.
Yaa chɔg baabuu guŋŋ di ga hel Nɔfa
la n chɔɔwɛ guŋŋ di ga
hel Mɛdɛba la.”
31Awia, Izrɛl hina faa so Amɔri hina hɛri.
32Denii Moosis faa hum nɛra bá la ga daani Jaza na, Izrɛl hina lɔ boljigzi la n bar baa la hina, di kpegli baa, di duŋŋi Amɔri hina la n faa du a biine la, ba lii. 33Denii ba bir kpa ŋmɛnɛɛ la n chɔɔwɛ di ra la Basan barii la, Basan Koori Ɔɔg ni u laallɔɔra maa faa lii ba ga chem ba ni Ɛdrɛi, di lɔ baa laal.
34Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔmuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, n kpa u ni u laallɔɔra ani u hɛri maanii di du i nonee biini. Ɛɛu gunla hiŋ faa ɛɛ Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn la n faa di kora Hɛsbɔn la.”
35Awia, ba faa kpu Koori Ɔɔg, u biibaala, u laallɔɔra ani u nɛra maa nyaamm, ka so de.

english_text:
1Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho.
King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
2-3When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked. 4They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.”
So King Balak 5 sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said:
I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory. 6They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
7The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
8“Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
9During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
10“They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them 11to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
12But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
13The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
14The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
15Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones. 16They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab, 17I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
18Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God. 19You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
20That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
21So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials.
Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
22Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him. 23When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
24Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side. 25When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
26The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around. 27So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
28When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
29“You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
30“But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?”
“No,” Balaam admitted.
31Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
32The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab. 33If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
34Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
35“It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials.
King Balak Meets Balaam
36When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab. 37Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
38“I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
39They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth, 40where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
41The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_text:
Koori Balak n hummɛ yir Balaam wia
1Denii Izrɛl hina vol guŋŋ di ga hel Moab lɛla ga chɔɔ hiini Jɔɔdan muu, di chaŋ bol bolzeŋ Jɛriko la n du u baŋgia bɛl la.
2Zipɔ biibaal Balak n ɛɛ Moab hina koori, n na gunla maa Izrɛl hina n dau Amɔri hina la, 3ɔnsii werge faa chol u ni u nɛra maa ni dikuu Izrɛl hina n kpillɛ werge wia.
4Denii Moab hina la faa ŋɔ Midian hina nabɔnzi be, “Nɛkpila naa daŋ chɔgi kuna la maa n bar yaa, gunla nabal n ɔɔ hee kooree ka ka a zɛɛtiree la.”
Awia, Koori Balak 5faa hum nɛra ba la ga yir Bɛɔ biibaal Balaam n du Pɛtɔ n dugli Muu Yufretis n du u hɛri la. Koori Balak faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Nɛra baŋhina lii Ijip hɛrii di ba, ba wa tɔ hɛri maanii keŋ milmilmil di so dugliŋ. 6Awia, ba di wa see baa nua, dikuu baŋ dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge kaaliŋ wia. Aŋhinabe, n daŋ jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di kpegli baa, di duŋŋi baa lii n hɛri. N zummɔ lugɔ di i haŋ kissi nɛra, a ba na kissaare, di i kaa wa see nɛra ge nua, nuuseezi ɔɔ di baabuu.”
7Denii Moab ni Midian hina nabɔnzi kpa vugaa kebee di kaali. Baŋ ga hel Balaam be, ba kaluu gunla Koori Balak n ŋɔwɛɛ la.
8Balaam ŋɔ ba be, “Ií chɔɔ bɔnnaa, kɛrɛ n ŋɔ tɛɛ ia gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ŋɔ tɛŋ.” Awia, a Moab hina sitɔɔra la faa chɔɔ u be.
9A hamuŋa hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi ba Balaam be di wa pɛɛzuu, “Baala bɛlaarɛ du i be naanɛi?”
10Balaam ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Zipɔ biibaal Balak la n ɛɛ Moab hina koorii hum baa bá wa ŋɔ n be, 11‘Nɛra baŋhinaa lii Ijip hɛri di wa tɔ a hɛri maa. Awia, ba filaŋkeŋ di wa see baa nua tɛŋ. Aŋhinabe, n daŋ jaa wer lɔ baa duŋŋi.’ ”
12Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Balaam be, “Gilɛɛ wa gil i ni baa ra la. A waa dɛkkɛ i wàá see a nɛra nua, dikuubɛɛwiai, n kissi baabuu.”
13Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Balaam izi di ŋɔ Koori Balak sitɔɔra la be, “Ií bir ra la ii hɛri, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ n ni ia la.”
14Awia, Moab hina sitɔɔra la bir kaali Balak be di ga ŋɔ, “Balaam vɛɛwɔɔ ú hiŋ yaa di ba.”
15Denii Koori Balak kaa hum sitɔɔra kpila la n faa ɛɛ nɛtɔga nɛnnɛ di kaali lugli hora la. 16Ba kpa amaniye naa di lii Balak be, di ga tɛɛ Balaam di ŋɔ,
“Jaande maa, gilɛɛ wa gil kummaa wàá tɔi n be balaa ŋmɛnɛɛ, 17dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ turgii a kim nɛnnɛ maa, di ɛɛ wii la maa hin niŋ ŋɔ ń ɛɛ. Ba di wa see a nɛra naa nua di tɛŋ.”
18Ka Balaam ŋɔ ba be, “Haali di Koori Balak kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ di su u kooridia tɛŋ gba, ka maa wer ɛɛ wizeŋ gɛɛ wijiga maa di bɛri Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii ni. 19Ií chɔɔ ɛŋ gunla banla n chɔɔwɛ la, ka n binni na wii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ kaa ŋɔ n be.”
20Kɔraawiizi ba Balaam be a hamuŋa ni di wa ŋɔ, “Nɛra naa n ballɛ di wa yirii naa wia, hiŋ baa di la, ka í ga ɛɛ gunla maa min niŋ ŋɔ i be.”
Balaam kawee wia
21Balaam izi chɔɔzi ni, di bɔg u kawee di hiŋ Moab sitɔɔra la kaali. 22Ka Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh werge maa dikuu u laŋaa la wia, denii Kɔraawiizi mɛlika faa teŋuu ŋmɛnɛɛ. Balaam faa tinni u kaweere, u balaa banɛɛ faa jaa u ni. 23A kawee n wa na Kɔraawiizi mɛlika n kpogli tokobi di chi a ŋmɛnɛɛ, u bɛɛ zuu pir. Balaam ra lɔɔzuu, ú biruu lii ŋmɛnɛɛ.
24Denii Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la ga chi a ŋmɛnɛɛ bɔr la n faa fɔɔwɛ werge, grepu daazi kooni anɛɛ baambaaŋ, bia koŋlaa chi a ŋmɛnɛɛ keŋkere bɛl maa. 25Denii a kawee n wa na Kɔraawiizi mɛlika, u ga pɛli a koŋlii, Balaam kpa u naa lɔ a koŋlii bɛl werge. Awia, u faa kaa ra lɔɔzuu.
26Denii Kɔraawiizi mɛlika hiŋ kaa tuzi di la see di ga chi bɔr la n fɔɔwɛ werge, bɔgaalii maa waa kaa hoo de yemmaa. 27A kawee n wa na Kɔraawiizi mɛlika, u chɔɔ hɛri. Balaam baaŋ faa fuuh werge maa, u kpa u kpala di ra lɔɔzuu. 28Denii Kɔraawiizi pilli a kawee nua u ŋɔ tɛɛ Balaam, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛi i lɔɔziŋ buhoro naa maanɛi?”
29Balaam ŋɔ a kawee be, “I kpambuu di birgi gɛnii! Di n faa kpogli tokobi, n daŋ faa kpui filaŋkennaa maa.”
30A kawee ŋɔ Balaam be, “I himmaa kawee lɛi miŋŋ, hinna tinniŋ wa lii ni zinaa, gunnɛ n ɔɔ ra ɛɛi?”
Balaam ŋɔ “Akai.”
31Denii Kɔraawiizi pilli Balaam siwee u na Kɔraawiizi mɛlika n chigɛ a ŋmɛnɛɛ di kpogli tokobi. Awia, u faa chol pi hɛri.
32Kɔraawiizi mɛlika pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i lɔɔzi i kawee buhoro naa maa gunnɛi? N ballɔɔ ń wa teŋii ŋmɛnɛɛ, dikuu volaa la hinna vol la n waa dɛkkɛ wia. 33A kawee nambuu di bir a buhoro hìŋ́ maa. Di u faa waa bittɛ, n faa kpui wibii maa, ka faa giluu.”
34Balaam ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika be, “N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. N faa waa zummɛ lugɔ hinuu teŋiŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ. Ka di n laŋaa hiŋ wɛɛ pattɛ, n daŋ bir.”
35Kɔraawiizi mɛlika ŋɔ u be, “Hiŋ baa di la, ka ga ŋɔ wii la min niŋ ŋɔ i be di tɛɛ baa.” Awia, Balaam ni Koori Balak sitɔɔra hiŋ faa kaali.
36Koori Balak n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Balaam ra bau, u lii ú ga chem u ni bolzeŋ bɛl banna yir Ar, n du Muu Aanɔn nua, Moab hina hɛri magbɔɔ. 37Koori Balak ga pɛɛzuu, “N faa waa felee di hum nɛra i be siaahmu nii? Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i faa waa ballɛi? Màá wer turgiibuu a kim gɛɛ?”
38Balaam bir di ŋɔ u be, “Too, n ballɔɔ la. Ka bɛɛ fɔŋŋaa n dɔɔ ń wer ŋɔ wii bɛlɛi? Wii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ŋɔ tɛŋ, waabuu n ŋɔ.”
39Denii Balaam ni Koori Balak la Kiriaf Huzɔf. 40Koori Balak ga kpu nauna ni peeza di lizi mbusu, di kpa aŋhina tɛɛ u sitɔɔra la n faa du u be la ni Balaam. 41Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Koori Balak kpogli Balaam di la Bamɔf Baal, denii u ga na a Izrɛl hina yeŋ.

english_text:
Balaam's First Message
1Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
2After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar. 3Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
4When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
5The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak. 6When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
7Balaam said:
“King Balak of Moab brought me
from the hills of Syria
to curse Israel
and announce its doom.
8But I can't go against God!
He did not curse
or condemn Israel.
* 9“From the mountain peaks,
I look down and see Israel,
the obedient people of God.
10They are living alone in peace.
And though they are many,
they don't bother
the other nations.
“I hope to obey God
for as long as I live
and to die in such peace.”
11Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
12Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.”
Balaam's Second Message
13Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.” 14So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
15“Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
16The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak. 17Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings.
Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
18Balaam answered:
“Pay close attention
to my words—
19God is no mere human!
He doesn't tell lies
or change his mind.
God always keeps his promises.
20“My command from God
was to bless these people,
and there's nothing I can do
to change what he has done.
21Israel's king is the Lord God.
He lives there with them
and intends them no harm.
22With the strength of a wild ox,
God led Israel out of Egypt.
23No magic charms can work
against them—
just look what God has done
for his people.
24They are like angry lions
ready to attack;
and they won't rest
until their victim
is gobbled up.”
25Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
26“I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.”
Balaam's Third Message
27Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.” 28So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
29Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
30After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi amaniye lugli uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Balaam wia
1Balaam ŋɔ Koori Balak be, “Ma mbusu lizibɔra aniidaanɛɛ ɛŋ di tɛŋ, di lauri nabala aniidaanɛɛ ni pebala aniidaanɛɛ di wa tɛŋ.” 2Koori Balak ɛɛ gunla Balaam n ŋɔwɛɛ la, ba nɛra banɛɛ hiŋ maa faa kpu nabala ni pebala kpaŋkpaŋa di lizi mbusu, mbusu lizibɔra la maa ni.
3Denii Balaam faa ŋɔ Koori Balak be, “Chi ɛŋ i mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hiŋ be, ka ń lii kɛrii di ga na. Aŋhinabe, Kɔraawiizi daŋ ba n be.” Denii u ga tinni giŋgimii bɛl n waa daazi ni kooree dɔɔwɛ u bɛŋ.
4Kɔraawiizi ba u be, u ŋɔ, “N ma mbusu lizibɔra aniidaanɛɛrɛ, di kpu nabal ni pebal di lizi mbusu bɛl maa ni.”
5Kɔraawiizi bagli Balaam gunla u niŋ ga ŋɔ tɛɛ Koori Balak di ŋɔ, “Kpa amaniye naa di ga tɛɛ Koori Balak.”
6Awia, u faa bir la Koori Balak be di ga nau, di u ni Moab hina sitɔɔra haa chigɔ u mbusu lizaa kuna la kɛrii. 7Denii Balaam lizi amaniye naa di ŋɔ,
“Moab hina Koori Balakii yiriŋ di ba,
u yirimbuu di lii Siiria
wiifurii bizenaa biine.
U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ba di wa see Izrɛl hina nua tɛŋ.
Ba di wa tɛɛ
baa chɔgri.’
8Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ di see
nɛra la Kɔraawiizi
n waa seewe nuai?
Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ di tɛɛ nɛra la
Kɔraawiizi n waa chɔgri
tɛɛwɛi?
9N na baabuu di lii bizenaa nyuuni,
di ra binni baa di lii
giŋgimee nyuuni.
Ba ɛɛ hɛri la hina n kuttɛɛ,
di zum lugɔ ba na
kissaare di kaali
hɛssi hina maa.
10Izrɛl naanna duwɔɔrɛ lugɔ nyɔɔ,
ba waa kuraa dɔɔwɛ.
Gil ń siu lugɔ nɛra la wia n deŋlee,
ń tuna ge du
lugɔ ba hora!”
11Denii Koori Balak ŋɔ Balaam be, “Ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛŋ gunnɛi? N ba i ninɛɛ lugɔ í wa see n dɔma nua, ka haa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ ka bir di kissi baa!”
12Balaam bir ŋɔ, “A waa dɛkkɛ min niŋ ŋɔ gunla Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ di du n nuaa?”
Kɔraawiizi amaniye nɛɛhiŋ uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Balaam wia
13Denii Koori Balak ŋɔ u be, “Ba ya kaali bɔr la hin niŋ ga na Izrɛl hina nɛnnɛ. Ka ba yeŋ bɛnnɛ í ga na. Denii í see baa nua tɛŋ.” 14U kpogluu la Zɔfim koo Bizeŋ Pisga nyuu, di ga ma mbusu lizibɔra aniidaanɛɛ, di kpu nabal ni pebal, di lizi mbusu a bɛl maa ni.
15Balaam ŋɔ Koori Balak be, “Chi i mbusu lizaa kuna naa be bɔnnaa, ka ń la ende di ga chem Kɔraawiizi ni.”
16Kɔraawiizi ba u be di wa kpa amaniye di du u nua di ŋɔ, “Bir la Koori Balak be dí ga kpa amaniye naa tɛu.”
17Awia, u faa bir la Koori Balak be di ga nau di u ni Moab hina sitɔɔra chigɔ u mbusu lizaa kuna la be. Koori Balak pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔi?”
18Denii Balaam lizi Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa,
“Koori Balak, izi dí nuu.
Zipɔ biibaal, á nuu n be.
19Kɔraawiizi waa newee ɛɛwɛ lugɔ ú kanni kara
gɛɛ di ɛɛ newee
lugɔ ú bir u nfɛrɛ.
U ɔɔ ŋɔ wiarɛ ka wàá ɛɛawaa?
U ɔɔ ŋɔ nuarɛ
ka wàá hiŋuuwaa?
20U ŋɔ ń kissi, u teŋ kissoore,
màá wer biruu.
21Maa nyuchɔgii maa nawɛɛ Izrɛl hina ni,
gɛɛ di na biinichɔg
ba biini.
Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la du ba benii.
Ba ra chaasi di ra ŋɔ
lugɔ waabuu ba Koori.
22Kɔraawiizii kpogli baa di lii Ijip hɛri,
ba dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa
lugɔ pir nabal.
23Ba wàá wer kpa kabirɛ
gɛɛ hiri maa
di ɛɛ baa wiimaa.
Filaŋkeŋ, nɛra daŋ ŋɔ Izrɛl hina wia di ŋɔ,
‘Na gunla Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ!’
24A nɛra duwɔɔrɛ lugɔ bunyinniina,
ba kazi ba bɔraa
alugɔ bunyiŋ n waa heezi,
see uŋ di sel la uŋ lauwɛ tuŋ,
di nyɔɔ u chal.”
25Denii Koori Balak ŋɔ Balaam be, “Gilɛɛ wàá see baa nua gɛɛ di wàá kissi baa maa!”
26Balaam bir ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ kalɛɛ lugɔ a dɛkkɔɔ miŋ ɛɛ wii la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ?”
Kɔraawiizi amaniye horohiŋ uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Balaam wia
27Denii Koori Balak ŋɔ Balaam be, “Ba ya la yembɛl. Aŋhinabe, a daŋ ga par Kɔraawiizi, ú gil i see baa nua tɛŋ.” 28Koori Balak kpogli Balaam di la Bizeŋ Pɛɔ nyuu, bɔr la hin niŋ wer chi ka ra binni a hɛribɔduma la.
29Balaam ŋɔ, “Ma mbusu lizibɔra aniidaanɛɛ ɛŋ di tɛŋ, dí lauri nabala aniidaanɛɛ ni pebala aniidaanɛɛ dí wa tɛŋ.” 30Koori Balak ɛɛ gunla Balaam n faa ŋɔwɛɛ la, di lau nabal ni pebal di lizi mbusu a bɛl maa ni.

english_text:
1Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert 2and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him, 3and Balaam said:
“I am the son of Beor,
and my words are true,
so listen to my message!
4It comes from the Lord,
the God All-Powerful.
I bowed down to him
and saw a vision of Israel.
5“People of Israel,
your camp is lovely.
6It's like a grove of palm trees
or a garden beside a river.
You are like tall aloe trees
that the Lord has planted,
or like cedars
growing near water.
7You and your descendants
will prosper like an orchard
beside a stream.
Your king will rule with power
and be a greater king
than Agag the Amalekite.
8With the strength of a wild ox,
God led you out of Egypt.
You will defeat your enemies,
shooting them with arrows
and crushing their bones.
9 Like a lion you lie down,
resting after an attack.
Who would dare disturb you?
“Anyone who blesses you
will be blessed;
anyone who curses you
will be cursed.”
10When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times. 11Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
12Balaam answered, “I told your messengers 13that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me. 14So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.”
Balaam's Fourth Message
15Balaam said:
“I am the son of Beor,
and my words are true,
so listen to my message!
16My knowledge comes
from God Most High,
the Lord All-Powerful.
I bowed down to him
and saw a vision of Israel.
17“What I saw in my vision
hasn't happened yet.
But someday, a king of Israel
will appear like a star.
He will wipe out you Moabites
and destroy those tribes
who live in the desert.
18Israel will conquer Edom
and capture the land
of that enemy nation.
19The king of Israel will rule
and destroy the survivors
of every town there.
20“And I saw this vision
about the Amalekites:
Their nation is now great,
but it will someday
disappear forever.
21“And this is what I saw
about the Kenites:
They think they're safe,
living among the rocks,
22but they will be wiped out
when Assyria conquers them.
23“No one can survive
if God plans destruction.
24Ships will come from Cyprus,
bringing people who will invade
the lands of Assyria and Eber.
But finally, Cyprus itself
will be ruined.”
25After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_text:
1Balaam n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ a par Kɔraawiizii lugɔ ú kissi Izrɛl hina la, waa kaa la ú ga pɛɛzi gɛɛ di kpa hiri, gunla uŋ ɔɔ faa ɛɛ la, ka bir u siwee di chaŋ a hɛribɔduma. 2Balaam n wa binnɛɛ di na Izrɛl hina la n chɔɔgɛɛ di hiŋzi ba dizi di wa kaali, Kɔraawiizi Duma izuu, 3u lizi Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa, di ŋɔ,
“Kɔraawiizi amaniye la uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ
Bɛɔ biibaal Balaam la,
chaanɔɔrɛ.
4Nɛr la n na nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔbee amaniyee keŋ,
unla n na na wia lugɔ deeza biini di ra lii
Kɔraawiizi La N Ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ be,
ɔɔ choluu tɛr, u siwee pilli.
5Izrɛl hina,
ii tanti diini wessoo werge!
6A chɔɔ kaali alugɔ walli,
alugɔ kambola
n du muu kɛrii,
alugɔ daazi aŋhina
banna yir alozi Kɔraawiizi n duuwe,
alugɔ hɛriŋkpol daazi
n chigɛ niiri kɛraa.
7Ba daŋ na donii werge,
ba kunduulaa
na nii werge.
Ba koori daŋ kaali Koori Agag werge maa,
u kora daŋ dɔɔ girme
di yaa werge di la bɔɔnɛɛ.
8Kɔraawiizi kpogli baabuu di lii Ijip hɛri,
di ɔɔ naa ra tɛɛ baa
alugɔ pir nabal.
Ba ra ligli ba dɔma
di ra purgi ba hoga,
di ŋmuuri ba hobee.
9Ba ɔɔ giŋŋuu alugɔ bunyiŋ ka chɔɔgi,
alugɔ bunyinniina,
anɛɛ n niŋ sɛɛ lalli baai?
Banla n na kissi ia daŋ na kissaa,
ka nuuseezi di banla
n na see ia nuuzi!”
10Denii Koori Balak baaŋ fuuh Balaam ni werge. U lɔ kpaa di ŋɔ u be, “N yiriibuu lugɔ í wa see n dɔma nua, ka i wa kissi baa buhoro maa. 11A kpo filaŋkennaa maa! N faa ŋɔ lugɔ n daŋ turgii nɛnnɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi waa sɛɛwɛ.”
12Balaam ŋɔ u be, “N faa ŋɔ i balaa la hiŋ hummɛ n be labuu, 13‘Haali di Koori Balak kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ di su u kooridia tɛŋ gba, ka màá wer ɛɛ n kipar, di winaniirɛ gɛɛ wichɔgiirɛ, see wii la bɛŋ Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ń ŋɔ.’ 14Filaŋkeŋ, n bittɔɔ di ra kaali n nɛra be, ka n na karfiibuu gunla Izrɛl hina naa n niŋ kɛrɛ bɛl dau i nɛra.”
Kɔraawiizi amaniye naazuhiŋ uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Balaam wia
15Denii Balaam lizi Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa, di ŋɔ,
“Kɔraawiizi amaniye la uŋ kpawɛɛ
tɛɛ Bɛɔ biibaal Balaam la,
chaanɔɔrɛ.
16Nɛr la n na nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔbee
amaniyee keŋ,
unla n na na wia lugɔ deeza biini di ra lii
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋaa maa hiŋ be,
ɔɔ choluu tɛr, u siwee pilli.
17Wii la mìŋ́ nawɛɛ lugɔ deeza biini la,
haa waa ɛɛwɛ.
Ka ŋmɛnɛbɛl Izrɛl hina koori bɛl
daŋ lii lugɔ chinchiŋwilii.
U daŋ dim Moab hina sitɔɔra,
di chɔgi Sɛf dizi maa.
18U daŋ lɔ Ɛdɔm hɛri di kpegluu,
di lauri ba dɔma,
ka Izrɛl hina
fɔŋŋa ra nyaŋŋi.
19Izrɛl hina koori,
daŋ chɔgi Ɛdɔm bolzenaa la
n kawɛɛ la hina maa.”
Kɔraawiizi amaniye tunahiŋ uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Balaam wia
20Denii Balaam faa na Amalɛk hina wia lugɔ deeza biini, di lizi Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa,
“Amalɛk hinaa faa ɛɛ hɛssi maa fɔŋŋa hina,
ka a tuna maa,
ba daŋ dim.”
21Denii u na Kɛn hina wia lugɔ deeza biini, di lizi Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa.
“Ii sognibɔr la waa tɔɔrɔɔ maa dɔɔwɛ,
ii so nɛnnɛ
alugɔ zumbee n du daŋ
bii bɔɔ n du chiŋ,
22ka ba daŋ chɔgi ii Kɛn hina,
di Asiiria hɛri hina wa
kpegli ia di lauri.”
23Denii u lizi u Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa.
“Eei, anɛɛ n niŋ wer di miibɔɔ
di Kɔraawiizi wa ɛɛ kennei?
24Muugberzenaa daŋ
lii Saiprɔs muuzeŋ
kɛrii di ba,
Ba daŋ wa kpegli Asiiria ni Ɛba hina,
ka ba gba daŋ wa chol.”
25Denii Balaam jaa izi di kpo u bol, ka Koori Balak ge kpa u ŋmɛnɛɛ di kaali.

english_text:
The Israelites Worship Baal
1While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women. 2These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
3The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor. 4So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
5Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
6Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family. 7Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear 8and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease, 9but 24,000 Israelites had already died.
10The Lord said to Moses, 11“In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me. 12-13But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
14The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe. 15And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
16The Lord told Moses, 17-18“The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina ni Moab hina wia
1Izrɛl hina n na ba di wa so Sitim la, ba baala lauri Moab hina haana di ra nyiŋŋi. 2A haana ɔɔ jaa yir baa, ba ni baa ga kpau di ra la ba vuga kuaribɔra, di ra di a diwee di ra kuaraa. 3Awia, Izrɛl hina jaa ba ni di ra jaami vug Baal n du Pɛɔ la. Guŋ gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh ba ni werge maa.
4Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Lau Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra la n ɛɛ guŋ, di kpuuzi baa bɔchaaŋ n see, guŋ daŋ lizi n baaŋfuuihchɔgii la di lii Izrɛl hina maa ni.”
5Awia, Moosis jaa ŋɔ a Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra la be, “Ií bɛl maa kpu baala la n jaa a nɛra ni di ra kuari ba vug Baal la n du Pɛɔ la.”
6Izrɛl hina la bɛl lau Midian hina haaŋ bɛl, di zuu u tanti dia Moosis ni a nɛra maa sibɔɔ, di ba ra wii ni dɔgnya Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua. 7Finɛhas la n ɛɛ Ɛliaza biibaal, u naabaal ge ɛɛ Aarɔn la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ n wa na guŋ, u lii a bɔr la baŋ chaalɛɛ hiŋ, di ga kpa kandaa, 8di hiŋ a Izrɛl hinuu guŋŋ di ga zuu a tanti dia, uŋ ga zuuwɛ, u yag a baal, u saagi di ga zuu a haaŋ ni ba siuzi. A guŋ jaa gil wiilchɔgaa la n lauri Izrɛl hina la jaa tuŋ. 9Ka banla n tɛŋ siuzɛɛ faa du nɛra kagboŋa tokko ni anaazu.
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 11“Finɛhas la n ɛɛ Ɛliaza biibaal, u naabaal ɛɛ Aarɔn n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la, lizi n baannɛ di lii Izrɛl hina ni, dikuu gunla un ɛɛwɛ la wia, n baaŋ waa kaa ra fuuh Izrɛl hina ni. Waa sɛɛwɛ u kuari vug maa, see miŋ, guŋ wiarɛ maa sɛɛwɛ n chɔgi baa la. 12Awia, ŋɔ u be, dí n na nyiŋŋuu yá dɔɔ bampirsɔna nuukpaŋ. 13Dí u ni u dee maa daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehina di hanna la, dikuu uŋ faa aah siwii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi na girme, di faa lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih dikuu Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa wia.”
14Izrɛl hinuu la baŋ faa kpau u ni Midian hina haaŋ, di kpu la, sɔnnɛ Zimri. U mɛɛ sɔnnɛ Salu, waa faa ɛɛ Simɛɔn hina dee la bɛl sitɔɔri. 15Midian hina haaŋ la baŋ faa kpuwɛɛ hiŋ ge sɔnnɛ Kɔzbi, u ge mɛɛrɛ Zur n faa ɛɛ Midian hina iri bɛl dee sitɔɔri.
16Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 17“A ɛɛ a Midian hina alugɔ i dɔma di kpuuzi baa, 18dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa ra ɛɛ iabuu lugɔ ba dɔma, di dar ia ii ra kuari ba vug Baal n du Pɛɔ la, di faa gil bá kpu Kɔzbi la n ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri bɛl biihaaŋ la, wiilchɔgaa saŋa la.”

english_text:
The Israelites Are Counted a Second Time
1 After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron, 2“I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man 20 years and older who is able to serve in Israel's army.”
3Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them 4what the Lord had said about counting the men 20 years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
5-7There were 43,730 men from the tribe of Reuben, the oldest son of Jacob. These men were from the clans of Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. 8Pallu was the father of Eliab 9and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord. 10That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed 250 men as a warning to the other Israelites. 11But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
12-14There were 22,200 men from the tribe of Simeon; they were from the clans of Nemuel, Jamin, Jachin, Zerah, and Shaul.
15-18There were 40,500 men from the tribe of Gad; they were from the clans of Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Ozni, Eri, Arod, and Areli.
19-22There were 76,500 men from the tribe of Judah; they were from the clans of Shelah, Perez, and Zerah, as well as Hezron and Hamul, whose ancestor was Perez. Judah's sons Er and Onan had died in Canaan.
23-25There were 64,300 men from the tribe of Issachar; they were from the clans of Tola, Puvah, Jashub, and Shimron.
26-27There were 60,500 men from the tribe of Zebulun; they were from the clans of Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
28-34There were 52,700 men from the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph; they were from the clan of Machir, the clan of Gilead his son, and the clans of his six grandsons: Iezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida, and Hepher. Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, but he had five daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
35-37There were 32,500 men from the tribe of Ephraim son of Joseph; they were from the clans of Shuthelah, Becher, Tahan, and Eran the son of Shuthelah.
38-41There were 45,600 men from the tribe of Benjamin; they were from the clans of Bela, Ashbel, Ahiram, Shephupham, Hupham, as well as from Ard and Naaman, the two sons of Bela.
42-43There were 64,400 men from the tribe of Dan; they were all from the clan of Shuham.
44-47There were 53,400 men from the tribe of Asher; they were from the clans of Imnah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and from the two clans of Heber and Malchiel, the sons of Beriah. Asher's daughter was Serah.
48-50There were 45,400 men from the tribe of Naphtali; they were from the clans of Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
51The total number of Israelite men listed was 601,730.
52 The Lord said to Moses, 53“Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one, 54so the larger tribes have more land than the smaller ones. 55-56I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
57The tribe of Levi included the clans of the Gershonites, Kohathites, Merarites, 58as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram, 59the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. 60 Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. 61 But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
62In the tribe of Levi there were 23,000 men and boys at least a month old. They were not listed with the other tribes, because they would not receive any land in Canaan.
63Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho. 64None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive, 65 except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_text:
Nɛra kuraa nɛɛhiŋ wia
1A wiila n wa tunnɛ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn biibaal Ɛliaza be, 2“Kur Izrɛl hina maa ba diini biini, di chi banla n di binni tokko ni saga, n kpekke di hel laal lɔi.” 3Awia, di lii Moab hina lɛla la n chɔɔ Jɔɔdan muu kɛrii, di chaŋ bolzeŋ Jɛriko la, n du u baŋgia bɛl labuu, Moosis ni Ɛliaza la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la ŋɔ ba be, 4“Ií kur a baala la maa n di binni tokko ka sag gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ ú ɛɛ la.”
Izrɛl hina la n faa lii Ijip labuu keŋ.
5Di lii Jekɔb biinabɔma Rubin dee biini nɛraa faa,
Hanɔk domee,
Palu domee,
6Hɛzrɔn domee,

Guŋ faa ɛɛwɔɔ di ɛɛ karfaa tɛɛ a Izrɛl hina banla n kawɛɛ la. 11Ka Kora dee la maa faa waa dimme kɔrai.
12Simɛɔn dee domeezii faa,

Jakin domee,

Ɛri domee,

ani Zɛra domee.

29Manasɛ dee,

Asriɛl domee,

Bɛl maa daŋ na u hor ú ɛɛ u kapɛttɛ kuŋ di lii gunla maga baŋ sɛbi ba sɔna di mag. 55Gil bá ta kuna dikuu a hɛri wia. Suge maa daŋ di ba naabaala sɔŋ. 56Ií ta kuna di bɔnni a kapɛttɛzi bɛl maa di tɛɛ banla nɛra n kpillɛ ani banla nɛra n waa kpil la maa.”

Gɛsɔn domee,
Kɔhaf domee,
Mɛrari domee.

Libni domee,
Hɛbrɔn domee,
Mali domee,
Musi domee,
Kɔra domee.

english_text:
The Daughters of Zelophehad Are Given Land
1Zelophehad was from the Manasseh tribe, and he had five daughters, whose names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
2One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
3You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord.
Our father left no sons 4to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
5Moses asked the Lord what should be done, 6and the Lord answered:
7 Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
8Tell the Israelites that when a man dies without a son, his daughter will inherit his land. 9If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land. 10But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land. 11And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it.
Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader
(Deuteronomy 31.1-8)
12 The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites. 13After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron, 14because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
15Moses replied, 16“You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel. 17 Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
18 The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place. 19Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader 20and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you. 21 But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
22Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people, 23 then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.
translation_text:
Zɛlɔfɛhad biihambizi wia
1Mala, Noowa, Hɔgla, Milka ani Tirza faa ɛɛ Zɛlɔfɛhad biihaanaa. Zɛlɔfɛhad mɛɛrɛ faa Hɛfa, Hɛfa ge mɛɛ ɛɛ Giliad, u ge mɛɛ ɛɛ Makir, Makir ge mɛɛ ɛɛ Manasɛ, u ge mɛɛ ɛɛ Joosɛf. 2A hɔl bɛl a biihaana izi la ga chem Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza, Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi ani Izrɛl hina maa ni Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua di ŋɔ, 3“Yaa mɛɛ siuwɔɔ hɛribɔduma la biini. U faa waa Kɔra harbɔɔ hiŋra la biini jaawɛ, baabuu faa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua la. Ka u siuwɔɔ dikuu u himmaa wichɔgaa wia, di waa biibaal lullɛ. 4Bɛɛ wiarɛ yaa mɛɛ sɔŋ dim u domee biini, dikuu uŋ waa biibaal lullɛ wiai? Ií tɛɛ yaa, yaa kapɛttɛ di lii yaa mɛɛ lulla biini.”
5Denii Moosis kpa ba wia maa di wa dau Kɔraawiizi see. 6Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, 7“Kennaa Zɛlɔfɛhad biihaana naa n na ŋɔ naa ɛɛ wibiire. A dɛkkɔɔ í tɛɛ baa ba kapɛttɛ di lii ba mɛɛ lulla biini. Di kpa ba mɛɛ kapɛttɛ kuna la maa di jaa baa.
8Ií ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Di nɛr maa haŋ wa siu di waa biibaal dɔɔwɛ, ií kpa u kapɛttɛ tɛɛ u biihaaŋ. 9Di waa biihaaŋ ge gba dɔɔwɛ, ií kpaa tɛɛ u kpɛɛma gɛɛ u niwee. 10Di waa kpɛɛnna gɛɛ niuna dɔɔwɛ, ií kpaa tɛɛ u mɛɛbee gɛɛ u mɛɛzeŋ. 11Di u mɛɛ waa mɛɛ ni maa bie maa dɔɔwɛ, ií kpa a kapɛttɛ kuna tɛɛ u lulli himmaa la n lii ba dee biini. Waabuu niŋ wer dia. A kennaa daŋ ɛɛ Gbɔg tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ ú ɛɛ la.’ ”
Josua n kpa Moosis gawa wia
12Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Tinni Abarim bizenaa nyuuni, di ga na hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la. 13Di i wa nau tuŋ, i ge gba daŋ siu gunla i kpɛɛma Aarɔn n siuwɛ la, 14dikuubɛɛwiai, ii maanii faa gbɛlliŋ, di vɛɛ n nua di lii Mɛriba la n dugli bolzeŋ Kadɛs n du Zin Hɛribɔduma la. Saŋa la Izrɛl hina n nuumɛɛ ra duŋ de la, ii ge gba faa waa n fɔŋŋa la n ɛɛ naniinanii la tɔgzɛɛ ba sibɔɔ.”
15Denii Moosis ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, 16“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la n na tɛɛ kummaa miibɔɔ, n na suŋŋiibuu, lizi sitɔɔri di tɛɛ a nɛra, 17waabuu niŋ ɔɔ ra tɔ ba see laal biini, guŋ gil i nɛra gilɛɛ ɛɛ lugɔ peeza la n waa binni dɔɔwɛ.”
18Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Lizi Nun biibaal Josua la n niŋ wer hum a huma, di kpa i nonee sag u nyuu, di kissuu. 19Gil ú chi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza ani nɛra la maa see, í kpau bagli baa lugɔ waa niŋ jaa wa ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri. 20Kpa i fɔŋŋazeŋ la yeŋ tɛu, Izrɛl hina maa ra nuu u nua, di ra tɔgzuu. 21U daŋ ɔɔ dɛlli Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza la n niŋ ɔɔ kpa Urim ni Tumim di ra zum n kipar labuu. Di u wa ŋɔ bá lii, ba daŋ lii, di u wa ŋɔ bá zuu, ba daŋ zuu.”
22Denii Moosis jaa ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la. Di lau Josua lii chi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza ani nɛra la maa n chaali de la see, 23ka jaa kpa u nonii sag u nyuu, di lizuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

english_text:
Regular Daily Sacrifices
(Exodus 29.38-43; Leviticus 6.8-13)
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the people of Israel:
Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
3Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them; 4one will be sacrificed in the morning, and the other in the evening. 5Along with each of them, one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. 6This sacrifice to please me was first offered at Mount Sinai. 7Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering. 8The second ram will be sacrificed that evening, along with the other offerings, just like the one sacrificed that morning. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
The Sacrifice on the Sabbath
The Lord said:
9-10On the Sabbath, in addition to the regular daily sacrifices, you must sacrifice two rams a year old to please me. These rams must have nothing wrong with them, and they will be sacrificed with a drink offering and two kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil.
The Sacrifices on the First Day of the Month
The Lord said:
11On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me. 12Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram, 13and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
14-15Offer two liters of wine as a drink offering with each bull, one and a half liters with the ram, and one liter with each of the young rams.
Finally, you must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
These sacrifices are to be offered on the first day of each month, in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
The Sacrifices during Passover and the Festival of Thin Bread
(Leviticus 23.4-8)
The Lord said:
16 Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year. 17 The following day will begin the Festival of Thin Bread, which will last for a week. During this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast.
18On the first day of this festival, you must rest from your work and come together for worship. 19Bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me. 20Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram, 21and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. 22Also offer a goat as a sacrifice for the sins of the people. 23-24All of these are to be offered each day of the festival in additional to the regular sacrifices, and the smoke from them will please me. 25Then on the last day of the festival, you must once again rest from work and come together for worship.
The Sacrifices during the Harvest Festival
(Leviticus 23.15-22)
The Lord said:
26 On the first day of the Harvest Festival, you must rest from your work, come together for worship, and bring a sacrifice of new grain. 27Offer two young bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. 28Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram, 29and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. 30Also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin. 31The animals must have nothing wrong with them and are to be sacrificed along with the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_text:
Hɔpizi biimaa mbusuzi lizaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 2“Gil Izrɛl hina ɔɔ kpa diwee la ban niŋ ɔɔ fuuh di ra lizi mbusu la sɔɔh n summɛ ra tɛŋ la, bɔɔni saŋazi la miŋ dauwɛ la. 3Ŋɔ ba be, ‘Kuna la iin niŋ kpa di lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii di ra tɛŋ la daŋ ɛɛ pebala anɛɛ la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ, gunla iin ɔɔ ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii saŋa maa la, á ɛɛ hɔpizi biimaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii. 4Ɛɛ kpu a pebal bɛl chɔɔzi ni, di kaa kpu bɛl ge duana ni, 5di kpa mbusu lizaa mia sakɔla kookoo tassa suul, di koozi ɔlivi nuu pirintua ni keza ni, di buu lizi mbusu tɛŋ. 6A keŋ mbusu naa lizaa faa chɔɔwɔɔ tɛɛ ia di lii Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu, lugɔ ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ di ra pariŋ. 7Di kaa kpa siŋ pirintua ni keza di jaa a sel bɛl maa ni, di wa fug a siŋ di waari mbusu lizibɔr hiŋ ni di tɛŋ. 8I daŋ kpu pebinɛɛhiŋ la ge duaninsɔŋ, dí kpa kuna la hiŋ faa kpawɛɛ jaa chɔɔzinhor la ni, dí fuuuh alugɔ chɔɔzinhor la, u sɔɔh du sum di pariŋ.
Heezaa Hɔpizii mbusu lizaa wia
9Heezaa Hɔpizii la, lau peballi anɛɛ la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, n kpekke nɛnnɛ, di kpa mbusu lizaa siŋ ani mbusu lizaa mia sakɔla kookoo tassazi anɛɛ suul baŋ kpa nuu koozi di lizi mbusu. 10Anniibuu niŋ ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpizii maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii, di kpa hɔpizi biimaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la jaa.
Baagu maa mbusu lizaa wia
11Baagu maa lugli hɔpizii, ií ɔɔ kpa naballi anɛɛ, pebal ani peballi aniidaanɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ, di lizi mbusu di fuuah tɛŋ. 12Ii daŋ kpa mbusu lizaa mia sakɔla kookoo tassazi ahoro, di kpa nuu di koozi a ni, di jaa a nabal bɛl maa ni, ka a pebalwaa, nuu kookoo tassazi anɛɛrɛ ií kpa jaa u ni, di lizi mbusu lizaa mia, 13guŋ himmaanii ií ɔɔ kpa mia sakɔla kookoo tassa suul di jaa peballi la bɛl maa ge ni, di lizi mbusu lizaa mia. Annii daŋ ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ. 14Siŋ pirintua ni kezaa ií ɔɔ kpa jaa a nabal bɛl maa ni, di pebal genii, siŋ pirintuani anɛɛrɛ ií ɔɔ kpa jaa u ni, di pebalee genii, siŋ pirintuarɛ ií ɔɔ kpa jaa u ni. Baagu maa lugli hɔpizii, bina maa biini mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii lizaarɛ guŋ. 15Di kpa jaa a keŋ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ani siŋ iiŋ ɔɔ lizi di ra ɛɛ guŋ saŋa maa la, buballɛ ií ɔɔ lizi, di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛŋ.
Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ dii mbusu lizaa wia
16A dɛkkɔɔ ií ɔɔ ra di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la bina maa, lugli baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl, di ra tɔgziŋ. 17A baagu naa hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔl maa, ií ɔɔ ra di iihinaa, di ra hee paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. 18A lugli hɔpizii, ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami, ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma. 19Ií kpa naballi anɛɛ ni pebal ani peballi aniidaanɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ, di lizi mbusu fuuah tɛŋ. 20Ii daŋ kpa sakɔla kookoo tassazi ahoro, di kpa nuu koozi a ni, di jaa a nabal bɛl maa ni, ka a pebalwaa, sakɔla kookoo tassazi anɛɛrɛ ií kpa jaa u ni, di lizi mbusu lizaa mia, 21guŋ himmaanii ií ɔɔ kpa sakɔla kookoo tassa di jaa pebalee maa ge ni, di lizi mbusu lizaa mia. Annii daŋ ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ. 22Ií ɔɔ kpa bubal di jaa, ú ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih lizaa dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia mbusu lizaa. 23Ií ɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ di jaa chɔɔziŋ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la ni, alugɔ iiŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ la. 24Ií ɔɔ kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii diwee la di ɛɛ guŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Ii daŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ di jaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni siŋ la ni, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ di tɛŋ. 25Ií ɔɔ chaali a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl la, di jaami ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa.
Kuna Kumaa Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia
26Ií ɔɔ chaali dɔŋa Kuna Kumaa Hɔpizizeŋ dii hɔl la iiŋ ɔɔ kpa mifalaa di waa tɛŋ la, di jaami, ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa. 27Ií kpa naballi anɛɛ di lizi mbusu di fuuh ani pebal ni peballi aniidaanɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, a sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ. 28Ii daŋ kpa mbusu lizaa mia kookoo tassazi ahoro, di kpa nuu koozi a ni, dí jaa a naballi bɛl maa ni, ka a pebalwaa, kookoo tassazi anɛɛrɛ ií kpa jaa u ni, 29di kpa sakɔla kookoo tassakpaŋ jaa pebalee bɛl maa ni. 30Ií ɔɔ kpa bubal jaa, ú ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih lizaa mbusu dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia. 31Ií ɔɔ kpa siŋ jaa bɛl maa ni di lizi mbusu, saŋa maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la ani mbusu lizaa mia la ni. Ií ɔɔ ra du tau di gil a sel bɛl maa du kpeg nɛnnɛ.’ ”

english_text:
The Sacrifices at the Festival of Trumpets
(Leviticus 23.23-25)
The Lord said:
1On the first day of the seventh month, you must rest from your work and come together to celebrate at the sound of the trumpets. 2Bring to the altar one bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me. 3Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram, 4and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. 5You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin. 6These sacrifices will be made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices and the sacrifices for the first day of the month. The smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
The Sacrifices on the Great Day of Forgiveness
(Leviticus 23.26-32)
The Lord said:
7 The tenth day of the seventh month is the Great Day of Forgiveness. On that day you must rest from all work and come together for worship. Show sorrow for your sins by going without food, 8and bring to the altar one young bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me. 9Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram, 10and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. 11A goat must also be sacrificed for the sins of the people. You will offer these sacrifices in addition to the sacrifice to ask forgiveness and the regular daily sacrifices.
The Sacrifices during the Festival of Shelters
(Leviticus 23.33-44)
The Lord said:
12 Beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and continuing for seven days, everyone must celebrate the Festival of Shelters in honor of me.
13On the first day, you must rest from your work and come together for worship. Bring to the altar 13 bulls, 2 full-grown rams, and 14 rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me. 14Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the rams, 15and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. 16You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These are to be offered in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
17-34For the next six days of the festival, you will sacrifice one less bull than the day before, so that on the seventh day, seven bulls will be sacrificed. The other sacrifices and offerings must remain the same for each of these days.
35On the eighth day, you must once again rest from your work and come together for worship. 36Bring to the altar one bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me. 37You must also offer the proper grain sacrifices and drink offerings of wine with each animal. 38And offer a goat as the sacrifice to ask forgiveness for the people. These sacrifices are made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
39You must offer all these sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, together with any offerings that are voluntarily given or given because of a promise.
40Moses told the people of Israel everything the Lord had told him about the sacrifices.
translation_text:
Bensunoniinazi Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia
1Kɔraawiizi ga Moosis be di kaa ŋɔ, “Baaguzi aniidaanɛɛ lugli hɔpizii, ií ɔɔ chaali dɔŋa be di jaami, ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma. Ií ɔɔ huuh bensunoniinazi a hɔpizii. 2Ií ɔɔ lau nabalee, pebal ani peballi aniidaanɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ lizi mbusu di fuuah, á ɛɛ sɔɔh la n summɛ tɛŋ. 3Ií ɔɔ kpa mbusu lizaa mia sakɔla kookoo tassazi ahoro ani nuu di koozi dɔŋa ni, di kpaa jaa a nabal la ni, di kpa sakɔla kookoo tassazi anɛɛ di jaa pebal la ni, di lizi mbusu lizaa mia, 4di kpa kookoo tassa jaa a pebalee bɛl maa ni. 5Di kpa bubal ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih ii ni. 6Annii maa daŋ jaa hɔpizi biimaa, baagu maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, mia ani siŋ mbusuzi la ni, gunla baŋ baglɛɛ la, á ɛɛ mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa la sɔɔh n summɛ di tɛŋ.
Kɔraawiizi Baaŋfuuih Lizaa Hɔpizi wia
7A baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ naa hɔpizaa fi hɔl, ií ɔɔ chaali dí jaami, ka gilɛɛ waa di gɛɛ di waa hum huma maa. 8Ií ɔɔ kpa nabalee ni pebal ani peballi aniidaanɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ, di lizi mbusu di fuuah, á sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ. 9Ií ɔɔ kpa sakɔla kookoo tassazi ahoro ni nuu di koozi dɔŋa ni, di kaa ɛɛ sakɔla kookoo tassazi anɛɛ di jaa a pebal ge ni, di kpaa lizi mbusu. 10Ií ɔɔ kpa sakɔla libee suul di jaa a pebalee bɛl maa ni. 11Ií ɔɔ kpa bubal ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di jaa wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa ni, di ra lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih ii ni ani saŋa maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii, mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ.
Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia
12A baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔl, ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami, ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa gunla iin ɔɔ ra hum la. Ií ɔɔ di iihinaa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ di ra tɔgzi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. 13Ií ɔɔ kpa naballi fidaahoro, pebala anɛɛ ani peballi fidaanaazu, n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ, di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii, ú ɛɛ sɔɔh la n summɛ tɛŋ. 14Ií ɔɔ ɛɛ kookoo tassazi ahoro ani nuu di koozi dɔŋa ni di jaa a naballi fidaahoro la bɛl maa ni, di lizi mbusu lizaa mia, di kaa ɛɛ kookoo tassazi anɛɛ di jaa a pebala anɛɛ la ge bɛl maa ni. 15A peballi fidaanaazu la ge bɛl maa, sakɔla kookoo tassa suulle ií ɔɔ kpa jaa u ni. 16Ií ɔɔ kpa bubal kpaŋ di jaa, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di jaa hɔpizi biimaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ani mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ la ni, gunla iiŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ la.
17A hɔpizaa anɛɛhiŋ hɔl, ií ɔɔ lau naballi fidaanɛɛ, pebala anɛɛ ani peballi fidaanaazu n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, n kpekke nɛnnɛ, 18di ɛɛ a mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ sirya, gunla baŋ baglɛɛ la. 19Ií ɔɔ kpu bubal jaa, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di jaa hɔpizi biimaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ani mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ la ni.
20A hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ hɔl, ií ɔɔ kpu naballi fidikpaŋ ni pebala anɛɛ ani peballi fidaanaazu la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ. 21Lau a naballi, a pebala ani peballi la maa jaa mbusuzi lizaa mia ni a siŋ ni, gunla baŋ baglɛɛ la. 22Ií ɔɔ lau bubal kpaŋ di jaa a ni, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ la maa jaa.
23A hɔpizaa anaazuhiŋ hɔl, ií ɔɔ kpu naballi fi ni pebala anɛɛ ani peballi fidaanaazu la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, n kpekke nɛnnɛ. 24Lau a naballi, a pebala ani a peballi maa jaa a mbusuzi lizaa mia ni a siŋ ni, gunla baŋ baglɛɛ la. 25Ií ɔɔ lau bubal di jaa a ni, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ la maa di jaa.
26A hɔpizaa anuehiŋ hɔl, ií ɔɔ kpu naballi kabɛl ni pebala anɛɛ ani peballi fidaanaazu la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ. 27Lau a naballi, a pebala ani a peballi maa di jaa mbusuzi lizaa mia ni a siŋ ni, gunla baŋ baglɛɛ la. 28Ií ɔɔ lau bubal kpaŋ jaa a ni, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ la maa di jaa.
29A hɔpizaa anumbɛlhiŋ hɔl, ií ɔɔ kpu naballi ŋmantannaazi ni pebala anɛɛ ani peballi fidaanaazu la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ. 30Lau a naballi, a pebala ani a peballi maa di jaa a mbusuzi lizaa mia ni a siŋ ni, gunla baŋ baglɛɛ la. 31Ií ɔɔ lau bubal jaa a ni, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ la maa di jaa.
32A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, ií ɔɔ kpu naballi aniidaanɛɛ ni pebala anɛɛ ani peballi fidaanaazu la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ. 33Lau a naballi, a pebala ani a peballi maa jaa mbusuzi lizaa mia ni a siŋ ni, gunla baŋ baglɛɛ la. 34Ií ɔɔ lau bubal di jaa a ni, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ la maa di jaa.
35A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ, ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami, ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa. 36Ií ɔɔ kpu nabalee, pebal ani peballi aniidaanɛɛ la n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa n kpekke nɛnnɛ, di lizi mbusu di fuuah, á sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ. 37Lau a nabalee, a pebal ani a peballi maa di jaa mbusuzi lizaa mia ni a siŋ ni, gunla baŋ baglɛɛ la. 38Ií ɔɔ lau bubal jaa a ni, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, di kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ la maa di jaa.
39Widaulaa la n chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, mbusuzi lizaa mia ni siŋ ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa la iin niŋ ɔɔ ra ligzi ii hɔpizizenaa dii saŋazii guŋ, di kpa jaa ii nuuzi la iin lɛɛwɛ ani ii kipar mbusuzi lizaa ni.”
40Awia, Moosis faa bagli Izrɛl hina gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

english_text:
Making Promises to the Lord
1The Lord told Moses to say to Israel's tribal leaders:
2 When one of you men makes a promise to the Lord, you must keep your word.
3Suppose a young woman who is still living with her parents makes a promise to the Lord. 4If her father hears about it and says nothing, she must keep her promise. 5But if he hears about it and objects, then she no longer has to keep her promise.
