So I am giving you fair warning today, and I call the earth and the sky as witnesses. If you ever make idols, the Lord will be angry, and you won't have long to live, because the Lord will let you be wiped out. 27 Only a few of you will survive, and the Lord will force you to leave the land and will scatter you among the nations. 28There you will have to worship gods made of wood and stone, and these are nothing but idols that can't see or hear or eat or smell.
29-30 In all of your troubles, you may finally decide that you want to worship only the Lord. And if you turn back to him and obey him completely, he will again be your God. 31The Lord your God will have mercy—he won't destroy you or desert you. The Lord will remember his promise, and he will keep the agreement he made with your ancestors.
32-34When the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, you saw how he fought for you and showed his great power by performing terrifying miracles. You became his people, and at Mount Sinai you heard him talking to you out of fiery flames. And yet you are still alive! Has anything like this ever happened since the time God created humans? No matter where you go or who you ask, you will get the same answer. No one has ever heard of another god even trying to do such things as the Lord your God has done for you.
35-36 The Lord wants you to know he is the only true God, and he wants you to obey him. That's why he let you see his mighty miracles and his fierce fire on earth, and why you heard his voice from that fire and from the sky.
37The Lord loved your ancestors and decided that you would be his people. So the Lord used his great power to bring you out of Egypt. 38Now you face other nations more powerful than you are, but the Lord has already started forcing them out of their land and giving it to you.
39So remember that the Lord is the only true God, whether in the sky above or on the earth below. 40Today I am explaining his laws and teachings. And if you always obey them, you and your descendants will live long and be successful in the land the Lord is giving you.
Safe Towns
41-43 Moses said, “People of Israel, you must set aside the following three towns east of the Jordan River as Safe Towns: Bezer in the desert highlands belonging to the Reuben tribe; Ramoth in Gilead, belonging to the Gad tribe; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to the Manasseh tribe. If you kill a neighbor without meaning to, and if you had not been angry with that person, you can run to one of these towns and find safety.”
The Second Speech: Moses Tells What the Lord Demands
Israel at Beth-Peor
44-46The Israelites had come from Egypt and were camped east of the Jordan River near Beth-Peor, when Moses gave these laws and teachings. The land around their camp had once belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon. But Moses and the Israelites defeated him 47and King Og of Bashan, and took their lands. These two Amorite kings had ruled the territory east of the Jordan River 48from the town of Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River gorge, north to Mount Hermon. 49Their land included the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, as far south as the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
translation_text:
A dɛkkɔ Izrɛl hina n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua
1Denii Moosis ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu n be. Ií ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni naa, minna nyiŋŋi n bagli ia naa. Ií ra hiŋaa di dɔɔ miibɔɔ, di wer zuu di foozi hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la ii mɛɛwaa n na hum la, n na tɛɛ ia la di dɔɔ. 2Wia naa minna tɛɛ ia naa, ií gilɛɛ waa jaa wiimaa a ni gɛɛ di waa lizi wiimaa di ra ha. Ka ií ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia naa.
3Ii himmaa siwee na Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaarɛ Bizeŋ Pɛɔ nyuu. U faa kpuuzi nɛra la maa n faa ra kuari vug Baal Bizeŋ Pɛɔ nyuu labuu, 4ka ii banla waa n lawuu kpogli chigigi la haa ra nyinuu zinaa.
5Ií na, n bagli iabuu Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni gunla uŋ ŋɔ ń ɛɛ la, ií wer di ra hiŋaa, hɛri la iinna la ii ga zuu di foozi dɔɔ la biini. 6Ií ra hiŋaa nɛnnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, gunnɛ niŋ bagli ii nunzuma dɔɔi ani ii wia zɛɛ zumaa. Di durnya hɛssi hina la wa nuu Gbɔgni naa, ba daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Wibii maa, hɛrzeŋ naa hina ɛɛ nunzunnaa, di ra nuu wia zɛɛ.’ 7Hɛrzeŋbɛlii nɛra vugrɛ dugli baa kennaa Kɔraawiizi n dugli yaa, yaa ɔɔ ra suŋŋuu saŋa maa naanɛi? 8Hɛrzeŋ bɛliirɛ kaa du de di dɔɔ girme, di dɔɔ gbɔgni la wia n dɔɔ wibii, alugɔ annii miŋ kpawɛɛ di ra dau ii see zinaa naanɛi?
9Ama, ií ra du tau, dí gilɛɛ waa suuh wia la ii siwee n nawɛɛ naa gɛɛ di gil a wàá lii ii biine, ii de dui saŋa. Ií kpaa di ra bagli ii biizi ani ii naanna. 10Ií ra liizi a hɔl la iiŋ chigɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ la. A hɔllɛ u ŋɔ n be, ‘Chaali a nɛra bá ba n be di wa nuu n wiŋɔɔlaa, guŋ gil bá ra ɔmiŋ saŋa la maa ban niŋ du a hɛri di birgi mag, di kpaa ra bagli ba biizi.’
11Ii faa ballɔɔ di wa chi a bizeŋ zɛɛ, ka u maa faa ra lau niŋ zagzagzag, nyɔɔzi tɔ de maa kuull di ga chug chiŋ, bɔr biri limpiriŋ. 12Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ ia di lii a niŋ biini. Ii faa ra nuu u wiŋɔzi, ka ii waa kummaa nawɛɛ lugɔ newee. Loobii bɛnnɛ ii faa nuu. 13U faa ŋɔ u ni ia nuukpaŋ wiarɛ. Aabuu u Gbɔgni Fi la uŋ ŋɔ ií ra hiŋ, u sɛbaa dau bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ ni la. 14Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ n benii a saŋa lugɔ n bagli ia u Gbɔgni, ií ra hiŋaa hɛri la iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu, ii ga foozi dɔɔ la biini.”
Vuga kuaraa wia
15Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “A hɔl la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ wia tɛɛ ia lii niŋ biini Bizeŋ Sinaai la, ii faa waa kummaa nawɛɛ a niŋ biini. Awia, ií ra du iihinaa tau nɛnnɛ, 16di gilɛɛ waa chɔg iihinaa di waa kuari kummaa, ú ra ɛɛ ii vug, di ii kuaruubuu u li baal gɛɛ haaŋ 17gɛɛ sel gɛɛ zumbee 18gɛɛ kuntuuzii gɛɛ nyiŋ. 19Di ii wa binni chiŋ di na wiizi gɛɛ baagu gɛɛ chinchiŋwilaa, ií gilɛɛ waa kuaraa. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kpaabuu tɛɛ hɛssi la hina n wɔɔ zummɛ la lugɔ ba ra kuari. 20Ka iawaa, Kɔraawiizi lizi iabuu di lii tɔɔrɔɔ n lugɔ ninzeŋ biini, Ijip hɛri. U ɛɛ gunnɛ, ií birgi u kapɛttɛ kuna alugɔ iin jaa ɛɛ zinaa naa.
21Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuhwoo n ni dikuu ii wia. U hɛɛhzi ni biinichɔg lugɔ màá gi Jɔɔdan muu naa di zuu hɛrnanii la unna tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuŋ la. 22N daŋ siu hɛri naa biini. Màá gi Jɔɔdan muu naa. Ka iawaa daŋ giu di ga foozi a hɛrsum di dɔɔ. 23Ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ waa suuh Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋ la u ni ia n ɛɛwɛ la wia. Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa ú ra li kummaa, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kiiwe, 24dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niŋ n na di kuna la. U ɛɛ zoma hinnɛ.
25Di ii wa du a hɛri di birgi, di jaa wa dɔɔ biizi ni naanna, di ii wa chɔg iihinaa di kuari vug maa, guŋ gil ii ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge maa di zuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ni, di gil u baaŋ fuuh, 26chiŋ ni hɛrii n daansɛɛ hina zinaa, ii daŋ siuzi manaŋ a hɛri naa iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu, ii ga dɔɔ la biini. Ii waa birgi de, ka ba kpuuzi ia nyaamm. 27Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɔ ia yaari durnya hɛssi hina biine. Ii tama bɛnnɛ niŋ ka ba biine. 28Denii ii jaa ra kuari vuga la newea n kuarɛɛ, a ɛɛ daazi gɛɛ bia la n waa na gɛɛ di ra nuu wia gɛɛ di ra di gɛɛ di ra nuu sɔɔh. 29Ka di ii wa du de ka ra nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɔr ni ii biine maa ani ii nfɛssi maa, ii daŋ nau. 30Di ii waa di dɔgnya, annii naa maa wa huuzi ia, ii daŋ bir ba Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la be, di waa hiŋuu. 31Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na suŋ nɛra ni la wia, wàá gil ia ta gɛɛ di kpuuzi ia gɛɛ di suuh nuukpaŋ la u ni ii naabaala n ɛɛwɛ, u hɛɛhzi u wibii dɔɔi wia la.”
32“Ií pɛɛzi faala wia di lii saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n ta newea mɔɔ ka ba lul ia la. Ií pɛɛzi durnya hina maa na, wizeŋ bɛl haa ɛɛwɔ di mag keŋ gɛɛ nɛra haa nuu keŋ wiaa? 33Nɛra baŋhina ŋmɛnɛ haa nuu Kɔraawiizi loobii di lii niŋ biini lugɔ iiŋ nuuwɛ naa, ka ba waa siuzɛɛa? 34Vug bɛl ŋmɛnɛ haa wetto lizi hɛri bɛl hina lii hɛri bɛl, ba ɛɛ u hora, gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ ia Ijip hɛri laa? Ii himmaa sibɔɔrɛ u kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii di gil wiilchɔgaa, laal, wizenaa ani nuukpuuri wia la n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, ɛɛ.
35Ii faa na annii naa maanii, guŋ gil ií zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu Kɔraawiizi. Di waa lɛi, bɛl maa waa kaa hoo. 36Chinne u faa du ka gil ii nuu u loobii, ú bagli ia wia. Hɛri genii u faa bagli ia u ninzeŋ, ii nuu u loobii di lii u biini. 37Dikuu uŋ nɔŋŋi ii naabaala la wiarɛ u faa lizi ia, di kpogli ia lii Ijip hɛri ni u fɔŋŋazeŋ, di ra bagli lugɔ u du ii benii, 38di duŋŋi hɛrzenaa la hina n kpekke kaali ia, di ii ra ba la. U ɛɛ gunnɛ ka kpa ba hɛssi tɛɛ ia, a ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuna alugɔ aŋ ɛɛwɛ filaŋkennaa.
39Awia, ií zum di gil a du ii biine zinaa, lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu dɔɔ chiŋ ni hɛri maa fɔŋŋa. Bɛl maa waa kaa hoo, di waa lɛi. 40Ií ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, guŋ gil wichɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa huuzi ii ni ii biizi ani ii naanna maa, ka ií wer so hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la, ú ɛɛ ii hor saŋaa saŋa maa.”
Hinlɛɛi bolzenaa wia
41Denii Moosis faa lizi bolzenaa ahoro la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii, 42a ɛɛ bola la nɛr n niŋ wer chɔ ga suah, di u wa foroo kpu u dɔŋhiŋ uŋ waa hahwɛɛ. U daŋ wer chɔ ga suah bɛl maa biini, di lɛɛ u hiŋ. 43A bolaa faa keŋ, Bɛza n du hɛribɔduma lɛl biini, Rubin dee hor, Ramɔf n du Giliad hɛri, Gad dee hor, Golan n du Basan hɛri, Manasɛ dee hor.
Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni kpai tɛɛ Izrɛl hina wia
44Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni ani u wibaglaa Moosis n faa kpawɛɛ dau Izrɛl hina see labuu guŋ. 45Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni u Gbɔgni naabuu Moosis faa kpa tɛɛ baa, baŋ faa lii Ijip hɛri 46di wa du waluu la n dugli Bɛf Piɔ la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la. A hɛri naa faa ɛɛ Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn la n faa ra di kora Hɛsbɔn la hɛrii, waabuu Moosis ni Izrɛl hina faa kpegli, di ba lii Ijip di ra ba la. 47U ni Basan Koori Ɔɔg hɛssii Izrɛl hina faa foozi Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii paga la. Baabuu faa Amɔri hina koora banɛɛ la. 48A hɛri naa faa lii bolzeŋ Aroa la n du Aanɔn Gɔmbɔɔluŋ nua labuu guŋŋ di ga hel Bizeŋ Siyɔn, u sɔŋ bɛllɛ Bizeŋ Hɛmɔn, 49di kpa Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii hɛri, di kaa lii de guŋŋ di ga hel Muuzensiwii la n du Bizeŋ Pisga bɔwillaa la maa jaa.

english_text:
The Ten Commandments
(Exodus 20.1-17)
1Moses called together the people of Israel and said:
Today I am telling you the laws and teachings that you must follow, so listen carefully. 2The Lord our God made an agreement with our nation at Mount Sinai. 3That agreement wasn't only with our ancestors but with us, who are here today. 4The Lord himself spoke to you out of the fire, 5but you were afraid of the fire and refused to go up the mountain. So I spoke with the Lord for you, then I told you that he had said:
6I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
7Do not worship any god except me.
8 Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth. 9 Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me and worship idols, I will punish your families for three or four generations. 10But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
11 Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
12 Show respect for the Sabbath Day—it belongs to me. 13 You have six days when you can do your work, 14but the seventh day of the week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your oxen or donkeys or any other animal, not even those foreigners who live in your towns. And don't make your slaves do any work. 15This special day of rest will remind you that I reached out my mighty arm and rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
16 Respect your father and mother, and you will live a long and successful life in the land I am giving you.
17 Do not murder.
18 Be faithful in marriage.
19 Do not steal.
20 Do not tell lies about others.
21 Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else.
22 When we were gathered at the mountain, the Lord spoke to us in a loud voice from the dark fiery cloud. The Lord gave us these commands, and only these. Then he wrote them on two flat stones and gave them to me.
The People Were Afraid
(Exodus 20.18-21)
Moses said to Israel:
23When fire blazed from the mountain, and you heard the voice coming from the darkness, your tribal leaders came to me 24and said:
Today the Lord our God has shown us how powerful and glorious he is. He spoke to us from the fire, and we learned that people can live, even though God speaks to them. 25But we don't want to take a chance on being killed by that terrible fire, and if we keep on hearing the Lord's voice, we will die. 26Has anyone else ever heard the only true God speaking from fire, as we have? And even if they have, would they live to tell about it? 27Moses, go up close and listen to the Lord. Then come back and tell us, and we will do everything he says.
28The Lord heard you and said:
Moses, I heard what the people said to you, and I approve. 29I wish they would always worship me with fear and trembling and be this willing to obey me! Then they and their children would always enjoy a successful life.
30Now, tell them to return to their tents, 31but you come back here to me. After I tell you my laws and teachings, you will repeat them to the people, so they can obey these laws in the land I am giving them.
Moses said:
32Israel, you must carefully obey the Lord's commands. 33Follow them, because they make a path that will lead to a long successful life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni fi wia
1Moosis faa chaali Izrɛl hina maa, di ŋɔ ba be,
“Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu Gbɔgni naa min niŋ bagli ia zinaa naa. Ií hellaa di ra hiŋaa nɛnnɛ. 2Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ni yaa faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ Bizeŋ Sinaai. 3Kɔraawiizi ni yaa mɛɛwaa bɛŋ lɛi faa ɛɛ a nuukpaŋ naa, ka yaa banla maa n du de zinaa naa nuubuu ɛɛ a nuukpaŋ. 4Kɔraawiizi faa ga niŋ biinii bizeŋ la nyuu, di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ ia, a chaani, ii na u duula. 5A saŋa hiŋ, minuu faa du ii ni Kɔraawiizi baambaaŋ, di ŋɔ u wiŋɔɔlii di tɛɛ ia, dikuu iiŋ faa ra ɔm a niŋ, di vɛɛ a bizeŋ nyuu tinnaa la wia. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
6‘Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n lɛɛ ia di lii Ijip hɛri, saŋa la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma de la.
7Ií gilɛɛ kaa wàá dɔɔ vuga maa di ra jaa n ni.
8Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa, ú li kuŋ n du chiŋ gɛɛ hɛri gɛɛ nii biini di ra tɛɛ iihinaa. 9Ií gilɛɛ waa togni di ra jaamaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛ zoma hinnɛ, di ra tɛr banla maa n hahŋ biizi, ba naanna, ba naanatɛɛri ani ba ge biizi digna, dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia, 10ka nɔŋŋi jiminizi kagboŋa nɛra la maa, n nɔŋŋiŋ, di ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni la.
11Ií gilɛɛ kpogli mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sɔŋ di ra dua. N daŋ tɛr nɛr la maa n niŋ ɛɛ guŋ digni.
12Ií ɔɔ ra di Heezaa Hɔpizii la, di gil ú ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinanii ii be, gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n ŋɔ ii be la. 13Ií ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛl di ra hum ii huma maa, 14ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ lawaa ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Awia, a waa dɛkkɛ ii ni ii biizi ni ii balaa, ii sela ani hɔɔhra la maa n du ii bola ra hum huma a hɔl hiŋ, bá ge wer heezi lugɔ ia. 15Ií ra liizi lugɔ ii faa ɛɛ yomaa Ijip hɛri, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii la di lizi ia di lii de. Awia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ŋɔ ii benii lugɔ ií ra tɔgzi Heezaa Hɔpizii la.
16A tɔgzi i mɛɛ ni i maa gunla Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n ŋɔwɛɛ la, í wer dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ, wichɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa huuzii hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n na tɛi naa biini.
17Gilɛɛ wàá kpu nɛr.
18Gilɛɛ wàá sɛm.
19Gilɛɛ wàá ŋmɛɛ.
20Gilɛɛ wàá kanni kara di ra chug i dɔŋhiŋ.
21Gilɛɛ wàá kɛlli i dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ ni. Gilɛɛ wàá kɛlli i dɔŋhiŋ dia gɛɛ hɛri gɛɛ u balii gɛɛ u sel gɛɛ u kuna maa ni.’
22Gbɔgni la Kɔraawiizi n faa siiwe tɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa bizeŋ la nyuu, di lii niŋ ni baama ani bɔbiri limpiriŋ werge biini labuu guŋ. U faa waa kaa kpa wiimaa di jaa. U faa sɛbaabuu dau bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ ni, di kpaa tɛŋ.
23Iiŋ faa nuu a loobii n lii a bɔbiri limpiriŋ werge biini, di a bizeŋ nyuu ra lau niŋ la, ii sitɔɔra ni ii nabɔnzi faa ba n benii, 24di wa ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la bagli yaabuu u zenni ni u girme, yaa nuu u loobii di lii niŋ biini. Zinaa, yaa zummɔ lugɔ newee wàá siu, di Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia tɛu. 25Ka filaŋkeŋ, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ya siuzɛi? Ninzeŋ naa daŋ di yaa, di yaa kaa nuu Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la loobii. 26Newee ŋmɛnɛ haa nuu Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la loobii, di lii niŋ biini, ka haa du dee? 27Tuzi hel di nuu gunla maa Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la n na ŋɔ, di ŋɔa tɛɛ yaa. Gunla maa un niŋ ŋɔ, yaa daŋ nuu, di hiŋaa.’
28Kɔraawiizi faa nuu gunla iiŋ ŋɔ n benii, di ŋɔ, ‘N nuu wia la nɛra naa n ŋɔ i be labuu. Wia la maa baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wessoo. 29Di ba daŋ dɔɔ nfɛrɛ naa dɔŋ, di ra tɔgziŋ, di ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni, guŋwaa, wiimaa daŋ kuari tɛɛ ba ni ba biizi nɛnnɛ, saŋa maa.
30La ga ŋɔ dí ba bir la ba tanti diini biine. 31Ka hiŋwaa du n be bɔnnaa, ń kpa widaulaa ni Gbɔgni la hin niŋ bagli baa, bá ra hiŋaa hɛri la min niŋ tɛɛ baa la biini di tɛi.’ ”
32Awia, Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ra du tau, di ɛɛ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la n ŋɔ ii be la. Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ bɛl maa hiŋaa. 33Ií ra hiŋ u wibaglaa la maa, guŋ gil ii nyɛɛli, di dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋra hɛri la uŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ ia la biini.”

english_text:
The Most Important Commandment
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord told me to give you these laws and teachings, so you can obey them in the land he is giving you. Soon you will cross the Jordan River and take that land. 2And if you and your descendants want to live a long time, you must always worship the Lord and obey his laws. 3Pay attention, Israel! Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he promised to give us this land that is rich with milk and honey. Be careful to obey him, and you will become a successful and powerful nation.
4 Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the only true God! 5 So love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength. 6 Memorize his laws 7and tell them to your children over and over again. Talk about them all the time, whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 8Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and foreheads to help you obey them. 9Write these laws on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
Worship Only the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10 The Lord promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you this land. Now he will take you there and give you large towns, with good buildings that you didn't build, 11and houses full of good things that you didn't put there. The Lord will give you wells that you didn't have to dig, and vineyards and olive orchards that you didn't have to plant. But when you have eaten so much that you can't eat any more, 12don't forget it was the Lord who set you free from slavery and brought you out of Egypt. 13 Worship and obey the Lord your God with fear and trembling, and promise that you will be loyal to him.
14Don't have anything to do with gods that are worshiped by the nations around you. 15If you worship other gods, the Lord will be furious and wipe you off the face of the earth. The Lord your God is with you, 16 so don't try to make him prove that he can help you, as you did at Massah. 17Always obey the laws that the Lord has given you 18-19and live in a way that pleases him. Then you will be able to go in and take this good land from your enemies, just as he promised your ancestors.
20Someday your children will ask, “Why did the Lord give us these laws and teachings?”
21Then you will answer:
We were slaves of the king of Egypt, but the Lord used his great power and set us free. 22We saw him perform miracles and make horrible things happen to the king, his officials, and everyone else. 23The Lord rescued us from Egypt, so he could bring us into this land, as he had promised our ancestors. 24-25That's why the Lord our God demands that we obey his laws and worship him with fear and trembling. And if we do, he will protect us and help us be successful.
translation_text:
Ií nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Widaulaa ni Gbɔgni la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ŋɔ ń bagli ia, ií ra hiŋaa hɛri la iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu ií ga dɔɔ la biinii guŋ, 2guŋ gil ii ni ii biizi ni ii naanna ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, ii de dui saŋa, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni maa minna bagli ia naa, ií wer di ra di iihinaa. 3Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu di ra du tau, di sɛɛ ra hiŋaa, wichɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa huuzi ia, ka ii wazi werge maa hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la biini, gunla Kɔraawiizi la ii mɛɛwaa n na hum la n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia la.
4Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu. Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ɛɛ kpaŋkpannɛ, bɛl maa waa kaa hoo. 5Ií gil ii bampiree maa lau Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di nɔŋŋuu ani ii biine maa, di kpa ii kpegzi maa du u ni. 6Ií gil Gbɔgni naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa du ii bampiree biine. 7Ií kpaa di bagli ii biizi. Ií ra ŋɔ a wia di ii wa du ii diini gɛɛ di ii waa vol ŋmɛnɛɛ, di ii wa chɔɔwɔ gɛɛ di ii wa izoo. 8Ií sɛbaa, di kpaa vɔɔzi ii nonee ni ii hilli, á ra liizi ia. 9Ií sɛbaa dau ii dominuuzi daazi ni ii gbessi maa ni.
10Di Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wa kpogli ia zuu hɛri la uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii naabaala, Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ ia, u dɔɔ bolzenaa la iiŋ waa mawɛɛ, a du wer werge, 11a diini suugi kunnanaa la iiŋ waa kuuhwɛ na, kɔlɔnzi iiŋ waa kiwee ani daazi la n na nɔŋ kooni iiŋ waa duuwe. Di ii wa dia di piŋzi, 12ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ waa suuh Kɔraawiizi la n lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma la wia.
13Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛŋ, di kpa u sɔŋ di ra hɛɛhzi. 14Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari nɛra la n bar ia la vuga, 15dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n du ii be la ra zomuu. U baaŋ daŋ fuuh ii ni werge maa, ú dim ia hɛri naa biini. 16Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wia di ŋɔ ií ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la di na, gunla iiŋ faa ɛɛwɛ Massa la. 17Ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la Gbɔgni maa uŋ tɛɛ ia la. 18Ií ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa ni winanaa Kɔraawiizi see, wichɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa huuzi ia, ka ií wer zuu hɛrsum la uŋ ŋɔ nua, di hɛɛhzi lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ii naabaala la biini, di foozuu dɔɔ, 19di duŋŋi ii dɔma maa gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.
20Di ii biizi ŋmɛnɛ wa pɛɛzi ia, ‘Gbɔgni naa Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la n ŋɔ yá ra hiŋaa naa, zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ?’ 21Ií ŋɔ ba be, ‘Yaa faa ɛɛ Ijip koori yomaa, ka Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ yaa, di lizi yaa lii Ijip hɛri ani u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii. 22Yaa sibɔɔrɛ Kɔraawiizi faa gil wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wia la n kpekke di kaa chum werge, chol Ijip hina, ba koori ani u diahina maa ni. 23U lizi yaabuu di lii de, ú kpogli yaa zuu hɛri la uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ, di ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ yaa naabaala la biini. 24Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ yá ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni naa di ra ɔmuu, guŋ gil yá ɔɔ nyɛɛli, di dɔɔ miibɔɔ. Aabuu guŋ zinaa naa. 25Di yaa ra du tau, di ra hiŋ Gbɔgni naa maa nɛnnɛ, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la sibɔɔ gunla uŋ baglɛɛ la, gunnɛ niŋ gil yaa wia deŋli.’ ”

english_text:
Force the Other Nations Out of the Land
(Exodus 34.11-16)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, the Lord your God will help you take the land of the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. These seven nations have more people and are stronger than Israel, but when you attack them, 2the Lord will force them out of the land. Then you must destroy them without mercy. Don't make any peace treaties with them, 3and don't let your sons and daughters marry any of them. 4If you do, those people will lead your descendants to worship other gods and to turn their backs on the Lord. That will make him very angry, and he will quickly destroy Israel.
5 So when you conquer these nations, tear down the altars where they worship their gods. Break up their sacred stones, cut down the poles that they use in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and throw their idols in the fire.
The Lord's Chosen People
Moses said:
6 Israel, you are the chosen people of the Lord your God. There are many nations on this earth, but he chose only Israel to be his very own. 7You were the weakest of all nations, 8but the Lord chose you because he loves you and because he had made a promise to your ancestors. Then with his mighty arm, he rescued you from the king of Egypt, who had made you his slaves.
9 You know that the Lord your God is the only true God. So love him and obey his commands, and he will faithfully keep his agreement with you and your descendants for a thousand generations. 10But if you turn against the Lord, he will quickly destroy you. 11So be sure to obey his laws and teachings I am giving you today.
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
(Deuteronomy 28.1-14; Leviticus 26.3-13)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If you completely obey these laws, the Lord your God will be loyal and keep the agreement he made with you, just as he promised our ancestors. 13The Lord will love you and bless you by giving you many children and plenty of food, wine, and olive oil. Your herds of cattle will have many calves, and your flocks of sheep will have many lambs. 14God will bless you more than any other nation—your families will grow and your livestock increase. 15You will no longer suffer with the same horrible diseases that you sometimes had in Egypt. You will be healthy, but the Lord will make your enemies suffer from those diseases.
Destroy the Nations and Their Gods
Moses said to Israel:
16When the Lord helps you defeat your enemies, you must destroy them without pity! And don't get trapped into worshiping their gods.
17You may be thinking, “How can we destroy these nations? They are more powerful than we are.” 18But stop worrying! Just remember what the Lord your God did to Egypt and its king. 19You saw how the Lord used his tremendous power to work great miracles and bring you out of Egypt. And he will again work miracles for you when you face these enemies you fear so much. 20Some of them may try to survive by hiding from you, but the Lord will make them panic, and soon they will be dead. 21So don't be frightened when you meet them in battle. The Lord your God is great and fearsome, and he will fight at your side.
22As you attack these nations, the Lord will force them out little by little. He won't let you get rid of them all at once—if he did, there wouldn't be enough people living in the land to keep down the number of wild animals. 23-24But when you attack your enemies, the Lord will make them panic, and you will easily destroy them. You will defeat their kings one after another until they are gone, and no one will remember they ever lived.
25After you conquer a nation, burn their idols. Don't get trapped into wanting the silver or gold on an idol. Even the metal on an idol is disgusting to the Lord, 26so destroy it. If you bring it home with you, both you and your house will be destroyed. Stay away from those disgusting idols!
translation_text:
Hɛssi hina duŋŋaa wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wa kpogli ia di zuu a hɛri, ií dɔɔu, di duŋŋi hɛssi naa hina, Hitti, Girgas, Amɔri, Keenan, Pɛriz, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina, hɛssi aniidaanɛɛ naa hina n kannɛ di du kpeg kaali ia la. 2Di u wa kpa baa du ii nonee biini, ii kpegli baa, ií chɔgi baa nyaamm. Ií ni baa gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa suŋ ba ni. 3Ií gilɛɛ waa paagi ba haana. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa ii biihaana di ra tɛɛ ba biibaala gɛɛ di waa nyiŋŋi ba biihaana di ra tɛɛ ii biibaala. 4Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, ba daŋ gil ii biibaala vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa, ka ra kuari vuga. Guŋ gil u baaŋ fuuh ii ni, ú chɔgi ia manaŋ. 5Awia, ií purgi ba mbusu lizibɔra ni ba bia la baŋ baŋzɛɛ tɛɛ ba vug Baal, di kuugi ba vughaaŋ Asɛra daabaŋlaa la maa, di fuuah. 6Ii ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛmbɛŋ horaa. U lizi iabuu di lii durnya hɛssi nɛra maa biine, ií ɛɛ u nɛra, di ɛɛ u daama la unna tɔgzi werge maa la.
7Kɔraawiizi waa ia nɔŋŋɛɛ di lizi ia, dikuu iiŋ kpillɛ di kaali nɛra wia. Iabuu faa fiiwe werge. 8Kɔraawiizi n nɔŋŋi ia, di kaa hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii naabaala la wiarɛ, u lizi ia ani u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii, di lɛɛ ia lii hɛri la biini iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma, Ijip koori faa dɔɔ ia la. 9Awia, a dɛkkɔɔ ií zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. U wia dɔɔ wibiire. U nɔŋŋaa nuukpaŋ la ɔɔ du jiminizi kagboŋa nɛra la n nɔŋŋuu di ra hiŋ u widaulaa benii.
10Ka banla waa n hauh la,
ba kinturgaare chɔgaa,
u daŋ chɔgi baa manaŋ.
11Awia, ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, ka ra hiŋ a widaulaa ni Gbɔgni naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.
12Di ii ra du a Gbɔgni naa tau nɛnnɛ, di ra hiŋaa, guŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ lau u ni ia nɔŋŋaa nuukpaŋ la, di kpogli nɛnnɛ, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua di hɛɛhzi tɛɛ ii naabaala la. 13U daŋ nɔŋŋi ia di kissi ia, di gil ii wazi. U daŋ kissi ii biizi ni ii pattikuna, aabuu ii mia ni siŋfalaa ani nuu. U daŋ gil ii sela wazi, hɛri la biini uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ ii naabaala be lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ ia la. 14Ii daŋ na kissaa di kaali nɛra maa, durnya naa biini. Ii baal maa gɛɛ haaŋ maa gɛɛ ii kundɛɛzaa maa wàá nyaa bie. 15Kɔraawiizi daŋ guu ia di lii wiila maa biini. Wàá gil wiilchɔgaa la iiŋ zummɛ Ijip hɛri la chol ii ni. Ka u daŋ gil a chol banla maa n hah ia ni. 16A dɛkkɔɔ ií kpu nɛra la maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ kpa du i nonee biini. Ií gilɛɛ waa suŋ ba ni. Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari ba vuga, á wa birgi sidɛɛzi ii be, di lauri ia.
17Aŋhinabe, ii daŋ ŋɔ ii biine, ‘Hɛssi naa hina kpekkoo kaali yaa. Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ duŋŋi baai?’ 18Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm baa. Ií ra liizi gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n dau Ijip hina ni ba koori maa la. 19Ii himmaa siwee na tɔɔrɔɔzenaa ni wizenaa ani nuukpuuri wia la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii, di lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri labuu. Guŋ himmaanii ú ɛɛ nɛra naa iinna ɔm naa. 20Di kaa kpa jaa, u daŋ kpa chirinchaazi di ta ba ni, haali banla n niŋ na bahinaa di chɔ suahzi la gba daŋ siuzi. 21Ií gilɛɛ gil ba wia dɔɔ ia ɔnsii, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, du ii benii. U zenni kannɔɔ werge. U wia ge dɔɔ ɔnsii werge. 22Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la danna duŋŋi a nɛra tama tama. Wàá gil ii kpu baa kakpaŋ. Di guŋ lɛi, sechɔgaa daŋ wazi, di ra koozi ia. 23Ka Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kpa a nɛra du ii nonee biini, di gil bá bugmi werge maa guŋŋ, ií wa kpu baa. 24U daŋ kpa ba koora du ii nonee biini, ii dim ba sɔna durnya naa biini. Nɛr maa waa hoo ú ni ia wer lɔ dɔŋa. Ii daŋ kpu ba maa. 25Ií fuuh ba vuga maa. Ií gilɛɛ waa kɛlli saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ la baŋ kpawɛɛ bɔgaa la ni, di wa kpaa ra birgi ii hora. A daŋ gil ii chol, dikuu aŋ ɛɛ kuna la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n kiiwe wia. 26Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa a kuŋkiilii naa bɛl maa di waa zuu ii diini, di guŋ lɛi, Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgi ii nuu maa. Ií kii u wia werge maa, di hauh, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi dau u chɔgaa saŋaa.”

english_text:
The Lord Takes Care of You
Moses said:
1Israel, do you want to go into the land the Lord promised your ancestors? Do you want to capture it, live there, and become a powerful nation? Then be sure to obey every command I am giving you.
2Don't forget how the Lord your God has led you through the desert for the past 40 years. He wanted to find out if you were truly willing to obey him and depend on him, 3 so he made you go hungry. Then he gave you manna, a kind of food that you and your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was teaching you that people need more than food to live—they need every word that the Lord has spoken.
4Over the past 40 years, your clothing hasn't worn out, and your feet haven't swollen. 5 So keep in mind that the Lord has been correcting you, just as parents correct their children. 6Obey the commands the Lord your God has given you and worship him with fear and trembling.
7The Lord your God is bringing you into a good land with streams that flow from springs in the valleys and hills. 8-9You can dig for copper in those hills, and the stones are made of iron ore. And you won't go hungry. Wheat and barley fields are everywhere, and so are vineyards and orchards full of fig, pomegranate, and olive trees, and there is plenty of honey.
Don't Forget the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10After you eat and are full, give praise to the Lord your God for the good land he gave you. 11 Make sure that you never forget the Lord or disobey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. If you always obey them, 12you will have plenty to eat, and you will build good houses to live in. 13You will get more and more cattle, sheep, silver, gold, and other possessions.
14But when all this happens, don't be proud! Don't forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and that it was the Lord who set you free. 15Remember how he led you in that huge and frightening desert where poisonous snakes and scorpions live. There was no water, but the Lord split open a rock, and water poured out so you could drink. 16He also gave you manna, a kind of food your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was testing you to make you trust him, so that later on he could be good to you.
17When you become successful, don't say, “I'm rich, and I've earned it all myself.” 18Instead, remember that the Lord your God gives you the strength to make a living. That's how he keeps the promise he made to your ancestors.
19-20But I'm warning you—if you forget the Lord your God and worship other gods, the Lord will destroy you, just as he destroyed the nations you fought.
translation_text:
Ií gilɛɛ waa suuh Kɔraawiizi wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ra du tau, di ra hiŋ Gbɔgni naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa. Guŋ gil ii wer dɔɔ miibɔɔni di wazi, di zuu hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua, lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ii naabaala la biini, di foozuu dɔɔ. 2Ií ra liizi gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n tɔ ii see hɛribɔduma biini, binni tokkoanɛɛ naa, ú gil ii pɛssi. U ɛɛ ia na, di zum wia la n du ii bampiree, di ii daŋ hiŋ gɛɛ ii wàá hiŋ u Gbɔgni ni u widaulaa. 3U faa kpa lɔzii kpu ia, ka tɛɛ ia maana, diwii la ii ni ii naabaala maa n waa zummɛ, ii di. U ɛɛ gunnɛ u pɛssi ia. Ka u ŋɔ ú bagli iabuu lugɔ diwee bɛŋ lɛi ra tɛɛ nɛr miibɔɔ. Ka Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii bɛl maa gba daŋ wer tɛu miibɔɔ. 4Ii laala faa waa siuwɛ gɛɛ ii naazi ɔrgi, binni tokkoanɛɛ naa maa biini. 5Ií zum gunla baal n ɔɔ ra tɛr u biibaal digni la, gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɔɔ ra tɛrgi ii digna la.
6Ií ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la widaulaa, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi, di ra tɔgzuu werge maa. 7Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kpogli iabuu di ra zuu hɛrsum la n dɔɔ gɔŋa, niiri n chɔɔgɛɛ, bulli n pogzee di ra pal walli biine ani giŋgimee nyuuni. 8Hɛri la n dɔɔ huuti, baali, grepu ni fig daazi, pomegranet, ɔlivi nuu ani huuhnuu. 9U ɛɛ hɛri la iiŋ wàá nyaa diwee gɛɛ kunnanaa maanii. Hɛri la bia n dɔɔ lugbia, ii wer ki lugbiaahmu lii u giŋgimee biini.
10Di ii wa diwoo di piŋ, ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, dikuu uŋ tɛɛ ia hɛrsum wia. 11Ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa suuh u wia, di vɛɛ u Gbɔgni naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa. 12Di guŋ lɛi, di ii wa diwoo piŋ, di ma diinanaa so, 13di ii sela, ii saliŋhuŋŋa, ii saliŋ ani ii kundɔɔlaa maa wa wazɔɔ, 14denii ií jaa dɔɔ barabara, di suuh Kɔraawiizi la n lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri la, iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma la wia. 15Waabuu faa kpogli ia di ga hɛribɔduma n wassɛ werge, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii la biini la. A hɛri la n faa waa nii dɔɔwɛ, ka dɔɔ hɛrikuna ni nuunzi la siri n kpolle. U faa gillɔɔ nii lii bikpeg ni, ií nyɔɔ. 16U faa tɛɛ iabuu maana ií di a hɛribɔduma biini. A ɛɛ kuna la ii naabaala n faa waa zummɛ, ú gil ii pɛssi, di kaa ɛɛ ia di na, a tuna, ii wia maa wer kuari. 17Aŋhinabe, ii daŋ ŋɔ ii biine, ‘Yaa fɔŋŋa ni kpegzii tɛɛ yaa daama naa.’ 18Ama, ií ra liizi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu ra tɛɛ ia daama nai fɔŋŋa. Waabuu ra ɛɛ wia naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u wia haa dɔɔ wibiire zinaa, di tɛɛ nuukpaŋ la u ni ii naabaala n ɛɛwɛ la.
19Di ii ŋmɛnɛ maa haŋ wa suuh Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wia, ka ra kuari vuga gɛɛ di ra tɔgzaa, n di guŋ daansɛɛrɛ zinaa lugɔ u daŋ kpu ia, wibii maa. 20Gunla uŋ kpu hɛssi nɛra ii sibɔɔ la, gunnɛ ú kpu ia, dikuu iiŋ waa u nua hiŋŋɛ wia.”

english_text:
Why the Lord Will Help Israel
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to me! You will soon cross the Jordan River and go into the land to force out the nations that live there. They are more powerful than you are, and the walls around their cities reach to the sky. 2Some of these nations are descendants of the Anakim. You know how tall and strong they are, and you've heard that no one can defeat them in battle. 3But the Lord your God has promised to go ahead of you, like a raging fire burning everything in its path. So when you attack your enemies, it will be easy for you to destroy them and take their land.
4-6After the Lord helps you wipe out these nations and conquer their land, don't think he did it because you are such good people. You aren't good—you are stubborn! No, the Lord is going to help you, because the nations that live there are evil, and because he wants to keep the promise he made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
When Israel Made an Idol
(Exodus 32)
Moses said to Israel:
7Don't ever forget how you kept rebelling and making the Lord angry the whole time you were in the desert. You rebelled from the day you left Egypt until the day you arrived here.
8At Mount Sinai you made the Lord so angry that he was going to destroy you. 9-11 It happened during those 40 days and nights that I was on the mountain, without anything to eat or drink. He had told me to come up there so he could give me the agreement he made with us. And this agreement was actually the same Ten Commandments he had announced to you when he spoke from the fire on the mountain. The Lord had written them on two flat stones with his own hand. But after giving me the two stones, 12he said:
Moses, hurry down the mountain to those people you led out of Egypt. They have already disobeyed me and committed the terrible sin of making an idol.
13I've been watching the Israelites, and I've seen how stubborn and rebellious they are. 14So don't try to stop me! I am going to wipe them out, and no one on earth will remember they ever lived. Then I will let your descendants become an even bigger and more powerful nation than Israel.
Moses said:
15Fire was raging on the mountaintop as I went back down, carrying the two stones with the commandments on them. 16I saw how quickly you had sinned and disobeyed the Lord your God. There you were, worshiping the metal idol you had made in the shape of a calf. 17So I threw down the two stones and smashed them before your very eyes.
18-20I bowed down at the place of worship and prayed to the Lord, without eating or drinking for 40 days and nights. You had committed a terrible sin by making that idol, and the Lord hated what you had done. He was angry enough to destroy all of you and Aaron as well. So I prayed for you and Aaron as I had done before, and this time the Lord answered my prayers.
21It was a sin for you to make that idol, so I threw it into the fire to melt it down. Then I took the lump of gold, ground it into powder, and threw the powder into the stream flowing down the mountain.
22 You also made the Lord angry when you were staying at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-Hattaavah. 23 Then at Kadesh-Barnea the Lord said, “I am giving you the land, so go ahead and take it!” But since you didn't trust the Lord, you rebelled and disobeyed his command. 24In fact, you've rebelled against the Lord for as long as he has known you.
25After you had made the idol in the shape of a calf, the Lord said he was going to destroy you. So I lay face down in front of the Lord for 40 days and nights 26and prayed:
Our Lord, please don't wipe out your people. You used your great power to rescue them from Egypt and to make them your very own. 27Israel's ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob obeyed you faithfully. Think about them, and not about Israel's stubbornness, evil, and sin. 28If you destroy your people, the Egyptians will say, “The Lord promised to give Israel land, but he wasn't powerful enough to keep his promise. In fact, he hated them so much that he took them into the desert and killed them.” 29But you, our Lord, chose the people of Israel to be your own, and with your mighty power you rescued them from Egypt.
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina dignikpega wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu. Ii jaa ra nyiŋŋi Jɔɔdan muu giirɛ, ií ga foozi hɛssi la hina n kaali ia hɛssi. Ba kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge kaali ia, di dɔɔ bolzenaa n kannɛzi werge, a dɔɔ koŋlaa la n gaa chug chiŋ. 2A nɛra ɛɛ Anak hina la n helle kpabaa kpabaanɛ! Ii zum ba wiarɛ di kaa nuu baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ wer chem Anak hina ninɛi?’ 3Ka n na nyiŋŋuu ií zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu tɔ ii see di ra gi Jɔɔdan muu la. U ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niŋ la n na di kuna. U daŋ chɔgi baa di gɛrgi baa mɔɔ, ii sibɔɔ. Denii ií duŋŋi baa di dim baa manaŋ, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia la.
4Di Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wa duŋŋi baa ii sibɔɔ, ií gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ ii biine, ‘Kɔraawiizi ba yaa ninɛɛ bɔnnaa, yá wa lɛɛ hɛri naa di dɔɔ, dikuu yaa wideŋlaa wia.’ Akai, a hɛssi naa hina biinikpola wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi ra nyiŋŋi ú duŋŋi baa ii sibɔɔ la. 5A waa lugɔ ii wideŋlaa gɛɛ ii wibii dɔɔi wiarɛ, ii ra la ií ga foozi ba hɛssi di dɔɔ, ka a hɛssi naa hina biinikpola wiarɛ ú duŋŋi baa, di gil gunla uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ ii naabaala, Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb be la, su u maga. 6Ií zum a zɛɛ nɛnnɛ lugɔ ii wideŋlaa wia lɛi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ra tɛɛ ia hɛrsum naa, ií dɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ɛɛ dignikpega hinaa.
7Ií ra liizi gunla iiŋ faa gillɛ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh hɛribɔduma biini la. Di lii a hɔl la iiŋ lii Ijip hɛri guŋŋ di wa hel ɛŋ la, ii faa ra diubuu mmɔri. 8Iiŋ faa du Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ la, ii faa ɛɛ wiarɛ di gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u faa ra nyiŋŋi ú kpu ia. 9Miŋ faa tinni bizeŋ la nyuu ń lɛɛ bipɛntɛnzi la, Kɔraawiizi n sɛbi u ni ia nuukpaŋ wia a ni la, n faa du denii hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ, di maa kummaa diwee gɛɛ di nyɔɔ nii gba. 10Kɔraawiizi faa tɛmbuu bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la uŋ kpa u nonibii di sɛbi a ni la. U Gbɔgni la uŋ faa ga ninlau biini di sii a wia tɛɛ ia bizeŋ la nyuu, a hɔl la iiŋ chaali u zɛɛ la.
11A hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ la n wa tunnɛ, Kɔraawiizi faa kpa a bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la uŋ sɛbi a nuukpaŋ wia a ni labuu tɛŋ. 12Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, ‘Tuu manaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, i nɛra la hiŋ kpoglee lii Ijip hɛri la chɔkkɔɔ, di ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Ba wia waa kaa dɔɔ wibii. Ba bir hattɛ kpu n widaulaa la, ka ŋmɛɛri saliŋ di kuari vug tɛɛ bahinaa.’
13Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, ‘N na nɛra naabuu, wibii maa. Ba dɔɔ dignikpegaa! 14Giliŋ bɔɔiih ka n kpu baa, di dim ba sɔŋ durnya naa biini. Ka gil hìŋ́ Moosis ɛɛ hɛri la hina n niŋ dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge mɛɛ. I nɛra daŋ du kpil werge di kaali baa.’
15Awia, n faa bir lii a bizeŋ nyuu di tuu, di u haa ra lau niŋ zagzagzag, di a nuukpaŋ bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la du n nonee. 16Denii n binni di na lugɔ ii ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ni, dikuu iiŋ faa kpa saliŋ di ŋmɛɛri, di kuari vug u li nabii wia. Ii faa bir hattɛ manaŋ di kpu ŋmɛnɛɛ la uŋ ŋɔ ii ra hiŋ la. 17Awia, n faa kpa a bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la miŋ kpoglee la, di viiri hɛri, a purgi burburbur, ii sibɔɔ.
18Denii n faa kaa chol pi hɛri Kɔraawiizi see, hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ, di maa kummaa diwee gɛɛ di nyɔɔ nii gba, dikuu wichɔgaa la maa iiŋ faa ɛɛwɛ, di zuu u ni, di gil u baaŋ fuuh la wia. 19Ɔnsii faa lawimbuu dikuu u baaŋ la n chummɛ werge wia. U baaŋ faa fuuhwoo di hel lugɔ ú chɔgi ia, ka u faa kaa nuu di tɛŋ. 20Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Aarɔn gba ninɛɛ, di hel lugɔ ú chɔguu, ka a saŋa hiŋ, n faa suŋŋi wiizi tɛɛ u ge gba. 21N faa kaa kpa ii wichɔgii kuŋ la, a nabii la iiŋ kuarɛɛ la di fuuh, di purguu, di namuu u bii kɔlɔlɔlɔ lugɔ hɛɛhriikɔl, di kpaa ta nii la n faa lii a bii nyuu di pal ra tuu hɛri la biini.
22Ii faa kaa giluu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh Tabɛra, Massa ani Kibrɔf Hataava maa.
23Kɔraawiizi n faa gillɛ ii lii Kadɛs Bania la, u faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ií izi la ga foozi hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia la.’ Ka ii faa diu mmɔri. Ii faa wɔɔ yardɛɛ gɛɛ di hiŋ u nua. 24Di haŋ lii saŋa la maa miŋ zum ia la, ii kpoŋŋoo di ra di Kɔraawiizi mmɔri.
25N faa chɔɔwɔɔ pi Kɔraawiizi see hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ, dikuu uŋ ŋɔ ú kpu ia la wia. 26N faa suŋŋuu di ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, gilɛɛ waa kpu i nɛra. Ba ɛɛ i kapɛttɛ hiŋ yauwɛ lii Ijip hɛri ani i fɔŋŋazeŋ ni i banonii labuu. 27A liizi i balaa Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb wia, ka suuh a nɛra naa kpoŋaa, ba biinikpola ani ba wichɔgaa naa wia. 28Di guŋ lɛi, hɛri la biini hiŋ lizi yaa lii la hina daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi n waa wette ú kpogli baa di zuu hɛri la uŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ baa la ani uŋ hah baa wiarɛ, u kpogli baa ba hɛribɔduma biini, ú wa kpu. 29Ka ba ɛɛ i nɛraa, di ɛɛ i kapɛttɛ hiŋ lizɛɛ lii Ijip hɛri ani i fɔŋŋazeŋ ni i banoniire.’ ”

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Exodus 34.1-10)
Moses said to the people:
1The Lord told me to chisel out two flat stones, just like the ones he had given me earlier. He also commanded me to make a wooden chest, then come up the mountain and meet with him. 2He told me that he would write on the new stones the same words he had written on the ones I broke, and that I could put these stones in this sacred chest.
3So I made a chest out of acacia wood, and I chiseled two flat stones like the ones I broke. Then I carried the stones up the mountain, 4where the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them, just as he had done the first time. The commandments were exactly what he had announced from the fire, when you were gathered at the mountain.
After the Lord returned the stones to me, 5I took them down the mountainside and put them in the chest, just as he had commanded. And they are still there.
Aaron Died
(Numbers 20.22-29)
Moses said to Israel:
6 Later we set up camp at the wells belonging to the descendants of Jaakan. Then we moved on and camped at Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became the priest. 7Next, we camped at Gudgodah and then at Jotbathah, where there are flowing streams.
The Levites Were Appointed To Carry the Chest
Moses said to Israel:
8 After I put the two stones in the sacred chest, the Lord chose the tribe of Levi, not only to carry the chest, but also to serve as his priests at the place of worship and to bless the other tribes in his name. And they still do these things. 9The Lord promised that he would always provide for the tribe of Levi, and that's why he won't give them any land, when he divides it among the other tribes.
The Lord Answered the Prayers of Moses
(Exodus 34.9,10,27-29)
Moses said to Israel:
10 When I had taken the second set of stones up the mountain, I spent 40 days and nights there, just as I had done before. Once again, the Lord answered my prayer and did not destroy you. 11Instead, he told me, “Moses, get ready to lead the people into the land that I promised their ancestors.”
What the Lord Wants
Moses said:
12People of Israel, what does the Lord your God want from you? The Lord wants you to respect and follow him, to love and serve him with all your heart and soul, 13and to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. Do this, and all will go well for you.
14Everything belongs to the Lord your God, not only the earth and everything on it, but also the sky and the highest heavens. 15Yet the Lord loved your ancestors and wanted them to belong to him. So he chose them and their descendants rather than any other nation, and today you are still his people.
16Remember your agreement with the Lord and stop being so stubborn. 17 The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind. 18 The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing. 19And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
20Respect the Lord your God, be faithful, and serve only him, making promises in his name. 21Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
22 When your ancestors went to live in Egypt, there were only 70 of them. But the Lord has blessed you, and now there are more of you than there are stars in the sky.
translation_text:
Moosis n kaa lɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni la wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “A guŋ saŋa, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, ‘Sɛɛh bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ alugɔ lugli hora la, di kpaa tinni a bizeŋ nyuu di ba n be. Kuari daazi dakka di jaa. 2Ń kaa sɛbi wia la n faa du lugli hora la hiŋ purgee la ni. Denii í jaa kpaa du a dakka biini.’
3Awia, n kpa akeesia daa di kuari a dakka, di sɛɛh a bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ alugɔ lugli hora la, di kpaa tinni a bizeŋ nyuu. 4Kɔraawiizi kaa sɛbi a Gbɔgni Fi la uŋ faa felee sɛbi lugli hora la ni, di faa sii a wia di tɛɛ ia bizeŋ la nyuu di lii ninlau biini, ii chaalaa hɔpizii la. Denii u kpaa tɛŋ. 5Awia n jaa lii a bizeŋ nyuu di tuu, di kpa a bipɛntɛnzi du dakka la miŋ kuarɛɛ la biini gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ n be la. A haa du u biini filaŋkeŋ.”
6Izrɛl hina faa lii Jaakan hina kɔlɔnzi, di vol guŋŋ di ga hel yembɛl banna yir Mɔsɛra. Aarɔn siu de, ba huguu, ka u biibaal Ɛliaza kpa u gawa, di birgi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ. 7Ba lii de di vol guŋŋ di ga hel Gudgoda, di kaa lii de di la Jɔtbata hɛri n dɔɔ gɔŋa n dɔɔ niiri. 8A saŋa hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi faa lizi Levi dee di tɛɛ u hiŋ, bá ra chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la, di ra humuu, di kpa u sɔŋ di ra kissi nɛra. Gunnɛ ba haa ra ɛɛ haali ni zinaa. 9Awiarɛ Levi dee waa kapɛttɛ dɔɔwɛ ba lulla biini la. Kɔraawiizii ba kapɛttɛ, gunla uŋ ŋɔ ba be la.
10“N faa du a bizeŋ nyuurɛ hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ alugɔ lugli la. Kɔraawiizi faa kaa nuu tɛŋ a saŋa hiŋ gba. A faa waa u kipar ɛɛwɛ lugɔ ú kpu ia. 11Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ n be, ‘La ga tɔ a nɛra see, bá la ga foozi hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ba naabaala lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ baa la, ú ɛɛ ba hor.’ ”
Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi
12Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, filaŋkeŋ, ií ra nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na nyiŋŋi ii be. Ií ra ɔmuu, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi maa, di nɔŋŋuu, di ra humuu ani ii bampiree maa. 13Ií ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni ni u widaulaa naa maa miŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, á hiini ia.
14Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu dɔɔ chinchiŋ, di kpa hɛri ani kuna la maa n du u ni. 15Ka Kɔraawiizi faa nɔŋŋi ii naabaalaa werge, di lizi ia, di lii hɛssi hina maa biine, gunla an duwɛɛ zinaa naa. 16Ií chɛr manni filaŋkeŋ, di gilɛɛ kaa dɔɔ dignikpega. 17Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu kaali vuga maa. Waabuu dɔɔra maa Dɔɔri. Waabuu dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge. Waa baŋhina ra tɔgzi kaali baŋhina. Nɛr maa wàá wer tɛu kuna, ka u ɛɛ wia leu. 18U ɔɔ ra lɛɛ lalbiizi ni luhaana nuuzii, di lɛɛ wibii di ra tɛɛ baa. U ɔɔ nɔŋŋi hɔɔhrii, di ra tɛu diwee ni laala. 19Awia, ií nɔŋŋi hɔɔhra, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii gba faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa Ijip hɛri. 20Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra humuu nɛnnɛ. Ií lawuu kpogli chigigi, di kpa u sɔŋ di ra hɛɛhzi. 21Ií ra chɔluu. Waabuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia di tɛɛ ia, a wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge ii himmaa sibɔɔ la. 22Ii naabaala la n faa la Ijip hɛri la maa faa du nɛra tokkoahoro ni fii. Ka filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la gillɔɔ ii wazi, di du kpil alugɔ chinchiŋwilaa.”

english_text:
If You Are Loyal to the Lord, He Will Bless You
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord is your God, so you must always love him and obey his laws and teachings. 2Remember, he corrected you and not your children. You are the ones who saw the Lord use his great power 3 when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people. 4 And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
5You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here. 6 And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
7With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
8Soon you will cross the Jordan River, and if you obey the laws and teachings I'm giving you today, you will be strong enough to conquer the land 9that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time. 10It's better land than you had in Egypt, where you had to struggle just to water your crops. 11But the hills and valleys in the promised land are watered by rain from heaven, 12because the Lord your God keeps his eye on this land and takes care of it all year long.
13 The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him, 14-15he will send rain at the right seasons, so you will have more than enough food, wine, and olive oil, and there will be plenty of grass for your cattle.
16But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods, 17the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
18 Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them. 19Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 20Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates. 21Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
22Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants, 23he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack. 24 You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea. 25No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
26You have a choice—do you want the Lord to bless you, or do you want him to put a curse on you? 27Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you. 28But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
29 After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal. 30You know that these two mountains are west of the Jordan River in land now controlled by the Canaanites living in the Jordan River valley. The mountains are west of the road near the sacred trees of Moreh on the other side of Gilgal.
31Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there, 32be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
translation_text:
Ií nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi di ra hiŋ u nua
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra hiŋ u kipar, u widaulaa ani u Gbɔgni saŋa maa. 2Ií ra liizi zinaa lugɔ ii biizi lɛi faa na gunla Kɔraawiizi dignitɛraa n duwɛɛ, u zenni, u fɔŋŋazeŋ 3ani u banonii ni wizenaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ Ijip hina baambaaŋ la. Anla uŋ kpawɛɛ dau Ijip koori ni u hɛri hina maa la. 4Ii na gunla uŋ ɛɛ Ijip hina laallɔɔra ni ba zagra ni a torkozi, di gil Muuzeŋaahmu di baa, saŋa la baŋ faa ra dau ii luge ani gunla uŋ chɔgi baa, ba wia tuŋ nyaamm la. 5Ii biizi lɛi na wia la uŋ ɛɛwɛ di tɛɛ ia hɛribɔduma la biini mɔɔ, ka ii wa hel bɔnnaa 6ani gunla uŋ ɛɛ Ɛliab n lii Rubin dee biini biibaala Datan ni Abiram la. U faa gillɔɔ hɛri peri, di di ba ni ba diini hina, ba tanti diini ani ba kuna maa, Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ. 7Ii himmaa siweere faa na wizenaa naa maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ.
8Awia, ií ra hiŋ Gbɔgni naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, guŋ gil ií wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di gi Jɔɔdan muu naa, di ga lɔ a nɛra ka foozi a hɛri, di dɔɔ, 9di wer dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋra hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la, Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ii naabaala ni ba naanna la biini. 10Hɛri la iinna zuu ii foozi la waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ Ijip hɛri la iiŋ lii u biini, di ɔɔ faa duu kuna di ra mizaa nii lugɔ kambol kuna la. 11Ka hɛri la iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu ii foozi di dɔɔ naa, dooŋ ɔɔ ra ba denii nɛnnɛ, u dɔɔ bizenaa ni walli. 12Kɔraawiizi waa u wia ra sɛɛ. U siwee ɔɔ du u ninɛɛ, bina maa biini.
13Awia, di ii ra hiŋ widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra humuu ni ii bampiree ani ii biine maa, 14u daŋ gil dooŋ ra nɛɛ ii hɛri u saŋazi, yuu gɛɛ hɛhchaaŋ, ií wer na mia, siŋfalii ani ɔlivi nuu, 15di na kooree ge tɛɛ ii sela, di na diwee la maa iinna nyiŋŋi.
16Ií ra du tau, di guŋ lɛi, ba daŋ dar ia, ií bir di ra kuari vuga, di ra tɔgzaa. 17Denii Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh ii ni werge maa, ú lau dooŋ, wàá ka ba. A hɛri wàá ka lii diwee, ii siuzi a hɛrsum la Kɔraawiizi n na tɛɛ ia la biini. 18Ií gil n wiŋɔzi naa du ii bampiree ni ii nfɛssi biine, di sɛbaa, di kpaa vɔɔzi ii nonee ni ii hilli, á ra liizi ia. 19Ií kpaa bagli ii biizi, di ra ŋɔ a wia, di ii wa du ii diini gɛɛ di ii waa vol ŋmɛnɛɛ, di ii wa chɔɔwɔ gɛɛ di ii wa izoo. 20Ií sɛbaa dau ii dominuuzi daazi ani ii gbessi maa ni, 21guŋ gil ii ni ii biizi hɔpizaa du kpil, hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ ii naabaala la biini, gunla chiŋ n niŋ guali hɛri ni, di birgi mag la.
22Di ii ra hiŋ widaulaa naa maa minna tɛɛ ia naa nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi maa, di lawuu kpogli chigigi, 23guŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ duŋŋi hɛssi naa hina maa n du ii see naa. Ii daŋ kpegli hɛssi la hina n kpillɛ, di du kpeg kaali ia la. 24Bɔr la maa iin niŋ kpa ii naazi jag, daŋ birgi ii hor. Ii hɛri daŋ chi hɛribɔduma guŋŋ di ga hel Lɛbanɔn, di kaa chi Muu Yufretis di ga hel Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn. 25Newee maa wàá wer karsi ia. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kpa ɔnsii werge ni bɔsai, di ta hɛri la maa iin niŋ la hina ni, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la, bá ra ɔm ia.
26Zinaa, n kpa kissaa ni nuuseeire di ra dau ii see, ií lizi bɛl. 27Ii daŋ na kissaa, di ii ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa. 28Nuuseei daŋ di ia, di ii wa vɛɛ u widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, di bir har kpua, ka ra kuari vuga la iiŋ faa waa zummɛ. 29Di Kɔraawiizi wa kpogli ia zuu hɛri la iinna la ii ga foozi di dɔɔ la, ii daŋ sii kissaa naa wia Bizeŋ Gɛrizim nyuu, di sii nuuseei naa ge wia Bizeŋ Ɛbal nyuu. 30Alugɔ iiŋ zummɛ la, bizenaa naa du Jɔɔdan muu baŋgia bɛl ŋmɛnɛɛ wiicholiire, di dugli Mɔrɛ daazenaa la n du Keenan hina hɛri la n du Jɔɔdan Waluu, di dugli Gilgal la. 31Ii ra nyiŋŋi Jɔɔdan muu giirɛ, ií ga foozi hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la. Di ii wa foozuu di so de, 32ií ra du tau, ka ra hiŋ widaulaa ni Gbɔgni naa maa miŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.”

english_text:
Only One Place To Worship the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
1Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land. 2But the nations that live there worship other gods. So after you capture the land, you must completely destroy their places of worship—on mountains and hills or in the shade of large trees. 3 Wherever these nations worship their gods, you must tear down their altars, break their sacred stones, burn the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and smash their idols to pieces. Destroy these places of worship so completely that no one will remember they were ever there. 4Don't worship the Lord your God in the way those nations worship their gods.
5-19 Soon you will cross the Jordan, and the Lord will help you conquer your enemies and let you live in peace, there in the land he has given you. But after you are settled, life will be different. You must not offer sacrifices just anywhere you want to. Instead, the Lord will choose a place somewhere in Israel where you must go to worship him. All of your sacrifices and offerings must be taken there, including sacrifices to please the Lord and any gift you promise or voluntarily give him. That's where you must also take one tenth of your grain, wine, and olive oil, as well as the first-born of your cattle, sheep, and goats. You and your family and servants will eat your gifts and sacrifices and celebrate there at the place of worship, because the Lord your God has made you successful in everything you have done. And since Levites will not have any land of their own, you must ask some of them to come along and celebrate with you.
Sometimes you may want to kill an animal for food and not as a sacrifice. If the Lord has blessed you and given you enough cows or sheep or goats, then you can butcher one of them where you live. You can eat it just like the meat from a deer or gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat. But you must not eat the blood of any animal—let the blood drain out on the ground.
20-21The Lord has promised that later on he will give Israel more land, and some of you may not be able to travel all the way from your homes to the place of worship each time you are hungry for meat. But the Lord will give you cattle, sheep, and goats, and you can butcher any of those animals at home and eat as much as you want. 22It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
23-24 But don't eat the blood. It is the life of the animal, so let it drain out on the ground before you eat the meat. 25Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
26-27All sacrifices and offerings to the Lord must be taken to the place where he chooses to be worshiped. If you offer a sacrifice to please the Lord, all of its meat must be burned on the altar. You can eat the meat from certain kinds of sacrifices, but you must always pour out the animal's blood on the altar.
28If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful.
Worship the Lord in the Right Way
Moses said:
29Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.
30But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?” 31No, you should not! The Lord hates the disgusting way those nations worship their gods, because they even burn their sons and daughters as sacrifices.
32 Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
translation_text:
Bɔkpaŋ la ban ninna jaami Kɔraawiizi wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Gbɔgni naabuu ií ra hiŋ nɛnnɛ, hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la ii mɛɛwaa n na hum la n na tɛɛ ia, di ii wa sogo u biini. 2Ií chɔgi a hɛssi hina vuga kuaribɔra la n du bizenaa, giŋgimee nyuuni ani daazenaa n lɔɔwɛ werge zɛɛzi la maa. 3Ií purgi ba mbusu lizibɔra ni ba bia baŋ baŋzɛɛ tɛɛ vug Baal la, di fuuh ba vughaaŋ Asɛra daajaŋra la. Ií purgi ba vuga la baŋ kuarɛɛ la maa, di dim a sɔna a hɛri biini nyaamm.
4Ií gilɛɛ waa jaami Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la gunla banna kuari ba vuga la. 5Ii daŋ ɔɔ chaali bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi tɛɛ ia, ii ra jaamuu la. Ií daŋ ɔɔ ba de, di waa jaamuu u sibɔɔ. 6Ií ɔɔ kpa ii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, mbusuzi lizaa kuna, ii kuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa, nuuzi la iin lɛɛwɛ, ii kipar sunzaazi, ii sunzaazi kuna ani ii sela biilugla di ba de. 7Ii ni ii diini hina ɔɔ di, di gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see de, dikuu uŋ kissi ia wia.
8Ií gilɛɛ gil bɛl maa wàá ɛɛ u kipar wia lugɔ yaa n na ɛɛ ɛŋ zinaa naa, 9dikuubɛɛwiai, ii haa waa a heezaa bɔr ani kapɛttɛ la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la helle. 10Ama, ii daŋ gi Jɔɔdan muu di ga so hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ la. Denii ú jaa gil ii na heezaa lii ii dɔma la maa n bar ia la be, ka jaa so ni bampirsɔna. 11Denii ií jaa kpa ii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, ii mbusuzi lizaa kuna, ii kuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa, ii sunzaazi la iinna tɔgzi la, di ba bɔr la un niŋ lizi tɛɛ ia, ii ra jaamuu la, gunla miŋ baglɛɛ la. Ií kpa anla maa iin lɛɛ nuuzi lugɔ ii daŋ tɛɛ la, di jaa. 12Denii ií jaa di iihinaa ni bɔsɔna, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sibɔɔ. Ii ni ii biibaala ni biihaana, ii balaa ani Levi dee la n du ii bola la, n waa ba himmaa hɛri gɛɛ kapɛttɛ maa dɔɔwɛ la. 13Ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ waa kpa ii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa di waa lizi mbusu bɔr la n par ia. 14Ií ɔɔ ra lizaa bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi lii ii dizi bɛl biini. Denii ií ɔɔ ɛɛ wia la maa miŋ bagli ia la.
15Ama, ii daŋ wer kpuuzi ii sela ii bola la waa bɛl maa biini, di hee a ola gunla maa maga iinna nyiŋŋi gunla iiŋ ɔɔ hee weema gɛɛ burŋa ol la, di lii Kɔraawiizi kissaa biini. Banla maa n doŋŋe gɛɛ di ba waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be la, daŋ wer heeu. 16Ka a waa dɛkkɛ lugɔ ii hee chal waa. Ií bizaa ta hɛri alugɔ nii la. 17Ií gilɛɛ waa di ii kuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa, aabuu ii mia, ii siŋfalii, ii nuu, ii sela biilugla gɛɛ kunla maa iiŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ ii daŋ tɛɛ anla maa n ɛɛ ii sunzaazi ani sunzinanaa di jaa, ii himmaa bola biine. 18Ii daŋ ɔɔ diabuu bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi. Ii ni ii biibaala, ii biihaana, ii balaa ani Levi dee la maa n du ii bola la. Ii daŋ ɔɔ gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sibɔɔ, wii la maa iin niŋ ɛɛ biini. 19Ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ waa kizi Levi dee wia ra ta, saŋa la maa iin niŋ du ii hɛri la.
20Di Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wa gillɔ ii hɛri yaa, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la, di ol waa kɛlli ia, ii ŋɔ, ‘Yaa ra nyiŋŋi olle.’ Guŋwaa, ii daŋ hee ol gunla maa maga iinna nyiŋŋi. 21Di bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na nyiŋŋi u sɔŋ du la wa nɛɛwɔ ii be, ii daŋ wer kpu sela la aŋhina Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ ia la, gunla miŋ baglɛɛ la. Ii daŋ heea ii bola gunla maa maga iinna nyiŋŋi. 22Ií heea gunla iin niŋ hee weema gɛɛ burŋa la. Banla n doŋŋe gɛɛ di ba waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be la, maanii niŋ wer heea. 23Ka ií ra du tau di gilɛɛ waa hee a challi, dikuubɛɛwiai, chal labuu miibɔɔ. A waa dɛkkɛ iiŋ hee a ni a challi. 24A waa dɛkkɛ iiŋ hee a chal. Ií fugaa ta hɛri lugɔ nii. 25Ií gilɛɛ waa hee a chal, guŋ gil wiimaa du wer tɛɛ ii ni ii biizi, dikuu wideŋlaa la iin ninna ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi sibɔɔ wia.
26Ií ɔɔ kpa ii sunzaazi ni anla iiŋ lɛɛ nua ŋɔ ii daŋ tɛɛ la, di la bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lizi la. 27Ií ɔɔ lizi ii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la mbusu lizibɔr la ni, a ola ni a challi maa. Ii daŋ ɔɔ fug ii mbusuzi sela challi, di dau Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la mbusu lizibɔr la zɛɛ, ka ii daŋ wer hee a ola waa. 28Ií ra du tau, di ra hiŋ widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia naa, guŋ gil wichɔgii maa wàá huuzi ii ni ii biizi, dikuu iin ninna ɛɛ wia la n wesse di kaa deŋli, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sibɔɔ wia.
29Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ duŋŋi hɛssi la nɛra iinna nyiŋŋi ii lɔ, ka foozi ba hɛssi la. Di ii wa duŋŋi baa ka so ba hɛri, 30Kɔraawiizi wa chɔgi baa ii sibɔɔ, ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ waa pɛɛzi ba vuga wia, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ hɛssi naa hina ra kuari ba vugai? Yaa gba ra nyiŋŋi ya ra ɛɛ guŋ himmaanii.’ Di ii wa ɛɛ guŋ, a daŋ birgi sidɛɛzi di lauri ia. 31Ií gilɛɛ waa jaami Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, gunla banna kuari ba vuga la, dikuubɛɛwiai, wikuna la Kɔraawiizi n kiiwee ba ra ɛɛ. Haali ba biibaala ni biihaana maanii ba ɔɔ fuuh, di ra ligzi mbusuzi, di ra tɛɛ ba vuga.
32Wia la maa miŋ ŋɔ ií ra ɛɛ la, ií ɛɛ ania maa ka ra hiŋaa. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa wiimaa di ra jaa a ni gɛɛ di wa teŋ wiimaa di ra ha.”

english_text:
Don't Worship Other Gods
Moses said to Israel:
1-2Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.” 3If the prophet says this, don't listen! The Lord your God will be watching to find out whether or not you love him with all your heart and soul. 4You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling, 5because he rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
If a prophet tells you to disobey the Lord your God and to stop worshiping him, then that prophet is evil and must be put to death.
6-10 Someone else may say to you, “Let's worship other gods.” That person may be your best friend, your brother or sister, your son or daughter, or your own dear wife or husband. But you must not listen to people who say such things. Instead, you must stone them to death. You must be the first to throw the stones, then others from the community will finish the job. Don't show any pity.
The gods worshiped by other nations have never done anything for you or your ancestors. People who ask you to worship other gods are trying to get you to stop worshiping the Lord, who rescued you from slavery in Egypt. So put to death anyone who asks you to worship another god. 11And when the rest of Israel hears about it, they will be afraid, and no one else will ever do such an evil thing again.
12After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns. 13You may hear that some worthless people have talked everyone there into worshiping other gods, even though these gods had never done anything for them. 14You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country, 15you must take your swords and kill every one of them, and their livestock too. 16-17Gather all the possessions of the people who lived there, and pile them up in the marketplace, without keeping anything for yourself. Set the pile and the whole town on fire, and don't ever rebuild the town. The whole town will be a sacrifice to the Lord your God. Then he won't be angry anymore, and he will have mercy on you and make your nation stronger, just as he promised your ancestors. 18That's why you must do what the Lord your God says is right. I am giving you his laws and teachings today, and you must obey them.
translation_text:
Vuga kuaraa wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di dɔgtɛɛ gɛɛ nɛr la n na na wia deeza biini wa lii ii biini, di sii lugɔ wizeŋ gɛɛ nuukpuuri wii daŋ ɛɛ, 2di a widee la wia uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wa ɛɛwɔ, u ŋɔ, ‘Ií gil ya ra kuari vuga,’ vuga la iiŋ faa waa zummɛ, 3ií gilɛɛ waa nuu ra tɛɛ a dɔgtɛɛ naa gɛɛ unla n na a wia deeza biini la. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ra nyiŋŋuu ú ɛɛ ia na, di zum di ii nɔŋŋuubuu ni ii bampiree ni ii biine maa gɛɛ. 4Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu dɛkkɛ iinna hiŋ, di ra ɔmuu. Ií ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni di ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra, di ra humuu, di lawuu kpogli chigigi. 5A dɔgtɛɛ gɛɛ a deeza biini wia nai hiŋ la dɛg kpuirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u amaniye la uŋ lizɛɛ la ra bagluu lugɔ ií vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Waabuu lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri, bɔr la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma la. A hiŋ kipattɛ ií bir har kpu ŋmɛnɛɛ la uŋ ŋɔ ií ra hiŋ la. A dɛkkɔɔ ii lizi wichɔgaa lii ii biini.
6Di i bɛl maa kpɛɛma gɛɛ u niwee himmaa gɛɛ u biibaal gɛɛ u biihaaŋ gɛɛ u haaŋ la uŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ gɛɛ u dammu ra nyiŋŋuu ú suahzi murguu, di ŋɔ lugɔ ú gaa kuari vuga la u ni u mɛɛwaa n faa waa zummɛ, 7nɛra la n bar ia la vuga, di a duglɔɔ gɛɛ di a du bɔɔnɛɛrɛ, 8ú gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ gɛɛ di nuu ra tɛu. Ú gilɛɛ waa suŋ u ni. Ú gilɛɛ waa giluu gɛɛ di ra mɔgluu. 9Ú kpuu. Waabuu dɛkkɛ un niŋ feli tɔ see di kpuu, ka nɛra ge haa wa hiinuu. 10Ií lɔɔzuu ni bia di kpu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra nyiŋŋuu ii vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum. Waabuu lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yom la. 11Denii Izrɛl hina maa nuu guŋ, ɔnsii lau baa, nɛr maa wàá ka lii ii biini di ɛɛ a guŋ wichɔgaa maa.
12Di ii wa nuuwɔ banna ŋɔ bola la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n tɛɛ ia ŋɔ ií so la bɛl maa biini lugɔ 13biinikpola hina izoore ii biini, di dar ba bol hina, di ra ŋɔ lugɔ bá gaa kuari vuga la ii ni ii mɛɛwaa n faa waa zummɛ, 14ií pɛɛzi di pigzi a wia biini nɛnnɛ. Di a ɛɛ wibii, daansɛɛ du de di ra bagli lugɔ wia naa Kɔraawiizi kiiwe naa ɛɛwɔɔ ii biini, 15guŋwaa, a dɛkkɔɔ ií kpuuzi nɛra la maa n du a bol hiŋ biini. Ií chɔgi a bol ni u nɛra ni u kundɛɛzaa maa nyaamm. 16Ií chaali a bol kuna maa dau ba bossibaaŋ, di fuuh a bol ni u kuna maa, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. U daŋ ɛɛ diŋgela di hanna la. Ba wàá ka bir mau maa. 17Ií gilɛɛ waa gil kuna la maa n dɛg chɔgaa la bɛl maa waa du ii be. Guŋ daŋ gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ wàá fuuh ii ni. U daŋ suŋ ii ni di na ii sinyɛna, di gil ii wazi gunla uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii naabaala la, 18dikuu iinna sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni la minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, di ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee u sibɔɔ wia.”

english_text:
Don't Mourn like Other Nations
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, you are the Lord's children, so when you mourn for the dead, you must not cut yourselves or shave your forehead. 2 Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods.
Animals That Can Be Eaten
(Leviticus 11.1-47)
3 Don't eat any disgusting animals.
4-5You may eat the meat of cattle, sheep, and goats; wild sheep and goats; and gazelles, antelopes, and all kinds of deer. 6It is all right to eat meat from any animals that have divided hoofs and also chew the cud.
7But don't eat camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. These animals chew the cud but do not have divided hoofs. You must treat them as unclean. 8And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!
9You can eat any fish that has fins and scales. But there are other creatures that live in the water, 10and if they do not have fins and scales, you must not eat them. Treat them as unclean.
11You can eat any clean bird. 12-18But don't eat the meat of any of the following birds: eagles, vultures, falcons, kites, ravens, ostriches, owls, sea gulls, hawks, pelicans, ospreys, cormorants, storks, herons, and hoopoes. You must not eat bats. 19Swarming insects are unclean, so don't eat them. 20However, you are allowed to eat certain kinds of winged insects.
21 You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. You may give it to foreigners who live in your town or sell it to foreigners who are visiting your town.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Give the Lord Ten Percent of Your Harvest
Moses said:
22 People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest. 23Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.
24But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest, 25then sell this part and take the money there instead. 26When you and your family arrive, spend the money on food for a big celebration. Buy cattle, sheep, goats, wine, beer, and if there are any other kinds of food that you want, buy those too. 27And since people of the Levi tribe won't own any land for growing crops, remember to ask the Levites to celebrate with you.
28Every third year, instead of using the ten percent of your harvest for a big celebration, bring it into town and put it in a community storehouse. 29The Levites have no land of their own, so you must give them food from the storehouse. You must also give food to the poor who live in your town, including orphans, widows, and foreigners. If they have enough to eat, then the Lord your God will be pleased and make you successful in everything you do.
translation_text:
Diudoŋa ani anla n waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ii ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la biizii. Awia, ií gilɛɛ waa mɔnni ii bɔra gɛɛ di waa fuŋ ii hilli dikuu lalaa wia. 2Ii ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nɛraa. U lizi iabuu lii durnya hɛssi nɛra maa biine, ií ɛɛ u daama la unna tɔgzi werge maa la.
3Ií gilɛɛ waa di kunla maa n doŋŋe u be. 4Sela naabuu ii wer di ra di, nauna, peeza, buuna, 5weenzi, burunzi, baambuugizi, chɛhzi, wilaa ani nagma. 6Ii daŋ wer di sel la maa naafiraa n bargɛɛ bɔra anɛɛ, u kaa ug ra hee. 7Ka anla n ukke ra hee, a naafiraa bargi biini la, ií gilɛɛ waa hee nyugma, chooma ani aahri. A waa dɛg ii dii, dikuubɛɛwiai, a doŋŋoo Kɔraawiizi be. 8Pereku gba doŋŋoo, haali u naafiraa n bargɛɛ gba, ka waa ukke ra hee. U ol waa dɛg heei gɛɛ u siwii waa dɛg gbɔgzaa.
9Kunnyinee la maa n du nii biini di dɔɔ sɔɔhri ni hɛga waa, ii daŋ wer dia. 10Ka anla n nyaa sɔɔhri ni hɛga la, ií gilɛɛ waa dia. A doŋŋoo, a wer tɛɛ ia.
11Ii daŋ wer di zumbee la maa n waa doŋŋe. 12Zumbizi naabuu ii ra kii, dikuubɛɛwiai, a doŋŋoo, aabuu chig, duu iri maa, 13kɔlaahmu, kɔlbiŋŋu iri maa, 14dugli iri maa, kikiu ge iri maa, 15niilaaraa, keezaa iri maa 16kukubalee, niilaaraazeŋ, 17kikiu iri maa, niilaaraa, 18namɛŋŋu ge iri maa, lalaakpakpa ani ziŋ.
19Ií ra kii kunzaahrijigzi maa. 20Ka kunnyinee la maa n dɔɔ keeri, a waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be, ii daŋ wer dia.
21Ií gilɛɛ waa di kunla maa n siu u hiŋ ni. Ii daŋ wer kpau tɛɛ hɔɔhra la maa n du ii bola, bá di gɛɛ ii daŋ wer yoou tɛɛ baa. Iawaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛmbɛŋ horaa.
Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa bubii di ra daali u maa ilanii biini.”
Kuna bɔra fi bɔkpaŋ wia
22Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ɔɔ bargi ii pattikuna maa bɔra fi, di lizi a bɔkpaŋ dau bina maa. Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ. 23Ií ɔɔ ra di ii mia, siŋfalaa, nuu fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa ani ii sela lugli biizi, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see, bɔr la un niŋ lizi tɛɛ ia, ii ra jaamuu la. Guŋ daŋ gil ii helli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la tɔgzaa, saŋa maa. 24Di a bɔr nɛɛwɔɔ werge, ii wàá wer la ii kuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kissi ia ii na la ni, 25ií kpaa chɛr saliŋhuŋŋu, di kpaa la bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi la. 26Ií kpa a saliŋhuŋŋu di yau kunla maa iinna nyiŋŋi, naunaa, peezaa ani siŋ gɛɛ siŋ maa iri baŋ du bura gɛɛ kunla maa iinna nyiŋŋi. Denii ii ni ii diini hina maa dia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see, ii bɔra sɔɔni ia. 27Ií gilɛɛ waa suuh Levi dee la n du ii bola la wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waa ba himmaa hɛssi gɛɛ kapɛttɛzi dɔɔwɛ.
28Binni ahoro maa tuna, ií ɔɔ chaali a bina kuna bɔra fi bɔkpaŋ di dau ii bola. 29Levi dee la n waa ba himmaa hɛssi gɛɛ kapɛttɛzi dɔɔwɛ la, hɔɔhra, lalbiizi ani luhaana la n du ii bola la, ba di wa di, di piŋ. Guŋ gil Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kissi ia, ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini.”

english_text:
Loans
(Leviticus 25.1-7)
Moses said:
1-2Every seven years you must announce, “The Lord says loans do not need to be paid back.” Then if you have loaned money to another Israelite, you can no longer ask for payment. 3This law applies only to loans you have made to other Israelites. Foreigners will still have to pay back what you have loaned them.
4-6No one in Israel should ever be poor. The Lord your God is giving you this land, and he has promised to make you very successful, if you obey his laws and teachings that I'm giving you today. You will lend money to many nations, but you won't have to borrow. You will rule many nations, but they won't rule you.
7 After the Lord your God gives land to each of you, there may be poor Israelites in the town where you live. If there are, then don't be mean and selfish with your money. 8Instead, be kind and lend them what they need. 9Be careful!
