23‘Nuuseei di baal la maa n niŋ nyiŋŋi u hila.’
Denii á nɛra maa ŋɔ, ‘Ami!’
24‘Nuuseei di baal la maa n niŋ suahzi kpu u dɔŋhiŋ.’
Denii á nɛra maa ŋɔ, ‘Ami!’
25‘Kɔraawiizi daŋ see baal la maa n lɛɛ kebee gɛɛ kummaa, ka kpu nɛr la n waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ nua.’
Denii á nɛra maa ŋɔ, ‘Ami!’
26‘Nuuseei di baal la maa n waa Gbɔg naa ra hiŋ.’
Denii á nɛra maa ŋɔ, ‘Ami!’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
Moses said to Israel:
1-2 Today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. Always obey them, and the Lord will make Israel the most famous and important nation on earth, and he will bless you in many ways.
3The Lord will make your businesses and your farms successful.
4You will have many children. You will harvest large crops, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats will produce many young.
5You will have plenty of bread to eat.
6The Lord will make you successful in your daily work.
7The Lord will help you defeat your enemies and make them scatter in all directions.
8The Lord your God is giving you the land, and he will make sure you are successful in everything you do. Your harvests will be so large that your storehouses will be full.
9If you follow and obey the Lord, he will make you his own special people, just as he promised. 10Then everyone on earth will know that you belong to the Lord, and they will be afraid of you.
11The Lord will give you a lot of children and make sure that your animals give birth to many young. The Lord promised your ancestors that this land would be yours, and he will make it produce large crops for you.
12The Lord will open the storehouses of the skies where he keeps the rain, and he will send rain on your land at just the right times. He will make you successful in everything you do. You will have plenty of money to lend to other nations, but you won't need to borrow any yourself.
13Obey the laws and teachings that I'm giving you today, and the Lord your God will make Israel a leader among the nations, and not a follower. Israel will be wealthy and powerful, not poor and weak. 14But you must not reject any of his laws and teachings or worship other gods.
The Lord Will Put Curses on You if You Disobey
(Leviticus 26.14-46)
Moses said:
15Israel, today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. And if you don't obey them all, he will put many curses on you.
16Your businesses and farms will fail.
17You won't have enough bread to eat.
18You'll have only a few children, your crops will be small, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats won't produce many young.
19The Lord will make you fail in everything you do.
20No matter what you try to accomplish, the Lord will confuse you, and you will feel his anger. You won't last long, and you may even meet with disaster, all because you rejected the Lord.
21-23The Lord will send terrible diseases to attack you, and you will never be well again. You will suffer with burning fever and swelling and pain until you die somewhere in the land that you captured.
The Lord will make the sky overhead seem like a bronze roof that keeps out the rain, and the ground under your feet will become as hard as iron. Your crops will be scorched by the hot east wind or ruined by mildew. 24He will send dust and sandstorms instead of rain, and you will be wiped out.
25The Lord will let you be defeated by your enemies, and you will scatter in all directions. You will be a horrible sight for the other nations to see, 26and no one will disturb the birds and wild animals while they eat your dead bodies.
27The Lord will make you suffer with diseases that will cause oozing sores or crusty itchy patches on your skin or boils like the ones that are common in Egypt. And there will be no cure for you! 28You will become insane and go blind. The Lord will make you so confused, 29that even in bright sunshine you will have to feel your way around like a blind person, who cannot tell day from night. For the rest of your life, people will beat and rob you, and no one will be able to stop them.
30A man will be engaged to a woman, but before they can get married, she will be raped by enemy soldiers. Some of you will build houses, but never get to live in them. If you plant a vineyard, you won't be around long enough to enjoy the first harvest. 31Your cattle will be killed while you watch, but you won't get to eat any of the meat. Your donkeys and sheep will be stolen from you, and no one will be around to force your enemies to give them back. 32Your sons and daughters will be dragged off to a foreign country, while you stand there helpless. And even if you watch for them until you go blind, you will never see them again.
33You will work hard on your farms, but everything you harvest will be eaten by foreigners, who will mistreat you and abuse you for the rest of your life.
34What you see will be so horrible that you will go insane, 35and the Lord will punish you from head to toe with boils that never heal.
36The Lord will let you and your king be taken captive to a country that you and your ancestors have never even heard of, and there you will have to worship idols made of wood and stone. 37People of nearby countries will shudder when they see your terrible troubles, but they will still make fun of you.
38You will plant a lot of seed, but gather a small harvest, because locusts will eat your crops. 39You will plant vineyards and work hard at taking care of them, but you won't gather any grapes, much less get any wine, because the vines themselves will be eaten by worms. 40Even if your olive trees grow everywhere in your country, the olives will fall off before they are ready, and there won't be enough olive oil for combing your hair.
41Even your children will be taken as prisoners of war.
42Locusts will eat your crops and strip your trees of leaves and fruit.
43Foreigners in your towns will become wealthy and powerful, while you become poor and powerless. 44You will be so short of money that you will have to borrow from those foreigners. They will be the leaders in the community, and you will be the followers.
More Curses for Disobedience
Moses said:
45Israel, if you don't obey the laws and teachings that the Lord your God is giving you, he will send these curses to chase, attack, and destroy you. 46Then everyone will look at you and your descendants and realize that the Lord has placed you under a curse.
47If the Lord makes you wealthy, but you don't joyfully worship and honor him, 48he will send enemies to attack you and make you their slaves. Then you will live in poverty with nothing to eat, drink, or wear, and your owners will work you to death.
49Foreigners who speak a strange language will be sent to attack you without warning, just like an eagle swooping down. 50They won't show any mercy, and they will have no respect for old people or pity for children. 51They will take your cattle, sheep, goats, grain, wine, and olive oil, then leave you to starve.
52All over the land that the Lord your God gave you, the enemy army will surround your towns. You may feel safe inside your town walls, but the enemy will tear them down, 53while you wait in horror. Finally, you will get so hungry that you will eat the sons and daughters that the Lord gave you. 54-55Because of hunger, a man who had been gentle and kind will eat his own children and refuse to share the meal with his brother or wife or with his other children. 56-57 A woman may have grown up in such luxury that she never had to put a foot on the ground. But times will be so bad that she will secretly eat both her newborn baby and the afterbirth, without sharing any with her husband or her other children.
Disobedience Brings Destruction
Moses said to Israel:
58You must obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Because if you don't respect the Lord, 59he will punish you and your descendants with incurable diseases, 60like those you were so afraid of in Egypt. 61Remember! If the Lord decides to destroy your nation, he can use any disease or disaster, not just the ones written in The Book of God's Law.
62There are as many of you now as the stars in the sky, but if you disobey the Lord your God, only a few of you will be left. 63The Lord is happy to make you successful and to help your nation grow while you conquer the land. But if you disobey him, he will be just as happy to pull you up by your roots.
64Those of you that survive will be scattered to every nation on earth, and you will have to worship stone and wood idols that never helped you or your ancestors. 65You will be restless—always longing for home, but never able to return. 66You will live in constant fear of death. 67Each morning you will wake up to such terrible sights that you will say, “I wish it were night!” But at night you will be terrified and say, “I wish it were day!”
68I told you never to go back to Egypt. But now the Lord himself will load you on ships and send you back. Then you will even try to sell yourselves as slaves, but no one will be interested.
translation_text:
Nua hiŋaa kissaazi wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di ii ra sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nuuzi maa, di ra hiŋ u wiŋɔɔlaa naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa nɛnnɛ, u daŋ gil ii dɔɔ sɔŋ kaali durnya naa hɛssi hina maa. 2Ii daŋ na kissaazi naa maa, a du ii be bɔr la maa iinna la, di ii ra sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua.
3Kɔraawiizi daŋ kissi ia ii bola ni ii kooni maa biine.
4U daŋ kissi ii biizi, ii pattikuna ani ii sela biizi maa.
5Kɔraawiizi daŋ kissi ii mia ni diwee la iin niŋ kpaa di daali.
6U daŋ kissi ii wiɛɛlaa maa.
7Di ii dɔma wa ballɔ bá wa lɔ ia, u daŋ kpegli baa tɛɛ ia. Di ba ga bɔkpaŋ ba, ka bɔkpilaa bá ga di chɔ yaari.
8Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kissi ii huma, di gil ii buugazi suugi. U daŋ kissi ia hɛri la unna tɛɛ ia la biini.
9Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii chi chigigi, di ɛɛ u nɛnanaananaa gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la, di ii ra ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi. 10Denii durnya nɛra maa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi lizi iabuu tɛɛ u hiŋ, di ra ɔm ia. 11U daŋ gil ii nyɛɛli werge. Ii biizi, ii sela ani ii kooni kuna daŋ wazi werge maa, hɛri la uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ tɛɛ ii naabaala lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ ia la biini.
12Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil dooŋ ba u balaa saŋa, di lii u dia la n du chiŋ, daama su u biini la. U daŋ kissi ii huma maa, hɛssi hina ba di waa kim ii be, ka iawaa waa kim di lii ba be. 13Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ gil ii tɔ hɛssi hina maa see. Wàá gil ii tɔ har. Ii daŋ ɔɔ nyɛɛli saŋa maa. Ii wàá ɛɛ wiimaa huhzi, di ii ra sɛɛ u widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, di ra hiŋaa nɛnnɛ. 14Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ a hiŋaa tama maa gɛɛ di waa kuari vug maa.”
Nuuseezi dikuu dignikpega wia
15Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ama, di ii waa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua ra sɛɛ, ii waa u widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa ra hiŋ nɛnnɛ, nuuseezi naa maa daŋ di ia, di tɛɛ ia tɔɔrɔɔ.
16Kɔraawiizi daŋ see ia nuuzi ii bolzenaa ni ii kooni maa biine.
17U daŋ see ii mia ani diwee la maa iin niŋ kpaa di daali nua.
18Kɔraawiizi daŋ see ia nua, ii biizi, ii pattikuna ani ii sela, a wàá wazi.
19U daŋ see ii wiɛɛlaa maa nua.
20U daŋ see ia nuuzi, di gil ii bugmi, di hau ii ni, ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini, guŋŋ bá wa chɔg ia manaŋ, ii wia tuŋ dikuu wichɔgaa la iiŋ ɛɛwɛ, di kizuu ta wia. 21Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil wiilchɔgaa chol ii ni, di ra ba saŋa la un niŋ kpu ia hɛri la iinna zuu ii dɔɔ la biini. 22U daŋ kpa wiila la n gillɛ nɛr ra kɔgi werge la, di ta ii ni, ii bɔra wenzi di ɔrgi. Ii hɛri wenzi werge, hil chi, pewem gil ii pattikuna pɔɔh, ii di tɔɔrɔɔ guŋŋ, ii maa wa siuzi. 23Chiŋ daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ danyɛ, hɛri ge ɛɛ lugɔ lugbii. 24Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil nyɔɔ ni hɛɛhriichaa lii chiŋ di chol ii hɛri lugɔ dooŋ, di ra ba saŋa la iin niŋ tuŋ nyaamm.
25Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii dɔma kpegli ia. Bɔkpannɛ ii ga lɔ baa, ka bɔkpilaa ii ga di chɔ yaari. Ii wia daŋ gil durnya kossi hina maa nuuzi kpu. 26Ii daŋ siuzi, ii bɔrahɔna birgi diwee tɛɛ zumbizi ni pir sela maa. Nɛr maa wàá du de, ú ɔnzaa a kaali.
27Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa Ijip kunsɔna la ha ii ni, á ɛɛ ŋmɛrzenaa, di ra lii nii, di ra huhrgi. Nɛr maa wàá wer chaa ia. 28U daŋ kpa chugla, nyuŋŋaa ani bugmaa ha ii ni. 29Wibaŋkaŋchiirii ni, ka ii danna largi bɔra alugɔ nyuŋŋa. Wii la maa iin niŋ ɛɛ wàá dɔɔ siwee. Hɔpizii maa, ba danna fir ia di ra ŋmɛɛ ia, ka nɛr maa wàá du de, ú lɛɛ ia.
30Ii daŋ dɔɔ sɛnna di ra nyiŋŋi ii paa baa, ka nɛra baŋhinaa niŋ paa baa. Ii daŋ ma diini, ka ii wàá zuu a biine. Ii daŋ par grepu daazi kooni, ka ii wàá faari a nɔna dii. 31Ba daŋ kpu ii nabala ii see, ka ii wàá heea. Ba daŋ foozi ii kauzi, ka ba wàá biraa tɛɛ ia. Ba daŋ kpa ii peeza tɛɛ ii dɔma, ka nɛr maa wàá lɛɛa tɛɛ ia. 32Ba daŋ kpa ii biibaala ni biihaana tɛɛ hɛri bɛl hina. Ii pɛɛ ii siwee, di binni ba bir balaa ŋmɛnɛɛ guŋŋ di wa kuuh. Ii wàá dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ií ɛɛ wiimaa. 33Nɛra la iiŋ waa zummɛɛ niŋ di ii hɛri kuna la iiŋ kpa ii fɔŋŋa di par na. Ii wàá dɔɔ kummaa di nɛfiraa ni nɛsunnaa bɛŋ lɛi, ii de dui saŋa. 34Wia la iin ninna na daŋ gil ii ɛɛ lugɔ chuglahina. 35Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil i naahiine ni i naazi ɔrgi kunsɔna la n na wii werge, ba wàá weraa chaa. A daŋ yaari di lii i naapaala ga hel i nyuubaana.
36Kɔraawiizi daŋ duŋŋi ii ni koori la iiŋ lizɛɛ ŋɔ ú ra binni ia la, di kaali hɛrduma la ii ni ii mɛɛwaa n waa zummɛ. Denii ii ra kuari vuga la n ɛɛ daazi ni bia. 37Ii wia daŋ kpu nɛra nuuzi, ba hah ia, di ra ɛɛ ia chɛɛtɛ hɛssi la maa biine Kɔraawiizi n niŋ duŋŋi ia ii ga du la.
38Ii daŋ duu kuna werge, ka tamaa bɛnnɛ ii kum, dikuubɛɛwiai, lotorozi daŋ di a maa. 39Ii daŋ par grepu daazi kooni, ka ii wàá nyɔɔ a nɔna siŋ gɛɛ di chaali a nɔna, dikuubɛɛwiai, sandulee niŋ dia. 40Ii daŋ dɔɔ ɔlivi daazi ii hɛri maa biini, ka ii wàá na a nuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɔna maanii niŋ war. 41Ii daŋ dɔɔ biizi, ka ba wàá du ii be, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii dɔma daŋ lɔ ia, di lauri baa kaali hɛrdumazi, bá ga birgi yoma. 42Lotorozi kpila miiih daŋ tɔ ii daazi ni ii kooni kuna maa ni, di dia.
43Hɔɔhra la n du ii biini la fɔŋŋa danna jaa, ka iawaa hor hanna tuu zɛɛ. 44Ii danna kim kebee di ra lii ba be, ka baawaa wàá kim di lii ii be. Ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ nyuu, ii ge ɛɛ lugɔ diŋ.
45Nuuseezi naa maa daŋ di ia. A daŋ di ia di ra ba saŋa la ii wia n niŋ tuŋ, dikuu iiŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua, di vɛɛ u widaulaa hiŋaa la wia. 46A daŋ ɛɛ daansɛɛ wii ani witittaa tɛɛ ii ni ii naanna, di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa. 47Dikuu iiŋ waa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la hummɛ ni bɔsɔna ni biinihuŋŋu, saŋa la iiŋ nyɛɛlɛɛ la wia. 48Lɔzi, niinyɔgzi, laala nyaai ani nyaachɔgiirɛ, ii kpa di ra hum ii dɔma la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ gil bá wa lɔ ia la. Napattaa baŋaa lugbidaarɛ ú kpa sag ii baŋaazi, di ra ba saŋa la un niŋ kpuuzi ia nyaamm.
49Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil hɛri bɛl hina n lii bɔɔnɛɛ ba, di wa lɔ ia. Ba daŋ lii hɛri tuna alugɔ chig n lii chiŋ di ra tuu hɛri, ii wàá ra nuu ba mɔɔri. 50Hɛri la hina n dɔɔ sikpegii, ba waa nabɔnzi ra tɔgzi gɛɛ di ra suŋ bichalli ni. 51Ba daŋ kpuuzi ii kundɛɛzaa biizi, di chɔgi ii kooni kuna maa. Ba wàá gil ii mia, siŋfalii gɛɛ ii sela biizi bɛl maa guŋŋ, di ra ba saŋa la ii wia maa n niŋ chɔgi. 52Ba daŋ fɔɔ ii bolzenaa maa n du ii hɛri guŋŋ, di ra ba saŋa la a koŋliizenaa la n kpekke, ii yardaa la n niŋ chogli. Ba daŋ fɔɔ bolzenaa la maa n du hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la.
53Tɔɔrɔɔ la n niŋ huuzi ia saŋa la ii dɔma n niŋ fɔɔ ia la wia, ii daŋ hee ii biizi. Biizi la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n tɛɛ ia la ola. 54Haali baal la maa n dɔɔ sisɔna di ra suŋ nɛra ni, wàá suŋ u lulli himmaa gɛɛ u haaŋ la uŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ gɛɛ u biizi la n kawɛɛ ni. 55Wàá sɛɛ kpa u bie la ol unna hee la tɛɛ bɛl maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, kunla maa uŋ dɔɔwɛɛ guŋ. Tɔɔrɔɔ la ii dɔma n niŋ gil u huuzi ia saŋa la baŋ fɔɔ ii bolzenaa maa la wia. 56Haali haaŋ la n dɔɔ sisɔna di ra suŋ nɛra ni werge, di dɔɔ daama werge, waa hɛri ra vol la, daŋ dɔɔ wii ni u jaari la uŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ ani u biizi, 57dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ siryaa ú suahzi hee u biifula ni u dɔŋ, dikuu saŋa la ii dɔma n fɔɔ ia ani tɔɔrɔɔ ni biinichɔg la baŋ kpawɛɛ ta ii ni la wia.
58Di ii waa Gbɔg naa wiŋɔɔlaa ra hiŋ nɛnnɛ, gunla baŋ sɛbaa hɔnnaa biini, di ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sɔŋ la wia n na kpu nua, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge la, 59u daŋ gil wiilchɔgaa la wia n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, chol ii ni ii naanna ni, di tɔɔri ia werge di birgi. 60U daŋ gil Ijip hina wiila la maa iinna ɔm la chol ii ni, a wàá ta ia. 61Kɔraawiizi daŋ kaa gil wiila ni hɛhchɔg irizi la wia baŋ waa sɛbɛɛ Gbɔg Hɔnnaa biini, chol ii ni guŋŋ di ra ba ii siuzaa saŋa. 62Iiŋ faa kpillɛ werge lugɔ chinchiŋwilaa la, ka ii daŋ ka tama, dikuu iiŋ waa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua hiŋŋɛ wia. 63Gunla am par Kɔraawiizi, u gil ii daama ni ii biizi wazi werge la, gunnɛ a paruu, ú gil ii wia bir pɛɛ, ú kpuuzi ia. Ba daŋ duŋŋi ia lii hɛri la biini iinna zuu ií dɔɔ la.
64Denii Kɔraawiizi gil ii yaari a hɛssi maa biine, di lii hɛri tuna bɛl di ga hel bɛl. Denii ii ra kuari vuga la n ɛɛ daazi ni bia, ii ni ii naabaala n faa waa zummɛ. 65A hɛssi naa biine, ii wàá dɔɔ bampirsɔna gɛɛ heezaa bɔr, ií kpa ii naazi jag. Denii Kɔraawiizi gil kafɔŋ lau ia, ii yaa siwee di ra ɛɛ tamii pɛɛ, bɔhuaih lau ia. 66Ii danna fɔŋ ii miibɔɔni wia saŋa maa. Ɔnsii werge lau ia hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi maa. Ii wàá zum wia la n niŋ huuzi ia. 67Chɔɔzi ni, ii daŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Di duanaa faa keŋ!’ Duana ge, ii ŋɔ, ‘Di chɔɔzii faa keŋ!’ Ɔnsii werge la n niŋ lau ia ani wia la ii siwee n ninna na la wiarɛ ii ra ŋɔ guŋ. 68Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii bir zuu muugberzenaa kaali Ijip, bɔr la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ii wàá ka la la. Denii ii kpa iihinaa di yoo ra tɛɛ ii dɔma, ií ɛɛ ba yombaala ni haana. Ka nɛr maa wàá yau ia.”

english_text:
The Agreement in Moab
1So Moses finished telling the Israelites what they had to do in order to keep the agreement the Lord was making with them in Moab, which was in addition to the one the Lord had made with them at Mount Sinai.
The Third Speech: Israel Must Keep Its Agreement with the Lord
The Lord Is Your God
2-3Moses called the nation of Israel together and told them:
When you were in Egypt, you saw the Lord perform great miracles that caused trouble for the king, his officials, and everyone else in the country. 4-6He has even told you, “For 40 years I, the Lord, led you through the desert, but your clothes and your sandals didn't wear out, and I gave you special food. I did these things so you would realize that I am your God.”
But the Lord must give you a change of heart before you truly understand what you have seen and heard.
7 When we first camped here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan attacked, but we defeated them. 8 Then we captured their land and divided it among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
Keep the Agreement
Moses said:
9Israel, the Lord has made an agreement with you, and if you keep your part, you will be successful in everything you do. 10-12Today everyone in our nation is standing here in the Lord's presence, including leaders and officials, parents and children, and even those foreigners who cut wood and carry water for us. We are at this place of worship to promise that we will keep our part of the agreement with the Lord our God.
13-15In this agreement, the Lord promised that you would be his people and that he would be your God. He first made this promise to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and today the Lord is making this same promise to you. But it isn't just for you; it is also for your descendants.
16-17When we lived in Egypt, you saw the Egyptians worship disgusting idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. Then as we traveled through other nations, you saw those people worship other disgusting idols. 18 So make sure that everyone in your tribe remains faithful to the Lord and never starts worshiping gods of other nations.
If even one of you worships idols, you will be like the root of a plant that produces bitter, poisonous fruit. 19You may be an Israelite and know all about the Lord's agreement with us, but he won't bless you if you rebel against him. You may think you can get away with it, but you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you. 20-21The Lord will be furious, and instead of forgiving you, he will separate you from the other tribes. Then he will destroy you, by piling on you all the curses in The Book of God's Law, and you will be forgotten forever.
22The Lord will strike your country with diseases and disasters. Your descendants and foreigners from distant countries will see that your land 23 has become a scorching desert of salt and sulfur, where nothing is planted, nothing sprouts, and nothing grows. It will be as lifeless as the land around the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, after the Lord became angry and destroyed them.
24People from other nations will ask, “Why did the Lord destroy this country? Why was he so furious?”
25And they will be given this answer:
Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, but after he brought them out of Egypt and made an agreement with them, they rejected the agreement 26and decided to worship gods that had never helped them. The Lord had forbidden Israel to worship these gods, 27-28and so he became furious and punished the land with all the curses in The Book of God's Law. Then he pulled up Israel by the roots and tossed them into a foreign country, where they still are today.
29The Lord our God hasn't explained the present or the future, but he has commanded us to obey the laws he gave to us and our descendants.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi ni Izrɛl hina nuukpaŋ ɛɛi Moab hɛri wia
1Kɔraawiizi ni Izrɛl hina nuukpaŋ la uŋ ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ u ni Izrɛl hina ɛɛ Moab hɛri la widaulaarɛ keŋ, di kpa jaa unla u ni baa n faa ɛɛwɛ Bizeŋ Sinaai la.
2Denii Moosis chaali Izrɛl hina maa, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ii siwee na wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ dau Ijip koori, u nabɔnzi ni u hɛri maanii. 3Ii himmaa siwee na a wiilchɔgaa, wizenaa ani a nuukpuuri wiarɛ. 4Ka haali ni zinaa, Kɔraawiizi haa waa ia tɛɛwɛ nfɛssi la n zum wia zɛɛ gɛɛ siwee la n na na gɛɛ digna la n na nuu wiarɛ. 5Binni tokkoanɛɛ la maa biini miŋ tɔ ii see hɛribɔduma biini la, ii laalaa ni ii gawa waa kɔzɛɛ. 6Ii faa waa paanuu nawɛɛ ra hee gɛɛ siŋ gɛɛ siŋ waa iri maa baŋ du bura di ra nyɔɔ, see maana bɛŋ. N faa ɛɛ gunnɛ, ií zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la.
7Yaa n faa wa hel ɛŋ, Hɛsbɔn Koori Sihɔn ni Basan Koori Ɔɔg faa liwɔɔrɛ bá lɔ yaa, ka yaa kpegli baa. 8Yaa faa foozi ba hɛri, di bɔnnuu tɛɛ Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ.
9Ií ra hiŋ nuukpaŋ naa widaulaa nɛnnɛ, guŋ gil ií nyɛɛli ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini. 10Ii banla maa n chigɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see zinaa naa, ii sitɔɔraa ani ii nɛzenaa, ii nabɔnzi, Izrɛl hina baala la maa n kawɛɛ, 11ii biizi ni haana ani hɔɔhra la n du ii chɔɔribɔra di ra teŋri daazi, di dɔɔ nii ra tɛɛ ia la, 12ii chi ɛnnɛ, ii ni Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛ nuukpaŋfalii. Nuukpaŋfalii la u ni ia n na ɛɛ zinaa, u hɛɛhzi di ra bagli guŋ la, 13awia, ii ɛɛ u nɛraa zinaa, u ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia ani gunla uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ tɛɛ ii mɛɛwaa Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb la. 14Ii bɛŋ be lɛi u ra ɛɛ nuukpaŋ naa ni u nuuŋɔɔlii naa, 15ka u ra ɛɛubuu ni ii banla n chigɛ u see zinaa naa ani ii naanna maa.
16Ii maa zum gunla yaa n faa duwɛɛ Ijip hɛrii ani gunla yaa n ga hɛrkpila maa biine, ka wa hel ɛnnɛ. 17Ii faa na ba vuga la n ɛɛ daazi, bia, saliŋhuŋŋa ani saliŋ la Kɔraawiizi n hahwɛɛ labuu, ba biine. 18Ií ɛɛ ania, baal gɛɛ haaŋ gɛɛ domee gɛɛ dee maa n du ii biini zinaa naa, bampirii gilɛɛ wa bir di ra lii Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ni, ú gaa kuari a hɛssi naa hina vuga. Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ daa lunni siri n kpolle werge.
19Di a hiŋ wa nuu gunla nuukpaŋ naa wiŋɔɔlaa n na bagli, ɔɔ kissi u hinnɛ, di ra fɛ lugɔ u daŋ na u hiŋ, haali unna hiŋ u himmaa kipar ŋmɛnɛɛ gba. Guŋ daŋ gil Kɔraawiizi chɔgi wichɔgɛɛra ni nɛnanaa maa. 20Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá gil tɛɛ a hiŋ. Ka u daŋ kpa u baaŋfuuih di kpu a hiŋ. Nuuseezi la maa n du hɔnnaa biini daŋ diu, guŋŋ Kɔraawiizi wa dim u sɔŋ durnya naa biini. 21Kɔraawiizi daŋ lizuu lii Izrɛl hina dizi maa biini, di gil hɛhchɔg chol u ni gunla nuukpaŋ naa nuuseezi la baŋ sɛbɛɛ du Gbɔg Hɔnnaa biini n na bagli.
22Ii biizi la n niŋ hiŋ ii ni, ni jiminizi la n niŋ ba ni hɔɔhra la n niŋ lii hɛhjaŋa la daŋ na biinichɔg wia la n niŋ huuzi ia, a hɛri biini ani wiila la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ ta ii ni.
23A hɛri maa daŋ hil di chɔɔ pɛɛ, jilbi ni yazii niŋ tɔ u maa. Ba wàá duu kummaa, kummaa ge wàá lii de, daazi ni kooree gba wàá wer lii de. Ii hɛri daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ bolzenaa Sɔdɔm, Gɔmɔra, Adma ani Zɛbɔyim. A ninɛɛ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh werge, u chɔgaa la. 24Hɛssi hina maa daŋ pɛɛzi, ‘Bɛɛ n gillɛ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ hɛri naa kennei? Bɛɛ n gillɛ u baaŋ fuuh kennei?’
25Kenne bá bagli a zɛɛ, ‘Nɛra naa vɛɛ ba ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋ labuu. Nuukpaŋ la ba ni Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la n ɛɛwɛ la, saŋa la uŋ lizi baa lii Ijip hɛri la. 26Ba faa gaa kuari vugaa, di ra tognaa. Vuga la baŋ faa waa zummɛ. Vuga la uŋ waa baa tɛɛwɛ. 27Awiarɛ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh a hɛri naa hina ni, u gil nuuseezi la maa n du hɔnnaa biini di baa la. 28Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh werge maa. U baaŋfuuih hiŋ biinii u lizi baa lii ba hɛri, di kpa baa ta hɛrduma biini, ba du de haali ni zinaa.’
29Wia aŋhina du denii, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la gil a suah, ka u Gbɔg la waa, u pilluubuu, yàá ni yaa naanna ra sɛɛ u wia, saŋaa saŋa maa.”

english_text:
The Lord Will Bring You Back
Moses said to Israel:
1 I have told you everything the Lord your God will do for you, and I've also told you the curses he will put on you if you reject him. He will scatter you in faraway countries, but when you realize that he is punishing you, 2return to him with all your heart and soul and start obeying the commands I have given to you today. 3-4Then he will stop punishing you and treat you with kindness. He may have scattered you to the farthest countries on earth, but he will bring you back 5to the land that had belonged to your ancestors and make you even more successful and powerful than they ever were.
6You and your descendants are stubborn, but the Lord will make you willing to obey him and love him with all your heart and soul, and you will enjoy a long life.
7Then the Lord your God will remove the curses from you and put them on those enemies who hate and attack you.
8You will again obey the laws and teachings of the Lord, 9and he will bless you with many children, large herds and flocks, and abundant crops. The Lord will be happy to do good things for you, just as he did for your ancestors. 10But you must decide once and for all to worship him with all your heart and soul and to obey everything in The Book of God's Law.
Choose Life, Not Death
Moses said to Israel:
11You know God's laws, and it isn't impossible to obey them. 12 His commands aren't in heaven, so you can't excuse yourselves by saying, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are in heaven, and no one can go up to get them, then bring them down and explain them to us.” 13And you can't say, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are across the sea, and someone must go across, then bring them back and explain them to us.” 14No, these commands are nearby and you know them by heart. All you have to do is obey!
15 Today I am giving you a choice. You can choose life and success or death and disaster. 16-18I am commanding you to be loyal to the Lord, to live the way he has told you, and to obey his laws and teachings. You are about to cross the Jordan River and take the land that he is giving you. If you obey him, you will live and become successful and powerful.
On the other hand, you might choose to disobey the Lord and reject him. So I'm warning you that if you bow down and worship other gods, you won't have long to live.
19Now I call the sky and the earth to be witnesses that I am offering you this choice. Will you choose for the Lord to make you prosperous and give you a long life? Or will he put you under a curse and kill you? Choose life! 20 Be completely faithful to the Lord your God, love him, and do whatever he tells you. The Lord is the only one who can give life, and he will let you live a long time in the land that he promised to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi be balaa nyɛɛlaa wia
1Moosis kaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Di kissaazi ni nuuseezi naa maa miŋ kpawɛɛ ra dau ii see zinaa naa maa wa du ii be, ií kpaa du ii biine, bɔr la maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ gil ii yaari hɛssi biine la. 2Di ii ni ii biizi wa bittɔ ba Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la be, di ra sɛɛ u nua ni ii biine, ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa gunla miŋ bagli ia zinaa naa, 3guŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ suŋ ii ni. U daŋ gil ii lii hɛssi la biine uŋ gillɛ ii yaari la, di bir ba Jɛrusalɛm, di wa gil ii kaa nyɛɛli. 4Haali di ii yaarɔɔrɛ la hɛssi magazi gba, ka Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kaa chaali ia di bir ba ii ni Jɛrusalɛm. 5U daŋ bir ba ii ni hɛri la n faa ɛɛ ii naabaala hor la, ii foozuu dɔɔ la. U daŋ gil ii nyɛɛli di wazi di kaali ii mɛɛwaa. 6Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ gil ii ni ii naanna chɛr ii manni, di gilɛɛ kaa dɔɔ dignikpega ka nɔŋŋuu ni ii biine, ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa, di wer du a hɛri. 7U daŋ bir nuuseezi la du ii dɔma la n hah ia, di faa ra fir ia la ni. 8Ii daŋ kaa ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra, di ra hiŋ u widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa. 9Denii Kɔraawiizi gil ii nyɛɛli, ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini. Ii biizi ni ii sela daŋ wazi, ii kooni kuna lɛɛ werge. U bɔra daŋ kaa sɔɔni, ú gil ii nyɛɛli gunla uŋ faa gillɛ ii mɛɛwaa nyɛɛli la. 10Ka a dɛkkɔɔ ii ra sɛɛ u nua, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni naa baŋ sɛbɛɛ du Gbɔg Hɔŋ naa biini. A dɛkkɔɔ ií bir ba u be ni ii biine ni ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa.
11Wia naa miŋ kpawɛɛ ra tɛɛ ia zinaa naa waa kpol gɛɛ di du bɔɔnɛɛ. 12Chiŋ lɛi u du, ii ra pɛɛzi, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ tinni di ga ba u ni hɛri, yá wer nuu wia la n du u biini, di ra sɛɛawɛi?’ 13Waa muuzeŋ baŋgia bɛl duwɛɛ ge, ii ra pɛɛzi, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ gi, di ga ba u ni wa tɛɛ yaa, yá nuu di ra sɛɛ u wiai?’ 14Akai, a wiŋɔɔlii dugli iabuu werge maa, di du ii nuuzi ni ii biine, guŋ gil ii ra sɛɛ u wia.
15Ií ra nuu! Winanaa ni wichɔgaa gɛɛ miibɔɔ ni siurɛ n kpa ra dau ii see zinaa la. Ií lizi bɛl. 16N na ŋɔ ii benii zinaa lugɔ ií nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi, di ra sɛɛ u widaulaa ani u Gbɔgni wia. Di ii ra ɛɛ guŋ, ii daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ di wazi. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kissi ia hɛri la iinna zuu, ií foozi di dɔɔ la biini.
17Ka di ii wa dɔɔ dignikpega di vɛɛ a nuui, ka bir gaa kuari vuga di ra tognaa, 18n na ŋɔ ii benii zinaa lugɔ ba daŋ chɔgi ia. Ii wàá birgi hɛri la biini iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu ii foozi di dɔɔ la.
19Zinaa, n na yir chiŋ ni hɛrii, á diŋ daansɛɛ lugɔ n kpa miibɔɔ ni siu, kissaa ani nuuseezii di ra dau ii see. Awia, ií lizi miibɔɔ, ii ni ii biizi wer dɔɔu, 20di wer nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra nuu u wiŋɔzi, di lawuu kpogli chigigi. Kɔraawiizii ii miibɔɔ. U daŋ gil ii di biŋkpila hɛri la uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ii mɛɛwaa Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb la biini.”

english_text:
Final Speeches and the Death of Moses
Joshua Is Appointed the Leader of Israel
1Moses again spoke to the whole nation of Israel:
2 I am 120 years old, and I am no longer able to be your leader. And besides that, the Lord your God has told me that he won't let me cross the Jordan River. 3-5 But he has promised that he and Joshua will lead you across the Jordan to attack the nations that live on the other side. The Lord will destroy those nations just as he destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings. Just remember—whenever you capture a place, kill everyone who lives there.
6Be brave and strong! Don't be afraid of the nations on the other side of the Jordan. The Lord your God will always be at your side, and he will never abandon you.
7Then Moses called Joshua up in front of the crowd and said:
Joshua, be brave and strong as you lead these people into their land. The Lord made a promise long ago to Israel's ancestors that this land would someday belong to Israel. That time has now come, and you must divide up the land among the people. 8 The Lord will lead you into the land. He will always be with you and help you, so don't ever be afraid of your enemies.
Read These Laws
9Moses wrote down all of these laws and teachings and gave them to the priests and the leaders of Israel. The priests were from the Levi tribe, and they carried the sacred chest that belonged to the Lord. 10-11 Moses told these priests and leaders:
Each year the Israelites must come together to celebrate the Festival of Shelters at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. You must read these laws and teachings to the people at the festival every seventh year, the year when loans do not need to be repaid. 12-13Everyone must come—men, women, children, and even the foreigners who live in your towns. And each new generation will listen and learn to worship the Lord their God with fear and trembling and to do exactly what is said in God's Law.
Israel Will Reject the Lord
14The Lord told Moses, “You will soon die, so bring Joshua to the sacred tent, and I will appoint him the leader of Israel.”
Moses and Joshua went to the sacred tent, 15and the Lord appeared in a thick cloud right over the entrance to the tent. 16The Lord said:
Moses, you will soon die. But Israel is going into a land where other gods are worshiped, and Israel will reject me and start worshiping these gods. The people will break the agreement I made with them, 17and I will be so furious that I will abandon them and ignore their prayers. I will send disasters and suffering that will nearly wipe them out. Finally, they will realize that the disasters happened because I abandoned them. 18They will pray to me, but I will ignore them because they were evil and started worshiping other gods.
19Moses and Joshua, I am going to give you the words to a new song. Write them down and teach the song to the Israelites. If they learn it, they will know what I want them to do, and so they will have no excuse for not obeying me. 20I am bringing them into the land that I promised their ancestors. It is a land rich with milk and honey, and the Israelites will have more than enough food to eat. But they will get fat and turn their backs on me and start worshiping other gods. The Israelites will reject me and break the agreement that I made with them.
21When I punish the Israelites and their descendants with suffering and disasters, I will remind them that they know the words to this song, so they have no excuse for not obeying me.
I will give them the land that I promised, but I know the way they are going to live later on.
22Moses at once wrote down the words to the song, and he taught it to the Israelites.
23 The Lord told Joshua, “Be brave and strong! I will help you lead the people of Israel into the land that I have promised them.”
24Moses wrote down all these laws and teachings in a book, 25then he went to the Levites who carried the sacred chest and said:
26This is The Book of God's Law. Keep it beside the sacred chest that holds the agreement the Lord your God made with Israel. This book is proof that you know what the Lord wants you to do. 27I know how stubborn and rebellious you and the rest of the Israelites are. You have rebelled against the Lord while I have been alive, and it will only get worse after I am gone. 28So call together the leaders and officials of the tribes of Israel. I will bring this book and read every word of it to you, and I will call the sky and the earth as witnesses that all of you know what you are supposed to do.
29I am going to die soon, and I know that in the future you will stop caring about what is right and what is wrong, and so you will disobey the Lord and stop living the way I told you to live. The Lord will be angry, and terrible things will happen to you.
The Song of Moses
30Moses called a meeting of all the people of Israel, so he could teach them the words to the song that the Lord had given him. And here are the words:
translation_text:
Josua n kpa Moosis gawa wia
1Denii Moosis lii di ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa, 2“N jaa di binni kalfa ni tokkoo filaŋkeŋ, màá ka wer tɔ ii see. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n benii, ‘Hàá gi Jɔɔdan muu.’ 3Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la himmaanii niŋ tɔ ii see di gi. U daŋ chɔgi hɛssi naa hina n du ii see naa maa, ií foozi ba hɛssi di dɔɔ. Josua ge daŋ tɔ ii see di gi, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la. 4Gunla Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛ Amɔri hina Koora Sihɔn ni Ɔɔg, di chɔgi ba ni ba hɛri la, gunnɛ ú ɛɛ ba ge. 5Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa baa du ii nonee biini. Ií ɛɛ baa gunla miŋ ŋɔ ii be naa. 6Ií chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bɔkpega. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɔm gɛɛ di waa dɔɔ bɔhuaih, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ni iabuu ra vol. Wàá ɛɛ ii wia vɛɛlai maa. Wàá gil ii ta maa.”
7Denii Moosis yir Josua di ŋɔ u be Izrɛl hina maa see, “Chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bɔkpega, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ni nɛra naabuu niŋ zuu hɛri la wia Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ tɛɛ ba naabaala lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ baa la. A dɛkkɔɔ i bɔnnuu tɛɛ baa, ú ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ. 8Kɔraawiizi himmaanii niŋ tɔ i see, di du i be. Wàá ɛɛ ii wia vɛɛlai maa. Wàá gil ii ta maa. Gilɛɛ waa ɔm, gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ bɔhuaih.”
Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg karmaa wia
9Awia, Moosis faa sɛbi Gbɔg naa, di kpau tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la n ɔɔ ra chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ni Izrɛl nabɔnzi maa. 10Denii Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Binni aniidaanɛɛ tuna maa, iiŋ ɔɔ gil kima ra tɛɛ dɔŋa, Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ dii saŋa la, 11Izrɛl hina maa n ɔɔ chaali Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see, bɔr la un niŋ lizi la, ii daŋ ɔɔ karmi Gbɔg naa bá nuu. 12Gil a nɛra maa ɔɔ chaali, baala, haana, biizi ani hɔɔhra la maa n du ii bola la. Bá maa wer nuu, di helli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɔmaa, di ra hiŋ widaulaa la maa n du a Gbɔg naa biini nɛnnɛ. 13Ba biizi la n waa Gbɔg naa zummɛ la dɛkkɔɔ bá nuu la, di helli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɔmaa, saŋa la maa iin niŋ du a hɛri naa iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu, ií foozi di dɔɔ naa biini.”
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Izrɛl hina dignikpega wia
14Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Filaŋkeŋ i siu hɔpizii duglɔɔrɛ. Yir Josua, í nuu chi n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini, ń tɛu huma.” Awia, Moosis ni Josua faa la de.
15Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ba de lugɔ baama n du miriti di la chiŋ, di wa chi a Tanti Dia dominua. 16Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “I daŋ la ga chɔɔ i mɛɛwaa be, ka nɛra naa daŋ bir gaa jaami vuga la baŋ waa zummɛ, hɛri la banna nyiŋŋi bá zuu naa biini. Ba daŋ vɛɛŋ, di chɔgi nuukpaŋ la n ni baa n ɛɛwɛ la. 17A hɔl hiŋ, n baaŋ daŋ fuuh ba ni ń vɛɛ baa, di bir har kpu baa, ka ba kpu baa. Tɔɔrɔɔzenaa kpila ni anuula daŋ huuzi baa, ba pɛɛzi a hɔl hiŋ, ‘Kɔraawiizi n waa hoo yaa be wia lɛi, tɔɔrɔɔzenaa naa chol yaa nii?’ 18Wibii maa, n daŋ bir har kpu baa a hɔl hiŋ, dikuu ba biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la banna ɛɛ, di ra kuari vuga la wia.”
19Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis ni Josua be, “Ií sɛbi yir naa tɛɛ iihinaa, Moosis bagli Izrɛl hina ú yiraa, bá ra yiruu, ú di daansɛɛ tɛŋ ba wia. 20Di n wa kpogli baa zuu hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la biini, miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ba naabaala la, di ba wa nawɔɔ ra di, di nyɛɛli, ba daŋ bir di ra kuari vuga, di ra tognaa. Ba daŋ vɛɛŋ, di chɔgi n ni baa nuukpaŋ la. 21Di hɛhchɔgni ni anuula kpila wa chol ba ni, yir naa daŋ di ba daansɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba naanna wàá suuuh. N zum wia la ban niŋ ɛɛu mɔɔ, ka n haa kpogli baa zuu hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ baa la biini.” 22Awia, Moosis sɛbi a yir dau a hɔl hiŋ, di bagli Izrɛl hina u yiraa.
23Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ Nun biibaal Josua, “Chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bɔkpega, di gilɛɛ ra ɔm, dikuubɛɛwiai, i daŋ kpogli Izrɛl hina di zuu hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ baa la. N daŋ du i be.”
24Moosis n wa sɛbi Gbɔg naa wiŋɔɔlaa maa di wa tuŋ, 25kenne u faa ŋɔ Levi dee la n chigɛ Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la be, 26“Ií kpa Gbɔg Hɔnnaa dau Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la kɛrii. U daŋ chɔɔ de di ra di ii daansɛɛ. 27N zum gunla iiŋ kpoŋŋe di dɔɔ dignikpegaa. Di ii kpoŋŋo Kɔraawiizi be n de dui saŋa, ii kpoŋaa daŋ nyaŋŋi, di n siuwɔ. 28Ií yir ii dizi la maa nabɔnzi ni ba nabɔnzenaa, ń ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ baa, ka yir chiŋ ni hɛri á diŋ daansɛɛ. 29N zummɔ lugɔ di n wa siuwɔ, ii daŋ haŋ chɔguu kɔrai, di bir har kpu wia naa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia naa. A wàá birgi ka hɛhchɔg chol ii ni, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh ii ni, dikuu vuga la iiŋ kuarɛɛ wia.”
Moosis yir wia
30Denii Moosis faa kurgi a yir wiŋɔɔlaa maa, di lii u lugli di ga hel u tuna, Izrɛl hina la maa n chaalɛɛ la see.

english_text:
1Earth and Sky,
listen to what I say!
2Israel, I will teach you.
My words will be like gentle rain
on tender young plants,
or like dew on the grass.
3Join with me in praising
the wonderful name
of the Lord our God.
4The Lord is a mighty rock,
and he never does wrong.
God can always be trusted
to bring justice.
5But you lie and cheat
and are unfaithful to him.
You have disgraced yourselves
and are no longer worthy
to be his children.
6Israel, the Lord is your Father,
the one who created you,
but you repaid him
by being foolish.
7Think about past generations.
Ask your parents
or any of your elders.
They will tell you
8 that God Most High
gave land to every nation.
He assigned a guardian angel
to each of them,
9but the Lord himself
takes care of Israel.
10Israel, the Lord discovered you
in a barren desert
filled with howling winds.
God became your fortress,
protecting you as though
you were his own eyes.
11The Lord was like an eagle
teaching its young to fly,
always ready to swoop down
and catch them on its back.
12Israel, the Lord led you,
and without the aid
of a foreign god,
13he helped you
capture the land.
Your fields were rich
with grain.
Olive trees grew
in your stony soil,
and honey was found
among the rocks.
14Your flocks and herds
produced milk and yogurt,
and you got choice meat
from your sheep and goats
that grazed in Bashan.
Your wheat was the finest,
and you drank the best wine.
15Israel, you grew fat and rebelled
against God, your Creator
you rejected the Mighty Rock,
your only place of safety.
16You made God jealous and angry
by worshiping disgusting idols
and foreign gods.
17 You offered sacrifices
to demons, those useless gods
that never helped you,
new gods that your ancestors
never worshiped.
18You turned away
from God, your Creator;
you forgot the Mighty Rock,
the source of your life.
19You were the Lord's children,
but you made him angry.
Then he rejected you 20and said,
“You are unfaithful
and can't be trusted.
So I won't answer your prayers;
I'll just watch and see
what happens to you.
21 You worshiped worthless idols,
and made me jealous
and angry!
Now I will send a cruel
and worthless nation
to make you jealous and angry.
22“My people, I will breathe out fire
that sends you down
to the world of the dead.
It will scorch your farmlands
and burn deep down
under the mountains.
23I'll send disaster after disaster
to strike you like arrows.
24You'll be struck by starvation
and deadly diseases,
by the fangs of wild animals
and poisonous snakes.
25Young and old alike
will be killed in the streets
and terrified at home.
26“I wanted to scatter you,
so no one would remember
that you had ever lived.
27But I dreaded the sound
of your enemies saying,
‘We defeated Israel with no help
from the Lord.’ ”
28People of Israel,
that's what the Lord
has said to you.
But you don't have good sense,
and you never listen
to advice.
29If you did, you could see
where you are headed.
30How could one enemy soldier
chase a thousand
of Israel's troops?
Or how could two of theirs
pursue ten thousand of ours?
It can only happen if the Lord
stops protecting Israel
and lets the enemy win.
31Even our enemies know
that only our God
is a Mighty Rock.
32Our enemies are grapevines
rooted in the fields
of Sodom and Gomorrah.
The grapes they produce
are full of bitter poison;
33their wine is more deadly
than cobra venom.
34But the Lord has written
a list of their sins
and locked it in his vault.
35 Soon our enemies will get
what they deserve—
suddenly they will slip,
and total disaster
will quickly follow.
36 When only a few
of the Lord's people remain,
when their strength is gone,
and some of them are slaves,
the Lord will feel sorry for them
and give them justice.
37But first the Lord will say,
“You ran for safety to other gods—
couldn't they help you?
38You offered them wine
and your best sacrifices.
Can't those gods help you now
or give you protection?
39Don't you understand?
I am the only God;
there are no others.
I am the one who takes life
and gives it again.
I punished you with suffering.
But now I will heal you,
and nothing can stop me!
40“I make this solemn promise:
Just as I live forever,
41I will take revenge
on my hateful enemies.
I will sharpen my sword
and let it flash
like lightning.
42My arrows will get drunk
on enemy blood;
my sword will taste the flesh
and the blood of the enemy.
It will kill prisoners,
and cut off the heads
of their leaders.”
43 Tell the heavens to celebrate
and all gods to bow down
to the Lord,
because he will take revenge
on those hateful enemies
who killed his people.
He will forgive the sins of Israel
and purify their land.
44-45Moses spoke the words of the song so that all the Israelites could hear, and Joshua helped him. When Moses had finished, 46he said, “Always remember this song I have taught you today. And let it be a warning that you must teach your children to obey everything written in The Book of God's Law. 47The Law isn't empty words. It can give you a long life in the land that you are going to take.”
Moses Will See the Land
48 Later that day the Lord said to Moses:
49Go up into the Abarim Mountain range here in Moab across the Jordan River valley from Jericho. And when you reach the top of Mount Nebo, you will be able to see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to Israel. 50Then you will die and be buried on the mountaintop, just as your brother Aaron died and was buried on Mount Hor. 51Both of you were unfaithful to me at Meribah Spring near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. I am God, but there in front of the Israelites, you did not treat me with the honor and respect I deserve. 52So I will give the land to the people of Israel, but you will only get to see it from a distance.
translation_text:
1Moosis yir labuu keŋ,
“Hɛri ni chiŋ, ií ra nuu n wiŋɔɔlaa,
ií ra nuu wii la
min niŋ ŋɔ nɛnnɛ.
2N baglaa daŋ ɛɛu lugɔ dooŋ n na ba,
di chol hɛri lugɔ ŋmɛnii.
N wiŋɔzi daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ dooŋ n mussɛɛ
kunjigzi n haa ra hel ni,
di ɛɛ lugɔ dooŋ
n mussɛɛ kooree ni.
3N daŋ dargi Kɔraawiizi,
ú nɛra bagli u zenni
ni u girme wia.
4Kɔraawiizii ii guurikpeg lugɔ Bizeŋ,
waa lewaa dɔɔwɛ,
di ra di wibii.
Ú wiɛɛlaa maa biini.
Kɔraawiizi wia dɔɔ wibiire,
waa dar.
U wiɛɛlaa maa deŋloore
gunla n dɛkkɛ.
5Ka ii wia waa wibii dɔɔwɛ,
ii waa dɛg ii ɛɛ u nɛra.
Ii ɛɛ nɛra la
n na ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, di dɔɔ daraa.
6Kenne dɛkkɛ iin ninna ɛɛ Kɔraawiizia?
Gɛnaa ni nfɛrnyaara!
Waabuu ii Mɛɛ ni ii Taari,
waabuu gillɛ ii ɛɛ hɛri bɛl hina.
7Ií ra liizi faala wia,
ii pɛɛzi ii mɛɛwaa ni ii maawaa,
bá bagli ia wia la n ɛɛwɛ a saŋa.
Ií pɛɛzi nabɔnzi,
bá bagli ia faala wia.
8Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu
tɛɛ hɛssi hina maa ba hɛssi.
Waabuu ɔɔ dau nɛra maa duuribɔra.
Di ɔɔ gil mɛlika ra binni
hɛri maa hina ni.
9Ka Jekɔb naanna waa,
u lizi baabuu tɛɛ u hiŋ.
10U faa na baabuu banna juuri
hɛribɔduma biini,
bɔr la n waa kummaa dɔɔwɛ,
peu chaazi de maa nyaamm la.
U faa guu baabuu, di binni ba ni
gunla un niŋ guu u hiŋ la.
11Di ɛɛ lugɔ chig la
n na bagli u biizi zaaih,
di ɔɔ yaa u keeri
di ra chamaa la.
Kɔraawiizi faa waa sɛɛwɛ
Izrɛl hina chol.
12Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ faa tɔ u nɛra see,
di hɛrduma bɛl maa
vug faa wɔɔ hiinee.
13Giŋgimee nyuuni maa
faa ɛɛ ba kundɔɔlaarɛ,
ba faa ra di
ba kooni kuna.
Ba faa na huuhnuurɛ
di ra di bia la biine,
ba ɔlivizi daazi faa lɛɛ
a bia hɛri biini.
14Ba nauna ni buuna faa dɔɔ ilanii werge,
ba peeza ni buuna
ani naunaa
faa wessoo werge maa.
Ba mia ni siŋ
faa waa dɔŋ dɔɔwɛ.
15Kɔraawiizi nɛra faa ra nyɛɛli werge,
ka dɔɔ dignikpega,
ba faa pɔllɔɔ di piŋ werge.
Ba faa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n ta baa labuu,
di vɛɛ ba Lɛɛri la
n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la.
16Ba vuga kuaraa la faa gillɔɔ
Kɔraawiizi bɔra
faa ra wii werge maa.
Ba wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛwɛ la
faa gillɔɔ u baaŋ fuuh.
17Ba faa ra lizi mbusuzi
di ra tɛɛ
tinnanchɔgaa la
n waa Kɔraawiizi ɛɛwɛ.
Vuga la baŋ faa waa zummɛ,
vuga la Izrɛl hina n haa
waa a nuuzi hiŋŋɛ.
18Ba faa suuh Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la
n ɛɛ ba Lɛɛri,
di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la,
unla n tɛɛ baa miibɔɔ la wiarɛ.
19Kɔraawiizi n wa na guŋ,
u baaŋ fuuh,
u vɛɛ u biibaala
ni u biihaana ta.
20Di faa ŋɔ, ‘Màá ka hiini baa.
Denii ń na wii la
n niŋ huuzi dignikpega
ni wibii nyaara naa.
21Ba kpa vugaa di gil n baaŋ fuuh.
N bɔra faa ra wii,
dikuu ba vuga la
n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ wia.
Awia, n daŋ gil ba bɔra ra wii,
dikuu hɛri la hina n ɛɛ
nɛjagazi wia,
di gil ba na baaŋ,
dikuu nɛra la n waa
wia zummɛ wia.
22N baaŋfuuih daŋ izi lugɔ ninlau,
di fuuh hɛri kummaa.
U daŋ zuu hɛri, di ga hel lalaa bol,
di ga fuuh
bizenaa zɛɛzi maa.
23N daŋ gil hɛhchɔgni la
n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ
ra chol ba ni,
alugɔ minna ta baa
n hobee maa.
24Lɔzi ni bɔwemaa niŋ kpuuzi baa,
wiilchɔgaarɛ niŋ
kpuuzi baa.
N daŋ gil sechɔgaa lauri baa
di gil hɛrikuna la
siri n kpolle werge
dunzi baa.
25Laal daŋ gil ba ŋmɛnizenaa suugi ni lalaa,
ɔnsii werge chol ba ni,
ba diini biine.
Biipɔllaa ni suŋgure daŋ siuzi,
biifulli gɛɛ nɛzɛŋzi gba
wàá na bahinaa.
26N daŋ vii kpuuzi baa nyaamm,
nɛr maa wàá ka
liizi ba wia,
27ka màá sɛɛ gil ba dɔma ra ta bara
lugɔ baabuu kpegli n nɛra,
ka n himmaanii
kpuuzi baa la.’
28Izrɛl hina ɛɛ nɛra la
n waa nfɛrɛ dɔɔwɛɛ.
Ba waa nunzuma
maa dɔɔwɛ.
29Ba waa wette bá na wii la
n gillɛ ba kpegli baa,
gɛɛ di zum wii la
n ɛɛ baa la zɛɛ.
30Bɛɛ n gillɛ nɛkpaŋ wer kpegli
nɛra kagboŋei,
nɛra banɛɛ kpegli
nɛra kagboŋa fiei?
Kɔraawiizi la banna hum
labuu vɛɛ baa ta.
Unla n ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
labuu kpa baa
tɛɛ ba dɔma.
31Ba dɔma zummɔ lugɔ
ba himmaa vuga
la waa kpeg.
A waa fɔŋŋazeŋ dɔɔwɛ
lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la
Izrɛl hina n na hum la.
32Ba dɔma la n dɔɔ biinikpola
lugɔ Sɔdɔm ni
Gɔmɔra hina la,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ grepu daazi la
n na nɔŋ nɔŋkpola,
a ɛɛ lugɔ siri la,
33lugɔ siŋ la baŋ kpa
hɛrikuŋ siri di daali.
34Kɔraawiizi ra liizi
ba dɔma wiɛɛlaa labuu.
U ra kpaŋ saŋa la n dɛkkɛ
ú tɛr ba dignaa.
35Kɔraawiizii niŋ turgi baa a kim.
Saŋa ra bau ban niŋ chol,
ba chɔgaa hɔpizi duglɔɔrɛ.
36Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ u nɛra,
di u wa nawɔɔ
ba fɔŋŋa n tunnɛ.
U daŋ suŋ banla n na humuu la ni,
di u wa nawɔɔ lugɔ
ba waa hiini dɔɔwɛ.
37Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi u nɛra,
‘Lee vuga la
n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge,
ii yardaa la duɛi?
38Ii mbusuzi lizaa kuna nuurii,
ii faa kpa di ra tɛɛa,
di ra tɛɛa siŋ.
Ií gil a ba wa hiini ia filaŋkeŋ,
ií gil a chɔ wa lɛɛ ia!
39N bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi,
vug maa waa
kummaa ɛɛwɛ.
Minuu ɔɔ kpu, di kaa tɛɛ miibɔɔ,
di du pira, di kaa chaa.
Nɛr maa wàá wer tɔ
n wiɛɛlaa ŋmɛnɛɛ.
40Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la,
lɔ n bampiriire
di hɛɛhzi lugɔ
41di n wa sazi n tokobi la n na nyɛgzi,
di kpau ń di seriya,
n daŋ turgi n dɔma
ba wichɔgaa kim,
di tɛr banla
n hahŋ la digna.
42Ba chal daŋ lii n hobee ni,
di ra toŋzi.
N daŋ kpuuzi banla maa
n na diŋ mmɔri la
ni n tokobi.
Màá gil nɛr la maa n niŋ yooŋ.
Haali banla n na pira
ni banla baŋ laurɛɛ la
maanii niŋ siuzi.’
43Hɛssi hina,
a dɛkkɔɔ ii ra chɔli
Kɔraawiizi nɛra.
U ɔɔ tɛr nɛra la maa
n na kpuuzi
baa la dignaa.
U ra turgi u dɔmaa
ba wichɔgaa kim,
ka gil u nɛra waa
wichɔgaa di ra
tɛɛ baa.”
44Moosis ni Nun biibaal Josuarɛ kur yir naa wiŋɔbee, Izrɛl hina wer nuu. 45Moosis n wa kur wia naa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina tuŋ, 46u ŋɔ, “Ií ra du tau ka ra hiŋ widaulaa naa maa miŋ tɛɛ ia zinaa naa. Ií dammaa ra tɛɛ ii biizi, bá ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua ni wibii. 47Widaulaa naa waa wipɛɛri ɛɛwɛ. A ɛɛ ii miibɔɔrɛ. Ií ra hiŋaa, di wer du hɛri la iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu ii so la, di birgi.”
Moosis n niŋ siu Bizeŋ Nɛbɔ nyuu wia
48A hɔl hiŋ maanii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, 49“La ga tinni Abarim bizenaa la n du Moab hina hɛri, a ni bolzeŋ Jɛriko chaŋ dɔŋa la, di ga tinni Bizeŋ Nɛbɔ, di binni Keenan hina hɛri la miŋ ŋɔ ń kpa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la. 50I daŋ siu a bizeŋ nyuu, di ga chɔɔ i naabaala be, gunla i kpɛɛma Aarɔn n siu Bizeŋ Hɔɔ nyuu la, 51dikuubɛɛwiai, ii maa faa nyaa wibiire n be, Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ, saŋa la iiŋ faa du Mɛriba niiri bɔr la n dugli bol la banna yir Kadɛs, u du Zin Hɛribɔduma la. Ii faa gbɛllimbuu a nɛra sibɔɔ. 52Awia, i daŋ chi bɔɔnɛɛ ka binni hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la, ka hàá zuu u biini.”

english_text:
Moses Blesses the Tribes of Israel
1Moses was a prophet, and before he died, he blessed the tribes of Israel by saying:
2The Lord came from Mount Sinai.
From Edom, he gave light
to his people,
and his glory was shining
from Mount Paran.
Thousands of his warriors
were with him, and fire
was at his right hand.
3 The Lord loves the tribes
of Israel,
and he protects his people.
They listen to his words
and worship at his feet.
* 4I called a meeting
of the tribes of Israel
and gave you God's Law.
5Then you and your leaders
made the Lord your king.
6Tribe of Reuben, you will live,
even though your tribe
will always be small.
7The Lord will listen to you,
tribe of Judah, as you beg
to come safely home.
You fought your enemies alone;
now the Lord will help you.
8 At Massah and Meribah Spring,
the Lord tested you,
tribe of Levi.
You were faithful,
and so the priesthood belongs
to the Levi tribe.
9Protecting Israel's agreement
with the Lord
was more important to you
than the life of your father
or mother,
or brothers or sisters,
or your own children.
10You teach God's laws to Israel,
and at the place of worship
you offer sacrifices
and burn incense.
11I pray that the Lord will bless
everything you do,
and make you strong enough
to crush your enemies.
12The Lord Most High loves you,
tribe of Benjamin.
He will live among your hills
and protect you.
13Descendants of Joseph,
the Lord will bless you
with precious water
from deep wells
and with dew from the sky.
14Month by month, your fruit
will ripen in the sunshine.
15You will have a rich harvest
from the slopes
of the ancient hills.
16The Lord who appeared
in the burning bush
wants to give you the best
the land can produce,
and it will be a princely crown
on Joseph's head.
17The armies of Ephraim
and Manasseh
are majestic and fierce
like a bull or a wild ox.
They will run their spears
through faraway nations.
18Be happy, Zebulun,
as your boats set sail;
be happy, Issachar,
in your tents.
19The sea will make you wealthy,
and from the sandy beach
you will get treasure.
So invite the other tribes
to celebrate with you
and offer sacrifices to God.
20Tribe of Gad,
the Lord will bless you
with more land.
So shout his praises!
Your tribe is like a lion
ripping up its victim.
21Your leaders met together
and chose the best land
for your tribe,
but you obeyed the Lord
and helped the other tribes.
22Tribe of Dan,
you are like a lion cub,
startled by a snake.
23The Lord is pleased with you,
people of Naphtali.
He will bless you
and give you the land
to the west and the south.
24The Lord's greatest blessing
is for you, tribe of Asher.
You will be the favorite
of all the other tribes.
You will be rich with olive oil
25and have strong town gates
with bronze and iron bolts.
Your people will be powerful
for as long as they live.
26Israel, no other god
is like ours—
the clouds are his chariot
as he rides across the skies
to come and help us.
27The eternal God
is our hiding place;
he carries us in his arms.
When God tells you
to destroy your enemies,
he will make them run.
28Israel, you will live in safety;
your enemies will be gone.
The dew will fall from the sky,
and you will have plenty
of grain and wine.
29The Lord has rescued you
and given you more blessings
than any other nation.
He protects you like a shield
and is your majestic sword.
Your enemies will bow in fear,
and you will trample
on their backs.
translation_text:
Moosis n dibee tɛɛ Izrɛl dizi wia
1Kissaazi naabuu Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis faa dibi tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, ka siu. 2Kenne u ŋɔ,
“Kɔraawiizi faa lii Bizeŋ Sinaairɛ di ba,
di ɛɛ lugɔ wiizi n liwɛɛ
di guali Ɛdɔm hina ni,
di ra chaani u nɛra ni,
di lii Bizeŋ Paran nyuu.
U ni mɛlikazi kagboŋa fii ballɛ,
di lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag,
di lii u bizeŋ bɔwillaa.
3Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋi u nɛraa,
di ra guu banla
n ɛɛ u hora la.
Awia, yaa ɔɔ togni u seere,
di ra sɛɛ u widaulaa.
4Yaa ra sɛɛ Gbɔg la
Moosis n tɛɛ yaa la wiarɛ,
u ɛɛ yaa hɛri kunzenne yaa be.
5Kɔraawiizi birgi Izrɛl hina koorii,
saŋa la ba dizi
ni ba sitɔɔra n chaalɛɛ la.”
6Kenne Moosis ŋɔ Rubin dee wia,
“Haali Rubin nɛra n waa kpil la gba,
ka ba wàá dim.”
7Kenne u ŋɔ Juda dee wia,
“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
á nuu ba wile di ra lɛɛ baa.
Gil ba ni dizi la n kawɛɛ la,
kaa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ.
Yoo ra tɛɛ baa, di ra hiini baa,
bá ra kpegli ba dɔma.”
8Kenne u ŋɔ Levi dee wia,
“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
di ba wa ta
Urim ni Tumim,
gil i kipar chaani
i huŋhunna Levi dee
la wia n dɔɔ wibii la be.
I faa ɛɛ baabuu di na Massa,
di gil ba wia dɔɔ wibii
Mɛriba niiri la bɔr.
9Ba faa ra tɔgzii ani wibii kaali
ba mɛɛwaa, maawaa,
lulla ani biizi.
Ba faa ra hiŋ i widaulaarɛ, di faa dɔɔ wibii
i nuukpaŋ la wia biini.
10Ba daŋ bagli i nɛra bá ra hiŋ i Gbɔg la.
Ba danna lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa,
i mbusu lizibɔr la ni.
11N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
hiini ba dizi bá hel,
di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa.
Gil ba wiɛɛlaa maa parii.
Kpu ba dɔma maa,
di dim baa.”
12Kenne u ŋɔ Bɛnjamin dee wia,
“Dee naabuu Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋi,
di ra guu baa la.
U ra guu baabuu hɔpizi biimaa,
di du ba biini.”
13Kenne u ŋɔ Joosɛf dee wia,
“Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ba hɛri,
di tɛɛ baa dooŋ,
niiri ra lii hɛri.
14Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ba hɛri,
ba daazi nɔna ra aah,
di du wer nɛnnɛ,
bina maa.
15Bá faala maa giŋgimee la maa
tɔ ni daazi nɔna la
n summɛ werge.
16Bá hɛri su ni kunla maa n wesse,
di lii Kɔraawiizi
kissaa la biini.
Waabuu ŋɔ wia lii kasagee la
n na lau niŋ la biini la.
Kɔ́raawiizi gil kissaazi naa ba Joosɛf dee be,
dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu sitɔɔri
u lulla biini.
17Joosɛf dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa lugɔ nabal,
u nyigzi ɛɛ lugɔ
pir nabal nyigzi.
Ɛfram ni Manasɛ
laallɔɔra kagboŋa
helloo kpabaa,
di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa lugɔ nabala.
Gunla pir nau n ɔɔ lau nɛr la,
gunnɛ bá ɛɛ ba dɔma,
di taari baa
kaali hɛri tunazi.”
18Kenne u ŋɔ Zɛbulɔn ni Isaka dizi wia,
“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
gil Zɛbulɔn kɔɔzaa
muuzeŋ biini la wazi,
Isaka daama ge
wazi bol.
19Ba ɔɔ yir hɔɔhraa ba ba bizeŋ la nyuu,
di waa ligzi mbusuzi la
n dɛkkɛ de.
Ba ɔɔ na ba daamaa lii muuzeŋ biini
ani hɛɛhriichaa la n chɔɔ
u nua la biini.”
20Kenne u ŋɔ Gad dee wia,
“Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la
n gillɛ ba hɛri du kaŋ.
Gad chɔɔwɔɔ guu lugɔ bunyiŋ,
ú dum nonii teŋ gɛɛ
ú fugzi nyuhɔŋ.
21A hɛri bɔnanii labuu ba faa lɛɛ dɔɔ.
Nabɔma diiribɔttɛ
ba tɛɛ baa.
Ba faa ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi
widaulaa ni u gbɔgnii,
saŋa la Izrɛl sitɔɔra
n faa chaalɛɛ la.”
22Kenne u ŋɔ Dan dee wia,
“Dan ɛɛ bunyiŋbiire,
di zaah lii Basan barii.”
23Kenne u ŋɔ Naftali dee wia,
“Naftali wia par Kɔraawiizii,
u kissuu werge.
Ba hɛri chɔɔwɔɔ lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag,
di ga chug
Galilii muuzeŋ.”
24Kenne u ŋɔ Asɛ dee wia,
“Asɛ dee na kissaare kaali dizi maa.
Kɔ́raawiizi gil
u lulla maa nɔŋŋuu.
Ú hɛri dɔɔ
ɔlivi daazi nɛnnɛ.
25Ú bola dominuuzi
dɔɔ lugbia gbessi
di ra guuu.
Ú fɔŋŋa ni
u hɔpizaa mɛgzi.”
26U kaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be,
“Izrɛl hina, vug maa waa lugɔ
Kɔraawiizi la
iinna hum la.
Unla n ɔɔ ga chiŋ di waa kaali,
di du baama biini
ni zenni ni girme,
di ra ba ú wa hiini ia la.
27Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa
labuu ɛɛ ii guuri.
U nonee la n du de
saŋa maa labuu
kpogli ia.
Waabuu ɔɔ tɔ ii see
di ra duŋŋi ii dɔma,
di ŋɔ ií chɔgi ba maa
nyaamm la.
28Awia, Jekɔb naanna duwɔɔrɛ
ni bampirsɔna,
di so bɔɔiih,
hɛri la n dɔɔ mia ni siŋ werge la,
bɔr la ŋmɛnii
n ɔɔ lii chiŋ chol,
di gil hɛri sɔɔni la biini.
29Izrɛl hina, bɔsɔna hinaa ia!
Nɛr maa waa hoo
di ɛɛ lugɔ ia.
Hɛri la hina
Kɔraawiizi n lɛɛwɛ.
Kɔraawiizi himmaanii
ii laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ
ni ii tokobi.
U daŋ guu ia,
di kpegli ii dɔma tɛɛ ia.
Ii dɔma daŋ ba
di waa suŋŋi ia,
ií suŋ ba ni,
ka ii daŋ fɛrgi baa dau.”

english_text:
The Death of Moses
1Sometime later, Moses left the lowlands of Moab. He went up Mount Pisgah to the peak of Mount Nebo, which is across the Jordan River from Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land as far north as Gilead and the town of Dan. 2He let Moses see the territories that would soon belong to the tribes of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, as far west as the Mediterranean Sea. 3The Lord also showed him the land in the south, from the valley near the town of Jericho, known as The City of Palm Trees, down to the town of Zoar.
4 The Lord said, “Moses, this is the land I was talking about when I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give land to their descendants. I have let you see it, but you will not cross the Jordan and go in.”
5And so, Moses the Lord's servant died there in Moab, just as the Lord had said. 6The Lord buried him in a valley near the town of Beth-Peor, but even today no one knows exactly where. 7Moses was 120 years old when he died, yet his eyesight was still good, and his body was strong.
8The people of Israel stayed in the lowlands of Moab, where they mourned and grieved 30 days for Moses, as was their custom.
Joshua Becomes the Leader of Israel
9Before Moses died, he had placed his hands on Joshua, and the Lord had given Joshua wisdom. The Israelites paid attention to what Joshua said and obeyed the commands that the Lord had given Moses.
Moses Was a Great Prophet
10 There has never again been a prophet in Israel like Moses. The Lord spoke face to face with him 11and sent him to perform powerful miracles in the presence of the king of Egypt and his entire nation. 12No one else has ever had the power to do such great things as Moses did for everyone to see.
translation_text:
Moosis siu wia
1Denii Moosis lii Moab lɛl di ga tinni Bizeŋ Nɛbɔ, di ga hel Bizeŋ Pisga nyuu, Jɛriko wiifurii. Denii Kɔraawiizi bagluu a hɛri maa, di lii Giliad di ga hel Dan, 2Naftali maa, Ɛfram ni Manasɛ hɛssi maa, Juda hɛri maa guŋŋ di ga wiicholii di ga hel Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn, 3di kpa Nɛgɛv ni a paga maa, di lii Jɛriko Waluu, Abɛ Daazi Bolzeŋ di ga chug Zoa. 4Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Hɛri naabuu n hɛɛhzi ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ kpa tɛɛ Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb la, miŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ n daŋ kpau tɛɛ ba naanna la. N gillɔɔ i nau ni siwii, ka hàá gi di zuu u biini.”
5Denii Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis siu Moab hɛri, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la. 6Kɔraawiizi faa huguubuu Moab hɛri, waluu la n chaŋ Bɛf Piɔ la biini. Haali ni zinaa, nɛr maa waa u ŋmam bɔr zummɛ. 7Binni kalfa ni tokkoo Moosis faa di ka siu, ka u siwee faa waa gɛrgɛɛ gɛɛ u fɔŋŋa tuŋ. 8Izrɛl hina faa wii Moosis lee Moab hɛri lɛl la biini, hɔpizaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ.
9Nun biibaal Josua faa dɔɔ nunzuma werge, dikuu Moosis n faa kpa u nonee sag u ni, di suŋŋi wiizi tɛu la wia. Awia, Izrɛl hina faa nuu ra tɛu, di ra hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga Moosis be di ŋɔ tɛɛ baa la.
10Di haŋ lii a saŋa, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ maa waa kaa lii Izrɛl hɛri lugɔ Moosis. U ni Kɔraawiizi faa ra ŋɔ wiarɛ dɔŋa be, a ra chaani nɛnnɛ. 11U faa ɛɛ wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wia la Kɔraawiizi n humuu ŋɔ ú ga ɛɛ Ijip hɛri, di du Ijip koori ni u nabɔnzenaa ani a hɛri maa ni labuu Izrɛl hina sibɔɔ. 12Nɛr maa haa waa fɔŋŋazeŋ baglɛɛ gɛɛ di ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia la n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, Moosis n faa ɛɛwɛ Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ la.

english_text:
Joshua Becomes the Leader of Israel
1Moses, the Lord's servant, was dead. So the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been the assistant of Moses. The Lord said:
2My servant Moses is dead. Now you must lead Israel across the Jordan River into the land I'm giving to all of you. 3 Wherever you go, I'll give you that land, as I promised Moses. 4It will reach from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains in the north, and to the northeast as far as the great Euphrates River. It will include the land of the Hittites, and the land from here at the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea on the west. 5 Joshua, I will always be with you and help you as I helped Moses, and no one will ever be able to defeat you.
6-8 Long ago I promised the ancestors of Israel that I would give this land to their descendants. So be strong and brave! Be careful to do everything my servant Moses taught you. Never stop reading The Book of the Law he gave you. Day and night you must think about what it says. If you obey it completely, you and Israel will be able to take this land.
9I've commanded you to be strong and brave. Don't ever be afraid or discouraged! I am the Lord your God, and I will be there to help you wherever you go.
The Eastern Tribes Promise To Help
10Joshua ordered the tribal leaders 11to go through the camp and tell everyone:
In a few days we will cross the Jordan River to take the land that the Lord our God is giving us. So prepare as much food as you'll need for the march into the land.
12 Joshua told the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
13-14The Lord's servant Moses said that the Lord our God has given you land here on the east side of the Jordan River, where you could live in peace. Your wives and children and your animals can stay here in the land Moses gave you. But all of you that can serve in our army must pick up your weapons and lead the men of the other tribes across the Jordan River. They are your relatives, so you must help them 15conquer the land that the Lord is giving them. The Lord will give peace to them as he has given peace to you, and then you can come back and settle here in the land that Moses promised you.
16The men answered:
We'll cross the Jordan River and help our relatives. We'll fight anywhere you send us. 17-18If the Lord our God will help you as he helped Moses, and if you are strong and brave, we will obey you as we obeyed Moses. We'll even put to death anyone who rebels against you or refuses to obey you.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n bagli Josua wia la un niŋ ɛɛ
1Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n wa siuwɛ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Nun biibaal Josua la n ɛɛ Moosis hiini la be, 2“Josua, n balii Moosis siuwɔɔ. Awia, ɛɛ sirya filaŋkeŋ, di izi tɔ n nɛra Izrɛl hina see, ií gi Jɔɔdan muu di la hɛri la minna nyiŋŋi n tɛɛ baa la. 3N daŋ tɛɛ i ni n nɛra bɔr la maa iin niŋ kpa ii naazi jag, gunla miŋ faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Moosis la. 4Ii hɛri magbɔɔ daŋ chi wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma la guŋŋ di ga chug Lɛbanɔn bizenaa la n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag. Di kaa lii Muu Yufretis la n du wiifurii la, di ga Hitti hina hɛri di ra la Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn la n du wiicholii la. 5Nɛr maa wàá wer kpeglii maa, i de dui saŋa. Gunla miŋ faa du Moosis be la, gunnɛ ń du i ge gba be. Màá gilii ta gɛɛ di ɛɛ i wia vɛɛlai maa.
6Awia, chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega, dikuubɛɛwiai, hinuu niŋ tɔ a nɛra naa see di la hɛri la miŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ ba naabaala la. 7Chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega. A du tau di wer hiŋ Gbɔg la n balii Moosis n tɛi la, gilɛɛ wa bir har di ra kpuu, ka i wiɛɛlaa maa wer lii siwee, bɔr la maa hin niŋ la. 8Ɛɛ ra karmi Gbɔg Hɔnnaa di ra tɛɛ a nɛra saŋa maa, di gilɛɛ waa gar. Ka ra helluu hɔpizaa ani hamuŋa maa, í wer di ra ɛɛ wia la maa baŋ sɛbɛɛ du u biini la. Denii í nyɛɛli, i wiɛɛlaa maa ge lii siwee nɛnnɛ. 9Maa ŋɔ í chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpegaa? Gilɛɛ gil i bɔra waa sa di waa huah, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la daŋ du i be, bɔr la maa hin niŋ la.”
10Denii Josua jaa ŋɔ a nɛra sitɔɔra be, 11“Ií gaagi a chɔɔribɔr maa di ŋɔ a nɛra maa be lugɔ bá ɛɛ sirya di nyiŋŋi diwee nɛnnɛ, hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, ba daŋ gi Jɔɔdan muu di ga foozi hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la n na tɛɛ baa la, di so.”
12Denii Josua chaali Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ, di ŋɔ ba ge be, 13“Ií ra liizi gunla Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia la, ‘Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ra tɛɛ iabuu Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii paga naa, ií so.’ 14Ii haana ni ii biizi ani ii sela waa daŋ wer du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii bɔnnaa Moosis n tɛɛ ia naa, ka ii laallɔɔra la waa vɔɔ nɛnnɛ, di tɔ see gi a muu di ga hiini ii dɔŋahina Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ la, 15di ra la saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ wa tɛɛ baa a hɛri, Jɔɔdan muu wiicholii paga la bá so gunla uŋ tɛɛ ia la, bá ge wa wer foozi hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ baa la. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ tuŋ, ii daŋ jaa wer bir ba di wa so ii himmaa hɛri naa Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n tɛɛ ia, a Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii naa.”
16Denii ba sɛɛ tɛɛ Josua, di ŋɔ, “Wii la maa hin niŋ ŋɔ yá ɛɛ, yaa daŋ ɛɛu. Bɔr la maa ge hin niŋ hum yaa, yaa daŋ la. 17Yaa daŋ hiŋ i nua gunla yaa n hiŋ Moosis nua la. Kɔ́raawiizi la hinna hum la du i be, gunla uŋ faa du Moosis be la. 18Nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ i nua, bá kpuu. Awia, chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bɔkpega!”

english_text:
Rahab Helps the Israelite Spies
1 Joshua chose two men as spies and sent them from their camp at Acacia with these instructions: “Go across the river and find out as much as you can about the whole region, especially about the town of Jericho.”
The two spies left the Israelite camp at Acacia and went to Jericho, where they decided to spend the night at the house of a prostitute named Rahab.
2But someone found out about them and told the king of Jericho, “Some Israelite men came here tonight, and they are spies.” 3-7So the king sent soldiers to Rahab's house to arrest the spies.
Meanwhile, Rahab had taken the men up to the flat roof of her house and had hidden them under some piles of flax plants that she had put there to dry.
The soldiers came to her door and demanded, “Let us have the men who are staying at your house. They are spies.”
She answered, “Some men did come to my house, but I didn't know where they had come from. They left about sunset, just before it was time to close the town gate. I don't know where they were going, but if you hurry, maybe you can catch them.”
The guards at the town gate let the soldiers leave Jericho, but they closed the gate again as soon as the soldiers went through. Then the soldiers headed toward the Jordan River to look for the spies at the place where people cross the river.
8Rahab went back up to her roof. The spies were still awake, so she told them:
9I know that the Lord has given Israel this land. Everyone shakes with fear because of you. 10 We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea so you could leave Egypt. And we heard how you destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River. 11We know that the Lord your God rules heaven and earth, and we've lost our courage and our will to fight.
12Please promise me in the Lord's name that you will be as kind to my family as I have been to you. Do something to show 13that you won't let your people kill my father and mother and my brothers and sisters and their families.
14“Rahab,” the spies answered, “if you keep quiet about what we're doing, we promise to be kind to you when the Lord gives us this land. We pray that the Lord will kill us if we don't keep our promise!”
15Rahab's house was built into the town wall, and one of the windows in her house faced outside the wall. She gave the spies a rope, showed them the window, and said, “Use this rope to let yourselves down to the ground outside the wall. 16Then hide in the hills. The men who are looking for you won't be able to find you there. They'll give up and come back after a few days, and you can be on your way.”
17-20The spies said:
You made us promise to let you and your family live. We will keep our promise, but you can't tell anyone why we were here. You must tie this red rope on your window when we attack, and your father and mother, your brothers, and everyone else in your family must be here with you. We'll take the blame if anyone who stays in this house gets hurt. But anyone who leaves your house will be killed, and it won't be our fault.
21“I'll do exactly what you said,” Rahab promised. Then she sent them on their way and tied the red rope to the window.
22The spies hid in the hills for three days while the king's soldiers looked for them along the roads. As soon as the soldiers gave up and returned to Jericho, 23the two spies went down into the Jordan valley and crossed the river. They reported to Joshua and told him everything that had happened. 24“We're sure the Lord has given us the whole country,” they said. “The people there shake with fear every time they think of us.”
translation_text:
Bolzeŋ Jɛriko daanaa na wia
1Denii Josua suahzi hum baala banɛɛ di lii bolzeŋ Sitim, dí ba la ga daani Keenan hɛri, fɔŋfɔŋ bolzeŋ Jɛriko, di na gunla un duwɛɛ. Awia, ba kpa la ga zuu hahsɛnsɛnni bɛl banna yir Rahab dia, di du de.
2Nɛbɛl ga ŋɔ bolzeŋ Jɛriko koori be, “Na! Izrɛl hina baŋhina ba ɛnnɛ hamuŋa naa, bá wa daani a hɛri naa di na.” 3Denii a koori hum di ŋɔ Rahab be, “Gil baala la n ba i dia la wa lii chaaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ballɔɔ bá wa daani yaa hɛri naa maa di na.”
4Ka a haaŋ kpa a baala suah, ka ŋɔ, “Ba faa ba n benii, ka maa zum bɔr la baŋ liwɛɛ. 5Bɔr n waa lauri siwee, ba ra tɔɔgi a bol dominuuzenaa la, a saŋaa ba lii kaali, maa zum bɔr la baŋ gawɛɛ. Ií ra vol manaŋ, aŋhinabe, ii daŋ huuzi baa ŋmɛnɛɛ di lauri baa.” 6Ka u faa kpogli baa tinni sal, di ga suah bagni uŋ kpawɛɛ dau zɛɛ. 7A koori nɛra la jaa lii di ra dau ba luge, di ga bɔr la baŋ gawɛɛ di ra gi Jɔɔdan muu la. Baŋ haŋ waa lii, ba tɔ a bolzeŋ domininuuzeŋ.
8Mɔɔ ka a baala chɔɔ a hamuŋa ni, Rahab tinni ba be sal, 9di ŋɔ ba be, “N zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kpa hɛri naabuu tɛɛ ia, guŋ wia, ɔnsii lau nɛraa werge maa hɛri naa biini, dikuu ii wia. 10Yaa nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ Muuzeŋaahmu la hiihzi dikuu ii wia labuu, saŋa la iiŋ waa lii Ijip hɛri la. Di kaa nuu gunla iiŋ kpuuzi Sihɔn ni Ɔɔg la n ɛɛ Amɔri hina koora banɛɛ la n faa du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii labuu. 11Yaa n wa nuu guŋ, ɔnsii lau yaa werge, nɛr maa bɔra huah dikuu ii wia. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa di koraa chiŋ ani hɛri. 12Awia, ii gaafura ka hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi alugɔ ii daŋ suŋ n ni n nɛra maa ni, dikuu kennaa miŋ suŋ ii ni naa wia. Ií ɛɛ wii bɛl di bagliŋ, ń yardi ia 13lugɔ ii wàá kpuuzi n mɛɛ ni n maa, n niuna, n kpɛɛnna ani ba lulla maa.”
14A baala ŋɔ u be, “Kɔ́raawiizi kpuuzi yaa, di yaa waa haŋ wa ɛɛ kennaa yaa n niŋ ŋɔ naa! Di haa yaa wolo wa pillɛɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi wa hiini yaa, yaa foozi a hɛri, yaa daŋ suŋ i ni di lɛɛi.”
15Denii u jaa kpa ŋmɛŋ di ga tokoro ha, bá ga u ni di tuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u dia la faa choŋŋi a bol koŋliizeŋ ninɛɛ. 16U faa ŋɔ ba benii, “Ií la giŋgimee bɔr la ga suah de hɔpizaa ahoro, di a nɛra la n na nyiŋŋi ia la wa bittɔ ba, ií jaa lii di ra la.”
17A baala ŋɔ u be, “Hɛɛhzaa naa hiŋ gillɛ yaa hɛɛhzi naa wàá wer chi, 18di haa haŋ wa kpa a ŋmɛŋaahmu naa di vɔɔ tokoro la yaa n ga u ni di tuu la, di kaa chaali i mɛɛ ni i maa, i kpɛɛnna, i niuna ani i lulla maa i dia naa biini, di yaa wa zuu a hɛri. 19Di ba bɛl maa waa haŋ wa du i dia hiŋ, ka lii bossee ba wa kpuu, u haahkɛ daŋ chug u hiŋ. Ka di bɛl maa haŋ du i dia biini, ba wa kpuu, u haahkɛ daŋ chug yaa. 20Ka di i haŋ wa fuzi yaa wia naa, guŋwaa, hɛɛhzaa la yaa n hɛɛhzɛɛ la wàá ka chi.”
21U ŋɔ, “N sɛɛ gunla iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ labuu.” Ka ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ ba kaali. Ka u jaa kpa a ŋmɛŋaahmu la di vɔɔ a tokoro.
22A baala la n ga daani a hɛri la, la ga suah a giŋgimee bɔr. A koori nɛra la sɛu di nyiŋŋi baa guŋŋ hɔpizaa ahoro di wa huhzi, ka bir ba bol. 23Denii a baala banɛɛ hiŋ jaa lii a giŋgimee bɔr di wa gi Jɔɔdan muu la, di la ga bagli wia la maa n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Josua. 24Ba ŋɔ Josua be, “Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ yaabuu a hɛri maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ɔnsii teŋ lau de nɛra maanii yaa wia.”

english_text:
Israel Crosses the Jordan River
1Early the next morning, Joshua and the Israelites packed up and left Acacia. They went to the Jordan River and camped there that night. 2Two days later their leaders went through the camp, 3-4shouting, “When you see some of the priests carrying the sacred chest, you'll know it is time to cross to the other side. You've never been there before, and you won't know the way, unless you follow the chest. But don't get too close! Stay about a kilometer back.”
5Joshua told the people, “Make yourselves acceptable to worship the Lord, because he is going to do some amazing things for us.”
6Then Joshua turned to the priests and said, “Take the chest and cross the Jordan River ahead of us.” So the priests picked up the chest by its carrying poles and went on ahead.
7The Lord told Joshua, “Beginning today I will show the people that you are their leader, and they will know that I am helping you as I helped Moses. 8Now, tell the priests who are carrying the chest to go a little way into the river and stand there.”
9Joshua spoke to the people:
Come here and listen to what the Lord our God said he will do! 10The Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites control the land on the other side of the river. But the living God will be with you and will force them out of the land when you attack. And now, God is going to prove that he's powerful enough to force them out. 11-13Just watch the sacred chest that belongs to the Lord, the ruler of the whole earth. As soon as the priests carrying the chest step into the Jordan, the water will stop flowing and pile up as if someone had built a dam across the river.
The Lord has also said that each of the twelve tribes should choose one man to represent it.
14The Israelites packed up and left camp. The priests carrying the chest walked in front, 15until they came to the Jordan River. The water in the river had risen over its banks, as it often does in springtime. But as soon as the feet of the priests touched the water, 16-17the river stopped flowing, and the water started piling up at the town of Adam near Zarethan. No water flowed toward the Dead Sea, and the priests stood in the middle of the dry riverbed near Jericho while everyone else crossed over.
translation_text:
Jɔɔdan muu gii wia
1Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Josua ni Izrɛl hina maa izi lii bolzeŋ Sitim, bɔr la baŋ chɔɔwɛ la, di la Jɔɔdan muu baŋgia, di ga chɔɔ de mɔɔ, ka haa gi. 2Hɔpizaa ahoro n wa bɛrɛɛ, Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra la izi di gaagi ba chɔɔribɔr la biini, 3di ra ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Di ii haŋ wa na Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la, n chigɛ Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di ra vol, bɛl maa izi u duuribɔr di ra hiŋuu. 4Denii ii zum ŋmɛnɛɛ la iin niŋ ga, dikuu ii ŋmɛnɛ maa n haa waa ɛŋ gawɛɛ la wia. Ka ii tɛɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la bɔr lugɔ nogumzi kagboŋaanɛɛ, di gilɛɛ waa dugluu.”
5Josua jaa ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Bɛl maa sɔ u hiŋ di lizi u doŋa ha ka ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii Kɔraawiizi be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u daŋ kɛrɛ ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia ii biini.”
6Josua jaa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la be, “Ií kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di tɔ a nɛra see di ra vol.” Ba jaa kpau di tɔ ba see.
7Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be, “Zinaa, n daŋ faari di gil i dɔɔ girme ni zenni Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ. Bá zum lugɔ gunla miŋ faa du Moosis be la, gunnɛ n du i gba be. 8Ŋɔ n kizeehina la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la be lugɔ di ba wa hel Jɔɔdan muu kɛrii, bá zuu nii la biini tama ka chi.”
9Josua ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, “Ií ba di wa nuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wiŋɔzi. 10Kenne ií chi zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la du ii benii. Wibii maa, u daŋ duŋŋi Keenan, Hitti, Hivi, Pɛriz, Girgas, Amɔri ani Jɛbus hina ii sibɔɔ, 11di ii wa na Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la n tɔ ii see di gi Jɔɔdan muu. 12Awia, ií lizi baala fidibanɛɛ, nɛkpaŋ maa lii Izrɛl dee maa biini. 13Di Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n chigɛ Kɔraawiizi la, n ɛɛ durnya maa Dɔɔri, Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la haŋ wa zuu Jɔɔdan muu nii, u palaa daŋ teŋ, chiŋ nii la izi chi bɔkpaŋ alugɔ koŋlii.”
14A nɛra maa n wa izee bɔr la baŋ chɔɔwɛ la, di ra la bá ga gi Jɔɔdan muu la, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la jaa tɔ ba see. 15Di kuna kumaa saŋaa, Jɔɔdan muu la jaa su yaari u kɛraa maa, ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la, n haŋ wa kpa ba naazi jag a nii biini, 16a chiŋ nii la palaa teŋ, di chaali chɔɔ bɔkpaŋ bol bɛl banna yir Adam, n du Zarɛtan hɛri. Ka u zɛɛ bɔpallii la waa n pallɛ di ra zuu Muuzensiwii biini la, jaa teŋ kɔrai. Denii a nɛra maa jaa ga bɔr la n chaŋ bolzeŋ Jɛriko la di gi. 17Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la faa chigɔ a Jɔɔdan muu baambaaŋ bɔhiliirɛ guŋŋ, ka Izrɛl hina maa jaa wa gi.

english_text:
