29Bɔra naabuu Moosis faa kpa di tɛɛ Manasɛ dee yeŋ domeezi, 30ba bɔr faarɔɔrɛ lii Mahanam, di kpa Basan Koori Ɔɔg kora diiribɔr maa di jaa, di kpa Manasɛ biibaal Jayir bola tokkoahoro la maa n du Basan la di jaa. 31Di kaa kpa Giliad yeŋ ani Astarɔf ni Ɛdrɛi la n ɛɛ Basan Koori Ɔɔg bolzenaa la. A bɔra naa maanii ba faa kpa di tɛɛ Manasɛ biibaal Makir domeezi yeŋ.
32Kenne Moosis faa bɔnni a hɛri la n du Jɛriko ani Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii, di u faa haa du Moab lɛl biini. 33Moosis faa waa yemmaa mɔnnɛ tɛɛ Levi dee la waa, ú birgi ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ nuarɛ tɛɛ baa lugɔ waabuu ninna tɛɛ baa kunla maa banna nyiŋŋi.

english_text:
The Land West of the Jordan River
1-5 Nine and a half tribes still did not have any land, although two and a half tribes had already received land east of the Jordan River. Moses had divided that land among them, and he had also said that the Levi tribe would not receive a large region like the other tribes. Instead, the people of Levi would receive towns and the nearby pastures for their sheep, goats, and cattle. And since the descendants of Joseph had become the two tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, there were still nine and a half tribes that needed land. The Lord had told Moses that he would show those tribes how to divide up the land of Canaan.
When the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the leaders of the families and tribes of Israel met to divide up the land of Canaan, the Lord showed them how to do it.
Joshua Gives Hebron to Caleb
6 One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua:
You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me. 7 I was 40 years old at the time Moses sent me from Kadesh-Barnea into Canaan as a spy. When I came back and told him about the land, everything I said was true. 8The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God. 9 The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
10Joshua, it was 45 years ago that the Lord told Moses to make that promise, and now I am 85. Even though Israel has moved from place to place in the desert, the Lord has kept me alive all this time as he said he would. 11I'm just as strong today as I was then, and I can still fight as well in battle.
12So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
13Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants. 14And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
15Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim.
There was peace in the land.
translation_text:
Jɔɔdan muu wiicholii hɛssi bɔnnaa wia
1Bɔra naabuu Izrɛl hina di, a ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuna, Keenan hɛri biini. Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza ni Nun biibaal Josua ani Izrɛl dizi sitɔɔra labuu faa bɔnni a hɛri. 2Dizi kabɛl ni kezaa ba faa ta kuna, a bagli gunla ban niŋ bɔnni a hɛri tɛɛ baa gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis ɛɛ la. 3Moosis faa kpa Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii hɛri labuu tɛɛ dizi anɛɛ ni keza la, ú ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ, ka waa Levi dee la waa tɛɛwɛ yemmaa. 4Joosɛf naanna faa ɛɛ dizi anɛɛrɛ, baabuu faa Manasɛ ani Ɛfram dizi. Ka Levi dee la faa waa a hɛri yemmaa nawɛɛ. Bola bɛnnɛ ba faa na di so. A laŋgarazi ge ɛɛ ba sela diiribɔra. Guŋ bɛnnɛ ba faa na. 5Izrɛl hina faa bɔnni a hɛrii nɛnnɛ, gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ ba bɔnnuu la.
Baŋ kpa bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn tɛɛ Kalɛb wia
6A hɔl bɛl, Kɛniz hinuu Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb ni Juda dee nɛra baŋhina la Josua be Gilgal. Kalɛb ga ŋɔ Josua be, “I zum gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ u dɔgtɛɛ Moosis, di lii n nii wia biini saŋa la yaa n faa du Kadɛs Bania la. 7N faa di binni tokkoanɛɛrɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis faa humiŋ lii Kadɛs Bania lugɔ ń la Keenan hɛri di ga daanuu na gunla un duwɛɛ. Miŋ wa lii de ba, n ŋɔ u be wii la maa miŋ ga na denii ani biinihuŋŋu. 8Ama, n ni banla n faa laŋŋɛ la waa, wa du yaa nɛraa ɔnsii ani bɔhuaih. Miŋwaa faa hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ gunla n dɛkkɛ lugɔ n hiŋ. 9A hɔl hiŋ, Moosis hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua, di ŋɔ, ‘Hɛri la hiŋ volle la daŋ birgi i ni i biizi kapɛttɛ di hanna la, dikuu hiŋ wette hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum nɛnnɛ ni biinihuŋŋu wia.’
10Binni na! Filaŋkennaa, Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ mìŋ́ Kalɛb du de ni miibɔɔ, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la. U gillɔɔ n du de binni tokkoanɛɛ ani anue, di lii saŋa la uŋ ŋɔ guŋ tɛɛ Moosis, saŋa la Izrɛl hina n faa haa du hɛribɔduma di ra juuri la. Minuu keŋ zinaa, di di binni tokkoanaazu ni anue. 11N haa kpekkoo gunla miŋ faa kpekke, saŋa la Moosis n humiŋ a ŋmɛnijaŋ la. N daŋ haa wer vol guŋ, di haa wer la ga yoo laal gba haali ni zinaa. 12Awia, n na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ í kpa a giŋgimee nyuuni hɛri di tɛŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua di tɛŋ a hɔl hiŋ la. I himmaa faa nuuwɔɔ lugɔ Anak hina la n faa helle kpabaa faa du de, di ma koŋlaa di bar ba bolzenaa, a du kpeg werge la. Ka di Kɔraawiizi chigɔ n har, n daŋ duŋŋi ba maa lii a hɛri, gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.”
13Denii Josua kissi Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb, ka kpa bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn hɛri tɛu ú ɛɛ u kapɛttɛ. 14Bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn haa ɛɛ Kɛniz hinuu Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb ni u dee maa bɔttɛ haali ni zinaa, dikuu gunla uŋ faa kpa u biinihuŋŋu maa di hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la wia. 15Bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn sɔnnɛ faa Kiriaf Aaba. Anak hina nɛkpeg bɛl banna yir Aaba sɔnnɛ ba faa kpa dawuu.
Bampirsɔna jaa du a hɛri.

english_text:
Judah's Land
1The clans of the Judah tribe were given land that went south along the border of Edom, and at its farthest point south it even reached the Zin Desert. 2Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea. 3As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka, 4and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
5Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea.
The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea. 6From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe. 7From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel, 8and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites.
Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley. 9At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
10From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah. 11It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea, 12which was Judah's western border.
The clans of Judah lived within these borders.
Caleb's Land
(Judges 1.12-15)
13 Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
14Caleb attacked Hebron and forced the three Anakim clans of Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai to leave. 15Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher. 16He told his men, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
17Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, and Caleb let him marry Achsah. 18Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
19She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.”
Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
Towns in Judah's Land
20The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
21-32The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following 29 towns with their surrounding villages:
Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur, Kinah, Dimonah, Aradah, Kedesh, Hazor of Ithnan, Ziph, Telem, Bealoth, Hazor-Hadattah, Kerioth-Hezron, which is also called Hazor, Amam, Shema, Moladah, Hazar-Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-Pelet, Hazar-Shual, Beersheba and its surrounding villages, Baalah, Iim, Ezem, Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah, Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah, Lebaoth, Shilhim, and Enrimmon.
33-36The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following 14 towns with their surrounding villages:
Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
37-41The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following 16 towns with their surrounding villages:
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
42-44The fourth region was located in the central part of the lower foothills, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages:
Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah.
45-47The fifth region was located along the Mediterranean seacoast, and it had the following towns with their surrounding settlements and villages:
Ekron and the towns between there and the coast, Ashdod and the larger towns nearby, Gaza, the towns from Gaza to the Egyptian Gorge, and the towns along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
48-51The sixth region was in the southwestern part of the hill country, and it had the following eleven towns with their surrounding villages:
Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath-Sannah, which is now called Debir, Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh.
52-54The seventh region was located in the south-central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages:
Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth-Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath-Arba, which is now called Hebron, and Zior.
55-57The eighth region was located in the southeastern part of the hill country, and it had the following ten towns with their surrounding villages:
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah.
58-59The ninth region was located in the central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages:
Halhul, Beth-Zur, Gedor, Maarath, Beth-Anoth, and Eltekon.
The tenth region was located in the north-central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following eleven towns with their surrounding villages:
Tekoa, Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem, Peor, Etam, Culon, Tatam, Shoresh, Kerem, Gallim, Bether, and Manahath.
60The eleventh region was located in the northern part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following two towns with their surrounding villages:
Rabbah, and Kiriath-Baal, which is also called Kiriath-Jearim.
61-62The twelfth region was located in the desert along the Dead Sea, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages:
Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, Salt Town, and En-Gedi.
The Jebusites
63 The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_text:
Hɛri la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Juda dee wia
1A hɛri bɔr la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Juda dee ni ba domeezi, ga chug Ɛdɔm hɛri magaa, di ga de ga hel Zin Hɛribɔduma la n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag tuna.
2U wiifurii nodig wiikakag naa magbɔɔ faarɔɔrɛ lii Muuzensiwii wiifurii nodig wiikakag tuna, 3di ga de guŋŋ di ga gilli bɔr la banna yir Nuuma Ŋmɛnɛɛ wiifurii nodig wiikakag la, di lii de ga chug Zin Hɛribɔduma, di gilli di ga hel Kadɛs Bania wiifurii nodig wiikakag. Denii u kaa lii de di ga bɛri Hɛzrɔn di ga chug Adar. Di bir kpau guŋŋ bar di ga chug bolzeŋ Kaka. 4U ga de guŋŋ di ga bɛri di ga chug bolzeŋ Azmɔn, di ga choŋŋi Ijip gɔŋ, di ga tuŋ muuzeŋ. Juda hɛri wiifurii nodig wiikakag magbɔɔrɛ faa guŋ.
5U wiifurii magbɔɔrɛ Muuzensiwii di ga hel Jɔɔdan muu nua.
U wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag magbɔɔ ge faari a muuzeŋ bɔr la Jɔɔdan muu n ɔɔ waa zuu la, 6di tinni ga hel yembɛl banna yir Bɛf Hɔgla, di kaa kpau guŋŋ di ra la Bɛf Araba wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, di ga hel Bohan Bii la baŋ faa kpa Rubin biibaal Bɔhan sɔŋ di dawuu la. 7Di kaa chi de magbɔɔ di kaa kpau ga Akɔ Waluu di tinni ga hel Dɛbir, di kaa kpau di ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag paga guŋŋ di ga hel Gilgal n chaŋ Adumim Ŋmɛnɛɛ n du gɔŋluŋ wiifurii nodig wiikakag. Di kaa kpau guŋŋ di ga hel niiri aŋhina banna yir Ɛn Sɛmɛs, di lii de ga hel Ɛn Rɔgɛl. 8U magbɔɔ kaa ga Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu, di hiihni Jɛbus hina bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm wiifurii nodig wiikakag bɔwillii, di lii de tinni giŋgimii la n du Hinɔm Waluu wiicholii, u du Rɛfam Waluu wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag tuna la. 9A magbɔɔ kaa lii a bii nyuu di ga hel Nɛftɔa bulli la. Di lii de di kpau guŋŋ di ga hel bola la n du Bizeŋ Ɛfrɔn nyuu la. Di kaa bir tuu di ra la bolzeŋ Baala. 10Denii u magbɔɔ hiŋ mɔŋ di ga wiicholii di lii a bolzeŋ Baala ga hel Bizeŋ Sɛɛ, di ga de hiihni Bizeŋ Jiarim wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii la, di tuu ra la bolzeŋ Bɛf Sɛmɛs, di gilli ga chug bolzeŋ Timna. 11A bɔr magbɔɔ kaa chi de di kpau guŋŋ di ga hel Ɛkrɔn wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii, di bir chaŋ bolzeŋ Sikɛrɔn di ga hel Bizeŋ Baala, di kaa kpau guŋŋ di ga chug bolzeŋ Jabniil. Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn nuarɛ u magbɔɔ ga tuŋ.
12U wiicholii magbɔɔ faa ɛɛ a muuzeŋ nua.
Magazi naabuu faa bar Juda dee domeezi la.
13Di lii gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Josua be la wia, u faa mɔŋ Juda dee hɛri la yeŋ tɛɛ Jɛfunɛ bie Kalɛb. U kpa Kiriaf Aaba la banna yir bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn la tɛu. Anak dee naabaal sɔnnɛ faa Aaba, u sɔnnɛ ba faa kpa dau a bolzeŋ naa. 14Denii Kalɛb jaa duŋŋi a Anak dee domeezi Sɛsai ni Ahiman ani Talmai lii de. 15Denii u kaa lii de di ga lɔ bolzeŋ la banna yir Dɛbir, de sɔnnɛ faa Kiriaf Sɛfa. 16Kalɛb ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa n niŋ wer kpegli Kiriaf Sɛfa, n daŋ kpa n biihaaŋ Aksa tɛɛ a hiŋ ú kpa.” 17U niwee Kɛnaz biibaal Ɔtniɛllɛ wette ga lɔ baa di kpegli baa. Awia, Kalɛb jaa kpa ú biihaaŋ Aksa hiŋ tɛu, u birgi u haaŋ. 18Aksa n wa yuu Ɔtniɛl, u ŋɔ u be, “Ŋɔ n mɛɛ be lugɔ ú tɛi hɛri di jaa.” Aksa n ga hel u mɛɛ be, di ra tuu u kawee nyuu. U mɛɛ pɛɛzuu. “A summɔaa? Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋi ŋɔ n ɛɛ tɛinɛi?” 19U ŋɔ, “Ɛɛ wizeŋ bɛl tɛŋ. I suŋ n ninɛɛ di tɛŋ hɛri lii Nɛgɛv biini. Gaafura! Kpa bulli di jaaŋ.” Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, Kalɛb kpa a bulli la n du chiŋ ani zɛɛ la maa tɛu.
20Juda dee ni u domeezi lulla kapɛttɛ diiribɔraa keŋ. 21Juda dee bolzenaa la n du Ɛdɔm magbɔɔ wiifurii nodig wiikakag labuu,
Kabziil, Ɛda, Jagur, 22Kina, Dimɔna, Adada, 23Kɛdɛs, Hazɔr, Itnan, 24Zif, Tɛlɛm, Bialɔf, 25Hazɔr Hadata, Kɛriɔf Hɛzrɔn la n ɛɛ Hazɔr la, 26Amam, Sɛma, Mɔlada, 27Hazar Gada, Hɛsmɔn, Bɛf Pɛlɛt, 28Hazar Sual, bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba, Bizɔtia, 29Baala, Iim, Ɛzɛm, 30Ɛltɔlad, Kɛsil, bolzeŋ Hɔma, 31Ziklag, Madmana, Sansana, 32Lɛbayɔf, Silhim, Ain ani Rimɔn. A maa kpau du bola tokko ni kabɛl ani a boljigzi.
33Bolzenaa la n du wiicholii giŋgimee zɛɛzi, ba faa kpa tɛɛ Juda hinaa keŋ,
Ɛstayɔl, Zɔra, Asna, 34Zanoa, Ɛn Ganim, Tapua, Ɛnam, 35Jamuf, Adulam, Soko, Azɛka, 36Saaram, Aditam, Gɛdɛra ani Gɛdɛrɔtam. Bolzenaa fidaanaazu ni a boljigzi.
37Anla n jaawɛɛ kaa, Zɛnan, Hadasa, Migdal Gad, 38Dilian, Mizpa, Jɔktiil, 39Lakis, Bɔzkaf, Ɛglɔn, 40Kabɔn, Lamas, Kitlis, 41Gɛdɛrɔf, Bɛf Dagɔn, Naama ani bolzeŋ Makɛda. A ge du bolzenaa fidaanumbɛl ni a boljigzi.
42Aŋhinaa kaa, Libna, Ɛta, Asan, 43Ifta, Asna, Nɛzib, 44Keila, Akzib ani Marɛsa, a ge du bolzenaa kabɛl ni a boljigzi.
45Di kpa Bolzeŋ Ɛkrɔn ni u boljigzi maa 46ani u wiicholii paga bola la maa n faa dugli Asdɔd ni a boljigzi maa jaa. 47Haali Asdɔd ni u boljigzi ani Gaza ge ni u boljigzi maa, guŋŋ di ga lii gɔŋ la n du Ijip magbɔɔ, di kaa kpa Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn nua la maa di wa kaali.
48A hɛri bɔr la uŋ kaa na lii giŋgimee hɛri jaa labuu keŋ, bolzenaa Samir, Jatir, Soko, 49Dana, Kiriaf Sana la, n ɛɛ Dɛbir la, 50Anab, Ɛstɛmɔ, Anim, 51Gɔsɛn, Hɔlɔn ani Gilo, a ge maa du bolzenaa fidikpaŋ ni a boljigzi.
52Di kaa kpa Arab, Duma, Ɛsan, 53Janim, Bɛf Tapua, Afɛka, 54Humta, Kiriaf Aaba la n ɛɛ bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn ani Ziɔ, a ge maa du bolzenaa kabɛl ni a boljigzi.
55Di kaa kpa Mayɔn, Kamɛl, Zif, Juta, 56Jɛzriil, Jɔkdiam, Zanoa, 57Keen, Gibia ani Timna, a ge du bolzenaa fi ni a boljigzi.
58Anla n kaa jaau kaa, Halhul, Bɛf Zur, Gɛdɔ, 59Maaraf, Bɛf Anɔf ani Ɛltɛkɔn, a ge maa du bolzenaa anumbɛl ni a boljigzi.
60Di kaa kpa Kiriaf Baal la, n ɛɛ Kiriaf Jiarim la ani Raba, a ge maa du bolzenaa anɛɛ ni a boljigzi.
61Di kaa lii hɛribɔduma ge bola la n kaa jaau, Bɛf Araba, Midin, Sɛkaka, 62Nibsan, Yazi bolzeŋ ani Ɛn Gɛdi, a maa du bolzenaa anumbɛl ni a boljigzi.
63Ka Juda dee la faa waa wette duŋŋi Jɛbus hina la n faa du Jɛrusalɛm la waa, di lii a hɛri biini. Haali ni zinaa, ba ni baabuu haa kpauwɛ so.

english_text:
Ephraim's Land
1-4Ephraim and Manasseh are the two tribes descended from Joseph, and the following is a description of the land they received. The southern border of their land started at the Jordan River east of the spring at Jericho. From there it went west through the desert up to the hill country around Bethel. From Bethel it went to Luz and then to the border of the Archites in Ataroth. It continued west down to the land that belonged to the Japhlet clan, then went on to Lower Beth-Horon, Gezer, and the Mediterranean Sea.
5The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon 6-8and the Mediterranean Sea. Their northern border started on the east at Janoah, curved a little to the north, then came back south to Michmethath and Tappuah, where it followed the Kanah Gorge west to the Mediterranean Sea.
The eastern border started on the north near Janoah and went between Janoah on the southwest and Taanath-Shiloh on the northeast. Then it went south to Ataroth, Naarah, and on as far as the edge of the land that belonged to Jericho. At that point it turned east and went to the Jordan River. The clans of Ephraim received this region as their tribal land. 9Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
10 Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_text:
Hɛri la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Ɛfram ni Manasɛ dizi wia
1Hɛri la baŋ mɔnnɛ tɛɛ Joosɛf dee la faarɔɔrɛ di lii Jɔɔdan muu la n dugli bolzeŋ Jɛriko, di tinni ga Jɛriko niiri wiifurii di ga zuu hɛribɔduma, di lii de ga zuu Bɛtɛl giŋgimee hɛri. 2Di lii bolzeŋ Bɛtɛl la banna yir Luuz, di ga de gilli ga zuu bolzeŋ Atarɔf, bɔr la Aaki domee n duwɛɛ la. 3U kaa chɔɔ guŋŋ di tuu ga wiicholii, di ga lii Jaflɛt hina hɛri, haali guŋŋ di ga hel Zɛɛ Bɛf Hɔrɔn hɛri, di kaa chi de di ga lii bolzeŋ Gɛza, guŋŋ di ga chug Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn la nua.
4Kenne Joosɛf naanna Manasɛ ani Ɛfram dizi di ba kapɛttɛ.
Hɛri la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Ɛfram dee wia
5Bɔra naabuu ba faa kpa tɛɛ Ɛfram dee.
U magbɔɔ faarɔɔrɛ lii Atarɔf Adar n du wiifurii di ga hel Chiŋ Bɛf Hɔrɔn, 6di kpau guŋŋ di ga chug Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn la. Di lii bolzeŋ Mikmɛtaf n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, di mɔŋ ga wiifurii di ga bɛri bolzeŋ Taanaf Silo, di ga lii Janoa n du wiifurii. 7Di kaa lii Janoa tuu la bolzenaa Atarɔf ni Naara, di kaa ga hel bolzeŋ Jɛriko di ga Jɔɔdan muu lii. 8Di la bolzeŋ Tapua, a magbɔɔ ga wiicholii di ga hel Kana Faalim, di ga tuŋ Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn nua. Ɛfram dee domeezi kapɛttɛ diiribɔttɛ guŋ ba tɛɛ baa. 9Ɛfram faa kaa na bolzenaa ni boljigzi aŋhina di lii Manasɛ hina kapɛttɛ la biini.
10Ba faa waa Keenan hina la waa duŋŋɛɛ di lii Gɛza, ka gil baa ba du ba be di birgi ba yoma, haali zinaa, ba ni baabuu haa du de.

english_text:
Manasseh's Land West of the Jordan River
1-6 Manasseh was Joseph's oldest son, and Machir was Manasseh's oldest son. Machir had a son named Gilead, and some of his descendants had already received the regions of Gilead and Bashan because they were good warriors. The other clans of the Manasseh tribe descended from Gilead's sons Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. The following is a description of the land they received.
Hepher's son Zelophehad did not have any sons, but he did have five daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. One day the clans that were descendants of Zelophehad's five daughters went to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the leaders of Israel. The people of these clans said, “The Lord told Moses to give us land just as he gave land to our relatives.”
Joshua followed the Lord's instructions and gave land to these five clans, as he had given land to the five clans that had descended from Hepher's brothers. So Manasseh's land west of the Jordan River was divided into ten parts.
7The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring. 8The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
9-10Then the border went west to the Kanah Gorge and ran along the northern edge of the gorge to the Mediterranean Sea. The land south of the gorge belonged to Ephraim. And even though there were a few towns that belonged to Ephraim north of the gorge, the land north of the gorge belonged to Manasseh.
The western border of Manasseh was the Mediterranean Sea, and the tribe shared a border with the Asher tribe on the northwest and with the Issachar tribe on the northeast.
11Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands:
Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
12 But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them. 13When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave.
Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
14One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
15Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
16“Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
17“Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful, 18so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_text:
Hɛri la n du wiicholii ba faa kpa tɛɛ Manasɛ dee la wia
1Joosɛf biinabɔmaa Manasɛ. Manasɛ ge biinabɔma sɔnnɛ Makir. Makir faa ɛɛ Giliad hina naabaallɛ, di du kpeg di ra lɔ laal werge. Awia, ba faa kpa Giliad ni Basan la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii paga la tɛɛ baa. 2Jɔɔdan muu wiicholii hɛri labuu ba faa kpa di tɛɛ domeezi la n kawɛɛ, di lii Manasɛ dee biini. Baabuu faa, Abiɛza, Hɛlɛk, Asriɛl, Sɛkɛm, Hittia ani Sɛmida. Joosɛf biibaal Manasɛ naanna biibaala sɔnaa faa guŋ, di ɛɛ ba domeezi nabɔnzi. 3Zɛlɔfɛhad la n ɛɛ Hɛfa biibaal di ɛɛ Manasɛ, Makir ani Giliad naana la, faa waa biibaala dɔɔwɛ. Biihambizi bɛnnɛ u faa dɔɔ. Ba sɔnaa faa, Mala ni Noowa ni Hɔgla ni Milka ani Tirza. 4Ba faa ba Ɛliaza la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ ni Nun biibaal Josua ani Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi maa be di wa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii lugɔ ú tɛɛ yaa ge kapɛttɛ gunla unna tɛɛ a baala maa di lii deere dee maa biini la.” Baŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, Josua jaa mɔŋ bɔr tɛɛ baa, gunla uŋ mɔnnɛ tɛɛ ba mɛɛ ani ba mɛɛzenaa biizi, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la. 5Hɛssi la maa baŋ tɛɛ Manasɛ la faa du bɔra fi, di kpa Giliad ni Basan bolzenaa la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la di jaa. 6Manasɛ dee biihaana ni ba biibaal n di kapɛttɛ la wia, ba jaa kpa Giliad hɛri tɛɛ u naanna la n kawɛɛ.
7Manasɛ dee bɔr magbɔɔ faa faarɔɔrɛ di lii Asɛ di ga hel Mikmɛtaf la n du bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm wiifurii la. Di lii de ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di ga kpa nɛra la n du Ɛn Tapua la di jaa. 8Hɛssi la maa n bar Tapua la maa ɛɛ Manasɛ dee horaa, ka Tapua himmaa la n du Manasɛ magbɔɔ la ɛɛ Ɛfram hina hor. 9Denii a magbɔɔ ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di ga hel Kana Faalim. Bola faa du de di ɛɛ Ɛfram hora di koozi Manasɛ hora biini, ka Manasɛ magbɔɔrɛ faa a faalim wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag paga, di kpau guŋŋ ga chug Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn la. 10A hɛri wiifurii nodig wiikakag faa ɛɛ Ɛfram hina hotte, u wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ge ɛɛ Manasɛ hina hor. Manasɛ bɔr faa chug a muuzeŋ labuu, u ni Asɛ du magbɔɔ wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, u ni Isaka ge magbɔɔ du wiifurii.
11Isaka ni Asɛ dizi hɛssi biine, Manasɛ deere faa dɔɔ bola naa, Bɛf San, Ibliam, Ɛndɔ, Taanak, Mɛgidɔ hina ani bola la maa n baraa la, di kpa Dɔɔ la n du muuzeŋ nua la.
12Ka Manasɛ hina la waa, waa wette so bola naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waa wette duŋŋi Keenan hina la lii a bola. 13Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Izrɛl hina jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di ra fir Keenan hina, ba hum ra tɛɛ baa, ka ba faa waa baa duŋŋɛɛ lii a hɛri waa biini.
14Joosɛf dee ge ba Josua be di wa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi kissi yaabuu werge, yaa du kpil, ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i mɔŋ a hɛri bɔkpaŋ bɛŋ tɛɛ yaa, ú ɛɛ yaa kapɛttɛi?”
15Josua ŋɔ, “Di Ɛfram hɛri la n ɛɛ giŋgimee bɔr la waa kaŋ tɛɛ ia, guŋwaa, ii la kɔrni la n du Pɛriz ni Rɛfa hina bɔra la biini, di ga mɔŋ bɔr di par di jaa.”
16Denii ba bir ŋɔ u be, “A giŋgimee bɔr hɛri wàá hel yaa, ka Keenan hina la n soge lɛla la biini dɔɔ lugbia torkozii, banla maa n du Bɛf San ni u bola la n baruu ani banla n du Jɛzriil Waluu la.”
17Denii Josua jaa ŋɔ Ɛfram ni Manasɛ dee la n lii Joosɛf dee biini la be, “Iiŋ kannɛ di kaa du kpeg kennaa, n daŋ tɛɛ ia hɛri jaa. 18A giŋgimee nyuu bɔr la gba daŋ ɛɛ ii hor. Haali uŋ ɛɛ kɔr la gba, ka ii daŋ paruu, ú ɛɛ ii kundɔɔlii, di lii u tuna bɛl di ga hel bɛl. Ka Keenan hina la waa, ii daŋ duŋŋi baa lii de, haali baŋ dɔɔ lugbia torkozi di du kpeg la gba.”

english_text:
Joshua Gives Out the Rest of the Land
1After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent. 2There were still seven tribes without any land, 3-7so Joshua told the people:
The Judah tribe has already settled in its land in the south, and the Joseph tribes have settled in their land in the north. The tribes of Gad, Reuben, and East Manasseh already have the land that the Lord's servant Moses gave them east of the Jordan River. And the people of Levi won't receive land like the other tribes. Instead, they will serve the Lord as priests.
But the rest of you haven't done a thing to take over any land. The Lord God who was worshiped by your ancestors has given you the land, and now it's time to go ahead and settle there.
Seven tribes still don't have any land. Each of these tribes should choose three men, and I'll send them to explore the remaining land. They will divide it into seven regions, write a description of each region, and bring these descriptions back to me. I will find out from the Lord our God what region each tribe should get.
8Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
9The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh. 10Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided.
Benjamin's Land
11Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north. 12Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert. 13-14From there it went to Luz, which is now called Bethel. The border ran along the ridge south of Luz, then went to Ataroth-Orech and on as far as the mountain south of Lower Beth-Horon. At that point it turned south and became the western border. It went as far south as Kiriath-Baal, a town in Judah now called Kiriath-Jearim.
15Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring. 16From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
17At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe. 18The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley. 19Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River. 20The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border.
These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
21-24One region of Benjamin's tribal land had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Those towns were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, Emek-Keziz, Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Chephar-Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba.
25-28In the other region there were the following 14 towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town.
These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_text:
A hɛri bɔr la n kawɛɛ bɔnnaa wia
1Izrɛl hina n jaa dɔɔ a hɛri maa fɔŋŋa la, ba maa chaali bol la banna yir Silo, di baŋ ba ni Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia, 2ka ba faa haa waa Izrɛl hina dizi aniidaanɛɛ la waa tɛɛwɛ bá kapɛttɛ hɛssi. 3Denii Josua pɛɛzi baa, “Ɛrɛɛ dɔnnɛ ií so birgi mag, ka izi foozi a hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala n na hum la n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia lai? 4Ií lizi nɛra bahoro lii dee maa biini. N daŋ hum baa, bá la ga daani a hɛri na, di sɛbi bagli gunla un duwɛɛ ani u bɔra la dee maa n na nyiŋŋi, ka bir ba n be. 5Ií daŋ bɔnni a hɛri bɔra aniidaanɛɛ. Juda dee daŋ du ba bɔr n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere, Joosɛf ge dee du ba bɔr, wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere. 6Di ii wa sɛbi a bɔra aniidaanɛɛhiŋ duula tuŋ, ií kpaa ba ɛŋ di wa tɛŋ, ń ta kuna Kɔraawiizi see tɛɛ ia. 7Ka a Levi dee la waa, wàá na a hɛri yemmaa ú ɛɛ ba hor. Baawaa kapɛttɛɛ baŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, di ra hum u huma. Gad dee ni Rubin dee ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ waa teŋ faa na ba kapɛttɛzii Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii paga, Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n faa tɛɛ baa la.”
8Josua ŋɔ tɛɛ banla baŋ lizɛɛ ba ra la bá ga daani a hɛri na la be, “Ií la ga daani a hɛri maa, di sɛbi gunla un duwɛɛ dau, ka bir ba di wa ŋɔ n be, ń ta kuna Kɔraawiizi see bolzeŋ Silo bɔnnaa tɛɛ ia, ú bagliŋ gunla min niŋ bɔnni de tɛɛ dee maa.” 9Awia, a nɛra la ga gaagi a hɛri maa, di bɔnni de bɔra aniidaanɛɛ, di sɛbi u duula maa ni a bolzenaa sɔna, ka bir ba Josua be Silo, bɔr la baŋ baŋzi bá tantizi di chɔɔ la. 10Josua jaa ta kuna Silo, Kɔraawiizi see tɛɛ baa, ka bɔnni a hɛri tɛɛ Izrɛl hina dizi la n kawɛɛ la maa.
Hɛri la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Bɛnjamin dee la wia
11Bɛnjamin dee domeezii ba feli bɔnni a hɛri tɛɛ. Ba hɛri faa chɔɔ Juda ni Joosɛf dizi hɛssi baambaannɛ.
12A hɛri wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag magbɔɔ faarɔɔrɛ lii Jɔɔdan muu, di ga bɛri bolzeŋ Jɛriko wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii, di ga wiicholi ga hel giŋgimee hɛri, di ga chug Bɛf Avɛn hɛribɔduma. 13U magbɔɔ kaa chi de, di kpau guŋŋ di ga hel Luuz la banna yir Bɛtɛl wiifurii nodig wiikakag bɔwillii, di ga de tuu la Atarɔf Adar la n du bizeŋ nyuu, di du yembɛl banna yir Bɛf Hɔrɔn bɔwillii wiifurii nodig wiikakag la.
14Di lii bizeŋ la n chaŋ Bɛf Hɔrɔn wiifurii nodig wiikakag, a magbɔɔ bir ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di hiihni wiicholiii paga, di ga lii Kiriaf Baal, ba faa kaa ra yiruu Kiriaf Jiarim la, n ɛɛ Juda hina bolzeŋ. U wiicholii magbɔɔrɛ faa guŋ.
15U wiifurii nodig wiikakag magbɔɔ la faarɔɔrɛ lii Kiriaf Jiarim laŋgara, di kpau guŋŋ di ga lii Nɛftɔa bulli. 16A magbɔɔ kaa tuu ga hel bizeŋ la n chaŋ Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu la zɛɛ, n du Rɛfam Waluu wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere la. Di lii de ga Hinɔm Waluu di hiini Jɛbus hina bolzeŋ wiifurii nodig wiikakag bɔwillii la, di ga hel bolzeŋ Ɛn Rɔgɛl. 17Di kaa lii de di ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di ga hel Ɛn Sɛmɛs niiri, di kaa kpau ga lii yembɛl banna yir Gɛlilɔf n chaŋ Adumim Ŋmɛnɛɛ. Di kaa lii de di kpau guŋŋ di ga hel Bɔhan Bii la. Bɔhan naa faa ɛɛ Rubin biibaallɛ. 18Di kaa lii de di kpau guŋŋ ga hel yembɛl banna yir Bɛf Araba wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii, di lii de tuu ga hel Jɔɔdan Waluu. 19U kaa lii de di ga hel Bɛf Hɔgla wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii di ga de ga chug bɔr la Jɔɔdan muu n gaa zuu Muuzensiwii la. U wiifurii nodig wiikakag magbɔɔrɛ faa guŋ.
20Jɔɔdan muu labuu faa ba wiifurii magbɔɔ.
Bɛnjamin domeezi kapɛttɛ magbɔɔnii faa guŋ.
21Bolzenaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Bɛnjamin dee domeezii keŋ,
Jɛriko, Bɛf Hɔgla, Ɛmɛk Kɛziz, 22Bɛf Araba, Zɛmaram, Bɛtɛl 23Avim, Para Ɔfra, 24Kɛfar Amɔni, Ɔfni ani Gɛba. A maa du bola fidaanɛɛ ani a boljigzi.
25Di kaa kpa Gibiɔn, Rama, Bɛɛrɔf, 26Mizpa, Kɛfira, Mɔza, 27Rɛkɛm, Irpiil, Tarala, 28Zɛla, Hɛlɛf, Jɛbus hina bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm, Gibia ani Kiriaf Jiarim. A maa du bolzenaa fidaanaazu ni a boljigzi.
Bɛnjamin dee domeezi kapɛttɛ diiribɔraa faa guŋ, baŋ tɛɛ baa.

english_text:
Simeon's Land
1Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders. 2-6 In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following 13 towns with their surrounding villages:
Beersheba, Shema, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Balah, Ezem, Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susah, Beth-Lebaoth, and Sharuhen.
7In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages:
Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
8Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
9Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon.
Zebulun's Land
10-12Zebulun was the third tribe chosen to receive land. The southern border for its clans started in the west at the edge of the gorge near Jokneam. It went east to the edge of the land that belongs to the town of Dabbesheth, and continued on to Maralah and Sarid. It took in the land that belongs to Chislothtabor, then ended at Daberath.
The eastern border went up to Japhia 13and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah 14and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
15Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
16This is the tribal land, and these are the towns and villages of the Zebulun clans.
Issachar's Land
17-23Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following 16 towns with their surrounding villages:
Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh.
Asher's Land
24-26Asher was the fifth tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans included the following towns:
Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph, Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal.
Asher's southern border ran from the Mediterranean Sea southeast along the Shihor-Libnath River at the foot of Mount Carmel, 27then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel, 28Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon. 29-31Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.
Asher had a total of 22 towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob.
Naphtali's Land
32-34Naphtali was the sixth tribe chosen to receive land. The southern border for its clans started in the west, where the tribal lands of Asher and Zebulun meet near Hukkok. From that point it ran east and southeast along the border with Zebulun as far as Aznoth-Tabor. From there the border went east to Heleph, Adami-Nekeb, Jabneel, then to the town called Oak in Zaanannim, and Lakkum. The southern border ended at the Jordan River, at the edge of the town named Jehudah. Naphtali shared a border with Asher on the west.
35-39The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included 19 towns with their surrounding villages. The following towns had walls around them:
Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth, Adamah, Ramah, Hazor, Kedesh, Edrei, Enhazor, Iron, Migdalel, Horem, Beth-Anath, and Beth-Shemesh.
Dan's Land
40-46Dan was the seventh tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans included the following towns:
Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh, Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah, Elon, Timnah, Ekron, Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath, Jehud, Azor, Beneberak, Gath-Rimmon, Mejarkon, and Rakkon.
Dan's tribal land went almost as far as Joppa. 47-48 Its clans received this land and these towns with their surrounding villages.
Later, when enemies forced them to leave their tribal land, they went to the town of Leshem. They attacked the town, captured it, and killed the people who lived there. Then they settled there themselves and renamed the town Dan after their ancestor.
Joshua's Land
49-51The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_text:
A hɛri bɔr la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Simɛɔn dee wia
1A hɛri bɔnnaa nɛɛhiŋ biini, Simɛɔn dee domeezii ba kaa tɛɛ hiŋ. Ba kapɛttɛ bɔr faa du Juda hɛri biinii. 2Ba bolzenaare faa,
Bɛɛsiba, Siiba, Mɔlada, 3Hazar Sual, Bala, Ɛzɛm, 4Ɛltɔlad, Bɛtul, bolzeŋ Hɔma, 5Ziklag, Bɛf Makabɔf, Hazar Susa, 6Bɛf Lɛbayɔf ani Saruhɛn. A maa du bolzenaa fidaahoro ni a boljigzi.
7Anla n kaa jaau, bolzenaa Ain, Rimɔn, Ɛta ani Asan. A ge du bolzenaa anaazu ani a boljigzi, 8ani boljigzi la maa n baraa la guŋŋ di ga chug Baalaf Bɛɛ baŋ kaa ra yir Rama u du Nɛgɛv la. Bɔra naabuu faa ɛɛ Simɛɔn dee domeezi kapɛttɛ diiribɔra. 9Ba faa mɔŋ Juda dee bɔr yenne tɛɛ Simɛɔn dee, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba bɔr la faa kannɔɔ werge. Awia, Simɛɔn dee hiŋ jaa na ba hor di lii Juda dee hor la biini.
A hɛri bɔr la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Zɛbulɔn dee wia
10Zɛbulɔn dee domeezii ba faa kpa a hɛri bɔra ahorohiŋ di tɛɛ. Ba hɛri magbɔɔ faa chɔɔwɔɔ guŋŋ di ga chug bolzeŋ Sarid. 11U magbɔɔ chi de di ga wiicholii di ga hel bolzeŋ Marala ga chug bolzeŋ Dabɛsɛf, di kaa lii de guŋŋ di ga hel gɔŋ la n du Jɔkniam wiifurii la. 12U keŋkere bɛl magbɔɔ ge ga Sarid wiifurii di ga zuu Kislɔf Tabɔ hɛri, di lii de ga hel bolzeŋ Dabɛraf, di bɛri ga hel bolzeŋ Jafia. 13U kaa chi de ga u wiifurii paga di ga hel bolzenaa Gaf Hɛfa ni Ɛf Kazin di ga Rimɔn lii, di bir chaŋ yembɛl banna yir Nia. 14Denii a hɛri magbɔɔ bar ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di ga hel bolzeŋ Hanatɔn di ga tuŋ Ifta Ɛl Waluu. 15Anla n faa kaa jaau, Kataf, Nahalal, Simrɔn, Idala ani Bɛtlihɛm. A bolzenaa faa du fidaanɛɛ ni a boljigzi.
16Bolzenaa naa ni a boljigzii faa Zɛbulɔn dee domeezi kapɛttɛ.
Isaka dee hɛri wia
17Isaka dee domeezii ba faa kpa a hɛri bɔra anaazuhiŋ tɛɛ. 18Bolzenaa la n faa jaa ba bɔr biinii keŋ, Jɛzriil, Kɛsulɔf, Sunɛm 19Hafaram, Siɔn, Anaharaf, 20Rabif, Kisiɔn, Ɛbɛz, 21Rɛmɛf, Ɛn Ganim, Ɛn Hada ani Bɛf Pazɛz. 22U magbɔɔ hiŋ ga de di ga chug Tabɔ ni Sahazuma ani Bɛf Sɛmɛs guŋŋ di ga tuŋ Jɔɔdan muu la. A bolzenaa maa faa du fidaanumbɛl ani a boljigzi.
23Isaka dee domeezi kapɛttɛ diiribɔttɛ guŋ.
Asɛ dee hɛri wia
24A hɛri bɔra anue hinnɛ ba kpa tɛɛ Asɛ dee domeezi. 25Bolzenaa la n faa jaa ba bɔr biinii keŋ, Hɛlkaf, Hali, Bɛtɛn, Aksaf, 26Alamɛlɛk, Amad ani Misal. U wiicholii magbɔɔ ga chug Muu Sihɔ Libnaf n du Bizeŋ Kamɛl zɛɛ. 27U magbɔɔ kaa chi de di bir ga wiifurii di chaŋ bolzeŋ Bɛf Dagɔn di ga chug Zɛbulɔn dee hɛri magbɔɔ ni Ifta Ɛl Waluu, di ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di ga chug bolzenaa Bɛf Ɛmɛk ani Nɛyɛl, di bɛri Kabul n du nomɛɛl paga 28ni Ɛbrɔn, Rɛhɔb, Hamɔn ani Kana guŋŋ di ga hel bolzeŋ Saidɔn. 29U magbɔɔ hiŋ kaa bir chaŋ bolzeŋ Rama di ga hel bolzeŋkpeg Taaya, di bir chaŋ yembɛl banna yir Hɔsa, di ga Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn la n du Akzib hɛri la, 30Uma, Afɛk ani Rɛhɔb. A maa du bolzenaa tokko ni anɛɛ ni a boljigzi.
31Asɛ dee domeezi kapɛttɛ diiribɔttɛ faa guŋ.
Naftali dee hɛri wia
32A hɛri bɔra anumbɛl hinnɛ ba kpa tɛɛ Naftali dee domeezi.
33Ba magbɔɔ faa faarɔɔrɛ di lii Hɛlɛf di ga hel daazeŋ bɛl n du Zaananim, di ga bɛri hɛssi Adami Nɛkɛb ani Jabniil, di ga hel Lakum, di ga tuŋ Jɔɔdan muu. 34U wiicholii magbɔɔ la ge ga bolzenaa Aznɔf Tabɔ ani Hukkɔk lii, di faa ga chug Zɛbulɔn n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere, di ga chug Asɛ n du wiicholii, di ga chug Jɔɔdan muu n du wiifurii. 35Ba bolzeŋkpegaa faa Zidim, Zɛɛ, Hammaf, Rakaf, Kinɛrɛf, 36Adama, Rama, Hazɔr, 37Kɛdɛs, Ɛdrɛi, Ɛn Hazɔr, 38Ayɔn, Migdal Ɛl, Hɔrɛm, Bɛf Anaf ani Bɛf Sɛmɛs. A maa du bolzenaa fidikabɛl ani a boljigzi.
39Naftali dee domeezi kapɛttɛ diiribɔttɛ faa guŋ.
Dan dee hɛri wia
40A hɛri bɔra aniidaanɛɛ hinnɛ ba kpa tɛɛ Dan dee domeezi. 41Bolzenaa la n faa jaa Dan dee kapɛttɛ ninɛɛ keŋ, Zɔra, Ɛstayɔl, Ir Sɛmɛs, 42Saalbim, Aijalɔn, Itla, 43Ɛlɔn, Timna, Ɛkrɔn, 44Ɛltɛkɛ, Gibɛtɔn, Baalaf, 45Jɛhud, Bɛnɛ Bɛrak, Gaf Rimɔn, 46Mɛ Jakɔn ani Rakɔn, di kpa hɛri la n chaŋ Jɔpa la.
47Ka a faa kpolloo tɛɛ Dan dee bá di ba kapɛttɛ bɔr. Awia, ba faa la ga lɔ bolzeŋ Layis hina, di kpu baa ka so de, di kpa ba naabaal sɔŋ Dan dawuu. 48A bolzenaa naa ni a boljigzii faa ɛɛ Dan dee domeezi kapɛttɛ bɔr.
Josua dee hɛri wia
49Izrɛl hina n wa bɔnni a hɛri tuŋ, ba jaa kpa u yembɛl tɛɛ Nun biibaal Josua, u ɛɛ u kapɛttɛ ba biini, 50gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ la. Ba tɛu bolzeŋ Timnaf Sɛra la uŋ faa suŋŋɛɛ, u du Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri la. U bir kuaruu ma, di so de.
51A bɔra naabuu Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza, Nun biibaal Josua ani Izrɛl dizi domeezi sitɔɔra faa ta kuna Silo, di bɔnni, Kɔraawiizi see, U Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua. Kennaabuu ba faa bɔnni a hɛri.

english_text:
The Safe Towns
(Numbers 35.9-15; Deuteronomy 19.1-13)
1 One day the Lord told Joshua:
2When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns. 3-4If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
5One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies. 6The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder.
Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
7The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns:
Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
8The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River:
Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
9These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_text:
Hinlɛɛi bolzenaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be, 2“Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be bá lizi bolzenaa la aŋhina, á ɛɛ bolzenaa la nɛra n niŋ ɔɔ chɔ ga zuu di lɛɛ bahinaa gunla miŋ faa gillɛ Moosis ŋɔ i be la. 3Di nɛr maa wa kpu nɛr di waa kuttɛɛ, u daŋ wer chɔ la de, di lɛɛ u hiŋ, a lalii lulli himmaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpu nɛr la n kpuu la, gilɛɛ wa nau, di kpuu turgi a kim. 4Di a hiŋ wa chɔwɔɔ ú ga zuu bolzenaa naa bɛl maa, ú chi a bol dominuuzeŋ, di ŋɔ u nua wia tɛɛ a bol nabɔnzi. Ba jaa lɛɛu di tɛu bɔr u ni baa du. 5Di lalii la lulli himmaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpuu la, wa duŋŋi unla n kpuu la luge, ú wa kpuu turgi a kim, á bol hina gilɛɛ wa kpau ra tɛu, dikuubɛɛwiai, waa kuttɛɛ kpu u nɛr hiŋ. 6U daŋ du a bolzeŋ guŋŋ ba wa diu seriya nɛra baaŋ, di kaa ra ba saŋa la Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la n du de a saŋa hiŋ n niŋ wa siu. Denii ú jaa bir la u bol la un chɔwɛɛ lii la.”
7Awia, ba jaa lizi bolzeŋ Kɛdɛs n du Naftali giŋgimee bɔr, Galilii hɛri, di lizi bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm n du bolzeŋ Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri bɔr ani bolzeŋ Kiriaf Aaba la n ɛɛ bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, Juda dee giŋgimee hɛri la. 8Bolzenaa la baŋ faa lizɛɛ Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii ani bolzeŋ Jɛriko wiifurii hɛribɔduma lɛl labuu, Bɛza n du Rubin dee hɛri biini ni Ramɔf n du Giliad hɛri, Gad dee bɔr ani Golan n du Basan, Manasɛ dee bɔr. 9Izrɛl hinuu maa gɛɛ hɔɔhri la maa n du ba biini wa kpu nɛr di waa kuttɛɛ, daŋ wer chɔ ga zuu a bola naa bɛl maa, lalii la lulli himmaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpu nɛr la n kpuu la, gilɛɛ wa nau di kpu, di ba waa u seriya diwee nɛra baaŋ.

english_text:
Levi's Towns
1-2 While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
3Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi. 4The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive.
The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given 13 towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. 5The other members of the Kohath clans received 10 towns from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and West Manasseh. 6The clans that were descendants of Gershon were given 13 towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and East Manasseh. 7The clans that were descendants of Merari received 12 towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
8The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did.
Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
9-19The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given 13 towns and the pastureland around them. Nine of these towns were from the tribes of Judah and Simeon and four from Benjamin.
Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, Holon, Debir, Ashan, Juttah, and Beth-Shemesh were from Judah and Simeon. Hebron, located in the hill country of Judah, was earlier called Arba's Town. It had been named after Arba, the ancestor of the Anakim. Hebron's pasturelands went along with the town, but its farmlands and the villages around it had been given to Caleb. Hebron was also one of the Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Gibeon, Geba, Anathoth, and Almon were from Benjamin.
Towns from Ephraim, Dan, West Manasseh
20-26The rest of the Kohath clans of the Levi tribe received ten towns and the pastureland around them. Four of these towns were from the tribe of Ephraim, four from Dan, and two from West Manasseh.
Shechem, Gezer, Kibzaim, and Beth-Horon were from Ephraim. Shechem was located in the hill country, and it was also one of the Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Elteke, Gibbethon, Aijalon, and Gath-Rimmon were from Dan.
Taanach and Jibleam were from West Manasseh.
Towns from East Manasseh, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali
27-33The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received 13 towns and the pastureland around them. Two of these towns were from the tribe of East Manasseh, four from Issachar, four from Asher, and three from Naphtali.
Golan in Bashan and Beeshterah were from East Manasseh.
Kishion, Daberath, Jarmuth, and En-Gannim were from Issachar.
Mishal, Abdon, Helkath, and Rehob were from Asher.
Kedesh in Galilee, Hammothdor, and Kartan were from Naphtali. Golan in Bashan and Kedesh in Galilee were also Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Towns from Zebulun, Reuben, Gad
34-40The rest of the Levi clans were descendants of Merari, and they received twelve towns with the pastureland around them. Four towns were from the tribe of Zebulun, four from Reuben, and four from Gad.
Jokneam, Kartah, Rimmonah, and Nahalal were from Zebulun.
Bezer, Jazah, Kedemoth, and Mephaath were from Reuben. Bezer was located in the desert flatlands east of the Jordan River across from Jericho.
Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Jazer were from Gad.
Bezer and Ramoth in Gilead were Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
41-42The people of the Levi tribe had a total of 48 towns within Israel, and they had pastures around each one of their towns.
Israel Settles in the Land
43The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it. 44There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win. 45The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_text:
Levi dee bolzenaa wia
1Denii Levi dee nabɔnzi ba Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza, Nun biibaal Josua ani Izrɛl hina dizi nabɔnzi be, 2Silo la n du Keenan hɛri la, di wa ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis benii lugɔ ií tɛɛ yaa bolzenaa ya so ani bɔra la yaa sela ge n ninna di.” 3Awia, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la wia, Izrɛl hina la faa lizi ba bolzenaa ani ba sela diiribɔra di lii ba himmaa kapɛttɛzi biine, di tɛɛ Levi dee.
4Kɔhaf dee domeezi labuu ba feli bɔnni a bolzenaa tɛɛ, baabuu faa Levi dee di lii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Aarɔn naanna biini. Ba faa tɛɛ baabuu bolzenaa fidaahoro di lii Juda, Simɛɔn ani Bɛnjamin dizi hora biine. 5Ba lizi bolzenaa fi di lii Ɛfram ni Dan dizi domeezi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ hɛssi di tɛɛ Kɔhaf domee la n kawɛɛ la, a birgi ba hora.
6Isaka, Asɛ, Naftali dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ la domeezi n du Basan hɛri la, bolzenaa fidaahoroo ba tɛɛ Gɛsɔn naanna.
7Rubin, Gad ani Zɛbulɔn dizi kpa bolzenaa fidaanɛɛ tɛɛ Mɛrari naanna.
8Awia, Izrɛl hina hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis, lugɔ ú bɔnni bolzenaa ani sela diiribɔra tɛɛ Levi dee la.
9Izrɛl hina lizi a bolzenaa naa lii Juda ani Simɛɔn dizi hora biini. 10A keŋ bolzenaare ba kpa tɛɛ Aarɔn naanna la n jaa Kɔhaf domee la n du Levi dee biini la, di lii kuna la baŋ tawɛɛ, a feli chol ba ni la wia.
11Ba kpa bolzeŋ Kiriaf Aaba la n du Juda hɛri giŋgimee bɔr ni u sela diiribɔra di jaa. 12Ka hɛri la ni a boljigzi la n bar bolzeŋ labuu ba faa feli kpa tɛɛ Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb, a ɛɛ u kapɛttɛ.
13Bolzenaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Aarɔn naannaa, hinlɛɛi bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, nɛr ɔɔ wer chɔ la de, di u wa kpu nɛr, di waa kuttɛɛ ni Libna, 14Jatir, Ɛstɛmɔa, 15Hɔlɔn, Dɛbir, 16Ain, Juta ani Bɛf Sɛmɛs. Bolzenaa kabɛl naa ani a sela diiribɔraa ba lizi lii Juda ni Simɛɔn dizi biine.
17Bolzenaa la baŋ lizɛɛ lii Bɛnjamin dee biini di tɛɛ baabuu, Gibiɔn, Gɛba, 18Anatɔf, Almɔn ani a sela diiribɔra. A ge du bolzenaa anaazu.
19Bolzenaa fidaahoro ni a sela diiribɔraa ba faa kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Aarɔn naanna la.
20Kɔhaf domeezi la n lii Levi dee biini la n kawɛɛ labuu, ba kpa bolzenaa naa ni a sela diiribɔra, di lii Ɛfram dee biini di tɛɛ baa.
21Bolzenaa anaazuu ba kpa tɛɛ baa. Aabuu, hinlɛɛi bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm la n du Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri ni u sela diiribɔra ni Gɛza, 22Kibzam, Bɛf Hɔrɔn ani a sela diiribɔra.
23Bolzenaa anaazu naabuu ba tɛɛ baa di lii Dan dee bɔr biini, Ɛltɛkɛ, Gibɛtɔn, 24Aijalɔn, Gaf Rimɔn ani a sela diiribɔra.
25Bolzenaa la Manasɛ dee yeŋ ge n lizɛɛ tɛɛ baabuu keŋ, Taanak ni Gaf Rimɔn ani a sela diiribɔra, a ge du bolzenaa anɛɛ.
26Bolzenaa fi naa ni a sela diiribɔraa ba faa lizi tɛɛ Kɔhaf domeezi la n kawɛɛ.
27Gɛsɔn domee la n lii Levi dee biini la ge kaa na bolzenaa anɛɛ naa,
di lii Manasɛ dee yeŋ la be.
Hinlɛɛi bolzeŋ Golan n du Basan hɛri la ni Bi Ɛstara ani a sela diiribɔra.
28Bolzenaa la baŋ nawɛɛ lii Isaka dee bɔr biinii keŋ,
Kisiɔn, Dabɛraf, 29Jamuf, Ɛn Ganim ani a sela diiribɔra. A ge du bolzenaa anaazu.
30Asɛ ge dee bɔr biini, bolzenaa la baŋ nawɛɛrɛ, Misal, Abdɔn, 31Hɛlkaf, Rɛhɔb ani a sela diiribɔra. A ge du bolzenaa anaazu.
32Di kaa lii Naftali dee biini,
hinlɛɛi bolzeŋ Kɛdɛs n du Galilii hɛri, Hamɔf Dɔɔ, Katan ani a sela diiribɔra, a ge du bolzenaa ahoro.
33Bolzenaa fidaahoro ani a sela diiribɔraa ba lizi tɛɛ Gɛsɔn domeezi la.
34Levi dee la n kawɛɛ di ɛɛ Mɛrari domee hina la genii ba kpa bolzenaa naa ge tɛɛ di lii Zɛbulɔn dee hɛri. Aabuu, Jɔkniam, Kata, 35Dimna ani Nahalal. A ge du bolzenaa anaazu ni a sela diiribɔra.
36Rubin dee biini, bolzenaa la baŋ nawɛɛrɛ keŋ, Bɛza, Jahaz, 37Kɛdɛmɔf ani Mɛfaaf. A ge du bolzenaa anaazu ni a sela diiribɔra.
38Di lii Gad dee ge bɔr biini, bolzenaa la baŋ nawɛɛrɛ keŋ, hinlɛɛi bolzeŋ Ramɔf la n du Giliad hɛri la ni Mahanam, 39Hɛsbɔn ani Jaza. A ge du bolzenaa anaazu ani a sela diiribɔra.
40Bolzenaa fidaanɛɛrɛ ba faa lizi tɛɛ Mɛrari domeezi la n faa ɛɛ Levi dee la n kawɛɛ.
41Bolzenaa la baŋ faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Levi dee di lii Izrɛl hina hɛri magazi la maa du, bolzenaa tokkoanɛɛ ni ŋmantannaazi ani a sela diiribɔra. 42A bolzenaa naa bɛl maanii faa dɔɔ sela diiribɔr di baruu chem.
43Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa hɛri la maa uŋ faa hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ u daŋ tɛɛ ba naabaala la, ba faa wer di kpegli ba dɔma, ka foozi de maa di so. 44Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ baabuuu bampirsɔna a hɛri maa biini, gunla himmaa uŋ faa hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ba naabaala la. Ba dɔma bɛl maa faa waa wette kpegli baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa kpa ba dɔmaa di du ba nonee biini. 45Nuuŋɔɔlinanaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la maanii wa ɛɛwɛ ni wibii.

english_text:
The Two and a Half Tribes Return Home
1Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
2-3 You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives. 4The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
5Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
6-9You've become rich from what you've taken from your enemies. You have big herds of cattle, lots of silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and plenty of clothes. Take everything home with you and share with the people of your tribe.
I pray that God will be kind to you. You are now free to go home.
The tribes of Reuben and Gad started back to Gilead, their own land. Moses had given the land of Bashan to the East Manasseh tribe, so they started back along with Reuben and Gad. God had told Moses that these two and a half tribes should conquer Gilead and Bashan, and they had done so.
Joshua had given land west of the Jordan River to the other half of the Manasseh tribe, so they stayed at Shiloh in the land of Canaan with the rest of the Israelites.
10-11The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river.
When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done, 12the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes. 13But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes. 14Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
15Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
16 All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him? 17 Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin. 18Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again.
If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation. 19If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar. 20 Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
21The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
22The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar, 23and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
24-25We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.”
Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord. 26That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord. 27-29To build another altar for offering sacrifices would be the same as turning our backs on the Lord and rebelling against him. We could never do that! No, we built the altar to remind us and you and the generations to come that we will worship the Lord. And so we will keep bringing our sacrifices to the Lord's altar, there in front of his sacred tent. Now your descendants will never be able to say to our descendants, “You can't worship the Lord.”
But if they do say this, our descendants can answer back, “Look at this altar our ancestors built! It's like the Lord's altar, but it isn't for offering sacrifices. It's here to remind us and you that we belong to the Lord, just as much as you do.”
30-31Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
32Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes. 33The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
34The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_text:
Wiifurii hina dizi n bittɛ la ba bola wia
1Denii Josua yir Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ ba maa chaali bɔkpaŋ, 2u ŋɔ ba be, “Ii ɛɛ wii la maa Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n ŋɔwɛɛ labuu, di kaa nuu n nua di ɛɛ wia la maa miŋ ŋɔ ii ɛɛ la. 3Haali di wa lii ni zinaa, ii haa waa ii lulla Izrɛl hina gillɛ ha tama maa. Ii wettoo du tau nɛnnɛ, di hiŋ Gbɔgni la maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia labuu. 4Awia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n tɛɛ ii lulla heezaa gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la, ií bir la ii bola la n du hɛri la Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia, Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la. 5Ka ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di hiŋ Gbɔgni la maa Moosis n tɛɛ ia la. Ií nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi ani u widaulaa maa. Ií lawuu chigigi, di ra humuu ni ii biine ni ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa.”
6Denii Josua suŋŋi wiizi di kissi baa, ka ta baa ŋmɛnnɛ ba kaali ba bola. 7Moosis faa kpa Basan hɛrii di tɛɛ Manasɛ dee yeŋ. Di kaa kpa Jɔɔdan muu wiicholii hɛri la ge tɛɛ ba dee yeŋ la n kawɛɛ. Denii Josua suŋŋi wiizi di kissi baa, ka ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ ba kaali, 8di ŋɔ, “Ií bir la ii bola ga bɔnni ii daama werge naa iiŋ paagɛɛ lii ii dɔma be naa, tɛɛ ii lulla la maa, ii sela, saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ, danyɛ, lugbia ani ii laala la maa.”
9Awia, Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ la maa, gil Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ Silo n du Keenan hɛri, ka bir di ra la Giliad n ɛɛ ba himmaa hɛri, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be di ŋɔ ú tɛɛ baa la.
10Baŋ wa hel bol la banna yir Gɛlilɔf n dugli Jɔɔdan muu, Keenan hɛri la, Rubin ani Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee la yeŋ maa kpau di ma mbusu lizibɔzeŋ de. 11Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba ma mbusu lizibɔttɛ Gɛlilɔf, n dugli Jɔɔdan muu, Keenan hɛri magbɔɔ ba keŋkere la, 12ba maa izi kakpaŋ di ga chaali Silo, di ɛɛ sirya bá la ga lɔ baa laal.
13Awia, Izrɛl hina feli hum Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza biibaal Finɛhas, ú la Giliad di ga huuzi Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ la de. 14U ni Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra fii ba faa hum. Dizi fi la biini, nɛkpaŋkpaŋaa ba lizi, bɛl maa faa ɛɛ dia nabɔma, Izrɛl domeezi la biini.
15Baŋ ga hel Giliad hɛri la, ba ŋɔ tɛɛ Rubin, Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ la maa be, 16“Yaa chigɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra maa naarɛ di ra ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ni, di bir har kpuu, ka ma ii himmaa mbusu lizibɔr di vɛɛuwɛi? 17Ii ra liizi yaa wichɔgaa la yaa n ɛɛwɛ Bizeŋ Pɛɔ, Kɔraawiizi kpa wiilchɔgaa tɔɔri u nɛra la. Yaa haa ra di tɔɔrɔɔrɛ dikuu a wia. A wichɔgii naa waa kukkɛɛa? 18Ii daŋ vɛɛ u hiŋaa filaŋkeŋ? Di ii vɛɛ u hiŋaa zinaa, u baaŋ daŋ fuuh Izrɛl hina maa ni kɛrɛ. 19Di ii ra fɛu lugɔ ii hɛri waa dɛg Kɔraawiizi jaamaa, amɔ, ií gi a muu naa di ra ba yaa be Kɔraawiizi hɛri, bɔr la Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia n duwɛɛ, ya bɔnni a hɛri di tɛɛ ia. Ka ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua gɛɛ yaa nua, di kaa waa ma mbusu lizibɔr di ra tɛɛ iihinaa. Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔkpaŋkpaŋ bɛnnɛ du de, bɛl maa waa kaa hoo. 20Kɔraawiizi faa waa Izrɛl hina maa duwɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ, saŋa la Zɛra biibaal Akan n faa ŋmɛɛ kuna la baŋ lizɛɛ di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi laa? U bɛŋ lɛi faa siuwɛ dikuu a wichɔgaa hiŋ wia.”
21Denii Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ la bir ŋɔ a Izrɛl hina yeŋ domeezi nabɔnzi hiŋ be, 22“Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ bɛnnɛ du de! U bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi! U bɛnnɛ zum wii la wia yaa n mau. Yaa ra nyiŋŋuu ii ge zum guŋ! Di yaa dɔɔ dignikpegaa ya vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua, amɔ, ií gilɛɛ gil yá kaa du de ni miibɔɔ zinaa. 23Di yaa ma mbusu lizibɔttɛ di tɛɛ yaa hinaa, lugɔ ya bir har kpu Kɔraawiizi, gɛɛ yaa n niŋ kpa de di birgi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa gɛɛ mia gɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizibɔr, guŋwaa Kɔ́raawiizi himmaa tɛr yaa digna.
24Gunlɛi! Ɔnsiirɛ lau yaa, yaa mau, dikuubɛɛwiai, kɛrɛ bɛl ii naanna gilɛɛ wa ŋɔ yaa naanna be, ‘Bɛɛ ii ni Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la dɔɔi? 25Kɔraawiizii kpa Jɔɔdan muu hiŋ di ɛɛ yaa ni ia magbɔɔ, ii ni Kɔraawiizi waa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ. Awia, ii naanna daŋ wer gil yaa naanna vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaamaa.’
26Awiarɛ yaa ma mbusu lizibɔr, ka waa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa gɛɛ mbusuzi lizibɔr ɛɛwɛ. 27Ka u daŋ ɛɛ daansɛɛ kuŋ tɛɛ yaa ni ia filaŋkeŋ ani jiminizi maa n niŋ ba, lugɔ ya ra jaami Kɔraawiizi u Tanti Dia ni yaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, mbusuzi lizaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa. Denii ii naanna wàá wer ŋɔ yaa naanna be, ‘Ií ni Kɔraawiizi waa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ.’
28Di ba wa ŋɔ guŋ, yaa naanna daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Ií na, mbusu lizibɔr naabuu yaa naabaala ma, u li Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la. Ba wàá lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa gɛɛ mbusuzi lizaa u ni, u ɛɛ daansɛɛ kunnɛ tɛɛ yaa ni ia.’
29Kɔ́raawiizi ra la a ni bɔɔnɛɛ, ya waa vɛɛ u nua hiŋaa gɛɛ di wa bir luŋ kpuu, di ma yaa himmaa mbusu lizibɔr, di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni mbusuzi lizaa mia ani mbusuzi lizaa maa u ni. Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la mbusu lizibɔr naa n chigɛ u Tanti Dia dominua la bɛnnɛ dɛkkɛ banna ɛɛ guŋ u ni.”
30Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Finɛhas ani a domeezi sitɔɔra fi la maa, n wa nuu gunla Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ n ŋɔwɛɛ la, ba bɔra jaa sɔɔni baa werge maa. 31Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza biibaal Finɛhas ŋɔ ba be, “Zinaa, yaa zummɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du yaa benii, dikuu iiŋ waa wichɔgaa maa ɛɛwɛ di zuu u ni gunla yaa n faa fɛwɛɛ la wia. Ka ii lɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa ha, di lii Kɔraawiizi baaŋ biini.”
32Denii Ɛliaza biibaal Finɛhas ani nabɔnzi la jaa gil baa Giliad hɛri, ka bir la Keenan di jaa ga ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, wii la maa n ɛɛwɛ. 33Denii Izrɛl hina maa bɔra jaa sɔɔni baa werge maa, ba ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi. Ba waa kaa ra liizi lugɔ ba ni baa yoo laal, di chɔgi ba hɛri.
34Rubin ani Gad dizi la maa jaa ra yir mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ mawɛɛ la, ‘Daansɛɛ.’ Di kaa ŋɔ, “U ɛɛ daansɛɛrɛ tɛɛ yaa ni baa maa lugɔ Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ du de.”

english_text:
Joshua's Farewell Speech
1The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age. 2One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them:
I am now very old. 3You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land. 4-5There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
6Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
7Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods. 8Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
9When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you. 10 Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised. 11Be sure to always love the Lord your God. 12-13Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
14I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken. 15-16Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
translation_text:
Josua wiŋɔtuna Izrɛl sitɔɔra be wia
1Biŋkpila n wa bɛrɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi jaa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina heezaa di lii ba dɔma be. A saŋa di Josua jaa zɛŋ werge, 2u chaali Izrɛl hina maa, ba nabɔnzi ani ba sitɔɔra, di ŋɔ ba be, “N jaa zɛŋuu werge filaŋkeŋ. 3Ii himmaa na wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛ hɛssi naa maa hinaa, dikuu ii wia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu faa naawɛ tɛɛ ia. 4Ií ra liizi gunla miŋ bɔnni a hɛri tɛɛ ia, u ɛɛ ii dizi kapɛttɛ, di lii hɛssi la yaa n haa waa wette lɛɛ ani anla yaa n lɛɛwɛ maa, di lii Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii hɛri la guŋŋ, di ga hel Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn la, n du wiicholii la. 5Hɛssi naa maa daŋ birgi ii hora, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ duŋŋi a nɛra maa di lii de filaŋkeŋ, ka ii ga so de, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia la.
6Awia, ií chiiri zɛɛ, di ra du tau, di ra hiŋ wia la maa un dauwɛ tɛɛ ia, Moosis Gbɔgni Hɔŋ biini la nɛnnɛ. Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ a hiŋaa tama maa. 7Ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ wa gil ii ni hɛssi naa hina n haa du ii be naa, wàá kpau wiimaa biini gɛɛ di wàá yirgi ba vuga sɔna di ra hɛɛhzaa. Ií gilɛɛ waa kuaraa gɛɛ di togni ra jaamaa. 8Ií lau Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la chigigi, gunla iin lawuu di wa lii zinaa naa.
9Kɔraawiizii duŋŋi nɛkpega la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge di lii hɛssi naa biini di tɛɛ ia, di wa lii ni zinaa, di nɛr maa haa waa wette kpegli ia. 10Ii bɛl maa daŋ wer duŋŋi nɛra kagboŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu naawɛ di ra tɛɛ ia, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia la. 11Awia, ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la.
12Ka di ii wa bir luŋ kpuu, di gil ii ni a hɛssi hina n kawɛɛ la dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, di ra paagi dɔŋa biizi, ii ni baa kpau di ra ɛɛ wia, 13guŋwaa, ii zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, wàá ka duŋŋi a hɛssi naa hina lii ii hɛri naa biini. Ba daŋ du ii be di ɛɛ lugɔ ŋmɛmbizi ni sidɛɛzi, di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ virinzi di ra viiri ii hara ani sɔɔhri di ra tɔɔhzi i siwee guŋŋ ii wa dim, di lii a hɛrsum naa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n tɛɛ ia naa biini.”
14Josua kaa ŋɔ, “Filaŋkeŋ, n saŋa jaa heluu. Ii maa zummɔ ni ii biine, ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa lugɔ nuuŋɔɔlinanaa la maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia la, bɛl maa waa ɛɛwɛ huhzi. A maanii u ɛɛ, waa bɛl maa ɛɛwɛ huhzi! 15Gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nuuŋɔɔlinanaa la maa n wa ɛɛwɛ la, gunnɛ ú gil wichɔgaa la ge maa uŋ karfi ia lugɔ a daŋ huuzi ia la, ɛɛ guŋŋ ú wa chɔgi ia lii hɛrsum naa uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia naa biini. 16Di ii haŋ wa vɛɛ u ni ia Nuukpaŋ la uŋ karfi ia la wia, ka la gaa kuari vuga di ra tognaa, u baaŋ daŋ fuuh ii ni, ú dim ia manaŋ lii hɛrsum naa uŋ tɛɛ ia naa biini.”

english_text:
We Will Worship and Obey the Lord
1Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent. 2 Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel:
Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor. 3 But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants. 4 Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
5-6 Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea. 7Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched.
You lived in the desert for a long time, 8 then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land. 9 King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you. 10But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
11 You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all. 12 Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
13 You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
14Then Joshua told the people:
Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt. 15But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
16The people answered:
We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord. 17The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went. 18And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
19Joshua said:
The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it. 20If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
21But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
22Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?”
“Yes, it's true,” they answered.
23Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
24The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
25Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel 26and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem 27and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
28Joshua sent everyone back to their homes.
Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
29Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of 110. 30 The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
31As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
32 When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for 100 pieces of silver from Hamor, the founder of Shechem. The town and the field both became part of the land belonging to the descendants of Joseph.
33When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi ni Izrɛl hina n kaa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ wia
1Denii Josua chaali Izrɛl dizi nabɔnzi, sitɔɔra, seriya diire ani ba nabɔnzenaa maa, ba wa chaali bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm Kɔraawiizi see.
2Josua ŋɔ a nɛra maa be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Faa la, ii naabaala, di kpa Abraham ni Nahɔ mɛɛ Tɛra jaa, faa sogo Muu Yufretis keŋkere la hinnɛ di faa ra kuari vuga. 3Ka n wa lizi ii naabaal Abraham, di kpogluu gi Muu Yufretis, di la ga zuu Keenan hɛri di tɛu naanna kpila. N tɛubuu Aizik, 4u lul Jekɔb ni Ɛsau. N kpa Ɛdɔm giŋgimee hɛri la tɛɛ Ɛsau, ka Jekɔb ni u biibaala waa la Ijip hɛri di ga so de.
