But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
27Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert. 28Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
29Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert. 30I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
31By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon. 32They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood. 33 Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.”
“You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here. 34Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.”
That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there. 35It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord.
The Army Rescues Jonathan
36Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!”
The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.”
“Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
37Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?”
This time God did not answer. 38Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering. 39I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.”
No one said a word.
40Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.”
Everyone agreed.
41 Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?”
The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army. 42Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.”
The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned. 43“Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!”
“I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
44“Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
45“No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
46Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home.
Saul Fights His Enemies
47-48When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles.
Saul's Family
49-51Saul's wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz. They had three sons: Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. They also had two daughters: The older one was Merab, and the younger one was Michal.
Abner, Saul's cousin, was the commander of the army. Saul's father Kish and Abner's father Ner were sons of Abiel.
War with the Philistines
52Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_text:
1A hɔl bɛl Jonatan izi di ŋɔ biipɔllii la n na kpogli u dɔŋkuna la be, “Ba yá la a keŋkere la Filisti hina n chɔɔwɛ la.” Unna ɛɛ annii maa, di waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ u mɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl be.
2A saŋa, di Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra ge faa sogo Gibia danzɛɛkɛrii nɔna n lugɔ pomegranet daa zɛɛ, yembɛl banna yir Migrɔn. A laallɔɔra la maa n faa du u be la hel kalfaanumbɛl. 3Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahija gba faa jaa ba ninɛɛ de, di laali Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ tagtakpurii ifɔd. U faa ɛɛ Ikabɔd kpɛɛma Ahitub biibaallɛ, Ahitub ge mɛɛrɛ faa Finɛhas. Finɛhas ge mɛɛrɛ Ɛli la n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ di du Silo, di ra humuu la. Nɛr maa faa waa zummɛ lugɔ Jonatan waa kaa du ba be.
4Ŋmɛnɛɛ la n faa chɔɔwɛ di ra la Mikmas, Jonatan faa ga di ra la Filisti hina chɔɔribɔr la, faa chɔɔ bizenaa anɛɛ baambaannɛ. A bizenaa sɔnaa Bɔzɛz ani Sɛnɛ. 5A bizeŋ bɛl chi wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di chaŋ Mikmas, bɛl ge chi wiifurii nodig wiikakag di chaŋ Gɛba.
6Jonatan ŋɔ biipɔllii la n kpogli u dɔŋkuna la be, “Ba yá la Filisti hina naa n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la chɔɔribɔr. Aŋhinabe, Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ yaa nua di yoo tɛɛ yaa. Wiimaa wàá wer tɔ Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ ú lɛɛ yaa huhzi, haali di yaa du tama gɛɛ yaa kpillɔ gba.”
7Denii a biipɔllii ŋɔ u be, “Wii la maa dee hinna nyiŋŋi i ɛɛ, n chigɔ i hattɛ ani n biini, n kpegzi ani n nfɛrɛ maa.”
8Denii Jonatan ŋɔ u be, “Guŋwaa, ba yá la a Filisti hina be, di ga gil bá na yaa. 9Di ba wa ŋɔ yaa be lugɔ yá chi de, bá ba yaa be, yaa daŋ chi, yaa wàá la ba be. 10Ka di ba wa ŋɔ yá ra ba ba be waa, yaa daŋ tinni di la ba be de. A gunnɛ ya kpa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kpa baabuu du yaa nonee biine.”
11Denii ba jaa kpa ba hiŋ di lii chaaŋ di bagli Filisti hina. Filisti hina ŋɔ, “Ií na! Hibru hinaa gɔŋŋɛɛ di ra lii bɔɔni la biine baŋ suahzɛɛ, di ra ba la.” 12Filisti hina chi ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ, ka pozi Jonatan ni a biipɔllii hiŋ ni werge maa, di ŋɔ, “Ií tuzi hel ka na, yaa daŋ bagli ia wii bɛl!”
Denii Jonatan ŋɔ a biipɔllii la n kpogli u dɔŋkuna hiŋ be, “Tinni di ra hiŋiŋ. Kɔraawiizi kpa baabuu du Izrɛl hina nonee!”
13Denii Jonatan tɔ see di gɔŋŋi di ra tinni, u balii la n kpogli u dɔŋkuna la ge ra hiŋuu. Baŋ ga hel baa, Jonatan yagzi baa di ra haazi, u balii la ge jaa ra kpuuzi baa. 14A lugli pigaa hiŋ biini, Jonatan ni u balii hiŋ faa kpuuzi baala tokkoo, alugɔ kato keza biini.
Izrɛl hina n kpegli Filisti hina wia
15Denii ɔnsii ni bɔsai lau a Filisti hina maa. Laallɔɔra la n liwɛɛ bá ga yoo di foozi kuna ani laallɔɔra la n du ba chɔɔribɔr la biini la bɔra ra sa, hɛri zigli werge maa. Kɔraawiizii faa gillɛ a bɔsai werge chol ba ni la.
16Koori Sɔɔl laallɔɔra la n du Gibia, Bɛnjamin dee hɛri di ra du tau la na Filisti laallɔɔra n na yaari bɔr maa. 17Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ laallɔɔra la n du u be la, “Ií chaali yaa nɛra la maa bɔkpaŋ, yá zum banla n waa hoo yaa be.” Baŋ wa chaalɛɛ, ba na lugɔ Jonatan ni u baliirɛ waa hoo ba be.
18Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahija be, “Kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ba.” A guŋ saŋa, di u du Izrɛl hina la be. 19Koori Sɔɔl n na ŋɔ wia ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la maa, di Filisti hina bugmaa ra nyaŋŋi. Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ be, “Gil wiimaa ɛɛi!”
20Denii Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra la maa chaali di kpa la a laal bɔr. Baŋ ga hel de, ba na di Filisti hina la bugmaa nyaŋŋɔɔ, ba kpa tokobizi di ra ŋmɛnni dɔŋa. 21Hibru hina la n faa jaa a Filisti hina ni di la ba chɔɔribɔr la, bir lii di ga jaa Izrɛl hina la, n faa du Koori Sɔɔl ani Jonatan be la ni. 22Izrɛl hina la maa n faa suah Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri la, n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Filisti hina la maa chɔwɔɔ la, ba jaa lii ba, di wa jaa ba dɔŋahina ni a laal biini. 23Ba lɔ baa guŋŋ di ga bɛri bɔr la banna yir Bɛf Avɛn, Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ Izrɛl hina a hɔl hiŋ.
Wia la n ɛɛwɛ a laal harbɔɔ wia
24A saŋa naa, di lɔzi lau Izrɛl laallɔɔra, ba ra bɛɛli, dikuu Koori Sɔɔl n faa hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Nuuseei di nɛr la maa n niŋ di diwee mɔɔ, ka bɔr duani, di maa haŋ wa kpegli n dɔma.” Awia, ba bɛl maa faa waa diwee.
25Denii ba maa vol guŋŋ di ga zuu kɔr bɛl biini, di huuhnuurɛ su de maa. 26Huuhnuu su a daazi maa ni, ka ba bɛl maa wàá diwee, dikuu banna ɔm Koori Sɔɔl nuuseei la wia. 27Ka Jonatan waa faa waa nuuwɛ lugɔ u mɛɛ hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ lugɔ nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa di kummaa a hɔl hiŋ. Awia, u faa lalli u daŋkpala ga yag a huuhnuu, di kpa ga du u nua, u siwee chaani kakpaŋ. 28Denii a laallɔɔra bɛl ŋɔ u be, “I mɛɛ hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ di du gbɔg lugɔ di nɛr maa haŋ wa di kummaa, á gbɔg diu! Aabuu gillɛ nɛra naa maa ra bɛɛli la.”
29Denii Jonatan ŋɔ, “Tɔɔrɔɔrɛ n mɛɛ du yaa gunla. Miŋ di a huuh tama naa gba, ka ii na gunla n siwee n chaanɛɛ. 30Amɔ, di a laallɔɔra faa di Filisti hina diwee la baŋ foozee la aŋhina, a guŋ vii waa hiini baa werge maa? Yaa vii wàá kpuuzi a Filisti hina naa werge maa?”
31Izrɛl hina n wa kpuuzi Filisti hina guŋŋ di lii Mikmas di ga bolzeŋ Aijalɔn, kuuhni ni lɔzi jaa lau baa werge maa, a hɔl hiŋ. 32Ba kiiri lauri ba dɔma peeza, ba nauna ni a biizi, di kpua, di mɔnnaa huuri, di ra hee ni a challi. 33Denii nɛbɛl ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Na, a baalaa ɛɛ wichɔgaa di ra zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di ra hee ol ni chal.”
Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ii zuu Kɔraawiizi ninɛɛ la. Ií billi bizeŋ ba ɛŋ kakpaŋ.” 34U jaa ŋɔ, “La ga kali baa, dí bɛl maa lau u nauna ni peeza di ba bɔnnaa, di wa kɔrgaa hee. Ií gilɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di ra hee ol ni chal.”
Bɛl maa jaa lau u navarga a hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa ni, di ba de, di wa kɔrguu. 35Denii Koori Sɔɔl ma mbusu lizibɔr tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. U lugli mbusu lizibɔttɛ guŋ, uŋ mawɛɛ.
36Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gil ya la hamuŋa ni, di ga pig Filisti hina, di kpuuzi baa, di foozi ba kuna guŋŋ di ga hel chɔɔzimpikke ni, di gilɛɛ gil bɛl maa kaa ka.”
Ba maa ŋɔ u be, “Ɛɛ gunla maa n parii.”
Ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la ŋɔ, “Ií gil ya pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di na mɔɔ.”
37Koori Sɔɔl pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “Ń la ga pig Filisti hinaa? I daŋ kpa baa du yaa Izrɛl hina noneea?” Kɔraawiizi wɔɔ hagzɛɛ a hɔl hiŋ.
38Koori Sɔɔl jaa ŋɔ u laallɔɔra sitɔɔra maa be, “Ií chaali bɔnnaa, yá na wii la yaa n ɛɛwɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni zinaa. 39N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa, unla n lɛɛ Izrɛl hina la, di ŋɔ nua lugɔ haali di u haŋ wa di n biibaal Jonatan gba, bá kpuu.” Ka nɛr maa waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ.
40Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Izrɛl hina maa be, “Ií chi ende, ka n ge ni n biibaal Jonatan chi bɔnnaa.”
A nɛra maa ŋɔ, “Ɛɛ gunla n parii.”
41Koori Sɔɔl jaa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, di ŋɔ, “Bagliŋ a wii naa zɛɛ.” Denii ba ta kuna a chol Jonatan ni Sɔɔl ni, ka a nɛra waa maa lii. 42Koori Sɔɔl kaa ŋɔ, “Ií kaa taa dikuu n ni n biibaal Jonatan ge wia.” Baŋ wa taa, a chol Jonatan ni.
43Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Jonatan be, “Bagliŋ wii la hiŋ ɛɛwɛ.”
Jonatan ŋɔ u be, “Wibiire, n kpa n daŋkpalaa di chug huuhnuu tama di di. Amɔ, ń siu guŋ wiaa?”
44Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u be, “Di mɛɛ kpuwɛɛ, amɔ, Kɔraawiizi kpuŋ!”
45Ka a nɛra ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “A waa dɛkkɛ Jonatan n siuwɛ. Na gunla uŋ ɛɛ wizeŋ di lɛɛ Izrɛl hina ha. Akai! Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la sɔŋ biini, u nyuhuŋ gba wàá chol hɛri, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii hiinuu, u ɛɛ guŋ.” A nɛra faa ɛɛ gunnɛ di lɛɛ Jonatan, ba wɔɔ kpuwɛɛ.
46Denii Koori Sɔɔl jaa gil a Filisti hina duŋŋaa, ka ba bir kaali ba hɛri.
47Koori Sɔɔl n wa di kora Izrɛl hɛri, u faa volloo di lɔ ba dɔma la n soge di bar baa la. Baabuu, Moab, Ammɔn, Ɛdɔm hina, Zoba koora ani Filisti hina. Banla maa uŋ ga lɔwɛɛ, u ɔɔ kpegli baabuu. 48U yoowoo banni ni, di kpegli Amalɛk hina, di lɛɛ Izrɛl hina lii banla maa n ɔɔ faa ra lɔ baa laal la nonee biini.
Koori Sɔɔl diahina wia
49Koori Sɔɔl biibaalaa faa Jonatan, Isvi ani Malki Sua. U biihambinabɔma sɔnnɛ faa Mɛrab, u kalugu ge sɔnnɛ faa Mikal. 50U haaŋ sɔnnɛ faa Ahinoam, u ge mɛɛrɛ faa Ahimaz. Koori Sɔɔl laallɔɔra sitɔɔri ge sɔnnɛ faa Abna, u ge mɛɛrɛ faa Nɛɛr. Nɛɛr ge faa ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl naaraa. 51Koori Sɔɔl mɛɛ Kis ni Abna mɛɛ Nɛɛr faa ɛɛ Abiɛl biibaalaa.
52Di lii Koori Sɔɔl de dui saŋa maa, Izrɛl hina ni Filisti hina faa ra lɔ laallɛ werge maa. Koori Sɔɔl faa haŋ wa na biipɔllikpeg maa, u ɔɔ lawuubuu jaa u laallɔɔra ni.

english_text:
Saul Disobeys the Lord
1 One day, Samuel told Saul:
The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord: 2 “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
3“Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
4Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were 210,000 troops in all, and 10,000 of these were from Judah. Saul organized them, 5then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack. 6Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.”
The Kenites left, 7and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt. 8Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag. 9Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak.
The Lord Rejects Saul
10The Lord told Samuel, 11“Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.”
Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night. 12Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
13Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
14“Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
15“The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
16“Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.”
“All right,” Saul answered.
17Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel. 18When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites. 19Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
20“But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation. 21All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
22“Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him. 23Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
24“I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead. 25Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
26“No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
27 As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore! 28Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you. 29Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
30Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
31Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord. 32Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!”
Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
33But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
34Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah. 35Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again.
The Lord Chooses David To Be King
The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n vɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl wia
1A hɔl bɛl, Samuɛl ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Minuu Kɔraawiizi faa hum, n waarii nuu, di tɔi kora u nɛra Izrɛl hina ni. Awia, a nuu amaniye la n lii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ be. 2U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N daŋ tɛr Amalɛk hina digna, dikuu gunla baŋ faa pig Izrɛl hina di lɔ baa, saŋa la baŋ lii Ijip hɛri di ra ba la wia. 3Filaŋkeŋ, la ga lɔ Amalɛk hina, di chɔgi ba kundɔɔlaa maa nyaamm. Gilɛɛ waa gil baa. Kpuuzi ba baala, haana, bichalli ani ba biifulli, ba nauna ni peeza, nyugmazi ani kauzi maa nyaamm.’ ”
4Awia, Koori Sɔɔl faa chaali u laallɔɔra maa bolzeŋ Tɛlam. Ba kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ lii Izrɛl hɛri, ba kagboŋa fi ge lii Juda hɛri. 5Koori Sɔɔl izi di la bolzeŋ Amalɛk, di ga so ba saga waluu biini. 6U ŋɔ Kɛn hina be, “Ií lii Amalɛk hina be, ń gilɛɛ wa kpu ii ni baa maa. Dikuubɛɛwiai, ii faa ɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa winanaa, saŋa la baŋ lii Ijip hɛri di ra ba la.” Awia, Kɛn hina jaa bargi ba hiŋ di lii Amalɛk hina hiŋ ni.
7Denii Koori Sɔɔl la ga lɔ Amalɛk hina hiŋ, di lii Havila hɛri, guŋŋ di ga hel Suur n du Ijip hɛri wiifurii. 8Di lau Amalɛk hina Koori Agag, ka jaa kpu u nɛra la n kawɛɛ la maa nyaamm. 9Ka Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra faa gil Koori Agag ani penanaa, nananaa, a biinanaa ani kunla maa n wesse di ra par baa. Ba faa waa sɛɛwɛ bá chɔgi annii waa maa. Ka anla waa banna gbɛlli, a gɛrgi la waa maanii ba chɔgi nyaamm.
10Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Samuɛl be, 11“A ɛɛmbuu biinichɔg miŋ lizi Sɔɔl u ɛɛ koori, dikuubɛɛwiai, u bir hattɛ kpuŋ, waa sɛɛwɛ ú hiŋ n widaulaa.” Samuɛl biini chɔgi werge maa dikuu guŋ wia, u jaa lɔ wile di suŋŋi wiizi a hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi.
12Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Samuɛl izi di ra la ú ga na Koori Sɔɔl, ka nuu lugɔ u la bol bɛl banna yir Kamɛl di ga baŋ liize bii u tɛɛ u hiŋ sɔŋ, ka bɛri kaali Gilgal.
13Samuɛl n wa nau, Koori Sɔɔl jaamuu, ka ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi kissii! N ɛɛ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ń ɛɛ labuu tuŋ.”
14Ka Samuɛl ŋɔ, “Peeza ni nauna wiraa lɛi n na nuu naa?”
15Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “A laallɔɔraa lauraa lii Amalɛk hina la be. Ba lizi anla n wessee bá wa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la, ka anla waa maa n kawɛɛ maanii yaa kpu nyaamm.”
16Samuɛl bir ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Siigi! A nuu n be, ń ŋɔ wii la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛŋ dɛɛla saŋkara ni.”
Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ n be.”
17Samuɛl ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Haali hiŋ faa waa i hinna tɔgzi, ka hiŋ lɛi ɛɛ Izrɛl dizi la maa nabɔmaa? Kɔraawiizii waarii nuu, i ɛɛ Izrɛl hina koori, 18di humii, di baglii gunla hin niŋ ga ɛɛ, di ŋɔ, ‘La di ga chɔgi biinikpola hina Amalɛk hina la. Ga lɔ baa laal, di dim baa!’ 19Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua hiŋaa, ka hahzi foozi kuna lii a laal bɔr, di ɛɛ wichɔgaa zuu Kɔraawiizi ninɛi?”
20Ka Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “N hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ, di la ga ɛɛ wia la uŋ humiŋ ŋɔ ń ga ɛɛ labuu. N ga kpu Amalɛk hina la maa deere nyaamm. Ka lau ba Koori Agag la waa di ba. 21A laallɔɔra ge lauri ba nauna ani peeza la maa n kpekke la, di kpaa ba, bá wa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la, Gilgal biini.”
22Ka Samuɛl bir ŋɔ,
“Mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa
ni mbusuzi lizaarɛ
ɛɛ wizeŋ werge kaali
Kɔraawiizi nua hiŋaa?
Kɔraawiizi nua hiŋaarɛ bɔ mbusuzi lizaa.
Hiŋ hiŋ u nuarɛ bɔ,
hiŋ kpa pebala nuuri
lizi mbusu di fuuah tɛu.
23Dignikpega ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ Kɔraawiizi be lugɔ hinna vug,
kpoŋaa ge ɛɛ wichɔgaa
lugɔ vuga kuaraa.
Dikuu hiŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua wia,
u vɛɛibuu lugɔ
hàá kaa di a kora.”
24Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Samuɛl be, “Wibiire, n ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, di vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua hiŋaa ani i baglaa. N laallɔɔraa n faa ra ɔm. Aabuu gillɛ n nuu ba nua, di ɛɛ wia la n par baa. 25Awia, jaande maa, gil n wichɔgaa tɛŋ, ka ba ya la ń ga jaami Kɔraawiizi.”
26Ka Samuɛl ŋɔ u be, “Màá bir n nii la. I vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ, u gba vɛɛi lugɔ hàá ka ɛɛ Izrɛl hina koori!”
27Uŋ wa ŋɔ u be guŋ ka bir ŋɔ ú kaali, Koori Sɔɔl lau u tagtajaŋ nua tɛr, u piili. 28Samuɛl ŋɔ u be, “Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ Izrɛl hina koraa lii i be zinaa, di kpau tɛɛ i dɔŋhiŋ la n bɔi. 29Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, u dɔɔ girme la, waa kara ra kanni, waa u nfɛrɛ ra bir, waa newee ɛɛwɛ lugɔ u bir u nfɛrɛ.”
30Koori Sɔɔl kaa ŋɔ Samuɛl be, “N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, gaafura, ka kpaŋ girme Izrɛl hina ni ba nabɔnzi maa see, di gil yá bir la ń ga jaami Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la.” 31Awia, Samuɛl jaa bir u ni Koori Sɔɔl maa kpa di la, u ga jaami Kɔraawiizi.
32Denii Samuɛl ŋɔ, “Ií lau Amalɛk hina Koori Agag di wa tɛŋ.”
Agag ba u be, u bɔra ra sa, ka u ra fɛ u biini, “Wibii maa, ba wàá ka kpuŋ!”
33Ka Samuɛl bir ŋɔ u be,
“Gunla hiŋ haŋ kpa tokobi kpuuzi nɛra biizi,
ba maawaa nyaa baa la,
gunnɛ ń ge kpui,
í maa ge nyaai
alugɔ u dɔŋahina la.”
Denii Samuɛl kpuu Kɔraawiizi see Gilgal biini.
34Ka bir kaali Rama. Koori Sɔɔl ge kpo u bol Gibia. 35Di lii a hɔl hiŋ, Samuɛl waa kaa la ga binni Koori Sɔɔl na maa, ka wa siu, haali u biini n faa chɔkkɛ werge maa dikuu Koori Sɔɔl wia gba. Kɔraawiizi gba biini faa chɔkkɔɔ dikuu uŋ lizi Koori Sɔɔl, u ɛɛ Izrɛl hina koori wia.

english_text:
1 One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
2Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.”
“Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me, 3then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
4Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
5“Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
6When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
7 But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
8Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
9Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
10One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men. 11 Do you have any other sons?”
“Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.”
“Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
12Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
13Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on.
Samuel returned home to Ramah.
David Plays the Harp for Saul
14The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him. 15“It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him. 16“Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
17“All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
18“A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
19Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
20Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul. 21David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons. 22Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
23 Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_text:
Samuɛl n waari Deevid nyuu nuu wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Samuɛl be, “Ɛrɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋi ŋɔ í wii tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl di birgi magɛi, haali miŋ vɛɛu lugɔ waa kaa ɛɛ Izrɛl hina koorei? Ɛɛ ɔlivi nuu di du i nyigaa biini, ń humii Jɛssɛ la n du Bɛtlihɛm la be. N lizi u biibaala la bɛllɛ, ú ɛɛ koori.”
2Ka Samuɛl ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ di la denei? Di Koori Sɔɔl wa nuu guŋ, u daŋ kpuŋ.”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Lau nalor di ra la, di ga ŋɔ, ‘N na bau ń wa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 3Ga yir Jɛssɛ di la mbusu lizibɔr, ń ga baglii gunla hin niŋ ɛɛ. I daŋ ga yiili a nuu di waari unla min niŋ baglii la nyuu.’ ”
4Samuɛl ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la. Uŋ ga hel Bɛtlihɛm, ɔnsii lau a bol nabɔnzi, ba chem u ni, ba bɔra ra sa. Ba pɛɛzuu, “A summɔɔ i ba yaa bee?”
5Samuɛl ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, a summɔɔ. N ballɔɔ ń wa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ií sɔ lizi ii doŋa ha, di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be, ka ba ya la mbusu lizibɔr.” Denii u sɔ Jɛssɛ ni u biizi di lizi ba doŋa ha, ba ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be, ka u ni baa jaa la mbusu lizibɔr la.
6Baŋ wa hel de, Samuɛl na Ɛliab, u nfɛrɛ biini, u ŋɔ, “Wibii maa, nɛr la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛrɛ chigɛ u see bɔnnaa la.”
7Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Samuɛl be, “Gilɛɛ ra binni u bunɔɔnni ni u jaŋzi, n vɛɛubuu. Maa wia la newea n na binni la ra binni. Newea ɔɔ ra binni bɔrahɔŋ duulazii, ka miŋwaa ɔɔ ra binni newea bampireere.”
8Denii Jɛssɛ yir Abinadab, u ge wa lii Samuɛl see, ka Samuɛl ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi waa u gba lizɛɛ.” 9Jɛssɛ kaa gil Samma ge lii di wa chi, Samuɛl kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi waa u gba lizɛɛ.” 10Jɛssɛ biibaala baniidaanɛɛ maanii u gil ba ga u see wa kaali kpaŋkpaŋa, ka Samuɛl ŋɔ u be, “Akai! Kɔraawiizi waa bannii bɛl maa lizɛɛ.” 11Denii u pɛɛzi Jɛssɛ, “I biibaala hiŋ maanii keŋŋ?”
Jɛssɛ ŋɔ, “Ba bichala hiŋ haa du de. Ka u ra nɔɔni peezaa.”
Samuɛl bir ŋɔ, “Gil ba yiruu, di waa ballɛ, yaa wàá lizi mbusu.”
12Denii Jɛssɛ hum bá ga yiruu, u ba. U faa ɛɛ bunɔɔnnɛ di du kpeg, u duula du wer.
Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Izi yiili a nuu waaruu, waabuu guŋ!”
13Denii Samuɛl kpa a nyigaa ni nuu di yiili waaruu, ú kpɛɛnna hiŋ see. Di haŋ chi a hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi Duma izi Deevid fɔŋŋa ni. Ka Samuɛl jaa bir kaali Rama.
Deevid n du Koori Sɔɔl dia wia
14Kɔraawiizi Duma jaa lii Koori Sɔɔl ni, ka u gil tinnanchɔgii izuu, di ra tɔɔruu.
15Koori Sɔɔl balaa ŋɔ u be, “Na, Kɔraawiizii gillɛ tinnanchɔgii izii di ra tɔɔrii la. 16Jara, awia, gil ya la ga nyiŋŋi nɛr la n zum kem lɔi nɛnnɛ. Di Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ wa gil tinnanchɔgii izii di ra tɔɔrii, u daŋ ɔɔ lɔu i bɔra sɔɔnii, í na alaanfia.”
17Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u balaa be, “Ií ga nyiŋŋi nɛr la n zum u lɔi nɛnnɛ, di wa tɛŋ.”
18U balaa la bɛl ŋɔ, “N zum Bɛtlihɛm hinuu Jɛssɛ la biibaal bɛl n zum kem lɔirɛ nɛnnɛ. U maa ni bampirii, di kaa ɛɛ laallɔɔri. U zum wiŋɔzii werge maa, di kaa ɛɛ bunɔɔŋ ge jaa. Kɔraawiizi du u benii.”
19Denii Sɔɔl jaa hum balaa Jɛssɛ be, di ŋɔ, “Gil i biibaal Deevid la n na nɔɔni peeza la ba.” 20Awia, Jɛssɛ kpa paanuu, hur ni siŋ ani bupɔl, di lau kawee di kpaa sag u ni, di gil u biibaal Deevid kpaa la ga tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl.
21Deevid kpaa di ba Koori Sɔɔl be di waa humuu. U wia par Koori Sɔɔl werge maa. U jaa gil Deevid ɛɛ nɛr la bɛl n na chi u dɔŋkuna di ra la laal bɔr. 22Denii Koori Sɔɔl tili di ŋɔ Jɛssɛ be, “Gil Deevid du n be bɔnnaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u wia sɔɔni n bɔraa werge maa.”
23Di Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ wa gil tinnanchɔgii izi Koori Sɔɔl, Deevid ɔɔ kpa u kemne di ra lɔ. Koori Sɔɔl bɔra maa ɔɔ jaa sɔɔnuu. U biini waa ɔɔ kaa chɔgi. Tinnanchɔgii hiŋ ɔɔ jaa giluu.

english_text:
Goliath Challenges Israel's Army
1The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah. 2-3King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
4The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall. 5-6He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about 57 kilograms. He carried a bronze sword strapped on his back, 7and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
8Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel:
Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me! 9If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves. 10Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
11Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing.
David Decides To Challenge Goliath
12David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons: 13-14the oldest was Eliab, the next was Abinadab, and Shammah was the third. The three of them had gone off to fight in Saul's army.
David was Jesse's youngest son. 15 He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
16Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for 40 days.
17One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp. 18And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right. 19They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
20David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry. 21The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
22David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well. 23While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
24When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off. 25They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
26David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
27The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
28David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
29“Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?” 30Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
31Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came. 32“Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
33“You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
34But David told him:
Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear, 35I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
36Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God! 37The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine.
“All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
38Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear. 39David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things.
“I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.”
David took off the armor 40and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath.
David Kills Goliath
41Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield. 42When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him. 43 “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods 44and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
45David answered:
You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
46Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God. 47Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
48When Goliath started forward, David ran toward him. 49He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground. 50 David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
51 David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head.
When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away. 52But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
53When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp. 54David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent.
David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
55After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?”
“Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
56“Then find out!” Saul told him.
57When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head.
Abner took David to Saul, 58and Saul asked, “Who are you?”
“I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_text:
Deevid ni Goliaf wia
1Denii Filisti hina vɔɔ laal, di la ga chaali bol bɛl banna yir Soko n du Juda hɛri la, di lii de ga chɔɔ yembɛl banna yir Ɛfɛs Damim n du Soko ani Azɛka baambaaŋ. 2Koori Sɔɔl ge ni Izrɛl hina ge chaali, di ga baŋzi ba tantizi Ɛla Waluu, di ɛɛ sirya nɛnnɛ, bá ga lɔ Filisti hina. 3A Filisti hina la ga chi giŋgimii bɛl nyuu. Izrɛl hina ge chi bɛl nyuu. Ka waluu jaa chɔɔ ba bambaaŋ.
4Baal bɛl faa du a Filisti laallɔɔra la biini, ba ra yiruu Goliaf, u ɛɛ ba kpegleg di lii Gaf. U faa lii a Filisti hina chɔɔribɔr, ú wa karsi Izrɛl hina. U faa helloo kpabaa, u jaŋzi kaali naapezi kabɛl. 5U faa hi danyɛ kahuro, di kaa laali danyɛ tagta, u tɔgzi ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kagboŋa anue. 6Danyɛ ge tɔ u gballi, di kpa danyɛ kandaa ge sag u baŋaa. 7U kandaa daa faa lugɔ kɔɔrɛɛ daarɛ, u nua bɔpupula tɔgzi ge ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaanumbɛl. Nɛr la n na kpogli u laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ uŋ kpawɛɛ di ra teŋ kandaazi ni hobee tɔ u see.
8Goliaf izi chi di pozi Izrɛl hina ni, di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii lii di wa chi di ra nyiŋŋi ii yoo laalɛi? Maa Filisti hinuu ɛɛwɛ gɛɛ, ii ge ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl balaa? Ií lizi unla n na yir u hiŋ baal, ú tuu ba n nuu chem dɔŋa. 9Di u wa wetto kpegliŋ di kpuŋ, guŋwaa, yaa daŋ birgi ii balaa. Ka di n ge wa kpegluu di kpuu, ii ge daŋ birgi yaa balaa, di ra hum yaa. 10Awia, Izrɛl laallɔɔra, ií ba ya karsi dɔŋa zinaa! Ií lizi unla n ŋɔ u ɛɛ baallɛ, ú ba n nuu lɔ dɔŋa!” 11Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra la n wa nuu a Filisti hinuu wiŋɔzi hiŋ, ɔnsii jaa lau baa werge maa, ba bɔra ra sa.
12Deevid faa ɛɛ Ɛfraf hinuu Jɛssɛ biibaallɛ di lii Bɛtlihɛm n du Juda hɛri. Jɛssɛ biibaala faa du ŋmantannaazi. Koori Sɔɔl de dui saŋa la, u faa zɛŋŋɔɔ werge maa. 13Jɛssɛ biibambinabɔnzi bahoroo faa hiŋ Koori Sɔɔllɛ di la a laal. U biibambinabɔma hinnɛ faa Ɛliab, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Abinadab, horohiŋ ɛɛ Samma. 14Deevidii faa ɛɛ bichala Jɛssɛ biibaala biini. U biibambinabɔnzi bahoroo faa hiŋ Koori Sɔɔl la. 15Ka Deevid waa ɔɔ lii Koori Sɔɔl be, di ra ba Bɛtlihɛm, di waa binni u mɛɛ peeza ka bir ra la.
16Hɔpizii maa chɔɔzi ni duana, Goliaf naa ɔɔ faa liiu chi di ra ŋɔ Izrɛl hina ba, bá karsi dɔŋa, guŋŋ hɔpizaa tokkoanɛɛ.
17A hɔl bɛl, Jɛssɛ ŋɔ u biibaal Deevid be, “Kpa mihallaa kookoo tassazi fi naa ani paanuubire fi naa, di hahzi ga tɛɛ i kpɛɛnna, a laal bɔr. 18Kpa waagazi fi naa, di jaa ra la ga tɛɛ ba nabɔma la n na binni ba ni la. Binni i kpɛɛnna hiŋ di na gunla baŋ duwɛɛ, gil kumbɛl hiŋii lii ba be ba, ń zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ ba du denii. 19Ba du Koori Sɔɔl ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa be, Ɛla Waluu biini, di ra yoo Filisti hina laal.”
20Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Deevid izi di vɔɔ u bunni di kpa lii ra la, gunla u mɛɛ n ŋɔ u be la, ka jaa gil a peeza hiŋ di du penɔɔni bɛl nonee. Uŋ ga hel bá chɔɔribɔr bɔr, di ba kaa ɛɛ sirya bá ga chi ba chignibɔra, di ra lɔ laal wile. 21Izrɛl laallɔɔra ni Filisti laallɔɔra jaa chi ba chignibɔra, di chaŋ dɔŋa. 22Deevid chug u bunni di chiŋŋi nɛr la n na binni ba kuna di ra tɛɛ baa be, ka chɔ di hel a laal bɔr di ga jaami u kpɛɛnna hiŋ. 23U ni baa n na ŋɔ wia la, di Goliaf la n ɛɛ Filisti hina kpegleg di lii Gaf la liiwɔɔ chi, di ra karsi Izrɛl hina gunla uŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ la. Deevid nuu guŋ. 24Izrɛl hina n wa nau, ɔnsii werge lau baa, ba chɔ lii u be.
25Izrɛl hina jaa ra ŋɔ, “Ií na a baal! U ɔɔ liiu di ra gbɛlli Izrɛl hina. Nɛr la maa n niŋ wer kpuu, koori ŋɔ u daŋ tɛu daama werge. U daŋ kaa kpa u biihambie ge tɛu, ú ɛɛ haaŋ, di lizi lampoo turgaa lii u mɛɛ dia, Izrɛl hɛri.”
26Deevid pɛɛzi a nɛra la n chigɛ dugluu la, “Bɛɛ bá ɛɛ tɛɛ nɛr la n niŋ wer kpu Filisti hinuu naa, di lizi hiihzi naa Izrɛl hina ninɛi? Anɛɛ unla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ naa, lugɔ u danna gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa laallɔɔrai?” 27Ba bir ŋɔ u be wii la ban niŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ baal la n niŋ kpu Goliaf.
28Deevid kpɛɛma Ɛliab nuu u ni baala la n na ŋɔ wia, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ i ba ɛŋ í wa ɛɛi? Anɛɛ i gil a petama la tɛɛ a hɛribɔduma biinei? N zummɔ hinna tɔgzi i hiŋ, di dɔɔ biinikpola. A laal naa lɔi binnaa bɛŋ wiarɛ i kuu ba ɛŋ!”
29Denii Deevid ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛi? A waa dɛkkɛ min niŋ wer pɛɛzi wii bɛlaa?” 30Denii u jaa bir pɛɛzi nɛbɛl a wii himmaa ni u nyuu. U ge kaa ŋɔ u be gunla himmaa banla n faa ŋɔwɛɛ la. 31Denii a nɛra baŋhina nuu gunla Deevid n ŋɔwɛɛ la, di la ga ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, u hum ŋɔ bá ga yiruu.
32Deevid ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ ra ɔm Filisti hinuu naa! N daŋ la ga yoou.”
33Sɔɔl ŋɔ u be, “I ɛɛ bichalaa lugɔ i ni baal naa wer yoo. U ɛɛ laallɔɔrii lii u pɔlaa saŋa maa guŋŋ wa lii zinaa.”
34Ka Deevid ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Jara, mìŋ́ i balii ra binni n mɛɛ peezaa. Di bunyiŋ gɛɛ munu haŋ wa lau a peeza bɛl maa di ra kaali, 35n ɔɔ duŋŋuubuu di ga lɔu ta ka lɛɛu. Di u haŋ wa bir ú lawiŋ ge, n ɔɔ lau u hunaa ka lɔɔzuu kpu. 36N ɔɔ weruu kpu bunyinzi ani munuzi maa. Gunnɛ ń wer kpu Filisti hinuu naa n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ naa gba, dikuu unna gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa laallɔɔra wia. 37Kɔraawiizi la n lɛɛŋ lii bunyinzi ani munuzi maa be la, daŋ lɛɛŋ lii Filisti hinuu naa gba be.”
Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Deevid be, “A la, Kɔ́raawiizi du i be.”
38Denii Sɔɔl kpa u himmaa laal laala tɛɛ Deevid, di kaa kpa u danyɛ kahuro ge tɛu, u hi. 39Deevid kpa Sɔɔl tokobi di vɔɔ mari a laala, ka waa wette ú vol, dikuu uŋ wàá laalɛɛ mani wia.
U ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Jara, màá wer laali a laala, dikuubɛɛwiai, a waŋ manɛɛ.” Awia, u jaa wiraa. 40Denii u kpa u penɔɔni kpala di tuu gɔŋ biini, di hɔɔzi loglogbia anue, di du u hur la uŋ ɔɔ laali di ra nɔɔni u peeza la biini, ka jaa kpogli u bilori di tuzi di ra hel Filisti hinuu hiŋ.
41Goliaf ge lii di ra chem Deevid ni, ka nɛr la ge n kpogli ú laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ la tɔ u see di ra ba. 42Baŋ waa dugluu, u binni Deevid di u ɛɛ bichala, di kaa ɛɛ bunɔɔŋ di dɔɔ alaanfia nɛnnɛ jaa, u ra gbɛlluu. 43Denii u ŋɔ Deevid be, “Nuahinnɛ miŋ, i kpa kpala di ra ba n bee?” Ka jaa yirgi u vuga di ra see Deevid nua, 44di ŋɔ u be, “Ba ɛŋ ń kpui tɛɛ zumbizi ani pir sela a di!”
45Deevid ge ŋɔ Goliaf be, “I kpa kandaa ni tokobii di ra ba n be, ka miŋwaa ra ba i benii ani Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ, n ɛɛ Izrɛl laallɔɔra Kɔraawiizi la hiŋ gbɛllɛɛ la sɔŋ biinii. 46Zinaa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpai du n nonee biini, ń kpui, di teŋ i nyuu, ka kpuuzi i laallɔɔra tɛɛ zumbizi ni pir sela, á di. Denii durnya hina maa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la du denii. 47Banla maa ge n chaali bɔnnaa zum lugɔ tokobi ni kandaa lɛi Kɔraawiizi kpa di ra lɛɛ nɛra. A laal ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hotte, u daŋ kpa ii maa du yaa nonee biini.”
48Goliaf n tuzɛɛ ra heluu la, Deevid ge jaa kɛɛhzi manaŋ di ra chemuu, bɔr la ban niŋ lɔ dɔŋa la. 49Ka jaa hau u hur biini di lizi bii du u bilori, di viguu, ka tau, u ga lɔ Goliaf hile di harmi zuu, u chol hɛri pi.
50Deevid faa kpu Goliaf ani bilori, di waa tokobi kpawɛɛ.
51Denii Deevid kɛɛhzi ga chi guali Goliaf ni, di pam Goliaf tokobi, di kpuu. Uŋ wa kpuu tuŋ, u kpa a tokobi teŋ u nyuu.
Filisti hina n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba kpegleg siuwɔɔ, ba bir kɛɛhzi. 52Izrɛl ni Juda hina la chaasi, ka duŋŋi baa guŋŋ ga hel Gaf ani Ɛkrɔn dominuuzi. Banla baŋ kpuuzɛɛ ge chɔɔgi Saaram ŋmɛnɛɛ, guŋŋ di ga hel Ɛkrɔn ni Gaf. 53Izrɛl hina gil a Filisti hina duŋŋaa, ka bir ba di wa paagi ba kuna maa ba chɔɔribɔr la. 54Deevid kpa Goliaf nyuu di ba Jɛrusalɛm, ka kpa u dɔŋkuna la ge di dau u himmaa tanti dia biini.
55Deevid n na la ú ga chem Goliaf ni la, Koori Sɔɔl binnuu, ka pɛɛzi u laallɔɔra maa nabɔma Abna, “Anɛɛ biere a biipɔllii naanɛi?”
Abna bir ŋɔ, “Jara, maa zum nɛr la biibaal n ɛɛu.”
56A koori ŋɔ, “Pɛɛzi nɛr la biibaal n ɛɛu.”
57Saŋa la Deevid n kpu Goliaf di teŋ u nyuu ba la, Abna kpogluu di ba Koori Sɔɔl be, di u haa kpogli a nyuu.
58Koori Sɔɔl pɛɛzuu, “Biipɔllii, anɛɛ biere hinnɛi?”
Deevid ŋɔ, “Jara, n mɛɛrɛ i balii Jɛssɛ di lii Bɛtlihɛm.”

english_text:
1David and Saul finished talking, and soon David and Jonathan became best friends. Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself. 2From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
3Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends. 4Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
5David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers.
Saul Becomes David's Enemy
6David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps. 7 They sang:
Saul has killed
a thousand enemies;
David has killed
ten thousand!
8This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.” 9Saul never again trusted David.
10The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand. 11Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
12Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him. 13Saul put David in charge of 1,000 soldiers and sent him out to fight. 14The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles. 15This made Saul even more afraid of David. 16But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
17One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
18David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
19But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
20Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy, 21and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
22-23Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?”
“I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
24The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said. 25Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed 100 Philistines!” 26The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess.
King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out, 27David and his men left and killed 200 Philistines. David brought back the proof that Saul had demanded and showed it to him, so he could marry Michal. Saul agreed to let David marry Michal. 28King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David. 29But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
30The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_text:
Koori Sɔɔl n na zom Deevid ni wia
1Deevid ni Koori Sɔɔl n wa ŋɔ wia tuŋ, Jonatan bampirii lau Deevid, u jaa nɔŋŋuu werge maa alugɔ u hiŋ. 2Di haŋ chi a hɔl hiŋ, Koori Sɔɔl gil Deevid du u be. Waa kaa sɛɛ ú la ga du u mɛɛ dia. 3Denii Jonatan ni Deevid jaa ɛɛ dammunaa nuukpaŋ, dikuu Jonatan n nɔŋŋuu alugɔ u hiŋ wia. 4Jonatan wir u tagtajaŋ bɛl uŋ laalɛɛ, tɛɛ Deevid, di kaa kpa u laal tagta, u tokobi, u hoo ani u kurhɔŋ di tɛu.
5Wii la maa Koori Sɔɔl n ɔɔ hum Deevid ŋɔ ú ɛɛ, ɔɔ ɛɛubuu nɛnnɛ. Koori Sɔɔl jaa gil u ɛɛ u laallɔɔra nabɔma. Guŋ sɔɔni a nɛra ni Koori Sɔɔl nabɔnzi maa bɔra.
6Deevid n wa kpu Goliaf, ka a laallɔɔra maa bir di ra ba bol la, Izrɛl hɛri bola haana maa lii, di yir yira di ra sa di ra lɔ kemzi, di ra yigzi kuna di ra chem Koori Sɔɔl ni ani bɔsɔna. 7Banna sa la, ba ra yir yira di ra ŋɔ,
“Koori Sɔɔl kpu kagboŋaa,
Deevid ge kpu
kagboŋa fizi.”
8Koori Sɔɔl n wa nuu gunla banna yir la, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa. U fɛ u biini, “Ba ra tɛɛ Deevidii kagboŋa fizi, ka ra tɛŋ kagboŋa bɛŋ, bɛɛ bá kaa tɛu di a kora lɛiyɛi?” 9Di haŋ lii a guŋ saŋa hiŋ, Koori Sɔɔl lizi siwii sag Deevid ni, dikuu zoma wia.
10Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi gil tinnanchɔgii ba di wa izi Koori Sɔɔl kpegzi ni. U ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ u dia biini. A saŋa di Deevid ge sogo di ra lɔ u kem gunla uŋ ɔɔ ra lɔu saŋa maa la. Di Koori Sɔɔl ge kpogli u kandaa. 11Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u biini, “N daŋ yag Deevid pɛli koŋlii.” U tau, ka Deevid du gbaŋ, u tau kir bunɛɛ maa.
12Koori Sɔɔl faa ra ɔm Deevid, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n du u be ka kizi waabuu Sɔɔl ha wia. 13Awia, u lizi Deevid lii u be, di gil u tɔ laallɔɔra kagboŋ see, bá ra lɔ laal. 14Wii la maa Deevid n ɔɔ ɛɛ, ɔɔ ɛɛubuu nɛnnɛ, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n du u be wia. 15Koori Sɔɔl n wa na gunla unna ɛɛ wia nɛnnɛ la, u jaa ra ɔmuu werge maa. 16Ka Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa nɔŋŋi Deevid werge, dikuu uŋ ɔɔ tɔ ba see laal biini, ba ra kpegli ba dɔma wia.
17A hɔl bɛl Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Deevid be, “N daŋ kpa n biihambinabɔma Mɛrab tɛi. Ka n na nyiŋŋuu lugɔ í humiŋ nɛnnɛ, di kaa yoo Kɔraawiizi laalzi di jaa.” Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u biini, “Màá kpa n nonii gbɔgzuu, ka n daŋ gil Filisti hina ɛɛ guŋ!”
18Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Anɛɛ miŋ gɛɛ n domee gɛɛ n mɛɛ diahina, Izrɛl hina biini lugɔ ń ɛɛ koori hilai?” 19Ka Mɛrab kpai n wa helle, u mɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl waa kaa sɛɛ kpau tɛɛ Deevid gunla uŋ felee ŋɔ la. Ka bir gil Adriɛl la n lii Mɛhɔla la kpau.
20Denii Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ bɛl banna yir Mikal, ge bampirii bir lau Deevid, u ra nyiŋŋuu. Baŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl, u bɔra sɔɔnuu. 21U ŋɔ u biini, “N daŋ gil ú kpau. A guŋ daŋ tɛŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ ń kpau du Filisti hina nonee biini, bá kpuu.” Ka jaa ŋɔ Deevid be, “I kaa na bɔttɛ lugɔ í ɛɛ n hila.”
22Denii Koori Sɔɔl hum u nabɔnzi, bá la Deevid be u bɛŋ, di ga ŋɔ, “Na, i wia par koori ni u nabɔnzii. Awia, sɛɛ i hila ɛɛu.”
23Baŋ ŋɔ annii maa wa tuŋ, Deevid ŋɔ, “Ii zummɔ lugɔ wijigzii koori hila ɛɛi gɛɛ? Mìŋ́ ge nyaari naa, á bɛlaa biinii n duɛi?”
24Koori Sɔɔl nabɔnzi la n wa ŋɔ u be gunla Deevid ge n ŋɔwɛɛ, 25Koori Sɔɔl ge kaa ŋɔ, “Ií la ga ŋɔ Deevid be lugɔ hila kuna la minna nyiŋŋi u be maanii lugɔ, ú ga kpu Filisti hina baala kalfa, di mɔnni ba hɛna hɔna wa tɛŋ, di turgi n dɔma wichɔgaa kim.” Ka Koori Sɔɔl faa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ Filisti hina kpu Deevid.
26A nabɔnzi n kaa ba Deevid be di wa ŋɔ gunla maa Koori Sɔɔl n ŋɔwɛɛ la, u bɔra jaa sɔɔnuu werge maa un niŋ ɛɛ koori hila wia Mɔɔ ka u haaŋ kpai hɔpizii wa hel, 27Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la ga kpu Filisti hina kalfaanɛɛ di mɔnni ba hɛna hɔna kalfaanɛɛ, di wa tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl. Awia, u jaa kpa u biihaaŋ Mikal tɛu.
28Koori Sɔɔl n wa zummɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du Deevid benii, u biihaaŋ Mikal ge kaa ra nyiŋŋuu la, 29u Deevid ɔmaa jaa bir nyaŋŋi, u ɛɛ u dɔm u de dui maa.
30Filisti laallɔɔra sitɔɔra la ɔɔ haa lii di ba waa lɔ baa laal. Saŋa maa, di ba haŋ wa ba, Deevid ɔɔ lii di kpu baa werge maa, kaali Koori Sɔɔl laallɔɔra sitɔɔra la bɛl maa, guŋ gil u dɔɔ sɔŋ werge maa.

english_text:
Saul Tries To Have David Killed
1One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends, 2-3and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
4-5The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
6Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
7Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
8The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat.
Michal Helps David Escape
9-10One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
11 Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning.
Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!” 12She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off, 13Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
14The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
15Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
16When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
17“Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!”
She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!”
Samuel Helps David Escape
18Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
19Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
20Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
21When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them. 22Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?”
“At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
23Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village, 24 he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_text:
Koori Sɔɔl n na nyiŋŋi ú kpu Deevid wia
1A hɔl bɛl Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u biibaal Jonatan ani u nabɔnzi be lugɔ bá la ga kpu Deevid. Ka Jonatan ge faa nɔŋŋi Deevid wia werge maa, a guŋ waa u bɔra sɔɔnɛɛ. 2Denii Jonatan jaa ga ŋɔ u be, “A du tau nɛnnɛ, di nyiŋŋi bɔr suah kɛrɛ chɔɔzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, n mɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi i kpuirɛ. 3N daŋ gil n ni n mɛɛ wa chi pir bɔr la hin niŋ suah la paga, ka ń ŋɔ i wia tɛu, di nuu gunla un niŋ ŋɔ. Di u wa ŋɔ wii maa, n daŋ wa ŋɔ i be.”
4Jonatan jaa bagli winanaa la maa Deevid n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ u mɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl, di ŋɔ, “Jara, gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ i balii Deevid wichɔgii maa. Waa wichɔgii maa ɛɛwɛ di zuu i ni. Wii la uŋ ɛɛwɛ la hiiniibuu, di lii tɔna tɛi werge maa. 5U kpa u miibɔɔrɛ chɛr siu, gunla uŋ wette kpu Goliaf la. Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ gunnɛ, di gil Izrɛl hina maa kpegli ba dɔma. I na guŋ, i bɔra sɔɔni. Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ŋɔ í ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di kpu nɛnanii pɛɛpɛɛi?”
6Koori Sɔɔl nuu gunla maa Jonatan n ŋɔwɛɛ la, di jaa hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa lugɔ màá ka kpu Deevid.”
7Denii Jonatan yir Deevid, di bagli wia la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ u mɛɛ, dikuu u wia la. Ka jaa kpogluu ba u mɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl be, u nuu kaa du ú dia gunla baŋ faa duwɛɛ saŋa maa la.
8Denii laal kaa izi, Deevid la ga lɔ Filisti hina werge maa, ba maa chɔ yaari.
9A hɔl bɛl Kɔraawiizi kaa gil tinnanchɔgii wa izi Koori Sɔɔl, di u sogo u dia biini, di kpogli u kandaa. Ka Deevid ge so di ra lɔ u kem. Unna lɔ u kem la, 10Koori Sɔɔl tau kandaa, di fɛ lugɔ u vii yaguu di mari koŋlii, ka Deevid du gbaŋ, u tau kir, ka a kandaa ga yag koŋlii di baŋ de. A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa maanii Deevid chɔ lii di ga suah.
11Koori Sɔɔl lizi nɛra bá la Deevid dia di ga guu, di u wa izoo chɔɔzi ni, bá kpuu. Ka u haaŋ Mikal n wa nuu guŋ, u ŋɔ u be, “Di haa haŋ chɔ di suah hamuŋa naa ka hɔpizi, ba daŋ kpui.” 12Awia, Mikal hiinuu, u ga tokoro lii, di chɔ ga suah. 13Denii Mikal kpa vug dau u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni, di kpa buuŋ huna di bɔg u nyuu, ka kpa wɛjɛ tɔu.
14Koori Sɔɔl n hum u balaa lugɔ ba ga lau Deevid ba, baŋ ga helle, Mikal ŋɔ ba be lugɔ u ra wiiu.
15Denii Koori Sɔɔl kaa hum u balaa hiŋ, dí ba bir la ga binni Deevid na, ka ŋɔ ba be, “Ií lalli u ni u kunchɔɔrikuŋ maa ba, ń kpuu.” 16Ka u balaa hiŋ n kpawɛɛ di ga zuu ŋɔ ba binni, di vugrɛ chɔɔ a kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni, buuŋ huna tɔ ú nyuu.
17Koori Sɔɔl pɛɛzi Mikal, “Ɛrɛɛ i dariŋ kennaa, di gil n dɔm lii di chɔ kaalɛi?”
Denii Mikal ŋɔ u be, “U ŋɔ n benii lugɔ di maa haŋ gil u chɔ, u daŋ kpuŋ.”
18Denii Deevid chɔ la Samuɛl be Rama, di ga ŋɔ u be wii la maa Koori Sɔɔl n ɛɛu. U ni Samuɛl kpa di la yembɛl banna yir Nayɔf, di ga so de. 19Denii Sɔɔl nuu lugɔ Deevid du Nayɔf n du Rama. 20Awia, u hum u balaa dí ba ga lawuu ba. Baŋ ga hel de, ba na Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi n chaali bɔkpaŋ di ra sa, ka ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini. Samuɛl faa ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri. Kakpaŋ, Kɔraawiizi Duma izi baa, ba ge jaa ra ŋɔ a guŋ wiŋɔzi. 21Ba ba wa ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be gunla maa n du de. Denii u kaa lizi nɛra, di hum ba ge de himmaa, baŋ ga hel de, ba ge kaa ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini. 22A tuna maa, u himmaa izi di ra la Rama. Uŋ ga hel kɔlɔŋzeŋ la n du yembɛl banna yir Sɛku, u pɛɛzi, “Lee Samuɛl ni Deevid duɛi?”
Ba ŋɔ u be, “Ba du Nayɔf n du Rama.”
23Unna la de la, Kɔraawiizi Duma izi u gba. U ra sa ka ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ waa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini guŋŋ di ga hel Nayɔf. 24Uŋ ga hel de, u wir u koori tagtazi, ka chi Samuɛl see di ra sa, di ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini. Gunnɛ u kpogli di chɔɔ guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi. Banla n na guŋ ra pɛɛzi dɔŋa, “Koori Sɔɔl ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la bɛllɛ gɛɛ?”

english_text:
Jonathan Helps David Escape
1David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
2“My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
3“Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
4Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
5 David answered:
Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day. 6If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
7If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me. 8Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
9“Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
10“How will you do that?” David asked.
11“Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered.
When they got there, 12Jonathan said:
I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you. 13But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise.
I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father. 14-15 Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
16Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
17Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend. 18After this Jonathan said:
Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty. 19By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock. 20I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock, 21and send my servant to find the arrows.
You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!” 22But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go. 23But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
24So David hid there in the field.
During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat 25by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty. 26Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
27The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
28-29Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
30Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born. 31You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
32“Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
33Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David. 34Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
35In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along 36and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.”
The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him. 37When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?” 38Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!”
The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan, 39but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew. 40Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
41After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder. 42Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.”
David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_text:
Deevid ni Jonatan wia
1Denii Deevid chɔ lii Nayɔf n du Rama, di la Jonatan be di ga pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛi? Bɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ n ɛɛi? Bɛɛ n ɛɛ di zuu i mɛɛ ni, u ra nyiŋŋi ú lizi n miibɔɔi?”
2Jonatan ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi la a ni bɔɔnɛɛ! Hàá siu! Na, n mɛɛ wàá sɛɛ ɛɛ wizeŋ gɛɛ wijiga maa, di waa n be ŋɔwɛɛ. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ú kpa annii suah n ninɛi? Wibii lɛi!”
3Ka Deevid hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ, “Wibii maa, i mɛɛ zum gunla hinna nyiŋŋi n wiarɛ werge maa, aabuu gillɛ u ŋɔ, ‘Màá gil Jonatan zum gunla minna fɛ. Di u zummɔ, u biini daŋ chɔgi werge maa.’ N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa lugɔ n ni siu waa kaa du nɛɛ.”
4Jonatan ŋɔ Deevid be, “Wii la maa hinna nyiŋŋi, n daŋ ɛɛu.”
5Denii Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Na, kɛrɛɛ Baagufalii Hɔpizizeŋ Dii, a dɛg lugɔ n ni koori kpau di. Ama, gil ń la pir, di di ga nyiŋŋi bɔr suah, di ra ba hɔbil duana ni. 6Di i mɛɛ wa nyiŋŋiŋ huhzi ka ra pɛɛzi n wia, ŋɔ u be, ‘Deevid suŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ ú la u bol Bɛtlihɛm, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba dɔɔ ba domee bina maa mbusu lizaarɛ.’ 7Di u wa ŋɔ, ‘Guŋ wesso,’ amɔ, i balii daŋ na u hiŋ. Ka di u baaŋ haŋ wa fuuh waa, guŋwaa, u ra nyiŋŋi n kpuirɛ wibii maa. 8Ɛɛ ania maa ka suŋ n ni, dikuu nuukpaŋ la yaa n ɛɛwɛ Kɔraawiizi be la wia. Di n hor waa sum, amɔ, í himmaa kpuŋ! Ka gilɛɛ waa kpaŋ di ra du i mɛɛ nonee biini, ú kpu.”
9Jonatan ŋɔ, “Akai, màá sɛɛ ɛɛ guŋ! Di n zummɔ tama maa lugɔ n mɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi i kpuirɛ wibii maa, màá ŋɔ i bee?”
10Deevid bir pɛɛzuu, “Anɛɛ n niŋ ŋɔ n be, di i mɛɛ wa nyɛg i ninɛi?”
11Denii Jonatan ŋɔ Deevid be, “Gil ya la pir.” Ba la.
12Jonatan kaa ŋɔ Deevid be, “N na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum labuu ɛɛ yaa daansɛɛ hiŋ! Hɔbil saŋa naa dɔŋ, n daŋ pɛɛzi n mɛɛ i wia, di nuu gunla un niŋ ŋɔ. Di u wa ŋɔ winanii maa, n daŋ gil i nuu. 13Ka di n mɛɛ wa fɛ i kpui wia, ka n vɛɛ i be ŋɔi, í chɔ lɛɛ i hiŋ, Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ. Kɔ́raawiizi du i be gunla uŋ faa du n mɛɛ be la. 14Ama, bagliŋ i nɔŋŋaa himmaa la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ alugɔ Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋaa, n de dui biini, guŋ gil ba gilɛɛ waa kpuŋ. 15Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ n lulla nɔŋŋaa, haali di Kɔraawiizi waa chɔgi hìŋ́ Deevid dɔma maa dee nyaamm, a hɛri naa biini.
16Gilɛɛ waa gil n nii nuukpaŋ la yaa n ɛɛwɛ la wàá chɔgi. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, Kɔ́raawiizi tɛr i digni.”
17Denii Jonatan kaa gil Deevid ŋɔ nua lugɔ ú nɔŋŋuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, Jonatan nɔŋŋi Deevidii alugɔ u hiŋ.
18Jonatan kaa ŋɔ Deevid be, “Kɛrɛ daŋ ɛɛ Baagufalii Hɔpizizeŋ Dii. Hàá du de, nɛra na guŋ, dikuu i sognibɔr n niŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ wia. 19Hɔbil, di bɔr waa duani, chɔ di ga suah bɔr la hiŋ faa ga suahwɛ, saŋa la wia naa n faarɛɛ la, di gaa kpaŋiŋ bii Ɛzɛl zɛɛ. 20N daŋ ta hobee ahoro di du de paga alugɔ miŋ na kumbɛl, di ra tau la. 21Denii ń hum biibambie lugɔ ú la ga nyiŋŋi a hobee ba. Di n haŋ wa ŋɔ u be, ‘Binni keŋkere naa, denii a hobee du, paagaa ba.’ Guŋwaa, a ba. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ wiimaa waa hoo un niŋ ɛɛi, siaahmu waa hoo. 22Ka di i haŋ wa nuu miŋ ŋɔ a biibambie be lugɔ a hobee du seere, guŋwaa chɔ di ra la bɔɔnɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii ra lizii a siaahmu biini la. 23Ama, wia la yaa n ŋɔwɛɛ la, a liizaa, di zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ yaa daansɛɛ hiŋ, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”
24Denii Deevid suah a pir biini guŋŋ a Baagufalii Hɔpizizeŋ Dii wa hel. Koori Sɔɔl la ga so ú di a diwee. 25U so u sognibɔr gunla uŋ ɔɔ ra so saŋa maa, di pɛli koŋlii, u ni Jonatan chaŋ dɔŋa. Abna ge so di hiŋ Sɔɔl ni. Ka Deevid waa sognibɔr la chɔɔ pɛɛ. 26A hɔl hiŋ, Koori Sɔɔl waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Deevid ɛɛ wiibɛllɛ di doŋ Kɔraawiizi be, awiarɛ waa ballɛ. 27Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, a Baagufalii Hɔpizeŋ Dii hɔpizaa anɛɛhiŋ hɔl, di Deevid sognibɔr la haa chɔɔ pɛɛ. Denii Koori Sɔɔl jaa pɛɛzi u biibaal Jonatan, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ, dɛɛla ni zinaa maa, Jɛssɛ biibaal waa ballɛ ú wa dei?”
28Jonatan ŋɔ, “Deevid suŋŋimbuu ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ ú la Bɛtlihɛm. 29U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Gil ń la, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa diahina dɔɔ mbusu lizaarɛ bol, n kpɛɛma ge ŋɔ ń ba. Di n wia parii, gil n la ga na n lulla.’ Awiarɛ waa diiribɔr ballɛ la.”
30Denii Koori Sɔɔl baaŋ fuuh Jonatan ni werge maa. U ŋɔ, “Hìŋ́ hahjaga ni dignikpega hiŋ biibaal naa! Filaŋkeŋ n jaa zumuu nɛnnɛ lugɔ i chigɔ Deevid hattɛ. I kpa hiihzii di kpu i hiŋ ani i maa! 31Di Jɛssɛ biibaal naa daŋ haŋ du durnya naa ni miibɔɔ, haa ba kora naa dii maa. Hum bá ga yiruu filaŋkeŋ maa u ba. A dɛkkɔɔ ú siu!”
32Jonatan pɛɛzi u mɛɛ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ŋɔ i kpuuwɛi? Bɛɛ u ɛɛi?” 33Ka Koori Sɔɔl ta Jonatan kandaa, ú vii kpuu. Denii Jonatan jaa zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ u mɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi Deevid kpuirɛ, wibii maa.
34Jonatan baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u lɔ izi a diwee zɛɛ. A hɔl hiŋ waa, Jonatan waa kummaa diwee. U biini chɔgi werge, dikuu u mɛɛ hiihnyaai wia la uŋ ɛɛ Deevid la wia.
35Chɔɔzi ni, Jonatan izi di la a pir, Deevid be, gunla baŋ ta jina la. Unna la la, u lau biibambijiga di hiŋ u hiŋ. 36Denii u ŋɔ a bie be, “Chɔ la ga nyiŋŋi hobee naa min niŋ ta naa ba.” A bie n na la la, u ta hobii du u see. 37A bie n wa hel bɔr la Jonatan n ta a hobii u chol la, Jonatan yiruu, di ŋɔ, “A hobii haa du see!” 38Denii u pozi werge maa di ŋɔ, “A chɔ manaŋ di ga kpau, gilɛɛ waa chi!” A bie la ga kpau di bir ba di wa tɛɛ u dɔɔri hiŋ. 39A bie waa faa waa zum wii la n na ɛɛ. Jonatan ni Deevid bɛnnɛ faa zum wii la banna ɛɛ. 40Jonatan jaa kpa u dɔŋkuna di tɛɛ a bie, ka ŋɔ, “Kpaa di bir a kpo bol.”
41A bie n wa kaalɛɛ tuŋ, Deevid faa izi lii a bii wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere, di ba Jonatan be, di wa tognuu buhoro, di willi u nyuu. Ka ba jaa faami dɔŋa di ra wii. Ka Deevidii faa wiiwe werge.
42Jonatan ŋɔ Deevid be, “A la ani bɔsɔna, yaa ŋɔ dammunaa nuarɛ tɛɛ dɔŋa Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini. Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ n nii maa daansɛɛ hiŋ, di kaa ɛɛ i naanna ani n ge naanna maa daansɛɛ hiŋ, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.” Denii Deevid kaali, ka Jonatan bir kpo.

english_text:
Ahimelech Helps David
1 David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
2“I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else. 3Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
4“The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
5“Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
6 The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
7It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
8David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
9 The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.”
“It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!”
David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
10David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish. 11 The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing,
‘Saul has killed
a thousand enemies;
David has killed
ten thousand’?”
12 David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish. 13 So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
14“Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me? 15I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_text:
Deevid n chɔ Koori Sɔɔl wia
1Deevid kpa la Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk be, bol bɛl banna yir Nɔb. Ahimɛlɛk n wa nau, u hassi, u bɔra ra sa, u pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ i ra vol i bɛnnɛi? Ɛrɛɛ nɛr maa waa i ni jaawɛi?”
2Denii Deevid ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk be, “Koorii humiŋ di ŋɔ n wa ɛɛ wii bɛl, di ŋɔ n be, ‘Gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa wàá zum a widee.’ Ama, n kali n laallɔɔraa bá ra chemiŋ yembɛl. 3Bɛɛ diweere i dɔɔi? Tɛŋ paanuuzi anue gɛɛ kunla maa hin niŋ wer na.”
4Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ ŋɔ Deevid be, “Maa paanuuduma maa dɔɔwɛ, see paanuunanaananaa la baŋ ɔɔ chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la bɛnnɛ du de, di i laallɔɔra la ni haana waa chɔɔwɛ waa, lɛɛ ga tɛɛ baa.”
5Deevid ŋɔ, “Wibiiire, yaa ni haana waa ɔɔ ra chɔɔ di yaa haŋ wa ɛɛ sirya lugɔ ń lii. Ba haŋ wa ŋɔ ba vol voldumazi gba, ka ba ni haana waa ɔɔ ra chɔɔ, di gilɛɛ waa pɛɛzi volaa naa dɔŋ!” 6Awia, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la kpa a paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, a binaa di wa tɛu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa kpa a falaarɛ di wa dau a teebulnaniinanii ni, ka lizaa.
7A hɔl naa, di Koori Sɔɔl penɔɔna nabɔma banna yir Dɔwɛg n ɛɛ Ɛdɔm hinuu du de, di ra jaami Kɔraawiizi.
8Deevid pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk, “Haa kandaa gɛɛ tokobi maa dɔɔwɛ ɛŋŋ? Maa dɔŋkuŋ maa ni ballɛ, dikuu a koori huma la n ɛɛ siaahmu werge maa wia.”
9Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la ŋɔ, “Tokobi la n ɛɛ Goliaf la n ɛɛ Filisti hinuu, hiŋ kpuwɛɛ Ɛla Waluu labuu du ɛŋ. Waabuu ba kpa yakɔza di bɔɔri, u teli Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii tagtakpurii la har. Di i ra nyiŋŋuu, í kpa. Tokobi maa waa hoo ɛŋ, di u bɛŋ lɛi.”
Deevid ŋɔ, “Tokobi maa waa hoo lugɔu, kpau tɛŋ!”
Deevid n du Gaf wia
10A hɔl hiŋ, Deevid chɔ lii Koori Sɔɔl be, di kaali Gaf Koori Akis be. 11Ka Koori Akis balaa ŋɔ u be, “Deevid naa lɛi ɛɛ hɛri naa koori laa? Waa lɛi ba kpa du yira, baŋ ɔɔ waa sa, di ra yir,
‘Koori Sɔɔl kpu kagboŋaa,
ka Deevid kpu
kagboŋa fizi laa?’ ”
12Deevid kpa a wia hiŋ maa di du u biini, ɔnsii jaa lawuu werge maa dikuu Gaf Koori Akis wia. 13Uŋ faa du ba nonee biini la, u ɔɔ kutti ɛɛ u hiŋ lugɔ nɛr nyuu n waa hoo, di ra ɛɛ wia lugɔ chuglahiŋ, di ra piizi ba dominuuzenaa gbessi, di gil u nuuhaari pal di ra tuu u taŋhuna ni.
14Koori Akis ŋɔ u nabɔnzi la be, “Ií na a baal naa! U nyuu waa hoo, bɛɛ wiarɛ ii kpogluu di wa tɛnnɛi? 15N nyaa chugla hinaa lugɔ ii kaa kpogli baal naa wa tɛŋ, u ra ɛɛ wia naa dizi n sibɔɔ? A dɛkkɔɔ a baal naa dɔŋ n waa zuu n diaa?”

english_text:
People Join David
1 When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there. 2A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of 400 men.
3David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.” 4So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
5One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest.
Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
6Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him. 7He told them:
Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done. 8But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
9 Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub. 10Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
11Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came, 12Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.”
“Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
13Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
14“Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him. 15This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
16“Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
17Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!”
But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
18Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!”
On that same day, Doeg killed 85 priests. 19Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep.
Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
20Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David 21and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
22David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me. 23Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_text:
Deevid n du bolzenaa Adulam ni Mizpa wia
1Deevid lii bolzeŋ Gaf di chɔ la ga zuu bii bɔɔ bɛl n du Adulam. U kpɛɛnna, u mɛɛ ani ba diahina maa n wa nuu u wia de, ba maa la ga du u be de. 2Banla maa n ɛɛ anuula hina, kindiire ani biinichɔg hina ba, di wa chaali, u birgi ba sitɔɔri. Baala la n faa du u be la du lugɔ kalfaanaazu.
3Deevid lii de di la Mizpa la n du Moab hɛri la, di ga ŋɔ de koori be, “I daŋ gil n maa ni n mɛɛ ba di wa so ii be, ka ń binni na wii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ɛɛ tɛŋŋ?” 4A koori sɛɛ, di gil ba ba wa so u be, di ra la saŋa la maga Deevid n du a bii bɔɔ la.
5Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Gad ba di wa ŋɔ Deevid be, “Gilɛɛ suah a bii bɔɔ naa, izi la Juda hɛri.” Denii Deevid jaa izi di kpa la Hɛrɛf kɔr biini, di ga du de.
Koori Sɔɔl n kpu Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Nɔb biini wia
6A hɔl bɛl, Koori Sɔɔl so Gibia giŋgimii nyuu, tamaris daa bɛl bɔsɔŋ, di kpogli u kandaa, u nabɔnzi chaali chi baruu.
