Ba wa ŋɔ u be lugɔ ba na Deevid ni u laallɔɔraa. 7Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ ba be, “Bɛnjamin dee baala, ii ra nuu! Jɛssɛ biibaal naa daŋ mɔnni hɛssi ni pattibɔra tɛɛ ii maa? U daŋ gil ii maa ɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa ani nɛra kalfazi sitɔɔraa? 8A gunnɛ gillɛ ii maa chi n nii? Nɛr maa sɛɛwɛ ú ŋɔ n be, n biibaal ni Jɛssɛ biibaal n ɛɛ nuukpaŋ wia. N wia waa ii bɛl maa titte gɛɛ ú wa ŋɔ n be, gunla n biibaal n chugzi n balii di ra du ŋɔ ú chɔɔ guuŋ, gunla unna ɛɛ zinaa naa.”
9Denii Dɔwɛg la n ɛɛ Ɛdɔm hinuu la gba faa chi Koori Sɔɔl nabɔnzi la be, di ŋɔ, “N faa na Jɛssɛ biibaal la n ba Ahitub biibaal, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk be, Nɔb. 10Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi tɛu. U kaa tɛu diwee ge jaa, haali di kpa Goliaf la n ɛɛ Filisti hinuu la tokobi la gba di jaau.”
11Awia, Koori Sɔɔl hum dí ba ga yir Ahitub biibaal Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk ani u mɛɛ ni ba dee la maa n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, n du Nɔb la, bá ba. Ba jaa ba. 12Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ahitub biibaal, a nuu!”
U ŋɔ, “Jara, n na nuu.”
13Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ni Jɛssɛ biibaal chi n ni, haali i tɛu paanuu ani tokobi, di kaa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi tɛuwɛi? U birgi dignikpega hiŋ, di ga suah di guuŋ alugɔ kennaa unna ɛɛ zinaa naanɛi?”
14Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk ŋɔ koori be, “I nabɔnzi naa maa biini, ú bɛliirɛ dɔɔ wibii lugɔ i hila Deevidei? Waabuu ɛɛ i laallɔɔra la n na binnii la nabɔma, i diahina maa ge ra tɛu tɔgzuu. 15A waa lugɔ a hɔl naa bɛnnɛ n faari di pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di ra tɛu. Akai! Gilɛɛ wa kpa wia di ra chug n ni n diahina pɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, maa wiimaa zummɛ di lii a wia naa biini, tama maa.”
16Ka Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk, i ni i diahina maanii niŋ siu.”
17Denii koori ŋɔ laallɔɔra la n na binnuu la be, “Ií bir kpuuzi Kɔraawiizi kizeehina naa, dikuu baŋ lɛɛwɛ jaa Deevid ni wia. Ba zummɔɔ unna chɔ, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ n be.”
Ka koori laallɔɔra la waa sɛɛwɛ bá izi kpu Kɔraawiizi kizeehina hiŋ.
18Denii u ŋɔ Dɔwɛg be, “Hiŋwaa kpu a kizeehina naa maa.” Ɛdɔm hinuu Dɔwɛg la kpu ba maa. A hɔl hiŋ, baala tokkoanaazu ni banuere u kpu, di ba haa laali ba Kizeehina pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaa tagtakpuree. 19U gil ba kpu Nɔb hina la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, baala ni haana, ba bichalli ni biifulli, ba nauna, ba kauzi ani ba peeza maa.
20Ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk biibaal Abiata waa na bɔr chɔ la Deevid be. 21Uŋ ga hel de, u ŋɔ Deevid be lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl kpu Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la maanii nyaamm. 22Denii Deevid ŋɔ Abiata be, “A hɔl la miŋ na Ɛdɔm hinuu Dɔwɛg de la, n zummɔ lugɔ u daŋ ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be. Awia, i mɛɛ ni u diahina maa siu chugimbuu. 23Du n be ɛŋ, di gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Koori Sɔɔl ra nyiŋŋi n nii maa kpuirɛ. I daŋ na i hiŋ n be bɔnnaa.”

english_text:
David Rescues the Town of Keilah
1One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
2David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?”
“Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
3But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
4David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
5David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
6-8Meanwhile, Saul heard that David was in Keilah. “God has let me catch David,” Saul said. “David is trapped inside a walled town where the gates can be locked.” Saul decided to go there and surround the town, in order to trap David and his men. He sent messengers who told the towns and villages, “Send men to serve in Saul's army!”
By this time, Abiathar had joined David in Keilah and had brought along everything he needed to get answers from God.
9David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
10David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me. 11Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.”
“Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
12David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?”
“Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
13David and his 600 men got out of there fast and started moving from place to place. Saul heard that David had left Keilah, and he decided not to go after him.
Jonathan Says David Will Be King
14David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
15One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him. 16But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David. 17“Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
18 They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh.
David Escapes from Saul
19 Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon. 20If you come, we will help you catch him.”
21Saul told them:
You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you. 22Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky. 23Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
24The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert. 25Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert.
Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him. 26Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men, 27when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
28Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
29David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_text:
Deevid n lɛɛ Keila hina wia
1Baŋ wa ŋɔ Deevid be, “Na, Filisti hinaa kpa laal di ga fɔɔ bol bɛl banna yir Keila, di ra paagi ba diwee, ba pilli.” 2Awia, u faa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “A dɛkkɔɔ ń la ga yoo Filisti hina naa?”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Izi la ga yoo baa, di lɛɛ Keila hina ta.”
3Ka Deevid laallɔɔra la ŋɔ u be, “Haali yaa n du Juda naa, ka ɔnsii lau yaabuu. A kaa ɛɛ lugɔ ya la Keila ga lɔ a Filisti hina naa?”
4Denii Deevid kuari pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, u ŋɔ u be, “Izi la Keila, n daŋ kpa Filisti hina du i nonee, í kpegli baa.” 5Awia, Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la Keila, di ga yoo Filisti hina di kpu bakpila maa, ka lauri ba sela maa. U faa lɛɛ Keila hinaa lii Filisti hina nonee biini, ba dɔɔ bahinaa. 6Saŋa la Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk biibaal Abiata n faa chɔwɛɛ la Deevid be la, u faa kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ tagtakpurii ifɔd labuu di ba.
Koori Sɔɔl n dau Deevid luge wia
7Koori Sɔɔl n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Deevid du Keila, u jaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi kpaubuu du n nonee biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, u lau u hinnɛ, uŋ zuu bol la baŋ ma koŋlii bar chem, u dɔɔ lugbia dominuukpega labuu.” 8Awia, Koori Sɔɔl yir u laallɔɔra maa, di ŋɔ bá la ga fɔɔ Deevid ni u laallɔɔra Keila, di lɔ baa.
9Deevid n wa zummɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl vɔɔ ú kpui jinaa di ra nyiŋŋuu la, u ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata be, “Kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehina tagtakpurii ifɔd la ba.” 10Denii Deevid ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, mìŋ́ i balii nuuwɔɔ nɛnnɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl ɛɛ siryaa ú ba Keila, di wa chɔgi u ni u nɛra maa dikuu n wia. 11Keila hina daŋ kpaŋ du u nonee biiniaa? Koori Sɔɔl daŋ ba ɛŋ gunla i balii n nuuwɛ naa? N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, gil i balii zum.”
Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “U daŋ ba.”
12Deevid kuari pɛɛzi, “Keila hina daŋ kpa n ni n laallɔɔra maa du Koori Sɔɔl nonee?”
Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Ba daŋ ɛɛ guŋ.”
13Awia, Deevid ni u laallɔɔra kalfaanumbɛl la maa lii Keila di ra gaagi bɔrazi. Koori Sɔɔl n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Deevid chɔwɔɔrɛ lii Keila, waa kaa la de.
14Deevid la ga suah Zif Hɛribɔduma giŋgimee hɛri. Koori Sɔɔl ɔɔ izuu hɔpizi biimaa, di gaagi ra nyiŋŋuu. Ka Kɔraawiizi faa waa sɛɛwɛ kpa Deevid du u nonee biini.
15Deevid faa du Hɔrɛs, Zif Hɛribɔduma biini, di nuu lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl ballɔɔ, ú wa kpuu. 16Denii Jonatan izi di la Deevid be Hɔrɛs, di gaa duu bɔkpega ú haa vɛɛ yardi Kɔraawiizi, 17di ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm, dikuubɛɛwiai, n mɛɛ Sɔɔl wàá wer kpui. I daŋ di Izrɛl kora, ń ge ra hiŋ i ni. Haali n mɛɛ gba zum gunnɛ.” 18Denii ba nɛra banɛɛ hiŋ maa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ Kɔraawiizi see. Jonatan bir kpo, ka Deevid waa haa du Hɔrɛs.
19Denii Zif hina baŋhina la Koori Sɔɔl be Gibia, di ga ŋɔ, “Deevid la lɛi suah Hɔrɛs giŋgimee hɛri la n du Bizeŋ Hakila barii, Jɛsimɔn wiifurii nodig wiikakag laa? 20Jara, i daŋ wer ba de saŋa la maa hinna nyiŋŋi. Di i wa ballɔ, yaa daŋ hiinii lawuu.”
21Denii Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ia, dikuu n wia n tir ia kennaa wia! 22Ií haa la ga binni na nɛnnɛ, di zum bɔra la uŋ ɔɔ ra la ani nɛra la n nau de. Ba ŋɔ n benii lugɔ u dɔɔ nunzumaa werge. 23Ií la ga binni bɔra la maa n ɛɛ bɔsuahlaa, di zumaa nɛnnɛ, ka ba wa ŋɔ n be, n ni ii maa la ga dau u luge di lawuu, haali di Juda hɛri maa gbaa ya pigzi.”
24Denii ba bir tɔ see Koori Sɔɔl ni, di la Zif. A saŋa naa di Deevid ni u laallɔɔra du Mayɔn Hɛribɔduma, di suah Jɔɔdan Waluu n du Jɛsimɔn wiifurii nodig wiikakag. 25Denii Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra jaa faari di ra nyiŋŋuu. Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u izi chɔ di ga suah giŋgimii bɛl n du Mayɔn Hɛribɔduma. Koori Sɔɔl n wa nuu guŋ, u izi la de di gaa nyiŋŋuu.
26Koori Sɔɔl faa ga a giŋgimii keŋkere bɛllɛ di ra nyiŋŋuu. Deevid ge ni u laallɔɔra ga u keŋkere bɛl di ra hahzi, bá chɔ, Koori Sɔɔl gilɛɛ waa na baa. Saŋa la Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra n waa dugli baa, di ra nyiŋŋi ba lauri baa, 27ka nɛbɛl ba wa ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Jara, ba manaŋ! Filisti hina kaa waa lɔ yaa hɛrii.” 28Denii Koori Sɔɔl gil Deevid nyiŋŋaa, ka la ú ga lɔ Filisti hina. Awiarɛ ba ra yir a bɔr hiŋ Sɛla Hamalɛkɔf la. 29Deevid jaa lii de di la gaa zuu Ɛn Gɛdi bia bɔɔni.

english_text:
David Lets Saul Live
1When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi. 2Saul led 3,000 of Israel's best soldiers out to look for David and his men near Wild Goat Rocks at En-Gedi. 3 There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself.
David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave. 4They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.”
David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing. 5Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that, 6-7 and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.”
Saul left the cave and started down the road. 8Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance.
Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low 9and said:
Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you? 10You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!” 11Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
12I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you. 13An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
14 Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea. 15I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
16“David, my son—is that you?” Saul asked. Then he started crying 17and said:
David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you. 18You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance. 19If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
20I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that. 21Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
22So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_text:
Deevid n vɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl kpui wia
1Saŋa la Koori Sɔɔl n wa yoo Filisti hina ka bir ba la, nɛbɛl ŋɔ u be, “Deevid du Ɛn Gɛdi Hɛribɔduma labuu.” 2Denii Koori Sɔɔl lizi u laallɔɔra kagboŋa ahoro la, n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ Izrɛl hɛri maa biini, bá la ga nyiŋŋi Deevid ni u laallɔɔra, bɔr la banna yir Pir Buuna Bia la.
3Denii u wa hel peliga la n du a ŋmɛnikɛrii, di bii bɔɔ du de, Koori Sɔɔl jaa zuu de, ú bɛɛ zahara. Di Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la ge du a bii bɔɔ lume. 4Deevid laallɔɔra ŋɔ u be, “Zinaa hɔpizii naa wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ kpa i dɔm du i nonee biini, í ɛɛu gunla n parii.’ ” Denii Deevid suahzi di ga mɔŋ Koori Sɔɔl tagta nua, di waa zummɛ.
5Deevid n wa ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ, u biini bir chɔgi werge maa, dikuu uŋ mɔŋ Koori Sɔɔl tagta la wia, 6u bir ŋɔ u laallɔɔra la be, “Kɔ́raawiizi ra la a ni bɔɔnɛɛ, ń waa ɛɛ n dɔɔri wichɔgii maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu Kɔraawiizi lizi u ɛɛ koori.” 7Kenne u ŋɔ, ka nyɛgi ba ni lugɔ bá gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl wiimaa. Koori Sɔɔl jaa lii a bii bɔɔ di ra kaali.
8Denii Deevid lii a bii bɔɔ hiŋ biini, di yir Koori Sɔɔl, “Jara,” U bir binni, Deevid jaa chɔɔ pi, 9ka ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Ɛrɛɛ i ra nuu nɛra nuuzi lugɔ mìŋ́ Deevid ra nyiŋŋi i kpuirɛi? 10I himmaa siwii nawɔɔrɛ zinaa lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kpaibuu du n nonee, a bii bɔɔ naa biini. Baŋhina ŋɔ ń kpui, n vɛɛ ka ŋɔ, ‘Màá lalli n nonii gbɔgzi n dɔɔri, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu Kɔraawiizi lizi u ɛɛ koori.’ 11N mɛ, na i tagta yenne du n nonii la! N mɔŋ u yenne, ka maa sɛɛwɛ ń kpui. Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu i zum filaŋkeŋ lugɔ maa ɛɛwɛ leu gɛɛ di vɛɛi, maa wichɔgii maa ɛɛwɛ di zuu i ni, ka i ra daaziŋ í kpu. 12Kɔ́raawiizii niŋ di n nii maa seriya. Waabuu niŋ turgii i wichɔgaa la maa hinna ɛɛŋ la kim, ka miŋwaa nonii wàá gbɔgzii. 13Gunla baŋ ɔɔ ta sɛɛlii faa maa di ŋɔ la, ‘Wichɔgɛɛra benii wichɔgaa ra lii.’ Awia, màá kpa n nonii gbɔgzii maa.
14Anɛɛ Izrɛl koori lii di ra nyiŋŋi ú lauwɛi? Anɛɛ lugee i ra dawɛi? Nuahiŋ siwii gɛɛ kariŋgbai? 15Kɔraawiizii niŋ di yaa maa seriya. Waabuu niŋ bagli unla hor n waa sum. Waabuu niŋ di wibii di lɛɛŋ lii i nonee biini.”
16Deevid n wa ŋɔwɛɛ tuŋ, Koori Sɔɔl pɛɛzuu, “N biibaal Deevid, i loobiire n na nuu naa?” Koori Sɔɔl jaa chɛɛhgi werge maa, 17ka ŋɔ, “I ɛɛ biinihuŋŋu hinnɛ werge kaaliŋ. I ɛɛmbuu nɛnnɛ, ka miŋwaa ɛɛi chumaa. 18Zinaa, i baglimbuu winanaa la hiŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛŋ. Kɔraawiizi kpambuu du i nonee biini, ka haa sɛɛwɛ kpuŋ. 19Di baal wa na u dɔm, ɔɔ giluubuu u kaali di wàá duu piraa? Kɔ́raawiizi kissii werge maa, dikuu kennaa hiŋ suŋ n ni zinaa naa wia! 20N zummɔɔ nɛnnɛ maa lugɔ i daŋ di kora Izrɛl hɛri. Á kora chi nɛnnɛ. 21Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu í ŋɔ nua, di hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini, lugɔ hàá kpu n dee maa gɛɛ di dim n sɔŋ lii n mɛɛ diahina biini.”
22Denii Deevid ŋɔ a nua, di hɛɛhzi tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl.
Koori Sɔɔl jaa bir kaali bol, ka Deevid ni u laallɔɔra bir kaali ba suahribɔr la.

english_text:
Samuel Dies
1Samuel died, and people from all over Israel gathered to mourn for him when he was buried at his home in Ramah. Meanwhile, David moved his camp to Paran Desert.
Abigail Keeps David from Killing Innocent People
2-3Nabal was a very rich man who lived in Maon. He owned 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats, which he kept at Carmel. His wife Abigail was sensible and beautiful, but he was from the Caleb clan and was rough and mean.
4One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it. 5-6So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal:
I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you. 7I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep.
When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them. 8Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing.
My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
9David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
10This is what he said:
Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days. 11What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
12The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
13“Everybody get your swords!” David ordered.
They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other 400 followed David.
14-16Meanwhile, one of Nabal's servants told Abigail:
David's men were often nearby while we were taking care of the sheep in the fields. They were very good to us, they never hurt us, and nothing was ever stolen from us while they were nearby. With them around day or night, we were as safe as we would have been inside a walled city.
David sent some messengers from the desert to wish our master well, but he shouted insults at them. 17He's a bully who won't listen to anyone.
Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
18Abigail quickly got together 200 loaves of bread, two large clay jars of wine, the meat from five sheep, a large sack of roasted grain, 100 handfuls of raisins, and 200 handfuls of dried figs. She loaded all the food on donkeys 19and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
20Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
21David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults. 22I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
23Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David. 24Then she said:
Sir, please let me explain! 25Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him!
I didn't see the men you sent, 26-27but please take this gift of food that I've brought and share it with your followers. The Lord has kept you from taking revenge and from killing innocent people. But I hope your enemies and anyone else who wants to harm you will end up like Nabal. I swear this by the living Lord and by your life.
28Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live. 29The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
30The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you, 31and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people.
When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
32David told her:
I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today. 33And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people. 34If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
35David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
36Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night. 37But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone. 38Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
39-40David heard that Nabal had died. “I praise the Lord!” David said. “He has judged Nabal guilty for insulting me. The Lord kept me from doing anything wrong, and he made sure that Nabal hurt only himself with his own evil.”
David and Abigail Are Married
Abigail was still at Carmel. So David sent messengers to ask her if she would marry him.
41She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
42Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
43David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives. 44 Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_text:
Samuɛl siu wia
1Denii Samuɛl siu, Izrɛl hina maa chaali di wii u lee, ka jaa huguu u bol Rama.
Deevid ni Abigeel wia
Denii Deevid ni u laallɔɔra izi di la ga chɔɔ Mayɔn Hɛribɔduma. 2Baal bɛl faa du bolzeŋ Mayɔn, di dɔɔ hɛri bol bɛl banna yir Kamɛl. U faa ɛɛ daama hinnɛ werge maa, di dɔɔ buuna kagboŋ ani peeza kagboŋa ahoro. U ɔɔ faa ra fuŋ u peeza hunaa de. 3U sɔnnɛ faa Nabal, u haaŋ ge sɔnnɛ faa Abigeel. A haaŋ faa ɛɛ nunzunnii di ɛɛ toloori, ka u jaari faa ɛɛ Kalɛb domee hinuu di du nyɛg, di kaa dɔɔ biinikpola.
4Deevid n du a hɛribɔduma la, u nuu lugɔ Nabal ra fuŋ u peeza hunaa. 5Awia, u hum biipɔllaa fi, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií la Kamɛl di ga jaami Nabal tɛŋ. 6Ií ŋɔ u be, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ i ni i diahina miibɔɔjaŋ! Ú kissi i kundɔɔlaa maa!
7N nuuwɔɔ lugɔ i ra fuŋ i peeza hunaa. Yaa ni i penɔɔna maa n faa du Kamɛl la, yaa ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa wichɔgii maa kpawɛɛ di dau baa, gɛɛ di ŋmɛɛ ba kundɔɔlii bɛl maa gba. 8Pɛɛzi i penɔɔna hiŋ, ba daŋ ŋɔ i be. Yaa ba i benii hɔpizizeŋ dii saŋa naa, suŋ n biipɔllaa naa ni, di tɛɛ i balaa ni mìŋ́ i biibaal Deevid kunla maa hiŋ dɔɔwɛ.’ ”
9Deevid balaa hiŋ n wa hel Nabal be, ba lizi Deevid amaniye hiŋ tɛu, ka jaa ra kpaŋ.
10Nabal pɛɛzi baa, “Anɛɛ Deevid naanɛi? Anɛɛ Jɛssɛ biibaal naanɛi? Zinaa hɔpizii naa, balaa kpila maanii ra chɔ ba dɔɔra. 11Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń kpa n diwee ni nii ani sela la miŋ kpuwɛɛ, ń tɛɛ n balaa n na fuŋ n peeza huna, di tɛɛ nɛra la miŋ waa zummɛi?”
12Denii Deevid balaa hiŋ bir kaali. Baŋ ga helle, ba bagli gunla maa Nabal n ŋɔwɛɛ. 13Deevid ŋɔ u laallɔɔra be, “Ií kpa ii tokobizi laali!” Ba jaa kpaa, ka u ge himmaa kpa u hor. Laallɔɔra kalfaanaazuu faa hiŋuu di la, ka ba kalfaanɛɛ ge so di ra binni ba diwee ni ba dɔŋkuna.
14Nabal balaa la bɛl la u haaŋ Abigeel be, di ga ŋɔ, “Deevid hum u balaarɛ ba ba wa jaami yaa dɔɔri, ka u chagzi baa. 15Ka a nɛra naa faa ɛɛ yaabuu nɛnnɛ. Saŋa la maa yaa n faa du pir di dugli baa la, ba ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa yaa wichɔgii maa ɛɛwɛ, yaa kummaa ge faa waa leuwe. 16Wibii maa, ba ɔɔ faa ra du yaa taurɛ wibaŋzi ni hahmuŋzi maa, saŋa la yaa n ɔɔ nɔɔni yaa peeza di ga dugli baa la. 17Awia, binni a wii naa di na gunla hin niŋ ɛɛ, di guŋ lɛi yaa ni yaa dɔɔri ani u diahina maanii du siaahmu biini. Nɛr maa wàá wer ŋɔ wia tɛu u nuu, dikuu u biinikpola werge wia.”
18Abigeel lɔ izi kakpaŋ, di kpa paanuuzi kalfaanɛɛ, siŋ hure anɛɛ, peɔɔzaa anue, mihallaa bɔɔtizi anue, grepu nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ mari dɔŋa a hil kalfa ani fig nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ mari dɔŋa a hil ge kalfaanɛɛ, di kpaa vɔɔ sag kauzi ni. 19Denii u ŋɔ u balaa be, “Ií kpaa ra tɔ see n na ba.” Ka waa sɛɛwɛɛ ŋɔ u jaari Nabal be.
20Denii Abigeel tinni u kawee di wa hel bizeŋ bɛl zɛɛ gɔmbɔɔ, di Deevid ni u laallɔɔraa tuuwe ra chem u ni. 21Deevid jaa ra fɛ u biini, “Kuuhni naa maa miŋ kuuhwɛ di binni baal naa kundɔɔlaa hɛribɔduma naa biini, bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa leu naa, ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. U bittɔɔ kpa wichɔgaa di ra turgiŋ n winanaa kim. 22N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ kɛrɛ chɔɔzi, di maa u ni u nɛra maa kpuwɛɛ, Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ!”
23Abigeel n wa na Deevid, u lii u kawee nyuu tuu manaŋ, di giŋŋi u see, di willi u nyuu. 24Uŋ giŋŋi u see hiŋ, u ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, gil a sɔnchɔgii chug n bɛŋ. Jaande maa, ka nuu gunla i balii n niŋ ŋɔ. 25Awia, gilɛɛ gil n dɔɔri wàá hagzi biinikpola hiŋ Nabal naa. U sɔŋ duulaa u du la, u sɔŋ hiŋ zɛɛrɛ, Gɛnii, gunnɛ gillɛ u ra ɛɛ gɛnni wia la. N dɔɔri, miŋwaa faa waa i balaa la hiŋ hummɛ la nawɛɛ.
26Kɔraawiizii laafii, haa i dɔma naa kpuwɛɛ í turgi baa ba wichɔgaa kim. Awia, n kpa Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa sɔnnɛ hɛɛhzi di ra tɛi lugɔ, i dɔm la maa n na fɛ i ni wichɔgaa, daŋ na dignitɛraa alugɔ Nabal. 27Awia, n dɔɔri, gaafura, ka lɛɛ n sunzaa naa tɛɛ i laallɔɔra. 28Jaande maa, ka gil mìŋ́ i balii wichɔgaa tɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ haŋ giluu i ni i naanna di Izrɛl kora di hanna la, dikuu hinna yoo u laalzi wia. Gilɛɛ waa gil bá waa na wichɔgii maa i ni, i de dui maa biini. 29Haali nɛbɛl n na nyiŋŋii ú kpui naa gba, ka Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la daŋ lɛɛi gunla nɛr n ɔɔ ra du u kumpazi tau la. Ka i dɔma waa, u daŋ ta baa gunla baŋ ɔɔ ta bilori la. 30Di Kɔraawiizi wa ɛɛ winanaa la maa uŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ hìŋ́ n dɔɔri, di gil i ɛɛ Izrɛl koori la, 31n dɔɔri, i biini wàá chɔgi gɛɛ di tirii, dikuu hiŋ kpu nɛra pɛɛpɛɛ gɛɛ di bir turgi nɛra ba wichɔgaa kim wia. Di Kɔraawiizi wa kissii, n dɔɔri, jaande maa, gilɛɛ waa suuh n wia.”
32Denii Deevid ŋɔ Abigeel be, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la dɛg chɔlaarɛ, uŋ humii zinaa, i wa chem n ni! 33Kɔ́raawiizi kissii, dikuu nfɛrnanii naa hiŋ tɛŋ di bir n liize, di gil maa wichɔgaa ɛɛwɛ di kpu nɛra zinaa, di turgi baa ba wichɔgaa kim naa wia. 34Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum labuu gillɛ maa ia kpuwɛɛ. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa lugɔ di i faa waa n ni wa chemme manaŋ, hɔɔ daŋ vii waa pizi, di n kpu Nabal ni baala la maa n ɛɛ u nɛra la nyaamm.”
35Denii Deevid lɛɛ kuna la uŋ kpawɛɛ di ba wa tɛu la, ka jaa ŋɔ, “Bir di ra kpo ni bɔsɔna. N daŋ ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.”
36Abigeel n bittɛ la Nabal be, di u du dia di ra di diuzenaa alugɔ koori, u bɔra sɔɔni, u dɛɛzi werge maa. Awia, u faa waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ wiimaa tɛu, ka hɔɔ wa pizi. 37Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzi ni, di siŋ la jaa lii Nabal siwee, u haaŋ ŋɔ u be wia la maa n dɛɛ ɛɛwɛ. Uŋ wa nuu guŋ, u banchule lɔ werge maa, u bɔra siu, u gbɛr kakpaŋ. 38Hɔpizaa fi harbɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi lɔu, u siu.
39Deevid n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Nabal siuwɔ, u ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ jaannɛ, uŋ turgi Nabal u wichɔgaa kim, dikuu uŋ chagziŋ wia, ka waa gillɛ n ɛɛ wichɔgii maa. U tɛr Nabal dignii, di gil u wichɔgaa laŋŋi u ni.”
Denii Deevid hum nɛra Abigeel be lugɔ u ra nyiŋŋuubuu, ú kpa ɛɛ haaŋ. 40U balaa la Kamɛl di ga ŋɔ Abigeel be, “Deevidii hum yaa i be, lugɔ ya wa kpai ba, í birgi u haaŋ.”
41Awia, Abigeel giŋŋi di willi u nyuu, ka ŋɔ, “Mìŋ́ i baliirɛ keŋ, n ɛɛ siryaa ń humii, di sanzi i balaa naazi.” 42Denii Abigeel izi manaŋ, di tinni u kawee, u balaa banue la n du u be la duu. Ba ni Deevid balaa la maa kpa di la, u ga birgi Deevid haaŋ. 43Deevid faa kpa Ahinoam n lii Jɛzriil, banɛɛ hiŋ maa faa jaa ɛɛ u haana. 44Ka Koori Sɔɔl faa kpa u biihaaŋ Mikal la n faa ɛɛ Deevid haaŋ la, di tɛɛ Layis biibaal Palti n lii bol bɛl banna yir Galim.

english_text:
David Again Lets Saul Live
1 Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
2Saul took 3,000 of Israel's best soldiers and went to look for David there in Ziph Desert. 3Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert.
When David heard that Saul was following him, 4he sent some spies to find out if it was true. 5Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them. 6David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?”
“I will!” Abishai answered.
7That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
8Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
9“Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king. 10As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle. 11 But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
12David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep. 13David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance. 14“Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?”
Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
15“Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight. 16You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
17Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?”
“Yes it is, Your Majesty. 18Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime? 19Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods. 20Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
21“David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
22“Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it. 23The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right. 24I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
25“David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!”
David in Philistia
Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_text:
Deevid n kaa vɛɛ Sɔɔl kpui wia
1A hɔl bɛl, Zif hina la Koori Sɔɔl be Gibia, di ga ŋɔ, “Deevid lɛi suah Bizeŋ Hakila n chaŋ Juda Hɛribɔduma laa?”
2Denii Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔkpega kagboŋa ahoro, la Zif hɛribɔduma, bá ga nyiŋŋi Deevid de. 3Koori Sɔɔl ga chɔɔ dugli ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛl n chɔɔ Bizeŋ Hakila la n chaŋ Jɛsimɔn nyuu, ka Deevid du a hɛribɔduma biini. Uŋ wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl duŋŋi u lugee di ba de la, 4u hum nɛra, bá la ga daani de na, dí Koori Sɔɔl ba denii wibii maa?
5Denii Deevid izi di kpa la bɔr la Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra n wa chɔɔwɛ la. U ga na bɔr la Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra nabɔma Nɛɛr biibaal Abna n chɔɔwɛ. Koori Sɔɔl faa chɔɔ u laallɔɔra hiŋ baambaannɛ, ka ba chɔɔ baruu.
6Denii Deevid pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Hitti hinuu Ahimɛlɛk ni Zɛruya biibaal Abisai n ɛɛ Joab lulli la, “Ú bɛliirɛ niŋ duŋ la Koori Sɔɔl chɔɔribɔrɛi?”
Abisai ŋɔ, “N nii daŋ la.”
7Denii Deevid ni Abisai la a laallɔɔra be a hamuŋa ni, di Koori Sɔɔl chɔɔ ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ di ra chɔɔ dɔɔ, ka u kandaa baŋ di dugli u nyuu. Abna ni u laallɔɔra ge chɔɔ baruu.
8Abisai ŋɔ Deevid be, “Kɔraawiizi kpa i dɔnnɛ du i nonee zinaa. Gil ń yaguu ni n kandaa kakpaŋ di pɛli hɛri, màá tɔɔuh bunɛɛ!”
9Ka Deevid ŋɔ Abisai be, “Gilɛɛ kpuu! Anɛɛ n niŋ wer kpa nonii gbɔgzi nɛr la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ, di waa di bilchɔgɛi?” 10Deevid kaa ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la, lugɔ Kɔraawiizi himmaanii niŋ kpuu gɛɛ u saŋaa niŋ wa hel gɛɛ laal biinii bá kpuu. 11Kɔraawiizi gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ lugɔ n wa kpa n nonii di ra gbɔgzi nɛr la uŋ lizɛɛ. Gil ya kpa u kandaa ani u lɔŋgɔm waa di ra la.”
12Denii Deevid kpa kandaa la ni lɔŋgɔm la n dugli Koori Sɔɔl nyuu la, ba kaali, di nɛr maa faa waa baa nawɛɛ gɛɛ di zum guŋ, gɛɛ di izi dɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii faa gillɛ ba chɔɔ a guŋ dɔbɛrii.
13Denii Deevid gi a waluu baŋgia bɛl, di ga chi giŋgimii nyuu bɔɔnɛɛ. 14Ka jaa gbooli yir Koori Sɔɔl laallɔɔra ani Nɛɛr biibaal Abna, di ŋɔ, “Abna, hàá sɛɛ n be gɛɛ?”
Abna bir ŋɔ, “Anɛɛ n na yir koorei?”
15Deevid bir ŋɔ u be, “Abna, baal lɛi hiŋ? Anɛɛ n lugɔi, Izrɛl hɛri biinei? Ɛrɛɛ haa i dɔɔri koori guuwei? Nɛbɛl ballɔɔ ú wa kpuu. 16Gunla hiŋ ɛɛwɛ la waa wer. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la lugɔ i ni i laallɔɔra maanii dɛg kpui, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii waa wette guu ii dɔɔri la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ u ɛɛ koori la. Ií binni de na, lee a koori kandaa ni u lɔŋgɔm la n chigɛ dugli u nyuu la duɛi?”
17Koori Sɔɔl nuu Deevid loobii, di zum lugɔ waabuu. Di yiruu, “N biibaal Deevid, i loobiire naa?”
Deevid sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, minuu, n dɔɔri koori. 18Bɛɛ wiarɛ hìŋ́ n dɔɔri, ra duŋŋi míŋ̀ i balii kennei? Bɛɛ n ɛɛi? Bɛɛ bilchɔgrɛ n dɔɔi? 19Awia, Jara, a nuu míŋ̀ i balii wiŋɔzi naa. Di Kɔraawiizii gillɛ i ra yooŋ, guŋwaa, n daŋ lizi mbusu lizaa kuna tɛu. Ka di nɛraa ɛɛ guŋ, nuuseei di baa Kɔraawiizi see! Ba duŋŋimbuu filaŋkeŋ lii hɛri la miŋ di kapɛttɛ Kɔraawiizi be la, ka ŋɔ, ‘La gaa kuari hɛrdumazi vuga.’ 20Awia, n na suŋŋiibuu lugɔ i gilɛɛ wa gil n siu bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n waa duglɛɛ. Bɛɛwiarɛ Izrɛl koori lii di ra nyiŋŋi mìŋ́ nɛr la n lugɔ kariŋgbai, gɛɛ kpaaŋ n ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi zaahri bizenaa nyuuni lai?”
21Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. Bir a ba, n biibaal Deevid, dikuubɛɛwiai, i vɛɛ n miibɔɔ lizaarɛ zinaa, màá kaa ɛɛ ania ń dui pira maa. N ɛɛ wiarɛ lugɔ gɛnii, di leu werge, wibii maa.”
22Ka Deevid ŋɔ, “Koori kandaarɛ keŋ. Gil i biipɔllaa la bɛl gi wa lɛɛu. 23Nɛr la wia n deŋlee, u kaa dɔɔ wibii daŋ na tɔna Kɔraawiizi be. U kpaibuu du n nonee zinaa, ka màá kpa n nonii di gbɔgzi nɛr la uŋ lizɛɛ u ɛɛ koori. 24Kennaa miŋ vɛɛ i miibɔɔ lizaa zinaa naa, Kɔ́raawiizi vɛɛ n ge miibɔɔ lizaa guŋ, di lɛɛŋ lii tɔɔrɔɔ maa biini!”
25Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Deevid be, “N biibaal Deevid, Kɔ́raawiizi kissii. I daŋ ɛɛ wizenaa, i wia kuari.”
Denii Deevid bir kaali, ka Koori Sɔɔl ge bir kpo bol.

english_text:
1but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
2-3David and his 600 men went across the border to stay in Gath with King Achish the son of Maoch. His men brought their families with them. David brought his wife Ahinoam whose hometown was Jezreel, and he also brought his wife Abigail who had been married to Nabal from Carmel. 4When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
5One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
6Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
7David was in Philistia for a year and four months. 8The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns. 9Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there.
After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish, 10who would ask, “Where did you attack today?”
David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.” 11That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.”
David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia. 12But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_text:
Deevid n ga soge Filisti hina biini wia
1Denii Deevid fɛ nfɛrɛ, di ŋɔ, “Hɔpizii bɛl, Koori Sɔɔl daŋ kpuŋ. Wii la n dɛkkɛ min niŋ ɛɛ maanii, miŋ chɔwɛɛ kaali Filisti hɛri. Gunnɛ niŋ gil Koori Sɔɔl gil n nyiŋŋaa Izrɛl hɛri naa biini, ka n na n hiŋ.”
2Denii Deevid ni u laallɔɔra kalfaanumbɛl la n du u be la, izi di la Gaf baal bɛl baŋ faa yir Mayɔk, u biibaal Koori Akis be. 3Deevid ni u laallɔɔra ni ba diinihina la so Gaf, di jaa Koori Akis ni. Deevid ge ni u haana banɛɛ, Jɛzriil hinuu Ahinoam ni Kamɛl hinuu Abigeel ge n ɛɛ Nabal luhaaŋ la. 4Koori Sɔɔl n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Deevid chɔwɔɔ kaali Gaf, u jaa gil u nyiŋŋaa.
5Denii Deevid ŋɔ Koori Akis be, “Di i dɔɔ n bila, tɛŋ bɔr i hɛri naa bola naa bɛl biini, ń ga so de. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ míŋ̀ i balii nii so koori bolzeŋ naa biinei?”
6Awia, Koori Akis kpa Ziklag tɛu, de haŋ ɛɛ Juda koora bɔr, di wa lii ni zinaa. 7Deevid faa so Filisti hɛri biŋkpaŋ ni baaguzi anaazu.
8A guŋ saŋa, Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la ga lɔ Gɛsur, Girzi ani Amalɛk hina la n faa soge a hɛri faala maa, di lii Suur di ga hel Ijip hɛri la. 9Deevid haŋ wa pig yemmaa, waa ɔɔ gil baal gɛɛ haaŋ maa du de ni miibɔɔ, ka ɔɔ lauri peeza, nauna, kauzi ani nyugmazi, di paa ba laala jaa. Ka ɔɔ kaa bir ba Koori Akis be.
10Koori Akis haŋ wa pɛɛzuu, “Lee i ga lɔ zinaa, di paa kunai?” Deevid ɔɔ ŋɔ, “Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii” gɛɛ “Jɛramiil dee hɛri” gɛɛ “Kɛn hina hɛri.” 11Deevid waa ɔɔ gil baal gɛɛ haaŋ maa du de ni miibɔɔ, ú kpogli baa ba Gaf, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa fɛwɔɔrɛ, “Aŋhinabe, ba daŋ la ga ŋɔ, ‘Kenne Deevid ɛɛ.’ ” Gunnɛ u faa ra ɛɛ, saŋa la uŋ soge Filisti hɛri la. 12Koori Akis yardi Deevid, di ŋɔ u biini, “U himmaa nɛra Izrɛl hina hauhbuu werge maa, guŋ daŋ gil u ɛɛ n balii di hanna la.”

english_text:
Saul Asks To Talk with Samuel's Ghost
1-3 Samuel had died some time earlier, and people from all over Israel had attended his funeral in his hometown of Ramah.
Meanwhile, Saul had been trying to get rid of everyone who spoke with the spirits of the dead. But one day the Philistines brought their soldiers together to attack Israel.
Achish told David, “Of course, you know that you and your men must fight as part of our Philistine army.”
David answered, “That will give you a chance to see for yourself just how well we can fight!”
“In that case,” Achish said, “you and your men will always be my bodyguards.”
4The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa. 5Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear. 6 So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet. 7Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.”
His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
8That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
9The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
10Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
11 “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked.
“Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
12When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
13“Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.”
She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
14“What does it look like?”
“It looks like an old man wearing a robe.”
Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
15“Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked.
“I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
16Samuel said:
If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do. 17 I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing! 18 When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you. 19Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
20At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
21The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked. 22Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
23“No, I won't eat!”
But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed. 24At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread. 25Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_text:
Koori Sɔɔl ni Ɛndɔ vugri wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Filisti hina chaali ba laallɔɔra, bá la ga lɔ Izrɛl hina laal. Koori Akis ŋɔ Deevid be, “Zum lugɔ i ni i laallɔɔra daŋ duŋ, di ga yoo Izrɛl hina.”
2Deevid ŋɔ, “Denii i himmaa na gunla i balii n niŋ wer ɛɛ.”
Koori Akis ge ŋɔ, “Guŋ wesso, n daŋ kpai ɛɛ n guuri, n de dui biini maa di hanna la.”
3A saŋa naa, di Samuɛl jaa siu, Izrɛl hina maa wii u lee, ka huguu u bol Rama. Koori Sɔɔl ge faa duŋŋi vugra ani ijɔzi lii a hɛri.
4Denii a Filisti hina izi ga baŋzi ba tantizi di chɔɔ bolzeŋ bɛl banna yir Sunɛm. Koori Sɔɔl ge chaali Izrɛl hina laallɔɔra, ba ge ga chɔɔ Bizeŋ Gilbɔa. 5Koori Sɔɔl n wa na Filisti laallɔɔra la, ɔnsii ni biinichɔg lawuu werge maa.
6U pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi gunla un niŋ ɛɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu, di lii deeza gɛɛ Urim ni Tumim tai biini gɛɛ dɔgtɛɛzi be. 7Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u balaa be, “Ií nyiŋŋi haaŋ la n ɛɛ vugri ń la u ga vugiŋ.”
Ba ŋɔ, “Bɛl du Ɛndɔ.”
8Denii Koori Sɔɔl bɔg hamuŋa ni, di kur. U ni u laallɔɔra banɛɛ kpa di la a haaŋ be. Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Yir lalii la sɔŋ min niŋ yir duma, di pɛɛzuu tɛŋ.”
9Denii a haaŋ ŋɔ u be, “Wibii maa, i zum wii la Koori Sɔɔl n ɛɛwɛnɛ. U duŋŋi vugra ni ijɔzii lii Izrɛl hɛri. Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ba í wa heŋ sidɛɛ, di lawiŋ ń siuwɛi?”
10Ka Koori Sɔɔl hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la sɔŋ biini, nɛr maa wàá tɛr i digni dikuu guŋ wia.”
11Denii a haaŋ pɛɛzuu, “Lalbɛliirɛ i ra nyiŋŋi ń yir tɛinɛi?”
Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Samuɛl.”
12A haaŋ n wa yir Samuɛl di na u duma n na ba, u lɔ wile werge maa, di ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Ɛrɛɛ i dariŋ gunnɛi? Koori Sɔɔllɛ hiŋ!”
13Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm! Bɛɛ i nai?”
A haaŋ ŋɔ, “N na nɛr dumaa n na lii hɛrii.”
14Koori Sɔɔl pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ u duɛi?”
U ŋɔ, “U ɛɛ bazɛŋaa, di laali tagtajaŋ di ra ba.”
Denii Koori Sɔɔl jaa zum lugɔ Samuɛllɛ, u chɔɔ hɛri di pi.
15Samuɛl ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Ɛrɛɛ i tɔɔriŋ, di yiriŋ ba ɛnnɛi?”
Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Biinichɔg wergee lawiŋ. Filisti hinaa wa fɔɔŋ ni laal, ka Kɔraawiizi vɛɛŋ ta. Waa kaa sɛɛ ga u dɔgtɛɛzi be di nuu ra tɛŋ gɛɛ di lii deeza gba biini. Awiarɛ n yirii, í wa bagliŋ gunla min niŋ ɛɛ.”
16Denii Samuɛl ŋɔ u be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i yiriŋ, saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n vɛɛi, di birgi i dɔmɛi? 17Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ wia la uŋ ga n be ŋɔ lugɔ a daŋ ɛɛi labuu tuŋ. Kɔraawiizi foozi Izrɛl kora labuu lii i be, tɛɛ i dɔŋhiŋ Deevid. 18Dikuu hiŋ vɛɛ u nua hiŋaa, haa Amalɛk hina maa kpuwɛɛ, di chɔgi ba kundɔɔlaa maa nyaamm la wiarɛ, u kpa a keŋ wii naa di ra dawii zinaa la. 19Awia, u daŋ kpa i ni Izrɛl hina maa du Filisti hina nonee. Kɛrɛ, i ni i biibaala daŋ wa jaa mìŋ́ Samuɛl ni. Kɔraawiizi daŋ kaa kpa Izrɛl laallɔɔra ge du Filisti hina nonee biini.”
20Kakpaŋ, ɔnsii lau Koori Sɔɔl werge, u chol hɛri di tɛr chɔɔ, dikuu gunla Samuɛl n ŋɔwɛɛ la wia. Waa kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa tama maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa waa kummaa diwee di lii chɔɔzi maa guŋŋ di ga hel hamuŋa.
21A haaŋ n wa ba Sɔɔl be, di na gunla bɔsai ni ɔnsii n lawuu la, u ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, mìŋ́ i balii hiŋ i nuarɛ, di kpa n miibɔɔ chɛr siu, di ɛɛ wii la maa hiŋ ŋɔ ń ɛɛ tɛi labuu. 22Jaande maa, a nuu míŋ̀ i balii be, gil n tɛi diwee í di, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ra la.”
23U vɛɛ ka ŋɔ, “Màá di.”
Ka u nɛra la hiini a haaŋ di ra fɔrguu lugɔ ú di, u jaa sɛɛ, di izi so u karjaŋ ni.
24A haaŋ ge dɔɔ ú nabii n pɔllɛ nɛnnɛ, u lawuu kpu manaŋ. Di ɛɛ sau di ɔɔzi paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ. 25Denii u kpaa wa tɛɛ Sɔɔl ni u nɛra hiŋ ba di. A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa maanii, ba lii kaali.

english_text:
The Philistines Send David Back
1The Philistines had brought their whole army to Aphek, while Israel's army was camping near Jezreel Spring. 2-3The Philistine rulers and their troops were marching past the Philistine army commanders in groups of 100 and 1,000. When David and his men marched by at the end with Achish, the commanders said, “What are these worthless Israelites doing here?”
“They are David's men,” Achish answered. “David used to be one of Saul's officers, but he left Saul and joined my army a long time ago. I've never had even one complaint about him.”
4The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted:
Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers. 5 The Israelites even dance and sing,
“Saul has killed
a thousand enemies;
David has killed
ten thousand!”
6Achish called David over and said:
I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along. 7Go on back home and try not to upset them.
8“But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
9Achish said:
I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle. 10You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
11David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_text:
Koori Akis n gillɛ Deevid bir kaali Ziklag wia
1A saŋa, di Filisti hina chaali ba laallɔɔra maa, Afɛk. Ka Izrɛl hina ge la ga baŋzi ba tantizi di chɔɔ Jɛzriil bule kɛrii. 2Filisti hina koora banue maa lii, di tɔ ba laallɔɔra sugezi kalfazi ani kagboŋa sezi. Deevid ni u laallɔɔra ni Koori Akis ge laallɔɔra tɔ har. 3Filisti laallɔɔra sitɔɔra na baa, di pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛ Hibru hina naa ra nyiŋŋi ɛnnɛi?”
Koori Akis bir ŋɔ, “Deevidii. U faa ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl nabɔma bɛllɛ. U du n benii di bɛri bina, di haŋ lii a hɔl la uŋ lii Koori Sɔɔl be di ba n be maa, n haa waa wichɔgii maa nawɛɛ u ni.”
4Ka Filisti laallɔɔra sitɔɔra hiŋ ŋɔ Koori Akis be ani baaŋfuuih, “Gil a baal bir kaali bɔr la hiŋ tɛu la. Gilɛɛ gil yaa nuu la a laal. Di a haŋ wa chi siaahmu, u daŋ bir di ra yoo yaa. Gunla un niŋ ɛɛ u dɔɔri bɔra kaa sɔɔni maanii, un niŋ bir kpu yaa. 5Di kaa kpa jaa, Deevid naa wia lɛi a ba kpa di ra yir yira ani chɔlaa lugɔ,
‘Koori Sɔɔl kpu kagboŋaa,
ka Deevid kpu
kagboŋa fizi laa’?”
6Denii Koori Akis yir Deevid di ŋɔ u be, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa labuu lugɔ i wia dɔɔ wibiire n be. A daŋ faa pariŋ lugɔ n nii la a laal. Di haŋ lii a hɔl la hiŋ ba n be di wa lii ni zinaa, maa wichɔgii maa nawɛɛ i ni. Ka n dɔŋa koora la waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ i jaa yaa ni. 7Awia, bir di ra kpo ani bɔsɔna, gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wiimaa, ba baana waa fuuh.”
8Ka Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛi? Haŋ lii a hɔl la maa miŋ ba i be la di wa lii ni zinaa, bɛɛ wichɔgiirɛ i na n ninɛi? N dɔɔri, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ n nii wàá wer la ń ga yoo i dɔmai?”
9Koori Akis bir ŋɔ u be, “N zummɔɔ lugɔ i wia dɔɔ wibiire alugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl, ka Filisti hina koora ŋɔ ba wàá sɛɛ lugɔ i ni yaa la a laal. 10Awia, feli izi chɔɔzi ni di lau i dɔɔri balaa la i ni baa n ballɛ la, di biraa kpo.”
11Awia, Deevid ni u laallɔɔra feli izi chɔɔzi ni, di bir ba Filisti hɛri, ka Filisti hina la ge kpa di ra la Jɛzriil.

english_text:
David Rescues His Soldiers' Families
1It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground, 2and had taken away the women and children. 3When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive. 4They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more. 5 David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
6David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength, 7 and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.”
Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David. 8Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?”
“Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
9-10David led his 600 men to Besor Gorge, but 200 of them were too tired to go across. So they stayed behind, while David and the other 400 men crossed the gorge.
11Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water, 12some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
13“Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?”
“I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick. 14We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
15“Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked.
“Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
16He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah. 17David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
18David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag. 19No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen, 20including their livestock.
David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
21On the way back, David went to the 200 men he had left at Besor Gorge, because they had been too tired to keep up with him. They came toward David and the people who were with him. When David was close enough, he greeted the 200 men and asked how they were doing.
22Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
23But David said:
My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked. 24Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
25David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
26David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
27-31This is a list of the towns where David sent gifts: Bethel, Ramoth in the Southern Desert, Jattir, Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Racal, the towns belonging to the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites, Hormah, Bor-Ashan, Athach, and Hebron. He also sent gifts to the other towns where he and his men had traveled.
translation_text:
Deevid n chɔgi Amalɛk hina wia
1Hɔpizaa ahoroo Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la kpa di bir hel Ziklag. A saŋa naa, di Amalɛk hina teŋ wa lɔ Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag, di foozi ba kuna ka fuuh bolzeŋ Ziklag maa, 2di lauri ba haana ni banla maa n du de, nɛzɛŋzi ni biipɔllaa ni suŋgure maa. Ba waa ba bɛl maa kpuwɛɛ, ka lauri baa kaali.
3Deevid ni u laallɔɔra n wa hel Ziklag, ba na lugɔ a bol maanii fuuhwe, haali ba lauri ba haana ani ba biizi maa kaali. 4Denii Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la jaa chɛɛhgi guŋŋ, ba fɔŋŋa maa wa tuŋ. 5Ba faa lauri Deevid haana banɛɛ Jɛzriil hinuu Ahinoam ani Kamɛl hinuu Nabal luhaaŋ Abigeel maanii kaali. 6Biinichɔg jaa lau Deevid werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u wia faa ra fuuh u laallɔɔra hiŋ baannɛ. Ba faa ra nyiŋŋi ba paagi bia lɔɔzuu, dikuu baŋ waa kaa na ba biizi wia. Ka Kɔraawiizi la unna hum faa duu bɔkpega.
7Denii Deevid ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata n ɛɛ Ahimɛlɛk biibaal be, “Kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehina tagtakpurii ifɔd la wa tɛŋ.” Abiata kpau di wa tɛu. 8Denii Deevid pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “Ń dau a laallɔɔra naa n wa chɔgi yaa bol naa luge gɛɛ? N daŋ huuzi baa?”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Lii dau ba luge, i daŋ huuzi baa, di lɛɛ i nɛra hiŋ.”
9Denii Deevid ni u laallɔɔra kalfaanumbɛl la maa izi, di kpa guŋŋ di ga hel Bɛsɔ Faalim, baŋhina so de, 10dikuu ba kalfaanɛɛ n kuuhwɛ werge maa wia. Ka Deevid ni ba kalfaanaazu la n kawɛɛ la waa haa ra la.
11Ba ga na Ijip hinuu bɛl pir biini, di lawuu ba Deevid be, ba tɛu nii ni diwee, 12fig nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ, a hil yeŋ ani grepu nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ, a hil anɛɛ. U dia, fɔŋŋa ba u be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa waa kummaa diwee gɛɛ di nyɔɔ nii hɔpizaa ahoro.
13Deevid pɛɛzuu, “I dɔɔrii anɛɛ, lee i liiyɛi?”
U ŋɔ, “Ijip hinuurɛ miŋ, n ɛɛ Amalɛk hinuu bɛl yonne. N na wiiu hɔpizaa ahoro n bɛrɛɛ, n dɔɔri hiŋ vɛɛŋ ta. 14Yaa ga lɔ Kɛrɛf hina la n du Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag ani Kalɛb domeere, ka fuuh Ziklag ge jaa.”
15Denii Deevid pɛɛzuu, “I daŋ wer tɔ n see, di ga bagliŋ bɔr la nɛra naa n wa lɔ yaa di paa yaa kuna naa n duwɛɛ?”
U ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh. Ama, hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ hàá kpuŋ gɛɛ di kpaŋ ga tɛɛ n dɔɔri la.”
16U tɔ Deevid see di la bɔr la baŋ duwɛɛ la, di ba yaari de maa, di ra di ka ra nyɔɔ, di ra sa, dikuu kuna la baŋ paagɛɛ werge lii Filisti ani Juda hina be la wia. 17Deevid lɔ baa chɔɔzimpikke ni guŋŋ hɔɔ waa pizi, ba biipɔllaa kalfaanaazu bɛnnɛ faa wette tinni nyugmazi di chɔ kaali. Ka banla waa maa n kawɛɛ la, waa wette na bɔr chɔ kaali. 18Deevid lɛɛ kuna la maa Amalɛk hina n paagɛɛ la, di kpa ú haana banɛɛ la jaa. 19Ba kummaa faa waa a nɛra be leuwe, haali ba biihaana ani biibaala gba. A maanii Deevid lɛɛ ba. 20U faa bir foozi peeza ani nauna, u nɛra duŋŋaa di tɔ see, ka ra ŋɔ, “Deevid kunaa keŋ.”
21Denii Deevid ba u laallɔɔra kalfaanɛɛ la n faa kuuhwɛ, ba waa wette hiŋuu, u gil baa Bɛsɔ Faalim la be. Ba lii chem u ni u laallɔɔra la n du u be la ni. Baŋ wàá dugli baa, Deevid jaami baa. 22Ka banla ni Deevid n laŋŋɛ la nɛchɔgaa ani kalu nyiŋŋe baŋhina ŋɔ, “Dikuu baŋ vɛɛ de laŋaa la wia, yaa wàá bɔnni a kuna di tɛɛ baa. Ama, bɛl maa kpogli u haaŋ ni biizi waa di ra la.”
23Ka Deevid ŋɔ, “Akai, n lulla, ii gilɛɛ ɛɛ chumaa, dikuu kuna naa Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ yaa naa wia. U guu yaabuu, di kpa yaa dɔma du yaa nonee. 24Akai! Anɛɛ niŋ nuu gunla iinna ŋɔ naanɛi? Banla n soge di ra binni yaa kuna ani banla maa n la a laal la maanii niŋ di mɛgzi. Yaa maa daŋ bɔnnaa di mɛgzi.” 25Kenne Deevid dau tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ba ra hiŋ, haali ni zinaa.
26Deevid n wa hel Ziklag, u kpa a kuna aŋhina tɛɛ Juda nabɔnzi la n ɛɛ u dammuzi, di ŋɔ, “Kuna la miŋ foozee di lii Kɔraawiizi dɔma benii keŋ.”
27U faa bɔnnaabuu tɛɛ banla maa n du bolzenaa Bɛtɛl, Ramɔf n du Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii, Jatir, 28Aroa, Sifmɔf, Ɛstɛmɔa 29ani Rakal. Di kaa kpa Jɛramiil domee hina, Kɛn hina 30ani banla ge n du bolzenaa Hɔma, Bɔr Asan, Atak, 31bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn ani bɔra la maa u ni u laallɔɔra n laŋŋɛ la maa.

english_text:
Saul and His Sons Die
1Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed. 2The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua. 3The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
4Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him.
Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it. 5When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
6Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day. 7The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
8The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa. 9-10The Philistines cut off Saul's head and pulled off his armor. Then they put his armor in the temple of the goddess Astarte, and they nailed his body to the city wall of Beth-Shan. They also sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the good news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
11The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body. 12So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them. 13They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_text:
Koori Sɔɔl n kpu u hiŋ wia
1A kaa wa ɛɛ lugɔ Filisti ni Izrɛl hina kaa ra lɔ laal, ba kpu Izrɛl hina galga maa Bizeŋ Gilbɔa nyuu, ka baŋhina chɔ. 2Filisti hina faa duŋŋi Koori Sɔɔl ani u biibaala guŋŋ di ga kpu Jonatan, Abinadab ani Malki Sua. 3A laal faa jaa du kpeg werge, ba bar Koori Sɔɔl, di viruu hobii, di duu pira werge maa.
4Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ biipɔllii la n kpogli u dɔŋkuna be, “Pam i tokobi di tɔɔhŋ kpu, di guŋ lɛi, nɛra naa n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ naa daŋ ba wa ɛɛŋ chɛɛtɛ, di sunniŋ.”
Ka ɔnsii faa lau a biipɔllii werge maa, waa sɛɛwɛ ú kpuu. Denii Koori Sɔɔl pam u himmaa tokobi, di bir tɔɔh u hiŋ kpu. 5A biipɔllii n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl siuwɔɔ, u ge pam u himmaa tokobi di tɔɔh u hiŋ, di siu jaa u ni. 6Denii Koori Sɔɔl, u biibaala bahoro, u balii ani u laallɔɔra maa faa kpau siu, a hɔl hiŋ.
7Izrɛl hina la n soge di hiini waluu ani ba banla n du Jɔɔdan muu baŋgia la, n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba laallɔɔra maa chɔwɔɔrɛ la, Koori Sɔɔl ge ni u biibaala maa siu la, ba ge maa chɔ ka ka ba bola. Filisti hina la jaa ba di wa so ba bola hiŋ.
8Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Filisti hina ba, bá wa wir a lalaa kuna, ba na Koori Sɔɔl ani u biibaala bahoro la maa n siuwɛ chɔɔ Bizeŋ Gilbɔa nyuu. 9Ba teŋ Koori Sɔɔl nyuu, di wir u laal laala, ka hunzi nɛra Filisti hina bola maa, lugɔ bá sii guŋ amaniyesuma, ba vuga diini biine ani ba nɛra maa be. 10Ba kpa u dɔŋkuna di ga dau ba vughaaŋ Astɔrɛf dia biini, ka kpau kpaahzi mari ba bolzeŋ Bɛf San koŋlii ni.
11Bolzeŋ Jabɛs Giliad hina n wa nuu gunla Filisti hina la n dau Koori Sɔɔl la, 12ba nɛkpega izi hamuŋa ni di vɔɔ, di la Bɛf San, di ga lizi Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaala hiŋ a koŋlii ni, di kpa baa ba Jabɛs, di wa fuuh baa de. 13Ka paa ba hoga di wa hug tamaris daa zɛɛ, Jabɛs biini. Ka vɔɔ nua hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

english_text:
David Finds Out about Saul's Death
1Saul was dead.
Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag. 2Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
3David asked, “Where did you come from?”
The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
4“Who won the battle?” David asked.
The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
5David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
6 The young man replied:
I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him. 7When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
8Saul asked me, “Who are you?”
“An Amalekite,” I answered.
9Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
10So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
11At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow. 12They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
13David asked the young man, “Where is your home?”
The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
14-16David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!”
Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!”
David Sings in Memory of Saul
17David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan, 18 and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
19Israel, your famous hero
lies dead on the hills,
and your mighty warriors
have fallen!
20Don't tell it in Gath
or spread the news
on the streets of Ashkelon.
The godless Philistine women
will be happy
and jump for joy.
21Don't let dew or rain fall
on the hills of Gilboa.
Don't let its fields
grow offerings for God.
There the warriors' shields
were smeared with mud,
and Saul's own shield
was left unpolished.
22The arrows of Jonathan struck,
and warriors died.
The sword of Saul cut
the enemy apart.
23It was easy to love Saul
and Jonathan.
Together in life,
together in death,
they were faster than eagles
and stronger than lions.
24Women of Israel, cry for Saul.
He brought you fine red cloth
and jewelry made of gold.
25Our warriors have fallen
in the heat of battle,
and Jonathan lies dead
on the hills of Gilboa.
26Jonathan, I miss you most!
I loved you
like a brother.
You were truly loyal to me,
more faithful than a wife
to her husband.
27Our warriors have fallen,
and their weapons
are destroyed.
translation_text:
Deevid n nuu Koori Sɔɔl siu wia
1Koori Sɔɔl siu har, Deevid jaa lii bɔr la uŋ kpegli Amalɛk hina la, di bir ba wa du Ziklag hɔpizaa anɛɛ. 2A hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ, baal bɛl lii Koori Sɔɔl chɔɔribɔr di piili u laala, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa waari u nyuu, di ra bagli u biinichɔg. Uŋ wa hel Deevid be, u giŋŋi u see di jaamuu girme ni.
3Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Lee i liiyɛi?”
U ŋɔ, “N chɔwɔɔrɛ lii Izrɛl hina chɔɔribɔr la.”
4Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛwɛnɛi? Ŋɔ n be.”
U ŋɔ, “Yaa laallɔɔra maanii chɔwɛɛ lii a laal biini yaari. Ba kpila ge maa kaa siu. Haali Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan gba siuwɔɔ.”
5Denii Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛ zum lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan gba siuwɔɔwɛi?”
6A biipɔllii hiŋ ŋɔ, “Bizeŋ la banna yir Gilbɔa la nyuurɛ n chi, ka na Koori Sɔɔl n chigɛ dɛlli u kandaa, ka u dɔma la ni ba zagra ni a torkozi baruu tuŋ. 7Uŋ wa bittɛ di ŋɔ u binni, di minuu, u yiriŋ. N pɛɛzuu, ‘Bɛɛ i ŋɔ n ɛɛi?’
8U pɛɛziŋ, ‘Anɛɛ hinnɛi?’
N ŋɔ, ‘Amalɛk hinuurɛ miŋ.’
9Denii u ŋɔ n be, ‘Ba wa kpuŋ, n na piraa werge maa, di ra nyiŋŋi n siu.’
10Denii n tuzi heluu di kpuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, n zummɔ lugɔ di u wa chol hɛri, wàá ka piri. N jaa pilli u saliŋ kahuro la uŋ hiwee la, di lizi u nonii gbuŋ ge, aabuu keŋ n kpa ba ń wa tɛi, n dɔɔri.”
11Deevid ni u laallɔɔra maa lau ba laala piili ni biinichɔg, 12di wii werge maa di ra tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan ani Izrɛl hina la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra, ka vɔɔ nua guŋŋ di ga hel duana ni, dikuu baŋ siu laal biini wia.
13Deevid ŋɔ a biipɔllii la n wa lizi a amaniye hiŋ be, “Lee i liiyɛi?”
U ŋɔ, “N ɛɛ Amalɛk hinuurɛ, ka du i hɛri.”
14Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ɔnsii wɛɛ lauwɛ lugɔ i kpu nɛr la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ u ɛɛ koorei?”
15Denii Deevid yir u laallɔɔra la bɛl, di ŋɔ u be, “Kpuu!” U la ga ŋmɛnuu, u chol siu. 16Deevid ŋɔ u be, “I wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi i ni, i himmaa nuarɛ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ, i kpu koori la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛnɛ.”
Deevid n wii Koori Sɔɔl ni Jonatan lee wia
17Deevid jaa yir biinichɔg yir naa dikuu Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan wia, 18di ŋɔ bá bagli Juda hina a yir. Ba sɛbuubuu du Jasaa Hɔŋ biini.
19“Yaa sitɔɔra siuwɔɔ chɔɔ Izrɛl hɛri giŋgimee nyuuni!
Yaa laallɔkpega
werge la chogloore!
20Ií gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ a wia bolzenaa Gaf biini
gɛɛ Askɛlɔn ŋmɛnizi.
Ií gilɛɛ waa gil Filisti hina haana bɔra sɔɔni,
di gilɛɛ wa gil banla
n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ
biihaana bɔra sɔɔni.
21Gilɛɛ gil dooŋ gɛɛ sɔnii
wàá chol Gilbɔa
giŋgimee ni,
gil u kooni chɔɔ pɛɛ
saŋa maa!
Dikuu laallɔkpega laal pɛrɛtuzenaa
chɔɔ denii ni hiihzi,
ba waa kaa kpa nuu
di ra billi Koori Sɔɔl hor.
22Jonatan hoo faa waa tawɛɛ ra kir,
Koori Sɔɔl ge faa kpu
nɛkpila werge
ni u tokobi,
di faa kpuuzi nɛkpega
ani u dɔma.
23Koori Sɔɔl ni Jonatan de dui saŋa,
nɛra faa nɔŋŋi baabuu,
di ra tɔgzi baa,
ba faa waa bargɛɛ
siu gba biini.
Ba faa gbaŋŋɔɔ kaali chigni,
di du kpeg
kaali bunyinzi.
24Izrɛl haana, ií wii ra tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl,
u faa ɔɔ ra tɛɛ iabuu
pɛɛŋaahma la yoolazi
n kpolle werge,
di ra bɔg ia
ni saliŋ kuna.
25Laallɔkpega la chogloore
ba kpuuzi baabuu
laal biini.
Jonatannɛ siuwɛ chɔɔ
giŋgimee nyuuni.
26N wiiwoo ra tɛi,
n badɔŋ Jonatan,
i faa nɔŋŋimbuu werge!
I nɔŋŋaa faa kpekkoo
kaali haana nɔŋŋaa.
27Laallɔkpega chogloore,
ba dɔŋkuna
bir pɛɛ.”

english_text:
David Becomes King of Judah
1Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?”
The Lord answered, “Yes.”
David asked, “Which town should I go to?”
“Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
2 David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel. 3David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
4 The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
5David sent messengers to tell them:
The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler, 6and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done. 7Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage.
Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
8Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim 9and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin. 10Ishbosheth was 40 years old at the time, and he ruled for two years. But the tribe of Judah made David their king, 11and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years.
The War between David and Ishbosheth
12One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon. 13Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side. 14Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!”
Joab agreed, 15and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men. 16They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.” 17Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
18Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field, 19and he ran straight after Abner, without looking to the right or to the left.
20When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?”
Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
21Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.”
But Asahel refused to stop.
22Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
23But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still. 24But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert. 25Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
26Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
27Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!” 28Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
29Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
30As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were 19 missing besides Asahel. 31But David's soldiers had killed 360 of Abner's men from the tribe of Benjamin. 32Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_text:
Baŋ tɔ Deevid Juda kora wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Deevid pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, “N Dɔɔri, ń la Juda bola naa bɛl di ga soo?”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Ɛɛh, a la.”
Deevid kaa pɛɛzi, “Ń la ga so u bɛlii?”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Ga so bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn.”
2Denii Deevid kpogli u haana banɛɛ, u ni baa la de, bɛllɛ faa Jɛzriil hinuu Ahinoam, bɛl genii faa Nabal n lii Kamɛl luhaaŋ Abigeel la. 3Deevid faa kaa kpogli u laallɔɔra la n faa du u be la maa ni ba diinihina, ba maa la ga so bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn ani u boljigzi. 4Denii Juda hina ba bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, di wa fug nuu waari Deevid nyuu, di tɔu kora, u jaa ɛɛ Juda hina maa koori.
Koori Deevid n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ bolzeŋ Jabɛs la, n du Giliad hɛri hina hug Koori Sɔɔllɛ, 5u hum ŋɔ ba ga ŋɔ ba be. “Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ia, iiŋ suŋ ii dɔɔri Koori Sɔɔl ni, di huguu la wia. 6Kɔ́raawiizi ra ɛɛ ia nɛnnɛ di dɔɔ wibii ni ia, n gba daŋ suŋ ii ni di hiini ia guŋ himmaa, dikuu kennaa iiŋ ɛɛwɛ naa wia. 7Awia, ií chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bampirii! Ii Koori Sɔɔl siuwɔɔ, ka Juda hina jaa waari n nyuu nuu, di tɔŋ kora.”
Laal n chol Koori Deevid ni Koori Sɔɔl diinihina ni wia
8Ama, Abna la n ɛɛ Nɛɛr biibaal, di kaa ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl laallɔɔra sitɔɔri la, faa lau Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf, ba chɔ la Mahanam. 9Denii u ga tɔu kora, u ɛɛ Giliad, Asɛ, Jɛzriil, Ɛfram, Bɛnjamin ani Izrɛl hina maa koori.
10Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf naa faa ra di a kora Izrɛl hina ni, di u di binni tokkoanɛɛ. U di a koraa binni anɛɛ. Ka Juda dee la waa faa sɛɛ di ra hiŋ Koori Deevid nua lugɔ waabuu ba koori. 11Denii Koori Deevid so bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, di di kora Juda dee ni, binni aniidaanɛɛ ni baaguzi anumbɛl.
12A hɔl bɛl, Nɛɛr biibaal Abna ani Isbɔsɛf nabɔnzi izi Mahanam, di kpa la bolzeŋ Gibiɔn. 13Zɛruya biibaal Joab ni Koori Deevid nabɔnzi la ga chem ba ni Gibiɔn pol. Baŋhina so a pol baŋgia bɛl, baŋhina ge so bɛl.
14Denii Abna ŋɔ Joab be, “Lizi i biipɔllaa, ya ge lizi yaa biipɔllaa, bá lɔ dɔŋa ya na.”
Joab ŋɔ, “Wibiire i ŋɔ, ya ɛɛ guŋ.”
15Denii Abna lizi nɛra fidibanɛɛ lii Bɛnjamin dee biini, ba chi tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf. Joab ge lizi nɛra fidibanɛɛ ba chi tɛɛ Koori Deevid. 16Denii ba zuu dɔŋa, bɛl maa lau u dɔŋhiŋ nyuu, ka pam u tokobi di chug u loŋŋi, ba maa kpau chol, di siu. Awia, ba jaa ra yir bɔr n du Gibiɔn hɛri la, Hɛlkaf Hazurim.
17A hɔl hiŋ, a laal faa kpekkoo werge maa. Ka Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra kpegli Abna ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra la.
18Zɛruya biibaala bahoro la faa du denii, baabuu, Joab, Abisai ani Asahɛl la n faa ra chɔ werge lugɔ weema la. 19Denii u lii di ra duŋŋi Abna, haali waa yemmaa bɛɛwɛ. 20Abna bir binnuu, ka ŋɔ, “Asahɛl, hinuu naa?”
U ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh!”
21Abna ŋɔ u be, “Gil n duŋŋaa! A duŋŋi laallɔɔra naa bɛl, di foozi kuna la uŋ kpoglee.” Ka Asahɛl vɛɛ ka haa ra duŋŋuu.
22Abna kaa ŋɔ Asahɛl be. “Gil n duŋŋaa! Ɛrɛɛ i ra firiŋ ń kpuinɛi? Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ binni i kpɛɛma Joab siweei?”
23Ka Asahɛl vɛɛ ka ra duŋŋuu. Denii Abna kpa u kandaa di bir yaguu, u saagi ga lii u harbɔɔ. U chol siu. Di nɛr maa hanna ba di wa hel bɔr la Asahɛl n siuwɛ hiŋ, ɔɔ chiu.
24Ka Joab ni Abisai ge haa ra duŋŋi Abna guŋŋ di ga hel Amma giŋgimii la n dugli Gia, ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Gibiɔn hɛribɔduma la, di wiizi jaa ra zuu. 25Denii Bɛnjamin dee laallɔɔra la jaa wa bar Abna, di chi giŋgimii bɛl nyuu, ba chigni bɔra.
26Denii Abna ŋɔ kpegzi ni tɛɛ Joab, “Amɔ, yaa kalu naa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛɛa? Haa zummɛ lugɔ a tuna maa, dɔŋhahzi bɛnnɛ niŋ wa kaa? Yaa ɛɛ ii lullaa. Ɛrɛɛ á birgi mag, ka í ŋɔ i nɛra be lugɔ bá gil yaa duŋŋaai?”
27Joab ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la lugɔ di i faa waa keŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, n laallɔɔra naa faa waa gil i ni i laallɔɔra duŋŋaa guŋŋ di ra ba hɔpizaa.”
28Denii Joab jaa huuh u bensunoniina, u laallɔɔra la maa nuu, di gil Izrɛl hina duŋŋaa. A kalu jaa tuŋ.
29A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa maanii Abna ni u laallɔɔra vol Jɔɔdan Waluu biini guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi, ba gi Jɔɔdan muu la di bir ba Mahanam.
30Denii Joab n wa gil Abna duŋŋaa, u chaali u laallɔɔra maa di na lugɔ ba fidikabɛllɛ waa hoo, di kpa Asahɛl jaa. 31Ka Koori Deevid laallɔɔra la faa kpu Bɛnjamin dee laallɔɔra la n faa ra hiŋ Abna la kalfaahoro ani tokkoahoro. 32Ba kpa Asahɛl di la Bɛtlihɛm di ga pilli ba dia bɔɔzeŋ, di huguu. Denii Joab ni u laallɔɔra jaa lii hamuŋa ni, di vol guŋŋ, baŋ waa hel bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn di hɔpizɔɔ.

english_text:
1This battle was the beginning of a long war between the followers of Saul and the followers of David. Saul's power grew weaker, but David's grew stronger.
David's Sons Born in Hebron
(1 Chronicles 3.1-4)
2-5Several of David's sons were born while he was living in Hebron. His oldest son was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel. David's second son was Chileab, whose mother was Abigail, who had been married to Nabal from Carmel. Absalom was the third. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of King Talmai of Geshur. The fourth was Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith. The fifth was Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital. The sixth was Ithream, whose mother was Eglah, another one of David's wives.
Abner Decides To Help David
6As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family. 7He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
8Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth:
Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
9I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him! 10 God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
11Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
12Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
13David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
14 David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed 100 Philistines so I could marry her.”
