15Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish. 16Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
17Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now. 18So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
19Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do. 20Abner took 20 soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
21After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.”
David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble.
Joab Kills Abner
22Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village. 23Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
24Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone! 25You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
26Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it. 27When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel.
Abner's Funeral
28David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death! 29Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
30Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
31David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!”
David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried. 32Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly. 33Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner:
Abner, why should you
have died like an outlaw?
34No one tied your hands
or chained your feet,
yet you died as a victim
of murderers.
Everyone started crying again. 35Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
36Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did. 37Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
38David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died? 39I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_text:
1Laal la n faa chol Koori Sɔɔl ni Koori Deevid laallɔɔra baaŋ la, faa du denii birgi werge. Koori Deevid fɔŋŋa faa ra jaa, ka Koori Sɔɔl diahina ge gɛrga faa ra nyaŋŋi.
2Biibaala la Koori Deevid n faa lullɛ Hɛbrɔnnɛ keŋ, u biinabɔmaa Amnɔn, u maa ɛɛ Ahinoam la n lii Jɛzriil.
3Nɛɛhinnɛ Kiliab, u maarɛ faa Abigeel, Nabal luhaaŋ la n lii Kamɛl, horohinnɛ Absalɔm, u maarɛ faa Gɛsur Koori Talmai biihaaŋ Maaka la. 4Naazuhinnɛ Adonija, u maarɛ Hagif, nuehinnɛ Sɛfatia, u maarɛ Abital, 5numbɛlhiŋ genii Itriam, u maarɛ Ɛgla la n faa ɛɛ Koori Deevid haana la bɛl.
Abna n ga jaa Koori Deevid ni wia
6Laal la n faa chol Koori Deevid laallɔɔraa ni Koori Sɔɔl diahina ni la, a saŋaa Abna fɔŋŋa ra jaa werge Koori Sɔɔl diahina be. 7A hɔl bɛl, Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf kpa wia chug Abna lugɔ u lau u mɛɛ hahjiga Aaya biihaaŋ Rizpaa di chɔɔ.
8Abna n wa nuu gunla Isbɔsɛf n ŋɔwɛɛ la, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u ŋɔ, “I fɛ lugɔ n daŋ ŋmaabi i mɛɛ Koori Sɔɔllɛa? I fɛ lugɔ Judaa n na humaa? Di haŋ lii a lugli la maa, n dɔɔ wibiire tɛɛ i mɛɛ, u lulla ani u dammuzi maa, di lɛɛi lii Koori Deevid be. Ka zinaa i kpa haaŋ wia di ra chugiŋ! 9Kɔ́raawiizi turgiŋ a kim, di maa haŋ ɛɛ wii la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua di hɛɛhzi lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ Koori Deevid la ɛɛwɛ 10lugɔ u daŋ lɛɛ a kora lii Koori Sɔɔl be tɛɛ Koori Deevid u ra binni Izrɛl ni Juda hina ni, di chi bolzeŋ Dan di ga hel bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba la.” 11Isbɔsɛf waa kaa wer dɔɔ nua un niŋ ŋɔ wiimaa tɛɛ Abna, dikuu unna ɔmuu wia.
12Denii Abna hum dí ba ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Anɛɛ n dɔɔ a hɛrɛi? Gil n nii ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, ń hiinii di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, bá maa sɛɛ lugɔ ba koorii hiŋ, di ra hiŋii.”
13Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Guŋ wesso, n daŋ gil ya ɛɛ nuukpaŋ. Ka wikpaŋ bɛllɛ n na nyiŋŋi lii i be, di i waa ba, lau Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ Mikal di ra ba, di haa u ni ballɛ, amɔ, gilɛɛ waa dugliŋ.” 14Denii Koori Deevid hum dí ba ga ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf be, “Gil n bir na n haaŋ Mikal la miŋ kpa Filisti baala kalfa hɛna hɔna turgi u kim la.”
15Isbɔsɛf n wa nuu guŋ, u lɛɛu lii u jaari Layis biibaal Paltiɛl be. 16U jaari wii hiŋuu guŋŋ di ga hel bol la banna yir Bahurim la. Denii Abna ŋɔ u be, “Biraa kpo.” U jaa bir kaali.
17A harbɔɔ, Abna la Izrɛl nabɔnzi be, di ga ŋɔ, “Saŋa maa, ii faa ra nyiŋŋuu Koori Deevid ɛɛ ii koori. 18Awia, ií tɔu a kora filaŋkeŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ nuarɛ tɛɛ Koori Deevid, ‘N balii Koori Deevid ninɛɛ ń ga lɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina di lii Filisti hina ni ba dɔma maa nonee biini.’ ”
19Abna kaa ga ŋɔ Bɛnjamin dee nɛra be Koori Deevid kora dii hiŋ wia, ka bɛri la bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn di ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be gunla Izrɛl hina ni Bɛnjamin dee maa n na nyiŋŋi ba ɛɛ. 20Abna ni u nɛra tokko n wa ba Koori Deevid be, bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, u ɛɛ diuzenaa tɛɛ baa. 21Denii Abna ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Gil n la ga chaali Izrɛl hina maa n dɔɔri koori be, bá sɛɛ lugɔ hinuu niŋ ɛɛ ba koori. Denii bá ŋɔ nua, i ni baa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, bá sɛɛ lugɔ ba danna humii, di ra sɛɛ i nua. Guŋ daŋ gil i wer di ra binni Izrɛl hina maa ni gunla hinna nyiŋŋi.” Awia, Koori Deevid sɛɛ wia la maa Abna n ŋɔwɛɛ la, di jaa tau ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ ú ra la ani bɔsɔna.
Joab n kpu Abna wia
22A saŋa hiŋ, di Koori Deevid laallɔɔra baŋhina Joab n tɔ ba see, lii ba dɔma bola di kpogli kuŋkpila maa baŋ foozee laal biini, di ra ba. A guŋ saŋa, di Abna faa waa kaa du Koori Deevid be, bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, dikuu Koori Deevid n teŋ tau ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ u ra kpo ani bampirsɔna wia. 23Ka Joab ni a laallɔɔra n wa helle, u nuu lugɔ Nɛɛr biibaal Abna ba Koori Deevid benii, u tau ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ u ra kpo ni bampirsɔna.
24Denii Joab la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ wideere i ɛɛ kennei? Abna n ba i be la, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i gil u bir kaali gunnɛi? Too, u kaalɔɔu! 25I zum nɛr la dee Nɛɛr biibaal Abna n ɛɛwɛ. U ballɔɔ ú wa darii, di zum i nfɛrɛ ni i wiɛɛlaa maa ŋmɛnizi gunla anna vol.”
26Joab n wa lii Koori Deevid be, u hum ŋɔ bá ga yir Abna. Ba ga huuzuu Sira kɔlɔŋ zɛɛ, di kpogluu ba. Ka Koori Deevid faa waa guŋ zummɛ. 27Abna n wa bittɛ ba bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn la, Joab lii chem u ni a dominuuzeŋ nua, di lawuu lii kɛrii lugɔ unna nyiŋŋi ú ŋɔ wia tɛɛ u bɛŋ la. Denii u chug u hia, u siu. Abna n kpu u niwee Asahɛl la wiarɛ, u kuu kpuu di turgi a kim la.
28Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi zummɔ lugɔ n ni n harbɔɔ hiŋra waa Abna kpui naa wia zummɛ. 29Kɔ́raawiizi tɔɔri Joab ni u diahina maa, dikuu Abna siu naa wia. Di gil baabaaso gɛɛ bɔchɔgaa ɔɔ du u dee biini, baŋhina ɔɔ birgi gbɛraa, di kaa gil bá kpuuzi baŋhina ni tokobi, baŋhina ge ɛɛ lɔzima ani nyaara di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”
30Joab ni u lulli Abisai kpu Abnaa dikuu uŋ kpu ba lulli Asahɛl laal biini, Gibiɔn wia.
31Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ tɛɛ Joab ni a nɛra la maa n du u be la, dí ba lau ba tagtaazi piili, ka kpa ba gbɔglɔŋ tagtazi laali, di tɔ Abna see di ra wii, Koori Deevid ge gba himmaa ra hiŋ a lalii. 32Hɛbrɔnnɛ ba hug Abna, Koori Deevid wii werge maa, u ŋmam bɔr. A nɛra maa gba wii.
33Denii Koori Deevid jaa yir lee yir naa di ra tɛɛ Abna, di ŋɔ,
“A dɛkkɔ Abna n siuwɛ
lugɔ gɛniiyaa?
34Ba waa u nonee vɔɔzɛɛ,
gɛɛ di du u naazi yɔlɔzi.
Ka u siu lugɔ nɛr la
biinikpola hina n kpuwɛɛ!”
A nɛra maa kaa kuari wii werge maa.
35Denii ba maa ba Koori Deevid be di wa ŋɔ lugɔ ú ɛɛ ania maa ka di diwee a hɔl hiŋ. Ka Koori Deevid vɛɛ, ka hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ, “Akai, di n haŋ wa di kummaa ka wiizi chol, Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ.” 36A nɛra maa jaa pessi gunla uŋ ɛɛwɛ la, ba bɔra sɔɔni. Wibii maa, u wiɛɛlaa maa faa par baabuu. 37A hɔl hinnɛ Izrɛl hina maa jaa ta Koori Deevid haahkɛ, lugɔ u nonii waa hoo Abna siu hiŋ wia biini, tama maa.
38Denii Koori Deevid jaa ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií waa zummɛ lugɔ sitɔɔrizenne siuwɛ Izrɛl hɛri zinaa? 39Haali Kɔraawiizi n liziŋ n ɛɛ koori naa, ka Zɛruya biibaal fɔŋŋa kaalimbuu. Kɔ́raawiizi turgi a keŋ wichɔgɛɛra naa ba wichɔgaa kim.”

english_text:
Ishbosheth Is Killed
1Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
2Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. 3The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
4 Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
5One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting 6-7in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them.
Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long. 8Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
9David answered:
I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble! 10 When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
11You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
12Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_text:
Isbɔsɛf kpui wia
1Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Abna siuwɔ bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, u bɔra huah. Ɔnsii lau Izrɛl hina ge maa werge. 2A saŋa naa, di Isbɔsɛf dɔɔ laallɔɔra sitɔɔra banɛɛ. Ba ɔɔ faa tɔ see di ra lɔ ba dɔma. Ba sɔnaa Baana ni Rɛkab. Ba mɛɛrɛ faa Rimɔn la n ɛɛ Bɛɛrɔf hinuu, di lii Bɛnjamin dee biini la. Ba faa ra yir ba gbaa Bɛnjamin nɛra, 3dikuubɛɛwiai, Bɛɛrɔf hina faa chɔwɔɔrɛ ga so bol bɛl banna yir Gitam, di birgi hɔɔhra haali ni zinaa.
4Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Jonatan ge faa dɔɔ biibaallɛ, ba ra yiruu Mɛfibɔsɛf, u faa ɛɛ gbɛrii. Binni anuere u faa di, ka ba nuu Koori Sɔɔl ni Jonatan wia Jɛzriil. U binni izi kpau di ra chɔ. Ka uŋ faa ra yali siwee wia, u lii u nonee chol, di birgi gbɛrii.
5Denii Bɛɛrɔf hinuu Rimɔn biibaala Rɛkab ni Baana izi di ra la Isbɔsɛf dia, baŋ ga hel de, di wiizi baŋŋɔ, u chɔɔ di ra heezi. 6Ba ga bɛri zuu u diisee lugɔ banna zuu bá ga ɛɛ mia la, ka tɔɔh u hia, ka Rɛkab ni u lulli Baana jaa ɛɛ fɛɛɛ chɔ kaali.
7Baŋ zuu u dia la, di u chɔɔ u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni. Baŋ tɔɔuh kpu la, ba teŋ u nyuu, di kpau lii ga Jɔɔdan Waluu biinii, di vol a hahmuŋa maa guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi. 8Ba kpa Isbɔsɛf nyuu hiŋ di wa tɛɛ Koori Deevid, bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, ka ŋɔ u be, “I dɔm Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf nyuurɛ keŋ, waabuu faa ra nyiŋŋi u lizi i miibɔɔ la. Zinaa, Kɔraawiizi turgi i kinnɛ, di gil i kpegzi ni i zenni di Koori Sɔɔl ni u naanna.”
9Koori Deevid ŋɔ Bɛɛrɔf hinuu Rimɔn biibaala Rɛkab ni Baana be, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de, di liziŋ lii tɔɔrɔɔzi maa biine la. 10Baal bɛl faa ba n benii Ziklag, di wa ŋɔ, ‘Koori Sɔɔl siuwɔɔ.’ N faa lawuubuu di kpuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a baal faa fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ amaniyesumaa u ba ú wa lizi tɛŋ. Ka u kinturgaare guŋ. 11Ɛrɛɛ á du tɛɛ nɛchɔgaa la n kpu nɛr la n waa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ, ka chɔɔ u dia biini, ba ga kpuuwɛi? Awia, n daŋ kpu ia di turgi a kim, ii wia tuŋ hɛri naa biini!”
12Denii Koori Deevid jaa gil u laallɔɔra lau Rɛkab ni Baana kpu, di mɔnni ba nonee ni naapezi, ka kpa baa ga vɔɔ sag bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn bule kɛrii. Ka kpa Isbɔsɛf nyuu ga hug Abna ŋmam, bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn.

english_text:
David Becomes King of Israel
(1 Chronicles 11.1-3)
1Israel's leaders met with David at Hebron and said, “We are your relatives. 2Even when Saul was king, you led our nation in battle. And the Lord promised that someday you would rule Israel and take care of us like a shepherd.”
3During the meeting, David made an agreement with the leaders and asked the Lord to be their witness. Then the leaders poured olive oil on David's head to show that he was now the king of Israel.
4 David was 30 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 40 years. 5He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for 33 years.
How David Captured Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 11.4-9; 14.1,2)
6 The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
7-9David told his troops, “You will have to go up through the water tunnel to get those Jebusites. I hate people like them who can't walk or see.”
That's why there is still a rule that says, “Only people who can walk and see are allowed in the temple.”
David captured the fortress on Mount Zion, then he moved there and named it David's City. He had the city rebuilt, starting with the landfill to the east. 10David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
11King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
12David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people.
David's Sons Born in Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 14.3-7)
13After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children. 14His sons who were born there were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, 15Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, 16Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
David Fights the Philistines
(1 Chronicles 14.8-17)
17The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress. 18So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
19David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?”
The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
20David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.” 21David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
22Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley. 23David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered:
Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees. 24Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
25David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid n birgi Izrɛl hɛri maa koori wia
1Izrɛl hina dizi maa chaali, ba Koori Deevid be bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, di wa ŋɔ, “Na, yaa ɛɛ i challɛ. 2A saŋa la, Koori Sɔɔl n faa haa ɛɛ yaa koori la, ka hinuu ɔɔ faa tɔ Izrɛl hina see, ba gaa yoo laal. Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ i be, ‘I danna binni n nɛra Izrɛl hina ni, di ɛɛ ba koori.’ ”
3Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi maa n wa ba Koori Deevid be, bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn la, u ni baa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ Kɔraawiizi see, ka ba waaruu nuu, di tɔu Izrɛl kora. 4Binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔɔ Koori Deevid faa di, ka di a kora. U faa di a koraa genii binni tokkoanɛɛ. 5Uŋ faa du bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn la, binni aniidaanɛɛ ani baaguzi anumbɛllɛ, u faa di kora Juda ni, di kaa ba Jɛrusalɛm ge di wa kpa binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni ahoro, di di kora Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa ni.
Koori Deevid n kpegli Jɛrusalɛm hina
6Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra maa izi la Jɛrusalɛm, bá ga lɔ Jɛbus dee la n du de la. A Jɛbus dee ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Hàá wer na bɔr zuu ɛŋ, nyuŋŋa ni gbɛraa gba bɛnnɛ niŋ duŋŋii lii a bol biini.” Ba faa fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Koori Deevid wàá wer zuu a bolzeŋ biini. 7Ka Koori Deevid faa wer kpegli a Bolzeŋ Ziɔn diikpeg, Deevid Bolzeŋ la.
8A hɔl hiŋ, Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Nɛr la n niŋ kpegli Jɛbus hina naa, see ú ga bɔr la baŋ kuarɛɛ nii ga de di ra pal la, di la gbɛraa ani nyuŋŋa naa n ɛɛ Koori Deevid dɔma naa be. Awiarɛ ba ɔɔ faa ŋɔ, ‘Gbɛraa ani nyuŋŋa wàá zuu a kooridia maa la.’ ”
9Denii Koori Deevid ga zuu a diikpeg, di du de, di jaa ra yiruu, Deevid Bolzeŋ, di ma bar a bolzeŋ maa, haali bɔwillaa la maa baŋ paagi bia suugi la. 10Denii u jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ faa du u benii.
11A saŋaa Taaya Koori Hiram hum u balaa Koori Deevid be, di gil ba kpa hɛriŋkpol daazi, ba ni kapintazi ani maara, bá wa ma kooridia tɛu. 12Koori Deevid jaa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ u kora hiŋ chi nɛnnɛ, di dɔɔ girme werge, dikuu u nɛra Izrɛl hina wia.
13Koori Deevid n wa lii bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn la, u kaa kpa hahkpila Jɛrusalɛm biini di jaa, di lul biibaala ni biihaana kpila. 14Biibaala la baŋ lullɛ de la sɔnaa keŋ, Samua, Sobab, Netan, Solomɔn, 15Ibhar, Ɛlisua, Nɛfɛg, Jafia, 16Ɛlisama, Ɛliada ani Ɛlifɛlɛt.
Koori Deevid n kpegli Filisti hina wia
17Filisti hina n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba waari Deevid nyuurɛ nuu, di tɔu Izrɛl kora la, ba laallɔɔra maa vɔɔ lii, di gaa nyiŋŋuu. Koori Deevid nuu guŋ, di izi chɔ ga zuu diikpeg la. 18Di Filisti hina ballɔ wa yaari Rɛfam Waluu, di su de maa. 19Awia, Koori Deevid faa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi na, di ŋɔ, “Ń la ga lɔ Filisti hina naa? I daŋ gil n kpegli baa?”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “A la, n daŋ kpa baa du i nonee biini, wibii maa.”
20Awia, Koori Deevid kpa di la Baal Pɛrazim, di ga kpegli baa, ka jaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n kpegli n dɔma alugɔ nii n suwee di kpu nɛra la.” Awia, ba jaa ra yir de Baal Pɛrazim. 21Filisti hina faa gil ba vuga ha de, Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra paagaa kaali.
22Denii Filisti hina kaa kuari ba Rɛfam Waluu, di wa yaari de maa. 23Koori Deevid kaa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, u ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ deŋli baa la, bar baa di la ba har, di lɔ baa daazi la banna yir balsam la see. 24Di i haŋ wa nuu laallɔɔra naazi gbɔga a balsam daazi nyuuni, lii chem ba ni laal manaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, guŋ daŋ bagli lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi tɔ i seere, ń kpu Filisti laallɔɔra hiŋ.” 25Denii Koori Deevid ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la. U jaa kpu Filisti hina la, di lii Gibiɔn guŋŋ di ga hel Gɛza.

english_text:
David Brings the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 13.1-14; 15.1—16.3,43)
1David brought together 30,000 of Israel's best soldiers and 2 led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
3 They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart, 4with Ahio walking in front of it. 5Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
6But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest. 7The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
8David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
9David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?” 10He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
11-12 The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.”
At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating. 13The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow. 14He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth. 15He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
16Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
17They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar, 18then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. 19 He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home.
Michal Talks to David
20David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
21David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him. 22I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
23Michal never had any children.
translation_text:
Baŋ kpa Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ba Jɛrusalɛm wia
1Koori Deevid kaa chaali Izrɛl laallɔɔra la n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, kagboŋa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, 2di tɔ ba see la Baala n du Juda, bá ga kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la sɔŋ n sag u ni, u di kora chɛrubzi baambaaŋ la. 3Ba la ga zuu Abinadab dia la n hɔŋ giŋgimii ni la, di kpa a Dakka hɔŋ torkofalii ni. Abinadab biibaala Uza ni Ahiore faa ra binni a torkofalii ni. 4A Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka n hɔŋ u ni la, Ahio jaa tɔ u see di ra vol. 5Banna la la, Koori Deevid ni Izrɛl hina maa jaa ra sa, di ra yir yira ni ba fɔŋŋa maa, di ra lɔ kemzi, janjalanzi, di ra yigzi kuna, di ra lɔ pɛrɛtuzi, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi werge maa.
6Ka baŋ wa hel baal bɛl banna yir Nakɔn pila, a navargazi lɔ naa, Uza tɛr u nonii lau a Dakka. 7Kakpaŋ, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Uza ni, dikuu uŋ wɔɔ tɔgzɛɛ wia. U lɔu, u chol hɛri siu chɔɔ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka kɛrii.
8Denii Koori Deevid baaŋ fuuh dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n tɛr Uza digni ni baaŋfuuih wia. Ba jaa ra yir de Pɛrɛz Uza, haali ni zinaa.
9A hɔl hiŋ, ɔnsii lau Koori Deevid dikuu Kɔraawiizi wia, u ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ Dakka naa ɛɛ ba n benei?” 10U faa waa kaa ra nyiŋŋi ú kpa a Dakka ba u be bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm, ka jaa bir kpau la Gaf hinuu Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm dia. 11Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ jaa du Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm diahina be baaguzi ahoro. Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa kissi u ni u diahina maa.
12Denii ba la ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be gunla Kɔraawiizi n kissi Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm ani u diahina maa, dikuu Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la n du u dia la wia. Awia, Koori Deevid la Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm dia di ga kpa a Dakka ba Deevid bolzeŋ la, di ra di u hiŋ, u bɔra sɔɔni werge maa. 13Banla n ga chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka di ra ba hiŋ haŋ wa vol nogumzi anumbɛl maa, Koori Deevid ɔɔ giluu ba chi, ka u kpu nabal ni nabii la n pɔllɛ nɛnnɛ, di lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 14Koori Deevid kpa pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii vɔɔ u chara di ra sa, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi ni u fɔŋŋa maa. 15Denii Koori Deevid ni Izrɛl hina maa ra di bahinaa, di ra chaasi ani bɔsɔna, di ra huuh ba bensunozi, di chi a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka di ra ba Jɛrusalɛm.
16Baŋ chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka di ra zuu Jɛrusalɛm la, di Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ Mikal chigɔ tokoro di ra binni baa. U na gunla Koori Deevid n na sa, di zaahzi ra chiiri ani bɔsɔna, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la, u wia ra fuuh u baaŋ, u ra gbɛlluu.
17Baŋ wa zuu Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ ni a bol biini, ba kpau ga chiŋŋi Tanti Dia la biini Koori Deevid n gillɛ ba baŋ, ú ɛɛ u chiŋŋi bɔr la. Koori Deevid jaa lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 18Uŋ wa lizi a keŋ mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa ni dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi naa maa tuŋ, u kissi a nɛra maa, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ sɔŋ biini. 19Ka jaa tɛɛ Izrɛl baal ni haaŋ maa paanuubire ni olɔɔzaa ani grepu nɔŋhilaa. Denii bɛl maa jaa kaali u dia.
20Koori Deevid n wa bittɛ la dia ú ga jaami u diahina, Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ Mikal lii chem u ni, di ŋɔ u be, “Izrɛl koori nyiŋŋi sɔnzenne tɛɛ u hiŋ zinaa. U ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ genii, di wir u hiŋ, di ra sa u dia yoŋhaana see!”
21Koori Deevid bir ŋɔ Mikal be, “Kɔraawiizii n faa sa di ra chɔli. U lizimbuu ka vɛɛ i mɛɛ ni u diahina maa, n ɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa sitɔɔri, di ra binni ba ni. Awia, n danna sa di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi saŋa maa. 22Keŋ waarɛ ń jaa du n hiŋ hiihzi werge, i ra fɛ lugɔ maa kummaa ɛɛwɛ. Ka a haana naa waa be, n ɛɛ nɛzenne di dɔɔ girme!”
23Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ Mikal faa waa bie maa dɔɔwɛ ka wa siu.

english_text:
The Lord's Message to David
(1 Chronicles 17.1-15)
1King David moved into his new palace, and the Lord let his kingdom be at peace. 2Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
3Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
4That night, the Lord told Nathan 5to go to David and give him this message:
David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me? 6I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them. 7I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
8 David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people. 9Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
10I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did 11when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you.
Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings. 12 I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler, 13and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me. 14 I will be his father, and he will be my son.
When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents. 15But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you. 16 I will make sure that one of your descendants will always be king.
17Nathan told David exactly what he had heard in the vision.
David Gives Thanks to the Lord
(1 Chronicles 17.16-27)
18David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed:
Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us, 19and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people? 20I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say. 21You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
22 Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true. 23 And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here. 24You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
25And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants. 26Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.” 27After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
28 Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise. 29Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Koori Deevid wia
1Koori Deevid n jaa wa zuu u kooridia biini di so, Kɔraawiizi gil u dɔma waa kaa ra tɔɔruu. U jaa so bɔɔiih. 2Denii u ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan be, “Na, miŋwaa ra zuu diinanii la baŋ kpa hɛriŋkpol daazii di ma, ka Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la waa chi tanti dia biini!”
3Netan bir ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Ɛɛ gunla maa i bampirii n lauwɛ. Kɔraawiizi du i benii.”
4A hɔl hamuŋa ni, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Netan be, 5“La ga ŋɔ n balii Koori Deevid be lugɔ n ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Hiŋ lɛi niŋ ma dia di tɛŋ n na zuu. 6Maa dia maa biini duwɛɛ di haŋ lii a hɔl la miŋ lɛɛ Izrɛl hina lii Ijip hɛri, di wa lii ni zinaa. Bɔr la maa n ni baa n ɔɔ la, tanti dia biinii n ɔɔ du. 7Bɔr la maa n ni Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ la, n ŋmɛnɛ haa ŋɔ ba sitɔɔri bɛl maa miŋ lizɛɛ ŋɔ u ra binni n nɛra Izrɛl hina ni be lugɔ ú ma hɛriŋkpol daazi dia di tɛŋwaa?’
8Awia, ŋɔ n balii Koori Deevid be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, ‘N liziibuu lii peeza nɔɔnaa biini, di gil i di kora n nɛra Izrɛl hina ni. 9N du i benii bɔr la maa hiŋ faa laŋŋɛ, di gil i kpegli i dɔma maa. Filaŋkeŋ, n daŋ gil i dɔɔ sɔnzeŋ alugɔ durnya nɛzenaa n dɔɔwɛ la. 10N daŋ tɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina sognibɔr, di gil bá so de, de ɛɛ ba himmaa hɛri. Nɛr maa wàá kaa ra tɔɔri baa. Biinikpola hina wàá kaa ra fir baa gunla baŋ faa ra ɛɛ baa lugli la, 11di haa ra ɛɛ baa saŋa la maa miŋ lizi baa ba ra binni Izrɛl hina ni la.
N na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii daŋ gil i ni i naanna ra di kora saŋaa saŋa maa. 12Di i saŋa wa hello i ga chɔɔ i naabaala be, n daŋ gil i himmaa biibaal kpa i gawa, ń gil u kora chi nɛnnɛ. 13Waabuu niŋ wa ma Dia tɛŋ. N daŋ gil u kora chi di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. 14N daŋ ɛɛ u mɛɛ, ú ge ɛɛ n biibaal. Di u haŋ wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, n daŋ tɛr u digni gunla mɛɛ n ɔɔ tɛr u biibaal digni la. 15N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá vɛɛ u nɔŋŋaa gunla miŋ vɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl nɔŋŋaa, di lizuu ka gil i kpa a kora la. 16I dia ni i kora daŋ chi di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.’ ”
17Netan jaa ga ŋɔ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la, di tɛɛ Koori Deevid.
Koori Deevid wiisuŋŋaa wia
18Denii Koori Deevid jaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la di so, ka ŋɔ,
“Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, anɛɛ ń ni n diahinai, i teŋ ɛɛ wia mag keŋ tɛɛ yaai? 19Alugɔ guŋ n waa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ i be gba. I kaa bagli gunla i balii diahina wia n niŋ wa du ŋmɛnɛbɛl. Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, kenne i ɔɔ kpa di ra dau nɛraa?
20Ɛrɛɛ ń kaa ŋɔi? I zum mìŋ́ i balii biini maanii, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa. 21Dikuu i wiŋɔɔlii ni i kipar wia, i ɛɛ wizeŋ naabuu, di gil mìŋ́ i balii zumuu.
22Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, i dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa werge. Nɛr maa waa hoo lugɔi. Yaa himmaa digna nuuwɔɔ lugɔ i bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi. 23Hɛri maa hina waa hoo di ɛɛ lugɔ i nɛra Izrɛl hina, hiŋ lɛɛwɛ lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini, ba ɛɛ i hora la. Nuukpuuri wia la hiŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ baa la gillɔɔ i sɔŋ yaari durnya maa biini. I lɛɛ i nɛraa lii Ijip hɛri, di ɛɛ ɔnsii werge wia, di duŋŋi hɛssi hina ni ba vuga ba see, saŋa la baŋ liiwɛ di ra ba la. 24I gillɔɔ i nɛra Izrɛl hina ɛɛ i hora di hanna la, i birgi Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.
25N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, filaŋkeŋ, gil nua la hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ dikuu i balii ni u diahina wia la chi nɛnnɛ di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa. Ɛɛ gunla maa hiŋ ŋɔ nua la. 26Guŋ gil i sɔŋ dɔɔ girme, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Denii nɛra jaa ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ra binni Izrɛl hina ni.’ I daŋ gil i balii Koori Deevid domee du de, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
27Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ tɛɛ i balii lugɔ i daŋ gil u naanna ɛɛ koora. Awia, i balii dɔɔ bɔkpegaa ú suŋŋi wiizi naa. 28Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, i ɛɛ Kɔraawiizii! I wiŋɔzi dɔɔ wibiire. Hinuu ŋɔ nua lugɔ i daŋ ɛɛ winanaa naa tɛɛ i balii. 29Awia, gil a parii filaŋkeŋ, í kissi i balii naanna, bá du de di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, kenne i ŋɔ nua tɛŋ lugɔ i daŋ ɛɛ. Wibii, a keŋ ɛɛi daŋ gil n naanna na kissaa, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

english_text:
A List of David's Victories in War
(1 Chronicles 18.1-13)
1Later, David attacked and badly defeated the Philistines. Israel was now free from their control.
2David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
3David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob. 4In the battle, David captured 1,700 cavalry and 20,000 foot soldiers. He also captured war chariots, but he destroyed all but 100 of them. 5When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed 22,000 of them. 6He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
7Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem. 8He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
9-10King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze. 11David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from 12Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Amalek, and from King Hadadezer of Zobah.
13 David fought the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed 18,000 of their soldiers. When he returned, he built a monument. 14David left soldiers all through Edom, and the people of Edom had to accept him as their ruler.
Wherever David went, the Lord helped him.
A List of David's Officials
(1 Chronicles 18.14-17)
15David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
16Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army.
Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
17Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests.
Seraiah was the secretary.
18Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard.
David's sons were priests.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid dɔma kpeglaa wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Koori Deevid la ga lɔ Filisti hina laal, di kpegli baa, ba sɛɛ u dɔɔra. U foozi Mɛtɛg Ama lii Filisti hina nonee biini.
2Koori Deevid kaa kpegli Moab hina ge. Denii u gil ba chɔɔ hɛri, u kpa ŋmɛŋ mɛgzi baa. U guŋ bɔra anɛɛ nɛra maanii u ɔɔ gil ba kpuuzi, ka ɔɔ gil u horohiŋ waa nɛra du de. Awia, ba birgi u balaa, di ɔɔ lizi hɛri kuna di waa tɛu.
3Koori Deevid kaa lɔ Rɛhɔb biibaal Hadadɛɛza la n faa ɛɛ Zoba koori laal, saŋa la Koori Hadadɛɛza n faa laŋŋɛ, ú kaa ga gil Muu Yufretis kɛraa bola maa birgi u hora la. 4Koori Deevid foozi ba laal torkozi kagboŋ, di lauri a zagra torko zuura ge kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛ ani laallɔɔra la ge n na vol kagboŋa tokko. Denii Koori Deevid gil ba chaahzi a zagra maa zaŋŋuzi, ka gil zagra kalfa n na tɛrgi torkozi hora.
5Siiria hina n lii Damaskus la n wa ballɛ, bá wa hiini Zoba Koori Hadadɛɛza, Koori Deevid faa kpu ba laallɔɔra kagboŋa tokko ni anɛɛ. 6Awia, Koori Deevid jaa kpa u laallɔɔra baŋhina soŋŋi Damaskus n du Siiria hɛri, bá ra guu de, di dɔɔ ba fɔŋŋa, di gil ba ra lizi hɛri kuna di waa tɛu. Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ faa giluu Koori Deevid kpegli u dɔma, bɔr la maa uŋ ɔɔ la.
7Koori Deevid paagi laal saliŋ pɛrɛtuzenaa la n ɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza laallɔɔra nabɔnzi hora, di kpaa ba Jɛrusalɛm. 8Di lii bolzenaa la banna yir Tɛba ni Bɛrɔtai n faa ɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza hora la, Koori Deevid faa paagi danyɛ werge maa.
9Hamaf Koori Tuu n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Koori Deevid kpegli Hadadɛɛza ni u laallɔɔra maanii la, 10Koori Tuu hum u biibaal Joram, ú ga jaami Koori Deevid, dikuu uŋ kpegli Koori Hadadɛɛza laal biini wia. Koori Tuu ni Koori Hadadɛɛza ge faa ra lɔ laallɛ. Joram faa kpa saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa ani danyɛ kuŋkuaraa di wa sunzi Koori Deevid.
11Koori Deevid faa kpa a kuna naabuu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, gunla uŋ faa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ la maa uŋ faa foozee lii hɛssi hina la maa uŋ kpeglee be tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la. 12Baabuu Ɛdɔm, Moab, Ammɔn, Filisti ani Amalɛk hina maa. U kaa kpa kuna la maa uŋ foozee lii Koori Hadadɛɛza be la tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.
13Koori Deevid n wa kpu Ɛdɔm laallɔɔra kagboŋa fidiŋmantannaazi, waluu la banna yir Yazi Waluu biini la, u sɔnzeŋ werge jaa yaari bɔr maa.
14U kpa u laallɔɔra soŋŋi Ɛdɔm hɛri biini maa. Ɛdɔm hina maa jaa birgi Koori Deevid balaa. Kɔraawiizii ɔɔ faa gil Koori Deevid kpegli u dɔma, bɔr la maa uŋ laŋŋɛ.
Koori Deevid nabɔnzi wia
15Denii Koori Deevid faa di kora, Izrɛl hɛri hina maa ni, di ra di wibii, di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa u nɛra maa be. 16Zɛruya biibaal Joabrɛ faa ɛɛ ba laallɔɔra maa nabɔma, Ahilud biibaal Jɛhɔsafat ge faa sɛbi ba wiɛɛlaa di ra dau. 17Ahitub biibaal Zadɔk ni Abiata biibaal Ahimɛlɛk genii faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina. Sɛraaya ge faa ra sɛbi a koori hɔna. 18Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaayaa faa ra binni Kɛrɛf ni Pɛlɛf hina ni. Koori Deevid biibaala ge faa ra biruu liize.

english_text:
David Is Kind to Mephibosheth
1 One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.” 2David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.”
“Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
3 David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.”
Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
4“Where is he?” David asked.
Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
5-6David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down.
David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?”
“Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
7David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
8Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
9David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family. 10You and your 15 sons and 20 servants will work for Mephibosheth. You will farm his land and bring in his crops, so that Saul's family and servants will have food. But Mephibosheth will always eat with me at my table.”
11-13Ziba replied, “Your Majesty, I will do exactly what you tell me to do.” So Ziba's family and servants worked for Mephibosheth.
Mephibosheth was lame, but he lived in Jerusalem and ate at David's table, just like one of David's own sons. And he had a young son of his own, named Mica.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid ni Mɛfibɔsɛf wia
1A hɔl bɛl, Koori Deevid pɛɛzi, “Nɛbɛl haa kawɔɔrɛ di du de lii Koori Sɔɔl naanna biini, ń ɛɛ winanii bɛl tɛu, dikuu Jonatan wiaa?”
2A saŋa, di Koori Sɔɔl diahina balii bɛl banna yir Ziba faa du de. Denii ba yiruu ba Koori Deevid see, u pɛɛzuu, “Hinuu Ziba laa?”
U sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, i baliirɛ miŋ.”
3Koori pɛɛzuu, “Nɛbɛl haa du denii lii Koori Sɔɔl dia, ń ɛɛu winanaa gunla miŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi laa?”
Ziba ŋɔ, “Jonatan biibaal bɛl haa du denii, di ɛɛ gbɛrii.”
4A koori pɛɛzi, “Lee u duɛi?”
Ziba ŋɔ, “U du Ammiɛl biibaal Makir la n du bolzeŋ Lo Dɛba dia.”
5Denii Koori Deevid hum, dí ba la ga yiruu ba.
6Jonatan biibaal Mɛfibɔsɛf la n ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl naana n wa ba Koori Deevid be, u togni u see di jaamuu girme ni.
Koori Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Hinuu ba ra yir Mɛfibɔsɛf laa?”
U sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, i baliirɛ miŋ.”
7Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm, n daŋ ɛɛi winanaa, dikuu i mɛɛ Jonatan wia. N daŋ bir kpa i naabaal Koori Sɔɔl hɛri maa tɛi, ka n nii kpau di ra di n dia.”
8Mɛfibɔsɛf togni u see girme ni, di ŋɔ, “Jara, maa nuahiŋsiwii bɔwɛɛ, ka i ra tɛŋ a girme naa dɔŋaa?”
9Denii Koori Deevid yir Koori Sɔɔl balii Ziba, di ŋɔ u be, “N kpa i dɔɔri Koori Sɔɔl ani u diahina kundɔɔlaa maanii di ra tɛɛ u naana Mɛfibɔsɛf, á ɛɛ u hora. 10I ni i biizi ani i balaarɛ niŋ jaa ra hum u koo huma di ra tɛu, di ɔɔ chaali a koo kuna maa ba u dia, diwee wer du de nɛnnɛ, tɛɛ u diahina maa. Ka n ni Mɛfibɔsɛf waa danna di.” Biibaala fidibanue ani balaa tokkoo Ziba faa dɔɔ.
11Denii Ziba ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “N daŋ ɛɛ wii la maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ŋɔ ń ɛɛ, n dɔɔri.” Awia, Mɛfibɔsɛf ɔɔ jaa ra di kooridia lugɔ u biilullii.
12Mɛfibɔsɛf faa dɔɔ u biipɔllijiga bɛllɛ, ba ra yiruu Mika. Ziba ni u diahina maanii faa ɛɛ Mɛfibɔsɛf balaa, di ra humuu. 13Mɛfibɔsɛf jaa ga du Jɛrusalɛm, di faa ra di Koori Deevid dia, u faa ɛɛ gbɛriirɛ.

english_text:
Israel Fights Ammon
(1 Chronicles 19.1-19)
1Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king. 2David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
3But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.” 4Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away. 5They were terribly ashamed.
When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
6The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah, 1,000 were from the king of Maacah, and 12,000 were from the region of Tob. 7David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
8The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
9Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans. 10He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites. 11Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you. 12Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
13Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them. 14When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
15The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again. 16Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
17David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them. 18The Arameans attacked, but then they ran from Israel. David killed 700 chariot drivers and 40,000 cavalry. He also killed Shobach, their commander.
19When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid n kpegli Ammɔn hina wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Ammɔn Koori Nahas siu, ka u biibaal Hanun kpa u gawa, di di a kora. 2Denii Koori Deevid lɔ nfɛrɛ di ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛ winanaa tɛɛ Koori Nahas biibaal Koori Hanun, gunla u mɛɛ n faa ɛɛŋ winanaa la.” Awia, Koori Deevid jaa hum nɛra, bá ga jaami Koori Hanun, u mɛɛ lee.
Koori Deevid laallɔɔra hiŋ n ga hel Ammɔn hɛri, di la bá ga jaami Koori Hanun, 3Ammɔn nabɔnzi ŋɔ Koori Hanun be, “I ɛɛ tamiirɛ lugɔ Koori Deevid n na tɔgzi i mɛɛ wiarɛ u gil nɛra naa ba, bá wa jaamii u lee gɛɛ? Ba waa ballɛ lɛi bá wa daani a hɛri na, ka wer kpegli yaa?” 4Awia, Koori Hanun gil ba lauri Koori Deevid laallɔɔra la, di fuŋ ba taŋhuna keŋkerezi, di mɔnni ba bɔmbɔga, bá zɛɛpume baambaana, ka ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ.
5Baŋ wa ŋɔ Koori Deevid be guŋ, u hum u balaa bá ga chem ba ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa du baabuu hiihzi werge maa. Koori Deevid tili ba be, di ŋɔ, “Ií du bolzeŋ Jɛriko guŋŋ ii taŋhunazi wa hel mɔɔ, ka ii jaa ra ba.”
6Ammɔn hina n jaa wa zum lugɔ ba wia ra fuuh Koori Deevid baannɛ werge maa la, ba jaa ga kpa Siiria hina laallɔɔra kagboŋa tokko la n na vol naazi lii bolzenaa Bɛf Rɛhɔb ani Zoba, di kpa Maaka koori ge ni u laallɔɔra kagboŋ ni laallɔɔra kagboŋa fidaanɛɛ ge lii Tɔb hɛri jaa.
7Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u hum Joab ni u laallɔɔra maa, bá ga lɔ baa. 8Ammɔn hina lii chi, di ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya ba bolzeŋ dominua, ka Siiria laallɔɔra la n lii Zoba ni Rɛhɔb ani laallɔɔra la ge n lii Tɔb ni Maaka la n ballɛ, bá wa hiini baa la chi a laŋgara.
9Denii Joab na lugɔ a laallɔɔra baŋhina chigɔ u seere, baŋhina ge chi u har. Awia, u lizi u laallɔɔra la baŋhina n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, Izrɛl laallɔɔra biini, u ni baa yoo Siiria hina la. 10Ka gil u niwee Abisai ge tɔ banla n kawɛɛ la see, bá yoo Ammɔn hina la. 11Joab ŋɔ Abisai be, “Di Siiria hina haŋ waa kpegliŋ, í ra chɔ n wile. Ka di Ammɔn hina hiŋ ge waa kpeglii, n ge daŋ wa chɔ i wile. 12Chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega! Gil ya dɔɔ bampirii di yoo, di lɛɛ yaa nɛra ani Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la bolzenaa. N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ gunla n dɛkkɛ u be.”
13Joab ni u laallɔɔra la, bá ga lɔ Siiria laallɔɔra la, ka Siiria laallɔɔra hiŋ bir chɔ. 14Ammɔn hina la n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Siiria hina la bittɔɔ di ra chɔ la, ba ge chɔ lii Abisai be, di bir zuu ba bolzeŋ la biini. Denii Joab bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.
15Siiria hina la n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina kpegli baabuu la, ba kaa chaali. 16Denii Koori Hadadɛɛza gil ba ga yir Siiria laallɔɔra la n du Muu Yufretis wiifurii baŋgia la di wa jaa, di gil Sobak la n ɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza laallɔɔra nabɔma ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri, ba la bolzeŋ Hɛlam.
17Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u chaali Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa, di gi Jɔɔdan muu di la Hɛlam. Siiria laallɔɔra hiŋ ge ɛɛ sirya, bá ni Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra lɔ dɔŋa. 18Ka ba chɔ lii Izrɛl hina be. Koori Deevid faa kpu ba torko zuura kalfaaniidaanɛɛ ani ba laallɔɔra la n na vol naazi ge kagboŋa tokkoanɛɛ. U faa kaa kpu ba laallɔɔra nabɔma Sobak ge jaa. 19Koora la maa Koori Hadadɛɛza n faa kpeglee la maa n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina kpegli baabuu la, ba la ga di kuu Izrɛl hina be, Izrɛl hina jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ba ni.
Awia, Siiria hina la jaa ra ɔm Ammɔn hina hiinaa.

english_text:
David and Bathsheba
(1 Chronicles 20.1a)
1 It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
2-4Late one afternoon, David got up from a nap and was walking around on the flat roof of his palace. A beautiful young woman was down below in her courtyard, bathing as her religion required. David happened to see her, and he sent one of his servants to find out who she was.
The servant came back and told David, “Her name is Bathsheba. She is the daughter of Eliam, and she is the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”
David sent some messengers to bring her to his palace. She came to him, and he slept with her. Then she returned home. 5But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
6David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.”
Joab sent Uriah 7to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?” 8Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house. 9But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
10Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
11Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
12Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.”
Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day, 13David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards. 14Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab. 15The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
16Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers. 17When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
18Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war. 19He gave the messenger these orders:
When you finish telling the king everything that has happened, 20he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall? 21 Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?”
Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
22The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him. 23He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate. 24Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
25David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
26When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him. 27Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son.
The Lord's Message for David
The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_text:
Koori Deevid ni Batsiiba wia
1Wem maga, saŋa la koora n ɔɔ ra la laal la, Koori Deevid hum u laallɔɔra nabɔma Joab ani Izrɛl hɛri laallɔɔra maa, bá ga lɔ Ammɔn hina di kpegli baa, ka fɔɔ bolzeŋ Raba hina ge. Ka Koori Deevid waa faa du Jɛrusalɛm.
2Duaniŋ barii bɛl, Koori Deevid izi dɔɔ wibaŋa ni, di tinni sal di vol ra bar, denii u na haaŋ bɛl n wesse werge maa n na sɔ nii. 3Koori Deevid jaa hum nɛr, dí u la ga zum haaŋ la dee n ɛɛwɛ. A baal la, ka ba wa ŋɔ u be, “Ɛliam biihaaŋ Batsiibaa, u ɛɛ Hitti hinuu Yuria haaŋ.” 4Denii Koori Deevid hum u balaa, ba ga yiruu. Uŋ wa ballɛ, u lawuu nyiŋŋi. A guŋ saŋa, di u ɛɛ u doŋa tuŋ, ka sɔ u hiŋ di jaa ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii Kɔraawiizi be. U tau, u bir kaali dia. 5Aŋ wa ɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ, a haaŋ hum dí ba ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be lugɔ u kpogli hiarɛ.
6Awia, Koori Deevid tili Joab be lugɔ ú gil Hitti hinuu Yuria ba wa nau. Joab n wa nuu guŋ, u tau ŋmɛnɛɛ u ba Koori Deevid be. 7Yuria n ballɛ, Koori Deevid pɛɛzuu gunla Joab ni u laallɔɔra n duwɛɛ ani gunla a laal wia n na vol. 8Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Yuria be, la dia ga sɔ nii. Yuria lii. Koori Deevid jaa kpa sunzaa dí ba ga tɛu. 9Ka Yuria vɛɛ u dia laŋaa, ka chɔɔ Koori Deevid balaa la n ɔɔ chɔɔ ra guu u dominuuzeŋ la be.
10Koori Deevid n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Yuria waa sɛɛwɛ la dia, u pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ haa dia laŋŋɛi? I lii bolle birgi.”
11Yuria ŋɔ u be, “Izrɛl ani Juda hina du laal biinii, Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la gba du bá be de. N nabɔma Joab ni u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi maa chɔɔ lɛl biinii. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ miŋwaa la dia, di ga di, di nyɔɔ, ka n ni n haaŋ chɔɔi? N hɛɛhzii, màá ɛɛ a guŋ widee maa!”
12Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Yuria be, “Guŋwaa, chɔɔ zinaa, ka kɛrɛ n tai ŋmɛnɛɛ í bir kaali.” U jaa chɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm hɔpizaa anɛɛ. 13Koori Deevid yiruu, u nuu di, di gil u dɛɛzi. Ka a hamuŋa hiŋ, Yuria kaa vɛɛ dia laŋaa, ka kpa u kita lii chɔɔ kooridia guure chɔɔribɔr.
14Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzi ni, Koori Deevid sɛbi hɔŋ tɛɛ Yuria, dí u kpa ra la ga tɛɛ Joab. 15Kenne Koori Deevid sɛbi a hɔŋ biini, “Kpa Yuria du a laal bɔkpeg, ka chɔ lii u be, bá kpuu.”
16Awia, Joab ni u laallɔɔra n wa fɔɔ a bolzeŋ, u jaa taa Yuria du bɔr la ba dɔma hiŋ n kpekke, di siili ba ni. 17A bolzeŋ laallɔɔra n wa liwɛɛ lɔ Joab ni u laallɔɔra hiŋ, ba faa kpu Koori Deevid laallɔɔra baŋhinaa, haali di kpu Hitti hinuu Yuria gba jaa.
18Denii Joab jaa hum nɛr ú la ga bagli wia la maa n ɛɛwɛ a laal biini tɛɛ Koori Deevid. 19U ŋɔ nɛr la uŋ hummɛ la be, “Di i haŋ wa bagli a koori a laal wiimaa tuŋ, 20aŋhinabe, u baaŋ daŋ fuuh, ú pɛɛzii, ‘Ɛrɛɛ ii la ga dugli a bolzeŋ werge maa guŋ, ii lɔ baai? Ií waa zummɛ lugɔ ba daŋ ga ba koŋlaa ni di ra virgi ia hobeea? 21Ií waa liizi gunla baŋ faa kpu Gidiɔn biibaal Abimɛlɛk laa? Tɛbɛzii, haaŋ faa kpa nam ga koŋlii ni ta, di lɔu kpu. Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii zum guŋ ka la ga dugli a koŋliiwei?’ Di u wa pɛɛzii keŋ, ŋɔ u be lugɔ ba kpu u balii Hitti hinuu Yuria gbaa jaa.”
22A baal la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ wia la maa Joab n humuu ŋɔ ú wa ŋɔ u be la. 23U ŋɔ, “Yaa dɔma hiŋ faa kpekkoo werge maa kaali yaa, haali ba lii a bol biini di wa lɔ yaa a bol laŋgara. Ka yaa nyaŋŋi baa, di taa baa ga du a bol dominuuzeŋ. 24Jara, ka ba laallɔɔra hiŋ baŋhina ga a koŋlii ni di virgi yaa hobee, di kpu yaa baala la baŋhina. Haali ba kpu i balii Hitti hinuu Yuria gbaa jaa.”
25Koori Deevid ŋɔ a huŋhunni be, “Ga ŋɔ Joab be dí u gilɛɛ gil ú biini chɔgi dikuu guŋ wia, laal waa maa biini, hàá wer zum nɛr la n niŋ siu. Ŋɔ u be lugɔ ú chiiri zɛɛ di lɔ a bolzeŋ hina, di puruu.”
26Batsiiba n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba kpu u jaari Yuria, u wiiu werge maa. 27A lee wia n wa tunnɛ, Koori Deevid jaa gil ba ga kpogli Batsiiba ba u dia, u wa birgi u haaŋ, di lul biibaal tɛu. Ka a wii naa Koori Deevid n ɛɛwɛ naa faa waa Kɔraawiizi pattɛ.

english_text:
1 and he sent Nathan the prophet to tell this story to David:
A rich man and a poor man lived in the same town. 2The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle, 3but the poor man had only one little lamb that he had bought and raised. The lamb became a pet for him and his children. He even let it eat from his plate and drink from his cup and sleep on his lap. The lamb was like one of his own children.
4One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
5David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die! 6And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
7Then Nathan told David:
You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul 8and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more. 9Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
10“Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace. 11 Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on. 12What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
13-14David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.”
“Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.” 15Then Nathan went back home.
David's Young Son Dies
The Lord made David's young son very sick.
16So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor. 17His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
18After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
19David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants.
“Yes, he did,” they answered.
20David got up off the floor; he took a bath, combed his hair, and dressed. He went into the Lord's tent and worshiped, then he went back home. David asked for something to eat, and when his servants brought him some food, he ate it.
21His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
22David answered:
While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.” 23But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me.
Solomon Is Born
24David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon 25and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.”
The End of the War with Ammon
(1 Chronicles 20.1b-3)
26Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress 27and sent a messenger to tell David:
I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply. 28Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
29David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city 30and took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about 35 kilograms of gold, and there was a valuable jewel on it. David put the jewel on his own crown. He also carried off everything else of value. 31David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities.
David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_text:
Netan n jugmi Koori Deevid wia
1Kɔraawiizi hum u dɔgtɛɛ Netan Koori Deevid be, u ga ŋɔ u be, “Baala banɛɛ baŋhinaa faa du de di ra zuu bol kpaŋ, bɛl ɛɛ dɔɔŋ bɛl ge ɛɛ nyaari. 2Dɔɔŋ la dɔɔ peeza ni nauna werge maa, 3ka nyaari la waa kummaa dɔɔwɛ, pelor kpaŋ bɛnnɛ u ge wer yau. U faa dɛɛzuu guŋŋ u wa hel nɛnnɛ, u ni a baal biizi maa du u dia. A peezi nuu ɔɔ kpau kunyɔɔrikuŋ, di kpau di ra di, u ɔɔ lawuu dau u naazi. A baal ɔɔ faa ra ɛɛubuu alugɔ u biihaaŋ.
4Denii a hɔl bɛl, hɔɔhri bɛl wa zuu a dɔɔŋ, ka waa sɛɛwɛ ú lau u peeza gɛɛ u nauna bɛl maa hɔɔhruu. Ka ga lau a nyaari la pekpaŋ la uŋ dɔɔwɛ la di kpu hɔɔhruu.”
5Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u baaŋ fuuh a baal wia werge maa, u ŋɔ Netan be, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la lugɔ baal la n ɛɛ a guŋ wii naa dɛg kpuirɛ. 6A dɛkkɔɔ u kpa peeza anaazu di bir turgi a peezi kim, dikuu a keŋ sikpegii ni biinikpola wia naa uŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ a baal, waa u ni sunne la wia.”
7Denii Netan ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Hinuu a bádee. Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘N tɔibuu Izrɛl hina kora, di lɛɛi lii Koori Sɔɔl be. 8N kpa i dɔɔri dia ni u haana maanii du i nonee, di kpa Izrɛl ni Juda hina tɛi. Di annii faa waa i siwii suwee, n daŋ faa tɛi aŋhina jaa. 9Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i vɛɛ n widaulaa, ka ɛɛ a keŋ wichɔgaai? I gillɔɔ ba kpu Hitti hinuu Yuria laal biini. I gillɔɔ Ammɔn hina kpuu, ka i kpa u haaŋ. 10Awia, jimini maa biini, i naanna baŋhina daŋ ɔɔ siu siukpega, dikuu hiŋ vɛɛ n nua ka kpa Hitti hinuu Yuria haaŋ wia.’
11N daŋ gil dɔgnya ni tɔɔrɔɔ werge lii i himmaa dia, di chol i ni. N daŋ kpa i haana tɛɛ i lulli himmaa bɛl, u ni baa nyiŋŋi dɔŋa bɔchaaŋ, í sibɔɔ. 12I suahwɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ, ka miŋwaa daŋ gil guŋ ɛɛ bɔchaaŋ yeŋgeleŋ, Izrɛl hina maa na.”
13Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Netan be, “N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ zuu Kɔraawiizi ni.”
Netan bir ŋɔ u be, “Kɔraawiizi gil i wichɔgaarɛ tɛi, hàá siu. 14Dikuu hiŋ gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi werge naa wia, biibaal la un lullɛ tɛi la daŋ siu.”
15Denii Netan kpa kaali dia. Ka Kɔraawiizi gil wiila chol a bie la Yuria haaŋ n lullɛ tɛɛ Koori Deevid la ni. 16Koori Deevid suŋŋi wiizi lugɔ u faa gil a bie nyaagi. Di ɔɔ vɔɔ nua, di zuu du u diichɔɔlii hamuŋa maa, di ɔɔ chɔɔ hɛri guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi. 17U dia nabɔnzi ɔɔ zuu u be di ra suŋŋuu lugɔ u izi a hɛri, ka u vɛɛ, di ɔɔ vɛɛ diwee gba dii.
18A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl, a bie siu. Ɔnsii lau koori balaa, gunla ban niŋ ɛɛ ŋɔ u be a bie siu wia. Ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Bie naa n faa haa ra nyiŋ gba, ka waa sɛɛwɛ ú nuu yaa fɔrgaa. Ka kennaa n jaa ɛɛ naa waa nyaŋŋɛɛaa? Di u wa nuu guŋ, a guŋ daŋ wer gil u ɛɛ u hiŋ wichɔgii bɛl gba.”
19Koori Deevid n wa nuuwɛ u balaa hiŋ n na munni dɔŋa be, u jaa zum lugɔ a bie siuwɔɔ. U pɛɛzi baa, “A bie siuwɔɔ gɛɛ?”
Ba ŋɔ “Ɛɛh u siuwɔɔ.”
20Denii Koori Deevid izi, di fɔgli nuusɔɔhraa, ka kpa kundumazi bɔg, di zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia jaamuu. Ka bir la dia di ga gil ba ba diwee ni wa tɛu, u di.
21U balaa pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra ɛɛ kennei? A bie n faa ra nyiŋ, i ra wiiu di vɔɔ nua, ka uŋ wa siuwɛ, i jaa izi di di diwee!”
22U ŋɔ, “A bie n faa haa du de ni miibɔɔ la, n vɔɔ nuarɛ di wii, di faa fɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ na n sinyɛna, di giluu tɛŋ. 23Ka filaŋkeŋ, uŋ jaa siu naa, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń kaa ra vɔɔ nuai? N daŋ kaa wer gil ú dɔɔ miibɔɔa? Akai! Minuu niŋ la u be, waabuu wàá ka wer ba n be.”
24Denii Koori Deevid tig u haaŋ Batsiiba bampirii, ka u nuu chɔɔ, u kpogli hia, di lul biibaal, ba dau u sɔŋ Solomɔn. Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋi a bie werge maa. 25Awia, u jaa hum u dɔgtɛɛ Netan lugɔ u ga dau a bie sɔŋ Jɛdidia.
26A saŋa naa di Joab ni u laallɔɔra haa du a laal biini, di ra lɔ Ammɔn hina la n du ba bolzeŋ Raba la, di faa foozi ba koori diikpeg. 27Denii Joab hum balaa dí ba ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “N lɔ bolzeŋ Raba hinaa, di foozi ba nii bɔr. 28Awia, chaali i laallɔɔra la n kawɛɛ la, bá wa lɔ a bolzeŋ, ú birgi i hor. Di n lɔwɔɔ foozuu, ba daŋ kpa n sɔŋ dawuu.”
29Denii Koori Deevid chaali u laallɔɔra maa, ba kpa la Raba di ga lɔ baa, di kpegli baa. 30Koori Deevid pilli ba vug Mɔlɛk kahuro la baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari di lii u nyuu, di kpau hi. U tɔgzi faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ kilozi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazu. Ba faa kpa binanaa la yoola n kpollene, di margi u ni. Koori Deevid jaa paagi kuna la maa n dɔɔ tɔna werge lii a bolzeŋ biini, 31ka gil nɛra la maa n du de la lii, u du baa huma, ba kpa sɔɔzi ni piŋgaasizi ani kpaŋfɔzi di ra hum, di kaa ra mɔnni birkissizi. Ammɔn bola nɛra maanii Koori Deevid faa gil ba ra ɛɛ guŋ, ka u ni u laallɔɔra maa jaa bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.

english_text:
Amnon Disgraces Tamar
1David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her. 2But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
3Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted, 4and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.”
Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
5Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
6So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
7David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.” 8When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched. 9Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it.
Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone, 10he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.”
Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom. 11But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
12She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting! 13Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
14But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her. 15Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
16She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.”
But Amnon would not listen. 17He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
18The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her.
The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves. 19Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away.
Absalom Kills Amnon
20Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.”
Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely. 21When David heard what had happened to Tamar, he was very angry. But Amnon was his oldest son and also his favorite, and David would not do anything to make Amnon unhappy.
22Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
23Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there. 24Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
25David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
26Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.”
David asked, “Why should he go with you?” 27But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom.
Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king. 28But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
29Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
30While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.” 31David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
32Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him. 33Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead, 34and Absalom has run away.”
One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
35Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
36No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly. 37-38 David was sad for a long time because Amnon was dead.
David Lets Absalom Come Home
Absalom had run away to Geshur, where he stayed for three years with King Talmai the son of Ammihud. 39David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_text:
Amnɔn ni Taama wia
1Koori Deevid biibaal Absalɔm faa dɔɔ niuhambiere, ba ra yiruu Taama. U faa ɛɛ toloorii werge, ka u faa haa waa yuuwɛ. Amnɔn, Koori Deevid biibaala la bɛl faa ra nyiŋŋuu.
2Amnɔn faa ra nyiŋŋi Taamaa werge. Awia, u faa waa wette di ra kpogli u hiŋ, dikuu Taama wia, a guŋ gil u ra wii. Taama n faa haa waa baal zummɛ wia, a faa du kpol tɛɛ Amnɔn gunla un niŋ ɛɛ nau, di nyiŋŋuu.
3Amnɔn faa dɔɔ u dammu bɛllɛ, u sɔnnɛ Jonadab. U mɛɛrɛ Simɛya, Koori Deevid kpɛɛma faa. Jonadab faa zum wiarɛ werge maa. 4A hɔl bɛl Jonadab pɛɛzuu, “Hiŋ ɛɛ koori biibaal, ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i biini ɔɔ ra chɔgi hɔpizi biimaa kennei? Hàá ŋɔ n bee?”
Amnɔn ŋɔ u be, “N na nyiŋŋi n kpɛɛma Absalɔm niuhambie Tamattɛ.”
5Denii Jonadab ŋɔ u be, “La ga chɔɔ, di kutti ɛɛ lugɔ hinna wii la. Di i mɛɛ wa ballɔ ú wa binnii na, ŋɔ u be, ‘N na nyiŋŋuu lugɔ n niuhambie Taama ɛɛ diwee wa tɛŋ ń di. N na nyiŋŋuu u wa daalaa n dia, n na binnuu ka u ra daali. N kaa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ u himmaa mɔŋ a diwee di ra tɛŋ.’ ”
6Awia, Amnɔn jaa kutti chɔɔ, di ɛɛ lugɔ unna wii la. Koori Deevid n wa ballɛ ú wa nau, u ŋɔ u be, “N na nyiŋŋuu ń niuhambie Taama ba di wa daali diunanaa tɛŋ n sibɔɔ, haali u himmaa mɔnni di ra tɛŋ.”
7Koori Deevid hum ba ga ŋɔ Taama be lugɔ ú la u kpɛɛma Amnɔn dia di ga daali diwee tɛu. 8Awia, Taama la u kpɛɛma Amnɔn dia, di u chɔɔwɔ, u ga kpa sau di ŋmir, di ɔɔzi paanuu u sibɔɔ, 9di kpau du pɛrɛtu biini wa tɛu.
Amnɔn vɛɛ dii, ka ŋɔ, “Gil nɛra la maa n du n be la lii.” Ba maa lii. 10Denii u ŋɔ Taama be, “Kpa a paanuu di zuu n be wa tɛŋ.” Taama kpa a paanuu di zuu u be, u chɔɔribɔr. 11Ka uŋ kpa a paanuu di ga dugluu lugɔ u di, u jau, ka ŋɔ u be, “N niuhambie, ba ya chɔɔ!”
12Taama jaa ŋɔ u be, “Akai! N kpɛɛma, gilɛɛ firiŋ n nii chɔɔ! Wii naa dɔŋ waa dɛkkɛ uŋ ɛɛwɛ Izrɛl hɛri! Gilɛɛ ɛɛ a keŋ biinikpola wii naa! 13Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ n hiihzi tunɛi? Ka i geu? I daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ biinikpola hina la bɛl n gɛnnɛ Izrɛl hɛri. Jaande, ga ŋɔ koori be, u daŋ sɛɛ lugɔ i kpaŋ ɛɛ i haaŋ, wàá vɛɛ.” 14Ka waa sɛɛwɛ nuu gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, ka firuu, di lawuu chɔɔ, dikuu u fɔŋŋa n siili u ni wia.
15Denii Amnɔn jaa bir hauh werge maa, di kaali gunla uŋ faa nɔŋŋuu la gba, di ŋɔ u be “Izi lii!”
16Taama ŋɔ u be, “Akai! Gilɛɛ duŋŋiŋ. A guŋ daŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge maa, di kaali wii naa hiŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛŋ naa gba.”
Ka Amnɔn waa sɛɛwɛ nuu tɛu. 17U yir u balii di ŋɔ u be, “Lau haaŋ naa lii bossee, ka kar a dominua.” 18Denii u balii hiŋ lawuu lii bossee, ka lau a dominua kar. Di Taama laali u tagtajaŋ bɛl yoola n kpolle, ba zɛuzuu nɛnnɛ, koori biihambizi la n haa waa baala zummɛ, n ɔɔ ra laali. 19Denii u ɛɛ hɔɔhri waari u nyuu, ka piili u tagtajaŋ hiŋ, ka paa u nonee sag u nyuu, di wii ra kaali.
20U kpɛɛma Absalɔm n wa chem u ni, u pɛɛzuu, “I kpɛɛma Amnɔn ɛɛibuu wii bɛl gɛɛ? N niuhambie, gil wiraa, i kpɛɛmaa. Gilɛɛ kpaa du i biini.” Denii Taama jaa du u kpɛɛma Absalɔm dia ú bɛŋ.
21Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa. 22Dikuu hiihzi la Amnɔn n kpawɛɛ kpu Taama la wia, Absalɔm hah Amnɔn werge maa, ka waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ wichɔgii gɛɛ winanii maa tɛu.
Absalɔm n kpu Amnɔn wia
23Binni anɛɛ n wa bɛrɛɛ, ba ra fuŋ Absalɔm peeza huna bolzeŋ la banna yir Baal Hazɔr la n dugli Ɛfram magbɔɔ, u yir kooribiibaala maa de. 24Denii u la Koori Deevid ge be di ga ŋɔ, “Jara, i balii ra fuŋ u peeza hunaa, i ni i nabɔnzi daŋ wer ba, yaa ni ia kpau di a diuzenaa?”
25Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Akai, n biibaal! Yaa maa wàá wer la, dikuubɛɛwiai, a daŋ ɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ werge maa tɛi.” Ka Absalɔm ra fɔrguu lugɔ u la, ka Koori Deevid vɛɛ, ka ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi ga kissuu.
26Denii Absalɔm ŋɔ, “Di hàá wer la, jaande maa, gil n niwee Amnɔn waa la.”
Koori Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ u nii la denei?” 27Ka Absalɔm haa aah siwii di suŋŋuu werge maa lugɔ u gil u nuu la. Denii Koori Deevid jaa beeli huhzi, ka ŋɔ Amnɔn ni a kooribiibaala maa nuu la.
28Absalɔm ŋɔ u balaa be, “Ií ra du tau, di ii haŋ wa na Amnɔn n dɛɛzɛɛ, n ŋɔ ii be, ‘Ií lɔ Amnɔn ta,’ guŋwaa, ií kpuu. Ii gilɛɛ waa ɔm, minuu tɛɛ ia ŋmɛnɛɛ. Ií chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bampirii.” 29Denii Absalɔm balaa jaa ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, di kpu Amnɔn. Koori Deevid biibaala la maa izi kakpaŋ, di tinni ba kauzi chɔ.
30Baŋ haa du ŋmɛnɛɛ di chɔ ra kpo la, nɛbɛl feli ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Absalɔm kpu i biibaala la maa, bɛl maa waa kawɛɛ!” 31Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u izi di lau u laala piili, ka chɔɔ hɛri ani biinichɔg, u balaa la maa n chigɛ u kɛra la gba piili ba laala.
32Ka Jonadab la n ɛɛ Koori Deevid kpɛɛma Simɛya biibaal ŋɔ, “Jara, a waa wibii ɛɛwɛ lugɔ i biibaala hiŋ maanii ba kpu. Amnɔn bɛnnɛ ba kpu. Kenne Absalɔm ra fɛ di lii a hɔl la Amnɔn n nyiŋŋi u niuhambie Taama la. 33Awia, gilɛɛ waa binni lugɔ gunla baŋ wa ŋɔ i be la ɛɛ wibiire. Amnɔn bɛnnɛ siuwɛ.”
34A saŋa naa, di Absalɔm waa teŋ chɔwɔɔ leu, dikuu uŋ kpu Amnɔn wia.
Denii Koori Deevid laallɔɔri la n chigɛ a bolzeŋ koŋlii ni di ra du tau la, na nɛra n ga lii Haronam n du giŋgimii nyuu ŋmɛnɛɛ di ra ba. A laallɔɔri la ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be wii la un nawɛɛ.
35Jonadab ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Na, i biibaala hinnɛ keŋ, gunla himmaa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.”
36Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ waa tuŋ, di u biibaala hinnɛ wiiwe di wa zuu. Koori Deevid ge ni u balaa la maa jaa ra chɛɛhgi werge maa.
37Ka Absalɔm chɔ kaali Amihud biibaal Talmai n ɛɛ Gɛsur koori be. Ka Koori Deevid ɔɔ wii u biibaal Aminɔn, hɔpizi biimaa.
38Absalɔm n chɔwɛɛ la Gɛsur la, u ga du denii binni ahoro. 39Ka Koori Deevid n wa wii Amnɔn lee, u bampirii tig, u kaa ra nyiŋŋi u na Absalɔm ni siwii.

english_text:
1Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom, 2-3and he sent someone to bring in the wise woman who lived in Tekoa. Joab told her, “Put on funeral clothes and don't use any makeup. Go to the king and pretend you have spent a long time mourning the death of a loved one.” Then he told her what to say.
4The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
5David asked, “What's the matter?”
She replied:
My husband is dead, and I'm a widow. 6I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other. 7Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land.
Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
8“Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
9The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
10He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
11“Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!”
He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
12Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?”
“Yes,” he answered.
13The woman said:
Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back. 14We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
15Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help. 16In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
17 I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
