18Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!”
The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
19David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?”
The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say, 20but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
21David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
22Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
23Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem, 24David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father.
Absalom Was Handsome
25No one in all Israel was as handsome and well-built as Absalom. 26His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
27Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful.
Absalom Finally Sees David
28Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father. 29He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused. 30Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
31Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
32Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
33Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_text:
Absalɔm n bittɛ ba Jɛrusalɛm wia
1Zɛrua biibaal Joab zum lugɔ Koori Deevid ra nyiŋŋuu u na Absalɔm, dikuu u wia n du u bampirii werge maa wia. 2Awia, Joab hum lugɔ ba la ga yir hahnunzunni bɛl n du bolzeŋ Tɛkua. A haaŋ n wa ballɛ, u ŋɔ u be, “Kutti ɛɛ lugɔ hiŋ na lee, di kpa i lilaala laali, di gilɛɛ wa kpa nuunanii maa di ra fɔgli. Ɛɛ lugɔ haaŋ n na lee, di wii ni biinichɔg hɔpizikpila maa. 3Ka jaa la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ u be wia naa minna nyiŋŋi n ŋɔ i be naa.” Denii Joab ŋɔ wii la maa n du de tɛu.
4Tɛkua hina haaŋ hiŋ kpa la Koori Deevid be, di ga giŋŋi di jaamuu girme ni, ka ŋɔ, “Jara, hiiniŋ!”
5A koori pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋei?”
U ŋɔ, “N ɛɛ luhaaŋ la n ɛɛ nyaarii. 6N faa dɔɔ biibaala banɛɛrɛ. A hɔl bɛl kalu zuu baa ba ra naa, nɛr maa ge faa waa hoo de un niŋ lɛɛ baa. Bɛl lɔ u dɔŋhiŋ kpu. 7Awia, n domee nɛra maa kpa a wia chugiŋ, di ŋɔ n kpa n biibaal la n kawɛɛ la tɛɛ baa, bá kpu, di turgi unla kim. Di ba ɛɛ guŋ, màá ka dɔɔ biibaal. Màá ka dɔɔ tamii maa, ń jaari ge sɔŋ dim.”
8Koori ŋɔ, “Izi di ra kpo. N daŋ binni a biini.”
9Ka a haaŋ ŋɔ, “Jara, wii la maa hin niŋ ɛɛ, ka n ni n diahinaa niŋ di a bilchɔg, i ni i diahina waa bilchɔg maa dɔɔwɛ.”
10Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa ŋɔi wiimaa, lawuu ba n be, wàá ka tɔɔrii.”
11A haaŋ ŋɔ, “Jara, suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la, ú hiini n lulli himmaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpu n biibaal naa di turgi unla kim, gilɛɛ waa kpuu, di wàá ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge.”
A koori ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de, ba wàá ɛɛ i biibaal hiŋ wijiga maa.”
12Denii a haaŋ ŋɔ, “Jara, gil n kaa ŋɔ wikpaŋ bɛl.”
Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “A ŋɔ.”
13A haaŋ ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ɛɛ a keŋ wichɔgaa du Kɔraawiizi nɛra ninɛi? Haa gillɛ i himmaa biibaal n chɔwɛɛ ga du hɛrduma bir ba. Awia, i himmaanii i tɛɛ bilchɔg, a kennaa wia hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa biini. 14Yaa maa daŋ siuzi, yaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nii baŋ bizɛɛ ta, a waa kaa dɔɔ paai la. Haali Kɔraawiizi n waa ɔɔ gil lalii bir izi siu biini gba, ka koori waa daŋ wer gil nɛr lii bɔr la uŋ chɔwɛɛ la la, bir ba.
15Jara, awiarɛ n ba i be, í suŋ n ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɛra gillɔɔ ɔnsii lawiŋ. Aŋhinabe di n ŋɔ i be, i daŋ ɛɛ wii la maa min niŋ suŋŋii. 16Awiarɛ n fɛ lugɔ i daŋ nuu n be, di lɛɛŋ lii unla n na nyiŋŋi u kpu n ni n biibaal, di lizi yaa lii hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ ú nɛra la biini.
17Awia, filaŋkeŋ, i balii ra ŋɔu, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi gil hìŋ́ n dɔɔri koori wiŋɔɔlii tɛŋ bɔsɔna, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl, di zum winanaa ni wichɔgaa. Kɔ́raawiizi la hinna hum la du i be.’ ”
18Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ a haaŋ be, “N na nyiŋŋuu ń pɛɛzii wii bɛl, ŋɔ wibii tɛŋ.”
A haaŋ ŋɔ, “Jara, pɛɛziŋ wii la maa hinna nyiŋŋi.”
19Koori Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Joab nonii waa wia naa biini jaawɛaa?”
A haaŋ ŋɔ, “Jara n du de, nɛr maa wàá wer ga yemmaa lii i wiŋɔzi biini. Ɛɛh, i balii Joabuu bagliŋ gunla min niŋ ɛɛ ani gunla min niŋ ŋɔ. 20I balii Joab ɛɛ kenne di gil wia deŋli. Jara, i dɔɔ nunzumaa lugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl, di zum wii la maa n na ɛɛ hɛri naa biini.”
21Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, Koori Deevid ŋɔ Joab be, “Guŋ wesso. N daŋ ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. La ga kpogli a biipɔllii Absalɔm ba.”
22Joab n wa nuu guŋ, u togni hɛri di jaami Koori Deevid, ka ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, Kɔ́raawiizi kissii. I gillɔɔ n zum zinaa lugɔ i dɔɔ n bilaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, i nuu n suŋŋaarɛ.”
23Denii Joab jaa la Gɛsur, di ga kpogli Absalɔm di bir ba Jɛrusalɛm. 24Ka Koori Deevid ŋɔ Joab be, “Gil u ra la u dia. Maa nyiŋŋi n nau ni siwii.” Absalɔm jaa kpa la u dia, di waa koori nawɛɛ ni siwii.
25Di lii Izrɛl hina baala maa biini, ba bɛl maa waa hoo di ɛɛ bunɔɔŋ lugɔ Absalɔm. Di haŋ chi u nyuu di wa tuu u naazi, u yemmaa waa gardama maa dɔɔwɛ. 26U faa dɔɔ nyuhunaa werge, di ɔɔ ra funaa kakpaŋ, bina maa biini, di a wa sukko werge. Di u wa funaa, a tɔgzi ɔɔ ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaanɛɛrɛ, gunla banna mɛgzaa kooridia la.
27Absalɔm biizi faa du banaazu, baala bahoro ni biihambikpaŋ. U biihaaŋ hiŋ sɔnnɛ faa Taama. U faa ɛɛ toloori werge maa.
28Absalɔm faa du Jɛrusalɛmnɛ binni anɛɛ, di waa Koori Deevid nawɛɛ ni siwii. 29Denii Absalɔm hum Joab bɔr lugɔ ú ba, ú humuu Koori Deevid be, ka Joab vɛɛ balaa. U kaa hum u bɔr, ka u haa vɛɛ. 30Absalɔm ŋɔ u balaa be, “Ií na, n ni Joab kooni pɛli dɔŋaa, u dɔɔ baali. Ií la ga fuuah.” U balaa hiŋ la ga fuuh a koo maa.
31Joab n wa nuu guŋ, u hahzi di kpa la Absalɔm be u dia, di ga pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ wiarɛ i balaa la ga fuuh n kooi?”
32Absalɔm ŋɔ u be, “Na, n hum i bɔttɛ lugɔ í ba ń humii Koori Deevid be, í ga pɛɛzuu lugɔ bɛɛ wiarɛ n lii Gɛsur ba ɛnnɛi? Ka ii vɛɛ balaa. Di n faa haa du de gba bɔ n ɛŋ balaa naa. Awia, la ga ŋɔ u be lugɔ n na nyiŋŋuu ń nuu na dɔŋa. Di u wa nawɔɔ lugɔ n ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, ú kpuŋ.”
33Awia, Joab la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ gunla maa Absalɔm n ŋɔwɛɛ la. Koori hum dí ba ga yir Absalɔm. Absalɔm n wa ballɛ, u togni jaami Koori Deevid. Koori Deevid faamuu, di suuzuu.

english_text:
Absalom Rebels against David
1Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had 50 men run in front. 2He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?”
If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,” 3Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours. 4I wish someone would make me the judge around here! I would be fair to everyone.”
5Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them. 6That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
7Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord, 8when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
9David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron. 10-12He took 200 men from Jerusalem with him, but they had no idea what he was going to do. Absalom offered sacrifices in Hebron and sent someone to Gilo to tell David's advisor Ahithophel to come.
More and more people were joining Absalom and supporting his plot. Meanwhile, Absalom had secretly sent some messengers to the northern tribes of Israel. The messengers told everyone, “When you hear the sound of the trumpets, you must shout, ‘Absalom now rules as king in Hebron!’ ”
David Has To Leave Jerusalem
13A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
14David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
15The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
16-17David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him.
They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city. 18Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the 600 soldiers who had followed him from Gath. Their commander was Ittai.
19David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king! 20You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
21Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
22“Then come on!” David said.
So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David.
David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
23The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
24Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
25Then David said:
Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again. 26But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
27Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back. 28I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
29Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there. 30David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
31Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!”
David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!”
David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
32When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head. 33David told him:
If you come with me, you might slow us down. 34Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.”
Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans. 35Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace. 36Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
37David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_text:
Absalɔm n suahzɛɛ ta jinachɔgaa wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Absalɔm nyiŋŋi torko, zagra ani baala tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, bá ɔɔ tɔ u see di ra chɔ. 2U ɔɔ feluu izi di ga teŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ la n chɔɔwɛ di gaa zuu a bolzeŋ dominuuzeŋ la. Di nɛr maa haŋ wa kpa u wia di ra ba koori be ú kuari, Absalɔm ɔɔ yir a hinnɛ di pɛɛzuu, “Lee bolle i liiyɛi?” A hiŋ ɔɔ jaa bagluu bol la ni dee la biini uŋ liwɛɛ. 3Absalɔm ɔɔ ŋɔ a hiŋ be, “I hor summɔɔ, ka koori nɛr maa waa hoo ɛŋ ú nuu tɛi.” 4Absalɔm ɔɔ kaa ŋɔ, “Alako ba faa lizimbuu n ɛɛ hɛri naa seriya diiri! Guŋwaa, di nɛr la maa kpa wia ba n be, n daŋ ɔɔ dia ni wibii.”
5Awia, di nɛr maa haŋ wa ba u be, di ŋɔ u tognuu, Absalɔm ɔɔ feluu faamuu, di suuzuu. 6Kenne Absalɔm kpa di ra ɛɛ Izrɛl hina la maa n ɔɔ ba Koori Deevid be, ú di u wia ni wibii la. Guŋ jaa gil ba nɔŋŋuu werge maa kaali Koori Deevid.
7Binni anaazu n wa bɛrɛɛ, Absalɔm ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Jara, tɛŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ ń la bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn di ga lizi nua bɛl miŋ lɛɛwɛ Kɔraawiizi be. 8Saŋa la miŋ faa du Gɛsur la n du Siiria labuu n lɛɛ a nua, di ŋɔ, ‘Di Kɔraawiizi hiiniŋ n wer hel Jɛrusalɛm, n daŋ ga jaamuu bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn biini.’ ”
9Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “A la ni bampirsɔna.” Absalɔm jaa kpa kaali bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn.
10Absalɔm n ga hel bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, u suahzi hum nɛra Izrɛl hɛri maa, di ŋɔ, “Di ii haŋ wa nuu bensunoniina n wiiwe, bɛl maa ŋɔ lugɔ Absalɔmnɛ koori, bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn!” 11Baala kalfaanɛɛrɛ Absalɔm faa yir lii Jɛrusalɛm, ba duu la, ka ba faa waa u jina la zummɛ. 12Absalɔm n gaa lizi u mbusuzi hiŋ, u hum dí ba ga yir Gilo hinuu Ahitɔfɛl, ú lii Gilo ba. Waabuu faa ra bir Koori Deevid liize. Awia, Absalɔm jaa ra na harbɔɔchigna, u jinachɔgii la jaa ra du kpeg.
Koori Deevid n chɔwɛɛ lii Jɛrusalɛm wia
13Denii nɛbɛl wa ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Izrɛl hina maanii chɔwɛɛ di ra hiŋ Absalɔm ka kai.”
14Denii Koori Deevid yir u nabɔnzi la maa n du Jɛrusalɛm la, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ya chɔ lii ɛŋ, di guŋ lɛi, Absalɔm wàá gil yaa. Yá lii manaŋ, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ wa kpuuzi yaa ni a bolzeŋ hina maa ge di jaa!”
15Denii Koori Deevid zɛɛsogna hiŋ ŋɔ u be, “Gunla maa hiŋ nawɛɛ, yaa maa hotte.”
16Awia, a koori ni u diahina maa lii, ka u hahjigzi fi bɛnnɛ u gil ba so di ra binni u dia. 17Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la maa n lii Jɛrusalɛm la, ga chi a bol tuna. 18Koori Deevid ni u nabɔnzi chi ka ra binni u laallɔɔra, Kɛrɛf ni Pɛlɛf hina maa ani Giti hina n lii Gaf laallɔɔra kalfaanumbɛl la maa n duu la maa wa bɛri kaali.
19A koori bir ŋɔ Giti hinuu Ittai la n lii Gaf be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i hiŋ yaa di ra lanɛi? Bir di ra la Koori Absalɔm be. I ɛɛ famaruurɛ, di chɔ wa du ɛŋ. 20I ɛŋ balaa haa waa birgee. Ka ń gil i vol di ra juuriaa? Maa zum n nyuu chaŋribɔr. Awia, bir zuu a bolzeŋ di lauri i hɛri nɛra, i ni baa ra la. Kɔ́raawiizi ga suŋ i ni, di hiinii.”
21Ka Ittai ŋɔ a koori be, “Jara, n hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa lugɔ bɔr la maa hin niŋ la, n niibuu, haali di siurɛ ń nii maa kpau siu gba.”
22Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Guŋwaa, yaa ra la!” Denii Ittai ni u nɛra ani ba lulla maa jaa hiŋ dɔŋa di lii a bol biini.
23Nɛra la maa n du a de hɛri kɛraa la ra wii werge maa, saŋa la Koori Deevid ni u nɛra n wa bɛrɛɛ di ra kaali la. Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra hiŋ kpa di ga Kidrɔn Waluu, di bir chaŋ hɛribɔduma.
24Zadɔk gba faa jaa ba ninɛɛ. Ka haali Levi dee la maa ge n faa du u be la chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di ra la. Ba ga chuguu chiŋŋi, Abiata lizi mbusuzi guŋŋ a nɛra maa wa lii a bol biini tuŋ.
25Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Zadɔk be, “Bir kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ zuu a bolzeŋ biini. Di n wia par Kɔraawiizi, u daŋ gil n bir ba Jɛrusalɛm di wa na a Dakka u Dia biini. 26Ka di n wia wɔɔ pattɛ, n ɛɛ siryaa lugɔ ú ɛɛŋ gunla maa n paruu.”
27Koori Deevid ŋɔ Zadɔk ge be, “Sinaari lɛi hiŋŋ? Bir di ra zuu a bolzeŋ ani bampirsɔna. Kpogli i biibaal Ahimaz ani Abiata biibaal Jonatan, í ni baa ra la. 28N daŋ so a muu yarizi hɛribɔduma naa biini, di ra kpaŋ saŋa la hin niŋ wa ŋɔ wii bɛl tɛŋ.” 29Denii Zadɔk ni Abiata kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ, di bir zuu Jɛrusalɛm ga so de.
30Ka Koori Deevid kpa kuŋ tɔ u nyuu, di wii ra tinni Ɔlivizi Bizeŋ nyuu di ra kaali ni u naadumazi. A nɛra la maa u ni baa n na la la maa, ge kpa kuna tɔɔgi ba nyuuni, di wii ra hiŋuu. 31Koori Deevid n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Ahitɔfɛl ge gba jaa a nɛra la ni Absalɔm n ɛɛ ú kpui sirya la biinii, u suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hin niŋ gil Ahitɔfɛl wiŋɔzi la maa uŋ ga ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Absalɔm, di bir u nfɛrɛ la maa ɛɛ wipɛɛri!”
32Koori Deevid n wa hel a bizeŋ nyuu, bɔr la baŋ ɔɔ ra jaami Kɔraawiizi la, di Aaki hinuu Husai la du de di ra kpaŋuu. Haali di lau u laalaa piili, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa waari u nyuu. 33Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Di i haŋ hiŋiŋ la, i wia daŋ ɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ tɛŋ. 34Ka di i wa bittɔ la a bolzeŋ, ga ŋɔ Absalɔm be, ‘N dɔɔri, n daŋ ɛɛ i balii, n faa ɛɛ i mɛɛ baliirɛ, n jaa ra nyiŋŋuu ń ɛɛ i balii filaŋkeŋ.’ I daŋ wer ga a guŋ ni, di hiiniŋ di chɔgi Ahitɔfɛl baglaa la. 35Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Zadɔk ni Abiata maa daŋ du de. Ŋɔ ba be wii la maa hin niŋ nuu lii a kooridia. 36Gil ba hum ba biibaala Ahimaz ni Jonatan, bá wa ŋɔ n be wii la maa hiŋ nuuwɛ.”
37Denii Koori Deevid dammu Husai bir kpa ba Jɛrusalɛm. Uŋ wa hel de, di Absalɔm hanna zuu a bolzeŋ biini.

english_text:
Ziba Gives Food to David
1 David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying 200 loaves of bread, 100 handfuls of raisins, 100 figs, and some wine.
2“What's all this?” David asked.
Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
3 “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked.
Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
4David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.”
Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.”
Shimei Curses David
5David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives. 6He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
7Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing, 8the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
9Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
10David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
11Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers:
My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me. 12But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
13David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them. 14When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better.
Hushai Meets Absalom
15By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem. 16David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
17But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
18Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen. 19Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.”
Ahithophel's Advice
20Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
21Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
22 Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
23Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid ni Ziba wia
1Koori Deevid n wa lii a giŋgimii nyubaaŋ di tuu la see tama, u chem Mɛfibɔsɛf balii Ziba ni, di u chigɔ ra kpaŋuu, di kpogli kauzi, a chi paanuuzi kalfaanɛɛ, grepu nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ mari dɔŋa a hil kalfa ani fig nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ mari dɔŋa a hil ge kalfa.
2Koori Deevid pɛɛzi Ziba, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i chi kuna naa banɛi?”
Ziba ŋɔ, “Koori diahinaa dɔɔ a kauzi naa, bá ra tinni. A paanuuzi ani daanɔna naa ge ɛɛ a baala horaa, bá kpa di. Banla maa ge n wa kuuhwɛ a hɛribɔduma biini, daŋ wer nyɔɔ a siŋ, fɔŋŋa kaa ba.”
3Denii Koori Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Lee i dɔɔri Koori Sɔɔl naana Mɛfibɔsɛf la duɛi?”
Ziba ŋɔ u be, “U du Jɛrusalɛm. U ra fɛu lugɔ Izrɛl hina daŋ kpa u naabaal Koori Sɔɔl kora la tɛu.”
4Koori Deevid ŋɔ Ziba be, “Kuna la maa n ɛɛ Mɛfibɔsɛf kuna jaa ɛɛ i horaa.”
Ziba ŋɔ, “Ani i huma n dɔɔri, gil n wia ra parii saŋaa saŋa maa.”
Simei n see Koori Deevid nua wia
5Koori Deevid n waa dugli bol bɛl banna yir Bahurim, baal bɛl n lii Koori Sɔɔl domee biini lii de ba. U sɔnnɛ faa Simei, u mɛɛrɛ Gɛra. Uŋ faa ra ba hiŋ, u faa ra see Koori Deevidii nua, ka ra ba. 6Haali Koori Deevid nabɔnzi, u laallɔɔra ani u guure maa n baruu gba, ka Simei faa ra taazi ba maanii bia. 7Simei n na see baa a nua la, u ŋɔ, “Vol kaali! Nɛkpuuri ni karkanni naa! 8Hinuu foozi Koori Sɔɔl kora, di kaa lau u diahina maa ge di kpuuzi jaa. Kɔraawiizii hanna turgii i wichɔgaa la maa hiŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl ni u diahina la maa kim la. Kɔraawiizi kpa a koraa tɛɛ i biibaal Absalɔm. I kora dii chɔkkɔɔ, nɛkpuuri naa!”
9Denii Zɛruya biibaal Abisai ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “N dɔɔri, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ vasiwii naa ra chagzii kennaanɛi? Gil n la ga teŋ u nyuu!”
10Ka Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Zɛruya biibaala, bɛɛ n ni ia kpawɛi? Di Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ u be lugɔ ú seeŋ nua, anɛɛ n niŋ wer ŋɔ lugɔ ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ u ra ɛɛ gunnɛi?”
11Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Abisai ni nabɔnzi la maa be, “Ií na! N himmaa biilullii n na nyiŋŋi n kpui, ɛrɛɛ bá kaa ŋɔ Bɛnjamin dee hinuu naa wiai? Ií gil u ra seeŋ nua, Kɔraawiizii tɛu a guŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ. 12Aŋhinabe, Kɔraawiizi daŋ suŋ n ni, di bir tɛŋ winanaa, dikuu zinaa nuuseezi naa wia.”
13Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra hiŋ kpa ba ŋmɛnɛɛ di ra kaali, ka Simei ge ra hiŋ baa, di kpa a giŋgimii nyuu keŋkere bɛl di ra kaali, ka ra chagzuu, di paagi bia di ra vuuruu, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa ra viiruu. 14A tuna maa, Koori Deevid ni nɛra la maa n du u be la kpa di ga hel bɔr la banna la la, di ba maa dee jaa kuuh werge. Ba so de di heezi nɛnnɛ.
Absalɔm n du Jɛrusalɛm wia
15A saŋa naa, di Absalɔm ni Izrɛl hina maa teŋ ba Jɛrusalɛm, Ahitɔfɛl ge gba faa jaa ba ninɛɛ. 16Denii Aaki hinuu Husai n ɛɛ Koori Deevid dammu la, la Absalɔm be, di ga ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ koori miibɔɔjaŋ!”
17Ka Absalɔm pɛɛzi Husai, “Kenne ba ra nɔŋŋi dammuua? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ haa i dammu hiŋŋɛ kaalɛi?”
18Husai ŋɔ Absalɔm be, “Akai, nɛr la Kɔraawiizi ni a nɛra naa ani Izrɛl hina maa n lizɛɛrɛ ń hiŋ, di du u be saŋa maa. 19Di kaa kpa jaa, n dɔɔri, anɛɛ ń na hum, di hiŋ lɛiwɛi? Gunla miŋ hummɛ tɛɛ i mɛɛ la, gunnɛ ń hum tɛɛ i gba.”
20Denii Absalɔm ŋɔ Ahitɔfɛl be, “Bir yaa liize. Ɛrɛɛ i ŋɔ ya ɛɛi?”
21Ahitɔfɛl ŋɔ, “Lau i mɛɛ hahjigzi la uŋ gillɛ ba so di ra binni u dia la nyiŋŋi. Di Izrɛl hina maa haŋ wa nuu guŋ, guŋ daŋ gil i wia ra sɔɔhri i mɛɛ miizi, di du banla maa n du i be la bɔkpega nɛnnɛ.” 22Awia, Absalɔm sɛɛ guŋ, ba baŋ tanti dia a kooridia sal, u lau u mɛɛ hahjigzi hiŋ nyiŋŋi, Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ.
23A saŋa, di Ahitɔfɛl faa haŋ ŋɔ wia, a ɔɔ faa ɛɛu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi benii a lii. Koori Deevid ni Absalɔm maa ɔɔ faa hiŋaabuu.

english_text:
1Ahithophel said to Absalom:
Let me choose 12,000 men and attack David tonight, 2while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David, 3since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war.
Hushai Fools Absalom
4Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan. 5Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
6Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
7Hushai said:
This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good. 8You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others. 9He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else.
As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed. 10Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
11My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself, 12and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die! 13If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
14Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom.
Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
15At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given. 16Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
17Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David. 18But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard. 19The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
20Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?”
The woman answered, “They went across that stream.”
The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
21After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
22David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side.
Ahithophel Kills Himself
23When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place.
Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
24David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel. 25Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah. 26The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead.
Friends Bring Supplies to David
27After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
28-29Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese.
They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_text:
Husai n dar Absalɔm wia
1Ahitɔfɛl ŋɔ Absalɔm be, “Gil n lizi baala kagboŋa fidaanɛɛ, di duŋŋi Koori Deevid luge hamuŋa naa. 2N daŋ piguu, di u haa kuuhwɔ di pɛssi, ɔnsii lawuu, ú nɛra maa chɔ yaari, ka n kpu u bɛŋ, 3ka lauri banla maa n kawɛɛ wa tɛi. Di nɛr la hinna nyiŋŋi la haŋ siu, banla maa n kawɛɛ la daŋ chɔ ba waa hiŋii, di birgi i nɛra.” 4A keŋ jina naa faa par Absalɔm ni Izrɛl nabɔnzi maa.
5Ka Absalɔm ŋɔ, “Ií yir Husai, ya nuu gunla u ge n niŋ ŋɔ.” 6Husai n wa ballɛ, Absalɔm ŋɔ u be gunla Ahitɔfɛl n ŋɔwɛɛ la tɛu, ka ŋɔ, “Kenne Ahitɔfɛl ŋɔ ya ɛɛ. Ya ɛɛ guŋ gɛɛ? Di guŋ lɛi, bagli yaa gunla yaa n niŋ ɛɛ.”
7Husai bir ŋɔ u be, “Gunla Ahitɔfɛl n baglɛɛ la waa wer filaŋkeŋwaa. 8I zum i mɛɛ ni u laallɔɔra naabuu, baŋ kpekke werge di zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, u kaa ɛɛ nɛchɔgii alugɔ bunyinniina biizi baŋ paawɛ. Di kaa kpa jaa, i mɛɛ zum laal siweere werge, wàá sɛɛ chɔɔ u laallɔɔra hiŋ be hahmuŋa naa. 9Aŋhinabe, keŋ u teŋ suah bii bɔɔ gɛɛ yembɛl gba. Di Koori Deevid haŋ wa feli wa pig i laallɔɔra, di kpuuzi baŋhina, guŋwaa, nɛr maa daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ u kpegli baabuu tuŋ. 10Haali i laallɔɔri la n dɔɔ bampirii alugɔ bunyiŋ gba, ɔnsii daŋ lawuu, u bɔra ra sa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Izrɛl hina maa zummɔ lugɔ i mɛɛ ɛɛ laallɔɔrikpegre. Banla ge n du u be la dɔɔ bampirii werge.
11Awia, wii la min dɔɔwɛɛ keŋ. Gil Izrɛl hina maa, di haŋ lii Dan dee hɛri la n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag guŋŋ di ga hel bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba la n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag la, ba du kpil werge lugɔ muuzeŋ nua hɛɛhriichaa la maa chaali i be. Í himmaa tɔ ba see di la a laal. 12Denii yá piguu, bɔr la maa yaa n niŋ nau alugɔ ŋmɛnii n chol hɛri la. U ni u nɛra hiŋ bɛl maa wàá ka. 13Di u wa chɔwɔɔ zuu bolzeŋ maa, denii Izrɛl hina maa kpa ŋmɛnni ba, yá tɛrgi a bolzeŋ maa nyaamm di ga du waluu biini.”
14Absalɔm ni Izrɛl hina maa ŋɔ, “Husai baglaa naabuu bɔ Ahitɔfɛl hor la.” Keŋ ɛɛwɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii faa gillɛ ba vɛɛ Ahitɔfɛl baglaa hiŋ, ka ú kpa hɛhchɔg ta Absalɔm ni.
15Husai ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Zadɔk ni Abiata be, gunla Ahitɔfɛl n ŋɔ Absalɔm ni Izrɛl nabɔnzi be ani gunla u ge n ŋɔwɛɛ. 16Husai kaa ŋɔ, “Awia, ií hum bá la manaŋ di ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, ‘Gilɛɛ wàá chɔɔ a muu. Giu la hɛribɔduma la ka hɔpizi. Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ, di guŋ lɛi, i ni i nɛra maanii bá wa kpu.’ ”
17Abiata biibaal Jonatan ni Zadɔk biibaal Ahimaz faa du Ɛn Rɔgɛl bule la n du Jɛrusalɛm laŋgaraa di ra kpaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa wàá wer zuu a bolzeŋ bá na baa. Biihambie bɛl n ɛɛ balii ɔɔ jaa la gaa ŋɔ ba be wii la maa n du de. Ba ge ɔɔ la Koori Deevid be di ga ŋɔ wii la baŋ nuuwɛ tɛu. 18A hɔl bɛl, biipɔllii bɛl na baa, di la ga ŋɔ Absalɔm be. Awia, ba nɛra banɛɛ hiŋ jaa chɔ la Bahurim, di ga du baal bɛl dia. U faa ki kɔlɔnnɛ u diŋŋee hiŋ biini, ba chɔ ga zuu u biini di suah. 19A baal haaŋ kpa kuŋ tɔ a kɔlɔŋ nua, di kpa mia yaazi u ni, nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa zum ba wia. 20Absalɔm laallɔɔra n ballɛ di wa pɛɛzi a haaŋ, “Lee Jonatan ni Ahimaz duɛi?”
A haaŋ ŋɔ, “Ba gi a gɔŋ naa di kaali.”
Denii a baala pigzi ba dia hiŋ maa guŋŋ ka ba waa baa nawɛɛ. Ba jaa bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.
21A nɛra n wa kaalɛɛ tuŋ, Ahimaz ni Jonatan lii a kɔlɔŋ biini, di la ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Izi manaŋ di gi a muu naa filaŋkeŋ! Ahitɔfɛl ta i kpui jinaa.” 22Denii Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra maa jaa izi di ra gi Jɔɔdan muu. Hɔɔŋ waa pizi di ba maa giwɔɔ.
23Ahitɔfɛl n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba waa sɛɛwɛ hiŋ u nua la, u tinni u kawee la u bol, di ga zuu u dia, di kossuu nɛnnɛ, ka sag ŋmɛŋ. Ba kpau hug ba dia bɔɔzeŋ.
24Koori Deevid waa faa chɔwɔɔrɛ kaali Mahanam. Ka Absalɔm ge ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa gi Jɔɔdan muu la. 25A saŋa naa, di Absalɔm faa lizi Amasaa, u lɛɛ Joab bɔr di ɛɛ u laallɔɔra sitɔɔri. Amasa mɛɛ sɔnnɛ faa Jɛta, n lii Izrɛl. U maarɛ faa Abigeel. Abigeel ge mɛɛ sɔnnɛ faa Nahas, u niwee faa ɛɛ Joab maa Zɛruya. 26Absalɔm ni Izrɛl hina kpa ga chɔɔ Giliad hɛri.
27Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra n wa hel Mahanam, Nahas biibaal Ammɔn hinuu Sobi n lii bolzeŋ Raba, Ammiɛl biibaal Makir n lii bolzeŋ Lo Dɛba ani Giliad hinuu Bazilai n lii bol bɛl banna yir Rogelim, 28kpa kuŋchɔɔrikuna, tassazi ani viini. Di kaa kpa huuti, baali, sau, miɔɔzaa, siga, 29huuhnuu, waagazi ani peeza, di wa tɛɛ Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra, bá di, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ lɔzi ni niinyɔgzi lau a nɛraa, ba kuuh a hɛribɔduma biini.

english_text:
David Gets Ready for Battle
1David divided his soldiers into groups of 100 and groups of 1,000. Then he chose officers to be in command of each group. 2He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
3But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth 10,000 of us. It would be better for you to stay in town and send help if we need it.”
4-6David said, “All right, if you think I should.”
Then in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he said, “Joab! Abishai! Ittai! For my sake, be sure that Absalom comes back unharmed.”
David stood beside the town gate as his army marched past in groups of 100 and in groups of 1,000.
Joab Kills Absalom
The war with Israel took place in Ephraim Forest. 7-8Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
9Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by, 10and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
11Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
12The man answered, “Even if you paid me 1,000 pieces of silver here and now, I still wouldn't touch the king's son. We all heard King David tell you and Abishai and Ittai not to harm Absalom. 13He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
14Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!”
Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest. 15Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off. 16Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers. 17They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it.
Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
18When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today.
Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
19Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
20Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
21Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
22Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.”
Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
23“I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted.
“All right then, run!” Joab said.
Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
24Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town 25and shouted down to tell David.
David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.”
The runner was getting closer, 26when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!”
David said, “He must have some news too.”
27The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.”
This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
28Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
29“Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked.
Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
30David told him, “Stand over there and wait.”
Ahimaaz went over and stood there. 31The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
32“Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked.
The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!”
David Cries for Absalom
33David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_text:
Absalɔm siu wia
1Koori Deevid chaali u laallɔɔra la maa, di bargi baa sugezi kagboŋa ani kalfazi, di lizi ba sitɔɔra. 2Denii u bargi baa di du sugezi ahoro, di gil Joab, u niwee Abisai ani Gaf hinuu Ittai, bɛl maa ɛɛ suge sitɔɔri. A koori ŋɔ ba be, “N ni ia daŋ la.”
3Ka u laallɔɔra hiŋ ŋɔ, “A waa dɛkkɛ hiŋ la a laal, dikuubɛɛwiai, di a wa aah yaa ni yaa ra chɔ, ba baga wàá du yaa ni, haali di yaa galga gba haŋ siu, ka ba baga lɛi. I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ yaa nɛra kagboŋa fi ba be. Hiŋ du bolzeŋ ka ra hiini yaa, aabuu bɔ.”
4A koori sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa n par ia.”
Awia, a koori chi a bol dominuuzeŋ kɛrii, ka u laallɔɔra hiŋ jaa hiŋ dɔŋa sugezi kalfa ani kagboŋa di waa kaali. 5A koori ŋɔ u laallɔɔra sitɔɔra Joab, Abisai ani Ittai be, “Ií kuu n wia di ga suŋ biipɔllii Absalɔm ni.” A laallɔɔra maa nuu gunla Koori Deevid n kpawɛɛ di ra karfi ba sitɔɔra hiŋ.
6Koori Deevid laallɔɔra hiŋ la pir, di ga lɔ Izrɛl hina laal Ɛfram kɔr biini. 7Koori Deevid laallɔɔra faa kpegli Izrɛl hina hiŋ de, di kpu ba laallɔɔra werge, kagboŋa tokko, a hɔl hiŋ. 8A laal jaa yaari a hɛri maa, ba banla n faa siuwɛ a kɔr biinii faa kpillɛ kaali banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ a laal biini.
9Denii Absalɔm wa pirgi Koori Deevid laallɔɔra hiŋ de, di u tinni u kawee. A kawee hiŋ kpau chɔ ga zuu daakpeg bɛl zɛɛ, u kela lau u nyuu, u sag di ra zeeli, ka a kawee chɔ ra kaali.
10Koori Deevid laallɔɔra hiŋ bɛl n wa na guŋ, u ŋɔ Joab be, “N na Absalɔm n sag daa nyuu di ra zeeli.”
11Joab ŋɔ a baal be, “Hiŋ nau de la, ɛrɛɛ hɔɔ kpuwɛɛi? Di i faa kpuu, n daŋ vii tɛi saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau fi ani laallɔɔrikpeg belenti.”
12A baal ge bir ŋɔ u be, “Haali di i tɛŋ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kagboŋ gba, ka màá lalli n nonii lɔ koori biibaal naa. Yaa faa nuuwɔɔ a koori n na karfi i ni Abisai ani Ittai di ŋɔ, ‘Ií kuu n wia di suŋ a biipɔllii Absalɔm ni.’ 13Di n faa vɛɛ a koori nua ka kpu Absalɔm, n daŋ faa du siaahmu biini. A koori daŋ nuu guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, wiimaa waa u ni ra suah. A guŋ saŋa, hàá kaa lɛɛ n nua di mɔgliŋ.”
14Joab ŋɔ, “Màá ka chɔgi n saŋa di nuu i wiŋɔjagazi naa.” Ka kpa kandaazi ahoro di yag Absalɔm bampirii, di u haa sag de di ra nyiŋ. 15Denii Joab laallɔɔra fi wa hel di bar Absalɔm, di keezi kpuu.
16Joab gil ba huuh ba bensunoniina, a laallɔɔra jaa gil Izrɛl hina hiŋ duŋŋaa, ka bir ba. 17Ba kpa Absalɔm ga ha bɔɔzeŋ bɛl, a kɔr biini, di paagi bia tɔu kulululu. Ka Izrɛl hina chɔ kaali ba bola.
18Absalɔm de dui saŋa la, u faa baŋ biirɛ yembɛl banna yir Koori Waluu. U ɛɛ gunnɛ, dikuu uŋ faa waa biibaal dɔɔwɛ ba kpau di ra liizuu wia. U jaa kpa u himmaa sɔŋ dau a bii, ba ra yiruu Absalɔm Bii. Haali ni zinaa, gunnɛ ba haa ra yiruu.
Koori Deevid n wii u biibaal Absalɔm wia
19Denii Zadɔk biibaal Ahimaz ŋɔ Joab be, “Gil n chɔ ga kali Koori Deevid lugɔ Kɔraawiizi lɛɛubuu lii u dɔma nonee biini.”
20Joab ŋɔ u be, “Akai! Hiŋ lɛi niŋ la a amaniye naa ni zinaa. I daŋ ŋmɛnɛ wer la aŋhina ni, ka zinaa waa hor naa, hiŋ lɛi niŋ la u ni, dikuu koori biibaal n siuwɛ wia.”
21Denii Joab bir ŋɔ u yom bɛl n ɛɛ Itiopia hinuu be, “La ga ŋɔ koori be wii la hiŋ nawɛɛ.” A Itiopia hinuu tognuu, ka chɔ kaali.
22Ka Zadɔk biibaal Ahimaz kaa ŋɔ Joab be, “Haali gunla maa an niŋ wa du tɛŋ, ka i gil n lii di ra hiŋ Itiopia hinuu naa har.”
Ka Joab ŋɔ u be, “N biibaal, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi i lanɛi? Hàá na kinturgaa maa, di i la de.”
23Ahimaz haa vɛɛ ka ŋɔ, “Haali gunla maa an niŋ wa du tɛŋ, ka i gil n chɔ di ra hiŋuu.”
Awia, Joab ŋɔ, “A la.” Denii Ahimaz chɔ guŋŋ di ga bɛri a Itiopia hinuu ni Jɔɔdan Waluu.
24Di Koori Deevid waa faa sogo a bolzeŋ biini dominua ni baŋgia dominua baambaaŋ. Denii a de guuri ga a dominua koŋlii ni tinni a dominua sal, di na baal bɛl bɛŋ n na chɔ. 25A guuri yir a koori di ŋɔ u be.
A koori ŋɔ, “Di u bɛnnɛ, guŋwaa, u daŋ dɔɔ amaniyesuma.” Ka a baal ra dugli.
26Denii a guuri kaa na baal bɛl n na chɔ, u yir a dominuuguuri, di ŋɔ, “Na, baal bɛllɛ kaa chɔ ra ba la!”
A koori ŋɔ, “Amaniyesumaa u ge nii kpa ra ba.”
27A guuri ŋɔ, “Lugli hiŋ la ra chɔu lugɔ Zadɔk biibaal Ahimaz.”
A koori ŋɔ, “U ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ, amaniyesumaa u kpa ra ba.”
28Ahimaz chaasi, ka togni a koori di ŋɔ, “Jara, wiimaa mɛgzɔɔrɛ! Chɔli Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la, u tɛibuu fɔŋŋa i kpegli banla n na karsii la!”
29A koori pɛɛzi, “Absalɔm dɔɔ alaanfiarɛ naa?”
Ahimaz ŋɔ, “Jara, saŋa la Joab n na humiŋ i be la, di wia aŋhina ra koozi de, ka maa zum wii la n ɛɛwɛ.”
30A koori ŋɔ, “Kaali chi ɛŋ di ra kpaŋ.” Awia, u tuzi lii kɛrii chi.
31Denii a Itiopia hinuu chɔ hel Koori Deevid be, di ŋɔ, “Jara, n dɔɔ amaniyesumaa n tɛi! Kɔraawiizi lɛɛibuu lii i dɔma maa nonee biini zinaa, banla maa n na karsii di ra vɛɛ i nua la.”
32Koori Deevid pɛɛzi a Itiopia hinuu, “Absalɔm dɔɔ alaanfiarɛ naa?”
U ŋɔ, “Jara, a daŋ faa pariŋ gunla n huuzuu la, faa huuzi i dɔma la maa ani banla maa n na karsii la.”
33Denii Koori Deevid biini chɔgi werge. U jaa tinni dia la n hɔŋ a dominuuzeŋ ni, ú wii. Unna tinni la, u wii di ra ŋɔ, “Hoi, n biibaal Absalɔm. N biibaal, n biibaal Absalɔm! Di n faa siuwɛ waa bɔ hiŋ siuwɛ naa! Hoi n biibaal Absalɔm, n biibaal!”

english_text:
1Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
2David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness. 3The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
4David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
5Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him:
You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well. 6You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
7Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
8David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him.
Israel and Judah Want David Back
After Israel's soldiers had all returned home, 9-10everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
11When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said:
Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home? 12He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
13And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
14Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.”
David Starts Back for Jerusalem
15David started back and had gone as far as the Jordan River when he met the people of Judah. They had gathered at Gilgal and had come to help him cross the river.
16 Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and 171,000 others from Benjamin had come with him.
Ziba, the chief servant of Saul's family, also came to the Jordan River. He and his 15 sons and 20 servants waded across to meet David. 18Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do.
Shimei Meets with David
Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David. 19He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it. 20I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
21But Abishai shouted, “You should be killed for cursing the Lord's chosen king!”
22David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!” 23Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed.
Mephibosheth Meets with David
24-25 Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
26He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and 27then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right. 28After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
29David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
30Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.”
Barzillai Returns Home
31 Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him. 32Barzillai was 80 years old. He was very rich and had sent food to David in Mahanaim.
33David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
34Barzillai answered:
Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live. 35I'm already 80 years old, and my body is almost numb. I can't taste my food or hear the sound of singing, and I would be nothing but a burden. 36I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me. 37Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
38David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
39David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but 40Chimham crossed the river with David.
Israel and Judah Argue
All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river. 41The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
42The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
43Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!”
The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_text:
1Ba ga ŋɔ Joab be, “A koori biini chɔkkɔɔ, u ra wii dikuu Absalɔm wia.” 2Awia, Koori Deevid laallɔɔra bɔra n niŋ faa sɔɔni, bá ra di bahinaa, dikuu baŋ kpegli ba dɔma wia la, ka ba biine bir chɔgi baa a hɔl hiŋ. Ba faa nuuwɔɔ lugɔ a koori biini chɔkkɔɔ werge, dikuu u biibaal hiŋ wia. 3Denii a laallɔɔra suahzi di wa zuu a bolzeŋ biini alugɔ nɛra n chɔwɛɛ lii laal biini, hiihzi lau baa la. 4A koori fɔɔ u siwee ka ra wii werge maa, di ra ŋɔ, “Hoi, n biibaal, Absalɔm! Hoi, Absalɔm, n biibaal, n biibaal!”
5Denii Joab zuu dia la biini a koori be, di ŋɔ, “I kpa hiihzii kpu i laallɔɔra maa zinaa. Banla n lɛɛ i ni i biizi, i haana ani i hahjigzi maa miibɔɔni la. 6I haa nɔŋŋi banla n haihbuu, ka hah banla n nɔŋŋiibuu! I gillɔɔ a chaani nɛnnɛ maa lugɔ i laallɔɔra sitɔɔra ani i laallɔɔra maa ɛɛ kumpɛɛrii i be. N nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ i bɔra daŋ faa sɔɔnii, di yaa maa faa siuwɔ zinaa, ka i biibaal Absalɔm du de. 7Awia, lii ga du i laallɔɔra hiŋ bɔkpega. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ di haa haŋ ɛɛ guŋ, di kpa ra ba kɛrɛ chɔɔzi, i laallɔɔra naa bɛl maa wàá ka du i be. Gunnɛ niŋ ɛɛ wichuma werge di kaali hɛhchɔg la maa n huuzii guŋŋ di lii pɔlaa saŋa la.”
8Denii Koori Deevid jaa izi lii di ga so a dominuuzeŋ la nua. Baŋ ga ŋɔ laallɔɔra hiŋ be, “A koori sogo a dominuuzenne,” ba maa ba u be.
Koori Deevid n bittɛ ba Jɛrusalɛm wia
A saŋa naa, di Izrɛl hina maa chɔwɔɔ kaali ba bola. 9Izrɛl hina dizi la maa ra di dɔŋa hɔɔzi, di ra ŋɔ, “A koorii lɛɛ yaa lii yaa dɔma nonee biini, di lɛɛ yaa lii Filisti hina be. Ka filaŋkeŋ u kuu u biibaal Absalɔm wia di chɔ ka ka a hɛri. 10Yaa tɔ Absalɔm kora lugɔ u ra binni yaa ni, ka u siu laal biini. Awia, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yaa wàá gil Koori Deevid kaa bir banɛi?”
11Izrɛl hina wiŋɔzi hiŋ maa hel Koori Deevid. Awia, u hum Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Zadɔk ni Abiata lugɔ ba la ga pɛɛzi Juda nabɔnzi, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii tɔ har ií hiini bá kaa kpogli a koori ba u dianɛi? 12Ii ɛɛ n lullaa, yaa maa ɛɛ chakpaŋ. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii tɔ har, ii kaa kpogliŋ banɛi?” 13Koori Deevid ŋɔ dí ba ga ŋɔ Amasa ge be, “Yaa waa chakpaŋ ɛɛwɛ lɛiyaa? Di haŋ lii zinaa, n liziibuu í lɛɛ Joab bɔr di ɛɛ n laallɔɔra sitɔɔri. Di maa haŋ ɛɛ guŋ, Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ!”
14U wiŋɔzi la par Juda baala hiŋ werge maa alugɔ baŋ ɛɛ kpaŋ wia. Ba hum ba ga ŋɔ a koori be, “Í ni i nɛra maa bir di ra ba.”
15Denii a koori bir di ra ba, di vol guŋŋ wa hel Jɔɔdan muu. A saŋa, di Juda baala ba Gilgal, bá wa chem u ni, di kpogluu gi a muu. 16Gɛra biibaal Simei n lii Bɛnjamin dee biini, di lii Bahurim, hahzi la Jɔɔdan muu ú ga chem Koori Deevid ni. 17Bɛnjamin dee nɛra kagbonne faa jaa u ni, di kpa Koori Sɔɔl diahina balii Ziba, di kaa kpa u biibaala fidibanue ani u balaa ge tokko. Ba maa hahzi la Jɔɔdan muu, bɔr la a koori n duwɛɛ la. 18Ba gi a muu, bá ga kpogli a koori ni u diahina wa gi, di ɛɛ wia la maa unna nyiŋŋi.
Simei n wa gi Jɔɔdan muu la, u chol pi a koori see, 19di ŋɔ u be, “Jara, n na suŋŋiibuu werge maa, suuh wichɔgaa la miŋ ɛɛi, a hɔl la hinna lii Jɛrusalɛm la. Gilɛɛ wa kpaa di ra ɛɛŋ wiimaa gɛɛ di kaa ra liizi a wia kɔrai. 20N zummɔ lugɔ n ɛɛibuu wichɔgaa. Aabuu gillɛ n feli nɛr maa lii Joosɛf diahina biini di ba ɛŋ, ń wa chem i ni la.”
21Denii Zɛruya biibaal Abisai ŋɔ, “A waa dɛkkɛ baŋ kpu Simei dikuu a kennaa wiaa? U see nɛr la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ di tɔu kora labuu nua.”
22Koori Deevid bir ŋɔ, “Zɛruya biibaala, bɛɛ n ni ia kpauwɛi? Ii birgi n dɔmaa zinaa! A dɛkkɔ baŋ kpu nɛr Izrɛl biini zinaa? Ii fɛ lugɔ maa zummɛ lugɔ minuu Izrɛl hina koori zinaa?” 23A koori hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Simei, “Hàá siu.”
24Koori Sɔɔl naana Mɛfibɔsɛf ge lii ú ga chem a koori ni. Waa u naazi sanzɛɛ, waa u nuuhuna ge funnɛ gɛɛ di chag u kuna gba, di lii saŋa la a koori n liwɛɛ, ka kaa bir ba la. 25Mɛfibɔsɛf n lii Jɛrusalɛm di ga chem a koori ni la, a koori pɛɛzuu, “Mɛfibɔsɛf, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ haŋ hiŋŋɛ lanɛi?”
26U ŋɔ, “Jara, i zummɔ lugɔ n ɛɛ gbɛriirɛ. N faa ŋɔ n balii benii lugɔ ú bɔg n kawee ń tinnuu, n nii la, ka u dariŋ. 27Jara, u chɔg n sɔnnɛ i be. Jara, i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl. Awia, ɛɛ gunla maa n parii. 28N naabaal naanna waa wiimaa dɛkkɛ di lii i be di siu bɛŋ lɛi, ka i tɛɛ i baliirɛ bɔr u jaa banla n na di i be. Awia, a waa dɛkkɛ n kaa suŋŋii kummaa.”
29A koori ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ kaa ŋɔ wiimaa. Í ni Ziba ga bɔnni i hɛri la.”
30Mɛfibɔsɛf ŋɔ a koori be, “Jara, gil Ziba kpogli u maa. Hiŋ bittɛ ba bol ni bɔsɔna naa gba kukkimbuu.”
31Giliad hinuu Bazilai faa lii Rogelim ba Jɔɔdan muu ú wa hiini Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra bá gi. 32Bazilai naa faa ɛɛ bazɛŋaa, u binni faa du tokkoanaazu. Saŋa la Koori Deevid n faa du Mahanam la, u faa ra hiini Koori Deevidii ni diwee, dikuu uŋ faa ɛɛ dɔɔŋ wia. 33A koori ŋɔ Bazilai be, “Gil n nii maa gi a muu di la Jɛrusalɛm ga so, ń na binni i ni.”
34Ka Bazilai ŋɔ a koori be, “Binni aŋmɛnɛɛ n kaa di lugɔ n hiŋii la Jɛrusalɛmnɛi? 35N teŋ di binni tokkoanɛɛrɛ. Kummaa waa kaa du sum n be. Maa kaa zum diwee gɛɛ siŋ suma, maa kaa wer di ra nuu yiryitta loobee. Jara, n wia daŋ ga ɛɛibuu tɔɔrɔɔ bɛŋ. 36Maa a keŋ kinturgaa naa dɛkkɛ. Hiŋwaa gil n dui gi Jɔɔdan muu, di la see tama. 37Taŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ ń bir di ra la bol di ga siu dugli n mɛɛ ni n maa ŋmama. Ka n biibaal Kimhannɛ keŋ. Jara, gil i nuu gi di ra la. Gaa dawuu gunla maa n parii.”
38Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “N nuuwɔɔ, n ni Kimham daŋ la. Wii la maa n parii, n daŋ ɛɛ tɛu. Wii la maa ge hinna nyiŋŋi n be, n daŋ ɛɛu tɛi.”
39Awia, a nɛra maa tɔ see di gi a Jɔɔdan muu, ka a koori ge jaa gi. Koori Deevid faami Bazilai, di suuzuu, ka kissuu. Bazilai jaa bir kpo.
40A koori n faa giwɛɛ di la Gilgal la, Kimham waa faa hiŋuubuu gi. Juda hina laallɔɔra maa ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra yeŋ wa jaa, ba maa du a koori gi.
41Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, Izrɛl baala maa ba a koori be, di waa ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yaa lulla Juda hina baala ŋmɛɛ koori ni u diahina maa di kpogli baa gi Jɔɔdan muu, di kpa u laallɔɔra maa gba jaai?”
42Juda baala maa ŋɔ Izrɛl baala be, “Yaa ɛɛ gunnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa ni a koori lullɔɔ nɛnnɛ. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii baana fuuh a guŋ wiai? Yaa di a koori diweere gɛɛ di kpa u kumbɛlɛi?”
43Denii Izrɛl baala bir ŋɔ Juda baala be, “Yaa dɔɔ a koorii bufi, gunla iiŋ dɔɔu la, haali di u ɛɛ ii bɛl gba. Ka ɛrɛɛ ii ra gbɛlli yaa gunnɛi? Ií gilɛɛ suuh lugɔ yaabuu felee ŋɔ a koori bir balaa wia!”
Ka Juda hina faa ra ŋɔ kpegzi ani baaŋ ni, di kaali gunla Izrɛl hina n na ŋɔ la.

english_text:
Sheba Rebels against David
1 A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
2So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
David's Ten Wives
3 David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows.
The Army Goes after Sheba
4David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
5Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days. 6So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.”
Joab Kills Amasa
7Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops. 8They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
9Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss. 10Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying.
Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba. 11One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
12Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket. 13After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba.
Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
14Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
15Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down.
A Wise Woman Saves the Town
16A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!” 17When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?”
“Yes, I am,” he answered.
She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.”
“All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
18She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem. 19We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
20Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town! 21That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.”
The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
22She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab.
Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem.
Another List of David's Officials
23Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army.
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
24Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force.
Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
25Sheva was the secretary.
Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
26Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_text:
Siiba n di Koori Deevid mmɔri wia
1Denii baal bɛl banna yir Bikri biibaal Siiba n lii Bɛnjamin dee biini, di ɛɛ kalu nyiŋŋi, faa jaa ba ni, huuh bensunoniina werge maa, ka pozi di ŋɔ,
“Izrɛl hina, beedee yaa ni Koori Deevid kora la dɔɔ bɔnnaai?
Yaa ni Jɛssɛ biibaala waa
kummaa bɔnnaa dɔɔwɛ.
Aa! Izrɛl hina, ií ra la ii diini.”
2Awia, Izrɛl hina waa vɛɛ Koori Deevid, ka ga hiŋ Siiba di ra la. Ka Juda hina waa sɛɛ Koori Deevid wia, di du u be, di duu lii Jɔɔdan muu guŋŋ di ga hel Jɛrusalɛm.
3Koori Deevid n wa bittɛ la u dia Jɛrusalɛm biini, u lau u hahjigzi fi la uŋ faa gillɛ ba ra binni u dia la, di du dia bɛl biini, di gil ba ra guu baa. U ra dɛɛzi baa, ka waa kaa sɛɛ u ni bɛl maa chɔɔ. Waa kaa sɛɛ ba lii chaaŋ maa di ra ba ba siu. Ba faa jaa du lugɔ luhaana.
4Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Amasa be, “Yir Juda baala lugɔ ba maa chaali n be hɔpizaa ahoro biini, í ge gba jaa ba ni.” 5Ka Amasa n laŋŋɛ ú ga yir Juda laallɔɔra la, u ga birgi kaali saŋa la Koori Deevid n tɛu la.
6Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Abisai be, “Bikri biibaal Siiba daŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa kaali gunla Absalɔm n ɛɛwɛ la gba. Awia, lau n laallɔɔra di dau u luge, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ chɔ zuu bolzeŋkpega la biine, yaa wàá ka nau lau.” 7Awia, Joab laallɔɔra, koori guure ani laallɔɔra la maa n kawɛɛ la lii Jɛrusalɛm, di ra dau Siiba luge.
8Baŋ ga hel bizeŋ la n du Gibiɔn, Amasa chem ba ni. Di Joab ge laali u laal kuna di kpa u tokobi suu u too di kirsi u chara. Uŋ volle di ra la see la, a tokobi lii chol.
9Joab ŋɔ Amasa be, “N niwee, jaanjaamu, i du ɛrɛɛ?” Denii Joab jaa tɛr u nonii lau Amasa taŋhuna lugɔ unna nyiŋŋi ú suuzuu la. 10Ka Amasa salli lugɔ Joab kpogli tokobii. Joab tɔɔh u hia, u looree vir lii chol hɛri, Amasa siu kakpaŋ. Awia, waa kaa tɔɔuh bunɛɛ. Ka Joab ni u niwee Abisai haa ra dau Siiba luge.
11Joab laallɔɔra la bɛl wa chi Amasa be, ka ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa n nɔŋŋi Joab, di sɛɛ Koori Deevid wia, amɔ, ú ra hiŋ Joab!” 12Amasa chɔɔ u chal biini a ŋmɛnibaaŋ. Joab laallɔɔri hiŋ na lugɔ a laallɔɔra maa ballɔɔ di waa chi de. Awia, u tuuzuu lii a ŋmɛnɛɛ di ga dau pir, di yaa tagta tɔu. 13Uŋ wa tuuzi Amasa lii a ŋmɛnɛɛ tuŋ, a nɛra maa hiŋ Joab di ra dau Siiba luge.
14Siiba ga Izrɛl hina dizi maa biine guŋŋ di ga hel bolzeŋkpeg la banna yir Abɛl Bɛf Maaka la. Bikri domee baala maa chaali hiŋuu zuu a bolzeŋ biini. 15Joab ni u laallɔɔra maa n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Siiba du de, ba la ga fɔɔ a bolzeŋ, di ta pizenaa pɛli u koŋlii, di kaa faari di ra ki a koŋlii zɛɛ, ú chol. 16Hahnunzunni bɛl du a bolzeŋ lɔ wile werge maa di ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu! Ií ra nuu! Ií ŋɔ Joab be lugɔ ú ba ɛŋ, n ŋɔ wia tɛu.” 17Joab la, u pɛɛzuu, “Hinuu Joab laa?”
U ŋɔ “Ɛɛh, minuu.”
A haaŋ ŋɔ, “A nuu gunla i balii n niŋ ŋɔ.”
Joab ŋɔ, “N na nuuu.”
18U ŋɔ, “Faala maa, a ba ŋɔu, ‘La bolzeŋ Abɛl di ga na i wia zɛɛ.’ Guŋ himmaanii ba ɛɛ la. 19Yaabuu ɛɛ bampirsɔna ni wibii hina Izrɛl hɛri. I ra nyiŋŋuu i chɔgi bolzeŋ la n ɛɛ Izrɛl bola maa nyuu hiŋ. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi i chɔgi Kɔraawiizi kundɔɔliiyɛi?”
20Joab ŋɔ, “Akai! N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá sɛɛ chɔgi ii bolzeŋ naa! 21Gunlɛi kɔrai! Baal bɛl banna yir Siiba, u ɛɛ Bikri biibaal, n lii Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri, faarɔɔrɛ di ra di Koori Deevid mmɔri. Ií lawuu tɛɛ yaa, ka ń gil bolzeŋ naa.”
A haaŋ ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ kpa u nyuu ha danzɛɛkɛrii tɛi.” 22Denii a haaŋ zuu a bol biini di ga ŋɔ a bol hina be gunla unna fɛ. Ba jaa teŋ Siiba nyuu, di tau tɛɛ Joab. Joab huuh bensunoniina lugɔ u laallɔɔra gil a bolzeŋ, ka bir di ra kpo. Denii Joab ge bir kaali Koori Deevid be Jɛrusalɛm.
23Joab faa ɛɛ Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa nabɔmaa. Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya genii faa ɛɛ a koori guure nabɔma. 24Adoniram genii faa ra binni banla baŋ ɔɔ fir ba ra hum huma la nabɔma. Ahilud biibaal Jɛhɔsafat ge faa sɛbi wia di ra dau. 25Siva ge faa ɛɛ ba seriya dii dia karchi. Zadɔk ni Abiata ge faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina. 26Ira la n lii bolzeŋ Jayir ge faa ɛɛ Koori Deevid kizeehina la bɛl.

english_text:
The Gibeonites Hang Saul's Descendants
1While David was king, there were three years in a row when the nation of Israel could not grow enough food. So David asked the Lord for help, and the Lord answered, “Saul and his family are guilty of murder, because he had the Gibeonites killed.”
2 The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land.
David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them. 3He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
4The Gibeonites answered, “Silver and gold from Saul and his family are not enough. On the other hand, we don't have the right to put any Israelite to death.”
David said, “I'll do whatever you ask.”
5They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel. 6Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.”
“I'll give them to you,” David said.
7 David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul. 8 But Saul and Rizpah the daughter of Aiah had two sons named Armoni and Mephibosheth. Saul's daughter Merab had five sons whose father was Adriel the son of Barzillai from Meholah. David took Rizpah's two sons and Merab's five sons and 9turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest.
Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
10Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain.
The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
11-12 Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan. 13-14David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land.
The Descendants of the Rephaim
(1 Chronicles 20.4-8)
15One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines. 16One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms. 17 But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine.
David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
18There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
19There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
20There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. 21But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
22David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_text:
Baŋ kpu Koori Sɔɔl naanna wia
1Saŋa la Koori Deevid n faa ɛɛ koori la, lɔchɔgii bɛl faa wa cholloo werge maa, binni ahoro. Koori Deevid faa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi wii la n gillɛ guŋ ɛɛ. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “N gillɔɔ a lɔzi chol dikuu Koori Sɔɔl ni u diahina n ɛɛ nɛkpuura wia. U kpu Gibiɔn hinaa.” 2Gibiɔn hina faa waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ. Ba faa ɛɛ Amɔri hina yenne, di faa du tama. Izrɛl hina faa hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ di ŋɔ nua lugɔ ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá kpu baa. Ka Sɔɔl faa ra nyiŋŋi ú dim baa, dikuu uŋ nɔŋŋi Izrɛl ni Juda hina werge wia. 3Awia, Koori Deevid faa chaali Gibiɔn hina, di ŋɔ ba be, “Bɛɛ ii ra nyiŋŋi ń ɛɛ tɛɛ ia? N na nyiŋŋuu ń turgi wichɔgaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ ia la kim, guŋ gil ii kissi Kɔraawiizi nɛra.”
4Ba ŋɔ, “Kebee gɛɛ saliŋ gɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋu wàá wer kuari yaa ni Koori Sɔɔl diahina kalu la, yaa ge waa nyiŋŋi yá kpu Izrɛl hinuu maa.”
Denii Deevid pɛɛzi, “Ka bɛɛ ii jaa ra nyiŋŋi ŋɔ ń ɛɛ tɛɛ ia?”
5Ba ŋɔ, “Koori Sɔɔl nfɛrɛɛ lugɔ ú dim yaa, yá gilɛɛ ka du Izrɛl hɛri yemmaa. 6Awia, lau u naanna la n ɛɛ baala baniidaanɛɛ tɛɛ yaa, yá kpu baa Gibia la n ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ la bol.”
A koori ŋɔ, “N daŋ kpa baa di tɛɛ ia.”
7Ka Koori Deevid faa gil Jonatan biibaal Mɛfibɔsɛf, Sɔɔl naana waa, dikuu nua la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ u mɛɛ la wia. 8Koori Deevid faa lau Aaya biihaaŋ Rizpa biibaala Aamɔni ni Mɛfibɔsɛf, u ni Koori Sɔɔl n lullɛ. U kaa lau Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ Mɛrab biibaala, u ni Bazilai biibaal Adriɛl n lii Mɛhɔla n lullɛ. 9Koori Deevid kpa baa tɛɛ Gibiɔn hina, ba kpu baa dau giŋgimii nyuu, Kɔraawiizi see. Ba nɛra baniidaanɛɛhiŋ maanii ba faa kpau kpu, saŋa la baŋ faari baali kumaa la.
10Denii Sɔɔl hahjiga Aaya biihaaŋ Rizpa, kpa gbɔglɔŋ du pampanni bii nyuu, bɔr la a lalaa n chɔɔwɛ la. Di du de, a baali kumaa saŋa guŋŋ di ga hel sazau dooŋ balaa saŋa. Hɔpizaa saŋa, u ɔɔ duŋŋi zumbizi lii ba be, hamuŋzi ge, u duŋŋi pir sela. 11Koori Deevid n wa nuu gunla Rizpa n ɛɛwɛ la, 12u izi la Jabɛs Giliad hina be, di ga paa Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan hoga. Giliad hina faa ŋmɛɛabuu lii Bɛf San, bɔr la Filisti hina n faa sag baa ŋmɛŋ, saŋa la baŋ kpu Koori Sɔɔl, Gilbɔa la. 13Denii Koori Deevid paa Koori Sɔɔl, Jonatan ani baala baniidaanɛɛ la maa baŋ faa kpuwɛɛ la hoga lii de. 14Ba hug Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan hoga Koori Sɔɔl mɛɛ Kis ŋmam, Zɛla n du Bɛnjamin hɛri, gunla Koori Deevid n faa ŋɔ bá ɛɛ la. Kɔraawiizi jaa nuu ba wiisuŋŋaa tɛɛ a hɛri maa.
Izrɛl ni Filisti hina laalzi wia
15A hɔl bɛl, Filisti ni Izrɛl hina kaa ra yoo laal. Deevid izi tɔ u nɛra see, bá ga yoo a Filisti hina hiŋ. Baŋ gaa yoo baa la, u wa kuuh werge maa. 16Denii Isbi Bɛnɔb n ɛɛ Rafa naana bɛl, u danyɛ kandaa nyuu tɔgzi bɛŋ faa ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaahoro, u kaa laali tokobifalii, faa fɛ lugɔ u daŋ wer kpu Koori Deevid. 17Ka Zɛruya biibaal Abisai ba wa mɔgli Deevid, di kpa u kandaa yag a Filisti hinuu kpu. Denii Koori Deevid laallɔɔra la hɛɛhzi tɛu, di ŋɔ, “Yaa nii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka la laal, dikuubɛɛwiai, hinuu Izrɛl hina tamii, yaa waa nyiŋŋi ya nyaai.”
18Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, laal kaa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, bol bɛl banna yir Gɔb. A saŋaa Husa hinuu Sibɛkai faa kpu Rafa naana bɛl banna yir Saf la.
19Laal bɛl kaa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, Gɔb. A laal naa biinii Jaarɛ Ɔrɛgim biibaal Ɛlhanan n lii Bɛtlihɛm, faa kpu Gaf hinuu Goliaf la kandaa daa n faa gbosse lugɔ kɔɔrɛɛ daa la.
20Denii laal bɛl kaa wa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, Gaf. Bazeŋ bɛl n faa helle kpabaa, di dɔɔ nonibee ani naanibee anumbɛlaa, di ge ɛɛ Rafa naana bɛl, 21ge faa ɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa chɛɛtɛ. Awia, Koori Deevid niwee Simɛya biibaal Jonatan faa lii kpuu.
22Ba nɛra banaazu naabuu faa ɛɛ Rafa naanna, Gaf. Ba maanii Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra faa kpu laal biini.

english_text:
David Sings to the Lord
(Psalm 18.1-50)
1David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
2Our Lord and our God,
you are my mighty rock,
my fortress, my protector.
3You are the rock
where I am safe.
You are my shield,
my powerful weapon,
and my place of shelter.
You rescue me and keep me
safe from violence.
4I praise you, our Lord!
I prayed to you,
and you rescued me
from my enemies.
5Death, like ocean waves,
surrounded me,
and I was almost swallowed
by its flooding waters.
6Ropes from the world
of the dead
had coiled around me,
and death had set a trap
in my path.
7I was in terrible trouble
when I called out to you,
but from your temple
you heard me
and answered my prayer.
8Earth shook and shivered!
The columns supporting the sky
rocked back and forth.
You were angry
9and breathed out smoke.
Scorching heat and fiery flames
spewed from your mouth.
10You opened the heavens
like curtains,
and you came down
with storm clouds
under your feet.
11You rode on the backs
of flying creatures.
You appeared
with the wind as wings.
12Darkness was your tent!
Thunderclouds filled the sky,
hiding you from sight.
13Fiery coals lit up the sky
in front of you.
14 Lord Most High, your voice
thundered from the heavens.
15You scattered your enemies
with arrows of lightning.
16You roared at the sea,
and its deepest channels
could be seen.
You snorted,
and the earth shook
to its foundations.
17You reached down from heaven,
and you lifted me
from deep in the ocean.
18You rescued me from enemies
who were hateful
and too powerful for me.
19On the day disaster struck,
they came and attacked,
but you defended me.
20When I was fenced in,
you freed and rescued me
because you love me.
21You are good to me, Lord,
because I do right,
and you reward me
because I am innocent.
22I do what you want
and never turn to do evil.
23I keep your laws in mind
and never turn away
from your teachings.
24I obey you completely
and guard against sin.
25You have been good to me
because I do right;
you have rewarded me
for being innocent
by your standards.
26You are always loyal
to your loyal people,
and you are faithful
to the faithful.
27With all who are sincere
you are sincere,
but you treat the unfaithful
as their deeds deserve.
28You rescue the humble,
but you look for ways
to put down the proud.
29Our Lord and God,
you are my lamp.
You turn darkness to light.
30You help me defeat armies
and capture cities.
31Your way is perfect, Lord,
and your word is correct.
You are a shield for those
who run to you for help.
32You alone are God!
Only you are a mighty rock.
33You are my strong fortress,
and you set me free.
34 You make my feet run as fast
as those of a deer,
and you help me stand
on the mountains.
35You teach my hands to fight
and my arms to use
a bow of bronze.
36You alone are my shield,
and by coming to help me,
you have made me famous.
37You clear the way for me,
and now I won't stumble.
38I kept chasing my enemies
until I caught them
and destroyed them.
39I destroyed them!
I stuck my sword
through my enemies,
and they were crushed
under my feet.
40You helped me win victories
and forced my attackers
to fall victim to me.
41You made my enemies run,
and I killed them.
42They cried out for help,
but no one saved them;
they called out to you,
but there was no answer.
43I ground them to dust,
and I squashed them
like mud in the streets.
44You rescued me
from my stubborn people
and made me the leader
of foreign nations,
who are now my slaves.
45They obey and come crawling.
46They have lost all courage
and from their fortresses
they come trembling.
47You are the living Lord!
I will praise you!
You are a mighty rock.
I will honor you
for keeping me safe.
48You took revenge for me,
and you put nations
in my power.
49You protected me
from violent enemies,
and you made me much greater
than all of them.
50 I will praise you, Lord,
and I will honor you
among the nations.
51You give glorious victories
to your chosen king.
Your faithful love for David
and for his descendants
will never end.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid n kpegli u dɔma yittɛ keŋ
1Yir naabuu Koori Deevid faa yir tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, dikuu uŋ lɛɛu lii u dɔma maa ni Koori Sɔɔl nonee biini wia.
2A yittɛ keŋ,
“Kɔraawiizii n guuri,
waabuu n kpegzi bɔr.
3Waabuu ra guuŋ,
di n du u be,
n daŋ na n hiŋ.
U ra gberimbuu
lugɔ laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ.
Waabuu n Lɛɛri,
waabuu ra guuŋ
di ra lɛɛŋ nɛra la
n na fir nɛra werge be.
4N yir Kɔraawiizi la n dɛg chɔlaa labuu,
awia, u lɛɛmbuu di lii
n dɔma be.
5Siu faa barimbuu alugɔ muuzeŋ nii n na lɔ,
niikpeg kpeglimbuu.
6Ŋmam ŋmɛnni bɔɔrimbuu,
siu heŋ u sidɛɛzi.
7N biinichɔg biini, n yir Kɔraawiizii,
di lɔ wile tɛu ú hiiniŋ.
U nuu n loobiire lii u Dia biini,
di nuu n wiraa.
8Denii hɛri ziigi di zigli,
chiŋ ge zɛɛzi zigli,
a zigloore dikuu
Kɔraawiizi baaŋ
n fuuhwe wia!
9Nyɔɔzi faa ra lii u miibɔɔni,
ninlau n na di kuna
ra lii u nua,
niŋhɔla ge ta
di ra lii de.
10U peri chiŋ di tuu ba,
baama biŋŋu du
u naazi zɛɛ.
11U tinni chɛrubzi di ra zaah,
di so peu keeri ni
di ra kaali.
12U kpa bɔbirii tɔ u hiŋ,
baama biŋŋe
n dɔɔ nii werge baruu.
13Di lii u chachaaŋ la biini,
dooŋ pogzi,
di ra nyɛgzi.
14Kɔraawiizi pozoore alugɔ dooŋ di lii chiŋ,
ba nuu Kɔraawiizi La N
Kaali Kummaa la loobii.
15U taazi u hobeere, u dɔma yaari,
u kpa nazaa
di gil ba ra chɔ.
16Muuzeŋ zɛɛ lii chɔɔ.
Hɛri zɛɛzi ge
maa chɔɔ pɛɛ,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi n nyɛgi u dɔma ni,
di kpa baaŋfuuih
di ra pogzi ba ni wia.
17U lii chinne tuu di wa lawiŋ,
di tɛriŋ lii niivile biini.
18U lɛɛmbuu lii n dɔma n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la be,
di lɛɛŋ lii n haahra la
n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge
kaaliŋ la be.
19Ba faa fɔɔmbuu saŋa la min du siaahmu biini la,
ka Kɔraawiizi faa lɛɛŋ.
20U lɛɛmbuu lii siaahmu biini,
dikuu n wia
n paruu wia.
21Kɔraawiizi turgimbuu dikuu n wideŋlaa ɛɛi wia.
U kissimbuu dikuu
miŋ waa wichɔgii
maa ɛɛwɛ wia.
22N hiŋ Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnizii,
maa wichɔgaa ɛɛwɛ,
di bir har kpu
Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la.
23U Gbɔgni maanii n hiŋ.
Maa u widaulaa la
ge vɛɛwɛ ta.
24Maa wichɔgii maa dɔɔwɛ u be,
n ɔɔ lizi n hinnɛ
di lii wichɔgaa
maa biini.
25Kɔraawiizi turgimbuu dikuu n wideŋlaa ɛɛi
ni miŋ waa wichɔgii
maa dɔɔwɛ wia.
26I wia dɔɔ wibiire tɛɛ
banla wia n dɔɔ wibii.
I wia ge du wer tɛɛ
banla n waa
wichɔgii maa dɔɔwɛ.
27I dɔɔ biinihuŋŋuu tɛɛ banla n dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu,
ka hah banla
n ɛɛ biinikpola hina.
28I ra lɛɛ banla n dɔɔ sisɔnaa,
ka gil banla
n na jigsi la ra tuu zɛɛ.
29N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ n fintina
di ra chaaniŋ,
di gil n bɔbiri
birgi bɔchaaŋ.
30Hinuu tɛŋ fɔŋŋa n lɔ n dɔma
di kpegli baa.
31Kɔraawiiziwaa, u ŋmɛnizi maanii deŋlee.
U ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ
tɛɛ banla maa
n na nyiŋŋi ú guu baa.
32Anɛɛ n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di u bɛŋ lɛiyɛi?
U bɛnnɛ ɛɛ yaa guuri.
33Kɔraawiizi tɛmbuu fɔŋŋa,
di gil n ŋmɛnɛɛ chaani.
34U gillɔɔ n naazi ɛɛ lugɔ weema naazi,
u ɔɔ giluu n chi
bizenaa nyuuni
di na n hiŋ.
35U ra baglimbuu laal lɔi,
ń ɔɔ wer ta hoo la gba
n kpekke werge.
36N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i guumbuu di lɛɛŋ,
n ni binnaa la gillɔɔ
n du kpeg,
i hiinaa gillɔɔ n dɔɔ sɔŋ.
37I kuari ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ u du war tɛŋ,
guŋ gil n gilɛɛ
waa lɔ naa.
38N duŋŋi n dɔmaa di ga kpegli baa.
Maa har bittɛ,
di miŋ wa chɔgi baa
tuŋ la lɛi.
39N lɔ baabuu ta hɛri, ba waa kaa wer bá izi,
ba chɔɔgi n naazi zɛɛ.
40I tɛmbuu fɔŋŋa nɛnnɛ, n lɔ laal
di kpegli n dɔma.
41I gillɔɔ n dɔma chɔ lii n be,
n chɔgi n haahra.
42Ba lɔ wilee di ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa, ka nɛr maa waa baa lɛɛwɛ,
di lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi,
ka waa nuuwɛ
tɛɛ baa.
43N nam baabuu ba ɛɛ lugɔ nyɔɔ.
N na fɛrgi baabuu
alugɔ kpɛchɛgaa
n chɔɔ ŋmɛnizenaa.
44I lɛɛmbuu lii nɛkpoŋlaa be,
di gil n ɛɛ
hɛssi maa koori.
Nɛra la maa
miŋ faa waa zummɛ
jaa birgi n balaarɛ.
45Di ba haŋ wa nuu n wiŋɔzi, ba ɔɔ sɛɛ n dɔɔraa,
hɔɔhra ɔɔ giŋŋi n see.
46Ba maa bɔra huahwɔɔ,
ba lii ba diikpega ba,
ba bɔra ra sa.
47Kɔraawiizi du denii! Ií ra chɔli n Lɛɛrikpeg!
Ií ra sii Kɔraawiizi la
n kpekke,
di lɛɛŋ la zenni.
48U ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n na lɛɛ n nuarɛ,
u gillɔɔ hɛssi hina
ra sɛɛ n dɔɔra,
49di lɛɛŋ lii n dɔma be.
I gillɔɔ n kpegli n dɔma,
di lɛɛŋ lii
nɛchɔgaa be.
50N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
awia, n daŋ chɔlii
hɛssi maa hina be.
N daŋ yir yira
di ra dargii.
51U gillɔɔ u koori du kpeg,
di bagli u nɔŋŋaa la
n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la,
