di ra tɛɛ unla baŋ waari nuu
di lizi la,
di ra tɛɛ Koori Deevid
ni u naanna
saŋaa saŋa maa.”

english_text:
David's Last Words
1These are the last words of David the son of Jesse.
The God of Jacob chose David
and made him a great king.
The Mighty God of Israel
loved him.
When God told him to speak,
David said:
2The Spirit of the Lord
has told me what to say.
3Our Mighty Rock,
the God of Jacob, told me,
“A ruler who obeys God
and does right
4is like the sunrise
on a cloudless day,
or like rain that sparkles
on the grass.”
5I have ruled this way,
and God will never break
his promise to me.
God's promise is complete
and unchanging;
he will always help me
and give me what I hope for.
6But evil people are pulled up
like thornbushes.
They are not dug up by hand,
7but with a sharp spear
and are burned on the spot.
The Three Warriors
(1 Chronicles 11.10-19)
8These are the names of David's warriors:
Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed 800 men with his spear.
9The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran, 10except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
11Next was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. One time the Philistines brought their army together to destroy a crop of peas growing in a field near Lehi. The rest of Israel's soldiers ran away from the Philistines, 12but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
13One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley 14and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress, 15and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
16The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice 17and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.”
The Three Warriors did these brave deeds.
The Thirty Warriors
(1 Chronicles 11.20-47)
18Joab's brother Abishai was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and in one battle he killed 300 men with his spear. He was as famous as the Three Warriors 19and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
20Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion. 21Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it. 22-23Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
24-39Some of the Thirty Warriors were:
Asahel the brother of Joab
Elhanan the son of Dodo from Bethlehem
Shammah from Harod
Elika from Harod
Helez the Paltite
Ira the son of Ikkesh from Tekoa
Abiezer from Anathoth
Mebunnai the Hushathite
Zalmon the Ahohite
Maharai from Netophah
Heleb the son of Baanah from Netophah
Ittai the son of Ribai from Gibeah of the tribe of Benjamin
Benaiah from Pirathon
Hiddai from the streams on Mount Gaash
Abialbon from Beth-Arabah
Azmaveth from Bahurim
Eliahba from Shaalbon
Jashen
Jonathan the son of Shammah the Hararite
Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite
Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai from Maacah
Eliam the son of Ahithophel from Gilo
Hezro from Carmel
Paarai the Arbite
Igal the son of Nathan from Zobah
Bani the Gadite
Zelek from Ammon
Naharai from Beeroth, who carried the weapons of Joab the son of Zeruiah
Ira the Ithrite
Gareb the Ithrite
Uriah the Hittite
There were 37 in all.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid wiŋɔtuna wia
1Jɛssɛ biibaal Koori Deevidii, baal la Kɔraawiizi n faa gillɛ u ɛɛ nɛzeŋ. Waabuu Kɔraawiizi la Jekɔb n faa ra hum la lizi ú ɛɛ koori. U faa kaa ɛɛ Izrɛl hina yirsuma yittii. Koori Deevid wiŋɔzi tunaa keŋ.
2“Kɔraawiizi Duma ga n ninɛɛ di ra ŋɔ wia,
u wiŋɔzi du n nuarɛ.
3Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
Izrɛl hina Bizeŋ ŋɔ n benii,
‘Koori la n na
binni nɛra ni wibii,
di kpa Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa
di ra binni baa,
4u ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baama n waa hoo,
wiizi ra fur chɔɔzi ni,
wiizi ɔɔ gil kooree ra nyɛgzi,
di dooŋ wa chaazɔɔ.’
5Gunnɛ Kɔ́raawiizi kissi n naanna,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n nuu
ɛɛ nuukpaŋ la
n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛɛ.
Nuukpaŋ la n waa chɔgaa dɔɔwɛ,
nuuŋɔɔlii la
n waa biraa dɔɔwɛ.
N winyiŋŋii maanii guŋ.
Gunnɛ niŋ gil
n na kunla minna tami.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil
guŋ ɛɛ wibii maa.
6Ka ba daŋ kpa wichɔgɛɛra
ha lugɔ sɔɔhri,
ba wàá wer kpa
nodumazi gbɔgzaa la.
7Nɛr la maa n niŋ gbɔgzaa,
see u kpa lugbii kuŋkuarii
gɛɛ kandaa.
Ba daŋ fuuah nyaamm.”
Koori Deevid laallɔkpega wia
8Koori Deevid laallɔkpega la sɔnaa keŋ, Takɛmɔn hinuu Jɔsɛb Basɛbɛf, waabuu faa Laallɔkpega Bahoro la sitɔɔri. U faa kpa u kandaarɛ kpu nɛra kalfa ŋmantannaazi, laalkpaŋ biini.
9Unla n faa hiŋ u ni genii Ahɔ domee hinuu Dɔdai biibaal Ɛliaza. U faa ɛɛ ba laallɔkpega bahoro la bɛllɛ. A hɔl bɛl, u ni Koori Deevid faa karsi Filisti hina n chaali yembɛl banna yir Pas Damim, bá lɔ laal, ka Izrɛl hina faa bir chɔ, 10ka Ɛliaza waa faa chi de chigigi, di yoo a Filisti hina guŋŋ u nonii wa sɔm dar, waa kaa wer ú kpa u tokobi tɔɔh nɛr gba. A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi faa lɔ laal di kpegli Filisti hina werge. A laal n wa tunnɛ, Izrɛl laallɔɔra la bir ba bɔr la Ɛliaza n duwɛɛ la, di wa wir a lalaa laal kuna.
11Horohiŋ genii Agii biibaal Samma n lii yembɛl banna yir Harar. A saŋa, di Filisti laallɔɔra kaa chaali Lɛhi, bɔr la siga n suwee biini. Izrɛl laallɔɔra chɔ, 12ka Samma waa faa chi a koo baaŋ chigigi, di yoo Filisti hina la, di kpu baa. Kɔraawiizi faa gil ba kpegli baa nɛnnɛ.
13Kuna kumaa saŋa n wa helle, laallɔkpega tokko ni kpɔrgɔ la bahoro, faa tuu ba Koori Deevid be, Adulam bii bɔɔ, di Filisti laallɔɔra suge bɛl faa chɔɔ Rɛfam Waluu biini. 14A saŋa hiŋ, di Koori Deevid faa du diikpeg biini, ka Filisti laallɔɔra suge bɛl wa chɔɔ Bɛtlihɛm. 15Denii niinyɔgzi wa lau Koori Deevid werge maa, u ŋɔ, “N bɔra daŋ vii sɔɔni, di nɛbɛl vii la kɔlɔŋ la n dugli Bɛtlihɛm dominuuzeŋ la, di ga ɛɛ nii wa tɛŋ ń nyɔɔ!” 16Denii a laallɔkpega bahoro la izi, di peri Filisti laallɔɔra la baaŋ, di la a kɔlɔŋ di ga ɛɛ nii wa tɛɛ Koori Deevid, ka u vɛɛ a nyɔɔi, ka bizaa ta hɛri tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, 17ka ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, màá wer nyɔɔa! A daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ baala naa n tulmee naa challɛ n na nyɔɔ gunla!” Awia, u vɛɛ a nyɔɔi.
Wizenaa naabuu laallɔkpega bahoro naa faa ɛɛ.
18Joab niwee Abisairɛ faa ɛɛ a Laallɔkpega Tokko Ni Kpɔrgɔ La N Faa Dɔɔ Sɔŋ la sitɔɔri. U maarɛ faa Zɛruya. U faa kpa u kandaarɛ di kpu laallɔɔra kalfaahoro, di jaa dɔɔ sɔŋ werge ba biini. 19Waabuu ba faa ra tɔgzi werge kaali Bahoro la. Awia, u faa jaa ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri, haali uŋ faa waa ba ni jaawɛ gba.
20Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya n lii bolzeŋ Kabziil ge faa ɛɛ laallɔkpega la bɛllɛ. U ge gba faa ɛɛ wizenaare, di kpu Moab hina laallɔkpega banɛɛ. U faa ga tuu bɔɔ bɛllɛ waari hɔpizii, di kpu bunyiŋ.
21U faa kaa kpu Ijip hinuu bɛl n helle kpabaa. Haali a Ijip hinuu n kpogli kandaa gba, ka Bɛnaaya faa kpa guliire lɔu, ka foozi u kandaa hiŋ, di kpuu. 22Bɛnaaya gba faa dɔɔ sɔnnɛ, alugɔ Laallɔkpega Bahoro La. Wizenaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛɛ guŋ. 23Waabuu ba faa ra tɔgzi werge kaali Laallɔkpega Tokko Ni Kpɔrgɔ la bɛl maa, ka u faa waa Laallɔkpega Bahoro La ni jaawɛ. Koori Deevid jaa gil u ɛɛ u guure nabɔma.
24Banla n kaa jaa a Laallɔkpega Tokko Ni Kpɔrgɔ ninɛɛ keŋ,
Joab niwee Asahɛl ani Dɔdɔ biibaal Ɛlhanan n lii Bɛtlihɛm,
25Harɔd hina Samma,
ni Ɛlika,
26Pɛlɛt hinuu Hɛlɛz,
Ikɛs biibaal Ira n lii Tɛkua,
27Abiɛza n lii Anatɔf,
Husa hinuu Mɛbunai,
28Ahɔ hinuu Zalmɔn,
Nɛtɔfaf hina Maharai
29ni Baana biibaal Hɛlɛd,
Ribai biibaal Itai n lii Gibia n du Bɛnjamin,
30Piratɔn hinuu Bɛnaaya,
Hidai n lii Gaas faalime biine,
31Aaba hinuu Abi Albɔn,
Baahum hinuu Azmavɛf,
32Saalbɔn hinuu Ɛliaba,
Jasɛn biibaala,
Jonatan 33n ɛɛ Harar hinuu Sama biibaal,
Harar hinuu Saraa biibaal Ahiam,
34Maaka hinuu Ahasbai biibaal Ɛlifɛlɛt,
Gilo hinuu Ahitɔfɛl biibaal Ɛliam,
35Kamɛl hinuu Hɛzrɔ,
Aabai hinuu Paarai,
36Netan biibaal Igal n lii Zoba,
u naabaal ɛɛ Hagri,
37Ammɔn hinuu Zɛlɛk,
Bɛɛrɔf hinuu Naharai la n faa ra kpogli Zɛruya biibaal Joab laal kuna,
38Ira ni Garɛb n ɛɛ Itri hina,
39Hitti hinuu Yuria.
Ba maa faa du laallɔɔra tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni baniidaanɛɛ.

english_text:
David Counts the People
(1 Chronicles 21.1-6)
1The Lord was angry with Israel again, and he made David think it would be a good idea to count the people in Israel and Judah. 2So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
3Joab answered, “I hope the Lord your God will give you 100 times more soldiers than you already have. I hope you will live to see that day! But why do you want to do a thing like this?”
4But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people. 5They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer. 6They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon. 7They came to the fortress of Tyre, then went through every town of the Hivites and the Canaanites. Finally, they went to Beersheba in the Southern Desert of Judah. 8After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them 9 months and 20 days.
9Joab came and told David, “In Israel there are 800,000 who can serve in the army, and in Judah there are 500,000.”
The Lord Punishes David
(1 Chronicles 21.7-17)
10After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
11Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad 12-13to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him:
You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
14David was really frightened and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
15-16So that morning, the Lord sent an angel to spread a horrible disease everywhere in Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. And before it was over, 70,000 people had died.
When the angel was about to destroy Jerusalem, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused and told the angel, “That's enough! Don't touch them.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
17David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!”
David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place
(1 Chronicles 21.18—22.1)
18-19That same day the prophet Gad came and told David, “Go to the threshing place that belongs to Araunah and build an altar there for the Lord.”
So David went.
20Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low, 21and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?”
David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
22Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire. 23Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
24But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for 50 pieces of silver. 25Then he built an altar for the Lord. He offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings.
The Lord answered the prayers of the people, and no one else died from the terrible disease.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid n kur u laallɔɔra wia
1Kɔraawiizi baaŋ kaa fuuh Izrɛl hina ni werge maa. U gil Koori Deevid kpa tɔɔrɔɔ ta ba ni. Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “La ga kur Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa.” 2Awia, Koori Deevid ŋɔ Joab ni u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi be, “Ií la ga kur Izrɛl hina la maa n hel laal lɔi, di lii bolzeŋ Dan di ga hel bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba. N na nyiŋŋuu ń zum ba maga.”
3Ka Joab ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Jara, Kɔ́raawiizi la hinna hum la gil Izrɛl laallɔɔra wazi naa bukalfa, di kaali kennaa baŋ makkɛ naa, i siwii na. Jara, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi i ɛɛ a wii naanɛi?” 4Ka Koori Deevid faa waa nuuwɛ tɛɛ Joab ni u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi. Awia, ba faa lii a koori be bá ga kur Izrɛl laallɔɔra.
5Ba jaa ga gi Jɔɔdan muu di ga chɔɔ dugli Aroa wiifurii nodig wiikakag bolzeŋ la n du a waluu baambaaŋ, Gad hɛri la. Ba lii de la Jaza n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, 6di kpa ga hel Giliad hɛri di ga lii bolzeŋ Kadɛs n du Hitti hina hɛri la. Ba kaa lii de la Dan, di ga wiicholii ga hel bolzeŋ Saidɔn. 7Denii ba ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di la bolkpeg Taaya, guŋŋ di ga hel Hivi ni Keenan hina bola. A tuna maa, ba ga hel bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba n du Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma la. 8Baaguzi kabɛl ni hɔpizaa tokkoo ba faa kpa gaagi a hɛri maa, ka bir ba Jɛrusalɛm, 9di wa bagli baala la n niŋ wer lɔ laal maga tɛɛ Koori Deevid. Baala la n lii Izrɛl faa du kagboŋa kalfa ŋmantannaazi, Juda ge, baala kagboŋa kalfaanue.
10Koori Deevid n wa kur a baala tuŋ, u biini chɔgi werge, u ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa dikuu wii naa miŋ ɛɛwɛ naa wia! Gaafura, gil mìŋ́ i balii wichɔgaa tɛŋ. N ɛɛ gɛnni wiarɛ werge.”
11Mɔɔ ka Koori Deevid izi chɔɔl chɔɔzi ni, di Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u dɔgtɛɛ Gad la n faa ɛɛ Koori Deevid sinaari la be, 12“La ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, dí kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘N na tɛibuu wia ahoro. Lizi bɛl, ń gil u huuzii.’ ” 13Awia, Gad la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ u be gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la, di pɛɛzuu, “Ú bɛliirɛ í lizɛi? Lɔzi chol i hɛri binni ahoro gɛɛ i kpa baaguzi ahoro di chɔ ra lii i dɔma be gɛɛ wiilchɔgii chol i hɛri naa hɔpizaa ahoroi? Awia, fɛ nfɛrɛ ka ŋɔ n be gunla min niŋ ga ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be.”
14Koori Deevid ŋɔ Gad be, “N biini chɔkkɔɔ werge maa! Gil Kɔraawiizi tɛr yaa digna, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nɛsunaa kannɔɔ werge maa, gilɛɛ gil newea tɛr n digni.” 15Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa gil wiilchɔgii chol Izrɛl hɛri, di lii a hɔl hiŋ chɔɔzi ni di ga hel saŋa la uŋ baglɛɛ la. Di chi a hɛri tuna bɛl di ga hel bɛl, nɛra kagboŋa tokkoahoro ni fii siuwɛ. 16Saŋa la a mɛlika n waa nyiŋŋi u chɔgi Jɛrusalɛm la, Kɔraawiizi biini kaa chɔgi, dikuu a tɔɔrɔɔzeŋ wia, u ŋɔ a mɛlika be, “Gil guŋ! A kukkɔɔrɛ!” A guŋ saŋa, di a mɛlika chigɔ Jɛbus hinuu Arauna pila.
17Koori Deevid n wa na a mɛlika n na kpuuzi a nɛra la, u ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Minuu ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Bannii waa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ peeza. Bɛɛ ba ɛɛi? Tɛr n ni n diahina digna.”
18A hɔl hiŋ, Gad la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ, “Izi tinni la Jɛbus hinuu Arauna pila, di ga ma mbusu lizibɔr de tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.” 19Awia, Koori Deevid faa hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, di ɛɛ gunla Gad n ŋɔ u be la. 20Arauna n wa na a koori ni u nabɔnzi n na ba, u la ga giŋŋi u see di willi, u hile ga gbɔgzi hɛri, 21ka ŋɔ, “Jara, asummua?”
Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “I pila naabuu n na nyiŋŋi ń yau, di ma mbusu lizibɔr tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Aŋhinabe, a wiilchɔgii naa daŋ tuŋ.”
22Arauna ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Jara, kpa kunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi di lizi mbusu. Navargazii keŋ, kpaa lizi mbusu di fuuah. Milɔɔri daazi ni a nabala baŋaa daazii keŋ, bá kpa chem niŋ.” 23Arauna kpa a maa tɛɛ Koori Deevid, ka ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi la hinna hum la lɛɛ i kuaraa hiŋ.”
24Ka Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Akai, n daŋ turgaa. Màá lizi mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la miŋ waa u kim lɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la.”
Awia, u yau a pila ani a navargazi, saliŋhuŋŋu kebisau tokkoanɛɛ ni fi. 25Denii Koori Deevid ma mbusu lizibɔr de tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi. Kɔraawiizi nuu u wiisuŋŋaa, a wiilchɔgii tuŋ Izrɛl hɛri.

english_text:
David in His Old Age
1King David was now an old man, and he always felt cold, even under a lot of blankets. 2His officials said, “Your Majesty, we will look for a young woman to take care of you. She can lie down beside you and keep you warm.” 3-4They looked everywhere in Israel until they found a very beautiful young woman named Abishag, who lived in the town of Shunem. They brought her to David, and she took care of him. But David did not have sex with her.
Adonijah Tries To Become King
5-6 Adonijah was the son of David and Haggith. He was Absalom's younger brother and was very handsome. One day, Adonijah started bragging, “I'm going to make myself king!” So he got some chariots and horses, and he hired 50 men as bodyguards. David did not want to hurt his feelings, so he never asked Adonijah why he was doing these things.
7Adonijah met with Joab the son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest and asked them if they would help him become king. Both of them agreed to help. 8But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's bodyguards all refused.
9Adonijah invited his brothers and David's officials from Judah to go with him to Crawling Rock near Rogel Spring, where he sacrificed some sheep, cattle, and fat calves. 10But he did not invite Nathan, Benaiah, David's bodyguards, or his own brother Solomon.
11 When Nathan heard what had happened, he asked Bathsheba, Solomon's mother:
Have you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has made himself king? But David doesn't know a thing about it. 12You and your son Solomon will be killed, unless you do what I tell you. 13Go say to David, “You promised me that Solomon would be the next king. So why is Adonijah now king?”
14While you are still talking to David, I'll come in and tell him that everything you said is true.
15Meanwhile, David was in his bedroom where Abishag was taking care of him because he was so old. Bathsheba went in 16and bowed down.
“What can I do for you?” David asked.
17Bathsheba answered:
Your Majesty, you promised me in the name of the Lord your God that my son Solomon would be the next king. 18But Adonijah has already been made king, and you didn't know anything about it. 19He sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. And he invited Abiathar the priest, Joab your army commander, and all your sons to be there, except Solomon, your loyal servant.
20Your Majesty, everyone in Israel is waiting for you to announce who will be the next king. 21If you don't, they will say that Solomon and I have rebelled. They will treat us like criminals and kill us as soon as you die.
22Just then, Nathan the prophet arrived. 23Someone told David that he was there, and Nathan came in. He bowed with his face to the ground 24and said:
Your Majesty, did you say that Adonijah would be king? 25Earlier today, he sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. He invited the army commanders, Abiathar, and all your sons to be there. They are already eating and drinking and shouting, “Long live King Adonijah!” 26But he didn't invite me or Zadok the priest or Benaiah or Solomon. 27Did you say they could do this without telling the rest of us who would be the next king?
Solomon Becomes King
28David said, “Tell Bathsheba to come here.” She came and stood in front of him. 29-30Then he said, “The living Lord God of Israel has kept me safe. And so today, I will keep the promise I made to you in his name: Solomon will be the next king!”
31Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and said, “Your Majesty, I pray that you will live a long time!”
32Then David said, “Tell Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to come here.”
When they arrived, 33he told them:
Take along some of my officials and let Solomon ride my own mule to Gihon Spring. 34When you get there, Zadok and Nathan will pour olive oil over Solomon's head to show that he is the new king of Israel. Then order someone to blow a trumpet and tell everyone to shout, “Long live King Solomon!” 35Bring him back here, and he will take my place as king. He is the one I have chosen to rule Israel and Judah.
36Benaiah answered, “We will do it, Your Majesty. I pray that the Lord your God will let it happen. 37The Lord has always watched over you, and I pray that he will now watch over Solomon. May the Lord help Solomon to be an even greater king than you.”
38Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah left and took along the two groups of David's special bodyguards. Solomon rode on David's mule as they led him to Gihon Spring. 39Zadok the priest brought some olive oil from the sacred tent and poured it on Solomon's head to show that he was now king. A trumpet was blown and everyone shouted, “Long live King Solomon!” 40Then they played flutes and celebrated as they followed Solomon back to Jerusalem. They made so much noise that the ground shook.
41Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
42Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
43Jonathan answered:
No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king. 44-45Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city. 46Solomon is now king.
47And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!”
David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed 48and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
49Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could. 50Adonijah himself was afraid of what Solomon might do to him, so he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
51Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
52Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.” 53Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah.
After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_text:
Adonija n tɔ u hiŋ kora wia
1Saŋa la Koori Deevid n wa zɛŋŋɛ werge, waari ɔɔ faa ra kpuubuu, haali baŋ ɔɔ faa kpa kita di tɔu gba. 2Awia, u balaa ŋɔ u be, “Jara, gil ya nyiŋŋi toloori la n haa waa baal zummɛ, ú du i be di ra binni i ni. U daŋ ɔɔ chɔɔ i kɛra, di gil i bɔra ra wenzi.”
3Denii ba faa gaagi Izrɛl hɛri maa guŋŋ di ra nyiŋŋi toloonanii, di jaa wa na toloori bɛl banna yir Abisag. U faa ɛɛ Sunɛm hinuurɛ. Ba kpau wa tɛɛ a koori. 4A biihaaŋ naa faa ɛɛ toloorii werge maa. U faa ra du a koori tau, di ra chɔɔ u be. Ka a koori nuu faa waa dɔŋa nyiŋŋee.
5A saŋa hiŋ, Koori Deevid haaŋ Hagif biibaal Adonija faa lizi u hiŋ, di ŋɔ, “N daŋ birgi koori.” Awia, u faa nyiŋŋi zagra ni a torkozi, di ɛɛa sirya, di nyiŋŋi baala tokkoanɛɛ ni fi la n niŋ tɔ u see di jaa. 6U mɛɛ ŋmɛnɛ maa faa haa wɔɔ hagzɛɛ ú wiɛɛlaa wia maa, di pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra ɛɛ kennei?” Adonija gba faa ɛɛ bunɔɔnnɛ werge maa, di faa ɛɛ Koori Deevid biibaala nabɔnnɛɛhiŋ, di ra hiŋ Absalɔm ni. 7U faa na Zɛruya biibaal Joab ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata, ba sɛɛ tɛu. 8Ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk, Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan, Simei, Rei ani laallɔɔra la n na guu Koori Deevid la waa maa faa waa Adonija harbɔɔ chigɛ.
9A hɔl bɛl, Adonija kpa peeza, nauna ani napɔla la n vuhwɛɛ nɛnnɛ, di lizi mbusu Zɔhɛlɛf bii la n dugli Ɛn Rɔgɛl bule la nyuu. U faa yirgi u niuna la n ɛɛ kooribiibaala ani Juda baala la n faa ɛɛ koori nabɔnzi maanii. 10Ka u faa waa Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan gɛɛ Bɛnaaya gɛɛ laallɔɔra la n na guu koori ani u niwee Solomɔn waa yittɛ.
11Denii Netan jaa pɛɛzi Solomɔn maa Batsiiba, “Haa nuuwɛ lugɔ Hagif biibaal Adonija birgi koorii, di yaa dɔɔri Koori Deevid waa zummɛa? 12Awia, gil n baglii filaŋkeŋ gunla hin niŋ ɛɛ lɛɛ i ni i biibaal Solomɔn maa miibɔɔni. 13La ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, ‘Jara, haa hɛɛhzɛɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ i balii lugɔ wibii maa, i biibaal Solomɔnnɛ niŋ kpa i gawa di so i koorikara nii? Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Adonija birgi koorei?’ 14I daŋ haa du denii di ra ŋɔ a wia, ka mìŋ́ Netan jaa wa zuu di sɛɛ jaai lugɔ wibiire i ra ŋɔ.”
15Awia, Batsiiba jaa zuu ú ga na a koorizɛŋa u dia biini, bɔr la Sunɛm hinuu Abisag n na du u tau la. 16Denii Batsiiba jaa ga giŋŋi a koori see. A koori pɛɛzuu, “Beedee i ra nyiŋŋei?”
17U ŋɔ u be, “Jara, i kpa Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la sɔnnɛ hɛɛhzi tɛɛ mìŋ́ i balii, di ŋɔ lugɔ n biibaal Solomɔnnɛ niŋ kpa i gawa di so i koorikara ni. 18Ka Adonija birgi koorii filaŋkeŋ, di hìŋ́ Jara waa zummɛ. 19U kpa nakpila ni napɔla la n vuhwɛɛ nɛnnɛ ani peezaa, di yir i biibaala maa, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata ani laallɔɔra nabɔma Joab, ba chaali, u lizi mbusu, ka waa i biibaal Solomɔn waa yittɛ. 20Jara, Izrɛl hina maa ra binni i siweere, bá zum lii i be, nɛr la n niŋ kpa i gawa di di kora, di i wa siuwɔ. 21Di guŋ lɛi, ka hìŋ́ Jara wa kaalɔɔ di ga chɔɔ i naabaala be, ba daŋ yir n ni n biibaal Solomɔn nɛchɔgaa, di tɔɔri yaa.”
22Batsiiba faa haa ra ŋɔ a wiarɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan wa zuu. 23Ba ŋɔ a koori be, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan ballɔɔ.” Netan jaa la ga togni a koori see di jaamuu.
24Uŋ wa jaamuu tuŋ, u ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri koori! Hinuu tɛɛ nua lugɔ Adonija kpa i gawa di so i kara ni gɛɛ? 25Zinaa, u kpa nabalkpila, napɔla la n vuhwɛɛ nɛnnɛ ani peezaa lizi mbusu, di yirgi i biibaala maa ni i laallɔɔra nabɔma Joab ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata. Haali filaŋkeŋ gba, u ni baa haa ra di a diuzenaare, di ra nyɔɔ, ka ra ŋɔ, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ Koori Adonija miibɔɔjaŋ!’ 26Ama, waa mìŋ́ i balii ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk, Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya ani i biibaal Solomɔn waa yittɛ. 27Amɔ, kenne Jara ɛɛ, di waa gillɛ u balaa zum nɛr la n niŋ kpa u gawa di di kora, di so u koorikara nii?”
Koori Deevid n tɔ Solomɔn kora wia
28Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Ií yir Batsiiba ú ba.” Ba yiruu, u zuu wa chi a koori see.
29A koori ja hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la n lɛɛŋ lii tɔɔrɔɔ maa biini la sɔŋ biini, 30wibii maa, n daŋ ɛɛ zinaa gunla miŋ faa kpa Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la sɔŋ, di hɛɛhzi tɛi lugɔ i biibaal Solomɔnnɛ niŋ kpa n gawa, di so n kara ni la, gunnɛ niŋ ɛɛ.”
31Denii Batsiiba jaa giŋŋi hɛri jaamuu, ka ŋɔ, “Jara, Kɔ́raawiizi tɛi miibɔɔjaŋ!”
32Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Ií yir Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan ani Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya, bá ba.” Baŋ wa ballɛ, 33u ŋɔ ba be, “Ií lau n balaa jaa iihinaa ni, di gil n biibaal Solomɔn tinni n himmaa kawee la, ií kpogluu la Gihɔn bule. 34Di ii ga hel de, ií gil Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk ani Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan fug nuu waari Solomɔn nyuu, di tɔu Izrɛl kora. Denii ií huuh bensuno, ka chaasi di ŋɔ, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ Koori Solomɔn miibɔɔjaŋ!’ 35Denii ií nuu bir ba n be, ú wa so n koorikara ni, di kpa n gawa, di ra binni a hɛri. Waabuu n lizi ú ɛɛ Izrɛl ni Juda hina koori.”
36Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya jaa sɛɛ a koori be, di ŋɔ, “Ami! Kɔ́raawiizi la Jara n na hum la gil guŋ ɛɛ. 37Gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa du hìŋ́ Jara be la, ú du Koori Solomɔn ge be guŋ, di gil ú kora nyɛɛli kaali i hor!”
38Awia, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan, Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya, Kɛrɛf ani Pɛlɛf hina maa ga kpa Solomɔn soŋŋi u mɛɛ Koori Deevid himmaa kawee ni, di kpogluu la Gihɔn bule. 39Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk la faa ga kpa nyigaa bɛl n su ɔlivi nuu, lii Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la biini, di fug waari Solomɔn nyuu. Ka ba jaa huuh bensunoniina, a nɛra ra chaasi di ra ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ Koori Solomɔn miibɔɔjaŋ!” 40Denii a nɛra maa faa hiŋuu di ra ba, di ra huuh kaloopeezi, di ra sa ani bɔsɔna werge maa, haali ba kɔɔi gil hɛri zigli.
41Adonija ni banla maa uŋ faa yittɛ, di diuzenaa la di ra tuŋ, nuu a kɔɔi. Joab n wa nuu a bensunoniina wiraa la, u pɛɛzi, “Kɔɔi naa zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ, a bolzeŋ biinei?”
42Uŋ faa haa ra ŋɔ a wia la, di Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata biibaal Jonatan wa zuuwɔ. Denii Adonija ŋɔ u be, “Zuu ba! I ɛɛ wibii hinnɛ, awia, i ba amaniyesuma ninɛɛ.”
43Jonatan bir ŋɔ, “Akai! Yaa dɔɔri Koori Deevid tɔ Solomɔnnɛ kora. 44Koori Deevid hum Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan, Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya, Kɛrɛf ani Pɛlɛf hina maanii, di gil ba kpau soŋŋi koori himmaa kawee ni. 45Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk ni Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan ga fug nuurɛ waari u nyuu, di tɔu kora Gihɔn bule. Denii ba lii di ba a bolzeŋ biini, di ra yir yira ni bɔsɔna, di ra chaasi la. Haali a bol biini maa ra zigli. Ba kɔɔi hinnɛ ii ra nuu la. 46Haali, Koori Solomɔn teŋ ga sogo koorikara la ninɛɛ. 47Di kaa kpa jaa, koori nabɔnzi gba maa ballɔɔ di waa jaami Koori Deevid, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi la hinna hum la gil Solomɔn sɔŋ kaali i sɔŋ, di gil ú kora ge du tɔg kaali i hor!’ Denii Koori Deevid willi u nyuu di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi, ú kunchɔɔrikuna ni, 48di ra ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum dɛg chɔlaarɛ. U gillɔɔ n siwii na nɛr la n niŋ so n koorikara ni zinaa.’ ”
49Nɛra la Adonija n faa yittɛ la n wa nuu guŋ, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa, ba maa izi yaari. 50Adonija n faa ra ɔm Koori Solomɔn wia, u faa la ga lau mbusu lizibɔr la nyigzi kpogli. 51Denii ba ŋɔ Koori Solomɔn be, “Adonija ra ɔmiibuu, dikuu guŋ wia, u laŋŋɔɔ ga lau mbusu lizibɔr nyigzi la kpogli. U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Gil Koori Solomɔn hɛɛhzi tɛŋ zinaa lugɔ wàá sɛɛ kpu mìŋ́ u balii.’ ”
52Awia, Koori Solomɔn bir ŋɔ, “Di u wa ɛɛ wibii hiŋ, u nyuhuŋ gba wàá chol hɛri, ka di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ siu.” 53Denii Koori Solomɔn faa hum nɛra, ba ga kpogli Adonija lii mbusu lizibɔr ba. U wa togni Koori Solomɔn. A koori faa ŋɔ u be, “Izi di ra la i dia.”

english_text:
David's Instructions to Solomon
1Not long before David died, he told Solomon:
2My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave. 3Do what the Lord your God commands and follow his teachings. Obey everything written in the Law of Moses. Then you will be a success, no matter what you do or where you go. 4You and your descendants must always faithfully obey the Lord. If you do, he will keep the solemn promise he made to me that someone from our family will always be king of Israel.
5 Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him 6in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
7 The sons of Barzillai from Gilead helped me when I was running from your brother Absalom. Be kind to them and let them eat at your table.
8 Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him. 9Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed.
David Dies
10-11 David was king of Israel 40 years. He ruled 7 years from Hebron and 33 years from Jerusalem. Then he died and was buried in Jerusalem. 12 His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom.
Adonijah Is Killed
13One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
“Yes. 14I just want to talk with you.”
“All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
15“You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed. 16Would you do me a favor?”
“What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
17 “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
18“All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
19When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side. 20Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?”
Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
21“Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
22Solomon said:
What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
23I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me. 24The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
25“Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died.
Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
26 Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said:
Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father. 27 But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore.
And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true.
Joab Is Killed
28Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection. 29When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?”
Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.”
Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
30Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!”
“No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.”
Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
31-32Solomon replied:
Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders. 33Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
34Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
35Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest.
Shimei Is Killed
36Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city! 37If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
38“That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
39About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were, 40he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
41Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back. 42Solomon sent for him and said:
Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you? 43You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
44I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did. 45But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
46“Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died.
Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid karfaa tuna tɛɛ Koori Solomɔn wia
1Koori Deevid siu n wa helle, u karfi u biibaal Koori Solomɔn, di ŋɔ, 2“N saŋa jaa heluu. Awia, chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega, 3di ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la ŋmɛnizi, u widaulaa ani u Gbɔgni la maa baŋ sɛbɛɛ du Moosis Gbɔgni Hɔŋ biini la. Gunnɛ niŋ gil i wer nyɛɛli i wiɛɛlaa maa biini ani bɔr la maa ge hin niŋ la. 4Di i ra ɛɛ guŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ hiŋ u nua la uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛŋ lugɔ n naanna danna di Izrɛl kora di hanna la, di ba ra du tau, di ra hiŋ u widaulaa ni wibii ba biine ni ba kpegzi ani ba nfɛssi maa.
5Wii bɛl haa jaawɔɔ. A liizi gunla Zɛruya biibaal Joab n ɛɛŋ, di faa kpu Izrɛl laallɔɔra nabɔnzi banɛɛ la. Nɛɛr biibaal Abna ani Jɛta biibaal Amasa. U faa kpu baabuu saŋa la bɔr n sɔɔnɛɛ lugɔ laal biini. Ba challi faa chɔg u kirsɔɔ ni u gawa. 6Awia, tɛr u digni ni nunzuma, ka gilɛɛ wa gil u waa siu ni bampirsɔna.
7Ka kpogli Giliad hinuu Bazilai biibaala waa nɛnnɛ. Gil ba ɔɔ ba i dia i ni baa kpau di ra di, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa ɛɛmbuu nɛnnɛ, saŋa la miŋ faa chɔwɛɛ di ra lii i kpɛɛma Absalɔm be la.
8Kaa ra liizi lugɔ Gɛra biibaal Simei la n lii Bɛnjamin dee biini la, n lii Bahurim la du i benii. U faa seembuu nua a hɔl la miŋ la Mahanam la. U faa tuuwoo wa huuziŋ Jɔɔdan muu nua, ka n faa kpa Kɔraawiizi sɔnnɛ hɛɛhzi lugɔ màá kpuu ni tokobi. 9Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u dignitɛraa. Zum gunla hin niŋ ɛɛ, di gil bá kpuu.”
Koori Deevid siu wia
10Denii Koori Deevid faa jaa la ga chɔɔ u naabaala be ani bampirsɔna, ba huguu Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm la. 11U faa di Izrɛl koraa binni tokkoanɛɛ, binni aniidaanɛɛ bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn biini, binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni ahoro ge Jɛrusalɛm biini. 12Gunnɛ a faa ɛɛ, Solomɔn kpa u mɛɛ Koori Deevid gawa di di a kora, u kora ge faa chi chigigi werge maa.
Adonija siu wia
13Denii Hagif biibaal Adonija la faa la Koori Solomɔn maa Batsiiba be. Batsiiba pɛɛzuu, “A summɔaa?”
Adonija sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, a summɔɔ.” 14Ka jaa ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ wiibɛllɛ di ra nyiŋŋi n ŋɔ tɛi.”
Batsiiba ŋɔ, “A ŋɔ.”
15U ŋɔ, “I zummɔ lugɔ kora naa ɛɛ n hotte. Izrɛl hina maa faa zummɔ lugɔ minuu ba koori. Ka guŋ waa wette ɛɛ, ka a kora kpa la n niwee be, dikuu guŋ n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kipar wia. 16Awia, n dɔɔ wikpaŋ bɛllɛ di ra nyiŋŋi n suŋŋi. Jaande, gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ.”
Denii Batsiiba tɛu ŋmɛnɛɛ dí u suŋŋi.
17Adonija ŋɔ, “Jaande maa, suŋŋi Koori Solomɔn lugɔ ú kpa Sunɛm hinuu Abisag tɛŋ ń kpa, n zummɔ lugɔ wàá vɛɛ.”
18Batsiiba ŋɔ, “Guŋ wesso. N daŋ ŋɔ a koori be tɛi.”
19Awia, Batsiiba la Koori Solomɔn be ú ga lizi Adonija amaniye la tɛu. Uŋ ga zuuwɛ, koori izi tognuu, di jaamuu, ka bir so u koorikara ni, ka gil ba kpa a kara bɛl ge chiŋŋi u nodig, u maa ge so.
20Batsiiba jaa ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ wijiga bɛllɛ di ra nyiŋŋi ń suŋŋii, gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ.”
A koori ŋɔ, “N ma, bɛɛwɛi? Suŋŋi, màá vɛɛ.”
21U maa ŋɔ, “Gil Sunɛm hinuu Abisag yuu i kpɛɛma Adonija.”
22Denii Koori Solomɔn bir ŋɔ u maa be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i suŋŋi Abisag di ra tɛɛ Adonijai? Guŋwaa, suŋŋi n kora naa gba tɛu, dikuu uŋ ɛɛ n kpɛɛma wia. Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata ni Zɛruya biibaal Joab ge gba chigɛ u hattɛ!”
23Denii Koori Solomɔn hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ, di Adonija waa u miibɔɔ kpawɛɛ turgi u winyiŋŋii naa kim! 24N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de, unla n hiiniŋ n wer so n mɛɛ Koori Deevid koorikara naa ni chigigi, di kaa dau koori domee tɛɛ n ni naanna gunla uŋ faa ŋɔ nua la. Adonija daŋ siu zinaa!” 25Awia, Koori Solomɔn faa tɛɛ Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya ŋmɛnɛɛ, u ga kpu Adonija.
Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata duŋŋaa ani Joab siu wia
26Denii Koori Solomɔn faa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata waa be, “Bir di ra la i koo la n du Anatɔf. I gba dɛg siurɛ, ka màá kpui filaŋkeŋ. I ɔɔ faa chi Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka labuu di tɔ n mɛɛ Koori Deevid see, di kaa hiinuu di tɔɔrɔɔ.” 27Awia, Koori Solomɔn faa lizi Abiata lii Kɔraawiizi kizeehina huma biini. Guŋ faa gil gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ Silo, di ra bagli Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛli dia wia la ɛɛ wibii.
28Joab ni Adonija n faa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, haali Joab n faa waa Absalɔm har chigɛ gba, n wa nuu guŋ, u chɔ ga zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia, di ga lau mbusu lizibɔr nyigzi la kpogli. 29Ba ga ŋɔ Koori Solomɔn be lugɔ Joab chɔwɔɔrɛ la Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia, di ga chi mbusu lizibɔr la kɛrii. Denii Koori Solomɔn tɛɛ Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya ŋmɛnɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “La ga kpuu!”
30Awia, Bɛnaaya ga zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la di ŋɔ Joab be, “A koori ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Wa lii!’ ”
Ka Joab bir ŋɔ, “Akai, n daŋ siu ɛŋ.”
Bɛnaaya bir la ga kali koori gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ.
31Denii a koori ŋɔ u be, “Ga ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. La ga kpuu, di huguu, guŋ gil n ni n mɛɛ diahina wàá ka di bilchɔg, dikuu nɛnanaa la Joab n kpuwɛɛ la wia. 32Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr Joab digni, dikuu banla uŋ faa kpuwɛɛ, di n mɛɛ Koori Deevid waa zummɛ la wia. U faa kpu baala banɛɛrɛ, Nɛɛr biibaal Abna, Izrɛl laallɔɔra nabɔma ani Jɛta biibaal Amasa, Juda laallɔɔra nabɔma. Ba maanii faa ɛɛ nɛnanaa kaaluu. 33Awia, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi Joab ani u naanna waa maa ninɛɛ, di hanna la saŋa maa. Ama, Kɔ́raawiizi bɔsɔna du Koori Deevidwaa ni u naanna maa, u dia ani u kooridomee la be, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”
34Awia, Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya faa la ga kpu Joab, ba huguu u himmaa hɛri, hɛribɔduma biini. 35Gunnɛ a ɛɛ, a koori faa kpa Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya du Joab bɔr, u ɛɛ u laallɔɔra nabɔma, di kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk ge du Abiata bɔr.
Simei siu wia
36Denii Koori Solomɔn hum bá ga yir Simei, ú ba. Uŋ wa ballɛ, u ŋɔ u be, “Ma dia Jɛrusalɛm biini di ra zuu, ka gilɛɛ waa la yemmaa. 37A hɔl la maa hin niŋ izi gi Kidrɔn Waluu, zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ i daŋ siu, wibii maa, í wichɔgaa laŋŋi i ni.” 38Simei ŋɔ koori be, “Jara, gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wessoo. Mìŋ́ i balii daŋ ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.” Awia, Simei faa so Jɛrusalɛm birgi werge.
39Ka binni ahoro n wa bɛrɛɛ, Simei yoma banɛɛ baŋhina chɔ kaali Maaka biibaal Gaf Koori Akis be. Denii ba faa ga kali Simei guŋ, di ŋɔ, “I yoma la du Gaf hɛri.” 40Uŋ wa nuu guŋ, u izi bɔg u kawee, di la Koori Akis be, Gaf hɛri, ú ga nyiŋŋi u yoma hiŋ. U faa ga na baabuu de, di kpogli baa bir ba. 41Ka Koori Solomɔn n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Simei la Gaf hɛrii ka bir ba la, 42u hum di yiruu, u ba, u ŋɔ u be, “Maa gillɛ i hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini lugɔ a hɔl la maa hin niŋ la yemmaa, í zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ i daŋ siuwaa? A saŋa hiŋ, i faa ŋɔ n benii gunla miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wessoo, awia i daŋ hiŋ guŋ. 43Ka bɛɛ n gillɛ haa i nua la hiŋŋɛ, ka vɛɛ n widaulii lai?”
44Koori Solomɔn faa kaa ŋɔ Simei be, “I zummɔɔ nɛnnɛ i biini, wichɔgaa la maa hiŋ ɛɛ n mɛɛ Koori Deevid. Filaŋkennaa waa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ turgii í wichɔgaa la kim. 45Ka mìŋ́ Koori Solomɔnwaa daŋ na kissaa, Koori Deevid kora ge chi nɛnnɛ, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”
46Denii a koori faa jaa tɛɛ Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya ŋmɛnɛɛ, u la ga kpu Simei.
Gunnɛ faa ɛɛwɛ, Koori Solomɔn kora faa jaa chi chigigi.

english_text:
The Lord Makes Solomon Wise
(2 Chronicles 1.1-13)
1Solomon signed a treaty with the king of Egypt and married his daughter. She lived in the older part of Jerusalem until the palace, the Lord's temple, and the wall around Jerusalem were completed.
2At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines. 3Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
4 The most important shrine was in Gibeon, and Solomon had offered more than 1,000 sacrifices on that altar.
5One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
6Solomon answered:
My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king. 7Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader. 8And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
9Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
10-11God said:
Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions. 12So I'll make you wiser than anyone who has ever lived or ever will live.
13I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king. 14If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
15Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials.
Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
16One day two women came to King Solomon, 17and one of them said:
Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home, 18and three days later her baby was born. Nobody else was there with us.
19One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died. 20Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
21In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
22“No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!”
“The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!”
They argued back and forth in front of Solomon, 23until finally he said, “Both of you say this live baby is yours. 24Someone bring me a sword.”
A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered, 25“Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
26“Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.”
The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
27Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
28Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_text:
Koori Solomɔn n suŋŋi nunzuma wia
1Koori Solomɔn ni Ijip koori faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ, guŋ gil u kpa Ijip koori biihaaŋ. U faa kpaubuu ba Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la, mɔɔ ka haa wa ma u himmaa kooridia, Kɔraawiizi Dia ani koŋlii la n bar Jɛrusalɛm la. 2Izrɛl hina faa haa ra lizi ba mbusuzii giŋgimee nyuuni, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa haa waa Kɔraawiizi Dia mawɛɛ. 3Koori Solomɔn faa nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizii, di ra hiŋ gunla u mɛɛ Koori Deevid n bagluu la, ka uŋ faa kpa sela di ra lizi mbusuzi, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma giŋgimee nyuuni la bɛnnɛ faa kawɛɛ.
4Awia, Koori Solomɔn faa la Gibiɔnnɛ di ga lizi mbusuzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, denii mbusu lizibɔra la maa ú zeŋ faa du. U faa kpa sela kagbonne, di lizi mbusu di fuuah de. 5Kɔraawiizi faa ba Koori Solomɔn be Gibiɔn hamuŋa ni, deeza biini, di wa ŋɔ u be, “Suŋŋi kunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi, ń tɛi.”
6Koori Solomɔn ŋɔ u be, “I faa nɔŋŋi i balii n mɛɛ Koori Deevidii werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra hiŋiibuu ni wibii, u wia maa deŋli, di kaa dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu ge jaa. I haa ra suŋ u ninɛɛ werge maa, di tɛu biibaal u so u koorikara ni zinaa.
7N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, filaŋkeŋ, i gillɔɔ mìŋ́ i balii Koori Solomɔn kpa n mɛɛ gawa, di di kora. N ɛɛ bichalaa, maa n see ni n har zummɛ. 8Mìŋ́ i baliirɛ keŋ, di du i nɛra la hiŋ lizɛɛ biini, ba kpillɔɔ werge maa, ba wàá wer kur baa. 9Awia, gil i balii ɛɛ nunzunni la n niŋ wer ra zum wia zɛɛzi, di wer ra binni i nɛra ni, di ɔɔ wer zum wideŋlaa ani anla n waa deŋlee. Anɛɛ n niŋ wer binni i nɛra naa n dɔɔ sɔŋ werge naa ninɛi?”
10Koori Solomɔn wiisuŋŋaa la par Kɔraawiizi. 11Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Dikuu hiŋ suŋŋi keŋ ka gil miibɔɔjaŋ ni daama gɛɛ i dɔma siuzaa, ka ra nyiŋŋi nunzuma, í wer di ra di wibii wia, 12n daŋ ɛɛ gunla hiŋ suŋŋɛɛ la. N daŋ tɛi nunzuma ni wia zɛɛ zumaa werge la nɛr maa n haa waa dɔɔwɛ mɔɔ gɛɛ nɛr maa ge ŋmɛnɛ n niŋ wa dɔɔ. 13Haali n daŋ tɛi kunla gba hiŋ waa suŋŋɛɛ. N daŋ tɛi daama ani zenni. Koori maa wàá lugɔi, i de dui saŋa. 14Di i wetto di ra hiŋ n ŋmɛnizi n widaulaa ani n Gbɔgni nɛnnɛ, gunla i mɛɛ Koori Deevid n faa ɛɛwɛ la, n daŋ tɛi miibɔɔjaŋ.”
15Denii Koori Solomɔn hassi izi, di na lugɔ deezaa.
U jaa bir la Jɛrusalɛm di ga chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, di lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa ni dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi. Ka gil ba daali diuzenaa tɛɛ u balaa ni u nabɔnzi maa.
Koori Solomɔn n di seriyakpol bɛl wia
16A hɔl bɛl, hahsɛnsɛnna banɛɛ baŋhina faa chi dɔŋa ba Koori Solomɔn be. 17Denii bɛl ŋɔ, “Jara, n ni haannaabuu ra zuu. U sibɔɔrɛ, ka n lul biibaal. 18A hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, u ge lul biibaal. N nuu bɛnnɛ du a dia.
19Denii hamuŋa ni, haaŋ naa billi chɔɔ u bie ni, u siu. 20Hɛuh n wa hɛɛhzɛɛ, u izi wa kpa n bie lii n kɛra, di ga dau u kɛra, di mìŋ́ i balii ra chɔɔ dɔɔ, ka kpa u biisiwii la dau n kɛra. 21Denii hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzi ni, n izi ŋɔ n lau il du n bie, di u siuwɔ. Ka miŋ wa binnuu na nɛnnɛ, n na lugɔ n bie la miŋ lullɛ la lɛi.”
22Denii a haaŋ la hiŋ ŋɔ, “Akai! Biinyinii labuu n bie, i hotte u siwii la.”
Ka hahlugli la haa vɛɛ ŋɔ, “Akai! U siwii labuu i hor, u nyinii la ge ɛɛ n hor.”
Ba maa faa chi a koori see di ra bil dɔŋa.
23Denii Koori Solomɔn ŋɔ, “Unnii ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N biere u nyinii la, i hotte u siwii la.’ Ka unla hiŋ ge ŋɔ, ‘Akai! I hotte siuwɛ la, n hotte ra nyiŋ la.’ ”
24Awia, a koori ŋɔ, “Ií kpa tokobi di wa tɛŋ.” Ba kpa a tokobi wa tɛu. 25U ŋɔ, “Ií lau biinyinii la chah anɛɛ, di kpa u yeŋ tɛɛ unnii, di kpa u yeŋ ge tɛɛ unla hiŋ.”
26Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, unla bie n ɛɛu la na u sinyɛna werge maa, awia, u ŋɔ a koori be, “Jara, jaande maa, kpa a biinyinii la tɛɛ n dɔŋhiŋ la, gilɛɛ waa kpuu!”
Ka unla hiŋ ŋɔ, “Akai! Yaa bɛl maa wàá dɔɔ a biinyinii, ií chauh!”
27Denii a koori jaa ŋɔ, “Ií kpa a biinyinii la tɛɛ a lugli hiŋ la. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpuu, waabuu u maa.”
28Izrɛl hina maa n wa nuu a koori seriya dii la, a kpu ba nuuzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi benii u na nunzuma, di ra di seriya ni wibii.

english_text:
Solomon's Officials
1-6Here is a list of Solomon's highest officials while he was king of Israel:
Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah sons of Shisha were the secretaries;
Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the government records;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the army commander;
Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the regional officers;
Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king's advisor;
Ahishar was the prime minister;
Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor.
7Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year. 8These were the twelve officers:
The son of Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.
9The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
10The son of Hesed was in charge of the towns of Arubboth and Socoh, and the region of Hepher.
11The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
12Baana son of Ahilud was in charge of the towns of Taanach and Megiddo. He was also in charge of the whole region of Beth-Shan near the town of Zarethan, south of Jezreel from Beth-Shan to Abel-Meholah to the other side of Jokmeam.
13The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had 60 walled towns with bronze bars on their gates.
14Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of the territory of Mahanaim.
15Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
16Baana son of Hushai was in charge of the territory of Asher and the town of Bealoth.
17Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in charge of the territory of Issachar.
18Shimei son of Ela was in charge of the territory of Benjamin.
19Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived.
And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah.
The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
20There were so many people living in Judah and Israel while Solomon was king that they seemed like grains of sand on a beach. Everyone had enough to eat and drink, and they were happy.
21 Solomon ruled every kingdom between the Euphrates River and the land of the Philistines down to Egypt. These kingdoms paid him taxes as long as he lived.
22Every day, Solomon needed 5,000 liters of fine flour, 10,000 liters of coarsely-ground flour, 2310 grain-fed cattle, 20 pasture-fed cattle, 100 sheep, as well as deer, gazelles, and geese.
24Solomon ruled the whole region west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and he was at peace with all of the countries around him. 25Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
26 Solomon had 40,000 stalls of chariot horses and 12,000 chariot soldiers.
27Each of the twelve regional officers brought food to Solomon and his household for one month of the year. They provided everything he needed, 28as well as barley and straw for the horses.
Solomon's Wisdom
29Solomon was brilliant. God had blessed him with insight and understanding. 30-31 He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel. 32 Solomon wrote 3,000 wise sayings and composed more than 1,000 songs. 33He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish. 34Kings all over the world heard about Solomon's wisdom and sent people to listen to him teach.
translation_text:
Koori Solomɔn nabɔnzi wia
1Koori Solomɔn faa di Izrɛl maa koraa. 2U nabɔnzenaare faa keŋ,
Zadɔk biibaal Azariaa faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ.
3Sisa biibaala Ɛlihɔrɛf ni Ahija faa ɛɛ nabɔnzi, di ra sɛbi ba hɔna.
Ahilud biibaal Jɛhɔsafat ge faa ra sɛbi ba faala wia hɔna di ra dau.
4Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaayaa faa ɛɛ u laallɔɔra maa nabɔma.
Zadɔk ni Abiata ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina.
5Netan biibaal Azaria ge faa ɛɛ a hɛri bariizi nabɔnzi binni.
Netan biibaal Zabud la ge faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ ni nɛr la ge n na bir a koori liize.
6Ahisa faa ra binni a kooridia ni u wikpoglaa maa.
Abda biibaal Adoniram faa ɛɛ nɛr la n na binni ba humkpega ni.
7Koori Solomɔn faa dɔɔ bariizi fidaanɛɛrɛ Izrɛl hɛri maa di wa chem. A bɛl maanii faa dɔɔ u nabɔma, u ɔɔ kɛɛ kuna di waa tɛɛ a koori ni u diahina maa. Ba bɛl maanii ɔɔ faa ɛɛ guŋ baagu bir, bina maa biini. 8Ba ge sɔnaa keŋ,
Bɛn Hur, waabuu faa ɛɛ Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri la binni.
9Bɛn Dɛka faa ra binni bolzenaa Makaz, Saalbim, Bɛf Sɛmɛs ani Ɛlɔn Bɛf Hanan hɛssi.
10Bɛn Hɛsɛd ge faa ra binni bolzenaa Arubɔf, Soko ani Hitti hɛri.
11Bɛn Abinadab ge faa ra binni Nafɔf Dɔɔ hɛri ni. Waabuu faa kpa Koori Solomɔn biihaaŋ Tafaf.
12Ahilud biibaal Baana ge faa ra binni bolzenaa Taanak, Mɛgidɔ ani Bɛf San barii la n dugli bol la banna yir Zarɛtan, n du bol la banna yir Jɛzriil wiifurii nodig wiikakag guŋŋ di ga hel a bolzenaa Abɛl Mɛhɔla ani Jɔkmiam.
13Bɛn Gɛba ge faa ra binni bolzeŋ Ramɔf n du Giliad hɛri, Giliad boljigzi la n faa ɛɛ Manasɛ naana Jayir domee bɔr ani Aagɔb barii la n du Basan, a maa faa ɛɛ bolzenaa tokkoahoro la baŋ ma koŋlaa baraa, a dominuuzenaa dɔɔ danyɛ daazi, ba kpa di ra karaa la.
14Ido biibaal Ahinadab la ge faa dɔɔ Mahanam barii.
15Ahimaz la ge n faa kpa Koori Solomɔn biihaaŋ Basɛmaf la faa ra binni Naftali barii ni.
16Husai biibaal Baana ge faa ra binni Asɛ barii ni bol bɛl banna yir Alɔf.
17Parua biibaal Jɛhɔsafat faa ra binni Isaka barii ni.
18Ɛla ge biibaal Simei faa ra binni Bɛnjamin barii ni.
19Uri biibaal Gɛba la faa ra binni Giliad barii la n faa ɛɛ Amɔri Koori Sihɔn ni Basan Koori Ɔɔg hɛssi ni Gɛba bɛnnɛ faa ɛɛ de barii binni.
Koori Solomɔn kora nyɛɛlaa wia
20Juda ni Izrɛl hina faa kpillɔɔ werge maa alugɔ muuzeŋ nua hɛɛhriichaa. Ba faa ɔɔ diu, di nyɔɔ, di dɔɔ bɔsɔna ge werge maa. 21Koori Solomɔn faa dɔɔ ba hɛssi maa fɔŋŋaa di lii Muu Yufretis guŋŋ di ga hel Filisti hɛri, di kaa kpa guŋŋ di ga hel Ijip hɛri magbɔɔ. A hɛssi naa hina maanii ɔɔ faa lizi hɛri kuna di waa tɛɛ Koori Solomɔn, di faa ɛɛ u balaa u de dui saŋa.
22Kuna la baŋ ɔɔ faa kɛɛ tɛɛ Koori Solomɔn hɔpizi biimaa, ɔɔ faa ɛɛ sakɔla kilozi kagboŋa ahoro ni sanyaaraa kilozi kagboŋa anumbɛl. 23Nauna la ge baŋ ɔɔ tɔ di dɛɛzaa a pɔl nɛnnɛ la ge fi, anla ge n ɔɔ gaagi di ra di kooree ge tokko ani peeza ni buuna ge kalfa. Di kaa kpa chɛhzi, burunzi, chaŋkpalinzi ani zaahra la n wesse nɛnnɛ. 24U faa di Muu Yufretis wiicholii hɛssi maa koraa, di lii Tifsa guŋŋ di ga hel Gaza n du wiicholii. Bampirsɔna faa du u ni hɛssi hina la maa n baruu la baaŋ. 25Koori Solomɔn de dui saŋa, Izrɛl ni Juda hɛssi maa faa dɔɔ bampirsɔnaa, di chi Dan guŋŋ di ga hel bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba. Nɛr maa faa dɔɔ u grepu ni fig daazii.
26Koori Solomɔn faa dɔɔ diini kagboŋa tokkoanɛɛrɛ tɛɛ u zagra la n na tɛrgi torkozi. Anla ge n waa torkozi ra tɛrgi ɛɛ kagboŋa fidaanɛɛ.
27Di Koori Solomɔn nabɔnzenaa la bɛl maa kɛɛi baagu haŋ wa lii, u ɔɔ faa kɛɛu di wa tɛɛ u ni banla maa n ɔɔ faa ra di u be labuu. Ba ɔɔ faa aah siwiire lugɔ koori gilɛɛ waa nyaa kummaa. 28Ba faa ɔɔ kaa aah siwiire, di ra ba mia ni kooree ni, di waa tɛɛ u zagra la n na tɛrgi torkozi ge.
Koori Solomɔn nunzuma wia
29Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ Koori Solomɔnnɛ nunzuma ni wia zɛɛ zumaa werge di ga bɛri. 30Nɛr maa faa waa hoo a wiifurii keŋkere hiŋ, di dɔɔ nunzuma lugɔ Koori Solomɔn. Haali u faa dɔɔ nunzumaa kaali Ijip hɛri hina nunzunna maa. 31U faa dɔɔ nunzumaa kaali baal maa, haali di kpa Ɛtan la n faa ɛɛ Ɛzra domee hinuu la gba. Di faa kaa dɔɔ nunzuma kaali Hɛman, Mahɔl biibaala Kalkɔl ani Dada. Awia, u sɔŋ faa yaari hɛssi la maa n baruu la biine. 32U ta sɛɛliizi kagboŋa ahoro, di yir yira ge kagboŋ ni anue. 33U faa bagli daazi wiarɛ, di chi Lɛbanɔn hɛriŋkpola guŋŋ di ga hel hisɔp la n na fur koŋlaa ni la. U faa kaa bagli nɛra genii sela, zumbizi, kuntuuzaa ani nyinni wia. 34Hɛssi maa koora n faa nuu Koori Solomɔn nunzuma la wia, ɔɔ faa hum nɛraa ba ba di waa nuu u wiŋɔzi.

english_text:
Solomon Asks Hiram To Help Build the Temple
(2 Chronicles 2.1-16)
1King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
2Solomon sent a message back to Hiram:
3Remember how my father David wanted to build a temple where the Lord his God could be worshiped? But enemies kept attacking my father's kingdom, and he never had the chance. 4Now, thanks to the Lord God, there is peace in my kingdom and no trouble or threat of war anywhere.
5 The Lord God promised my father that when his son became king, he would build a temple for worshiping the Lord. So I've decided to do that.
6I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
7Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!” 8Then he sent back his answer:
I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need. 9My workers will carry them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea. They will tie the logs together and float them along the coast to wherever you want them. Then they will untie the logs, and your workers can take them from there.
To pay for the logs, you can provide the grain I need for my household.
10Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar and pine logs he needed. 11In return, Solomon gave Hiram over 2,000 tons of wheat and almost 4,000 liters of pure olive oil each year.
12The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other.
Solomon's Workers
13Solomon ordered 30,000 people from all over Israel to cut logs for the temple, 14 and he put Adoniram in charge of these workers. Solomon divided them into three groups of 10,000. Each group worked one month in Lebanon and had two months off at home.
15He also had 80,000 workers to cut stone in the hill country of Israel, 70,000 workers to carry the stones, 16and over 3,000 assistants to keep track of the work and to supervise the workers. 17He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
18Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Dia mai sirya ɛɛi wia
1Taaya Koori Hiram n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Koori Solomɔn kpa u mɛɛ Koori Deevid gawaa la, u hum u nabɔnzi u be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ni Koori Deevid faa summɔɔ. 2Koori Solomɔn ge faa bir tɛu tile naa, di ŋɔ,
3“I zummɔ lugɔ hɛssi la hina maa n bar n mɛɛ Koori Deevid la, faa ra yooubuu laal. Awiarɛ u faa waa wette ú ma Kɔraawiizi la unna hum la Dia tɛu sɔŋ, see Kɔraawiizi wa kpegli u dɔma maa tɛu mɔɔ. 4Ka filaŋkeŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la, tɛmbuu heezaa lii keŋkerezi maa. Dɔma gɛɛ hɛhchɔg maa waa kaa hoo. 5Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu ń ma Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la Diarɛ, di tɛu sɔŋ, alugɔ uŋ faa ŋɔ n mɛɛ Koori Deevid be, ‘I biibaal la n niŋ wa kpa i gawa labuu niŋ ma Dia tɛŋ.’
6Awia, tɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ bá teŋri Lɛbanɔn hɛriŋkpola daazi tɛŋ. N nɛra daŋ wa hiini i nɛra di hum a huma. N daŋ turgi i nɛra hiŋ di mag gunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi. I zummɔ genii lugɔ yaa waa nɛr dɔɔwɛ, u zum daazi teŋraa nɛnnɛ lugɔ Saidɔn hina.”
7Hiram n wa nuu Koori Solomɔn tile la, a faa paruubuu werge maa, u ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ jaannɛ werge maa zinaa, dikuu uŋ tɛɛ Koori Deevid biibaal la siwee n chaanɛɛ, u di hɛrzeŋ la kora wia.”
8Awia, Koori Hiram faa tili ŋɔ Koori Solomɔn be,
“N nuu i tile labuu. N daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi. N daŋ tɛi a hɛriŋkpola daazi ni daananaa. 9N balaa daŋ tuuzaa lii Lɛbanɔn hɛri tuu muuzeŋ, di vɔɔzaa mari dɔŋa alugɔ muugbessi, a pal di ga hel bɔr la maa hin niŋ bagli. A bɔdeere n balaa ga puraa tɛi. Ama, n winyiŋŋiire lugɔ í ra tɛɛ n ni n diahina diwee.”
10Gunnɛ a faa ɛɛ, Koori Hiram faa tɛɛ Koori Solomɔn hɛriŋkpola daazi ni daananaa la maa unna nyiŋŋi. 11Ka Koori Solomɔn ge faa tɛɛ Koori Hiram mia kilozi kagboŋa kalfaanumbɛl ni tokkoahoro ni aniidaanɛɛ, a ɛɛ u ni u diahina maa diwee. U faa kaa kpa ɔlivizi nuu himmaa pirintuani kagboŋa kalfaanumbɛl di jaa. Bina maanii Koori Solomɔn ɔɔ faa ɛɛ guŋ. 12Kɔraawiizii faa tɛɛ Koori Solomɔn nunzuma gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛu la. Bampirsɔna faa du Koori Hiram ni Koori Solomɔn baannɛ. A guŋ wia, ba faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ.
13Koori Solomɔn faa gillɔɔ baala kagboŋa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ faa ɛɛ u humkpega huŋhunna, Izrɛl hɛri maa. 14U faa bargi baabuu kagboŋa fizi, di gil ba la Lɛbanɔn hɛri. Ba ɔɔ faa ga hum denii baagu kpaŋ, ka bir ba bol ge di wa di baaguzi anɛɛ. Adoniramnɛ faa ra binni a humkpega ni. 15Koori Solomɔn bunchigna faa du baala kagboŋa tokkoahoro ni fi. Banla ge n faa ra sɛɛhzi bia giŋgimee nyuuni ge faa du kagboŋa tokkoanaazu. 16Banla ge n faa ra binni a huŋhunna di ra bagli baa a huma, faa du kagboŋa ahoro ni kalfaahoro. 17A koori faa ŋɔ bá sɛɛh bizennanaa, bá chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ zɛɛ. 18Koori Solomɔn, Koori Hiram huŋhunna ani bolzeŋ Gɛbal hina huŋhunna maanii faa teŋri a daazi di kuaraa, di sɛɛhzi a bia ge bá ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ.

english_text:
The Outside of the Temple Is Completed
1Solomon's workers started building the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year. It had been 4 years since Solomon became king of Israel, and 480 years since the people of Israel left Egypt.
2The inside of the Lord's temple was 27 meters long, 9 meters wide, and 13.5 meters high. 3A four-and-a-half-meter porch went all the way across the front of the temple. 4The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
5-6Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
7Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.
8The entrance to the bottom storage rooms was on the south side of the building, and stairs to the other rooms were also there. 9The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards.
The workers finished building the outside of the temple. 10Storage rooms just over two meters high were all around the temple, and they were attached to the temple by cedar beams.
11The Lord told Solomon:
12-13If you obey my commands and do what I say, I will keep the promise I made to your father David. I will live among my people Israel in this temple you are building, and I will not desert them.
14So Solomon's workers finished building the temple.
The Inside of the Temple Is Furnished
(2 Chronicles 3.8-14)
15The floor of the temple was made out of pine, and the walls were lined with cedar from floor to ceiling.
16 The most holy place was in the back of the temple, and it was nine meters square. Cedar boards standing from floor to ceiling separated it from the rest of the temple. 17The temple's main room was 18 meters long, and it was in front of the most holy place.
18The inside walls were lined with cedar to hide the stones, and the cedar was decorated with carvings of gourds and flowers.
19The sacred chest was kept in the most holy place. 20-22 This room was nine meters long, nine meters wide, and nine meters high, and it was lined with pure gold. There were also gold chains across the front of the most holy place. The inside of the temple, as well as the cedar altar in the most holy place, was covered with gold.
23 Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made from olive wood to put in the most holy place. Each creature was four and a half meters tall 24-26and four and a half meters across. They had two wings, and the wings were just over two meters long. 27Solomon put them next to each other in the most holy place. Their wings were spread out and reached across the room. 28The creatures were also covered with gold.
29The walls of the two rooms were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures. 30Even the floor was covered with gold.
31-32The two doors to the most holy place were made out of olive wood and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures. The doors and the carvings were covered with gold. The door frame came to a point at the top.
33-34The two doors to the main room of the temple were made out of pine, and each one had two sections so they could fold open. The door frame was shaped like a rectangle and was made out of olive wood. 35The doors were covered with gold and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
36The inner courtyard of the temple had walls made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams.
37Work began on the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year, four years after Solomon became king of Israel. 38Seven years later the workers finished building it during Bul, the eighth month of the year. It was built exactly as it had been planned.
translation_text:
Koori Solomɔn n ma Kɔraawiizi Dia wia
1Binni kalfaanaazu ni tokkoanaazu hiŋ biini, di lii saŋa la Izrɛl hina n faa lii Ijip hɛri la, Koori Solomɔn kora dii Izrɛl hina ni, binni anaazuhiŋ, baaguzi anɛɛhiŋ la banna yir Ziv la biinii u faari Kɔraawiizi Dia la mai.
2Kɔraawiizi Dia la Koori Solomɔn n faa mawɛɛ la jaŋzi faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nogumzi tokkoahoro, u wassi ge faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi tokko, u chiŋ laŋaa ge faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ. 3Jaŋgal bɛl baŋ faa mawɛɛ u loŋ see ni a Dia wassi faa ɛɛ kpannɛ, alugɔ nogumzi tokko, di ga saagi a Dia see alugɔ nogumzi fi. 4U faa du tokorozii a Dia koŋlaa ni a baŋgizi fɔɔ, ka a biine du war, di hiŋzi dɔŋa ni. 5U faa ma diibizi aŋhina genii di hiini a Dia keŋkerezi ni u harbɔɔ koŋlaare. 6A diini faa hɔŋzi dɔŋa ninɛɛ. U zɛɛ himmaa dia la wassi faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi anue. Nɛɛhiŋ la ge hɔŋ u ni di saagi, u wassi faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi anumbɛl. Horohiŋ ge kaa hɔŋ u ni di saagi, u wassi faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi aniidaanɛɛ. U faa ma bɔra a saagi a koŋlii ni, ba kpa dolli sagzi a ni, di ma a diibizi hɔŋ a ni, a dolli gilɛɛ waa zuu a koŋlii ni.
7Banna ma a Dia, bia la baŋ sɛɛhzɛɛ bia purgi bɔr bɛnnɛ ba kpa mau. Awia, silii gɛɛ lugbii kummaa faa waa kaa gbɔgzi u mai bɔr guŋŋ ka ba wa mau tuŋ.
8U zɛɛ himmaa dia la dominua faa du u wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkeree. Ba faa ma lɔŋaa di ga hel u sal nɛɛhiŋ la, bɛl ge kaa lii de di ga hel horohiŋ la. 9Awia, Koori Solomɔn faa ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hinnɛ tuŋ, di kpa dolzenaa ani hɛriŋkpol daapiahni guu. 10A diini la uŋ faa mawɛɛ di hiini a Dia koŋlaa maa la, bɛl maa chiŋ laŋaa faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nogumzi anue. Ba faa kpa hɛriŋkpol dollii gua, a mari a Dia.
11Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Koori Solomɔn be, 12“Dia naa hinna ma naa, di i sɛɛwɔ di ra hiŋ n widaulaa, di ra sɛɛ n baglaazi, di ra hiŋ n nuuzi maa, n daŋ ga i ni di ɛɛ gunla miŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ i mɛɛ Koori Deevid la. 13N daŋ du n nɛra Izrɛl hina be, màá gil baa ta.”
14Awia, Koori Solomɔn faa ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ tuŋ. 15U faa kpa hɛriŋkpol daapiahnii di mɛɛri u biini koŋlaa maa ni, di lii hɛri ga chug u sabile. Di kaa kpa daananaa daapiahni ge mɛɛri u hɛri maa di wa kaali. 16U faa kpa hɛriŋkpol daapiahnii teŋ a Dia lume, di lii u hɛri ga chug sabile, de jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko, di ɛɛ Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la. 17A loŋ la n du a Bɔnaniinanii naa see jaŋgzi faa ɛɛ nogumzi tokkoanɛɛrɛ. 18A Dia biini maa faa ɛɛ hɛriŋkpol daapiahnii, ba faa zɛuzaa, a ɛɛ lugɔ keuni ni fiiri. U koŋlaa maanii ba faa kpa hɛriŋkpol daazi mɛɛri. Ba faa waa kaa ra na bii maa.
19U faa kuari a diiseere, ú kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la chiŋŋi de. 20A diisee naa jaŋzi, u wassi ani u chiŋ laŋaa maa mɛgzaazi faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi tokkozi. U faa kpa saliŋ himmaanii tɔ a diisee biini maa di wa kaali, di faa kpa hɛriŋkpol daazi mɛɛri mbusu lizibɔr la ge. 21Koori Solomɔn faa kpa saliŋ himmaanii tɔ Kɔraawiizi Dia biini maa, di faa kpa saliŋ yɔlɔzi ge teŋ a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la baŋ tɔ saliŋ la dominua. 22Awia, a Dia biini maanii ba faa tɔ ni saliŋ. Haali u biini mbusu lizibɔr la maa.
23U faa kpa ɔlivizi daazii sɛɛh chɛrubzi anɛɛ, di kpaa chiŋŋi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la biini, bɛl maa chiŋ laŋaa faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi fi. 24A chɛrubzi lugli hiŋ keekpaŋ maa jaŋzi faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nogumzi anue. Awia, di lii kee bɛl nua di ga hel bɛl nua ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nogumzi fi. 25Nɛɛhiŋ la ge gba, guŋ himmaanii, dikuubɛɛwiai, a faa li dɔŋaa di kaa mɛgzi. 26A chɛrubzi naa bɛl maa chiŋ laŋaa faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nogumzi fi. 27U faa kpaabuu chiŋŋi a Dia Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la biini, di gil a keeri yaa. Bɛl kee gaa chug a Dia keŋkere koŋlii bɛl, unla hiŋ ge kee bɛl gaa chug a keŋkere bɛl koŋlii. Ka anla n kawɛɛ ge gaa chug dɔŋa a dia baambaaŋ. 28A chɛrubzi naa gba maanii Koori Solomɔn faa kpa saliŋ tɔ.
29A loŋ ni a diisee biini koŋlaa maanii u faa sɛɛh chɛrubzi, abɛ daazi ani fiiri dau a ni. 30Haali a diini hɛssi maanii u faa tɔ ni saliŋ.
31U faa kpa ɔlivizi daazii kuari gbera du a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la dominua, u ɛɛ gberkpara, di faa dɔɔ kɛraa daazi anue. 32U faa gillɔɔ ba sɛɛh chɛrubzi a gberkpara ni, di kaa sɛɛh abɛ daazi ge ni fiiri a ni, di jaa. A maanii u faa gil ba kpa saliŋ tɔ. 33Guŋ himmaanii u kaa gil ba kuari gbera daazi aŋhina anaazu du a loŋ la ge dominua. 34U faa kaa gil ba kpa daananaa kuari gberkpara anɛɛ n na kpɛu, 35ba kaa sɛɛh chɛrubzi, abɛ daazi ani fiiri la n pillɛɛ, di mɛgzi dɔŋa, di kpa saliŋ tɔ a ni gbɔlɔŋgbɔlɔŋ.
36U faa kaa gil ba kpa binanaa ma u biini diŋŋee la solaa ahoro ni hɛriŋkpol dolli baŋ ŋmɛnnɛɛ ge solkpaŋ, guŋŋ di wa mau tuŋ.
37Koori Solomɔn kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ, Ziv baagu biinii, ba faa chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Dia la zɛɛ. 38Binni fidikpaŋhiŋ ge biini, baagu ŋmantannaazi la banna yir Buul la biinii, ba faa ma Kɔraawiizi Dia la, u wijigzi ani u wikpoglaa maa tuŋ. Binni aniidaanɛɛrɛ Koori Solomɔn faa kpa mau tuŋ.

english_text:
Solomon's Palace Is Built
1Solomon's palace took 13 years to build.
2-3Forest Hall was the largest room in the palace. It was 44 meters long, 22 meters wide, and 13.5 meters high, and was lined with cedar from Lebanon. It had 4 rows of cedar pillars, 15 in a row, and they held up 45 cedar beams. The ceiling was covered with cedar. 4Three rows of windows on each side faced each other, 5and there were three doors on each side near the front of the hall.
6Pillar Hall was 22 meters long and 13.5 meters wide. A covered porch supported by pillars went all the way across the front of the hall.
7Solomon's throne was in Justice Hall, where he judged cases. This hall was completely lined with cedar.
8 The section of the palace where Solomon lived was behind Justice Hall and looked exactly like it. He had a similar place built for his wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt.
9From the foundation all the way to the top, these buildings and the courtyard were made out of the best stones carefully cut to size, then smoothed on every side with saws. 10The foundation stones were huge, good stones—some of them four and a half meters long and others three and a half meters long. 11The cedar beams and other stones that had been cut to size were on top of these foundation stones. 12The walls around the palace courtyard were made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams, just like the front porch and the inner courtyard of the temple.
Hiram Makes the Bronze Furnishings
(2 Chronicles 3.15-17; 4.1-10)
13-14Hiram was a skilled bronze worker from the city of Tyre. His father was now dead, but he also had been a bronze worker from Tyre, and his mother was from the tribe of Naphtali.
King Solomon asked Hiram to come to Jerusalem and make the bronze furnishings to use for worship in the Lord's temple, and he agreed to do it.
15Hiram made two bronze columns eight meters tall and almost two meters across. 16For the top of each column, he also made a bronze cap just over two meters high. 17The caps were decorated with seven rows of designs that looked like chains, 18with two rows of designs that looked like pomegranates.
19The caps for the columns of the porch were almost two meters high and were shaped like lilies.
20The chain designs on the caps were right above the rounded tops of the two columns, and there were 200 pomegranates in rows around each cap. 21Hiram placed the two columns on each side of the main door of the temple. The column on the south side was called Jachin, and the one on the north was called Boaz.
22The lily-shaped caps were on top of the columns.
This completed the work on the columns.
23Hiram also made a large bowl called the Sea. It was just over two meters deep, about 4.5 meters across, and 13.5 meters around. 24Two rows of bronze gourds were around the outer edge of the bowl, ten gourds to every 45 centimeters. 25The bowl itself sat on top of twelve bronze bulls with three bulls facing outward in each of four directions. 26The sides of the bowl were 75 millimeters thick, and its rim was like a cup that curved outward like flower petals. The bowl held about 40,000 liters.
27Hiram made ten movable bronze stands, each one over a meter high, almost two meters long, and almost two meters wide. 28-29The sides were made with panels attached to frames decorated with flower designs. The panels themselves were decorated with figures of lions, bulls, and winged creatures. 30-31Each stand had four bronze wheels and axles and a round frame 68 centimeters across, held up by four supports 45 centimeters high. A small bowl rested in the frame. The supports were decorated with flower designs, and the frame with carvings.
The side panels of the stands were square, 32and the wheels and axles were underneath them. The wheels were about 68 centimeters high 33and looked like chariot wheels. The axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were made out of bronze.
34-35Around the top of each stand was a 22-centimeter strip, and there were four braces attached to the corners of each stand. The panels and the supports were attached to the stands, 36and the stands were decorated with flower designs and figures of lions, palm trees, and winged creatures. 37Hiram made the ten bronze stands from the same mold, so they were exactly the same size and shape.
38 Hiram also made ten small bronze bowls, one for each stand. The bowls were almost two meters across and could hold about 800 liters.
39He put five stands on the south side of the temple, five stands on the north side, and the large bowl at the southeast corner of the temple.
40Hiram made pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls.
A List of Everything inside the Temple
(2 Chronicles 4.11—5.1)
This is a list of the bronze items that Hiram made for the Lord's temple: 41two columns; two bowl-shaped caps for the tops of the columns; two chain designs on the caps; 42400 pomegranates for the chain designs; 43ten movable stands; ten small bowls for the stands; 44a large bowl; twelve bulls that held up the bowl; 45pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls.
Hiram made these bronze things for Solomon 46near the Jordan River between Succoth and Zarethan by pouring melted bronze into clay molds.
47There were so many bronze things that Solomon never bothered to weigh them, and no one ever knew how much bronze was used.
48 Solomon gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar; the table that held the sacred loaves of bread; 49 ten lampstands that went in front of the most holy place; flower designs; lamps and tongs; 50cups, lamp snuffers, and small sprinkling bowls; dishes for incense; fire pans; and the hinges for the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
51 After the Lord's temple was finished, Solomon put into its storage rooms everything that his father David had dedicated to the Lord, including the gold and the silver.
translation_text:
Koori Solomɔn n ma u kooridia wia
