1Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel, 2and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
3Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam. 4-5 David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
6-7 The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king.
Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 8Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king.
King Asa of Judah
(2 Chronicles 15.16—16.6,11-13)
9Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel, 10and he ruled 41 years from Jerusalem. His grandmother was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
11Asa obeyed the Lord, as David had done. 12 He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made. 13His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
14As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines. 15He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
16Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel. 17One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
18When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria: 19“Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
20Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali. 21When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
22Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
23Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease. 24Asa died and was buried in the tomb of his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jehoshaphat then became king.
King Nadab of Israel
25Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years. 26Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
27-28Baasha son of Ahijah was from the tribe of Issachar, and he made plans to kill Nadab. When Nadab and his army went to attack the town of Gibbethon in Philistia, Baasha killed Nadab there. So in the third year of Asa's rule, Baasha became king of Israel.
29 The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family, 30because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
31Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
32King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war.
King Baasha of Israel
33Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled 24 years from Tirzah. 34Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_text:
Juda Koori Abija wia
1Nɛbat biibaal Izrɛl Koori Jeroboam kora dii binni fidiŋmantannaazihiŋ biinii Koori Abija faa di Juda kora, 2di so Jɛrusalɛm biini, binni ahoro. U maa sɔnnɛ faa Maaka la n faa ɛɛ Abisalɔm biihaaŋ.
3U ge gba faa ɛɛ wichɔgaa la maa u mɛɛ n faa ɛɛwɛ labuu. U bampirii faa waa Kɔraawiizi la unna hum la lauwɛ nɛnnɛ gunla u naabaal Koori Deevid n faa duwɛɛ la. 4Ka Koori Deevid wia, Kɔraawiizi faa tɛubuu biibaal, u ɛɛ lugɔ fintina Jɛrusalɛm biini, ú kpa u gawa di di kora, di gil Jɛrusalɛm dɔɔ fɔŋŋa. 5Koori Deevid faa ɛɛ gunla n deŋlee Kɔraawiizi benii, u faa waa u widaulii maa vɛɛwɛ, u de dui maa biini, di u ni Hitti hinuu Yuria wia la bɛŋ lɛi.
6Laal la n faa du Koora Rehoboam ni Jeroboam baaŋ la faa haa du denii Abija de dui maa biini. 7Wia la maa Koori Abija n faa ɛɛwɛ u kora dii saŋa la, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Juda Koora Faala Hɔna biine. Laal faa du Koora Abija ni Jeroboam baannɛ.
8Ka Koori Abija faa siu, ba huguu Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini. Denii u biibaal Asa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.
Juda Koori Asa wia
9Izrɛl Koori Jeroboam kora dii binni tokkohiŋ biinii Asa ge faa di Juda kora. 10U faa di a koraa Jɛrusalɛm biini, binni tokkoanɛɛ ni kpaŋ. U naarɛ faa Maaka la n faa ɛɛ Abisalɔm biihaaŋ la.
11Koori Asa faa ɛɛ gunla n deŋleere Kɔraawiizi be, gunla u naabaal Koori Deevid n faa ɛɛwɛ la. 12U faa duŋŋi a vuga kuaribɔra basɛnsɛnna ni hahsɛnsɛnna la maanii lii a hɛri, ka faa chɔgi vuga la maa u mɛɛwaa n kuarɛɛ la. 13Haali, u faa wir u naa Maakaa lii wiche biini, dikuu uŋ faa baŋ vughaaŋ Asɛra n chummɛ daa, di ra kuaruu wia. Koori Asa faa ŋmɛŋ a daarɛ ta, di kpau ga fuuh Kidrɔn Waluu biini. 14Haali, uŋ faa waa a vuga kuaribɔra chɔkkɛ a giŋgimee nyuuni gba, ka u bampirii faa lau Kɔraawiizii nɛnnɛ, ú de dui maa biini. 15U faa kpa kuna la baŋ kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ kuari la u ni u mɛɛ n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi labuu du Kɔraawiizi Dia biini.
16Laal faa chol Juda Koori Asa ani Izrɛl Koori Baasa baannɛ, ba kossi dii biini, saŋa maa. 17Izrɛl Koori Baasa faa lɔ Juda hina, di kpegli baa, di foozi Rama, di ma koŋlii baruu, nɛr maa gilɛɛ kaa wer lii gɛɛ zuu Juda koori hɛri.
18Denii Koori Asa jaa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ la maa n kawɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia daama kuna dauribɔra ani u himmaa kooridia hora di jaa, di kpaa hum u nabɔnzi dí ba la Siiria Koori Bɛn Hadad la n faa du Damaskus di ra di kora, u mɛɛ faa ɛɛ Tabrimɔn, u naabaal ge ɛɛ Hɛziɔn la be, di ga ŋɔ, 19“Gil n nii dɔɔ nuukpaŋ gunla n mɛɛ ni i mɛɛ n faa dɔɔwɛ la. Awia, n na sunziibuu saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ, ka í gil i ni Izrɛl Koori Baasa nuukpaŋ la tuŋ, gunnɛ niŋ gil ú lizi u laallɔɔra lii n hɛri.”
20Denii Koori Bɛn Hadad nuu Koori Asa nua la, di hum u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi, bá ga lɔ Izrɛl laal. Ba faa ga kpegli Ijɔn, Dan, Abɛl Bɛf Maaka ani hɛri la n dugli Galilii muuzeŋ maa, di kpa Naftali bolzenaa maa jaa. 21Koori Baasa n wa nuu guŋ, u faa gil Rama mai, ka la ga so Tirza.
22Denii Koori Asa faa du gbɔg lugɔ Juda hina maa la ga chi bia ani daazi la maa Koori Baasa n faa kpawɛɛ di ra ma la lii Rama ba. Koori Asa kpaa ma Gɛba n du Bɛnjamin ani Mizpa.
23Wia la aŋhina n ɛɛwɛ Koori Asa kora dii biini wia la maa uŋ wette di ɛɛ ani bolzenaa la maa uŋ faa ma koŋlaa bar, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Juda Koora Faala Hɔna biine. Ama, u zɛŋaa saŋa la, wiila faa lau u naazii, u gbɛr. 24Denii u faa jaa siu, ba huguu u naabaala hugribɔr, Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini. Ka u biibaal Jɛhɔsafat faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.
Izrɛl Koori Nadab wia
25Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ biinii, Koori Jeroboam biibaal Nadab faa di Izrɛl kora. Binni anɛɛ bɛnnɛ u faa di a kora. 26U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ Kɔraawiizi be alugɔ u mɛɛ, di faa gil Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ wichɔgaa.
27Ahija biibaal Baasa n faa lii Isaka dee biini, faa ta u kpui jinaa, di kpuu Filisti hina bolzeŋ bɛl banna yir Gibɛtɔn, di Koori Nadab ni Izrɛl hina maa faa ra nyiŋŋi ba fɔɔ a bol ni laal. 28Koori Baasa faa kpu Koori Nadabrɛ, Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni ahorohiŋ biini, ka faa lɛɛ u bɔr di di a kora.
29Uŋ haŋ faari u kora dii, u kpu Koori Jeroboam lulla maa. U faa waa kpaŋkpaŋ maa gillɛ, ba maanii u faa chɔgi di lii gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga u dɔgtɛɛ Silo hinuu Ahija be, di ŋɔ la. 30A guŋ ɛɛwɔɔ dikuu Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ, di gil Izrɛl hina maa ge ɛɛa, Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la baaŋ fuuh werge la wia.
31Wia la aŋhina Koori Nadab n ɛɛwɛ u kora dii saŋa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. 32Laal faa du Juda Koori Asa ani Izrɛl Koori Baasa baannɛ, ba kossi dii saŋa maa.
Izrɛl Koori Baasa wia
33Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni ahorohiŋ biinii, Ahija biibaal Baasa faa di Izrɛl kora, di du Tirza biini, binni tokko ni anaazu. 34U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di hiŋ Koori Jeroboam hiŋaa la, di gil Izrɛl hina gba ɛɛ wichɔgaa.

english_text:
1The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
2Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry 3that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam. 4Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
5-7Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family!
Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king.
King Elah of Israel
8Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for 25 years, and he ruled from Tirzah for two years.
9Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah.
One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister, 10when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
11As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed. 12Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned. 13Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
14Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Zimri of Israel
15-16Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah.
Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day. 17At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked. 18When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire. 19Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
20Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Omri of Israel
21After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri. 22Omri's followers were stronger than Tibni's, so Tibni was killed, and Omri became king of Israel 23in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah.
Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah, 24then he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for 6,000 pieces of silver. He built a town there and named it Samaria, after Shemer who had owned the hill.
25Omri did more evil things than any king before him. 26He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
27Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 28Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king.
King Ahab of Israel
29Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled 22 years from Samaria.
30Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him. 31He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal. 32Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria 33and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
34 While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_text:
1Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ u dɔgtɛɛ Hanani biibaal Jehu be lugɔ ú ga lizi amaniye naa tɛɛ Koori Baasa, di ŋɔ, 2“I faa waa kummaa ɛɛwɛ, ka n gil i ɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina sitɔɔri. Ka filaŋkennaa, i ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ alugɔ Koori Jeroboam, di gil n nɛra ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Guŋ gil n baaŋ fuuh werge maa. 3Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu ń dim i ni i lulla maa, di gil i dia ɛɛ lugɔ Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam dia. 4Nuuzihinaa niŋ di i dia hinuu la maa n niŋ siu a bolzeŋ biini, duuni ge di unla ge n niŋ siu pir biini.”
5Wia la aŋhina Koori Baasa n ɛɛwɛ u kora dii saŋa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. 6Koori Baasa faa siu, ba huguu Tirza biini. Ka u biibaal Ɛla kpa u gawa di di a kora.
7Amaniye naa faa ga Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jehu benii di ba Koori Baasa ni u diahina be, dikuu wichɔgaa la maa uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ zuu Kɔraawiizi ni la wia. U faa fuuh Kɔraawiizi baannɛ, dikuu wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ lugɔ Koori Jeroboam n faa ɛɛwɛ ani uŋ kaa kpu Koori Jeroboam lulla maa wia.
Izrɛl Koori Ɛla wia
8Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni anumbɛlhiŋ biinii, Koori Baasa biibaal Ɛla faa di Izrɛl kora, di so Tirza binni anɛɛ.
9U nabɔma Zimri n faa ɛɛ u torkozi yeŋ binni, faa ta u kpui jina. A hɔl bɛl, Koori Ɛla faa du Tirza, Aaza la n faa ra du kooridia tau la dia, di nyɔɔ siŋ di ra dɛɛzi. 10Denii Zimri wa zuu di yag Koori Ɛla ta, di kpuu. Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii guŋ ɛɛ. Ka jaa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.
11Uŋ haŋ faari a kora dii, u faa kpu Koori Baasa lulla maanii. U faa waa ba baal maa gillɛ, haali di u ɛɛ u lulli gɛɛ u dammu gba. 12Awia, Koori Zimri faa chɔgi Koori Baasa waa lulla maanii gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga u dɔgtɛɛ Jehu be, di ŋɔ labuu. 13Koori Baasa ni u biibaal Koori Ɛla faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, di gil Izrɛl hina maa ge ɛɛa, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh, dikuu baŋ faa ra kuari vuga wia.
14Wia la aŋhina Koori Ɛla n faa ɛɛwɛ u kora dii saŋa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.
Izrɛl Koori Zimri wia
15Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, Koori Zimri faa di Izrɛl kora Tirza biini, hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. A saŋa, di ba laallɔɔra faa chaali dɔŋa, di fɔɔ Filisti hina bolzeŋ Gibɛtɔn. 16Izrɛl hina la n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Koori Zimri ta Koori Ɛla jinaa di kpuu la, ba lizi Ɔmri n ɛɛ ba laallɔɔra nabɔma, di tɔu Izrɛl kora a hɔl hiŋ, ba chaalibɔr la biini. 17Denii Koori Ɔmri ni Izrɛl hina la maa n du u be la, lii Gibɛtɔn di vɔɔ laal di ga fɔɔ Tirza. 18Koori Zimri n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba kpegli a bolzenne la, u chɔ zuu a kooridia diikpeg, ka duu niŋ. Awia, u faa siu, 19dikuu wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, gunla Koori Jeroboam n faa ɛɛwɛ, di gil Izrɛl hina maa ge ɛɛa la wia.
20Wia la aŋhina Koori Zimri n faa ɛɛwɛ u kora dii biini ani u jinachɔgaa wiɛɛlaa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.
Izrɛl Koori Ɔmri wia
21Denii Izrɛl hina la faa bargi bɔra anɛɛ, ba yeŋ chi Ginaf biibaal Tibni har lugɔ ú ɛɛ koori, ka ba yeŋ ge chi Ɔmri har. 22A tuna, Ɔmri harbɔɔchigna la faa kpegli Tibni harbɔɔchigna la. Awia, Tibni faa siu, ka Ɔmri kpa a kora.
23Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni kpaŋhiŋ biinii, Ɔmri faa di Izrɛl kora. Binni fidaanɛɛrɛ u faa di a kora. U faa sogo Tirzaa binni anumbɛl. 24Koori Ɔmri faa yau bolzeŋ Samaria giŋgimii bɛl, saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi tokkoahoro ni fi, di lii baal bɛl banna yir Sɛmɛ be, di ma bolzeŋ a giŋgimii nyuu, di ma koŋliizeŋ baruu. Di kpa Sɛmɛ la n faa dɔɔu la sɔŋ dawuu, Samaria.
25Ama, Koori Ɔmri faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa Kɔraawiizi be kaali banla maa n tɔ u see di di kora la. 26U faa hiŋ Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam wiɛɛlaa ni u wichɔgaa la maa, uŋ faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina ɛɛ, di gil Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la baaŋ faa fuuh, dikuu baŋ faa ra kuari vuga la n waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ wia.
27Wia la aŋhina Koori Ɔmri n faa ɛɛwɛ, u kora dii saŋa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. 28Denii Koori Ɔmri faa siu, ba huguu bolzeŋ Samaria biini. Ka u biibaal Ahab kpa u gawa, di di a kora.
Izrɛl Koori Ahab wia
29Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni ŋmantannaazihiŋ biinii, Koori Ɔmri biibaal Ahab faa di Izrɛl kora, di faa so Samaria, di di a kora binni tokko ni anɛɛ. 30Koori Ɔmri biibaal Koori Ahab faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, Kɔraawiizi be, di kaali banla maa n feluu di kora la. 31U faa waa nawɛɛ lugɔ Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la ɛɛ wizenne, ka faa ga kpa Saidɔn Koori Ɛtbaal biihaaŋ, Jɛzɛbɛl, di faari ra kuari vug Baal, di ra tɔgzuu. 32U faa ma vug Baal diarɛ, Samaria, di ma mbusu lizibɔr u biini. 33Koori Ahab faa baŋ vughaaŋ Asɛra daarɛ, di kaa ɛɛ wikpila maa jaa, di faa gil Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la baaŋ fuuh werge maa, di kaali Izrɛl koora la maa n diwee ka tɛu la.
34Koori Ahab kora dii saŋa, Bɛtɛl baal bɛl banna yir Hiɛl, bittɔɔ ma bolzeŋ Jɛriko. U biibambilugli Abiram faa siu, uŋ wa chiŋŋi a bol zɛɛ tuŋ. U bichala hiŋ Sɛgub ge faa siu, saŋa la uŋ wa du a bol koŋlii dominuuzenaa tuŋ. Annii naa maa ɛɛwɔɔ gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga Nun biibaal Josua be, di ŋɔ la.

english_text:
Elijah Stops the Rain
1 Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
2Later, the Lord said to Elijah, 3“Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek. 4You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
5Elijah obeyed the Lord and went to live near Cherith Creek. 6Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek. 7But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain.
Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
8The Lord told Elijah, 9 “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
10When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked. 11As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
12The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
13Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me. 14The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
15The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time. 16The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil.
Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
17Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
18The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
19“Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed 20and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.” 21 Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
22The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again. 23Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
24“You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_text:
Duglizi n tɛɛ Ɛlija diwee wia
1Tisbi hinuu Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlija la n lii Giliad hɛri la ŋɔ Koori Ahab be, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n ni Izrɛl hina n na hum, u du de saŋa maa labuu lugɔ dooŋ gɛɛ ŋmɛnii wàá ka chol, binni aŋmɛnɛ biini, di maa guŋ wa ŋɔwɛɛ lɛi.”
2Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Ɛlija be, 3“Lii bɔnnaa, di ga wiifurii, di ga suah Kɛrif Gɔmbɔɔluŋ la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la. 4I danna nyɔɔ gɔnjiga bɛl nii, ka n gil duglizi ra dɛɛzii de.”
5Denii u ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la, di la a Kɛrif Gɔmbɔɔluŋ la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la, di ga du de. 6A duglizi ɔɔ faa wa tɛu paanuu ni ol chɔɔzi ni duana maa. U ɔɔ nyɔɔ nii a gɔŋ biini. 7Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, a gɔŋ hiihzi, dikuu dooŋ n waa ba wia.
Ɛlija ni Zarɛfaf luhaaŋ wia
8Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, 9“La bol la banna yir Zarɛfaf n dugli bolzeŋ Saidɔn, di gaa zuu de. N lizi luhaaŋ bɛllɛ de, di ŋɔ ú ra tɛi diwee.” 10Ɛlija la Zarɛfaf. Uŋ gaa hel a bol dominuuzeŋ, di luhaaŋ bɛl ra nyiŋŋi daazi. U yiruu ŋɔ u be, “Jaande maa, ɛɛ nii wa tɛŋ ń nyɔɔ.” 11A haaŋ n na la ú ga ɛɛ a nii la, u kaa yiruu ŋɔ u be, “Jaande maa, mɔŋ paanuu jaa wa tɛŋ.”
12Ka a luhaaŋ bir ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n du de saŋa maa la, maa paanuu dɔɔwɛ. Sau tama bɛnnɛ n dɔɔ n saulee biini ni nuu tama ge n nuulee biini. N na nyiŋŋi daazi tamaa ń la bol, di ga ɔɔzi paanuu, n ni n biibaal hee, ka siuzi.”
13Ɛlija ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm. La bol ga ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa. Ama, feli ga ɔɔzi paanuujiga lii kunla hiŋ dɔɔwɛ la biini, di wa tɛŋ mɔɔ, ka jaa ga ɔɔzi, í ni i biibaal ge hee. 14Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘A sau lee wàá nyaa sau maa, a nuu lee ge wàá hil maa, di ga hel a hɔl la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ gil dooŋ kaa ba hɛri naa.’ ”
15Awia, u kpa la ga ɛɛ gunla Ɛlija n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu la. Hɔpizii maanii diwee ɔɔ du de, tɛɛ Ɛlija, haaŋ la ani u diahina. 16A sau lee waa sau nyaawɛ maa, a nuu lee ge faa waa hillɛ maa, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Ɛlija be, di ŋɔ la.
17Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, a haaŋ la n dɔɔ a dia la biibaal ra wii. U wiila la ra nyaŋŋi. A tuna maa, u heeza teŋ. 18Denii a luhaaŋ ŋɔ Ɛlija be, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ, beedee wiarɛ i kpa ra chuginnɛi. I ballɔɔ í wa liiziŋ n wichɔgaa wia, ka kpu n biibaal gɛɛ?”
19Ɛlija ŋɔ, “Kpa i biibaal la ba.” U lɛɛu u nonee biini, di kpau di tinni la dia la uŋ duwɛɛ chiŋ la, di ga kpau dau u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni. 20Ka lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, i kpa biinichɔgrɛ ta luhaaŋ naa minna zuu u be naa ninɛɛ, di gil u biibaal siwaa?” 21Ka jaa izi di chɔɔ pi a biibaal ni buhoro, ka kaa lɔ wile di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, gil biibaal naa kaa bir dɔɔ miibɔɔ!”
22Denii Kɔraawiizi nuu Ɛlija suŋŋaa la, a biibaal kaa bir dɔɔ miibɔɔ.
23Ɛlija kpau tuu tɛɛ u maa, ka ŋɔ u be, “Na, i biibaal la ra nyinuu!”
24Denii a haaŋ ŋɔ Ɛlija be, “Filaŋkennaa, n jaa zumuu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛrɛ hiŋ. U wiŋɔɔlii maa ge hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, ɛɛ wibii.”

english_text:
Elijah Proves He Is the Lord's Prophet
1-2For three years no rain fell in Samaria, and there was almost nothing to eat anywhere. The Lord said to Elijah, “Go and meet with King Ahab. I will soon make it rain.” So Elijah went to see Ahab.
3-4At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid 100 of them in two caves and gave them food and water.
Ahab sent for Obadiah 5and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass. 6You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
7As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
8“Yes. Go tell Ahab I'm here.”
9Obadiah replied:
King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong. 10I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country. 11Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
12What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me.
I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy. 13I even hid 100 of the Lord's prophets in caves when Jezebel was trying to kill them. I also gave them food and water. 14Do you really want me to tell Ahab you're here? He will kill me!
15Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
16Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah.
Ahab went to meet Elijah, 17and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
18Elijah answered:
You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
19Call together everyone from Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. Be sure to bring along the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table.
20Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel. 21Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!”
The people did not say a word.
22Then Elijah continued:
I am the Lord's only prophet, but Baal has 450 prophets.
23Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
24The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God.
“That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
25Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
26They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
27At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
28The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped, 29and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
30Elijah told everyone to gather around him while he repaired the Lord's altar. 31-32 Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about 14 liters. 33He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood.
He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this, 34he told them to do it two more times. They did exactly as he said 35until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
36When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed:
Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command. 37Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
38The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch. 39When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
40Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.”
So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them.
It Starts To Rain
41Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
42 Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground 43and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.”
The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
44After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.”
Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
45-46A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_text:
Ɛlija ni vug Baal dɔgtɛɛzi wia
1A hil binni ahorohiŋ biini, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Ɛlija be, “La ga kpa i hiŋ bagli Koori Ahab, ka n jaa gil dooŋ ba.” 2Awia, Ɛlija la ú ga kpa u hiŋ bagli Koori Ahab.
A saŋa naa, di lɔchɔgii faa nyaŋŋɔɔ bolzeŋ Samaria biini. 3Koori Ahab faa yir Obadia la n faa ra binni kooridia wikpoglaa ni. Obadia faa ɛɛ nɛr la n yardi Kɔraawiizii, di hiŋuu nɛnnɛ. 4A saŋa hiŋ, Koori Ahab haaŋ Jɛzɛbɛl n faa ra kpuuzi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la, Obadia faa lau ba kalfaa, ga suah bia bɔɔni anɛɛ aŋhina biine. Ba tokkoanɛɛ ni fi du bɔɔ naa, ba tokkoanɛɛ ni fi ge du bɛl, ka u ra tɛɛ baa diwee ni nii. 5Koori Ahab ŋɔ Obadia be, “Yá gaagi a hɛri ni bulli ni walli maa na. Aŋhinabe, yaa daŋ na kooree di ra dɛɛzi yaa zagra ni kauzi, gunnɛ niŋ gil yaa wàá kpu yaa sel maa.” 6Awia, ba bɔnni a hɛri bɔr la ban niŋ gaagi la. Koori Ahab ga keŋkere bɛl, Obadia ge ga keŋkere bɛl.
7Obadia n na la la, Ɛlija chem u ni. Obadia zumuu kakpaŋ, di togni hɛri di ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri Ɛlija, hinuu naa?”
8U sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, minuu. La ga ŋɔ i dɔɔri Koori Ahab be lugɔ minuu du ɛŋ.”
9Obadia pɛɛzi, “Beedee wichɔgiirɛ n ɛɛi, i ra nyiŋŋi i kpa mìŋ́ i balii, tɛɛ Koori Ahab, ú kpuɛi? 10N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum, u du de saŋa maa la lugɔ koori gillɔɔ ba gaagi durnya hɛssi naa maa biine, di ra nyiŋŋii. Di hɛri bɛl maa hina wa ŋɔwɔɔ lugɔ ba wɛɛ nawɛɛ, u ɔɔ giluu ba hɛɛhzi lugɔ ba wàá wer nai. 11Ka i ra ŋɔ n be filaŋkeŋ lugɔ ń ga ŋɔ n dɔɔri be lugɔ hinuu du ɛŋ. 12Maa zum bɔr la Kɔraawiizi Duma la n niŋ kpai kaali, di n wa lii i be. Di n laŋŋɔ ga ŋɔ Koori Ahab be, ka u wa nyiŋŋii huhzi, u daŋ kpuŋ. Haali mìŋ́ i balii n jaami Kɔraawiizi di lii n bichal saŋa maa gba. 13N dɔɔri, haa nuuwɛ gunla miŋ ɛɛwɛ saŋa la Jɛzɛbɛl n faa ra kpuuzi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi laa? N faa lauri ba kalfaa di ga suah bia bɔɔni anɛɛ aŋhina biine, ba tokkoanɛɛ ni fi du bɛl maa biini, n na tɛɛ baa diwee ni nii. 14Ka filaŋkeŋ, i ra ŋɔ n be lugɔ ń la n dɔɔri Koori Ahab be, di ga ŋɔ, ‘Ɛlijaa du ɛŋ.’ U daŋ kpuŋ!”
15Ka Ɛlija ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la n du de saŋa maa, n na humuu la lugɔ n daŋ kpa n hiŋ bagli Koori Ahab zinaa.”
16Awia, Obadia la ga ŋɔ Koori Ahab be. Koori Ahab la ú ga chem Ɛlija ni. 17Uŋ ga na Ɛlija, u ŋɔ u be, “Hinuu naa? Hinuu ra koozi Izrɛl hɛri laa?”
18Ka Ɛlija ŋɔ, “Maa Izrɛl ra koozi. I ni i mɛɛwaa domee labuu ra koozuu. Ií vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nuuzii, ka ra kuari vug Baala. 19Awia, chaali Izrɛl hina la maa n du a hɛri, bá chem n ni Bizeŋ Kamɛl nyuu. Kpogli vug Baal dɔgtɛɛzi kalfaanaazu ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi la ani vughaaŋ Asɛra dɔgtɛɛzi kalfaanaazu la ge, Jɛzɛbɛl n na binni ba ni la, jaa.”
20Awia, Koori Ahab hum bá yirgi Izrɛl hina maa, di chaali ba ni a dɔgtɛɛzi la maa, Bizeŋ Kamɛl nyuu. 21Ɛlija la a nɛra be, di ga ŋɔ, “Saŋa bɛliirɛ ii gil aanai? Di Kɔraawiizii kaali Baal, ií ra humuu, di vug Baal genii, kaali Kɔraawiizi, ií ra humuu.” Ka a nɛra waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ, ka sigli. 22Awia, Ɛlija jaa ŋɔ ba be, “N bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la n kawɛɛ. Ka vug Baal waa dɔɔ dɔgtɛɛzi kalfaanaazu ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi. 23Ií nyiŋŋi nabala anɛɛ tɛɛ yaa. Di gil ba lizi bɛl, di kpuu, di mɔnnuu jigzi sag daazi ni, ka gilɛɛ waa du niŋ. N ge kpu bɛl, di ɛɛ guŋ. 24Ií yir ii vug la sɔŋ, n ge yir Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ, unla maa n wa sɛɛwɛ, di gil niŋ ba, waabuu Kɔraawiizi.”
Denii a nɛra maa ŋɔ “Kennaa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa wessoo.”
25Ɛlija ŋɔ Baal dɔgtɛɛzi la be, “Ií feli lizi nabal la bɛl di kuaruu, dikuu iiŋ kpillɛ wia. Ií yir ii vug hiŋ sɔŋ, ka gilɛɛ waa chem niŋ di ra du u ni.”
26Denii ba lau a nabal la baŋ tɛɛ baa la kpu, di kuaruu. Ka jaa yir Baal sɔŋ di lii chɔɔzi maa guŋŋ wiizi wa baŋ. Ba ra pogzi di ra ŋɔ, “Hoi, Baal, nuu yaa be!” Ka ba waa wiimaa nuuwɛ. Nɛr maa waa sɛɛwɛ, ka ba sa di ra bar mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kuarɛɛ la.
27Wiizi n wa baŋŋɛ, Ɛlija jaa ra ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛ, di ra ŋɔ, “Ií ra pogzi werge maa! U ɛɛ vugrɛ, wibii maa! Aŋhinabe, u ra fɛ nfɛrɛɛ gɛɛ di ra hum huma aŋhina gɛɛ di vol ŋmɛnɛɛ. Aŋhinabe, u ra chɔɔ dɔɔrɛ, a dɛg lugɔ ii lalluu!!” 28Ba jaa ra pogzi werge, di ra mɔnni bahinaa ni ba tokobizi ni kandaazi, gunla baŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ la, guŋŋ ba challi waa lii. 29Wibaŋkanchirii n wa bɛrɛɛ, di ba haa aah siwii di ra kaabi ba vug la guŋŋ, ba duaniŋmbusu lizaa saŋa wa hel. Ka ba haa waa wiimaa nuuwɛ, nɛr maa ge waa sɛɛwɛ gɛɛ di hagzi baa.
30Denii Ɛlija jaa ŋɔ a nɛra la maa be, “Ií tuzi hel n be bɔnnaa.” Ba ba u be, di chaali baruu. U bir kuari Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la n faa purgee la, di ma. 31Ɛlija faa paagi bia fidaanɛɛrɛ, a bɛl maa chi tɛɛ ba dizi fidaanɛɛ la, n ɛɛ Jekɔb la Kɔraawiizi n faa dau u sɔŋ Izrɛl la, naanna. 32U kpa a bia di ma mbusu lizibɔr, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini, di ki bɔɔ baruu, u du luŋ lugɔ nii pirintuani fidaanaazu, wer suu. 33U jaa paa daazi sag u ni, ka lau a nabal mɔnni, sagzi a daazi ni. Ka ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií ɛɛ nii suugi keubizi anaazu, di fug waari mbusu lizaa ol ni a daazi maa ni.”
34U kaa ŋɔ, “Ií kaa ɛɛ guŋ.” Ba kaa kuari ɛɛ guŋ.
U kaa ŋɔ, “Ií kaa ɛɛ guŋ buhoro hiŋ.” Ba kaa ɛɛ guŋ. 35A nii jaa pal tuu mbusu lizibɔr kɛraa, haali di su a bɔɔ la gba.
36Mbusu lizaa saŋa n wa helle, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlija jaa lii chi, di suŋŋi wiizi, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb n na hum, gil nɛr maa zum zinaa lugɔ hinuu Kɔraawiizi, Izrɛl hɛri. N ge ɛɛ i balii, di ɛɛ wia naa maa gunla hiŋ ŋɔ n ɛɛ la. 37Sɛɛ tɛŋ, n Dɔɔri, sɛɛ tɛŋ, nɛra naa zum lugɔ hinuu Kɔraawiizi, di kaa zum ge lugɔ i kaa ra bir ba bampireere di ra du i ni.”
38Denii Kɔraawiizi niŋ wa chol mbusu lizaa ol ni, di fuuh a ni a daazi, a bia ani de hɛɛhraa la maa, di gil nii la n du bɔɔ la biini la gba hiihzi.
39A nɛra n wa na guŋ, ba maa chɔɔ pi hɛri, ka lɔ wile, di ra ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ Dɔɔri! U bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi!”
40Denii Ɛlija ŋɔ kpegzi ni, “Ií lauri vug Baal dɔgtɛɛzi la. Ií gilɛɛ wa gil bɛl maa ra chɔ!” Ba lauri baa. Ɛlija gil ba kpogli baa la Kisɔn Waluu, di ga kpu baa de.
41Denii Ɛlija ŋɔ Koori Ahab be, “La ga di, ka nyɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n nuu dozeŋ wiraare.” 42Awia, Koori Ahab la ú ga di ka nyɔɔ. Ka Ɛlija tinni Bizeŋ Kamɛl nyuu di ga bugni, di kpa u nyuu du u naazi biini.
43Denii u ŋɔ u balii be, “La ga binni muuzeŋ barii na.”
U la ga binni na, ka bir wa ŋɔ, “Kummaa waa hoo de.”
Ɛlija kaa ŋɔ ú bir la guŋŋ buniidaanɛɛ.
44Buniidaanɛɛ hiŋ la, u wa ŋɔ, “N na baama lugɔ newee nonii maga, n na lii a muuzeŋ biinii.”
Awia, Ɛlija ŋɔ u be “Chɔ la ga ŋɔ Koori Ahab be, ‘Zuu i torko kaali, dooŋ gilɛɛ wa tɔi du ɛŋ.’ ”
45A guŋ saŋa, di dooŋ teŋ tinnɔ, peu izi, dozeŋ faari balaa. Awia, Koori Ahab faa zuu u zagu torko, di chɔ di ra kaali Jɛzriil. 46Denii Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa wa izi Ɛlija, u lau u tagtajaŋ kirsi u chara kiŋkiŋ, di chɔ ga tɔ Koori Ahab see guŋŋ di ga lii Jɛzriil.

english_text:
Elijah Runs Away from Ahab and Jezebel
1Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets. 2She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
3Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there, 4 then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.” 5Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep.
Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.” 6Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
7Soon the Lord's angel woke him again and said, “Get up and eat, or else you'll get too tired to travel.” 8So Elijah sat up and ate and drank.
The food and water made him strong enough to walk 40 more days. At last, he reached Mount Sinai, the mountain of God, 9and he spent the night there in a cave.
The Lord Appears to Elijah
While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
10 He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
11“Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.”
All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake. 12Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire.
Finally, there was a gentle breeze, 13and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave.
A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
14Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
15 The Lord said:
Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria. 16 Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
17Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
18 But 7,000 Israelites have refused to worship Baal, and they will live.
Elisha Becomes Elijah's Assistant
19Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
20Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said.
“You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
21Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_text:
Ɛlija n chɔwɛɛ kaali Bizeŋ Sinaai wia
1Denii Koori Ahab faa ga bagli gunla maa Ɛlija n ɛɛwɛ la ani gunla uŋ kpuuzi Baal dɔgtɛɛzi la maa tɛɛ u haaŋ Jɛzɛbɛl. 2Awia, Jɛzɛbɛl hum nɛr ú la Ɛlija be, di ga ŋɔ, “Vuga la kpuŋ, di kɛrɛ saŋa naa, di maa i miibɔɔ lizɛɛ gunla hiŋ ɛɛ vug Baal dɔgtɛɛzi la.”
3Denii ɔnsii faa lau Ɛlija, u chɔ ú lɛɛ u hiŋ. Uŋ wa hel Bɛɛsiba n du Juda hɛri, u gil u balii de, 4ka waabuu himmaa vol lugɔ hɔpizikpaŋ volaa, di ga zuu hɛribɔduma, di ga so daapuza bɛl zɛɛ, di suŋŋi wiizi lugɔ u vii siu, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, a kukkɔɔrɛ guŋ, lɛɛ n miibɔɔ, maa n naabaala bɔwɛɛ.”
5Denii u chɔɔ a daa zɛɛ, di foozi chɔɔ dɔɔ.
Kakpaŋ, mɛlika bɛl wa gbɔgzuu, di ŋɔ, “Izi di di!” 6Denii u binni u kɛra, di paanuu baŋ kpa niŋhɔla ɔɔzi ani nii lɔŋgɔnnɛ chigɛ, u hee ka nyɔɔ nii la, ka kaa billi chɔɔ.
7Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la kaa kuari ba u be bunɛɛhiŋ, di wa gbɔgzuu ka ŋɔ, “Izi di di, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ŋmɛnɛɛ la jaŋŋɔɔ werge.” 8Awia, u kaa izi di di, ka nyɔɔ. Un na fɔŋŋa lii a diwee be la, u wer vol guŋŋ hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ, di ga hel Bizeŋ Sinaai n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Bizennaniinanii la. 9Uŋ wa hel de la, u zuu bii bɔɔ bɛl, di chɔɔ de a hamuŋa hiŋ.
Kɔraawiizi n ba Ɛlija be wia
Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Ɛlija, beedee i ra ɛɛ ɛnnɛi?”
10U ŋɔ, “N siaahmuu hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ wia. Izrɛl hina la vɛɛ i ni baa nuukpaŋ dɔɔi labuu, di purgi i mbusu lizibɔra, di kpuuzi i dɔgtɛɛzi maa ni tokobizi. N bɛnnɛ kawɛɛ, ba kaa ra nyiŋŋi bá kpu n ge.”
11Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Lii ga chi a bizeŋ nyuu n see, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ wa ga de kaali.” Denii pezeŋ bɛl n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge wa lɔ bizenaa pergi, di purgi bia Kɔraawiizi see, ka u faa waa hoo a peu biini. A peu n wa kaalɛɛ, hɛri zigli werge, ka u faa waa hoo u gba biini. 12Guŋ ge n wa ɛɛwɛ tuŋ, ninlau ge ba, ka Kɔraawiizi faa waa hoo a ninlau gba biini. A niŋ ge harbɔɔ, u nuu munnaa. 13Ɛlija n wa nuu a munnaa, u tɛr u tagtajaŋ di fɔɔ u siwee, ka lii chi a bii bɔɔ la uŋ faa duwɛɛ la nua.
Denii loobii bɛl pɛɛzuu, “Beedee i ra ɛɛ ɛnnɛi, Ɛlija?”
14U ŋɔ, “N siaahmuu hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ wia. Izrɛl hina la vɛɛ i ni baa nuukpaŋ dɔɔi labuu, di purgi i mbusu lizibɔra, di kpuuzi i dɔgtɛɛzi maa ni tokobizi. N bɛnnɛ kawɛɛ, ba kaa ra nyiŋŋi bá kpu n ge.”
15Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Bir kpa ŋmɛnɛɛ la hiŋ kpawɛɛ ba la, di la Damaskus hɛribɔduma. Di i ga hel de, í waari baal bɛl banna yir Hazɛl nyuu nuu, ú ɛɛ Siiria koori. 16Kaa waari Nimsi biibaal Jehu nyuu nuu, ú ge ɛɛ Izrɛl koori. Kaa waari Safat biibaal Ɛlisa n lii Abɛl Mɛhɔla nyuu nuu, ú ge kpa i gawa, di ɛɛ n dɔgtɛɛ. 17Unla maa Hazɛl n waa nawɛɛ kpu, Jehu daŋ kpuu. Ɛlisa ge kpuuzi banla maa Jehu n waa nawɛɛ kpu. 18Ama, nɛra kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛrɛ n dɔɔ tɛɛ n hiŋ Izrɛl biini, ba waa giŋŋee jaami vug Baal gɛɛ di suuzuu.”
Ɛlisa yiraa wia
19Denii Ɛlija faa lii de di ga na Safat biibaal Ɛlisa, di u kpogli navargazi anɛɛ di ra par. Baala fidikpaŋ ge faa du u see, di kpogli navargazi anɛɛgaa di ra par. Ɛlija la u be, di ga kpa u tagtajaŋ laaluu. 20Denii Ɛlisa jaa gil paraa, ka chɔ di ra hiŋ Ɛlija, di ra ŋɔ, “Gil n ga ta n mɛɛ ni n maa, ka jaa waa hiŋii.”
Ɛlija ŋɔ, “Biraa la, ka ra liizi gunla miŋ ɛɛi la.”
21Awia, Ɛlisa giluu ka bir kaali, di ga lau u nauna anɛɛ la kpu. Di kpa a nauna baŋaa daazi la chem niŋ, di daali a ola, tɛɛ a nɛra ba hee, ka u izi di ra hiŋ Ɛlija, di birgi u hiini.

english_text:
Syria Attacks Israel
1King Benhadad of Syria called his army together. He was joined by 32 other kings with their horses and chariots, and together they marched to Samaria and attacked. 2Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel, 3“Ahab, give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your strongest sons!”
4“Your Majesty,” Ahab replied, “everything I have is yours, including me.”
5Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children. 6But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
7Ahab called a meeting with the leaders of Israel and said, “Benhadad is causing real trouble. He told me to give him my wives and children, as well as my silver and gold. And I agreed.”
8“Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
9So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.”
When Benhadad got his answer, 10he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
11Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
12Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
13At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
14“Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked.
The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.”
“But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked.
“You will!” the prophet replied.
15So Ahab called together the 232 young soldiers and the 7,000 troops in Israel's army, and he got them ready to fight the Syrians.
Israel Defeats the Syrians
16-17At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front.
King Benhadad of Syria and the 32 kings with him were drunk when the scouts he had sent out ran up to his tent, shouting, “We just now saw soldiers marching out of Samaria!”
18“Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
19The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle, 20and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses, 21but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots.
Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
22Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.”
Syria Attacks Israel Again
23Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained:
Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
24Here's what you should do. First, get rid of those 32 kings and put army commanders in their places. 25Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out.
Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
26In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel. 27The Israelites also prepared to fight. They marched out to meet the Syrians, and the two armies camped across from each other. The Syrians covered the whole area, but the Israelites looked like two little flocks of goats.
28The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
29For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed 100,000 Syrian troops. 30The rest of the Syrian army ran back to Aphek, but the town wall fell and crushed 27,000 of them.
Benhadad also escaped to Aphek and hid in the back room of a house. 31His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
32They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.”
“Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
33Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.”
“Go get him,” Ahab said.
When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
34Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.”
Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go.
A Prophet Condemns Ahab
35About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused, 36 and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
37The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
38The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
39When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay 3,000 pieces of silver. 40But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.”
Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
41The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets. 42The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
43Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_text:
Koori Bɛn Hadad n lɔ bolzeŋ Samaria hina laal wia
1Siiria Koori Bɛn Hadad faa chaali u laallɔɔra maa, koora tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni banɛɛ faa hiŋuu ni ba zagra ani torkozi. Denii u faa la ga fɔɔ bolzeŋ Samaria hina, di lɔ baa. 2Ka hum nɛra Izrɛl Koori Ahab bolzeŋ Samaria biini, di ra ŋɔ, “Kenne Koori Bɛn Hadad ŋɔ, 3‘I saliŋhuŋŋa ni i saliŋ maa ɛɛ n horaa, haali i hahnanaa ni i biikpega maa gba ɛɛ n horaa.’ ”
4Izrɛl koori sɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, n sɛɛwɔɔ, n ni n kuna maa ɛɛ i horaa.”
5Denii huŋhunna kaa bir ba di wa ŋɔ, “Kenne Koori Bɛn Hadad ŋɔ, ‘N ŋɔ bá wa kalii lugɔ n na nyiŋŋi i saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ, i haana ani i biizii. 6Awia, kɛrɛ saŋa naa dɔŋ, n daŋ hum n nabɔnzi, bá wa pigzi i kooridia ani i nabɔnzi diini na. Ba daŋ foozi kuna la maa n dɔɔ tɔna i be, di chi a maa kaali.’ ”
7Izrɛl Koori Ahab chaali u hɛri maa nabɔnzi di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií na gunla baal naa n na nyiŋŋi yaa ni wia! U hum n haana, biizi, saliŋhuŋŋa ani saliŋ bɔttɛ, mɔɔ kpollee.”
8Ka a nabɔnzi ni a nɛra la maa ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ waa hagzuu gɛɛ di wàá tɛu kuna la unna nyiŋŋi la.”
9Awia, u ŋɔ tɛɛ Koori Bɛn Hadad balaa la, “Ií ga ŋɔ n dɔɔri be, ‘I balii daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa hiŋ felee ŋɔ la, ka i tile nɛɛhiŋ naa waa, màá wer.’ ” Ba izi kpa a amaniye, di bir ga tɛɛ Koori Bɛn Hadad.
10Denii Koori Bɛn Hadad kaa tili Koori Ahab be, di ŋɔ, “Ń vuga tɛr n digni werge maa, gunla n dɛkkɛ, di maa bolzeŋ Samaria chɔkkɛ nyaamm! U yemmaa wàá ka ka, lugɔ n laallɔɔra kpa du ba nonee kaali.”
11Ka Izrɛl koori la bir ŋɔ, “Ií ga ŋɔ Koori Bɛn Hadad be, ‘Nɛr la n na laali u laal laala, waa dɛkkɛ unna ta bara lugɔ unla n na wiraa.’ ”
12Koori Bɛn Hadad faa nuu amaniye naabuu, di u ni a koora du ba tanti diini biine, di ra nyɔɔ siŋ. Denii u ŋɔ u laallɔɔra be, “Ií ɛɛ sirya di lɔ baa!” Awia, ba jaa ɛɛ sirya, bá lɔ bolzeŋ Samaria hina.
Koori Ahab n kpegli Koori Bɛn Hadad wia
13Guŋ n na ɛɛ la, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ bɛl ba Izrɛl Koori Ahab be, di wa ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘I na Siiria laallɔɔrakpila naa? N daŋ kpa baa du i nonee biini zinaa, denii i zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”
14Denii Koori Ahab pɛɛzi, “Ka anɛɛ n niŋ ɛɛ gunnɛi?”
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ hiŋ bir ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘A laallɔɔra biipɔllaa la pagazi nabɔnzi la n na binni labuu niŋ ɛɛ guŋ.’ ”
Koori Ahab kaa pɛɛzi, “Ka anɛɛ n niŋ faari a laallɛi?”
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ hiŋ ŋɔ, “Hinuu niŋ faaruu.”
15Awia, Koori Ahab jaa chaali u laallɔɔra biipɔllaa la pagazi nabɔnzi n na binni la maa, ba ɛɛ kalfaanɛɛ ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni banɛɛ. U kaa chaali Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ la, ba ge ɛɛ baala kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛ. 16Ba jaa izi wibaŋa bɛl di ra la, di Koori Bɛn Hadad ni koora tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni banɛɛ la, du ba tanti diini biine, di nyɔɔ siŋ di ra dɛɛzi. 17Koori Ahab laallɔɔra biipɔllaarɛ faa tɔ see.
A guŋ saŋa, di Koori Bɛn Hadad faa hum nɛra, bá ga binni na. Ba bir ba wa ŋɔ u be, “Baala vɔɔ laallɛ lii bolzeŋ Samaria di ra ba.”
18Koori Bɛn Hadad ŋɔ, “Di ba ra bau bá wa di kuu, ií lauri baa nyinee, di ba kaa ra bau bá wa lɔ laal ge, ií lauri baa nyinee.”
19Izrɛl laallɔɔra biipɔllaa la pagazi nabɔnzi n na binni la, faa vɔɔ lii a bolzeŋ biini di tɔ see, ka a laallɔɔra du ba har. 20Ba bɛl maa faa kpu u dɔm la u nuu n na naa la. Siiria hina n na gunla, ba chɔ, ka Izrɛl hina la ra duŋŋi baa. Siiria Koori Bɛn Hadad tinni zagu, u ni u zagtinna la baŋhina ge gba chɔ kaali. 21Ka Izrɛl Koori Ahab ni u laallɔɔra chɔ ga huuzi Siiria laallɔɔra la ni ba zagra ni a torkozi, di kpu baa werge.
22A guŋ harbɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la kaa bir ba Izrɛl koori la be, di wa ŋɔ, “Ɛɛ sirya nɛnnɛ, di guu i hiŋ, di na gunla n dɛkkɛ hin niŋ ɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, bina wem saŋa, Siiria koori la daŋ kaa wa lɔi laal.”
23Awia, Siiria koori nabɔnzi biruu liize, di ŋɔ, “Ba vuga ɛɛ giŋgimee vugaa. Awiarɛ ba dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge maa kaali yaa la. Ka di yaa ni baa lɔ dɔŋa lɛla biine, aana waa hoo, yaa daŋ kpegli baa. 24Awia, lizi koora tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni banɛɛ la, ka nyiŋŋi laallɔɔra nabɔnzi baŋhina du ba bɔra. 25A dɛkkɔɔ hiŋ kaa nyiŋŋi laallɔɔra ge, ba hel banla baŋ kpuuzɛɛ la, di nyiŋŋi zagra ni torkozi, a ge zuu anla n leuzee la bɔɔ. Di guŋ ɛɛwɔ, yaa daŋ jaa wer lɔ Izrɛl hina laal, lɛla biine. Guŋwaa, aana maa waa hoo, yaa daŋ wer kpegli baa.” Denii u nuu gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, di ɛɛ guŋ.
26Wem saŋa n wa helle, Koori Bɛn Hadad chaali Siiria hina, ba la Afɛk, bá ga lɔ Izrɛl hina laal. 27Izrɛl hina la ge n wa chaalɛɛ, ba tɛɛ baa ba laallɔɔrikuna, ba lii la bá ga chem baa. Izrɛl hina la ga chɔɔ chaŋ baa, di ɛɛ lugɔ buuna n chaalɛɛ chɔɔ bɔra anɛɛ, tama tama, ka Siiria hina la faa yaari de maa.
28Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la faa ba wa ŋɔ Izrɛl Koori Ahab be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Dikuu Siiria hina la n na fɛ lugɔ n ɛɛ giŋgimee Kɔraawiizii, ka maa lɛla waa Kɔraawiizi ɛɛwɛ wia, n daŋ kpa ba laallɔɔrakpila naa maa du i nonee biini, í jaa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”
29Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, di Siiria ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa du ba chɔɔribɔra chaŋ dɔŋa. A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl, ba jaa faari a laal. Izrɛl hina la kpu Siiria laallɔɔra la kagboŋa kalfa. 30Banla n kawɛɛ chɔ zuu bolzeŋ Afɛk biini, bɔr la koŋlii n faa cholle kpu ba nɛra kagboŋa tokko ni baniidaanɛɛ la. Koori Bɛn Hadad ge faa chɔ zuu a bolzeŋ biini, di ga suah diisee bɛl biini.
31Denii u nabɔnzi ŋɔ u be, “Na, yaa nuuwɔɔ lugɔ Izrɛl koora ɔɔ ra na nɛra sinyɛnaa. Gil ya kpa gbɔglɔnzi kirsi yaa charazi, di kpa ŋmɛnni vɔɔzi yaa nyuuni di la Izrɛl koori be, aŋhinabe, u daŋ na i sinyɛna, wàá ka kpui.”
32Ba jaa kpa gbɔglɔnzi kirsi ba charazi, di kpa ŋmɛnni vɔɔzi ba nyuuni, di la Izrɛl koori be, di ga ŋɔ, “I balii Koori Bɛn Hadad ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Jaande maa, gilɛɛ waa kpuŋ.’ ”
Denii Koori Ahab pɛɛzi, “U haa dɔɔ miibɔɔrɛa? U ɛɛ n lullii.”
33Koori Bɛn Hadad balaa n nuu gunla, ba fɛ lugɔ guŋ ɛɛ winanaarɛ, awia, ba sɛɛ manaŋ, di ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, i lulli Bɛn Hadad haa du denii!”
Koori Ahab ŋɔ, “Ií la ga kpogluu ba.” Koori Bɛn Hadad n wa ballɛ, Koori Ahab gil u zuu u himmaa torko biini.
34Denii Koori Bɛn Hadad ŋɔ, “N daŋ bir kpa bolzenaa la maa n mɛɛ n foozee lii i mɛɛ be la tɛi. I daŋ wer dauri yauzi Damaskus gunla n mɛɛ n faa ɛɛwɛ bolzeŋ Samaria la.”
Awia, Koori Ahab ŋɔ, “Di yaa daŋ ɛɛ nuukpaŋ waa, n daŋ gil i dɔɔ i hiŋ.” Denii u nuu ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, ka u giluu, u kaali.
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ n hau Koori Ahab ni wia
35A saŋa naa, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ u dɔgtɛɛ bɛl be, di u ŋɔ u dɔŋhiŋ be, “Kpa i dɔŋkuŋ lɔŋ!” Ka u dɔŋhiŋ la vɛɛ.
36Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ hiŋ ŋɔ, “Dikuu hiŋ waa Kɔraawiizi nua hiŋŋɛ wia, di i haŋ wa lii n be, bunyiŋ daŋ lawii.” U dɔŋhiŋ hiŋ n wa lii u be di ra kaali, bunyiŋ ga lawuu, di kpuu.
37Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la kaa ga na baal bɛl, di ŋɔ, “Jaande, lɔŋ!” Awia, a baal lɔu werge, di duu pira. 38Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la kpa chimu vɔɔ u siwee, di bɔg kur, ka la ga chi ŋmɛnikɛrii, di ra kpaŋ Izrɛl koori. 39Koori Ahab n waa bɛri, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la yiruu di ŋɔ, “I balii zuu a laal biinii, laallɔɔri bɛl kpogli u laal yom ba n be, di wa ŋɔ, ‘A du baal naa tau, di u haŋ wa leu, i miibɔɔrɛ í kpa turgi u kim gɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazuu í kpa turgi u kim.’ 40Ka i balii siwii n faa aahwɛɛ ni wia aŋhina wia, a baal chɔ di leu.”
Izrɛl koori ŋɔ, “I himmaa di i hiŋ seriyaa, i daŋ turgi a kim.”
41Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la jaa lau chimu la uŋ kpawɛɛ vɔɔ u siwee la, di wir manaŋ, Izrɛl koori la jaa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la bɛllɛ. 42U ŋɔ a koori be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘I gillɔɔ baal la miŋ aah siwii lugɔ u siu, ka i giluu wia, i miibɔɔrɛ i kpa turgi u miibɔɔ kim, i laallɔɔra ge kpa ba hora turgi u laallɔɔra hora kim.’ ”
43Baaŋfuuih ni biinichɔg lau a koori werge maa, u kaali u kooridia, bolzeŋ Samaria biini.

english_text:
Jezebel Has Naboth Killed
1Naboth owned a vineyard in Jezreel near King Ahab's palace.
2One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
3Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
4So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
5Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
6“I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
7“Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
8-10Jezebel wrote a letter to each of the leaders of the town where Naboth lived. In the letters she said:
Call everyone together and tell them to go without eating today. When they come together, give Naboth a seat at the front. Get two liars to sit facing him and swear that Naboth has cursed God and the king. Then take Naboth outside and stone him to death!
She signed Ahab's name to the letters and sealed them with his seal. Then she sent them to the town leaders.
11After receiving her letters, they did exactly what she had asked. 12They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front. 13The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
14The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
15As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.” 16Ahab got up and went to take over the vineyard.
Elijah Condemns Ahab
17The Lord said to Elijah the prophet, 18“King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over. 19Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ”
When Elijah found him, 20Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.”
Elijah answered:
Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates. 21Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free. 22Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
23 And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel. 24Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
25-29When Ahab heard this, he tore his clothes in sorrow and wore sackcloth day and night. He was depressed and refused to eat.
Some time later, the Lord said, “Elijah, do you see how sorry Ahab is for what he did? I won't punish his family while he is still alive. I'll wait until his son is king.”
No one was more determined than Ahab to disobey the Lord. And Jezebel encouraged him. Worst of all, he had worshiped idols, just as the Amorites had done before the Lord forced them out of the land and gave it to Israel.
translation_text:
Nabɔf grepu daazi koo wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, wii bɛl faa izi dikuu Jɛzriil hinuu bɛl banna yir Nabɔf grepu daazi koo wia. A koo naa faa du Jɛzriillɛ, di dugli Koori Ahab dia. 2Denii Koori Ahab ŋɔ Nabɔf be, “Kpa i koo naa tɛŋ ú birgi n hor, dikuubɛɛwiai, u dugli n diarɛ. N na nyiŋŋuu ń kpau kuari dɔpaŋhoori kambol. N daŋ tɛi u nanii bɛl di du u bɔɔ gɛɛ di i ra nyiŋŋi, n daŋ turgii u kim.”
3Ka Nabɔf ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi ra la a ni bɔɔnɛɛ lugɔ ń kpa n mɛɛwaa kapɛttɛ tɛi.”
4Awia, Koori Ahab kaali bol ani baaŋfuuih ni biinichɔg, dikuu Jɛzriil hinuu Nabɔf n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ, “Màá tɛi n mɛɛwaa kapɛttɛ wia.” Denii u chɔɔ u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni baaŋfuuih ni biinichɔg, di bir u siwee chaŋ koŋlii, di vɛɛ diwee dii.
5U haaŋ Jɛzɛbɛl zuu wa pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i biini chɔgi, i vɛɛ diwee diiyei?”
6Denii u ŋɔ u be “Guŋ ɛɛwɔɔ dikuu miŋ ŋɔ Jɛzriil hinuu Nabɔf la be lugɔ ú yoo u grepu daazi koo tɛŋ gɛɛ di u ra nyiŋŋi, n tɛu hɛri bɛl yembɛl di du u bɔɔ, ka u vɛɛ wia.”
7Ka Jɛzɛbɛl ŋɔ, “Kenne hìŋ́ Izrɛl koori maa ra ɛɛa? Izi di di, di gil i bɔra ra pur. N daŋ lɛɛ Jɛzriil hinuu Nabɔf koo la tɛi.”
8Awia, u faa kpa Ahab sɔŋ di sɛbi hɔna, di kpa u koori nonibisig jagaa, di kpaa hum ba ga tɛɛ bolzeŋ la Nabɔf n duwɛɛ la nabɔnzi. 9A hɔna biini, u faa sɛbɔɔrɛ,
“Ií dau nuuvɔɔi hɔpizii, di tɛɛ Nabɔf nabɔmbɔr, a hɔl, ú so. 10Ka ii gil karkanna banɛɛ chi u sibɔɔ, di kanni kara chuguu lugɔ u see Kɔraawiizi ni koori maanii nua. Denii ií lawuu lii, di lɔɔzuu bia kpu.”
11Awia, a nabɔnzi ni nɛzenaa la n du Nabɔf bolzeŋ la ɛɛ gunla maa Jɛzɛbɛl n ŋɔwɛɛ u hɔna la biine la. 12Ba sii, di dau nuuvɔɔri hɔpizii, di gil Nabɔf so nabɔmbɔr, a nɛra biini. 13Denii karkanna banɛɛ faa lii chi u see, di kanni kara chɔguu a nɛra maa see di ŋɔ, “Nabɔf see Kɔraawiizi ni yaa koori la maanii nua.” Awia, ba faa lawuu lii a bolzeŋ danzɛɛkɛrii, di lɔɔzuu bia kpu. 14Denii ba jaa tili Jɛzɛbɛl, di ŋɔ, “Ba lɔɔzi Nabɔfuu bia kpu.”
15Jɛzɛbɛl n haŋ waa nuu lugɔ ba lɔɔzi Nabɔfuu bia kpu la, u ŋɔ Koori Ahab be, “Izi la ga lɛɛ Jɛzriil hinuu Nabɔf grepu daazi koo la uŋ vɛɛwɛ ú yoo tɛi la dɔɔ. Waa kaa du de, u siuwɔɔ.” 16Koori Ahab n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Nabɔf siuwɔɔ la, u izi la u jaa ga lɛɛ u koo la di dɔɔ.
17Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Tisbi hinuu Ɛlija be, 18“Izi la ga huuzi bolzeŋ Samaria Koori Ahab. U du Nabɔf grepu daazi koo la uŋ laŋŋɛ ú ga lɛɛ dɔɔ labuu. 19Ŋɔ u be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Haa baal bɛl kpuwɛɛ lɛi ka foozi u kundɔɔlaa?’ Ŋɔ u be lugɔ kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Bɔr la nuuzihina n lenni Nabɔf chal la, denii a lenni i ge gba hor, wibii maa!’ ”
20Koori Ahab ŋɔ Ɛlija be, “N dɔm, i jaa nambuu!”
Ɛlija ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, n naibuu, hiŋ aah siwii wichɔgaa ɛɛi, Kɔraawiizi be wia. 21Awia, Kɔraawiizi ra ŋɔ i benii, ‘N daŋ gil hɛhchɔg chol i ni werge maa. N daŋ tuŋ i naanna maa, di kpu baal maa, haali yom gɛɛ unla n dɔɔ u hiŋ lii Koori Ahab naanna biini, Izrɛl hɛri. 22N daŋ gil i dia du lugɔ Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam ani Ahija biibaal Koori Baasa diini n faa du gunla, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ɛɛmbuu n baaŋ fuuh, di kaa gil Izrɛl hina ge ɛɛ wichɔgaa.’
23Jɛzɛbɛl ge wia biini, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Nuuzihina daŋ hee Jɛzɛbɛl, bolzeŋ Jɛzriil danzɛɛkɛrii. 24Nuuzihinaa niŋ hee Koori Ahab lulla la n niŋ siuzi bolzeŋ biini, ka duuni ge di banla n niŋ siuzi pir biini.’ ”
25Nɛr maa haa waa siwii aahwɛ wichɔgaa ɛɛi ni, Kɔraawiizi be, alugɔ Koori Ahab haaŋ Jɛzɛbɛl n chigɛ u har, u ɛɛ la. 26Koori Ahab faa ɛɛ wichɔgaa la Kɔraawiizi n kiiwe wergee, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra kuari vugaa alugɔ Amɔri hina la Kɔraawiizi n duŋŋɛɛ lii a hɛri, saŋa la Izrɛl hina n na ba la.
27Koori Ahab n wa nuu a wiŋɔzi naa, u tɛr u laala piili, ka kpa gbɔglɔŋ laala di laali, di vɔɔ nua. Ɔɔ faa chɔɔu hamuŋa maa ni a gbɔglɔŋ laala, di ɔɔ ra vol bɔɔiih ni biinichɔg, hɔpizi biimaa.
28Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Tisbi hinuu Ɛlija be, 29“I na gunla Koori Ahab n tuu u hiŋ n benɔu? Uŋ tuu u hiŋ n be naa wia, màá gil a hɛhchɔg chol u ni, u de dui saŋa. Ama, n daŋ gil u chol u domee ni, u biibaal de dui saŋa.”

english_text:
Micaiah Warns Ahab about Disaster
(2 Chronicles 18.2-27)
1For the next three years there was peace between Israel and Syria. 2During the third year King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to visit King Ahab of Israel.
3Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.” 4Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?”
“Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command. 5But first, let's ask the Lord.”
6Ahab sent for about 400 prophets and asked, “Should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?”
“Yes!” the prophets answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
7But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
8“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 9Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
10All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
11Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
12All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
13Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
14“I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
15Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
16“Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
17 He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
18Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring bad news!”
19 Micaiah replied:
Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 20The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 21then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
22“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it.”
23This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
24Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
25Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
26Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 27Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
28Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(2 Chronicles 18.28-34)
29Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 30Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
31The king of Syria had ordered his 32 chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 32So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them, 33they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
34However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
35The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He bled so much that the bottom of the chariot was covered with blood, and by evening he was dead.
36As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
37Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there. 38Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
39Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 40Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king.
King Jehoshaphat of Judah
(2 Chronicles 20.31—21.1)
41Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel. 42Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
43-46Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, and during his rule he was at peace with the king of Israel.
He got rid of the rest of the prostitutes from the local shrines, but he did not destroy the shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king, including his brave deeds and military victories, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
47The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
48Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed. 49Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
50Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Ahaziah of Israel
51Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
52Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin. 53Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Mikaaya n karfi Koori Ahab wia
1Binni ahoro biini, Siiria ni Izrɛl hina faa waa kaa ra lɔ laal. 2Ka binni ahorohiŋ la biini, Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa la ú ga na Izrɛl koori.
3Koori Ahab faa pɛɛzi u nabɔnzi, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yaa waa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ, yá bir lɛɛ Ramɔf Giliad hɛri lii Siiria koori benei? Yaa hotte!”
4Awia, u faa pɛɛzi Koori Jɛhɔsafat, “I daŋ la ga hiiniŋ ya lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hinaa?”
Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat ŋɔ, “N nii maa ɛɛ kpannɛ, n laallɔɔra ɛɛ i laallɔɔra, n zagra ge ɛɛ i zagra.” 5Koori Jɛhɔsafat ŋɔ Izrɛl koori be, “Pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi na mɔɔ.”
6Awia, Izrɛl Koori Ahab faa chaali dɔgtɛɛzi kalfaanaazu, di pɛɛzi baa, “Ń la ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hina laal gɛɛ n gilɛi?”
Ba ŋɔ, “La, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa baa du hìŋ́ koori nonee biini.”
7Ka Koori Jɛhɔsafat pɛɛzi, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ maa waa hoo ɛŋ, yaa n niŋ pɛɛzuu naa?”
8Ka Izrɛl Koori Ahab bir ŋɔ Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat be, “Baal bɛl haa du de, yaa n niŋ wer pɛɛzuu di zum Kɔraawiizi kipar, ka n hauhbuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa wiimaa baglɛɛ un niŋ wa ɛɛ n be, u du wer, di a chɔgaa bɛŋ lɛi. Waabuu Imla biibaal Mikaaya.”
Koori Jɛhɔsafat ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ ra ŋɔ guŋ!”
9Denii Izrɛl koori la ŋɔ u nabɔnzi bɛl be, “La ga yir Imla biibaal Mikaaya, dí u ba manaŋ.”
10A koora banɛɛ hiŋ jaa laali ba koorilaala, di so ba koorikassi ni, pila la n dugli bolzeŋ Samaria dominuuzeŋ la, ka a dɔgtɛɛzi maa jaa ra ŋɔ ba be gunla n niŋ wa ɛɛ. 11Ka ba bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Zɛdɛkia, u mɛɛ faa di Kɛnaana, faa luu lugbia nyigzi aŋhina, di ŋɔ Koori Ahab be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘I daŋ kpa nyigzi naa yagzi Siiria hina la guŋŋ di wa kpu baa nyaamm.’ ”
12A dɔgtɛɛzi la maa n kawɛɛ la faa ra ŋɔ guŋ himmaa, “La ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hina laal, i daŋ kpegli baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa baa du i nonee biini.”
13Nɛr la baŋ hummɛ ŋɔ ú ga yir Mikaaya la ŋɔ u be, “Na, a dɔgtɛɛzi la maa ra ŋɔu lugɔ a koori daŋ kpegli baa. Awia, ga gil i ni baa wiŋɔzi ɛɛ kpaŋ, í ŋɔ nɛnnɛ.”
14Ka Mikaaya ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de, gunla un niŋ ŋɔ n be, gunnɛ ń ŋɔ tɛu!”
15Uŋ ga hel ba be, Koori Ahab pɛɛzuu, “Mikaaya, ya la ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hina laal gɛɛ ya gilɛi?”
Mikaaya ŋɔ, “Ií ga lɔ baa, di kpegli baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa baa du hìŋ́ koori nonee biini.”
16Koori Ahab ŋɔ u be, “Buŋmɛnɛɛ ń gil i hɛɛhzi lugɔ hàá dariŋ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biinei?”
17Denii Mikaaya ŋɔ, “N na Izrɛl hina maa n yaari giŋgimee nyuunii alugɔ peeza n waa nɔɔni dɔɔwɛ. Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Nɛra naa waa sitɔɔri dɔɔwɛ. Gil bɛl maa ra la bol ni bampirsɔna.’ ”
18Izrɛl Koori Ahab ŋɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat be, “Maa i be ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u haa waa winanii maa baglɛɛ un niŋ wa ɛɛ n be, di wichɔgaa bɛŋ lɛiyaa?”
19Ka Mikaaya haa vɛɛ ŋɔ, “Awia, a nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii. N na Kɔraawiizi n soge u koorikara ni u bol, u mɛlikazi maa chaali chi baruu u nodig ni u nomɛɛl keŋkerezi maa. 20Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ dar Koori Ahab ú la ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hina laal, bá kpuuwɛi?’ Unnii ŋɔ keŋ, unnii ŋɔ keŋ. 21A tuna maa, duma bɛl jaa wa lii chi Kɔraawiizi see, di ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ daruu.’
22Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzuu, ‘Beedee i kpa ɛɛ gunnɛi?’
U ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ la ga kpa kara du u dɔgtɛɛzi maa nuuzi.’
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘I daŋ wer daruu, wibii maa. La ga ɛɛ guŋ.’
23Awiarɛ Kɔraawiizi kpa kara du i dɔgtɛɛzi naa maa nuuzi la. U baglɔɔrɛ lugɔ hɛhchɔg daŋ chol i ni.”
24Denii Kɛnaana biibaal Zɛdɛkia la ga chɛ Mikaaya lia, ka pɛɛzuu, “Saŋa bɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Duma lii n be di ga ŋɔ wia tɛinɛi?”
25Ka Mikaaya bir ŋɔ u be, “A hɔl la hin niŋ chɔ ga zuu diisee di suah labuu i zum.”
26Denii Izrɛl koori ŋɔ, “Ií lau Mikaaya di bir la ga tɛɛ a bolzeŋ binni Amɔn ni a koori biibaal Joas, 27ka ŋɔ, ‘Kenne koori ŋɔ, Ií tɔ baal naa dia di ra tɛu paanuu ni nii bɛŋ, guŋŋ n wa bir ba, ni alaanfia.’ ”
28Mikaaya ŋɔ ni bɔkpega, “Di i wa wetto bir ba ni alaanfia, guŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi waa n be gawɛɛ di ŋɔ wia.” Ka kaa ŋɔ, “Ií maa lɛɛ n wiŋɔzi naa di dau bɔr la nii n waa lul.”
Koori Ahab siu wia
29Denii Izrɛl koori ni Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat, faa kpa di la Ramɔf Giliad. 30Izrɛl koori ŋɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat be, “N daŋ bɔg, ba wàá ka zumiŋ, ka zuu a laal biini, ka hiŋwaa laali i koorilaala.” Awia, Izrɛl koori faa bɔg, di suah u hiŋ, ka zuu a laal biini.
31A saŋa, di Siiria koori la faa ŋɔ u torkozi ni a zagra nabɔnzi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni banɛɛ be, “Ií gilɛɛ waa lɔ nɛr maa, di Izrɛl koori bɛŋ lɛi.” 32Awia, Siiria torkozi ni a zagra nabɔnzi la n wa na Koori Jɛhɔsafat, ba fɛ lugɔ Izrɛl koorii, wibii maa, di bir bá yoou, ka Koori Jɛhɔsafat lɔ wile, 33a torkozi ni a zagra nabɔnzi n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Izrɛl koori lɛi, ba faa gil u duŋŋaa.
34Ka nɛbɛl faa ra taazi u hobee gunla maa, bɛl ga Izrɛl koori laal laala bɔchoŋŋii baambaaŋ, di yaguu. A koori jaa ŋɔ u torko miŋŋi be, “Kpogliŋ lii a kalu naa biini, ba dumbuu pira.” 35A laal faa kpekkoo a hɔl hiŋ werge maa, ka a koori dɛlli u torko biini, u siwee chaŋ Siiria hina la. Ka u pira la chal faa ra chuuri a torko biini. Awia, u siu a hɔl hiŋ duana ni. 36Wiizi n waa chol, nɛbɛl sii a laallɔɔra biini, di ŋɔ, “Baal maa bir di ra la u hɛri ni u bol!”
37Gunnɛ a faa ɛɛ, Koori Ahab siu, ba kpau ba bolzeŋ Samaria, di wa hug. 38Ka ba faa ga loori u torko, bolzeŋ Samaria pol bɛl, sɛnsɛnna n faa ra sɔ nii, nuuzihina wa lenni u chal gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.
39Koori Ahab wiɛɛlaa la n kawɛɛ u kora dii saŋa ani wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, u kooridia la uŋ faa mawɛɛ, di kpa bala nyina bɔg u biini ani bolzenaa la uŋ faa ma koŋlaa bar la, a maanii ba faa sɛbi du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. 40Koori Ahab faa jaa siu, ba huguu u naabaala hugribɔr, ka u biibaal Ahazia kpa u gawa, di di a kora.
Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat wia
41Izrɛl Koori Ahab kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ biinii, Koori Asa biibaal Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa di Juda kora. 42Binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔɔ Koori Jehosafat faa di, ka di a kora. U faa di a koraa binni tokko ni anue Jɛrusalɛm biini. U maarɛ faa Silhi biihaaŋ Azuba. 43Wiimaa biini, u faa hiŋ u mɛɛ Koori Asa hiŋaarɛ nɛnnɛ, di ɛɛ wideŋlaa Kɔraawiizi be. Ama, u faa haa waa vuga kuaribɔra la chɔkkɛ. Awia, a nɛra faa haa ra lizi mbusuzii, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma de. 44Koori Jɛhɔsafat ni Izrɛl koori la gba faa summɔɔ.
45Koori Jɛhɔsafat wiɛɛlaa la n kawɛɛ u kora dii saŋa ani wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ banni ni, u laal lɔi wia, a maanii ba faa sɛbi du Juda Koora Faala Hɔna biine. 46U faa duŋŋi vuga kuaribɔra basɛnsɛnna ni hahsɛnsɛnna la n kawɛɛ u mɛɛ Koori Asa kora dii saŋa la lii a hɛri. 47Awia, koori maa faa waa kaa hoo Ɛdɔm hɛri a saŋa. Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa lizi, nɛr la n na hiŋ u ni, u ra binni de ni.
48A saŋa hiŋ, Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa kuari kɔɔkɔɔzi muugberzenaare, á ɔɔ la Ɔfir hɛri, di gaa chi saliŋ. Ka a waa wette la de, a maanii faa chɔkkɛ muuzeŋ biini, Ɛziɔn Gɛba. 49A saŋa hiŋ, Koori Ahab biibaal Koori Ahazia faa ŋɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat be, “Gil n nɛra ni i nɛra ra saa a muugberzenaa.” Ka Koori Jɛhɔsafat vɛɛ.
50Denii Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa siu, ba huguu u naabaala hugribɔr la, Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini. Ka u biibaal Jɛhɔram faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.
Izrɛl Koori Ahazia wia
51Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat kora dii binni fidaaniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, Koori Ahab biibaal Koori Ahazia faa di Izrɛl kora, di du Samaria. Binni anɛɛrɛ u faa di a kora. 52Koori Ahazia faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ Kɔraawiizi be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa hiŋ u mɛɛ Koori Ahab, u maa Jɛzɛbɛl ani Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam ŋmɛnizi la n faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ wichɔgaa labuu. 53U faa ra kuari vug Baallɛ, di ra tɔgzuu, di faa gil Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la baaŋ fuuh, gunla u mɛɛ Koori Ahab n faa ɛɛwɛ la.

english_text:
The Lord Condemns Ahaziah
1-2Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah.
One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
3About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury. 4Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
5When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
