35Dan dee ge baala la n faa hel laal lɔi, faa du baala kagboŋa tokko ni ŋmantannaazi ani kalfaanumbɛl, 28,600,
36di lii Asɛ ge dee biini, laallɔɔra la n faa zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, di ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya, faa du baala kagboŋa tokkoanɛɛ, 40,000.
37Di lii Rubin, Gad ani Manasɛ dizi yeŋ domeezi yeŋa n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii baŋgia, di faa vɔɔ laal ni dɔŋkuna iri maa, faa du baala kagboŋa kalfa ni tokko, 120,000.
38Bannii maa faa ɛɛ laallɔɔraa, di faa lizi bahinaa di ra hum laal huma. Ba faa ba Hɛbrɔnnɛ di wa ɛɛ sirya lugɔ bá tɔ Koori Deevid Izrɛl maa kora. Izrɛl hina la maa gba n faa kawɛɛ, la faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ lugɔ bá tɔ Koori Deevid a kora. 39A laallɔɔra faa di hɔpizaa ahoroo Koori Deevid be, di ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba lulla faa tɛɛ baabuu a guŋ kuna. 40Haali ba dɔŋahina gba n faa lii bɔɔnɛɛzi, alugɔ Isaka, Zɛbulɔn ani Naftali hɛssi, faa gillɔɔ kauzi, zagra, nyugmazi ani navargazi chi diwee di waa tɛɛ baa. Ba faa dɔɔ kuŋkpila maanii lugɔ sau, fig ni grepu nɔŋhilaa baŋ ɛhzɛɛ mari dɔŋa, siŋ, nuu, nauna ani peeza, dikuubɛɛwiai, bɔsɔna faa du Izrɛl hɛrii.

english_text:
David Moves the Sacred Chest to Jerusalem
(2 Samuel 6.1-12a)
1Some time later, David talked with his army commanders, 2-3and then announced to the people of Israel:
While Saul was king, the sacred chest was ignored. But now it's time to bring the chest to Jerusalem. We will invite everyone in Israel to come here, including the priests and the Levites in the towns surrounded by pastureland. But we will do these things only if you agree, and if the Lord our God wants us to.
4The people agreed this was the right thing to do.
5David gathered everyone from the Shihor River in Egypt to Lebo-Hamath in the north. 6 Then he led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They went there to get the sacred chest and bring it to Jerusalem, because it belonged to the Lord God, whose throne is above the winged creatures on the lid of the chest.
7The sacred chest was still at Abinadab's house, and when David and the crowd arrived there, they brought the chest outside and placed it on a new ox cart. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio guided the cart, 8while David and the crowd danced and sang praises to the Lord with all their might. They played music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
9But when they came to Chidon's threshing place, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of the chest to stop it from falling. 10The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
11David then got angry with God for killing Uzzah. So he named that place “Attack on Uzzah,” and it's been called that ever since.
12David was afraid what the Lord might do to him, and he asked himself, “Should I really be the one to take care of the sacred chest?” 13So instead of taking it to Jerusalem, David decided to take it to the home of Obed-Edom, who lived in the town of Gath.
14 The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-Edom, his family, and everything he owned.
translation_text:
Baŋ bittɛ kpa Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ba wia
1Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi la maa n faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa gɛɛ kalfazi nabɔma, faa sogo bɔkpannɛ di na dɔŋa. 2Denii u jaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la maa n chaalɛɛ la be, “Di ii sɛɛwɔ, a kaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ge kipar, ií gil ya tili di kali yaa lulla la maa n du Izrɛl hɛri maa ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee la n du ba be ba bola ni ba laŋgarazi, lugɔ bá ba di wa jaa yaa ni. 3Ií gil ya bir ga kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di ba yaa be, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa faa waa u wia pɛɛzɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl kora dii saŋa la.” 4Denii nɛra la maa n faa chaalɛɛ la sɛɛ, dikuu guŋ n faa deŋlee ba maa be wia.
5Denii Koori Deevid chaali Izrɛl hina maa, di lii Muu Sihɔ n du Ijip guŋŋ di ga chug Hamaf Ŋmɛnɛɛ, lugɔ ba ga kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di lii Kiriaf Jiarim ba. 6Koori Deevid ni a nɛra faa la bolzeŋ Baala, ba ra yiruu Kiriaf Jiarim la, de du Juda hɛri la, bá ga kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ n sag u ni la, u ra di kora chɛrubzi baambaaŋ la.
7Denii ba faa la ga lizi a Dakka la lii Abinadab dia, di kpau hɔŋ torkofalii ni, di gil Uza ni Ahio ra du u tau, di ra bagli a nauna ŋmɛnɛɛ. 8Koori Deevid ni Izrɛl hina maa jaa ra sa, di ra yir yira ni ba fɔŋŋa maa, di ra lɔ kemzi, janjalanzi, di ra yigzi kuna, di ra lɔ pɛrɛtuzi, di ra huuh bensunozi di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi werge maa.
9Ka baŋ wa hel baal bɛl banna yir Kidɔn pila, a navargazi lɔ naa, Uza tɛr u nonii di lau a Dakka. 10Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Uza ni, u lɔu ta de, u siu u see, dikuu uŋ tɛr u nonii lau a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka wia.
11Denii Koori Deevid baaŋ fuuh, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n tɛr Uza digna ni baaŋfuuih wia. Ba jaa ra yir de Pɛrɛz Uza haali ni zinaa.
12A hɔl hiŋ, ɔnsii lau Koori Deevid dikuu Kɔraawiizi wia, u ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ Dakka naa ɛɛ ba n benei?” 13Awia, u faa waa a Dakka kpawɛɛ ba u be, bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm, ka jaa bir kpau la Gaf hinuu Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm dia. 14Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ jaa du Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm diahina be baaguzi ahoro. Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa kissi u diahina ani kuna la maa un dɔɔwɛ.

english_text:
David's Palace in Jerusalem
(2 Samuel 5.11-16)
1King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. They brought along carpenters and stone workers, and enough cedar logs to build David a palace. 2David now knew that the Lord had made him a powerful king of Israel for the good of his people.
3After David moved to Jerusalem, he married more women and had more sons and daughters. 4-7His children born there were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
David Defeats the Philistines
(2 Samuel 5.17-25)
8When the Philistines heard that David had become king of Israel, they came to capture him. But David heard about their plan and marched out to meet them in battle. 9The Philistines had already camped in Rephaim Valley and were raiding the nearby villages.
10David asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help me win?”
The Lord told David, “Yes, attack them! I will give you victory.”
11David and his army marched to Baal-Perazim, where they attacked and defeated the Philistines. He said, “I defeated my enemies because God broke through them like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.” 12Then David ordered his troops to burn the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
13Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley. 14David asked God what he should do, and God answered, “Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind them where the balsam trees are. 15Wait there until you hear the treetops making the sound of marching troops. That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army. So you must then attack quickly!”
16David obeyed God and he defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Gibeon to the entrance to Gezer.
17From then on, David became even more famous, and the Lord made all the nations afraid of him.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid wiɛɛlaa Jɛrusalɛm biini wia
1A saŋaa Taaya Koori Hiram hum u balaa Koori Deevid be, di gil ba kpa hɛriŋkpol daazi, ba ni kapintazi ani maara, bá wa ma kooridia tɛu. 2Koori Deevid jaa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ u kora hiŋ chi nɛnnɛ, di dɔɔ girme werge, dikuu u nɛra Izrɛl hina wia.
3Koori Deevid kaa kpa hahkpila Jɛrusalɛm biini di jaa, di lul biibaala ni biihaana kpila. 4Biibaala la baŋ lullɛ de tɛu la sɔnaa keŋ, Samua, Sobab, Netan, Solomɔn, 5Ibhar, Ɛlisua, Ɛlpɛlɛt, 6Nɔga, Nɛfɛg, Jafia, 7Ɛlisama, Bɛɛliada ani Ɛlifɛlɛt.
Koori Deevid n kpegli Filisti hina wia
8Filisti hina n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba waari Koori Deevid nyuurɛ nuu, di tɔu Izrɛl maa kora la, ba laallɔɔra maa vɔɔ lii, di gaa nyiŋŋuu. Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u lii la ú ga chem ba ni. 9Di Filisti hina la ballɔ wa lɔ Rɛfam Waluu hina laal, di foozi ba kuna. 10Awia, Koori Deevid faa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di na, di ŋɔ, “Ń la ga lɔ Filisti hina naa? I daŋ gil n kpegli baa?”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “A la, n daŋ kpa baa du i nonee biini.”
11Awia, Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la jaa izi di la Baal Pɛrazim, di faa ga kpegli baa, ka jaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n kpegli n dɔma alugɔ nii n suwee di kpu nɛra la.” Awia, ba jaa ra yir de Baal Pɛrazim. 12Filisti hina faa gil ba vuga ha de, Koori Deevid ŋɔ lugɔ ba fuuh a maa.
13Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Filisti hina kaa wa fɔɔ a waluu hina ni laal, di foozi ba kuna. 14Koori Deevid kaa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ deŋli baa di la, bar baa di la keŋkere bɛl, di lɔ baa balsam daazi la see. 15Di i haŋ wa nuu laallɔɔra naazi gbɔga a balsam daazi nyuuni, lii chem baa ni laal, dikuubɛɛwiai, guŋ daŋ bagli lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi tɔ i seere, ń kpu Filisti laallɔɔra hiŋ.” 16Denii Koori Deevid faa ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la. Ba jaa kpu Filisti laallɔɔra la, di lii Gibiɔn guŋŋ di ga hel Gɛza.
17Awia, Koori Deevid sɔŋ faa yaari a hɛssi maa. Kɔraawiizi gil a hɛssi maa hina faa ra ɔmuu.

english_text:
David Gets Ready To Bring the Sacred Chest to Jerusalem
1David had several buildings built in Jerusalem, and he had a tent set up where the sacred chest would be kept. 2 He said, “Only Levites will be allowed to carry the chest, because the Lord has chosen them to do that work and to serve him forever.”
3Next, David invited everyone to come to Jerusalem and watch the sacred chest being carried to the place he had set up for it. 4He also sent for Aaron's descendants and for the Levites. The Levites that came were: 5Uriel, the leader of the Kohath clan, and 120 of his relatives; 6Asaiah, the leader of the Merari clan, and 220 of his relatives; 7Joel, the leader of the Gershon clan, and 130 of his relatives; 8Shemaiah, the leader of the Elizaphan clan, and 200 of his relatives; 9Eliel, the leader of the Hebron clan, and 80 of his relatives; and 10Amminadab, the leader of the Uzziel clan, with 112 of his relatives.
11David called together these six Levites and the two priests, Zadok and Abiathar. 12He said to them, “You are the leaders of the clans in the Levi tribe. You and your relatives must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean and acceptable to the Lord. Then you may carry the sacred chest that belongs to the Lord God of Israel and bring it to the place I have prepared for it. 13The first time we tried to bring the chest to Jerusalem, we didn't ask the Lord what he wanted us to do. He was angry with us, because you Levites weren't there to carry the chest.”
14The priests and the Levites made themselves clean. They were now ready to carry the sacred chest 15 on poles that rested on their shoulders, just as the Lord had told Moses to do.
16David then told the leaders to choose some Levites to sing and play music on small harps, other stringed instruments, and cymbals. 17-21The men chosen to play the cymbals were Heman the son of Joel, his relative Asaph the son of Berechiah, and Ethan the son of Kushaiah from the Merari clan. Some of their assistants played the smaller harps: they were Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah. Others played the larger harps: they were Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Azaziah, and two of the temple guards, Obed-Edom and Jeiel.
22Chenaniah was chosen to be the music director, because he was a skilled musician.
23-24Four Levites were then appointed to guard the sacred chest. They were Berechiah, Elkanah, Obed-Edom, and Jehiah.
Finally, David chose priests to walk in front of the sacred chest and blow trumpets. They were Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer.
The Sacred Chest Is Brought to Jerusalem
(2 Samuel 6.12-22)
25David, the leaders of Israel, and the army commanders were very happy as they went to Obed-Edom's house to get the sacred chest. 26God gave the Levites the strength they needed to carry the chest, and so they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
27David, the Levites, Chenaniah the music director, and all the musicians were wearing linen robes, and David was also wearing a linen cloth. 28While the sacred chest was being carried into Jerusalem, everyone was celebrating by shouting and playing music on horns, trumpets, cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments.
29Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing in honor of the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_text:
Baŋ kpa Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ba Jɛrusalɛm wia
1Koori Deevid n wa ma diini u Bolzeŋ la biini tuŋ, u jaa kuari bɔr di baŋ tanti dia ú du Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la. 2Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Levi dee la bɛnnɛ ninna chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la, dikuubɛɛwiai, baabuu Kɔraawiizi lizi lugɔ ba ra chi a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka, di ra humuu saŋaa saŋa maa.”
3Awia, Koori Deevid chaali Izrɛl hina maa Jɛrusalɛm biini, ka ú kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di ba bɔr la uŋ kuarɛɛ, ú duu la. 4U faa chaali Aarɔn naanna ni Levi dee,
5di lii Kɔhaf naanna biini,
Uriɛllɛ faa ba sitɔɔri, u ni u lulla kalfa ni tokko, 120,
6di lii Mɛrari naanna ge biini,
ba sitɔɔrii Asaaya, u ni u lulla kalfaanɛɛ ni tokko, 220,
7banla n lii Gɛsɔn ge naanna biini,
ba sitɔɔrii faa Jowɛl, u ni u lulla kalfa ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, 130,
8Ɛlizafan naanna ge biini,
ba sitɔɔrii faa Sɛmaaya, u ni u lulla kalfaanɛɛ, 200,
9Hɛbrɔn naanna ge biini,
ba sitɔɔrii faa Ɛliɛl, u ni u lulla tokkoanaazu, 80,
10di lii Uziɛl naanna biini,
ba ge sitɔɔrii faa Aminadab, u ni u lulla kalfa ni fidaanɛɛ, 112.
11Denii Koori Deevid faa chaali Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Zadɔk, Abiata ani Uriɛl, di lii Levi dee ge biini, Asaaya, Jowɛl, Sɛmaaya, Ɛliɛl ani Aminadab, 12di ŋɔ ba be, “Iabuu Levi dizi sitɔɔra. Awia, ii ni ii dɔŋahina Levi dee la sɔ iihinaa, di lizi ii doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be, ka la ga kpa Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di ba bɔr la miŋ kuarɛɛ ń duu la. 13Ii Levi dee la n faa waa u ni ballɛ lugli la wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la baaŋ faa fuuh yaa ni la. Yaa faa wɔɔ pɛɛzɛɛ gunla un niŋ bagli yaa, ya ɛɛ.”
14Awia, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee faa sɔ lizi ba doŋa ha ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be, ka bá jaa wer la ga kpa Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ba. 15A Levi dee jaa kpa a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ani daajaŋra aŋhina n lawuu kpogli, di sag ba baŋaazi, gunla Moosis n faa baglɛɛ, di lii Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii biini la.
16Koori Deevid ŋɔ Levi dee la nabɔnzi be lugɔ ba lizi ba lulla baŋhina, bá ɛɛ yiryitta, di ra yir yirsuma di ra lɔ kemzi, janjalanzi ani pɛrɛtuzi. 17Awia, a Levi dee lizi Jowɛl biibaal Hɛman, di lii u lulla biini, di kaa lizi Bɛrɛkia biibaal Asaf ge ani Kusaaya biibaal Ɛtan ge di lii ba lulla Mɛrari domee ge biini. 18Ba ge be, banla n faa ballɛ di waa hiini baabuu, Zɛkaria, Jaaziɛl, Sɛmiramɔf, Jɛhiɛl, Uni, Ɛliab, Bɛnaaya, Maasɛya, Matitia, Ɛlifɛlɛhu, Miknɛya ani ba dominuuguure Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm ni Jɛyɛl.
19A yiryitta Hɛman, Asaf ani Ɛtannɛ ba faa lizi, ba ra lɔ danyɛ pɛrɛtuzi. 20Zɛkaria, Aziɛl, Sɛmiramɔf, Jɛhiɛl, Uni, Ɛliab, Maasɛya ani Bɛnaaya genii faa ra lɔ janjalanzi alugɔ Alamɔf, 21baŋhina genii Matitia, Ɛlifɛlɛhu, Miknɛya, Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm, Jɛyɛl ani Azaziaa faa ra tɔ see di ra lɔ ba kemzi gunla banna lɔ Sɛminif la. 22A Levi dee nabɔma Kɛnaniaa faa a yiryitta nabɔma. U humaa faa guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa zum yira yiraarɛ werge.
23Bɛrɛkia ani Ɛlkanaa ba faa lizi, ba ra guu Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la dia dominua. 24Sɛbania, Jɔsafat, Nɛtanɛl, Amasai, Zɛkaria, Bɛnaaya ani Ɛliɛza n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina labuu ba faa lizi ba ra huuh bensunozi a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka see. Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm ni Jɛhia genii faa ra guu a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la dia dominua.
Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la kpai la Jɛrusalɛm wia
25Denii Koori Deevid, Izrɛl nabɔnzi ani laallɔɔra kagboŋa nabɔnzi maa la ni bɔsɔna, bá ga kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di lii Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm dia, 26dikuu Kɔraawiizi n faa hiini Levi dee la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka wia, nabala aniidaanɛɛ ni pebala ge aniidaanɛɛrɛ ba faa kpa lizi mbusu. 27Koori Deevid faa laali pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii tagtajaŋ, gunla Levi dee la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka ani a yiryitta ni ba nabɔma Kɛnania n laalɛɛ la. Koori Deevid faa kaa laali tagtakpurii sag. 28Awia, Izrɛl hina la maanii faa laŋŋɛ ni bɔsɔna, di ra chaasi, di ra yir yira, di ra lɔ danyɛ pɛrɛtuzi, janjalanzi ani kemzi, di ga kpa a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka di ba. 29Baŋ kpa Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ di ra zuu Deevid Bolzeŋ la, Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ Mikal ga tokoro, di na Koori Deevid n na sa, di ra di u hiŋ, u wia ra fuuh u baaŋ.

english_text:
1They put the sacred chest inside the tent that David had set up for it, then they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. 2After David had finished, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord 3and gave every person in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins.
4David appointed some of the Levites to serve at the sacred chest; they were to play music and sing praises to the Lord God of Israel. 5Asaph was their leader, and Zechariah was his assistant. Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and another man named Jeiel were appointed to play small harps and stringed instruments. Asaph himself played the cymbals, 6and the two priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to blow trumpets every day in front of the sacred chest.
David's Song of Praise
(Psalms 105.1-15; 96.1-13; 106.1,47,48)
7That same day, David instructed Asaph and his relatives for the first time to sing these praises to the Lord:
8Praise the Lord
and pray in his name!
Tell everyone
what he has done.
9Sing praises to the Lord!
Tell about his miracles.
10Celebrate and worship
his holy name
with all your heart.
11Trust the Lord
and his mighty power.
Worship him always.
12Remember his miracles
and all his wonders
and his fair decisions.
13You belong to the family
of Israel, his servant;
you are his chosen ones,
the descendants of Jacob.
14The Lord is our God,
bringing justice
everywhere on earth.
15We must never forget
his agreement and his promises,
not in thousands of years.
* 16 God made an eternal promise
17to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
18when he said, “I'll give you
the land of Canaan.”
19At the time there were
only a few of us,
and we were homeless.
20We wandered from nation
to nation, from one country
to another.
21 God did not let anyone
mistreat our people.
Instead he protected us
by punishing rulers
22and telling them,
“Don't touch my chosen leaders
or harm my prophets!”
23Everyone on this earth,
sing praises to the Lord.
Day after day announce,
“The Lord has saved us!”
24Tell every nation on earth,
“The Lord is wonderful
and does marvelous things!
25The Lord is great and deserves
our greatest praise!
He is the only God
worthy of our worship.
26Other nations worship idols,
but the Lord created
the heavens.
27Give honor and praise
to the Lord,
whose power and beauty
fill his holy temple.”
28Tell everyone of every nation,
“Praise the glorious power
of the Lord.
29He is wonderful! Praise him
and bring an offering
into his temple.
Worship the Lord,
majestic and holy.
30Everyone on earth, now tremble!”
The world stands firm,
never to be shaken.
31Tell the heavens and the earth
to be glad and celebrate!
And announce to the nations,
“The Lord is King!”
32Command the ocean to roar
with all of its creatures
and the fields to rejoice
with all of their crops.
33Then every tree in the forest
will sing joyful songs
to the Lord.
He is coming to judge
all people on earth.
34 Praise the Lord
because he is good to us,
and his love never fails.
35Say to him, “Save us, Lord God!
Bring us back
from among the nations.
Let us celebrate and shout
in praise of your holy name.
36 Lord God of Israel,
you deserve to be praised
forever and ever.”
After David finished, the people shouted, “Amen! Praise the Lord!”
David Appoints Worship Leaders at Jerusalem and Gibeon
37David chose Asaph and the Levites in his clan to be in charge of the daily worship at the place where the sacred chest was kept. 38Obed-Edom and 68 of his relatives were their assistants, and Hosah and Obed-Edom the son of Jeduthun were the guards.
39David also chose Zadok the priest and his relatives who were priests to serve at the Lord's sacred tent at Gibeon. 40They were to offer sacrifices on the altar every morning and evening, just as the Lord had commanded in the Law he gave Israel. 41 Heman and Jeduthun were their assistants, as well as the other men who had been chosen to praise the Lord for his never-ending love. 42Heman and Jeduthun were also responsible for blowing the trumpets, and for playing the cymbals and other instruments during worship at the tent. The Levites in Jeduthun's clan were the guards at Gibeon.
43 After that, everyone went home, and David went home to his family.
translation_text:
1Ba kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di wa chiŋŋi Tanti Dia la biini, Koori Deevid n kuarɛɛ bá duu la, di lizi mbusuzi lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 2Koori Deevid n wa lizi a keŋ mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa ni dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi naa maa tuŋ, u jaa kissi a nɛra maa, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini. 3Ka jaa tɛɛ Izrɛl baal ni haaŋ maa paanuubire ni olɔɔzaa ani grepu nɔŋhilaa.
4U faa lizi Levi dee la baŋhinaa, bá ra hum Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum ni U Ni Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, di ra suŋŋi wiizi, di ra jaamuu, di ra chɔluu. 5Asafuu ba faa lizi u ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri, Zɛkariaa faa hiŋ u ni. Jɛyɛl, Sɛmiramɔf, Jɛhiɛl, Matitia, Ɛliab, Bɛnaaya, Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm ani Jɛyɛl, baabuu dɛkkɛ ba ra lɔ janjalanzi ni kemzi. Asaf ge ra lɔ danyɛ pɛrɛtuzi. 6Kizeehina Bɛnaaya ni Jahaziɛl genii niŋ ɔɔ ra huuh bensunozi, Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, saŋa maa. 7A hɔl hinnɛ Koori Deevid kpa yir naa tɛɛ Asaf ni u dɔŋahina, bá ra yir di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi.
8Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi, di ra sii u zenni wia.
Ií gil hɛssi maa hina
zum u wiɛɛlaa wia.
9Ií yir yira
di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi,
di ra bagli wizenaa la
uŋ ɛɛwɛ wia.
10Ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni, dikuu yaa n ɛɛ u hora wia,
di gil banla maa
n na jaamuu la bɔra ra pur.
11Ií dɛlli Kɔraawiizi ni u fɔŋŋazeŋ la,
di ra binni u siwee saŋa maa.
12Ií ra liizi wizenaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ,
u nuukpuuri wia
ani seriyazi la uŋ diwee.
13Kɔraawiizi balii Izrɛl naanna,
Jekɔb biibaala la
uŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ u hiŋ la.
14Waabuu Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum,
u widaulaa ɛɛ
durnya maa horaa.
15U ra liizi u nuukpaŋ la wiarɛ saŋa maa.
U ŋɔ nuarɛ tɛɛ
jiminizi kagboŋa nɛra.
16Nuukpaŋ naabuu u ni Abraham faa ɛɛ la,
nua la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ
tɛɛ Aizik la.
17Kɔraawiizi ni Jekɔb faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ,
nuukpaŋ la n niŋ du de
di hanna la.
18U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ kpa Keenan hɛri tɛi,
ú ɛɛ i kapɛttɛ.”
19Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ gunnɛ, saŋa la
u nɛra n faa haa waa kpil,
di ɛɛ hɔɔhra
di du Keenan hɛri la.
20Ba faa ra juuruu,
di ɔɔ lii hɛri naa di ga lii unnii,
di lii kora naa
di ga zuu kora bɛl biini.
21Ka Kɔraawiizi faa waa gillɛ
nɛr maa sunni baa.
Uŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi
ú guu baa la wia,
u faa hau koora ninɛɛ,
22di ŋɔ, “Ií gilɛɛ waa gbɔgzi
banla miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hiŋ la,
di gilɛɛ waa du
n dɔgtɛɛ maa pira.”
23Ií yir yira di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi!
Durnya hina maa,
ií yir yir di ra tɛu,
di ra darguu!
Ií ra sii hɔpizi biimaa,
amaniyesuma la
n na bagli ii lɛɛi wia la.
24Ií ra sii u girme la wia
di ra tɛɛ hɛssi maa hina
ani u nuukpuuri wia la
wia di ra tɛɛ nɛra maa.
25Kɔraawiizi zenni kannɔɔ,
di dɛg chɔlaa werge maa.
Waabuu dɛg ɔmaa
kaali vuga maa.
26A hɛssi maa vuga ɛɛ kuna la baŋ kuarɛɛnɛ,
ka Kɔraawiizii ta chiŋ.
27Girme ni zenni du u benii,
fɔŋŋa ge ni bɔsɔna
du u Dia.
28Hɛri naa hina maa, ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi.
Ií ra chɔli u girme
ani u fɔŋŋa la.
29Ií ra dargi Kɔraawiizi la n dɔɔ girme la.
Ií kpa sunzaa kuna ba u be.
Ií ra giŋŋi unla
n ɛɛ naniinanii la,
di u wa ballɔ.
30Durnya hina maa, ií gil ii bɔra ra sa u sibɔɔ!
Waabuu gillɛ hɛri
chi nɛnnɛ, waa ziigi la.
31Chiŋ ani hɛri, ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni!
Ií ŋɔ hɛssi hina maa be
lugɔ Kɔraawiizii koori!
32Muuzeŋ ani kunnyinee la maa n du i biini la,
ií ge gba ra ɛɛ guŋ.
Kooni ani kuna la maa n du ii biine,
ií ra di iihinaa alugɔ nɛra!
33Kɔr daazi maa ge daŋ yir yira ni bɔsɔna,
a daŋ yir yira Kɔraawiizi see,
di u wa ballɔ.
U ra bau ú wa di
durnya naa seriya.
34Ií ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u wia wessoo.
U nɔŋŋaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.
35Ií lɔ wile di ŋɔ,
“Lɛɛ yaa,
yaa Lɛɛri Kɔraawiizi.
Chaali yaa, di lɛɛ yaa lii
hɛssi hina nonee biine.
Ya kaa waa jaamii,
di ra dargi i sɔnnaniinanii la,
yaa bɔra sɔɔni
i chɔlaa biini.”
36Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la,
dɛg chɔlaarɛ, saŋaa saŋa maa!
A nɛra maa jaa ŋɔ, “Ami!” ani “Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi!”
37Koori Deevid faa gil Asaf ni u dɔŋahina la ra hum Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, di ra ɛɛ gunla maa n dɛkkɛ, bá ra ɛɛ hɔpizi biimaa la. 38U faa kaa gil Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm ni u dɔŋahina tokkoahoro ni ŋmantannaazi la ge ra hiini baa. Jɛdutun biibaal Ɔbɛb Ɛdɔm ni Hɔsa faa ɛɛ dominuuzenaa guure.
39Koori Deevid faa gil Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk ni u dɔŋahina faa ra binni ba jaamibɔr ni, di ra hum Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la biini, Gibiɔn, 40di ra lizi mbusuzi lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, di ra fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, chɔɔzi ni duana maa, di ra hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi widaulaa la uŋ sɛbɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la. 41Banla n faa du ba benii, Hɛman, Jɛdutun ani banla baŋ yir ba sɔna, di lizi baa ŋɔ bá ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nɔŋŋaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ. 42Hɛman ni Jɛdutunnɛ faa ra binni ba bensunozi huuih, ba danyɛ pɛrɛtuzi ani ba yira kuna saŋa la baŋ ɔɔ waa yir Kɔraawiizi chɔlaa yira la. Jɛdutan biibaalaa faa ra guu a dominuuzeŋ.
43Denii a nɛra maa jaa bir kaali ba bola. Koori Deevid ge bir la u bol, ú ga kissi u diahina.

english_text:
The Lord's Message to David
(2 Samuel 7.1-17)
1Soon after David moved into his new palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest is kept in a tent.”
2Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you—do what you want.”
3That night, the Lord told Nathan 4to go to David and tell him:
David, you are my servant, so listen carefully: You are not the one to build a temple for me. 5I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them. 6I chose special leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
7David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people. 8Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
9I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace. They will no longer have to tremble with fear—evil nations won't bother them, as they did 10when I let judges rule my people, and I will keep your enemies from attacking you.
Now I promise that like you, your descendants will be kings. 11I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried beside your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler, 12and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me. 13 I will be like a father to him, and he will be like a son to me. I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you. 14I will make sure that your son and his descendants will rule my people and my kingdom forever.
15Nathan told David exactly what the Lord had said.
David Gives Thanks to the Lord
(2 Samuel 7.18-29)
16David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. He sat there and prayed:
Lord God, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us, 17and yet you have promised to do even more for my descendants. You are treating me as if I am a very important person. 18I am your servant, and you know my thoughts. What else can I say, except that you have honored me? 19It was your choice to do these wonderful things for me and to make these promises.
20No other god is like you, Lord—you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true. 21And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so that your people could live here. 22You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
23 Lord God, please do what you promised me and my descendants. 24Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord All-Powerful rules Israel and is their God.”
My kingdom will be strong, 25because you are my God, and you have promised that my descendants will be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
26You are the Lord God, and you have made this good promise to me. 27Now please bless my descendants forever, and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already blessed my family, and I know you will bless us forever.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Koori Deevid wia
1Koori Deevid n jaa wa zuu u kooridia biini, u ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan be, “Na! Miŋwaa ra zuu diinanii la baŋ kpa hɛriŋkpol daazii di ma, ka Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la waa chi tanti dia biini.”
2Netan bir ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Ɛɛ gunla maa i bampirii n lauwɛ, Kɔraawiizi du i benii.”
3A hɔl hamuŋa ni, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Netan be,
4“La ga ŋɔ n balii Koori Deevid be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Hiŋ lɛi niŋ ma dia tɛŋ n na zuu. 5Maa dia maa biini duwɛɛ, di haŋ lii a hɔl la miŋ lɛɛ Izrɛl hina lii Ijip hɛri, di wa lii ni zinaa. Bɔr la maa n ni baa n ɔɔ la, tanti dia biinii n ɔɔ du. 6Bɔr la maa n ni Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ la, n haa ŋɔ ba sitɔɔri bɛl maa miŋ lizɛɛ ŋɔ u ra binni n nɛra ni be lugɔ ú ma hɛriŋkpol daazi dia tɛŋŋ?’
7Awia, ŋɔ n balii Koori Deevid be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔ, ‘N liziibuu lii peeza nɔɔnaa biini, di gil i di kora n nɛra Izrɛl hina ni. 8N du i benii bɔr la maa hiŋ faa laŋŋɛ, di gil i kpegli i dɔma maa. Filaŋkeŋ, n daŋ gil i dɔɔ sɔŋ alugɔ durnya nɛzenaa n dɔɔwɛ la. 9N daŋ tɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina sognibɔr, di gil bá so de, de ɛɛ ba himmaa hɛri, nɛr maa wàá kaa ra tɔɔri baa. Biinikpola hina wàá kaa ra fir baa gunla baŋ faa ra ɛɛ baa lugli la, 10saŋa la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n faa lizi sitɔɔra, bá ra tɔ n nɛra Izrɛl hina see la. Awia n daŋ kpegli i dɔma maa.
N na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii niŋ ma dia tɛi. 11Di i saŋa wa hello i ga chɔɔ i naabaala be, n daŋ gil i himmaa biibaal kpa i gawa, ń gil u kora chi nɛnnɛ. 12Waabuu niŋ wa ma Dia tɛŋ. N daŋ gil u kora chi di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. 13N daŋ ɛɛ u mɛɛ, ú ge ɛɛ n biibaal. N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá vɛɛ u nɔŋŋaa gunla miŋ faa vɛɛ unla n diwee ka tɛi la. 14N daŋ gil u ra binni n dia ni n kora ni, di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa. U kora wàá tuŋ maa.’ ”
15Netan jaa ga ŋɔ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la tɛɛ Koori Deevid.
Koori Deevid wiisuŋŋaa wia
16Denii Koori Deevid jaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia di so, ka ŋɔ,
“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, anɛɛ ń ni n diahinai, i teŋ ɛɛ wia di mag keŋ tɛɛ yaai? 17Alugɔ guŋ n waa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ i be gba. I kaa bagli gunla i balii diahina wia n niŋ wa du ŋmɛnɛbɛl. N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, i binnimbuu alugɔ minuu ɛɛ nɛtɔg werge di kaali nɛr maa.
18Ɛrɛɛ ń kaa ŋɔi? I zum mìŋ́ i balii biini maanii. 19N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, dikuu i balii ani i kipar wia, i ɛɛ wizeŋ naabuu, di gil n zum i nuuŋɔɔlizenaa la hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wia.
20N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, nɛr maa waa hoo lugɔi. Yaa himmaa digna nuuwɔɔ lugɔ i bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi. 21Hɛri maa hina waa hoo di ɛɛ lugɔ i nɛra Izrɛl hina, hiŋ lɛɛwɛ lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini, ba ɛɛ i hora la. Nuukpuuri wia la hiŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ baa la gillɔɔ i sɔŋ yaari durnya maa biini. I lɛɛ i nɛraa lii Ijip hɛri, di ɛɛ ɔnsii werge wia, di duŋŋi hɛssi hina la n du ba see, saŋa la baŋ liiwɛ di ra ba la. 22I gillɔɔ i nɛra Izrɛl hina ɛɛ i hora di hanna la, i birgi Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.
23N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, filaŋkeŋ, gil nua la hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ dikuu i balii ni u diahina wia la chi nɛnnɛ di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa. Ɛɛ gunla maa hiŋ ŋɔ nua la, 24guŋ gil i sɔŋ dɔɔ girme, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Denii nɛra jaa ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum labuu ra binni ba ni.’ I daŋ gil i balii Koori Deevid domee du de, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
25Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ tɛɛ i balii lugɔ i daŋ gil u naanna ra di kora. Awia, i balii dɔɔ bɔkpegaa ú suŋŋi wiizi naa. 26N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hinuu Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ nua lugɔ i daŋ ɛɛ winanaa naa tɛɛ i balii. 27Awia, a pariibuu filaŋkeŋ lugɔ i kissi i balii naanna, bá du de di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hinuu kissi baa, awia, ba daŋ na kissaa di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

english_text:
A List of David's Victories in War
(2 Samuel 8.1-14)
1Later, David attacked and defeated the Philistines. He captured their town of Gath and the nearby villages.
2David also defeated the Moabites, and so they had to accept him as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
3While King Hadadezer of Zobah was trying to gain control of the territory near the Euphrates River, David met him in battle at Hamath and defeated him. 4David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 chariot drivers, and 20,000 soldiers. And he crippled all but 100 of the horses.
5When troops from the Syrian kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed 22,000 of them. 6Then David stationed some of his troops in Damascus, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
7Hadadezer's officers had carried gold shields, but David took these shields and brought them back to Jerusalem. 8 He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Tibhath and Cun, which had belonged to Hadadezer. Later, Solomon used this bronze to make the large bowl called the Sea, and to make the pillars and other furnishings for the temple.
9-10King Tou of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Tou heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David on his victory. Hadoram also brought him gifts made of gold, silver, and bronze. 11David gave these gifts to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold he had captured from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.
12 Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed 18,000 of their troops. 13Then he stationed troops in Edom, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler.
Everywhere David went, the Lord gave him victory in war.
A List of David's Officials
(2 Samuel 8.15-18)
14David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
15Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army.
Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
16Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests.
Shavsha was the secretary.
17Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard.
David's sons were his highest-ranking officials.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid n kpegli u dɔma wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Koori Deevid faa la ga lɔ Filisti hina laal, di kpegli baa, ba sɛɛ u dɔɔra. U foozi Gaf ni u kɛraa bola maa, di lii Filisti hina nonee biini.
2Koori Deevid faa kpegli Moab hina ge. Awia, ba birgi u balaa, di ɔɔ lizi hɛri kuna di waa tɛu.
3Denii Koori Deevid faa lɔ Zoba Koori Hadadɛɛzaa laal, guŋŋ di ga hel Hamaf. A saŋa, di Koori Hadadɛɛza faa laŋŋɔ ú ga gil Muu Yufretis kɛraa bola maa birgi u hora. 4Koori Deevid foozi ba laal torkozi kagboŋ, di lauri a torko zuura ge kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛ ani laallɔɔra la ge n na vol kagboŋa tokko. Denii Koori Deevid gil ba chaahzi a zagra maa zaŋŋuzi, ka gil zagra kalfa n na tɛrgi torkozi hora.
5Siiria hina n lii Damaskus la n wa ballɛ, bá wa hiini Zoba Koori Hadadɛɛza, Koori Deevid faa kpu ba laallɔɔra kagboŋa tokko ni anɛɛ. 6Awia, Koori Deevid jaa kpa u laallɔɔra baŋhina di soŋŋi Damaskus n du Siiria hɛri, bá ra guu de, di dɔɔ ba fɔŋŋa, di gil ba ra lizi hɛri kuna di waa tɛu. Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ faa giluu Koori Deevid kpegli u dɔma, bɔr la maa uŋ ɔɔ la.
7Koori Deevid faa paagi laal pɛrɛtuzenaa la baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari, Koori Hadadɛɛza laallɔɔra nabɔnzi n kpoglee la, di ba Jɛrusalɛm. 8Di lii bolzenaa Tɛba ni Kun n faa ɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza hora la, Koori Deevid faa paagi danyɛ werge la Solomɔn n kpawɛɛ, di kuari Kolzeŋ la banna yir Muuzeŋ la, ligee ani tassakpila maa.
9Hamaf Koori Tuu n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Koori Deevid kpegli Zoba Koori Hadadɛɛza ni u laallɔɔra maanii la, 10Koori Tuu hum u biibaal Hadoram, ú ga jaami Koori Deevid, dikuu uŋ faa kpegli Koori Hadadɛɛza laal biini wia. Koori Tuu ni Koori Hadadɛɛza ge faa ra lɔ laallɛ. Hadoram faa kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa ani kuna irizi la maa baŋ kpa danyɛ kuari, di wa sunzi Koori Deevid.
11Koori Deevid faa kpa a kuna naabuu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, gunla uŋ faa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ la maa uŋ foozee lii hɛssi la hina uŋ kpeglee la maa be la. Baabuu, Ɛdɔm, Moab, Ammɔn, Filisti ani Amalɛk hina maa.
12Zɛruya biibaal Abisai faa kpu Ɛdɔm laallɔɔra kagboŋa fidiŋmantannaazii Yazi Waluu biini. 13U faa kpa u laallɔɔraa soŋŋi Ɛdɔm hɛri biini maa. Ɛdɔm hina maa jaa birgi Koori Deevid balaa. Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ Koori Deevid fɔŋŋa, u kpegli u dɔma, bɔr la maa uŋ laŋŋɛ.
Koori Deevid nabɔnzi wia
14Denii Koori Deevid faa di kora Izrɛl hina maa ni, di ra di wibii, di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa u nɛra maa be. 15Zɛruya biibaal Joabrɛ faa ɛɛ ba laallɔɔra maa nabɔma, Ahilud biibaal Jɛhɔsafat ge ɛɛ ba karchi di sɛbi ba wiɛɛlaa ra dau. 16Ahitub biibaal Zadɔk ani Abiata biibaal Ahimɛlɛk genii faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina. Savsa ge ɛɛ a koori karchi. 17Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaayaa faa ra binni Kɛrɛf ni Pɛlɛf hina ni. Koori Deevid biibaala ge faa ra biruu liize.

english_text:
Israel Fights Ammon and Syria
(2 Samuel 10.1-19)
1Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king. 2David said, “Nahash was kind to me, so I will be kind to his son.” He sent some officials to Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
But when David's officials arrived at Ammon, 3the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, “Do you really believe King David is honoring your father by sending these men to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our country, so he can come and destroy it.”
4Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off and their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away. 5They were terribly ashamed.
When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message that told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
6The Ammonites realized they had made David furious. So they paid 34 tons of silver to hire chariot troops from Mesopotamia and from the Syrian kingdoms of Maacah and Zobah. 7Thirty-two thousand troops, as well as the king of Maacah and his army, came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonite troops also left their towns and came to prepare for battle.
8David heard what was happening, and he sent out Joab with his army. 9The Ammonite troops marched to the entrance of the city and prepared for battle, while the Syrian troops took their positions in the open fields.
10Joab saw that the enemy troops were lined up on both sides of him. So he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Syrians. 11Then he put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and told them to fight against the Ammonites. 12Joab told his brother, “If the Syrians are too much for me to handle, come and help me. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you. 13Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the towns of our Lord God. I pray he will do whatever pleases him.”
14Joab and his soldiers attacked the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them. 15When the Ammonite troops saw that the Syrians had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab then returned to Jerusalem.
16As soon as the Syrians realized they had been defeated, they sent for their troops that were stationed on the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led these troops to Ammon.
17David found out what the Syrians were doing, and he brought Israel's entire army together. They crossed the Jordan River, and he commanded them to take their positions facing the Syrian troops.
Soon after the fighting began, 18the Syrians ran from Israel. David killed 7,000 chariot troops and 40,000 regular soldiers. He also killed Shophach, their commander.
19When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and accepted him as their new ruler. The Syrians never helped the Ammonites again.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid n kpegli Ammɔn ni Siiria hina wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Ammɔn Koori Nahas siu, ka u biibaal Hanun kpa u gawa, di di a kora. 2Denii Koori Deevid lɔ nfɛrɛ, di ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛ winanaa tɛɛ Koori Nahas biibaal Koori Hanun, dikuubɛɛwiai, u mɛɛ faa ɛɛmbuu winanaa.” Awia, Koori Deevid jaa hum nɛra bá ga jaami Koori Hanun, u mɛɛ lee.
Koori Deevid laallɔɔra n ga hel Ammɔn hɛri, di la bá ga jaami Koori Hanun, 3Ammɔn nabɔnzi ŋɔ Koori Hanun be, “I ɛɛ tamiirɛ lugɔ Koori Deevid n na tɔgzi i mɛɛ wiarɛ u gil nɛra naa ba, bá wa jaamii u leea? Ba waa ballɛ lɛi bá wa daani a hɛri na, ka wer wa kpegluuwaa?” 4Awia, Koori Hanun lauri Koori Deevid laallɔɔra la, di gil ba fuŋ ba taŋhuna, di mɔnni ba bɔmbɔga, bá zɛɛpume baambaana, ka duŋŋi baa.
5Nɛbɛl n wa bagli ba wia tɛɛ Koori Deevid, u hum u balaa bá ga chem ba ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa du baabuu hiihzi werge maa. Koori Deevid tili ba be, di ŋɔ, “Ií du bolzeŋ Jɛriko guŋŋ ii taŋhunazi wa hel mɔɔ, ka ii jaa ra ba.”
6Ammɔn hina n jaa wa zum lugɔ ba wia ra fuuh Koori Deevid baannɛ werge maa la, Koori Hanun ni Ammɔn hina kpa saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi kagboŋa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazu, bá ga kpa torkozi ni a zuura, di lii bolzenaa Naharam, Maaka ani Zoba n du Siiria hɛri. 7Ba faa ga kpa torkozi ani a zuura kagboŋa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anɛɛ, di kaa kpa Maaka koori ni u laallɔɔra, ba maa wa chaali chɔɔ di dugli Mɛdɛba. Ammɔn hina laallɔɔra ge faa ɛɛ sirya lii ba bola, bá ga yoo a laal.
8Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u hum Joab ni u laallɔɔra maa, bá ga lɔ baa. 9Ammɔn hina lii di chi, di ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya ba bolzeŋ dominua, ka koora la n ballɛ, bá wa hiini baa la ge ni ba laallɔɔra chi laŋgara.
10Denii Joab na lugɔ a laallɔɔra baŋhina chigɔ u seere, baŋhina ge chi u har. Awia, u lizi u laallɔɔra la baŋhina n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, Izrɛl laallɔɔra biini, ú ni baa yoo Siiria hina la. 11Ka gil u niwee Abisai ge tɔ banla n kawɛɛ la see, bá yoo Ammɔn hina la. 12Joab ŋɔ Abisai be, “Di Siiria hina haŋ waa kpegliŋ, a chɔ n wile, di Ammɔn hina ge waa kpeglii, n ge daŋ chɔ i wile. 13Chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega! Gil ya dɔɔ bampirii di yoo, di lɛɛ yaa nɛra ani Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la bolzenaa. Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ gunla n dɛkkɛ u be.”
14Joab ni u laallɔɔra la, bá ga lɔ Siiria laallɔɔra, ka Siiria laallɔɔra hiŋ bir chɔ. 15Ammɔn hina la n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Siiria hina la bittɔɔ di ra chɔ la, ba ge chɔ lii u niwee Abisai be, di bir zuu ba bolzeŋ la biini. Denii Joab bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.
16Siiria hina n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina kpegli baabuu la, ba hum nɛra bá ga yir Siiria laallɔɔra di lii Muu Yufretis wiifurii baŋgia di wa jaa, di gil Sofak n faa ɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza laallɔɔra nabɔma, ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri.
17Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u chaali Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa, ba gi Jɔɔdan muu, di ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya, di ga chi ba chignibɔra, di chaŋ Siiria laallɔɔra, di yoo baa. 18Ka ba chɔ lii Izrɛl hina be. Koori Deevid faa kpu ba torko zuura kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛ ani ba laallɔɔra la n na vol ge kagboŋa tokkoanɛɛ. U faa kaa kpu ba laallɔɔra nabɔma Sofak ge di jaa.
19Koora la maa n faa ra sɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza dɔɔra la, n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina kpegli baabuu la, ba la ga di kuu Koori Deevid be, di jaa birgi u balaa. Awia, Siiria laallɔɔra la faa waa kaa ɛɛ sirya lugɔ ba kaa hiini Ammɔn hina maa.

english_text:
The End of the War with Ammon
(2 Samuel 11.1; 12.26-31)
1 The next spring, the time when kings go to war, Joab marched out in command of the Israelite army and destroyed towns all over the country of Ammon. He attacked the capital city of Rabbah and left it in ruins. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
2Later, David himself went to Rabbah, where he took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about 34 kilograms of gold, and there was a valuable jewel on it. David put the jewel on his crown, then carried off everything else of value. 3He forced the people of Rabbah to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He also did the same thing with the people in all the other Ammonite towns.
David then led Israel's army back to Jerusalem.
The Descendants of the Rephaim
(2 Samuel 21.15-22)
4Some time later, Israel fought a battle against the Philistines at Gezer. During this battle, Sibbecai from Hushah killed Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were defeated.
5 In another battle against the Philistines, Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
6Another one of the Philistine soldiers who was a descendant of the Rephaim was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. During a battle at Gath, 7he made fun of Israel, so David's nephew Jonathan killed him.
8David and his soldiers killed these three men from Gath who were descendants of the Rephaim.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid n kpegli bolzeŋ Raba hina wia
1Wem maga, saŋa la koora n ɔɔ ra la laal la, Joab faa tɔ Izrɛl laallɔɔra seere, ba lii ga chɔgi Ammɔn hɛri, ka la ga fɔɔ bolzeŋ Raba ge, ka Koori Deevid waa faa du Jɛrusalɛm. Denii Joab faa lɔ bolzeŋ Raba, di puruu. 2Koori Deevid pilli ba vug Mɔlɛk kahuro baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari di lii u nyuu, di kpau hi. U tɔgzi faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ kilozi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazu. Ba faa kpa binanaa la yoola n kpollene, di margi u ni. Koori Deevid jaa paagi kuna la maa n dɔɔ tɔna werge, di lii a bolzeŋ biini, 3ka gil nɛra la maa n du de la lii, u du baa huma. Ba kpa sɔɔzi ni piŋgaasizi ani kpaŋfɔzi di ra hum. Ammɔn bola nɛra maanii Koori Deevid faa gil ba ra ɛɛ guŋ, ka u ni u laallɔɔra maa jaa bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.
Filisti hina lɔi wia
4Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, laal kaa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, bol bɛl banna yir Gɛza. A saŋaa Husa hinuu Sibɛkai faa kpu Rɛfa naannaa bɛl banna yir Sipai. Guŋ gil Filisti hina sɛɛ ba dɔɔra.
5Laal bɛl kaa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, Jayir biibaal Ɛlhanan ge faa kpu Gaf hinuu Goliaf niwee Laami la kandaa daa n faa gbosse lugɔ kɔɔrɛɛ daa la. 6Denii laal bɛl kaa wa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, Gaf. Bazeŋ bɛl n faa helle kpabaa, di dɔɔ nonibee ani naanibee anumbɛlaa, di ge ɛɛ Rafa naana bɛl, 7faa ra ɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa chɛɛtɛ. Awia, Koori Deevid niwee Simɛya biibaal Jonatan, faa lii di kpuu. 8Banniibuu faa ɛɛ Rafa naanna, Gaf. Ba maanii Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra faa kpu laal biini.

english_text:
David Counts the People
(2 Samuel 24.1-9)
1Satan decided to cause trouble for Israel by making David think it was a good idea to find out how many people there were in Israel and Judah. 2David told Joab and the army commanders, “Count everyone in Israel, from the town of Beersheba in the south all the way north to Dan. Then I will know how many people can serve in my army.”
3Joab answered, “Your Majesty, even if the Lord made your kingdom a hundred times larger, you would still rule everyone in it. Why do you need to know how many soldiers there are? Don't you think that would make the whole nation angry?”
4But David would not change his mind. And so Joab went everywhere in Israel and Judah and counted the people. He returned to Jerusalem 5and told David that the total number of men who could serve in the army was 1,100,000 in Israel and 470,000 in Judah. 6Joab refused to include anyone from the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he still disagreed with David's orders.
God Punishes Israel
(2 Samuel 24.10-17)
7David's order to count the people made God angry, and he punished Israel. 8David prayed, “I am your servant. But what I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Please forgive me.”
9The Lord said to Gad, one of David's prophets, 10“Tell David that I will punish him in one of three ways. But he will have to choose which one it will be.”
11Gad went to David and told him:
You must choose how the Lord will punish you: 12Will there be three years when the land won't grow enough food for its people? Or will your enemies constantly defeat you for three months? Or will the Lord send a horrible disease to strike your land for three days? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God who sent me.
13David was miserable and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
14So the Lord sent a horrible disease on Israel, and 70,000 Israelites died. 15Then he sent an angel to destroy the city of Jerusalem. But just as the angel was about to do that, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused the people, and he told the angel, “Stop! They have suffered enough.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
16David saw the Lord's angel in the air, holding a sword over Jerusalem. He and the leaders of Israel, who were all wearing sackcloth, bowed with their faces to the ground, 17and David prayed, “It's my fault! I sinned by ordering the people to be counted. They have done nothing wrong—they are innocent sheep. Lord God, please punish me and my family. Don't let the disease wipe out your people.”
David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place
(2 Samuel 24.18-25)
18The Lord's angel told the prophet Gad to tell David that he must go to Araunah's threshing place and build an altar in honor of the Lord. 19David followed the Lord's instructions.
20Araunah and his four sons were threshing wheat at the time, and when they saw the angel, the four sons ran to hide. 21Just then, David arrived, and when Araunah saw him, he stopped his work and bowed down.
22David said, “Would you sell me your threshing place, so I can build an altar on it to the Lord? Then this disease will stop killing the people. I'm willing to pay whatever you say it's worth.”
23Araunah answered, “Take it, Your Majesty, and do whatever you want with it. I'll even give you the oxen for the sacrifice and the wheat for the grain sacrifice. And you can use the threshing-boards for the fire. It's all yours!”
24But David replied, “No! I want to pay you what they're worth. I can't just take something from you and then offer the Lord a sacrifice that cost me nothing.”
25So David paid Araunah 600 gold coins for his threshing place. 26David built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. David prayed, and the Lord answered him by sending fire down on the altar. 27Then the Lord commanded the angel to put the sword away.
28When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayer, he offered more sacrifices there at the threshing place, 29-30because he was afraid of the angel's sword and did not want to go all the way to Gibeon. That's where the sacred tent that Moses had made in the desert was kept, as well as the altar where sacrifices were offered to the Lord.
translation_text:
Koori Deevid n kur u laallɔɔra wia
1Denii Sitaani faa ra nyiŋŋi u du Izrɛl hina wia biini, di dar Koori Deevid ú kur Izrɛl hina. 2Awia, Koori Deevid ŋɔ Joab ni u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi be, “Ií la ga kur Izrɛl hina, di lii Bɛɛsiba di ga hel bolzeŋ Dan. Ka jaa bir wa ŋɔ n be. N na nyiŋŋuu ń zum ba maga.”
3Ka Joab ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Jara, Kɔ́raawiizi gil u laallɔɔra wazi naa bukalfa, di kaali kennaa baŋ makkɛ naa. Jara, ba maa lɛi ɛɛ i balaa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi i ɛɛ kennei? Jara, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi Izrɛl hina maa di bilchɔgɛi?”
4Ka Koori Deevid faa waa nuuwɛ tɛɛ Joab. Awia, Joab faa izi gaagi Izrɛl hɛri maa, di kur a nɛra ka bir ba Jɛrusalɛm, 5di wa bagli baala la n niŋ wer lɔ laal maga tɛɛ Koori Deevid. Izrɛl maa biini, ba laallɔɔra la n niŋ wer kpogli tokobizi faa du baala kagboŋa kagboŋ ni kagboŋa kalfa. Juda ge laallɔɔra faa du kagboŋa kalfaanaazu ni tokkoahoro ni fi. 6Ka Joab faa waa Levi ni Bɛnjamin waa dizi la kutte, dikuubɛɛwiai, koori widaulii la faa wɔɔ pattɛ. 7A wii naa faa ɛɛ wichɔgiirɛ Kɔraawiizi be. Awia, u faa tɛr Izrɛl hina digna.
8Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, dikuu wii naa miŋ ɛɛwɛ naa wia! Gaafura, gil mìŋ́ i balii wichɔgaa tɛŋ. N ɛɛ gɛnni wiarɛ werge maa.”
9Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Koori Deevid sinaari Gad be, 10“La ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, dí kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘N na tɛibuu wia ahoro. Lizi bɛl, ń gil u huuzii.’ ”
11Awia, Gad la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Lizi unla n parii. 12Lɔchɔgii chol i hɛri binni ahoro gɛɛ i dɔma kpeglii baaguzi ahoro gɛɛ wiilchɔgii chol i hɛri naa hɔpizaa ahoro, Kɔraawiizi mɛlika ra kpuuzi Izrɛl hina, a hɛri yemmaanɛi?’ Awia, ŋɔ n be gunla min niŋ ga kali unla n humiŋ la.”
13Koori Deevid ŋɔ Gad be, “N biini chɔkkɔɔ werge maa! Gil Kɔraawiizi tɛr n digni, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nɛsunaa dɔɔi kannɔɔ werge maa, gilɛɛ gil newea tɛr n digni.”
14Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa gil wiilchɔgii chol Izrɛl hɛri, ba baala kagboŋa tokkoahoro ni fi siu. 15Kɔraawiizi faa hum u mɛlika lugɔ ú wa chɔg Jɛrusalɛm. Uŋ gaa ɛɛ gunla, Kɔraawiizi na guŋ, u biini kaa chɔgi, dikuu a tɔɔrɔɔzeŋ wia, u ŋɔ a mɛlika be, “Gil guŋ! A kukkɔɔrɛ!” A guŋ saŋa, di a mɛlika chigɔ Jɛbus hinuu Arauna pila.
16Koori Deevid binni chiŋ, di na Kɔraawiizi mɛlika n chigɛ chiŋ ni hɛri maa baambaaŋ, di tɛr u tokobi guali Jɛrusalɛm ni. Koori Deevid ni u nabɔnzi n laali gbɔglɔŋ laala la, chogli pi hɛri.
17Koori Deevid ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Miŋ lɛi ŋɔ bá kur a laallɔɔraa? Minuu ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Bannii waa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ peeza. Bɛɛ ba ɛɛi? N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, tɛr n ni n diahina digna. Gilɛɛ gil wiilchɔgii naa ra kpuuzi i nɛra.”
18Denii Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la tɛɛ Gad ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ ú la ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Izi tinni di la Jɛbus hinuu Arauna pila, di ga ma mbusu lizibɔr de tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.” 19Awia, Koori Deevid faa hiŋ gunla Gad n faa kpa Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ di ŋɔ la.
20A saŋa, di Arauna faa ra lɔ huuti. U wa ŋɔ u binni, di mɛlikaa. U biibaala banaazu n faa du u be, chɔ ga suah. 21Arauna n haŋ wa na Koori Deevid n na ba, u lii a pila ga giŋŋi u see, di willi u nyuu, u hile ga gbɔgzi hɛri.
22Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Kpa i pila naa tɛŋ, ń ma mbusu lizibɔr tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Aŋhinabe, a wiilchɔgii naa daŋ tuŋ. Yoo a pila tɛŋ gunla n parii.”
23Arauna ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Jara, kpau di ɛɛ gunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi. A nuu, n daŋ tɛi navargazi naa, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa. Daazi la baŋ kpawɛɛ ra lɔ a huuti la ge ɛɛ nindaazi, a huuti ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa hora. Minuu niŋ tɛi annii naa maa.”
24Ka Koori Deevid bir ŋɔ u be, “Akai, n na nyiŋŋuu ń yau de gunla n dɛkkɛ. Màá kpa kunla n ɛɛ i hor tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi gɛɛ di kpa kuna la n ɛɛ pɛɛ di lizi mbusu, di fuuh a kuna.”
25Awia, Koori Deevid faa turgi Arauna saliŋ kebisau kalfaanumbɛl, 26ka ma mbusu lizibɔr de tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di lizi mbusuzi lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi u ni. U faa suŋŋi wiizi, Kɔraawiizi nuu tɛu, di gil ninlau lii chiŋ, di wa fuuh mbusu lizaa kuna hiŋ de.
27Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia a mɛlika be, u bir kpa u tokobi suu u too biini. 28Koori Deevid n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi nuu u suŋŋaa labuu, Jɛbus hinuu Arauna pila la, u lizi mbusuzi de. 29A saŋa, di Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la Moosis n faa kuarɛɛ, di ba du hɛribɔduma ani mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la baŋ ɔɔ ra fuuh kuna u ni la, haa du ba jaamibɔr, Gibiɔn giŋgimii nyuu. 30Koori Deevid faa waa wette la de di ga pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi na, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi mɛlika tokobi labuu.

english_text:
1David said, “The temple of the Lord God must be built right here at this threshing place. And the altar for offering sacrifices will also be here.”
David Prepares To Build the Temple
2David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to come to Jerusalem. Then he assigned some to cut blocks of stone for building the temple. 3He got a large supply of iron to make into nails and hinges for the doors, and he provided so much bronze that it could not be weighed. 4He also brought an endless supply of cedar logs from the cities of Sidon and Tyre.
5He said, “The temple for the Lord must be great, so that everyone in the world will know about it. But since my son Solomon is young and has no experience, I will make sure that everything is ready for the temple to be built.”
That's why David did all these things before he died.
David Instructs Solomon To Build the Temple
6David sent for his son Solomon and told him to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel. 7 He said:
My son, I wanted to build a temple where the Lord my God would be worshiped. 8But some time ago, he told me, “David, you have killed too many people and have fought too many battles. That's why you are not the one to build my temple. 9But when your son becomes king, I will give him peace throughout his kingdom. His name will be Solomon, because during his rule I will keep Israel safe and peaceful. 10Solomon will build my temple. He will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. In fact, one of his descendants will always rule in Israel.”
11Solomon, my son, I now pray that the Lord your God will be with you and keep his promise to help you build a temple for him. 12May he give you wisdom and knowledge, so that you can rule Israel according to his Law. 13 If you obey the laws and teachings that the Lord gave Moses, you will be successful. Be strong and brave and don't get discouraged or be afraid of anything.
14I have all the supplies you'll need to build the temple: You have more than 3,000 tons of gold and over 34,000 tons of silver. There's also plenty of wood, stone, and more bronze and iron than I could weigh. Ask for anything else you need. 15I have also assigned men who will cut and lay the stone. And there are carpenters and people who are experts in working with 16gold, silver, bronze, and iron. You have plenty of workers to do the job. Now get started, and I pray that the Lord will be with you in your work.
17David then gave orders for the leaders of Israel to help Solomon. 18David said:
The Lord our God has helped me defeat all the people who lived here before us, and he has given you peace from all your enemies. Now this land belongs to the Lord and his people. 19Obey the Lord your God with your heart and soul. Begin work on the temple to honor him, so that the sacred chest and the things used for worship can be kept there.
translation_text:
1Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Ɛnnɛ dɛkkɛ bá ma Kɔraawiizi Dia ni mbusu lizibɔr, Izrɛl hina ɔɔ ra fuuh kuna u ni, di ra lizi mbusuzi.”
Kɔraawiizi Dia mai sirya ɛɛi wia
2Koori Deevid faa gil ba chaali hɔɔhra la maa n du Izrɛl hɛri. U binni ba biini di lizi bisɛɛhra bá sɛɛhzi bia, bá kpa ma Kɔraawiizi Dia. 3U faa lizi lugbia ge werge bá kpa kuari kpulozi di kpaahzi a Dia dominuuzi gbessi ani anla n niŋ lauraa kpogli. U kaa lizi danyɛ werge baŋ waa wer mɛgzi a tɔgzi. 4U faa kaa tɛɛ baa hɛriŋkpol daazenaa werge baŋ wàá wer kur, dikuubɛɛwiai, Saidɔn ani Taaya hina faa ba a kpila maa ninɛɛ, di wa tɛu.
5Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “N biibaal Solomɔn haa ɛɛ bichalaa, waa wia zummɛ nɛnnɛ. Dia naa ge yaa n niŋ ma tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi naa, dɛkkɔɔ uŋ wesse werge di dɔɔ girme ni sɔŋ, hɛssi hina maa be. Awia, n daŋ ɛɛ u sirya nɛnnɛ.” Denii Koori Deevid jaa ɛɛ u sirya nɛnnɛ mɔɔ ka siu.
6Awia, u yir u biibaal Solomɔn, di ŋɔ dí u ma Dia tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la. 7Kenne Koori Deevid ŋɔ Solomɔn be, “N biibaal, n na nyiŋŋuu ń vii ma Dia tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la sɔŋ. 8Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, ‘I kpu nɛraa werge maa, di kaa yoo laalkpila. Awia, hiŋ lɛi niŋ ma Dia di tɛŋ sɔŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, i kpu nɛraa werge n sibɔɔ, hɛri naa biini. 9Ama, i daŋ lul biibaal la n niŋ wa ɛɛ bampirsɔna hiŋ, di na heezaa. N daŋ gil u na heezaa lii u dɔma maa be. U sɔŋ daŋ di Solomɔn. N daŋ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina bampirsɔna, bá so bɔɔiih u kora dii saŋa. 10Waabuu niŋ wa ma n Dia. U daŋ ɛɛ n biibaal, ń ge ɛɛ u mɛɛ. N daŋ gil u kora chi di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.’
11Awia, n biibaal, Kɔ́raawiizi du i be filaŋkeŋ, í wer ma a Dia tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum, gunla uŋ ŋɔ i daŋ ɛɛ la. 12Kɔ́raawiizi tɛi laakal ani wia zɛɛ zumaa, di u wa gillɔ i ra di kora Izrɛl hina ni, guŋ gil í ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la Gbɔg. 13Di i ra hiŋ Gbɔgni ni widaulaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis, u tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la nɛnnɛ, i wia maa daŋ kuari. Chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega, di gilɛɛ gil ɔnsii waa lawii gɛɛ i bɔra waa huah.
14N hummɔɔ nɛnnɛ, di wer chaali Kɔraawiizi Dia la mai kuna, saliŋ tɔgzi n hel kilozi kagboŋa kagboŋ bɔra ahoro ni kagboŋa kalfaanaazu, saliŋhuŋŋa tɔgzi n hel kilozi kagboŋa kagboŋ bɔra tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazu, danyɛ ni lugbia werge baŋ wàá wer mɛgzi a tɔgzi ni daazi ani bia. Awia, nyiŋŋi aŋhina jaa. 15I dɔɔ huŋhunna kpilaa, bisɛɛhra, maara ani kapintazi. Di kaa dɔɔ nɛra la ge n zum huma maa nɛnnɛ. 16Banla n zum saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa, danyɛ ani lugbia huma maanii i dɔɔ, ba du kpil werge maa. Awia, faari a huma filaŋkeŋ. Kɔ́raawiizi du i be.”
17Denii Koori Deevid faa ŋɔ Izrɛl sitɔɔra maa be lugɔ ba hiini u biibaal Solomɔn. 18Kenne u ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la waa ii be duwɛɛ lɛiyaa? Waa ia tɛɛwɛ bampirsɔna lɛi, ii so bɔɔiih? U kpa hɛri naa nɛraa du n nonee biini, ba sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra dɔɔra. 19Awia, ií aah siwii di ra hum Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum ni ii biine, ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa. Ií faari di ra ma u Dia, ii wer kpa U Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka ani kuna la maa n ɛɛ kunnanaananaa, di ɛɛ u hora la, di wa du a Dia la yaa n niŋ ma di tɛɛ u sɔŋ girme la biini.”

english_text:
David Assigns the Levites Their Duties
1 David was old when he chose his son Solomon to be king of Israel. 2Some time later, David called together all of Israel's leaders, priests, and Levites. 3He then counted the Levite men who were at least 30 years old, and the total was 38,000. 4He said, “Twenty-four thousand of the Levites will be in charge of the temple, 6,000 will be temple officials and judges, 54,000 will be guards at the temple, and 4,000 will praise the Lord by playing the musical instruments I have given them.”
6David then divided the Levites into three groups according to the clans of Levi's sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
7Gershon had two sons: Ladan and Shimei. 8Ladan was the father of Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel. 9They were all family leaders among their father's descendants. Shimei was the father of Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. 10-11Later, Shimei had four more sons, in the following order: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah. But Jeush and Beriah didn't have many children, so their descendants were counted as one family.
12Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. 13 Amram was the father of Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were chosen to be in charge of all the sacred things. They served the Lord by offering sacrifices to him and by blessing the people in his name. 14-15Moses, the man of God, was the father of Gershom and Eliezer, and their descendants were considered Levites. 16Gershom's oldest son was Shebuel. 17Rehabiah, who was Eliezer's only son, had many children. 18The second son born to Kohath was Izhar, and his oldest son was Shelomith. 19Hebron, the third son of Kohath, was the father of Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam. 20Kohath's youngest son, Uzziel, was the father of Micah and Isshiah.
21Merari had two sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish. 22Eleazar had no sons, only daughters, and they married their uncle's sons. 23Mushi the second son of Merari, was the father of Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
24These were the clans and families of the tribe of Levi. Those who were 20 years and older were assigned to work at the Lord's temple.
25David said:
The Lord God of Israel has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever. 26 And so, the Levites won't need to move the sacred tent and the things used for worship from place to place. 27From now on, all Levites at least 20 years old 28 will serve the Lord by helping Aaron's descendants do their work at the temple, by keeping the courtyards and rooms of the temple clean, and by making sure that everything used in worship stays pure. 29They will also be in charge of the sacred loaves of bread, the flour for the grain sacrifices, the thin wafers, any offerings to be baked, and the flour mixed with olive oil. These Levites will weigh and measure these offerings.
30Every morning and evening, the Levites are to give thanks to the Lord and sing praises to him. 31They must also give thanks and sing praises when sacrifices are offered on each Sabbath, as well as during New Moon Festivals and other religious feasts. There must always be enough Levites on duty at the temple to do everything that needs to be done. 32They were once in charge of taking care of the sacred tent; now they are responsible for the temple and for helping Aaron's descendants.
translation_text:
Levi dee wia
1Koori Deevid n wa zɛŋŋɛ werge maa, u gil u biibaal Solomɔn di Izrɛl kora.
2U faa chaali Izrɛl hɛri sitɔɔra maa, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee. 3Ba faa kur a Levi dee la n ɛɛ baala di di binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni saga, ba ɛɛ baala kagboŋa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni ŋmantannaazi. 4Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Nɛra kagboŋa tokko ni anaazu daŋ lii bannii biini, di ra binni Kɔraawiizi Dia mai ni. Ba kagboŋa anumbɛl ge ɛɛ nabɔnzi ni sitɔɔra. 5Kagboŋa anaazu ɛɛ banla n ninna guu ba dominuuzi. Kagboŋa anaazu ge ɔɔ kpa kunlɔɔlaa la miŋ tɛɛ baa, bá kpa di yir yira ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la.”
6Koori Deevid faa bargi Levi dee la bɔra ahoro, di hiŋzi ba domeezi, Gɛsɔn, Kɔhaf ani Mɛrari.
Gɛsɔn domee wia
7Gɛsɔn domee hinaa,
Ladan ani Simei.
8Ladan biibaalaa,
Jɛhiɛl, u biibambilugli, di kpa Zɛtam ani Jowɛl.
9Simei ge biibaalaa,
Sɛlɔmɔf, Haziɛl ani Haran.
Ladan domeezi nabɔnzii faa la.
10Simei biibaalaa,
Jahaf, Ziza, Jɛyus ani Bɛria.
11Jahafuu u biibambilugli, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Ziza. Ka Jɛyus ani Bɛria waa faa waa biibaala kpila lullɛ. Awia, ba faa kur baa lugɔ domeekpaŋ.
Kɔhaf domee wia
12Kɔhaf ge biibaalaa,
Amram, Izhar, Hɛbrɔn ani Uziɛl.
13Amram ge biibaalaa,
Aarɔn ni Moosis.
Ba faa lizi Aarɔn ni u naannaa, bá ra lizi kunnanaananaa himmaa la doŋa, a ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora, bá ɔɔ kaa ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuna ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ra humuu di ra kissi nɛra u sɔŋ biini, saŋaa saŋa maa. 14Ka ba faa kur Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis waa biibaala, di jaa Levi dee ni.
15Moosis biibaalaa,
Gɛsɔm ani Ɛliɛza.
16Gɛsɔm naannaa,
Subɛl, u biibambilugli.
17Ɛliɛza ge naannaa,
Rɛhabia, u biibambilugli. Ɛliɛza faa waa kaa dɔɔ biibaala baŋhina maa jaa. Ama, Rɛhabia waa biibaala faa kpillɔɔ werge maa.
18Izhar biibaalaa, Sɛlɔmif, u biibambilugli. 19Hɛbrɔn ge biibaalaa, Jɛria, u biibambilugli, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Amaria, horohiŋ Jahaziɛl, naazuhiŋ Jɛkamiam.
20Uziɛl ge biibaalaa,
Maika, u biibambilugli, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Issia.
Mɛrari domee wia
21Mɛrari biibaalaa,
Mali ani Musi.
Mali ge biibaalaa,
Ɛliaza ani Kis.
22Ɛliaza faa waa biibaal maa lullɛ ka siu. Biihambizii u faa lul. Ba naara Kis biibaala faa paa baa.
23Musi biibaalaa,
Mali, Ɛda ani Jɛrimɔf.
24Banniibuu faa ɛɛ Levi naanna domeezi ni ba diini nabɔnzi baŋ sɛbɛɛ dau, di kur baa kpaŋkpaŋa. Ba faa di binni tokko ni sagaa, di ɛɛ huŋhunna Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini. 25Koori Deevid faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la tɛɛ u nɛraa bampirsɔna, di jaa wa du ba be Jɛrusalɛm biini, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. 26Awia, Levi dee waa kaa dɔɔ lugɔ ba ra chi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ani kuna la maa, baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra hum huma u biini la.” 27Di lii Koori Deevid wiŋɔɔlaa tuna biini, Levi dee la n faa hel binni tokko ka ra sag labuu ba faa kur.
28Levi dee humaa faa lugɔ ba ɔɔ ra hiini Aarɔn naanna, di ra hum Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, di ra du Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋee ani u diibizi tau. Bá ɔɔ lizi kuna la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ, di ra hum huma a Dia biini la doŋa ha, á ɛɛ kunnanaananaa saŋa maa. 29Baabuu faa ra du paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, sau la baŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra lizi mbusuzi, kɛrɛkɛssizi la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ, a ɔɔzaa ni a koozaa ni kuna mɛgzaa ni. 30Baabuu niŋ ɔɔ kaa chi chɔɔzi ni duana maa, di ra jaami Kɔraawiizi, di ra chɔluu, 31di ba wa fuuh kuna di lizi mbusu, di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Heezaa Hɔpizii gɛɛ Baagufalii Hɔpizizenaa ani Hɔpizizenaa aŋhina. Baabuu faa dɔɔwɛ lugɔ ba ra hum Kɔraawiizi huma saŋa maa, gunla n dɛkkɛ ban niŋ mag ani ŋmɛnizi la baŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ baa la.
32Awia, Levi dee faa ra hum ba humaa nɛnnɛ, Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia ani u Bɔnaniinanii la biini. Ba ɔɔ kaa hiini ba lulla Aarɔn naannaa, ba ra hum huma Kɔraawiizi Dia biini.

english_text:
David Assigns the Priests Their Duties
1Aaron's descendants were then divided into work groups. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. 2 But Nadab and Abihu died long before their father, without having any sons. That's why Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
3David divided Aaron's descendants into groups, according to their assigned work. Zadok, one of Eleazar's descendants, and Ahimelech, one of Ithamar's descendants, helped David.
4Eleazar's descendants were divided into 16 groups, and Ithamar's were divided into eight groups, because Eleazar's family included more family leaders. 5However, both families included temple officials and priests, and so to make sure the work was divided fairly, David asked God what to do.
6As each group was assigned their duties, Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the Levite wrote down the name of the family leader in charge of that group. The witnesses were David and his officials, as well as Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the family leaders from the clans of the priests and the Levites.
7-18Each group of priests went by the name of its family leader, and they were assigned their duties in the following order: Jehoiarib, Jedaiah, Harim, Seorim, Malchijah, Mijamin, Hakkoz, Abijah, Jeshua, Shecaniah, Eliashib, Jakim, Huppah, Jeshebeab, Bilgah, Immer, Hezir, Happizzez, Pethahiah, Jehezkel, Jachin, Gamul, Delaiah, Maaziah. 19These men were assigned their duties at the temple, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded their ancestor Aaron.
The Rest of the Levites Are Assigned Their Duties
20Here is a list of the other descendants of Levi:
Amram was the ancestor of Shubael and Jehdeiah.
21Rehabiah was the ancestor of Isshiah, the oldest son in his family.
22Izhar was the father of Shelomoth and the grandfather of Jahath.
23Hebron had four sons, in the following order: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
24Uzziel was the father of Micah and the grandfather of Shamir.
25Isshiah, Micah's brother, was the father of Zechariah.
26Merari was the father of Mahli, Mushi, and Jaaziah.
27Jaaziah had three sons: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri. 28-29Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish. Eleazar had no sons, but Kish was the father of Jerahmeel. 30Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
These were the descendants of Levi, according to their clans. 31Each one was assigned his duties in the same way that their relatives the priests had been assigned their duties. David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the family leaders of the priests and Levites were the witnesses.
translation_text:
Huma la baŋ faa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina wia
1Aarɔn naanna sugezii keŋ,
Aarɔn biibaalaa faa Nadab, Abihu, Ɛliaza ani Itama. 2Nadab waa ni Abihu faa feli ba mɛɛrɛ siu, di ba waa biibaala maa lullɛ. Awia, Ɛliaza ani Itama faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina. 3Ɛliaza naana Zadɔk ani Itama naana Ahimɛlɛkii faa hiini Koori Deevid, u bargi baa di du ba huma bɔra, bá ra hum. 4Ba faa bargi Ɛliaza naannaa sugezi fidaanumbɛl, di bargi Itama ge hora sugezi ŋmantannaazi, dikuubɛɛwiai, baala la n faa ɛɛ diini nabɔnzi faa kpillɔɔ Ɛliaza naanna biini, di kaali Itama hora. 5Awia, ba faa ta kunaa, bá zum banla n niŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia nabɔnzi ani kizeehina.
6Nɛtanɛl biibaal, Sɛmaaya la n faa ɛɛ Levi ni karchi la, sɛbi ba sɔna a koori ni a nabɔnzi see, di dau. A nabɔnzii faa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk, Abiata biibaal Ahimɛlɛk ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee domeezi nabɔnzi. Ba ɔɔ faa lizi domee bɛl nɛra lii Ɛliaza naanna biini, di lizi baŋhina ge lii Itama hora biini.
7Lugli kuntaalii faa chol Jɛhɔyarib ni,
nɛɛhiŋ ge chol Jɛdaaya ni,
8horohiŋ chol Harim ni,
naazuhiŋ chol Sɛyɔrim ni,
9nuehiŋ chol Malkija ni,
numbɛlhiŋ chol Mijamin ni,
10niidaanɛɛhiŋ chol Hakɔz ni,
ŋmantannaazihiŋ chol Abija ni,
11kabɛlhiŋ chol Jesua ni,
fihiŋ chol Sɛkania ni,
12fidikpaŋhiŋ chol Ɛliasib ni,
fidaanɛɛhiŋ chol Jakim ni,
13fidaahorohiŋ chol Hupa ni,
fidaanaazuhiŋ chol Jɛsɛbiab ni,
14fidaanuehiŋ chol Bilga ni,
fidaanumbɛlhiŋ chol Ima ni,
15fidaaniidaanɛɛhiŋ chol Hɛzir ni,
fidiŋmantannaazihiŋ chol Hapizɛz ni,
16fidikabɛlhiŋ chol Pɛtahia ni,
tokkohiŋ chol Jɛhɛzkɛl ni,
17tokko ni kpaŋhiŋ chol Jakin ni,
tokko ni anɛɛhiŋ chol Gamul ni,
18tokko ni ahorohiŋ chol Dɛlaaya ni,
tokko ni anaazuhiŋ chol Maazia ni.
19Kennaabuu ba faa lizi baa, ba ra hum Kɔraawiizi huma, di ba ɔɔ wa zuu u Dia la biini. Widaulaa la ba naabaal Aarɔn n faa dauwɛ tɛɛ baa, gunla Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la n faa bagluu lugɔ u ɛɛ labuu guŋ.
Levi dee la n kawɛɛ wia
20Levi dee la n kawɛɛrɛ keŋ,
Amram biibaallɛ Subɛl,
Subɛl ge biibaala, ba nabɔmaa faa Jɛdɛya.
21Rɛhabia biibambiluglii Issia.
22Izhar biibaalaa, Sɛlɔmɔf,
Sɛlɔmɔf ge biibaalaa, Jahaf.
23Hɛbrɔn biibaala, Jɛriaa u biibambilugli, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Amaria, horohiŋ ɛɛ Jahaziɛl, naazuhiŋ ɛɛ Jɛkamiam.
24Uziɛl biibaallɛ faa Maika,
Maika ge biibaallɛ Samir.
25Maika niwee ɛɛ Issia.
Issia ge biibaallɛ Zɛkaria.
26Mɛrari biibaalaa,
Mali ni Musi.
Jaazia biibaallɛ Beno,
27Mɛrari biibaalaa,
Jaazia, Bɛnɔ, Soham, Zakur ani Ibri.
28Mali biibaallɛ, Ɛliaza la n waa biibaal maa lullɛ la.
29Kis biibaallɛ,
Jɛramiil.
30Musi ge biibaalaa Mali, Ɛda ani Jɛrimɔf.
Levi dee la diini hinaa faa la. 31Ba faa kaa ta kuna, bá zum ba humazi, Koori Deevid, Zadɔk, Ahimɛlɛk, domeezi nabɔnzi, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee maa see, gunla ba kpɛɛma Aarɔn naanna n faa ɛɛwɛ la. Gunla baŋ faa ra tɔgzi ba biinabɔmahiŋ diahina la guŋ himmaanii ba faa ra tɔgzi ba bichalahiŋ diahina.

english_text:
David Assigns the Temple Musicians Their Duties
1David and the temple officials chose the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to be in charge of music. They were to praise the Lord by playing cymbals, harps and other stringed instruments. Here is a list of the musicians and their duties:
2Asaph's four sons, Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, were under the direction of their father and played music whenever the king told them to.
3Jeduthun's six sons, Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, were under the direction of their father and played harps and sang praises to the Lord.
4Heman had 14 sons: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamtiezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth. 5Heman was one of the king's prophets, and God honored Heman by giving him 14 sons and 3 daughters. 6His sons were under his direction and played cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments during times of worship at the temple.
Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman took their orders directly from the king.
7There were 288 of these men, and all of them were skilled musicians. 8David assigned them their duties by asking the Lord what he wanted. Everyone was responsible for something, whether young or old, teacher or student.
9-31The musicians were divided into 24 groups of twelve, and each group went by the name of their family leader. They were assigned their duties in the following order: Joseph, Gedaliah, Zaccur, Zeri, Nethaniah, Bukkiah, Asarelah, Jeshaiah, Mattaniah, Shimei, Uzziel, Hashabiah, Shebuel, Mattithiah, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Joshbekashah, Hanani, Mallothi, Eliathah, Hothir, Giddalti, Mahazioth, and Romamtiezer.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Dia yiryitta wia
1Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi faa lizi Asaf, Hɛman ani Jɛdutun biibaala baŋhinaa, bá ra hum Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi huma, di ra lɔ kemzi, janjalanzi ani danyɛ pɛrɛtuzi. Nɛra la n faa ra hum a huma naabuu keŋ,
2Di lii Asaf biibaala biini, Zakur, Joosɛf, Nɛtania ani Asarɛla. Asafuu faa ra binni u biibaala naa ni, ba ra ŋɔ gunla n niŋ wa huuzi nɛra, di koori haŋ wa ŋɔ ba ɛɛ guŋ.
3Di lii Jɛdutun ge biibaala biini, Gɛdalia, Zɛri, Jɛsaaya, Simei, Hasabia ani Matitia. Ba mɛɛ Jɛdutunnɛ faa ra binni ba ni, di ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi nɛra. Ba ɔɔ ra lɔ kemzi, di yir yira ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi, di ra jaamuu.
4Di lii Hɛman ge biibaala biini, Bukkia, Matania, Uziɛl, Subɛl, Jɛrimɔf, Hanania, Hanani, Ɛliata, Gidalti, Romamti Ɛza, Jɔsbɛkasa, Malɔti, Hɔtir ani Mahaziɔf. 5Koori sinaari Hɛman biibaalaa faa bannii maa. Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ nuarɛ lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ Hɛman a biibaala naa, bá gil u dɔɔ sɔŋ. Kɔraawiizi faa tɛubuu biibaala fidaanaazu ani biihaana ge bahoro.
6A baala naa maa mɛɛwaarɛ faa ra binni ba ni, ba ra lɔ danyɛ pɛrɛtuzi, janjalanzi ani kemzi, di ra hum Kɔraawiizi huma, Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini. A koorii faa ra binni Asaf, Jɛdutun, Hɛman 7ani ba lulla ni. Ba bagli baa nɛnnɛ, ba zum kuna lɔi ani yira yiraa, di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ba maa faa du baala kalfaanɛɛ ani tokkoanaazu ni ŋmantannaazi. 8Ba faa ɛɛ biipɔllaa ni nabɔnzii, baŋhina ɛɛ bagla, baŋhina ge ɛɛ hella. Ba faa ta kunaa, bá zum ba humazi.
9A lugli kuntaalii faa chol Joosɛf ni,
di lii Asaf dee biini,
u ni u biibaala ni u lulla faa du baala fidibanɛɛ.
Nɛɛhiŋ chol Gɛdalia
ni u lulla ni,
u biibaala faa du fidibanɛɛ.
10Horohiŋ chol Zakur ni,
u biibaala ni u lulla faa du fidibanɛɛ.

20Fidaahorohiŋ chol Subɛl ni,

21Fidaanaazuhiŋ chol Matitia ni,

english_text:
The Temple Guards Are Assigned Their Duties
1The temple guards were also divided into groups according to clans.
Meshelemiah son of Kore was from the Korah clan and was a descendant of Asaph. 2He had seven sons, who were born in the following order: Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, 3Elam, Jehohanan, and Eliehoenai.
4-5 Obed-Edom had been blessed with eight sons: Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai.
6-7Shemaiah was the father of Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, Elihu, and Semachiah. They were all respected leaders in their clan. 8There were 62 descendants of Obed-Edom who were strong enough to be guards at the temple.
9Eighteen descendants of Meshelemiah were chosen for this work.
10-11Hosah, from the Merari clan, was the father of Shimri, Hilkiah, Tebaliah, and Zechariah. Hosah had made Shimri the family leader, even though he was not the oldest son. Thirteen men from Hosah's family were chosen to be temple guards.
12The guards were divided into groups, according to their family leaders, and they were assigned duties at the temple, just like the other Levites. 13Each group, no matter how large or small, was assigned a gate to guard, and they let the Lord show them what he wanted done.
14Shelemiah was chosen to guard the East Gate. Zechariah his son was a wise man and was chosen to guard the North Gate. 15Obed-Edom was then chosen to guard the South Gate, and his sons were chosen to guard the storerooms. 16Shuppim and Hosah were chosen to guard the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road.
The guards were assigned the following work schedule: 17Each day six guards were on duty on the east side of the temple, four were on duty on the north side, and four were on duty on the south side. Two guards were stationed at each of the two storerooms, 18four were stationed along the road leading to the west courtyard, and two guards stayed in the court itself.
19These were the guard duties assigned to the men from the clans of Korah and Merari.
Guards Are Assigned to the Treasury
