13Solomon received almost 23 tons of gold each year, 14not counting what the merchants and traders brought him. The kings of Arabia and the leaders of Israel also gave him gold and silver.
15Solomon made 200 gold shields that weighed over three kilograms each. 16He also made 300 smaller gold shields that weighed almost two kilograms, and he put these shields in his palace in Forest Hall.
17His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold. 18It had a gold footstool attached to it and armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on each side of the throne, 19and there were two lion statues on each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
20Solomon's cups and dishes in Forest Hall were made of pure gold, because silver was almost worthless in those days.
21Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
22Solomon was the richest and wisest king in the world. 23-24Year after year, other kings came to hear the wisdom God had given him. And they brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
25 Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his horses and chariots, and he owned 12,000 horses that he kept in Jerusalem and other towns.
26 He ruled all the nations from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of Philistia in the south, as far as the border of Egypt.
27While Solomon was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as the sycamore trees in the western foothills. 28 Solomon's horses were brought in from other countries, including Musri.
Solomon Dies
(1 Kings 11.41-43)
29Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the records of Nathan the prophet, Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh, and Iddo the prophet who wrote about Jeroboam son of Nebat. 30After Solomon had ruled 40 years from Jerusalem, 31he died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_text:
Siiba Wiche n ba Koori Solomɔn be wia
1Siiba Wiche n wa nuu Koori Solomɔn sɔnzeŋ wia, u ba Jɛrusalɛm ú wa ɛɛu na, di pɛɛzuu wikpola aŋhina. U ba nyugmazi kpila werge ni, a chi dɔzi tiuzaa kuna, saliŋ werge ani binanaa la yoola n kpolle. Denii u ba Koori Solomɔn be, ba ŋɔ wia, u ŋɔ wia la maa n du u biini. 2Denii Koori Solomɔn faa bagli u pɛɛzaazi la maa zɛɛzi tɛu. Wiimaa faa waa kpol u be, u bagluu huhzi. 3A Siiba Wiche n wa nuu Koori Solomɔn nunzuma, di na kooridia la uŋ mawɛɛ, 4diwee la unna di, u nabɔnzenaa sogaa, u balaa laala, banla n na kpogli u sinlibizi laala ani mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa la uŋ lizɛɛ ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la, u nua faa kpu werge maa.
5U ŋɔ a koori be, “Wia la maa miŋ nuuwɛ n himmaa hɛri, a ra bagli i nunzuma ni wia la maa hiŋ ɛɛwɛ la, ɛɛ wibiire. 6Ama, n faa waa sɛɛwɛ, di miŋ ballɛ, n himmaa siwii wa na naa lɛi. Wibii maa, tama bɛŋ gbaa ba bagli tɛŋ. I nunzuma kaali gunla miŋ nuuwɛ labuu werge maa. 7Bɔsɔna hinaa i nɛra! Bɔsɔna hinaa i nabɔnzi la n ɔɔ chi i be saŋa maa, di ra nuu i nunzuma wiŋɔɔlaa la. 8Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la dɛg chɔlaarɛ. I wia paruubuu u gil i di kora, dikuu u nɔŋŋaa la uŋ nɔŋŋi Izrɛl hina, di ra nyiŋŋi bá du de saŋa maa wiarɛ, u gil i di kora, wibii dii ni wideŋlaa ɛɛi du de.”
9Denii u faa tɛɛ a koori saliŋ kilozi n bɛri kagboŋa anaazu, dɔzi tiuzaa kuna werge ani binanaa la yoola n kpolle. Nɛr maa ŋmɛnɛ maa faa wɔɔ kaa tɛɛ dɔzi kuna, a du wer lugɔ anla Siiba Wiche n tɛu la.
10Koori Hiram baala ani Koori Solomɔn baala faa chi saliŋ ni daananaa ani binanaa la yoola n kpolle lii Ɔfir hɛri, di ba. 11A koori faa kpa a daazi naa kuari lɔŋa Kɔraawiizi Dia ani u kooridia la. Di kaa kpaa kuari kemzi ni janjalanzi tɛɛ u yiryitta. Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa waa kaa na a dɔŋa Juda hɛri.
12Koori Solomɔn faa tɛɛ Siiba Wiche la kunla maa uŋ suŋŋɛɛ. U faa tɛubuu kuna kaali anla uŋ wa tɛu la. U ni nɛra la n duu ba la faa jaa bir kaali ba hɛri.
Koori Solomɔn daama wia
13Saliŋ gunla maga Koori Solomɔn n ɔɔ na bina maa biini tɔgzi ɔɔ faa ka tama ka a hel kilozi kagboŋa tokko ni ahoro. 14A waa ɔɔ jaa lampoo la uŋ ɔɔ faa na lii u kɔkɔɔza ani u nabɔnzi la n na binni a hɛri yeŋa la be. Haali Lɔrbizi koora ani Izrɛl hɛri yeŋa nabɔnzi, ɔɔ faa ba saliŋ ani saliŋhuŋŋaa ninɛɛ di waa tɛu.
15Koori Solomɔn faa kuari saliŋ laal pɛrɛtuzenaa kalfaanɛɛrɛ, di kpa saliŋ tɔgzi n na hel kilozi aniidaanɛɛ, di tɔ bɛl maa ni. 16U kaa kuari a jigzi ge kalfaahoro, di kpa saliŋ tɔgzi n na hel kilozi ahoro, di tɔ bɛl maa ni. A koori faa kpaa dau u kooridia loŋ la banna yir Lɛbanɔn Kɔr la biini.
17Denii a koori kaa kuari koorikarzeŋ bɛl, di kpa bala nyina tɔ u biini maa, ka kpa saliŋ himmaa ge tɔ u baŋgia. 18A koorikara faa dɔɔ lɔŋa anumbɛllɛ, ka u naazi chignibɔr faa ɛɛ saliŋ karjiga. A kara sognibɔr keŋkere bɛl maa faa dɔɔ nonii sagribɔttɛ, ba kuari bunyiŋ chiŋŋi bɛl maa kɛrii. 19Bunyinzi fidaanɛɛrɛ faa chigɛ a lɔŋa anumbɛl la ni. Bɛl maa chi lɔŋ maa tuna. Ba ŋmɛnɛ haa waa a koorikara naa dɔŋ kuarɛɛ tɛɛ hɛri maa koori. 20Koori Solomɔn kɔpuzi maanii faa ɛɛ saliŋ, haali u kooridia loŋ la banna yir Lɛbanɔn Kɔr biini gba tassazi ni viini maa faa ɛɛ saliŋ himmaanii. Ba faa waa saliŋhuŋŋa kpawɛɛ di kuari kummaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa wàá ra tɔgzi, Koori Solomɔn de dui saŋa la. 21U faa dɔɔ muugberkpilaa, ba kpaa ra kɔɔzi. Koori Hiram balaarɛ faa ra binni a ni. Binni ahoro maa biini, a ɔɔ biruu ba, di chi saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa, bala nyina, gbajaaguzi ani gbɛɛri irizi maa, di ba.
22Koori Solomɔn faa dɔɔ daama ani nunzumaa werge kaali koori maa, durnya naa biini. 23Koora ɔɔ faa lii durnya naa yemmaanii di ba u be, bá wa nuu di na nunzuma la Kɔraawiizi n tɛu la wia. 24Bina maa, nɛr la maa n ɔɔ faa ba, ɔɔ wa sunzuubuu saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ, laala, dɔŋkuna, dɔzi tiuzaa kuna, zagra ani kauzi.
25Koori Solomɔn faa dɔɔ zagra ni torkozi diini kagboŋa anaazuu. A zagra faa du kagboŋa fidaanɛɛ. U kpaa du torkozi bolzenaa la, aŋhina ge du u be, Jɛrusalɛm biini. 26Waabuu faa ra di kora, koora la maa n faa du Muu Yufretis di ga hel Filisti hɛri, guŋŋ di ga hel Ijip hɛri maga maa ni. 27Koori Solomɔn faa gillɔɔ saliŋhuŋŋa pur Jɛrusalɛm alugɔ bia, hɛriŋkpol daazi ge su bɔr maa alugɔ fig daazi n du giŋgimee zɛɛzi. 28Ijip hɛri ani hɛssi aŋhinaa Koori Solomɔn faa ra yau u zagra.
Koori Solomɔn siu wia
29Ama, Koori Solomɔn kora dii saŋa, u wiɛɛlaa maa, di lii u lugli saŋa di ga hel u tuna, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan Faala Hɔna biine, Silo hinuu Ahija Kɔraawiizi amaniye Faala Hɔna biine ani Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ido winaalaa n faa ra bagli Nɛbat biibaal Jeroboam wia, Faala Hɔna biine. 30Koori Solomɔn faa di Izrɛl maa koraa Jɛrusalɛm biini, binni tokkoanɛɛ. 31Uŋ wa siuwɛ, ba huguu u mɛɛ Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la biini, ka u biibaal Rehoboam faa kpa u gawa di di a kora.

english_text:
Some of the People Rebel against Rehoboam
(1 Kings 12.1-20)
1Rehoboam went to Shechem where everyone was waiting to crown him king.
2Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he returned from Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon. 3The people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said, 4“Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
5Rehoboam replied, “Come back in three days for my answer.” So the people left.
6Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
7They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should be kind and promise to make their work easier.”
8But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials. 9He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
10His younger advisors said:
Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak. 11He made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
12Three days later, Jeroboam and the others came back. 13Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. He spoke bluntly 14and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested. He said: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
15-19 When the people realized that Rehoboam would not listen to them, they shouted: “We don't have to be loyal to David's family. We can do what we want. Come on, people of Israel, let's go home! Rehoboam can rule his own people.”
Adoniram was in charge of the work force, and Rehoboam sent him to talk to the people. But they stoned him to death. Then Rehoboam ran to his chariot and hurried back to Jerusalem.
Everyone from Israel's northern tribes went home, leaving Rehoboam to rule only the people from Judah. And since that day, the people of Israel have been opposed to David's descendants in Judah. All of this happened just as Ahijah the Lord's prophet from Shiloh had told Jeroboam.
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina n di Koori Rehoboam mmɔri wia
1Denii Koori Rehoboam faa la bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm, bɔr la Izrɛl hina maa n faa chaalɛɛ bá tɔu kora la. 2Nɛbat biibaal Jeroboam la n faa chɔwɛɛ kaali Ijip hɛri, dikuu Koori Solomɔn wia la n wa nuu guŋ, u lii de di bir ba. 3Denii ba hum bá ga yir Jeroboam, u ni Izrɛl hina maa la Koori Rehoboam be, di ga ŋɔ, 4“I mɛɛ faa sunni yaabuu, yaa hum humkpega werge maa, ka di hiŋwaa daŋ gil yaa sunnaa, guŋwaa, yaa daŋ humii.” 5Koori Rehoboam ŋɔ, “Ií bir har ka ba hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl.” Awia, denii a nɛra kpa kaali. 6Koori Rehoboam pɛɛzi nabɔnzi la n faa ra hum u mɛɛ Koori Solomɔn u de dui saŋa la, “Ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔ tɛɛ a nɛra naanɛi?” 7Ba ŋɔ u be, “Di i daŋ suŋ ba ni, di ɛɛ ba kipar, di sɛɛ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, ba ge danna humii ni biinihuŋŋu saŋa maa.”
8Ka Koori Rehoboam vɛɛ a nabɔnzi baglaa hiŋ, ka pɛɛzi biipɔllaa la n ɛɛ u saara di ra humuu la. 9“Ɛrɛɛ ii ra fɛi? Ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔ nɛra naa n na ŋɔ n be lugɔ ń suŋ ba ni, di gil ba tɔɔrɔɔ bɔ naanɛi?”
10Denii u saara la ŋɔ u be, “Ŋɔ a nɛra naa n ŋɔ i be lugɔ i mɛɛ faa chug baabuu buntɔga, ka hiŋwaa gil a du fug tɛɛ baa. Ŋɔ ba be, ‘N nonibikeŋkelaa gbosso kaali n mɛɛ chara! 11N mɛɛ faa chug iabuu buntɔga, miŋwaa daŋ gil a nyaŋŋi. N mɛɛ faa viiri iabuu ni virinzi, bulaalizii miŋwaa kpa viiri ia.’ ”
12Hɔpizaa ahoro n wa helle, Jeroboam ni a nɛra maa bir la Koori Rehoboam be, gunla uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ bá bir ba u be hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl la. 13Denii a koori faa vɛɛ gunla a nabɔnzi n ŋɔwɛɛ la, di kaa nyɛg a nɛra ni werge maa, 14ka faa hiŋ biipɔllaa la baglaa la, di ŋɔ, “N mɛɛ faa chug iabuu buntɔga, ka miŋwaa daŋ gil a nyaŋŋi. N mɛɛ faa viiri iabuu ni virinzi, ka miŋwaa daŋ viiri ia ni bulaalizi!” 15Awia, a koori faa waa a nɛra suŋŋaa la nuuwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, a keŋ wiɛɛlaa naa faa lii Kɔraawiizi benii. Wia la Kɔraawiizi n faa ga u dɔgtɛɛ Silo hinuu Ahija be, di ŋɔ tɛɛ Nɛbat biibaal Jeroboam la, na ɛɛi.
16Izrɛl hina maa n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ a koori waa nuuwɛ tɛɛ baa la, ba ŋɔ u be,
“Yaa ni Koori Deevid naanna waa wiimaa kpauwɛ!
Bɛɛ bá ɛɛ tɛɛ yaai?
Awia, Izrɛl hina,
ií ra la ii bola!
Koori Deevid naanna,
ií ra binni iihinaa ni!”
Denii Izrɛl hina maa bir kaali ba bola. 17Ka Izrɛl hina la n faa du Juda bola la waa, Koori Rehoboam faa haa di koraa ba ni.
18Koori Rehoboam faa hum Adoniram la n na binni huma la baŋ ɔɔ fir nɛra ba ra hum la ni Izrɛl hina be, ka ba paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu. Ama, Koori Rehoboam waa faa ɛɛ ania, di zuu u zagra torko chɔ kaali Jɛrusalɛm. 19Awia, Izrɛl hina maanii faa izee di chi Koori Deevid naanna ni, di wa lii ni zinaa.

english_text:
Shemaiah the Prophet Warns Rehoboam
(1 Kings 12.21-24)
1After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and regain control of the whole country. So he called together 180,000 soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.
2Meanwhile, the Lord had told Shemaiah the prophet 3to tell Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin, 4“The Lord warns you not to go to war against the people from the northern tribes—they are your relatives. Go home! The Lord is the one who made these things happen.”
Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord's message and did not attack Jeroboam and his troops.
Rehoboam Fortifies Cities in Judah
5Rehoboam ruled from Jerusalem, and he had several cities in Judah turned into fortresses so he could use them to defend his country. These cities included 6Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa, 7Beth-Zur, Soco, Adullam, 8Gath, Mareshah, Ziph, 9Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah, 10Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. After he had fortified these cities in the territories of Judah and Benjamin, 11he assigned an army commander to each of them and stocked them with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine, 12as well as with shields and spears. He used these fortified cities to keep control of Judah and Benjamin.
The Priests and the Levites Support Rehoboam
13The priests and Levites from the northern tribes of Israel gave their support to King Rehoboam. 14And since Jeroboam and the kings of Israel that followed him would not allow any Levites to serve as priests, most Levites left their towns and pasturelands in Israel and moved to Jerusalem and other towns in Judah. 15 Jeroboam chose his own priests to serve at the local shrines in Israel and at the places of worship where he had set up statues of goat-demons and of calves.
16But some of the people from Israel wanted to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done. So they followed the priests and Levites to Jerusalem, where they could offer sacrifices to the Lord. 17For the next three years, they lived in Judah and were loyal to Rehoboam and his kingdom, just as they had been loyal to David and Solomon.
Rehoboam's Family
18Rehoboam married Mahalath, whose father was Jerimoth son of David, and whose mother was Abihail the daughter of Eliab and granddaughter of Jesse. 19Rehoboam and Mahalath had three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. 20Then Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom. Their sons were Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
21Rehoboam had 18 wives, but he also married 60 other women, and he was the father of 28 sons and 60 daughters. Rehoboam loved his wife Maacah the most, 22so he chose their oldest son Abijah to be the next king. 23Rehoboam was wise enough to put one of his sons in charge of each fortified city in his kingdom. He gave them all the supplies they needed and found wives for every one of them.
translation_text:
1Koori Rehoboam n wa hel Jɛrusalɛm, u chaali Juda domee hina ani Bɛnjamin dee la. Ba maa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfa ni tokkoanaazu, bá la ga lɔ Izrɛl domee la laal, di bir lɛɛ a kora tɛɛ Rehoboam.
2Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u dɔgtɛɛ Sɛmaaya be, 3“Ŋɔ Koori Solomɔn biibaal, Juda Koori Rehoboam ani Izrɛl hina la maa n du Juda ni Bɛnjamin la be, 4kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Ií gilɛɛ waa la, ii ni ii lulla gaa lɔ laal. Bɛl maa ra la u bol, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii gillɛ guŋ ɛɛ.’ ” Denii ba nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la, di bir kpo ba bola, ba waa kaa la ga lɔ Jeroboam laal.
Koori Rehoboam n ma koŋlaa bar bolzenaa wia
5Koori Rehoboam faa jaa so Jɛrusalɛm, di ma koŋlaa bar Juda bola á hiini baa, bá wer di ra guu bahinaa. 6Aabuu faa Bɛtlihɛm, Etam, Tɛkua, 7Bɛf Zur, Soko, Adulam, 8Gaf, Marɛsa, Zif, 9Adoram, Lakis, Azɛka, 10Zɔra, Aijalɔn ani Hɛbrɔn. A bolzenaa naa maanii faa ɛɛ ba bolzeŋkpega, Juda ni Bɛnjamin hɛssi biine. 11Koori Rehoboam faa kuari bɛl maa guuribɔraa nɛnnɛ, di lizi laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ba ra binni a ni. U faa ra tɛɛ baa diwee, ɔlivi nuu ani siŋ. 12U faa dau laal pɛrɛtuzenaa ani kandaazii, a bolzenaa naa maa biine, á du kpeg nɛnnɛ. Awia, Juda ni Bɛnjamin waa hɛssi faa ɛɛ u horaa.
13Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la waa n faa du Izrɛl hɛri maa, faa ra hiŋ Koori Rehoboannɛ. 14A Levi dee la faa gil ba sela diiribɔra ani ba kundɔɔlaa maanii, ka ba Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm, dikuubɛɛwiai, Koori Jeroboam ni u biibaala faa waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ bá ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina. 15Ka faa lizi u himmaa kizeehina, ba du ba giŋgimee nyuuni vuga kuaribɔra, di ra kuari vuga la uŋ mawɛɛ lugɔ buuna ni nabizi. 16Banla waa maa n faa lii Izrɛl dizi biine, ba bampiree lau Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, faa hiŋ a Levi dee ba Jɛrusalɛm, bá wa lizi mbusu kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la. 17Ba faa gillɔɔ Juda hɛri Koori Rehoboam kora chi nɛnnɛ, di chi u har binni ahoro, di ra hiŋ Koori Deevid ani Koori Solomɔn hiŋaa la, a guŋ saŋa.
Koori Rehoboam domee wia
18Koori Rehoboam faa kpa Mahalaf la mɛɛ n faa ɛɛ Koori Deevid biibaal Jɛrimɔf, u maa ge faa ɛɛ Abiheel n ɛɛ Jɛssɛ biibaal Ɛliab ge biihaaŋ. 19Mahalaf faa lul biibaala bahoro, Jɛyus, Sɛmaria ani Zaham. 20Koori Rehoboam kaa kpa Absalɔm biihaaŋ Maaka. U ge faa lul Abija, Atai, Ziza ani Sɛlɔmif. 21Koori Rehoboam faa ra nyiŋŋi Absalɔm biihaaŋ Maaka labuu kaali u haana ani u hahjigzi. U haana faa du fidaŋmantannaazi, u hahjigzi ge faa du tokkoahoro. U biibaala faa du tokko ni ŋmantannaazi, u biihaana ge tokkoahoro.
22Koori Rehoboam faa lizi Maaka biibaal Abija, u ɛɛ u biibaala maa nabɔma, ú wa wer gil u di kora wia. 23Koori Rehoboam faa ɛɛ nunzuma wiarɛ, di kpa u biibaala hiŋ soŋŋi Juda ni Bɛnjamin hɛssi biine maa ani bolzenaa la n ɛɛ ba bolkpega la biine, ba ɛɛ a nabɔnzi. U faa tɛɛ baabuu kuŋkpila, di paa hahkpila ge tɛɛ baa jaa.

english_text:
King Shishak of Egypt Invades Judah
(1 Kings 14.25-28)
1Soon after Rehoboam had control of his kingdom, he and everyone in Judah stopped obeying the Lord. 2So in the fifth year of Rehoboam's rule, the Lord punished them for their unfaithfulness and allowed King Shishak of Egypt to invade Judah. 3Shishak attacked with his army of 1,200 chariots and 60,000 cavalry troops, as well as countless Egyptian soldiers from Libya, Sukkoth, and Ethiopia. 4He captured every one of the fortified cities in Judah and then marched to Jerusalem.
5Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah had gone to Jerusalem to escape Shishak's invasion. And while they were there, Shemaiah the prophet told them, “The Lord says that because you have disobeyed him, he has now abandoned you. The Lord will not help you against Shishak!”
6Rehoboam and the leaders were sorry for what they had done and admitted, “The Lord is right. We have deserted him.”
7When the Lord heard this, he told Shemaiah:
The people of Judah are truly sorry for their sins, and so I won't let Shishak completely destroy them. But because I am still angry, 8he will conquer and rule them.
Then my people will know what it's like to serve a foreign king instead of serving me.
9 Shishak attacked Jerusalem and took all the valuable things from the temple and from the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
10Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe. 11Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he had finished worshiping.
12Rehoboam turned back to the Lord, and so the Lord did not let Judah be completely destroyed, and Judah was prosperous again.
Rehoboam's Rule in Judah
(1 Kings 14.21,29-31)
13Rehoboam was 41 years old when he became king, and he ruled 17 years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon. Rehoboam was a powerful king, 14but he still did wrong and refused to obey the Lord.
15Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king, including a history of his family, is written in the records of the two prophets, Shemaiah and Iddo. During Rehoboam's rule, he and King Jeroboam of Israel were constantly at war. 16When Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah became king.
translation_text:
Ijip Koori Sisak n lɔ Juda hina laal wia
1Koori Rehoboam kora n wa chigɛ nɛnnɛ, u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa la, u ni Izrɛl hina maa faa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni la hiŋaa. 2Dikuu baŋ faa waa Kɔraawiizi ra hiŋ ani wibii wia, Ijip Koori Sisak faa wa lɔ Jɛrusalɛm hinaa laal, Koori Rehoboam kora dii binni anuehiŋ biini. 3U faa kpa laal torkozi kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ, zagtinna kagboŋa tokkoahoro ani laallɔɔrakpila baŋ wàá wer kuruu lii Libia, Sukki ani Itiopiarɛ ba. 4Koori Sisak faa kpegli Juda bolzeŋkpega labuu, ka faa jaa ra la ú ga lɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina ge.
5Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Sɛmaaya faa ba Koori Rehoboam ni Juda hina nabɔnzi la n faa chaali Jɛrusalɛm biini be, dikuu banna ɔm Koori Sisak wia, di ŋɔ ba be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Ií vɛɛmbuu, awia filaŋkeŋ, n vɛɛ iabuu tɛɛ Koori Sisak.’ ”
6A koori ni Izrɛl nabɔnzi la sɛɛ chɔgri, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi hor deŋloore, u hor summɔɔ.”
7Kɔraawiizi n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba sɛɛ chɔgrii la, u ŋɔ u dɔgtɛɛ Sɛmaaya be, “Baŋ sɛɛ chɔgri wia, màá ka chɔgi baa. Awia, n daŋ lɛɛ baa. Màá ka ga Koori Sisak ni, di gil n baaŋ fuuh Jɛrusalɛm hina ni. 8Ama, ba daŋ birgi u balaa, gunnɛ bá zum gunla n humaa ani hɛrdumazi koora humaa n kuttɛ.”
9Ijip Koori Sisak n wa lɔ Jɛrusalɛm laal la, u faa chi Kɔraawiizi Dia ni a kooridia daama kuna la maa kaali. Kummaanii u faa chi, haali laal pɛrɛtuzenaa la Koori Solomɔn n faa kpa saliŋ kuari la gba. 10Awia, Koori Rehoboam faa kpa danyɛ luu aŋhina du a bɔɔ. Ka faa gil ba tauduura nabɔnzi la n na binni a kooridia dominua la ra du a tau. 11Saŋa maa, di a koori haŋ waa la Kɔraawiizi Dia, a tauduura la ɔɔ faa chiabuu di ra hiŋuu, ka bir chia ba a chɔɔribɔr.
12Dikuu Koori Rehoboam n faa sɔɔni siwii wia, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa waa kaa fuuh u ni. Awia, u faa wɔɔ kaa kpu. Wibii maa, ka winanaa faa haa du Juda hɛrii.
13Koori Rehoboam faa sogo Jɛrusalɛmnɛ di ra di kora, u fɔŋŋa ra jaa. U binni faa du tokkoanɛɛ ni kpaŋ. U faa di a koraa binni fidaaniidaanɛɛ, Jɛrusalɛm biini, bolzeŋ la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ Izrɛl hina dizi maa biine lugɔ de ɛɛ bɔr la ban ninna chɔluu di ra jaamuu la. Koori Rehoboam maa sɔnnɛ faa Naama, u faa ɛɛ Ammɔn hinuu. 14Koori Rehoboam faa ɛɛ koorichɔgiirɛ, dikuu uŋ faa waa nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa wia.
15Wia la maa Koori Rehoboam n ɛɛwɛ u kora dii saŋa, di lii u lugli di ga hel u tuna, ba sɛbaabuu du Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi Sɛmaaya ni Ido Faala Hɔna n na bagli lulla ŋmɛnizi wia biine. Laal faa du Koori Rehoboam ni Koori Jeroboam baannɛ, saŋaa saŋa maa. 16Ka Koori Rehoboam faa siu, ba huguu u naabaala hugribɔr, Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la biini, ka u biibaal Abija faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

english_text:
King Abijah of Judah
(1 Kings 15.1-8)
1Abijah became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel, 2and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah.
Some time later, Abijah and King Jeroboam of Israel went to war against each other. 3Abijah's army had 400,000 troops, and Jeroboam met him in battle with 800,000 troops.
4Abijah went to the top of Mount Zemaraim in the hills of Ephraim and shouted:
Listen, Jeroboam and all you Israelites! 5The Lord God of Israel has made a solemn promise that every king of Israel will be from David's family. 6But Jeroboam, you were King Solomon's official, and you rebelled. 7Then right after Rehoboam became king, you and your bunch of worthless followers challenged Rehoboam, who was too young to know how to stop you.
8Now you and your powerful army think you can stand up to the kingdom that the Lord has given to David's descendants. The only gods you have are those gold statues of calves that Jeroboam made for you. 9You don't even have descendants of Aaron on your side, because you forced out the Lord's priests and Levites. In their place, you appoint ordinary people to be priests, just as the foreign nations do. In fact, anyone who brings a bull and seven rams to the altar can become a priest of your so-called gods.
10But we have not turned our backs on the Lord God! Aaron's own descendants serve as our priests, and the Levites are their assistants. 11Two times every day they offer sacrifices and burn incense to the Lord. They set out the sacred loaves of bread on a table that has been purified, and they light the lamps in the gold lampstand every day at sunset. We follow the commands of the Lord our God—you have rejected him! 12That's why God is on our side and will lead us into battle when the priests sound the signal on the trumpets. It's no use, Israelites. You might as well give up. There's no way you can defeat the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped.
13But while Abijah was talking, Jeroboam had sent some of his troops to attack Judah's army from behind, while the rest attacked from the front. 14Judah's army realized they were trapped, and so they prayed to the Lord. The priests blew the signal on the trumpet, 15and the troops let out a battle cry. Then with Abijah leading them into battle, God defeated Jeroboam and Israel's army. 16The Israelites ran away, and God helped Judah's soldiers slaughter 17500,000 enemy troops. 18Judah's army won because they had trusted the Lord God of their ancestors.
19Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
20Jeroboam never regained his power during the rest of Abijah's rule. The Lord punished Jeroboam, and he died, but Abijah became more powerful.
21Abijah had a total of 14 wives, 22 sons, and 16 daughters. 22Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
translation_text:
Juda Koori Abija wia
1Izrɛl Koori Jeroboam kora dii binni fidiŋmantannaazihiŋ biinii Koori Abija faa di Juda kora, 2di so Jɛrusalɛm binni ahoro. U maa sɔnnɛ faa Maaka, u ɛɛ Gibia hinuu Uriɛl biihaaŋ.
Laal faa du Koori Abija ani Koori Jeroboam baannɛ. 3Koori Abija faa kpa laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaanaazu la n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, di la a laal. Koori Jeroboam ge kpa laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfa ŋmantannaazi la n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, di wa chem u ni.
4A laallɔɔra la n wa chemme Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri, Koori Abija tinni chi Bizeŋ Zɛmaram nyuu, ka ŋɔ, “Koori Jeroboam ni Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu n be! 5Ii waa zummɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, kpa Izrɛl koraa tɛɛ Koori Deevid ni u naannaa saŋaa saŋa maa, dikuu yazi nuukpaŋ la u ni Koori Deevid n ɛɛwɛ, waa chɔgaa dɔɔwɛ laa? 6Ka Koori Solomɔn nabɔma Nɛbat biibaal Jeroboam faa lii u dɔɔri har. 7Nɛkuna baŋhina faa hiŋ u har, ka vɛɛ Koori Solomɔn biibaal Rehoboam wia, dikuu uŋ faa ɛɛ bichala, waa wia zummɛ nɛnnɛ wia, u faa waa wette ú chi di huuzi baa.
8Ka filaŋkeŋ, ii jaa ɛɛ sirya ií vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kora la n du Koori Deevid naanna nonee la wia. Wibii maa, ii laallɔɔra kpillɔɔ werge, ii kaa dɔɔ saliŋ nabizi vuga la Jeroboam n kuarɛɛ tɛɛ ia la. 9Ii waa Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Aarɔn naanna ani Levi dee la duŋŋɛɛ lɛi ta, ka lizi ii himmaa kizeehina gunla hɛrdumazi hina n na ɛɛ laa? Nɛr la maa n ɔɔ ba wa kpa nabalee ni pebala aniidaanɛɛ di gil ba sɔu, di lizi u doŋa ha, ka u ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii ii vuga be, ɔɔ birgi a kizeehinnɛ.
10Ka yaa waa, yaa waa Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la vɛɛwɛ ta. Kizeehina la n na hum Kɔraawiizi huma la ɛɛ Aarɔn naannaa, ka Levi dee la ɔɔ ra hiini baa. 11Chɔɔzi ni duana maa, ba ɔɔ lizi mbusuzii di fuuh a kuna ni daahɛgsɔɔhsuma tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ba ɔɔ kpa paanuurɛ sag mbusu lizaa tɛɛbul la n waa doŋa dɔɔwɛ Kɔraawiizi be la ni, di choŋŋi fintinazi la n hɔŋzi saliŋ fintina daa ni la duana maa. Yaa ra hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la n na nyiŋŋuu. Ka iawaa vɛɛubuu ta. 12Kɔraawiizi du yaa benii, di ɛɛ yaa sitɔɔri. U kizeehinaa niŋ huuh bensunozi di yir yaa, yaa ni ia lɔ laal. Izrɛl baala, ií gilɛɛ gil ii ni Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala n na hum la naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii wàá wer kpegluu.”
13A saŋa, di Koori Jeroboam gillɔ u laallɔɔra baŋhina bar di ga so saga Juda hina la harbɔɔ, bá wer fɔɔ baa, ka baŋhina ge chi ba see. 14Denii Juda hina bir na, di ba fɔɔ baabuu ba see ni ba har maa. Ba lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la huuh ba bensunozi, 15ka Juda laallɔɔra la lɔ laal wile. Baŋ lɔ a laal wile la, Kɔraawiizi gil Koori Abija ni Juda laallɔɔra la kpegli Koori Jeroboam ani Izrɛl laallɔɔra la maa nɛnnɛ. 16Denii Izrɛl laallɔɔra ra chɔ, ka Kɔraawiizi kpa baa du Juda laallɔɔra la nonee. 17Koori Abija ni u laallɔɔra la faa kpu bakpila maa, a hɔl hiŋ. Izrɛl hina laallɔkpega kagboŋa kalfaanuere ba kpu. 18Denii Juda laallɔɔra la faa kpegli Izrɛl laallɔɔra, dikuu baŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la wia.
19Koori Abija ni u laallɔɔra faa duŋŋi Koori Jeroboam laallɔɔra la, di ga foozi ba bolzenaa Bɛtɛl, Jɛsana, Ɛfrɔn ani a kɛraa boljigzi maa. 20Koori Jeroboam faa waa kaa wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa maa, Koori Abija de di saŋa la. Denii Kɔraawiizi tɛr u digni, u siu.
21Koori Abija faa jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge maa, di kpa haana fidibanaazu, di lul biibaala tokko ni banɛɛ, biihaana fidibanumbɛl.
22Koori Abija kora dii saŋa, u wiɛɛlaa ni u wiŋɔɔlaa maa, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ido Faala Hɔna biine.

english_text:
King Asa of Judah
1Abijah died and was buried in Jerusalem. Then his son Asa became king, and Judah had ten years of peace.
2Asa obeyed the Lord his God and did right. 3He destroyed the local shrines and the altars to foreign gods. He smashed the stone images of gods and cut down the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah. 4Then he told everyone in Judah to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done, and to obey his laws and teachings. 5He destroyed every local shrine and incense altar in Judah.
6The Lord blessed Judah with peace while Asa was king, and so during that time, Asa fortified many of the towns. 7He said to the people, “Let's build walls and defense towers for these towns, and put in gates that can be locked with bars. This land still belongs to us, because we have obeyed the Lord our God. He has given us peace from all our enemies.” The people did everything Asa had suggested.
8Asa had a large army of brave soldiers: 300,000 of them were from the tribe of Judah and were armed with shields and spears; 280,000 were from Benjamin and were armed with shields and bows.
Judah Defeats Ethiopia's Army
9Zerah from Ethiopia led an army of 1,000,000 soldiers and 300 chariots to the town of Mareshah in Judah. 10Asa met him there, and the two armies prepared for battle in Zephathah Valley.
11Asa prayed:
Lord God, only you can help a powerless army defeat a stronger one. So we depend on you to help us. We will fight against this powerful army to honor your name, and we know that you won't be defeated. You are the Lord our God.
12The Lord helped Asa and his army defeat the Ethiopians. The enemy soldiers ran away, 13but Asa and his troops chased them as far as Gerar. It was a total defeat—the Ethiopians could not even fight back!
The soldiers from Judah took everything that had belonged to the Ethiopians. 14The people who lived in the villages around Gerar learned what had happened and were afraid of the Lord. So Judah's army easily defeated them and carried off everything of value that they wanted from these towns. 15They also attacked the camps where the shepherds lived and took a lot of sheep, goats, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_text:
Koori Asa n kpegli Itiopia hina wia
1Koori Abija faa siu, ba huguu Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la biini. Denii u biibaal Asa kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Bampirsɔna faa du a hɛrii binni fi, ú kora dii hiŋ saŋa.
2Koori Asa faa ɛɛ gunla n wesse di par Kɔraawiizi la unna hum labuu. 3U faa chɔgi hɛrdumazi vuga mbusu lizibɔra ani a kuaribɔra la n du giŋgimee nyuuni labuu, di purgi vuga la n ɛɛ bia, di teŋri vughaaŋ Asɛra daazi la baŋ baŋzɛɛ la ta. 4U faa ŋɔ Juda hina benii, dí ba ra ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la kipar, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni ani u baglaazi. 5U faa chɔgi a vuga kuaribɔra la n du a giŋgimee nyuuni ani daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔra, Juda hɛri bola maa biine. Awia, u kora dii saŋa, bampirsɔna faa du a hɛri biini maanii. 6U faa ma koŋlaa bar Juda bolzenaa, dikuu a hɛri n faa dɔɔ bampirsɔna wia. U ni nɛr maa faa waa laal dɔɔwɛ a guŋ saŋa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa tɛubuu bampirsɔna.
7U faa ŋɔ Juda hina be, “Ií gil ya ma koŋlaa bar bolzenaa naa, á du kpeg, di dɔɔ tauduura sognibɔra a chine, di dɔɔ dominuuzenaa la n dɔɔ lugbidaazi, bá ra karaa. A hɛri naa haa ɛɛ yaa hotte, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na humuu, u tɛɛ yaa bampirsɔna.” Awia, ba maa, guŋ gil ba nyɛɛli.
8Koori Asa faa dɔɔ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaahoroo Juda, ba maa dɔɔ laal pɛrɛtuzenaa ani kandaazi. Di kaa dɔɔ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ ni tokkoanaazu, Bɛnjamin ge dee biini. Ba gba faa dɔɔ laal pɛrɛtujigzi ani hozi. A laallɔɔra naa maa faa ɛɛ laallɔkpegaa.
9Denii Itiopia hinuu Zɛra ni u laallɔɔrakpila ani u laal torkozi kalfaahoro, faa ba Marɛsa, bá ni Juda hina lɔ laal. 10Awia, Koori Asa ni u laallɔɔra faa lii bá ga chem baa, di faa ga ɛɛ sirya Zɛfata Waluu la n dugli Marɛsa la.
11Denii Koori Asa faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la unna hum, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, nɛr maa waa hoo lugɔi un niŋ hiini gɛrgi, ú wer chi di huuzi fɔŋŋa hiŋ. Hiini yaa, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum. I ninɛɛ yaa dɛlli. I sɔŋ biinii yaa ba yá wa chem laallɔɔrakpila naa. N Dɔɔri, hinuu yaa ra hum, gilɛɛ gil newee kpeglii.”
12Denii Kɔraawiizi faa hiini Koori Asa ni Juda hina, ba kpu Itiopia hina la. Itiopia hina la n kawɛɛ faa ra chɔ, 13ka Koori Asa ni u laallɔɔra la faa duŋŋi baa guŋŋ di ga hel Gɛra, di kpu bakpila maa. Kɔraawiizi ni u laallɔɔra faa kpegli baa. Denii Juda laallɔɔra la faa paagi ba kuna werge maa di kaali. 14Ba faa jaa chɔgi boljigzi la maa n du Gɛra kɛraa la, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ ɔnsii chol a bola hina ni. A laallɔɔra faa paagi kuna werge di lii a boljigzi biine, dikuubɛɛwiai, kuna faa du a biinee werge. 15Ba faa kaa fɔɔ ba senɔɔna chɔɔribɔra di lɔ baa, ka duŋŋi pekpila, bukpila ani nyugmazi, di bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.

english_text:
Asa Destroys the Idols in Judah
1Some time later, God spoke to Azariah son of Oded. 2At once, Azariah went to Asa and said:
Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
3For a long time, the people of Israel did not worship the true God or listen to priests who could teach them about God. They refused to obey God's Law. 4But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
5There was so much confusion in those days that it wasn't safe to go anywhere in Israel. 6Nations were destroying each other, and cities were wiping out other cities, because God was causing trouble and unrest everywhere.
7So you must be brave. Don't give up! God will honor you for obeying him.
8As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
9Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
10In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem. 11That same day, they took 700 bulls and 7,000 sheep and goats from what they had brought back from Gerar and sacrificed them as offerings to the Lord. 12They made a solemn promise to faithfully worship the Lord God their ancestors had worshiped, 13and to put to death anyone who refused to obey him. 14The crowd solemnly agreed to keep their promise to the Lord, then they celebrated by shouting and blowing trumpets and horns. 15Everyone was happy because they had made this solemn promise, and in return, the Lord blessed them with peace from all their enemies.
16Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother. 17As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel. 18He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
19There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
translation_text:
Koori Asa n bittɛ kuari a hɛri wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi Duma izi Ɔdɛd biibaal Azaria, 2u lii di ga chem Koori Asa ni, di ŋɔ u be, “Jara, Juda ani Bɛnjamin dee, ií ra nuu n be. Kɔraawiizi du ii benii, di ii du u be. Di ii ra nyiŋŋi u bɔr, ii daŋ nau, ka di ii vɛɛu ta, u ge daŋ vɛɛ ia ta. 3Saŋa bɛl n bɛrɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi himmaa faa waa Izrɛl hina be duwɛɛ. Ba faa waa u Dia kizeehiŋ gba dɔɔwɛ ú ra bagli baa gɛɛ di dɔɔ u gbɔg gba. 4Ka tɔɔrɔɔ n wa huuzi baa, ba bir Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la be, di nyiŋŋi u bɔr, di nau. 5A saŋa hiŋ, gaagaa faa dɔɔ ɔnsiirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, tɔɔrɔɔ ni koozaa faa su hɛssi maanii. 6Hɛri bɛl hina ɔɔ faa ra kpegli bɛl hinaa, bolzeŋ bɛl hina kpegli bɛl hora, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii faa gillɛ tɔɔrɔɔ ni biinichɔg chol ba ni. 7Ka iawaa, ii chiiri zɛɛ, di gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra ra huah, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii huma dɔɔ kinturgaare.”
8Koori Asa n wa nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii naa lii Ɔdɛd biibaal Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Azaria be, u faa dɔɔ bɔkpega, di chɔgi vuga la maa n du Juda ni Bɛnjamin hɛssi la. Haali di lizaa lii bola la maa baŋ kpeglee, a du Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri la. Ka bir kuari Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la n faa chigɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia dominua jaŋgal see la ma.
9Ka faa jaa chaali Juda ni Bɛnjamin dee maa ni nɛra la maa n lii Ɛfram, Manasɛ ani Simɛɔn dizi la n wa soge ba be la. Nɛkpila maanii faa ballɛ di wa jaa Koori Asa ni, di so Izrɛl hɛri, u kora dii saŋa, dikuu baŋ wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du u benii wia.
10A nɛra maa faa wa chaali Jɛrusalɛm, Asa kora dii binni fidaanuehiŋ, baaguzi ahorohiŋ biini. 11A saŋa, ba kpa nauna kalfaaniidaanɛɛ ani peeza ni buuna kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛ, di lii sela la baŋ laurɛɛ lii laal biini la, di lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 12Ka ba jaa ŋɔ nua lugɔ ba ni Kɔraawiizi daŋ dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, bá nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la bɔr, ni ba biine, ba kpegzi ani ba nfɛssi maa. 13Nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la wia, bá kpuu. Haali di a hiŋ ɛɛ nɛjiga gɛɛ nɛzeŋ, baal gɛɛ haaŋ gba. 14Ba faa hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini lugɔ ba danna hiŋ u ni, di chaasi, di huuh bɛŋkunazi ni bensunozi. 15Juda hina maa bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ a guŋ wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ ni biinihuŋŋu, di faa ra nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi bɔr siaahmu ni, di nau. Awia, Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ baa bampirsɔna ba sogaa biini.
16Koori Asa faa wir u naa Maakaa lii wiche biini, dikuu uŋ faa baŋ vughaaŋ Asɛra n chummɛ daa, di ra kuaruu wia. Koori Asa faa ŋmɛŋ a daarɛ ta, di kuuguu, di kpau ga fuuh Kidrɔn Waluu biini. 17Haali, uŋ faa waa a vuga kuaribɔra chɔkkɛ a giŋgimee nyuuni Izrɛl gba, ka u bampirii faa lau Kɔraawiizii nɛnnɛ, ú de dui maa biini. 18U faa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ kuŋkuaraa la, u ni u mɛɛ n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi labuu du Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini.
19Laal faa waa kaa hoo, di Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anuehiŋ biini lɛi.

english_text:
King Baasha of Israel Invades Judah
(1 Kings 15.16-22)
1In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's rule, King Baasha of Israel invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, and he put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
2When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria: 3“I think we should sign a peace treaty, just as our fathers did. This silver and gold is a present for you. Would you please break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel and force him to leave my country?”
4Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept. 5When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
6Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood.
Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
7Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said:
You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army. 8Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them. 9The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
10When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people.
Asa Dies
(1 Kings 15.23,24)
11Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 12In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help. 13He died two years later.
14Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_text:
Koori Asa kora dii binni tuna wia
1Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anumbɛlhiŋ biinii Izrɛl Koori Baasa faa lɔ Juda hina di kpegli baa, di foozi Rama, di ma koŋlii baruu. Nɛr maa gilɛɛ kaa wer lii gɛɛ di zuu Juda koori hɛri.
2Denii Koori Asa jaa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ lii Kɔraawiizi Dia daama dauribɔra ani u himmaa kooridia hora di jaa, di kpaa hum dí ba la Siiria Koori Bɛn Hadad la n faa du Damaskus di ra di kora la be, di ga ŋɔ, 3“Gil n nii dɔɔ nuukpaŋ gunla n mɛɛ ni i mɛɛ n faa dɔɔwɛ la. Awia, n na sunziibuu saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ naa, ka gil i ni Izrɛl Koori Baasa nuukpaŋ la tuŋ. Gunnɛ niŋ gil ú lizi u laallɔɔra lii n hɛri.”
4Koori Bɛn Hadad nuu Koori Asa nua la, di hum u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi, bá ga lɔ Izrɛl laal. Ba faa ga kpegli Ijɔn, Dan, Abɛl Mam ani Naftali bolzenaa la n ɛɛ ba kuna dauribɔra la maa. 5Koori Baasa n wa nuu guŋ, u faa gil Rama mai. 6Koori Asa n wa nuu guŋ, u gil Juda hina maa la Rama, di ga chi bia ani daazi la maa Koori Baasa n faa kpawɛɛ di ra ma la ba. U kpaa ma Gɛba ni Mizpa.
7A saŋa hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Hanani faa ba Koori Asa be, di wa ŋɔ, “Dikuu hiŋ dɛlli Siiria koori ka gil Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum wia, hàá ka wer kpegli Siiria laallɔɔra. 8Itiopia ni Libia hina laallɔɔra faa kpillɔɔ, di dɔɔ laal torkozi ni zagtinna, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge maa. Ka hiŋ faa dɛlli Kɔraawiizi wia, u faa kpa baabuu du i nonee biini. 9Kɔraawiizi ra du nɛr maa wiɛɛlaa taurɛ durnya naa biini, di ra tɛɛ banla maa bampiree n lawuu nɛnnɛ fɔŋŋa. Ka i ɛɛ gɛnni wiarɛ. Awia, di haŋ lii zinaa di ra la, i daŋ du laal biini.”
10Koori Asa n wa nuu guŋ, u baaŋ faa fuuh Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Hanani ni werge maa, u lawuu tɔ dia. A guŋ saŋaa Koori Asa faa jaa ra sunni a nɛra baŋhina werge maa.
Koori Asa siu wia
11Koori Asa kora dii saŋa, u wiɛɛlaa di lii u lugli saŋa di ga hel u tuna, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Juda ani Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. 12U kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni kabɛlhiŋ biini, wiila aŋhina faa lau u naazii. Haali u wiila hiŋ n faa ɛɛ siaahmu werge gba, ka u faa waa Kɔraawiizi suŋŋɛɛ ú hiinuu, ka faa ra nyiŋŋi alaanfia nɛchaara be. 13U kora dii binni tokkoanɛɛ ni kpaŋhiŋ biinii u faa siu. 14Ba huguu bii bɔɔ bɛl uŋ faa tukke dau u hiŋ, Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini. Ba faa kpaubuu dau kunchɔɔrikuŋ la baŋ mizɛɛ ni kunsɔɔhrisuma aŋhina ni tulaalenanaa. U lee biini, u nɛra faa chem ninzenne di wiiu.

english_text:
King Jehoshaphat of Judah
1Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king and strengthened his defenses against Israel. 2He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
3-4When Jehoshaphat's father had first become king of Judah, he was faithful to the Lord and refused to worship the god Baal as the kings of Israel did. Jehoshaphat followed his father's example and obeyed and worshiped the Lord. And so the Lord blessed Jehoshaphat 5and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected, 6he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
7In the third year of Jehoshaphat's rule, he chose five officials and gave them orders to teach the Lord's Law in every city and town in Judah. They were Benhail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah. 8Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along. 9They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
10The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat. 11Philistines brought him silver and other gifts to keep peace. Some of the Arab people brought him 7,700 rams and the same number of goats.
12As Jehoshaphat became more powerful, he built fortresses and cities 13where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers 14from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans.
Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had 300,000 soldiers under his command. 15Jehohanan was second in command, with 280,000 soldiers under him. 16Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with 200,000 soldiers under him.
17Eliada was a brave warrior who commanded the troops from Benjamin. He had 200,000 soldiers under his command, all of them armed with bows and shields. 18Jehozabad was second in command, with 180,000 soldiers under him. 19These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
translation_text:
Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat wia
1Koori Asa biibaal Jɛhɔsafat faa kpa u mɛɛ Koori Asa gawa, di di kora, di ɛɛ u hiŋ sirya nɛnnɛ, di Izrɛl hina wa ŋɔ ba lɔu laal. 2U faa gillɔɔ laallɔɔra du Juda bolzenaa la maa, baŋ ma koŋlaa baraa la biine. Di faa gil baŋhina so Juda hɛri yeŋa ani Ɛfram bola la u mɛɛ Koori Asa n faa kpeglee di foozi la.
3Kɔraawiizi faa du Koori Jɛhɔsafat benii, dikuu uŋ faa ra hiŋ gunla u naabaal Koori Deevid n faa hiŋŋɛ, di lii u bichalli saŋa maa wia. U faa waa vug Baal ra kuari. 4Ka faa ra hum Kɔraawiizi la u mɛɛ n faa ra hum la, di ra hiŋ u baglaazi, ka gil Izrɛl hina wiɛɛlaa. 5Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa gil u kora chi nɛnnɛ, u dɔɔ a hɛri fɔŋŋa. Juda hina maa ɔɔ faa kpa kuna di wàá sunzuu, u faa dɔɔ daama ani girme werge maa. 6U bampirii faa lau Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ nɛnnɛ. U faa kaa chɔgi vuga kuaribɔra ani vughaaŋ Asɛra daabaŋlaa, Juda hɛri.
7Koori Jɛhɔsafat kora dii binni ahorohiŋ biini, u faa hum u nabɔnzi Bɛn Heel, Obadia, Zɛkaria, Nɛtanɛl ani Mikaaya, bá la Juda bola ga bagli baa. 8U faa gil Levi dee, Sɛmaaya, Nɛtania, Zɛbadia, Asahɛl, Sɛmiramɔf, Jɛhɔnatan, Adonija, Tobija, Tɔb Adonija ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Ɛlisama ni Jɛhɔram jaa ba ni. 9Ba faa kpa Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni hɔŋ la, di gaagi Juda hɛri bola maa, di ra bagli a nɛra.
10Kɔraawiizi faa gil ɔnsii chol hɛssi hina la maa n bar Juda hina ni. Awia, ba faa waa sɛɛwɛ bá ba wa lɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat laal. 11Filisti hina baŋhina faa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni kuna aŋhina di wa sunzi Koori Jɛhɔsafat, a ɛɛ ba hɛri kinturgaa. Lɔrbizi ge faa wa tɛu pebala kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛ ni kalfaaniidaanɛɛ, buuna ge kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛ ni kalfaaniidaanɛɛ.
12Koori Jɛhɔsafat fɔŋŋa faa jaa ra jaa werge maa. Awia, u faa ma diikpega ani bolzenaa la banna chiŋŋi kuna Juda biini 13ani diwee ni ba kunnyiŋŋaa aŋhina werge Juda bolkpila maa biine. U faa gillɔɔ nɛra la n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ du Jɛrusalɛm biini. 14Kennaabuu u faa lizi u laallɔɔra lii domeezi biine.
Di lii Juda domee biini,
Adnaa faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra
kagboŋa kalfaahoro sitɔɔri, 300,000.
15Jɛhɔhanan faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ ni tokkoanaazu sitɔɔri, 280,000.
16Zikri biibaal Amasia la n kpa u hiŋ tɛɛ lugɔ u danna hum Kɔraawiizi la, ge ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ sitɔɔri, 200,000.
17Di lii Bɛnjamin domee biini,
Ɛliada n faa ɛɛ laallɔkpeg, faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ nabɔma, 200,000, ba faa dɔɔ hozi ani laal pɛrɛtuzi,
18di kpa Jɛhɔzabad, u ge ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfa ni tokkoanaazu, 180,000 la n ɛɛ sirya ni ba dɔŋkuna, bá lɔ laal, sitɔɔri.
19A laallɔɔra naabuu a koori faa dɔɔ di jaa banla n faa du a bola la baŋ ma koŋlaa baraa, Juda hɛri maa la.

english_text:
Micaiah Warns King Ahab of Israel
(1 Kings 22.1-28)
1Jehoshaphat was now very rich and famous. He signed a treaty with King Ahab of Israel by arranging the marriage of his son and Ahab's daughter.
2One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead, 3and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?”
“Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command. 4But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
5Ahab sent for 400 prophets and asked, “Should I attack the city of Ramoth?”
“Yes!” the prophets answered. “God will help you capture the city.”
6But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
7“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 8Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
9All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
10Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
11All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
12Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
13“I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
14Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
15Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
16 Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
17Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
18Micaiah replied:
I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 19The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 20then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
21“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
22Ahab, this is exactly what has happened. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
23Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
24Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
25Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 26Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
27Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(1 Kings 22.29-35)
28Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 29Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
30The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 31So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop. 32And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
33However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
34The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Mikaaya n hau Koori Ahab ni wia
1Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa ɛɛ dɔɔnnɛ di dɔɔ girme werge maa. U ni Izrɛl Koori Ahab faa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ. Guŋ gil u biibaal kpa Koori Ahab biihaaŋ. 2Binni aŋhina n wa bɛrɛɛ, u la bolzeŋ Samaria, ú ga na Koori Ahab. Koori Ahab faa kpu peeza ani nauna di hɔɔhri u ni u nɛra, ka suŋŋuu lugɔ ú ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad laal. 3Izrɛl Koori Ahab, faa pɛɛzi Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat, “I daŋ la ga hiiniŋ ya lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hinaa?”
Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat ŋɔ, “N nii maa ɛɛ kpannɛ, n nɛra ɛɛ i nɛraa. Yaa daŋ hiinii lɔ a laal.” 4Koori Jɛhɔsafat ŋɔ Izrɛl koori be, “Pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi na mɔɔ.”
5Awia, Izrɛl Koori Ahab faa chaali dɔgtɛɛzi kalfaanaazu, di pɛɛzi baa, “Yá la ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hina laal gɛɛ n gilɛi?”
Ba ŋɔ, “La, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa baa du hìŋ́ koori nonee biini.”
6Ka Koori Jɛhɔsafat pɛɛzi, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ maa waa hoo ɛŋ, yaa n niŋ pɛɛzuu naa?”
7Ka Izrɛl Koori Ahab bir ŋɔ Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat be, “Baal bɛl haa du de, yaa n niŋ wer pɛɛzuu di zum Kɔraawiizi kipar, ka n hauhbuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa wiimaa baglɛɛ un niŋ wa ɛɛ n be u du wer, di a chɔgaa bɛŋ lɛi. Waabuu Imla biibaal Mikaaya.”
Koori Jɛhɔsafat ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ ra ŋɔ guŋ!”
8Denii Izrɛl koori la ŋɔ u nabɔnzi bɛl be, “La ga yir Imla biibaal Mikaaya, dí u ba manaŋ.”
9A koora banɛɛ hiŋ jaa laali ba koorilaala, di so ba koorikassi ni, pila la n dugli bolzeŋ Samaria dominuuzeŋ la, ka a dɔgtɛɛzi maa jaa ra ŋɔ ba be gunla n niŋ wa ɛɛ. 10Ka ba bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Zɛdɛkia, u mɛɛ faa di Kɛnaana, faa luu lugbia nyigzi aŋhina, di ŋɔ Koori Ahab be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘I daŋ kpa nyigzi naa di yagzi Siiria hina la guŋŋ di wa kpu baa nyaamm.’ ”
11A dɔgtɛɛzi la maa n kawɛɛ la faa ra ŋɔ guŋ himmaa, “La ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hina laal, i daŋ kpegli baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa baa du i nonee biini.”
12Nɛr la baŋ hummɛ ŋɔ ú ga yir Mikaaya la ŋɔ u be, “Na, a dɔgtɛɛzi la maa ra ŋɔu lugɔ a koori daŋ kpegli baa. Awia, ga gil i ni baa wiŋɔzi ɛɛ kpaŋ, í ŋɔ nɛnnɛ.”
13Ka Mikaaya ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de, gunla Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la n niŋ ŋɔ n be, gunnɛ ń ŋɔ tɛu!”
14Uŋ ga hel ba be, Koori Ahab pɛɛzuu, “Mikaaya, ya la ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hina laal gɛɛ ya gilɛi?”
Mikaaya ŋɔ, “Ií ga lɔ baa, di kpegli baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa baa du hìŋ́ koori nonee biini!”
15Koori Ahab ŋɔ u be, “Buŋmɛnɛɛ ń gil i hɛɛhzi lugɔ hàá dariŋ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biinei?”
16Denii Mikaaya ŋɔ, “N na Izrɛl hina maa n yaari giŋgimee nyuunii alugɔ peeza n waa nɔɔni dɔɔwɛ. Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Nɛra naa waa sitɔɔri dɔɔwɛ. Gil bɛl maa ra la bol ni bampirsɔna.’ ”
17Izrɛl Koori Ahab ŋɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat be, “Maa i be ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u haa waa winanii maa baglɛɛ un niŋ wa ɛɛ n be, di wichɔgaa bɛŋ lɛiyaa?”
18Ka Mikaaya haa vɛɛ ŋɔ, “Awia, a nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii. N na Kɔraawiizi n soge u koorikara ni u bol, u mɛlikazi maa chaali chi u nodig ni u nomɛɛl keŋkerezi maa. 19Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ dar Izrɛl Koori Ahab ú la ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hina laal, bá kpuuwɛi?’
Unnii ŋɔ keŋ, unnii ŋɔ keŋ. 20A tuna maa, duma bɛl jaa wa lii chi Kɔraawiizi see, di ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ daruu.’
Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzuu, ‘Ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛ daruuwɛi?’ 21U ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ la ga kpa kara du u dɔgtɛɛzi maa nuuzi.’ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘I daŋ wer daruu, wibii maa. La ga ɛɛ guŋ.’
22Awiarɛ Kɔraawiizi kpa kara du i dɔgtɛɛzi naa maa nuuzi la. U baglɔɔrɛ lugɔ hɛhchɔg daŋ chol i ni.”
23Denii Kɛnaana biibaal Zɛdɛkia la ga chɛ Mikaaya lia, ka pɛɛzuu, “Saŋa bɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Duma lii n be di ga ŋɔ wia tɛinɛi?”
24Ka Mikaaya bir ŋɔ u be, “A hɔl la hin niŋ chɔ ga zuu diisee di suah labuu i zum.”
25Denii Izrɛl koori ŋɔ, “Ií lau Mikaaya di bir la ga tɛɛ a bolzeŋ binni Amɔn ni a koori biibaal Joas, 26ka ŋɔ, ‘Kenne koori ŋɔ, Ií tɔ baal naa dia di ra tɛu paanuu ni nii bɛŋ, guŋŋ n wa bir ba, ni alaanfia.’ ”
27Mikaaya ŋɔ ni bɔkpega, “Di i wa wetto bir ba ni alaanfia, guŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi waa n be gawɛɛ di ŋɔ wia.” Ka kaa ŋɔ, “Ií maa lɛɛ n wiŋɔzi naa di dau bɔr la nii n waa lul.”
Koori Ahab siu wia
28Denii Izrɛl Koori Ahab ni Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat, faa kpa la Ramɔf Giliad. 29Izrɛl koori ŋɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat be, “N daŋ bɔg, ba wàá ka zumiŋ, ka zuu a laal biini, ka hiŋwaa laali i koorilaala.” Awia, Izrɛl koori faa bɔg, di kur, ka zuu a laal biini.
30A saŋa, di Siiria koori la faa ŋɔ u laal torkozi ni a zagra nabɔnzi be, “Ií gilɛɛ waa lɔ nɛr maa, di Izrɛl koori bɛŋ lɛi.” 31Awia, Siiria laal torkozi ni a zagra nabɔnzi la n wa na Koori Jɛhɔsafat, ba fɛ lugɔ Izrɛl koorii, di bir bá yoou, ka Koori Jɛhɔsafat lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ú wa hiinuu. Kɔraawiizi faa bir a nɛra lii u be. 32Awia, a laal torkozi ni a zagra nabɔnzi n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Izrɛl koori lɛi, ba faa gil u duŋŋaa. 33Ka nɛbɛl faa ra taazi u hobee gunla maa, bɛl ga Izrɛl koori laal laala bɔchoŋŋii baambaaŋ, di yaguu. A koori jaa ŋɔ a torko miŋŋi be, “Kpogliŋ lii a kalu naa biini, ba dumbuu pira.” 34A laal faa kpekkoo a hɔl hiŋ werge maa, ka a koori dɛlli u torko biini, u siwee chaŋ Siiria hina la guŋŋ bɔr wa duani. Wiizi n waa zuu, u siu.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem. 2But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said:
By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you! 3But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord.
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
5He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah 6and told them:
Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide. 7So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
8Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem. 9He told them:
Faithfully serve the Lord! 10The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
11Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_text:
1Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat n wa bittɛ la u dia Jɛrusalɛm biini ani alaanfia, 2Hanani biibaal Jehu n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ lii chem u ni, di ŋɔ u be, “A dɛkkɔɔ hiŋ laŋŋɛ ga hiini biinikpola hina, di kaa nɔŋŋi banla n hah Kɔraawiiziaa? Dikuu guŋ wia, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ na fuuh i ninɛɛ. 3Ama, i wia wessoo tama, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ligzi vughaaŋ Asɛra daabaŋlaa labuu a hɛri maa, i bampirii ge kaa lau Kɔraawiizi.”
Koori Jɛhɔsafat n lizi sitɔɔra wia
4Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa so Jɛrusalɛm, ka lii di gaagi nɛra la n soge bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba guŋŋ di ga hel Ɛfram giŋgimee maga la biine, di ra du baa bɔkpega lugɔ ba bir ba Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n faa ra hum la be. 5U faa lizi sitɔɔra Juda hɛri bolzenaa la n kpekke la bɛl maa biini. 6U ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii waa seriya diwee di ra tɛɛ nɛra, Kɔraawiizii ii di di ra tɛɛ. Waabuu ɔɔ du ii be saŋa maa di ii wàá di seriya. 7Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi ii bampiree biine. Ií ɔɔ pessi wia nɛnnɛ, ka di seriya, dikuubɛɛwiai, seriya dikara ni seriya dii ni nɔŋŋaa gɛɛ kuna lɛɛi ka di seriya waa hoo Kɔraawiizi be.”
8Jɛrusalɛm biini ge, Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa kaa lizi Levi dee, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Izrɛl domeezi nabɔnzi, bá ra binni Kɔraawiizi kiizi la hiŋaa ani kaluzi laafaa wia. 9U faa tɛɛ baa nuuzi naa, “Ií ra hum ni wibii ni ii biine maa, di ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi. 10Di wiimaa ɔɔ wa lii ii dɔŋahina la n du bolzenaa la be di ba, haali di a ɛɛ nɛkpui wia gɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni gɛɛ u widaulaa gɛɛ u baglaazi wia, ií ɔɔ ŋɔ ba be dí ba gilɛɛ kaa wàá ɛɛ wichɔgaa di ra zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di guŋ lɛi, u baaŋ daŋ fuuh ii ni ii lulla ni werge maa. Di ii ra ɛɛ guŋ, ii wàá dɔɔ chɔgri maa.
11Amaria n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔmaa ninna binni ii ni, Kɔraawiizi wia maa biini, Ismɛl biibaal Zɛbadia ge n ɛɛ Juda dizi nabɔma genii ninna binni ii ni koori wiɛɛlaa maa biini. Levi dee la genii niŋ ɛɛ ii nabɔnzi. Ií ɔɔ ra hum ii huma ani bɔkpega. Kɔ́raawiizi hiini banla maa n ninna ɛɛ nɛnnɛ.”

english_text:
Moab and Ammon Are Defeated
1Some time later, the armies of Moab and Ammon, together with the Meunites, went to war against Jehoshaphat. 2Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
3Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow. 4They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
5After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard 6and prayed:
You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you. 7 Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever. 8Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you. 9They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
10 You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed. 11Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us. 12Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
13While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple, 14the Lord's Spirit suddenly spoke to Jahaziel, a Levite from the Asaph clan. 15 Then Jahaziel said:
Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side! 16So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley. 17 You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
18Jehoshaphat bowed low to the ground and everyone worshiped the Lord. 19Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
20Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.” 21Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing:
“Praise the Lord!
His love never ends.”
22As soon as they began singing, the Lord confused the enemy camp, 23so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
24When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground. 25So Jehoshaphat and his troops went into the camp to carry away everything of value. They found a large herd of livestock, a lot of equipment, clothes, and other valuable things. It took them three days to carry it all away, and there was still some left over.
26Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
27-28Jehoshaphat led the crowd back to Jerusalem. And as they marched, they played harps and blew trumpets. They were very happy because the Lord had given them victory over their enemies, so when they reached the city, they went straight to the temple.
29When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid 30to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace.
Jehoshaphat Dies
(1 Kings 22.41-50)
31Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. 32Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, 33but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
34Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
35While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel. 36They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber. 37But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_text:
Koori Jɛhɔsafat n kpegli Moab ni Ammɔn hina wia
1Annii harbɔɔ, Moab ni Ammɔn hina laallɔɔra ani Miɔn hina faa ba, bá wa lɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat laal. 2Baala baŋhina faa ba wa ŋɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat be, “Laallɔɔrakpila maa lii Ɛdɔm, a Muuzensiwii baŋgia labuu di ra ba, bá wa lɔi laal, haali ba teŋ hel Hazazɔn Tama la banna yir Ɛn Gɛdi labuu.” 3Ɔnsii faa chol Koori Jɛhɔsafat ni, u ŋɔ u daŋ pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi na. Ka faa ŋɔ lugɔ Juda hina maa vɔɔ nua. 4Juda hina faa lii Juda bola maa di wa chaali, bá suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi, ú hiini baa.
5Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa izi chi Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina la maa n chaalɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋifalii la see, 6di ŋɔ,
“Kɔraawiizi la yaa naabaala n na hum, hiŋ lɛi du chiŋ laa? Hinuu ra di kora hɛssi naa maa kossi ni. Fɔŋŋa ni kpegzi maa du i nonee biinii, nɛr maa wàá wer chi i see. 7Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, hiŋ lɛi duŋŋi nɛra la n faa soge hɛri naa, ka kpau tɛɛ i nɛra Izrɛl hina, i dammu Abraham naanna, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa laa? 8Ba sogo u biinii di ma Diinaniinanii naa dikuu i sɔŋ wia, di ŋɔ, 9‘Di wichɔgii maa wa chol yaa ni, di ɛɛ dignitɛraa, di laallɛ gɛɛ wiilchɔgii gɛɛ lɔchɔgiirɛ, yaa daŋ chi i Dia naa see, i sibɔɔ, di lɔ wile tɛi ni biinichɔg, i daŋ nuu, di lɛɛ yaa ta.’
10Ka filaŋkennaa, Ammɔn, Moab ani Bizeŋ Sɛɛ hina, ballɔɔ bá wa lɔ yaa. Saŋa la yaa naabaala n faa lii Ijip hɛri di ra ba la, i faa waa sɛɛwɛ bá zuu a hɛssi naa biine. Awia, yaa naabaala faa bar baabuu ha, ba waa sɛɛwɛ chɔg baa. 11Jaa na gunla baŋ bittɛ ra nyiŋŋi ba kpa dau yaa, di ra nyiŋŋi ba duŋŋi yaa lii hɛri la hiŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ yaa, u ɛɛ yaa kapɛttɛ kuŋ la biini. 12Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, hàá tɛr ba dignaa? Yaa waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ, yá lɔ laallɔɔrakpila naa n na nyiŋŋi bá lɔ yaa naa. Yaa waa zum gunla yaa n niŋ ɛɛ. Awia, yaa ra binni i siweere, í hiini yaa.”
13Juda baala ni haana ni ba bichalli maa faa chi Kɔraawiizi see. 14Uŋ faa chigɛ de la, Kɔraawiizi Duma faa wa izi Jahaziɛl, u mɛɛrɛ faa Zɛkaria, Zɛkaria ge mɛɛ faa ɛɛ Bɛnaaya, Bɛnaaya ge mɛɛ faa ɛɛ Jɛyɛl, Jɛyɛl ge mɛɛ faa ɛɛ Matania, u faa ɛɛ Levi di lii Asaf dee biini.
15Denii Jahaziɛl jaa ŋɔ, “A nuu, Koori Jɛhɔsafat ni nɛra la maa n du Juda ani Jɛrusalɛm! Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm gɛɛ di gil ii bɔra huah, dikuu a laallɔɔrakpila naa wia. A laal waa ii hor ɛɛwɛ, Kɔraawiizi hotte. 16Kɛrɛ, ií vɔɔ tuu chem ba ni. Ba daŋ ga Ziz bia fɔɔlii ŋmɛnɛɛ la di ra tinni. Ií daŋ huuzi baa Jɛruɛl hɛribɔduma faalim la tuna. 17Ia lɛi niŋ lɔ a laal naa. Iawaa ga chi ii chigni bɔra, di chiiri zɛɛ, ka na gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lɛɛ ia. Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm! Ií gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra huah. Kɛrɛ, ií lii ga chem ba ni, Kɔraawiizi daŋ du ii be!’ ”
18Denii Koori Jɛhɔsafat giŋŋi di willi, u hile ga chug hɛri, Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina la maa ge ɛɛ guŋ, di jaami Kɔraawiizi. 19Levi dee la baŋhina n ɛɛ Kɔhaf ni Kɔra dɔmeezi faa izi chi chiŋ, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, bombombom!
20Chɔɔzimpikke ni, ba kpa di ra la Tɛkua hɛribɔduma la. Banna la la, Koori Jɛhɔsafat ga chi ka ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu n be, Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina! Ií yardi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nɛnnɛ, di wer chi. Ií yardi u dɔgtɛɛzi la, gunnɛ niŋ gil a kuari tɛɛ ia.” 21Uŋ wa pɛɛzi a nɛra na, u lizi yiryitta, bá laali ba tagtajaŋra la baŋ ɔɔ laali hɔpizizenaa la, di tɔ laallɔɔra la see di yir yira, di ra ŋɔ, “Ií ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nɔŋŋaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.”
22Baŋ faarɛɛ di ra yir yira, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la, Kɔraawiizi gil Ammɔn, Moab ani Bizeŋ Sɛɛ hina la n faa vɔɔwɛ di ra ba bá wa lɔ Juda hina la, bɔra ra sa. 23Ammɔn ni Moab laallɔɔra la bir pig Bizeŋ Sɛɛ hina la, di kpu ba maa nyaamm. Baŋ wa kpu Bizeŋ Sɛɛ laallɔɔra la tuŋ, ba ge bir pig dɔŋa.
24Saŋa la Juda laallɔɔra n ga hel bɔr la hiŋ ɔɔ chi ka ra binni de hɛribɔduma la, ba na di a laallɔɔrakpila la maa siuwɔ chɔɔ. Ba dɔma hiŋ bɛl maa faa waa kawɛɛ. 25Awia, Koori Jɛhɔsafat ni u laallɔɔra la ga paagi ba kuna. Ba ga na dɔŋkuna ni laala ani kuŋkpila werge maa n dɔɔ tɔna, a faa du kaŋ werge maa. A kuna n faa kannɛ werge maa wia, hɔpizaa ahoroo ba kpa chia. 26A hɔpizaa anaazuhiŋ hɔl, ba chaali Bɛraka Waluu biini di chɔli Kɔraawiizi. Guŋ wiarɛ ba ra yir de Bɛraka Waluu haali ni zinaa.
27Denii Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa tɔ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm laallɔɔra la see ba bir la Jɛrusalɛm ani bɔsɔna, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ ba kpegli ba dɔma. 28Ba faa zuu Jɛrusalɛm di ra lɔ kemzi di ra huuh bensunozi, di la Kɔraawiizi Dia la.
29A hɛssi hina maa n wa nuuwɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n kpegli Izrɛl hina dɔma la, ɔnsii faa lau baa. 30Koori Jɛhɔsafat kora bɔr hina faa jaa dɔɔ bampirsɔna, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n faa tɛu heezaa lii u dɔma maa be wia.
Koori Jɛhɔsafat kora dii tuna wia
31Koori Jɛhɔsafat binni faa du tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anue, ka u di Juda kora. U faa di a koraa binni tokko ni anue, Jɛrusalɛm biini. U maarɛ faa Silhi biihaaŋ Azuba. 32U faa hiŋ u mɛɛ Koori Asa hiŋaarɛ nɛnnɛ, di ɛɛ wideŋlaa Kɔraawiizi be. 33Ama, u faa haa waa vuga kuaribɔra la chɔkkɛ. Awia, a nɛra bampiree faa haa waa Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n faa ra hum la lauwɛ di ga tuŋ.
34Koori Jɛhɔsafat wiɛɛlaa maa di lii u kora dii lugli di ga hel u tuna, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Hanani biibaal Jehu Faala Hɔna la n du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.
35Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat ni Izrɛl Koori Ahazia la n faa dɔɔ biinikpola werge la, ɛɛ nuukpaŋ bɛl. 36Ba faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ di kuari kɔkɔɔzi muugberzenaa aŋhina, Ɛziɔn Gɛba Muuzeŋ nua. Baŋ wa kuaraa tuŋ, 37Marɛsa hinuu Dɔdavahu biibaal Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛliɛza, faa ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Koori Jɛhɔsafat, di ŋɔ, “Dikuu i ni Koori Ahazia n ɛɛ nuukpaŋ la wia, Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgi kuna la iiŋ kuarɛɛ la.” Awia, a muugberzenaa maa faa chɔgi.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Jehoram of Judah
(2 Kings 8.16-24)
2King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. 3Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
4After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders. 5He was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled eight years from Jerusalem.
6Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong, 7 but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
8 While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king. 9Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night, 10but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time.
Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped. 11Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
12One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said:
I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather. 13Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
14Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own. 15You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
16The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram. 17They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
18After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease. 19About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
20Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled 8 years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_text:
1Denii Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa siu, ba huguu u naabaala hugribɔr la, Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la biini. Ka u biibaal Jɛhɔram faa kpa u gawa di di a kora.
2Koori Jɛhɔram niwizii faa Azaria, Jɛhiɛl, Zɛkaria, Azariahu, Maikil ani Sɛfatia. Izrɛl Koori Jɛhɔsafat biibaalaa faa bannii maa. 3Ba mɛɛ faa tɛɛ baabuu saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ, kuna la n dɔɔ tɔna ani Juda bolzeŋkpega la. Ama, u faa kpa a koraa tɛɛ Jɛhɔram, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu faa u biibambinabɔma.
4Saŋa la Koori Jɛhɔram n wa chigɛ nɛnnɛ, u kpu u niuna maa ani Izrɛl nabɔnzi baŋhina. 5Koori Jɛhɔram faa di binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anɛɛrɛ, ka di a kora, di du Jɛrusalɛm biini, binni ŋmantannaazi. 6U faa ra hiŋ Izrɛl koora ŋmɛnizii, gunla Koori Ahab diahina n faa ɛɛwɛ la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa kpa Koori Ahab biihaannɛ, di faa ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge maa di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni. 7Ka nua la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Koori Deevid la wia, u faa waa nyiŋŋi ú chɔgi Koori Deevid dia. U faa ŋɔ nuarɛ lugɔ u daŋ ɔɔ gil u naana bɛl di kora di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
8Koori Jɛhɔram kora dii saŋa, Ɛdɔm hina faa vɛɛ Juda hina dɔɔra sɛɛirɛ, ka tɔ ba himmaa koori. 9Awia, Koori Jɛhɔram, u nabɔnzi ani u laal torkozi maa faa la de. Ka Ɛdɔm hina la faa go u ni u torkozi nabɔnzi la, ka u izi hamuŋa ni di suahzi ga ba baambaaŋ chɔ. 10Haali ni zinaa, Ɛdɔm hina waa kaa ra sɛɛ Juda hina dɔɔra.
A guŋ saŋa himmaanii bolzeŋ Libna hina gba faa waa kaa ra sɛɛ Juda hina dɔɔra, dikuubɛɛwiai, Koori Jɛhɔram faa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la u naabaala n faa ra hum la wiarɛ ta. 11U faa kaa ma vuga kuaribɔra genii Juda hɛri giŋgimee nyuuni, di gil Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina leu, di ra kuari vugkpila, ka gil Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa.
12Koori Jɛhɔram faa na hɔŋ lii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlija be. A hɔŋ ra ŋɔ,
“Kenne Kɔraawiizi la i naabaal Koori Deevid n faa ra hum la ŋɔ, ‘Haa i mɛɛ Koori Jɛhɔsafat gɛɛ i naabaal Juda Koori Asa hiŋaa la hiŋŋɛ, 13ka hiŋ Izrɛl koora hiŋaa la, di kaa gil Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina ra kuari vuga gunla Koori Ahab n faa ra ɛɛ la. I kaa kpu i himmaa niuna n ɛɛ i mɛɛ domee hina di bɔi. 14Awia, filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr i ni i nɛra, i biizi ani i haana digna, di chɔgi kuna la maa hiŋ dɔɔwɛ. 15Hiwiilchɔgii daŋ lau i looree, di tɔɔrii guŋŋ a wa lii chaaŋ.’ ”
16Kɔraawiizi faa gil Filisti ni Lɔrbizi la n faa soge dugli Itiopia hina la n faa soge muuzeŋ nua la, faa ba wa lɔ Koori Jɛhɔram laal. 17Ba faa wa lɔ baa laal di kpegli baa, ka chi kuna la maa n du a kooridia, u biibaala ani u haana maa kaali. Ba faa waa biibaal maa gillɛ tɛu, di u biibambijiga Ahazia bɛŋ lɛi.
18Annii maa harbɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi faa gil hiwiilchɔgii la n waa chaai dɔɔwɛ, wa lau Koori Jɛhɔram looree. 19A guŋ saŋa biini, binni anɛɛ n wa helle, a wiila faa gil u looree wa lii chaaŋ, u faa siu ni bɔwiila werge. U nɛra faa waa ninzeŋ chemme di kpau girme, ú lee biini, gunla baŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ u naabaala la.
20Koori Jɛhɔram binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anɛɛhiŋ biinii, u faa di a kora, di so Jɛrusalɛm biini binni ŋmantannaazi. Nɛr maa biini faa waa chɔkkɛ, uŋ siuwɛ la. Ba faa huguu Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la biini. Ama, ba faa wɔɔ hukke bá koora hugribɔr la.

english_text:
King Ahaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 8.25-29; 9.21,27,28)
1Earlier, when the Arabs led a raid against Judah, they killed all of Jehoram's sons, except Ahaziah, the youngest one. So the people of Jerusalem crowned him their king. 2He was 22 years old at the time, and he ruled only one year from Jerusalem.
Ahaziah's mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel, 3and she encouraged her son to sin against the Lord. He followed the evil example of King Ahab and his descendants. 4In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors.
Their advice led to his downfall. 5He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle, 6and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him. 7It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death.
When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family, 8and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah.
