1-6Much later, when Artaxerxes was king of Persia, Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylonia. Ezra was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Azariah. His other ancestors were Hilkiah, Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub, Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki, Abishua, Phinehas, Eleazar, and Aaron, the high priest.
Ezra was an expert in the Law that the Lord God of Israel had given to Moses, and the Lord made sure that the king gave Ezra everything he asked for.
7Other Jews, including priests, Levites, musicians, the temple guards, and servants, came to Jerusalem with Ezra. This happened during the seventh year that Artaxerxes was king.
8-9God helped Ezra, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month of that seventh year, after leaving Babylonia on the first day of the first month. 10Ezra had spent his entire life studying and obeying the Law of the Lord and teaching it to others.
Artaxerxes Gives a Letter to Ezra
11Ezra was a priest and an expert in the laws and commands that the Lord had given to Israel. One day King Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter which said:
12 Greetings from the great King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and expert in the teachings of the God of heaven.
13-14Any of the people of Israel or their priests or Levites in my kingdom may go with you to Jerusalem if they want to. My seven advisors and I agree that you may go to Jerusalem and Judah to find out if the laws of your God are being obeyed.
15When you go, take the silver and gold that I and my advisors are freely giving to the God of Israel, whose temple is in Jerusalem. 16Take the silver and gold that you collect from everywhere in Babylonia. Also take the gifts that your own people and priests have so willingly contributed for the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
17Use the money carefully to buy the best bulls, rams, lambs, grain, and wine. Then sacrifice them on the altar at God's temple in Jerusalem. 18If any silver or gold is left, you and your people may use it for whatever pleases your God. 19Give your God the other articles that have been contributed for use in his temple. 20If you need to get anything else for the temple, you may have the money you need from the royal treasury.
21Ezra, you are a priest and an expert in the laws of the God of heaven, and I order all treasurers in Western Province to do their very best to help you. 22They will be allowed to give as much as 3.4 tons of silver, 10 tons of wheat, 2,000 liters of wine, 2,000 liters of olive oil, and all the salt you need.
23They must provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that he won't be angry with me and with the kings who rule after me. 24We want you to know that no priests, Levites, musicians, guards, temple servants, or any other temple workers will have to pay any kind of taxes.
25Ezra, use the wisdom God has given you and choose officials and leaders to govern the people of Western Province. These leaders should know God's laws and have them taught to anyone who doesn't know them. 26Everyone who fails to obey God's Law or the king's law will be punished without pity. They will either be executed or put in prison or forced to leave their country, or have all they own taken away.
Ezra Praises God
27Because King Artaxerxes was so kind, Ezra said:
Praise the Lord God of our ancestors! He made sure that the king honored the Lord's temple in Jerusalem. 28God has told the king, his advisors, and his powerful officials to treat me with kindness. The Lord God has helped me, and I have been able to bring many Jewish leaders back to Jerusalem.
translation_text:
Ɛzra Jɛrusalɛm balaa wia
1Annii maa n wa ɛɛwɛ tuŋ, di Aatazɛgzisii Pɛsia hɛri koorizeŋ. A saŋa di baal bɛl faa du de, ba ra yiruu Ɛzra. U mɛɛrɛ faa Sɛraaya, Sɛraaya ge mɛɛrɛ faa Azaria, Azaria ge mɛɛrɛ faa Hilkia, 2Hilkia ge mɛɛrɛ faa Salum, Salum ge mɛɛrɛ faa Zadɔk, Zadɔk ge mɛɛrɛ faa Ahitub, 3Ahitub ge mɛɛrɛ faa Amaria, Amaria ge mɛɛrɛ faa Azaria, Azaria ge mɛɛrɛ faa Mɛrayɔf, 4Mɛrayɔf ge mɛɛrɛ faa Zɛrahia, Zɛrahia ge mɛɛrɛ faa Uzi, Uzi ge mɛɛrɛ Bukki, 5Bukki ge mɛɛrɛ Abisua, Abisua ge mɛɛrɛ faa Finɛhas, Finɛhas ge mɛɛrɛ faa Ɛliaza, Ɛliaza ge mɛɛrɛ Aarɔn la n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la, 6Ɛzra naa faa lii Babilɔnnɛ di ba. U faa ɛɛ baglii, di zum Moosis gbɔg la Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum n faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis labuu nɛnnɛ. Kɔraawiizi faa du u benii di nɔŋŋuu. Awia, kunla maa uŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi di ŋɔ koorizeŋ la be, a koori ɔɔ tɛubuu. 7Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biini, Izrɛl hina baŋhina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee, yiryitta, Kɔraawiizi Dia dominua guure ani u Dia balaa baŋhina ge izi ba Jɛrusalɛm.
8Ɛzra faa ba Jɛrusalɛmnɛ Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi anuehiŋ biini. 9A bina lugli baagu, lugli hɔpiziirɛ u faa lii Babilɔn, di faari u ŋmɛnɛɛ hiŋ volaa, di zuu Jɛrusalɛm a baagu anuehiŋ la lugli hɔpizii hɔl. Ɛzra faa wettoo vol a ŋmɛnɛɛ naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la uŋ faa ra hum la du u benii. 10Ɛzra faa aah siwiire ú helli Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg la, di ra hiŋuu nɛnnɛ, di ra bagli Izrɛl hina a widaulaa ani a Gbɔgni maa.
Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis hɔŋ uŋ sɛbɛɛ tɛɛ Ɛzra wia
11Hɔnnaabuu Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis faa sɛbi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra, n faa ɛɛ bagli, di zum Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni u Gbɔgni ŋmɛnizi la uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la.
12“Mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzisii sɛbi hɔnnaa di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra, n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la Gbɔg bagli.
N na jaamii.
13N dauwɔɔ lugɔ Izrɛl hinuu maa, Levi dee ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ maa n du n hɛri naa, di ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ ú bir la Jɛrusalɛm, daŋ wer la. 14Awia, n ni n zɛɛsogna baniidaanɛɛ ra hum iabuu, ii la Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm di ga daani na gunla banna hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la Gbɔg la n du i be la. 15Di kaa kpa jaa, di ii waa la, ii kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa la n ni n zɛɛsogna n kpawɛɛ ra sunzi Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, u Dia du Jɛrusalɛm la di ra la. 16Ií kaa kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa la maa iin nawɛɛ lii Babilɔn hɛri ani sunzaazi la Izrɛl hina ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina n lizɛɛ, dikuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la Dia n du Jɛrusalɛm biini la wia di ra la. 17Kebee gunla maa iiŋ wa nawɛɛ, ii ɛɛ ania di kpaa yau nabala, pebala, peballi, mia ani siŋ di kpaa lizi mbusuzi ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, u Dia mbusu lizibɔr la ni, Jɛrusalɛm biini. 18Denii i ni i lulla Jus hina jaa wer kpa saliŋhuŋŋa la ni saliŋ la maa n kawɛɛ di ɛɛ gunla maa iinna nyiŋŋi, á par Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. 19Ií kpa kuna la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia la ga tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, Jɛrusalɛm, bá kpaa di ra jaamuu u Dia biini. 20Di ii waa nyiŋŋi kunla maa lugɔ ii kpa ra hum Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la Dia la huma, ií lizuu lii n daama dauribɔr biini.
21Mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis dauwɔɔ lugɔ Muu Yufretis wiicholii hɛri daama dauribɔra binna maa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la Gbɔg bagli, kunla maa unna nyiŋŋi di lii ii be nɛnnɛ, 22á hel lugɔ saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi kagboŋa ahoro ni kalfaanaazu, huuti ge kilozi kagboŋa fi, siŋ galɔnzi kalfaanue ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, ɔlivi nuu guŋ ani yazi gunla maga unna nyiŋŋi. 23Ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, kunla maa Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ n na nyiŋŋi ii tɛɛ baa, bá kpa hum u Dia la huma, ií ɔɔ nyiŋŋaa tɛɛ baa, u baaŋ gilɛɛ waa fuuh n ni n biibaal maa ni. 24Ií gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina gɛɛ Levi dee gɛɛ u Dia yiryitta gɛɛ u Dia guure gɛɛ nɛr la maa n na hum u Dia la huma maa lampoo gɛɛ hɛri kuna gɛɛ kuŋkɛɛlaa.
25Ka hìŋ́ Ɛzra, kpa nunzuma la Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n tɛi la, di lizi i nabɔnzi ni i sitɔɔra la n zum Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la Gbɔgni la, bá ra binni Muu Yufretis wiicholii paga nɛra maa ni, di ra di baa seriya, ka bagli banla maa ge n waa a Gbɔgni zummɛ. 26Nɛr la maa n ŋɔ wàá hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la Gbɔg gɛɛ n gbɔg, a dɛkkɔɔ bá tɛr u digni manaŋ, di kpuu gɛɛ di duŋŋuu gɛɛ di foozi u kuna maa gɛɛ di tɔu dia.”
Ɛzra n chɔli Kɔraawiizi wia
27Ɛzra ŋɔ, “Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la yaa naabaala n faa ra hum la! Waabuu gillɛ a par koorizeŋ lugɔ u ra tɔgzi u Dia la n du Jɛrusalɛm la. 28Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ koorizeŋ, u zɛɛsogna ani u nabɔnzi nɔŋŋiŋ, dikuu aŋ paruu wia. Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la n du n be wia, n dɔɔ bɔkpegaa di chaali Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra, n ni baa la.”

Domeezi sitɔɔra la ni Ɛzra n kaa bir ba wia
1Domeezi sitɔɔra la ni ba nɛra la baŋ faa sɛbi ba sɔna, ba ni mìŋ́ Ɛzra lii Babilɔn hɛri, saŋa la Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis n faa ra di kora labuu keŋ,
2Gɛsɔm, n lii Finɛhas naanna biini,
Daniɛl n lii Itama naanna biini, 3Sɛkania biibaal Hatus n lii Koori Deevid naanna biini.
Zɛkaria n lii Parɔs naanna biini. Baala kalfa ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fii, 150, faa jaa u ni di sɛbi ba sɔna.
4Zɛrahia biibaal Ɛliɛhɔnai n lii Pahaf Moab naanna biini. Baala kalfaanɛɛrɛ, 200, faa jaa u ni.
5Sɛkania, u mɛɛrɛ Jahaziɛl n lii Zattu naanna biini. Baala kalfaahoroo, 300, faa jaa u ni.
6Jonatan biibaal Ɛbɛd n lii Adin naanna biini. Baala tokkoanɛɛ ni fii, 50, faa jaa u ni.
7Atalia biibaal Jɛsaaya n lii Ɛlam dee biini. Baala tokkoahoro ni fii, 70, faa jaa u ni.
8Maikil biibaal Zɛbadia n lii Sɛfatia naanna biini. Baala tokkoanaazuu, 80, faa jaa u ge ni.
9Jɛhiɛl biibaal Obadia n lii Joab naanna biini. Baala kalfaanɛɛ ni fidiŋmantannaazii, 218, faa jaa u ni.
10Jɔsifia biibaal Sɛlɔmif n lii Bani naanna biini. Baala kalfa ni tokkoahoroo, 160, faa jaa u ge ni,
11Bɛbai naanna, u biibaal Zɛkaria ni baala tokko ni ŋmantannaazii, 28, faa jaa u ni.
12Hakatan biibaal Jɔhanan n lii Azgad naanna biini. Baala kalfa ni fii, 110, faa jaa u ni.
13Saŋa bɛllɛ Ɛlifɛlɛt, Jiwɛl ani Sɛmaaya n lii Adonikam naanna biini faa tɔ har ba. Baala tokkoahoroo, 60, faa jaa ba ni.
14Utai ni Zakur n lii Bigvai naanna biini. Baala tokkoahoro ni fii, 70, faa jaa ba ge ni.
Ɛzra n bittɛ ba Jɛrusalɛm wia
15Denii mìŋ́ Ɛzra chaali a nɛra maa, bɔr la baŋ peree nii ga de di pal ra la bol la banna yir Ahava, yaa n chɔɔwɛ hɔpizaa ahoro la. N na lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina du denii, ka Levi dee la waa, waa hoo. 16Denii n hum ŋɔ bá yir Levi dee sitɔɔra kabɛl, baabuu, Ɛliɛza, Ariɛl, Sɛmaaya, Ɛlnatan, Jarib, Ɛlnatan, Netan, Zɛkaria ani Mɛsulam, di kaa kpa ba nunzunna naa, Jɔyarib ni Ɛlnatan jaa. 17Denii n gil ba la Ido n faa ɛɛ Kasifia hina sitɔɔri be, di bagli baa gunla ban niŋ ŋɔ Ido ni u lulla la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia huŋhunna la n du Kasifia la be, bá ge lizi balaa bá waa hum Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini. 18Kɔraawiizi n nɔŋŋi yaa la wia, ba tɛɛ yaabuu Sɛrɛbia, n faa zum huma nɛnnɛ, u lii Levi dee biini, di ɛɛ Mali naana, di kpa u niuna ni u biizi, ba maa ɛɛ baala fidiŋmantannaazi, 18. 19Denii ba kaa tɛɛ yaa Hasabia ni Jɛsaaya n lii Mɛrari naanna biini, ni u lulla, ba ge maa du baala tokko, 20. 20Di kaa kpa Kɔraawiizi Dia huŋhunna kalfaanɛɛ ni tokko, 220, Koori Deevid ni u nabɔnzi n faa lizɛɛ bá ra hiini Levi dee la. Ba maa sɔnaa ba faa sɛbi du hɔŋ biini.
21Yaa n faa chaali bɔr la baŋ peree nii ga de di pal ra la Ahava la, mìŋ́ Ɛzra faa gil yaa vɔɔ nua, guŋ gil yaa siwii sɔɔni, yá suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ú gil yaa ni yaa biizi ni yaa kundɔɔlaa wer vol a ŋmɛnɛɛ ni alaanfia. 22A faa ɛɛmbuu hiihzi werge maa lugɔ ń suŋŋi a koori, ú gil laallɔɔra ni zagtinna baŋhina tɔ yaa see, di guu yaa dɔma ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, n faa kpa yardaa di ŋɔ a koori be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋaa ni u fɔŋŋa du nɛr la maa n yarduu, di ra hiŋ u nua benii. Ka banla maa n wɔɔ yardɛɛ di vɛɛu la waa, u baaŋfuuih du ba ninɛɛ. 23Denii yaa faa vɔɔ nua di suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ u guu yaa, u faa nuu yaa wiisuŋŋaa la.
24Denii n jaa lizi kizeehina sitɔɔra Sɛrɛbia, Hasabia ani ba lulla fi, ba ɛɛ baala fidibanɛɛ. 25N mɛgzi saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ ani kuna la maa a koorizeŋ, u zɛɛsogna, u karchizenaa ani Izrɛl hina maa n faa kɛɛwɛ ŋɔ ba kpa hiini Kɔraawiizi Dia huma la, di kpaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la. 26N faa mɛgzi saliŋhuŋŋa tɔgzi n hel kilozi kagboŋa fidikabɛl ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, 19,500, saliŋhuŋŋa kuŋkuaraa tɔgzi n hel kilozi kalfaahoro, 300, saliŋ tɔgzi n hel kilozi kalfaahoro, 300, 27saliŋ tassazi tɔgzi n kaali kilozi ŋmantannaazi, 8, ani danyɛ tassanyɛgzaa anɛɛ baŋ vɔglɛɛ a tɔgzi hel saliŋ tassa, di tɛɛ baa.
28Denii n jaa ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ni kuna naa ɛɛ kunnanaananaarɛ Kɔraawiizi be. A saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ naa ɛɛ ii sunzaarɛ iin tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala n faa ra hum la. 29Awia, ii ra binnaa di ra du a tau nɛnnɛ, guŋŋ di ra ba saŋa la iin niŋ mɛgzaa Kɔraawiizi kizeehina diini biine, Jɛrusalɛm, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina sitɔɔra, Levi dee ani Izrɛl hina domeezi nabɔnzi maa sibɔɔ.” 30Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la faa lɛɛ a saliŋhuŋŋa, a saliŋ ani kunnanaananaa la baŋ mɛgzɛɛ la, di kpoglaa la Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la Dia, Jɛrusalɛm.
31Lugli baagu hiŋ hɔpizaa fidaanɛɛ hɔllɛ yaa lii bɔr la baŋ peree ba ra yiruu Ahava la, nii pal lii de di ra la Jɛrusalɛm la. Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la faa du yaa benii, di guu yaa dɔma ni ŋmɛɛna ni, yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ hiŋ biini. 32Yaa n wa hel Jɛrusalɛm, yaa faa heezoore hɔpizaa ahoro.
33A hɔpizaa anaazuhiŋ hɔl la, yaa kpa la Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la Dia, di ga mɛgzi a saliŋhuŋŋa, a saliŋ ani kunnanaananaa la maa, di kpaa tɛɛ Yuria biibaal Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Mɛrɛmɔf. U ni Finɛhas biibaal Ɛliaza, Levi naana Jesua biibaal Jɔzabad ani Binui biibaal Noadia maanii faa du u be. 34A kuna maanii ba faa kur di mɛgzaa, di sɛbi a maa magazi dau hɔŋ biini, a guŋ saŋa hiŋ.
35Denii nɛra la maa baŋ faa laurɛɛ la Babilɔn, ka ba bir ba Jɛrusalɛm la, jaa lizi mbusuzi di fuuh a kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la. Ba faa lizi nabala fidaanɛɛ, dikuu Izrɛl hina maa wia. Di kaa kpa pebala tokkoanaazu ni fidaanumbɛl, peballi ge tokkoahoro ni fidaaniidaanɛɛ. Denii ba kaa lizi buuna ge fidaanɛɛ, di lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Annii maa faa ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaare tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 36Denii ba faa kpa koorizeŋ widaulaa hɔŋ la, tɛɛ Muu Yufretis wiicholii paga nabɔnzi ni ba nabɔntɔga, ba faa jaa ra hiini a nɛra ani Kɔraawiizi Dia huma la maa.

english_text:
Ezra Condemns Mixed Marriages
1Later the Jewish leaders came to me and said:
Many Israelites, including priests and Levites, are living just like the people around them. They are even guilty of some of the horrible sins of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
2Some Israelite men have married foreign women and have let their sons do the same thing. Our own officials and leaders were the first to commit this disgusting sin, and now God's holy people are mixed with foreigners.
3This news made me so angry that I ripped my clothes and tore hair from my head and beard. Then I just sat in shock 4until the time for the evening sacrifice. Many of our people were greatly concerned and gathered around me, because the God of Israel had warned us to stay away from foreigners.
Ezra's Prayer
5At the time of the evening sacrifice, I was still sitting there in sorrow with my clothes all torn. So I got down on my knees, then lifted my arms, 6and prayed:
I am much too ashamed to face you, Lord God. Our sins and our guilt have swept over us like a flood that reaches up to the heavens. 7Since the time of our ancestors, all of us have sinned. That's why we, our kings, and our priests have often been defeated by other kings. They have killed some of us and made slaves of others; they have taken our possessions and made us ashamed, just as we are today.
8But for now, Lord God, you have shown great kindness to us. You made us truly happy by letting some of us settle in this sacred place and by helping us in our time of slavery. 9We are slaves, but you have never turned your back on us. You love us, and because of you, the kings of Persia have helped us. It's as though you have given us new life! You let us rebuild your temple and live safely in Judah and Jerusalem.
10Our God, what can we say now? Even after all this, we have disobeyed the commands 11that were given to us by your servants the prophets. They said the land you are giving us is full of sinful and wicked people, who never stop doing disgusting things. 12 And we were warned not to let our daughters and sons marry their sons and daughters.
Your prophets also told us never to help those foreigners or even let them live in peace. You wanted us to become strong and to enjoy the good things in the land, then someday to leave it to our children forever.
13You punished us because of our terrible sins. But you did not punish us nearly as much as we deserve, and you have brought some of us back home. 14Why should we disobey your commands again by letting our sons and daughters marry these foreigners who do such disgusting things? That would make you angry enough to destroy us all! 15Lord God of Israel, you have been more than fair by letting a few of us survive. But once again, our sins have made us ashamed to face you.
translation_text:
Ɛzra wiisuŋŋaa dikuu hɛrdumazi biihaana paai wia
1Baŋ wa ɛɛ annii maa tuŋ, Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra ba mìŋ́ Ɛzra be, di wa ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee la haa waa bahinaa bargɛɛ lii nɛra la baŋ soge dugli la ni ba wikuna ɛɛi biini, aabuu Keenan, Hitti, Pɛriz, Jɛbus, Ammɔn, Moab, Ijip ani Amɔri hina maa n na ɛɛ la. 2Ba paagi ba biihaanaa, di nyiŋŋi baŋhina ge tɛɛ ba biibaala. Awia, ba gillɔɔ nɛra la n ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa koozi nɛra la n bar baa la biini. Ba sitɔɔra ni ba nabɔnzi tɔ see, ba wibii nyaai naa biini.”
3Miŋ wa nuu wia naa, a chɔgi n biini werge maa, n lau n laala piili, di kpuzi n nyuhuna ni n taŋkulo huna ka so, n bɔra huah. 4Nɛra la maa n faa nuu Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la wiŋɔzi, ɔnsii lau baa ba bɔra ra sa la, ba jaa chaali bariŋ, dikuu banla baŋ faa laurɛɛ kaali Babilɔn la n bittɛ ba la wibii nyaai naa wia. Denii n faa so ni bɔhuaih, guŋŋ duana mbusu lizaa wa hel.
5Duana mbusu lizaa n wa helle, n izi di lii bɔr la miŋ faa soge ni bɔhuaih ni n laalipiilaa la, di giŋŋi, di yaa n nonee chiŋ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la, 6di suŋŋuu ŋɔ,
“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, hiihzi lawimbuu werge maa, n ŋmaabi. Awia, màá wer lalli n nyuu i sibɔɔ. Yaa wichɔgaa nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ, yaa chɔgri ge ga chug baama. 7Di lii yaa naabaala saŋa la guŋŋ di wa lii zinaa, yaa bilchɔg kannɔɔ werge maa, dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wia. Ba faa kpu yaa ni yaa koora ani i kizeehinaa, di lauri baŋhina birgi yoma, di paagi yaa kuna maa, yaa birgi sɔkpassi kuna hɛrdumazi koora nonee biine, alugɔ zinaa naa.
8Ka filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, i suŋ yaa ninɛɛ saŋa kpurii naa biini, di gil yaa baŋhina ka, di du de ni bɔsɔna, Diinaniinanii naa biini. I lɛɛ yaabuu lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini, di gil yaa na bɔchaaŋ. 9Yaa faa ɛɛ yomaa, ka haa yaa gillɛ ha a tɔɔrɔɔ biini. I bagli yaabuu i nɔŋŋaa Pɛsia hina koorizenaa see, di tɛɛ yaa miibɔɔfalii. Yaa na ŋmɛnɛɛ di kaa wer ma hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizizeŋ Dia n faa puree la. Di gil yaa so Juda hɛri ni Jɛrusalɛm biine ni bɔsɔna.
10Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, ɛrɛɛ ya ŋɔ annii naa maa harɛi? Yaa gbɛlli i widaulaa la 11hiŋ ga i balaa n ɛɛ i dɔgtɛɛzi be tɛɛ yaa, saŋa la hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, ‘Hɛri la iinna zuu ii dɔɔ la, ɛɛ hɛri la n doŋŋee, dikuu u nɛra wikuna wia. Dikuu ba wiɛɛlaa la miŋ kiiwe la wia, ba gillɔɔ ba wichɔgaa doŋa su a hɛri maa. 12Awia, ii gilɛɛ waa kpa ii biihaana di ra tɛɛ ba biibaala gɛɛ di waa kpa ba biihaana di ra tɛɛ ii biibaala. Ií gilɛɛ waa gil ii ni baa wàá ɛɛ dammunaa nuukpaŋ, ŋmɛnɛ maa. Guŋ daŋ gil ii dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, di di a hɛri kunnanaa guŋŋ di wa gilaa tɛɛ ii biizi, a ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuna, di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.’
13Wia naa n ɛɛ yaa be naa zɛɛ bɔttɛ lugɔ yaa wiɛɛlaa ani yaa bilchɔg n kannɛ werge wia, ka Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, haa yaa digna tɛrgɛɛ di hel gunla yaa wichɔgaa n makkɛ, ka gil yaa bannii ka, di haa du de. 14Awia, a dɛkkɔ yaa n niŋ kaa chɔgi i widaulaa, di kaa gil yaa ni banla n na ɛɛ i wikiilaa ra paagi dɔŋaa? Di yaa kaa ɛɛ guŋ, i baaŋ wàá fuuh yaa ni werge maa, í chɔgi yaa, bɛl maa wàá ka kaa? 15Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, i wia deŋloore! Yaa banniibuu kawɛɛ zinaa. Yaabuu keŋ di chi i see, di di bilchɔg. Yaa bɛl maa waa dɛkkɛ lugɔ u chi i see gba.”

english_text:
The Plan for Ending Mixed Marriages
1While Ezra was down on his knees in front of God's temple, praying with tears in his eyes and confessing the sins of the people of Israel, a large number of men, women, and children gathered around him and cried bitterly.
2Shecaniah son of Jehiel from the family of Elam said:
Ezra, we have disobeyed God by marrying these foreign women. But there is still hope for the people of Israel, 3if we follow your advice and the advice of others who truly respect the laws of God. We must promise God that we will divorce our foreign wives and send them away, together with their children.
4Ezra, it's up to you to do something! We will support whatever you do. So be brave!
5Ezra stood up and made the chief priests, the Levites, and everyone else in Israel swear that they would follow the advice of Shecaniah. 6Then Ezra left God's temple and went to spend the night in the living quarters of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He felt sorry because of what the people had done, and he did not eat or drink a thing.
7-8The officials and leaders sent a message to all who had returned from Babylonia and were now living in Jerusalem and Judah. This message told them to meet in Jerusalem within three days, or else they would lose everything they owned and would no longer be considered part of the people that had returned from Babylonia.
9Three days later, on the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem and sat in the temple courtyard. It was a serious meeting, and they sat there, trembling in the rain.
10Ezra the priest stood up and said:
You have broken God's Law by marrying foreign women, and you have made the whole nation guilty! 11Now you must confess your sins to the Lord God of your ancestors and obey him. Divorce your foreign wives and don't have anything to do with the rest of the foreigners who live around here.
12Everyone in the crowd shouted:
You're right! We will do what you say. 13But there are so many of us, and we can't just stay out here in this downpour. A lot of us have sinned by marrying foreign women, and the matter can't be settled in only a day or two.
14Why can't our officials stay on in Jerusalem and take care of this for us? Let everyone who has sinned in this way meet here at a certain time with leaders and judges from their own towns. If we take care of this problem, God will surely stop being so terribly angry with us.
15Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were the only ones who objected, except for the two Levites, Meshullam and Shabbethai.
16Everyone else who had returned from exile agreed with the plan. So Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of the families, and he listed their names. They started looking into the matter on the first day of the tenth month, 17and they did not finish until the first day of the first month of the next year.
The Men Who Had Foreign Wives
18-19Here is a list of the priests who had agreed to divorce their foreign wives and to sacrifice a ram as a sin offering:
Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah from the family of Joshua son of Jozadak and his brothers; 20Hanani and Zebadiah from the family of Immer; 21Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah from the family of Harim; 22Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah from the family of Pashhur.
23Those Levites who had foreign wives were: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (also known as Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
24Eliashib, the musician, had a foreign wife.
These temple guards had foreign wives:
Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
25Here is a list of the others from Israel who had foreign wives:
Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah from the family of Parosh;
26Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah from the family of Elam;
27Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza from the family of Zattu;
28Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai from the family of Bebai;
29Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth from the family of Bani;
30Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh from the family of Pahath Moab;
31-32Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon, Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah from the family of Harim;
33Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei from the family of Hashum;
34-37Maadai, Amram, Uel, Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi, Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasu from the family of Bani;
38-42Shimei, Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah, Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai, Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah, Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph from the family of Binnui;
43Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah from the family of Nebo.
44These men divorced their foreign wives, then sent them and their children away.
translation_text:
A nɛra n sɛɛ ba wichɔgaa chɔgri wia
1Ɛzra n faa ra suŋŋi wiizi, di ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa, ka faa ra wii di chol hɛri, Kɔraawiizi Dia la see la, Izrɛl baala ni haana ani bichalli kpila maa faa wa baruu. Ba ge gba maa faa ra wii werge. 2Denii Jɛhiɛl biibaal Sɛkania n ɛɛ Ɛlam domee hinuu naana faa ŋɔ Ɛzra be, “Yaa waa wibii dɔɔwɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la be, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa paagi hɛrdumazi nɛra la n bar yaa biihaanaa. Ka Izrɛl hina haa dɔɔ tamiirɛ. 3Awia, filaŋkeŋ, gil yaa ni Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ɛɛ nuukpaŋ u see, yá duŋŋi a keŋ haana ni ba biizi, gunla hìŋ́ Ɛzra ani banla n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la widaulaa n niŋ bagli. Gil ya ɛɛ gunla u Gbɔg n na bagli. 4Ɛzra, izi chiŋ, a wii naa du i noneere. Yaa daŋ chi i har. Awia, dɔɔ bɔkpega, di ɛɛ guŋ.”
5Denii Ɛzra izi hɛɛhzi di du Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee ani Izrɛl hina maa, lugɔ bá hiŋ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. Ba hɛɛhzi guŋ. 6Awia, Ɛzra jaa lii Kɔraawiizi Dia la see, di la Ɛliasib biibaal Jɛhɔhanan chɔɔribɔr. Uŋ faa du de la, waa diwee, waa nii ge nyɔɔwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa haa ra wiiu, dikuu banla baŋ laurɛɛ kaali Babilɔn, ka ba bir ba la wibii nyaai wia.
7Denii ba faa sii di bar Juda hɛri ni Jɛrusalɛm maa, lugɔ banla maa n bittɛ ba la, ba maa chaali Jɛrusalɛm, ka ŋɔ, dí 8nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ chaalaa naa balaa hɔpizaa ahoro biini, u daŋ nyaa u kundɔɔlaa maa, gunla nabɔnzi n dauwɛ, ka bá lizuu lii banla n bittɛ ba la biini.
9A hɔpizaa ahoro biini, Juda ni Bɛnjamin dee baala maa chaali Jɛrusalɛm. A baaguzi kabɛlhiŋ, u hɔpizaa tokko hɔl, di a nɛra maa chaalɔɔ di so Kɔraawiizi Dia la bossee. Ba maa biine faa chɔgi werge maa, dikuu a wii n faa ɛɛ siaahmu ani dooŋ n faa ra ba werge wia. 10Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra izi chi, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ii waa wibii dɔɔwɛ. Ií paagi hɛrdumazi biihaanaa. Guŋ kaa gil Izrɛl hina bilchɔg nyaŋŋi. 11Awia, filaŋkeŋ, ii sɛɛ ii wichɔgaa chɔgri, Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala n faa ra hum la be, ka ra ɛɛ u kipar. Ií bargi iihinaa lii nɛra la n bar ia ani ii hɛrdumazi haana la be.”
12Denii a nɛra maa sɛɛ werge maa, di ŋɔ, “I di wibiire! Firaarɛ ya ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. 13Ka nɛra la n chaali bɔnnaa kpillɔɔ werge maa. A ge kaa ɛɛ yuu, awia, yaa wàá wer so baŋgia. A wii naa ge waa kaa ɛɛ hɔpizikpaŋ gɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ wiɛɛlii, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa kpila maa jaa a wii naa biinii. 14Ií gil yaa nabɔnzi chi a nɛra maa naazi di ɛɛ wiimaa. Denii bá gil unla maa n dɔɔ hɛrduma haaŋ u bol lii ba, saŋa la baŋ dauwɛ, di kpa bol maa nabɔnzi ni sitɔɔra jaa, guŋŋ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la baaŋ wa sɔɔni yaa ni, dikuu a wii naa wia.” 15Asahɛl biibaal Jonatan ni Tikva biibaal Jazɛya bɛnnɛ faa di a wii naa mmɔri. Mɛsulam ni Sabɛtai la n faa lii Levi dee biini sɛɛ jaa baa.
16Awia, banla n faa bittɛ lii Babilɔn ba la, ɛɛ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. Kizeehiŋ Ɛzra faa lizi baala la n ɛɛ domeezi nabɔnzi di lii domee maa biini, ba sɛbi ba sɔna dau. Baaguzi fihiŋ lugli hɔpizii hɔl, ba so bá pigzi ba wia, 17di lii lugli baagu lugli hɔpizii hɔl, ba tuŋ baala la maa n paa hɛrdumazi haana la wia.
Banla n faa paa hɛrdumazi haana wia
18Banla n faa paa hɛrdumazi haanaa sɔnaa keŋ, di lii Kɔraawiizi kizeehina naanna biini,
Jɔzadak biibaal Jesua naanna ani u lulla, Maasɛya, Ɛliɛza, Jarib ani Gɛdalia. 19Ba bɛl maanii faa ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ vɛɛ u haaŋ. Bɛl maanii faa lizi pebal lii u sela biini, bá lizi u bilchɔg mbusu.
20Ima naanna biini, Hanani ni Zɛbadia.
21Harim ge naanna biini,
Maasɛya, Ɛlija, Sɛmaaya, Jɛhiɛl ani Uzzia.
22Pasur naanna biini,
Ɛliɔnai, Maasɛya, Ismɛl, Nɛtanɛl, Jɔzabad ani Ɛlasa.
23Levi dee ge biini,
Jɔzabad, Simei, Kɛlaaya, ba kaa ra yiruu Kɛlita la, Pɛtahia, Juda ani Ɛliɛza.
24Yiryitta ge biini,
Ɛliasib.
Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuguure ge biini,
Salum, Tɛlɛm ani Uri.
25Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ biini,
Parɔs naanna,
Ramia, Izia, Malkija, Mijamin, Ɛliaza, Malkija ani Bɛnaaya.
26Ɛlam ge naanna,
Matania, Zɛkaria, Jɛhiɛl, Abdi, Jɛrɛmɔf ani Ɛlija.
27Zatu ge naanna,
Ɛliɔnai, Ɛliasib, Matania, Jɛrɛmɔf, Zabad ani Aziza.
28Bɛbai ge naanna,
Jɛhɔhanan, Hanania, Zabai ani Atlai.
29Bani ge naannaa,
Mɛsulam, Maluk, Adaaya, Jasub, Sɛɛl ani Jɛrɛmɔf.
30Pahaf Moab naanna,
Adna, Kɛlal, Bɛnaaya, Maasɛya, Matania, Bɛzalɛl, Binui ani Manasɛ.
31Harim ge naannaa,
Ɛliɛza, Isija, Malkija, Sɛmaaya, Simɛɔn, 32Bɛnjamin, Maluk ani Sɛmaria.
33Hasum ge naannaa,
Matɛnai, Mattatta, Zabad, Ɛlifɛlɛt, Jɛrɛmia, Manasɛ ani Simei.
34Bani ge naanna,
Maadai, Amram, Uyɛl, 35Bɛnaaya, Bɛdɛya, Kɛluhi, 36Vania, Mɛrɛmɔf, Ɛliasib, 37Matania, Matɛnai ani Jaasu.
38Binui ge naanna,
Simei, 39Sɛlɛmia, Netan, Adaaya, 40Maknɛdɛbai, Sasai, Sarai, 41Azarɛl, Sɛlɛmia, Sɛmaria, 42Salum, Amaria ani Joosɛf.
43Nɛbɔ naanna,
Jɛyɛl, Matitia, Zabad, Zɛbina, Jaddai, Jowɛl ani Bɛnaaya.
44A nɛra naa maanii faa paa hɛrdumazi haana, baŋhina ni ba hora faa lul biizii, ka ba duŋŋi ba ni a biizi maa.

english_text:
Nehemiah's Prayer
1I am Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and in this book I tell what I have done.
During the month of Chislev in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes ruled Persia, I was in his fortress city of Susa, 2when my brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped from being captives in Babylonia. I also asked them about the city of Jerusalem.
3They told me, “Those captives who have come back are having all kinds of troubles. They are terribly disgraced, Jerusalem's walls are broken down, and its gates have been burned.”
4When I heard this, I sat down on the ground and cried. Then for several days, I mourned; I went without eating to show my sorrow, and I prayed:
5 Lord God of heaven, you are great and fearsome. And you faithfully keep your promises to everyone who loves you and obeys your commands. 6I am your servant, so please have mercy on me and answer the prayer that I make day and night for these people of Israel who serve you. I, my family, and the rest of your people have sinned 7by choosing to disobey you and the laws and teachings you gave to your servant Moses.
8 Please remember the promise you made to Moses. You told him that if we were unfaithful, you would scatter us among foreign nations. 9 But you also said that no matter how far away we were, we could turn to you and start obeying your laws. Then you would bring us back to the place where you have chosen to be worshiped.
10Our Lord, I am praying for your servants—those you rescued by your great strength and mighty power. 11Please answer my prayer and the prayer of your other servants who gladly honor your name. When I serve the king his wine today, make him pleased with me and let him do what I ask.
translation_text:
Nɛhɛmia wiisuŋŋaa wia
1Hakalia biibaal Nɛhɛmia wiŋɔɔlaarɛ keŋ.
Binni tokko n wa helle, baagu la banna yir Kislɛv biini, Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii saŋa, di mìŋ́ Nɛhɛmia faa du bolzeŋ la banna yir Susa. 2Denii n niwee Hanani ni baala baŋhina lii Juda ba. N pɛɛzi baa gunla Jus hina la baŋ laurɛɛ kaali Babilɔn, ka ba bir ba Juda la wia ani gunla Jɛrusalɛm wia n duwɛɛ.
3Denii ba ŋɔ n be, “Banla maa baŋ laurɛɛ ka ba bir ba Juda la, du tɔɔrɔɔ ni hiihzi biinii. Jɛrusalɛm koŋlaa maanii purgee, ba fuuh u dominuuzenaa ge maa.”
4Miŋ wa nuu wia naa, n so di wii ni biinichɔg, di vɔɔ nua hɔpizaa anɛɛ, di suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ, 5di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ, di dɔɔ sɔŋ, i wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge la, i ɔɔ ra hiŋ i ni i nɛra nuukpaŋ labuu. I nɔŋŋaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ banla n nɔŋŋii di ra hiŋ i widaulaa la be. 6Keŋŋi digna, di pilli i siwee nuu i balii n suŋŋii di ra tɛɛ i balaa Izrɛl hina, wibaŋa ni hamuŋa maa. N ŋɔ n sɛɛ chɔgrii lugɔ yaa Izrɛl hina, di kpa n ni n mɛɛ diahina maa jaa, ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ zuu i ni. 7Yaa ɛɛ biinikpola wiarɛ di zuu i ni. Yaa waa sɛɛwɛ hiŋ i wiŋɔɔlaa, i widaulaa ani i Gbɔgni la hiŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ i balii Moosis la.
8A liizi i baglaazi la hiŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis, di ŋɔ, ‘Di ii wanna hiŋ ni wibii, n daŋ gil ii maa yaari hɛrdumazi biine. 9Ka di ii daŋ bir ba n be ni wibii, di ra hiŋ n wiŋɔɔlaa, haali ii banla gba baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛhjaŋa la, n daŋ chaali ia di bir ba bɔr la miŋ lizɛɛ, n sɔŋ du de la.’
10Ba ɛɛ i balaa ni nɛra la hiŋ kpa i fɔŋŋazeŋ ni i banonii di lɛɛu. 11Kɔraawiizi, keŋŋi digna di nuu mìŋ́ i balii naa ni i balaa la maa n na kpa i sɔŋ girme wiisuŋŋaa. Gil mìŋ́ i balii na n kipar zinaa, di gil n wia par baal naa.”
Minuu faa ra kpogli a koorizeŋ siŋ libee.

english_text:
Nehemiah Goes to Jerusalem
1During the month of Nisan in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king, I served him his wine, as I had done before. But this was the first time I had ever looked depressed. 2So the king said, “Why do you look so sad? You're not sick. Something must be bothering you.”
Even though I was frightened, 3 I answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! I feel sad because the city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”
4The king asked, “What do you want me to do?”
I prayed to the God who rules from heaven. 5Then I told the king, “Sir, if it's all right with you, please send me back to Judah, so that I can rebuild the city where my ancestors are buried.”
6The queen was sitting beside the king when he asked me, “How long will it take, and when will you be back?” The king agreed to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
7Then I asked, “Your Majesty, would you be willing to give me letters to the governors of the provinces west of the Euphrates River, so that I can travel safely to Judah? 8I will need timber to rebuild the gates of the fortress near the temple and more timber to construct the city wall and to build a place for me to live. And so, I would appreciate a letter to Asaph, who is in charge of the royal forest.” God was good to me, and the king did everything I asked.
9The king sent some army officers and cavalry troops along with me, and as I traveled through the Western Provinces, I gave the letters to the governors. 10But when Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about what had happened, they became very angry, because they didn't want anyone to help the people of Israel.
Nehemiah Inspects the Wall of Jerusalem
11Three days after arriving in Jerusalem, 12I got up during the night and left my house. I took some men with me, without telling anyone what I thought God wanted me to do for the city. The only animal I took was the donkey I rode on. 13I went through Valley Gate on the west, then south past Dragon Spring, before coming to Garbage Gate. As I rode along, I took a good look at the crumbled walls of the city and the gates that had been torn down and burned. 14On the east side of the city, I headed north to Fountain Gate and King's Pool, but then the trail became too narrow for my donkey. 15So I went down to Kidron Valley and looked at the wall from there. Then before daylight I returned to the city through Valley Gate.
16None of the city officials knew what I had in mind. And I had not even told any of the Jews—not the priests, the leaders, the officials, or any other Jews who would be helping in the work. 17But when I got back, I said to them, “Jerusalem is truly in a mess! The gates have been torn down and burned, and everything is in ruins. We must rebuild the city wall so that we can again take pride in our city.”
18Then I told them how kind God had been and what the king had said.
Immediately, they replied, “Let's start building now!” So they got everything ready.
19When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about our plans, they started insulting us and saying, “Just look at you! Do you plan to rebuild the walls of the city and rebel against the king?”
20I answered, “We are servants of the God who rules from heaven, and he will make our work succeed. So we will start rebuilding Jerusalem, but you have no right to any of its property, because you have had no part in its history.”
translation_text:
Nɛhɛmia n bittɛ la Jɛrusalɛm wia
1Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii binni tokkohiŋ biini, baagu la banna yir Niisan la, n kpa siŋ la ń ga tɛu, di u ra di. U ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa nawɛɛ n biini n chɔkkɛ. 2Denii u pɛɛziŋ, “Zinaa ɛrɛɛ i biini chɔgi, hiŋ waa wiiyɛi? A daŋ ɛɛ biinichɔg wiarɛ.”
Uŋ pɛɛzi gunla, ɔnsii lawiŋ, 3ka n ŋɔ u be, “Jara, Kɔ́raawiizi gil i du de saŋa maa. Bɛɛ n baani n biini wàá chɔgɛi? Bolzeŋ la miŋ liwɛɛ, n naabaala ŋmama du de la maanii purgee, u dominuuzenaa ge maa fuuh.”
4A koorizeŋ pɛɛziŋ, “Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋi n ɛɛ tɛinɛi?”
Denii n suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ, 5ka ŋɔ a koorizeŋ be, “Jara, di n wia parii, nuu n suŋŋaa, di gil n la Juda, n naabaala hɛri la baŋ hug baa la, di ga kuari a bolzeŋ ma.”
6A saŋa, di a koorizeŋ ni u haaŋ sogo, u pɛɛziŋ, “Ɛrɛɛ í ga birgi mag ani saŋa bɛɛ i bir banɛi?” A paruu, u tɛŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ. Awia, n tɛu saŋa la min niŋ la ka bir ba.
7Denii n kaa suŋŋuu ŋɔ ú tɛŋ hɔna, ń kpa la ga tɛɛ Muu Yufretis baŋgia hɛri nabɔnzi, bá gil nɛra tɔ n see di binniŋ guŋŋ ń ga hel Juda ni alaanfia. 8N kaa ŋɔ u be lugɔ ú tɛŋ hɔŋ, ń ga tɛɛ baal la banna yir Asaf la n na binni koori kɔrni la, ú tɛŋ daazi ń teŋri ga kuari gbessi du diikpeg la n dugli Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuzenaa, a bolzeŋ koŋliizeŋ ani n dia. Kɔraawiizi n faa du n be wia, kunla maa miŋ suŋŋɛɛ lii a koori be, u tɛmbuu. 9Denii n faa kpa la Muu Yufretis baŋgia hɛri nabɔnzi la be, di ga kpa a hɔna tɛɛ baa. A koorizeŋ faa gillɔɔ laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ni banla n tinni zagra faa tɔ n see ga hel de.
10Denii baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Sanbalat, u lii Bɛf Hɔrɔn ni u dɔŋhiŋ bɛl banna yir Tobia, n faa ɛɛ Ammɔn hina nabɔma bɛl, nuu lugɔ nɛbɛl ballɔɔ, ú wa kuari Izrɛl hina bolzeŋ la ma. A guŋ faa ra fuuh ba baana werge maa.
Nɛhɛmia n gaagɛɛ binni Jɛrusalɛm koŋlaa wia
11N kpa la Jɛrusalɛm, di ga du de hɔpizaa ahoro. 12N ni baala tama izi hamuŋa bɛl, ka maa nɛr maa be ŋɔwɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ du n bampirii lugɔ ń wa ɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm. A saŋa, kuntinnaa faa waa hoo, di kawee la miŋ tinnɛɛ la bɛŋ lɛi.
13Hamuŋa ni, n ga Waluu Dominuuzeŋ la lii, di kpa la unla banna yir Hohobia Kɔlɔŋ la, di kaa lii de di kpa la unla banna yir Nabina Dominuuzeŋ la. Aabuu n binni, di na gunla Jɛrusalɛm koŋlaa maa n purgee ni gunla u dominuuzenaa maa n fuuhwe. 14N lii de la Bule Dominuuzeŋ la, di lii de ga hel Koori Pol la. Ka bɔr faa waa hoo, n kawee ga. 15Awia, n tuu a waluu a hamuŋa ni, di binni a koŋlii. A tuna, n kaa bir ga a Waluu Dominuuzeŋ la zuu a bolzeŋ biini. 16A nabɔnzi faa waa zum bɔr la maa miŋ kaalɛɛ gɛɛ wii la minna ɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n faa haa waa Jus hina gɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina gɛɛ nabɔnzenaa gɛɛ ba nabɔnzi gɛɛ nɛra la n niŋ hum a huma la be ŋɔwɛɛ, wii la miŋ ballɛ ń wa ɛɛ.
17Awia, n ŋɔ ba be, “Ií na tɔɔrɔɔ la biini yaa n duwɛɛ. Jɛrusalɛm maanii purgee chɔɔ, u dominuuzenaa maa fuuh. Ií gil ya kuari Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii la ma. Di yaa ɛɛ guŋ, yaa wàá ka du hiihzi biini.” 18N jaa ŋɔ ba be gunla Kɔraawiizi n suŋ n ni ani wii la koorizeŋ la n ŋɔ n be.
Ba sɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “Ií gil ya faari di kuari a koŋlii ma.” Awia, ba faari di ra hum a hunnanii naa.
19Sanbalat la n ɛɛ Bɛf Hɔrɔn hinuu, Tobia la n ɛɛ Ammɔn hina nabɔma ani Gɛsɛm la n ɛɛ Lɔrbi la n wa nuu guŋ, ba ra mam yaa, di ra ɛɛ yaa chɛɛtɛ, di ra ŋɔ, “Beedee ii ra ɛɛ kennei? Ii ra di a koorizenne mmɔri gɛɛ?”
20Denii n ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la daŋ tɛɛ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ ani fɔŋŋa, yá wer mau, dikuu yaa n ɛɛ u balaa wia. Yaa daŋ bir mau. Ama, iawaa nonii waa Jɛrusalɛm kapɛttɛ ni jaawɛ.”

english_text:
Rebuilding the Wall of Jerusalem
1These are the people who helped rebuild the wall and gates of Jerusalem:
The high priest Eliashib and the other priests rebuilt Sheep Gate and hung its doors. Then they dedicated Sheep Gate and the section of the wall as far as Hundred Tower and Hananel Tower.
2The people of Jericho rebuilt the next section of the wall, and Zaccur son of Imri rebuilt the section after that.
3The family of Hassenaah built Fish Gate. They put the beams in place and hung the doors, then they added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
4Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, completed the next section of the wall.
Meshullam, son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel, rebuilt the next section, and Zadok son of Baana rebuilt the section beside that.
5The next section was to be repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their town leaders refused to do the hard work they were assigned.
6Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah restored Ancient Gate. They put the beams in place, hung the doors, and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. 7Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the men from Gibeon and Mizpah rebuilt the next section of the wall. This section reached as far as the house of the governor of West Euphrates Province.
8Uzziel son of Harhaiah the goldsmith rebuilt the next section.
Hananiah the perfume maker rebuilt the section next after that, and it went as far as Broad Wall.
9Rephaiah son of Hur ruled half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall.
10The section after that was close to the home of Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and he rebuilt it.
Hattush son of Hashabneiah constructed the next section of the wall.
11Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath Moab rebuilt the section after that, and they also built Oven Tower.
12Shallum son of Hallohesh ruled the other half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. Shallum's daughters also worked with him.
13Hanun and the people who lived in the town of Zanoah rebuilt Valley Gate. They hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. They also rebuilt the wall for 440 meters, all the way to Garbage Gate.
14Malchijah son of Rechab ruled the district of Beth-Haccherem, and he rebuilt Garbage Gate. He hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
15Shallum son of Colhozeh ruled the district of Mizpah, and he rebuilt Fountain Gate. He put a cover over the gateway, then hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. He also rebuilt the wall at Shelah Pool. This section was next to the king's garden and went as far as the stairs leading down from David's City.
16Nehemiah son of Azbuk ruled half of the district of Beth-Zur, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. It went as far as the royal cemetery, the artificial pool, and the army barracks.
Levites Who Worked on the Wall
17The Levites who worked on the next sections of the wall were Rehum son of Bani; Hashabiah, who ruled half of the district of Keilah and did this work for his district; 18Binnui son of Henadad, who ruled the other half of the district of Keilah; 19Ezer son of Jeshua, who ruled Mizpah, rebuilt the section of the wall that was in front of the armory and reached to the corner of the wall; 20Baruch son of Zabbai eagerly rebuilt the section of the wall that went all the way to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest; 21Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, built up to the far end of Eliashib's house.
Priests Who Worked on the Wall
22Here is a list of the priests who worked on the wall:
Priests from the region around Jerusalem rebuilt the next section of the wall.
23Benjamin and Hasshub rebuilt the wall in front of their own houses.
Azariah, who was the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah, rebuilt the section in front of his house.
24Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section of the wall from Azariah's house to the corner of the wall.
25Palal son of Uzai rebuilt the next section, which began at the corner of the wall and the tower of the upper palace near the court of the guard.
Pedaiah son of Parosh rebuilt the next section of the wall. 26He stopped at a place near the Water Gate on the east and the tower guarding the temple. This was close to a section in the city called Ophel, where the temple workers lived.
Other Builders Who Worked on the Wall
27The men from Tekoa rebuilt the next section of the wall, and it was their second section. It started at a place across from the large tower that guarded the Temple, and it went all the way to the wall near Ophel.
28Some priests rebuilt the next section of the wall. They began working north of Horse Gate, and each one worked on a section in front of his own house.
29Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the wall in front of his house.
Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who looked after the East Gate, rebuilt the section after that.
30Hananiah and Hanun rebuilt the next section, which was the second section for them.
Meshullam son of Berechiah rebuilt the next section, which happened to be in front of his house.
31Malchijah, a goldsmith, rebuilt the next section, as far as the house used by the temple workers and merchants. This area was across from Gathering Gate, near the room on top of the wall at the northeast corner.
32The goldsmiths and merchants rebuilt the last section of the wall, which went from the corner room all the way to Sheep Gate.
translation_text:
Baŋ bittɛ ra ma Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii wia
1Kenne ba faa bir kuari a bolzeŋ koŋliizeŋ ma. Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Ɛliasib ni u dɔŋahina, faa kuari dominuuzeŋ la banna yir Peeza Dominuuzeŋ la ma, di kpau du Kɔraawiizi nonee, ka du u gbessi. Ba faa ma a koŋliizeŋ guŋŋ di ga hel dominuuzeŋ la banna yir Kalfa Diijaŋ ni Hananɛl Diijaŋ la, di kpau du Kɔraawiizi nonee.
2Bolzeŋ Jɛriko baala ge ma a koŋlii bɔr la n kaa ra hiŋ. Baŋ wa hel see, Imri biibaal Zakur ge ma hiŋ.
3Hasɛnaa biibaala ge kuari Nyinni Dominuuzeŋ la hiŋ, di du u dolli, gbessi, lugbidaazi ani u kattibɔra. 4Yuria biibaal Mɛrɛmɔf, u naabaal faa ɛɛ Hakɔz, ge ma a koŋlii bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ. Bɛrɛkia biibaal Mɛsulam, u naabaal faa ɛɛ Mɛsɛzabɛl, ge faa kuari a koŋlii yeŋ ma hiŋ. Baana biibaal Zadɔk ge kuari a koŋlii yeŋ ma hiŋ. 5Tɛkua baala ge kuari ma a koŋlii bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ. Banna ma la, ba nabɔnzenaa la n du a bol waa sɛɛwɛ bá hum huma la ba binna n tɛɛ baa la.
6Denii Pasia biibaal Jɔyada ni Bɛsɔdɛya biibaal Mɛsulam ge kaa kuari Jɛsana Dominuuzeŋ la hiŋ. Ba faa du u dolli, gbessi, lugbidaazi ani u kattibɔra. 7Gibiɔn hinuu Mɛlatia, Mɛrɔnɔf hinuu Jadɔn ani Gibiɔn ni Mizpa baala, ge ma a koŋlii guŋŋ di ga hel Muu Yufretis Wiicholii nabɔma dia. 8Hahaaya biibaal Uziɛl, n faa ɛɛ saliŋ luuri, kuari ma bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ. Hanania la ge n faa ɛɛ tulaale kuari, la genii faa ma bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ. Gunnɛ ba faa ɛɛ, di kuari Jɛrusalɛm koŋliizeŋ la maa ma guŋŋ di ga hel u bɔr la banna yir Koŋlii War la. 9Denii Hur biibaal Rɛfaaya, n faa ɛɛ nabɔma di ra binni Jɛrusalɛm keŋkere bɛl, ge faa kuari ma u yeŋ hiŋ. 10Harumaf biibaal Jɛdaaya ge kuari ma u bɔr la n dugli u dia, di hiŋ. Hasabnɛya biibaal Hatus ge kuari ma u yeŋ hiŋ. 11Harim biibaal Malkija ni Pahaf Moab biibaal Hasub genii kuarɛɛ ma u bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ ani u bɔr la banna yir Paanuu Ɔɔzibɔra Diijaŋ la. 12Halɔhɛs biibaal Salum la n faa ɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm keŋkere bɛl nabɔma ni u biihaana ge kuari ma u yeŋ hiŋ.
13Baal la baŋ faa ra yir Hanun ge ni Zanoa hinaa ge faa ma u bɔr la banna yir Waluu Dominuuzeŋ la. Baŋ wa kuaruu ma, ba du de domininuuzeŋ gbessi ni a kattibɔra. Ba faa kuaruubuu ma guŋŋ nogumzi kagboŋ, di ga hel u bɔr la banna yir Kpaga Dominuuzeŋ la.
14Rɛkab biibaal la baŋ faa ra yir Malkija n faa ɛɛ Bɛf Hakɛrɛm paga nabɔma, genii faa kuari Kpaga Dominuuzeŋ la, di du u dolli, gbessi, lugbidaazi ani u kattibɔra.
15Baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Kol Hɔzɛ biibaal Salum, n faa ɛɛ Mizpa paga nabɔma ge ma a koŋlii bɔr la banna yir Bule Dominuuzeŋ la. U faa kuaruubuu ma, di tɔ u nyuu, di du u gbessi ni a kattikuna. U kaa kuari ma Silɔam Pol koŋlii la n dugli Koori Kambol guŋŋ di ga hel lɔŋa la n lii Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ di tuu ra la la. 16Azbuk biibaal Nɛhɛmia la n faa ɛɛ Bɛf Zur paga yeŋ nabɔma ge faa kuari a koŋlii bɔr la n kawɛɛ la ma guŋŋ di chaŋ Koori Deevid Ŋmam, di ga hel pol la baŋ kiwee ani Laallɔkpega Dia la.
17Levi dee ni ba sitɔɔri Bani biibaal Rɛhum ge kuari ma hiŋ. Hasabia la n faa ɛɛ Keila paga yeŋ nabɔma, ge faa kuari ma ba paga koŋlii yeŋ di hiŋ. 18Baal bɛl ge baŋ faa ra yir Hɛnadad biibaal Binui n faa ɛɛ Keila paga yeŋ nabɔma, ni u bol hina faa kuari ma a koŋlii yeŋ di hiŋ. 19Baŋ ga hel de, Jesua biibaal Ɛza, n faa ɛɛ Mizpa nabɔma ge faa kuari a koŋlii bɔr la n du ba dɔŋkuna dia see guŋŋ di ga hel a koŋlii sirii. 20Baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Zabai ge biibaal Baruk faa aah siwii, di faari a sirii di kuaruu ma guŋŋ di ga hel Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Ɛliasib dominua. 21Yuria biibaal Mɛrɛmɔf, u naabaal ɛɛ Hakɔz, ge faa ma lii Ɛliasib dia dominua ga hel a dia tuna.
22Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n soge bar Jɛrusalɛm, ge ma a koŋlii yeŋ di hiŋ. 23Bɛnjamin ni Hasub ge faa kuari ma a koŋlii bɔra la n du ba dia see. Maasɛya biibaal Azaria, u naabaallɛ faa Anania, ge faa ma a koŋlii bɔr la n dugli u dia. 24Hɛnadad biibaal Binui ge kuari a koŋlii ma lii Azaria dia guŋŋ di ga hel a koŋlii sirii. 25Uzai biibaal Palal ge kuari a koŋlii yeŋ ma chaŋ a koŋlii sirii ni diijaŋ la n saagɛɛ lii kooridia chiŋ n dugli guuri diŋŋee la. Parɔs biibaal Pɛdaaya ge kuari ma hiŋ. 26Kɔraawiizi Dia balaa la n faa du Ɔfɛl giŋgimii la ge kuari a koŋlii ma guŋŋ di ga hel u wiifurii, di chaŋ Nii Dominuuzeŋ la, di ra la u diijaŋ la n saagɛɛ la zɛɛ. 27Tɛkua baala ge kaa ma a koŋlii guŋŋ lii diijaŋ la n saagɛɛ, di ga hel Ɔfɛl koŋlii la. Ba mai nɛɛhinnɛ guŋ.
28Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ge kuari ma a koŋlii bɔr la n pɛli Zagu Dominuuzeŋ la di ra la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag. Bɛl maa ma u dia see. 29Ima biibaal Zadɔk ge ma a koŋlii bɔr la n chaŋ u dia hiŋ. Sɛkania biibaal Sɛmaaya la n faa ɛɛ Wiifurii Dominuuzeŋ guuri ge ma a koŋlii yeŋ hiŋ. 30Sɛlɛmia biibaal Hanania ni Zalaf biibambinumbɛlhiŋ, Hanun ge kaa kuari a koŋlii yeŋ ma hiŋ. Bɛrɛkia biibaal Mɛsulam ge kuari a koŋlii bɔr la n chaŋ u dia ma. 31Saliŋ luuri Malkija ge kuari ma a koŋlii guŋŋ di ga hel Kɔraawiizi Dia balaa ni kɔkɔɔza dia n chaŋ Mifkad Dominuuzeŋ guŋŋ di ga chug dia la n du u sirii chiŋ la. 32Saliŋ luura ni kɔkɔɔza ge kuari a koŋlii tuna ma, di lii u sirii chiŋ dia guŋŋ di ga chug Peeza Dominuuzeŋ.

english_text:
Nehemiah's Enemies
1When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people. 2In front of his friends and the Samaritan army he said, “What is this feeble bunch of Jews trying to do? Are they going to rebuild the wall and offer sacrifices all in one day? Do they think they can make something out of this pile of scorched stones?”
3Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
4But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war. 5Don't forgive the mean and evil way they have insulted the builders.”
6The people worked hard, and we built the walls of Jerusalem halfway up again. 7But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry 8and decided to stir up trouble, and to fight against the people of Jerusalem. 9But we kept on praying to our God, and we also stationed guards day and night.
10Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song:
“So much rubble for us to haul!
Worn out and weary,
will we ever finish this wall?”
11Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
12On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side, 13and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows. 14Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
15Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
16From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers 17who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon. 18Even the workers who were rebuilding the wall strapped on a sword. The worker who was to blow the signal trumpet stayed with me.
19I told the people and their officials and leaders, “Our work is so spread out, that we are a long way from one another. 20If you hear the sound of the trumpet, come quickly and gather around me. Our God will help us fight.”
21Every day from dawn to dark, half of the workers rebuilt the walls, while the rest stood guard with their spears.
22I asked the men in charge and their workers to stay inside Jerusalem and stand guard at night. So they guarded the city at night and worked during the day. 23I even slept in my work clothes at night; my relatives, the workers, and the guards slept in theirs as well. And we always kept our weapons close by.
translation_text:
Nɛhɛmia dɔma wia
1Sanbalat n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ yaa Jus hina bittɔɔ kuari a koŋlii di ra ma la, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u ra ɛɛ yaa chɛɛtɛ. 2Awia, u jaa chi u dɔŋahina ni bolzeŋ Samaria hina laallɔɔra be, di ŋɔ, “Beedee Jus hina nɛvɛɛlaa naa ra ɛɛ gunnɛi? Ba kaa ra nyiŋŋuu bá bir kuari ba koŋlii naa maa? Ba daŋ lizi mbusuzii gɛɛ? Ba daŋ maubuu tuŋ hɔpizi kpaŋaa? Ba daŋ kaa wer kpa bifuuhlaa naa di maa?”
3Denii Ammɔn hinuu Tobia n chigɛ u kɛra la ge ŋɔ, “Beedee koŋliire ba ra ma kennei? Di nyɛgɛ gba haŋ tinni ba bia koŋlii naa ni gba, u daŋ chol.”
4Awia, n suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, nuu yaa be, dikuu banna gbɛlli yaa wia. Gil chagzaa naa banna chagzi yaa naa laŋŋi ba ni. Kpa baa du ba dɔma nonee, bá lɔ ba laal, di lauri baa kaali hɛrdumazi. 5Gilɛɛ gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa, di gilɛɛ suuh ba wichɔgaa wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba chagzi yaa banla n na mau.”
6Awia, yaa faa ma a koŋlii guŋŋ di ga hel u galga, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɛra maanii faa aah siwii.
7Denii Sanbalat, Tobia, Lɔrbizi, Ammɔn ani Asdɔd hina maa n faa wa nuuwɛ lugɔ yaa wettoo di ra ma Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii hiŋ, di ra fargi u bowooni, ba baana fuuh werge maa. 8Awia, ba maa ta jina bá ga lɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina, di koozi wia du yaa ni. 9Ka yaa faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, di lizi nɛra ba ra guu yaa wibaŋa ni hamuŋa maa.
10A biinii, Juda hina ŋɔ, “A maara bɔra ra huauh, hembugle la ge du kaŋ werge. Awia, yaa wàá wer kuari a koŋlii ma.”
11Yaa dɔma ge ŋɔ, “Mɔɔ ka ba zum guŋ gɛɛ di na yaa, di yaa zuu ba biini kpu baa, a huma tuŋ.”
12Denii Jus hina la n soge dugli baa la, ba di wa ŋɔ yaa be nua bufi, di ŋɔ, “Bɔr la maa iin niŋ ga, ba daŋ teŋ yaa di lɔ yaa.”
13Awia, n gil baŋhina lii domeezi biini, di vɔɔ ni ba tokobizi, kandaazi ani hozi, di ga guu ba bariizi koŋlii bɔra la baŋ faa haa waa mawɛɛ tuŋ la. 14Miŋ binni wia guŋŋ di wa kaali, n izi chi, ka ŋɔ nabɔnzenaa, nabɔnzi ani a nɛra maa be, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm baa. Ií ra liizi Kɔraawiizi la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge, u wia kaa dɔɔ ɔnsii werge la, ka izi naa tɛɛ ii lulla, ii biizi, ii haana ani ii diini.”
15Yaa dɔma n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ yaa zum ba jina la baŋ tawɛɛ la wiarɛ, Kɔraawiizi ge kaa chɔguu la, yaa jaa bir la a koŋlii bɔr, bɛl maa kaa gaa hum u huma.
16Di lii a hɔl hiŋ, n huŋhunna hiŋ yeŋ ɔɔ ra humuu, ka ba yeŋ ge laali ba laal laala di kpogli kandaazi, laal pɛrɛtuzi ani hozi di guu. Nabɔnzi la ge chi Juda hina la 17n na ma a koŋlii la har. Banla n na chi kuna ɔɔ kpa nonii bɛllɛ di ra hum, ka kpa bɛl ge di kpogli dɔŋkuŋ. 18A maara bɛl maa ge ɔɔ kpa u tokobi vɔɔ u chara ka ra hum. Nɛr la n ɔɔ faa ra huuh bensuno la ge ɔɔ chi n kɛra.
19Denii n ŋɔ a nabɔnzenaa, nabɔnzi ani a nɛra maa be, “Huma la bɔr wassɔɔ, yaa waa ɔɔ chi a koŋlii zɛɛ dugli dɔŋa. 20Di ii wa nuu bensunoniina wiraa bɔr la maa, ií ra ba yaa be de. Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la daŋ naa tɛɛ yaa!”
21Awia, yaa yeŋ ɔɔ faa ra humuu, ka yaa yeŋ ge kpogli kandaazi, di lii chɔɔzimpikke guŋŋ di ga hel saŋa la bɔr n ɔɔ waa lauri siwee, chinchiŋwilaa ra lii la. 22A saŋa hiŋ, n ŋɔ a nɛra be lugɔ baal maa ni u hiini ɔɔ du Jɛrusalɛm hamuŋa ni di ra guu yaa, ka di hɔɔ wa pizɔɔ bá ra hum. 23Miŋ gɛɛ n niuna gɛɛ n huŋhunna gɛɛ a guure n faa du n be la, bɛl maa faa waa u laala witte, ka ɔɔ kpogli u dɔŋkuŋ, haali di u waa la ú ga ɛɛ nii gba.

english_text:
Nehemiah's Concern for the Poor
1Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power 2and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
3Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
4Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards. 5We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
6When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry. 7 So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?”
Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders 8by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
9I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us. 10My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return. 11Now give back the fields, vineyards, olive orchards, and houses you have taken and also the interest you have been paid.”
12The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.”
So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property. 13Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.”
The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised.
Nehemiah Is Generous
14I was governor of Judah from the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king until the thirty-second year. And during these entire twelve years, my relatives and I refused to accept the food that I was allowed. 15Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them. 16I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing. 17I usually fed 150 of our own Jewish people and their leaders, as well as foreign visitors from surrounding lands. 18Each day one ox, six of the best sheep, and lots of chickens were prepared. Then every ten days, a large supply of wine was brought in. I knew what a heavy burden this would have been for the people, and so I did not ask for my food allowance as governor.
19I pray that God will bless me for everything I have done for my people.
translation_text:
Nɛhɛmia n hiini nyaara wia
1A saŋa hiŋ, baala ni ba haana faa nuumi di ra du ba dɔŋa Jus hina. 2Baŋhina ra ŋɔ, “Yaa biizi kpillɔɔ werge. Yaa ra nyiŋŋi miarɛ yá di, di piri.”
3Denii baŋhina ge faa ra ŋɔ, “Yaa kpa yaa kooni, yaa grepu daazi kooni ani diinii dau talma, ka ya wer na mia nɛnnɛ a hel yaa dii, lɔchɔgii saŋa.”
4Baŋhina ge ŋɔ, “Yaa kim kebeere turgi yaa kooni ni yaa grepu daazi kooni lampoo tɛɛ koori. 5Yaa maa ɛɛ nɛdeekpannɛ. Gunla ba biizi n duwɛɛ, gunnɛ yaa gba biizi du. Ka aabuu la, yaa biizii yaa kpa birgi yoma. Yaa biihaana baŋhinaa yaa kpa yoo, ba birgi yoma. Yaa waa fɔŋŋa maa dɔɔwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa kooni ni yaa grepu daazi kooni maanii birgi nɛra baŋhina hora.”
6Miŋ wa nuu ba nuumaa naa, n baaŋ fuuh werge maa. 7Denii n fɛ a wia nfɛrɛ guŋŋ ka hau a nabɔnzenaa ni a nabɔnzi ni, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ɛrɛɛ ii ra sag ii himmaa lulla nii gunnɛi?” Denii n chaali nɛkpila ya binni a wia biini. 8N ŋɔ ba be, “Filaŋkennaa, yaa bittɔɔ yau yaa lulla Jus hina la baŋ faa yoowe tɛɛ banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la. Ka ii kaa biruu ra yoo baa, ka ba kaa wa yoo baa tɛɛ yaa.” Denii ba maa faa so kirkirkir, dikuu baŋ waa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ ba ŋɔ wia.
9Denii n kaa ŋɔ, “Wii naa iinna ɛɛ naa waa deŋlee. A dɛkkɔɔ iinna hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa. Guŋ daŋ gil yaa dɔma la n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la, wàá na bɔr di ra ɛɛ yaa chɛɛtɛ. 10Miŋwaa ni n lulla ni n huŋhunna ra kim a nɛraa kebee ni mia, ka yaa wàá fir baa bá turgi. 11Ií gil ba kima maa tɛɛ baa, di kebeere gɛɛ mia gɛɛ siŋ gɛɛ ɔlivi nuurɛ. Ií bir kpa ba kooni, grepu daazi kooni maa ani ba diini tɛɛ baa manaŋ!”
12Ba ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ bir kpaa tɛɛ baa. Yaa wàá ka lɛɛ baa kummaa di jaa. Yaa daŋ hiŋ i nua.”
Denii n faa gil Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la maa chaali, di gil nabɔnzenaa ni nabɔnzi hɛɛhzi lugɔ ba daŋ ɛɛ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ hiŋ. 13Denii n lizi n tagta di zigluu, ka ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Kenne Kɔ́raawiizi zigli nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ nua naa hiŋaa. U dia ni u kundɔɔlaa maa daŋ lii u nonii.”
Awia, a nɛra maa ŋɔ, “Ami!” Ka ba jaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ, di ɛɛ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ba daŋ ɛɛ la.
14Di lii Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii binni tokkohiŋ biinii, ba liziŋ n ɛɛ nabɔma Juda hɛri guŋŋ di wa hel u binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anɛɛhiŋ. Binni fidaanɛɛrɛ guŋ, di n ni n lulla bɛl maa haa waa diwee la baŋ ɔɔ ra tɛɛ a hɛri nabɔma la diwee. 15Ka nabɔma la n faa diwee mɔɔ ka a wa heliŋ lawaa, ɔɔ faa ra sunni a nɛraa werge maa. U ɔɔ faa lɛɛ baabuu saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau tokkoanɛɛ, diwee ani siŋ hɔpizii maa. A nabɔma harbɔɔhiŋra ge ɔɔ faa kpogli baabuu di ra sunni, ka miŋwaa waa guŋ ɛɛwɛ, dikuu minna ɔm Kɔraawiizi wia. 16Ama, miŋwaa faa kpa n siaahmu maanii du a koŋlii mai wia biini. N huŋhunna maanii chaali a koŋlii zɛɛ, yaa ra hum a huma. Yaa waa hɛri maa lɛɛwɛ.
17Aŋ faa weruu ra tɛɛ Jus hina ni ba nabɔnzi kalfa ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fii diwee digiidigii, ba ra di, di ɔɔ kaa tɛɛ hɛrdumazi nɛra la n bar yaa la n ɔɔ faa ba n be diwee, ba maa ra di. 18Hɔpizii maa, nau, penanaa anumbɛl ani zagkpilaa ba ɔɔ faa daali tɛŋ. A hɔpizaa fi maa, siŋ maa deere ba ɔɔ faa daali su bɔr. Annii maa biini, ka maa ɔɔ faa lɛɛ kummaa lii a hɛri nabɔma kuntɛɛlaa biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɛra tɔɔrɔɔ faa nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ.
19Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, gil n wia parii, í ra liizi n wia, dikuu gunla miŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ nɛra naa wia.

english_text:
Plots against Nehemiah
1Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and our other enemies learned that I had completely rebuilt the wall. All I lacked was hanging the doors in the gates. 2Then Sanballat and Geshem sent a message, asking me to meet with them in one of the villages in Ono Valley. I knew they were planning to harm me in some way. 3So I sent messengers to tell them, “My work is too important to stop now and go there. I can't afford to slow down the work just to visit with you.” 4They invited me four times, but each time I refused to go.
5Finally, Sanballat sent an official to me with an unsealed letter, 6which said:
A rumor is going around among the nations that you and the other Jews are rebuilding the wall and planning to rebel, because you want to be their king. And Geshem says it's true! 7You even have prophets in Jerusalem, claiming you are now the king of Judah. You know the Persian king will hear about this, so let's get together and talk it over.
8I sent a message back to Sanballat, saying, “None of this is true! You are making it all up.”
9Our enemies were trying to frighten us and to keep us from our work. But I asked God to give me strength.
10One day I went to visit Shemaiah. He wasn't supposed to leave his house, but he said, “Let's hurry to the holy place of the temple and hide there. We will lock the temple doors, because your enemies are planning to kill you tonight.”
11I answered, “Why should someone like me have to run and hide in the temple to save my life? I won't go!”
12Suddenly I realized that God had not given Shemaiah this message. But Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to trick me 13and to frighten me into doing something wrong, because they wanted to ruin my good name.
14Then I asked God to punish Tobiah and Sanballat for what they had done. I prayed that God would punish the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who, together with her, had tried to frighten me.
The Work Is Finished
15On the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, the wall was completely rebuilt. It had taken 52 days. 16When our enemies in the surrounding nations learned that the work was finished, they felt helpless, because they knew that our God had helped us rebuild the wall.
17All this time the Jewish leaders and Tobiah had been writing letters back and forth. 18Many people in Judah were loyal to Tobiah for two reasons: Shecaniah son of Arah was his father-in-law, and Tobiah's son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah. 19The people would always tell me about the good things Tobiah had done, and then they would tell Tobiah everything I had said. So Tobiah kept sending letters, trying to frighten me.
translation_text:
Baŋ ta Nɛhɛmia wichɔgaa ɛɛi jina wia
1Sanbalat, Tobia ani Gɛsɛm la n ɛɛ Lɔrbi la ni yaa dɔma n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ n bittɔɔ kuari a koŋlii ma, haali di tɔɔgi u bowooni maa, ka n haa waa u dominuuzenaa gbessi waa duwɛɛ la, 2Sanbalat ni Gɛsɛm tili ŋɔ n be, “Ba ya na dɔŋa bola la bɛl n du Ono Lɛl biini.”
Ka ba faa ra ɛɛ dawarii bá ɛɛŋ wichɔgii bɛl. 3Denii n faa hum n balaa bá ga ŋɔ ba be, “N na ɛɛ wizeŋ bɛllɛ, awia, màá wer tuu ba ii be de. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń gil a huma ka tuu ba ii benei?” 4Bunaazu maanii ba faa tiliŋ keŋ himmaa, n ge ɔɔ bir ŋɔ a wikpaŋ.
5Denii bunue hiŋ, Sanbalat hum u balii, di sɛbi hɔŋ ŋɔ ú kpa wa tɛŋ, ka waa u nua tɔwɛɛ. 6Kenne u faa sɛbi a hɔŋ biini,
“Hɛssi maa hina nuuwɔɔ lugɔ i ni Jus hina la ɛɛ nuukpannɛ di ra nyiŋŋi ii du dɔŋ, awiarɛ ii bir kuari a koŋlii di ra ma. Gɛsɛm ge ŋɔ wibiire! Yaa kaa nuu lugɔ hinuu ra nyiŋŋi i birgi ba koori. 7A guŋ wia, i lizi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzii, bá sii i wia tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina, di ŋɔ, ‘Koori du Judaa!’ Filaŋkeŋ, a koorizeŋ daŋ nuu a wii naa. Awia, ba ya ta jina.”
8Denii n tili ŋɔ u be, “Wia naa maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa waa wibii ɛɛwɛ. I himmaa laakal wiŋɔɔlaarɛ.”
9Ba ra ɔnzi yaabuu, di ra fɛ, “Ba bɔra daŋ huah a huma humaa wia, bá gil a humaa.” Awia, n suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, tɛŋ fɔŋŋa filaŋkeŋ!”
10A hɔl bɛl, n la Dɛlaaya biibaal Sɛmaaya dia, u naabaal genii faa Mɛhɛtabɛl. U faa suah diarɛ, wàá ka wer lii baaŋ. U ŋɔ n be, “Gil ya la ga suah Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, ka tɔɔgi u dominuuzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ra nyiŋŋuu bá wa kpui hamuŋa naa.”
11Denii n ŋɔ u be, “Mìŋ́ baal du keŋ di chɔ ra suah? Ń chɔ ga suah Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, dikuu n miibɔɔ wiaa? Akai, màá ɛɛ guŋ!” 12N faa nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi lɛi hum Sɛmaaya. Sanbalat ni Tobiare lɔu paah, di ŋɔ ú wa ŋɔ wia du n ni. 13Ba kpaubuu ú wa ɔnziŋ, ń ɛɛ wichɔgaa lugɔ kennaa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa, bá jaa chɔg n sɔŋ, di duŋ hiihzi.
14Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, a liizi gunla Tobia ni Sanbalat n ɛɛwɛ. A liizi gunla dɔgtɛɛ Noadia la n ɛɛ haaŋ ni dɔgtɛɛzi la maa n faa ra nyiŋŋi bá ɔnziŋ la wia.
A koŋlii mai tunaa wia
15Baagu la banna yir Ɛlul, u hɔpizaa tokko ni anuehiŋ hɔllɛ, ba faa ma a koŋlii tuŋ. Hɔpizaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fidaanɛɛrɛ ba faa kpa mau tuŋ. 16Yaa dɔma ani hɛssi la maa hina n bar yaa n wa nuu guŋ, ɔnsii faa lau baa, ba bɔra huah, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa zummɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la hiinaare gillɛ a huma hum.
17A saŋa hiŋ, Juda hina nabɔnzenaa faa ra sɛbi hɔna kpila di ra tɛɛ Tobia, u ge bir sɛbi ra tɛɛ baa. 18Jus hinuu Ara biibaal Sɛkania n faa ɛɛ u hila wia, Juda hina kpila maanii faa chigɛ u har. Di kaa kpa jaa, u biibaal Jɛhɔhanan ge faa kpa Mɛsulam biihaannɛ. A Mɛsulam ge mɛɛrɛ faa Bɛrɛkia. 19A nɛra ɔɔ faa bagli wipazi la maa Tobia n ɛɛwɛnɛ tɛŋ, ka bir ga ŋɔ u be gunla n ge n ŋɔwɛɛ. Tobia sɛbi hɔna tɛŋ, di ra ɔnziŋ.

1After the wall had been rebuilt and the gates hung, then the temple guards, the singers, and the other Levites were assigned their work. 2I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, along with Hananiah, the commander of the fortress, because Hananiah could be trusted, and he respected God more than most people did. 3I said to them, “Don't let the gates to the city be opened until the sun has been up for a while. And make sure that they are closed and barred before the guards go off duty at sunset. Choose people from Jerusalem to stand guard at different places around the wall and others to stand guard near their own houses.”
A List of Exiles Who Returned
(Ezra 2.1-70)
4Although Jerusalem covered a large area, not many people lived there, and no new houses had been built. 5-6So God gave me the idea to bring together the people, their leaders, and officials and to check the family records of those who had returned from captivity in Babylonia, after having been taken there by King Nebuchadnezzar. About this same time, I found records of those who had been the first to return to Jerusalem from Babylon Province. By reading these records, I learned that they settled in their own hometowns, 7and that they had come with Zerubbabel, Joshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah.
8-25This is a list of how many returned from each family group: 2,172 from Parosh; 372 from Shephatiah; 652 from Arah; 2,818 from Pahath Moab, who were all descendants of Jeshua and Joab; 1,254 from Elam; 845 from Zattu; 760 from Zaccai; 648 from Binnui; 628 from Bebai; 2,322 from Azgad; 667 from Adonikam; 2,067 from Bigvai; 655 from Adin; 98 from Ater, also known as Hezekiah; 328 from Hashum; 324 from Bezai; 112 from Hariph; and 95 from Gibeon.
26-38This is a list of how many returned whose ancestors had come from the following towns: 188 from Bethlehem and Netophah; 128 from Anathoth; 42 from Beth-Azmaveth; 743 from Kiriath-Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth; 621 from Ramah and Geba; 122 from Michmas; 123 from Bethel and Ai; 52 from Nebo; 1,254 from Elam; 320 from Harim; 345 from Jericho; 721 from Lod, Hadid, and Ono; and 3,930 from Senaah.
39-42This is a list of how many returned from each family of priests: 973 descendants of Jeshua from Jedaiah; 1,052 from Immer; 1,247 from Pashhur; and 1,017 from Harim.
43-45This is a list of how many returned from the families of Levites: 74 descendants of Hodevah from the families of Jeshua and Kadmiel; 148 descendants of Asaph from the temple musicians; and 138 descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai from the temple guards.
46-56These are the names of the families of temple workers whose descendants returned: Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth, Keros, Sia, Padon, Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai, Hanan, Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah, Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim, Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur, Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha, Barkos, Sisera, Temah, Neziah, and Hatipha.
57-59Here are the names of Solomon's servants whose descendants returned: Sotai, Sophereth, Perida, Jaala, Darkon, Giddel, Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Amon.
60A total of 392 descendants of temple workers and of Solomon's servants returned.
61-62There were 642 who returned from the families of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, though they could not prove they were Israelites. They had lived in the Babylonian towns of Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer.
63-64The families of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai could not prove they were priests. The ancestor of the family of Barzillai had married the daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and had taken his wife's family name. But the records of these three families could not be found, and none of them were allowed to serve as priests. 65 In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until he lets us know if you really are priests.”
66-69There were 42,360 who returned, in addition to 7,337 servants and 245 musicians, counting both men and women. Altogether, they brought with them 736 horses, 245 mules, 435 camels, and 6,720 donkeys.
70-72Many people gave gifts to help pay for the materials to rebuild the temple. The governor himself gave 8 kilograms of gold, 50 bowls to be used in the temple, and 530 robes for the priests. Family leaders gave 153 kilograms of gold and 1,458 kilograms of silver. The rest of the people gave 153 kilograms of gold, 1,325 kilograms of silver, and 67 robes for the priests.
73 And so, by the seventh month, priests, Levites, temple guards, musicians, workers, and many of the ordinary people had settled in the towns of Judah.
