Denii u jaa vol di ra gaagi a bolzeŋkpeg biini maa di ra chɛɛhgi werge maa ni biinichɔg. 2Uŋ wa hel koori dominua, waa sɛɛwɛ u zuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waa ɔɔ sɛɛ nɛr la maa n laali gbɔglɔŋ laala zuu de. 3Hɛri la maa koori widaulifalii naa n haŋ wa hel, biinichɔg werge maa ɔɔ lau Jus hina la n du de labuu, ba ra vɔɔ nuuzi di ra chɛɛhgi werge maa. Bakpila maa ɔɔ chɔɔgi hɛrii ni ba gbɔglɔnzi, di ɛɛ hɔɔhri waari ba nyuuni maa.
4Biihambizi la n ɛɛ Ɛsta balaa ni nɛvaraa la n na du u tau la n wa ŋɔ Mɔdɛkai wia tɛu, biinichɔg faa lawuubuu werge maa. Denii u gil ba kpa laala aŋhina ga tɛu ú laali ka wir a gbɔglɔŋ la, ka u vɛɛa. 5Ɛsta yir koori nɛvaraa la bɛl n na binnuu, u sɔŋ di Hatak la, di humuu ú ga pɛɛzi Mɔdɛkai, ú bagli wii la n na tɔɔruu ani u zɛɛ.
6Denii Hatak kpa la Mɔdɛkai be, di u sogo a bolzeŋ bɔchaaŋ la n chɔɔ koori dominua nɛra ɔɔ ra so de la. 7Mɔdɛkai bagli wii la maa n huuzuu ani kebee la maga Haman n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ turgi di du koori daama kuna dauribɔr, ka bá kpu Jus hina maa la. 8U kaa kpa hɔŋ la n na bagli lugɔ ba dim Jus hina maa, la di gil u wia yaari Susa la bɛl tɛɛ Hataki ú ga tɛɛ Ɛsta, di chaani u wia siwee maa tɛu. U kaa ŋɔ a nɛvarii be lugɔ ú la Ɛsta be di ga ŋɔ u be, siaahmu maa lugɔ ú la koori be di ga suŋŋuu, ú na Jus hina la sinyɛna, di suŋ ba ni.
9Hatak bir la ga bagli wii la maa Mɔdɛkai n ŋɔwɛɛ la tɛɛ Ɛsta. 10Denii Ɛsta kaa ŋɔ Hatak be lugɔ ú la ga ŋɔ u be, 11“Koori zɛɛsogna ni nɛra la maa n du u kora hɛssi la zummɔ lugɔ widauliirɛ lugɔ nɛr la maa, baal gɛɛ haaŋ, n niŋ zuu koori be u dia biini diŋŋee la, di koori wɔɔ yittɛ lɛi, dɛg kpuirɛ. Ama, di koori lalli u saliŋ daŋkpala tɛruu waa, guŋ bɛnnɛ niŋ wer lɛɛu. Hɔpizaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔɔ zinaa, di koori haa wan yittɛ.”
12Hitaki n wa ŋɔ wia la Ɛsta n ŋɔwɛɛ naa tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai, 13kenne Mɔdɛkai ŋɔ ba bir ga ŋɔ Ɛsta be, “Wiche, gilɛɛ waa fɛ lugɔ hin du kooridia la wia, i bɛnnɛ niŋ na i hiŋ lii a Jus hina maa biini. 14Di i siigɔɔ wia naa biini, Jus hina daŋ na lɛɛi di lii yembɛl, ka ba daŋ chɔgi hiŋwaa ni i mɛɛ diahina maa. Di kennaa wiarɛ i wa ɛɛ koori haaŋ, i zummɔaa?”
15Denii Ɛsta ŋɔ ba bir ga ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai. 16“La ga chaali Jus hina la maa n du bolzeŋkpeg Susa la ii vɔɔ nua tɛŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa di gɛɛ di wàá nyɔɔ nii hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi ahoro maa. N ni n balaa ge daŋ ɛɛ guŋ. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, n daŋ la koori be, haali guŋ n niŋ chɔgi a widaulii la. Di n daŋ siu gba, ń siu.”
17Denii Mɔdɛkai izi kaali di ga ɛɛ gunla maa Ɛsta n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

english_text:
Esther Invites the King and Haman to a Dinner
1Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway. 2He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her.
When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter, 3the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
4Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
5The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.”
The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner, 6and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
7-8Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.”
Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
9Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry, 10but he did not say a thing.
When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh 11and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him. 12Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow. 13But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
14Haman's wife and friends said to him, “Have a gallows built about 22 meters high, and tomorrow morning ask the king to hang Mordecai there. Then later, you can have dinner with the king and enjoy yourself.”
This seemed like a good idea to Haman, and he had the gallows built.
translation_text:
Ɛsta n yir koori ni Haman wia
1Ba nuuvɔɔi hɔpizaa ahoro la n wa tunnɛ, Ɛsta kpa u Wiche laala bɔg, di zuu kooridia biini diŋŋee la ga chi u sognibɔr dominua. A saŋa, di koori sogo u koorikara ni, u siwee chaŋ u dominua. 2Uŋ wa na Wiche Ɛsta n chigɛ a loŋ biini, u wia paruu, u kpa u saliŋ daŋkpala la n du u nonii la tɛruu. Ɛsta tuzi heluu di ga gbɔgzi a daŋkpala nua.
3Denii a koori pɛɛzi, “N haaŋ Ɛsta, a summɔaa? Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋei? Haali di hɛssi la maa minna di kora a ni la kezaa i ra nyiŋŋi, a daŋ ɛɛ i hora.”
4Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Jara, di i sɛɛwɔ, gil i ni Haman ba n dia di wa di diuzenaa miŋ daalɛɛ ń tɛi zinaa.” 5A koorizeŋ ŋɔ, “Ií yir Haman ú ba ɛŋ manaŋ, yá ɛɛ Ɛsta kipar.”
Awia, koori ni Haman kpa la diuzenaa la Ɛsta n gillɛ ba daali la bɔr, bá ga di. 6Baŋ waa nyɔɔ siŋ la, koori kaa pɛɛzi Ɛsta, “Too, i winyiŋŋiire ɛrɛɛ? I daŋ nau. Haali di n kora hɛssi kezaa i ra nyiŋŋi, i daŋ naa.”
7Ɛsta bir ŋɔ, “N winyiŋŋiire keŋ, 8Di n wia parii, Jara, i ra nyiŋŋi i tɛŋ n winyiŋŋii, guŋwaa, gil í ni Haman ba kɛrɛ di wa di diuzenaa min niŋ daali tɛɛ ia. Di ii wa ballɔ, n daŋ jaa bagli wii la minna nyiŋŋi.”
Haman baaŋ n na fuuh Mɔdɛkai ni wia
9Haman n wa lii de a hɔl hiŋ, u bɔra sɔɔnuu werge maa, u ra munzi pɛɛpɛɛ. Ka uŋ wa na Mɔdɛkai kooridia dominua, di na lugɔ waa sɛɛwɛ izi gɛɛ di ɛɛ lugɔ ɔnsii lawuu u see, u baaŋ fuuh Mɔdɛkai ni werge maa. 10Ka Haman lau u hiŋ di kaali dia.
Uŋ ga hel dia, u yir u dammuzi ni u haaŋ Zɛrɛs, 11di ta bara dikuu u daama werge ni u biibaala kpila ani gunla maa koori n kpau girme, haali di tɛu nabɔmuu u dɔŋahina nabɔntɔga ni huŋhunna nabɔnzi ni wia. 12Haman kaa ŋɔ, “A maa lɛi gba. N bɛnnɛ Wiche Ɛsta yir n jaa koori ni di ga di diuzenaa la un daalɛɛ la. U kaa yir n ni koorii lugɔ kɛrɛ yá kaa wa di. 13Ka miŋ ɔɔ ra na Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai kooridia dominua la wia, annii maa wanna tɛɛ bɔsɔna.”
14U haaŋ Zɛrɛs ni u dammuzi maa ŋɔ u be, “Gil ba baŋ ŋmɛŋsagri daa, ú chiŋ laŋaa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi tokkoahoro ni fidaanue, í suŋŋi koori, kɛrɛ chɔɔzi ú gil ba sag Mɔdɛkai ŋmɛŋ u ni. Denii í ni koori jaa la a diuzenaa bɔr di ga di ni bɔsɔna.” Haman bɔra ra pur dikuu gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wia, u gil ba baŋ a daa.

english_text:
The King Honors Mordecai
1That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king. 2 When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king, 3the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?”
“Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
4About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
5The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.”
“Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
6When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?”
Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor. 7So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man, 8get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress. 9Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
10The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
11Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
12Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame. 13Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.” 14They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_text:
Gunla baŋ tɔgzi Mɔdɛkai wia
1A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa, a koori waa wette chɔɔ dɔɔ, awia u gil ba kpa u kora wia hɔŋ n na bagli u kora wiɛɛlaa di wa karmi tɛu. 2A hɔŋ biini, ba na lugɔ Mɔdɛkai ŋmɛnɛ lizi Bigtana ni Tɛrɛs la n faa ɛɛ Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis nabɔnzi di ra guu u dia dominua la woloo, dikuu baŋ faa ta jina bá kpuu wia. 3Koori pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛ sɔnnɛ Mɔdɛkai faa na dikuu keŋ wiai? Bɛɛ kinturgaare ba tɛuwɛi?” U balaa ŋɔ, “Ba waa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ tɛu.”
4A koori pɛɛzi, “Anɛɛ n du diŋŋee biinei?” A saŋa di Haman haŋ zuu kooridia diŋŋee la n dugli bossee la, ú wa ŋɔ wia koori be lugɔ ú tɛu ŋmɛnɛɛ ba kpu Mɔdɛkai ŋmɛŋsagri daa la ni uŋ gillɛ ba baŋ la.
5U balaa ŋɔ, “Hamannɛ chigɛ diŋŋee biini.”
A koori ŋɔ, “Ií yiruu ú ba.”
6Haman n wa zuuwɛ, koori pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ n dɛkkɛ ba ɛɛ tɛɛ nɛr la wia n na par koori, ú tɛu sɔnɛi?”
Haman fɛ u biini, “Nɛr du de koori n na nyiŋŋi ú tɛɛ sɔŋ di miŋ lɛiyaa?” 7Awia, u ŋɔ koori be, “Jara, di i ra nyiŋŋi í tɛɛ nɛr sɔŋ, 8gil ba kpa i himmaa laala la hinna laali la ba ani zagu bɛl hiŋ tinnɛɛ ka ka. Ba kpa pɛrɛtujiga pɛli u hile di ra bagli lugɔ i kunnɛ. 9Í jaa gil i nabɔnzenaa himmaa la bɛl kpa a koorilaala naa di bɔg baal la hinna nyiŋŋi í tɛɛ sɔŋ la, di gil u tinni a zagu. Denii í gil nabɔnzeŋ la tɔ u see, di tɛrguu di ra gaagi a bolzeŋ biini maa ra ŋɔ kpegzi ni, ‘Kenne koori ŋɔ ba ɛɛ ra tɛɛ baal la am paruu, ú tɛu sɔŋ.’ ”
10Koori ŋɔ Haman be, “Izi manaŋ, di gil ba tɛi a laala ni a zagu, í ɛɛ gunla hiŋ baglɛɛ naa, di tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai la n ɛɛ Jus hinuu la. Waabuu ɔɔ ra so n dia dominua la. A du tau, di ɛɛ wia la maa hiŋ baglɛɛ la. Gilɛɛ waa gil bɛl maa ɛɛi.”
11Awia, Haman nyiŋŋi a koorilaala ni u zagu, di bɔg Mɔdɛkai, di gil u tinni a zagu, u kpogluu ra gaagi a bolzeŋ biini maa di ra ŋɔ kpegzi ni, “Kenne ba ɛɛ ra tɛɛ baal la am par koori ú tɛu sɔŋ.”
12A guŋ n wa ɛɛwɛ tuŋ, Mɔdɛkai bir la kooridia dominua ga so, ka Haman hahzi di kaali u dia ni biinichɔg ni hiihzi werge maa. 13Uŋ wa hel dia, u bagli wii la maa n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ u haaŋ Zɛrɛs ni u dammuzi. Ba karfuu, di ŋɔ, “Mɔdɛkai jaa ra kpegliibuu la. U ge n ɛɛ Jus hinuu naa, i nuu wàá weraa ɛɛ, i wia daŋ chɔgi.” 14Baŋ haa ra ŋɔ wia la, di koori nɛvaraa ballɔ wa yir Haman, u ni baa hahzi kaali a diuzenaa Wiche Ɛsta n gillɛ ba daali la dii bɔr.

english_text:
Haman Is Punished
1The king and Haman were dining with Esther 2and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
3Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want, 4because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
5“Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
6Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!”
Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
7The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden.
Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
8Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!”
As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head. 9Then Harbona, one of the king's personal servants, said, “Your Majesty, Haman built a gallows 22 meters high beside his house, so he could hang Mordecai on it. And Mordecai is the very one who spoke up and saved your life.”
“Hang Haman from his own gallows!” the king commanded. 10At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_text:
Baŋ sag Haman ŋmɛŋ wia
1Haman ni a koori jaa la bá ni Wiche Ɛsta ga di. 2Baŋ kaa waa nyɔɔ siŋ a hɔpizaa anɛɛhiŋ naa ge, a koori kaa pɛɛzi Wiche Ɛsta, “N haaŋ Ɛsta, i winyiŋŋiire bɛɛ? Haali di n hɛssi naa kezaa i ra nyiŋŋi gba, n daŋ tɛi.”
3Wiche Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Jara, di n wia ra parii, i bɔra sɔɔni, amɔ í lɛɛ n ni n nɛra ha. N winyiŋŋiire guŋ. 4Ba ɛɛ siryaa bá kpu n ni n nɛra maa, yaa wia tuŋ kɔrai. Di ba faa yoo yaabuu yá birgi yoma, a faa wàá tiriŋ. N daŋ vii tɔ n nua, dikuubɛɛwiai, a tɔɔrɔɔ dii faa waa kunla min niŋ kuu u wia di ra tɔɔri hiŋ koori ɛɛwɛ.”
5Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis pɛɛzi u haaŋ Ɛsta, “A hinnɛ anɛɛ? Babɛliirɛ lɔ bampirii ú ɛɛ kennei?”
6Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Yaa chɔgri ni yaa dɔnnɛ bachɔgii Haman naa!”
Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, ɔnsii werge lau Haman, koori ni u haaŋ see. 7Denii koori la izi ni baaŋfuuih werge di gil u siŋ ka zuu kooridia kambol la biini. Ka Haman n teŋ zummɛ lugɔ koori tuŋ u wiarɛ la, u ka har a dia biini di ra fɔrgi Wiche Ɛsta, ú lɛɛ u miibɔɔ.
8Saŋa la koori n haŋ lii u dia kambol la biini di bir wàá zuu, di Haman ra nyiŋŋi ú giŋŋi di chɔɔ karjaŋ la Ɛsta n dɛlli u ni la di fɔrguu.
Koori la n wa na guŋ, u koobi di ŋɔ, “Ee, akubani! U daŋ pum n haaŋ haali n nuu n kpauwɛ soo?”
Koori nua n haŋ waa chol hɛri, di ba teŋ kpa kuŋ di vɔɔ Haman siwee. 9Denii Habɔna la n ɛɛ koori nɛvaraa la bɛl, di ɔɔ du u be di ra hiinuu la ŋɔ, “Jara, ŋmɛŋsagri daa bɛl n la chiŋ lugɔ nogumzi tokkoahoro ni fidaanue, chigɔ Haman danzɛɛkɛriirɛ. U faa baŋuubuu ú kpu Mɔdɛkai la n mɔgli hìŋ́ koori ha la.”
A koori ŋɔ, “Ií kpuu u ni!” 10Awia, ba ga kpu Haman a ŋmɛŋsagri daa la uŋ baŋŋɛ ú kpu Mɔdɛkai la ni. Denii koori baaŋ jaa sɔɔni tama.

english_text:
A Happy Ending for the Jews
1Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials 2and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
3Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!” 4King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther, 5and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed, 6and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
7King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews. 8 I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
9On the twenty-third day of Sivan, the third month, the king's secretaries wrote the law. They obeyed Mordecai and wrote to the Jews, the rulers, the governors, and the officials of all 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. The letters were written in every language used in the kingdom, including the Jewish language. 10They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
11-13In these letters the king said:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies.
A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
14-15Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth.
After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered, 16and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
17In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_text:
Koori widaulii n mɔgli Jus hina wia
1A hɔl himmaanii Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis kpa Jus hina dɔm Haman la kundɔɔlaa maa tɛɛ u haaŋ Ɛsta. Ɛsta ge bagli tɛɛ koori lugɔ Mɔdɛkai ɛɛ u lullii. Di haŋ lii a hɔl hiŋ, Mɔdɛkai ɔɔ jaa weruu zuu di ga chi koori see. 2Koori lizi u nonibisig la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, u kpa ra jag hɔna ni, u birgi widaulii la tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai. Haman benii koori faa lɛɛu. Ɛsta faa gil Mɔdɛkai dɔɔ fɔŋŋa Haman kundɔɔlaa maa ni.
3Ɛsta kaa giŋŋi koori see di ra wii, di ra fɔrguu, ú chɔgi Agag hinuu Haman jinachɔgii la uŋ tawɛɛ ú chɔgi Jus hina maa la. 4Denii koori kaa kpa u saliŋ daŋkpala la di tɛr Ɛsta, u izi chi u see, 5di ŋɔ, “Jara, di a parii di deŋli i be, n wia kaa sɔɔni i bɔra, gil bá kaa sɛbi widaulifalii hɔŋ, di bɔnni i hɛssi la maa di ra chɔgi unla Agag hinuu Hamɛdata biibaal Haman n faa felee sɛbi ŋɔ bá chɔgi Jus hina la maa n du i hɛssi maa la. 6Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ di lau n hiŋ, di wia wa huuzi n nɛrai? Màá wer so di ra binni ka ba kpu n diahina.”
7Koori Zɛgzis jaa ŋɔ u haaŋ Ɛsta ni Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai be, “N gillɔɔ ba sag Haman ŋmɛŋsagri daa la uŋ baŋŋɛ dikuu u jinachɔgii la un tawɛɛ, ú kpa ɛɛ Jus hina la wia. N kpa u kundɔɔlaa maanii tɛɛ Ɛsta. 8Ka widaulii la baŋ kpa mìŋ́ koori sɔŋ sɛbi, di kpa n nonibisig jag a ni la waa kaa dɔɔ biraa. Ama, ii daŋ wer sɛbi widaulifalii di hiini a Jus hina gunla maa n wesse ii be. Ií kpa n sɔŋ di sɛbuu, di kpa n nonibisig la di jag u ni, ú dɔɔ fɔŋŋa.”
9Ba chaali koori karchizi manaŋ. Baaguzi ahorohiŋ la banna yir Sivan la hɔpizaa tokko ni ahoro hɔllɛ guŋ. Ba sɛbi Mɔdɛkai widaulaa maa tɛɛ Jus hina, koora, hɛssi nabɔnzi ani nabɔntɔga la maa n du a hɛssi kalfa ni tokko ni aniidaanɛɛ la n chɔɔwɛ lii India hɛri di ga hel Itiopia hɛri la. Ba sɛbaabuu hɛssi la maa sɛbaa ni ba mɔɔrizi biine tɛɛ baa. Jus hina la gba, gunnɛ ba sɛbi tɛɛ ba ge ba sɛbaa ni ba mɔɔri biini. 10Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis sɔnnɛ Mɔdɛkai faa kpa di sɛbi a hɔna, di kaa kpa u fɔŋŋa nonibisig la jagaa. Koori balaa n tinni zagra baŋ dɛɛzɛɛ a ɛɛ koori hora di ra chɔ werge labuu ba kpa bɔnnaa.
11A hɔna ra bagluu lugɔ koori tɛɛ Jus hina la n du bolzenaa maa labuu fɔŋŋa, bá chaali dɔŋa di guu bahinaa. Di laallɔɔra maa wa lii iri gɛɛ a hɛssi bɛl maa biini di wàá yoo ba ni ba haana ni biizi, ba dɔɔ ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ bá wer kpu baa, di paagi ba dɔma hiŋ kuna di dɔɔ. 12Hɔpizii la baŋ lizɛɛ bá ɛɛ gunla Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis kora hɛssi la maa biine, ɛɛ hɔpizii la baŋ faa dauwɛ bá chɔgi Jus hina maa labuu. Baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaahoro hɔllɛ guŋ. 13A widaulifalii naa dɛkkɔɔ baŋ sɛbuu, di gil u wia yaari a hɛssi maa biine di tɛɛ mɔɔri iri maa hina. Ba ɛɛ gunnɛ Jus hina maa wer ɛɛ sirya di turgi ba dɔma ba wichɔgaa kim.
14Koori n wa tɛɛ baa a widaulii, huŋhunna la tinni koori zagra la di ra chɔ werge. Ba gil a widaulii wia ge yaari Susa diikpeg biini.
15Mɔdɛkai lii a koori see ni u bɔmbɔga n ɛɛ burgu di koozi a huŋŋa, di kaa tɔ wɛjɛ bɛl baŋ kpa pɛɛnnanii di nyɛr, u ɛɛ lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, di hi saliŋkahuro, a maa lugɔ koorilaala. A hɔl hiŋ, bolzeŋkpeg Susa hina di bahinaa werge maa ni bɔsɔna. 16Jus hina la waa be, bɔsɔna, bɔpuraa ani girme saŋaa di faa tɛɛ baa. 17Bolzeŋ maa biini, hɛssi maa biine ani bɔr la maa baŋ karmi a koori widaulii naa, Jus hina bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔnuu, ba chaali di ra di diuzenaa di ra di bahinaa werge maa. Nɛkpila n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ faa birgi Jus hina, dikuu baŋ jaa ra ɔm baa werge la wia.

english_text:
The Jews Destroy Their Enemies
1The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around, 2and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
3The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews. 4Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
5The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy. 6-10They killed 500 people in Susa, but they did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Haman had been one of the worst enemies of the Jews, and ten of his sons were among those who were killed. Their names were Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.
11Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa. 12Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
13Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
14King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa. 15Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed 300 more people. But they still did not take anything that belonged to their enemies.
16-17On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed 75,000 of their enemies, but the Jews did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Then on the fourteenth day of the month the Jews celebrated with a feast.
18 On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth. 19This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other.
The Festival of Purim
20Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces 21and told them:
Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar, 22the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
23They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration.
The Reason for the Festival of Purim
24 Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
25Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged. 26Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast. 27Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do. 28From now on, all Jewish families must remember to celebrate Purim on these two days each year.
29Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast. 30Copies of this letter were sent to Jews in the 127 provinces of King Xerxes. In the letter they said:
We pray that all of you will live in peace and safety.
31You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
32These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_text:
Jus hina n kpegli ba dɔma wia
1Baagu Adar la hɔpizaa fidaahoro hɔllɛ, koori widaulii naa fɔŋŋa faari. A hɔllɛ Jus hina dɔma faa ra fɛ lugɔ ba daŋ kpegli baa, di kpu baa. Ka wia la bir, Jus hina la kpegli nɛra la n hah baa la. 2Jus hina la n du ba bolzenaa la maa n du Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis kora hɛssi la maa chaali, bá yoo nɛra la n na nyiŋŋi ba dimaa la. Nɛra maa faa waa wette ba ni baa yoo, dikuubɛɛwiai, iri maa faa ra ɔm baabuu. 3A hɛssi maa nabɔntɔga ni koora, hɛssi nabɔnzi ani koori huŋhunna maa faa chi Jus hina la har, dikuu banna ɔm Mɔdɛkai werge wia. 4Mɔdɛkai faa ɛɛ nɛtɔgrɛ kooridia. U sɔŋ faa yaari a koori hɛssi maa, u fɔŋŋa ra jaa saŋa maa.
5Jus hina la faa kpa tokobizii yoo ba dɔma di kpu baa, di chɔgi baa werge maa. Ba faa ɛɛ nɛra la n hah baabuu ba kipar. 6Ba bolzeŋ Susa diikpeg biini, baala kalfaanuere ba kpu. 7Ba faa kpu Pasandata ge, Dalfɔn, Aspata, 8Pɔrata, Adalia, Aridata, 9Pamasta, Arisai, Aridai ani Vaizata. 10Bannii maa faa ɛɛ Haman biibaalaa. Waabuu faa ɛɛ Jus hina dɔm di ɛɛ Hamɛdata biibaal, ka ba faa waa sɛɛwɛ kpa ba kummaa.
11A hɔl hiŋ maanii ba kali koori nɛra la maga Jus hina n kpuwɛɛ Susa diikpeg biini. 12Koori ŋɔ u haaŋ Ɛsta be, “Jus hina la kpu nɛra kalfaanuere, di kpa Haman biizi fi jaa, Susa diikpeg naa biini. An du kennaa, nɛra baŋmɛnɛɛ ba kpu hɛssi la n kawɛɛ la biinei? Too, filaŋkeŋ bɛɛ i kaa ra nyiŋŋei? N daŋ ɛɛu tɛi.”
13Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Jara, di i sɛɛwɔ, tɛɛ Jus hina la n du Susa la ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ ba kɛrɛ kaa kpa zinaa widaulii naa di hum huma, di kpa Haman biibaala fi la baŋ kpuwɛɛ la sag ŋmɛŋsagri daazi ni.”
14Denii koori ŋɔ ba ɛɛ guŋ. Ba dau a widaulii Susa biini, di kpa Haman biibaala fi la baŋ kpuwɛɛ la di sag ŋmɛŋsagri daazi ni, nɛ́r maa na. 15Jus hina chaali Susa biini baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl la, di kaa kpu baala kalfaahoro, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ kpa ba kummaa.
16Jus hina la n du koori hɛssi la n kawɛɛ la ge chaali a saŋa, di guu bá lɛɛ bahinaa lii ba dɔma be. Ba faa wettoo kpu nɛra kagboŋa tokkoahoro ni fidaanue, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ paagi ba kuna. 17Baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaahoro hɔllɛ ba ɛɛ guŋ. Hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl la, ba heezi di di diuzenaa, ba bɔra faa sɔɔni baa werge, ba gil u birgi ba hɔpizizeŋ bɛl.
Purim Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia
18Ka Jus hina la n faa du Susa lawaa chaalɔɔrɛ hɔpizaa fidaahoro ni fidaanaazu hɔla, ka jaa heezi hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔl la di di diuzenaa, ba bɔra sɔɔni baa werge maa.
19Awiarɛ Jus hina la n du boljigzi la gil baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl la ɛɛ hɔpizizeŋ ba be, ba ɔɔ ra di diuzenaa ba bɔra sɔɔni baa, ba ra sunzi dɔŋa kuna.
20Mɔdɛkai faa sɛbi wia naabuu dau, di sɛbi hɔna tɛɛ Jus hina la maa n du Koori Zɛgzis hɛssi maa biine, banla n duglɛɛ ni banla n du bɔɔnɛɛ, 21di ra kali baa lugɔ ba gil baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaanaazu ni fidaanue hɔla la ɛɛ hɔpizizenaa, bá ra dia bina maa, 22di ra liizi saŋa la Jus hina n na lɛɛi lii ba dɔma be ani baagu la biini ba biinichɔg n birgi bɔsɔna, ba wiraa hɔpizii la birgi hiŋ dii hɔpizii. U sɛbɔɔrɛ tɛɛ baa bá gil hɔpizaa naa ɛɛ diuzenaa dii ni bɔsɔna hɔla, di ra tɛɛ dɔŋa diwee di ra sunzi nyaara.
23Awia, Jus hina la sɛɛ gunla Mɔdɛkai n sɛbɛɛ la lugɔ a hɔpizizenaa dii du de di hanna la. 24Dikuubɛɛwiai, Agag hinuu Hamɛdata biibaal Haman n ɛɛ Jus hina maa dɔm la, faa ta jinaa ú chɔgi baa, di faa ta kuna banna yir pur, ú zum hɔpizii la un niŋ chɔgi baa, ba wia tuŋ. 25Ka u jina naa n wa zuu koori digna, u faa gillɔɔ ba sɛbi hɔna di bagli lugɔ ba gil Haman nfɛrchɔgaa la un dɔɔwɛ Jus hina ni la bir laŋŋi u ni, di bir ŋɔ ba sag u ni u biibaala ŋmɛŋsagridaazi ni. 26Awia, ba faa ra yir a hɔpizaa naa Purim, dikuu wii la maa baŋ sɛbɛɛ a hɔnnaa biini ni wii la maa ban nawɛɛ ani wii la maa n ɛɛ baa la wia. 27Jus hina la dau lugɔ ba daŋ gil u ɛɛ ba naana wii, ba naanna ni banla maa n jaa ba ni ɔɔ ra tɔgzi hɔpizaa anɛɛ naa bina maa, di gilɛɛ waa gar. Bá ra dia gunla Mɔdɛkai n baglɛɛ ni saŋa la un dawaa la. 28Jimini maa hina ɔɔ ra tɔgzi hɔpizaa naa, ba diini maa, ba bolzenaa ani ba hɛssi maa biine. Jus hina gilɛɛ waa gil Purim hɔpizaa naa dii saŋa maa, di gilɛɛ gil a wia wàá dim ba naanna biini.
29Denii Abiheel biihaaŋ Wiche Ɛsta ni Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai la kpa fɔŋŋa la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛ di sɛbi hɔŋ di chi hɔnnɛɛhiŋ naa n na ŋɔ Purim wia naa har. 30Mɔdɛkai gil ba kpa a hɔna di ga tɛɛ Jus hina la n du hɛssi kalfa ni tokko ni aniidaanɛɛ la maa biine, Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis n faa ra di kora a ni la, di suŋŋi nɛnnɛ ra tɛɛ baa, di kaa ra du baa bɔkpega, 31di ŋɔ bá dau Purim hɔpizaa naa saŋazi gunla Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai ni Wiche Ɛsta n faa dauwɛ tɛɛ baa ani gunla baŋ faa dau hɔpizaa tɛɛ bahinaa ni ba dee lugɔ ban niŋ ɔɔ vɔɔ nua di ra wii, dikuu biinichɔg la n faa huuzi baa la wia. 32Ɛsta widaulii gillɔɔ gunla baŋ faa ŋɔ Purim ni u ŋmɛnizi wia chi nɛnnɛ. Ba faa sɛbuubuu du hɔna biine.

english_text:
The Greatness of Xerxes and Mordecai
1King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea. 2All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai. 3Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_text:
Mɔdɛkai zenni wia
1Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis faa tɛɛ u nɛra la n faa du u kora diiribɔr maanii kima, haali di ga chug muuzeŋ gba. 2Ba kaa sɛbi u wiɛɛlaa la maa uŋ kpa u fɔŋŋa ni u zenni ɛɛ, ni gunla maa un lalli Mɔdɛkai chiŋ di tɛu nabɔmuu. A maanii ba faa sɛbi du Mɛdia ni Pɛsia Koora Faala Hɔna biine. 3Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai labuu faa ɛɛ nabɔnzeŋ di ra hiŋ Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis ni. U faa ɛɛ nɛzenne Jus hina biini. U dɔŋahina faa ra tɔgzuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa hummɔɔ ba wia kuari, u ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa ba maa bɔra sɔɔni werge maa.

english_text:
Job and His Family
1Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
2Job had 7 sons and 3 daughters. 3He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pair of oxen, 500 donkeys, and a large number of servants. He was the richest person in the East.
4Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking. 5After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God.
Angels, the Lord, and Satan
6 One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them, 7the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
8Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
9 “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked. 10“You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere. 11Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
12The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.”
Then Satan left.
Job Loses Everything
13Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son, 14when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass, 15a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
16That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
17Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
18That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son, 19when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
20When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God 21 and said:
“We bring nothing at birth;
we take nothing
with us at death.
The Lord alone gives and takes.
Praise the name of the Lord!”
22In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_text:
Joob wia
1Baal bɛllɛ faa du de, u sɔnnɛ Joob. U faa du hɛri bɛl banna yir Uz. U faa ra jaami Kɔraawiizii, u wia dɔɔ wibii u be. Joob faa ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ, di ra du tau ni wichɔgaa ɛɛi. 2U faa dɔɔ biibaala baniidaanɛɛ ni biihaana bahoroo, 3di dɔɔ peeza ge kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛ, nyugmazi kagboŋa ahoro, napattaa kagboŋ ani kauzi kalfaanue, di kpa balaa kpila maa. Waabuu faa ɛɛ nɛzeŋ di dɔɔ daama werge, di kaali nɛra la maa n faa du de barii.
4U biibaala ɔɔ faa ra daali diuzenaare ba diini ka ra tɛɛ dɔŋa, ba ɔɔ yir ba niuhambizi bahoro la, ba ba, ba maa di ka nyɔɔ. 5Di ba diuzenaa dii haŋ wa tuŋ, Joob ɔɔ faa hum ba bɔttɛ, di sɔ lizi ba doŋa ha, bá ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be. U ɔɔ izuu chɔɔzimpikke ni, di lizi mbusu fuuh tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ra fɛ, “Aŋhinabe, n biizi ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, di see Kɔraawiizi nua ba bampiree biine.” Gunnɛ Joob ɔɔ faa ra ɛɛ, saŋaa saŋa maa.
Joob lugli ɛɛi na wia
6A hɔl bɛl, mɛlikazi chaali Kɔraawiizi be, Sitaani ge wa jaa ba ni. 7Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi Sitaani, “Lee i liiyɛi?”
Sitaani ŋɔ, “Hɛrii n du di gaagi ra bar.”
8Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi Sitaani, “Ɛrɛɛ n balii Joob wia duɛi? Nɛr maa waa hoo hɛri lugɔu. U wia dɔɔ wibiire, u ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ. U ra jaamimbuu, di ra du tau ni wichɔgaa ɛɛi.”
9Sitaani pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, “I ŋɔ pɛɛrɛ u ra jaamii? 10I ra guu u ni u diahina ni u kundɔɔlaa maanii nɛnnɛ, di kissuu u wiɛɛlaa maa biini. Guŋ gil u sela wazi, di yaari a hɛri maa biini. 11Ka di i gillɔ u kuna naa maa tuŋ, u daŋ seei nua, i sibɔɔ.”
12Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Sitaani be, “Guŋ wesso. Joob kundɔɔlaa maa du i nonee biinii, ka gilɛɛ waa gbɔgzi u himmaa.”
Denii Sitaani lii Kɔraawiizi be kaali.
13A hɔl bɛl, Joob biizi ba, ba kpɛɛma dia, di waa di diuzenaa, di ra nyɔɔ siŋ. 14Denii Joob balii bɛl chɔ ba u be, di wa ŋɔ, “Yaa kpogli navargazi labuu di ra par, ka kauzi la ge dugli de di ra di, 15kakpaŋ, Saba hina ba di wa lɔ yaa, di kpu n dɔŋahina maa, ka tigaa kaali. N bɛnnɛ liiwɛ di chɔ ba ń wa kalii!”
16Uŋ faa haa ra ŋɔ a wia, di a balii bɛl ballɔ di wa ŋɔ, “Dooŋ pozi peeza la ni i balaa la ninɛɛ, di fuuh ba maa, ka n bɛnnɛ liiwɛ, di chɔ ba ń wa kalii!”
17U ge n faa haa ra ŋɔ a wia, di a balii bɛl kaa ba, di wa ŋɔ, “Babilɔn hina ŋmɛɛna sugezi ahoro ballɔɔ di wa lɔ yaa, di kpu i balaa maa, ka tig i nyugmazi la maa kaali. N bɛnnɛ liiwɛ di chɔ ba ń wa kalii.”
18U ge n faa haa ra ŋɔ a wia, di a balii bɛl kaa ba, di wa ŋɔ, “I biizi du ba kpɛɛma diarɛ di ra di, di ra nyɔɔ siŋ. 19Denii pekpeg bɛl lii hɛribɔduma di wa yag a dia, u chol ba ni, ba maa siu. N bɛnnɛ liiwɛ, di chɔ ba ń wa kalii!”
20Denii Joob izi di lau u tagta jaŋ la uŋ laalɛɛ la, di piili ni biinichɔg, di gbaari u nyuu, ka chɔɔ pi, di ra jaami Kɔraawiizi, 21di ŋɔ,
“Ba lulimbuu ni chakpal,
chakpallɛ ń kaa kpa kaali.
Kɔraawiizii tɛɛwɛ, waabuu kaa lɛɛ,
u dɛg dargaarɛ.”
22Haali annii maa gba, ka Joob waa sɛɛwɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni.

english_text:
Job Loses His Health
1When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them, 2and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
3Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
4Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive. 5Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
6“All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.” 7Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
8Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery, 9his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
10Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God.
Job's Three Friends
11Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him. 12When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly. 13For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_text:
Sitaani n kaa ɛɛ Joob na wia
1A hɔl bɛl, mɛlikazi kaa chaali Kɔraawiizi be, Sitaani ge jaa ba ni. 2Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi Sitaani, “Lee i liiyɛi?”
Sitaani ŋɔ u be, “Hɛrii n du di ra gaagi.”
3Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa pɛɛzi Sitaani, “Ɛrɛɛ n balii Joob wia duɛi? Nɛr maa waa hoo hɛri lugɔu. U wia dɔɔ wibiire, u ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ. U ra jaamimbuu, di ra du tau ni wichɔgaa ɛɛi. U wia haa dɔɔ wibiire, haali hiŋ bir n liize ń chɔg u wia pɛɛpɛɛ la gba.”
4Sitaani ŋɔ, “Nɛr daŋ wer kpa u kundɔɔlaa maa chɛr u miibɔɔ. 5Ka di i kpa wiila ha u ni, u daŋ seei nua, i sibɔɔ!”
6Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Sitaani be, “Guŋ wesso. U du i nonee biinii, ka gilɛɛ waa gbɔgzi u miibɔɔ waa.”
7Denii Sitaani lii Kɔraawiizi be kaali, di ga kpa ŋmɛrchɔgaa n na wii werge ha Joob ni, di haŋ chi u naapaala biini guŋŋ ga lii u nyubaaŋ maa. 8Joob jaa so hul kɛrii, di kpa keŋlii ra kurgi u ŋmɛra hiŋ.
9U haaŋ ŋɔ u be, “I haa dɔɔ yardaawaa? See Kɔraawiizi nua, ka siu!”
10Joob bir ŋɔ, “I ra ŋɔ wiarɛ lugɔ hahgɛnii. Di Kɔraawiizi wa ɛɛ yaa winanaa, yaa ɔɔ sɛɛu. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ya ra nuumi, di u wa tɛɛ ya tɔɔrɔɔ waai?”
Annii maa biini, ka Joob waa wichɔgii maa ɛɛwɛ, u wiŋɔzi biini.
Joob dammuzi bahoro wia
11Denii Joob dammuzi bahoro, Tɛman hinuu Ɛlifaz, Suua hinuu Bildad ani Naama hinuu Zɔfar, n wa nuu tɔɔrɔɔzi la n huuzuu la, ba maa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di lii ba bola, di wa chem, bá ga jaami Joob, ka tig u bampirii. 12Baŋ du bɔɔnɛɛ ka nau, ba waa wette bá zumuu. Denii ba faari di ra chɛɛhgi werge, di piili ba tagtajaŋra ka ɛɛ hɛɛhraa di ra waari ba nyuuni, di ra bagli ba biinichɔg. 13Ka ba di wa so hɛri u be guŋŋ hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi aniidaanɛɛ, di bɛl maa waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba na gunla uŋ faa ra di dɔgnyaa werge.

english_text:
Job's First Speech
Blot Out the Day of My Birth
1 Finally, Job cursed the day
of his birth
2by saying to God:
3Blot out the day of my birth
and the night when my parents
created a son.
4Forget about that day,
cover it with darkness,
5and send thick, gloomy shadows
to fill it with dread.
6Erase that night from the calendar
and conceal it with darkness.
7Don't let children be created
or joyful shouts be heard
ever again in that night.
8Let those with magic powers
place a curse on that day.
9Darken its morning stars
and remove all hope of light,
10because it let me be born
into a world of trouble.
Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
11Why didn't I die at birth?
12Why was I accepted
and allowed to nurse
at my mother's breast?
13Now I would be at peace
in the silent world below
14with kings and their advisors
whose palaces lie in ruins,
15and with rulers once rich
with silver and gold.
16I wish I had been born dead
and then buried, never to see
the light of day.
17In the world of the dead,
the wicked and the weary rest
without a worry.
* 18Everyone is there—
19where captives and slaves
are free at last.
Why Does God Let Me Live?
20Why does God let me live
when life is miserable
and so bitter?
21 I keep longing for death
more than I would seek
a valuable treasure.
22Nothing could make me happier
than to be in the grave.
23Why do I go on living
when God has me surrounded,
and I can't see the road?
24Moaning and groaning
are my food and drink,
25and my worst fears
have all come true.
26I have no peace or rest—
only troubles and worries.
translation_text:
Joob nuumaa wia
1Annii naa tuna, Joob pilli u nua, di see hɔpizii la baŋ luluu la nua, 2di ŋɔ,
3“Kɔraawiizi, dim hɔpizii la baŋ luliŋ
ani hamuŋa la ge baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ,
‘Biibaallɛ ba lul la!’
4Gil a hɔpizii birgi bɔbiri,
di gilɛɛ kaa liizi u wia,
bɔchaaŋ maa gilɛɛ
waa chaani u ni.
5Gil bɔbiri werge ni biinichɔg tɔ u ni,
di gil baama tɔ u ni,
bɔbiri kpegli u chaanaa.
6A hamuŋa hiŋ ge, dimuu!
Ú gilɛɛ kaa jaa
bina hɔpizaa ni
gɛɛ bá kuruu du
baagu bɛl maa biini.
7Gil a hamuŋa dim,
bá gilɛɛ kaa waa nuu
bɔsɔna kɔɔi u biini.
8Ŋɔ vugra la n zum hɔpizaa nua seei,
di dɔɔ muuzeŋ
sechɔgii fɔŋŋa la be,
bá see a hɔpizii nua.
9Gil u chɔɔzinnua chinchiŋwilaa biri,
gil u hamuŋa kpaŋ
hɔpizaa huhzi,
di gilɛɛ waa na chɔɔzinnua.
10See hamuŋa la n gillɛ ba luliŋ
du tɔɔrɔɔ ni
biinichɔg werge biini la nua.
11Di n faa siuwɔ n maa hia biini
gɛɛ di faa siu n lulaa saŋa,
guŋ faa waa bɔɔ?
12Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ n maa faa lɛɛŋ
di dau u naazi ninɛi,
di gil n ɔzi u ilai?
13Di n faa siuwɔ, a du keŋ
n faa chɔɔwɔ ni bampirsɔna,
di chɔɔ di ra heezi,
14di jaa hɛri naa koorizenaa
ni ba zɛɛsogna ni
banla n faa ma bɔra
di tɛɛ bahinaa,
a jaa purgi
di birgi diŋgelli filaŋkennaa,
15di jaa nabɔnzenaa la diini
n faa suugi
saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa ni.
16Gɛɛ ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ba faa wan
kpawɛɛ hug
alugɔ baŋ lul biifula la
n siu u maa hia biini,
lugɔ biifula la ŋmɛnɛ
n waa hɔpizaa nawɛɛi?
17Ŋmam biinii biinikpola hina
ɔɔ gil ba wiɛɛlaa,
denii banla
n kuuhwɛ ra heezi.
18Banla baŋ laurɛɛ yoma
ge dɔɔ bampirsɔna,
ba waa ɔɔ kaa ra nuu
ba dɔɔra pogzaa.
19Nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa maanii du de,
yom ge na u hiŋ,
di lii u dɔɔri be.
20Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ banla n na di dɔgnya,
du de ni miibɔɔi,
di gil tɔɔrɔɔ diire du denei?
21Ba ra nyiŋŋi siu, ka waa ba,
di aah siwii ra nyiŋŋuu
kaali daama.
22Ba bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔni, di ra pur,
di ba wa zuu ŋmama biine.
23Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ba tɛɛ newee miibɔɔi,
unla ŋmɛnɛɛ n suahwɛ,
unla Kɔraawiizi n gottenei?
24Diwee n niŋ ɔɔ vii ba n be la,
ka a kpa ɛɛ himaa,
n na hɛm saŋa maa,
alugɔ nii n na pal.
25Wii la minna ɔm werge la,
ba n benii,
wii la miŋ waa nyiŋŋi
ń siwii na la, ɛɛ n benii.
26Maa bampirsɔna ni heezaa dɔɔwɛ,
n tɔɔrɔɔ ge waa tuŋ.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's First Speech
Please Be Patient and Listen
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2Please be patient and listen
to what I have to say.
* 3Remember how your words
4have guided and encouraged
many in need.
5But now you feel discouraged
when struck by trouble.
6You respect God and live right,
so don't lose hope!
7No truly innocent person
has ever died young.
8In my experience, only those
who plant seeds of evil
harvest trouble,
9and then they are swept away
by the angry breath of God.
10They may roar and growl
like powerful lions.
But when God breaks their teeth,
11they starve, and their children
are scattered.
A Secret Was Told to Me
12A secret was told to me
in a faint whisper—
13 I was overcome by sleep,
but disturbed by dreams;
14I trembled with fear,
15and my hair stood on end,
as a wind blew past my face.
16It stopped and stood still.
Then a form appeared—
a shapeless form.
And from the silence,
I heard a voice say,
17“No humans are innocent
in the eyes of God
their Creator.
18He finds fault with his servants
and even with his angels.
19Humans are formed from clay
and are fragile as moths,
so what chance do you have?
20Born after daybreak,
you die before nightfall
and disappear forever.
21Your tent pegs are pulled up,
and you leave this life,
having gained no wisdom.”
translation_text:
Ɛlifaz wiŋɔzi
1Denii Tɛman hinuu Ɛlifaz la ŋɔ,
2“Joob, di nɛr ŋɔ wia tɛi,
i baaŋ daŋ fuuah?
Ka anɛɛ n niŋ wer siigɛi?
3A liizi gunla hiŋ bagli nɛkpila,
di du nɛra la bɔra
n huahwɛ bɔkpega.
4Di hiini banla n lɔɔzi naazi,
bá wer chi nɛnnɛ.
5Ka filaŋkeŋ, tɔɔrɔɔ huuziibuu, i bɔra huah,
u chol i ninɛɛ, i nua kpu.
6I Kɔraawiizi jaamaa lɛi niŋ ɛɛ i yarda,
i wibii dɔɔi ge ɛɛ i tamiiyaa?
7Fɛ nfɛrɛ filaŋkeŋ,
nɛbɛliirɛ nyaa chɔgri,
ka u wia chɔgɛi?
Lee ba ŋmɛnɛ haa chɔgi
nɛr la wia n deŋleenei?
8N nawɔɔrɛ nɛra n na ta wichɔgaa jina,
banla ge n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa
ra di a tɔna.
9Kɔraawiizi heeza ɔɔ chɔgi baabuu kakpaŋ,
di u haŋ wa pozi ni baaŋ,
ba ɔɔ siuzuu.
10Biinikpola hina ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyinzi
n na wii, di ra uuhri,
ka Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ tɔɔgi a nuuzi,
di kuugi a nyina.
11Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyinzi la
n waa kummaa
nawɛɛ lauri ra diu,
di siu, a biizi maa yaari la.
12Wii bɛllɛ ba suahzi di wa munni tɛŋ,
ka maa nuuwɛ nɛnnɛ.
13Alugɔ hamuŋa deezikuna,
u chɔg n dɔɔrɛ.
14Ɔnsii ni bɔsai lawiŋ,
di gil n bɔra maa ra sa.
15Peu bɛl ta n siwee ni wa kaali,
n bɔra nyiiri.
16U chi, ka maa zum
kunla dee n ɛɛu.
Kumbɛl chi n sibɔɔ,
denii n nuu loobii bɛl
n na ŋɔ bɔɔiih,
17‘Newee wia daŋ wer deŋli,
kaali Kɔraawiizi,
gɛɛ di ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii
kaali u Taaria?
18Di Kɔraawiizi waa u balaa yardɛɛ,
di kpa chɔgri
ra tɛɛ u mɛlikazi,
19guŋwaa, banla n na zuu hɛɛhraa diini la zɛɛzi
n chigɛ hɛɛhraa biini,
banla ban niŋ pinti manaŋ,
di kaali kunjigzi
waa nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ!
20Chɔɔzimpikke di ga hel duaniŋ barii,
ba daŋ siu,
di ba waa ba wia zummɛ,
ba maa dee tuŋ kɔrai.
21Ba lɛɛ kuna la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛnɛ,
ba waa nunzuma dɔɔwɛ,
ka siu.’ ”

english_text:
Eliphaz Continues
Call Out for Help
1Job, call out for help
and see if an angel comes!
2Envy and jealousy
will kill a stupid fool.
3I have seen fools take root.
But God sends a curse,
suddenly uprooting them
4and leaving their children
helpless in court.
5Then hungry and greedy people
gobble up their crops
and grab their wealth.
6Our suffering isn't caused
by the failure of crops;
7it's all part of life,
like sparks shooting skyward.
8Job, if I were you,
I would ask God for help.
9 His miracles are marvelous,
more than we can count.
10God sends showers on earth
and waters the fields.
11He protects the sorrowful
and lifts up those
who have been disgraced.
* 12God swiftly traps the wicked
13 in their own evil schemes,
and their wisdom fails.
14Darkness is their only companion,
hiding their path at noon.
15God rescues the needy
from the words of the wicked
and the fist of the mighty.
16The poor are filled with hope,
and injustice is silenced.
Consider Yourself Fortunate
17 Consider yourself fortunate
if God All-Powerful
chooses to correct you.
18 He may cause injury and pain,
but he will bandage and heal
your cuts and bruises.
19God will protect you from harm,
no matter how often
trouble may strike.
20In times of war and famine,
God will keep you safe.
21You will be sheltered,
without fear of hurtful words
or any other weapon.
22You will laugh at the threat
of destruction and famine.
And you won't be afraid
of wild animals—
23they will no longer be fierce,
and your rocky fields
will become friendly.
24Your home will be secure,
and your sheep will be safe.
25You will have more descendants
than there are blades of grass
on the face of the earth.
26You will live a very long life,
and your body will be strong
until the day you die.
27Our experience has proven
these things to be true,
so listen and learn.
translation_text:
1Ɛlifaz bir ŋɔ, “Joob, di i ra nyiŋŋi, yir na,
anɛɛ n niŋ sɛɛi?
Mɛlikazi la bɛliirɛ niŋ sɛɛi?
2Gɛniirɛ baan na kpu,
zoma ge ra kpu faaza hiŋ.
3N himmaa na gɛnii n na nyɛɛli,
ka kakpaŋ, ba see u dia nua.
4U biizi wàá dɔɔ bahinaa,
nɛr maa waa hoo ú ŋɔ
lɛɛ baa seriya diiribɔr.
5Lɔzima daŋ di gɛnii pattikuna maa,
haali anla gba
n du sɔɔhri biini.
Niinyɔgzi hina ge ra zom,
dikuu u daama wia.
6Wichɔgaa waa hɛɛhraa biini ra lii lugɔ kunduulaa,
gɛɛ dɔgnya ni tɔɔrɔɔ dii
ra lii hɛri lugɔ kooree.
7Ka ba ɔɔ lul neweere du tɔɔrɔɔ biini,
gunla niŋ n ɔɔ ra pogzi,
di ra la chiŋ
alugɔ tuntummɔɔla la.
8Ka di minuu hiŋ,
n daŋ vii kpa n wia
tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.
9U ɔɔ ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia la
yaa n wàá wer zum a zɛɛ
di ɛɛ wizenaa la
yaa n wàá wer kur.
10U ɔɔ giluu dooŋ nɛɛ hɛri,
di gil kooni sɔɔni.
11U ɔɔ lalli banla n sɔɔni siwiire chiŋ,
di tɛɛ banla maa
n na wii bɔsɔna.
12U ɔɔ chɔgi biinikpola hina jinazii,
ba nunzuma bir pɛɛ.
13U ɔɔ lau nunzunnaa ba zumaa biini,
ba jinazi chɔgi.
14Bɔr ɔɔ biruu ba be bɔchaaŋ saŋa,
ba ra largi bɔra wibaŋkanchirii
alugɔ hamuŋa.
15Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ lɛɛ anuula hinaa lii
biinikpola hina wiŋɔɔlaa biini,
di lɛɛ baa lii fɔŋŋa hina la
n na sunni baa be.
16Awia, nyaari dɔɔ tamiirɛ,
ka tɔ unla wia
n waa wibii dɔɔwɛ nua.
17Nɛr la maa Kɔraawiizi n na deŋli,
nuu sumaa!
Awia, gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ dignitɛraa.
18U ɔɔ du nɛttɛ pira,
ka kaa vɔɔ u ŋmɛra,
di du nɛr wiila,
ka kaa chaau.
19U daŋ ɔɔ lɛɛi lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini,
saŋaa saŋa maa.
20Lɔchɔgii saŋa, u daŋ lɛɛi,
hàá siu laal biini,
u daŋ guui lii siu be.
21U daŋ guui lii i chɔgri be,
ɔnsii wàá lawii,
di chɔgaa wa ballɔ.
22I daŋ mam chɔgaa ni lɔchɔgii,
hàá ɔm pir sela.
23Hɛri la hin niŋ par wàá dɔɔ bia,
pir sela ge wàá ɛɛi wiimaa.
24I daŋ zum lugɔ i dia chigɔɔ nɛnnɛ,
di i wa kur i kundɔɔlaa maa,
i daŋ na lugɔ
bɛl maa waa leuwe.
25I biizi daŋ du kpil,
i naanna du kpil lugɔ kooree.
26I daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ,
di du kpeg mɔɔ ka siu,
alugɔ mia n ɔɔ bii nɛnnɛ mɔɔ
ka ba kumaa la.
27Joob, yaa pessi gunnɛ nɛnnɛ, u ɛɛ wibii.
Awia, nuu guŋ, di sɛɛ guŋ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
It's Impossible
1Job said:
2It's impossible to weigh
my misery and grief!
3They outweigh the sand
along the beach,
and that's why I have spoken
without thinking first.
4The fearsome arrows
of God All-Powerful
have filled my soul
with their poison.
5Do oxen and wild donkeys
cry out in distress
unless they are hungry?
6What is food without salt?
What is more tasteless
than the white of an egg?
7That's how my food tastes,
and my appetite is gone.
* 8How I wish that God
would answer my prayer
9and do away with me.
10Then I would be comforted,
knowing that in all of my pain
I have never disobeyed God.
11Why should I patiently hope
when my strength is gone?
12I am not strong as stone
or bronze,
13and I have finally reached
the end of my rope.
My Friends, I Am Desperate
14My friends, I am desperate,
and you should help me,
even if I no longer respect
God All-Powerful.
* 15But you are treacherous
16like streams that swell
with melting snow,
17then suddenly disappear
in the summer heat.
18I am like a caravan,
lost in the desert
while searching for water.
19Caravans from Tema and Sheba
20thought they would find water.
But they were disappointed,
21just as I am with you.
Only one look at my suffering,
and you run away scared.
What Have I Done Wrong?
22Have I ever asked any of you
to give me a gift
23or to purchase my freedom
from brutal enemies?
24What have I done wrong?
Show me,
and I will keep quiet.
25The truth is always painful,
but your arguments
prove nothing.
26Here I am desperate,
and you consider my words
as worthless as wind.
27Why, you would sell an orphan
or your own neighbor!
28Look me straight in the eye;
I won't lie to you.
29Stop accusing me falsely;
my reputation is at stake.
30I know right from wrong,
and I am not telling lies.
translation_text:
Joob wiŋɔzi
1Denii Joob bir ŋɔ,
2“Di ba daŋ vii wer mɛgzi
n dɔgnya ni n biinichɔg tɔgzi,
3a tɔgzi daŋ vii kaali muuzenaa hɛɛhriichaa,
aabuu gillɛ
n yali siwee ŋɔ wia.
4Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ virgimbuu u hobee,
a siri su n bɔra.
Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n tɔɔrɔɔzi
ra hiŋzi dɔŋa.
5Di kaukpoŋlii wa na koorii di ra di,
u ɔɔ ra wiiu waa,
gɛɛ navarga ra wii
di u wa na kooriihilaa
ra dia?
6Ba ɔɔ weruu di diusɛba la
n waa yazi dɔɔwɛɛa,
gɛɛ hal bɔhuŋŋu
la summɔɔwaa?
7Gunnɛ n diwee du,
n na kɔɔa.
8Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi wàá tɛŋ
kunla miŋ suŋŋɛɛnɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ wàá nuu
n wiisuŋŋaai?
9Kɔ́raawiizi vii pintiŋ,
di teŋ n miibɔɔ!
10Denii ń vii dɔɔ keŋ bampirii tigaa,
n bɔra sɔɔni,
haali n bɔra
n na waazi naa gba,
maa Dɔɔrinaniinanii la
wiŋɔzi hɔɔwɛ.
11Bɛɛ fɔŋŋaa n dɔɔ
lugɔ n haa dɔɔ tammiiyɛi?
Bɛɛ n kaa du de,
ú gil n dɔɔ kanyittei?
12N kpekkoo lugɔ biiyaa?
N bɔra ɛɛ danyɛɛwaa?
13Maa kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa n lɛɛ n hiŋ,
maa kaa dɔɔ bɔr la
min niŋ ga di na hiinaa.
14Di baal tamii wa tunnɔ,
a dɛkkɔ u na nɔŋŋaa ni hiinaa
lii u dammuzi be,
haali di u vɛɛ
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
ɔmaa gba.
15Ka n dammuzi, ii darimbuu,
alugɔ gɔŋa n ɔɔ ra pal,
ka hil di dooŋ waa teŋŋo la.
16Di dobia werge wa chollo,
di ŋmɛɛri sua,
17ka a palaa ɔɔ teŋuu lumaŋa ni,
wem maga, a maa ge hil.
18Nɛkpila ni ba nyugmazi leu,
di gaagi ra nyiŋŋi nii,
di zuu hɛribɔduma siu.
19Nɛkpila ni ba nyugmazi
lii Tɛma di ra nyiŋŋi nii.
Siiba kɔkɔɔza la n na vol ŋmɛnɛɛ,
ge dɔɔ tamii.
20Ka ba biine chɔgi werge, dikuubɛɛwiai ba faa dɔɔ tamiirɛ,
ka baŋ wa hel de,
ba bɔra huah.
21Ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ gɔŋa naa n be,
ii waa hiinaa maa dɔɔwɛ.
Ii na n duulaa, ɔnsii lau ia,
ii bir har.
22N ŋmɛnɛ haa ŋɔwɔɔ lugɔ
ii tɛŋ kumbɛl
gɛɛ ii turgi n kim,
di lii ii daama biiniaa
23gɛɛ ii lɛɛŋ lii n dɔm
ni sikpegii hiŋ bee?
24Ií bagliŋ wia, n siigi,
ií ŋɔ wii la miŋ ɛɛwɛ leu.
25Wibii ɔɔ ra wiiu,
ka ii mmɔri dii naa
waa wiimaa ra bagli.
26Ii ra nyiŋŋuu ii deŋli wia la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ laa,
di binni n wiŋɔzi pɛɛ
alugɔ peuwaa?
27Haali ii daŋ wer ta kuna di yoo lalbiizi,
di kpa ii badɔŋa chɛr daama!
28Jaande maa, ií ra binniŋ nɛnnɛ!
N daŋ sɛɛ kanni kara ii sibɔɔa?
29Ií na n sinyɛna,
di gilɛɛ gil ii wia nyaa wibii.
Ií bir fɛ nfɛrɛ,
di gilɛɛ gil n di bilchɔg.
30Biinikpola wia du n wiŋɔzi biiniaa?
Amɔ, maa zum
winanaa ni wichɔgaa?”

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
1Joob haa ŋɔ,
“Durnya naa
dui waa kpolaa?
U de dui waa ɛɛwɛ lɛi lugɔ
paahdiiri n na hum wergea?
2Gunla yom n ɔɔ ra kɛlli bɔr duani manaŋ
gɛɛ paahdiiri n ɔɔ ra kpaŋ
u kinturgaa ni manaŋ la,
3gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi tɛŋ baagukpila la
n waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ,
di kaa tɛŋ biinichɔg hamuŋzi.
4Di n haŋ wa chɔɔ, n ɔɔ ra fɛu,
‘Ɛrɛɛ a birgi mag,
ka n izei?’
Hɔɔ waa ɔɔ ra pizi manaŋ,
n chɔɔ di birgi guŋŋ
chɔɔzinnua wa hel.
5N bɔra maa ra lii sandule, wega tɔ u maa,
n ŋmɛra maa ra lii nii.
6N hɔpizaa gbaŋŋɔɔ kaali suahri gambo,
di ɔɔ wa tuŋ,
di maa tamii dɔɔwɛ.
7N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, a liizi
lugɔ n miibɔɔ
ɛɛ heeza kakpannɛ,
n siwee ŋmɛnɛ maa
wàá ka na bɔsɔna.
8Hinna naŋ filaŋkennaa,
hàá ka naŋ maa.
I daŋ nyiŋŋiŋ,
ka màá kaa du de.
9Gunla baama n ɔɔ leu kaali la,
gunnɛ nɛr la maa baŋ hukke,
waa ɔɔ kaa bir ba la.
10U ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka bir ba u dia,
u nɛra wàá ka zumuu maa.
11Awia, màá siigi,
n daŋ ŋɔ wia
n biinichɔg naa biini.
N daŋ nuumi dikuu n tɔɔrɔɔ naa
n kpolle wia.
12Minuu muuzeŋ gɛɛ
u vil sechɔgii, i ra guuŋŋ?
13Di n haŋ wa fɛ lugɔ n kunchɔɔrikuŋ
daŋ gil n bampirii tig,
n gbagrigbagri gil
n bɔwiila yɔɔ,
14ka a guŋ saŋa gbaa,
i kpa deeza ani
wia la minna na
a biine, di ra ɔnziŋ.
15Awia, a daŋ vii pariŋ,
di nɛr hanzi n baŋaa n siu,
aabuu bɔ n de dui,
ni dɔgnya ni tɔɔrɔɔ naa.
16N hah n de duirɛ, maa nyiŋŋi n du de di hanna la.
Giliŋ pɛrɛtɛ!
N de dui waa zɛɛ dɔɔwɛ.
17Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ newea ɛɛ kumpazɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra du
ba wiɛɛlaa tauwɛi?
18Ɛɛ pessi baabuu chɔɔzi maa,
di ɛɛ baa ra na saŋa maa.
19I ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá lizi siwii n nii,
gɛɛ di giliŋ pɛrɛtɛ,
n so bɔɔiih?
20Ee, newea binni,
di n ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ,
bɛɛ n ɛɛinɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i lizi siwii sag n ninɛi?
N ɛɛ buntɔgaa tɛi gɛɛ?
21Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ hàá gil
n wichɔgaa tɛnnɛi?
Dikuubɛɛwiai, a wàá birgi
ka n chɔɔ ŋmam biini.
I daŋ nyiŋŋi n bɔr,
ka màá ka du de.”

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
Bildad wiŋɔzi
1Denii Suua hinuu Bildad la ŋɔ,
2“Ɛrɛɛ i ŋɔ wia naa dɔŋa
birgi magɛi?
I wiŋɔzi ra kɔɔu alugɔ pekpeg,
ka a ɛɛ wipɛɛrii.
3Kɔraawiizi waa wibii dii ra birgi.
Kɔraawiizi La N Ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
waa wideŋlaa ra birgi.
4I biizi n faa ɛɛ wichɔgaa zuu u ni la,
u tɛr ba dignaa gunla n dɛkkɛ.
5Ka di i daŋ bir Kɔraawiizi be,
di suŋŋi Unla N Ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
6di i wia dɔɔ wibii di deŋli,
haali filaŋkeŋ gba,
u daŋ izi dikuu i wia,
di bir gil i nyɛɛli.
7I daama la maa n chɔkkɛ la daŋ ɛɛ pɛɛ,
a wàá dugli anla
Kɔraawiizi n niŋ kaa tɛi.
8Yaa naabaala faa ɛɛ nunzunnaa,
awia, helli lii ba be,
9dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa waa binɛɛ,
yaa waa wiimaa zummɛ,
yaa hɔpizaa hɛri naa biini
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ laalii.
10Ba daŋ baglii wia la baŋ hellee.
A nuu gunla
ban niŋ baglii nɛnnɛ.
11Nii biini koorii wàá wer hel
bɔr la nii n waa duwɛɛ,
nii bɔr bɛnnɛ a ra du.
12Haali di a haa ra hel,
di a mɔnnaa waa helle gba,
ka aabuu ɔɔ feli
koorii maa siu.
13Banla maa n suuh Kɔraawiizi wia,
gunnɛ ba laba du,
bá tamii chɔgi, di tuŋ.
14Kunla baŋ yardɛɛ ɛɛ kumpuriire,
kunla baŋ dɛllɛɛ ɛɛwɔɔ
lugɔ nandar kɛhkiah.
15Ba ɔɔ dɛlluubuu, u kaari,
di ɔɔ lawuu kpogli, u chah.
16Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ kunla
banna mizi nii nɛnnɛ,
wiizi baaŋ,
u lunne yaari a kambol biini maa.
17U lunne mil bia baŋ chaalɛɛ dau,
di ra nyiŋŋi bɔr a biine.
18Ka di ba wa kpuzuu,
waa ɔɔ kaa dɔɔ chignibɔr.
19Wibii maa, u miibɔɔ ɔɔ tunuu,
ka kuna aŋhina bir lii a hɛri.
20Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi
waa ɔɔ vɛɛ nɛr la
wia n deŋlee,
waa wichɔgɛɛra ra hiini.
21U daŋ haa gil i mam,
di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.
22U daŋ kpa hiihzi kpu i dɔma,
biinikpola hina ge
diini wàá ka du de.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Joob n ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Bildad
1Denii Joob bir ŋɔ,
2“Ɛɛh, n zummɔ lugɔ
wii naa ɛɛ wibiire.
Ka newee maa wia wàá wer
deŋli Kɔraawiizi be.
3Haali di nɛbɛl ra nyiŋŋi
ú diu mmɔri gba,
ka wàá wer na u pɛɛzaazi
kagboŋ bɛl maa zɛɛ tɛu.
4Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ nunzumaa,
di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge.
U ni nɛr maa wàá wer naa.
5U ɔɔ lalli bizenaare,
di a waa zummɛ,
di kpa baaŋ billaa, di purgaa.
6U ɔɔ zigli hɛrii,
di gil u zɛɛ ligee ra ziigi.
7U ɔɔ ŋɔ wiarɛ wiizi be, wàá ka chaani,
di ɔɔ tɔ
chinchiŋwilaa chaanaa.
8U bɛnnɛ yaa chiŋ,
di ra vol muuzenaa ni.
9Kɔraawiizii ta chinchiŋwilaa,
ba ra yir aŋhina
Belimbetia, Naanyɔɔ
ani anla n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag.
10U ɔɔ ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia la
yaa n wàá wer zum a zɛɛ
gɛɛ wizenaa la
yaa n wàá wer kur.
11Di u wa bɛri n ni, maa ɔɔ nau,
u ɔɔ ga n kɛraa kaali,
ka maa zum.
12Di u wa foozi kuŋ,
anɛɛ niŋ wer lawuuwɛi?
Anɛɛ n niŋ wer ŋɔ u be,
‘Bɛɛ i ra ɛɛ gunnɛi?’
13Kɔraawiizi baaŋ waa sɔɔni manaŋ,
di u wa fuuhwo.
Haali ɔɔ kpegli Rahab
ni u harbɔɔ hiŋra gbaa.
14Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń wer diu mmɔrɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ di wer na
wiŋɔzi di diu mmɔrɛi?
15Haali miŋ waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ gba,
ka maa wiŋɔɔlii dɔɔwɛ,
suŋŋaa bɛnnɛ ń suŋŋi
n Seriyadiiri,
ú na n sinyɛna.
16Haali di n samuu, u ba gba,
ka maa tamii ɛɛwɛ
lugɔ u daŋ nuu n be.
17U daŋ kpa pekpeg di pintiŋ,
di gil n ŋmɛra
bir du kpil jaa pɛɛpɛɛ.
18Wàá gil n bir na n heeza,
ka dɔgnya werge
bɛnnɛ ú kpa tɛŋ.
19Di kpegzi wiarɛ, waabuu kpekke!
Di a ɛɛ wibii dii wiarɛ,
anɛɛ n niŋ samuuwɛi?
20Haali di n wia deŋloo,
ka n nua daŋ tɛŋ chɔgri,
di n faa waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ gba,
ka u daŋ tɛŋ bilchɔg.
21Haali n wia n deŋlee gba,
ka n baga lɛi n hiŋ wia,
n hah n himmaa de duirɛ.
22A maa ɛɛ kpannɛ, awiarɛ n ŋɔ,
‘U ɔɔ chɔgi nɛra la
n waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ
ni biinikpola hina maanii.’
23Di wiilchɔgii wa ba siupirgii ni,
Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ ra ɛɛ nɛra la wia
n deŋleere chɛɛtɛ.
24Di hɛri wa du biinikpola hina nonee,
ɔɔ tɔɔgi ba sitɔɔra siweere.
Di waa lɛi, anɛɛwɛi?
25N hɔpizaa gbaŋŋɔɔ kaali chɔchɔɔri.
A ɔɔ kaaluu,
bɛl maa waa
ɔɔ ba bɔsɔna ni.
26A ɔɔ kaaluu lugɔ muugbessi la n gbaŋŋɛ nii nyuu,
alugɔ chigni n ɔɔ tuu
gbaŋzi ni fiiu,
di lau kuŋ la.
27Di n ŋɔ lugɔ n daŋ gil nuumaa,
di suuh n anuula
ka ra munzi,
28ka n haa ra ɔm n tɔɔrɔɔzii werge,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n zummɔ lugɔ
i daŋ haŋ tɛmbuu chɔgri.
29Hiŋ teŋ tɛŋ bilchɔg naa,
ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń kaa ra tɔɔri
n hiŋ pɛɛi?
30Haali di n sɔ fanfanni,
di kpa biikoo
sam n nonee gba,
31ka i daŋ taaŋ du niichɔgaa biini,
guŋ gil n laala gba kiiŋ werge.
32Waa newee ɛɛwɛ lugɔŋ,
n vii ŋɔ n hor,
ya vii bil dɔŋa seriya diiribɔr.
33Ka nɛr maa waa hoo
ú kuari n ni
Kɔraawiizi dɔŋa ni,
34ú gil n viiraa,
ni n ɔnzaa!
35Denii màá kaa ra ɔm wia ŋɔi,
ka aŋ du kennaa,
màá wer ŋɔ wia.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
1Joob haa ŋɔ, “N de dui bazimbuu.
Màá tɔ n nua, n daŋ nuumi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n biini
chɔkkɔɔ werge.
2N daŋ ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be,
‘Gilɛɛ tɛŋ bilchɔg,
ka bagliŋ wia la
miŋ ɛɛwɛ zuu i ni.
3N sunnaa pariibuu,
i hah kunla
i himmaa n tawɛɛ?
Ka ra munzi biinikpola hina
jinachɔgaa wia.
4I ra binni wiarɛ alugɔ yaa?
I ra na wiarɛ alugɔ neweaa?
5I hɔpizaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ newea n ɛɛ kunsiwaa,
gɛɛ i binni kpussoo
alugɔ newea horaa,
6alugɔ i pigzi di ra nyiŋŋi n wileulaa
ani n wichɔgaa,
7haali hiŋ zummɛ lugɔ
maa bilchɔg maa dɔɔwɛ gba,
ani lugɔ nɛr maa
wàá wer lɛɛŋ
lii i nonee biiniaa?
8I noneere maŋ, di kuariŋ.
I daŋ kaa bir
chɔgiŋ filaŋkeŋ?
9A liizi lugɔ hinuu kpa chuuri di maŋ,
i daŋ kaa gil
ń birgi hɛɛhraa filaŋkeŋ?
10I tɛɛ n mɛɛrɛ fɔŋŋa u luliŋ,
di gil n hel n maa hia biini.
11Hinuu kpa hoga ni diah,
di choŋŋi dɔŋa ni,
di kpa ol ni hɔŋ di tɔ a ni,
di kuari n bɔra.
12Hinuu tɛŋ miibɔɔ di ra ɛɛŋ winanaa,
di ra binni n ni, n du de.
13Ka filaŋkeŋ, n jaa zumuu lugɔ
a guŋ saŋa maa,
i suahzɔɔrɛ di ta n tɔɔraa jina.
14Di n ɛɛ wichɔgaa,
i daŋ naŋ, di tɛr n digni.
15Di n dɔɔ bilchɔgrɛ, wiarɛ huuziŋ!
Haali di maa
bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ gba,
ka màá wer lalli n nyuu,
dikuu hiihzi n lawiŋ,
n biini chɔgi werge wia.
16Di n ɛɛ wii bɛl di ŋɔ n jigsi u wia,
i ɔɔ ɛɛu alugɔ bunyiŋ,
di ra daaziŋ í kpu,
di ra bagliŋ
i fɔŋŋazeŋ la wia
n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge la.
17I gillɔɔ nɛfalaa ba di waa di n daansɛɛ,
di gil i baaŋfuuih ra jaa,
dikuu n wia,
di gil i laallɔɔra
waa lɔŋ digiidigii.
18Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i gil ba lulinnɛi?
A daŋ vii pariŋ
di n faa siuwɔ mɔɔ
ka nɛr maa naŋ.
19Di ba faa waŋ lullɛ
gɛɛ a faa ɛɛ lugɔ n bittɔɔ,
n lulli hɔl la ba hugiŋ,
a guŋ vii bɔ.
20N hɔpizaa waa helle lɛi tunaa?
Lii n be,
ka n wer di suma tama,
21ka kaali bɔr la baŋ waa laŋŋɛ, ka ra bir,
biinichɔg ni bɔbiri
limpiriŋ hɛri la,
22hamuŋa ni bɔbiri
ni basabasa werge hɛri la.
Haali de bɔchaaŋ gba
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bɔbiri.’ ”

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Zofa wiŋɔzi
1Denii Naama hinuu Zɔfar la ŋɔ,
2“Anɛɛ niŋ wer siigi,
dikuu wiŋɔjagazi naa wiai?
Ba daŋ tɛɛ
wiŋɔbala hiŋ naa wibiiyaa?
3I wiŋɔpɛɛri naa
daŋ wer gil nɛra siigia?
Nɛr maa wàá nyɛg i ni,
di i ra ɛɛ nɛra chɛɛtɛa?
4I ra ŋɔu lugɔ i wiŋɔzi maa ɛɛ wibiire,
di ra fɛ lugɔ i ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ.
5Ee, a daŋ vii pariŋ
di Kɔraawiizi daŋ ŋɔ wia,
alugɔ u vii pilli u nua
di ŋɔ wia du i ni,
6di vii pilli zumaa wolli tɛi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, zumaa
du bɔra anɛɛrɛ.
Zum keŋ, Kɔraawiizi teŋ suuh
i wichɔgaa aŋhinaa.
7I daŋ wer zum Kɔraawiizi
wisuahlaa zɛɛzi nɛnnɛa?
I daŋ wer pigzi di zum gunla
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
zenni ni u fɔŋŋa n makkɛa?
8A la chinne kaali hɛri,
bɛɛ i wer ɛɛi?
A luŋŋoo kaali ŋmam,
bɛɛ i wer zumɛi?
9A jaŋŋɔɔ kaali hɛri,
di du war kaali muuzeŋ.
10Di u ballɔ di wa lawii tɔ dia,
di ŋɔ u dii seriya,
anɛɛ n niŋ wer diu mmɔrɛi?
11Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi zum karkannaa,
di u wa na wichɔgaa,
waa ɔɔ zumaa?
12Gɛnaa daŋ faari nunzuma dɔɔi,
di kaukpoŋlaa biizi
wa pɛssɔɔ.
13Ka di i gillɔ i bampirii lawuu,
di lalli i nonee suŋŋuu,
14di gil i wichɔgaa ta,
di gil a ɛɛi,
a waa kaa du i dia,
15guŋwaa, i daŋ lalli i nyuu chiŋ,
ka hiihzi wàá lawii,
i daŋ chi chigigi, hàá ra ɔm.
16Wibii maa, i daŋ suuh i tɔɔrɔɔzi,
di ra liizii a wia,
alugɔ nii n pallɛ wa kaali.
17I de dui daŋ chaani kaali
wiizi n na chaani wibaŋa ni,
bɔbiri ge ɛɛ lugɔ chɔɔzi.
18I daŋ dɔɔ i hiŋ,
di dɔɔ tamii.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ guui,
i so bɔɔiih.
19I daŋ chɔɔ bɔɔiih,
nɛr maa wàá gil ɔnsii lawii,
nɛkpila maa ra nyiŋŋi
hiinaa i be.
20Ka biinikpola hina nyuŋŋi,
di nyiŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛ huhzi bá chɔ.
Ba tamii maanii
lugɔ ba daŋ siu.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
16just as he rules over liars
and those they lie to.
17God shames counselors,
turns judges into fools,
18and makes slaves of kings.
19God removes priests and others
who have great power—
20he confuses wise,
experienced advisors,
21puts mighty kings to shame,
and takes away their power.
22God turns darkness to light;
23he makes nations strong,
then shatters their strength.
24God strikes their rulers senseless,
then leaves them to roam
through barren deserts,
25lost in the dark, staggering
like someone drunk.
translation_text:
Joob n ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Zofa
1Denii Joob bir ŋɔ,
2“Mmɔri maa waa hoo,
iabuu ɛɛ a nɛra sichaana hina,
ii ni nunzumaa niŋ kpau siu!
3Ka n dɔɔ nfɛrɛɛ lugɔ ia,
ii wan bɔwɛɛ.
Anɛɛ n waa
annii naa maa zummɛi?
4N birgi chɛɛtɛ kunnɛ n dammuzi be,
haali miŋ yir Kɔraawiizi u sɛɛ,
ka n haa ɛɛ chɛɛtɛ kunnɛ,
haali n wia maa n deŋlee,
maa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ la gba!
5Banla n na di dɔgnya bilchɔg tɛɛi waa kpol,
di ii haa waa dɔgnya diwee na.
6Ka ŋmɛɛna la n na kpu nɛra,
diini waa koozi.
Banla ge n na fuuh Kɔraawiizi baaŋ,
ba himmaa kpegzii ba yatti,
di kaali Kɔraawiizi.
7Ií pɛɛzi sela, a daŋ bagli ia
gɛɛ zumbizi, a daŋ kali ia
8gɛɛ ií nuumi du hɛri kunnyinee ni,
a daŋ bagli ia
gɛɛ ií gil muuzeŋ nyinni kali ia.
9Annii maa, a bɛlaarɛ waa zummɛ
lugɔ Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ gunnɛi?
10U nonii biinii kunnyinii maa miibɔɔ
ani newee maa heeza du.
11Digni waa ɔɔ ɛɛ wiŋɔzi lɛi di ra na
alugɔ nuuzuŋŋi
n ɔɔ daŋ diwee na laa?
12Nɛbinaa lɛi dɔɔ nunzumaa?
Miibɔɔjaŋ lɛi ra ba
wia zɛɛ zumaa nii?
13Kɔraawiizi benii nunzuma ni fɔŋŋa du,
baglaa ni wia zɛɛ zumaa
ɛɛ u horaa.
14Kunla uŋ purgee, ba wàá ka wer biruu ma,
nɛr la Kɔraawiizi n tɔ dia,
ba wàá wer lizuu.
15Di u lau dooŋ, hil ɔɔ chiu,
di u wa pilluu ge, u chɔgi hɛri.
16Waabuu dɔɔ kpegzi,
di ra kpegli u dɔma.
Banla banna dar
ni banla n na dar baa,
maa ɛɛ u horaa.
17U ɔɔ foozi koora nunzumaa,
di gil sitɔɔra birgi gɛnaa.
18U ɔɔ wir kooraa,
ka gil ba birgi yoma.
19U ɔɔ tuu u kizeehina
ni nɛzenaare zɛɛ.
20U ɔɔ giluu banla
baŋ yardɛɛ nuuzi tɔɔgi,
di lizi bazɛŋzi ge
nunzuma ba ni.
21U ɔɔ ŋmaabi nabɔnzenaare,
di foozi fɔŋŋa hina dɔŋkuna.
22U ɔɔ giluu bɔbiri wia wolo lii chaaŋ,
di gil bɔbiri limpiriŋ
birgi bɔchaaŋ.
23U ɔɔ giluu hɛssi hina dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge,
ka bir chɔgi baa,
di gil hɛssi hina wazi,
ka bir yaari baa.
24U ɔɔ giluu hɛssi hina sitɔɔra birgi gɛnaa,
di ɔɔ gil ba bugmi,
di ra juuri hɛribɔduma biini.
25Ba ɔɔ ra largi bɔbiri biini,
di ra jiŋli alugɔ sinnyɔɔra.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Know and Understand
1I know and understand
every bit of this.
2None of you are smarter
than I am;
there's nothing you know
that I don't.
3But I prefer to argue my case
with God All-Powerful—
4you are merely useless doctors,
who treat me with lies.
5The wisest thing you can do
is to keep quiet 6and listen
to my argument.
7Are you telling lies for God
8and not telling the whole truth
when you argue his case?
9If he took you to court,
could you fool him,
just as you fool others?
10If you were secretly unfair,
he would correct you,
11and his glorious splendor
would make you terrified.
12Your wisdom and arguments
will blow away like dust.
Be Quiet While I Speak
13Be quiet while I speak,
and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
1Joob haa ŋɔ, “N siwee na wia naa maanii,
n digna nuua, n zum a zɛɛ.
2Wia la hiŋ zummɛ, n gba zumaabuu,
haŋ bɔwɛɛ.
3Ka n kipattɛ lugɔ n na ŋɔ wia,
di ra tɛɛ
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
n nuu ra di n wia mmɔri.
4Ii kpa karaa tɔ wibii ni,
ii maa ɛɛ tagzi hina la
n wàá wer chaa nɛr maanii!
5Di ii maa daŋ vii siigi,
guŋ daŋ vii ɛɛ
nunzuma tɛɛ ia.
6Ií siigi ka nuu n hor,
di nuu n mmɔri.
7Ii daŋ wer chi Kɔraawiizi naa,
di ŋɔ biinikpola wiŋɔzia?
Ii daŋ wer
kanni kara tɛuwaa?
8Ii daŋ wer lɛɛ u nuaa?
Ii daŋ wer lɛɛ
Kɔraawiizi hor di ŋɔ tɛuwaa?
9Di u binni ii wia nɛnnɛ na,
a daŋ du wer tɛɛ ia?
Ii daŋ wer daruu
gunla iin niŋ
wer dar neweaa?
10U daŋ hau ii ni, wibii maa,
di ii suahzɔɔ di ra lɛɛ u nua.
11U girme werge wàá ɔnzi ia, ii bɔra ra saa?
U ɔmaa werge daŋ gil
ɔnsii werge lau ia, ii hɔrmi.
12Ii sɛɛliizi ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ lugɔ hɔɔhri,
ii mmɔrizi ge ɛɛ lugɔ chuuri.
13Ií siigi, ka gil n ŋɔ wia,
ií gil wii la maa
n niŋ ba n be, bá.
14Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń tulmi,
di kpa n miibɔɔ
du n nonee biinei?
15Haali di u kpuŋ gba,
ka n tamii du u ninɛɛ,
n daŋ ŋɔ wia
di lɛɛ n hiŋ u sibɔɔ.
16Wibii maa, kenne niŋ wer lɛɛŋ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, biinikpola hina waa,
bɛl maa wàá kur ba u be!
17Ií ra nuu n wiŋɔzi naa nɛnnɛ,
ií gil ii digna nuu
gunla min niŋ ŋɔ.
18Miŋ jaa ɛɛ n wia sirya filaŋkennaa,
n zummɔ lugɔ
Kɔraawiizi wàá tɛŋ bilchɔg.
19Anɛɛ n niŋ tɛŋ bilchɔgɛi?
Di gunnɛ, n daŋ siigi ka siu.
20N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, tɛŋ kuna anɛɛ naa bɛŋ,
guŋ gil n gilɛɛ suah i ni.
21Gil n dignitɛraa!
Gilɛɛ kpa ɔnsii werge kpuŋ!
22Feli ŋɔ wia mɔɔ ka n ge ŋɔ
gɛɛ gil n feli ŋɔ wia mɔɔ,
ka i ŋɔ.
23Wileulaa ni wichɔgaa aŋmɛnɛɛ n ɛɛi?
Bagliŋ wia la miŋ ɛɛwɛ leu
ani n wichɔgaa.
24Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i bir i har kpunnɛi,
di ra fɛ lugɔ n ɛɛ i dɔmnɛi?
25I ra nyiŋŋi i ɔnzimbuu gɛɛ?
Maa kummaa ɛɛwɛ,
paŋhoohiliirɛ miŋ,
kɔliirɛ i ra naa la.
26I kpa wiarɛ chugiŋ,
di sɛbaa du hɔŋ biini,
haali n bichal saŋa
wichɔgaa gba.
27I du n naazii daa,
di ra pessi gunla maa
minna vol,
di zum n naajaglaa nɛnnɛ.
28Awia, newee bɔra ɔɔ ra tunuu
alugɔ kuŋ n pɔɔhwɛ,
alugɔ chau n mugzi tagta.”

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
