I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
1Joob haa ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa haaŋ n lullɛ,
u hɔpizaa waa kpil,
di kaa ɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ bɛŋ.
2U ɔɔ heluu manaŋ alugɔ fiiri, ka bir yɔl kaali,
gunla laalii
n ɔɔ wa kaali kilab la,
gunnɛ waa ɔɔ du de di birgi.
3I lizi siwiire sag a guŋ hiŋ nii?
I daŋ yiruu ba i be,
di wa diu seriyaa?
4Anɛɛ niŋ wer lizi kunla n waa doŋa dɔɔwɛ,
lii kunla n dɔɔ doŋa biinei?
Nɛr maa waa hoo!
5I dau newee hɔpizaa
ni u baaguzi magaa,
di dau magazi la
uŋ wàá wer bɛri.
6Awia, lizi siwii u ni, di giluu bɔɔiih,
di gil u hum u huma tuŋ
alugɔ paahdiiri.
7Haali di ba teŋ daa gba ha,
ka u dɔɔ tamiirɛ,
u daŋ kaa fur,
u bɔfuttaa la wàá ɛɛ huhzi.
8Aŋhinabe, u lunne daŋ bini,
u zɛɛkantirii siu,
9ka di u wa na nii tama gba,
u daŋ fur, di izi lugɔ daapuza.
10Ka newee waa ɔɔ siwuu, u wia tuŋ,
di u wa vɛɛ de dui,
lee ɔɔ kaa duɛi?
11Gunla muuzeŋ nii n ɔɔ kaali la,
gɛɛ gunla muuni n ɔɔ hiihzi
di pergi la,
12gunnɛ newee ɔɔ chɔɔ, wàá ka izi,
di chiŋ waa haŋ kaali,
newea wàá hassi izi
lii ba dɔɔ biini.
13N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
di i daŋ vii kpaŋ
suah ŋmam biini
guŋŋ i baaŋ wa sɔɔni,
di dau saŋa tɛŋ,
di wa liizi n wia,
a daŋ vii pariŋ!
14Di newee siuwɔ,
u daŋ kaa wer izi,
di dɔɔ miibɔɔa?
N humkpega hɔpizaa maa biini,
n daŋ kpaŋ guŋŋ
saŋananii wa hel.
15I daŋ yiriŋ, n sɛɛ,
i daŋ kɛlli kunla hiŋ tawɛɛ ni.
16Wibii maa, denii i ra pessi n volaa,
ka hàá ra binni n wichɔgaa.
17I daŋ gilaa tɛŋ, di gil a tuŋ,
i daŋ kpa n wichɔgaa suah
alugɔ nɛr n kpa kuna
suah dakka biini.
I daŋ tɔ n wichɔgaa.
18Gunla bizenaa zɛɛzi hɛɛhraa n ɔɔ ra mɔɔri,
bia ra lalli
di lii bɔr la aŋ chɔɔwɛ la
19ani gunla nii n ɔɔ ra hee bia,
dozenaa ge paa
hɛɛhraa kaali la,
gunnɛ i ɔɔ chɔgi newee tamii.
20I ɔɔ kpegli neweere kakpaŋ, u wia tuŋ,
i ɔɔ bir u siwee duulaa,
di duŋŋuu u kaali.
21Di ba ra kpa u biizi girme gba, ka waa ɔɔ zum,
di ba ra gbɛlli baa ge,
ka waa ɔɔ na guŋ.
22U himmaa bɔra wiila wiarɛ ɔɔ zum,
di wii ra tɛɛ u hiŋ.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Ɛlifaz n kaa ŋɔ wia
1Denii Tɛman hinuu Ɛlifaz la bir ŋɔ,
2“Joob, nunzunni waa dɛkkɛ
unna ŋɔ wia la
n waa zɛɛ dɔɔwɛ,
di ra kɔɔ nɛra digna.
3Nunzunni daŋ kpa wiŋɔpɛɛri di ra di mmɔri,
di ra ŋɔ wia la
n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛa?
4Ka i ra gbɛlli Kɔraawiizii,
di ra tɔ u jaamaa ŋmɛnɛɛ.
5I wiŋɔzi ra bagli i biinikpolaa,
daraa su i wiŋɔzi biini.
6I himmaa nua tɛibuu chɔgri, n hor lɛi,
i himmaa wiŋɔzi di i daansɛɛrɛ.
7Hinuu nɛr la baŋ luglɛɛ di lulaa?
Hinuu ba lul mɔɔ
ka giŋgimee haa du dee?
8I ra nuu Kɔraawiizi jinaziiwaa?
I bɛnnɛ dɔɔ nunzumaa?
9Bɛɛ wideere i zum, ka yaa wɔɔ zummɛi?
Bɛɛ wia zɛɛ zumaarɛ i dɔɔ,
ka yaa wɔɔ dɔɔwɛi?
10Yaa helli nunzumaa lii nyuhuŋŋa hina be,
banla n bini i mɛɛ gba.
11Gunla Kɔraawiizi n na tig i bampirii la wɛɛ kukkɛɛa,
wia baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ bɔɔiih di tɛii?
12Ɛrɛɛ i gil i tɔɔrɔɔ dii ra fuuh i baannɛi,
i siwii aah gunnɛi,
13guŋ wia, i baaŋ ra fuuh Kɔraawiizi ni werge,
di gil wiŋɔzi naa dɔŋa
ra lii i nuaa?
14Newee daŋ wer nyaa doŋaa?
Gɛɛ u wia deŋli Kɔraawiizi bee?
15Kɔraawiizi waa u mɛlikazi yardɛɛ,
haali a gba doŋŋoo u be,
16ba kaa waa ŋɔ newee n chummɛ werge,
di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa
alugɔ unna nyɔɔ nii.
17Joob, a nuu n be, ń baglii,
gil n ŋɔ i be wia la miŋ nawɛɛ,
18gunla nunzunna n bagliŋ,
ba waa wia la baŋ hellee
lii ba naabaala be,
bɛl maa kpawɛɛ suah n ni.
19Banla bɛŋ baŋ faa kpa a hɛri tɛɛ,
hɔɔhri maa faa waa
ba baambaaŋ na ga.
20Biinikpola hiŋ la n na sunni nɛra,
daŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ di hanna la,
u de dui maa biini.
21Ɔnsii ni bɔsai gbɔga su u digna,
bampirsɔna saŋa biini ge,
ŋmɛɛŋkpega ɔɔ wa tɔɔruubuu.
22Waa bɔbiri biini lii tamii dɔɔwɛ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u zummɔ lugɔ
nɛbɛl daŋ kpuu.
23U juurɔɔrɛ ra bar,
di birgi diwee tɛɛ duuni.
U zummɔ lugɔ
u siu hɔpizii helloo.
24Biinichɔg werge ni bɔra waazaa,
kpa ɔnsii wergee ta u ni,
alugɔ koorizeŋ na nyiŋŋi
ú wa lɔu laal,
25dikuubɛɛwiai, u zigli u nogurunne
di ra du Kɔraawiizi,
di ra gbɛlli
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
26di kpoŋ, di kpogli u dɔŋkuna,
di kiiri ra ba Kɔraawiizi be,
bá lɔ dɔŋa.
27Haali uŋ vuhwɛɛ,
u loŋŋa lii gba,
28ka u daŋ du diŋgelli
ni diiwooni la n na chogli biine.
29Wàá ka ɛɛ dɔɔŋ, u daama ge tuŋ,
haali u kundɔɔlaa yaari a hɛri.
30Wàá wer chɔ a bɔbiri biini,
ninlau daŋ fuuuh alugɔ niŋ
n fuuh daazi kela.
Kɔraawiizi nua peu
kpau kaali.
31Ú gilɛɛ waa dar u hiŋ,
di ra yardi kunla maa
n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, wàá na kummaa.
32U daŋ na u kinturgaa a su mɔɔ, ka u saŋa hel,
u daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ daazi kela n hillɛ,
a wàá ka fur la.
33U daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ grepu daa la nɔna
n waa aahwɛ ka war,
alugɔ daa fiiri n hillɛ.
34Nɛr la n waa Kɔraawiizi ra ɔm,
daŋ nyaa naanna.
Nɛra la n nɔŋŋi kebee ni kuna lɛɛi,
diini daŋ fuuh.
35Ba ɔɔ kpogli tɔɔrɔɔ hizii,
di lul wichɔgaa,
ba hizi suugi daraa.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Joob n kaa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Ɛlifaz
1Denii Joob bir ŋɔ Ɛlifaz be,
2“N nuu wikpilaa alugɔ annii,
i waa zum nɛr bampirii tigaa!
I gillɔɔ n biinichɔg nyaŋŋi!
3I wiŋɔjaŋra naa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛa?
Bɛɛ n kpogliinei,
i ra di mmɔri gunnɛi?
4N ge gba daŋ faa wer ŋɔ wia naa,
di i faa du n duula naa,
n gba daŋ faa wer
ŋɔ wia nɛnnɛ,
di du i ni,
di viigi nyuu dui.
5Ka n daŋ vii ŋɔ wia dui bɔkpega,
bampirii tigaa wiŋɔzi la
min niŋ vii ŋɔ,
daŋ tɛi bɔsɔna.
6Haali di n ŋɔ wia gba,
ka n bɔra waazaa wàá giliŋ,
di n kaa siigi ge,
a wàá kaali.
7N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n bɔra huah werge,
wibii maa, u kpu
n diahina maanii
tuŋ nyaamm.
8U vɔɔzimbuu, a guŋ di n daansɛɛ,
n kɔgaa nyaŋŋi,
di ra bagli n bilchɔg.
9U kpa baaŋ ni nyɛgzi wergee di ra naaŋ,
di hee u nyina di ra duŋ,
n haahri ra fiiliŋ ni hahzi.
10Nɛra ra mamiŋ,
di chɛ n lia gbɛlliŋ,
di ɛɛ nuukpaŋ bá naaŋ.
11Kɔraawiizi gilimbuu tɛɛ wichɔgɛɛra,
di kpaŋ du
biinikpola hina nonee biini.
12N sogaa faa wessoo tɛŋ,
ka u wa lau n wia chɔgi,
di hanzi n baŋaa,
di kpaŋ viiri hɛri.
U kpambuu birgi kunla baŋ kpawɛɛ
ra helli hoo tai,
13u hotaara bariŋ. Waa n ni sunne,
ka tɔɔhzi n siga,
di puri n kpol ta hɛri.
14U ɔɔ dumbuu pira, digiidigii,
di ra kiiri n ni alugɔ laallɔɔri.
15N kpa gbɔglɔnnɛ nyɛr laala di laali,
di so hɛɛhraa biini ni biinichɔg.
16N lɛɛzi aahwɔɔ dikuu wiraa wia,
maa kaa ra na nɛnnɛ,
17ka maa chɔgri maa dɔɔwɛ dikuu kalu wia,
n na suŋŋi wiizi ni biinihuŋŋu.
18Ee, hɛri, gilɛɛ waa tɔ n chal,
gilɛɛ gil n wiraa waa suah!
19Haali filaŋkennaa gba,
n daansɛɛ hiŋ
du Kɔraawiizi bol,
n hiini du chiŋ.
20N dammuzi ra mamimbuu,
miŋ fug sinii di ra du
Kɔraawiizi ni naa,
21u ɔɔ ra fɔrgi Kɔraawiizii dikuu nɛr wia,
gunla nɛr n ɔɔ suŋŋi
di ra tɛɛ u dammu la.
22Binni tama bɛnnɛ niŋ bɛri,
ka ń vol ŋmɛnɛɛ la baŋ ɔɔ la,
ba wàá kaa bir ba la.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
1Joob kaa ŋɔ, “N siu duglɔɔrɛ,
maa wette ra heezi,
maa kaa dɔɔ kummaa,
di ŋmam bɛŋ lɛi.
2Wibii maa, chɛɛtɛ ɛɛra barimbuu,
n na gunla banna mamiŋ.
3N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, n wia dɔɔ wibiire.
A nuu n wiŋɔzi.
Nɛr maa waa hoo
un niŋ ŋɔ hiiniŋ.
4I tɔ ba nfɛssii, ba wàá wer zum wia zɛɛ,
awia, hàá gil ba kpegliŋ.
5Faala maa sɛɛlii n ŋɔwɛɛ, dí nɛr ɔɔ ɛɛ u dammuzii sɔsɔgɔ
dikuu kebee wia,
u biizi di tɔɔrɔɔ,
dikuu guŋ wia.
6Nɛra jaa kpa a sɛɛlii naa di ra taŋ,
ba ɔɔ wa puuzi nuuhaarii
di ra du n siwee.
7N dɔgnya werge gillɔɔ n nyuŋŋi tuŋ,
n vaama ni n naazi
du lugɔ chaanii.
8Nɛra la n fɛwɛɛ lugɔ
ba wia deŋloore nuuzi kpu,
dikuu keŋ wia,
ba baana ra fuuh
banla n waa
Kɔraawiizi ra ɔm ni.
9Ama, banla wia n deŋlee,
daŋ haa lau
ba hiŋaazi kpogli.
Banla ge n waa doŋa dɔɔwɛ,
dɔɔ kpegzi jaa.
10Ka di ba maa wa chigɔ n see,
màá na nunzunni ba biini.
11N hɔpizaa tunnɔɔ, n jinazi maa bir pɛɛ,
gunnɛ n bampirii
winyiŋŋaa maa gba du.
12N dammuzi naa kpa hamuŋaa di birgi hɔpizaa,
di bɔr haŋ waa biri,
ba ɔɔ ŋɔu,
‘Bɔchaaŋ duglɔɔrɛ.’
13Di bol la bɛŋ tamii min dɔɔwɛɛ ŋmam,
di kpa n kunchɔɔrikuŋ
dau bɔbiri biini,
14amɔ, n daŋ ŋɔ ŋmam be, ‘Hinuu n mɛɛ,’
di ŋɔ sandul be,
‘Hinuu n maa
ni n niuhambie.’
15Lee waarɛ n tamii du naanɛi?
Anɛɛ n niŋ wer na
tamii la miŋ dɔɔwɛnɛi?
16N ni tamii daŋ kpau siwaa?
Yaa maa daŋ kpau zuu
hɛɛhraa biiniaa?”

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Bildad n kaa ŋɔ wia
1Denii Suua hinuu Bildad la bir ŋɔ,
2“Saŋa bɛliirɛ í gil i wiŋɔzi naanɛi?
Fɛ nfɛrɛ, ka yá ŋɔ wia.
3Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra yir yaa nauna,
di ŋɔ yaa ɛɛ gɛnaarɛi?
4I kpa baannɛ ra du i hiŋ pira,
bá kuu i wia di vɛɛ hɛri gɛɛ?
Kɔ́raawiizi tuzi
bizenaa a parii?
5Ba dinzi biinikpola hiŋ fintinaa,
wàá ka lau maa.
6Bɔchaaŋ la n du u tanti dia biini daŋ biri,
fintina la n chigɛ u kɛra la dim.
7U naazi la n faa kpekke la daŋ gɛrgi,
u himmaa jinazi taau ha.
8U vol ga zuu sidɛɛ ni,
u lawuu.
9Sidɛɛ lau u naalume,
ŋmɛmbee ge lawuu kiŋkiŋ.
10Ba kpa ŋmɛmbee di heu hɛri,
di kpa sidɛɛ ge
di heu ŋmɛnibee.
11Ɔnsii werge baruu,
di ra di u naagbora.
12Hɛhchɔg ra nyiŋŋi u chol u ninɛɛ,
di ɛɛ u sirya di u wa chollo.
13Wiilchɔgii tɔ u bɔra maa ni,
di gil u vaama ni naazi ra pɔɔh.
14Ba lizuu lii u dia la biini
uŋ faa duwɛɛ nɛnnɛ la,
di tuuzuu la lalaa bol.
15Niŋ du u dia biini,
ba fuuh jilbi yaari u duuribɔr.
16U ɛɛ lugɔ daa lunne
ni u kela maa n siuwɛ di hil.
17Ba wàá kaa ra liizi u wia
durnya naa biini, u sɔŋ dim.
18Ba duŋŋuubuu lii bɔchaaŋ
du bɔbiri biini,
di lizuu lii durnya.
19Waa biizi gɛɛ naanna dɔɔwɛ u nɛra biini,
u nɛr maa waa kaa ka.
20U laba la tir nɛra la
n du wiicholii ni wiifurii maa,
ɔnsii werge lau baa,
ba bɔra ra sa.
21Wibii maa, wichɔgɛɛri tunaa guŋ,
gunnɛ nɛr la n waa
Kɔraawiizi ra ɔm, laba du.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Joob n kaa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Bildad
1Denii Joob bir ŋɔ,
2“Ɛrɛɛ ii kpa wiŋɔzi di tɔɔriŋ werge,
di sunniŋ birgi magɛi?
3Iinna chagziŋ, a bufii keŋ.
Amɔ, hiihzi waa ia lauwɛaa?
4Di n ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ wibii maa,
ii wia lɛi, n nyuu wiarɛ.
5Haali di ii daŋ kpa iihinaa tɔgzi kaaliŋ,
di kpa n tɔɔrɔɔ dii
di ra chagziŋ,
6denii ii zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛwɔɔ leu n ni,
di kpa u asau lawiŋ.
7Haali minna wii, di ra ŋɔ, ‘U leu n ninɛɛ!’
Ka maa wiimaa ra nuu.
Haali minna yir ŋɔ ú hiiniŋ,
ka nɛr maa waa hoo,
ú di seriya ni wibii tɛŋ.
8U tɔ n ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ, awia, màá na bɔr kaali,
u kpa bɔbirii tɔ n ŋmɛnibee.
9U foozi n daama maanii,
di chɔgi n sɔŋ.
10U chɔgimbuu alugɔ baŋ purgi dia,
di gil n tamii tuŋ
alugɔ baŋ wigzi daa.
11U baaŋ ra fuuh n ninɛɛ werge,
u kuriŋ di ra jaa u dɔma ni.
12U hum u laallɔɔraa bá wa lɔŋ,
ba wa ki bɔɔni bar n dia,
di fɔɔŋ.
13U gillɔɔ n diahina kiziŋ ta,
di gil n birgi hɔɔhri
banla n zumiŋ be.
14N lulla maa kaalɔɔ nyaamm,
n dammuzi ge suuh n wia.
15N hɔɔhra ni n balaa wan zummɛ,
di ra ɛɛŋ lugɔ famaruu.
16N ɔɔ yir n balii, ka wàá sɛɛ,
haali di n suŋŋuu gba.
17N heeza ra sɔɔhri n haaŋ be,
n himmaa lulla ra kɔɔŋ.
18Haali bichalli maa ra gbɛlliŋ,
di ra mamiŋ, di ba wa naŋ.
19N badɔŋa himmaa kiiŋ werge maa,
banla min nɔŋŋɛɛ ge
bir di ra chagziŋ.
20Maa kaa ɛɛ kummaa,
see hɔŋ ni hoga bɛŋ,
a ka tama n vii siu.
21N dammuzi, ií na n sinyɛna,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii lɔŋ!
22Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra tɔɔriŋ werge
gunla Kɔraawiizi
n na ɛɛŋ lai?
N sunnaa haa waa ia kukkɛɛa?
23A daŋ vii pariŋ, di nɛbɛl sɛbi
n wiŋɔzi du hɔŋ biini
24gɛɛ di kpa kerge sɛɛhzaa dau bii ni,
á chɔɔ di hanna la!
25N zummɔ lugɔ n Lɛɛri ra nyinuu,
u daŋ ba a tuna
di wa ŋɔ wia lɛɛŋ.
26Di n bɔrahɔŋ wa tunnɔ,
ka miŋ haa du de naa,
n daŋ na Kɔraawiizi.
27N himmaa siwee daŋ nau,
a waa lugɔ nɛbɛl.
N na kɛlluu a saŋa vii ba!
28Di ii ŋɔwɔɔ, ‘Yaa daŋ tɔɔruu,
dikuu aŋ lii u be wia.’
29A dɛkkɔɔ iinna ɔm Kɔraawiizi tokobi,
di u baaŋ fuuhwo,
u daŋ kpau tɛr nɛra digna,
gunnɛ ii zum lugɔ
seriya diiri du denii.”

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
Zofa n kaa ŋɔ wia
1Denii Naama hinuu Zɔfar la bir ŋɔ,
2“Joob, i wiŋɔzi gillɔɔ n nfɛrɛ ra koozi,
a dɛg lugɔ n ŋɔ wia tɛi.
3I hau n ninɛɛ di gbɛlliŋ,
n nfɛrɛ tɛŋ lugɔ
n ŋɔ wia di chemii.
4Wibii maa, i zum gunla an duwɛɛnɛ,
di lii faala maa,
di haŋ lii saŋa la Kɔraawiizi
n ta newee hɛri naa.
5Biinikpola hiŋ bɔsɔna ni mamaa wàá birgi,
unla ge n waa Kɔraawiizi ra ɔm,
bɔsɔna maa keŋ tama.
6Haali u jigsi n ɔɔ du kaŋ werge,
u nyuu gaa chug baama gba,
7ka peu daŋ kpau kaali alugɔ u bina.
A tir banla n faa zumuu la,
ba ra ŋɔ, ‘Lee u duɛi?’
8U daŋ kaali lugɔ wia nai deeza biini,
ba wàá ka nau maa,
alugɔ hiŋ na wii
deeza biini hamuŋa ni.
9Nɛra la n faa nau la,
ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka nau,
ú duuribɔr chɔɔ pɛɛ.
10Ú biizi bir turgi kuna la
ba mɛɛ n foozee nyaara be la.
11U pɔlaa fɔŋŋa la uŋ dɔɔwɛ la,
u ni a maa
daŋ kpau birgi hɛɛhraa.
12Wichɔgaa summɔɔ u nua,
u kpa aŋhina du u nua
di ra mugzi,
13waa nyiŋŋi a tuŋ,
di gil a du u nua.
14Ka u diwee daŋ bir du nyɛg u hia biini,
di birgi lugɔ hɛrikuna siri u biini.
15U daŋ hɛɛhzi daama la maa uŋ liglee la.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil
u ug a maa ta.
16U daŋ suu hɛrikuna siri,
buzu dumuu kpu.
17Wàá na kissaazi la n kannɛ werge,
di lii Kɔraawiizi be
alugɔ muu n suwee la.
18U daŋ nyaa kunla maa uŋ kuuhwɛ na,
wàá di u soochi tɔna suma.
19Dikuu uŋ sunni nyaara, a ra nuu baa,
di foozi diini la
uŋ waa mawɛɛ wia.
20Wibii maa, u kunyiŋŋichɔgaa wàá tuŋ,
wàá wer kpa u daama
lɛɛ u hiŋ.
21Kummaa wàá ka, ú di,
u daama daŋ tuŋ.
22U daama saŋa, biinichɔg daŋ lawuu,
dɔgnya werge chol u ni.
23Di u haŋ wa di piŋ,
Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa
baaŋ werge tɔɔruu.
24Haali un ninna chɔ,
dikuu lugbii dɔŋkuna wia gba,
ka danyɛ hobii nua
n du chilachila, daŋ lawuu.
25U pamuu lii u harbɔɔ,
u nuunyɛgzii la ge lii u hiah.
Ɔnsii werge daŋ chol u ni,
u bɔra ra sa,
26u daama leu bɔbiri limpiriŋ biini.
Kɔraawiizi gil niŋ wa fuuuh,
di di kunla maa
n ka u dia biini.
27Chinchiŋ daŋ lizi u bilchɔg chaaŋ,
hɛri ge di u daansɛɛ guŋ.
28U kundɔɔlaa maa daŋ chɔgi,
Kɔraawiizi baaŋ hɔpizii la,
alugɔ nii n suwee
di paa kummaa kaali la.
29Laba la Kɔraawiizi n dauwɛ
tɛɛ biinikpola hiŋ,
ani kapɛttɛ la uŋ lizɛɛ
dawuubuu guŋ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
Joob n kaa ŋɔ wia
1Denii Joob bir ŋɔ,
2“Ií ra nuu n wiŋɔzi nɛnnɛ,
gil annii ɛɛ wia la
iiŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tig n bampirii.
3Ií diŋ kanyitti ka n ŋɔ wia,
di n wa ŋɔwɔɔ tuŋ,
ií jaa ra ɛɛŋ chɛɛtɛ.
4Newee ninɛɛ n nuumi ra duaa?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ màá nyaa kanyittei?
5Ií gil ii nuuzi kpu, ií ra binniŋ,
di fɔɔ ii nuuzi.
6Di n waa fɛ wia la n ɛɛŋ nfɛrɛ,
n nua ɔɔ kpuu,
ɔnsii lawiŋ, n bɔra ra sa.
7Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ biinikpola hina du de di ra bini,
ba fɔŋŋa ra jaai?
8Ba na ba biizi ni ba naanna,
n birgi nɛra di bar baa.
9Ba diini kpekkoo,
ɔnsii maa waa hoo ba be.
Kɔraawiizi waa ba digna ra tɛr.
10Ba nabala waa deezee di ra huhzi,
ba naniinazi ra lul nɛnnɛ,
a waa mizi.
11Ba biizi sa
di ra bar bɔr maa alugɔ pebizi.
12Biinikpola hina ɔɔ ra lɔ kemzi,
di ra yigzi kuna, di ra yir yira,
di ra huuh tiitoraa,
di ra di bahinaa.
13Ba de dui dɔɔ tɔna,
di ɔɔ siu ni bampirsɔna.
14Haali ba ɔɔ ŋɔ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ‘Gil yaa!
Yaa waa nyiŋŋi
yá zum i ŋmɛnizi.
15Anɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
lugɔ ya ra humuuwɛi?
Bɛɛ tɔnaa ya na,
di yaa ra jaamuuwɛi?’
16Ba fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ
ba himmaa fɔŋŋaa
gillɛ ba nyɛɛli.
Awia, màá sɛɛ gunla
biinikpola hina n na fɛ la.
17Saŋa kpila maa, biinikpola hina
ɔɔ zɛŋuu mɔɔ ka siu.
Buŋmɛnɛɛ dɔgnya ni tɔɔrɔɔ werge
haa huuzi baa,
laba la Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ baa
u baaŋ la biinei?
18Buŋmɛnɛɛ ba haa ɛɛ alugɔ kɔlaa peu benei,
alugɔ pekpeg n wa paa
zɔga kaalɛi?
19Ba ɔɔ ŋɔu, ‘Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ kpa dignitɛraarɛ,
di dau ra kpaŋ ba biizi.’
Gil u turgi baa ba himmaa a kim,
bá zum guŋ!
20Gil ba himmaa siwee na ba chɔgaa,
di gil ba di Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
baaŋ tɔɔrɔɔ.
21Di ba miibɔɔni tunnɔ,
ba baga lɛi kaa
ba biizi bɔsɔna wia.
22Anɛɛ n niŋ wer bagli Kɔraawiizi la
n na di nɛra la
n du bɔzenaa seriya nunzumai?
23Nɛbɛl ɔɔ siwuu,
di u haa kpekko, di dɔɔ bɔsɔna,
24u bɔra du wer nɛnnɛ,
nuu su u hoga biine maa.
25Bɛl ge siu ni biinichɔg werge,
u ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa
kunnanii maa suma diwee.
26Ka ba maa ɔɔ siwuu chɔɔ hɛɛhraa biini,
sandule di baa.
27N zum wii la iinna fɛu nɛnnɛ,
jinachɔgaa la iiŋ tawɛɛ
ií wa chɔgiŋ.
28Ii ɔɔ ŋɔu, ‘Nɛzeŋ la dia du lee filaŋkennei,
biinikpola hina
n faa ra zuuu lai?’
29Ii ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa nɛra la
n na vol ŋmɛnɛɛ pɛɛzɛɛa?
Ii waa amaniyezi la
baŋ ɔɔ wa lizi la pessee,
30lugɔ a hɔl la Kɔraawiizi baaŋ n ɔɔ fuuh,
u ra tɛr nɛra digna la,
biinikpola hinnɛ u ɔɔ gilaa?
31Anɛɛ n ɔɔ hau biinikpola hiŋ ni u sibɔɔi?
Anɛɛ n ɔɔ bir turguu
u wiɛɛlaa kimɛi?
32Ba ɔɔ chiubuu ga hug,
di gil nɛra chi
ra guu u ŋmam hiŋ.
33Nɛkpila werge maa ɔɔ duubuu,
di la u hugribɔr,
baŋhina du see,
baŋhina du har.
Haali hɛɛhraa gba
ɔɔ tɔ u bɔra ni guŋ bɔɔiih.
34Awia, ɛrɛɛ ii wer kpa ii wijagazi
tig n bampiriiyei?
Ii wiŋɔzi maa ɛɛ karaa!”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
Ɛlifaz n kaa ŋɔ wia
1Denii Teman hinuu Ɛlifaz la bir ŋɔ,
2“Newee daŋ wer dɔɔ tɔna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizia?
Haali nunzunni daŋ wer
dɔɔ tɔna tɛuwaa?
3Bɛɛ bɔsɔnaa Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ dɔɔ,
di i wia faa deŋlooi?
Bɛɛ tɔnaa ú vii na,
di i vii waa chɔgri maa dɔɔwɛi?
4Hinna ɔmuu wiarɛ u hau i ni,
di ra chugii wiaa?
5I biinikpola lɛi kannɛ wergea?
I wichɔgaa lɛi
waa maga dɔɔwɛɛa?
6I lɛɛ i lulla kunaa di dau talma pɛɛpɛɛ,
di lɛɛ ba laala,
ba waa kaa
dɔɔ kummaa bá laali.
7I faa kpolli nɛra la n kuuhwɛɛ nii,
di kpolli banla
lɔzi n na kpuu diwee,
8haali hiŋ faa ɛɛ fɔŋŋa hiŋ werge,
di dɔɔ hɛri, di ɛɛ girme hiŋ,
di so de gba.
9I faa vɛɛ luhaana hiinaare,
di kaa sunni lalbiizi ge.
10Awiarɛ sidɛɛzi bar i maa,
awiarɛ siaahmu huuzii,
ɔnsii werge lawii,
11awiarɛ bɔr biri limpiriŋ,
haa wette ra na,
awiarɛ a ɛɛ lugɔ
nii suwoore tɔ i ni.
12Kɔraawiizi duuribɔr
waa chinchiŋ kuna ni bɛrɛɛ lɛiyaa?
Ɔɔ willi ra binni chinchiŋwilaa,
haali aŋ du chinchiŋ
werge gba!
13Ka i ɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Bɛɛ Kɔraawiizi zumɛi?
Baamazi tɔ u ninɛɛ.
Ɛrɛɛ ú ɛɛ di yaa seriyai?
14Baama biŋŋe tɔubuu,
awia, waa wette ra na yaa.
U ɔɔ du chinchiŋ
ni hɛri baambaannɛ
di ra gaagi.’
15I haa aah siwiire,
í ra hiŋ ŋmɛnibinii la
wichɔgɛɛra n na hiŋ laa?
16Ba siuzɔɔrɛ mɔɔ, ka ba saŋazi haa hel,
alugɔ nii n ɔɔ su
di paagi diini kaali la.
17Ba ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi benii, ‘Gil yaa pɛrɛtɛ!
Bɛɛ hìŋ́ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
ɛɛ yaai?’
18Ka waabuu faa gillɛ kunnanaa suugi ba diini,
awia, maa chigɛ guu
biinikpola hina baglaa.
19Nɛra la wia n deŋlee,
na guŋ hina tɔɔrɔɔrɛ,
ba bɔra sɔɔni.
Banla n waa chɔgri maa dɔɔwɛ
ra ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛ, di ra ŋɔ,
20‘Wibii maa, ba chɔgi yaa dɔmaa,
niŋ di ba daama maa.’
21Joob, a sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔɔra,
bampirsɔna du i nuu baambaaŋ,
guŋ daŋ gil i nyɛɛli.
22A sɛɛ u baglaazi,
di kpa u wiŋɔzi du i bampirii.
23Di i bittɔ ba Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ be,
u daŋ lɛɛi,
di i gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi i dia,
24di kpa i saliŋ ha hɛɛhraa biini,
di kpa i salinnanaa
ha gɔŋluŋe biine.
25Denii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ɛɛ lugɔ i saliŋ,
di ɛɛ lugɔ saliŋhuŋŋu la
wia n na parii werge.
26Wibii maa, denii i na bɔsɔna lii u be,
di ra jaamuu ni biinihuŋŋu.
27I daŋ ɔɔ wii duu, u nuu tɛi,
di hiŋ nuuzi la hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ.
28Wia la maa hin niŋ ɔɔ lau, daŋ na ɛɛi,
i ŋmɛnizi maa chaani.
29Di nɛra wichɔgaa wa gillɔ ba sɔɔni siwii,
i suŋŋi wiizi,
u daŋ lalli baa chiŋ.
30Haali di nɛr haa di bilchɔg gba,
ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛu,
dikuu i wideŋlaa wia.
Dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɔɔ ra lɛɛ
nɛra la n waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛɛ,
di ra lii wichɔgaa ɛɛi biini.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.
translation_text:
Joob n kaa ŋɔ wia
1Denii Joob bir ŋɔ,
2“Haali ni zinaa, n haa ra nuumuu,
di ra di Kɔraawiizi mmɔri.
Ka u haa ra tɔɔrimbuu werge maa,
haali n ni
n hɛmaa naa maa gba.
3Di n vii zum bɔr la min niŋ nau,
di vii wer la u duuribɔr,
4n daŋ vii kpa n wiimaa dau u sibɔɔ,
n nuu di mmɔri.
5Ń nuu gunla un niŋ ŋɔ,
di zum wii la n du u be.
6U daŋ kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ la di tɔɔriŋ?
Akai, u daŋ keŋŋi digni
di nuu gunla min niŋ ŋɔ.
7Denii nɛr la wia n deŋlee
kpa u wia dau u see,
ú lɛɛŋ lii n seriya diiri be,
saŋaa saŋa maa.
8Ka miŋ la wiifurii, waa hoo de,
di la wiicholii, mɔɔ nawɛɛ de.
9Di u wa du huma wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag,
maa ɔɔ nau,
di u wa bittɔ la wiifurii nodig wiikakag,
maa ɔɔ na u laalii gba.
10Ka waabuu zum n vollibɔraa,
di u wa ɛɛŋ na,
n daŋ du wer alugɔ saliŋ.
11N na hiŋ u ŋmɛnizii ni wibii,
maa bɛɛwɛ ga keŋkere maa.
12N ɔɔ ra hiŋ u nuuzii,
di ra ɛɛ u kipar kaali n hor.
13Ka waa birgaa dɔɔwɛ.
Anɛɛ n niŋ wer karsuuwɛi?
Gunla maa n paruu,
gunnɛ u ra ɛɛ.
14Gunla un dauwɛ tɛŋ, gunnɛ ú ɛɛ,
a guŋ jinazi haa kpillɔɔ u be.
15Awiarɛ ɔnsii lawiŋ,
n bɔra ra sa u see.
Di n wa liizi annii naa maa wia,
n ɔɔ ra ɔmuubuu.
16Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n bɔra huah,
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
kpa bɔsairɛ ta n ni.
17Ka bɔbiri waa wette gil n siigi,
haali a bɔbiri limpiriŋ n gillɛ
maa kaa wer di ra na gba.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
1Joob haa ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
waa seriya dii saŋazi dauwɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ banla n na humuu,
ɔɔ nyiŋŋi a guŋ hɔpizaa huhzɛi?
2Nɛra ɔɔ tuzi magbɔɔni biarɛ,
bá hɛssi du kaŋ jaa,
di ŋmɛɛ peeza
di jaa ba hora ni, di ra dɛɛzi.
3Ba ɔɔ duŋŋi lalbie kaweere kaali,
di lɛɛ luhaaŋ navarga
dau talma.
4Ba waa ɔɔ gil nyaara na kunla n dɛg baa,
di fir baa ba maa chɔ suahzi.
5Nyaara ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
kaukpoŋlaa n du hɛribɔduma,
di bar di ra nyiŋŋi diwee.
De bɛnnɛ bá wer na diwee
tɛɛ ba biizi.
6Ba ɔɔ chaali diweere di lii kooni la
n waa ba hora ɛɛwɛ biine,
di du biinikpola hina
grepu daazi kooni,
di ra kuuni a nɔna.
7Ba ɔɔ kɔrgi bɔraa di chɔɔ hamuŋzi ni,
dikuu baŋ waa laala dɔɔwɛ wia.
Ba waa kummaa dɔɔwɛ,
bá tɔ waari saŋa.
8Dooŋ la n ɔɔ nɛɛ bizenaa ni la ɔɔ gilluu ba bɔra pɔɔh,
dikuu baŋ waa
duuribɔra dɔɔwɛ wia.
9Biinikpola hina ɔɔ tɔri lalbiere
lii u maa ila ni,
di foozi nyaari bie,
dikuu kim wia.
10Ka nyaara ɔɔ kɔrgi bɔra di ra vol,
dikuu ba laala nyaai wia,
di ɔɔ ra chi nɛra mia,
ka ra chɔɔ lɔzi.
11Ba ɔɔ ra ɛɛ nuu,
di daali siŋ di ra tɛɛ nɛra,
ka niinyɔgzi ra kpu baa.
12Banla n na siu la
hɛmaa nyaŋŋi a bolzeŋ biini.
Banla baŋ du pira ge ra chɛɛhgi,
di ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa,
ka Kɔraawiizi baga lɛi.
13Banla n na vɛɛ bɔchaaŋ du denii,
ba waa u ŋmɛnizi zummɛ
gɛɛ di ra hiŋaa.
14Di bɔr wa biroo, nɛkpuuri ɔɔ izuu,
di ra kpu nyaara
ni dɔgnya hina,
ka ra ŋmɛɛ hamuŋa ni.
15Sɛnsɛnni ɔɔ ra kpaŋ bɔr siwee lauraarɛ,
u ɔɔ fɛu, ‘Nɛr maa wàá naŋ,’
di kpa kuŋ tɔ u siwee.
16Nɛra ɔɔ ra kuugi gbessii,
di ra zuu diini hamuŋa ni.
Ka suahzi bɔchaaŋ saŋa,
ba waa nyiŋŋi
wiimaa ɛɛi bɔchaaŋ.
17Bɔbiri kilɛŋkilɛnnɛ ɛɛ ba maa chɔɔzi,
ba ni bɔbiri kunchɔgaa
ɔɔ ra di dammunaa.
18Ka ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ fufuu di sag nii nyuu,
ba hɛri ɛɛ lugɔ baŋ seeu nua,
guŋ gil nɛr maa wàá la
di ga hum
ba grepu daazi kooni.
19Gunla hil ni bɔwem
n ɔɔ gil dobia ŋmɛɛri la,
gunnɛ ŋmam ɔɔ keuzi
wichɔgɛɛra kaali.
20Ba maawaa wàá kaa ra liizi ba wia,
sandule di baa.
Ba wàá ɔɔ ra liizi wichɔgɛɛra wia,
ka ba kuugi lugɔ daa.
21Ba ɔɔ ra sunni hahbara
ni haaŋ la n ɛɛ biinyaarii,
ba waa luhaaŋ ge ra hiini.
22Ka Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ kpa u fɔŋŋaa
tuuzi nɛzenaa kaali.
Haali baŋ soge nɛnnɛ gba,
ka ba waa miibɔɔ tamii dɔɔwɛ.
23Aŋhinabe, u daŋ gil bá so ni bampirsɔna,
ka u lizi siwiire
sag ba ni saŋa maa.
24Ba ɔɔ dɔɔ sɔnnɛ tama,
ka ba wia tuŋ kɔrai.
Ba ɔɔ tuu baa zɛɛ
alugɔ ba dɔŋahina,
di chaali baa
alugɔ baŋ kum mia.
25Di guŋ waa ɛɛwɛ, anɛɛ n niŋ wer bagli
lugɔ kara hinnɛ miŋ,
di gil ń wiŋɔzi bir pɛɛi?”

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
Bildad n kaa ŋɔ wia
1Denii Suua hinuu Bildad la bir ŋɔ,
2“Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa,
di dɛg ɔmaa werge,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u gillɔɔ
u bol dɔɔ bampirsɔna.
3Anɛɛ n niŋ wer kur mɛlikazi la n na humuuwɛi?
Anɛɛ ninɛɛ Kɔraawiizi
bɔchaaŋ waa chaanɛi?
4Newee wia daŋ wer deŋli
gɛɛ di du paratata Kɔraawiizi bee?
5U be, baagu waa chaani nɛnnɛ,
chinchiŋwilaa ge
waa paratata duwɛɛ,
6ba waa ŋɔ newee n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ nakɛɛh bina
gɛɛ uŋ ɛɛwɛ
lugɔ sandulaa?”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Joob n kaa ŋɔ wia
1Denii Joob bir ŋɔ,
2“Na gunla hiŋ hiini nɛr la
n waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ!
Na gunla hiŋ lɛɛ
mìŋ́ gɛrgi naa di ta!
3Na gunla hiŋ bagli nɛr la
n waa nunzuma dɔɔwɛ, wia!
Na gunla hiŋ bagli
wia zɛɛ zumaa!
4Anɛɛ n baglii, i ŋɔ wia naanɛi?
Anɛɛ dumaa kpa i nua
ŋɔ wia naanɛi?
5Lalaa bɔra ra sau
hɛri zɛɛ niiri biine.
6Lalaa bol chɔɔwɔɔ kpantalaŋ Kɔraawiizi see.
Chɔgaa bɔr chɔɔ chaaŋ boii,
kummaa waa u ni tɔwɛɛ.
7U yaa wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag chinne, di tɔ bɔduma.
Di gil hɛri waa
kummaa ni hɔŋŋɛ.
8U kpa u baamazii fɔɔzi niiri,
ka a tɔgzi waa wette gil a pogzi.
9U yaa u baamazii
tɔ baagu bir siwee.
10U tii bɔr la chiŋ ni hɛri
n chem dɔŋaa dau niiri nyuuni,
u ɛɛ bɔchaaŋ ni bɔbiri magbɔɔ.
11Chinchiŋ ligee zigli, ɔnsii lawaa,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi n pozee wia.
12U kpa u fɔŋŋa di gil muuzeŋ chɔɔ bɔɔiih,
di kpa u nunzuma
ŋmuuri muuzeŋ biini
sechɔgii Rahab.
13U heezaa gillɛ chiŋ chaani,
di kpa u nonii kpu
hɛrikuŋ la n na chɔ.
14Ka annii haa ɛɛ u fɔŋŋa wiɛɛlaa tamaa,
yaa waa u wiɛɛlaa wia
tama maa zummɛ!
Anɛɛ n niŋ wer zum gunla
u fɔŋŋa n mɛkkɛnɛi?”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
1Joob haa ra ŋɔ wia, di ŋɔ,
2“N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
n du de saŋa maa la,
lugɔ wan tɛɛwɛ wibii,
ka gil n di dɔgnya werge,
3ka miŋ haŋ na dɔɔ miibɔɔ,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi
n tɛŋ heeza wia,
4n nua wàá ŋɔ biinikpola wia,
n nuuzuŋŋi wàá dar nɛr maa.
5N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá sɛɛ lugɔ wibiire ii ra ŋɔ,
di kpa ra ba n siu,
ka màá hɔɔ lugɔ
maa wibii dɔɔwɛ.
6N daŋ haa lau n wideŋlaa di kpogli nɛnnɛ,
màá gilaa ta maa.
N biini wàá tɛŋ chɔgri maa,
n de dui naa biini.
7Kɔ́raawiizi gil n dɔma laba ɛɛ lugɔ biinikpola hina laba,
ú tɛr n haahra digna
alugɔ wibii nyaara!
8Bɛɛ tamiirɛ banla n waa Kɔraawiizi ra hiŋ dɔɔi,
di u waa lizi ba miibɔɔnɛi?
9Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ ra nuu ba wiraare,
di biinichɔg werge wa lau baa?
10Ba daŋ na bɔsɔna,
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ bee?
Ba daŋ ɔɔ ra yir
Kɔraawiizi saŋazi maa?
11N daŋ bagli ia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa wia.
Màá kpa Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
ŋmɛnizi suah ii ni.
12Ii himmaa na gunnɛ,
ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra ŋɔ wia la
n waa zɛɛ maa dɔɔwɛi?
13Laba la Kɔraawiizi n dau biinikpola hinaa keŋ,
sikpegii hina ge kapɛttɛɛ keŋ
di lii Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ be.
14Haali di ba biizi kpillɔ gunla maa,
ka ba maa daŋ mag laal biini.
Ba dee ŋmɛnɛ wàá wer na
diwee á hel baa maa.
15Banla ge n niŋ lii laal biini,
wiilchɔgaarɛ niŋ kpu baa,
ka ba luhaana wàá wii baa.
16Haali baŋ dɔɔ saliŋhuŋŋa,
a du kaŋ werge alugɔ hɛɛhraa,
di dɔɔ laala a chɔɔ kulululu,
17ka nɛnanaarɛ niŋ dɔɔa di ra laali,
banla ge wia n dɔɔ wibii
bɔnni a saliŋhuŋŋa.
18Diini la ge baŋ mawɛɛ,
daŋ du lugɔ kunjigzi,
alugɔ nɛr la n na guu bɔr lɔɔ.
19Ba chɔɔ ni daama hamuŋa ni,
ka di ba haŋ wa izi chɔɔzi ni,
ba waa ɔɔ kaa naa.
20Ɔnsii werge daŋ pirgi baa,
di lɔ baa alugɔ nii n suwee,
pekpeg ta hamuŋa ni,
di kpa baa kaali.
21Wiifurii pekpeg kpa baa
lii ba diini kaali.
22U daŋ ta ba ni, wàá suŋ ba ni,
haali banna ɛɛ ania
lugɔ bá chɔ lii u biini,
di lɛɛ ba hiŋ gba.
23U danna ta ba ni fufufufu,
di lizi baa lii ba diini.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
1Joob kaa ŋɔ, “Bɔɔni du denii, ba ra ki saliŋhuŋŋa,
bɔr la banna ɔɔzi saliŋ ge du de.
2Ba ɔɔ ki lugbiarɛ lii hɛri,
di ŋmɛɛri lugbiaahmu lii bia ni.
3Newee ɔɔ zuu bɔbiri kilɛŋkilɛnnɛ,
di ra pigzi, di ra ki hɛri,
di ra nyiŋŋi kuna naa,
a bɔbiri biini.
4Ba ɔɔ lii bɔra la nɛra n duwɛɛnɛ,
di la ga ki bɔɔluŋe,
ni bɔra la newea
n haa waa volle maa,
di lauri ŋmɛnni,
di ra zeeli a bɔɔni biine.
5Hɛrii diwee ra lii,
ka u zɛɛ ɛɛ lugɔ
niŋ n koozi kummaa.
6Binanaa aŋhina yoola n kpolle,
ge ra lii u bia ni
u hɛɛhraa ge dɔɔ saliŋ.
7Kɔlaa maa waa de ŋmɛnɛɛ ra na,
duu maa ge wɔɔ ra na.
8Sechɔgaa naazi waa u ni ra jag,
bunyiŋ maa waa de ra daazi.
9Newea ra ki bikpega,
di ki bizenaa zɛɛzi, a lii chaaŋ.
10Ba furgi bɔɔni a bia ni,
di na binanaa la yoola n kpolle.
11Ba pigzi di na bɔra la muuni n faarɛɛ,
di gil wia la n suahwɛ lii chaaŋ.
12Ka lee nunzuma liiyɛi?
Lee wia zɛɛ zumaa duɛi?
13Newea waa guŋ
zɛɛ zumaa dɔɔwɛ.
Ba wàá wer nau nɛnyinee hɛri.
14Vil ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Waa hoo n biini.’
Muuzeŋ ŋɔ, ‘Waa hoo n be.’
15Ba wàá wer yau nunzuma ni saliŋ himmaa
gɛɛ di kpa saliŋhuŋŋu yawuu.
16Ba wàá wer kpa saliŋ himmaa
gɛɛ lɛgzi la yoola
n kpolle di yawuu.
17Hàá wer kpa saliŋ gɛɛ digii di mɛgzuu
gɛɛ saliŋ kuŋkuaraa di chɛruu.
18Nunzuma tɔna kaali
lɛgzi irizi la maa
yoola n kpollee.
19U yoola kpolloo
kaali kunnanaa la kɔkɔɔza
n ɔɔ kpa lii bɔɔnɛɛ.
20Lee nunzuma liiyɛi?
Lee wia zɛɛ zumaa duɛi?
21U suahwɔɔ, kunnyinii maa wàá wer nau,
haali zumbizi maa n du chiŋ
di ra zaah gba.
22Banla n du lalaa bol ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
‘U wia hunehune
tama bɛnnɛ yaa nuu.’
23Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ zum u ŋmɛnɛɛ,
u bɛnnɛ zum u duuribɔr,
24dikuubɛɛwiai, u bɛnnɛ ra na hɛri naa,
di ra na kuna la maa n du u ni.
25Saŋa la uŋ tɛɛ peu u fɔŋŋa la,
di mɛgzi niiri maa la,
26di du gbɔg tɛɛ dooŋ,
di dau ŋmɛnɛɛ tɛɛ
dooŋ pekpeg la,
27denii u binni nunzuma,
di u ɛɛ kunzenne,
di na lugɔ u wessoo, u ɛɛu na.
28Denii u ŋɔ newee be,
‘Kɔraawiizi ɔmaarɛ nunzuma,
wichɔgaa vɛɛi genii
wia zɛɛ zumaa.’ ”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
1Joob haa ra ŋɔ wia, di ŋɔ,
2“A vii ɛɛ lugɔ
n kaa du gunla
miŋ faa duwɛɛ labuu,
saŋa la Kɔraawiizi
n faa ra binni n ni la,
3saŋa la u fintina n faa ra chaaniŋ,
minna vol bɔbiri biini la!
4Hoi, hɔpizaa la biini miŋ faa nyɛɛlɛɛ la,
saŋa la Kɔraawiizi
n faa ɛɛ n bádɔŋ,
di kissi n dia la,
5saŋa la Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
n faa haa du n be,
n biizi bariŋ la,
6n sela faa tɛŋ nail werge,
n faa na nuu werge
bia hɛssi biine la.
7Di n faa haŋ wa la a bol chaalibɔr,
di ga so n sognibɔr,
8biipɔllaa ɔɔ faa nambuu, di tuzi lii kɛrii,
bazɛŋzi ge izi chi.
9A nɛra sitɔɔra ge ɔɔ gil wiŋɔzii,
ka kpa ba nonee fɔɔzi ba nuuzi.
10Nabɔnzenaa ge ɛɛ kirkirkir,
di gil wiŋɔzi.
11Nɛr la maa n ɔɔ faa nuu n wiŋɔzi,
ɔɔ ŋɔ n winanaa wiarɛ.
Banla ge n ɔɔ faa naŋ,
ɔɔ ra chɔlimbuu,
12dikuubɛɛwiai, n faa ɔɔ mɔgli nyaara la
n ɔɔ wii
di ra nyiŋŋi hiinaare
ani lalbiizi la n faa waa
nɛr maa dɔɔwɛ,
ú hiini baa la.
13Nɛra la n faa ra siu la diboore tɛŋ,
n gil luhaana dɔɔ bampirsɔna.
14N laali wideŋlaa alugɔ n laala.
Wibii diire faa ɛɛ
n tagtajaŋ ni n kahuro.
15Minuu faa ɛɛ nyuŋŋa siwee,
di ɛɛ gbɛraa naazi.
16Minuu faa ɛɛ dɔgnya hina mɛɛ,
di ɔɔ faa lɛɛ hɔɔhra wia
ŋɔ ra tɛɛ baa.
17Minuu ɔɔ faa chɔgi biinikpola hina fɔŋŋazi,
di ra lɛɛ banla
baŋ ɔɔ ra sunni.
18N faa fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ n daŋ siu n himmaa dia biini,
ń hɔpizaa du kpil
alugɔ hɛɛhriichaa.
19N faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ daa la lunne n ɔɔ ra na nii,
ŋmɛnii ɔɔ chol
u paŋhoori ni saŋa maa.
20N girme daŋ haŋ ɛɛ ufaliirɛ di du n ni saŋa maa,
n kpegzi ge wàá tuŋ maa.
21Nɛra ɔɔ ra nuu n benii nɛnnɛ, di n waa ŋɔ wia,
ba ɛɛ kirkirkir,
ka ra nuu n baglaa.
22Di n faa haŋ wa ŋɔ wia tuŋ,
ba waa ɔɔ kaa ŋɔ wia.
N wiŋɔzi ɔɔ faa ra zuu
ba dignaa guŋ bɔɔiih.
23Ba ɔɔ faa ra kpaŋimbuu,
alugɔ patta n na kpaŋ dooŋ,
di sɛɛ n wiŋɔzi
alugɔ sazau dooŋ.
24Di ba bɔra faa haŋ wa huah,
n ɔɔ munzuu du ba ni,
n bɔsɔna siwee
ɔɔ faa du baabuu bɔkpega.
25N ɔɔ bagli baabuu ŋmɛnizi,
ka so lugɔ ba koori.
N faa du ba biinii alugɔ koorizeŋ
n du u laallɔɔra biini.
N faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr la,
n faa ra tig
liwiire bampiree.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1Joob haa ŋɔ, “Ka baala la miŋ binɛɛ
ra ɛɛmbuu chɛɛtɛ filaŋkeŋ.
Banla miŋ faa wàá sɛɛ
bá mɛɛwaa jaa n nuuzihina ni,
di ra binni n peeza gba.
2Bɛɛ tɔnaa ba faa dɔɔ tɛnnɛi,
dikuu baŋ faa waa
kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa wiai?
3Ba siwee faa chogli di ziimi,
dikuu nyaari ni lɔzi wia.
Ba faa ra hee lunne la n hillɛ,
pir ni diŋgelli biine, hamuŋa ni.
4Ba faa kpuzi daapussi hɛribɔduma biini,
di ra hee, haali a lunne
n sɛppɛ werge gba!
5Ba dɔŋahina duŋŋi baa ta,
di pogzi ba ni
alugɔ baŋ ɛɛ ŋmɛɛna.
6Ba fir baa, ba ga du gɔŋhilaa
n du bia ni bɔɔni biine.
7Ba du pir biini di ra wii lugɔ kauzi,
di kɔrgi bɔra chaali dɔŋa
du daapussi zɛɛzi.
8Nɛra la n nyaa tɔna,
ba waa sɔna dɔɔwɛ,
ba duŋŋi baabuu lii a hɛri.
9Filaŋkeŋ, ba biibaala yir yiraa di ra ɛɛŋ chɛɛtɛ.
N birgi mɔmɔsia kuŋ ba biini.
10Ba kiiŋ, ba waa kaa ra nyiŋŋi bá dugliŋ,
haali di ɔɔ puuzi nuuhaari
di ra du n siwee.
11Dikuu Kɔraawiizi n jaa gil n gɛrgi,
di kpa tɔɔrɔɔ
di ha n ni filaŋkeŋ wia,
ba baana ra fuuh
n ni werge maa.
12Nɛkpila chaali lii n nodig di waa lɔɔziŋ,
di he sidɛɛzi bá lawiŋ,
di wa fɔɔŋ,
di ra nyiŋŋi bá kpuŋ.
13Ba tɔ n ŋmɛnɛɛ,
bá na bɔr chɔgiŋ,
ka nɛr maa waa ba ni nyɛkkɛ.
14Ba ra yooŋ alugɔ laallɔɔra n purgi koŋlii,
di ga de zuu,
di zaahzi waa chogli n ni.
15Ɔnsii werge nyaŋŋimbuu,
n nɛtti kaali alugɔ peu,
n nyɛɛlaa maa leu alugɔ baama.
16N miibɔɔ ra tuŋ guŋ bɔɔiih filaŋkeŋ,
n na di tɔɔrɔɔ hɔpizi biimaa.
17Hamuŋa ni, n hoga ɔɔ ra wii guŋ ŋmagakaka,
n bɔra wiila
n na dunziŋ waa tuŋ.
18Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋazeŋ la biini,
u lau n laalaa,
di hanzi n tagta du n baŋaa.
19U kpambuu ha kpɛchɛgaa biini,
maa hɛɛhraa ni hɔɔhri bɔwɛɛ.
20N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
n wiiwoo yirii, ka haa sɛɛwɛ.
N izi chi,
ka binnaa bɛnnɛ i binniŋ.
21I ra sunnimbuu sikpegii ni,
i kpa i fɔŋŋaa di ra tɔɔriŋ.
22I toombuu di la chiŋ,
di ra duŋŋiŋ peu biini,
di kpanna haazi
dooŋ pekpeg biini.
23N zummɔ lugɔ siu biinii i ra la n ni,
bɔr la hin lizɛɛ
dau nɛnyinee maa la.
24Wibii maa, nɛr maa wàá sɛɛ lɔɔzi
nɛr la wia n chɔkkɛ,
di u ra wii di ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa
ú tɔɔrɔɔ dii biini gba.
25N faa waa wiiwe dikuu banla
n du tɔɔrɔɔ biini wiaa?
N biini faa waa chɔkkɛ
dikuu nyaara wiaa?
26Ka di n waa tami winanaa ni,
wichɔgaarɛ ɔɔ ba,
di n waa nyiŋŋi bɔchaaŋ,
bɔbirii ɔɔ ba.
27N biinichɔg waa tuŋ,
anna di tɔɔrɔɔrɛ hɔpizi biimaa.
28N na bar ni biinichɔg werge,
wiizi waa n ni
ra nyaazi tama maa.
N chi nɛkpila biini,
di wii ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa.
29N birgi hohobiazi lullii,
di birgi kikiuzi badɔŋ.
30N bɔhɔŋ biri di ra fugzi.
Sɔsɔŋ gil n bɔra wenzi bambambam.
31N lɔ n kem di ra wii lee,
di huuh n tiitorii ge
di ra lɔ wile.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
1Joob kaa ŋɔ, “N ŋɔ nuarɛ lugɔ
màá binni toloori,
di ra kɛlli n nuu chɔɔ.
2Bɛɛ Kɔraawiizi n du chiŋ tɛɛ newea
gɛɛ bɛɛ kapɛttɛ kunnɛ
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ dau neweei?
3Biinikpola hina chɔgaa lɛiyaa,
hɛhchɔg tɛɛ
wichɔgɛɛra lɛiyaa?
4Waa n wiɛɛlaa maa zummɛ lɛi,
di ra kur n naajaglaa maa?
5Di n wia nyaa wibiire,
gɛɛ n hahzi
di ra nyiŋŋi nɛdaraa,
6gil Kɔraawiizi kpa mɛgzaa kuna la
n dɛkkɛ di mɛgzi n tɔgzi,
denii ú zum lugɔ
maa bilchɔg maa dɔɔwɛ.
7Di n naazi leu ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ,
di n siwee gillɔɔ
n bampirii lau wichɔgaa,
gɛɛ n nonee doŋ,
8guŋwaa, gil nɛra di kuna la min duuwe,
di gil bá kpuzi
n kunduulaa maa ta.
9Di n bampirii faa lau nɛbɛl haaŋ,
gɛɛ di faa suah pɛli
n dɔŋhiŋ dominua,
10guŋwaa, gil n haaŋ
nam baal bɛl mia,
di gil baala baŋhina
lawuu chɔɔ.
11Dikuubɛɛwiai, guŋ daŋ faa ɛɛ hiihzi
di ɛɛ wichɔgaa la ban niŋ kpa
diŋ seriya.
12Sɛnsɛŋ daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ niŋ di fuuhŋ,
di chɔgi n kundɔɔlaa
maa dee nyaamm.
13Di n faa di n balaa,
baala ni haana seriya kara,
saŋa la baŋ faa nuumɛɛ
ra duŋ,
14ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛi, di Kɔraawiizi wa ba n benei?
Ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔ, di u wa yiriŋ
lugɔ ń ŋɔ n nua wiai?
15Kɔraawiizi la n taŋ du n maa hia la lɛi ta baa?
Waa lɛi unla himmaa
n ta yaa maa dee
du yaa maawaa hizi biinea?
16N faa waa nyaara hiinaa vɛɛwɛ
gɛɛ di gil luhaana di dɔgnya.
17N faa waa diwee dɔɔwɛ, di dia n bɛŋ,
ka kpolli lalbiizi,
18ka n faa dɛɛzi baabuu
di lii n pɔlaa saŋa maa
alugɔ ba mɛɛ,
di guu luhaana
di lii n lulaa saŋa maa.
19Di n faa na waari n na kpu nɛbɛl
dikuu uŋ nyaa laala wia,
gɛɛ anuula hiŋ
n waa tagta dɔɔwɛ,
20aŋ faa tɛubuu laala la
baŋ kpa n himmaa
peeza huna suauh.
Denii u ɔɔ chɔliŋ u biini maa.
21Di n faa fini lalbiizii,
dikuu miŋ zummɛ lugɔ
n daŋ wer ŋɔ wia lii
seriya diiribɔr wia,
22guŋwaa, gil n vaama lii
n vaampɛrɛzi ni di chogli,
gil á kuugi,
di tɔrgi lii a kpuŋe ni.
23Dikuu minna ɔm Kɔraawiizi wia,
màá sɛɛ ɛɛ a guŋ widizi maa.
24Di n yarda faa du saliŋ ninɛɛ
gɛɛ di n faa ŋɔ
saliŋ himmaa benii,
‘Hinuu n kpaŋri,’
25di n faa di n hinnɛ dikuu n daama werge
ani nyɛɛlaa la
n kuuhni n tɛŋ wia,
26di n faa ra tɔgzi wiizii u chaanaa wia,
gɛɛ baagu, u volaa wessi ni wia,
27guŋ gil n bampirii suahzi lawaa,
n togni di sɛɛa dɔɔra,
28guŋwaa, annii gba daŋ vii ɛɛ wichɔgaa
ban niŋ kpa diŋ seriya,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n wia
faa wàá dɔɔ wibii Kɔraawiizi n du chiŋ be.
29N bɔra ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa sɔɔnɛɛ,
dikuu tɔɔrɔɔ n huuzi n dɔm wia
gɛɛ a pariŋ dikuu
hɛhchɔg n chol u ni wia.
30N faa waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ wiŋɔchɔgaa,
dikuu miŋ suŋŋi wiizi
ú siu wia.
31N diahina maanii zummɛ lugɔ
nɛr la maa n ba n be,
ɔɔ diu kukki nɛnnɛ,
32ka hɔɔhri maa wàá chɔɔ bossee hamuŋa ni, hɔpizi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɔɔ
pilli n dominuarɛ
tɛɛ ŋmɛnivolla saŋa maa.
33Baŋhina ɔɔ ɛɛ aniaa di suah ba wichɔgaa,
ka miŋwaa ŋmɛnɛ maa
haa waa n hora suahwɛ.
34N ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa gunla nɛra n niŋ ŋɔ ɔmmɛ,
n ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa siigɛɛ
gɛɛ di ɔm chaaŋ lii,
dikuu ba chɛɛtɛ wia.
35Amɔ, nɛr maa wàá nuu gunla minna ŋɔa?
N hɛɛhzɔɔ lugɔ
n wiŋɔɔlii maa ɛɛ wibiire.
Gil Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ sɛɛ n be,
gil nɛr la n na pag n ni
sɛbi n wia dau, ń na.
36Wibii maa, n daŋ vii kpa a sɛbaa
di laali n vaampɛrɛ,
gɛɛ di hiu alugɔ koorikahuro.
37N daŋ vii bagli Kɔraawiizi n wiɛɛlaa maa,
di ba u be banni ni.
38Di n faa ŋmɛɛ hɛri la minna paruu,
di foozuu lii u hina himmaa be,
39di n faa di de diweere,
ka gil lɔzi kpu banla n paraa,
40guŋwaa, gil choŋgolli ni kooree lii de,
ka gil huuti ni baali.”
Joob wiŋɔzi tunaa guŋ.

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
Ɛlihu wiŋɔzi
1Awia, baala bahoro naa jaa gil Joob koozaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ u himmaa wia deŋloore u be. 2Denii Ɛlihu baaŋ faa fuuh Joob ni werge, dikuu uŋ waa wibii kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ka kpau ra tɛɛ u hiŋ wia. Ɛlihu faa ɛɛ Buz hinuu Barakɛl n lii Ram domee biini biibaallɛ. 3U baaŋ ge kaa fuuh Joob dammuzi bahoro la ni werge maa, dikuu baŋ waa wette na wiimaa bá ŋɔ chem Joob, ka tɛu chɔgri wia. 4Ɛlihu faa gillɔɔ ba ŋɔ mɔɔ, ka u haa na bɔr di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Joob, dikuu baŋ faa binuu wia. 5Ka uŋ wa nawɛɛ lugɔ a baala bahoro la waa kaa dɔɔ wiimaa bá ŋɔ la, u baaŋ fuuh.
6Awia, Barakɛl biibaal Ɛlihu ŋɔ,
“Bichalaa miŋ,
iabuu nabɔnzi.
Awiarɛ n faa ra ɔm n ŋɔ
gunla miŋ zummɛ tɛɛ ia.
7N faa fɛwɔɔrɛ, ‘Nɛbinaarɛ ra bagli wia,
nɛra la ge n di biŋkpilaa
dɛkkɛ bá ra bagli nunzuma.’
8Ka duma la n du newee ni,
ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ heezaa,
di ra tɛu wia zɛɛ zumaa.
9Nɛbinaa bɛŋ lɛi dɔɔ nunzuma,
nɛzɛŋzi ge bɛŋ lɛi
ra zum wia la n deŋlee zɛɛzi.
10Awia, n na ŋɔ ii benii, ií ra nuu n be.
Ií gil n ŋɔ ii be
wii la miŋ zummɛ.
11N siigɔɔrɛ ka ii ŋɔ,
di nuu wia la iiŋ fɛwɛɛ.
Iiŋ faa ra fɛ nfɛssi
di ra nyiŋŋi wiŋɔbee la,
12n siigɔɔrɛ ka ii ŋɔ wia.
Ka ii bɛl maa waa wette bagli Joob lugɔ u leuwoo,
ii bɛl maa waa wette bagluu
u wiŋɔzi zɛɛzi.
13Ií gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ, ‘Yaa na nunzumaa,
newee lɛi niŋ ŋɔ guŋ,
see Kɔraawiizi.’
14Ka Joob waa u wiŋɔzi kpawɛɛ ga n be,
n gba wàá kpa ii bilaa la
ŋɔ wia tɛu.
15Joob, ba wiŋɔzi tunnɔɔ,
ba waa kaa dɔɔ
wiŋɔɔlii maa ban niŋ ŋɔ.
16Baŋ jaa siigi filaŋkennaa,
ba waa kaa dɔɔ
wiimaa ban niŋ ŋɔ naa,
ń haa ra kpaŋaa?
17N ge gba daŋ ŋɔ n hor.
N gba daŋ ŋɔ gunla
miŋ zummɛ tɛi.
18Wiŋɔzi su n nuarɛ,
màá gil a ka n biini.
19Wiŋɔzi su n biinii,
alugɔ siŋ n du lɔŋgɔŋfalii biini,
ba tɔ u nua,
u ra nyiŋŋi u pozi la.
20Awia, a dɛkkɔɔ miŋ ŋɔa, ka na n hiŋ.
A dɛkkɔɔ miŋ haa n nua
di ŋɔ wia tɛi.
21Màá chi bɛl maa har
gɛɛ di dɔɔ nuusum nɛr maa be.
22Di n faa dɔɔ nuusunnɛ nɛra be nɛnnɛ,
a faa wàá birgi
ka Kɔraawiizi tɛr n digni.”

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
1Ɛlihu kaa ŋɔ, “Awia, Joob,
a nuu n wiŋɔzi filaŋkeŋ.
Keŋŋi digna nuu
wia la maa min niŋ ŋɔ.
2N na nyiŋŋi n ŋɔ wia,
wia du n biinii.
3Biinihuŋŋu wiŋɔzii n na ŋɔ,
di ra ŋɔ wibii.
4Kɔraawiizi Dumaa taŋ,
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
heezaa ra tɛŋ miibɔɔ.
5Sɛɛ tɛŋ, di i daŋ wer,
di ɛɛ sirya chem n ni.
6N nii maa ɛɛ kpannɛ Kɔraawiizi be,
yaa maanii u kpa chuuri ma.
7Awia, gilɛɛ waa ɔmiŋ,
maa ba i tɔɔraa.
8Ka i wiŋɔzi maanii n nuu.
N nuuwɔɔ hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ,
9‘N ɛɛ biinihuŋŋu hinnɛ,
maa wichɔgii maa dɔɔwɛ.
Maa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be,
di nyaa bilchɔg.
10Ka Kɔraawiizi na chɔgri n ni,
di kpaŋ birgi u dɔm.
11U kpa yɔlɔzii di vɔɔzi n naazi,
di ra pessi n wiɛɛlaa maa.’
12Joob, n na ŋɔ i benii
lugɔ i leuwoo
annii biini, dikuubɛɛwiai,
Kɔraawiizi kaali
neweere werge maa.
13Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i nuumi ra du u ni,
lugɔ waa newee maa
wiŋɔzi ra nuuwɛi?
14Haali Kɔraawiizi n ɔɔ ŋɔ wia, di kuari ŋɔ,
ka nɛr maa waa ɔɔ keŋŋi digna
di ra nuu u wiŋɔzi.
15U ɔɔ ra ŋɔ wiarɛ hamuŋa ni,
di ra lii deeza ni wia nai lugɔ deeza biini,
yaa chɔɔribɔra,
saŋa la yaa n na chɔɔ dɔzi.
16Aŋhinabe, u daŋ ŋɔ wia du ba digna,
ɔnsii lau baa,
dikuu u wiŋɔzi hiŋ wia,
17ú bir newee lii wichɔgaa ɛɛi biini,
di lɛɛu jigsaa biini,
18ú lɛɛu lii siu biini,
bá gilɛɛ waa kpuu kalu biini.
19Gɛɛ u kpa wiila tɛr u digni,
di gil u hoga wiiu werge,
20guŋ gil u nua siu,
wàá ka zum diwee suma,
di kii diwee la n wesse werge.
21U bɔra maa tuŋ, di bir pɛɛ,
u hoga bɛŋ ka.
22A ka tama u siu, bá huguu,
ú kaali lalaa bol.
23Ka di Kɔraawiizi mɛlikazi kagboŋa la bɛl
wa chigɔ u har ú ŋɔ wia hinuu,
di ŋɔ wia la n deŋlee tɛu,
24di na u sinyɛna, di ŋɔ,
‘Lɛɛu, ú gilɛɛ waa siu.
N dɔɔ kunla min niŋ kpa
chɛr u miibɔɔrɛ.’
25Denii ú bɔra birgi kuŋfalii
alugɔ bichala bɔra,
di bir du alugɔ saŋa la
uŋ ɛɛ biipɔllii la.
26U ɔɔ ra suŋŋi wiizii,
Kɔraawiizi nuu ra tɛu.
U ɔɔ na Kɔraawiizii,
di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna,
Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ gil u wia deŋli.
27Denii u ŋɔ nɛra be,
‘N faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, di leu,
ka Kɔraawiizi gil tɛŋ.
28U lɛɛmbuu lii siu be,
ń du de di ra di bɔchaaŋ suma.’
29Annii maanii Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ ra ɛɛ,
di ra tɛɛ newee digiidigii,
30ú lɛɛu lii siu be,
guŋ gil ú de dui du sum.
31Joob, keŋŋi digni di nuu n be,
sigli ka n ŋɔ wia.
32Di i dɔɔ wiimaa i ŋɔ, ŋɔ ń nuu,
ŋɔa, dikuu minna nyiŋŋi
i wia chaani wia.
33Ka di guŋ lɛi, siigi ka ra nuu n be,
ń baglii nunzuma.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
translation_text:
1Denii Ɛlihu kaa ŋɔ,
2“Nunzunna, ií ra nuu n wiŋɔzi.
Ii banla n dɔɔ wia zɛɛ zumaa,
ií ra nuu n be.
3Digni ɔɔ ɛɛ wiŋɔbeere na
alugɔ nuuzuŋŋi
n ɔɔ daŋ diwee na la.
4Ií gil ya pessi na wia la n deŋlee,
ií gil ya kpau
helli wia la n wesse.
5Joob ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Maa chɔgri maa dɔɔwɛ,
ka Kɔraawiizi vɛɛ wibii dii tɛŋ.
6Haali miŋ dɔɔ bilii gba,
ka u yirimbuu karkanni.
Haali miŋ waa bilchɔg maa dɔɔwɛ gba,
ka u hobee dumbuu pira la
n waa chaai dɔɔwɛ.’
7Anɛɛ n lugɔ Jooboi,
di kpa Kɔraawiizi gbɛllaa
birgi barai?
8U ni wichɔgɛɛra ra kpau,
u ni biinikpola hina ra vol.
9Dikuubɛɛwiai, Joob ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
‘Newee waa ɔɔ na tɔna maa,
di u ra ɛɛ ania
ú ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kipar gba.’
10Awia, ii banla n na nuu wia zɛɛ,
ií ra nuu n be.
Kɔraawiizi ni wichɔgaa ɛɛi nɛɛwɔɔ,
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
wàá sɛɛ ɛɛ wia la n waa deŋlee.
11U ɔɔ turgi neweere wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ kim,
wia la n dɛguu di lii
u wiɛɛlaa biinii u ɔɔ dawuu.
12Hàá wer fɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ sɛɛ ɛɛ wia leu,
alugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
waa wibii ra di.
13Anɛɛ n lizuu ú dɔɔ fɔŋŋa hɛri ninɛi?
Anɛɛ n ŋɔ
ú ra binni durnya maanɛi?
14Di u faa ra nyiŋŋi,
di lizi u duma ni u heeza,
15newea maa daŋ vii siu,
di bir zuu hɛɛhraa biini.
16Joob, di i ra nuu wia zɛɛrɛ, a nuu keŋ,
a nuu gunla minna ŋɔ.
17Nɛr la n hah wibii dii,
daŋ wer binni nɛra nii?
I daŋ wer tɛɛ
Fɔŋŋa Hiŋ la bilchɔgaa?
18Waa lɛi unla n ɔɔ ŋɔ koorizenaa be,
‘Ií waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ,’
di ŋɔ nabɔnzenaa be,
‘Ii ɛɛ biinikpola hinaa’ laa?
19Waa nabɔnzenaa har ra chi,
waa dɔɔna nɔŋŋɛɛ kaali nyaara,
dikuu ba maa n ɛɛ
u nonee huma wia.
20Ba ɔɔ siwuu kiŋkiraŋ hɛhhɛɛhzi ni,
u ɔɔ zigli nɛraa ba siu,
u ɔɔ kpu nɛzenaare,
di nɛr maa wɔɔ hiinee.
21U siwee du newea vollibɔra maa ninɛɛ,
u ra na ba naajaglaa.
22Bɔbiri iri maa waa hoo,
wichɔgɛɛra suah de.
23Kɔraawiizi waa dɔɔwɛ lugɔ
ú dau saŋa tɛɛ newea
lugɔ ya la u be, ú di yaa seriya.
24Waa ɔɔ pɛɛzi na mɔɔ,
ka lizi nabɔnzenaa
ba nabɔmuu biine,
ka kpa bafalaa du ba bɔra.
25Dikuu uŋ zum ba wiɛɛlaa wia,
u ɔɔ lizi baabuu
di ha hamuŋa ni,
di pinti baa.
26U ɔɔ tɛrgi ba dignaa,
dikuu ba biinikpola wia,
bɔr la nɛr maa
n niŋ wer na baa,
27dikuu baŋ vɛɛ u hiŋaa,
ba baga waa kaa hoo
u ŋmɛnizi bɛl maa ni wia.
28Ba gillɔɔ nyaara wiraa heluu,
guŋ gil u nuu
anuula hina wiraa.
29Ka di u siigɔɔ,
anɛɛ n niŋ wer tɛu bilchɔgɛi?
Di u suah u hiŋ ge,
anɛɛ n niŋ wer nauwɛi?
Ka waabuu ra binni newea
ni hɛssi maa ni,
30ú gil nɛr la n wɔɔ ra jaami gilɛɛ di kora,
di gilɛɛ waa he nɛra sidɛɛzi.
31Aŋhinabe, nɛbɛl daŋ ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be,
‘N di bilchɔgrɛ,
màá ka gbɛllii maa.
32Bagliŋ kunla miŋ wàá wer na,
di n faa ɛɛwɔɔ leu,
màá ka ɛɛ guŋ.’
33A dɛkkɔɔ Kɔraawiizi turgii
i wiɛɛlaa kim gunla hinna nyiŋŋi,
dikuu hiŋ vɛɛ chɔgri sɛɛi wiaa?
Hinuu dɛkkɛ hiŋ fɛ nfɛrɛ na,
di ŋɔ wii la hiŋ zummɛ,
min lɛi.
34Nɛra la n na nuu wia zɛɛ, daŋ sɛɛ,
nunzunna la n na nuu n be,
daŋ ŋɔ n be,
35‘Joob waa zum wii la unna ŋɔ,
u wiŋɔzi waa zɛɛ dɔɔwɛ.’
36Ee, bá vii ɛɛ Joob na, di ga nyaŋŋi,
dikuu unna sɛɛ wia
alugɔ biinikpola hiŋ wia!
37U kpa dignikpegiire di jaa u wichɔgaa ni,
di ra ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi chɛɛtɛ,
di ra lɔ kpaa yaa see,
di ŋɔ wiŋɔjagazi werge,
di ra du u ni.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
13If God All-Powerful refuses
to answer their empty prayers,
14he will surely deny
your impatient request
to face him in court.
15Job, you were wrong to say
God doesn't punish sin.
16Everything you have said
adds up to nonsense.
translation_text:
1Denii Ɛlihu kaa ŋɔ,
2“Joob, i fɛ lugɔ keŋ deŋloorea?
I ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
‘Kɔraawiizi daŋ chaani
n wia siwee tɛŋ.’
3Ka i pɛɛzuubuu, ‘Bɛɛ tɔnaa n na,
ni bɛɛ winaniirɛ n na,
di lii miŋ waa
wichɔgaa ɛɛwɛ biinei?’
4N na nyiŋŋi ń ŋɔ
i ni i dammuzi benii,
5ií binni chiŋ na,
ií binni baamazi tiiih,
di ii na gunla aŋ la chiŋ werge
di guali ii ni.
6Di ii ɛɛ wichɔgaa,
bɛɛ a ɛɛ Kɔraawiizɛi?
Di ii chɔgri kannɔ,
bɛɛ a ɛɛuwɛi?
7Di ii wia deŋloo,
bɛɛ ii ra tɛuwɛi,
gɛɛ bɛɛ u ra lɛɛ
di ra lii ii nonee biinei?
8Ii biinikpola wiɛɛlaa ra buu nɛr la n du lugɔ iabuu,
ii wideŋlaa ra buu newea bɛŋ.
9Di ba ra sunni nɛra, ba ra hɛm,
ba ɔɔ wiiu ra nyiŋŋi nɛr
ú lɛɛ baa lii fɔŋŋa hina be.
10Ka nɛr maa wàá ŋɔ,
‘Lee n Taari Kɔraawiizi duɛi,
unla n ɔɔ gil n na yir yira,
haali miŋ du tɔɔrɔɔ biini,
11di ra bagli yaa wia werge kaali hɛri sela,
di gil yaa dɔɔ nunzuma
kaali zumbizi
n du chiŋ lai?’
12Waa ɔɔ sɛɛ, di newea waa yiruu
di ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa,
dikuu biinikpola hina
kpoŋaa wia.
13Wibii maa, waa ɔɔ ra nuu ba suŋŋipɛɛri,
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
baga waa hoo guŋ ni.
14Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ú jaa ɛɛ nuu,
dikuu iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ
ii wɔɔ ra nai,
lugɔ ii wia chɔɔ ú seere,
a dɛg lugɔ ii ra kpaŋuu wiai?
15Di kaa kpa jaa,
dí waa baaŋfuuih kpawɛɛ
di ra tɛr digni,
waa biinikpola wia
ra na tama maa.
16Awia, wiŋɔpɛɛrii Joob ra ŋɔ,
waa nfɛrɛ ra fɛ,
ka ŋɔ wikpila di ra jaa.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Be Patient a While Longer
1Elihu said:
2Be patient a while longer;
I have something else to say
in God's defense.
3God always does right—
and this knowledge
comes straight from God.
4You can rest assured
that what I say is true.
5Although God is mighty,
he cares about everyone
and makes fair decisions.
6The wicked are cut down,
and those who are wronged
receive justice.
7God watches over good people
and places them in positions
of power and honor forever.
8But when people are prisoners
of suffering and pain,
* 9God points out their sin
and their pride,
10then he warns them
to turn back to him.
11And if they obey,
they will be successful
and happy from then on.
12But if they foolishly refuse,
they will be rewarded
with a violent death.
Godless People Are Too Angry
13Godless people are too angry
to ask God for help
when he punishes them.
14So they die young
in shameful disgrace.
15Hard times and trouble
are God's way
of getting our attention!
16And at this very moment,
God deeply desires
to lead you from trouble
and to spread your table
with your favorite food.
17Now that the judgment
for your sins
has fallen upon you,
18don't let your anger
and the pain you endured
make you sneer at God.
19Your reputation and riches
cannot protect you
from distress,
20nor can you find safety
in the dark world below.
21Be on guard! Don't turn to evil
as a way of escape.
22God's power is unlimited.
