19ni nɛr la n na di daansɛɛkara,
ani nɛr la n kpa lulla nyuuni
di ra lɔ dɔŋa.
Sɛnsɛŋ karfaa wia
20N bie, a hiŋ i mɛɛ nua,
di gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ
i maa baglaa.
21Gil a du i bampirii saŋa maa,
di laalaa lugɔ baŋaakuna.
22Ba baglaa daŋ tɔ i see di i waa la ŋmɛnɛɛ,
di i waa chɔɔ,
a daŋ guui,
di i wa izoo chɔɔzi ni,
a daŋ baglii wia.
23Ba baglaa naa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ fintina, di ra chaanii.
Ba liize biraa
di baglii wia ge,
ɛɛ miibɔɔ ŋmɛnɛɛ.
24A daŋ lizii hahsɛnsɛnni be,
di lizii lii nɛbɛl haaŋ la
n dɔɔ nuusum be.
25Gilɛɛ waa gil u wessi ra darii,
di gilɛɛ waa gil
u siyazi waa lawii,
26dikuubɛɛwiai, sɛnsɛnni daŋ dui nyaari biini,
di i lau baal bɛl
haaŋ nyiŋŋi,
guŋ daŋ wer gil
i nyaa i miibɔɔ.
27I daŋ wer kpa niŋ pɛli i bampirii
ka i laala waa fuuah?
28I daŋ wer vol niŋhɔla ni
ka i naazi waa pooria?
29Guŋ himmaanii di baal lau ú dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ nyiŋŋi,
ba daŋ tɛr u digni.
30Di nɛr ŋmɛɛwɔ dikuu lɔzi n na kpuu wia,
nɛra wàá pag u ni.
31Ka di ba lawuu, u daŋ bir turgi
kunla uŋ ŋmɛɛwɛ la
guŋ buniidaanɛɛ jaa,
haali di a ɛɛwɔ lugɔ
ú yoo u dia kummaa gba.
32Baal la maa n lau hahdumazi di ra chɔɔ, gɛnnɔɔ werge,
unla n na ɛɛ guŋ
ra chɔg u hinnɛ.
33Lɔɔzaa ni hiihzii u hora saŋa maa,
u hiihzi dii
waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.
34A haaŋ jaari zoma baaŋ daŋ chum,
wàá dɔɔ nɛsunaa
di u ŋɔ ú turgi a kim.
35Wàá lɛɛ kinturgaa maa,
kummaa waa hoo
un niŋ su u siwii.

english_text:
The Foolishness of Unfaithfulness
1My son, pay close attention
and don't forget
what I tell you to do.
2Obey me, and you will live!
Let my instructions be
your greatest treasure.
3Keep them at your fingertips
and write them
in your mind.
4Let wisdom be your sister
and make common sense
your closest friend.
5They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
6From the window of my house,
I once happened to see
7some foolish young men.
8It was late in the evening,
sometime after dark.
9One of these young men
turned the corner
and was walking by the house
of an unfaithful wife.
10She was dressed fancy
like a woman of the street
with only one thing in mind.
11She was one of those women
who are loud and restless
and never stay at home,
12who walk street after street,
waiting to trap a man.
13She grabbed him and kissed him,
and with no sense of shame,
she said:
14“I had to offer a sacrifice,
and there is enough meat
left over for a feast.
15So I came looking for you,
and here you are!
16The sheets on my bed
are bright-colored cloth
from Egypt.
17And I have covered it
with perfume made of myrrh,
aloes, and cinnamon.
18“Let's go there
and make love all night.
19My husband is traveling,
and he's far away.
20He took a lot of money along,
and he won't be back home
before the middle
of the month.”
21And so, she tricked him
with all of her sweet talk
and her flattery.
22At once he followed her
like an ox on the way
to be slaughtered,
or like a fool on the way
to be punished
23and killed with arrows.
He was no more than a bird
rushing into a trap,
without knowing
it would cost him his life.
24My son, pay close attention
to what I have said.
25Don't even think about
that kind of woman
or let yourself be misled
by someone like her.
26Such a woman has caused
the downfall and destruction
of a lot of men.
27Her house is a one-way street
leading straight down
to the world of the dead.
translation_text:
Hahsɛnsɛnni karfaa wia
1N bie, a hiŋ n wiŋɔɔlaa,
di gil a du
i nfɛrɛ biini saŋa maa.
2A hiŋaa, di dɔɔ miibɔɔ!
A du n baglaazi naa tau
gunla hinna du
i siwii tau la,
3lawaa kpogli nɛnnɛ,
di gil a du i bampirii.
4Nɔŋŋi nunzuma alugɔ i niuhambie,
di gil wia zɛɛ nuui
ɛɛ i badɔŋ,
5a daŋ lɛɛi lii hahsɛnsɛnni
ni hahjaga nuusum be.
6A hɔl bɛl miŋ ga n dia tokoro
di ra binni baŋgia,
7n na wii bɛl lii
biipɔllaa la nfɛssi
n waa kaŋ biini,
di na biipɔllii la
n bugmee werge ba biini,
8di u ra vol ŋmɛnɛɛ la n dugli hahsɛnsɛnni bɛl dia,
di deŋli de ra la,
9di wiizi hanna zuu,
bɔr ra lauri siwee.
10Denii haaŋ bɛl chem u ni,
di bɔg lugɔ sɛnsɛnni
di ra murguu.
11U faa dɔɔ bampiriire di nyaa hiihzi,
u faa waa dia ra so.
12Ba ɔɔ faa naubuu ŋmɛnizi, yauzi
ani fɔɔliizi maa biine,
saŋa maa.
13A haaŋ faamuu di jaamuu,
di binnuu tiiih, ka ŋɔ,
14“N lizi n dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzii tuŋ zinaa,
a ola du dia.
15Hinuu n faa lii ń nyiŋŋi la,
di jaa nai.
16N kpa pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii la baŋ liiwe nɛnnɛɛ
lii Ijip hɛri,
di yaa tɔ
n kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni.
17N kpa mɛr, alozi
ani sinamɔnnɛ di mizi
n kunchɔɔrikuŋ.
18Ba ya nyiŋŋi dɔŋa guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi.
Gil ya di dɔŋa suma,
19dikuubɛɛwiai, n jaari waa hoo bol,
u vol ŋmɛnijannɛ.
20U kpa kebee wergee kaali,
wàá du bol lugɔ yauzi anɛɛ.”
21Awia, u murguu di kpu u nfɛrɛ,
di kpa wiŋɔsuma
daruu lau.
22U hiŋuu kakpaŋ
alugɔ baŋ lau nabal
di ra la bá ga kpu
gɛɛ chɛɛh n zaahwɛ chiiri sidɛɛ ni,
23denii hobii wa yag u bampirii,
alugɔ zumbee n yali siwee zuu ŋmɛmbee ni,
waa zummɛ lugɔ
guŋ daŋ tuŋ u miibɔɔ.
24Awia, n biizi, ií keŋŋi di ra nuu n be,
di ra du n wiŋɔɔlaa tau.
25Ií gilɛɛ wa gil ii bampiree ra lau a haaŋ naa dee,
di gilɛɛ wa leu
di ra hiŋzi u ŋmɛnizi.
26Waabuu baala kpila maa chɔgri,
baala kpilakpila
maanii u kpu.
27U dia ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ŋmam ŋmɛnɛɛ.
U diichɔɔlii ɛɛ lugɔ
siu duuribɔr.

english_text:
In Praise of Wisdom
1 With great understanding,
Wisdom is calling out
2as she stands at the crossroads
and on every hill.
3She stands by the city gate
where everyone enters the city,
and she shouts:
4“I am calling out
to each one of you!
5Good sense and sound judgment
can be yours.
6Listen, because what I say
is worthwhile and right.
7I always speak the truth
and refuse to tell a lie.
8Every word I speak is honest,
not one is misleading
or deceptive.
9“If you have understanding,
you will see that my words
are just what you need.
10Let instruction and knowledge
mean more to you than silver
or the finest gold.
11 Wisdom is worth much more
than precious jewels
or anything else you desire.”
Wisdom Speaks
12I am Wisdom—Common Sense
is my closest friend;
I possess knowledge
and sound judgment.
13If you respect the Lord,
you will hate evil.
I hate pride and conceit
and deceitful lies.
14I am strong, and I offer
sensible advice
and sound judgment.
15By my power kings govern,
and rulers make laws
that are fair.
16Every honest leader rules
with help from me.
17I love everyone who loves me,
and I will be found by all
who honestly search.
18I can make you rich and famous,
important and successful.
19What you receive from me
is more valuable
than even the finest gold
or the purest silver.
20I always do what is right,
21and I give great riches
to everyone who loves me.
22 From the beginning,
I was with the Lord.
I was there before he began
23to create the earth.
At the very first,
the Lord gave life to me.
24When I was born,
there were no oceans
or springs of water.
25My birth was before
mountains were formed
or hills were put in place.
26It happened long before God
had made the earth
or any of its fields
or even the dust.
27 I was there when the Lord
put the heavens in place
and stretched the sky
over the surface of the sea.
28I was with him when he placed
the clouds in the sky
and created the springs
that fill the ocean.
29I was there when he set
boundaries for the sea
to make it obey him,
and when he laid foundations
to support the earth.
30I was right beside the Lord,
helping him plan and build.
I made him happy each day,
and I was happy at his side.
31I was pleased with his world
and pleased with its people.
32 Pay attention, my children!
Follow my advice,
and you will be happy.
33Listen carefully
to my instructions,
and you will be wise.
34Come to my home each day
and listen to me.
You will find happiness.
35By finding me, you find life,
and the Lord will be pleased
with you.
36But if you don't find me,
you hurt only yourself,
and if you hate me,
you are in love with death.
translation_text:
Nunzuma chɔlaa wia
1Ií ra nuu, nunzuma ra yiruu,
wia zɛɛ zumaa ge ra gbooli!
2U chigɔ giŋgimee nyuuni
ni ŋmɛnichechemazii.
3U chigɔ bolzeŋ dominuuzi kɛraarɛ
di ra gbooli, di ra yirgi,
4di ra ŋɔ, “Nɛr maanii n na yir!
N gbooloore
di ra yir nɛr maa.
5Banla n waa wia zummɛ, ií helli nunzuma nɛnnɛ.
Gɛnaa, ií helli
wia zɛɛ zumaa.
6Ií ra nuu n be! Wipazii n ŋɔ ń ŋɔ tɛɛ ia.
Wia la maa
min niŋ ŋɔ deŋloore,
7wibiire n na ŋɔ,
n hah karaa.
8N baglaa maa dɔɔ wibiire di du wer.
Bɛl maa waa kara
ni daraa dɔɔwɛ.
9N wiŋɔɔlaa chaanɔɔrɛ tɛɛ nɛr la maa n na nuu wia zɛɛ,
di chaani tɛɛ banla ge maa
n dɔɔ nunzuma.
10Ií lizi n baglaa ka gil saliŋhuŋŋa,
di kpa nunzuma
ka gil salinnanii,
11dikuubɛɛwiai, nunzumaa dɔɔ tɔna
kaali rubizi,
hàá wer kpa kunla maa
hinna nyiŋŋi di mɛgzuu.
12Minuu nunzuma, di zum wia biini,
di dɔɔ nfɛrɛ,
di ra ŋɔ wia ni wibii.
13Kɔraawiizi ɔmaarɛ wichɔgaa haih.
N hah barabara,
dignikpega wia,
wichɔgaa ɛɛi
ani kara kannaarɛ.
14Liize biraa ni seriya dinanaa ɛɛ n horaa,
di dɔɔ wia
zɛɛ zumaa ni fɔŋŋa.
15Minuu ra hiini koora ba ra di kora,
sitɔɔra ge ra du
gbɔgni la wia
n dɔɔ wibii.
16Minuu ra hiini sitɔɔra ba ra tɔ nɛra see,
nabɔnzenaa ge ra di seriya
ni wibii hɛri naa.
17N nɔŋŋi banla maa n nɔŋŋimbuu,
banla n na nyiŋŋi n bɔr
daŋ naŋ wibii maa.
18N benii daama, girme, nyɛɛlaa
ani winanaa ɛɛi maa
fɔŋŋa du, n na bɔnni.
19N kunsunzaa bɔ salinnanii
ni saliŋhuŋŋa la
n wesse nɛnnɛ!
20N wiɛɛlaa maa deŋloore,
n na hiŋ wibii dii ŋmɛnizi.
21N ɔɔ ra tɛɛ banla n nɔŋŋimbuu daama,
di ɔɔ gil ba diini ra suugi
ni kundɔɔlaa.
22Minuu Kɔraawiizi feli ta mɔɔ,
ka haa ta kummaa.
23Minuu Kɔraawiizi feli ma lugli la,
mɔɔ ka durnya haa faari.
24Kɔraawiizi lulimbuu mɔɔ ka ta muuzenaa,
mɔɔ ka bulli faari niiri bulaa.
25Mɔɔ ka u chiŋŋi bizenaa
ni giŋgimee a chignibɔra,
di n du de,
26mɔɔ ka u ta hɛri ni kooni
gɛɛ durnya hɛɛhraa iri maa.
27N faa du denii ka u ta chiŋ,
di tii muuzeŋ ni chiŋ maga.
28N faa du denii ka u chiŋŋi baamazi chiŋ,
di ta niiri,
a pal gaa zuu muuni.
29N faa du denii ka u tii muuni magbɔɔni,
di ŋɔ á gilɛɛ waa yaa
di ra gillaa.
Kɔraawiizi n waa tii hɛri zɛɛ,
30minuu faa nɛr la
n zum nonee huma
di chi u kɛra,
minuu faa u sideŋŋa kuŋ
saŋa maa,
n bɔra ɔɔ faa sɔɔnuu
u be saŋa maa.
31N bɔra ge faa sɔɔni werge dikuu kuna la uŋ tawɛɛ la
ani newea dee maa wia!
32Awia, n biizi, ií ra nuu n be,
banla n na hiŋ
n ŋmɛnizi, nuu sumaa.
33Ií ra nuu n baglaa di dɔɔ nunzuma.
Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛu.
34Banla n na nuu n be,
di ɔɔ so n dominuuzi
di ra du n tau hɔpizi biimaa,
nuu sumaa.
35Unla maa naŋ, u na miibɔɔrɛ,
ú wia par Kɔraawiizi.
36Ka banla n nyiŋŋiŋ huhzi la, du bahinaarɛ pira,
banla maa n hahŋ,
nɔŋŋi siurɛ.”

english_text:
Wisdom Gives a Feast
1Wisdom has built her house
with its seven columns.
2She has prepared the meat
and set out the wine.
Her feast is ready.
3She has sent her servant women
to announce her invitation
from the highest hills:
4“Everyone who is ignorant
or foolish is invited!
5All of you are welcome
to my meat and wine.
6If you want to live,
give up your foolishness
and let understanding
guide your steps.”
True Wisdom
7Correct a worthless bragger,
and all you will get
are insults and injuries.
8Any bragger you correct
will only hate you.
But if you correct someone
who has common sense,
you will be loved.
9If you have good sense,
instruction will help you
to have even better sense.
And if you live right,
education will help you
to know even more.
10 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of wisdom.
To have understanding,
you must know the Holy God.
11I am Wisdom. If you follow me,
you will live a long time.
12Good sense is good for you,
but if you brag,
you hurt yourself.
A Foolish Invitation
13Stupidity is reckless,
senseless, and foolish.
14She sits in front of her house
and on the highest hills
in the town.
15She shouts to everyone
who passes by,
16“If you are stupid,
come on inside!”
And to every fool she says,
17“Stolen water tastes best,
and the food you eat in secret
tastes best of all.”
18None who listen to Stupidity
understand that her guests
are as good as dead.
translation_text:
Nunzuma ni gɛnaa wia
1Nunzuma ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ haaŋ n ma u dia,
di chigzuu
silminti ligee aniidaanɛɛ.
2U kpu selle daali diuzenaa,
di kpa siŋ jaa,
di chiŋŋi diiribɔr.
3U hum suŋgure la n ɛɛ u balaarɛ,
bá ga chi bɔr la
n la chiŋ zelelee,
di ra yirgi, di ra ŋɔ,
4“Banla maa n ɛɛ bambugee, ií wa zuu n be!”
Di ŋɔ gɛnaa ge be,
5“Ií wa di n diwee,
di nyɔɔ siŋ la min daalɛɛ.
6Ií gil ii bichal wia la, ka dɔɔ miibɔɔ,
di ra hiŋ
wia zɛɛ zumaa ŋmɛnizi.”
7Nɛr la maa n na deŋli chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri, ɔɔ ra na chagzaarɛ,
nɛr la maa ge n ɔɔ nyɛgi
biinikpola hiŋ ni,
ɔɔ na piraa.
8Gilɛɛ waa hau chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri ni, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ haih.
Hau nunzunni ni,
u daŋ nɔŋŋii.
9Bagli nunzunni wia, ú nunzuma jaa.
Bagli unla ge wia n deŋlee,
ú helli jaa.
10Nunzuma dɔɔi faaraarɛ Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa.
Dɔɔrinaniinanii zumaa
ge ɛɛ wia zɛɛ zumaa.
11Nunzuma daŋ jaai biŋkpila,
í de dui saŋa.
12Di i dɔɔ nunzuma, i daŋ di tɔna,
di i ra ɛɛu chɛɛtɛ ge,
i daŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ.
13Gɛnaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ haaŋ la n kɔɔwɛ di ra bar,
waa ɔɔ zum lugɔ
waa wiimaa zummɛ.
14U ɔɔ so u dominuarɛ
gɛɛ kara la n chigɛ bolzeŋ
bɔr la n la chiŋ zelele ninɛɛ,
15di ra yirgi banla n ga de di ra kaali,
ba huma wia ɛɛ siaahmu
ba be la.
16“Ií ba n dia, ii banla n ɛɛ bambugee!”
Di ŋɔ gɛnaa ge be,
17“Niiŋmɛɛlii summɔɔ,
diuŋmɛɛlaa ge
gba du sum!”
18Ka u hɔɔhra waa zummɛ lugɔ
u hɔɔhribinaa
du lalaa bolle filaŋkeŋ.

english_text:
Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some proverbs
of Solomon:
Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
make them sad.
2What you gain by doing evil
won't help you at all.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
3If you obey the Lord,
you won't go hungry;
if you are wicked,
God won't let you have
what you want.
4Laziness leads to poverty;
hard work makes you rich.
5At harvest season
it's smart to work hard,
but stupid to sleep.
6Everyone praises good people,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
7Good people are remembered
long after they are gone,
but the wicked
are soon forgotten.
8If you have good sense,
you will listen and obey;
if all you do is talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
9You will be safe,
if you always do right,
but you will get caught,
if you are dishonest.
10Deceit causes trouble,
and foolish talk
will bring you to ruin.
11The words of good people
are a source of life,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
12 Hatred stirs up trouble;
love overlooks the wrongs
that others do.
13If you have good sense,
it will show when you speak.
But if you are stupid,
you will be beaten
with a stick.
14If you have good sense,
you will learn all you can,
but foolish talk
will soon destroy you.
15Great wealth can be a fortress,
but poverty
is no protection at all.
16If you live right,
the reward is a good life;
if you are evil,
all you have is sin.
17Accept correction,
and you will find life;
reject correction,
and you will miss the road.
18You can hide your hatred
by telling lies,
but you are a fool
to spread lies.
19You will say the wrong thing
if you talk too much—
so be sensible and watch
what you say.
20The words of a good person
are like pure silver,
but the thoughts
of an evil person
are almost worthless.
21Many are helped
by useful instruction,
but fools are killed
by their own stupidity.
22When the Lord blesses you
with riches,
you have nothing to regret.
23Fools enjoy doing wrong,
but anyone with good sense
enjoys acting wisely.
24What evil people dread most
will happen to them,
but good people will get
what they want most.
25Those crooks will disappear
when a storm strikes,
but God will keep safe
all who obey him.
26Having a lazy person on the job
is like a mouth full of vinegar
or smoke in your eyes.
27If you respect the Lord,
you will live longer;
if you keep doing wrong,
your life will be cut short.
28If you obey the Lord,
you will be happy,
but there is no future
for the wicked.
29The Lord protects everyone
who lives right,
but he destroys anyone
who does wrong.
30Good people will stand firm,
but the wicked will disappear
from the land.
31Honest people speak sensibly,
but deceitful liars
will be silenced.
32If you obey the Lord,
you will always know
the right thing to say.
But no one will trust you
if you tell lies.
translation_text:
Koori Solomɔn sɛɛliizi
1Koori Solomɔn sɛɛliizii keŋ,
bie la n zum wia ɔɔ giluu u mɛɛ bɔra sɔɔni,
ka bie la n gɛnnɛ waa,
ɔɔ giluu u maa biini chɔgi.
2Daama la hiŋ ga ŋmɛnichuma na, waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ,
ka wideŋlaa daŋ wer
lɛɛ i miibɔɔ.
3Kɔraawiizi waa ɔɔ gil lɔzi ra kpu nɛr la wia n deŋlee,
ka waa ɔɔ gil
biinikpola hina na ba kipar.
4Yaara hina daŋ birgi nyaara,
ka banla n aah siwii
di ra hum waa,
daŋ birgi daama hina.
5Nɛr la n dɔɔ nunzuma ɔɔ aah siwiire
di ra chaali kuna,
kuna kumaa saŋa,
ka unla n ɔɔ ra chɔɔ dɔɔ kuna kumaa saŋa waa,
ɔɔ di hiihzii.
6Banla wia n deŋlee ɔɔ na kissaare,
ka wichɔgɛɛra waa wiŋɔɔlaa,
ɔɔ ra suah ba machɔgaarɛ.
7Ba wàá wer suuh nɛnanii wia,
ka ba daŋ suuh
nɛchɔgii waa sɔŋ manaŋ.
8Nunzunni ɔɔ sɛɛ baglaarɛ,
ka unla n na ŋɔ
gɛnni wia waa,
wia daŋ chɔgi.
9Nɛr la wia n dɔɔ wibii ɔɔ ra voluu ni bɔsɔna,
ka unla wia
n waa wibii dɔɔwɛ waa,
ba daŋ lawuu.
10Nɛr la n ɔɔ fɛri wibii dau, ra ba tɔɔrɔɔ ninɛɛ,
ka unla n ɔɔ lɔ bampirii
di di wibii, ra nyiŋŋi bɔsɔnaa.
11Nɛr la wia n deŋlee wiŋɔɔlaa ra tɛɛ miibɔɔrɛ,
ka wichɔgɛɛra waa wiŋɔɔlaa,
ɔɔ ra suah
ba nfɛrchɔgaarɛ.
12Hahzii ra izi kalu,
ka nɔŋŋaa ra ba giltɛɛi ni.
13Nunzunna ɔɔ ra ŋɔ nunzuma wiŋɔzii,
ka gɛnaa waa,
dɛg dignitɛraarɛ.
14Nunzunna ɔɔ dɔɔ nfɛrɛɛ di jaa,
ka gɛnaa wiŋɔzi
ra ba tɔɔrɔɔ ni.
15Daama hina daama ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bolzeŋkpeg ba be,
nyaari ge ra chɔgi nyaara.
16Nɛra la wia n deŋlee kinturgaare miibɔɔ,
ka biinikpola hina waa
kinturgaare tɔɔrɔɔ.
17Nɛra la n na nuu baglaa du miibɔɔ ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ,
ka banla n na vɛɛu
daŋ dar ba dɔŋahina,
bá leu.
18Nɛr la maa n na suahzi hahzi, ɛɛ karkannii,
unla ge n na
zɔɔzi nɛra ɛɛ gɛnii.
19Wiŋɔbala werge gillɔɔ nɛr ra ŋɔ wichɔgaa,
ka unla n na lau u nua
ɛɛ nunzunnii.
20Nɛr la wia n deŋlee wiŋɔzi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ saliŋhuŋŋu himmaa,
ka biinikpola hiŋ wifɛɛlaa
waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ.
21Nɛr la wia n deŋlee wiŋɔzi ra hiini nɛkpilaa,
ka gɛnaa daŋ siu.
22Kɔraawiizi kissaa ra ba daama ninɛɛ,
waa ɔɔ gil
biinichɔg jaa a ni.
23Wichɔgaa ɛɛi summɔɔ gɛnii be,
ka nunzumaa ra par
nɛr la n zum wia.
24Wia la biinikpola hina n na ɔm daŋ huuzi baa,
ka banla waa wia n deŋlee
daŋ na bá winyiŋŋaa.
25Di dooŋ pekpeg wa ballɔ, ɔɔ paagi biinikpola hinaa kaali,
ka banla wia n deŋlee
chi chigigi di hanna la.
26Gilɛɛ waa kpa yaarahiŋ huma,
di i ɛɛ guŋ,
u daŋ tɛi tɔɔrɔɔ lugɔ
sinnyɛg n ɔɔ gil
nyina ra nyiiri la
gɛɛ nyɔɔzi n ɔɔ zuu siwee la.
27Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa ɔɔ ra tɛɛ miibɔɔjannɛ,
ka biinikpola hiŋ waa,
saŋa waa ɔɔ hel.
28Banla wia n deŋlee tamii ɔɔ lii bɔsɔnaa,
ka biinikpola hina waa
tamii ɔɔ ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.
29Kɔraawiizi ra guu nɛra la wia n deŋleere,
ka ra chɔgi wichɔgɛɛra.
30Banla wia n deŋlee daŋ so ni bɔsɔna,
ka biinikpola hina
wàá du a hɛri birgi.
31Nɛr la wia n deŋlee wiŋɔzi ra ba nunzuma ninɛɛ,
ka karkanni wia daŋ tuŋ.
32Banla wia n deŋlee zum wiŋɔɔlaa la n dɛkkɛɛ,
ka biinikpola hina waa,
wiŋɔɔlaa ɛɛ karaa.

english_text:
Watch What You Say and Do
1The Lord hates anyone
who cheats,
but he likes everyone
who is honest.
2Too much pride
can put you to shame.
It's wiser to be humble.
3If you do the right thing,
honesty will be your guide.
But if you are crooked,
you will be trapped
by your own dishonesty.
4When God is angry,
money won't help you.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
5If you are truly good,
you will do right;
if you are wicked,
you will be destroyed
by your own sin.
6Honesty can keep you safe,
but if you can't be trusted,
you trap yourself.
7When the wicked die,
their hopes die with them.
8Trouble goes right past
the Lord's people
and strikes the wicked.
9Dishonest people use gossip
to destroy their neighbors;
good people are protected
by their own good sense.
10When honest people prosper
and the wicked disappear,
the whole city celebrates.
11Good people bring prosperity
to their city,
but deceitful liars
can destroy a city.
12It's stupid to say bad things
about your neighbors.
If you are sensible,
you will keep quiet.
13A gossip tells everything,
but a true friend
will keep a secret.
14 A city without wise leaders
will end up in ruin;
a city with many wise leaders
will be kept safe.
15It's a dangerous thing
to guarantee payment
for someone's debts.
Don't do it!
16A gracious woman
will be respected,
but a ruthless man
will only get rich.
17Kindness is rewarded—
but if you are cruel,
you hurt yourself.
18Meanness gets you nowhere,
but goodness is rewarded.
19Always do the right thing,
and you will live;
keep on doing wrong,
and you will die.
20The Lord hates sneaky people,
but he likes everyone
who lives right.
21You can be sure of this:
All crooks will be punished,
but God's people won't.
22A beautiful woman
who acts foolishly
is like a gold ring
on the snout of a pig.
23Good people want what is best,
but troublemakers
hope to stir up trouble.
24Sometimes you can become rich
by being generous
or poor by being greedy.
25Generosity will be rewarded:
Give a cup of water,
and you will receive
a cup of water in return.
26Charge too much for grain,
and you will be cursed;
sell it at a fair price,
and you will be praised.
27Try hard to do right,
and you will win friends;
go looking for trouble,
and you will find it.
28Trust in your wealth,
and you will be a failure,
but God's people will prosper
like healthy plants.
29Fools who cause trouble
in the family
won't inherit a thing.
They will end up as slaves
of someone with good sense.
30Live right, and you will eat
from the life-giving tree.
And if you act wisely,
others will follow.
31 If good people are rewarded
here on this earth,
all who are cruel and mean
will surely be punished.
translation_text:
1Kɔraawiizi hah nɛra la n na mɛgzi kuna di ra finuu,
ka a mɛgzaa nɛnnɛ
ra sɔɔni u bɔraa.
2Jigsi ra ba hiihzi ninɛɛ,
ka sisɔna ra tɛɛ nunzuma.
3Nɛnanaa wibii ra guu baabuu,
ka wibii nyaara ge
wibii nyaai ra chɔg baa.
4Daama wàá wer hiinii Kɔraawiizi seriya dii hɔl,
ka wideŋlaa daŋ
wer lɛɛi lii siu be.
5Wibii dɔɔi ɔɔ giluu de dui pɛssi tɛɛ nɛnanii,
ka biinikpola hina himmaanii
ɔɔ taa bahinaa ta.
6Nɛra la wia n deŋlee, ba wibii ɔɔ lɛɛ baabuu,
ka wibii nyaara waa,
wichɔgaa nyiŋŋaa
ɔɔ lau baabuu.
7Di biinikpola hina haŋ siuzi, ba tamii maa ɔɔ tunuu,
dikuu baŋ dɛlli
ba himmaa fɔŋŋazi ni wia.
8Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ lɛɛ banla wia n deŋleere lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini,
ka gil a huuzi
biinikpola hina waa.
9Biinikpola hiŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ wiarɛ chɔgi u dɔŋhiŋ,
ka nɛr la wia n deŋlee
nunzuma ɔɔ lɛɛ nɛttɛ.
10Di nɛr la wia n deŋlee wa nyɛɛlɔɔ, bɔsɔna ɔɔ du a bolzenne,
di biinikpola hiŋ wa siuwɔ,
bɔsɔna chaasaa
ge ɔɔ su denii.
11Nɛra la wia n deŋlee kissaa ɔɔ giluu bolzeŋ dɔɔ sɔŋ,
ka biinikpola hina wiŋɔzi
ɔɔ chɔguubuu.
12Nɛr la maa n na gbɛlli u dɔŋhiŋ nyaa nfɛrɛɛ,
ka nɛr la
n na nuu wia zɛɛ
ɔɔ siiguu.
13Nɛr la n na zɔɔzi nɛra ra pilli wollii,
ka unla wia n dɔɔ wibii
ra tɔ wollii.
14Di nunzunni waa haŋ du de, hɛri ɔɔ chɔguu,
ka di bagla kpila wa du de,
bampirsɔna ɔɔ du denii.
15Di i chigɔ tɛɛ hɔɔhri ka ú di kim, i daŋ wa di tɔɔrɔɔ,
hiŋ vɛɛwɛɛ bɔ.
16Hahpaa ba ra tɔgzi,
ka baala la n dɔɔ sikpegii
ɔɔ na daama bɛnnɛ.
17Baal la n dɔɔ bunya ra hiini u hinnɛ,
ka nɛchuma
ra tɔɔri u hinnɛ.
18Wichɔgɛɛra daama waa ɔɔ lii tɔna tɛɛ baa,
ka nɛnanaa kinturgaa wàá tuŋ.
19Nɛr la maa n aah siwii,
ú ɛɛ winanaa
daŋ na miibɔɔ,
ka unla waa n aah siwii
di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa,
daŋ siu.
20Kɔraawiizi hah biinikpola hinaa,
ka banla n waa
wiimaa dɔɔwɛ
wia paruubuu.
21Wibii maa, zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr wichɔgɛɛra digna,
ka banla wia n deŋlee
daŋ na bahinaa.
22Di haaŋ wesso ka waa mananaa dɔɔwɛ,
a ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
saliŋ nonibisig
n du pereku miizi.
23Nɛnanaa winyiŋŋaa tuna ɔɔ ɛɛ winanaarɛ,
ka di
biinikpola hina waa
wa na ba winyiŋŋaa,
nɛra baana ɔɔ ra fuuuh.
24I daŋ wer dɔɔ bunya ka ɛɛ dɔɔŋ werge,
ka nɛbɛl ge
nonii du kpeg,
ka u nyaa.
25Bunya hiŋ daŋ nyɛɛli,
unla ge n na hiini nɛra
daŋ na hiinaa.
26Nɛra ɔɔ ra see unla n na dau kuna
di ra kpaŋ
yoolkpol saŋaa nua,
ka ra kissi unla n ɔɔ yoo
di ra tɛɛ baa,
bá anuula saŋa.
27Di i nyiŋŋi nɛnnɛ, i daŋ na nɛnnɛ,
ka di i nyiŋŋi chumaa,
i daŋ na chumaa.
28Banla maa n yardi ba daama daŋ chogli
alugɔ hɛhchaaŋ
daazi n wattɛ.
Ka banla maa wia n deŋlee,
daŋ nyɛɛli alugɔ
yuuliŋ daazi n lɔɔwɛ.
29Nɛr la n na tɔɔri u diahina, peu bɛnnɛ ú kapɛttɛ.
Gɛnii ge daŋ ɛɛ
nunzunni balii.
30Nɛr la wia n deŋlee wiɛɛlaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ daa n na nɔŋ nɔna la n na tɛɛ miibɔɔ,
unla ge n na lɛɛ nɛra,
ɛɛ nunzunnii.
31Di nɛra la wia n deŋlee daŋ na ba kinturgaa hɛri naa biini,
bɛɛ n niŋ baani banla
n na gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi,
di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa
wàá na ba kinturgaai?

english_text:
You Can't Hide behind Evil
1 To accept correction is wise,
to reject it is stupid.
2The Lord likes everyone
who lives right,
but he punishes everyone
who makes evil plans.
3Sin cannot offer security!
But if you live right,
you will be as secure
as a tree with deep roots.
4A helpful wife is a jewel
for her husband,
but a shameless wife
will make his bones rot.
5Good people have kind thoughts,
but you should never trust
the advice of someone evil.
6Bad advice is a deadly trap,
but good advice
is like a shield.
7Once the wicked are defeated,
they are gone forever,
but no one who obeys God
will ever be thrown down.
8Good sense is worthy of praise,
but stupidity is a curse.
9It's better to be ordinary
and have only one servant
than to think you are somebody
and starve to death.
10Good people are kind
to their animals,
but a mean person is cruel.
11Hard working farmers have more
than enough food;
daydreamers are nothing more
than stupid fools.
12An evil person tries to hide
behind evil;
good people are like trees
with deep roots.
13We trap ourselves
by telling lies,
but we stay out of trouble
by living right.
14We are rewarded or punished
for what we say and do.
15Fools think they know
what is best,
but a sensible person
listens to advice.
16Losing your temper is foolish;
ignoring an insult is smart.
17An honest person
tells the truth in court,
but a dishonest person
tells nothing but lies.
18Sharp words cut like a sword,
but words of wisdom heal.
19Truth will last forever;
lies are soon found out.
20An evil mind is deceitful,
but gentle thoughts
bring happiness.
21Good people never have trouble,
but troublemakers
have more than enough.
22The Lord hates every liar,
but he is the friend of all
who can be trusted.
23Be sensible and don't tell
everything you know—
only fools spread
foolishness everywhere.
24Work hard, and you
will be a leader;
be lazy, and you
will end up a slave.
25Worry is a heavy burden,
but a kind word
always brings cheer.
26You are better off to do right,
than to lose your way
by doing wrong.
27Anyone too lazy to cook
will starve,
but a hard worker
is a valuable treasure.
28Living right is a pathway
that leads to life
and away from death.
translation_text:
1Nɛr la maa n sɛɛ baglaa, nɔŋŋi nunzumaa
ka unla ge n hah baglaa
ɛɛ gɛniirɛ.
2Nɛnanii wia ɔɔ par Kɔraawiizii,
ka nɛr la
n dɔɔ nfɛrchɔgaa waa,
ɔɔ jugmuubuu.
3Biinikpola hiŋ wàá wer chi,
ka nɛr la wia
n deŋlee waa,
daŋ chi chigigi.
4Hahpa ɔɔ giluu ba ra tɔgzi u jaari,
ka hahjaga ge ɔɔ ra du
u jaarii hiihzi
alugɔ nɛr n na
wii wiilnɔɔraa.
5Nɛra la wia n deŋlee jinazi ɔɔ dɔɔ wibiire,
ka biinikpola hina
baglaa dɔɔ daraa.
6Biinikpola hina wiŋɔzi ra kpuu,
ka nɛra la wia n deŋlee
wiŋɔzi ra lɛɛ nɛra.
7Biinikpola hina ɔɔ chɔguu, ba naanna ge wia tuŋ,
ka banla n wia deŋlee
naanna ɔɔ chiu chigigi.
8Nfɛrɛ hiŋ wia ɔɔ par nɛr maanii,
ka ba ɔɔ ra
gbɛlli bambuguu waarɛ.
9Hiŋ ɛɛ nɛsunni di ra humuu bɔ,
hinna yir i hiŋ nɛzeŋ
ka ra chɔɔ lɔzi.
10Banla maa wia n deŋlee, ɔɔ ra binni ba selaa nɛnnɛ,
ka biinikpola hina waa,
ɔɔ ra tɔɔri ba horaa.
11Patti la n aah siwii di ra hum, daŋ na diwee werge di ra di,
ka gɛnii waa,
ɔɔ ra chɔgi
u saŋaa humpɛɛri ni.
12Wii la maa biinikpola hina n ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu,
bá na wichɔgaa di ra ɛɛ,
ka banla wia
n deŋlee waa,
ɔɔ chiu chigigi.
13Biinikpola hina wiŋɔzi ɛɛ sidɛɛrɛ tɛɛ baa,
ka banla wia n deŋlee
ɔɔ lii tɔɔrɔɔ biinii.
14I kinturgaa daŋ wer lii i wiŋɔzi ni i wiɛɛlaa biini,
í na wia la n dɛgii.
15Gɛnii ɔɔ fɛu lugɔ u wiɛɛlaa deŋloore,
ka nunzunni waa,
ɔɔ ra nuu baglaarɛ.
16Gɛnii baaŋ waa birgi fuuih,
ka nunzunni waa,
ɔɔ lau u hinnɛ,
di ba wa chagzuu gba.
17Daansɛɛ diiri la wia n dɔɔ wibii, ɔɔ ra ŋɔ wibiire,
ka unla wia
n waa wibii dɔɔwɛ,
ɔɔ ra kanni karaa.
18Nfɛrnyaai wiŋɔzi ɔɔ ra tɔɔuh alugɔ tokobi,
ka nunzuma wiŋɔzi waa,
ɔɔ ra chaau.
19Wibii du denii saŋa maa,
ka kara waa dɔɔ magaa.
20Dawari ɔɔ su banla n ɔɔ ra ta wichɔgaa ɛɛi jina bampireere,
ka banla n ɔɔ ra ta
bɔsɔna wia jina,
dɔɔ bampirsɔnaa.
21Wichɔgii maa wàá wer huuzi nɛra la wia n deŋlee,
ka biinikpola hina waa,
tɔɔrɔɔ bɛnnɛ ba hor.
22Kɔraawiizi hah karkannaa,
ka nɔŋŋi banla wia
n dɔɔ wibii.
23Nunzunna waa ɔɔ ra jigsi ba nfɛrɛ dɔɔi wia,
ka gɛnaa ɔɔ ra yaari
ba gɛnni wiarɛ.
24Huma humaa werge daŋ gil i dɔɔ fɔŋŋa,
ka yaara daŋ gil
i ɛɛ yom.
25Biinichɔg ɔɔ ɛɛu lugɔ buntɔga chigaa,
bɔkpega ge dui wiŋɔzi
ra pur bɔraa.
26Nɛr la wia n deŋlee ɔɔ ra bir u dammuu liizinanaa,
ka biinikpola hiŋ waa,
ɔɔ giluu u ra leu.
27Yaara hiŋ wàá wer na ú kipar,
ka di i aah siwii
di ra hum,
i daŋ di tɔna werge.
28Wideŋlaa ŋmɛnɛɛ ɛɛ miibɔɔrɛ,
ka biinikpola wiɛɛlaa ge
ŋmɛnɛɛ ɛɛ siu.

english_text:
Wise Friends Make You Wise
1Children with good sense
accept correction
from their parents,
but stubborn children
ignore it completely.
2You will be well rewarded
for saying something kind,
but all some people think about
is how to be cruel and mean.
3 Keep what you know to yourself,
and you will be safe;
talk too much,
and you are done for.
4No matter how much you want,
laziness won't help a bit,
but hard work will reward you
with more than enough.
5A good person hates deceit,
but those who are evil
cause shame and disgrace.
6Live right, and you are safe!
But sin will destroy you.
7Some who have nothing
may pretend to be rich,
and some who have everything
may pretend to be poor.
8The rich may have
to pay a ransom,
but the poor don't have
that problem.
9The lamp of a good person
keeps on shining;
the lamp of an evil person
soon goes out.
10Too much pride causes trouble.
Be sensible and take advice.
11Money wrongly gained
will disappear bit by bit;
money earned little by little
will grow and grow.
12Not getting what you want
can break your heart,
but a wish that comes true
is a life-giving tree.
13If you reject God's teaching,
you will pay the price;
if you obey his commands,
you will be rewarded.
14Sensible instruction
is a life-giving fountain
that helps you escape
all deadly traps.
15Sound judgment is praised,
but people without good sense
are on the way to disaster.
16If you have good sense,
you will act sensibly,
but fools act like fools.
17Whoever delivers your message
can make things better
or worse for you.
18All who refuse correction
will be poor and disgraced;
all who accept correction
will be praised.
19It's a good feeling
to get what you want,
but only a stupid fool
hates to turn from evil.
20 Wise friends make you wise,
but you hurt yourself
by going around with fools.
21You are in for trouble
if you sin,
but you will be rewarded
if you live right.
22If you obey God,
you will have something
to leave your grandchildren.
If you don't obey God,
those who live right
will get what you leave.
23Even when the land of the poor
produces good crops,
they get cheated
out of what they grow.
24If you love your children,
you will correct them;
if you don't love them,
you won't correct them.
25If you live right,
you will have plenty to eat;
if you don't live right,
you will go away empty.
translation_text:
1Bie la n zum wia ɔɔ sɛɛ u mɛɛ ni u maa baglaarɛ,
ka chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri
ɔɔ vɛɛ nuuirɛ.
2Nɛnanaa ɔɔ di ba wiŋɔzi sumaa,
ka wibiinyaara ɔɔ nɔŋŋi
kaluu werge.
3Nɛr la maa n zum u nua kpoglaa ra du u miibɔɔ taurɛ,
ka nɛr la n waa
u nua kpoglaa zummɛ
ra kpu u hinnɛ.
4Yaara hina ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi kunaa werge, ka na tama,
ka banla n aah siwii
di ra hum daŋ nyɛɛli,
di na ba kipar nɛnnɛ.
5Banla wia n deŋlee hah karaa,
biinikpola hina ge
ra di hiihzi ni ŋmaaba.
6Banla wia n deŋlee ɔɔ na hiinaare bá de dui maa biini,
ka biinikpola hina
wiɛɛlaa ɔɔ chɔgi baabuu.
7Baŋhina ɔɔ ɛɛ nyaara ka ra ɛɛ lambaara lugɔ ba ɛɛ dɔɔnaa,
baŋhina ge ɛɛ dɔɔna
ka ra ɛɛ lambaara lugɔ
ba ɛɛ nyaaraa.
8Daama hina daŋ wer kpa kebee di lɛɛ bahinaa,
ka nɛr maa
wàá tɔɔri nyaara waa.
9Nɛr la wia n deŋlee, u de dui maa ɔɔ chaanuu alugɔ bɔchaaŋ,
ka biinikpola hina
hora ɔɔ ɛɛu
lugɔ baŋ dinzi
fintina kakpaŋ.
10Barabara ra ba hɔɔzi ninɛɛ,
banla n na nuu baglaa
ɛɛ nunzunnaa.
11Di i ga ŋmɛnichɔgaa na daama, a ɔɔ tunuu manaŋ,
ka humkpega humaa
na daama ɔɔ ra jaau.
12Tamii n waa ballɛ manaŋ ra ba bɔhuaih ninɛɛ,
ka kipar nai
ra tɛɛ miibɔɔ ni bɔsɔnaa.
13Nɛr la maa n na gbɛlli baglaa ra chɔg u hinnɛ,
ka unla maa ge
n na tɔgzaa daŋ di tɔna.
14Nunzunni baglaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bule la n na tɛɛ miibɔɔ,
di ra lɛɛ nɛr siu be.
15Ba ɔɔ ra tɔgzi nɛra la n dɔɔ nfɛrnanaarɛ,
ka wibiinyaara ɔɔ ra vol
ŋmɛnizi la n dɔɔ biarɛ.
16Nunzunna ɔɔ fɛ nfɛrɛɛ mɔɔ ka ɛɛ wia,
ka gɛnaa waa,
ɔɔ ra bagli ba bambugrii.
17Balii la wia n nyaa wibii ra zuu wia biinii,
ka unla wia n dɔɔ wibii
ra ba bampirsɔna ninɛɛ.
18Nɛr la n na vɛɛ baglaa daŋ nyaa, di di hiihzi,
ka unla n na nuu baglaa,
ba danna tɔgzuu.
19Kipar wii nai summɔɔ,
ka gɛnaa hah
wichɔgaa ɛɛi gilaarɛ.
20Di i dammu ɛɛ nunzunni, i daŋ dɔɔ nunzuma,
ka di i ra hiŋ gɛnaa,
gɛnni kizee daŋ mɔnii.
21Tɔɔrɔɔ ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi wichɔgɛɛra bɔttɛ,
ka kissaa ge ra nyiŋŋi
banla wia
n deŋlee bɔr.
22Nɛnanaa ɔɔ gil kapɛttɛɛ dau ba naanna,
ka wichɔgɛɛra hora
daŋ la nɛra la wia
n deŋlee be.
23Nyaari koo daŋ wer lii diwee werge,
ka banla n waa
wibii ra di,
ɔɔ gbaaraabuu kaali.
24Di i vɛɛ i biizi digna tɛraa, haa baa nɔŋŋɛɛ,
ka di i nɔŋŋi baa,
i daŋ tɛr ba digna.
25Nɛra la wia n deŋlee ɔɔ nau di di piŋ ba kipar,
ka biinikpola hina waa,
ɔɔ kpogli lɔzii.

english_text:
Wisdom Makes Good Sense
1A woman's family
is held together
by her wisdom,
but it can be destroyed
by her foolishness.
2By living right, you show
that you respect the Lord;
by being deceitful, you show
that you despise him.
3Proud fools are punished
for their stupid talk,
but sensible talk
can save your life.
4Without the help of an ox
there can be no crop,
but with a strong ox
a big crop is possible.
5An honest witness
tells the truth;
a dishonest witness
tells nothing but lies.
6Make fun of wisdom,
and you will never find it.
But if you have understanding,
knowledge comes easily.
7Stay away from fools,
or you won't learn a thing.
8Wise people have enough sense
to find their way,
but stupid fools get lost.
9Fools don't care
if they are wrong,
but God is pleased
when people do right.
10No one else can really know
how sad or happy you are.
11The tent of a good person
stands longer than the house
of someone evil.
12 You may think you are
on the right road
and still end up dead.
13Sorrow may hide
behind laughter,
and happiness may end
in sorrow.
14You harvest what you plant,
whether good or bad.
15Don't be stupid
and believe all you hear;
be smart and know
where you are headed.
16Only a stupid fool
is never cautious—
so be extra careful
and stay out of trouble.
17Fools have quick tempers,
and no one likes you
if you can't be trusted.
18Stupidity leads to foolishness;
be smart and learn.
19The wicked will come crawling
to those who obey God.
20You have no friends
if you are poor,
but you have lots of friends
if you are rich.
21It's wrong to hate others,
but God blesses everyone
who is kind to the poor.
22It's a mistake
to make evil plans,
but you will have loyal friends
if you want to do right.
23Hard work is worthwhile,
but empty talk
will make you poor.
24Wisdom can make you rich,
but foolishness leads
to more foolishness.
25An honest witness
can save your life,
but liars can't be trusted.
26If you respect the Lord,
you and your children
have a strong fortress
27and a life-giving fountain
that keeps you safe
from deadly traps.
28Rulers of powerful nations
are held in honor;
rulers of weak nations
are nothing at all.
29It's smart to be patient,
but it's stupid
to lose your temper.
30It's healthy to be content,
but envy can eat you up.
31If you mistreat the poor,
you insult your Creator;
if you are kind to them,
you show him respect.
32In times of trouble
the wicked are destroyed,
but even at death
the innocent have faith.
33Wisdom is found in the minds
of people with good sense,
but fools don't know it.
34Doing right brings honor
to a nation,
but sin brings disgrace.
35Kings reward servants
who act wisely,
but they punish those
who act foolishly.
translation_text:
1Hahnunzunni ɔɔ ra ma u diarɛ,
hahgɛnii ge ra puri u hor.
2Nɛr la wia n deŋlee ra ɔm Kɔraawiizii,
ka unla n na gbɛlluu ge
ra hiŋ ŋmɛnichɔgaa.
3Gɛnii wiŋɔzi ɔɔ giluu ba tɛr u digni,
ka nunzunni wiŋɔzi
ra guuubuu.
4Di nabala waa hoo a par, diwee ɔɔ nyaau,
ka di a du de,
diwee ɔɔ puruu.
5Wibii daansɛɛ diiri waa kara ra kanni,
ka kara hor waa,
kara bɛnnɛ ɔɔ su u nua.
6Chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi nunzumaa, ka wàá nau,
ka banla
n na nuu wia zɛɛ
ɔɔ na nfɛrɛɛ manaŋ.
7Gilɛɛ gil i ni gɛnaa ra kpau, dikuubɛɛwiai,
hàá wer na
nunzuma maa
lii ba be.
8Nunzunni ɔɔ zum wii la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ u ɛɛu,
ka gɛnii ɔɔ ra dar
u hinnɛ lugɔ u zummɔɔ.
9Gɛnii baga lɛi wichɔgaa ɛɛi wia,
ka nɛr la wia n deŋlee,
ɔɔ ra suŋŋi
u wichɔgaa giltɛɛirɛ.
10Nɛr maa zum u himmaa tɔɔrɔɔrɛ u biini,
gunnɛ nɛr maa ge
wàá wer hiinuu
di u bɔsɔna.
11Biinikpola hiŋ dia daŋ puri,
ka nɛr la wia
n deŋlee hor chi.
12Ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛl ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ uŋ wesse tɛɛ newee,
ka u tuna ɛɛ siu.
13Mamaa daŋ wer suah biinichɔg,
ka di mamaa la
wa tunnɔ, a biinichɔg
haa du denii.
14Nɛchɔgaa daŋ na gunla n dɛg baa,
nɛnanaa ge na
ba kinturgaa la n wesse.
15Nfɛrnyaari ɔɔ yardi wiimaanii,
ka nunzunni ɔɔ lɔ
nfɛrɛɛ nɛnnɛ
u wiɛɛlaa maa biini.
16Nunzunni ɔɔ ra du u hiŋ taurɛ, ú gilɛɛ waa zuu siaahmu biini,
ka gɛnii waa
ɔɔ yali siweere,
di ra ɛɛ wia
di ra zuu wia biini.
17Nɛr la n na na baaŋ manamanaŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ gɛnni wiarɛ,
ka nunzunni
ɔɔ ra lau u hinnɛ.
18Nfɛrnyaari ɔɔ di u gɛnni wia tɔnaa,
ka nunzunna waa
ɔɔ na nfɛrɛɛ jaa.
19Wichɔgɛɛra daŋ giŋŋi nɛnanaa sezi di sɛɛ baa dɔɔra,
biinikpola hina ge
wa giŋŋi ba dominuuzi
di ra sɛɛ baa dɔɔra.
20Nyaari waa dammu dɔɔwɛ,
ka dɔɔna waa
ɔɔ dɔɔ baabuu kpila.
21Di i gbɛlli i dɔŋhiŋ, i ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ,
ka nɛr la waa
n na hiini nyaara,
nuu sumaa.
22Di i ta wichɔgaa ɛɛi jina, i daŋ leu,
ka di i ta
winanaa ɛɛi jina,
i daŋ na nɔŋŋaa
ni wibii dɔɔi la
n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.
23Huma humaa dɔɔ tɔnaa,
ka so pɛɛ ni wiŋɔbala
waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ.
24Nunzunni kinturgaare daama,
gɛnaa ge hor ɛɛ gɛnni.
25Wibii daansɛɛ diiri ra mɔgli miibɔɔrɛ,
ka kara hor
ra ɛɛ sɔsɔgɔɔ.
26Baal la n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi bɔra daŋ sɔɔnuu.
U daŋ kpa nonee tɔ
a baal haaŋ
ni u biizi ni.
27Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bule la n na tɛɛ miibɔɔ,
di ra lɛɛ nɛr siu be.
28Nɛraa kora.
Di nɛra waa hoo,
kora ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.
29Nɛr la baaŋ n waa fuuh manaŋ, dɔɔ wia zɛɛ zumaarɛ werge,
unla ge baaŋ
n ɔɔ ra fuuh manaŋ,
ɔɔ ra ɛɛ gɛnni wiarɛ.
30Bampirsɔna ra du bɔkpegaa,
ka zoma ge ra tɛɛ wiila.
31Nɛr la n na sunni nyaara, ra chagzi Kɔraawiizi la n ta baabuu,
ka unla n na hiini baa
ra tɔgzuubuu.
32Wichɔgɛɛri wichɔgaa ɔɔ chɔguubuu,
ka unla n na
ɔm Kɔraawiizi
dɔɔ zuuribɔttɛ,
di u wa siuwɔ.
33Nunzuma ɔɔ du nɛr la n na nuu wia zɛɛ nfɛrɛ biinii,
hàá wer na
nunzuma gɛnaa be.
34Wideŋlaa ɛɛi ɔɔ giluu hɛri kuari,
ka wichɔgaa ɛɛi
kpa hiihzii,
di ra kpu nɛra maa.
35Koori maa ɔɔ dɔɔ bɔsɔnaa di u balii zum wia la unna ɛɛu,
ka u ɔɔ na baannɛ
du unla n na gba wia.

english_text:
The Lord Sees Everything
1A kind answer
soothes angry feelings,
but harsh words
stir them up.
2Words of wisdom
come from the wise,
but fools speak foolishness.
3The Lord sees everything,
whether good or bad.
4Kind words are good medicine,
but deceitful words
can really hurt.
5Don't be a fool
and disobey your parents.
Be smart! Accept correction.
6Good people become wealthy,
but those who are evil
will lose what they have.
7Words of wisdom
make good sense;
the thoughts of a fool
make no sense at all.
8The Lord is disgusted
by gifts from the wicked,
but it makes him happy
when his people pray.
9The Lord is disgusted
with all who do wrong,
but he loves everyone
who does right.
10If you turn from the right way,
you will be punished;
if you refuse correction,
you will die.
11If the Lord can see everything
in the world of the dead,
he can see in our hearts.
12Those who sneer at others
don't like to be corrected,
and they won't ask help
from someone with sense.
13Happiness makes you smile;
sorrow can crush you.
14Anyone with good sense
is eager to learn more,
but fools are hungry
for foolishness.
15The poor have a hard life,
but being content is as good
as an endless feast.
16It's better to obey the Lord
and have only a little,
than to be very rich
and terribly anxious.
17A simple meal with love
is better than a feast
where there is hatred.
18Losing your temper
causes a lot of trouble,
but staying calm
settles arguments.
19A lazy person refuses
to clear a thorny path,
but everyone who does right
walks on a smooth road.
20Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
despise them.
21Stupidity brings happiness
to senseless fools,
but everyone with good sense
follows the straight path.
22Without good advice
everything goes wrong—
it takes careful planning
for things to go right.
23Giving the right answer
at the right time
makes everyone happy.
24All who are wise follow a road
that leads upward to life
and away from death.
25The Lord destroys the homes
of those who are proud,
but he protects the property
of widows.
26The Lord hates evil thoughts,
but kind words please him.
27Being greedy causes trouble
for your family,
but you protect yourself
by refusing bribes.
28Good people think
before they answer,
but the wicked speak evil
without ever thinking.
29The Lord never even hears
the prayers of the wicked,
but he answers the prayers
of all who obey him.
30A friendly smile
makes you happy,
and good news
makes you feel strong.
31Healthy correction is good,
and if you accept it,
you will be wise.
32You hurt only yourself
by rejecting instruction,
but it makes good sense
to accept it.
33Showing respect to the Lord
will make you wise,
and being humble
will bring honor to you.
translation_text:
1Nuupɛr ra sɔɔni baannɛ,
ka nuunyɛg ge
ra izi baaŋ.
2Nunzunni wiŋɔzi ɔɔ ra tɛɛ nfɛrɛɛ,
ka gɛnii ɔɔ ra
ŋɔ gɛnni wiarɛ.
3Yemmaanii Kɔraawiizi siwee du,
di ra na wichɔgɛɛra
ni banla
n na ɛɛ winanaa.
4Wiŋɔnanaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ tagzi,
ka kara wiŋɔzi
ra ba biinichɔg ninɛɛ.
5Gɛnii ɔɔ vɛɛ u mɛɛ baglaarɛ,
ka unla n ɔɔ nuu
ɛɛ nunzunnii.
6Daama ɔɔ su nɛr la wia n deŋlee diarɛ,
ka biinikpola
hiŋ kunnaalaa
ɔɔ ra ba tɔɔrɔɔ ninɛɛ.
7Nunzunni wiŋɔzi ra tɛɛ nfɛrɛɛ,
gɛnii waa wiŋɔzi
wàá wer ɛɛ guŋ.
8Kɔraawiizi kii biinikpola hiŋ mbusuzi lizaarɛ,
ka unla wia n deŋlee
wiisuŋŋaa ra paruubuu.
9Kɔraawiizi hah biinikpola hiŋ wiɛɛlaarɛ,
ka nɔŋŋi banla
n na nyiŋŋi
wideŋlaa hora.
10Nɛr la maa n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa daŋ na dignitɛraa werge,
ka unla ge n hah
baglaa daŋ siu.
11Kɔraawiizi ra na wia la maa n du lalaa bolle,
ɛrɛɛ newea
bampiree biini wia
wer suah u ninɛi?
12Chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri kiire baglaa,
u ni nunzunna
waa kpau.
13Bɔsɔna ra ba siwee puraa ninɛɛ,
ka biinichɔg waa,
ɔɔ giluu nɛr nyɛm.
14Wibii lɔzi ɔɔ ra kpu nunzunnii,
ka gɛnaa ɔɔ piŋ
ni gɛnni wiarɛ.
15Nyaari waa be, hɔpizii maa ra ba tɔɔrɔɔ ninɛɛ,
ka bɔsɔna hina waa,
ɔɔ ra di de dui sumaa.
16Hiŋ dɔɔ tama ka ra ɔm Kɔraawiizii bɔ,
hiŋ dɔɔ kuna werge
ni tɔɔrɔɔ.
17Hin di kelaa ni nɔŋŋaarɛ bɔ,
hin di yoma ni hahzi.
18Nɛr la baaŋ n na fuuh manamanaŋ, chugzi kaluu di ra du,
ka kanyitti hiŋ
ra laafi kaluu.
19Yaara hiŋ ɔɔ dɔɔ tɔɔrɔɔrɛ ú de dui maa biini,
ka nɛr la waa
wia n deŋlee,
waa ɔɔ dɔɔ tɔɔrɔɔ maa.
20Bie la n zum wia ɔɔ giluu u mɛɛ bɔra sɔɔni,
ka bie la n gɛnnɛ waa,
ɔɔ giluu u maa biini chɔgi.
21Gɛnaa bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔni ba gɛnni wiarɛ,
ka nunzunni ɔɔ ra
ɛɛ wia la n deŋleere.
22Di baglaa nɛnnɛ waa hoo, jina taizi ɔɔ chɔguu,
ka di bagla kpila
du de, a ɔɔ kuaruu.
23Nɛr bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔnuu di u ŋɔ wii
chem saŋa la n dɛkkɛ!
24Nunzunna ɔɔ ra vol ŋmɛnɛɛ la n dɔɔ miibɔɔ di ra la chinne,
ka gil siu ŋmɛnɛɛ la
n na tuu zɛɛrɛ.
25Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ chɔgi barabara hiŋ diarɛ,
ka guu luhaaŋ
kundɔɔlaa nɛnnɛ.
26Kɔraawiizi hah wia la biinikpola hina n ɔɔ ra fɛu,
ka nɛnanaa waa
wifɛɛlaa ɔɔ paruubuu.
27Nɛr la n fini nɛra di na kebee ɔɔ ba biinichɔg ninɛɛ u diahina ni,
ka unla n hah
murgaa kuna
daŋ di miibɔɔ.
28Nɛnanii ɔɔ fɛ nfɛrɛɛ mɔɔ ka ra ŋɔ wia,
ka biinikpola hiŋ waa,
ɔɔ ra ŋɔ
wichɔgaa wiŋɔzii.
29Kɔraawiizi ni biinikpola hina nɛɛwɔɔ dɔŋa ni,
ka u ɔɔ ra nuu banla wia
n deŋlee wiisuŋŋaarɛ.
30Di i ra binni nɛra la bɔra n na pur, i bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔnuu,
amaniyesuma ge ra tɛɛ alaanfia.
31Nɛr la n na sɛɛ jugmaa, daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ,
di du nunzunna biini.
32Nɛr la maa n na vɛɛ baglaa ra tɔɔri u hinnɛ,
ka unla n sɛɛ
baglaa waa,
ra zum wia zɛɛrɛ.
33Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa ɛɛ baglaa ni nunzumaa.
Ɛɛ sɔɔni siwiire,
di na tɔgzaa.

english_text:
The Lord Has the Final Word
1We humans make plans,
but the Lord
has the final word.
2We may think we know
what is right,
but the Lord is the judge
of our motives.
3Share your plans with the Lord,
and you will succeed.
4The Lord has a reason
for everything he does,
and he lets evil people live
only to be punished.
5The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is conceited—
you can be sure
they will be punished.
6 If we truly love God,
our sins will be forgiven;
if we show him respect,
we will keep away from sin.
7When we please the Lord,
even our enemies
make friends with us.
8 It's better to be honest
and poor
than to be dishonest
and rich.
9We make our own plans,
but the Lord decides
where we will go.
10Rulers speak with authority
and are never wrong.
11The Lord watches to see
if we are fair
or if we cheat others.
12Justice makes rulers powerful.
They should hate evil
13and like honesty and truth.
14An angry ruler
can put you to death.
So be wise!
Don't make one angry.
15When a ruler is happy
and pleased with you,
it's like refreshing rain,
and you will live.
16It's much better to be wise
and sensible
than to be rich.
17God's people avoid evil ways,
and they protect themselves
by watching where they go.
18Too much pride
will destroy you.
19You are better off
to be humble and poor
than to get rich
from what you take by force.
20If you know what you're doing,
you will prosper.
God blesses everyone
who trusts him.
21Good judgment proves
that you are wise,
and if you speak kindly,
you can teach others.
22Good sense is a fountain
that gives life,
but fools are punished
by their foolishness.
23You can persuade others
if you are wise
and speak sensibly.
24Kind words are like honey—
they cheer you up
and make you feel strong.
25 Sometimes what seems right
is really a road to death.
26The hungrier you are,
the harder you work.
27Worthless people plan trouble.
Even their words burn
like a flaming fire.
28 Gossip is no good!
It causes hard feelings
and comes between friends.
29Don't trust violent people.
They will mislead you
to do the wrong thing.
30When someone winks
or grins behind your back,
trouble is on the way.
31Gray hair is a glorious crown
worn by those
who have lived right.
32Controlling your temper
is better than being a hero
who captures a city.
33We make our own decisions,
but the Lord alone
determines what happens.
translation_text:
1Newee ɔɔ ta wia jinaa,
ka Kɔraawiizii
ɔɔ bagli wia la
un niŋ ŋɔ a deŋli.
2Newee ɔɔ fɛ lugɔ u wiɛɛlaa maanii deŋlee,
ka Kɔraawiizii ra di
u biini wia seriya.
3Kpa i wiɛɛlaa maa du Kɔraawiizi nonee,
í jinazi maa wer na ɛɛi.
4Kɔraawiizi kuari kummaanii u himmaa wiɛɛlaa wia,
haali biinikpola hiŋ gba,
dikuu hɛhchɔg hɔpizii wia.
5Kɔraawiizi hah barabara hinnɛ,
zum lugɔ u daŋ tɛr
nɛra la n pɔɔhwɛ digna.
6Nɔŋŋaa ni wibii dɔɔi nɛnnɛ,
ɔɔ lizi Kɔraawiizi
baannɛ nɛr ni,
u gil u wichɔgaa tɛu.
Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa ge
ɔɔ gil nɛr
vɛɛ wichɔgaa ɛɛi.
7Di nɛr wiɛɛlaa par Kɔraawiizi,
u ɔɔ giluu
u ni u dɔma gba
du ni bɔsɔna.
8Hiŋ dɔɔ wibii ka nyaarɛ bɔ,
hiŋ ɛɛ dɔɔŋ
ka nyaa wibii.
9Newee ɔɔ ta u himmaa jinazii,
ka Kɔraawiizii
ɔɔ bagli u wiɛɛlaa.
10Koori nunzuma wiŋɔzi ɔɔ lii Kɔraawiizi benii,
a dɛkkɔ unna di wibii.
11Kɔraawiizi waa nyiŋŋi lugɔ ya ra fini dɔŋa kɔɔzaa biini.
Awiarɛ u gil
mɛgzaa kuna du de.
12Koori kii wichɔgaarɛ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, wibii diire
ɔɔ gil kora chi.
13Koori bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔnuu dikuu wiŋɔdeŋlaa wia,
u nɔŋŋi banla
n na ŋɔ wibiire.
14Koori baaŋ ɛɛ siu baliirɛ,
ka nunzunni
ɔɔ weruu laafuu.
15Di koori haŋ wa munzi, miibɔɔ ɔɔ du denii,
i wia n paruu ge
ɛɛ lugɔ sazau dooŋ.
16Hiŋ dɔɔ nunzumaa bɔ hiŋ dɔɔ saliŋ,
di dɔɔ wia zɛɛ zumaarɛ
bɔ hiŋ dɔɔ kebee.
17Nɛra la wia n deŋlee ŋmɛnɛɛ waa wichɔgaa dɔɔwɛ,
nɛr la maa n na hiŋ
a guŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ
dɔɔ u hinnɛ.
18Jigsi ra ba chɔgaa ninɛɛ,
kpoŋaa ra ba cholaa ni.
19Hiŋ dɔɔ sisɔna ka nyaarɛ bɔ,
hiŋ jaa nɛkpoŋlaa
ni di ra foozi.
20Nɛr la maa n na nuu baglaa daŋ nyɛɛli,
unla maa ge n yardi
Kɔraawiizi daŋ na bɔsɔna.
21Ba zum nunzunnii, dikuu u wia zɛɛ zumaa wia,
u wiŋɔzi sunzi wia,
nɛra ɔɔ sɛɛu tɛu.
22Wia zɛɛ zumaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bule la n na tɛɛ miibɔɔ di tɛɛ nɛr la n dɔɔu,
ka gɛnaa ge baglaa
ɛɛ saŋa chɔgaa.
23Nunzunni ɔɔ lɔ nfɛrɛɛ mɔɔ ka ŋɔ wia,
di wer ra bir nɛra nfɛssi.
24Wiŋɔnanaa summɔɔ lugɔ huuhnuu,
di ra tɛɛ
bɔsɔna ni alaanfia.
25Ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛl ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ uŋ wesse tɛɛ newee,
ka u tuna ɛɛ siu.
26Lɔzii ɔɔ gil balii ra hum,
dikuu unna nyiŋŋi
diwee wia.
27Nɛchɔgii ɔɔ ra ta wichɔgaa ɛɛi jinaa,
u wiŋɔzi ɛɛ lugɔ
ninzeŋ n na
haahri werge.
28Biinikpola hiŋ ra izi kaluu,
nɛzɔɔzaa ra bargi dammuzii.
29Kalu nyiŋŋe ɔɔ ra dar ba dɔŋa hinaa,
di gil ba ra na tɔɔrɔɔ.
30Nɛr la n na kamzi siwee ra ta wichɔgaa ɛɛi jina.
Nɛr la n na mir nua
ra nyiŋŋi chumaa ɛɛirɛ.
31Nyuhuŋhuŋŋa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ koorikahuro n dɔɔ girme,
nɛr la wia
n deŋleere ra dɔɔa.
32Hiŋ dɔɔ kanyittii bɔ, hiŋ ɛɛ baal, laal lɔi biini.
Hinlawaarɛ bɔ, hiŋ wette
kpegli bolzeŋ hina.
33Ba ɔɔ ta kunaa bá zum wii la n du de,
ka a wibaglaa maa
ɔɔ lii Kɔraawiizi benii.

english_text:
Our Thoughts Are Tested by the Lord
1A dry crust of bread eaten
in peace and quiet
is better than a feast eaten
where everyone argues.
2A wise slave
will be placed in charge
of a no-good child,
and that slave will be given
the same inheritance
that each child receives.
3Silver and gold are tested
by flames of fire;
our thoughts are tested
by the Lord.
4Troublemakers listen
to troublemakers,
and liars listen to liars.
5By insulting the poor,
you insult your Creator.
You will be punished
if you make fun
of someone in trouble.
6Grandparents are proud
of their grandchildren,
and children should be proud
of their parents.
7It sounds strange for a fool
to talk sensibly,
but it's even worse
for a ruler to tell lies.
8A bribe works miracles
like a magic charm
that brings good luck.
9You will keep your friends
if you forgive them,
but you will lose your friends
if you keep talking about
what they did wrong.
10A sensible person
accepts correction,
but you can't beat sense
into a fool.
11Cruel people want to rebel,
and so vicious attackers
will be sent against them.
12A bear robbed of her cubs
is far less dangerous
than a stubborn fool.
13You will always have trouble
if you are mean to those
who are good to you.
14The start of an argument
is like a water leak—
so stop it before
real trouble breaks out.
15The Lord doesn't like those
who defend the guilty
or condemn the innocent.
16Why should fools have money
for an education
when they refuse to learn?
17 A friend is there to help,
in any situation,
and relatives are born
to share our troubles.
18It's stupid to guarantee
someone else's loan.
19The wicked and the proud
love trouble and keep begging
to be hurt.
20Dishonesty does you no good,
and telling lies
will get you in trouble.
21It's never pleasant
to be the parent of a fool
and have nothing but pain.
22If you are cheerful,
you feel good;
if you are sad,
you hurt all over.
23Crooks accept secret bribes
to keep justice
from being done.
24Anyone with wisdom knows
what makes good sense,
but fools can never
make up their minds.
25Foolish children bring sorrow
and pain to their parents.
26It isn't fair
to punish the innocent
and those who do right.
27It makes a lot of sense
to be a person of few words
and to stay calm.
28 Even fools seem smart
when they are quiet.
translation_text:
1Kuuhiah dii ni bɔsɔnaa bɔ,
diuzenaa dii ni kalu.
2Yom la n zum wia daŋ di kora
u dɔɔri biijaga ni,
u nuu bɔnni u kapɛttɛ.
3Ninne ba ɔɔ kpa di ŋmɛɛri saliŋhuŋŋu ni saliŋ, bá zum a wessi,
gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ ɛɛ
newee bampirii na.
4Wichɔgɛɛra ɔɔ ra nuu biinikpola wiŋɔzii,
karkanna ge keŋŋi digna
di ra nuu chɔgaa wiŋɔzi.
5Banla n na ɛɛ nyaara chɛɛtɛ ra chagzi Kɔraawiizi la n ta baabuu,
banla ge bɔra n ɔɔ sɔɔni
dikuu baŋhina
cholaa wia,
daŋ na dignitɛraa.
6Nɛzɛŋzi girmee ba naanna,
gunnɛ biizi ge girme
ɛɛ ba maawaa
ni mɛɛwaa.
7Nuusuma waa dɛg gɛnii,
gunnɛ a waa dɛg koori
n na kanni kara.
8Nɛra baŋhina fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ kuna kpai tɛɛ nɛr,
daŋ wer gil ba nyɛɛli.
9Nɛr la maa n gil wia ra tɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ, ra nyiŋŋi nɔŋŋaarɛ,
ka nɛr la nua n waa tɔ,
u dɔŋhiŋ n ɛɛu wia ni,
ra bargi
dammuzii dɔŋa ni.
10Hiŋ hau nunzunni ni kakpaŋ,
ɔɔ hiinuubuu di kaali
hiŋ lɔɔzi gɛnii bukalfa.
11Wichɔgɛɛra ɔɔ ra di mmɔrii,
ka ba daŋ tɛr
ba digna werge.
12Hiŋ chem amani la biizi baŋ paawɛɛ dɔɔ alaanfia
kaali hiŋ chem gɛnii,
u gɛnni wiɛɛlaa biini.
13Di i kpa wichɔgaa di turgi winanaa kim,
wichɔgaa ŋmɛnɛ maa
wàá nyaa i dia.
14Kalu faaraa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna peri dampu,
awia gil a wii mɔɔ,
ka kalu izi.
15Kɔraawiizi hah banla n ɔɔ lɛɛ wibiire di ra tɛɛ biinikpola hina
ni banla n ɔɔ kpa bilchɔg
di ra tɛɛ banla wia
n deŋlee maanii.
16Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ í kpa kebee turgi gɛnii sukuru laŋaa,
uŋ wàá wer
helli nunzumai?
17Dammu ɔɔ dɔɔ nɔŋŋaarɛ saŋa maa,
tɔɔrɔɔ wiarɛ
ba ra lul lulli ge.
18Nfɛrnyaairɛ nɛr n chigɛ
tɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ u di kim.
19Nɛr la maa n nɔŋŋi naari, nɔŋŋi wichɔgaarɛ,
barabara hiŋ ge
ra ba tɔɔrɔɔ ni.
20Nfɛrchɔgaa hiŋ waa nyɛɛli,
wichɔgɛɛri ge
ɔɔ zuu tɔɔrɔɔ biinii.
21Nɛr la n lul gɛnii, tɛɛ u hinnɛ biinichɔg,
gɛnii ge mɛɛ
waa bɔsɔna ra dɔɔ.
22Bɔsɔna ɛɛ tagzi la n wessee,
ka biinichɔg ge
ra chɔgmi nɛttɛ.
23Biinikpola hiŋ ɔɔ suahzuu di lɛɛ kuna,
ú chɔgi wibii
dii ŋmɛnizi.
24Nunzunni ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi nunzuma wiɛɛlaarɛ saŋa maa,
ka gɛnii waa
ɔɔ dɔɔ wilaulii.
25Biigɛnii ra chɔgi u mɛɛ biinii,
di ɛɛ kuŋkpol ge tɛɛ
u maa la n luluu.
26A waa dɛkkɛ bá gil nɛnanii turgi bilchɔg kim,
dikuu u winanaa wia,
gɛɛ di tɛr
nabɔnzenaa digna
dikuu ba wibii dɔɔi wia.
27Nunzunni himmaa waa wia ra ŋɔ werge,
ka nɛr la n zum wia zɛɛ
ɔɔ lau u hinnɛ.
28Ba ɔɔ fɛ lugɔ gɛnii ɛɛ nunzunnii, di waa hagzi,
di u wa tɔ u nua ge,
u ɛɛ lugɔ nfɛrɛ hiŋ.

english_text:
It's Wrong To Favor the Guilty
1It's selfish and stupid
to think only of yourself
and to sneer at people
who have sense.
2Fools have no desire to learn,
instead they would rather
give their own opinion.
3Wrongdoing leads to shame
and disgrace.
4Words of wisdom
are a stream that flows
from a deep fountain.
5It's wrong to favor the guilty
and keep the innocent
from getting justice.
6Foolish talk will get you
into a lot of trouble.
7Saying foolish things
is like setting a trap
to destroy yourself.
8There's nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
9Being lazy is no different
from being a troublemaker.
10The Lord is a mighty tower
where his people can run
for safety—
11the rich think their money
is a wall of protection.
12Pride leads to destruction;
humility leads to honor.
13 It's stupid and embarrassing
to give an answer
before you listen.
14Being cheerful helps
when you are sick,
but nothing helps
when you give up.
15Everyone with good sense
wants to learn.
16A gift will get you in
to see anyone.
17You may think you have won
your case in court,
until your opponent speaks.
18Drawing straws is one way
to settle a difficult case.
19Making up with a friend
you have offended
is harder than breaking
through a city wall.
20Make your words good—
you will be glad you did.
21Words can bring death or life!
Talk too much, and you will eat
everything you say.
22 A man's greatest treasure
is his wife—
she is a gift from the Lord.
23The poor must beg for help,
but the rich can give
a harsh reply.
24Some friends don't help,
but a true friend is closer
than your own family.
translation_text:
1Nɛr la n waa nɛra ra nyiŋŋi, ka ra nyiŋŋi u bɛŋ kuaraa,
waa wibii maa ra nuu.
2Wia zɛɛ zumaa waa
gɛnii ra par,
ka ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi
u bagli u nunzuma.
3Di biinikpola haŋ wa ba, hahzi ɔɔ bau,
gunnɛ hiihzi
ni ŋmaaba ɔɔ ba.
4Nɛr wiŋɔzi daŋ wer du luŋ lugɔ muuzeŋ,
nunzuma wiŋɔzi ɛɛ lugɔ
gɔŋ niifalii n na pal.
5A waa dɛkkɛ hiŋ lɛɛ bilii tɛɛ biinikpola hiŋ,
ka kpa bilchɔg
tɛɛ nɛr la
n waa wichɔgii
maa ɛɛwɛ.
6Gɛnii wiŋɔɔlaa ɔɔ ɛɛ kalu nyiŋŋaare,
guŋ ɔɔ gil ba ra lɔɔzuu.
7Gɛnii nuarɛ ra kpuu,
u wiŋɔzi ge
ɛɛ lugɔ sidɛɛ tɛu.
8Zɔɔza wiŋɔzi summɔɔ alugɔ lɔgmɛnanaa nɛr n ɔɔ ligli,
a zuu u bɔra nɛnnɛ.
9Yaara hiŋ ɛɛ nɛr la
n na chɔgi kuna lullii.
10Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ diijaŋ la n kpekke,
nɛr la wia
n deŋlee ɔɔ chɔu
ga zuu u biini
di na u hiŋ.
11Daama hina daama ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bolzeŋkpeg ba be.
Ba ra fɛu lugɔ
nɛr maa wàá wer
tinni u koŋlii
n la chiŋ werge,
di bar bolzeŋ
di ra guu baa.
12Kpoŋaare ɔɔ tɔ chɔgaa see,
sisɔna ge tɔ tɔgzaa see.
13Hiihzi ni gɛnaarɛ hiŋ bagli nɛr wia mɔɔ,
ka haa nuu wii la n ɛɛwɛ.
14Newee miibɔɔ nyiŋŋaa wergee gillɛ u ra yoo wiila,
ka di u wa nyaau,
u tamii maa ɔɔ tunuu.
15Nfɛrɛ hina ɔɔ aah siwiire bá helli wifalaa,
nunzunni ge
ra nuu nfɛrɛ wia.
16Di i ra nyiŋŋi i na nɛzeŋ,
kpa kumbɛl ga sunzuu,
a wàá du kpol.
17Ba waa nɛkpaŋ amaniye ra nuu,
di ra tɛu bilii.
18Di nɛkpega banɛɛ kpogli wia,
ií ta kuna, Kɔraawiizi lizi
a wibii hiŋ.
19Dammu ni zuui kuaraarɛ kpolle kaali diikpeg kpeglaa.
Mmɔri dii
ra bargi dammuzii
alugɔ baŋ kpa lugbidaazi
kar dominua.
20Wiŋɔnanaa ra piŋuu lugɔ diunanaa,
di ra ba bɔsɔna ni.
21Nuarɛ ra kpu, waabuu kaa ra lɛɛ.
Awia, wiŋɔbala werge
ra ba wia ninɛɛ.
22Baal la n na haaŋ, na kumpaa,
a baal wia
ra par Kɔraawiizii.
23Nyaara ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu bá ra suŋ ba ni,
ka dɔɔna ge
ɔɔ ra chagzi baa.
24Dammukpila daŋ wer chɔgii,
ka badɔŋ waa,
ɔɔ pɛliibuu kaali i maabie.

english_text:
It's Wise To Be Patient
1It's better to be poor
and live right
than to be a stupid liar.
2Willingness and stupidity
don't go well together.
If you are too eager,
you will miss the road.
3We are ruined
by our own stupidity,
though we blame the Lord.
4The rich have many friends;
the poor have none.
5Dishonest witnesses and liars
won't escape punishment.
6Everyone tries to be friends
of those who can help them.
7If you are poor,
your own relatives reject you,
and your friends are worse.
When you really need them,
they are not there.
8Do yourself a favor
by having good sense—
you will be glad you did.
9Dishonest witnesses and liars
will be destroyed.
10It isn't right for a fool
to live in luxury
or for a slave to rule
in place of a king.
11It's wise to be patient
and show what you are like
by forgiving others.
12An angry king roars
like a lion,
but when a king is pleased,
it's like dew on the crops.
13Foolish children bring disgrace
to their fathers.
A nagging wife goes on and on
like the drip, drip, drip
of the rain.
14You may inherit all you own
from your parents,
but a sensible wife
is a gift from the Lord.
15If you are lazy
and sleep your time away,
you will starve.
16Obey the Lord's teachings
and you will live—
disobey and you will die.
17Caring for the poor
is lending to the Lord,
and you will be well repaid.
18Correct your children
before it's too late;
if you don't punish them,
trouble will come their way.
19People with bad tempers
are always in trouble,
and they need help
over and over again.
20Pay attention to advice
and accept correction,
so you can live sensibly.
21We may make a lot of plans,
but the Lord will do
what he has decided.
22What matters most is loyalty.
It's better to be poor
than to be a liar.
23Showing respect to the Lord
brings true life—
if you do it, you can relax
without fear of danger.
24Some people are too lazy
to lift a hand
to feed themselves.
25Stupid fools learn good sense
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being corrected.
26Disgraceful children
rob their father
and chase their mother away.
27If you stop learning,
you will forget
what you already know.
28A lying witness makes fun
of the court system,
and criminals think crime
is really delicious.
29A stupid fool should expect
to be punished.
translation_text:
1Hiŋ nyaawɛ ka ɛɛ wibii hiŋ,
aabuu bɔ hiŋ gɛnnɛ,
di nyaa wibii.
2Nɛr la n aah siwii u ɛɛ wii, ka nyaa nfɛrɛ, guŋ waa wer
gɛɛ nɛr la n na hahzi
werge daŋ wer leu.
3Di newee gɛnni wa chɔguu,
u ɔɔ ra pag
Kɔraawiizi ninɛɛ.
4Daama ra ba dammukpila ninɛɛ,
ka nyaari waa
ra duŋŋi baabuu.
5Kara daansɛɛ diiri daŋ na dignitɛraa,
gunnɛ karkanni gba.
6Nɛkpila maa ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu ba wia par hɛri nabɔma,
ka nɛr maa ge
dammu ɛɛ nɛr la
n na sunzi kuna.
7Di nyaari lulla vɛɛu, u dammuzi waa nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ.
U ɔɔ ra hiŋzi
di ra fɔrgi baa,
ka ba ra kaali.
8Nɛr la maa n na nunzuma nɔŋŋi u hinnɛ,
banla wia zɛɛ zumaa
n par baa daŋ nyɛɛli.
9Kara daansɛɛ diiri wàá kaali pɛɛ, di ba waa u digni tɛttɛ,
ba daŋ chɔgi
karkanni ge.
10A waa dɛkkɛ gɛnii n na di u hiŋ
gɛɛ yom di kora
kooribiizi ni!
11Nɛr la n dɔɔ nfɛrɛ baaŋ waa fuuh manaŋ.
Ba ɔɔ ra tɔgzuubuu,
dikuu uŋ ɔɔ gil wia
di ra tɛɛ nɛra wia.
12Koori baaŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyiŋ wiraa,
ka u nɛsunaa ɛɛ lugɔ
ŋmɛnii n sag kooree ni.
13Bie la n gɛnnɛ ra tɛɛ u mɛɛrɛ tɔɔrɔɔ,
haaŋ la n nɔŋŋi kalu,
ge wia ra fuuh baaŋ
alugɔ domarima.
14Mɛɛwaa ni maawaa daŋ wer gil diini ni daama
dau ba biibaala,
ka Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ
niŋ wer tɛɛ
baal haaŋ la
n na nuu wia zɛɛ.
15Yaara hiŋ ɔɔ chɔɔ dɔɔrɛ nɛnnɛ,
ka chɔɔ lɔzi.
16A hiŋ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni la, di dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ,
a vɛɛi ra ba siu ninɛɛ.
17Di i ra hiini nyaara, i ra du Kɔraawiizii kim,
u daŋ bir turgii a kim.
18Tɛr i biizi digna, di ba haa ɛɛ bichalli.
Di haa guŋ ɛɛwɛ,
i daŋ chɔgi ba de dui.
19Nɛr la n dɔɔ baaŋ werge daŋ turgi u kim.
Di i lɛɛ a hiŋ
lii wia biini,
i daŋ kaa kuari lɛɛu
lii aŋhina biini.
20Di i ra nuu baglaa, di ɛɛ sirya í helli,
i daŋ wa dɔɔ
nunzuma ŋmɛnɛbɛl.
21Newee ɔɔ kpa u nfɛrɛɛ ta wikpila jina,
ka Kɔraawiizi
kipattɛ niŋ ɛɛ.
22Nɛr har chigaa ɛɛ wizenne,
nyaari ge bɔ wibii nyaai.
23Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa ra tɛɛ miibɔɔ ni hiŋ dɔɔirɛ,
di ra guui.
24Diwee dii gba ɔɔ ra huah
yaara hiŋ bɔraa.
25Di i tɛr chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri digni, laakal nyaara daŋ helli wia,
di i hau nunzunni ni,
u nunzuma ɔɔ jaau.
26Bie la n na ɛɛ u mɛɛ chumaa
gɛɛ di duŋŋi u maa ha,
wia ɛɛ ŋmaaba
ni hiihzii nɛra be.
27N bie, di i haŋ wa vɛɛ baglaa nuui,
i bir hattɛ
kpu nunzuma la.
28Kara daansɛɛ diiri ra ɛɛ wibii dii chɛɛtɛɛ,
wichɔgaa ɛɛi du sum
tɛɛ biinikpola hina
lugɔ diwee.
29Ba daŋ tɔɔri chɛɛtɛ ɛɛra,
di lɔɔzi gɛnaa ge.

english_text:
Words of Wisdom Are Better than Gold
1It isn't smart to get drunk!
Drinking makes a fool of you
and leads to fights.
2An angry ruler
is like a roaring lion—
make either one angry,
and you are dead.
3It makes you look good
when you avoid a fight—
only fools love to quarrel.
4If you are too lazy to plow,
don't expect a harvest.
5Someone's thoughts may be
as deep as the ocean,
but if you are smart,
you will discover them.
6There are many who say,
“You can trust me!”
But can they be trusted?
7Good people live right,
and God blesses the children
who follow their example.
8When rulers decide cases,
they weigh the evidence.
9Can any of us really say,
“My thoughts are pure,
and my sins are gone”?
10Two things the Lord hates
are dishonest scales
and dishonest measures.
11The good or bad
that children do
shows what they are like.
12Hearing and seeing
are gifts from the Lord.
13If you sleep all the time,
you will starve;
if you get up and work,
you will have enough food.
14Everyone likes to brag
about getting a bargain.
15Sensible words are better
than gold or jewels.
16You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
17The food you get by cheating
may taste delicious,
but it turns to gravel.
18Be sure you have sound advice
before making plans
or starting a war.
19Stay away from gossips—
they tell everything.
20Children who curse their parents
will go to the land of darkness
long before their time.
21Getting rich quick
may turn out to be a curse.
22Don't try to get even.
Trust the Lord,
and he will help you.
23The Lord hates dishonest scales
and dishonest weights.
So don't cheat!
24How can we know
what will happen to us
when the Lord alone decides?
25Don't fall into the trap
of making promises to God
before you think!
26A wise ruler severely punishes
every criminal.
27Our inner thoughts are a lamp
from the Lord,
and they search our hearts.
28Rulers are protected
by God's mercy and loyalty,
but they must be merciful
for their kingdoms to last.
29Young people take pride
in their strength,
but the gray hairs of wisdom
are even more beautiful.
30A severe beating can knock all
of the evil out of you!
translation_text:
1Siŋ nyɔɔi werge ɔɔ giluu nɛr ra ŋɔ wia di ra kɔɔ, di birgi gɛnii.
Nɛr la maa
n kpa siŋ nyɔɔi
su siwii,
wàá dɔɔ nfɛrɛ.
2Koori baaŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyiŋ wiraa,
di nɛr fuuh u baaŋ,
u miibɔɔrɛ u kpa
di ra chɛr siu.
3Ba ɔɔ ra tɔgzi nɛr la n waa kalu ra nyiŋŋuu,
ka gɛnii waa maa
ɔɔ hahzuu ra nyiŋŋi kalu.
4Nɛr la n ɛɛ yaara hiŋ paraa saŋa,
wàá na diwee
kuna kpai saŋa.
5Newee nfɛrɛ wia luŋŋoo lugɔ kɔlɔŋ nii,
ka nunzunni
daŋ lizaa baŋgia.
6Nɛkpila daŋ wer ŋɔ lugɔ ba dɔɔ nɔŋŋaarɛ saŋa maa,
ka anɛɛ n niŋ wer na
nɛr la wia
n dɔɔ wibii nɛnnɛi?
7Nɛr wia n deŋlee de dui waa ɔɔ dɔɔ wichɔgii maa,
u biizi ɔɔ nuu sumaa,
ú siu har.
8Di koori hanna di seriya,
u ɔɔ ra pessi
a wikpoglaa maanii,
di ra ligzi a chɔgaa
di ra lii a nanaa biini.
9Anɛɛ n niŋ wer ŋɔ,
“Maa wichɔgii maa
dɔɔwɛ n biinei?”
10Kɔraawiizi kii banla n kpa fintime mɛgzi kunaa,
di ra mɛgzaa kuna.
11Bichala wiɛɛlaarɛ niŋ bagli lugɔ
u wia deŋloore
gɛɛ a wessoo.
12Kɔraawiizii tɛɛ yaa siwee ni digna,
ya ra na,
di ra nuu wia.
13Nɛr la n nɔŋŋi dɔɔ, hotte nyaari.
Aah siwii di ra hum,
denii i na
diwee di, ka ka.
14Kunyauri ɔɔ ra nuumuu kuŋ yoola n kpolle wiarɛ,
ka di u wa yawuu harha,
u jaa ra kaali
ka ra ta barabara.
15Nunzuma wiŋɔzi waa puttɛ ka dɔɔ tɔna,
di kaali saliŋ ni rubizi.
16Di nɛr gɛnnɔ, di chi tɛɛ hɔɔhri u di kim,
u himmaa kunnɛ
bá lɛɛ dau talma.
17Diuŋmɛɛlaa kpissɔɔ nua,
ka a harbɔɔ,
a ɔɔ birgi kuŋkpolaa
i nua biini.
18Di i ŋɔ i ta jina, gil ba birii liize nɛnnɛ a wer na ɛɛi,
gilɛɛ waa lɔ laal,
di haa baglaa nuuwɛ
lii nɛra be.
19Nɛzɔɔzaa ra pilli woloo,
awia, gilɛɛ gil
i ni wiŋɔbalahiŋ
wàá kpau.
20Di i see i mɛɛ gɛɛ i maa nua,
i hinnɛ i ra kpu alugɔ
fintina n dimme bɔbiri.
21Di i feloo di kapɛttɛ i de dui biini,
guŋwaa, hàá nuu suma
i de dui tuna.
22Gilɛɛ waa kpa wichɔgaa di ra turgi wichɔgaa kim.
Kpa i wiimaa du
Kɔraawiizi nonee,
u daŋ lɛɛi.
23Kɔraawiizi kii banla n kpa fintime mɛgzaa kunaa,
di ra mɛgzi kuna.
24Kɔraawiizii bagli yaa naazi kpai wia,
awia, ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ zum
yaa ŋmɛnivollaa zɛɛi?
25Ɛɛ fɛ nfɛrɛ nɛnnɛ mɔɔ ka ra lɛɛ nua Kɔraawiizi be,
di guŋ lɛi,
i daŋ ŋmɛnɛ wii,
n faa zummɔ.
26Koori la n zum wia ɔɔ pessuu, di zum biinikpola hiŋ,
di tɛr u digni,
wàá suŋ u ni.
27Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ neweere nfɛrɛ alugɔ fintina,
u ra chaanuu,
ú wer zum
u biini wifɛɛlaa.
28Koori la maa n dɔɔ nɔŋŋaa ni wibii saŋa maa, ɔɔ dɔɔ u hinnɛ.
U ɔɔ di koraa
birgi werge.
29Biipɔllaa girmee ba fɔŋŋa,
ka bazɛŋzi ge wessii
ba nyuhuŋhuŋŋa.
30Dignitɛraa ra lizi wichɔgaarɛ di ra ha,
ka ra tɛɛ mananaa.

english_text:
The Lord Is In Charge
1 The Lord controls rulers,
just as he determines
the course of rivers.
2We may think we are doing
the right thing,
but the Lord always knows
what is in our hearts.
3Doing what is right and fair
pleases the Lord
more than an offering.
4Evil people are proud
and arrogant,
but sin is the only crop
they produce.
5If you plan and work hard,
you will have plenty;
if you hurry to get rich,
you will end up poor.
6Cheating to get rich
is a foolish dream
and no less than suicide.
7You destroy yourself
by being cruel and violent
and refusing to live right.
8All crooks are liars,
but anyone who is innocent
will do right.
9 It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
10Evil people want to do wrong,
even to their friends.
11An ignorant fool learns
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being instructed.
12God is always fair!
He knows what the wicked do
and will punish them.
13If you won't help the poor,
don't expect to be heard
when you cry out for help.
14A secret bribe will save you
from someone's fierce anger.
15When justice is done,
good citizens are glad
and crooks are terrified.
16If you stop using good sense,
you will find yourself
in the grave.
17Heavy drinkers and others
who live only for pleasure
will lose all they have.
18God's people will escape,
but all who are wicked
will pay the price.
19It's better out in the desert
than at home with a nagging,
complaining wife.
20Be sensible and store up
precious treasures—
don't waste them
like a fool.
21If you try to be kind and good,
you will be blessed with life
and goodness and honor.
22One wise person can defeat
a city full of soldiers
and capture their fortress.
23Watching what you say
can save you
a lot of trouble.
24If you are proud and conceited,
everyone will say,
“You're a snob!”
25If you want too much
and are too lazy to work,
it could be fatal.
26But people who obey God
are always generous.
27 The Lord despises the offerings
of wicked people
with evil motives.
28If you tell lies in court,
you are done for;
only a reliable witness
can do the job.
29Wicked people bluff their way,
but God's people think
before they take a step.
30No matter how much you know
or what plans you make,
you can't defeat the Lord.
31Even if your army has horses
ready for battle,
the Lord will always win.
translation_text:
1Koori bampirii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ gɔŋ nii Kɔraawiizi nonii biini,
u ɔɔ biruubuu
u ra la bɔr la maa
n paruu.
2Newee ɔɔ fɛ lugɔ u wiɛɛlaa maanii deŋlee,
ka Kɔraawiizii ra di
u biini wia seriya.
3Hinna ɛɛ wideŋlaa di ra di wibiire ra par Kɔraawiizi
kaali mbusu lizaa.
4Kpoŋaa, barabara ani
biinikpola maa
ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ.
5Nɛr la n na ta wia jina nɛnnɛ, di aah siwii ra hum daŋ nyɛɛli,
ka siyala werge
ra ba nyaari ninɛɛ.
6Hiŋ kpa kara di dɔɔ kuna,
a waa birgi ka tuŋ,
ka kaa ɛɛ siu sidɛɛ tɛi.
7Biinikpola hina ɔɔ siuzuu, dikuu ba kalu wia,
dikuu baŋ waa sɛɛwɛ
bá ɛɛ wia la
n deŋlee wia.
8Bilchɔg hina ɔɔ ra hiŋ ŋmɛnizi la n waa deŋleere,
ka banla ge n waa
bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ
ra vol a deŋlaa.
9Sakɛrii sogaare bɔ,
i ni hahkalu hiŋ
n kpau dia.
10Biinikpola hiŋ ɔɔ ra kɛlli wichɔgaarɛ,
waa u dɔŋhiŋ ni ra suŋ.
11Di i tɛr chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri digni, laakal nyaara daŋ helli wia,
di ba wa bagli
nunzunni wia,
u ɔɔ dɔɔ
nunzumaa jaa.
12Kɔraawiizi wia deŋloore. U ɔɔ pessi biinikpola hiŋ dia wiarɛ,
ka kpau ta, u wia tuŋ.
13Nɛr la n tɔɔgi u digna, saŋa la nyaara n na wii la,
ba wàá nuu u ge wiraa,
u anuula saŋa.
14Hiŋ suahzɛɛ sunzi kuŋ ra sɔɔni baannɛ,
suahzaa tɛɛ kuŋ ge
ra pɛssi
baaŋfuuih werge.
15Wibii dii ɔɔ ɛɛ bɔsɔnaa tɛɛ banla n ɛɛ nɛnanaa,
ka ɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ werge
tɛɛ wichɔgɛɛra.
16Nɛr la maa n vɛɛ nfɛrnanaa
daŋ siu.
17Banla n nɔŋŋi sideŋŋa wia ɔɔ birgi nyaaraa,
siŋ, diunanaa ani hindii lɛi,
daama ŋmɛnɛɛ.
18A ba tɛr biinikpola hina dignaa saŋa bɛl,
bá lɛɛ banla n ɛɛ nɛnanaa,
di tɛr banla wia
n waa deŋlee ge hora,
di lɛɛ banla wia n deŋlee.
19Hiŋ du hɛribɔduma biini i bɛnnɛ bɔ,
i ni haaŋ la
n nɔŋŋi nuumaa
ni kalu n kpau dia.
20Nunzunni ɔɔ dɔɔ daamaa di ra di u hiŋ,
ka gɛnii ɔɔ di
u horaa manaŋ,
di u wa naa.
21Nɛr la maa n ɛɛ nɛnanii, di nɔŋŋi nɛra,
daŋ na miibɔɔ,
di nyɛɛli di na tɔgzaa.
22Nunzunni ɔɔ lɔ nɛra la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa bolzenne,
di puri u koŋliikpega
baŋ yardɛɛrɛ.
23Nɛr la maa n zum u nua kpoglaa,
ɔɔ lɛɛ u hinnɛ
lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini.
24Chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri dɔɔ barabaraa,
di ra ɛɛ kpoŋri wia.
25Yaara hiŋ kipar wiarɛ niŋ chɔguu,
dikuu uŋ vɛɛ
huma humaa wia.
26U hotte ú ɔɔ na werge,
ka unla n ɛɛ nɛnanii waa,
ɔɔ ra sunzuu.
27Kɔraawiizi kii wichɔgɛɛra mbusu lizaazii,
fɔŋfɔŋ di ba waa lizaa
ni nfɛrchɔgaa.
28Kara daansɛɛ diiri wàá kaali pɛɛ, di ba waa u digni tɛttɛ,
ka gil unla n na di wibii,
ŋɔ wia.
29Biinikpola hiŋ ɔɔ ra ta barabaraa,
ka nɛr la wia n deŋlee
ɔɔ fɛ nfɛrɛɛ
ka ra ɛɛ u wiɛɛlaa.
30Gunla maa newee jinazi ni u wia zɛɛ zumaa n duwɛɛ,
ka a wàá wer
nyaŋŋi Kɔraawiizi.
31A ba ɛɛ zaguu sirya laal hɔpizii,
ka Kɔraawiizii dɔɔ
laal lɔi kpeglaa fɔŋŋa.

english_text:
The Value of a Good Reputation
1A good reputation and respect
are worth much more
than silver and gold.
2The rich and the poor
are all created
by the Lord.
3When you see trouble coming,
don't be stupid
and walk right into it—
be smart and hide.
4Respect and serve the Lord!
Your reward will be wealth,
a long life, and honor.
5Crooks walk down a road
full of thorny traps.
Stay away from there!
6 Teach your children
right from wrong,
and when they are grown
they will still do right.
7The poor are ruled by the rich,
and those who borrow
are slaves of moneylenders.
8Troublemakers get in trouble,
and their terrible anger
will get them nowhere.
9The Lord blesses everyone
who freely gives food
to the poor.
10Arguments and fights
will come to an end,
if you chase away those
who insult others.
11The king is the friend of all
who are sincere
and speak with kindness.
12The Lord watches over everyone
who shows good sense,
but he frustrates the plans
of deceitful liars.
13Don't be so lazy that you say,
“If I go to work,
a lion will eat me!”
14The words of a bad woman
are like a deep pit;
if you make the Lord angry,
you will fall right in.
15All children are foolish,
but firm correction
will make them change.
16Cheat the poor to make profit
or give gifts to the rich—
either way you lose.
Thirty Wise Sayings
17Here are some sayings
of people with wisdom,
so listen carefully
as I teach.
18You will be glad
that you know these sayings
and can recite them.
19I am teaching them today,
so that you
may trust the Lord.
20I have written thirty sayings
filled with sound advice.
21You can trust them completely
to give you the right words
for those in charge of you.
–1–
22Don't take advantage
of the poor
or cheat them in court.
23The Lord is their defender,
and what you do to them,
he will do to you.
–2–
24Don't make friends with anyone
who has a bad temper.
25You might turn out like them
and get caught in a trap.
–3–
26Don't guarantee to pay
someone else's debt.
27If you don't have the money,
you might lose your bed.
–4–
28Don't move a boundary marker
set up by your ancestors.
–5–
29If you do your job well,
you will work for a ruler
and never be a slave.
translation_text:
1Sɔnnanii kaali daama dɔɔi werge,
banna tɔgzii, aabuu bɔ,
hiŋ dɔɔ saliŋhuŋŋa
ni saliŋ.
2Wii la dɔɔna ni nyaara maa n kpauwɛ zumuu lugɔ
Kɔraawiizii ta ba maa.
3Nunzunni ɔɔ na siaahmuu n na ba,
di suah u hiŋ,
ka nfɛrnyaari ɔɔ zuu
u biinii di tɔɔrɔɔ.
4Sisɔna ni Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa
ra ba daama, girme
ani miibɔɔ ninɛɛ.
5Sɔɔhri ni sidɛɛzi du biinikpola hina ŋmɛnizii,
ka nɛr la maa
n na du u hiŋ tau,
waa ɔɔ duglaa.
6Aah siwii di ra bagli bie ŋmɛnizi la n deŋlee,
di u wa binnɔ,
ka u daŋ haa ra hiŋaa.
7Gunla dɔɔŋ n ɔɔ ra di
fɔŋŋa nyaara ni la,
gunnɛ nɛr la n volle
di ra kim,
ɛɛ unla be
unna kim la, balii.
8Nɛr la n duu biinikpola ra kum tɔɔrɔɔrɛ,
bá chɔgi u baaŋfuuih
werge lugbidaa.
9Nɛr la n dɔɔ kisassa, nuu sumaa,
dikuu uŋ bɔnni u diwee
di ra tɛɛ nyaara wia.
10Duŋŋi chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri, denii hɔɔzi,
naari ani nɛchagzaa tuŋ.
11Nɛr la maa n nɔŋŋi biinihuŋŋu ni wiŋɔnanaa,
daŋ ɛɛ koori dammu.
12Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ ra du nunzunni taurɛ,
ka u ɔɔ chɔgi sɔsɔgɔ hiŋ
waa jinazi tairɛ.
13Yaara hiŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ dawarii lugɔ di u lii baŋgia,
bunyiŋ daŋ lawuu.
14Hahsɛnsɛnni wiŋɔzi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bɔɔluŋ,
banla Kɔraawiizi
baaŋfuuih n du ba ni
daŋ chol u biini.
15Bichala maanii gɛnɛɛ,
ka dignitɛraa daŋ duŋŋi
guŋ lii u be.
16Nɛr la n kpa nyaara sunnaa di gil u daama ra jaa,
gɛɛ di ra sunzi dɔɔna,
nyaarii niŋ ɛɛ u tuna.
Nunzuma wiŋɔɔlaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ wia
17Keŋŋi digna di ra nuu nunzunni wiŋɔzi,
di gil i bampirii
lau n baglaazi,
18dikuubɛɛwiai, a wessoo di i kpaa du i biini,
di gil a du i nua
saŋa maa.
19N na bagliibuu zinaa,
guŋ gil í yardi Kɔraawiizi.
20N sɛbi nunzunni wiŋɔzi tokko ni kpɔrgɔɔ tɛi,
nunzuma ni baglaa
su a biinee.
21Gunnɛ niŋ gil i ɔɔ zum wibii,
di ɔɔ ba amaniye la
n dɔɔ wibii ni,
di wa tɛɛ banla
n humii la.
Luglihiŋ
22Gilɛɛ waa fini nyaari dikuu u nyaari wia,
gɛɛ di wàá fini
dɔgnya hina seriya diiribɔr,
23dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii niŋ ŋɔ lɛɛ baa.
U daŋ piri nɛr la maa
n du baa pira.
Anɛɛhiŋ
24Gilɛɛ waa lau nɛr la baaŋ n na fuuh manamanaŋ dammu,
gɛɛ i nuu waa kpau,
25di guŋ lɛi,
i daŋ helli u wiɛɛlaa,
di zuu siaahmu biini.
Ahorohiŋ
26Gilɛɛ waa chi ra tɛɛ nɛbɛl ú di kim
gɛɛ di wàá dau
talma guŋ wia,
27di haa haŋ wa wer turguu,
ba daŋ foozi
i kunchɔɔrikuŋ
gba himmaa.
Anaazuhiŋ
28Ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa fini i dɔŋhiŋ,
di wàá tuzi faala maa
magbɔɔ bii la
ii naabaala n baŋŋɛ.
Anuehiŋ
29Huŋhunni la n zum huma nɛnnɛ,
danna hum koora huma,
ka a waa lugɔ
nɛsunne humaa ú ra hum.

english_text:
–6–
1When you are invited
to eat with a king,
use your best manners.
2Don't go and stuff yourself!
That would be just the same
as cutting your throat.
3Don't be greedy for all
of that fancy food!
It may not be so tasty.
–7–
4Give up trying so hard
to get rich.
5Your money flies away
before you know it,
just like an eagle
suddenly taking off.
–8–
6Don't accept an invitation
to eat a selfish person's food,
no matter how good it is.
7People like that take note
of how much you eat.
They say, “Take all you want!”
But they don't mean it.
8Each bite will come back up,
and all your kind words
will be wasted.
–9–
9Don't talk to fools—
they will make fun of you.
–10–
10Don't move a boundary marker
or take the land
that belongs to orphans.
11God All-Powerful is there
to defend them against you.
–11–
12Listen to instruction
and do your best to learn.
–12–
13Don't fail to correct
your children.
You won't kill them
by being firm,
14and it may even
save their lives.
–13–
15My children,
if you show good sense,
I will be happy,
16and if you are truthful,
I will really be glad.
–14–
17Don't be jealous of sinners,
but always honor the Lord.
18Then you will truly have hope
for the future.
–15–
19Listen to me, my children!
Be wise and have enough sense
to follow the right path.
20Don't be a heavy drinker
or stuff yourself with food.
21It will make you feel drowsy,
and you will end up poor
with only rags to wear.
–16–
22Pay attention to your father,
and don't neglect your mother
when she grows old.
23Invest in truth and wisdom,
discipline and good sense,
and don't part with them.
24Make your father truly happy
by living right and showing
sound judgment.
25Make your parents proud,
especially your mother.
–17–
26My son, pay close attention,
and gladly follow
my example.
27Bad women and unfaithful wives
are like a deep pit—
28they are waiting to attack you
like a gang of robbers
with victim after victim.
–18–
29Who is always in trouble?
Who argues and fights?
Who has cuts and bruises?
Whose eyes are red?
30Everyone who stays up late,
having just one more drink.
31Don't even look
at that colorful stuff
bubbling up in the glass!
It goes down so easily,
32but later it bites
like a poisonous snake.
33You will see weird things,
and your mind
will play tricks on you.
34You will feel tossed about
like someone trying to sleep
on a ship in a storm.
35You will be bruised all over,
without even remembering
how it all happened.
And you will lie awake asking,
“When will morning come,
so I can drink some more?”
translation_text:
Anumbɛlhiŋ
1Di i ni hɛri nabɔma waa di,
a du tau nɛnnɛ,
2di i ɛɛ dibala hiŋ,
a lau i hiŋ,
3di gilɛɛ waa kɛlli u diunanaa la maa n chigɛ de la ni,
aŋhinabe, u danna
nyiŋŋi u murgii.
Aniidaanɛɛhiŋ
4Gilɛɛ waa kpa kunyiŋŋichɔgaa di waa chɔgmi i hiŋ,
dɔɔ nunzuma,
di ra lau i hiŋ.
5Daama ɔɔ weruu kaali kakpaŋ
alugɔ an dɔɔ keeri
di zaah kaali la.
Ŋmantannaazihiŋ
6Gilɛɛ waa di kposiiri diwee,
gilɛɛ waa kɛlli
u diunanaa ni.
7U ɔɔ ŋɔ i benii, “Di ka nyɔɔ!”
Ka u biini maa lɛi u ra ŋɔ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɔɔ
ra liizi gunla
a kim n makkɛɛ.
8I daŋ hɛɛhzi u diunanaa hiŋ ta,
ka i wiŋɔnanaa la
hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu la ɛɛ pɛɛ.
Kabɛlhiŋ
9Di i ra bagli gɛnii wia, i hinnɛ i ra kuuh,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u baaŋ
daŋ fuuh.
Fihiŋ
10Gilɛɛ wàá tuzi faala maa magbɔɔ bii la
ii naabaala n baŋŋɛ,
di waa foozi lalbiizi hɛri,
11dikuubɛɛwiai, ba guuri Kɔraawiizi kpekkoo.
U himmaa daŋ kpa
ba wia pɛɛzii.
Fidikpaŋhiŋ
12Gil i bampirii lau baglaa,
di gil i digna
ra nuu nfɛrɛ wia.
Fidaanɛɛhiŋ
13Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ bie dignitɛraa,
lɔɔzaa wàá kpuu.
14Viiruu, di tɛr u digni,
di mɔgluu siu be.
