Fidaahorohiŋ
15N bie, di i daŋ ɛɛ nunzunni,
n bɔra daŋ sɔɔniŋ werge.
16A daŋ ɛɛŋ bɔsɔna werge maa,
di i waa ŋɔ
wia la n deŋlee,
di dɔɔ wibii.
Fidaanaazuhiŋ
17Gilɛɛ ra zom wichɔgɛɛra ni,
ka gil Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa
aah i siwii.
18A daŋ du wer tɛi kɛrɛ bɛl, wibii maa,
i tamii wàá ɛɛ pɛɛ maa.
Fidaanuehiŋ
19A nuu n bie, di dɔɔ nunzuma,
di ra hiŋ ŋmɛninanii.
20Gilɛɛ i ni sinnyɔɔri
ni dibala hina ra kpau,
21dikuubɛɛwiai, ba nyaari ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ ba ra vol la.
Dɔɔ chɔɔi werge gillɔɔ
nɛr a laali yakɔssi.
Fidaanumbɛlhiŋ
22A nuu i mɛɛ wiŋɔzi, di zum lugɔ waabuu lulii,
di gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli
i maa ú zɛŋaa saŋa.
23Nyiŋŋi wibii, di lawuu kpogli nɛnnɛ,
di kaa nyiŋŋi nunzuma,
mananaa ani
wia zɛɛ zumaa.
24Bie la n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi mɛɛ ɛɛ bɔsɔna hinnɛ.
Bɔsɔnaa biinunzunni dɔɔi.
25Awia, gil i mɛɛ ni i maa dɔɔ bɔsɔna,
Gil haaŋ la
n lulii la dɔɔ bɔsɔna!
Fidaaniidaanɛɛhiŋ
26N bie, gil i bampirii lawiŋ,
di ra hiŋ n wiɛɛlaa.
27Sɛnsɛnni ni hahyuuri la n na sɛm,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ sidɛɛ chuma.
28U ɔɔ suah di ra kpaŋ alugɔ ŋmɛɛŋ,
di gil baala kpilakpila
nyaa wibii ba haana be.
Fidiŋmantannaazihiŋ
29Anɛɛ dɔɔ wiai? Anɛɛ dɔɔ biinichɔgɛi?
Anɛɛ ɔɔ ra lɔ kalu
saŋa maanɛi?
Anɛɛ ra nuumɛi?
Anɛɛ bɔraa yigli chal pɛɛi?
Anɛɛ sibeere yigli chalɛi?
30A hinnɛ nɛr la n ɔɔ mari sindiini birgi,
di nyɔɔ siŋ
di ra koozi dɔŋa ni.
31Gilɛɛ gil siŋ waa darii, haali uŋ aahwɛ nɛnnɛ,
di ra nyɛgzi gilaasi biini,
u nyɔɔi du sum,
u ra tuu yɔmmmm.
32A tuna maa, u daŋ ɛɛi alugɔ dum n dumii,
alugɔ duŋkpola siri.
33I danna na wikuna,
hàá ka wer
di ra fɛ nfɛrɛ
di ra ŋɔ wia nɛnnɛ.
34I danna jiŋli alugɔ nɛr n du muugberzeŋ biini,
di sag u ŋmɛnni
ni muuzeŋ.
35Denii i ŋɔ, “Aŋhinabe, ba lɔmbuu ka a waa n ni zuuwɛ!
Maa zummɛ
baŋ lɔɔziŋ gba!
Saŋa bɛɛ ń izi
di kaa nyɔɔ sinɛi?”

english_text:
–19–
1Don't be jealous of crooks
or want to be their friends.
2All they think about
and talk about
is violence and cruelty.
–20–
3Use wisdom and understanding
to establish your home;
4let good sense fill the rooms
with priceless treasures.
–21–
5Wisdom brings strength,
and knowledge gives power.
6Battles are won
by listening to advice
and making a lot of plans.
–22–
7Wisdom is too much for fools!
Their advice is no good.
–23–
8No one but troublemakers
think up trouble.
9Everyone hates senseless fools
who think up ways to sin.
–24–
10Don't give up and be helpless
in times of trouble.
–25–
11Don't fail to rescue those
who are doomed to die.
12Don't say, “I didn't know it!”
God can read your mind.
He watches each of us
and knows our thoughts.
And God will pay us back
for what we do.
–26–
13Honey is good for you,
my children,
and it tastes sweet.
14Wisdom is like honey
for your life—
if you find it,
your future is bright.
–27–
15Don't be a cruel person
who attacks good people
and hurts their families.
16Even if good people
fall seven times,
they will get back up.
But when trouble strikes
the wicked,
that's the end of them.
–28–
17Don't be happy
to see your enemies trip
and fall down.
18The Lord will find out
and be unhappy.
Then he will stop
being angry with them.
–29–
19Don't let evil people
worry you
or make you jealous.
20They will soon be gone
like the flame of a lamp
that burns out.
–30–
21My children, you must respect
the Lord and the king,
and you must not make friends
with anyone who rebels
against either of them.
22Who knows what sudden disaster
the Lord or a ruler
might bring?
More Sayings That Make Good Sense
23Here are some more sayings
that make good sense:
When you judge,
you must be fair.
24If you let the guilty
go free,
people of all nations
will hate and curse you.
25But if you punish the guilty,
things will go well for you,
and you will prosper.
26Giving an honest answer
is a sign
of true friendship.
27Get your fields ready
and plant your crops
before starting a home.
28Don't accuse anyone
who isn't guilty.
Don't ever tell a lie
29or say to someone,
“I'll get even with you!”
30I once walked by the field
and the vineyard
of a lazy fool.
31Thorns and weeds
were everywhere,
and the stone wall
had fallen down.
32When I saw this,
it taught me a lesson:
33 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
34Suddenly poverty hits you
and everything is gone!
translation_text:
Fidikabɛlhiŋ
1Gilɛɛ ra zom wichɔgɛɛra ni,
gilɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi
ba bɔkpau,
2dikuu baŋ ɔɔ ra ta
kalu jina wia,
ba wiŋɔzi ge ra ba
tɔɔrɔɔ ni wia.
Tokkohiŋ
3Nunzumaa nɛr ɔɔ kpa ma dia,
wia zɛɛ zumaa ge gil
u du kpeg di chi nɛnnɛ.
4Nfɛrɛ dɔɔi ɔɔ giluu u diini maa suugi
ni daama
kunnanaa maa iri.
Tokko ni kpaŋhiŋ
5Hiŋ dɔɔ nunzumaa bɔ, hiŋ dɔɔ fɔŋŋa,
nfɛrɛ hiŋ ge
fɔŋŋa ra jaau.
6Awia, di haa haŋ wa na baglaa nɛnnɛ, gilɛɛ waa la laal,
dikuubɛɛwiai, laal lɔi
kpegli ra lii
bagla kpila benii.
Tokko ni anɛɛhiŋ
7Nunzuma wiŋɔzi luŋŋoo werge tɛɛ gɛnii.
Awia, di sitɔɔra
wa chaalɔɔ,
waa ɔɔ dɔɔ wiŋɔɔlii maa.
Tokko ni ahorohiŋ
8Nɛr la maa n na ta wichɔgaa jina,
daŋ di a guŋ sɔnchɔgii.
9Gɛnaa jina tai ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ,
nɛra maa ge
hah chɛɛtɛ ɛɛri.
Tokko ni anaazuhiŋ
10Di wia nyaŋŋii tɔɔrɔɔ saŋa,
i fɔŋŋa waa kaŋ.
Tokko ni anuehiŋ
11Lɛɛ banla baŋ laurɛɛ bá ga kpuuzi pɛɛpɛɛ la,
di gilɛɛ wa gil
bá kpuuzi baa.
12Di ii ŋɔ, “Yaa waa a wia zummɛ.”
Kɔraawiizii zum
newea maa bampiree,
di ra naa.
Waabuu ra binni ii de dui ni,
di zum lugɔ ii zummɔɔ!
U daŋ kpa nɛra maa
wiɛɛlaa di di baa seriya.
Tokko ni anumbɛlhiŋ
13N bie, a di huuhnuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a wessoo,
anla n lii a pɛɛna
ni di ra toŋzi la
summɔɔ tɛi.
14Guŋ himmaanii nunzuma du sum tɛi.
Di i nau,
i kɛrɛ bɛl de dui
daŋ du wer,
i tamii ge wàá tuŋ maa.
Tokko ni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ
15Gilɛɛ waa du alugɔ biinikpola hina la n ɔɔ chɔɔ guu,
bá ŋmɛɛ banla wia
n deŋlee diini kuna.
16Gunla maa maga banla wia n deŋlee n niŋ chol, ka ba daŋ izi,
ka hɛhchɔg daŋ chɔgi
biinikpola hina waa.
Tokko ni ŋmantannaazihiŋ
17Gilɛɛ gil a ɛɛi bɔsɔna di i dɔm wa chollo,
di gilɛɛ gil i bɔra sɔɔni
di u lɔ naa jiŋli,
18dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi biini daŋ chɔgi dikuu i wia,
guŋ gil u baaŋ
wàá ka fuuh u ni.
Tokko ni kabɛlhiŋ
19Gilɛɛ waa gil wichɔgɛɛra wia ra tɔɔrii,
di gilɛɛ waa zom
biinikpola hina ni,
20dikuubɛɛwiai, wichɔgɛɛri waa tamii dɔɔwɛ,
u wia daŋ tuŋ manaŋ.
Tokko ni kpɔrgɔhiŋ
21N bie, a ɔm Kɔraawiizi, di ra tɔgzi koori.
Gilɛɛ waa gil i ni nɛra la
n ɛɛ dignikpega hina
ra kpau wiimaa biini,
22dikuubɛɛwiai, a wàá birgi, ka hɛhchɔg chol keŋ hina ni.
Anɛɛ n zum bɔr la
Kɔraawiizi gɛɛ koori
dignitɛraa n niŋ tunɛi?
Nunzuma wiŋɔzi aŋhina
23Nunzunna wiŋɔzi aŋhinaa keŋ.
Di i binni nɛr siwee ka di seriya,
guŋ waa wer.
24Di seriya diiri la n ŋɔ biinikpola hiŋ be lugɔ
waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ,
nɛkpila daŋ seeu nua,
hɛssi hina maa
ŋɔ waa nɛnnɛ ɛɛwɛ.
25Ka banla n ɔɔ tɛr bilchɔg hina digna,
daŋ na kissaa.
26Hiŋ bittɛ sɛɛ wibii wiŋɔzi,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
i badɔŋ n faamii.
27Par i kooni tuŋ mɔɔ,
ka haa ma i dia.
28Gilɛɛ waa di daansɛɛkara di ra chug nɛr la,
n waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ.
29Gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛu gunla uŋ faa ɛɛŋ la!
N daŋ turguu a kim!”
30N ɔɔ ga yaara hina
ni nfɛrnyaara
kooni nuuzii,
31kooree ni sɔɔhri sug a maa biine,
a koŋlaa maa chogli.
32Denii n binnaa, di fɛ nfɛrɛ,
di helli wii naa lii de,
33daari di chɔɔ dɔɔ tama,
di kɔrgi i bɔra heezi tama,
34ka hinna chɔɔ dɔɔ la,
nyaari daŋ chol i ni
alugɔ ŋmɛɛŋchɔgii.

english_text:
More of Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some more
of Solomon's proverbs.
They were copied by the officials
of King Hezekiah of Judah.
2God is praised
for being mysterious;
rulers are praised
for explaining mysteries.
3Who can fully understand
the thoughts of a ruler?
They reach beyond the sky
and go deep in the earth.
4Silver must be purified
before it can be used
to make something of value.
5Evil people must be removed
before anyone can rule
with justice.
6 Don't try to seem important
in the court of a ruler.
7It's better for the ruler
to give you a high position
than for you to be embarrassed
in front of royal officials.
Be sure you are right
8before you sue someone,
or you might lose your case
and be embarrassed.
9When you and someone else
can't get along,
don't gossip about it.
10Others will find out,
and your reputation
will then be ruined.
11The right word
at the right time
is like precious gold
set in silver.
12Listening to good advice
is worth much more
than jewelry made of gold.
13A messenger you can trust
is just as refreshing
as cool water in summer.
14Broken promises
are worse than rain clouds
that don't bring rain.
15Patience and gentle talk
can convince a ruler
and overcome any problem.
16Eating too much honey
can make you sick.
17Don't visit friends too often,
or they will get tired of it
and start hating you.
18Telling lies about friends
is like attacking them
with clubs and swords
and sharp arrows.
19A friend you can't trust
in times of trouble
is like having a toothache
or a sore foot.
20Singing to someone
in deep sorrow
is like pouring vinegar
in an open cut.
21 If your enemies are hungry,
give them something to eat.
And if they are thirsty,
give them something
to drink.
22This will be the same
as piling burning coals
on their heads.
And the Lord
will reward you.
23As surely as rain blows in
from the north,
anger is caused
by cruel words.
24It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
25Good news from far away
refreshes like cold water
when you are thirsty.
26When a good person gives in
to the wicked,
it's like dumping garbage
in a stream of clear water.
27Don't eat too much honey
or always want praise.
28Losing self-control
leaves you as helpless
as a city without a wall.
translation_text:
Koori Solomɔn sɛɛliizii haa keŋ
1Koori Solomɔn sɛɛliizi aŋhina, Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia karchizenaa n binnɛɛ ka sɛbuu keŋ.
2Yaa ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizii dikuu u wisuahlaa wia,
di ra tɔgzi koora
dikuu a zɛɛzi baglaa wia.
3Gunla nɛr maa n wàá wer zum chiŋ maga ni hɛri luŋzi maga la,
gunnɛ nɛr maa
wàá wer zum
koori biini wia.
4Lizi saliŋhuŋŋa doŋa ha,
ka nɛr la
n zum nonii huma
kpau kuari kunnanii,
5gunnɛ di ba duŋŋi biinikpola hina lii koori be,
u kora daŋ chi,
dikuu wibii dii wia.
6Gilɛɛ waa kpa i hiŋ zenni koori see
gɛɛ di wàá tɔgzi i hiŋ,
7dikuubɛɛwiai, di u wa ŋɔ i be lugɔ i tinni wa so nabɔmbɔr,
aabuu bɔ, uŋ kpa
i bɔr hiŋ tɛɛ nabɔma.
8Gilɛɛ waa yali siwee di ra la seriya diiribɔr,
dikuu hiŋ na
wii bɛl wia,
ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛ a tuna,
di i dɔŋhiŋ la
wa ŋɔ wia dii,
hiihzi kpuinɛi?
9Awia, di i ni i dɔŋhiŋ di mmɔri,
gil i nuu bɛŋ ŋɔa.
Gilɛɛ waa kali nɛr maa,
10di guŋ lɛi, di nɛr maa wa nua, u daŋ kpa hiihzi kpui.
Denii hàá ka wer dɔɔ
sɔnnanii la
hiŋ faa dɔɔwɛ la.
11Wiŋɔzi ŋɔi nɛnnɛ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
baŋ kpa saliŋ margi
saliŋhuŋŋu ni.
12Nunzunni n hau nɛr la digna n na nuu wia,
wessoo kaali baŋaa kuŋ
baŋ kpa saliŋ
kuari tɛɛ nɛr.
13Balii la wia n dɔɔ wibii ra sɔɔni bɔraa
alugɔ wem
maga pechule.
U wia ɔɔ sɔɔni
u dɔɔri bɔraa.
14Nɛr la n ɔɔ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ sunzi, ka wàá ɛɛ guŋ,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baamazi ni
peu la n waa dooŋ dɔɔwɛ.
15Kanyitti ɔɔ weruu tɛɛ koori laakal,
wiŋɔzi bɔɔiih ge
ra bir nɛr la wia
n kpolle nfɛrɛ.
16Di i na huuhnuu, diu mɛgzi,
di i diu werge,
i daŋ hɛɛhzi.
17Di i ra la i dɔŋhiŋ dia digiidigii,
i wia daŋ wa bazuu.
18Kara kannaa chug nɛra ra du baabuu pira,
alugɔ hiŋ kpa gulii
lɔɔzi baa
gɛɛ hiŋ kpa tokobi
du baa pira
gɛɛ hiŋ kpa hobidiilaa
taazi baa.
19Hiŋ kpa i haali maa du nɛr la wia n waa wibii dɔɔwɛ ni,
ɛɛwɔɔ alugɔ hiŋ kpa
i nyiŋ la n na wii
di ra chaŋŋi kuna
gɛɛ di ra vol
i naa la n kuwee ni.
20Hiŋ yir yira la n na pur bɔra di ra tɛɛ biinichɔg hiŋ,
chummɔɔ lugɔ hiŋ wir
nɛr tagta waari saŋa
gɛɛ hiŋ kpa yazi
di ra billi ŋmɛr.
21Di lɔzi waa kpu i dɔm, nyiŋŋi diwee tɛu ú di.
Di niinyɔgzi lawuu,
ɛɛ nii tɛu ú nyɔɔ.
22Di i wetto ɛɛ guŋ tɛu, hiihzi daŋ lawuu.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ turgii a kim.
23Gunla wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag peu n ɔɔ ba dooŋ ni la,
gunnɛ zɔɔza
ra fuuh baaŋ.
24Sakɛrii sogaare bɔ,
i ni hahkalu hiŋ n kpau dia.
25Amaniyesuma n lii hɛhjaŋa
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niisɔŋ
tɛɛ niinyɔgzi hiŋ.
26Di nɛnanii sɛɛwɔ tɛɛ biinikpola hiŋ,
guŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
baŋ kpa siri du kɔlɔŋ
gɛɛ baŋ pur bule.
27Gunla huuhnuu dii werge n waa wer la,
gunnɛ sɔŋ nyiŋŋaa
werge waa wer.
28Nɛr la n wàá wer lau u hiŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
bolzeŋ la baŋ lɔwɛɛ
di purgi u koŋlaa.

english_text:
Don't Be a Fool
1Expecting snow in summer
and rain in the dry season
makes more sense
than honoring a fool.
2A curse you don't deserve
will take wings and fly away
like a sparrow or a swallow.
3Horses and donkeys
must be beaten and bridled—
and so must fools.
4Don't make a fool of yourself
by answering a fool.
5But if you answer any fools,
show how foolish they are,
so they won't feel smart.
6Sending a message by a fool
is like chopping off your foot
just to spite yourself.
7A fool with words of wisdom
is like an athlete
with legs that can't move.
8Are you going to honor a fool?
Why not shoot a slingshot
with the rock tied tight?
9A thornbush waved around
in the hand of a drunkard
is no worse than a proverb
in the mouth of a fool.
10It's no smarter to shoot arrows
at every passerby
than it is to hire a bunch
of worthless nobodies.
11 Dogs return to eat their vomit,
just as fools repeat
their foolishness.
12There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who says,
“I'm really smart!”
13Don't be lazy and keep saying,
“There's a lion outside!”
14A door turns on its hinges,
but a lazy person
just turns over in bed.
15Some of us are so lazy
that we won't lift a hand
to feed ourselves.
16A lazy person says,
“I am smarter
than everyone else.”
17It's better to take hold
of a mad dog by the ears
than to take part
in someone else's argument.
18It's no crazier to shoot
sharp and flaming arrows
19than to cheat someone and say,
“I was only fooling!”
20Where there is no fuel
a fire goes out;
where there is no gossip
arguments come to an end.
21Troublemakers start trouble,
just as sparks and fuel
start a fire.
22There is nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
23Hiding hateful thoughts
behind smooth talk
is like coating a clay pot
with a cheap glaze.
24The pleasant talk
of an enemy
hides more evil plans
25than can be counted—
so don't believe a word!
26Everyone will see through
those evil plans.
27 If you dig a pit,
you will fall in;
if you start a stone rolling,
it will roll back on you.
28Watch out for anyone
who tells lies and flatters—
they are out to get you.
translation_text:
1Gunla dooŋ n waa dɛg lumaŋa gɛɛ kuna kumaa saŋa la,
gunnɛ gɛnii waa dɛg tɔgzaa.
2Nuuseei wàá wer dii, di wɛɛ dɛkkɛ.
A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zumbee
n ɔɔ zaah di waa kaali,
ka waa togni la.
3Virma dɛg zaguu, kabarga ge dɛg kawee,
gunnɛ bulaali
dɛg gɛnii ge!
4Gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ gɛnii pɛɛzaazi,
di guŋ lɛi,
i daŋ gɛni lugɔu.
5Di gɛnii ŋɔ gɛnni wiŋɔzi, bir ŋɔ gɛnni wiŋɔzi chemuu,
ú zum lugɔ
waa wiimaa zummɛ.
6Hiŋ yatti gɛnii di kpa tile tɛu,
ɛɛ gɛnaarɛ alugɔ
hiŋ teŋri i naazi
gɛɛ hiŋ nyɔɔ siri.
7Gunla gbɛrii naazi n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ la,
gunnɛ gɛnii sɛɛliizi
waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ.
8Gɛnii tɔgzaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
nɛr n vɔɔ bii
mari bilori ni.
9Gɛnii sɛɛlii chummɔɔ lugɔ sɔɔh n tɔɔh nɛr la
n nyɔɔ siŋ dɛɛzi nonii,
di ku du.
10Nɛr la n kpa gɛnii huma,
ra tɔɔri nɛkpilaa.
11Gunla nuahiŋ n ɔɔ ug ka bir paagaa di la,
gunnɛ gɛnii ɔɔ ra
dammi u wiɛɛlaa.
12Gɛniirɛ dɔɔ tamii werge kaali
nɛr la n na fɛ lugɔ
u ɛɛ nunzunnii.
13Yaara hiŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ dawarii, lugɔ di u lii baŋgia,
bunyiŋ daŋ lawuu.
14Gunla gbera n ɔɔ ra birgi di ra la see ni har la,
gunnɛ yaara hiŋ ɔɔ chɔɔ
u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni
di ra birgi.
15Diwee dii gba ɔɔ ra huah
yaara hiŋ bɔraa.
16Yaara hiŋ ɔɔ ra fɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ nunzunnii,
di kaali nɛra baniidaanɛɛ la
n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ wia nɛnnɛ.
17Hiŋ kpa i nua jaa kalu la n waa i hor ɛɛwɛ biini,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hiŋ lau
nuahiŋ hɔɔhri digna.
18Chuglahiŋ n na
taazi hobee la n na kpu,
19ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr la n dar u dɔŋ
ka ŋɔ, “N na duau!”
20Di nindaazi bɛllɔ tuŋ, niŋ ɔɔ dimuu,
di zɔɔza ge tunnɔ,
kalu ɔɔ tunuu.
21Gunla hɔla n ɔɔ wo di mazi, daazi gil niŋ ra lau la,
gunnɛ kalu nyiŋŋi
ɔɔ ra du kalu.
22Zɔɔza wiŋɔzi summɔɔ alugɔ lɔgmɛnanaa nɛr n ɔɔ ligli,
a zuu u bɔra nɛnnɛ.
23Nɛr n ɔɔ kpa wiŋɔnanaa di suah u biinikpola la,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baŋ kpa
kunnyɛgzaa faa vii,
hàá wer zum lugɔ
chuurii ba kpa mau la.
24Machɔgaa hiŋ ɔɔ kpa wiŋɔsumaa suah u manni,
ú dar nɛra.
25Di u waa ŋɔ nɔŋŋaa wiŋɔzi gba, gilɛɛ waa yarduu,
wichɔgaa kpila maanii
su u biini.
26Haali uŋ kpa dawari suah u hahzi gba,
ka u biinikpola daŋ ŋmɛnɛ
lii chaaŋ, nɛr maa na.
27Di nɛr he u dɔŋhiŋ sidɛɛ, u daŋ bir lau u himmaa,
di u billi bii
ú ta u dɔŋhiŋ ni,
u daŋ bir ba u ni.
28Karkanni hah banla uŋ kanni karaa di ra chug,
nuusum ge ra ba
chɔgaa ni.

english_text:
Don't Brag about Tomorrow
1 Don't brag about tomorrow!
Each day brings
its own surprises.
2Don't brag about yourself—
let others praise you.
3Stones and sand are heavy,
but trouble caused by a fool
is a much heavier load.
4An angry person is dangerous,
but a jealous person
is even worse.
5A truly good friend
will openly correct you.
6You can trust a friend
who corrects you,
but kisses from an enemy
are nothing but lies.
7If you have had enough to eat,
honey doesn't taste good,
but if you are really hungry,
you will eat anything.
8When you are far from home,
you feel like a bird
without a nest.
9The sweet smell of incense
can make you feel good,
but true friendship
is better still.
10Don't desert an old friend
of your family
or visit your relatives
when you are in trouble.
A friend nearby is better
than relatives far away.
11My child, show good sense!
Then I will be happy
and able to answer anyone
who criticizes me.
12Be cautious and hide
when you see danger—
don't be stupid and walk
right into trouble.
13You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
14A loud greeting
early in the morning
is the same as a curse.
15The steady dripping of rain
and the nagging of a wife
are one and the same.
16It's easier to catch the wind
or hold olive oil in your hand
than to stop a nagging wife.
17Just as iron sharpens iron,
friends sharpen the minds
of each other.
18Take care of a tree,
and you will eat its fruit;
look after your master,
and you will be praised.
19You see your face in a mirror
and your thoughts
in the minds of others.
20Death and the grave
are never satisfied,
and neither are humans.
21Gold and silver are tested
in a red-hot furnace,
but we are tested by praise.
22No matter how hard
you beat a fool,
you can't pound out
the foolishness.
23You should take good care
of your sheep and goats,
24because wealth and honor
don't last forever.
25After the hay is cut
and the new growth appears
and the harvest is over,
26you can sell lambs and goats
to buy clothes and land.
27From the milk of the goats,
you can make enough cheese
to feed your family
and all your servants.
translation_text:
1Gilɛɛ waa jigsi dikuu kɛrɛ wia,
dikuubɛɛwiai, haa zum
wii la n niŋ ba.
2Gilɛɛ waa chɔli i hiŋ,
gil nɛra chɔlii.
3Bii tɔkkɔɔ, hɛɛhraa gba du tɔg,
ka gɛnii n fuuh i baannɛ
tɔkkɛ kaali a maa.
4Baaŋ chummɔɔ, baaŋfuuihchɔgaa ɛɛ lugɔ muu n suwee gi,
ka zomaa chummɛ
kaali a maa.
5Hiŋ hau nɛr ni u sibɔɔrɛ bɔ,
uŋ fɛ lugɔ
i baga lɛi u wia.
6I dammu n dui piraa bɔ,
ka di i dɔm faamii,
di jaamii, a du tau!
7Huuhnuu ɔɔ ɛɛu lugɔ aŋ sɛppɛ tɛɛ nɛr la n piŋŋɛ,
ka diukpola gba summɔɔ
tɛɛ nɛr la lɔzi n na kpu.
8Nɛr la maa n lii u dia ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
zumbee n lii u daŋ biini.
9Gunla tulaale ni daahɛgsɔɔhsuma sɔɔh n summɛ nɛr be la,
gunnɛ badɔŋ
baglaa du sum.
10Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ i dammu ni i mɛɛ dammu di ra ha.
Dikuubɛɛwiai, di wia wa huuzii,
baabuu niŋ
hiinii manaŋ,
di kaali i lulli la
n du bɔɔnɛɛ.
11N bie, n bɔra daŋ sɔɔniŋ di i birgi nunzunni!
Denii ń wer ŋɔ wia chem
n haahra nɛnnɛ,
di ba waa ŋɔ n wia.
12Nɛr la n dɔɔ nfɛrɛ nɛnnɛ ɔɔ na siaahmuu n na ba, di suah u hiŋ,
ka nfɛrnyaari ɔɔ zuu
u biinii di tɔɔrɔɔ.
13Di nɛr gɛnnɔ, di chi tɛɛ hɔɔhri u di kim,
u himmaa kunnɛ
bá lɛɛ dau talma.
14Di i feloo kɔɔ chɔɔzi i dɔŋhiŋ chɔɔzimpikke ni,
guŋ daŋ fuuh
u baaŋ alugɔ nuuseei.
15Hahkalu nyiŋŋi ge wia
ra fuuh baannɛ
alugɔ domarima.
16U laafaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hiŋ ŋɔ i laafi peu
gɛɛ hiŋ mur nuuteela.
17Gunla baŋ ɔɔ kpa lugbii di sazi u dɔŋ la,
gunnɛ nɛr ɔɔ helli
nunzuma lii u dɔŋhiŋ be.
18Nɛr la n na binni fig daa ni daŋ wer di u nɔna,
gunnɛ ba ra tɔgzi
nɛr la ge n na du
u nabɔma tau.
19Gunla nɛr n ɔɔ na u duula digii biini la,
gunnɛ u nfɛrɛ
ra bagli u manni.
20Gunla lalaa bol n waa su la,
gunnɛ newee siwii
waa su.
21Ninne ba ɔɔ kpa ŋmɛɛri saliŋhuŋŋu ni saliŋ,
bá zum a wessi,
gunnɛ ba ɔɔ kpa chɔlaa
ɛɛ newee na.
22Hàá wer bargi gɛnii lii u gɛnni ni,
haali di i
chɔguu alugɔ mia,
tugree biini gba.
23Zum gunla i sela n duwɛɛ,
di ra du a tau nɛnnɛ,
24dikuubɛɛwiai, daama waa ɔɔ du de di hanna la,
hɛssi hina gba
wàá du de
di hanna la.
25Di ba haŋ wa paa kɔlaa,
di ŋmɛnni bizenaa
nyuuni kooree,
kooriifalaa ɔɔ liiu,
di ra hel.
26I daŋ na peeza huna suah i laala,
di yoo buuna yau hɛri.
27I daŋ na buuna ilanii a hel
i ni i diahina ani i balaa.

english_text:
The Law of God Makes Sense
1Wicked people run away
when no one chases them,
but those who live right
are as brave as lions.
2In time of civil war
there are many leaders,
but a sensible leader
restores law and order.
3When someone poor takes over
and mistreats the poor,
it's like a heavy rain
destroying the crops.
4Lawbreakers praise criminals,
but law-abiding citizens
always oppose them.
5Criminals don't know
what justice means,
but all who respect the Lord
understand it completely.
6It's better to be poor
and live right,
than to be rich
and dishonest.
7It makes good sense
to obey the Law of God,
but you disgrace your parents
if you make friends
with worthless nobodies.
8If you make money by charging
high interest rates,
you will lose it all to someone
who cares for the poor.
9God cannot stand the prayers
of anyone who disobeys
his Law.
10By leading good people to sin,
you dig a pit for yourself,
but all who live right
will have a bright future.
11The rich think highly
of themselves,
but anyone poor and sensible
sees right through them.
12When an honest person wins,
it's time to celebrate;
when crooks are in control,
it's best to hide.
13If you don't confess your sins,
you will be a failure.
But God will be merciful
if you confess your sins
and give them up.
14The Lord blesses everyone
who is afraid to do evil,
but if you are cruel,
you will end up in trouble.
15A ruler who mistreats the poor
is like a roaring lion
or a bear hunting for food.
16A heartless leader is a fool,
but anyone who refuses
to get rich by cheating others
will live a long time.
17Don't give help to murderers!
Make them stay on the run
for as long as they live.
18Honesty will keep you safe,
but everyone who is crooked
will suddenly fall.
19Work hard, and you will have
a lot of food;
waste time, and you will have
a lot of trouble.
20God blesses his loyal people,
but punishes all who want
to get rich quick.
21It isn't right to be unfair,
but some people can be bribed
with only a piece of bread.
22Don't be selfish
and eager to get rich—
you will end up worse off
than you can imagine.
23Honest correction
is appreciated
more than flattery.
24If you cheat your parents
and don't think it's wrong,
you are a common thief.
25Selfish people cause trouble,
but you will live a full life
if you trust the Lord.
26Only fools would trust
what they alone think,
but if you live by wisdom,
you will do all right.
27Giving to the poor
will keep you from poverty,
but if you close your eyes
to their needs,
everyone will curse you.
28When crooks are in control,
everyone tries to hide,
but when they lose power,
good people are everywhere.
translation_text:
1Biinikpola hiŋ ɔɔ ra chɔu, di nɛr maa wɔɔ ra duŋŋi,
ka unla n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi,
ɔɔ dɔɔ bampiriire alugɔ bunyiŋ.
2Di hɛri maa nɛra waa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ba ɔɔ dɔɔ koorikpilaa,
ka unla sitɔɔra n ɛɛ nunzunna,
u ɔɔ dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa
chi nɛnnɛ.
3Koori la n na sunni nyaara,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ dooŋ la
n na chɔgi kuna.
4Banla n na vɛɛ Gbɔg hiŋaa, ɔɔ ra chɔli biinikpola hinaa,
ka banla ge n na hiŋaa,
ɔɔ ra naa baabuu.
5Biinikpola hina waa wibii zɛɛ zummɛ,
ka banla n na hiŋ
Kɔraawiizi zum
u zɛɛrɛ nɛnnɛ.
6Hiŋ nyaawɛ ka ɛɛ wibii hiŋ,
aabuu bɔ hiŋ dɔɔwɛ
ka i wia waa deŋlee.
7Biipɔllii la n na hiŋ Gbɔg ɛɛ nunzunnii,
ka unla n na hiŋ nɛjagazi,
kpa hiihzii ra kpu u mɛɛ.
8Nɛr la n na kim nɛra kebee di ra sag nii,
u daama daŋ wa
mag nɛr la
n nɔŋŋi nyaari wia
nonee biini.
9Nɛr la maa n vɛɛ gbɔg hiŋaa,
Kɔraawiizi kii
u wiisuŋŋaarɛ.
10Di i dar nɛr la wia n deŋlee u ɛɛ wichɔgaa,
i daŋ chol
i himmaa sidɛɛ biini,
ka unla wia n dɔɔ wibii,
daŋ di winanaa kapɛttɛ.
11Dɔɔŋ ɔɔ fɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ nunzunnii,
ka nyaari la
n zum wia zɛɛ
zum u mannii.
12Di nɛr la n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi haŋ wa nyɛɛli,
nɛr maa bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔnuu.
Ka di biinikpola hiŋ haŋ wa ɛɛ sitɔɔri,
nɛr maa ɔɔ
chɔu di ra suah.
13Nɛr la n na suah u wichɔgaa wàá nyɛɛli,
ka unla n ɔɔ vɛɛa,
di sɛɛ chɔgri,
Kɔraawiizi daŋ suŋ u ni.
14Nɛr la n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi saŋa maa, nuu sumaa,
ka unla n kpoŋŋe
daŋ na siaahmu werge.
15Koori la n dɔɔ biinikpola nyaara ni,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyiŋ
n na pogzi,
gɛɛ amani n nyɛkkɛ
di ra lauri baa.
16Koori la n gɛnnɛɛrɛ ra fir u nɛra,
ka unla n hah wikara,
daŋ di kora di birgi.
17Nɛr n na di tɔɔrɔɔ werge, dikuu uŋ kpu nɛr wia,
u himmaa bɔɔrɛ u ra ki.
Nɛr maa gilɛɛ mɔgluu.
18Nɛr la wia n deŋlee daŋ na u hiŋ,
ka unla wia
n waa deŋlee daŋ chol.
19Patti la n aah siwii di ra hum,
daŋ na diwee werge
di ra di,
ka gɛnii waa,
ɔɔ ra chɔgi
u saŋaa humpɛɛri ni.
20Banla wia n dɔɔ wibii daŋ na kissaa werge,
ka banla n hahzee
di ra nyiŋŋi
daama manaŋ,
daŋ zuu tɔɔrɔɔ biini.
21Di i binni nɛr siwee ka di seriya, guŋ waa wer.
Ka baŋhina ɔɔ
ɛɛ guŋ wichɔgaarɛ,
dikuu baŋ lɛɛ
kunjiga bɛl wia.
22Kpossiiri ɔɔ ra yali siweere ú birgi daama hiŋ manaŋ,
ka waa zummɛ lugɔ
nyaarii niŋ ba u ni.
23Di i di nɛr wibii di deŋluu,
aabuu niŋ paruu a tuna,
di kaali nuusum.
24Hiŋ kpa fɔŋŋa di ra ŋmɛɛ i mɛɛ ni i maa, ka ra ŋɔ,
“Bɛɛ a ra ɛɛi?”
A guŋ ɛɛ siaahmuu
alugɔ hiŋ kpu nɛr.
25Kposiiri ɔɔ koozi wiarɛ du nɛra,
ka unla n yardi
Kɔraawiizi daŋ nyɛɛli.
26Gɛniirɛ ra yardi u hiŋ,
unla n na hiŋ nunzuma
dɔɔ u hinnɛ.
27Nɛr la maa n na sunzi nyaara kuna wàá nyaa maa.
Ka nuuseezi daŋ di unla
n ɔɔ bir har kpu baa.
28Di biinikpola hiŋ haŋ wa ɛɛ sitɔɔri,
nɛr maa ɔɔ chɔu di ra suah,
ka di hɛhchɔg
wa chol u ni,
banla ge n na ɔm
Kɔraawiizi la ɔɔ nyɛɛluu.

english_text:
Use Good Sense
1If you keep being stubborn
after many warnings,
you will suddenly discover
you have gone too far.
2When justice rules a nation,
everyone is glad;
when injustice rules,
everyone groans.
3If you love wisdom
your parents will be glad,
but chasing after bad women
will cost you everything.
4An honest ruler
makes the nation strong;
a ruler who takes bribes
will bring it to ruin.
5Flattery is nothing less
than setting a trap.
6Your sins will catch you,
but everyone who lives right
will sing and celebrate.
7The wicked don't care
about the rights of the poor,
but good people do.
8Sneering at others is a spark
that sets a city on fire;
using good sense can put out
the flames of anger.
9Be wise and don't sue a fool.
You won't get satisfaction,
because all the fool will do
is sneer and shout.
10A murderer hates everyone
who is honest
and lives right.
11Don't be a fool
and quickly lose your temper—
be sensible and patient.
12A ruler who listens to lies
will have corrupt officials.
13The poor and all who abuse them
must each depend on God
for light.
14Kings who are fair to the poor
will rule a long time.
15Correct your children,
and they will be wise;
children out of control
disgrace their mothers.
16Crime increases
when crooks are in power,
but law-abiding citizens
will see them fall.
17If you correct your children,
they will bring you peace
and happiness.
18Without guidance from God
law and order disappear,
but God blesses everyone
who obeys his Law.
19 Even when servants are smart,
it takes more than words
to make them obey.
20There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who speaks
without thinking.
21Slaves that you treat kindly
from their childhood
will cause you sorrow.
22A person with a quick temper
stirs up arguments
and commits a lot of sins.
23Too much pride brings disgrace;
humility leads to honor.
24If you take part in a crime
you are your worst enemy,
because even under oath
you can't tell the truth.
25Don't fall into the trap
of being a coward—
trust the Lord,
and you will be safe.
26Many try to make friends
with a ruler,
but justice comes
from the Lord.
27Good people and criminals
can't stand each other.
translation_text:
1Nɛr la maa n kpoŋŋe di vɛɛ baglaa,
daŋ ŋmɛnɛ zuu wia biini,
wàá na lɛɛi.
2Di nɛr la n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi haŋ wa nyɛɛli, nɛr maa bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔnuu.
Ka di biinikpola hiŋ
haŋ wa ɛɛ sitɔɔri,
nɛr maa ɔɔ ra nuumuu.
3Nɛr la n na nyiŋŋi nunzuma ɔɔ tɛɛ u mɛɛrɛ bɔsɔna,
ka di u ni
sɛnsɛnna ra kpau,
u daama ɔɔ tunuu.
4Koori la n na di wibii ɔɔ giluu u hɛri chi nɛnnɛ,
ka unla n na
nyiŋŋi kebee
ɔɔ ra chɔguubuu.
5Di i ra chɔli nɛra ni nuusum,
sidɛɛrɛ i ra he i hiŋ la.
6Biinikpola hiŋ wichɔgaa ɔɔ biruu diu,
ka nɛr la wia n deŋlee
ɔɔ lii wia biinii,
di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.
7Banla wia n deŋlee ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu nyaari na wibii,
ka biinikpola hina waa
baga lɛi guŋ wia.
8Chɛɛtɛ ɛɛra daŋ wer koozi bolzeŋ,
ka nunzunna waa
ɔɔ sɔɔni baannɛ.
9Di nunzunni ni gɛnii la seriya diiribɔr,
gɛnii la ɔɔ ra mamuu,
di ra kɔɔ di ra chagzi,
bampirsɔna waa ɔɔ du de.
10Nɛra la n nɔŋŋi nɛkpui, ɔɔ hah nɛr la wia n dɔɔ wibiire,
ka banla wia n deŋlee
ɔɔ guu wibii hinnɛ.
11Gɛnii ɔɔ giluu u baaŋfuuih lii chaaŋ werge maa,
ka nunzunni ɔɔ weruu
di kanyitti di lau u hiŋ.
12Di koori ra nuu kara,
u zɛɛsogna maa
daŋ ɛɛ biinikpola hina.
13Kunnaabuu nyaara ni banla n na sunni baa maa dɔɔ,
Kɔraawiizii tɛɛ
ba maa siwee ba ra na.
14Koori la n na di nyaari seriya ni wibii,
daŋ di kora di birgi.
15Hiŋ tɛr bie digni di deŋluu ra tɛubuu nunzuma,
ka bie pɔɔih kpa hiihzii
ra kpu u maa.
16Di biinikpola hina haŋ wàá di nabɔmuu, wichɔgaa ɔɔ nyaŋŋuu.
Ka nɛra la wia n deŋlee,
daŋ du de
di na ba cholaa.
17Di i tɛr i biizi digna,
ba daŋ tɛi bɔsɔna
ni bampirsɔna.
18Hɛri la nɛra n waa Kɔraawiizi nua ra hiŋ, ɛɛ kuntaalaarɛ,
ka bɔsɔna hinaa
banla n na hiŋ
Kɔraawiizi nua.
19Nua bɛŋ kpai dɛɛzi balii wàá wer hinuu,
see dignitɛraa n jaawɛ.
Aŋhinabe u daŋ nuu
i wiŋɔzi hiŋ zɛɛ,
ka wàá hiŋaa.
20Gɛniirɛ dɔɔ tamii kaali
nɛr la n hahzee
di ra ŋɔ wia.
21Balii la baŋ pɔɔhwɛ lii u bichalli saŋa,
daŋ ŋmɛnɛ tɛi biinichɔg.
22Nɛr la baaŋ n waa birgi fuuih,
ɔɔ ra izi kaluu
di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge.
23Barabara hiŋ ɔɔ di hiihzii,
ka sisɔna hiŋ waa,
ɔɔ na girmee.
24Di i ra hiini ŋmɛɛŋ, i hinnɛ i ra du pira,
di i pilli u wolo,
ba daŋ tɛr i digni,
ka Kɔraawiizi
daŋ seei nua,
di i kaa tɔ u wolo ge.
25Newee ɔmaa ɛɛ sidɛɛrɛ,
ka nɛr la maa n yardi
Kɔraawiizi, na u hinnɛ.
26Nɛkpila maa ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi ba wia par koorii,
ka Kɔraawiizi benii
newee ɔɔ na wibii.
27Banla wia n deŋlee, ɔɔ hah biinikpola hinaa,
biinikpola hina
ge hah baa.

english_text:
The Sayings of Agur
1These are the sayings
and the message
of Agur son of Jakeh.
Someone cries out to God,
“I am completely worn out!
How can I last?
2I am far too stupid
to be considered human.
3I never was wise,
and I don't understand
what God is like.”
4 Has anyone gone up to heaven
and come back down?
Has anyone grabbed hold
of the wind?
Has anyone wrapped up the sea
or marked out boundaries
for the earth?
If you know of any
who have done such things,
then tell me their names
and their children's names.
5Everything God says is true—
and it's a shield for all
who come to him for safety.
6Don't change what God has said!
He will correct you and show
that you are a liar.
7There are two things, Lord,
I want you to do for me
before I die:
8Make me absolutely honest
and don't let me be too poor
or too rich.
Give me just what I need.
9If I have too much to eat,
I might forget about you;
if I don't have enough,
I might steal
and disgrace your name.
10Don't tell a slave owner
something bad about one
of the slaves.
That slave will curse you,
and you will be in trouble.
11Some people curse their father
and even their mother;
12others think they are perfect,
but they are stained by sin.
13Some people are stuck-up
and act like snobs;
14others are so greedy
that they gobble up
the poor and homeless.
15Greed has twins,
each named “Give me!”
There are three or four things
that are never satisfied:
16The world of the dead
and a childless wife,
the thirsty earth
and a flaming fire.
17Don't make fun of your father
or disobey your mother—
crows will peck out your eyes,
and buzzards will eat
the rest of you.
18There are three or four things
I cannot understand:
19 How eagles fly so high
or snakes crawl on rocks,
how ships sail the ocean
or people fall in love.
20An unfaithful wife says,
“Sleeping with another man
is as natural as eating.”
21There are three or four things
that make the earth tremble
and are unbearable:
22A slave who becomes king,
a fool who eats too much,
23a hateful woman
who finds a husband,
and a slave who takes the place
of the woman who owns her.
24On this earth four things
are small but very wise:
25Ants, who seem to be feeble,
but store up food
all summer long;
26badgers, who seem to be weak,
but live among the rocks;
27locusts, who have no king,
but march like an army;
28lizards, which can be caught
in your hand,
but sneak into palaces.
29Three or four creatures
really strut around:
30Those fearless lions
who rule the jungle,
31those proud roosters,
those mountain goats,
and those rulers
who have no enemies.
32If you are foolishly bragging
or planning something evil,
then stop it now!
33If you churn milk
you get butter;
if you pound on your nose,
you get blood—
and if you stay angry,
you get in trouble.
translation_text:
Agur wiŋɔɔlaa wia
1Wiŋɔzi naa lii Jakɛ biibaal Agur benii,
u ŋɔ tɛɛ Itiɛl ni Ukal.
2Minuu newea maa bambuguu,
maa newee nunzuma dɔɔwɛ.
3Maa nunzuma hellee
gɛɛ di zum
Dɔɔrinaniinanii la wia.
4Anɛɛ la Kɔraawiizi bol ka bir banɛi?
Anɛɛ n lau peu kuŋŋei?
Anɛɛ n kpa u banaaga fɔɔ niirɛi?
Anɛɛ n dau
hɛri magbɔɔnɛi?
U sɔnnɛ ɛrɛɛ, u biibaal ge sɔnnɛ ɛrɛɛ?
Ŋɔ n be, di i zummɔ!
5Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii maa ɛɛ wibiire,
u ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ laal pɛrɛtu,
di tɛɛ nɛr la maa
n chɔwɛɛ di wa zuuu.
6Gilɛɛ wa kpa wiŋɔdumazi di ra jaa u wiŋɔzi ni,
di guŋ lɛi,
u daŋ nyɛg i ni,
di gil i birgi kara hiŋ.
7“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, wia anɛɛrɛ n na suŋŋii mɔɔ, ka n siu,
jaande maa,
gilɛɛ waa kpolliŋ.
8Gilɛɛ wa gil n ŋmɛnɛ maa waa kanni kara,
di gilɛɛ waa gil
n ɛɛ nyaari
gɛɛ daama hiŋ,
ka ra tɛŋ
n hɔpizi biimaa diwee.
9Aŋhinabe, di n ɛɛ dɔɔŋ, n daŋ suuh i wia, di ŋɔ,
‘Anɛɛ Kɔraawiizɛi?’
Ka di n nyaawɔ ge, n daŋ ŋmɛɛ,
di chɔg u sɔnnaniinanii la.
10Gilɛɛ waa chɔg balii u dɔɔri see.
Di i ɛɛ guŋ,
a hiŋ daŋ bir seei nua,
í na wia.
11Nɛra baŋhina ɔɔ ra see ba mɛɛwaarɛ nuuzi,
ba waa ba maa waa
ra jaami ani ba huma.
12Nɛra baŋhina ɔɔ fɛ lugɔ ba waa doŋŋe,
ka doŋa bɛnnɛ
su ba bampiree.
13Nɛra baŋhina dɔɔ barabaraa ga bɛri,
di ra gbɛlli nɛra werge.
14Nɛra baŋhina ɔɔ dɔɔ sikpegiire,
di ra sunni nyaara
ni anuula hina,
gunnɛ ba ɛɛ di ra di.
15Kpaŋkpaŋziglii dɔɔ biihaana banɛɛ,
ba maa ra wii, di ra ŋɔ,
‘Tɛŋ, tɛŋ!’
Kuna ahoro aŋhina ge du de,
akai, a du anaazuu!
A waa diwee ra piŋ, aabuu,
16ŋmam, hahbara,
hɛri la n hillɛ
di ra nyiŋŋi donii
ani niŋ, a ŋmɛnɛ haa
waa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ,
a kukkɔɔrɛ!
17Nɛr la n na ɛɛ u mɛɛ chɛɛtɛ,
di ra gbɛlli u maa,
duglizi daŋ foŋzi u siwee,
duuni dia.
18Kuna ahoroo du de,
a wia ra kpu nua,
anaazu ge du de,
a zɛɛ zumaa du kpol
werge n be,
19gunla chig n ɔɔ ra lɛɛli chiŋ la,
gunla hɛrikuŋ
n ɔɔ ra goomi bii nyuu la,
gunla muugberzeŋ n ɔɔ sag nii nyuu di ra la la,
ani gunla baal ni haaŋ
n ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi dɔŋa la.
20Kenne hahsɛnsɛnni ɔɔ ra ɛɛ,
u ɔɔ sɛmuu,
di sɔ nii ka ŋɔ,
‘Maa wichɔgaa maa ɛɛwɛ!’
21Kuna ahoroo ɔɔ gil hɛri zigli,
anaazu ge ɔɔ gil a ra nuuu,
22aabuu, yom n birgi koori,
gɛnii la n dɔɔ
kunla maa unna nyiŋŋi,
23haaŋ la biini n kpolle n yuuwɛ,
gɛɛ balii n wa foozi
u dɔɔri jaari.
24Kunjigzi anaazuu du hɛri naa,
ka a dɔɔ
nunzumaa werge,
25aabuu, minni, a waa kpeg,
ka a ɔɔ chaali diweere
dau di ra kpaŋ yuu,
26kachazi waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ,
ka bia bɔɔnii a ra suah,
27lotorozi waa koori dɔɔwɛ,
ka ɔɔ ra voluu
lugɔ laallɔɔra,
28ger lawaa waa kpol,
ka u du koora diinii.
29Kuna ahoro aŋhina ge du de. Akai! A du anaazuu,
di ra vol banni ni,
30aabuu, bunyiŋ, waabuu ɛɛ sela koori,
waa bɛɛ ka ra tɛɛ
kummaa bɔr,
31zabal n ɔɔ ra vol barabara ni, bubal,
ani koori la
u laallɔɔra n baruu.
32Di i faa ɛɛ gɛnii di ra kpa i hiŋ zenni,
gɛɛ di ta wichɔgaa jina,
willi i nyuu ni hiihzi!
33Gunla baŋ ɔɔ yiigi nail la n du kɔŋkɔŋ biini, a wa lii nuu la,
di lɔ nɛr miizi
chal lii la,
gunnɛ nɛr baaŋfuuih
ɔɔ izi kalu.”

english_text:
What King Lemuel's Mother Taught Him
1These are the sayings
that King Lemuel of Massa
was taught by his mother.
2My son Lemuel, you were born
in answer to my prayers,
so listen carefully.
3Don't waste your life
chasing after women!
This has ruined many kings.
4Kings and leaders
should not get drunk
or even want to drink.
5Drinking makes you forget
your responsibilities,
and you mistreat the poor.
6Beer and wine are only
for the dying or for those
who have lost all hope.
7Let them drink and forget
how poor and miserable
they feel.
8But you must defend
those who are helpless
and have no hope.
9Be fair and give justice
to the poor and homeless.
In Praise of a Good Wife
10A truly good wife
is the most precious treasure
a man can find!
11Her husband depends on her,
and she never
lets him down.
12She is good to him
every day of her life,
13and with her own hands
she gladly makes clothes.
14She is like a sailing ship
that brings food
from across the sea.
15She gets up before daylight
to prepare food for her family
and for her servants.
16She knows how to buy land
and how to plant a vineyard,
17and she always works hard.
18She knows when to buy or sell,
and she stays busy
until late at night.
19She spins her own cloth,
20and she helps the poor
and the needy.
21Her family has warm clothing,
and so she doesn't worry
when it snows.
22She does her own sewing,
and everything she wears
is beautiful.
23Her husband is a well-known
and respected leader
in the city.
24She makes clothes to sell
to the shop owners.
25She is strong and graceful,
as well as cheerful
about the future.
26Her words are sensible,
and her advice
is thoughtful.
27She takes good care
of her family
and is never lazy.
28Her children praise her,
and with great pride
her husband says,
29“There are many good women,
but you are the best!”
30Charm can be deceiving,
and beauty fades away,
but a woman
who honors the Lord
deserves to be praised.
31Show her respect—
praise her in public
for what she has done.
translation_text:
Koori Lɛmuɛl maa wiŋɔɔlaa wia
1Wiŋɔzi naa lii Koori bɛl banna yir Lɛmuɛl,
u maa n bagluubuu keŋ,
2“I ɛɛ n biinɔŋŋiirɛ, Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ n wiisuŋŋaarɛ.
Ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔ i benei?
3Gilɛɛ waa kpa i fɔŋŋa di ra chɔɔ haana,
di kpa i kebee ra chɔg ba ni,
ba chɔgi kooraa.
4A nuu, Lɛmuɛl,
koora waa dɛg siŋ nyɔɔi
gɛɛ di ra kɛlli siŋkpega.
5Di ba haŋ wa nyɔɔ siŋ, ba ɔɔ suuh gbɔgnii,
di vɛɛ wia la
n dɛg nɛra ɛɛi.
6Nɛra la n na siu kunnɛ siŋkpeg,
di kaa ɛɛ banla biine
n chɔkkɛ werge kuŋ,
7gil bá nyɔɔ di suuh ba nyaari
ni ba biinichɔg wia.
8Ɛɛ ŋɔ wia lɛɛ banla n wàá wer ŋɔ wia lɛɛ bahinaa la,
di ɔɔ di wibii ra lɛɛ banla
n waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ.
9Ɛɛ ŋɔ wia di ra di seriya ni wibii di ra lɛɛ baa,
di ra lɛɛ nyaara
ni dɔgnya hina.”
Hahpa chɔlaa wia
10Hahpa nai kpolloo!
U dɔɔ tɔnaa werge
kaali rubizi!
11U jaari ɔɔ yarduubuu,
u jaari ŋmɛnɛ
wàá nyaa maa.
12U de dui maa biini,
winanaarɛ ɔɔ ra ɛɛu,
waa ɔɔ ra tɔɔruu.
13U ɔɔ ra humuu saŋa maa,
di ra kuari peezi huna ni
gessihuŋŋunanaa wɛjɛ.
14U ɔɔ la bɔɔnɛɛzii ga chi diwee di ra ba,
gunla kɔkɔɔza n ɔɔ kpa
muugberzenaa di ra ɛɛ la.
15U ɔɔ feluu izi chɔɔzimpikke ni,
di daali diwee
tɛɛ u diahina,
di ɔɔ bagli
u balaa ba humazi.
16Hahpa ɔɔ liiu nyiŋŋi hɛrnanii yau
di kpa u huma tɔna
yau grepu daazi koo.
17U ɔɔ dɔɔ bɔkpega ni fɔŋŋaa,
di ra hum werge.
18U ɔɔ aah siwiire u kɔɔzaa dɔɔ tɔna,
u ɔɔ humuu guŋŋ
hɛuh wa hɛɛhzi.
19U ɔɔ ra ta gonnii saŋa maa,
di ra suah u himmaa wɛjɛzi.
20U ɔɔ ra hiini nyaaraa,
di yaa nonee
di ra lɛɛ anuula hina.
21Gbaŋgbaŋ wia waa ɔɔ tiruu,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u diahina
maanii dɔɔ waari laala.
22U ɔɔ nyɛr u himmaa chɔɔribɔr kumpɛɛri kunaa,
u ɔɔ bɔg u hinnɛ
ni pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaa ni anla
n aahwɛ lugɔ zagbiiŋ niirɛ.
23U jaari ɔɔ dɔɔ sɔnnɛ nɛnnɛ,
di ra so bol nabɔnzi biini.
24U ɔɔ ra nyɛr bɔmbɔga ni belentizii,
di yooa ra tɛɛ kɔkɔɔza.
25U ɔɔ dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ni girmee,
waa wii la n niŋ
wa ɛɛ kɛrɛ ra ɔm.
26Nunzuma wiŋɔzii u ɔɔ ra ŋɔ,
u baglaa ge ra tɛɛ nfɛrɛ.
27U ɔɔ ra du wia la maa n na ɛɛ u dia taurɛ nɛnnɛ,
waa yaara dɔɔwɛ.
28U biizi ɔɔ ra chɔluubuu,
u jaari ge ɔɔ ra chɔluu,
di ra ŋɔ,
29“Hahpazi suwoore,
ka hinuu kaali ba maa.”
30Nuusum daŋ wer ɛɛ daraa, toloori ge dɔɔ tunaa,
ka haaŋ la n na ɔm
Kɔraawiizi dɛg chɔlaarɛ.
31Turguu wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ kim.
Nɛra maa ra tɔgzuu.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
De dui ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ
1Nunzunni la n faa ɛɛ Koori Deevid biibaal, di ɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm koori la wiŋɔɔlaarɛ keŋ,
2Kenne u ŋɔ, “Wipɛɛrii, wipɛɛrii!
De dui ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ!
Wiimaa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ!”
3Bɛɛ tɔnaa newee ɔɔ na di lii u huŋhunnaa maa biini,
uŋ aah siwii ra hum
durnya naa biinei?
4Jiminizi ra bau, jiminizi ra kaali,
ka durnya waa
duulaa u duula.
5Wiizi haa ra furuu di ra chol,
di ra la bɔr la uŋ futtɛ la,
ú kaa ga fur.
6Peu ɔɔ tau ra la wiifurii nodig wiikakag,
di bir ta ra la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag,
di ta ra bar saŋa maa.
7Niiri maa pallɔɔ di ra zuu muuzeŋ,
ka waa su.
A ɔɔ biruu la bɔr la aŋ liiwɛ,
di kaa ga faari.
8Wiimaa ɛɛ kuuhni la
nɛr n wàá wer bagli u wiarɛ.
Yaa siwee waa wia nawɛɛ ra piŋ,
yaa digna gba
waa nuuwɛ ra piŋ.
9Wii la n felee ɛɛ, daŋ kaa ɛɛ,
wii la baŋ ɛɛwɛ,
ba daŋ kaa kuari ɛɛu,
wifalii maa waa hoo
durnya naa biini.
10Ba ɔɔ ŋɔu,
“Na, wifalii bɛllɛ keŋ!”
Akai, a widee ɛɛwɔɔ birgi mɔɔ,
ka ba lul yaa.
11Ba waa faala hina wia ra liizi,
haali banla ban niŋ
haa lul gba,
banla n niŋ hiŋ baa
wàá liizi ba wia.
Nunzuma ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ
12Mìŋ́ Nunzunni naa faa ɛɛ Izrɛl koorii di so Jɛrusalɛm. 13N ɛɛ aniaa ń pigzi di helli wia la maa banna ɛɛ durnya naa biini, ń zum a zɛɛzi. Kɔraawiizi waa yaa tɛɛwɛ labananii. 14N na wia la maa banna ɛɛ durnya naa biinii. N na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ a ɛɛ wipɛɛrii. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu.
15Hàá wer deŋli kunla n golle
gɛɛ di kur kuna la
i siwee n waa na.
16Denii n ŋɔ n biini, “N birgi nɛzenne, di dɔɔ nunzuma werge kaali nɛr la maa n faa di kora Jɛrusalɛm, mɔɔ ka n wa diu. N zum kuna la nunzuma ni zumaa n ɛɛwɛnɛ.” 17N aah siwii ń zum gunla zumaa ni gɛnaa n kuttɛ ani gunla nunzuma ni chugla n kuttɛ. Denii n na lugɔ guŋ gba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ minna duŋŋi peu.
18Gunla i nunzuma n na jaa la,
gunnɛ wia ra tirii werge,
gunla i zumaa n kannɛ,
gunnɛ wia ra tɔɔrii.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Hindii ɛɛ wipɛɛrii
1Denii n ŋɔ ń di n hiŋ, di na gunla bɔsɔna n duwɛɛ. Ka n wa nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ wipɛɛrii a ge gba. 2N kaa na lugɔ mamaa ɛɛ gɛnni wiarɛ. Hindii gba waa ɔɔ hiinii. 3Miŋ aah siwii lugɔ n dɔɔ nunzuma la wia, n kpa siŋ di ra deŋŋi siwee, di ra di n hiŋ. N fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ gunnɛ niŋ gil nɛra ra di bahinaa, saŋa kpurii naa newea n dɔɔwɛ durnya biini naa.
4N wettoo ɛɛ wizenaa. N ma diinii, di par grepu daazi kooni. 5N kuari kambolnanaarɛ, di duu daazi irizi la n na nɔŋ, 6di ki bulli, ń na dua nii. 7N yau yomkpilaa, ba lul baŋhina ge n dia jaa. N faa dɔɔ selaa kaali nɛr la maa n faa felee du Jɛrusalɛm. 8N faa kaa chaali saliŋhuŋŋa ani saliŋ lii hɛssi la miŋ faa ra di kora a ni la daama kuna dauribɔra. Baala ni haana ɔɔ faa yir yira di ra deŋŋi n siwee. N kaa dɔɔ haana la baal maa n ninna kɛlli ú dɔɔ. 9Wibii maa, n faa ɛɛ nɛzenne. N zenni faa kaali nɛr la maa n faa felee du Jɛrusalɛm labuu werge maa. N nunzuma faa waa gillɛ n ɛɛ wia huhzi maa.
10Kunla maa miŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi, an naubuu.
N faa waa sideŋŋa maa vɛɛwɛ.
N bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ dikuu kunla maa miŋ hummɛ di na wia.
N tɔna maanii faa guŋ.
11Denii n pessi wia la maa miŋ ɛɛwɛ la
ani gunla miŋ aah siwii
di ɛɛa la wia,
di na lugɔ a faa ɛɛ wipɛɛrii.
A faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu,
a faa waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ.
Nunzuma ni gɛnaa ɛɛ wipɛɛrii
12A tuna maa, koori wàá wer ɛɛ wiimaa
kaali anla koora la
n tɔ u see n ɛɛwɛ la.
Awia, n faari di ra pessi nunzuma dɔɔi zɛɛ
gɛɛ chugla ni gɛnaa zɛɛzi.
13Ee, n na lugɔ nunzumaa bɔ gɛnaa
gunla bɔchaaŋ
n bɔ bɔbiri la.
14Nunzunna ɔɔ ra na bɔr la banna lau,
ka gɛnaa waa guŋ duwɛɛ.
N kaa na lugɔ
labakpannɛ chɔɔwɛ
tɛɛ ba maa.
15Denii n fɛ n biini,
“N ni gɛnaa maanii labakpaŋ huuzi.
Awia, bɛɛ tɔnaa n na
lii n nunzuma
werge la biinei?”
Awia, n ŋɔ n biini, “Maa kummaa nawɛɛ,
a maa ɛɛ wipɛɛrii.”
16Nɛr maa waa nunzunni gɛɛ gɛnii wia ra liizi.
Saŋa bɛl n niŋ wa hel,
ba daŋ suuh ba maa wia.
Nunzunni gɛɛ gɛnii, ba maa daŋ siu.
Kuuhni ɛɛ wipɛɛrii
17Awia, n de dui faa waa kaa wa dɔɔ zɛɛ tɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, wan tɛɛwɛ kummaa, di tɔɔrɔɔ bɛŋ lɛi. N de dui maa faa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ peure n na duŋŋi. 18Kuna la maa miŋ faa hummɛ na, faa waa kaa ɛɛ kummaa n be, dikuubɛɛwiai, n zummɔ lugɔ n daŋ gilaa tɛɛ n kapɛttɛ diiri. 19Aŋhinabe, u daŋ ɛɛ nunzunni gɛɛ gɛnii. Ka waabuu niŋ dɔɔ kuna la maa miŋ kuuhwɛ na. Kuna la maa n nunzuma n tɛŋ durnya naa biini, a maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. 20Awia, n biini faa faari chɔgi, dikuu miŋ kuuhwɛ werge la wia. 21Nɛr ɔɔ kpa u nunzuma ni u zumaarɛ di hum na kuna, ka a ɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ gilaa tɛɛ nɛr la n waa a kuuhni kuuhwɛ. A guŋ gba ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A guŋ waa wer! 22Nɛr ɔɔ ra humuu ni kafɔŋ u miibɔɔ saŋa. Ka bɛɛ tɔnaa ɔɔ na durnya naa biinei? 23Nɛr de dui biini maa, u wiɛɛlaa maa ɔɔ ra tɛubuu kafɔŋ ni biinichɔg. Haali hamuŋa, ka u nfɛrɛ waa ɔɔ chɔɔ bɔkpaŋ. A maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.
24Winanii la maa nɛr n niŋ wer ɛɛu lugɔ u ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, di lii u kuuhni biini. Ka a gba, n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi benii a lii. 25Ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛ na di ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, di u be lɛi a liiyɛi? 26Kɔraawiizii ra tɛɛ banla wia n paruu nunzuma ni zumaa ani bɔsɔna. Ka u ɔɔ giluu wichɔgɛɛra ra hum, di ra na kuna di ra dau, ú wa kpaa tɛɛ banla wia n paruu. A maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
translation_text:
Wiimaa dɔɔ saŋaa
1Wiimaa dɔɔ saŋaa,
di dɔɔ u hɔpizii
durnya naa biini.
2Lulaa ni siu dɔɔ a saŋazii,
kuna duui ni a kpuzaa ge
dɔɔ a saŋazi,
3kpui dɔɔ saŋa, chaai dɔɔ saŋa,
purgaa dɔɔ saŋa,
mai ge dɔɔ saŋa,
4biinichɔg ni bɔsɔna dɔɔ a saŋazi,
lee wiraa ni saizi ge
dɔɔ a saŋazi,
5bia yaaraa ni a chaalaa dɔɔ a saŋazi,
dɔŋa koraa ni dɔŋa vɛɛ koraa
dɔɔ a saŋazi,
6kuna nyiŋŋaa ni a lewaa dɔɔ a saŋazi,
a dawaa ni a kpai ha ge
dɔɔ a saŋazi,
7kuna piilaa ni a nyɛraa dɔɔ a saŋazi,
siigaa ni wia ŋɔi dɔɔ a saŋazi,
8nɔŋŋaa ni hahzi dɔɔ a saŋazi,
laal ni bampirsɔna ge
dɔɔ a saŋazi.
9Bɛɛ tɔnaa huŋhunni ɔɔ na di lii u kuuhni biinei? 10N na buntɔga la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ chug neweare. 11Saŋazi la n dɛkkɛɛ u dau tɛɛ wiimaa. U gillɔɔ newea dɔɔ kɛkɛluu, bá zum wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ ŋmɛnɛbɛl. Ka waa baa tɛɛwɛ bá wer zum u wiɛɛlaa zɛɛ nɛnnɛ di ga tuŋ, á kpu baa lɔzi. 12Awia, n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ newea hor maanii ba dɔɔ bɔsɔna, di aah siwii ra hum ba humazi, baŋ haa dɔɔ miibɔɔni naa. 13A dɛkkɔɔ newea maa ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, di ra di bahinaa lii kuna la baŋ kuuhwɛ na biini. Kɔraawiizi sunzaarɛ guŋ. 14N zummɔ lugɔ wii la maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ waa chɔgaa dɔɔwɛ maa. Newea wàá wer kpa wiimaa jaa a ni gɛɛ di lizi a yemmaa ha. Wikpaŋ la Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa n na bagli neweare lugɔ, bá ra ɔmuu werge.
15Wii la maa n ɛɛwɛɛ gɛɛ n niŋ haa wa ɛɛ,
faa ɛɛwɔɔ mɔɔ.
Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ giluu
wia bir di ra ɛɛ digiidigii.
16N kaa na lugɔ durnya naa biini,
biinikpolaa ɔɔ du bɔr la n dɛkkɛ wibii dii
ni wideŋlaa n niŋ du.
17Denii n fɛ n biini,
“Kɔraawiizi daŋ di
nɛnanaa ni nɛchɔgaa
maa seriya,
dikuubɛɛwiai, wiimaa ni wiɛɛlii maa daŋ ɛɛu,
saŋa la Kɔraawiizi
n dauwɛ tɛabuu.”
18Denii n kaa fɛ n biini, “Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ neweare di ra na, bá zum lugɔ ba waa sela bɔwɛɛ. 19A tuna maa, newea ni sela maa heeza ɛɛ kpannɛ. Bɛl maa ɔɔ siwuu. Kɔraawiizi taabuu a ɛɛ iri kpaŋ. Newee waa sel bɔwɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, de dui waa zɛɛ dɔɔwɛ tɛɛ bɛl maa. 20Bɔkpannɛ a maa ra la. Waabuu hɛɛhraa biini. Denii a maa lii, a daŋ bir kaali de. 21Ɛrɛɛ nɛr maa wer zum lugɔ newee duma ra la chinne, ka sel duma ra zuu hɛrɛi?”
22Denii n na lugɔ wizeŋ la newea n ninna ɛɛu, ban ninna di kuna la baŋ kuuhwɛ na labuu ni bɔsɔna. Ba wàá ka wer ɛɛ wiimaa. Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá wer zum wii la n niŋ ɛɛ, ba siu har.

english_text:
1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Nɛsunnaa, kuuhni ani dammu nyaai wia
1Denii n kaa binni nɛsunnaa la n su durnya naa biini,
di na banla banna sunni la n na wii,
ka nɛr maa waa hoo
ú tig ba bampiree.
Nɛr maa wàá hiini baa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛra la
n na sunni baa la dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa.
2N na lugɔ banla n siuzɛɛ nuu sumaa,
kaali nyinee.
3Ka banla n bɔ ba maanii,
banla baŋ haa waa lullɛ.
Baabuu haa waa durnya naa
wichɔgaa nawɛɛ la.
4N kaa helli wii la wia nɛra n aah siwii ra hum bá nyɛɛli. Ba dɔŋahina kuna dɔɔi wiarɛ ba ra ɛɛ guŋ. Ka a maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu.
5Ba ɔɔ ŋɔu lugɔ gɛniirɛ nɛr la maa
n niŋ kɔrgi u bɔra chi
ka lɔzi kpuu, ú siu.
6Aŋhinabe gunnɛ, ka hiŋ dɔɔ tama,
ka dɔɔ nfɛrkpaŋ,
aabuu bɔ hiŋ kpa i nonee
ra hum saŋa maa,
di ra duŋŋi peu.
7Wii bɛllɛ n kaa pessi de dui biini, u ɛɛ pɛɛ.
8Baal bɛllɛ faa du de, u bɛŋ.
Waa biibaal
gɛɛ maa bie dɔɔwɛ.
Ka u aah siwii ra hum saŋa maa,
ka u siwii waa su u daama la
uŋ dɔɔwɛ wia.
Anɛɛ wiarɛ u aah siwii ra hum kennei,
ka waa sɛɛwɛ ra di
u hiŋ naanɛi?
A keŋ gba ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ,
di ɛɛ biinichɔg werge maa.
9Nɛra banɛɛ wia bɔ nɛkpaŋ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba huma wia
daŋ dɔɔ siwee.
10Di bɛl wa chollo,
u dɔŋhiŋ daŋ lalluu.
Ka di nɛkpaŋ du u bɛŋ di wa chol,
wichɔgiirɛ werge maa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr maa
waa hoo, ú lalluu.
11Di bɔr sɔɔnɔɔ,
nɛra banɛɛ daŋ chɔɔ pɛli dɔŋa,
ba bɔra wenzi di duŋŋi waari.
Ka ɛrɛɛ waari ɛɛ lii i ni,
di i chɔɔ i bɛnnɛi?
12Nɛra banɛɛ daŋ wer lɛɛ bahinaa
lii siaahmu la
n niŋ kpegli nɛkpaŋ biini.
Kubooroobi la baŋ kpa gessibee ahoro
ŋmɛɛni chaih kpolloo.
13Biipɔllii la n ɛɛ nyaari ka zum wiarɛ bɔ koorizɛŋa la n gɛnnɛ, waa baglaa ra nuu. 14Aŋhinabe, a biipɔllii lii nɛra tɔi diarɛ di wa di kora, gɛɛ ba luluu ni nyaari, u kora diiribɔr biini. 15N na lugɔ banla maa n du durnya naa biini, ra hiŋ a biipɔllii la n niŋ wa kpa koori gawa labuu. 16Aŋhinabe, nɛra la koori n na di kora ba ni waa maga dɔɔwɛ. Ka di u wa siuwɔ, nɛr maa wàá chɔluu, dikuu u wiɛɛlaa wia. Guŋ gba ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa wia
1Di i ra la Kɔraawiizi Dia, a du tau nɛnnɛ. Hiŋ la de di gaa helli wia, aabuu bɔ hinna lizi mbusuzi gunla gɛnaa n na ɛɛ la. Baabuu banla n waa zummɛ lugɔ wideŋlaa kuttɔɔ wichɔgaa ni la.
2Ɛɛ fɛ nfɛrɛ ka ra ŋɔ wia,
di gilɛɛ hahzi
ŋɔ nua ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.
U du chinne,
i ge du hɛri,
awia, gilɛɛ waa
ŋɔ wia ra bɛri.
3Di i ra fɔŋ wia ni werge,
guŋ daŋ wer gil
i ra deezi deezichɔgaa.
Di i kaa ra ŋɔ wia ge werge,
guŋ daŋ gil i ŋɔ gɛnni wia.
4Awia, di i wa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ɛɛ́ hiŋ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la manaŋ. Wii la hiŋ ŋɔ nua, dí i daŋ ɛɛ la, ɛɛu. Kɔraawiizi waa gɛnii wia ra nyiŋŋi. 5Hiŋ waa nua ŋɔwɛɛ, aabuu bɔ hiŋ ŋɔu, ka hɔɔ hiŋŋɛ. 6Gilɛɛ wa gil i wiŋɔɔlaa ra dui wichɔgaa ɛɛi biini, di gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ be lugɔ i ra duau. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ í gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh i ninɛi? Gilɛɛ gil u wàá chɔgi kuna la maa hiŋ kuuhwɛ na la. 7Gunla maa hinna deezi gɛɛ hinna hum humpɛɛri gɛɛ hinna ŋɔ wia, ka a dɛkkɔɔ í ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi werge.
Daama ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ
8Gilɛɛ wa gil a tirii, di i wa na gɔminanti n na fir nyaara, waa wibii lɛɛwɛ ra tɛɛ baa gɛɛ di ra tɛɛ baa wia la n dɛg baa. Nabɔma maa dɔɔ u nabɔmaa u ra guuu. Nabɔnzenaa ge ɔɔ kaa guu ba maa. 9A koori himmaa gba, a hɛri kumpattaa ninɛɛ u dɛlli.
10Di i nɔŋŋi kebee, i siwii waa ba sui maa,
di i ra nyiŋŋi
í birgi daama hiŋ,
ka hàá wer na
kuna la maa hinna nyiŋŋi.
Pɛɛrɛ a maa.
11Di i dɔɔ daama werge,
nɛkpilaa ninna dii.
Tɔna la maa hinna na maanii,
banna yirii daama hiŋ.
12Aŋhinabe, huŋhunni daŋ na diwee ra di,
di ra kukki,
gɛɛ wàá na,
ka u daŋ wer
chɔɔ dɔɔ nɛnnɛ
hamuŋa ni.
Ka daama hiŋ waa kuŋkpila wia,
waa dɔɔ ra chɔɔ.
13Wichuma werge bɛllɛ n na durnya biini.
Nɛra ɔɔ ra dau kebeere di ra ba saŋa la ban niŋ wàá nyiŋŋaa,
14ka a maa ɔɔ wa lewuu,
dikuu ŋmɛnichuma bɛl uŋ kpaa ga wia,
wàá ka dɔɔ kummaa
ú gil dau u biizi.
15Gunla newee n waa ɔɔ kpogli kummaa
ba durnya naa la,
gunnɛ waa ɔɔ
kaa kpogli kummaa
lii u biini kaali.
Haali uŋ ɔɔ hum huma werge maa gba,
ka wàá wer kpa
kummaa kaali.
16A gunna wiiu werge!
Gunla newee n ɔɔ ba,
gunnɛ ɔɔ kaa kaali.
U ɔɔ ra kuuuh di ra ɛɛ ania
ka u kuuhni ɔɔ ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.
17U ɔɔ du bɔbirii,
u biini chɔgi,
kafɔŋ lawuu,
u baaŋ na fuuh,
u ra wii.
18Wii la miŋ nawɛɛrɛ keŋ, winanii la nɛr n niŋ wer ɛɛu lugɔ ú ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, di kpa kuna la uŋ kuuhwɛ na la, di ra di u hiŋ, miibɔɔkpurii naa Kɔraawiizi n tɛu naa biini. Newee labaa guŋ. 19Di Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ nɛr daama, di gil u ra di a suma, a dɛkkɔɔ ú ra tɛu jaaŋ ka ra di kuna la uŋ kuuhwɛ na la. Kɔraawiizii sunzuu. 20Dikuu Kɔraawiizi n tɛu bɔsɔna wia, waa ɔɔ kaa ra fɔŋ werge gunla u miibɔɔ n kpusse wia.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
7We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied. 8We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right. 9It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
10Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us. 11The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk? 12Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_text:
1N pessoore di na lugɔ wichɔgaa du durnya naa biinii werge. 2Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ tɛɛ nɛbɛllɛ daama ni girme. Wibii maa, ɔɔ tɛubuu kuna la maa unna nyiŋŋi, ka waa ɔɔ gil u ra di a suma. Ka hɔɔhri bɛllɛ ɔɔ lɛɛa di ra di. A guŋ ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A gunna wiiu werge.
3Nɛr daŋ wer dɔɔ biizi kalfa, di dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ, ka di waa bɔsɔna dɔɔwɛ di wa siu, ba wɔɔ hukke nɛnnɛ, guŋwaa, bie la n siu u maa hia, ka ba luluurɛ bɔu. Wii la miŋ nawɛɛrɛ guŋ. 4A bie naa lulaa waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ tɛu, u leuwoo bɔbiri biini, ba suuh u wia. 5Waa bɔchaaŋ nawɛɛ gɛɛ di zum gunla de dui n duwɛɛ, ka u na heezaare, 6di kaali nɛr la n waa de dui suma ra di, haali di u di binni kagboŋa anɛɛ gba. Ani a maa, ka bɔkpannɛ ba maa ra la.
7Nɛra ɔɔ ra hum ba humaa
bá na kumbɛl di,
ka ba waa ɔɔ wer
bá naa, á kukki baa.
8Ɛrɛɛ nunzunna bɔ gɛnaai?
Bɛɛ tɔnaa nyaari nai,
di u zum duiyɛi?
9A ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ,
a ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
hinna duŋŋi peu.
A wessoo í gil kunla hiŋ dɔɔwɛ su i siwii,
ka gil a dumazi nyiŋŋaa
di ra jaa saŋa maa.
10Wii la maa n na ɛɛ,
Kɔraawiizii dau guŋ
faala maa.
Nɛr maa zummɔ lugɔ u ni nɛr la
n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa kaaluu
wàá wer di mmɔri.
11Gunla maa maga nɛr n niŋ di mmɔri,
ka pɛɛrɛ,
wàá na hiinaa maa.
12Anɛɛ n niŋ wer zum wia la n dɛg yaa, yaa de dui naa n ɛɛ pɛɛ naa biinei? Miibɔɔ la n ɔɔ kaali lugɔ laalii lai? Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ zum wia la n niŋ waa ɛɛ durnya naa biini, yaa siu harɛi?

english_text:
The Best in Life
1 A good reputation
at the time of death
is better than loving care
at the time of birth.
2It's better to go to a funeral
than to attend a feast;
funerals remind us
that we all must die.
3Choose sorrow over laughter
because a sad face
may hide a happy heart.
4A sensible person mourns,
but fools always laugh.
5Correction from someone wise
is better by far
than praise from fools.
6Foolish laughter is stupid.
It sounds like thorns
crackling in a fire.
7Corruption makes fools
of sensible people,
and bribes can ruin you.
8Something completed is better
than something just begun;
patience is better
than too much pride.
9 Only fools get angry quickly
and hold a grudge.
10It isn't wise to ask,
“Why is everything worse
than it used to be?”
11Having wisdom is better
than an inheritance.
12Wisdom will protect you
just like money;
knowledge with good sense
will lead you to life.
13Think of what God has done!
If God makes something crooked,
can you make it straight?
14When times are good,
you should be cheerful;
when times are bad,
think about what it means.
God makes them both
to keep us from knowing
what will happen next.
Some of Life's Questions
15I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper. 16So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart! 17Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool. 18Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
19Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
20No one in this world always does right.
21Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you. 22Haven't you cursed many others?
23I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me. 24The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep. 25So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
26Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for. 27With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together, 28but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman. 29I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_text:
Nunzuma wia
1Sɔnnanii bɔ tulaale la yoola n kpolle,
gunnɛ i siwaa hɔpizii bɔ
i lulaa hɔpizii.
2Hinna la dia la biini banna wii lee,
bɔ unla biini
banna di diuzenaa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, a dɛkkɔɔ nyinee
ra liizi lugɔ ba daŋ siuzi.
3Biinichɔg bɔ mamaa,
u daŋ gil i nyɛm,
ka ɔɔ giluu
i wia zɛɛ zumaa ra jaa.
4Nɛr la maa n ɔɔ ra fɛ bɔsɔna bɛŋ wia ɛɛ gɛniirɛ.
Ka nunzunni waa
ɔɔ ra fɛ siu gba wiarɛ.
5Nunzunni n na hau i ni,
aabuu bɔ gɛnaa
n na chɔlii.
6Di gɛnii haŋ waa mam,
a ɔɔ ɛɛu lugɔ niŋ
n na fuuh sɔɔhri
a ra pogzi.
A ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.
7Aŋhinabe, nunzunnii hiŋ,
ka di i fini nɛbɛl,
i ra ɛɛu lugɔ gɛnii.
Di i lɛɛ kuna ka ra hiini nɛra,
i hinnɛ i ra chɔgi la.
8Wiimaa tunaa bɔ u luglaa,
kanyittii bɔ jigsi.
9A lau i hiŋ, di i baaŋ wa fuuhwo,
gɛniirɛ kpa wia
ra du u biini.
10Gilɛɛ waa pɛɛzi, di ra ŋɔ,
“Bɛɛ n baani wia
faa bɔ werge maa, faala lai?”
Nunzunni wipɛɛzaa
lɛi guŋ.
11Nɛr la maa n dɔɔ miibɔɔ dɛkkɔɔ u dɔɔ nunzuma.
A guŋ wessoo di ɛɛ lugɔ
hin di kapɛttɛ.
12Nunzuma daŋ wer guui lugɔ kebee n ɔɔ guui la,
di gil i dɔɔ i hiŋ.
Zumaa tɔnaa la.
13A fɛ Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa wia.
Nɛr daŋ wer deŋli kunla
Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ
u golaa?
14Di i wia ra kuari nɛnnɛ,
gil i bɔra sɔɔni.
Ka di tɔɔrɔɔ wa ballɔ,
a liizi lugɔ
Kɔraawiizii ɔɔ gil
bɔsɔna ni tɔɔrɔɔ
maa ra ba.
Hàá wer zum wii la
n niŋ wa ɛɛ.
15N de dui ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ, ka n wettoo na wiimaa.
Nɛnanaa ɔɔ weruu siuzi
ka nɛra baŋhina
du de birgi,
haali baŋ ɛɛ
nɛchɔgaa gba.
16Awia, gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ nɛnanii werge
gɛɛ di wàá ɛɛ
nunzunni werge.
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ
i kpu i hinnɛi?
17Gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ biinikpola werge
gɛɛ di wàá gɛŋ werge.
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ
i siu manannɛi?
18Gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ mannizi naa
bɛl maa werge.
Di i ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi di ra ɔmuu,
i wiimaa daŋ kuari.
19Wia la nunzuma dɔɔi n ɔɔ ɛɛ tɛɛ nɛr,
kaali wia la
bolzeŋ nabɔnzi fi
n niŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ a bolzeŋ.
20Nɛkpaŋ maa waa hoo durnya naa biini,
di hanna ɛɛ
wideŋlaa bɛŋ saŋa maa,
di u haa waa
wia ɛɛwɛ leu.
21Gilɛɛ ra nuu wia la maa nɛra n na ŋɔ,
di guŋ lɛi,
i daŋ nuu i balii
n na chagzii,
22dikuubɛɛwiai, i gba zummɔ lugɔ
i chagzi nɛraa
saŋa kpila maa.
23N kpa n nunzumaa ɛɛ annii naa maa na.
N faa ra fir n hinnɛ ń dɔɔ nunzuma,
ka guŋ faa kaalimbuu.
24Anɛɛ n niŋ wer zum de dui zɛɛi?
U wia luŋŋoo
werge tɛɛ yaa,
u zɛɛ zumaa
du kpol werge.
25Ka n faa aah siwiire werge maa, ń zum wia,
di pigzi ra helli wia,
di aah siwii ra fir n hiŋ,
ń na nunzuma ni
n pɛɛzaazi zɛɛzi,
di helli gunla biinikpola
ni gɛnaa n ɛɛ bambugri.
26Denii n na wii bɛl n chummɛ werge kaali siu,
waabuu haaŋ la
n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ sidɛɛ.
Nɔŋŋaa la uŋ nɔŋŋii la
daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ
asau di lawii.
U nonee la uŋ kpawɛɛ korii la,
daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ baŋ kpa
yɔlɔzi vɔɔzii.
Ka baal la wia n na par Kɔraawiizi,
daŋ wer lɛɛ u hiŋ,
ka u daŋ lau
wichɔgɛɛri waa.
27A Nunzunni ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ɛɛh, n na wia naabuu tama,
saŋa la minna nyiŋŋi n pɛɛzaazi zɛɛzi la.
28N nyiŋŋi
n pɛɛzaazi zɛɛzii,
ka maa bɛl maa nawɛɛ.
Baala kagboŋ biini, nɛkpannɛ n na ń wer tɔgzi.
Ka haana waa biini,
maa kpaŋkpaŋ
maa nawɛɛ.
29Wii la maa miŋ helleere keŋ,
Kɔraawiizi ta yaabuu,
yaa wia chaani,
ka yaa gil
yaa wia du kpol.”

english_text:
1Who is smart enough
to explain everything?
Wisdom makes you cheerful
and gives you a smile.
Obey the King
2If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise. 3Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind. 4The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?” 5If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it. 6Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything, 7though no one can tell the future. 8We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil. 9I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another?
Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
10I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense. 11When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime. 12They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying:
Everyone who lives right
and respects God
will prosper,
13but no one who sins
and rejects God
will prosper or live very long.
14There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens. 15So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
16Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world. 17I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_text:
1Nɛr la n dɔɔ nunzuma
bɛnnɛ ɔɔ zum wia zɛɛzi.
Nunzumaa ɔɔ gil ba ra munzi,
di gil ba nyɛmaa tuŋ.
A tɔgzi koori
2Ɛɛ gunla koori n ŋɔ í ɛɛ, ka gilɛɛ hahzi ŋɔ nua ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 3Koori daŋ wer ɛɛ wii la maa unna nyiŋŋi. Awia, chɔ lii u be, de waa wer. 4Koori dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa di ra ɛɛ wia, nɛr maa wàá wer diu mmɔri.
5Di i hanna hiŋ u widaulaa, wichɔgii maa wàá huuzii.
Nɛr la n zum wia,
u zum gunla ni saŋazi la
un niŋ ɛɛ gunnɛ.
6Wiimaa ɛɛi dɔɔ u saŋaa ni ŋmɛnɛɛ la n dɛg u ɛɛi.
Ka yaa zumaa waa kaŋ.
7Yaa bɛl maa waa zum wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ,
nɛr maa ge waa hoo
u ŋɔ yaa be.
8Nɛr maa wàá wer vɛɛ siu
gɛɛ di vɛɛ hɔpizii la
un niŋ siu.
Laal la yaa n wàá wer chɔ di lii u biinii guŋ,
yaa wàá wer fini
di lii u biini maa.
9Minna fɛ wia la maa banna ɛɛ durnya naa biini nfɛrɛ labuu n na annii maa. Durnya naa biini, baŋhina dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa, baŋhina ge ra di tɔɔrɔɔ dikuu ba fɔŋŋa hiŋ wia. 10Wibii maa, n na baŋ hugzi biinikpola hinaa, ka nɛra la n hug baa ka bir di ra kpo la, a chɔli baa bolzeŋ la himmaa biini baŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa la. A maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.
11Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ nɛra hahzi di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaai? Ba ra ɛɛ gunnɛ, dikuu baŋ waa wichɔgɛɛra digna ra tɛrgi manamanaŋ wia. 12Wichɔgɛɛri daŋ wer ɛɛ wichɔgaa kalfa, ka haa du de ni miibɔɔ. Wibii maa, n zum gunla banna ŋɔu, “Di i ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, wiimaa daŋ kuari. 13A wàá kuari tɛɛ wichɔgɛɛra waa. Ba miibɔɔni ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ laalii. Ba daŋ siuzi di ba haa ɛɛ biipɔllaa, dikuu baŋ waa Kɔraawiizi nua ra hiŋ wia.” 14Ka annii ɛɛ wijagazii. Na wia la n na ɛɛ durnya naa biini. Saŋa bɛl, ba ɔɔ kpa nɛchɔgii dignitɛraarɛ di tɛr nɛnanii digni. Nɛchɔgii na nɛnanii kinturgaa. Annii maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. 15Awia, wii la miŋ sɛɛwɛɛ lugɔ ya ra di yaa hinaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, sideŋŋa la bɛŋ yaa n dɔɔwɛ yaa de dui biinii, dii ni nyɔɔi, á tɛɛ yaa bɔsɔna. Yaa daŋ wer ɛɛ keŋ, di lii kuuhni la yaa n na kuuh, yaa de dui durnya naa biini naa.
16Di n haŋ wa ŋɔ n ɛɛ ania dɔɔ nunzuma, ń wer zum wia la n na ɛɛ durnya naa biini, n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ di i sogo hamuŋa ni hɔpizaa maa gba, 17ka hàá wer zum Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa zɛɛ. Gunla maa hin niŋ aah siwii, ka hàá wer zum a zɛɛ maa. Nunzunna daŋ ŋɔ ba zummɔɔ, ka ba waa zummɛ.

english_text:
One Day at a Time
1I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad. 2But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
3It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die. 4As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion. 5We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten. 6Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
7So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do. 8Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best. 9Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth. 10Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
11Here is something else I have learned:
The fastest runners
and the greatest heroes
don't always win races
and battles.
Wisdom, intelligence, and skill
don't always make you healthy,
rich, or popular.
We each have our own share
of misfortune.
12None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap.
Better To Be Wise than Foolish
13Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me. 14It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls. 15But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten. 16So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
17Words of wisdom spoken softly
make much more sense
than the shouts of a ruler
to a crowd of fools.
18Wisdom is more powerful
than weapons,
yet one mistake can destroy
all the good you have done.
translation_text:
Labakpannɛ chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ nɛr maa
1Annii maa wia, n fɛ nfɛrɛɛ nɛnnɛ, ka n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizii dɔɔ nunzunna ani nɛra la wia n deŋlee wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋa, haali ba nɛnɔŋŋaa ni ba nɛhahzi. Nɛr maa wàá wer zum wia la n du see di ra ba. 2Labakpannɛ nɛra maa dɔɔ, nɛra la wia n deŋlee, biinikpola hina, nɛnanaa, nɛchɔgaa, banla n waa doŋŋe, banla n doŋŋe, banla n na lizi mbusuzi ani banla n waa ra lizi.
Nɛnanii waa nɛchɔgii bɔwɛɛ.
Nɛr la n ɔɔ hɛɛhzi
di ŋɔ nua waa unla
n waa gunna ɛɛ bɔwɛɛ.
3Labakpannɛ ɔɔ huuzi ba maa. A wii naa waa deŋlee alugɔ wia la maa n na ɛɛ durnya naa biini. Nɛra de dui biini saŋa waa maa, wichɔgaa ni chuglaa su ba nfɛssi biine. Kakpaŋ, di ba siuzɔɔ. 4Ka nɛr la maa n du nyinee biini, u dɔɔ tamiirɛ. Nuahiŋ nyinii bɔ bunyiŋ siwii.
5Wibii maa, nyinee zummɔ lugɔ ba daŋ siuzi,
ka lalaa waa,
waa wiimaa zummɛ.
Ba wàá ka na kinturgaa maa,
ba wàá ka liizi ba wia maa.
6Ba nɔŋŋaa, ba hahzii
ani ba winyiŋŋaa
maanii siuwɛ.
Ba waa kaa jaa
durnya wiɛɛlaa
bɛl maa biini.
7A di i diwee di dɔɔ bɔsɔna, di ra nyɔɔ i siŋ, í bɔra ra kazi. A guŋ waa chummɛ Kɔraawiizi be. 8Dɔɔ bɔsɔna ni biinihuŋŋu saŋa maa. 9Gil i ni haaŋ la hiŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ la ra di iihinaa, i de dui saŋa naa Kɔraawiizi n tɛi, waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ naa biini. A di i hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, tɔna la maa hin niŋ na lii i kuuhni biinii guŋ. 10Wii la maa hinna ɛɛ, aah siwii di ra ɛɛu, dikuubɛɛwiai wiɛɛlii gɛɛ nfɛrɛ fɛi gɛɛ wia zɛɛ zumaa gɛɛ nunzuma waa hoo lalaa bol. Denii i ra la la.
