11N kaa na wikpaŋ bɛl durnya naa biini.
Banla n gbaŋŋɛ di ra chɔ lɛi ɔɔ di,
banla n dɔɔ
bampirii ge lɛi
ɔɔ wer lɔ laal
di kpegli ba dɔma.
Nunzunna ge waa ɔɔ wer
ba hum di na kuna di.
Banla n dɔɔ nfɛrɛ
ge lɛi ɔɔ ɛɛ dɔɔna.
Banla n wer wiɛɛlaa ge lɛi
ɔɔ ra na nabɔmuu.
Ka nyuchɔgii ɔɔ huuzi nɛr maanii.
12Hàá wer zum i hɔpizii.
Gunla sidɛɛ n ɔɔ lau zumbee a pirguu la,
gɛɛ sɔzaa n ɔɔ lau
nyinni gunla,
gunnɛ wichɔgaa ɔɔ pirgi yaa
saŋa la yaa
n waa gunna fɛ.
Nunzumaa bɔ gɛnaa
13Denii n kaa na wii bɛl, gunla durnya naa hina n na fɛ nunzuma wia. 14Boljiga bɛllɛ faa du de, u nɛra waa kpil. Koorizeŋ bɛl n kpekke faa vɔɔ laal di wa fɔɔu, ú purgi u koŋlaa ka zuu u biini. 15Nɛbɛl faa du u biini, di ɛɛ nyaari, ka faa dɔɔ nunzuma, di lɛɛ a bol hina. Ka nɛr maa faa waa u wia liizee. 16Saŋa maa, aŋ ŋɔu lugɔ nunzumaa bɔ fɔŋŋa, ka nɛr maa waa ɔɔ ra fɛ nyaara wia lugɔ ba ɛɛ nunzunnaa, di ra nuu ba wiŋɔɔlaa.
17Hinna nuu nunzunni wiŋɔɔlaa n du bɔɔiih,
aabuu bɔ gɛnaa koori
n na pogzi.
18Nunzuma wiɛɛlaa ra ɛɛ winanaarɛ werge kaali dɔŋkuna,
ka wichɔgɛɛri kpaŋkpaŋ
daŋ wer chɔgi
winaŋkpila.

english_text:
1A few dead flies in perfume
make all of it stink,
and a little foolishness
outweighs a lot of wisdom.
2Sensible thoughts lead you
to do right;
foolish thoughts lead you
to do wrong.
3Fools show their stupidity
by the way they live;
it's easy to see
they have no sense.
4Don't give up your job
when your boss gets angry.
If you stay calm,
you'll be forgiven.
5Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair: 6They honor fools, but dishonor the rich; 7they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
8 If you dig a pit,
you might fall in;
if you break down a wall,
a snake might bite you.
9You could even get hurt
by chiseling a stone
or chopping a log.
10If you don't sharpen your ax,
it will be harder to use;
if you are wise,
you'll know what to do.
11The power to charm a snake
does you no good
if it bites you anyway.
12If you talk sensibly,
you will have friends;
if you talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
13Fools begin with nonsense,
and their stupid chatter
ends with disaster.
14They never tire of talking,
but none of us really know
what the future will bring.
15Fools wear themselves out—
they don't know enough
to find their way home.
16A country is in for trouble
when its ruler is childish,
and its leaders
party all day long.
17But a nation will prosper
when its ruler is mature,
and its leaders
don't party too much.
18Some people are too lazy
to fix a leaky roof—
then the house collapses.
19Eating and drinking
make you feel happy,
and money can buy
everything you need.
20Don't let yourself think about
cursing the king;
don't curse the rich,
not even in secret.
A little bird might hear
and tell everything.
translation_text:
1Gunla nakɛɛhsiwaa n ɔɔ gil tulaale ra hɛhzi la,
gunnɛ gɛnaa tama maa,
ɔɔ wer chɔgi nunzuma la
n kannɛ werge.
2Nunzunna hotte wideŋlaa ɛɛi,
gɛnaa ge hotte
gɛnni wiɛɛlaa.
3Di ba wa chem hɔɔhra ni ŋmɛnɛɛ,
ba ɔɔ na ba gɛnaarɛ,
ba wiɛɛlaa ɔɔ giluu
nɛr maa zum lugɔ
ba ɛɛ gɛnaarɛ.
4Di i koori wa nyɛg i ni,
ka i gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u humaa.
Di i lau i hiŋ,
u daŋ wer gil
i wichɔgaa tɛi.
5Wichɔgii bɛl miŋ kaa na durnya naa biinii keŋ,
kooraa ra ɛɛ a wii naa.
6Gɛnaarɛ ba ɔɔ tɛɛ nabɔmuu,
ka gil dɔɔna.
7N na yoma n tinni zagra,
ka nabɔnzenaa
ra vol lugɔ yoma.
8Di i ki bɔɔ, i daŋ wer chol u biini.
Di i ra purgi koŋlii,
hɛrikuŋ daŋ wer dumii.
9Di i ra hum bia purgaa bɔr, bia daŋ dui pira.
Di i ra pergi daazi,
i daŋ wer na pira.
10Di i kpaŋfɔ waa di,
i vɛɛ u sazaa
ka kpogluu ra hum,
i daŋ kuuh werge.
Nunzuma wiarɛ hiŋ felee
lauri i wiɛɛlaa dau.
11Tɔna maa waa hoo,
hiŋ ŋɔ i helli
hɛrikuŋ pɛssaa,
ka u feli dumii.
12Nunzunna wiŋɔɔlaa ɔɔ giluu ba ra tɔgzi baa,
ka gɛnaa waa wiŋɔɔlaa
ra chɔgi baabuu.
13Gɛnni wiŋɔzii ba ɔɔ kpa faari,
a tuna maa,
a birgi chugla himmaa.
14Gɛnii waa wia
ŋɔwɛɛ ra kuuh.
Nɛr maa waa zum wii la n na ba,
nɛr maa ge
wàá wer bagli yaa,
wii la n niŋ ɛɛ
yaa siu har.
15Nɛr la n gɛnnɛ werge,
waa u dia
ŋmɛnɛɛ zummɛɛ,
niŋ chɔgi u hiŋ
ni humkpega.
16Di hɛri maa koori wa ɛɛ biipɔllii,
u nabɔnzi ra di
diuzenaa hamuŋa maa,
a hɛri hina
du tɔɔrɔɔ biinii.
17Ka hɛri la maa koori
n na dau u himmaa
nfɛrɛ biini widaulaa,
u nabɔnzi ra di
saŋazi la n dɛkkɛ,
di ra lauri bahinaa,
ba waa siŋ nyɔɔwɛ
ra dɛɛzi,
a hɛri hina nuu sumaa.
18Di nɛr dɔɔ yaara werge, wàá wer magzi u sal,
u daŋ lul guŋŋ
di wa chol.
19Hɔpizizeŋ dii ra tɛibuu bɔsɔna,
siŋ gil i bɔra ra kazi,
ka hàá wer na bɛl maa
di haa kebii dɔɔwɛ.
20Gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ koori wia i biini gba,
gɛɛ di wàá ŋɔ dɔɔŋ
wia i chɔɔribɔr.
Aŋhinabe, zumbee daŋ
ga baglaa tɛɛ baa.

english_text:
It Pays To Work Hard
1Be generous, and someday
you will be rewarded.
2Share what you have
with seven or eight others,
because you never know
when disaster may strike.
3Rain clouds always bring rain;
trees always stay
wherever they fall.
4If you worry about the weather
and don't plant seeds,
you won't harvest a crop.
5No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
6Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce.
Youth and Old Age
7Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun. 8Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
9Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
10Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_text:
Newee zumaa dɔɔ magaa
1Kpa i kebee ra hum huma hɛrdumazi biini,
ŋmɛnɛbɛl i daŋ na tɔna.
2Kpa i kebee du kuŋkpila ani bɔkpila biine.
Haa zum
hɔpizii la nyuchɔgii
n niŋ huuzii
durnya naa biini.
3Bɔr la maa paga daa n niŋ chol,
denii ú chɔɔ.
Di baama wa biroo ni donii,
dooŋ daŋ ba.
4Di i ra kpaŋ ŋɔ bɔr wa du wer,
hàá duu kuna,
hàá kumaa ge.
5Gunla hiŋ waa peu ŋmɛnɛɛ zummɛ,
gɛɛ gunla biifula n ɛɛwɛ
di ra hel
u maa hia biini la,
gunnɛ hàá wer zum Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa,
unla n ta kummaa la.
6A duu kuna chɔɔzi ni duana maa.
Hàá wer zum
di a maa daŋ lii nɛnnɛ
gɛɛ aŋhina daŋ lii
kaali aŋhina.
7Bɔchaaŋ wessoo,
di ra par siwee.
8Gil i bɔra sɔɔni i de dui saŋa.
Gunla hin niŋ du de
di birgi mag,
ka i ra liizi lugɔ siurɛ í siu di birgi werge.
Tamii maa waa hoo.
9Biipɔllaa, ií ra di ii pɔlaa tɔna.
Ií gil ii bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔni ia,
ii pɔlaa saŋa.
Ií ra ɛɛ wia la iinna nyiŋŋi,
di ra hiŋ
ii bampiree wilaulaa.
Ka ií ra liizi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi
daŋ di ii wiɛɛlaa,
maa seriya.
10Ií gilɛɛ gil wiimaa ra tir ia
gɛɛ di gil ii bɔra ra wii.
A wàá birgi
ka ii pɔlaa saŋa tuŋ.

english_text:
1Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
2Someday the light of the sun
and the moon and the stars
will all seem dim to you.
Rain clouds will remain
over your head.
3Your body will grow feeble,
your teeth will decay,
and your eyesight fail.
4The noisy grinding of grain
and the voices of singers
will be shut out
by your deaf ears,
but even the song of a bird
will keep you awake.
5You will be afraid
to climb up a hill
or walk down a road.
Your hair will turn as white
as almond blossoms.
You will feel lifeless
and drag along
like an old grasshopper.
We each go to our eternal home,
and the streets here are filled
with those who mourn.
6The silver cord snaps,
the golden bowl breaks;
the water pitcher is smashed,
and the pulley at the well
is shattered.
7So our bodies return
to the earth,
and the life-giving breath
returns to God.
8Nothing makes sense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense.
Respect and Obey God
9I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied. 10Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
11Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together. 12My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these.
There is no end to books,
and too much study
will wear you out.
13Everything you were taught can be put into a few words:
Respect and obey God!
This is what life
is all about.
14God will judge
everything we do,
even what is done in secret,
whether good or bad.
translation_text:
1Awia, a liizi i Taari wia i pɔlaa saŋa,
ka hɔpizaa ni binni la
n wàá du sum i be la ba.
A saŋaa i jaa ŋɔ lugɔ
de dui waa sum.
2A saŋaa wiizi, bɔchaaŋ,
baagu ani chinchiŋwilaa
wàá kaa ra chaani
nɛnnɛ i be.
Baama daŋ ɛɛu lugɔ dooŋ
n na nyiŋŋi balaa
saŋa maa i be.
3Denii nonee la hiŋ ɔɔ faa kpa
di guu i hiŋ la ra sa.
I naazi naa
n kpekke naa gba gɛrgi.
I nyina wàá ka du kpil,
í kpa ra chaŋŋi diwee.
I siwee ge
wàá ka ra na nɛnnɛ.
4I digna wàá ka ra nuu ŋmɛnizenaa kɔɔi.
Tama tamaa
i ra nuu manika kɔɔi
ani banna yir yira.
Ka zumbee wiraa gba
daŋ lallii dɔɔ biini.
5Bɔra la n du chiŋ wia daŋ dɔɔi ɔnsii,
volaa ɛɛ wii la
hin ninna ɔm.
I nyuhuna daŋ huuhzi, i ra guuzi.
Wiimaa wàá ka ra kɛllii.
A hɔl la yaa n niŋ la yaa tuna heezaa bɔr la,
wiraa daŋ su ŋmɛnizenaa.
6A liizi i Taari wia mɔɔ ka saliŋhuŋŋu yɔlɔ la chah,
saliŋ fintina la chol purgi.
Jaayir ŋmɛŋ chah,
hàá ka wer dɔɔ nii
lii kɔlɔŋ biini.
7Awia, yaa bɔrahɔna daŋ bir
zuu hɛɛhraa la
biini aŋ liwɛɛ la,
ka heeza la Kɔraawiizi
n kpawɛɛ dua la,
bir kaali u be.
8Nunzunni la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Annii naa maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.
A maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.”
A wia tuna
9Ka Nunzunni la n faa dɔɔ nunzuma la wia, u faa aah siwiire di ra bagli a nɛra wii la maa uŋ zummɛ. U faa helli sɛɛliizii, di ɛɛa na, ú zum a wibii. 10A Nunzunni faa ra nyiŋŋi bampirii tigaa wiŋɔɔlaarɛ, awia, u wiŋɔlaa la uŋ sɛbɛɛ la ɛɛ wibiire.
11Nunzunni wiŋɔɔlaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ penɔɔni daŋkpala. Sɛɛliizi la baŋ chaalɛɛ la ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ lugbia baŋ kpaahzɛɛ, a zuu nɛnnɛ. Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ yaa Nɔɔnikpaŋ labuu kpaa tɛɛ yaa. 12N biibaal, wii bɛl haa du de hin ninna du u tau. Hɔna sɛbaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ. Hellaa werge daŋ gil i kuuh.
13Annii naa maa har,
wikpaŋ bɛnnɛ
du de ń ŋɔ,
á ɔm Kɔraawiizi, di ra tɔgzuu,
di ra hiŋ u widaulaa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, a bɛŋ wiarɛ
Kɔraawiizi ta newea.
14Wia la maa yaa n niŋ ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ dia seriya,
di ananaarɛ
gɛɛ achɔgaarɛ,
haali anla yaa
n suahzɛɛ ɛɛ gba.

english_text:
Love Is Better than Wine
1 This is Solomon's
most beautiful song.
She Speaks:
2Kiss me tenderly!
Your love is better than wine,
3and you smell so sweet.
All the young women adore you;
the very mention of your name
is like spreading perfume.
* 4Hurry, my king! Let's hurry.
Take me to your home.
The Young Women Speak:
We are happy for you!
And we praise your love
even more than wine.
She Speaks:
Young women of Jerusalem,
it is only right
that you should adore him.
5My skin is dark and beautiful,
like a tent in the desert
or like Solomon's curtains.
6Don't stare at me
just because the sun
has darkened my skin.
My brothers were angry with me;
they made me work in the vineyard,
and so I neglected
my complexion.
7My darling, I love you!
Where do you feed your sheep
and let them rest at noon?
Don't let the other shepherds
think badly of me.
I'm not one of those women
who shamelessly follow
after shepherds.
He Speaks:
8My dearest, if you don't know,
just follow the path
of the sheep.
Then feed your young goats
near the shepherds' tents.
9You move as gracefully
as the pony that leads
the chariot of the king.
10Earrings add to your beauty,
and you wear a necklace
of precious stones.
11Let's make you some jewelry
of gold, woven with silver.
She Speaks:
12My king, while you
were on your couch,
my aroma was a magic charm.
13My darling, you are perfume
between my breasts;
14you are flower blossoms
from the gardens of En-Gedi.
He Speaks:
15My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
your eyes are those of a dove.
She Speaks:
16My love, you are handsome,
truly handsome—
the fresh green grass
will be our wedding bed
17in the shade of cedar
and cypress trees.
translation_text:
1Koori Solomɔn yir la uŋ yittɛ u du sum kaali yira maa labuu keŋ.
Lugli yir
Haŋfalii n na kɛlli u jaari ni wia
2Koriŋ, di bagliŋ i nɔŋŋaa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, i nɔŋŋaa
summɔ kaali siŋ.
3I sɔɔh summɔɔ lugɔ tulaale,
i sɔŋ ɛɛ lugɔ
baŋ mizi tulaale.
Awiarɛ suŋgure maa
ra nyiŋŋii.
4Lawiŋ ya chɔ kaali, a ɛɛ manaŋ!
Ɛɛ n koori,
di kpogliŋ zuu i dia.
Dammuzi
Yaa bɔra daŋ sɔɔni, i wia daŋ par yaa,
yaa daŋ chɔli i nɔŋŋaa
di kaali siŋ.
Haŋfalii
Awia, suŋgure
maanii ra nyiŋŋii!
5Jɛrusalɛm biihaana, n biroore ka du wer,
di biri lugɔ
Kɛda Hɛribɔduma tantizi,
ka du wer alugɔ
Koori Solomɔn
kooridia patiisazi.
6Ií gilɛɛ ra gbɛlliŋ dikuu n biraa wia,
dikuu wiizi n gillɛ
n biri wia.
N niubambinaa faa na baannɛ duŋ,
di gil n hum huma
grepu daazi koo biini.
N faa waa
n hiŋ kossaa saŋa dɔɔwɛ.
7N sɛnni, ŋɔ n be,
lee i nɔɔni i peeza la
á ga dei?
Lee a chɔɔ
heezi wibaŋai?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń gaagi di ra nyiŋŋii
penɔɔna baŋhina
peeza biinei?
Haŋfalii jaari
8Haa de zummɛa,
haana biini maa toloori?
La gaa hiŋ a peeza luge,
di nyiŋŋi kooree tɛɛ i bupɔla
n dugli penɔɔna tantizi la.
9N sɛnni, baala ra nyiŋŋiibuu
alugɔ Ijip koori zagra
n na tɛrgi torkozi,
n na nyiŋŋi zagniina.
10I nyuhuna wessoo di tɔ i giraa,
di chɔɔ i baŋaa lugɔ
baŋaakuna la
n wesse werge,
a yoola du kpol.
11Ka yaa daŋ kuari saliŋ dignikuna,
di kpa saliŋhuŋŋu
margi a ni tɛi.
Haŋfalii
12N koori faa chɔɔ u karjaŋ ninɛɛ,
n tulaale sɔɔh
tɔ bɔr maa.
13N sɛnni ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ tulaale,
di chɔɔ n bampirii.
14N sɛnni ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ pir daazi
n na fii Ɛn Gɛdi
grepu daazi kooni biini.
Haŋfalii jaari
15N sɛnni, i wessoo,
i ɛɛ suŋguruu werge,
i siwee ra nyɛgzi
lugɔ komma siwee.
Haŋfalii
16N sɛnni, i ɛɛ bunɔɔnnɛ werge!
I wia ra parimbuu!
Kooriilɛɛrii niŋ
ɛɛ yaa kunchɔɔrikuŋ.
17Hɛriŋkpol daazi niŋ ɛɛ yaa dia dolli,
daananaa ɛɛ
u saŋa ni daabii.

english_text:
Love Makes Everything Beautiful
She Speaks:
1I am merely a rose
from the land of Sharon,
a lily from the valley.
He Speaks:
2My darling, when compared
with other young women,
you are a lily among thorns.
She Speaks:
3And you, my love,
are an apple tree
among trees of the forest.
Your shade brought me pleasure;
your fruit was sweet.
4You led me to your banquet room
and showered me with love.
5Refresh and strengthen me
with raisins and apples.
I am hungry for love!
6Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
7Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Winter Is Past
She Speaks:
8I hear the voice
of the one I love,
as he comes leaping
over mountains and hills
9like a deer or a gazelle.
Now he stands outside our wall,
looking through the window
10and speaking to me.
He Speaks:
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
11Winter is past,
the rain has stopped;
12flowers cover the earth,
it's time to sing.
The cooing of doves
is heard in our land.
13Fig trees are bearing fruit,
while blossoms on grapevines
fill the air with perfume.
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
14You are my dove
hiding among the rocks
on the side of a cliff.
Let me see how lovely you are!
Let me hear the sound
of your melodious voice.
15Our vineyards are in blossom;
we must catch the little foxes
that destroy the vineyards.
She Speaks:
16My darling, I am yours,
and you are mine,
as you feed your sheep
among the lilies.
17Pretend to be a young deer
dancing on mountain slopes
until daylight comes
and shadows fade away.
translation_text:
Haŋfalii
1N ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Sarɔn pir daa fii
di ɛɛ yuuga
n du walli biine.
Haŋfalii jaari
2Gunla yuuga n chigɛ sɔɔhri biini la,
gunnɛ n sɛnni du
suŋgure biini.
Haŋfalii
3Gunla soom daa la n na nɔŋ nɔnsuma
n chigɛ kɔr biini la,
gunnɛ n sɛnni wia ra pariŋ
di kaali bunɔɔna maa.
4U kpoglimbuu ba u diuzenaa diiribɔr,
di kpa u kotowia tɔŋ,
di bagliŋ u nɔŋŋaa werge.
5Tɛŋ huu la n summɛ,
di gil n bir dɔɔ fɔŋŋa,
di tɛŋ sooma
n bir dɔɔ alaanfia!
I nɔŋŋaa werge
gillɔɔ n bɔra siu vɛlɛɛ.
6N sil u nomɛɛl ninɛɛ,
u nodig ge koriŋ.
7Jɛrusalɛm haana,
ií kpa chaŋkpalŋa
ani weema gbaŋzi
di ŋɔ nua tɛŋ lugɔ
ii wàá kpa ii nuuzi
di hau yaa nyiŋŋaa
wia biini,
ka yaa saŋa haa hel.
Yir nɛɛhiŋ
Haŋfalii
8N nuu n sɛnni loobiire.
Uŋ chɔwɛɛ lii bizenaa nyuuni di ra ba,
di chɔ gilgi giŋgimee
di ra ba n be.
9N sɛnni ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ weema,
alugɔ chɛɛh.
Na! U chigɔ koŋlii zɛɛrɛ,
di ga tokoro di ra liŋŋi,
di ga u bɔɔjigzi
di ra binni tiiih.
10N sɛnni ŋɔ wiarɛ n be,
“Izi, n sɛnni,
n sɛnninanii,
ba n nii ra la.
11Na! Yuu tunnɔɔ,
dooŋ kponnoo.
12Kuna fiiwɔɔ,
yira yiraa saŋa helloo,
yaa ra nuu
kommazi wiraa yaa hɛri.
13Fig nɔna faari aaihrɛ,
grepu daazi fiiri
sɔɔh tɔ bɔr maa.
Awia, izi n sɛnni,
n sɛnninanii,
a ba n nii ra la.”
Haŋfalii jaari
14I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ komma n suah
bii bɔɔ.
Gil n na i toloosiwee la,
di nuu i loobisum la.
15Ií lauri nyɛgɛzi la,
biljigzi la,
mɔɔ ka a chɔgi
yaa grepu daazi
n na fii.
Haŋfalii
16N sɛnni ɛɛ n hotte, n ge ɛɛ u hor.
U ra tɛɛ u peezaa diwee
yuugazi biini,
17guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi chɔɔzi ni,
hamuŋa kaali.
Bir ba alugɔ weema, n sɛnninanii,
alugɔ chɛɛh n du
bizenaa n du
kpurmakpurma nyuuni.

english_text:
Beautiful Dreams
She Speaks:
1While in bed at night,
I reached for the one I love
with heart and soul.
I looked for him,
but he wasn't there.
2So I searched through the town
for the one I love.
I looked on every street,
but he wasn't there.
3I even asked the guards
patrolling the town,
“Have you seen the one
I love so much?”
4Right after that, I found him.
I held him and would not let go
until I had taken him
to the home of my mother.
5Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles,
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
The Groom and the Wedding Party
Their Friends Speak:
6What do we see approaching
from the desert
like a cloud of smoke?
With it comes the sweet smell
of spices, including myrrh
and frankincense.
7It is King Solomon
carried on a throne,
surrounded by sixty
of Israel's best soldiers.
8Each of them wears a sword.
They are experts at fighting,
even in the dark.
9The throne is made of trees
from Lebanon.
10Its posts are silver,
the back is gold,
and the seat is covered
with purple cloth.
You women of Jerusalem
have taken great care
to furnish the inside.
11Now come and see the crown
given to Solomon by his mother
on his happy wedding day.
translation_text:
1Hamuŋa maa, n ɔɔ chɔɔ n kunchɔɔrikuŋ ninɛɛ,
di ra fɛ n sɛnninanii wia,
di ra nyiŋŋi u bɔr,
ka mɔɔ nawɛɛ.
2Awia, n daŋ izi gaagi di bar a bolzeŋ,
u ŋmɛnizenaa ni fɔɔliizi.
N daŋ nyiŋŋi unla min nɔŋŋɛɛ.
Denii n binni,
ka mɔɔ nawɛɛ.
3Tauduura la n na bar a bolzeŋ naŋ.
N pɛɛzi baa,
“Ií waa
n sɛnni nawɛɛa?”
4Miŋ haŋ waa gil baa, di n nau.
N lawuu, maa kaa gil u kaali,
ka kpogluu ba n maa dia,
dia la biini baŋ luliŋ la.
5Jɛrusalɛm haana,
ií kpa chaŋkpalŋa
ani weema gbaŋzi,
di ŋɔ nua tɛŋ lugɔ
ii wàá kpa ii nuuzi
di hau yaa nyiŋŋaa wia biini,
ka yaa saŋa haa hel.
Yir horohiŋ
Haŋfalii
6Anɛɛ n lii hɛribɔduma biini di ra ba
alugɔ nyɔɔzi n tɔwɛɛ,
di ra sɔɔhri daahɛgsɔɔhsuma
ni tulaale la
kɔkɔɔza n na yooi?
7Na! Koori Solomɔnnɛ soge u koorikara ni,
ba chiu di ra ba,
Laallɔɔra tokkoahoroo
ɛɛ u guure,
Izrɛl hina laallɔkpegaa.
8Ba maanii zum tokobi kpai lɔ laal nɛnnɛ,
di zum laal lɔi
siwee werge.
Bɛl maanii vɔɔwɛ di kpogli tokobi,
di ra guu hamuŋa wilezi.
9Koori Solomɔn sogo
u koorikara ninɛɛ,
ba chiu.
Daazi la n wesse nɛnnɛɛ
ba kpa sɛɛuh.
10Saliŋhuŋŋuu ba kpa tɔ u daazi la
baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra chiu,
di kpa saliŋ tɔ
u sognibɔr ni.
Wɛjɛ la n aahwɛ alugɔ zagbiiŋ niirɛ,
ba kpa tɔ u kaputtizi ni,
Jɛrusalɛm haanaa
kpa kunnanaa
la baŋ suahwɛɛ tɔ u biini
ni u har maa nɛnnɛ.
11Bolzeŋ Ziɔn haana,
ií ba wa na Koori Solomɔn.
U hi koorikahuro la
u maa n kpawɛɛ hiubuu,
a hɔl la uŋ kpa haaŋ la,
u bɔsɔna ni
u bɔpuraa hɔpizii la.

english_text:
What a Beautiful Bride
He Speaks:
1My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
as you look through your veil,
your eyes are those of a dove.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
2Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
3Your lips are crimson cords,
your mouth is shapely;
behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
4Your neck is more graceful
than the tower of David,
decorated with thousands
of warriors' shields.
5Your breasts are perfect;
they are twin deer
feeding among lilies.
6I will hasten to those hills
sprinkled with sweet perfume
and stay there till sunrise.
7My darling, you are lovely
in every way.
8My bride, together
we will leave Lebanon!
We will say goodbye
to the peaks of Mount Amana,
Senir, and Hermon,
where lions and leopards
live in the caves.
9My bride, my very own,
you have stolen my heart!
With one glance from your eyes
and the glow of your necklace,
you have stolen my heart.
10Your love is sweeter than wine;
the smell of your perfume
is more fragrant than spices.
11Your lips are a honeycomb;
milk and honey
flow from your tongue.
Your dress has the aroma
of cedar trees from Lebanon.
12My bride, my very own,
you are a garden, a fountain
closed off to all others.
13Your arms are vines,
covered with delicious fruits
and all sorts of spices—
henna, nard, 14saffron,
calamus, cinnamon,
frankincense, myrrh, and aloes
—all the finest spices.
15You are a spring in the garden,
a fountain of pure water,
and a refreshing stream
from Mount Lebanon.
She Speaks:
16Let the north wind blow,
the south wind too!
Let them spread the aroma
of my garden,
so the one I love
may enter and taste
its delicious fruits.
translation_text:
Haŋfalii jaari
1N sɛnni, na gunla hiŋ wesse!
Na gunla i siwee
n na nyɛgzi
i saata biini!
I nyuhuna pɛ lugɔ bukpila
n lii Giliad bizeŋ nyuu
di ra tuu.
2I nyina huuhzi
alugɔ baŋ fuŋ peeza huna
ka sɔa nii.
Bɛl maa waa foŋŋe,
a maa chigɔɔ
di hiŋzi dɔŋa ni nɛnnɛ.
3I nuuhɔna aah yorototo
alugɔ ŋmɛŋaahmu.
Di i haŋ waa ŋɔ wia,
a wessi ɔɔ nyaŋŋuu.
I giraa du wer
di suah i saata biini.
4I baŋaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Koori Deevid diijaŋ la,
n wesse werge maa la.
I laali baŋaakuŋ
u ɛɛ lugɔ
laal pɛrɛtuzi kagboŋ,
di bar.
5I ila ɛɛwɔɔ alugɔ weembizi anɛɛ
alugɔ chaŋkpalŋa biinɛɛri
n du yuugazi biini
di ra di.
6N daŋ so tulaale giŋgimii nyuu,
daahɛgsɔɔhsuma gindalee nyuu,
guŋŋ di ra ba saŋa la
hɔɔ niŋ wa pizi,
hamuŋa jaa tuŋ la.
7N sɛnni, na gunla hiŋ wesse,
di du kpeg nɛnnɛ!
8N haŋfalii, gil ya lii Lɛbanɔn bizenaa nyuuni tuu,
yá lii Lɛbanɔn nyuu tuu.
Yá lii Bizeŋ Amana nyuu tuu,
Bizenaa Sɛnir
ani Hɛmɔn nyuuni,
bɔra la bunyinzi
ni amanizi n duwɛɛ.
9N bampirii kuŋ ni n haŋfalii,
i sibinnaa ani
i baŋaa kuŋ
lau n bampiriire.
10N bampirii kuŋ ni n haŋfalii!
I nyiŋŋaa ra pur n bɔraa.
I nyiŋŋaa bɔ siŋ,
i tulaale sɔɔhri kaali
kunsɔɔhrisum maa.
11N sɛnni, huuhnuu kpissi du i nuuhɔna ninɛɛ,
i nuuzuŋŋi ɛɛ ilanii
ni huuhnuu tɛŋ.
I bɔmbɔga ra sɔɔhri
lugɔ Lɛbanɔn bɔmbɔga.
12N bampirii kuŋ ni n haŋfalii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ wolo kambol,
kambol la baŋ ma koŋlii bar,
i ɛɛ lugɔ nɛkpaŋ bule.
13Denii kuna ra izi nɛnnɛ.
A ra hel lugɔ daazi la n na nɔŋ nɛnnɛ lugɔ pomegranet,
di ra nɔŋ nɔnnanaa.
Kunsɔɔhrisuma ni jawala waa de nyaawɛ,
14daahɛgsɔɔhsuma irizi maa
alugɔ fraŋkinsɛns
ni mɛr du de.
15I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bule,
di ra tɛɛ a kambol nii,
di ɛɛ lugɔ gɔŋa n pallɛ lii
Lɛbanɔn bizenaa nyuuni
di ra tuu.
Haŋfalii
16Wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag peu, izi!
Wiifurii nodig wiikakag peu, izi!
Ba wa ta n kambol ni,
di gil u sɔɔhsum yaari!
Gil n sɛnni ba u kambol
di wa daŋ u nɔnnanaa.

english_text:
He Speaks:
1My bride, my very own,
I come to my garden
and enjoy its spices.
I eat my honeycomb and honey;
I drink my wine and milk.
Their Friends Speak:
Eat and drink until
you are drunk with love.
Another Dream
She Speaks:
2I was asleep, but dreaming:
The one I love was at the door,
knocking and saying,
“My darling, my very own,
my flawless dove,
open the door for me!
My head is drenched
with evening dew.”
3But I had already undressed
and bathed my feet.
Should I dress again
and get my feet dirty?
4Then my darling's hand
reached to open the latch,
and my heart stood still.
5When I rose to open the door,
my hands and my fingers
dripped with perfume.
6And I yearned for him
while he spoke to me,
but when I opened the door,
my darling had disappeared.
I searched and shouted,
but I could not find him—
there was no answer.
7Then I was found by the guards
patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.
They beat me up
and stripped off my robe.
8Young women of Jerusalem,
if you find the one I love,
please say to him,
“She is weak with desire.”
Their Friends Speak:
9Most beautiful of women,
why is the one you love
more special than others?
Why do you ask us
to tell him how you feel?
She Speaks:
10He is handsome and healthy,
the most outstanding
among ten thousand.
11His head is purest gold;
his hair is wavy,
black as a raven.
12His eyes are a pair of doves
bathing in a stream
flowing with milk.
13His face is a garden
of sweet-smelling spices;
his lips are lilies
dripping with perfume.
14His arms are branches of gold
covered with jewels;
his body is ivory
decorated with sapphires.
15His legs are columns of marble
on feet of gold.
He stands there majestic
like Mount Lebanon
and its choice cedar trees.
16His kisses are sweet.
I desire him so much!
Young women of Jerusalem,
he is my lover and friend.
translation_text:
Haŋfalii jaari
1N bampirii kuŋ ni n haŋfalii, n zuu n kambol biinii.
N chaali n mɛr ni
n daahɛgsɔɔhsumaa.
N di n huuhnuu ni huuhpɛɛnaa,
di nyɔɔ n siŋ ni ilanii.
Dammuzi
N dammuzi, ií ra di, di ra nyɔɔ,
guŋŋ ii wa dɛɛzi
ni nɔŋŋaa!
Yir naazuhiŋ
Haŋfalii
2N faa chɔɔ dɔɔrɛ ka ra liizi n sɛnni wia.
N deezi n sɛnni
n lɔ kɔkɔ, di ŋɔ,

1N bampirii kuŋ ni n haŋfalii, n zuu n kambol biinii.
N chaali n mɛr ni
n daahɛgsɔɔhsumaa.
N di n huuhnuu ni huuhpɛɛnaa,
di nyɔɔ n siŋ ni ilanii.
Dammuzi
N dammuzi, ií ra di, di ra nyɔɔ,
guŋŋ ii wa dɛɛzi
ni nɔŋŋaa!
Yir naazuhiŋ
Haŋfalii
2N faa chɔɔ dɔɔrɛ ka ra liizi n sɛnni wia.
N deezi n sɛnni
n lɔ kɔkɔ, di ŋɔ,
“Pilli ń zuu, n niuhambie,
n bampirii kuŋ ni n saliŋ.
Ŋmɛnii chol n nyuurɛ,
di pɔɔh n nyuhuna.”
3N teŋ wir n laalaa,
bɛɛwiarɛ ń kaa laalaawɛi?
N sanzi n naazii,
bɛɛwiarɛ ń kaa doŋaawei?
4N sɛnni ra pilli gberaa,
n bɔra ra nyurgi,
dikuu uŋ duglɛɛ wia.
5N izi ń pilluu,
miŋ ga lau a gbera pillibɔr la,
n nonee ni n nonibee
maa tɔ ni mɛr.
6N pilli a gbera tɛɛ n sɛnni,
di u teŋ kaalɔɔ.
N faa ra nyiŋŋuu ń nuu u loobii!
N nyiŋŋuu guŋŋ ka mɔɔ nawɛɛ,
di yiruu guŋŋ
ka waa sɛɛwɛ.
7A guure naŋ,
di ba ra bar a bolzeŋ.
Ba lɔɔziŋ, n bɔra yigli chal,
ka kpa n wɛjɛ kaali,
baabuu koŋlaa guure la!
8Jɛrusalɛm haana, ií ŋɔ nua tɛŋ
lugɔ di ii wa na n sɛnni,
ii daŋ kaluu
dí u nɔŋŋaa gillɔɔ n pɛssi.
Dammuzi
9Haana maa toloori,
i sɛnni kur
nɛr maa hor ninɛɛaa?
Bɛɛ waarɛ du de, di gil u wia tir werge
lugɔ ya ŋɔ nua tɛinɛi?
Haŋfalii
10N sɛnni ɛɛ bunɔɔnnɛ di du kpeg,
u dɔŋa kpaŋkpaŋaa
du nɛra kagboŋa fi biini.
11U nyuu ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ salinnanii,
u nyuhuna gurgi nɛnnɛ,
di biri lugɔ dugli.
12U siwee du wer alugɔ kommazi
n sɔ ilanii
di togni gɔŋ kɛrii.
13U giraa du wer alugɔ kambol la
n su kunsɔɔhrihsuma.
U nuuhɔna ɛɛ lugɔ
mɛr n lii yuugazi ni
di ra toŋzi.
14U nonee mai wessoo nɛnnɛ,
u ra du nonibisiga la
yoola n kpolle.
U bɔra vɔgli lugɔ baŋ vɔgli bala nyiŋ la
di kpa binanii burgu la
yoola n kpolle
di margi u ni.
15U naazi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bihuŋŋu ligee,
a zɛɛzi hɔŋrikuna
ɛɛ saliŋ.
U girme ni u zenni kannɔɔ
alugɔ Lɛbanɔn bizenaa
ni hɛriŋkpola la
n jaŋŋɛzi werge.
16U koraa summɔɔ,
u wiimaanii pariŋ.
Jɛrusalɛm haana,
gunnɛ n sɛnni hiŋ du.

english_text:
He Speaks:
1My bride, my very own,
I come to my garden
and enjoy its spices.
I eat my honeycomb and honey;
I drink my wine and milk.
Their Friends Speak:
Eat and drink until
you are drunk with love.
Another Dream
She Speaks:
2I was asleep, but dreaming:
The one I love was at the door,
knocking and saying,
“My darling, my very own,
my flawless dove,
open the door for me!
My head is drenched
with evening dew.”
3But I had already undressed
and bathed my feet.
Should I dress again
and get my feet dirty?
4Then my darling's hand
reached to open the latch,
and my heart stood still.
5When I rose to open the door,
my hands and my fingers
dripped with perfume.
6And I yearned for him
while he spoke to me,
but when I opened the door,
my darling had disappeared.
I searched and shouted,
but I could not find him—
there was no answer.
7Then I was found by the guards
patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.
They beat me up
and stripped off my robe.
8Young women of Jerusalem,
if you find the one I love,
please say to him,
“She is weak with desire.”
Their Friends Speak:
9Most beautiful of women,
why is the one you love
more special than others?
Why do you ask us
to tell him how you feel?
She Speaks:
10He is handsome and healthy,
the most outstanding
among ten thousand.
11His head is purest gold;
his hair is wavy,
black as a raven.
12His eyes are a pair of doves
bathing in a stream
flowing with milk.
13His face is a garden
of sweet-smelling spices;
his lips are lilies
dripping with perfume.
14His arms are branches of gold
covered with jewels;
his body is ivory
decorated with sapphires.
15His legs are columns of marble
on feet of gold.
He stands there majestic
like Mount Lebanon
and its choice cedar trees.
16His kisses are sweet.
I desire him so much!
Young women of Jerusalem,
he is my lover and friend.

english_text:
Their Friends Speak:
1Most beautiful of women,
tell us where he has gone.
Let us help you find him.
She Speaks:
2My darling has gone down
to his garden of spices,
where he will feed his sheep
and gather lilies.
3I am his, and he is mine,
as he feeds his sheep
among the lilies.
He Speaks:
4My dearest, the cities of Tirzah
and Jerusalem
are not as lovely as you.
Your charms are more powerful
than all of the stars
in the heavens.
5Turn away your eyes—
they make me melt.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
6Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
7Behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
8What if I could have
sixty queens, eighty wives,
and thousands of others!
9You would be my only choice,
my flawless dove,
the favorite child
of your mother.
The young women, the queens,
and all the others
tell how excited you are
as they sing your praises:
10“You are as majestic
as the morning sky—
glorious as the moon—
blinding as the sun!
Your charms are more powerful
than all the stars above.”
She Speaks:
11I went down to see if blossoms
were on the walnut trees,
grapevines, and fruit trees.
12But in my imagination
I was suddenly riding
on a glorious chariot.
Their Friends Speak:
13Dance! Dance!
Beautiful woman from Shulam,
let us see you dance!
She Speaks:
Why do you want to see
this woman from Shulam
dancing with the others?
translation_text:
Dammuzi
1Haana maa biini toloori,
lee i sɛnni kaalɛi?
Bagli yaa bɔr la barii i sɛnni n kaalɛɛ,
ya wer hiinii nyiŋŋuu.
Haŋfalii
2N sɛnni kaali u kambol,
bɔr la daahɛgsɔɔhsuma
n duwɛɛ la.
U ra tɛɛ u peezaa diwee a kambol biini,
di ra chaali yuugazi.
3N sɛnni ɛɛ n hotte, n ge ɛɛ u hor,
u ra tɛɛ u peezaa diwee
yuugazi biini.
Yir nuehiŋ
Haŋfalii jaari
4N nɔŋŋi, i wessoo lugɔ bolzeŋ Tirza,
di du wer lugɔ Jɛrusalɛm,
i girme ɛɛ lugɔ
laallɔɔra n kpogli tuutazi.
5Gilɛɛ ra binniŋ,
i siwee ra lawimbuu
alugɔ baŋ lɔ laal
di lau nɛr.
I nyuhuna pɛ lugɔ bukpila
n lii Giliad giŋgimee
nyuuni di ra tuu.
6I nyina huuhzi alugɔ peeza
baŋ sɔa nii, a ra ba.
Bɛl maa waa foŋŋe,
a maa chigɔɔ
di hiŋzi dɔŋa ni nɛnnɛ.
7I giraa du wer
di suah i saata biini.
8Gil kóori dɔɔ wichezi tokkoahoro,
hahjigzi tokkoanaazu
ani suŋgure la
n waa maga dɔɔwɛ!
9Ka kpaŋkpaŋ bɛnnɛ n na nyiŋŋi,
u wessoo alugɔ komma.
U bɛnnɛ ɛɛ u maa biihaaŋ
ani u biinɔŋŋii.
Haana maanii ɔɔ binnuu di ra chɔluu,
wichezi ni u hahjigzi
yir yira di ra chɔluu.
Dammuzi
10Anɛɛ n na ba alugɔ hɔɔ n na pizi kennei?
U ɛɛ suŋguruu di wermi,
di du wer alugɔ baagu,
di ra chaani alugɔ wiizi,
alugɔ chinchiŋwilaa
n hiŋ dɔŋa.
Haŋfalii jaari
11N lii almɔn daazi biinii tuu ba,
ń wa na kuna la
n faarɛɛ di fur
waluu biini,
ń wa na grepu ni pomegranet daazi fiiri.
12N bɔra ra zaguu,
i gillɔɔ màá wer di
i nyiŋŋaa kanyitti
alugɔ zagu ni
u torko zuuri
n na la laal.
Dammuzi
13Bir ba, bir ba, Sulam hinuu.
Bir ba, bir ba,
ya kaa nai!
Haŋfalii jaari
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra nyiŋŋi n binnaa
gunla nɛra
n na nyiŋŋi
saara binnaa lai?

english_text:
The Wedding Dance
He Speaks:
1You are a princess,
and your feet are graceful
in their sandals.
Your thighs are works of art,
each one a jewel;
2your navel is a wine glass
filled to overflowing.
Your body is full and slender
like a bundle of wheat
bound together by lilies.
3Your breasts are like twins
of a deer.
4Your neck is like ivory,
and your eyes sparkle
like the pools of Heshbon
by the gate of Bath-Rabbim.
Your nose is beautiful
like Mount Lebanon
above the city of Damascus.
5Your head is held high
like Mount Carmel;
your hair is so lovely
it holds a king prisoner.
6You are very beautiful,
so desirable!
7You are tall and slender
like a palm tree,
and your breasts are full.
8I will climb that tree
and cling to its branches.
I will discover that your breasts
are clusters of grapes,
and that your breath
is the aroma of apples.
9Kissing you is more delicious
than drinking the finest wine.
How wonderful and tasty!
She Speaks:
10My darling, I am yours,
and you desire me.
11Let's stroll through the fields
and sleep in the villages.
12At dawn let's slip out and see
if grapevines and fruit trees
are covered with blossoms.
When we are there,
I will give you my love.
13Perfume from the magic flower
fills the air, my darling.
Right at our doorstep
I have stored up for you
all kinds of tasty fruits.
translation_text:
Haŋfalii jaari
1I ɛɛ toloorii werge maa!
Na gunla i naazi
ni gawa n wesse!
I napɔga chol dɔŋa ni nɛnnɛ
alugɔ nɛr la
n zum nonii huma huŋhunnaa.
2I ulee ɛɛ gulegulee lugɔ tassa biini
n waa siŋ la
n koozi dɔŋa ni
nɛnnɛ ra nyaa.
I hia du lugɔ baŋ kum huuti dau kululu,
yuugazi baraa.
3I ila ɛɛwɔɔ alugɔ weembizi anɛɛ
alugɔ chaŋkpalŋa biinɛɛri.
4I baŋaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ diijaŋ la baŋ kpa bala nyina ma.
I siwee ɛɛ lugɔ bolzeŋ Hɛsbɔn polni la
n dugli a bolzeŋ
dominuuzeŋ la
banna yir Baf Rabim la.
I miizi wessoo lugɔ Lɛbanɔn diijaŋ la
n chigɛ chaŋ Damaskus la.
5I lalli i nyuurɛ chiŋ lugɔ Bizeŋ Kamɛl.
I nyuhumpɛttaa
ra nyɛgzuu
lugɔ agoonanii,
a wessi ɔɔ lau
koori bampiriire
alugɔ baŋ lɔ laal
di lau nɛr la.
6Na gunla hiŋ wesse, gunla hiŋ ɛɛ toloori,
gunla min dɔɔ
bɔsɔna nɛnnɛ,
dikuu i nyiŋŋaa wia.
7I ɛɛwɔɔ zɔrɔmm lugɔ kakubkpaŋkpargu daa,
i ila ɛɛ lugɔ u nɔna
n mari dɔŋa chuppu.
8N daŋ zinnuu di tɔrgi u nɔna.
I ila ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
grepu nɔna nyuu n be,
i heeza sɔɔh du sum
alugɔ maŋgozi sɔɔh,
9i nua lugɔ sinnanii.
Haŋfalii
A siŋ vii pal deŋli la n sɛnni be,
di gaa pal u nuuhɔna
ni u nyina ni guŋ bɔɔiih.
10N ɛɛ n sɛnni hotte,
n wia ra kɛlluu.
11N sɛnni, a ba, gil ya lii la a bolzeŋ nua,
di ga chɔɔ de hamuŋa naa.
12Yaa daŋ feli izi di binni grepu daazi kooni,
di na, di a ra fiiwɔ gɛɛ
di a fiiri pillɔɔ
gɛɛ di pomegranet daazi ra fii,
denii ń jaa nyiŋŋii.
13I daŋ nuu daa lunne la
n na hiini haana
ba ra lul
ni nɔnsuma la maa,
n dugli yaa
gbera la sɔɔh.
N sɛnni, afalaa ni abinaa
maanii n dawii.

english_text:
If Only You and I …
She Speaks:
1If you were my brother,
I could kiss you
whenever we happen to meet,
and no one would say
I did wrong.
2I could take you to the home
of my mother,
who taught me all I know.
I would give you delicious wine
and fruit juice as well.
3Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
4Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Their Friends Speak:
5Who is this young woman
coming in from the desert
and leaning on the shoulder
of the one she loves?
She Speaks:
I stirred up your passions
under the apple tree
where you were born.
6Always keep me in your heart
and wear this bracelet
to remember me by.
The passion of love
bursting into flame
is more powerful than death,
stronger than the grave.
7Love cannot be drowned
by oceans or floods.
It cannot be bought—
any offer would be scorned
no matter how great.
Their Friends Speak:
8We have a little sister
whose breasts
are not yet formed.
If someone asks to marry her,
what should we do?
9She isn't a wall
that we can defend
behind a silver shield.
Neither is she a room
that we can protect
behind a wooden door.
She Speaks:
10I am a wall around a city,
my breasts are towers,
and just looking at me
brings him great pleasure.
11Solomon has a vineyard
at Baal-Hamon,
which he rents to others
for a thousand pieces
of silver each.
12My vineyard is mine alone!
Solomon can keep his silver
and the others can keep
their share of the profits.
He Speaks:
13You are in the garden
with friends all around.
Let me hear your voice!
She Speaks:
14Hurry to me, my darling!
Run faster than a deer
to mountains of spices.
translation_text:
Haŋfalii
1Kunla faa ŋɔ lugɔ n niubambiere hiŋ,
alugɔ n maa illɛ i ɔzi.
Di n faa huuzii bossee,
n daŋ faa korii,
ka a wàá tir nɛr maa.
2N daŋ vii kpoglii di la n maa dia,
unla n dɛɛziŋ la.
N daŋ tɛi siŋ la sɔɔh n summɛ
alugɔ pomegranet siŋ, í nyɔɔ.
3N sil u nomɛɛl ninɛɛ,
u nodig ge koriŋ.
4Jɛrusalɛm haana, ií ŋɔ nua tɛŋ,
lugɔ ii wàá kpa ii nuuzi
di hau yaa
nyiŋŋaa wia biini,
ka yaa saŋa haa hel.
Yir numbɛlhiŋ
Dammuzi
5Anɛɛ n lii hɛribɔduma biini di ra ba,
u ni u sɛnni lau
dɔŋa nonee kennei?
Haŋfalii
N lalliibuu dɔɔ, soom zɛɛ,
bɔr la baŋ lulii la.
6Lizi i bampirii lii nɔŋŋaa maa ni, see n hor,
gilɛɛ kaa
wàá kor nɛr maa,
see n bɛŋ.
Dɔŋa nɔŋŋaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa alugɔ siu,
u zoma du kpeg
alugɔ ŋmam.
Dɔŋa nɔŋŋaa ɔɔ lau ninne,
di ra haahri
alugɔ ninzeŋ.
7Nii wàá wer dinzuu,
nii la maa n suwee
wàá wer diu.
Ka di nɛr la maa ra nyiŋŋi
ú kpa daama yau nɔŋŋaa,
hiihzii ú di.
Niubambinaa
8Yaa dɔɔ niuhambijigaa,
u ila haa waa suwee.
Bɛɛ yá ɛɛ tɛu
di biipɔllii
waa nyiŋŋuuwei?
9Di u vii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ koŋlii,
yaa daŋ ma
saliŋhuŋŋu diijaŋra
di hɔŋ u ni.
Di u vii kaa ɛɛu lugɔ dominua,
yaa daŋ kpa
hɛriŋkpol daapiahni mɛɛruu.
Haŋfalii
10N ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ koŋlii,
n ila ɛɛ lugɔ diijaŋra.
N sɛnni zummɔ lugɔ u benii
n na na bɔsɔna werge.
11Koori Solomɔn dɔɔ koonaniirɛ,
u du bɔr la
banna yir Baal Hamɔn.
Patta lɛɛu ra par, ka ra turguu,
bɛl maa ra turgi
saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kagboŋ.
12Gil Koori Solomɔn dɔɔ
saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kagboŋ,
patta la ge dɔɔ kalfaanɛɛ, a ɛɛ ba hora,
ka miŋwaa dɔɔ
n himmaa grepu daazi koore!
Haŋfalii jaari
13N sɛnni, gil n nuu i loobii
a kambol biini,
n dammuzi ra kpaŋuu
í ŋɔ wia!
Haŋfalii
14Ba n be, n sɛnni, alugɔ weema,
alugɔ chɛhbalee
n du bizenaa nyuuni,
bɔr la kunsɔɔhrisuma
n duwɛɛ.

english_text:
1 I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz.
And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah:
A Guilty Nation
2The Lord has said,
“Listen, heaven and earth!
The children I raised
have turned against me.
3Oxen and donkeys know
who owns and feeds them,
but my people won't ever learn.”
4Israel, you are a sinful nation
loaded down with guilt.
You are wicked and corrupt
and have turned from the Lord,
the holy God of Israel.
5Why be punished more?
Why not give up your sin?
Your head is badly bruised,
and you are weak all over.
6From your head to your toes
there isn't a healthy spot.
Bruises, cuts, and open sores
go without care
or oil to ease the pain.
A Country in Ruins
7Your country lies in ruins;
your towns are in ashes.
Foreigners and strangers
take and destroy your land
while you watch.
8Enemies surround Jerusalem,
alone like a hut
in a vineyard
or in a cucumber field.
9 Zion would have disappeared
like Sodom and Gomorrah,
if the Lord All-Powerful
had not let a few
of its people survive.
Justice, Not Sacrifices
10You are no better
than the leaders and people
of Sodom and Gomorrah!
So listen to the Lord God:
11 “Your sacrifices
mean nothing to me.
I am sick of your offerings
of rams and choice cattle;
I don't like the blood
of bulls or lambs or goats.
12“Who asked you to bring all this
when you come to worship me?
Stay out of my temple!
13Your sacrifices are worthless,
and your incense disgusting.
I can't stand the evil you do
on your New Moon Festivals
or on your Sabbaths
and other times of worship.
14I hate your New Moon Festivals
and all others as well.
They are a heavy burden
I am tired of carrying.
15“No matter how much you pray,
I won't listen.
You are too violent.
16Wash yourselves clean!
I hate your filthy deeds.
Stop doing wrong
17and learn to live right.
See that justice is done.
Defend widows and orphans
and help the oppressed.”
An Invitation from the Lord
18I, the Lord, invite you
to come and talk it over.
Your sins are scarlet red,
but they will be whiter
than snow or wool.
19If you willingly obey me,
the best crops in the land
will be yours.
20But if you turn against me,
your enemies will kill you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
21Jerusalem, you are like
an unfaithful wife.
Once your judges were honest
and your people lived right;
now you are a city
full of murderers.
22Your silver is fake,
and your wine
is watered down.
23Your leaders have rejected me
to become friends of crooks;
your rulers are looking
for gifts and bribes.
Widows and orphans
never get a fair trial.
24I am the Lord All-Powerful,
the mighty ruler of Israel,
and I make you a promise:
You are now my enemy,
and I will show my anger
by taking revenge on you.
25I will punish you terribly
and burn away everything
that makes you unfit
to worship me.
26Jerusalem, I will choose
judges and advisors
like those you had before.
Your new name will be
“Justice and Faithfulness.”
The Lord Will Save Jerusalem
27Jerusalem, you will be saved
by showing justice;
Zion's people who turn to me
will be saved
by doing right.
28But those rebellious sinners
who turn against me, the Lord,
will all disappear.
29You will be made ashamed
of those groves of trees
where you worshiped idols.
30You will be like a grove of trees
dying in a drought.
31Your strongest leaders
will be like dry wood
set on fire by their idols.
No one will be able to help,
as they all go up in flames.
translation_text:
1Baa bɛllɛ faa du de, u sɔnnɛ Amɔz. U biibaal sɔnnɛ faa Aizaaya. Aizaaya faa na Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm wia naabuu lugɔ deeza biini saŋa la Koora Uzzia, Jɔtam, Ahaz ani Hɛzɛkia n hiŋzi dɔŋa ni, di faa di Juda hɛri kora la.
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u nɛra wichɔgaa wia
2Chiŋ ni hɛri maa, ií ra nuu!
Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Biizi la n himmaa n dɛɛzɛɛ
birgi dignikpega hinaa,
di vɛɛ n nua.
3Nabal zum u dɔɔrii,
kawee gba zum bɔr la
u dɔɔri n na dɛɛzuu,
ka n nɛra Izrɛl hina wan zummɛ,
ba waa wia zɛɛ zummɛ.”
4Aa! Nɛchɔgaa!
Ii bilchɔg siili ii ninɛɛ.
Ii ɛɛ wichɔgɛɛra biizii
di nyaa wibii,
ii vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ.
Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii
labuu ii hah,
di bir ii hara kpuu.
5Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ba kaa lɔɔzi iai?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii haa kpogli
dignikpega di ra vɛɛ
Kɔraawiizi nuai?
Ii nyuuni maanii na pira,
ii bampiree maa
ge chɔgizi.
6Di chi ii naapaala biine di ra la ii nyuuni maanii
ɛɛ ŋmɛra di ɔrgi,
ka ba wàá chakkɛ,
ba wàá duwɛɛ nuu,
ba waa kaa vɔɔzaa ge.
7Ii hɛri maanii chɔkkɛ,
ii bolzenaa fuuh,
di birgi diŋgelli.
Ii kaa ra binni
ka hɔɔhra wa foozi
ii pattikuna
maa nyaamm.
8Bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm bɛnnɛ kawɛɛ,
di jaa ɛɛ lugɔ koolinlɔɔ
n chigɛ grepu daazi koo,
di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ pampanni n chigɛ kiime koo,
di ɛɛ lugɔ bolzeŋ
baŋ fɔɔwɛ.
9Di Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
faa waa
yaa baŋhina gillɛ,
yaa maa daŋ vii tuŋ nyaamm
alugɔ Sɔdɔm
ni Gɔmɔra hina
n faa tunnɛ la.
10Jɛrusalɛm nabɔnzi, ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Sɔdɔm hina.
Ií ra nuu
Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii.
Dignikpega hina lugɔ Gɔmɔra hina,
ií ra nuu
Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg la.
11U ŋɔ ii benii,
“Ii mbusukpila kuna la iinna lizi
di ra tɛŋ la,
bɛɛ a ɛɛnnɛi?
N lɔgɔ liwɔɔrɛ ii mbusu lizaa kuna la iiŋ ɔɔ ra fuuh la wia.
Bɛɛ tɔnaa ii sela la
iin dɛɛzɛɛ a pɔl werge la
nuuri iiŋ fuuhwe
tɛŋ la ge dɔɔi?
Maa kaa ra nyiŋŋi sela la
bɛl maa iiŋ ɔɔ fuuh
ra tɛŋ la.
Maa kaa ra nyiŋŋi n na
ii nabala, pebala gɛɛ
buuna la bɛl maa chal.
12Iiŋ ɔɔ wa ba n jaamaa la,
minuu ŋɔ ii ba
waa ginzi naazi
n diŋŋee di ra duŋŋ?
13A guŋ waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ tɛŋ.
Haali daahɛgsɔɔhsuma
iiŋ fuuhwe lizi mbusu
di ra tɛŋ la
sɔɔh chummɔɔ werge n be.
Ii Baagufalaa Hɔpizizenaa maa, Heezaa Hɔpizii ani jaamaa hɔpizizenaa dii la iiŋ ɔɔ chaali dɔŋa la,
a maa waa wer,
di ɛɛŋ lɔgɔ lii.
14N hah ii diuzenaa la iiŋ ɔɔ ra di Baagufalaa ni ii hɔpizizenaa biini labuu.
A wia bazimbuu
di ɛɛ buntɔgaa tɛŋ.
15Di ii ɔɔ kaa wa lalli ii nonee filaŋkeŋ, ii suŋŋi wiizi,
màá ka binni ia gba.
Haali di ii ra suŋŋi gunla maa,
ka màá nuu a bɛl maa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ii nonee maanii ɛɛ challi.
16Awia, ií sanzi ii nonee wichɔgaa ta ka du wer.
Ií gilɛɛ gil n kaa na
ii wikuna la.
Ií gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi,
17ka ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa.
Ií ra nyiŋŋi wibii dii,
di ra du banla
banna tɔɔri la bɔkpega,
di ra lɛɛ lalbiizi nuuzi,
di kaa yoo ra kuari
luhaana wia.”
18Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ,
“Ií ba ya lɔ nfɛrɛ.
Haali ii wichɔgaa n kannɛ ii ni,
di ɛɛ lugɔ kuŋ n kpoŋŋe
di aah lugɔ chal gba,
ka n daŋ gil
ii huuhzi alugɔ gonni.
19Di ii daŋ sɛɛ ra hiŋ n nuuzi lawaa,
ii daŋ na diwee nɛnnɛ
lii ii kooni di ra di.
20Ama, di ii dɔɔ dignikpega di ra vɛɛ n nuuzi hiŋaa waa,
ii dɔma daŋ wa
yoo ia laal
di kpu ia nyaamm.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔzii guŋ!”
21Bolzeŋ la nɛra wia n faa dɔɔ wibii la,
jaa ɛɛu lugɔ hahsɛnsɛnni!
Wibii hina faa su u biinii,
wideŋlaa faa du de,
ka filaŋkeŋ,
nɛkpuura bɛnnɛ du de!
22Jɛrusalɛm, i faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ saliŋhuŋŋa,
ka filaŋkeŋ, i jaa ɛɛu
lugɔ salimbina,
i faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ sinnanii,
ka filaŋkeŋ,
i jaa ɛɛu lugɔ nii.
23Ii nabɔnzi ɛɛ dignikpega hina
di ɛɛ ŋmɛɛna dammuzi.
Ba aah siweere di ra nyiŋŋi kundizi,
di kpa ba siwii sag a ni.
Ba wàá sɛɛ lɛɛ lalbiizi nuuzi,
ba wàá sɛɛ yoo
di ra kuari luhaana wia.
24Awia, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la,
Fɔŋŋa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina
n na hum la kaa ŋɔu,
“N daŋ turgi n dɔma ba wichɔgaa kim
ka n baaŋ jaa sɔɔniŋ.
25N daŋ du ia siaahmu
ka wer lizi ii widoŋa
ni ii wikuna maa
ii ni ha.
26Di n wa ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ, n daŋ bir tɛɛ ia nabɔnzi la wia n deŋlee
alugɔ banla iiŋ faa felee dɔɔ la.
Denii bá kaa ra yir Jɛrusalɛm
‘Wibii ni Wideŋlaa Bolzeŋ.’ ”
27Kɔraawiizi daŋ bir lɛɛ Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina ni wibii,
banla n bittɛ lii
ba wichɔgaa biinii
ú lɛɛ ni wideŋlaa.
28Ama dignikpeg hina ni wichɔgɛɛra maa daŋ tuŋ,
banla n vɛɛ
Kɔraawiizi la siu.
29Hiihzi daŋ kpu ia dikuu daazenaa la zɛɛzi iiŋ faa ra kuari vuga,
a par ia la.
Ii daŋ ŋmaabi dikuu kambola la
iiŋ lizɛɛ wia.
30Awia, ii daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ daazeŋ la n siuwɛ, u paŋhoori ra war,
di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ
kambol la n hillɛ.
31Nɛkpeg daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ kɔlii,
u wiɛɛlaa ge ɛɛ
alugɔ niŋ di fuuh u maa.
Nɛr maa wàá wer dinzi a niŋ.

english_text:
Peace That Lasts Forever
1This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
2In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills;
every nation will rush to it.
3Many people will come and say,
“Let's go to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
4 He will settle arguments
between nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never make war
or attack one another.
5People of Israel, let's live
by the light of the Lord.
Following Sinful Customs
6Our Lord, you have deserted
your people, Israel,
because they follow customs
of nations from the east.
They worship Philistine gods
and are close friends
of foreigners.
7They have endless treasures
of silver and gold;
they have countless horses
and war chariots.
8Everywhere in the country
they worship the idols
they have made.
9And so, all of them
will be ashamed and disgraced.
Don't forgive them!
A Day of Judgment
10 Every one of you,
go hide among the rocks
and in the ground,
because the Lord is fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious.
11When the Lord comes,
everyone who is proud
will be made humble,
and the Lord alone
will be honored.
12The Lord All-Powerful
has chosen a day
when those who are proud
and conceited
will be put down.
13The tall and towering
cedars of Lebanon
will be destroyed.
So will the oak trees of Bashan,
14all high mountains and hills,
15every strong fortress,
16all the seagoing ships,
and every beautiful boat.
17When that day comes,
everyone who is proud
will be put down.
Only the Lord will be honored.
18Idols will be gone for good.
19You had better hide
in caves and holes—
the Lord will be fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious
when he comes to terrify
people on earth.
20On that day everyone will throw
to the moles and bats
their idols of silver and gold
they made to worship.
21The Lord will be fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious
when he comes to terrify
people on earth—
they will hide in caves
and in the hills.
22Stop trusting the power
of humans.
They are all going to die,
so how can they help?
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ wia
1Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hɛri wii bɛl Amɔz biibaal Aizaaya n faa nawɛɛ lugɔ deeza biinii keŋ.
2Saŋa bɛl n na ba,
a bizeŋ la baŋ ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hɔŋ u nyuu la,
daŋ ɛɛ bizenzeŋ kaali
anla maa n baruu la,
durnya hɛssi nɛra maa
waa nyiŋŋi u bɔr.
3Nɛkpila maa daŋ ba de, di wa ŋɔ,
“Ií ba ya tinni Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ la,
di la Kɔraawiizi la
Jekɔb n na hum la Dia.
U daŋ bagli yaa u ŋmɛnizi,
guŋ gil ya wer
di ra vol u ŋmɛnibizi.”
U Gbɔg daŋ lii Ziɔn,
u wiŋɔɔlii lii Jɛrusalɛm.
4U daŋ di hɛssi hina seriyazi,
di laafi nɛkpila kaluzi.
A hɛssi hina maa daŋ kpa ba tokobizi luu para,
di kpa ba kandaazi ge
luu daazi kɛuraa kizizi.
Laalzi maa daŋ tuŋ.
Ba ge wàá kaa ra ɛɛ laal sirya.
5Izrɛl hina, ií ba
ya ra vol Kɔraawiizi
bɔchaaŋ la biini.
Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii wia
6N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i vɛɛ i nɛraa, Jekɔb diahina.
Ba ra hiŋ wiifurii hina
naana wiarɛ,
di ra vug lugɔ Filisti hina,
ba ni banla n waa
Kɔraawiizi zummɛ
kpau ra ɛɛ wia.
7Ba hɛri dɔɔ saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋaa werge,
ba daama
waa maga dɔɔwɛ.
Zagra su ba hɛri,
ba laal torkozi
waa maga dɔɔwɛ.
8Ba hɛri maanii su vuga.
Ba kuŋkuaraa sezii
ba ɔɔ gaa giŋŋi,
kuna la ba himmaa
nonee n kuarɛɛ.
9Kɔraawiizi daŋ tuu newea zɛɛ,
bá di hiihzi.
Gilɛɛ wa gil
ba wichɔgaa
di ra tɛɛ baa.
10Ií zuu bia bɔɔni.
Ií zuu suah hɛri,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ ani
u zenni ni u girme
n kannɛ werge wia!
11Hɔpizii bɛl ra bau,
ii jigsi ni
ii barabara la maa tuŋ.
Denii bá jaa ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi bɛŋ.
12Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ dau hɔpiziirɛ
tɛɛ banla maa n na jigsi
di ra tɔgzi bahinaa la
ni kuna la maa
banna chɔli,
bá di hiihzi.
13Lɛbanɔn hɛriŋkpol daazi la n jaŋŋɛ werge la
ni Basan daazenaa la maanii
ú chɔgi.
14U daŋ purgi bizenaa la maa n la chiŋ
ni giŋgimee.
15U daŋ purgi diijaŋra la n la chiŋ
ni diikpega koŋlaa.
16Di kaa chɔgi ba muugberzenaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra kɔɔzi
ni muugberzenaa
la n wesse la maa.
17Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil newea jigsi maa tuŋ,
bá barabara la maa tuŋ.
U bɛnnɛ bá tɔgzi a guŋ hɔpizii.
18Ba vuga la maa leu nyaamm.
19Newea daŋ chɔ suahzi bia bɔɔni
ni hɛri bɔɔni,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ wia,
di chɔ suah dikuu
u zenni ni u girme
n kannɛ werge wia,
di u wa izoo
ú zigli hɛri.
20A hɔl hiŋ, ba daŋ paa ba saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa vuga la
baŋ kuarɛɛ la ta
daŋgboŋzi ni tuŋŋizi.
21Di Kɔraawiizi baaŋ wa fuuhwo, u izi zigli hɛri,
newea danna ɔmuu,
di chɔ zuu bia ni hɛri bɔɔzenaa n luŋŋe werge biine,
dikuu u girme ni u zenni
n wesse werge la wia.
22Ií gilɛɛ kpa ii yarda du newea ni.
Bɛɛ tɔnaa ba dɔɔi?

english_text:
Judgment on Jerusalem and Judah
1The mighty Lord All-Powerful
is going to take away
from Jerusalem and Judah
everything you need—
your bread and water,
* 2soldiers and heroes,
judges and prophets,
leaders and army officers,
3officials and advisors,
fortunetellers and others
who tell the future.
4He will let children and babies
become your rulers.
5You will each be cruel
to friends and neighbors.
Young people will insult
their elders;
no one will show respect
to those who deserve it.
6Some of you will grab hold
of a relative and say,
“You still have a coat.
Be our leader and rule
this pile of ruins.”
7But the answer will be,
“I can't do you any good.
Don't make me your leader.
There's no food or clothing
left in my house.”
8Jerusalem and Judah,
you rebelled against
your glorious Lord—
your words and your actions,
made you stumble and fall.
9The look on your faces shows
that you are sinful as Sodom,
and you don't try to hide it.
You are in for trouble,
and you have brought it all
on yourselves.
The Wrong Kind of Leaders
10Tell those who obey God,
“You're very fortunate—
you will be rewarded
for what you have done.”
11Tell those who disobey,
“You're in big trouble—
what you did to others
will come back to you.”
12Though you are God's people,
you are ruled and abused
by women and children.
You are confused by leaders
who guide you
down the wrong path.
13The Lord is ready to accuse
and judge all nations.
14He will even judge
you rulers and leaders
of his own nation.
You destroyed his vineyard
and filled your houses
by robbing the poor.
15The Lord All-Powerful says,
“You have crushed my people
and rubbed in the dirt
the faces of the poor.”
The Women of Jerusalem
16The Lord says:
The women of Jerusalem
are proud and strut around,
winking shamelessly.
They wear anklets that jingle
and call attention
to the way they walk.
17But I, the Lord, will cover
their heads with sores,
and I will uncover
their private parts.
18-23When that day comes, I will take away from those women all the fine jewelry they wear on their ankles, heads, necks, ears, arms, noses, fingers, and on their clothes. I will remove their veils, their belts, their perfume, their magic charms, their royal robes, and all their fancy dresses, hats, and purses.
24In place of perfume,
there will be a stink;
in place of belts,
there will be ropes;
in place of fancy hairdos,
they will have bald heads.
Instead of expensive clothes,
they will wear sackcloth;
instead of beauty,
they will have ugly scars.
25The fighting men of Jerusalem
will be killed in battle.
26The city will mourn
and sit in the dirt,
emptied of its people.
translation_text:
Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina seriya dii wia
1Ií na! Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
ra nyiŋŋuu u teŋ
kuna la maa n na hiini
Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda
hina maa.
U daŋ teŋ ba diwee ni nii maa.
2U daŋ kpu ba hɛri
laallɔkpega ni laallɔɔra maa,
ba sitɔɔra ni ba dɔgtɛɛzi,
ba vugra ni ba nabɔnzi,
3ba laallɔɔra tokkoanɛɛ ni fi nabɔnzi, hɛri nabɔnzi,
banla n zum
nonee huma ani vugra.
4U daŋ jaa lizi biipɔllijigzi bá ɛɛ ba nabɔnzi,
di gil bichalli
ra binni ba ni.
5Nɛra danna sunni dɔŋa,
baal ni baal,
nɛr ni u dɔŋhiŋ.
Bichalli ra gbɛlli nɛzɛŋzi,
nɛdumazi ra gbɛlli nɛtɔga.
6Baal daŋ lau u lulli bɛl
u mɛɛ dia, di ŋɔ,
“Hiŋ dɔɔ laala wia, ɛɛ yaa nabɔma,
di ra binni
bolpurii naa ni.”
7Ka u daŋ ŋɔ siaahmu ni,
“Akai! Màá wer hiini ia.
Maa diwee gɛɛ laala dɔɔwɛ n dia.
Ií gilɛɛ kpaŋ ɛɛ
a nɛra sitɔɔri.”
8Jɛrusalɛm hina ra jiŋluu,
Juda hina ge ra chogli.
Ba wiŋɔɔlaa ni wiɛɛlaa ra zuu Kɔraawiizi ninɛɛ,
di ra gbɛlli u
girme la n du ba baaŋ la.
9Haali di i binni ba siwee, a ra bagluu lugɔ ba ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ
lugɔ Sɔdɔm hina,
ba wàá ra suah.
Wia daŋ huuzi baa!
Ba kpa hɛhchɔgrɛ
ta bahinaa ni.
10Ama, ŋɔ banla waa wia n deŋlee be lugɔ ba wia daŋ kuari.
Ba daŋ di
ba winanaa tɔna.
11Wia daŋ huuzi wichɔgɛɛra! Hɛhchɔg chol ba ninɛɛ!
Ba daŋ na ba wiɛɛlaa kinturgaa.
12Biipɔllaa ra sunni n nɛraa.
Haana ge ra di kora ba ni.
Ee, n nɛra! Ií sitɔɔra gillɔɔ ii leu,
di gil ii waa kaa ra
hiŋ a ŋmɛnibee.
13Kɔraawiizi sogo u seriya diiribɔttɛ.
U izoore ú di
nɛra seriya.
14U nɛra nabɔnzi ni ba sitɔɔra seriyaa
u ra di, di ŋɔ,
“Iabuu chɔgi n grepu daazi koo.
Nyaara la kuna iin foozee
ba be la su ii diinii.
15A zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ ii ra sunni n nɛrai,
di ra foozi nyaarai?
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ pɛɛzi ia guŋ.”
16Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina
haana ra tɔgzi
bahinaarɛ werge,
di ra vol jigsi ni,
di kpa gba siwee ge ra sɛm,
di ra vol, ba naachawaa
gbittizi ra gbɔgzi.
17Awia, n daŋ gil a haana nyuuni
mɔnni ŋmɛra, di gba.”
18A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ foozi kuna la baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra di toloo la. Ba gbittizi la baŋ kpawɛɛ du ba nachawaa, kuna la baŋ kpawɛɛ vɔɔzi ba nyuuni, ba baŋaa kuna, 19ba dignikuna, ba nonee gbittizi, ba saatazi, 20chimuzi, koga ani ba tulaalezi la maa wiarɛ niŋ tuŋ. 21Ba nonibisiga ni anla baŋ du ba miizizi, 22ba tagtajaŋra ni ba waari tagtazenaa, ba kebee hurnanaa, 23ba digee, ba pɛɛhuŋŋunanaa laalaa, ba nyuuni kuna ani ba saatazi la maa wiarɛ niŋ tuŋ.
24Ban niŋ ɔɔ mizi ba tulaalenanaa la, ka ba danna hɛhzi,
ŋmɛnni lɛɛ kirsɔɔzi bɔr,
nyugbaalaa lɛɛ nyuhuna bɔr,
gbɔglɔŋ lɛɛ wɛjɛnanaa bɔr,
niŋ pɛla lɛɛ toloori bɔr.
25Ba daŋ kpa tokobizi kpu ii baala.
Ii laallɔɔra siu laal biini.
26Nɛra daŋ so Bolzeŋ Ziɔn dominuuzenaa ni biinichɔg, di ra wii.
A bolzeŋ daŋ jaa ɛɛu lugɔ haaŋ baŋ dilgɛɛ
u so hɛri.

english_text:
1When this happens, seven women will grab the same man, and each of them will say, “I'll buy my own food and clothes! Just marry me and take away my disgrace.”
The Lord Will Bless His People Who Survive
2The time is coming when the Lord will make his land fruitful and glorious again, and the people of Israel who survive will take great pride in what the land produces. 3Everyone who is left alive in Jerusalem will be called special, 4after the Lord sends a fiery judgment to clean the city and its people of their violent deeds.
5 Then the Lord will cover the whole city and its meeting places with a thick cloud each day and with a flaming fire each night. God's own glory will be like a huge tent that covers everything. 6It will provide shade from the heat of the sun and a place of shelter and protection from storms and rain.
translation_text:
1A hɔl hiŋ, haana baniidaanɛɛ
daŋ lau bakpaŋ,
di ŋɔ, “Yaa danna di yaa himmaa diwee,
di nyiŋŋi
yaa himmaa laala.
Ka hiŋwaa sɛɛ í sɔŋ sag yaa ni,
ya gilɛɛ ka di hiihzi!”
Ba daŋ bir ma Jɛrusalɛm
2A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u Daa Kel lii, di du wer di dɔɔ girme. A hɛri daazi nɔna daŋ tɛɛ banla n kawɛɛ Izrɛl biini la girme ni sɔŋ. 3Banla maa n kawɛɛ Bolzeŋ Ziɔn biini, ba danna yir baa nɛnanaananaa. Banla sɔna baŋ sɛbɛɛ jaa nyinee la n du Jɛrusalɛm la ni. 4Kɔraawiizi daŋ sɔ Jɛrusalɛm haana doŋa ha. U daŋ kpa seriya ni niŋ dunzi lizi challi la maa n bizi Jɛrusalɛm hɛri la ha. 5Denii Kɔraawiizi jaa gil baama wa tɔ Bizeŋ Ziɔn ni banla maa n chaali de la ni. Hɔpizaa saŋa, u daŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ lugɔ nyɔɔzi, hamuŋa ge ú ɛɛ lugɔ ninlau. Kɔraawiizi girme daŋ jaari Jɛrusalɛm maa ni. 6U daŋ ɛɛ bɔsɔŋ tɔ ba ni, wibaŋa wem wia, di guu baa lii pekpeg ni dooŋ ni.

english_text:
A Song about a Vineyard
The Lord said:
1 I will sing a song
about my friend's vineyard
that was on the side
of a fertile hill.
2My friend dug the ground,
removed the stones,
and planted the best vines.
He built a watchtower
and dug a pit in rocky ground
for pressing the grapes.
He hoped they would be sweet,
but bitter grapes
were all it produced.
3Listen, people of Jerusalem
and of Judah!
You be the judge of me
and my vineyard.
4What more could I have done
for my vineyard?
I hoped for sweet grapes,
but bitter grapes
were all that grew.
5Now I will let you know
what I am going to do.
I will cut down the hedge
and tear down the wall.
My vineyard will be trampled
and left in ruins.
6It will turn into a desert,
neither pruned nor hoed;
it will be covered
with thorns and briars.
I will command the clouds
not to send rain.
7I am the Lord All-Powerful!
Israel is the vineyard,
and Judah is the garden
I tended with care.
I had hoped for honesty
and for justice,
but dishonesty
and cries for mercy
were all I found.
Isaiah Condemns Social Injustice
8You are in for trouble! You take over house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone else in all the land. 9But the Lord All-Powerful has made this promise to me:
Those large and beautiful homes will be left empty, with no one to take care of them. 10Four hectares of grapevines will produce only 27 liters of juice, and 180 liters of seed will produce merely 18 liters of grain.
11 You are in for trouble! You get up early to start drinking, and you keep it up late into the night. 12At your drinking parties you have the music of stringed instruments, tambourines, and flutes. But you never even think about all the Lord has done, 13and so his people know nothing about him. That's why many of you will be dragged off to foreign lands. Your leaders will starve to death, and everyone else will suffer from thirst.
14The world of the dead has opened its mouth wide and is eagerly waiting for the leaders of Jerusalem and for its noisy crowds, especially for those who take pride in that city. 15Its citizens have been put down, and its proud people have been brought to shame. 16But the holy Lord God All-Powerful is praised, because he has shown who he is by bringing justice. 17His people will be like sheep grazing in their own pasture, and they will take off what was left by others.
18You are in for trouble! The lies you tell are like ropes by which you drag along sin and evil. 19And you say, “Let the holy God of Israel hurry up and do what he has promised, so we can see it for ourselves.” 20You are headed for trouble! You say wrong is right, darkness is light, and bitter is sweet.
21You think you are clever and smart. 22And you are great at drinking and mixing drinks. But you are in for trouble. 23You accept bribes to let the guilty go free, and you cheat the innocent out of a fair trial.
24You will go up in flames like straw and hay! You have rejected the teaching of the holy Lord God All-Powerful of Israel. Now your roots will rot, and your blossoms will turn to dust.
25You are the Lord's people, but you made him terribly angry, and he struck you with his mighty arm. Mountains shook, and dead bodies covered the streets like garbage. The Lord is still angry, and he is ready to strike you again.
Foreign Nations Will Attack
26The Lord has signaled for the foreign nations to come and attack you. He has already whistled, and they are coming as fast as they can. 27None of them are tired. They don't sleep or get drowsy, and they run without stumbling. Their belts don't come loose; their sandal straps don't break. 28Their arrows are sharp, and their bows are ready. The hoofs of their horses are hard as flint; the wheels of their war chariots turn as fast as a whirlwind.
29They roar and growl like fierce young lions as they grab their victims and drag them off where no one can rescue them. 30On the day they attack, they will roar like the ocean. And across the land you will see nothing but darkness and trouble, because the light of day will be covered by thick clouds.
translation_text:
Grepu daazi koo wia yir
1N daŋ yir yir tɛɛ unla miŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ,
di ra bagli u
grepu daazi koo wia.
N nɔŋŋi dɔɔ grepu daazi koore
giŋgimii la n summɛ ni.
2U wigzi de bia maanii, di paagaa ga ha,
ka duu grepu daananaa de,
di ma tauduura dia u biini,
di ki bɔɔ bá ɔɔ
ra fɛrgi a nɔna de,
á nii ra lii.
Denii u faa jaa ra kpaŋ ú wa tɔrgi a grepunanaa,
ka a faa waa wer.
3“Filaŋkeŋ, Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina,
ií binni n ni
n koo naa wia na.
4Ɛrɛɛ n faa kaa ɛɛ n grepu daazi koo naa
di kaali kennaa
miŋ ɛɛwɛ naanɛi?
N faa ra tami grepunanaa ninɛɛ,
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ a nɔŋ
achɔgaa bɛnnɛi?
5Awia, n daŋ ŋɔ ii be
gunla min niŋ ɛɛ
n koo hiŋ.
N daŋ purgi koŋlaa la miŋ mawɛɛ baruu la,
ka gil pir sela fɛrgi
u maa chɔgi.
6N daŋ gil de birgi hɛribɔduma,
ba wàá ka kɛuri
de daazi kela
gɛɛ di kaa par de gba.
Ka choŋgolaa ni sɔɔhri
bɛnnɛ niŋ lii de.
Màá ka gil dooŋ gba
kaa nɛɛ de.”
7Too, Izrɛl hinaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
grepu daazi koo hiŋ.
Juda hina ɛɛ lugɔ
kambolnanii la daazi uŋ duuwe
ú bɔra sɔɔni a wia la.
U ra tami lugɔ ba wia daŋ dɔɔ wibii,
ka ba wia maa ɛɛ nɛkpui.
U ra tami lugɔ ba danna ɛɛ wideŋlaa,
ka u ra nuu
biinichɔg wiraa.
Wichɔgaa la nɛra n na ɛɛ wia
8Wia daŋ huuzi ii banla maa n na yauzi diini
ni kooni di ra jaa
anla iin dɔɔwɛ ni,
guŋ gil baŋhina wàá ka na zuuribɔra,
ii bɛmbɛŋ jaa so a hɛri.
9N nuuwɔɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la n ŋɔwɛɛ,
“Wibii maa, diizenaa la maa daŋ wa birgi diiwooni,
nɛr maa
wàá ka du a biine.
10Ba daŋ par grepu daazi koo katozi fi, ka a siŋ su galɔnzi anumbɛl bɛŋ,
di kpa kundee kookoo tassazi kalfa duu,
ka bir na
kookoo tassazi fi bɛŋ.”
11Wia daŋ huuzi ii banla n ɔɔ feli izi chɔɔzi ni
di chɔ ra nyiŋŋi
siŋ ií nyɔɔ la,
di nyɔɔu guŋŋ hɛuh wa hɛɛhzi,
ii dɛɛzi werge maa la.
12Ii diuzenaa bɔra, ii ɔɔ kpogli kemzi, janjalanzi,
kunyigzaa, kaloopezi
ani sinnii,
ka ii baga lɛi Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa wia,
di ra gbɛlli
u kuŋkuaraa.
13Awia, ba daŋ lauri n nɛra kaali hɛrdumazi,
dikuu baŋ waa
wia zɛɛ zummɛ wia.
Lɔzi daŋ kpu ba nabɔnzi,
niinyɔgzi ge nyaŋŋi
banla n kawɛɛ,
bá siuzi.
14Awia, lalaa bol chɔɔwɔɔ ra kpaŋ baa.
U haa u nuarɛ werge,
ú ligli Jɛrusalɛm nɛzenaa
ni banla n ɔɔ chaali
di ra kɔɔ,
di ra naa dɔŋa la.
15Nɛr maa daŋ di hiihzi,
bá siwii sɔɔni,
nɛkpoŋlaa gba siwii sɔɔni.
16Ka Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la daŋ na girme, dikuu unna di seriya ni wibii wia.
Dɔɔrinaniinanii la
daŋ bagli lugɔ
u wia deŋloore.
17Peeza ra di koorii a diŋgelli alugɔ a himmaa diiribɔr,
pebizi ra di koorii de.
18Wia daŋ huuzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, wichɔgaa vɔɔzi iabuu,
ii waa wette lɛɛ
iihinaa lii a biini.
19Ii banla n na ŋɔ, “Gil Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ manaŋ,
ú hahzi hum u huma,
ya na.
Gil a ba,
di gil wii la Izrɛl
Dɔɔrinaniinanii jina ɛɛ,
ya zumuu.”
20Wia daŋ huuzi banla n na yir wichɔgaa, winanaa,
di ra yir
winanaa ge wichɔgaa,
di kpa bɔbiri di ra yir bɔchaaŋ,
di ra yir
bɔchaaŋ ge bɔbiri,
di kpa kunsum di ra yir kuŋkpol,
di ra yir
kuŋkpol ge kunsum la.
21Wia daŋ huuzi banla n na yir bahinaa sichaana hina,
di ra binni lugɔ
baabuu nunzunna la.
22Wia daŋ huuzi banla n dɔɔ sɔŋ sinnyɔɔi biini,
di ɔɔ ra jigsi gunla
baŋ ɔɔ kpa sinni
koozi dɔŋa ni,
di ra nyɔɔ la,
23di ɔɔ ra lɛɛ kebee ka lɛɛ bilii ra tɛɛ bilchɔg hina,
ka gil bilii hina ra chol la.
24Dikuu guŋ wia, ba maa daŋ tuŋ kpɛlɛŋ
lugɔ niŋ n ɔɔ fuuh kɔlaa
ni kooriihilaa,
gunnɛ bá du lugɔ daa lunne
n ɔɔ pɔɔh, u fiiri war,
peu kpaa kaali
lugɔ nyɔɔ la,
dikuu baŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Gbɔg wia,
di gbɛlli Izrɛl
Dɔɔrinaniinanii la
Wiŋɔɔlii la wia.
25Guŋ wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ na fuuh u nɛra ni la.
U lalli u nonii
lɔ baa ta hɛri.
Bizenaa zigli,
nɛra siuzi chɔɔ
bol ŋmɛnizi
bɔr maa alugɔ kpaga.
Haali guŋ n ɛɛwɛ gba, ka u baaŋ haa waa sɔɔnɛɛ.
U haa lalli u noniire
ú kpu baa.
26U lalli tuutaa di ra yir hɛssi la n du bɔɔnɛɛ nɛra.
Gunla nɛra n ɔɔ fooli
di ra yir nuuzihina la,
gunnɛ u fooli
di yir banla
n du a hɛri tuna bá ba.
Baabuu hahzee ra ba la.
27Ba bɛl maa waa kuuh
gɛɛ di ra jiŋli,
ba bɛl maa waa daari
gɛɛ di ra chɔɔ dɔɔ gba.
Bɛl maa kirsɔɔ gba waa putte
gɛɛ u gau chɛh.
28Ba hobee ra di nɛnnɛ,
ba ɛɛ ba hozi tai sirya.
Ba zagra naafiraa ge du kpeg lugɔ bia,
ba laal torkozi
anna tɛrgi la ge
naazi ra birgi
manamanaŋ alugɔ vem.
29Ba danna kɔɔ alugɔ bunyiŋ,
di kaa ra uuhri
alugɔ bunyimpɔla.
Ba daŋ lauri nɛra kaali,
ka nɛr maa wàá wer
foozi baa lii ba be.
30A hɔl hiŋ, a laallɔɔra danna kɔɔ werge maa
alugɔ muuzeŋ n ɔɔ izi
di ra kɔɔ la.
Di nɛr binni a hɛri, u daŋ na bɔbiri ni biinichɔg,
baama ge daŋ tɔ
bɔchaaŋ ni, ú biri.

english_text:
A Vision of the Lord in the Temple
1 In the year that King Uzziah died, I had a vision of the Lord. He was on his throne high above, and his robe filled the temple. 2Flaming creatures with six wings each were flying over him. They covered their faces with two of their wings and their bodies with two more. They used the other two wings for flying, 3 as they shouted,
“Holy, holy, holy,
Lord All-Powerful!
The earth is filled
with your glory.”
4 As they shouted, the doorposts of the temple shook, and the temple was filled with smoke. 5Then I cried out, “I'm doomed! Everything I say is sinful, and so are the words of everyone around me. Yet I have seen the King, the Lord All-Powerful.”
6One of the flaming creatures flew over to me with a burning coal that it had taken from the altar with a pair of metal tongs. 7It touched my lips with the hot coal and said, “This has touched your lips. Your sins are forgiven, and you are no longer guilty.”
8After this, I heard the Lord ask, “Is there anyone I can send? Will someone speak for us?”
“I'll go,” I answered. “Send me!”
9 Then the Lord told me to go and speak this message to the people:
“You will listen and listen,
but never understand.
You will look and look,
but never see.”
The Lord also said,
10“Make these people stubborn!
Make them stop up
their ears,
cover their eyes,
and fail to understand.
Don't let them turn to me
and be healed.”
11Then I asked the Lord, “How long will this last?”
The Lord answered:
Until their towns are destroyed and their houses are deserted, until their fields are empty, 12and I have sent them far away, leaving their land in ruins. 13If only a tenth of the people are left, even they will be destroyed. But just as stumps remain after trees have been cut down, some of my chosen ones will be left.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n yir Aizaaya wia
1Bina la Koori Uzzia n siuwɛ la, mìŋ́ Aizaaya faa na Kɔraawiizii lugɔ deeza biini, di u sogo u koorikara la n la chiŋ di dɔɔ girme werge, tagtazeŋ un laalɛɛ faa tɔ u Dia biini maa. 2Kuna aŋhina banna yir sɛrafzi faa guali u ni. Bɛl maa faa dɔɔ keeri anumbɛl, di ɔɔ kpa anɛɛ tɔ u siwee di kaa kpa anɛɛ ge tɔ u naazi, ka kpa anɛɛ ge di ra zaah. 3A maa faa ŋɔ ra tɛɛ dɔŋa,
“Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ,
u girme su hɛri maa.”
4A loobee gil Kɔraawiizi Dia la zigli, nyɔɔzi faa su u biini maa.
5Denii n lɔ wile, di ŋɔ, “Wiarɛ huuziŋ! N wia chɔkkɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ nɛr la n waa zum winanaa ŋɔirɛ, di kaa du nɛra la nuuzi n waa winanaa ra ŋɔ ge be. N siwii na Koorizeŋ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu.”
6Denii a sɛrafzi la bɛl faa zaah di ba n be, di kpogli niŋhɔl uŋ kpa nyɔga lizi mbusu lizibɔr la. 7Denii u kpau di gbɔgzi n nuuhɔna, ka ŋɔ, “Na, niŋhɔl naa gbɔgzi i nuuhɔnaa, awia, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ lii i ninɛɛ, u gil i wichɔgaa tɛi.”
8Denii n nuu Kɔraawiizi n na pɛɛzi, “Anɛɛ n humɛi? Anɛɛ n niŋ lɛɛ yaa naazi lanɛi?”
Denii n ŋɔ, “Minuu keŋ. Humiŋ!”
9U ŋɔ, “La ga ŋɔ wia naa nɛra naa be,
‘Ba daŋ ŋɔ wia á zuu ii digna,
ka ii wàá wer zum a zɛɛ.
Ii daŋ aah siwii ii na a wia ŋmɛnɛɛ,
ka ii wàá wer zum a zɛɛ.’
10Gil nɛra naa dɔɔ dignikpega werge,
di gil ba digna taŋzi,
di kaa tɔɔgi ba siwee ge.
Di guŋ lɛi ba siwee daŋ vii na,
bá digna ge nuu,
bá bampiree bir,
bá zum a zɛɛ
di ra hiŋiŋ ń chaa baa.”
11Denii n ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, ɛrɛɛ a birgi magɛi?”
U ŋɔ,
“See bolzenaa la maa n purgee chɔɔ,
nɛr maa wàá ka du a biine,
a diini maa birgi diiwooni,
a kooni maa chɔgi ta,
12guŋŋ ń wa duŋŋi nɛr maa kaali bɔɔnɛɛ,
ka Izrɛl hɛri
birgi diŋgela.
13Haali di a nɛra bɔra fi bɔkpaŋ ka a hɛri biini gba,
ka ba daŋ wa fɔɔ baa
di kaa kuari chɔg a hɛri jaa.
Ka n nɛra Izrɛl hina daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ daazeŋ baŋ teŋŋe ka ka u zɛɛtirii,
a zɛɛtirii naa du hɛri
di kaa wa fur.”
A zɛɛtirii chigɔɔ tɛɛ n nɛra dufalii wia.

english_text:
Isaiah Offers Hope to King Ahaz
1 Ahaz, the son of Jotham and the grandson of Uzziah, was king of Judah when King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah son of Remaliah of Israel went to attack Jerusalem. But they were not able to do what they had planned. 2When news reached the royal palace that Syria had joined forces with Israel, King Ahaz and everyone in Judah were so terrified that they shook like trees in a windstorm.
3Then the Lord said to me:
Take your son Shearjashub and go see King Ahaz. You will find him on the road near the cloth makers' shops at the end of the canal that brings water from the upper pool. 4Tell Ahaz to stop worrying. There's no need for him to be afraid of King Rezin and King Pekah. They are very angry, but they are nothing more than a dying fire. Ahaz doesn't need to fear 5their evil threats 6to invade and defeat Judah and Jerusalem and to let the son of Tabeel be king in his place.
7I, the Lord, promise that this will never happen. 8-9Damascus is just the capital of Syria, and King Rezin rules only in Damascus. Samaria is just the capital of Israel, and King Pekah rules only in Samaria. But in less than 65 years, Israel will be destroyed. And if Ahaz and his officials don't trust me, they will be defeated.
A Son Named Immanuel
10Once again the Lord God spoke to King Ahaz. This time he said, 11“Ask me for proof that my promise will come true. Ask for something to happen deep in the world of the dead or high in the heavens above.”
12“No, Lord,” Ahaz answered. “I won't test you!”
13Then I said:
Listen, every one of you in the royal family of David. You have already tried my patience. Now you are trying God's patience by refusing to ask for proof. 14 But the Lord will still give you proof. A virgin is pregnant; she will have a son and will name him Immanuel. 15-16Even before the boy is old enough to know how to choose between right and wrong, he will eat yogurt and honey, and the countries of the two kings you fear will be destroyed. 17But the Lord will make more trouble for your people and your kingdom than any of you have known since Israel broke away from Judah. He will even bring the king of Assyria to attack you.
The Threat of an Invasion
18When that time comes, the Lord will whistle, and armies will come from Egypt like flies and from Assyria like bees. 19They will settle everywhere—in the deep valleys and between the rocks, on every thornbush and all over the pastureland.
20The Lord will pay the king of Assyria to bring a razor from across the Euphrates River and shave your head and every hair on your body, including your beard.
21Anyone who is able to save only one young cow and two sheep, 22will have enough milk to make yogurt. In fact, everyone left in the land will eat yogurt and honey.
23Vineyards that had 1,000 vines and were worth 1,000 pieces of silver will turn into thorn patches. 24You will go there to hunt with your bow and arrows, because the whole country will be covered with thornbushes. 25The hills where you once planted crops will be overgrown with thorns and thistles. You will be afraid to go there, and your cattle, sheep, and goats will be turned loose on those hills.
translation_text:
Amaniye tɛɛ Koori Ahaz wia
1Jɔtam biibaal Koori Ahaz, u naabaal faa ɛɛ Uzia, n wa di Juda kora, laal faa izi u ni Siiria Koori Rɛzin ni Izrɛl Koori Pɛka n ɛɛ Rɛmalia biibaal baaŋ. Ba ba Jɛrusalɛm di wa lɔ baa laal, ka ba faa waa wette kpegli baa. 2Baŋ wa ŋɔ Juda Koori Ahaz be lugɔ Siiria ni Ɛfram hina ɛɛ nuukpannɛ bá wa lɔ baa laal, ɔnsii faa lau Koori Ahaz ni u nɛra werge, ba bɔra ra sa alugɔ pezeŋ n ɔɔ ra ta kɔr daazi ni a ra ziigi gunla.
3Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Aizaaya be, “Í ni i biibaal Sɛɛr Jasub lii di ga chem Koori Ahaz ni. Ií daŋ ga huuzuu bɔr la baŋ peree, nii ga de di gaa zuu Chiŋ Pol la, denii du ŋmɛnɛɛ la n chɔɔwɛ di ra la Wɛjɛ Suahra Bɔr la. 4Kaluu lugɔ ú ra du tau, di lau u hiŋ di gilɛɛ gil u banchule ra lɔ. Ú gilɛɛ gil u bɔra huah dikuu Siiria Koori Rɛzin ni Rɛmalia biibaal Koori Pɛka baana n na fuuh wia. Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nindaazi n ɔɔ chɔɔ di ra di tama tama la. 5Siiria, Ɛfram hina ani Izrɛl Koori Rɛmalia biibaal ta jinaa di vɔɔ laal, di ra ba bá wa lɔ ia, di ra ŋɔ, 6‘Ií gil ya ga lɔ Juda hina di kpegli baa, ka bɔnni ba hɛri hiŋ tɛɛ dɔŋa, ka jaa tɔ Tabiil biibaal kora, ú ɛɛ Juda hɛri maa koori.’ 7Ama, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ,
‘Màá gil guŋ ɛɛ,
8dikuubɛɛwiai, Siiria bolzenne Damaskus,
Damaskus Koori Rɛzin
waa fɔŋŋa maa dɔɔwɛ.
Binni tokkoahoro ni anue biini,
Izrɛl hɛri maanii
niŋ purgi
di chɔgi kɔrai.
9Izrɛl hɛri bolzenne Samaria,
bolzeŋ Samaria ge Koori
Rɛmalia biibaal Pɛka,
waa fɔŋŋa maa dɔɔwɛ.
Di ii wan yardɛɛ di chi chigigi,
ii wàá wer chi maa.’ ”
10Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Koori Ahaz be, 11“Ŋɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum be lugɔ ń ɛɛ wii bɛl í na, di lalaa bolle gɛɛ chinchinne.”
12Ka a koori faa vɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “Màá ɛɛi na.”
13Denii Aizaaya ŋɔ, “Koori Deevid diahina, ií ra nuu nɛnnɛ. Di ii ra ɛɛ nɛra guŋŋ ba lɔgɔ wa lii, guŋ waa ia kukkɛɛa? Ií daŋ bir ra nyiŋŋi ii ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la ge di naa? 14Awia, Kɔraawiizi himmaanii niŋ ɛɛ wii bɛl, di bagli gunla un niŋ ɛɛ. Toloori bɛl, n waa baal zummɛ, daŋ kpogli hia di lul biibaal, bá ra yiruu Imanuɛl. 15Di u wa hello di zum wichɔgaa ni winanaa, huuhnuu ni nail daŋ ɛɛ u diwee. 16Mɔɔ ka a saŋa wa hel, koora banɛɛ la iinna ɔm werge maa la hɛssi daŋ birgi diŋgelli. 17Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil biinichɔg chol ii ni ii hɛri ani ii lulla maa ni, di kaali tɔɔrɔɔ la iin diwee, saŋa la Izrɛl n bargɛɛ lii Juda hɛri be guŋŋ di wa lii zinaa la. U daŋ gil Asiiria koori ba di wa du ia a keŋ tɔɔrɔɔ naa.
18A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ fooli yir Ijip laallɔɔra, bá lii gɔŋa nuuzi bɔɔnɛɛ ba alugɔ nakɛɛhzi, laallɔɔra ge lii Asiiria hɛri ba miiih lugɔ huuhbee. 19Ba maa daŋ ba wa yaari a hɛri maa. Ba daŋ du faalime ni bizenaa bɔɔni maa, di du sɔɔhri bɔra ni gɔŋa maa biine. 20A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil Asiiria koori ɛɛ lugɔ u fuŋ, di lii Muu Yufretis baŋgia di wa fuŋ ii nyuuni, ii naagballi huna ani ii taŋhuna maa. 21A hɔl hiŋ, napɔl ni buuna anɛɛ bɛnnɛ baal wer dɛɛzi. 22Nail n niŋ du de werge wia, naillɛ niŋ ɛɛ ba diwee. Banla maa n ka a hɛri la, huuhnuu ni nailsiwaarɛ bá ra di. 23A hɔl hiŋ, bɔr la maa grepu daazi kagboŋ n niŋ yoo lugɔ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kagboŋ, choŋgolaa ni sɔɔhri bɛnnɛ niŋ du de. 24Nɛra daŋ ɔɔ kpa ba hozi ni hobee di gaa kpaani de, dikuu choŋgolaa ni sɔɔhri n niŋ tɔ a hɛri maa wia. 25Nɛr maa wàá ka la a giŋgimii kɛraa la baŋ faa ra par la, dikuu de maa n niŋ birgi choŋgolaa ni sɔɔhri bɔr wia. Nauna, peeza ani buunaa niŋ jaa ra di koorii de.”

english_text:
A Warning and a Hope
1The Lord said, “Isaiah, get something to write on. Then write in big clear letters the name, MAHER-SHALAL-HASH-BAZ. 2I will tell Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah to serve as witnesses to this.”
3Sometime later, my wife and I had a son, and the Lord said, “Name him Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz. 4Because before he can say ‘Mommy’ or ‘Daddy,’ the king of Assyria will attack and take everything of value from Damascus and Samaria.”
5The Lord spoke to me again and said:
6These people have refused the gentle waters of Shiloah and have gladly gone over to the side of King Rezin and King Pekah. 7Now I will send the king of Assyria against them with his powerful army, which will attack like the mighty Euphrates River overflowing its banks. 8Enemy soldiers will cover Judah like a flood reaching up to your neck.
But God is with us.
He will spread his wings
and protect our land.
9All of you foreign nations,
go ahead and prepare for war,
but you will be crushed.
10Get together and make plans,
but you will fail
because God is with us.
11The Lord took hold of me with his powerful hand and said:
I'm warning you! Don't act like these people. 12 Don't call something a rebellious plot, just because they do, and don't be afraid of something, just because they are. 13I am the one you should fear and respect. I am the holy God, the Lord All-Powerful! 14-15 Run to me for protection. I am a rock that will make both Judah and Israel stumble and break their bones. I am a trap that will catch the people of Jerusalem—they will be captured and dragged away.
Isaiah and His Followers
16My message and my teachings are to be sealed and given to my followers. 17 Meanwhile, I patiently trust the Lord, even though he is no longer pleased with Israel. 18 My children and I are warning signs to Israel from the Lord All-Powerful, who lives on Mount Zion.
19Someone may say to you, “Go to the fortunetellers who make soft chirping sounds or ask the spirits of the dead. After all, a nation ought to be able to ask its own gods 20what it should do.”
None of those who talk like that will live to see the light of day! 21They will go around in great pain and will become so hungry that they will angrily curse their king and their gods. And when they try to find help in heaven 22and on earth, they will find only trouble and darkness, terrible trouble and deepest darkness.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n kpa Asiiria koorizeŋ hum u huma wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi faa kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Aizaaya be, “Kpa hɔŋ sɛbi sɔŋ naa dau u ni. Waabuu, Maha Salal Has Baz. 2N daŋ yir Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Yuria ni Zɛkaria biibaal Jɛbɛrɛkia la n ɛɛ wibii hina, bá di wia la hin niŋ sɛbi la daansɛɛ.”
