3Too, denii n ni n haaŋ chɔɔ, u kpogli hia lul biibaal. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Dau u sɔŋ Maha Salal Has Baz. 4Mɔɔ ka a bie zum u maa ni u mɛɛ yiraa, Asiiria koorizeŋ daŋ wa fɔɔ Damaskus ni bolzeŋ Samaria, di paagi ba kundɔɔlaa maa kaali.”
5Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be,
6“Dikuu nɛra naa n vɛɛ Silowa nii n na pal bɔɔiih,
ka gil ba bɔra ra sa
Koora Rɛzin ni Pɛka wia,
7N daŋ gil Asiiria
koorizeŋ ni u laallɔɔra
wa fɔɔ baa, di tɔ ba ni
gunla Muu Yufretis nii
n ɔɔ su werge,
di tɔ kuna ni la.
8A koori ni u laallɔɔra daŋ ba
wa gbaari Juda hɛri maa
alugɔ nii n suwee,
haali di wa hel ba baŋaazi.
U yaa u keerii tɔ
yaa hɛri ni.
Ee, Immanuɛl!”
9Hɛssi hina, ií lɔ laal wile, ka gil ii biine chɔgi!
Hɛhjaŋa hina, ií ra nuu.
Ií ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya,
ka gil ii biine chɔgi!
Ií ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya,
ka gil ii biine chɔgi!
10Ií ta jinaa di lau wii bɛl,
ka u daŋ wa chɔgi,
ii wilaulii wàá wer chi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi
du yaa benii.
Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi
11Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n benii ni u banonii, di ra karfiŋ lugɔ ń gilɛɛ ra hiŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ la nɛra naa na hiŋ la. U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
12“Gilɛɛ ra jaa banla n ɔɔ suahzi
di ra ta jinachɔgaa ni.
Gilɛɛ waa ɔm wia la banna ɔm,
gilɛɛ waa ɔmaa werge.
13Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la bɛnnɛ
í ra yir naniinanii,
u bɛnnɛ í ra ɔm werge,
14u daŋ ɛɛ bɔsuahlii,
ka ɛɛ lugɔ bii
tɛɛ Izrɛl domeezi anɛɛ la,
di gil nɛra ɔɔ lɔɔzi
ba naazi di ra jiŋli,
di kaa ɛɛ bii la
n niŋ gil bá chol.
U daŋ kaa ɛɛ lugɔ sidɛɛ
ni ŋmɛmbee tɛɛ
Jɛrusalɛm hina.
15Bakpila maa daŋ gargi kuna
di chogli, di kuugi,
bá kpa sidɛɛzi
lauri baa.”
16N hiŋra, ií gil n amaniyezi ni
n gbɔg du ii be nɛnnɛ.
17N daŋ kpaŋ Kɔraawiizi la
n bir u har kpu
Izrɛl hina la.
N daŋ yarduu.
18N ni n biizi la Kɔraawiizi n tɛŋ labuu keŋ. Yaa ɛɛ nɛra la n ɛɛ daansɛɛ kunaa Izrɛl hɛri di lii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la be. Waabuu du Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu la.
19Di nɛra wa ŋɔ ií la ga pɛɛzi vugra ni ijɔzi la n na munni wia, a waa dɛkkɛ nɛra n na pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi la banna humaa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii gaa pɛɛzi lalaa nyinee wiai? 20Ií gilɛɛ ra nuu gunla banna ŋɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, wibii waa hoo a biine. Ka ií ra nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlaa n na bagli ia. 21Ba daŋ kpa biinichɔg werge ni lɔzi di ra bar a hɛri biini. Di lɔchɔgii waa kpu baa, ba baana danna fuuh werge maa, ba ra see ba koori ni Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la nua. 22Ba daŋ ɔɔ bir binni hɛri di na biinichɔg werge ni bɔbiri limpiriŋ n du de, ɔnsii werge ɔɔ lau baa. Ka ba daŋ gbuuri baa ga du a bɔbiri hiŋ biini.

english_text:
1 But those who have suffered will no longer be in pain. The territories of Zebulun and Naphtali in Galilee were once hated. But this land of the Gentiles across the Jordan River and along the Mediterranean Sea will be greatly respected.
War Is Over
2 Those who walked in the dark
have seen a bright light.
And it shines upon everyone
who lives in the land
of darkest shadows.
3Our Lord, you have made
your nation stronger.
Because of you, its people
are glad and celebrate
like workers at harvest time
or like soldiers dividing up
what they have taken.
4You have broken the power
of those who abused
and enslaved your people.
You have rescued them
just as you saved your people
from Midian.
5The boots of marching warriors
and the blood-stained uniforms
have been fed to flames
and eaten by fire.
A Child Has Been Born
6A child has been born for us.
We have been given a son
who will be our ruler.
His names will be
Wonderful Advisor
and Mighty God,
Eternal Father
and Prince of Peace.
7 His power will never end;
peace will last forever.
He will rule David's kingdom
and make it grow strong.
He will always rule
with honesty and justice.
The Lord All-Powerful
will make certain
that all of this is done.
God Will Punish Israel
8The Lord had warned the people of Israel, 9and all of them knew it, including everyone in the capital city of Samaria. But they were proud and stubborn and said,
10“Houses of brick and sycamore
have fallen to the ground,
but we will build houses
with stones and cedar.”
11The Lord made their enemies attack them. 12He sent the Arameans from the east and the Philistines from the west, and they swallowed up Israel. But even this did not stop him from being angry, so he kept on punishing them. 13The people of Israel still did not turn back to the Lord All-Powerful and worship him.
14In one day he cut off their head and tail, their leaves and branches. 15Their rulers and leaders were the head, and the lying prophets were the tail. 16They had led the nation down the wrong path, and the people were confused. 17The Lord was angry with his people and kept punishing them, because they had turned against him. They were evil and spoke foolishly. That's why he did not have pity on their young people or on their widows and orphans.
18Evil had spread like a raging forest fire sending thornbushes up in smoke. 19The Lord All-Powerful was angry and used the people as fuel for a fire that scorched the land. They turned against each other 20like wild animals attacking and eating everyone around them, even their own relatives. But still they were not satisfied. 21The tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh turned against each other, then joined forces to attack Judah. But the Lord was still angry and ready to punish the nation even more.
translation_text:
Ba lul biere tɛɛ yaa
1Ama, biinichɔg werge wàá du de tɛɛ banla biine n chɔkkɛ la di hanna la. Akai. Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ Zɛbulɔn ni Naftali hɛssi hina siwii sɔɔni, ka ŋmɛnɛbɛl, u daŋ tɔgzi Galilii hina la n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ, di du muuzeŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ di hiini Jɔɔdan muu la.
2Nɛra la n na vol bɔbiri,
jaa na ninzeŋ bɛllɛ
unna chaani.
Siurɛ faa tɔ baa bɔbiri la,
ka bɔchaaŋ ge jaa bau
waa chaani ba ni.
3N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i gillɔɔ a hɛri nɛra wazi,
di kaa jaa baa bɔsɔna,
gunla nɛra n ɔɔ ra kum ba kuna,
ba bɔra sɔɔni baa la.
Ba danna chaasi ni bɔsɔna
gunla laallɔɔra
n ɔɔ kpegli ba dɔma
di paagi ba kuna
di ra bɔnni
ka ra ɛɛ la.
4Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi chaahzi ŋmɛnni la n vɔɔzi u nɛra
ni bulaali la baŋ kpawɛɛ
di ra viiri baa labuu,
gunla uŋ faa kpegli Midian hɛri laallɔɔra,
di kuugi ba nɛsunnaa
daŋkpala la.
5Laallɔɔri maa gauhure la uŋ kpawɛɛ lɔ laal
ni tagtazi la maa
chal n fɔgaa
maanii bá fuuh.
6Ba lul biere tɛɛ yaa,
biibaallɛ ba lul tɛɛ yaa,
waabuu ninna binni
a nɛra maa ni.
Ba danna yiruu,
Liize Biraa Hiŋ,
N Waa Dɔŋ Dɔɔwɛ,
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
Mɛɛ La N Du De Saŋa Maa,
Bampirsɔna Kooribie.
7U kora daŋ ɔɔ yaa di ra jaa
bampirsɔna du de,
di hanna la
saŋaa saŋa maa.
U daŋ so Koori Deevid koorikara ni,
di ra di kora,
u kora diiribɔr ni,
di gil u chi nɛnnɛ,
dikuu wibii
ni wideŋlaa wia
di hanna la
saŋaa saŋa maa.
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu niŋ aah siwii,
guŋ ɛɛ.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr Izrɛl hina digna
8Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia la
n niŋ wa huuzi
Izrɛl hinaa.
9Izrɛl hina maa, banla n du bolzeŋ Samaria, daŋ zum lugɔ waabuu ɛɛ guŋ.
Ba ra jigsi
di ra ta barabara,
di ra ŋɔ,
10“Yaa birkissi diini maanii purgee,
ka yaa daŋ sɛɛhzi bia
di bir maa,
ba teŋri fig daazi la maanii,
ka yaa daŋ chɔɔzi hɛriŋkpola
du a bɔɔ.”
11Ka Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ Koori Rɛzin dɔmaa fɔŋŋa, bá wa lɔ Izrɛl hina,
di du baa bɔkpega,
ba ra hahzi.
12Siiria hina n lii wiifurii ni Filisti hina n lii wiicholii,
ɛɛ siryaa bá kpu
Izrɛl hina maa nyaamm.
Haali guŋ gba n niŋ ɛɛ la, ka Kɔraawiizi baaŋ haa wàá sɔɔni.
U haa lalli u noniire ú tɔɔri baa.
13Ka a nɛra waa bittɛ ba unla n tɔɔri baa la be,
gɛɛ di nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la bɔr.
14Dikuu guŋ wia, hɔpizi kpannɛ Kɔ́raawiizi tɛr Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra ni u nɛra maa digna.
U daŋ teŋri ba nyuuni
ni ba diŋre.
15Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi ni ba nɛtɔgaa ɛɛ a nyuu,
dɔgtɛɛzi la ge
n kpa kara
di ra bagli nɛra la
ge ɛɛ a diŋ.
16Ba sitɔɔra la gillɔɔ ba leu,
banla ge banna
bagli la bugmi.
17Guŋ wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi bɔra waa sɔɔnɛɛ a biipɔllaa wia
gɛɛ ú na lalbiizi
ni luhaana sinyɛna.
Dikuubɛɛwiai, ba maanii ɛɛ biinikpola ni sɔsɔgɔ hina,
ba waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ.
Awia, u baaŋ haa waa sɔɔnɛɛ ba wia,
u haa lalli u noniire
ú tɔɔri baa.
18Wibii maa, ba biinikpola ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niŋ,
di ra fuuh choŋgolaa ni sɔɔhri,
di kaa ra di kɔrzeŋ ge maa,
u nyɔɔzi ra la chiŋ
werge maa.
19Dikuu Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ baaŋ wia,
a hɛri daŋ fuuh,
a nɛraa niŋ ɛɛ a nindaazi,
nɛr maa wàá gil u lulli.
20Ba daŋ ɔɔ di diwee ba nodig keŋkere,
ka ba wàá piŋ,
di kaa di ba nomɛɛl keŋkere ge,
ka lɔzi haa ra kpu baa.
Bɛl maa daŋ ɔɔ hee u himmaa bie ol.
21Manasɛ dee daŋ lɔ Ɛfram dee,
ba ge dee la bir lɔ
Manasɛ dee la.
A tuna, ba maa daŋ
chaali lɔ Juda dee la.
Haali guŋ gba n niŋ wa ɛɛ la, ka Kɔraawiizi baaŋ la haa wàá sɔɔni,
u nonii haa lallɔɔrɛ,
ú tɔɔri baa.

english_text:
1You people are in for trouble! You have made cruel and unfair laws 2that let you cheat the poor and needy and rob widows and orphans. 3But what will you do when you are fiercely attacked and punished by foreigners? Where will you run for help? Where will you hide your valuables? 4How will you escape being captured or killed? The Lord is still angry, and he isn't through with you yet!
The Lord's Purpose and the King of Assyria
5 The Lord says:
I am furious! And I will use the king of Assyria as a club 6to beat down you godless people. I am angry with you, and I will send him to attack you. He will take what he wants and walk on you like mud in the streets. 7He has even bigger plans in mind, because he wants to destroy many nations.
8The king of Assyria says:
My army commanders are kings! 9They have already captured the cities of Calno, Carchemish, Hamath, Arpad, Samaria, and Damascus. 10-11 The gods of Jerusalem and Samaria are weaker than the gods of those powerful nations. And I will destroy Jerusalem, together with its gods and idols, just as I did Samaria.
12The Lord will do what he has planned against Jerusalem and Mount Zion. Then he will punish the proud and boastful king of Assyria, 13who says:
I did these things by my own power because I am smart and clever. I attacked kings like a wild bull, and I took the land and the treasures of their nations. 14I have conquered the whole world! And it was easier than taking eggs from an unguarded nest. No one even flapped a wing or made a peep.
15King of Assyria, can an ax or a saw overpower the one who uses it? Can a wooden pole lift whoever holds it? 16The mighty Lord All-Powerful will send a terrible disease to strike down your army, and you will burn with fever under your royal robes. 17The holy God, who is the light of Israel, will turn into a fire, and in one day you will go up in flames, just like a thornbush. 18The Lord will make your beautiful forests and fertile fields slowly rot. 19There will be so few trees that even a young child can count them.
Only a Few Will Come Back
20A time is coming when the survivors from Israel and Judah will completely depend on the holy Lord of Israel, instead of the nation that defeated them. 21-22 There were as many people as there are grains of sand along the seashore, but only a few will survive to come back to Israel's mighty God. This is because he has threatened to destroy their nation, just as they deserve. 23The Lord All-Powerful has promised that everyone on this earth will be punished.
24Now the Lord God All-Powerful says to his people in Jerusalem:
The Assyrians will beat you with sticks and abuse you, just as the Egyptians did. But don't be afraid of them. 25Soon I will stop being angry with you, and I will punish them for their crimes. 26I will beat the Assyrians with a whip, as I did the people of Midian near the rock at Oreb. And I will show the same mighty power that I used when I made a path through the sea in Egypt. 27Then they will no longer rule your nation. All will go well for you, and your burden will be lifted.
28Enemy troops have reached the town of Aiath. They have gone through Migron, and they stored their supplies at Michmash, 29before crossing the valley and spending the night at Geba. The people of Ramah are terrified; everyone in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, has run away. 30Loud crying can be heard in the towns of Gallim, Laishah, and sorrowful Anathoth. 31No one is left in Madmenah or Gebim. 32Today the enemy will camp at Nob and shake a threatening fist at Mount Zion in Jerusalem.
33But the Lord All-Powerful
will use his fearsome might
to bring down the tallest trees
and chop off every branch.
34With an ax, the glorious Lord
will destroy every tree
in the forests of Lebanon.
translation_text:
1Wia daŋ huuzi nɛra la n na du gbɔgni la n waa deŋlee,
ni banla n na dau
nɛsunnaa widaulaa,
2bá kpolli nyaara wibii,
di kpolli n nɛra la
banna sunni la wibii,
di ra foozi luhaana kundiwee,
di ra ŋmɛɛ lalbiizi kuna!
3Ɛrɛɛ ii ɛɛ a hɔl la min niŋ tɔɔri ia,
di hɛhchɔg wa lii
bɔɔnɛɛ banɛi?
Anɛɛ benii ii chɔ la ú ga hiini iai?
Lee ii kpa
ii daama dawɛi?
4Wiimaa wàá ka du de
di nɛra la
baŋ la laurɛɛ biini tognaa
ni biinichɔg
gɛɛ di chogli chɔɔ
lalaa biini bɛŋ lɛi.
Ka Kɔraawiizi baaŋ haa waa sɔɔni,
u haa lalli u noniire,
ú tɔɔri ia.
Asiiria hina seriya dii wia
5Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Wia daŋ huuzi Asiiria hina la n ɛɛ n baaŋfuuih daŋkpala,
ba noniire n
baaŋfuuihchɔgii gulii du!
6N hum Asiiria hinaa bá ga lɔ nɛra la n wan zummɛ laal,
n hum baabuu
bá ga lɔ nɛra la n gillɛ
n baaŋ fuuh la laal.
Ba daŋ ga paagi ba daama kuna maa,
ka fɛrgi baa dau alugɔ
ŋmɛnizenaa kpɛchɛgaa.
7Ama, keŋ lɛi Asiiria koorizeŋ ra fɛ,
keŋ lɛi du u nyuu,
u horuu lugɔ ú chɔgi nɛra
di gil hɛrkpila
hina maa tuŋ.
8U ra ta barabara, di ŋɔ,
‘N laallɔɔra nabɔnzi
maa lɛi kooraa?
9N kpegli bolzenaa
Kalnɔ ni Kakɛmis,
Hamaf ni Aapad,
bolzeŋ Samaria
ani Damaskusii.
10N kpegli a hɛssi vugzenaa la
n kaali anla
n du bolzenaa Jɛrusalɛm
ni Samaria labuu.
11Màá dau Jɛrusalɛm hina ni
ba vuga gunla
miŋ faa dau
bolzeŋ Samaria hina
ni ba vuga laa?’ ”
12Di Kɔraawiizi wa tuŋ u huma la maa un niŋ ɛɛ Bizeŋ Ziɔn ni Jɛrusalɛm, u daŋ jaa ŋɔ, “N daŋ tɛr Asiiria koorizeŋ la digni, dikuu u jigsi, u barabara ani u sikpegii wia.” 13U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N himmaa fɔŋŋaa gillɛ n ɛɛ keŋ
ani n nunzuma miŋ dɔɔwɛ
ni n wia zɛɛ zumaa wia.
N lizi hɛssi magbɔɔnii,
n paagi ba kunaa lii ba
daamaa kuna dauribɔra,
n kpegli ba kooraa
lugɔ laallɔkpeg.
14Durnya hɛssi hina ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zumbee daŋ,
n paagi ba daama maa
alugɔ miŋ paagi hala.
Bɛl maa waa keeri lɔwɛɛ ɔnziŋ
gɛɛ di haa nua wii!”
15Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Siah daŋ wer ŋɔ lugɔ u fɔŋŋaa kaali u dɔɔria?
Kizee daŋ wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa
di ra mɔnni kuna
u hiŋ nii?
Virma waa ɔɔ lalli u hiŋ,
nɛttɛ ɔɔ lalluu.”
16Awia, ií jaa ra nuu filaŋkeŋ! Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
daŋ kpa wiila ta
Asiiria koorizeŋ
laallɔkpega ni,
bá gɛrgi gunla niŋ n ɔɔ
ra fuuh kuna la.
17Izrɛl hina Bɔchaaŋ Hiŋ la daŋ birgi niŋ,
ba Dɔɔrinaniinanii la
birgi ninlau.
U daŋ fuuh u sɔɔhri ni u choŋgolaa
hɔpizikpaŋ, nyaamm.
18U kɔrni daazi la n wesse ani u hɛrsuma la maanii
ú chɔgi lugɔ wiila
n ɔɔ lau nɛr di chɔguu la.
19U kɔrni daazi la ge n niŋ ka la wàá ka du kpil.
Awia, bichala gba
daŋ wer kuraa.
Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ wia
20A hɔl hiŋ, Izrɛl hina la
n niŋ ka wàá
ka dɛlli Asiiria hina la
n faa ra nyiŋŋi
bá chɔgi baa la ni.
Ba daŋ jaa yardi Kɔraawiizi bɛŋ ni wibii,
waabuu ba
Dɔɔrinaniinanii la.
21Izrɛl hina tama daŋ bir ba Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
banna hum la be.
22Haali Izrɛl hina n kpillɛ werge
alugɔ muunua
hɛɛhriichaa la,
ka ba tama bɛnnɛ niŋ ka,
di bir ba.
N daŋ chɔgi n nɛra,
ba dɛg gunnɛ.
23Ɛɛh, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
daŋ chɔgi a hɛri maa
gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.
24Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ,
“Ee, n nɛra la n du Bolzeŋ Ziɔn,
ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm Asiiria hina,
haali banna sunni ia gunla
Ijip hina n faa ɛɛ ia la gba.
25N baaŋ la n na fuuh ii ni la
daŋ sɔɔni manaŋ,
ka ú jaa bir di ra fuuh
Asiiria hina ni werge,
ń chɔgi baa.”
26Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
daŋ viiri baa ni u virma,
gunla uŋ faa kpu Midian hina
bizeŋ Ɔrɛb la.
U daŋ lalli u daŋkpala guali niiri ni,
gunla uŋ ɛɛwɛ Ijip la.
27A hɔl hiŋ,
u daŋ lizi a tɔɔrɔɔ la
baŋ faa ra tɔɔri ia la
lii ii be.
U daŋ lalli ba buntɔga la lii ii baŋaazi,
ba bunni hiŋ
daŋ wa chɔgi
dikuu iiŋ vuhwɛɛ
werge wia.
28Ií na, Asiiria laallɔɔrakpila la ra bau!
Ba zuu Ayafuu,
ba ga Migrɔn biinii,
ba dau ba bunnii Mikmas.
29Ba ra gi gɔŋ, ka ra ŋɔ,
“Yaa daŋ chɔɔ Gɛba saŋkara ni.”
Rama hina jaa ra ɔm,
Sɔɔl bol Gibia hina
ge ra chɔ.
30Galim hina biihaana, ií ra wii!
Layisa hina, ií ra nuu!
Anatɔf hina
wia dɔɔ sinyɛnaa!
31Madmɛna hina ra chɔu siaahmu maa.
Gɛbim hina,
ií ra fɔɔ ii nyuuni!
32Zinaa, ba daŋ wa chi Nɔb,
ba daŋ zigli ba nogurme
di ra du Bizeŋ Ziɔn ni,
Jɛrusalɛm giŋgimii ni.
33Ií na! Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
daŋ kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ
di ŋmuuri baa alugɔ
baŋ teŋri daazi kela,
a ra chogli la!
Ba barabara hina ni
ba nabɔnzenaa
daŋ chol di ŋmaabi.
34Fɔŋŋa Hiŋ la daŋ kpu baa gunla baŋ ɔɔ teŋri kɔr baambaaŋ daazi la.
Haali Lɛbanɔn daananaa
la chogli!

english_text:
Peace at Last
1 Like a branch that sprouts
from a stump,
someone from David's family
will someday be king.
2The Spirit of the Lord
will be with him
to give him understanding,
wisdom, and insight.
He will be powerful,
and he will know
and honor the Lord.
3His greatest joy will be
to obey the Lord.
This king won't judge
by appearances
or listen to rumors.
4The poor and the needy
will be treated with fairness
and with justice.
His word will be law
everywhere in the land,
and criminals
will be put to death.
5 Honesty and fairness
will be his royal robes.
6 Leopards will lie down
with young goats,
and wolves will rest
with lambs.
Calves and lions
will eat together
and be cared for
by little children.
7Cows and bears will share
the same pasture;
their young will rest
side by side.
Lions and oxen
will both eat straw.
8Little children will play
near snake holes.
They will stick their hands
into dens of poisonous snakes
and never be hurt.
9 Nothing harmful will take place
on the Lord's holy mountain.
Just as water fills the sea,
the land will be filled
with people who know
and honor the Lord.
God's People Will Come Back Home
10 The time is coming when one of David's descendants will be the signal for the people of all nations to come together. They will follow his advice, and his own nation will become famous.
11When that day comes, the Lord will again reach out his mighty arm and bring home his people who have survived in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Ethiopia, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the land along the coast. 12He will give a signal to the nations, and he will bring together the refugees from Judah and Israel, who have been scattered all over the earth. 13Israel will stop being jealous of Judah, and Judah will no longer be the enemy of Israel. 14Instead, they will get together and attack the Philistines in the west. Then they will defeat the Edomites, the Moabites, and the Ammonites in the east. They will rule those people and take from them whatever they want.
15 The Lord will dry up the arm of the Red Sea near Egypt, and he will send a scorching wind to divide the Euphrates River into seven streams that anyone can step across. 16Then for his people who survive, there will be a good road from Assyria, just as there was a good road for their ancestors when they left Egypt.
translation_text:
Jɛssɛ Kel wia
1Jɛssɛ biibaal Koori Deevid kora ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baŋ teŋ daa bɛl ha,
ka ka u zɛɛtirii.
Gunla daa zɛɛtirii
n ɔɔ bir fur
di dɔɔ kela la
gunnɛ koorifalii lii
Koori Deevid naanna biini.
2Kɔraawiizi Duma daŋ du u ni,
Duma la n na
bir nɛra laakal,
Duma la n na tɛɛ fɔŋŋa, zumaa
ani Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa.
3U bɔra daŋ sɔɔni dikuu unna hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua wia.
U ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá binni nɛr gɛɛ
kummaa duula ka diu seriya
gɛɛ di di kara seriya
gɛɛ di nuu ba ŋɔ.
4Ka u daŋ kpa u wideŋlaa di di anuula hina ni nyaara wia,
u daŋ kpa u nua wiŋɔzi lugɔ
daŋkpala di viiri a hɛri,
biinikpola hina siuzi.
5Wideŋlaare niŋ ɛɛ u kurhɔŋ,
u wibii ge ɛɛ u kirsɔɔ.
6A guŋ saŋa, munu ni pebii daŋ chɔɔ bɔkpaŋ,
amani ge ni buuŋ
chɔɔ dɔŋa be.
Nabizi ni bunyinzi danna di bɔkpaŋ,
ka bichala lɛɛ a maa see
á ra hiŋuu.
7Nau ni lɔɔl maa daŋ kpau ra di,
a biizi kpau chɔɔ.
Haali bunyiŋ ra di kooree
alugɔ nabal.
8Bichala la n na gɔŋŋi daŋ ɔɔ dua dugli dundugu bɔɔ,
bɛl ge ɔɔ kpa u nonii hau
dumkpola chɔɔribɔr.
9Gunnɛ kummaa wàá tɔɔri gɛɛ di chɔgi
mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi
bizennaniinanii la nyuu.
Gunla muuni n suugi niiri la,
gunnɛ hɛri naa ge
su nɛra la
n zum Kɔraawiizi.
10A hɔl hiŋ, Koorifalii daŋ lii Koori Deevid dee biini, di ɛɛ lugɔ tuuta tɛɛ nɛra ni ba dizi. Hɛssi nɛra daŋ chaali u be, dikuubɛɛwiai, hɛri la un niŋ du di ra heezi la daŋ dɔɔ girme. 11A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kaa chaali u nɛra la n kawɛɛ bunɛɛhiŋ. U daŋ gil ba lii Asiiria, Ijip, Patrɔs hɛssi, Itiopia, Ɛlam, Babilɔn, Hamaf ani hɛssi la maa n du muuzeŋ baaŋ la, di bir ba Izrɛl hɛri.
12U daŋ lalli u tuuta chiŋ,
di chaali Izrɛl hina la,
baŋ laurɛɛ kaali
hɛrdumazi la.
U daŋ chaali Juda dee la
n yaari durnya
hɛssi maa la.
13A tuna maa, Izrɛl hina wàá kaa ra zom Juda hina ni,
Juda hina ge
wàá ka ɛɛ
Izrɛl hina dɔma.
14Ba daŋ hiini dɔŋa lɔ Filisti hina la n du wiicholii la,
di hiini dɔŋa paagi
wiifurii hina kuna.
Ba daŋ kaa hiini dɔŋa
lɔ Ɛdɔm ni Moab
hɛssi di kpegli baa,
Ammɔn hina sɛɛ ba dɔɔra.
15Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil
Ijip muuzeŋ hiihzi,
U daŋ lalli u nonii guali
Muu Yufretis ni.
Pewem ba wa barguu
u birgi gɔŋa aniidaanɛɛ,
u gii wàá ka du kpol.
16U daŋ kuari ŋmɛnizeŋ tɛɛ u nɛra la n kawɛɛ
Asiiria hɛri la,
gunla uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ
tɛɛ Izrɛl hina,
saŋa la baŋ faa lii
Ijip hɛri di ra kaali la.

english_text:
A Song of Praise
1At that time you will say,
“I thank you, Lord!
You were angry with me,
but you stopped being angry
and gave me comfort.
2 I trust you to save me,
Lord God,
and I won't be afraid.
My power and my strength
come from you,
and you have saved me.”
3With great joy, you people
will get water
from the well of victory.
4At that time you will say,
“Our Lord, we are thankful,
and we worship only you.
We will tell the nations
how glorious you are
and what you have done.
5Because of your wonderful deeds
we will sing your praises
everywhere on earth.”
6Sing, people of Zion!
Celebrate the greatness
of the holy Lord of Israel.
God is here to help you.
translation_text:
Chɔlaa yir
1A hɔl hiŋ, i daŋ ŋɔ,
“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, n na chɔliibuu,
i baaŋ faa ra fuuh n ninɛɛ,
ka filaŋkeŋwaa, u sɔɔnɔɔrɛ,
i ra tig n bampirii.
2Wibii maa, hinuu n Lɛɛri.
N daŋ yardii,
màá kaa ra ɔm.
Hinuu n fɔŋŋa,
n daŋ yir yira di ra chɔlii.
Hinuu n Lɛɛri.”
3Gunla nɛr n ɔɔ dɔɔ nii
lii kɔlɔŋ biini nyɔɔ
u bɔra sɔɔni la,
gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra
bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔni,
di u wa lɛɛ baa.
4A hɔl hiŋ, i daŋ ŋɔ,
“Ií ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ. Ií ra yir u sɔŋ.
Ií gil durnya hɛssi nɛra maa
zum gunla uŋ ɛɛwɛ,
di ra tɔgzi u sɔŋ.
5Ií yir yira tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi
dikuu wizenaa la
uŋ ɛɛwɛ wia.
Ií gil durnya hɛssi nɛra maa
zum gunla uŋ ɛɛwɛ
di ra tɔgzuu.
6Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina, ií chaasi di yir yira ni bɔsɔna,
Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la
n du ii be la
dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa werge maa.”

english_text:
Babylon Will Be Punished
1 This is the message that I was given about Babylon:
2From high on a barren hill
give a signal, shout the orders,
and point the way
to enter the gates
of Babylon's proud rulers.
3The Lord has commanded
his very best warriors
and his proud heroes
to show how angry he is.
4Listen to the noisy crowds
on the mountains!
Kingdoms and nations
are joining forces.
The Lord All-Powerful
is bringing together
an army for battle.
5From a distant land
the Lord is coming
fierce and furious—
he brings his weapons
to destroy the whole earth.
6 Cry and weep!
The day is coming
when the mighty Lord
will bring destruction.
* 7All people will be terrified.
Hands will grow limp;
courage will melt away.
8Everyone will tremble with pain
like a woman giving birth;
they will stare at each other
with horror on their faces.
There Will Be No Mercy
9I, the Lord,
will show no mercy or pity
when that time comes.
In my anger I will destroy
the earth and every sinner
who lives on it.
10 Light will disappear
from the stars in the sky;
the dawning sun will turn dark,
and the moon
will lose its brightness.
11I will punish this evil world
and its people
because of their sins.
I will crush the horrible pride
of those who are cruel.
12Survivors will be harder to find
than the purest gold.
13I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am terribly angry—
I will make the sky tremble
and the earth shake loose.
14Everyone will run
to their homelands,
just as hunted deer run,
and sheep scatter
when they have no shepherd.
15Those men who are captured
will be killed by a sword.
16They will see their children
beaten against rocks,
their homes robbed,
and their wives abused.
17The Medes can't be bought off
with silver or gold,
and I'm sending them
to attack Babylonia.
18Their arrows will slaughter
the young men;
no pity will be shown
to babies and children.
The Lord Will Destroy Babylon
19 The city of Babylon
is glorious and powerful,
the pride of the nation.
But it will be like the cities
of Sodom and Gomorrah
after I, the Lord,
destroyed them.
20No one will live in Babylon.
Even nomads won't camp nearby,
and shepherds won't let
their sheep rest there.
21 Only desert creatures,
hoot owls, and ostriches
will live in its ruins,
and goats will leap about.
22Hyenas and wolves will howl
from Babylon's fortresses
and beautiful palaces.
Its time is almost up!
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr Babilɔn hina digna
1Amɔz biibaal Aizaaya faa na Babilɔn wia naabuu lugɔ deeza biini.
2Lalli tuuta giŋgimii la n waa daazi dɔɔwɛ nyuu!
Gbooli baa.
Kamzi baa
bá zuu nɛzenaa
dominuuzenaa la.
3Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u nɛra benii
lugɔ u yir u laallɔɔraa
bá hum u baaŋfuuhri huma,
banla bɔra n ninna pur
dikuu uŋ yoo u dɔma
kpegli wia.
4Ií ra nuu kɔɔi bizenaa nyuuni
lugɔ nɛkpila!
Ií kaa nuu kossi kɔɔi
alugɔ hɛssi nɛra
n na chaali dɔŋa!
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ
ra chaali laallɔɔra
bá ga yoo laal la.
5Ba lii hɛhjaŋa ni
hɛri magazii di ba.
Ba ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi
baaŋfuuihchɔgii dɔŋkunaa,
bá wa chɔgi a hɛri maa.
6Ií ra chɛɛhgi, dikuu Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ hɔpizii la n helle,
un niŋ chɔg kummaa wia.
7Dikuu guŋ wia, nɛr maa nonee daŋ siu,
u bɔra ge huah.
8Ɔnsii werge daŋ nyaŋŋi baa,
bá bɔra ra wii,
bá biine chɔgi werge,
bá ra gbargi lugɔ
haaŋ n ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi lulaa
di ra ɛɛ la.
Ba daŋ binni dɔŋa, bá nuuzi kpu,
bá siwee ge aah
dikuu ɔnsii wia.
9Ama, ii ra nuu! Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii la ra bau.
U daŋ ɛɛ hɔpizichɔgii,
Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh
werge maa,
ú chɔgi a hɛri
ni wichɔgɛɛra la maa
n du de la.
10Chinchiŋwilaa daŋ bir biri,
bɔchaaŋ wàá ka du de.
Wiizi daŋ fur di biri,
baagu ge wàá ka chaani.
11Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“N daŋ tɔɔri durnya hina dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia.
Biinikpola hina daŋ na
ba wichɔgaa kinturgaa.
N daŋ chɔgi banla maa n na jigsi
ani banla n waa
nɛra ni ra suŋ
di gil barabara hina
siwee sɔɔni.
12Banla n niŋ ka la, n daŋ gil ba ka tama lugɔ salinnanii la wia n kpolle,
di nyaa lugɔ Ɔfir saliŋ.
13Awia, n daŋ zigli chiŋ,
hɛri ge zigli lii
u chignibɔr la.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ daŋ bagli n baaŋfuuih,
a hɔl hiŋ.
14Hɔɔhra la n du Babilɔn daŋ chɔ kaali
ba himmaa hɛssi,
di yaari alugɔ kpaaŋ n na nyiŋŋi sejigzi pir a ra chɔ,
gɛɛ peeza n waa nɔɔni dɔɔwɛ la.
15Nɛra la maa ban niŋ lau, ba daŋ chugzi baa kaari,
ba daŋ kpa
tokobi kpu baa.
16Ba daŋ lauri ba bichalli di kpa baa viiri hɛri ba sibɔɔ, ba siuzi,
ka zuu ba diini di paagi ba kuna
ka punzi ba haana.”
17Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu! N daŋ gil Mɛdi hina la yoo Babilɔn hina,
ba baga waa hoo
saliŋhuŋŋa be,
hàá wer kpa saliŋ gba
murgi baa.
18A laallɔɔra daŋ taazi biipɔllaa hozi di kpuuzi,
ba wàá suŋ
biifulli gba ni,
ba wàá na
bichalli gba sinyɛna.
19Babilɔn kora n wesse kaali kossi maa la,
di kaa ɛɛ a Babilɔn hina
girme la,
ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔguu
gunla miŋ faa chɔgi
Sɔdɔm ni Gɔmɔra la.
20Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka ma, Babilɔn maa,
nɛr maa wàá ka de maa,
di hanna la
saŋaa saŋa maa.
Lɔrbizi wàá ka chɔɔ de,
penɔɔna wàá ka nɔɔni
ba peeza la de
a ga heezi.
21Ka hɛribɔduma selaa niŋ du de,
di wa su a diŋgela hiŋ.
Hohobiazi danna zuu de,
de birgi kukuballi
zuuribɔr,
haali sejigzi gba du de
di zaahzi ra bar.
22Munuzi daŋ ɔɔ du a koŋlii kɛraa di ra wii,
hohobiazi ge du
ba kooridiini biine la,
baŋ faa ra di suma.
U saŋa helloo,
a wàá ka birgi.”

english_text:
The Lord's People Will Come Home
1The Lord will have mercy on Israel and will let them be his chosen people once again. He will bring them back to their own land, and foreigners will join them as part of Israel. 2Other nations will lead them home, and Israel will make slaves of them in the land that belongs to the Lord. Israel will rule over those who once governed and mistreated them.
Death to the King of Babylonia!
3The Lord will set you free from your sorrow, suffering, and slavery. 4Then you will make fun of the King of Babylonia by singing this song:
That cruel monster is done for!
He won't attack us again.
5The Lord has crushed the power
of those evil kings,
6who were furious
and never stopped abusing
the people of other nations.
7Now all the world is at peace;
its people are celebrating
with joyful songs.
8King of Babylonia,
even the cypress trees
and the cedars of Lebanon
celebrate and say,
“Since you were put down,
no one comes along
to chop us down.”
9The world of the dead
eagerly waits for you.
With great excitement,
the spirits of ancient rulers
hear about your coming.
10Each one of them will say,
“Now you are just as weak
as any of us!
11Your pride and your music
have ended here
in the world of the dead.
Worms are your blanket,
maggots are your bed.”
12 You, the bright morning star,
have fallen from the sky!
You brought down other nations;
now you are brought down.
13 You said to yourself,
“I'll climb to heaven
and place my throne
above the highest stars.
I'll sit there with the gods
far away in the north.
14I'll be above the clouds,
just like God Most High.”
15But now you are deep
in the world of the dead.
16Those who see you will stare
and wonder, “Is this the man
who made the world tremble
and shook up kingdoms?
17Did he capture every city
and make earth a desert?
Is he the one who refused
to let prisoners go home?”
18When kings die, they are buried
in glorious tombs.
19But you will be left unburied,
just another dead body
lying underfoot
like a broken branch.
You will be one of many
killed in battle and gone down
to the deep rocky pit.
20You won't be buried with kings;
you ruined your country
and murdered your people.
You evil monster!
We hope that your family
will be forgotten forever.
21We will slaughter your sons
to make them pay for the crimes
of their ancestors.
They won't take over the world
or build cities
anywhere on this earth.
22The Lord All-Powerful has promised to attack Babylonia and destroy everyone there, so that none of them will ever be remembered again. 23The Lord will sweep out the people, and the land will become a swamp for wild animals.
Assyria Will Be Punished
24 The Lord All-Powerful
has made this promise:
Everything I have planned
will happen just as I said.
25I will wipe out every Assyrian
in my country,
and I will crush those
on my mountains.
I will free my people
from slavery
to the Assyrians.
26I have planned this
for the whole world,
and my mighty arm
controls every nation.
27I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have made these plans.
No one can stop me now!
The Philistines Will Be Punished
28 This message came from the Lord in the year King Ahaz died:
29 Philistines, don't be happy
just because the rod
that punished you
is broken.
That rod will become
a poisonous snake, and then
a flying fiery dragon.
30The poor and needy will find
pastures for their sheep
and will live in safety.
But I will starve some of you,
and others will be killed.
31Cry and weep in the gates
of your towns,
you Philistines!
Smoke blows in from the north,
and every soldier is ready.
32If a messenger comes
from a distant nation,
you must say:
“The Lord built Zion.
Even the poorest of his people
will find safety there.”
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina n bittɛ ba wia
1Ama, Kɔraawiizi daŋ suŋ Izrɛl dee la ni,
u daŋ kaa lizi baa
bá ɛɛ u himmaa nɛra,
di gil ba bir ba wa so
ba himmaa hɛri la.
Nɛra daŋ lii hɛrdumazi
wa jaa ba ni.
2Hɛssi hina daŋ hiini Izrɛl hina
ba bir ba ba himmaa hɛri.
Nɛra la ge n niŋ wa so ba be la
daŋ birgi ba balaa
di ra hum baa lii hɛri la
Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ baa la.
Banla n faa lauri Izrɛl hina
birgi ba yoma la
daŋ bir birgi Izrɛl hina yoma,
ka Izrɛl hina jaa dɔɔ
banla n faa ra fir baa werge
la maa fɔŋŋa.
3A hɔl la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lizi u nɛra lii tɔɔrɔɔ, biinichɔg ani sunnaa biini, ka jaa tɛɛ baa heezaa la, 4di u wa ɛɛ guŋ, ba daŋ jaa ra ɛɛ Babilɔn koori la chɛɛtɛ, di ra ŋɔ,
“Ií na nɛr la n faa ra sunni yaa la wia n chɔkkɛ!
Gunla u baaŋfuuih la
maa n bir pɛɛ.
5Kɔraawiizi chɔgi biinikpola hina fɔŋŋaa,
ba kora dii tuŋ.
6Ba fɔŋŋa ni baaŋfuuihre ba faa kpa
sunni nɛra di chɔgi baa,
di kaa kpegli hɛssi hina la n kawɛɛ,
ba faa waa laafaa dɔɔwɛ la.
7Ka filaŋkeŋwaa, a hɛssi hina jaa heezuu,
bampirsɔna du de,
ba maa ra yir yira.
8Haali Lɛbanɔn daananaa ni hɛriŋkpola danna jigsi di ra ŋɔ,
‘Hiŋ cholle filaŋkennaa,
nɛr maa wàá ka ba
di waa teŋri yaa.’
9Lalaa maa daŋ ɛɛ sirya di ra kpaŋ i balaa.
Ba daŋ izi jaamii.
Banla maa n faa ɛɛ sitɔɔra durnya hɛssi biini,
ni banla maa n faa
ɛɛ hɛssi koora,
ba maanii niŋ izi jaamii.
10Ba maa daŋ kpau ni loobikpaŋ di ŋɔ,
‘Filaŋkeŋwaa, yaa ni
i maa gɛrga ɛɛ kpannɛ,
i jaa ɛɛu lugɔ yaa.’
11Baŋ hugii la, i kora ni i fɔŋŋa la maa tunnɔɔ.
Janjalanzi la baŋ faa ra lɔ
i see la maa tunnɔɔ.
Filaŋkeŋwaa, sandulee jaa birgi i kunchɔɔrikuŋ,
di birgi i wɛjɛ.
12Ee, Babilɔn koori, chɔɔzimpikke chinchiŋwilii!
Na gunla hiŋ chol hɛri!
Hinla n faa wette kpegli durnya hɛssi nɛra la,
hinuu ba kpa ha hɛri la.
13I ŋɔwɔɔrɛ i biini,
‘N daŋ tinni la chiŋ
di ga bɛri Kɔraawiizi chinchiŋwilaa la ni,
di ga di n kora de.
N daŋ so n koorikara ni, vuga chaalibɔr
giŋgimii nyuu.
14N daŋ tinni ga bɛri a baamazi nyubaaŋ,
di birgi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi La
N Kaali Kummaa la.’
15Ka ba biriibuu i tuu la lalaa bol,
bɔluŋ.
16Lalaa n niŋ nai danna fiilii.
Ba ra fɛ nfɛssi ba biine
ka ra pɛɛzi dɔŋa,
‘Baal naa lɛi faa ra koozi hɛri ni durnya kossi,
nɛra bɔra ra sa laa?
17A baal naa lɛi chɔgi durnya di gil u maa birgi hɛribɔduma laa?
A koori naa lɛi
purgi durnya bolzenaa,
waa sɛɛwɛ ú pilli
u yoma ge ha,
bá la ba bola laa?’
18A hɛssi koora maa chɔɔgi ŋmama biinee ni girme,
bɛl maa dɔɔ u ŋmam.
19Ka ba waa hiŋwaa hukke, ka lizii di ta
alugɔ kelchuma baŋ teŋŋe ta.
Ba kpau i ni banla maa baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi laal biini,
di ga ta bɔɔzeŋ bɛl bia
n du u biini,
i chɔɔ ba maa zɛɛ,
alugɔ lalii la banna fɛrgi ni naazi.
20Ba wàá hugii koora hugribɔra,
dikuubɛɛwiai, i chɔgi i hɛrii
di kpuuzi i nɛra kpila maa.
Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá yir
i ni i dee maa sɔnnanii.
21Ií ɛɛ sirya kpu u biibaala,
dikuu ba naabaala
wichɔgaa wia,
bá gilɛɛ wazi di dɔɔ a hɛri
di ma bolzenaa
su u maa.”
22Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ,
“N daŋ izi yoo Babilɔn hina,
di gil ba sɔŋ dinzi.
N daŋ kpu ba biizi
ni ba naanna.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
23N daŋ gil Babilɔn hɛri birgi kikiuzi duuribɔr,
di gil ú birgi sɔɔhri
ni kpɛchɛgaa bɔr.
N daŋ gil kummaa wàá ka du de alugɔ baŋ chaazuu.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ!”
Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpu Asiiria hina
24Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu hɛɛhzɛɛ, di ŋɔ,
“Wibii maa, gunla miŋ ta jina la, guŋ himmaanii niŋ wa ɛɛ,
gunla miŋ dauwɛ,
gunnɛ niŋ ɛɛ.
25N daŋ kpu Asiiria hina la n du n hɛri la,
di fɛrgi baa ni naazi
n bizenaa la nyuuni.
N daŋ lɛɛ baa lii Asiiria hina fɔŋŋa biini,
di lɛɛ baa lii
ba sunnaa biini.
26Kenne n dau di ra nyiŋŋi ń ɛɛ durnya maa.”
N tɛr n noniire
ń du durnya hɛssi
nɛra maa siaahmu.
27Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu dau guŋ. Anɛɛ n niŋ wer teŋ guŋ ŋmɛnɛɛi?
Di u wa tɛr u nonii,
anɛɛ n niŋ wer lawuuwɛi?
Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpu Filisti hina
28Amaniye la miŋ faa nuuwɛ lii Kɔraawiizi be, bina la Koori Ahaz n siuwɛ labuu keŋ,
29Filisti hina maa, ii gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia werge,
ii dɔma fɔŋŋa n tunnɛ wia.
Haali guŋ n ɛɛwɛ la gba,
ka biinichɔg daŋ ba
kaali anla,
di chum lugɔ duŋkpola.
30N daŋ tɛɛ nyaara diwee bá di,
banla ge n ɛɛ
anuula hina la
daŋ chɔɔ ni bɔsɔna.
Ka iawaa, lɔchɔgii daŋ chol ii ni,
di kpu ii banla
n niŋ ka la maa.
31Filisti bolzenaa hina, ií ra chɛɛhgi!
Ií gil ɔnsii werge lau ia!
Laallɔɔrakpila werge lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ
di ra ba, nyɔɔ tɔ kuull,
bɛl maa ɛɛ laal lɔi siryaa,
ɔnsiiri waa hoo ba biini.
32Ɛrɛɛ ya ŋɔ banla Filisti hina n hummɛ
bá wa pɛɛzi
Jɛrusalɛm wia benei?
Ií ŋɔ ba be lugɔ Kɔraawiizii ma Jɛrusalɛm,
ú nɛra wer du de di na lɛɛi
lii ba sunnaa la biini.

english_text:
Moab Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Moab:
The towns of Ar and Kir
were destroyed in a night.
Moab is left in ruins!
2Everyone in Dibon has gone up
to the temple and the shrines
to cry and weep.
All of Moab is crying.
Heads and beards are shaved
because of what happened
at Nebo and Medeba.
3In the towns and at home,
everyone wears sackcloth
and cries loud and long.
4From Heshbon and Elealeh,
weeping is heard in Jahaz;
Moab's warriors scream
while trembling with fear.
Pity Moab
5I pity Moab!
Its people are running to Zoar
and to Eglath-Shelishiyah.
They cry on their way up
to the town of Luhith;
on the road to Horonaim
they tell of disasters.
6The streams of Nimrim
and the grasslands
have dried up.
Every plant is parched.
7The people of Moab are leaving,
crossing over Willow Creek,
taking everything they own
and have worked for.
8In the towns of Eglaim
and of Beerelim
and everywhere else in Moab
mournful cries are heard.
9The streams near Dimon
are flowing with blood.
But the Lord will bring
even worse trouble to Dimon,
because all in Moab who escape
will be attacked by lions.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgi Moab
1N faa nuu amaniye naabuu lii Kɔraawiizi be, u ra bagli Moab hɛri wia.
Hamuŋkpannɛ ba purgi
bolzenaa Aa ni Kir
maa burburbur!
2Dibɔn hina tinni la ba vuga dia
giŋgimee nyuuni
bá ga wii.
Moab hina ge chɛɛhgi
ra tɛɛ Nɛbɔ ni Mɛdɛba.
Ba fuŋ ba nyuuni
ni ba taŋhunazi
dikuu biinichɔg wia.
3Ba laali gbɔglɔnzi ŋmɛnizenaa.
Ba ra chɛɛhgi salli
ni chaali bɔra maa,
ba chɔɔgi pi di ra wii.
4Bolzenaa Hɛsbɔn ni Ɛlialɛ hina ra chɛɛhgi,
haali Jahaz hina
gba ra nuu ba chɛɛhgaa!
Guŋ wia, Moab laallɔkpega gba ra chɛɛhgi,
ba bɔra huah.
5N biini chɔkkɔɔ werge, dikuu Moab wia!
U nɛra maanii chɔwɛɛ
kaali Zoa
ni Ɛglaf Sɛlisiya.
Ba kpa Luhif ŋmɛnɛɛ tinni ra kaali,
di wii ra la.
Haali banla n kpa Hɔrɔnam ŋmɛnɛɛ,
wii di ra nuumi
ba chɔgaa wia.
6Nimrim gba niiri maanii hiihzɛɛ,
u kooree maa hil.
Kunlɛɛ maa waa kaa ka.
7Awia, ba paagi ba daama kuna baŋ faa nyiŋŋee dau,
di ga Daajaŋra Gɔmbɔɔluŋe la
di gi ra kaali.
8Moab hɛri magbɔɔ maanii a chɛɛhgaa hel,
haali di ga hel Ɛglam,
ba nuumaa
ga hel Bɛɛ Ɛlim.
9Dimɔn niiri maanii birgi chal,
ka Kɔraawiizi
daŋ gil ba wia
haa nyaŋŋi kaali guŋ.
Banla n na chɔ ba lɛɛ bahinaa,
ni banla n kawɛɛ
Moab hɛri la
maanii bá kpu
alugɔ bunyiŋ n ɔɔ lau sel ú di la.

english_text:
More Troubles for Moab
1Send lambs as gifts
to the ruler of the land.
Send them across the desert
from Sela to Mount Zion.
2The women of Moab
crossing the Arnon River
are like a flock of birds
scattered from their nests.
3Moab's messengers say
to the people of Judah,
“Be kind and help us!
Shade us from the heat
of the noonday sun.
Hide our refugees!
Don't turn them away.
4Let our people live
in your country
and find safety here.”
Moab, your cruel enemies
will disappear;
they will no longer attack
and destroy your land.
5Then a kingdom of love
will be set up,
and someone from David's family
will rule with fairness.
He will do what is right
and quickly bring justice.
Moab's Pride Is Destroyed
6We have heard of Moab's pride.
Its people strut and boast,
but without reason.
7Tell everyone in Moab
to mourn for their nation.
Tell them to cry and weep
for those fancy raisins
of Kir-Hareseth.
8Vineyards near Heshbon
and Sibmah
have turned brown.
The rulers of nations
used to get drunk
on wine from those vineyards
that spread to Jazer,
then across the desert
and beyond the sea.
9Now I mourn like Jazer
for the vineyards
of Sibmah.
I shed tears for Heshbon
and for Elealeh.
There will be no more
harvest celebrations
10or joyful and happy times,
while bringing in the crops.
Singing and shouting are gone
from the vineyards.
There are no joyful shouts
where grapes were pressed.
God has silenced them all.
11Deep in my heart I hurt
for Moab and Kir-Heres.
12It's useless for Moab's people
to wear themselves out
by going to their altars
to worship and pray.
13The Lord has already said all of this about Moab. 14Now he says, “The contract of a hired worker is good for three years, but Moab's glory and greatness won't last any longer than that. Only a few of its people will survive, and they will be left helpless.”
translation_text:
1Ií banla n chɔ laal ga du bolzeŋ Sɛla la n du hɛribɔduma biini la,
ií lau pepɔla
ga tɛɛ Juda hɛri koori
n du Jɛrusalɛm.
2Gunla baŋ ɔɔ duŋŋi zumbizi
a lii a daŋa biine
di zaah ra bar la,
gunnɛ Moab haana
du Muu Aanɔn
bɔdɛrɛdɛrɛzi di ra
nyiŋŋi ba gi.
3Ba ra wiiu di ra ŋɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina be,
“Ií hiini yaa, di bagli yaa,
ya zum wii la
yaa n niŋ lau.
Ií gil wibaŋkanchirii ɛɛ lugɔ hamuŋa
tɔ yaa ni,
di kpa yaa banla n lii yaa hɛri
chɔ ba la suah,
yaa dɔma gilɛɛ
waa na yaa.
4Ií gil Moab hina la n chɔwɛɛ du ii be.
Ií guu baa lii
ba chɔgri la be.”
Nɛr la n na sunni nɛra wia daŋ tuŋ,
chɔgaa tuŋ,
chɔgri leu a hɛri.
5Denii Koori Deevid naana bɛl ɛɛ́ koori.
U daŋ kpa nɔŋŋaa ni wibii
di ra di a kora.
U siwii daŋ aah ni wideŋlaa wia,
di gil wibii dii ge du de.
6Yaa nuu Moab hina karambani,
ba jigsaa werge ani
ba nɛgbɛllaa wiarɛ.
Ka ba ra ta barabara pɛɛ.
7Awia, Moab hɛri hina maanii ra lɔɔgi wilezi
dikuu Moab wia.
Ba daŋ wii, di ba wa liizi diunanaa la
baŋ faa ra di
bolzeŋ Kir Harɛsɛf la wia,
guŋ gil ba tamii tuŋ.
8Hɛsbɔn kooni kuna maanii hillɛ,
Sibma grepu daazi ge hil.
Hɛssi koora ŋmɛnni
a grepu daananaa
maa chɔgi.
A faa chigɔɔ guŋŋ di ga lii Jaza,
di talmi ra la hɛribɔduma la
n du wiifurii la.
A faa ta lunne guŋŋ ga hel
Muuzensiwii la n du wiicholii la.
9Awiarɛ n hiini Jaza hina di ra wii,
dikuu Sibma grepu
daazi chɔgaa la wia.
Ee, Hɛsbɔn! Ee, Ɛlialɛ!
N sinii ra paluu ii wia.
Ií wàá kaa ra zaahzi di ra chiiri ani bɔsɔna
dikuu ii daanɔŋaahma
ni ii pattikuna kpai wia.
10Bɔsɔna waa hoo ii kooni huŋhunna be,
nɛr maa waa kaa ra yir yira gɛɛ
di ra chaasi,
ii grepu daazi kooni biine,
nɛr maa ge waa kaa ra fɛrgi grepu nɔna, ú lizi siŋ.
Bɔsɔna chaasaa la maa tunnɔɔ.
11N wiiwoo ra tɛɛ Moab.
N biinichɔg min dɔɔwɛ tɛɛ
Kir Harɛsɛf kannɔɔ werge.
12Moab hina danna suŋŋi ba vuga, ba vuga kuaribɔra siaahmu ni,
ka ba ra kuuh pɛɛ.
Ba danna wii di ra dua,
ka a wàá wer hiini baa.
13Wii naabuu Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ lii Moab wia biini. 14Ka filaŋkeŋ ge, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Gunla paahdiiri n ɔɔ kur u hɔpizaa a tuŋ la, gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi kur binni ahoro tɛɛ Moab ni u nɛkpila, bá girme tuŋ kɔrai. U nɛra tama bɛnnɛ niŋ ka, banla n kawɛɛ la ge gɛrgi.”

english_text:
Damascus Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Damascus:
Damascus is doomed!
It will end up in ruins.
2The villages around Aroer
will be deserted,
with only sheep living there
and no one to bother them.
3Israel will lose its fortresses.
The kingdom of Damascus
will be destroyed;
its survivors will suffer
the same fate as Israel.
The Lord All-Powerful
has promised this.
Sin and Suffering
4When that time comes,
the glorious nation of Israel
will be brought down;
its prosperous people
will be skin and bones.
5Israel will be like wheat fields
in Rephaim Valley
picked clean of grain.
6It will be like an olive tree
beaten with a stick,
leaving two or three olives
or maybe four or five
on the highest
or most fruitful branches.
The Lord God of Israel
has promised this.
7At that time the people will turn and trust their Creator, the holy God of Israel. 8They have built altars and places for burning incense to their goddess Asherah, and they have set up sacred poles for her. But they will stop worshiping at these places.
9Israel captured powerful cities and chased out the people who lived there. But these cities will lie in ruins, covered over with weeds and underbrush.
10Israel, you have forgotten
the God who saves you,
the one who is the mighty rock
where you find protection.
You plant the finest flowers
to honor a foreign god.
11The plants may sprout
and blossom
that very same morning,
but it will do you no good,
because you will suffer
endless agony.
God Defends His People
12The nations are a noisy,
thunderous sea.
13But even if they roar
like a fearsome flood,
God will give the command
to turn them back.
They will be like dust,
or like a tumbleweed
blowing across the hills
in a windstorm.
14In the evening
their attack is fierce,
but by morning
they are destroyed.
This is what happens to those
who raid and rob us.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Damaskus chɔgaa wia
1Bolzeŋ Damaskus amaniye n lii Kɔraawiizi benii keŋ,
“Na! Damaskus wàá ka ɛɛ bolzeŋ.
U maa daŋ birgi diŋgela.
2Bolzenaa la n du Aroa hɛri la nɛra maa daŋ chɔ.
Bol sela danna di a biine,
haali di ɔɔ chɔɔgi de.
Nɛr maa wàá gil
ɔnsii lawaa.
3Izrɛl bolzeŋkpega daŋ purgi.
Damaskus wàá ka
dɔɔ u hiŋ.
Siiria hina la n kawɛɛ la daŋ di hiihzi
alugɔ Izrɛl hɛri hina.”
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
4Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “A hɔl hiŋ, Izrɛl hina girme daŋ tuŋ,
ba ɛɛ lugɔ nɛvuuhlii
n bittɛ kɔgi.
5Ba hɛri daŋ wa ɛɛ lugɔ baŋ ɔɔ kum mia chaalaa dau.
U daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ Rɛfam Waluu
kooni baŋ kum mia tuŋ,
ka nɛra ra kuunaa.
6Ba nɛkpaŋkpaŋa bɛnnɛ niŋ ka
gunla baŋ ɔɔ wa
tɔrgi ɔlivizi nɔna
ka a kpaŋkpaŋa haa sagzi a daazi nyuuni,
anɛɛ gɛɛ ahoro bɛŋ sagzi a chiŋ kela ni,
anaazu gɛɛ anue ge sagzi
a zɛɛ kela ni la.”
Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
7A hɔl hiŋ, nɛra daŋ dɛlli ba Taari ni,
di bir ba siwee tɛɛ
Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la.
8Ba wàá ka dɛlli mbusu lizibɔra la
ba himmaa n mawɛɛ ni.
Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka yardi ba vughaaŋ Asɛra daazi la
ni ba daahɛgsɔɔhsuma
fuuhribɔra la
ba himmaa n mawɛɛ la.
9A hɔl hiŋ, a bolzenaa la n faa kpekke, daŋ birgi kɔrni gunla Izrɛl hina n faa lɔ Hivi ni Amɔri hina laal, ba chɔ ka ka ba bolzenaa, a birgi kɔrni la. A maa daŋ birgi diŋgelli.
10Izrɛl hina, ii suuh ii Lɛɛri Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ.
U ɛɛ Bizeŋ n guali ii ninɛɛ,
ka ii waa u wia liizee.
Awia, haali iin niŋ chɔɔzi daananaa
ni grepu daananaa la,
iiŋ kpawɛɛ lii hɛrdumazi la,
11a hel di fii, chɔɔzi la iiŋ chɔɔzaa la,
ka ii wàá na a nɔna
tɔrgi ŋmɛnɛ maa.
Tɔna la iin niŋ na
daŋ ɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ ni wiila la
n waa chaai dɔɔwɛ bɛŋ.
12Hoi! Hɛssi kpila hina ra kɔɔu
alugɔ muuzeŋ nii n ɔɔ izi
di ra kɔɔ gunla
alugɔ nii n na pal
gbuŋgbuŋgbuŋ!
13Ama, nɛra la n na ba kpegzi ni
alugɔ niizenaa n na pal gunla,
ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ hau ba ni
bá bir chɔ
alugɔ peu n na kpa zɔga giŋgimee bɔr
gɛɛ pekpeg n ɔɔ ra kpa
nyɔɔ gunla.
14Duana ni, yaa dɔma ɔɔ giluu, ɔnsii werge chol yaa ni yaa ra fɔŋ,
ka di bɔr wa chaanɔɔ,
ba ɔɔ chɔu kaali bɔɔnɛɛ.
Banla n na tɔɔri yaa
di ra paagi yaa kuna la
kinturgaare guŋ.

english_text:
Ethiopia Will Be Punished
1 Downstream from Ethiopia
lies the country of Egypt,
swarming with insects.
2Egypt sends messengers
up the Nile River
on ships made of reeds.
Send them fast to Ethiopia,
whose people are tall
and have smooth skin.
Their land is divided by rivers;
they are strong and brutal,
feared all over the world.
3Everyone on this earth,
listen with care!
A signal will be given
on the mountains,
and you will hear a trumpet.
4The Lord said to me,
“I will calmly look down
from my home above—
as calmly as the sun at noon
or clouds in the heat
of harvest season.”
5Before the blossoms
can turn into grapes,
God will cut off the sprouts
and hack off the branches.
6Ethiopians will be food
for mountain vultures
during the summer
and for wild animals
during the winter.
7Those Ethiopians are tall and their skin is smooth. They are feared all over the world, because they are strong and brutal. But at that time they will come from their land divided by rivers, and they will bring gifts to the Lord All-Powerful, who is worshiped on Mount Zion.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr Itiopia hina digna
1Wiarɛ huuzi Itiopia hɛri hina, ba daŋ nuu keeri gbɔga
lii hɛri bɛl
n du ba hɛri
muuni baŋgia,
2n hum balaa ba kpa muugberjigzi la,
baŋ kpa
kooriikpega kuaraa
di ra saa a muuni ni.
Ií ra la, balaa la n gbaŋŋɛ!
Ií kpa amaniye la
nɛra la n jaŋŋɛ,
ba bɔra vɔgli be,
hɛri la hina n na nyiŋŋi kalu,
ba ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi,
muuni bargi ba hɛri la.
3Durnya nɛra maa,
ií ra nuu!
Di ba wa lalli ba laal tuuta chiŋ, bizenaa nyuuni,
ii daŋ nau.
Di ba wa huuh bensunoniina,
ii daŋ nuu.
4Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,
“N danna du ii tau bɔɔiih
di lii n duuribɔr
alugɔ wiliŋ n ɔɔ ra lii winyɛgii ni,
kɔɔl ge tɔ chɔɔzi ni
kuna kumaa saŋa la.”
5Mɔɔ ka a kumaa hel,
di fii di nɔŋ
di waa aah la,
a saŋaa n kpa n kizee kɛuri a kelfuttaa la
ni anla n taazi nonee
di yɛl la ha.
6Gunnɛ ya ɛɛ Itiopia laallɔɔra la maa bá siu,
di birgi diwee tɛɛ
a bizenaa nyuuni
zumbizi ni pir sela.
Zumbizi daŋ di a lalaa lumaŋa,
pir sela ge
kegzi a hoga yuu.
7A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ daŋ na kunsunzaa
lii nɛra la maa n ɛɛ nɛjaŋra, ba bɔra vɔgli,
ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii tɛɛ
nɛra bɔr maa,
ba ɛɛ kalunyiŋŋe di ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi,
muuni bargi ba hɛri la be.
Ba daŋ kpa ba kunsunzaa di wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la, Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu, bɔr la banna jaamuu la.

english_text:
Egypt Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Egypt:
The Lord comes to Egypt,
riding swiftly on a cloud.
The people are weak from fear.
Their idols tremble
as he approaches and says,
2“I will punish Egypt
with civil war—
neighbors, cities, and kingdoms
will fight each other.
3“Egypt will be discouraged
when I confuse their plans.
They will try to get advice
from their idols,
from the spirits of the dead,
and from fortunetellers.
4I will put the Egyptians
under the power of a cruel,
heartless king.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have promised this.”
Trouble along the Nile
5The Nile River will dry up
and become parched land.
6Its streams will stink,
Egypt will have no water,
and the reeds and tall grass
will dry up.
7Fields along the Nile
will be completely barren;
every plant will disappear.
8Those who fish in the Nile
will be discouraged
and mourn.
9None of the cloth makers
will know what to do,
and they will turn pale.
10Weavers will be confused;
paid workers will cry and mourn.
Egypt's Helpless Leaders
11The king's officials in Zoan
are foolish themselves
and give stupid advice.
How can they say to him,
“We are very wise,
and our families go back
to kings of long ago?”
12Where are those wise men now?
If they can, let them say
what the Lord All-Powerful
intends for Egypt.
13The royal officials in Zoan
and in Memphis
are foolish and deceived.
The leaders in every state
have given bad advice
to the nation.
14The Lord has confused Egypt;
its leaders have made it stagger
and vomit like a drunkard.
15No one in Egypt can do a thing,
no matter who they are.
16When the Lord All-Powerful punishes Egypt with his mighty arm, the Egyptians will become terribly weak and will tremble with fear. 17They will be so terrified of Judah that they will be frightened by the very mention of its name. This will happen because of what the Lord All-Powerful is planning against Egypt.
The Lord Will Bless Egypt, Assyria, and Israel
18The time is coming when Hebrew will be spoken in five Egyptian cities, and their people will become followers of the Lord. One of these cities will be called City of the Sun.
19In the heart of Egypt an altar will be set up for the Lord; at its border a shrine will be built to honor him. 20These will remind the Egyptians that the Lord All-Powerful is with them. And when they are in trouble and ask for help, he will send someone to rescue them from their enemies. 21The Lord will show the Egyptians who he is, and they will know and worship the Lord. They will bring him sacrifices and offerings, and they will keep their promises to him. 22After the Lord has punished Egypt, the people will turn to him. Then he will answer their prayers, and the Egyptians will be healed.
23At that time a good road will run from Egypt to Assyria. The Egyptians and the Assyrians will travel back and forth from Egypt to Assyria, and they will worship together. 24Israel will join with these two countries. They will be a blessing to everyone on earth, 25then the Lord All-Powerful will bless them by saying,
“The Egyptians are my people.
I created the Assyrians
and chose the Israelites.”
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr Ijip hina digna
1Kɔraawiizi amaniye bɛllɛ keŋ n faa kaa nuu, u ra bagli Ijip hɛri wia,
Ií na! Kɔraawiizi tinni baama n na chɔ wergee
di ra ba Ijip.
Ɔnsii lau Ijip vugaa, a bɔra ra sa u see,
Ijip hina ge maa
bɔra huah.
2Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“N daŋ gil Ijip hina himmaa bir ra naa dɔŋa.
Kpɛɛnzi ni niuna danna naa,
nɛra ni ba dɔŋahina ra naa,
bolzenaa ra naa dɔŋa,
koora ra naa dɔŋa.
3Ijip hina maa bɔra daŋ huah,
bá wilaulaa maa ge ɛɛ pɛɛ.
Ba danna pɛɛzi ba vuga ni lalaa,
bá zum wii la n na ɛɛ,
di ra la vugra ni ijɔzi be,
di gaa pɛɛzi bá na wii la
n du de.
4N daŋ jaa kpa Ijip hina
du koorichɔgii bɛl
nonee biini,
ú kpa nɛsunnaa
di ra binni baa.”
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
5Muu Naal daŋ hil,
u gɔmbɔɔ maa pergi.
6Bɔra la baŋ pergee niiri danna sɔɔhri puihpuihpuih,
Ijip gɔŋa niiri
daŋ ka tama di hiihzi.
A kɛraa kooree maa daŋ siu.
7A muunua pattikuna maa daŋ siu,
peu paa kaali.
8Nyinlaura danna him dikuu ba kebee nyiŋŋibɔr n chɔkkɛ wia,
gɔrga taara ra nuumi,
asau taara ge so chaamm
dikuu kummaa
n waa hoo ba di wia.
9Nɛra la n na suah wɛjɛhuŋŋunanaa
wàá ka dɔɔ tamii maa.
10Wɛjɛsuahra maa daŋ sɛu ba nuuzi so,
huŋhunna maa ge
so ni biinichɔg.
11Zoan nabɔnzi ɛɛ gɛnaarɛ.
Ijip koori nunzunna
baglaa la ɛɛ
gɛnni baglaarɛ.
Ɛrɛɛ ii ra ŋɔ Ijip koori be,
“N ɛɛ nunzunna la bɛllɛ,
di faa ɛɛ faala koora hiŋrɛi?”
12Ijip koori, lee i nunzunna la duɛi?
Gil bá baglii gunla
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
n niŋ dau Ijip.
13Zoan nabɔnzi birgi gɛnaarɛ,
ba dar Mɛmfis ge
nabɔnzii.
Baabuu niŋ faa bagli Ijip hina ba chi nɛnnɛ,
ka ba gillɔɔ ba leu.
14Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ ba siwee ra biri,
ba wiŋɔzi gil Ijip hina
wiɛɛlaa maa waa deŋlee,
ka ra jiŋli alugɔ sinnyɔɔri,
n ɔɔ ra hɛhrgi
u hɛɛhzaa biini la.
15Nɛr maa waa hoo Ijip hɛri, di dɔɔnnɛ gɛɛ nyaarii
gɛɛ nɛzeŋ gɛɛ nɛduma,
ú wer hiini baa.
16A hɔl hiŋ, Ijip hina daŋ gɛrgi alugɔ haana. Ɔnsii daŋ lau baa, ba bɔra ra sa, dikuu Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la n lalli u banonii, ú tɔɔri baa wia. 17Di ba ŋɔ bá ŋɔ Juda hina wia, guŋ daŋ gil ɔnsii werge lau Ijip hina, dikuu biinichɔg la Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ n dauwɛ, ú chol ba ni wia.
18A hɔl hiŋ, Ijip bolzenaa anue nɛra danna mɔɔ Izrɛl hina mɔɔri, di sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la dɔɔra. A bolzeŋ bɛl sɔŋ daŋ ɛɛ ‘Wiizi Bol.’
19A hɔl hiŋ, ba daŋ ma mbusu lizibɔr Ijip hɛri baambaaŋ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di kaa baŋ bii bɛl a hɛri magbɔɔ tɛu. 20A daŋ ɛɛ kuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la daansɛɛ kuna, Ijip hɛri. Di a nɛra wa wiiwo du Kɔraawiizi lugɔ ú hiini baa, dikuu ba dɔma n na sunni baa wia, u daŋ tɛɛ baa Lɛɛri, ú lɛɛ baa. 21Awia, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa u hiŋ bagli Ijip hina, bá zumuu. Wibii maa, a hɔl hiŋ, ba daŋ sɛɛ tɛu, di kpa ba mbusu lizaa kuna ni ba mia sunzaazi wa jaamuu, ka kpa tɛu. Ba daŋ ŋɔ nuuzi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ra hiŋaa ni wibii. 22Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa tɔɔrɔɔ ta Ijip hina ni. U daŋ lɔ baa ka bir chaa baa. Ba daŋ bir ba u be, ú nuu ba suŋŋaa di chaa baa.
23A hɔl hiŋ, ŋmɛninanii bɛl daŋ lii Ijip hɛri di ra la Asiiria hɛri, Ijip ni Asiiria hina ɔɔ jaa ga de di ra la dɔŋa hɛssi, di kpau ra jaami Kɔraawiizi. 24A hɔl hiŋ, Izrɛl, Ijip ani Asiiria hina daŋ dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, durnya hɛssi nɛra maa na hiinaa lii ba be. 25Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la daŋ kissi baa, di ŋɔ, “Ijip hina, miŋ gillɛ ii ɛɛ n nɛra, Asiiria hina la, miŋ tawɛɛ, Izrɛl hina, miŋ lizi ia tɛɛ n hiŋ.”

english_text:
Isaiah Acts Out the Defeat of Egypt and Ethiopia
1King Sargon of Assyria gave orders for his army commander to capture the city of Ashdod. 2About this same time the Lord had told me, “Isaiah, take off everything, including your sandals!” I did this and went around naked and barefoot 3for three years.
Then the Lord said:
What Isaiah has done is a warning to Egypt and Ethiopia. 4Everyone in these two countries will be led away naked and barefoot by the king of Assyria. Young or old, they will be taken prisoner, and Egypt will be disgraced. 5They will be confused and frustrated, because they depended on Ethiopia and bragged about Egypt. 6When this happens, the people who live along the coast will say, “Look what happened to them! We ran to them for safety, hoping they would protect us from the king of Assyria. But now, there is no escape for us.”
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n niŋ chɔgi Ijip ni Itiopia wia
1Bina la Asiiria Koorizeŋ Sagɔn, n hum u laallɔɔra nabɔnzeŋ, ú la ga lɔ Filisti hina laal, di kpegli bolzeŋ Asdɔd la, 2Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Amɔz biibaal Aizaaya be, “Wir i gbɔglɔŋ laala la, di lizi i gawa ge.” Aizaaya faa ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u be la, ka faa ra vol chakpal ni naadumazi.
3Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ, “N balii Aizaaya n vol chakpal ni naadumazi binni ahoro naa, gunna bagli tɔɔrɔɔ la dee min niŋ gil ú wa chol Ijip ni Itiopia hina ninɛɛ. 4Asiiria koorizeŋ daŋ lauri baa, bá birgi u yoma. U daŋ gil Ijip ni Itiopia nabɔnzi, ba biipɔllaa ani suŋgure maa ra vol chakpalli ni naadumazi, ba wàá tɔɔgi ba zɛɛpume tama maa. Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ hiihzi Ijip hina be werge maa. 5Banla n yardi Ijip ni Itiopia hina, di ra jigsi lugɔ baabuu niŋ wer lɛɛ baa la, ɔnsii daŋ wa lau baa, bá di hiihzi. 6Di a hɔl wa hello, banla n du Filisti muuzeŋ nua la danna ŋɔ, ‘Di wia naa dɔŋa wetto huuzi Ijip hina, beedee ya ge kaa wer ɛɛ di lɛɛ yaa hinaanɛi? Yaa faa dɛlli ba ninɛɛ lugɔ ba hiini yaa, Asiiria koorizeŋ la gilɛɛ wa wer ra ɛɛ yaa wiimaa.’ ”

english_text:
The Fall of Babylonia
1This is a message about a desert beside the sea:
Enemies from a hostile nation
attack like a whirlwind
from the Southern Desert.
2What a horrible vision
was shown to me—
a vision of betrayal
and destruction.
Tell Elam and Media
to surround and attack
the Babylonians.
The Lord has sworn to end
the suffering they caused.
3I'm in terrible pain
like a woman giving birth.
I'm shocked and hurt so much
that I can't hear or see.
4My head spins; I'm horrified!
Early evening, my favorite time,
has become a nightmare.
5In Babylon the high officials
were having a feast.
They were eating and drinking,
when someone shouted,
“Officers, take your places!
Grab your shields.”
6The Lord said to me,
“Send guards
to find out
what's going on.
7When they see cavalry troops
and columns of soldiers
on donkeys and camels,
tell them to be ready!”
8Then a guard said,
“I have stood day and night
on this watchtower, Lord.
9 Now I see column after column
of cavalry troops.”
At once someone shouted,
“Babylon has fallen!
Every idol in the city
lies broken on the ground.”
10Then I said, “My people,
you have suffered terribly,
but I have a message for you
from the Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel.”
How Much Longer?
11This is a message about Dumah:
From the country of Seir,
someone shouts to me,
“Guard, how much longer
before daylight?”
12From my guard post, I answered,
“Morning will soon be here,
but night will return.
If you want to know more,
come back later.”
13This is a message for Arabs who live in the barren desert in the region of Dedan:
You must order your caravans
14to bring water for those
who are thirsty.
You people of Tema
must bring food
for the hungry refugees.
15They are worn out and weary
from being chased by enemies
with swords and arrows.
16The Lord said to me:
A year from now the glory of the people of Kedar will all come to an end, just as a worker's contract ends after a year. 17Only a few of their warriors will be left with bows and arrows. This is a promise that I, the Lord God of Israel, have made.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n niŋ chɔgi Babilɔn wia
1Kɔraawiizi amaniye naabuu n faa nuu, u ra bagli Babilɔn wia.
Nɛra ra bau alugɔ vem n lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma,
di gbaari kuna ra ba.
Hɛri bɛl hina wia n dɔɔ ɔnsii wergee,
ba lii ra ba.
2N na wia aŋhinaa lugɔ deeza biini, a waa wer.
Sɔsɔgɔ hiŋ ra ɛɛ sɔsɔgɔ,
kumpaaga ra paagi kuna.
Ɛlam hina, ií lii lɔ baa laal! Mɛdi hina, ií fɔɔ baa!
N daŋ gil tɔɔrɔɔ
ni nuumaa la
Babilɔn hina
n bɔɔni la jaa tuŋ.
3Wia naa gillɔɔ n bɔra ra wiiŋ, di ra baari werge maa,
di ra wii werge lugɔ
hiwiila n ɔɔ lɔ haaŋ gunla.
Miŋ wa nuu gunla n na ɛɛ la, n bɔra maa huah,
wia la minna
na la ɛɛŋ witittii.
4N laakal maa leu,
n bɔra ra sa.
Wiizi cholaa n faa zuuŋ suma,
n chɔɔ ra heezi la,
jaa ɛɛŋ banchullɔi.
5Ií na! Ba daali diuzenaare,
di kuari ba diiribɔr,
di so ra di,
ka ra nyɔɔ sinni.
Laal nabɔnzi, ií izi
kpa ii laal pɛrɛtuzi!
6Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,
“La ga lizi tauduuri, ú so ra du tau.
Kunla maa uŋ wa nawɛɛ
ú ŋɔ i be.
7Di u wa na zagra
n na tɛrgi torkozi,
laallɔɔra ge tinni kauzi
ni nyugmazi,
ú ra du tau nɛnnɛ,
di gilɛɛ wa ta u hiŋ.”
8Denii a tauduuri la ra ŋɔ kpegzi ni,
“N nabɔma, hɔpizi biimaanii n ɔɔ chi n tau duuribɔr ɛŋ, di ra du tau,
hamuŋa maa ge,
aŋ chi bɔnnaabuu
di ra du tau.”
9Ií na baal bɛl n du torko biini,
zagra tɛrguu di ra ba!
U amaniyee keŋ,
“Babilɔn cholloo!
U vuga ge maa
chogli purgi.”
10N nɛra Izrɛl hina, iiŋ ɛɛwɛ lugɔ mia baŋ lɔwɛɛ, di hɛlaa la,
ií gil n ŋɔ ii be
gunla miŋ nuuwɛ
lii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la be,
Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina
n na hum la be.
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Ɛdɔm chɔgaa wia
11Kɔraawiizi amaniyee keŋ, di ra bagli Ɛdɔm wia.
Nɛbɛl yirimbuu lii Ɛdɔm, di ŋɔ,
“Tauduuri, hɔpizaa
daŋ haa birgiaa?
Saŋa bɛɛ bɔ́r chaanɛi?”
12A tauduuri sɛɛ, di ŋɔ,
“Hɔɔ ra pizuu,
ka bɔr ge
wàá ka birgi ka biri.
Ama, di i kaa ra nyiŋŋi ŋɔ i pɛɛzi guŋ,
kaa bir ba wa pɛɛzi.”
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Lɔrbizi hɛri chɔgaa wia
13N faa kaa nuu amaniye naa lii Kɔraawiizi be, u ra bagli Lɔrbizi hɛri wia.
Dɛdan hina n kpogli nyugmazi
di wa chɔɔ Lɔrbizi hɛri
daazi biine,
14ií kpa nii wa tɛɛ
banla niinyɔgzi
n na kpu,
Tɛma hina,
ií kpa diwee wa tɛɛ
banla n na chɔ laal.
15Ba chɔwɔɔrɛ ra lii tokobi be,
tokobi la baŋ pammɛ be,
hoo la baŋ ɛɛ sirya bá ta,
ani laal bɔwem be.
16Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ tɛŋ, “Gunla paahdiiri n na kur u hɔpizaa maga la, ií ge kur guŋ biŋkpaŋ biini, Kɛda zenni ni u girme la maa daŋ tuŋ. 17Kɛda hotaara la n na lɔ laal la tama bɛnnɛ niŋ ka.” Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum labuu ŋɔ guŋ!

english_text:
Trouble in Vision Valley
1This is a message about Vision Valley:
Why are you celebrating
on the flat roofs
of your houses?
2Your city is filled
with noisy shouts.
Those who lie drunk
in your streets
were not killed in battle.
3Your leaders ran away,
but they were captured
without a fight.
No matter how far they ran,
they were found and caught.
4Then I said, “Leave me alone!
Let me cry bitter tears.
My people have been destroyed,
so don't try to comfort me.”
5The Lord All-Powerful
had chosen a time
for noisy shouts and confusion
to fill Vision Valley,
and for everyone to beg
the mountains for help.
6The people of Elam and Kir
attacked with chariots
and carried shields.
7Your most beautiful valleys
were covered with chariots;
your cities were surrounded
by cavalry troops.
8Judah was left defenseless.
At that time you trusted in the weapons you had stored in Forest Palace. 9You saw the holes in the outer wall of Jerusalem, and you brought water from the lower pool. 10You counted the houses in Jerusalem and tore down some of them, so you could get stones to repair the city wall. 11Then you built a large tank between the walls to store the water. But you refused to trust the God who planned this long ago and made it happen.
A Time To Weep
12When all of this happened,
the Lord All-Powerful told you
to weep and mourn,
to shave your heads,
and wear sackcloth.
13 But instead, you celebrated
by feasting on beef and lamb
and by drinking wine,
because you said,
“Let's eat and drink today!
Tomorrow we may die.”
14The Lord All-Powerful
has spoken to me
this solemn promise:
“I won't forgive them for this,
not as long as they live.”
Selfish Officials Are Doomed
15The Lord All-Powerful is sending me with this message for Shebna, the prime minister:
16Shebna, what gives you the right to have a tomb carved out of rock in this burial place of royalty? None of your relatives are buried here. 17You may be powerful, but the Lord is about to snatch you up and throw you away. 18He will roll you into a ball and throw you into a wide open country, where you will die and your chariots will be destroyed. You're a disgrace to those you serve.
19The Lord is going to take away your job! 20-21He will give your official robes and your authority to his servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
Eliakim will be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the royal family of Judah. 22 The Lord will put him in charge of the key that belongs to King David's family. No one will be able to unlock what he locks, and no one will be able to lock what he unlocks. 23The Lord will make him as firm in his position as a tent peg hammered in the ground, and Eliakim will bring honor to his family.
24His children and relatives will be supported by him, like pans hanging from a peg on the wall. 25That peg is fastened firmly now, but someday it will be shaken loose and fall down. Then everything that was hanging on it will be destroyed. This is what the Lord All-Powerful has promised.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm chɔgaa wia
1Amaniye naabuu n faa nuu Kɔraawiizi be, u ra bagli Wia Nai Lugɔ Deeza Biini Waluu wia.
Beedee n na ɛɛ iai,
ii maa chɔ tinni salɛi?
2A bolzeŋ maa ra kɔɔu, dɔm izi bɔr maa.
Bɛɛwiarɛ a bolzeŋ naa
hina ra kɔɔ di ra di
bahinaa kennei?
Ii nɛra siuwɔɔ chɔɔ bɔr maa,
ka laal biini lɛi ba siu.
Tokobi lɛi kpu baa.
3Ii sitɔɔra maa chɔwɔɔrɛ.
Ba dɔma haa waa
hozi gba tawɛɛ,
ka lauri baa.
Ii banla maa baŋ laurɛɛ maanii ba kpogli kaali,
haali iiŋ faa chɔwɛɛ
di ii dɔma haa du
bɔɔnɛɛ la gba.
4Awia, n ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií giliŋ bɔɔiih,
ń wii werge,
ií gilɛɛ ra tig n bampirii,
dikuu n nɛra siu wia.”
5Ee, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ lizi hɔpiziirɛ,
nɛra n niŋ chɔ ra bar
di ra kɔɔ di bugmi
Wia Nai Lugɔ
Deeza Biini Waluu biini.
A hɔl la ban niŋ furgi koŋlaa,
di wii ra du bizenaa,
á lɛɛ baa.
6Ɛlam laallɔɔra kpa ba hozii
zuu ba laal torkozi,
di ra ba.
Nɛra la n lii Kir hɛri la ge kpogli
laal pɛrɛtuzenaa di ra ba.
7Ii walsuma maanii su laal torkozi,
zagtinna ge ga du
Jɛrusalɛm dominuuzenaa la.
8Koŋlaa ni kuna la maa n na lɛɛ Juda hɛri la maanii chɔkkɛ.
Guŋ n ɛɛwɛ, ii chɔwɔɔrɛ la
ii dɔmkuna dauri bɔr,
di ga paagi laal kuna la.
9Ii na gunla Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii n baruu la
bɔkpila maa n purgee
laal biinii,
ii chi nii du
Zɛɛ Pol la biini.
10Ii kur Jɛrusalɛm diinii,
di purgi aŋhinaa,
di lizi a binanaa
ií kuari a koŋlii ma,
u du kpeg.
11Ii ma nii bɔr bɛllɛ koŋlaa anɛɛ la baambaaŋ,
nii lii Polbinii la
di waa zuu u biini.
Ii ɛɛ annii naa maanii tuŋ, ka ii faa waa Kɔraawiizi la
n dau annii maa
saŋa maa uŋ ŋɔ
u daŋ ɛɛ la.
12Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la yir iabuu
di ŋɔ ii be a saŋa hiŋ,
dí ií ra wii, di ra chɛɛhgi,
dí ií fuŋ ii nyuuni, di laali gbɔglɔnzi,
guŋ bagli lugɔ
ii biine chɔkkɔɔ
ii wichɔgaa wia.
13Ka guŋ lɛi, ii ra sau di ra dua,
di kpuuzi nauna ni peeza
di ra hee, di ra nyɔɔ siŋ.
Ii ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií gil ya ra di, di ra nyɔɔ siŋ,
di kɛrɛ yaa daŋ siu,
yaa waa zum!”
14Ka Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ pilli wii naabuu bagliŋ di ŋɔ, “Màá gil ii wichɔgaa naa tɛɛ ia di ra la ii siuri hɔpizii.” Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
15Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“La ga na Sɛbna,
unla n ɛɛ
kooridiahina nabɔma la,
di lizi amaniye naa tɛu,
16‘Bɛɛ i ra ɛɛ ɛnnɛi? Anɛɛ n tɛi ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ
í kuari i ŋmam bɔnnaa,
di ra tug bii, girme bɔr naa,
di ra kuaruu nɛnnɛ,
de wa ɛɛ i hugribɔrɛi?
17I ra yir i hinnɛ nɛzeŋ, a du tau!
Kɔraawiizi ra nyiŋŋuu
ú kpai ha.
18U daŋ kpai lugɔ bɔɔl,
di tai i ga chol
hɛrzeŋ bɛl.
Denii i siu,
í laal torkonanaa
la ka de.
I gillɔɔ i dɔɔri
diahina di hiihzi.
19N daŋ duŋŋii lii i huma biini.
N daŋ lizii lii
i nabɔmbɔr la.’
20A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ yir n balii Hilkia biibaal Ɛliakim. 21N daŋ kpa i nabɔnlaala la laaluu, di kpa i kirsɔɔ kirsuu, di kpa fɔŋŋa la hiŋ faa dɔɔwɛ la tɛu. U daŋ jaa birgi Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina maa mɛɛ. 22N daŋ kpa nabɔmuu tɛu, Koori Deevid naana kora dii biini, di kaa tɛu nabɔmuu saafiibii, di u wa pillɔɔ, nɛr maa wàá wer tɔ, di u kaa tɔ ge, nɛr maa wàá wer pilli. 23N daŋ gil u chi u chignibɔr nɛnnɛ alugɔ baŋ kpa daasirii di kpaahzi koŋlii ni, waa ziigaa dɔɔwɛ la. Nɛra daŋ kuu girme la un dɔɔwɛ wia, di ra tɔgzi u diahina maa. 24U nɛra maa tɔɔrɔɔ daŋ sag u ni, alugɔ baŋ kpa hɛnni, tassazi ani viini maa sag daasirii ni la.”
25Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di a hɔl wa hello, daasirii la baŋ kpaahzɛɛ du koŋlii ni, waa ziigaa dɔɔwɛ la daŋ chol hɛri, kunla maa n faa sag u ni la gba chol.” Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ!

english_text:
The City of Tyre Will Be Punished
1 This is a message from distant islands about the city of Tyre:
Cry, you seagoing ships!
Tyre and its houses
lie in ruins.
2Mourn in silence,
you shop owners of Sidon,
you people on the coast.
Your sailors crossed oceans,
making your city rich.
3Your merchants sailed the seas,
making you wealthy by trading
with nation after nation.
They brought back grain
that grew along the Nile.
4Sidon, you are a mighty fortress
built along the sea.
But you will be disgraced
like a married woman
who never had children.
5When Egypt hears about Tyre,
it will tremble.
6All of you along the coast
had better cry and sail
far across the ocean.
7Can this be the happy city
that has stood for centuries?
Its people have spread
to distant lands;
8its merchants were kings
honored all over the world.
Who planned to destroy Tyre?
9The Lord All-Powerful planned it
to bring shame and disgrace
to those who are honored
by everyone on earth.
10People of Tyre,
your harbor is destroyed!
You will have to become farmers
just like the Egyptians.
Tyre Will Be Forgotten
11The Lord's hand has reached
across the sea,
upsetting the nations.
He has given a command
to destroy fortresses
in the land of Canaan.
12The Lord has said
to the people of Sidon,
“Your celebrating is over—
you are crushed.
Even if you escape to Cyprus,
you won't find peace.”
13Look what the Assyrians have done to Babylonia! They have attacked, destroying every palace in the land. Now wild animals live among the ruins. 14Not a fortress will be left standing, so tell all the seagoing ships to mourn.
15The city of Tyre will be forgotten for 70 years, which is the lifetime of a king. Then Tyre will be like that evil woman in the song:
16You're gone and forgotten,
you evil woman!
So strut through the town,
singing and playing
your favorite tune
to be remembered again.
17At the end of those 70 years, the Lord will let Tyre get back into business. The city will be like a woman who sells her body to everyone of every nation on earth, 18but none of what is earned will be kept in the city. That money will belong to the Lord, and it will be used to buy more than enough food and good clothes for those who worship the Lord.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ bolzeŋ Taaya chɔgaa wia
1Amaniye naabuu n faa nuu lii Kɔraawiizi be, u ra bagli bolzeŋ Taaya ge wia.
Ee, Taasis muugberzenaa saara, ií ra wii!
Ii muugberzenaa chignibɔr la
n du Taaya la chɔkkɔɔ!
Taaya ni u diini
maanii purgee.
U muugbessi chignibɔr
waa kaa hoo.
Iinna ba wa hel Saiprɔs labuu
ii nuu a guŋ amaniye.
2Ií banla n soge muuzeŋ baaŋ hɛri ni
Saidɔn kɔkɔɔza,
ií maa chi surumm.
Muugberzenaa saara
gillɔɔ ii dɔɔ daama.
3Ií ɔɔ ga muuzenaa biinii la Ijip hɛri ka ra ba,
di kpa Sihɔ mia
ni pattikuna la baŋ kpawɛɛ lii Muu Naal kɛraa di ba Taaya.
Taaya faa ɛɛ durnya
hɛssi maa yawaa.
4Saidɔn hina, ií gil hiihzi kpu ia. Muuzeŋ la n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ diikpeg, ii dɛlli u ni la, ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Lulaa hiwiila haa wan lɔwɛɛ maa,
n ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa
biibaala gɛɛ
biihaana dɛɛzɛɛ.”
5Di Ijip hina wa nuuwɔ lugɔ
ba chɔg Taayaa,
ba biine daŋ chɔgi
werge maa.
6Awia, ii banla maa n soge a muuzeŋ baaŋ hɛri,
ií ra chɛɛhgi,
di chɔ gi ra la Taasis!
7Nɛra la n du de barii maa ra ŋɔu lugɔ
bolbinii la n du de
faala maa la,
di gil nɛra bɔra sɔɔni,
u nɛra la bɔɔnɛɛ
di gaa yoo ba kuna la,
a ɛɛ wibiire lugɔ
ba chɔguubuuwaa?
8Anɛɛ n vɔɔ Taaya jina kennei?
Bolzeŋ la n faa dɔɔ
kuna la maa nɛra
n faa ra nyiŋŋi.
Bɔr la baŋ faa ra tɔgzi kɔkɔɔza lugɔ sitɔɔra,
di kaa ɛɛ bol la
u kɔkɔɔza n ɛɛ nɛzenaa,
di faa kaa ra
tɔgzi baa bɔr la
maa baŋ laŋŋɛ.
9Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu ɛɛ guŋ,
ú gil Taaya hina
siwii sɔɔni,
dikuu ba jigsi wia,
di faa kaa gil banla
banna tɔgzi ge,
durnya maa biini
siwii sɔɔni.
10Taasis hina, ií gaa par ii hɛri gunla Ijip hina n na par Muu Naal kɛraa la,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ii waa kaa dɔɔ
muugberzenaa chignibɔr.
11Kɔraawiizi tɛr u noniire guali muuzeŋ ni,
di gil u kossi nɛra
bɔra ra sa.
U dau Fonisia hɛri wiarɛ
lugɔ bá chɔgi
u diikpega.
12U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ee, Saidɔn hina,
iihinaa dii tunnɔɔ.
Haali di ii chɔwɔɔ la Saiprɔs gba,
ka ii wàá ga
na heezaa.”
13Ií binni Babilɔn hɛri na,
u nɛra waa kaa dɔɔ tɔna!
Asiiria hina gillɔɔ a bolzeŋ birgi
hɛribɔduma sela duuribɔr.
Ba faa fɔɔubuu, di ma diijaŋra n la chiŋ werge, di pɛgli u koŋlaa,
di purgi u diikpega maa,
u birgi diŋgela.
14Taasis muugberzenaa saara,
ií ra chɛɛhgi!
Ba chɔg ii diikpegre.
15A guŋ saŋa, ba daŋ suuh Taaya wia binni tokkoahoro ni fi, alugɔ koori kora dii binni maga. Ka a binni naa tuna, Taaya daŋ kaa bir wa du alugɔ yir bɛl banna yir, di ra bagli sɛnsɛnni bɛl wia, di ra ŋɔ,
16“Hahsɛnsɛnni la baŋ suuh i wia,
kpa kem lɔ
ra bar a bol biini.
A lɔu nɛnnɛ, di ra yir yirsuma,
bá kaa liizi i wia.”
17Di binni tokkoahoro ni fi la wa bɛrɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil Taaya kaa ra hum u huma. A bolzeŋ daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ hahsɛnsɛnni, di yoo u hiŋ di ra tɛɛ durnya kossi maa. 18Ka a saŋa, u humazi la maa tɔna daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hor. Ba wàá tɔ u daama la chiŋŋi, ka ba daŋ kpaa yau diwee werge ni laalinanaa di ra tɛɛ banla n na jaami Kɔraawiizi la.

english_text:
The Earth Will Be Punished
1The Lord is going to twist the earth out of shape and turn it into a desert. Everyone will be scattered, 2including ordinary people and priests, slaves and slave owners, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, the rich and the poor. 3The earth will be stripped bare and left that way. This is what the Lord has promised.
4The earth wilts away;
its mighty leaders melt
to nothing.
5The earth is polluted
because its people
disobeyed the laws of God,
breaking their agreement
that was to last forever.
6The earth is under a curse;
its people are dying out
because of their sins.
7Grapevines have dried up:
wine is almost gone—
mournful sounds are heard
instead of joyful shouts.
8No one plays tambourines
or stringed instruments;
all noisy celebrating
has come to an end.
9They no longer sing
as they drink their wine,
and it tastes sour.
10Towns are crushed and in chaos;
houses are locked tight.
11Happy times have disappeared
from the earth,
and people shout in the streets,
“We're out of wine!”
12Cities are destroyed;
their gates are torn down.
13Nations will be stripped bare,
like olive trees or vineyards
after the harvest season.
Praise the God of Justice
14People in the west shout;
they joyfully praise
the majesty of the Lord.
15And so, everyone in the east
and those on the islands
should praise the Lord,
the God of Israel.
16From all over the world
songs of praise are heard
for the God of justice.
But I feel awful,
terribly miserable.
Can anyone be trusted?
So many are treacherous!
There's No Escape
17Terror, traps, and pits
are waiting for everyone.
18If you are terrified and run,
you will fall into a pit;
if you crawl out of the pit,
you will get caught in a trap.
The sky has split apart
like a window thrown open.
The foundations of the earth
have been shaken;
19the earth is shattered,
ripped to pieces.
20It staggers and shakes
like a drunkard
or a hut in a windstorm.
It is burdened down with sin;
the earth will fall,
never again to get up.
21On that day the Lord
will punish the powers
in the heavens
and the kings of the earth.
22He will put them in a pit
and keep them prisoner.
Then later on,
he will punish them.
23Both the moon and sun will
be embarrassed and ashamed.
The Lord All-Powerful will rule
on Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
where he will show its rulers
his wonderful glory.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgi a hɛri
1Ií ra nuu! Kɔraawiizi ra nyiŋŋuu ú chɔgi a hɛri naa maa
ú puri chɔɔ burburbur.
U daŋ chɔgi a hɛri
di gil u nɛra chɔ yaari.
2Guŋ himmaanii niŋ huuzi
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina
ni nɛra maa,
gɛɛ dɔɔra ni balaa maa,
gɛɛ banla n na yoo kuna
ani banla ge n na yawaa,
gɛɛ banla ge n na di kima
ani banla be banna kim.
3Hɛri la maa daŋ chɔgi kɔrai,
kummaa wàá ka ka u biini.
Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ!
4A hɛri hillɔɔ, pattikuna maa siuzi,
a hɛri maa chɔgi.
Durnya nabɔnzenaa tuu zɛɛ.
5A hɛri hinaa chɔguu.
Ba vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ,
di chɔgi u Gbɔgni,
di kaa chɔgi u ni baa
nuukpaŋ la n waa
tunaa dɔɔwɛ la.
6Awiarɛ u nuuseei chɔgi hɛri naa ni u nɛra maa la.
Ba wichɔgaa kinturgaare guŋ.
Awiarɛ niŋ fuuh baa la,
ba tama bɛnnɛ kawɛɛ.
7Grepu daazi yɔllɔ, a nɔna la nii baŋ ɔɔ kpa ra ɛɛ siŋ la hiihzi,
Awia, banla bɔra
n ɔɔ sɔɔni,
ba ra chaasi la, jaa ra him,
8lɔŋgɔma yigzaa tuŋ,
nɛra la n na di bahinaa
la kɔɔi tuŋ,
kemzi la n ɔɔ faa gil
nɛra bɔra sɔɔni la siigi.
9Ba waa kaa ra yir yira ka ra nyɔɔ ba siŋ,
siŋkpega ge jaa du kpol
a nyɔɔra nuuzi.
10A bolzeŋ puri,
nɛr maa tɔ
u dominua kiŋkiŋ.
11Nɛra du ŋmɛnizi di ra wii siŋ wia.
Bɔsɔna tunnɔɔ,
ka biinichɔg
du de werge maa.
Suma maa waa
kaa hoo a hɛri.
12A bolzeŋ puroore di chɔgi,
ba lɔ a dominuuzenaa
maa kuugi.
13Gunnɛ niŋ ɛɛ durnya hɛssi
hina maa biine,
alugɔ baŋ ɔɔ zagi ɔlivi daa u nɔna chogli la,
gɛɛ baŋ ɔɔ ra kuuni
grepuzi kpaŋkpaŋa la
baŋ tɔrgɛɛ ka ka la.
14Banla n kawɛɛ ge danna yir yira ni bɔsɔna.
Banla n du wiicholii barii la
danna chɔli
Kɔraawiizi zenni la.
15Wiifurii barii hina ge, ií ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi girme.
Banla n soge
muuzeŋ baaŋ hɛri la,
ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la
Izrɛl hina n na hum la.
16Yaa ra nuu gunla banna yir yiraa lii durnya naa yemmaa,
di ra ŋɔ,
“Ií ra chɔli
Wideŋlaa Hiŋ la.”
Ka n ŋɔ, “N maanii ra tuŋ dikuu biinichɔg werge wia, wibii maa!
Wiarɛ huuziŋ.
Nɛchɔgaa ra ɛɛ sɔsɔgɔɔ bɔr maa.
Ba sɔsɔgɔ wiɛɛlaa la
jaa ra nyaŋŋuu.”
17Durnya hina, ɔnsii werge, bɔɔ ani sidɛɛ bɛnnɛ chɔɔwɛ,
di ra kpaŋ ia.
18Banla maa n ninna chɔ dikuu ɔnsii werge wia,
daŋ chol bɔɔ biini,
banla ge n niŋ lii a bɔɔ biini,
sidɛɛzi daŋ lauri baa.
Chiŋ daŋ pilli, dozeŋ chol,
durnya zigli.
19A durnya hɛri daŋ pergi,
di purgi,
di zigli werge maa.
20A hɛri daŋ jiŋli alugɔ sinnyɔɔri,
di kaa ra zigli alugɔ
peu n na ta
pampanni ni.
U wichɔgaa kannɔɔ werge maa,
awia, u daŋ chol,
wàá ka izi maa.
21A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɔɔri
fɔŋŋazi la n du chiŋ
ni koora la n du hɛri.
22Ba daŋ lauri baa tɔ dia,
gunla baŋ ɔɔ tɔ nɛra la,
ba du de hɔpizikpila,
ka ú wa tɔɔri baa.
23Denii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la jaa di u kora la
Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu.
Jɛrusalɛm biinii ú di a kora hiŋ
a nɛra nabɔnzi la maa see,
haali u girme la gil
hiihzi kpu wiizi ni baagu,
dikuu u girme la n niŋ gil
ba wàá ka zum
a chaanaa wia la.

english_text:
A Prayer of Thanks to God
1You, Lord, are my God!
I will praise you
for doing the wonderful things
you had planned and promised
since ancient times.
2You have destroyed the fortress
of our enemies,
leaving their city in ruins.
Nothing in that foreign city
will ever be rebuilt.
3Now strong and cruel nations
will fear and honor you.
4You have been a place of safety
for the poor and needy
in times of trouble.
Brutal enemies pounded us
like a heavy rain
or the heat of the sun at noon,
but you were our shelter.
5Those wild foreigners struck
like scorching desert heat.
But you were like a cloud,
protecting us from the sun.
You kept our enemies from singing
songs of victory.
The Lord Has Saved Us
6On this mountain
the Lord All-Powerful
will prepare for all nations
a feast of the finest foods.
Choice wines and the best meats
will be served.
7Here the Lord will strip away
the burial clothes
that cover the nations.
8 The Lord All-Powerful
will destroy the power of death
and wipe away all tears.
No longer will his people
be insulted everywhere.
The Lord has spoken!
9At that time, people will say,
“The Lord has saved us!
Let's celebrate.
We waited and hoped—
now our God is here.”
10 The powerful arm of the Lord
will protect this mountain.
The Moabites will be put down
and trampled on like straw
in a pit of manure.
11They will struggle to get out,
but God will humiliate them
no matter how hard they try.
12The walls of their fortresses
will be knocked down
and scattered in the dirt.
