translation_text:
Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi
1N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hinuu n na hum.
N danna tɔgzii
di ra chɔli i sɔŋ.
Hiŋ ɛɛ wibii hiŋ la wia,
i ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia la
hiŋ dauwɛ saŋa maa labuu.
2I gillɔɔ bolzenaa purgi, a hembugle chɔɔgi kulululu,
bolzeŋkpega la maa purgi.
Hɛhjaŋa bolzenaa puroore,
ba wàá ka wer maa maa.
3Awia, fɔŋŋa hina danna tɔgzii,
hɛssi hina bolzenaa
nɛra la n dɔɔ
sikpegii hina danna ɔmii.
4I ɛɛ bɔr la nyaara ni anuula hina n na suauh,
di kaa ɛɛ suahribɔr tɛɛ nɛra
dooŋ peu n na yag baa,
wiizi ge ra kpuu baa labuu.
Sikpegii hina ra bau
bá wa lɔ baa lugɔ
dooŋ pekpeg
n na yag koŋlii,
5di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ wiliŋ
n ɔɔ ra lii hɛribɔduma biini.
I gillɔɔ hɔɔhra la n na kɔɔ la siigi kakpaŋ
alugɔ baama n ɔɔ wa guali
bɔwem ni u bir sɔɔni la.
Gunnɛ sikpegii hina
yira la teŋ.
6Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la daŋ chi Bizeŋ Ziɔn naa nyuu,
di daali diuzenaa,
olnanaa ani sinnanaa himmaa,
tɛɛ hɛssi hina maa.
7Bizeŋ naa nyuurɛ ú pilli kasaŋa n tɔ durnya nɛra maa ni la,
8di chɔgi siu,
di hanna la,
saŋaa saŋa maa.
Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ fiizi nɛr maa sinii
lii nɛra maa siwee.
U daŋ lizi hiihzi la u nɛra n faa diwee la,
durnya naa biini.
Kɔraawiizi himmaanii ŋɔ guŋ!
9A hɔl hiŋ, u nɛra daŋ ŋɔ,
“Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi
la ya n na hum labuu keŋ.
Yaa yarduubuu, u lɛɛ yaa.
Kɔraawiizi la yaa n yardɛɛ labuu keŋ,
ií gil yaa bɔra sɔɔni,
dikuu uŋ lɛɛ yaa wia!”
10Kɔraawiizi nonii daŋ ɔɔ guali Bizeŋ Ziɔn naa ni.
Ka u daŋ fɛrgi Moab hɛri hinawaa
lugɔ baŋ ɔɔ fɛrgi kɔlaa
a zuu nabina biini
di pɔɔh gunla.
11Ba daŋ ɛɛ wiimaa bá lɛɛ bahinaa
ka pɛɛrɛ.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ba nunzuma
ni ba jigsi la maa tuŋ.
12U daŋ gil koŋliikpega la baŋ mawɛɛ bar ba bola purgi burburbur,
chɔɔ hɛri di birgi nyɔɔ.

english_text:
A Song of Victory
1The time is coming when the people of Judah will sing this song:
“Our city is protected.
The Lord is our fortress,
and he gives us victory.
2Open the city gates
for a law-abiding nation
that is faithful to God.
3The Lord gives perfect peace
to those whose faith is firm.
4So always trust the Lord
because he is forever
our mighty rock.
5God has put down our enemies
in their mountain city
and rubbed it in the dirt.
6Now the poor and abused
trample all over that city.”
The Lord Can Be Trusted
7Our Lord, you always do right,
and you make the path smooth
for those who obey you.
8You are the one we trust
to bring about justice;
above all else we want
your name to be honored.
9Throughout the night,
my heart searches for you,
because your decisions
show everyone on this earth
how to live right.
10Even when the wicked
are treated with mercy
in this land of justice,
they do wrong and are blind
to your glory, our Lord.
11 Your hand is raised and ready
to punish them,
but they don't see it.
Put them to shame!
Show how much you care for us
and throw them into the fire
intended for your enemies.
12You will give us peace, Lord,
because everything we have done
was by your power.
13Others have ruled over us
besides you, our Lord God,
but we obey only you.
14Those enemies are now dead
and can never live again.
You have punished them—
they are destroyed,
completely forgotten.
15Our nation has grown
because of you, our Lord.
We have more land than before,
and you are honored.
The Lord Gives Life to the Dead
16When you punished our people,
they turned and prayed
to you, our Lord.
17Because of what you did to us,
we suffered like a woman
about to give birth.
18But instead of having a child,
our terrible pain
produced only wind.
We have won no victories,
and we have no descendants
to take over the earth.
19Your people will rise to life!
Tell them to leave their graves
and celebrate with shouts.
You refresh the earth
like morning dew;
you give life to the dead.
20Go inside and lock the doors,
my people.
Hide there for a little while,
until the Lord
is no longer angry.
The Earth and the Sea Will Be Punished
21The Lord will come out
to punish everyone on earth
for their sins.
And when he does,
those who did violent crimes
will be known and punished.
translation_text:
Chɔlaa yir
1A hɔl hiŋ, nɛra la n du Juda hɛri daŋ yir yir naa,
yaa dɔɔ bolzeŋkpegre,
Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa bar
yaabuu alugɔ koŋlii.
2Ií pilli a bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa,
tɛɛ hɛri la nɛra wia
n deŋlee di dɔɔ wibii la zuu!
3Hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil nɛr la maa n dɛllii dɔɔ bɔsɔna nɛnnɛ,
dikuu uŋ yardii wia.
4Ií yardi Kɔraawiizi saŋaa saŋa maa.
Waabuu Bikpeg
la n na guu yaa di du de
saŋaa saŋa maa la.
5U gillɔɔ nɛra la n faa ra kpa bahinaa zenni la siwii sɔɔni,
di purgi ba bolkpeg.
U maanii u purgi dau hɛri,
6nyaara ra vol u ni,
nɛra la baŋ faa ra
sunni la ra fɛrguu.
7Ama, nɛra la wia n deŋlee la, ba ŋmɛnɛɛ chɔɔwɔɔ kpantalaŋ.
Kɔraawiizi, Wideŋlaa Hiŋ,
i gillɔɔ ba ŋmɛnɛɛ
du wer chɔɔ.
8N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, yaa ra hiŋ i widaulaa ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ.
Hinuu yaa ra binni.
Yaa kipattɛ lugɔ
i sɔŋ dɔɔ girme.
9Maa dɔɔ ra chɔɔ hamuŋa ni,
dikuu n bampirii n lawii wia,
n nfɛrɛ ge du i ni chɔɔzi ni.
Di i wa di hɛri seriya,
guŋ ɔɔ giluu durnya nɛra
helli wideŋlaa ɛɛi.
10Haali hinna suŋ biinikpola hina ni gba,
ka guŋ waa gillɛ
ba ra ɛɛ winanaa.
Haali di ba du nɛra la wia n deŋlee hɛri gba,
ka ba ɔɔ haa vɛɛu
ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa.
Ba waa hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi
zenni ra tɔgzi.
11N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i lalli i noniire chiŋ í tɛr nɛra digna,
ka ba wɔɔ nawɛɛ.
Gil ba na gunla hiŋ aah siwii i nɛra wia, hiihzi lau baa.
Gil niŋ la hiŋ chemme dau
i dɔma la fuuh baa.
12N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hinuu gillɛ bɔsɔna du yaa be.
Wia la maa yaa n wette ɛɛ la
lii i benii.
13Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, nɛra baŋhina faa di koraa yaa ni.
Ka i bɛŋ sɔnnɛ yaa ra tɔgzi.
14Banla yaa n faa hummɛ di ra tɛɛ la jaa siuzuu.
Ba dunzi ŋmɛnɛ maa
wàá ka bir ba.
I tɔɔri baabuu di chɔgi baa,
nɛr maa jaa suuh ba wia.
15N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i gillɔɔ yaa hɛri yaa,
u nɛra du kpil.
I gillɔɔ i sɔŋ dɔɔ girme,
di yaa yaa hɛri magbɔɔni.
16N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i nɛra biinichɔg saŋa la, ba nyiŋŋi i bɔttɛ.
Hiŋ tɛr ba digna la,
ba ba i benii wa suŋŋii
biinichɔg ni.
17Yaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hilula n lɔ haaŋ,
u ra birgi di ra wii.
Gunnɛ yaa faa du i be,
yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi.
18Hilula lɔ yaabuu, yaa ra gbargi dikuu yaa bɔra n na waazi wia,
ka yaa waa wette
lul kummaa,
di peu bɛŋ lɛi.
Yaa waa wette lɛɛ durnya naa,
yaa waa wette lul nɛra
bá su hɛri naa gba.
19I nɛra la n siuwɛ la daŋ bir wa dɔɔ miibɔɔ,
ba bɔrahɔna daŋ izi
siu biini.
Ii banla baŋ hukke,
ií izi ra yir yira
werge ni bɔsɔna!
Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛɛ lalaa miibɔɔ
lugɔ chɔɔzinŋmɛnii
n ɔɔ sɔɔni hɛri la.
20Awia, n nɛra, ií maa ra la ii diini,
di ga zuu ka tɔɔgi
ii dominuuzi!
Ií suahzi iihinaa tama,
di ra la saŋa la
Kɔraawiizi baaŋ
n niŋ wa sɔɔni la.
21Kɔraawiizi lii u duuribɔttɛ chiŋ di ra ba
ú wa tɛr durnya nɛra digna,
dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia.
Hɛri wàá ka wer suah nɛra la baŋ kpuuzɛɛ ba challi lii la.
Ba daŋ lii baŋgia,
nɛr maa na baa.

english_text:
1 On that day, Leviathan,
the sea monster,
will squirm and try to escape,
but the Lord will kill him
with a cruel, sharp sword.
Protection and Forgiveness
The Lord said:
2At that time you must sing
about a fruitful vineyard.
3I, the Lord, will protect it
and always keep it watered.
I will guard it day and night
to keep it from harm.
4I am no longer angry.
But if it produces thorns,
I will go to war against it
and burn it to the ground.
5Yet if the vineyard depends
on me for protection,
it will become my friend
and be at peace with me.
6Someday Israel will take root
like a vine.
It will blossom and bear fruit
that covers the earth.
7I, the Lord, didn't punish and kill
the people of Israel
as fiercely as I punished
and killed their enemies.
8I carefully measured out
Israel's punishment
and sent the scorching heat
to chase them far away.
9There's only one way
that Israel's sin and guilt
can be completely forgiven:
They must crush the stones
of every pagan altar
and place of worship.
The Lord Will Bring His People Together
10Fortress cities are left
like a desert
where no one lives.
Cattle walk through the ruins,
stripping the trees bare.
11When broken branches
fall to the ground,
women pick them up
to feed the fire.
But these people are so stupid
that the God who created them
will show them no mercy.
12The time is coming when the Lord will shake the land between the Euphrates River and the border of Egypt, and one by one he will bring all of his people together. 13A loud trumpet will be heard. Then the people of Israel who were dragged away to Assyria and Egypt will return to worship the Lord on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina lɛɛi wia
1A hɔl hiŋ,
Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa u tokobi,
u tokobi la
n chummɛ werge la,
di tɛr
muuzeŋ sechɔgii la n gbaŋŋɛ
di ra goomi la digni,
u daŋ kpu muuzeŋ biini sechɔgii la.
2A hɔl hiŋ,
Kɔraawiizi daŋ ŋɔ u grepu daazi koonanii bɛl wia,
3“N danna binni u ni,
di ra duu nii saŋa maa,
di ra du u tau bɔchaaŋ ni hamuŋa maa,
nɛr maa gilɛɛ wàá chɔguu.
4N baaŋ waa
a grepu daazi koo
ni ra fuuh.
Di nɛbɛl duu choŋgolaa ni sɔɔhri u biini,
n daŋ izi ga lɔu laal,
ka fuuh a maa.
5Ama, di ba wa sɛɛwɔ ba n be di ŋɔ ń guu baa,
guŋwaa, bá ba wa di kuu.”
6Saŋa bɛl ra bau, Izrɛl hina n ɛɛ Jekɔb naanna, daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ daa n du lunne,
di lɔɔ di fii nɔŋ,
u nɔna su
durnya naa maa.
7Kɔraawiizi waa Izrɛl hina lɔwɛɛ
alugɔ uŋ lɔ ba dɔma la.
Waa baa kpuwɛɛ
alugɔ uŋ kpu nɛra la
n faa ra kpu baa la.
8U tɛr ba dignaa, di gil ba lauri baa kaali hɛrdumazi.
U kpa fɔŋŋa alugɔ
wiifurii pekpeg
n chummɛnɛ
di kpa baa kaali.
9Gunla ban niŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa labuu keŋ,
bá purgi ba vuga
mbusu lizibɔra la maa,
di namaa a birgi sau,
di chɔg ba vughaaŋ Asɛra daazi
ni daahɛgsɔɔhsuma
fuuhribɔra la maa.
10Bolzeŋkpeg la daŋ birgi diŋgela,
de ɛɛ lugɔ hɛribɔduma,
nauna ra di de,
di chɔɔ de ra heezi,
di di u daazi ge paŋhoori
a maa tuŋ nyaamm.
11A nɛra ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ daazi kela n hillɛ, ba kuugaa ha,
haana paagaa
birgi nindaazi.
Dikuu Izrɛl hina n waa wia zɛɛ zummɛ wia,
ba Taari Kɔraawiizi
wàá na ba sinyɛna,
gɛɛ di suŋ ba ni.
12A hɔl hiŋ, di lii Muu Yufretis guŋŋ di ga hel Ijip hɛri magbɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ bargi u nɛra, di chaali baa kpaŋkpaŋa lii hɛssi alugɔ banna hɛl mia a ra lii a zɔga ni la. 13A hɔl hiŋ, ba daŋ nuu baŋ huuh bensunoniina bɛl. Banla n faa ra siuzi Asiiria ni banla n du Ijip la daŋ bir ba Jɛrusalɛm, di waa jaami Kɔraawiizi, u bizennaniinanii la nyuu.

english_text:
Samaria Will Be Punished
1The city of Samaria
above a fertile valley
is in for trouble!
Its leaders are drunkards,
who stuff themselves
with food and wine.
But they will be like flowers
that dry up and wilt.
2Only the Lord is strong
and powerful!
His mighty hand
will strike them down
with the force of a hailstorm
or a mighty whirlwind
or an overwhelming flood.
3Every drunkard in Ephraim
takes pride in Samaria,
but it will be crushed.
4Samaria above a fertile valley
will quickly lose its glory.
It will be gobbled up
like the first ripe fig
at harvest season.
5When this time comes,
the Lord All-Powerful
will be a glorious crown
for his people who survive.
6He will see that justice rules
and that his people are able
to defend their cities.
Corrupt Leaders Will Be Punished
7Priests and prophets stumble
because they are drunk.
Their minds are too confused
to receive God's messages
or give honest decisions.
8Their tables are covered,
completely covered,
with their stinking vomit.
9You drunken leaders
are like babies!
How can you possibly understand
or teach the Lord's message?
10You don't even listen—
all you hear is senseless sound
after senseless sound.
11 So, the Lord will speak
to his people
in strange sounds
and foreign languages.
12He promised you
perfect peace and rest,
but you refused to listen.
13Now his message to you
will be senseless sound
after senseless sound.
Then you will fall backwards,
injured and trapped.
False Security Is Fatal
14You rulers of Jerusalem
do nothing but sneer;
now you must listen
to what the Lord says.
15 Do you think you have
an agreement with death
and the world of the dead?
Why do you trust in your lies
to keep you safe from danger
and the mighty flood?
16 And so the Lord says,
“I'm laying a firm foundation
for the city of Zion.
It's a valuable cornerstone
proven to be trustworthy;
no one who trusts it
will ever be disappointed.
17Justice and fairness
will be the measuring lines
that help me build.”
Hailstones and floods
will destroy and wash away
your shelter of lies.
18Your agreement with death
and the world of the dead
will be broken.
Then angry, roaring waves
will sweep over you.
19Morning, noon, and night
an overwhelming flood
will wash you away.
The terrible things that happen
will teach you this lesson:
20Your bed is too short,
your blanket too skimpy.
21 The Lord will fiercely attack
as he did at Mount Perazim
and in Gibeon Valley.
But this time the Lord
will do something surprising,
not what you expect.
22So you had better stop sneering
or you will be in worse shape
than ever before.
I heard the Lord All-Powerful
threaten the whole country
with destruction.
All Wisdom Comes from the Lord
23Pay close attention
to what I am saying.
24Farmers don't just plow
and break up the ground.
25When a field is ready,
they scatter the seeds
of dill and cumin;
they plant the seeds
of wheat and barley
in the proper places
and sow other grains
around the edges.
26They learn this from their God.
27After dill and cumin
have been harvested,
the stalks are pounded,
not run over with a wagon.
28Wheat and barley are pounded,
but not beaten to pulp;
they are run over with a wagon,
but not ground to dust.
29This wonderful knowledge comes
from the Lord All-Powerful,
who has such great wisdom.
translation_text:
Wiarɛ huuzi Ɛfram hina
1Tɔɔrɔɔ daŋ huuzi Izrɛl hina bolzeŋ la
n chigɛ walsum baŋgia la.
U nɛra maanii ɛɛ sinnyɔɔra di ra jigsi u wia,
ka u fɔŋŋa ni u girme ra tuŋ
alugɔ fiiri n na siu la.
2Ií ra nuu! Kɔraawiizi lizi nɛbɛllɛ, di ɛɛu sirya,
u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge maa,
ú wa lɔ baa.
U daŋ ba lugɔ dobee ni dozeŋ n gillɛ
nii taali bɔr maa,
di ra chɔ gbuŋgbuŋgbuŋ,
di chɔg a hɛri.
3Izrɛl hina bolzeŋ la u nɛra n ɛɛ sinnyɔɔra di ra jigsi u wia la,
u daŋ chol,
nɛra kpa naazi
di ra fɛrguu.
4Ba sitɔɔra girme daŋ tuŋ
lugɔ fig nɔŋlugla
n haŋ waa aah,
di ba tɔrgaa di la.
5A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ
koorikahuro la
n dɔɔ girme,
u nɛra la n kawɛɛ la be.
6U daŋ gil ba sitɔɔra
nɔŋŋi wibii wia,
di kpa fɔŋŋa tɛɛ ba laallɔɔra la n ɔɔ chi
a bol dominuuzenaa
di ra yoo ba dɔma,
bá gilɛɛ wa wer
di ra zuu a bol la.
7Haali Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi ni u kizeehina maa ɔɔ nyɔɔ sinnɛ di ra dɛɛzi,
di ra jiŋli.
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi ɔɔ dɛɛzuu werge, ba waa ɔɔ kaa wer ra zum
wia la Kɔraawiizi
n ɔɔ pilli lugɔ deeza biini,
ra tɛɛ baa la zɛɛ.
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ge ɔɔ dɛɛzuu werge,
ba waa wette di wibii
di ra tɛɛ nɛra.
8Ba ɔɔ hɛɛhzuu di ra chɔgi ba diiribɔra maa,
de maa ɔɔ doŋ.
9Kenne nɛra ɔɔ ra ŋɔ mìŋ́ Aizaaya wia,
“Anɛɛ u ra bagli wiai?
Anɛɛ u ra bagli
u amaniye zɛɛi?
Bichalli la baŋ teŋ illɛ
u ra bagli wiaa?
10U ɔɔ haŋ mari wikpaŋ ninɛɛ
di ra dammi,
ií ra ɛɛ keŋ, ií ra ɛɛ keŋ!
Tama ɛŋ, tama ende!”
11Guŋ wia, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa nɛra n na mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi
ŋɔ wia tɛɛ u nɛra.
12U faa ŋɔ ba benii,
“Heezaa bɔttɛ keŋ
tɛɛ banla n kuuhwɛ.
Ií ba wa heezi!”
Ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá nuu.
13Awia, Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la un niŋ ŋɔ tɛɛ baa maanii lugɔ,
Ií ra ɛɛ keŋ, ií ra ɛɛ keŋ!
Tama ɛŋ, tama ende!
Gunnɛ bá jaa bir la har ga chogli,
ba dɔma he baa sidɛɛzi
di lauri baa kaali.
14Awia, ii banla n dɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm di ra gbɛlli nɛra la,
ií ra nuu gunla
Kɔraawiizi n na ŋɔ.
15Ií ra ta barabaraa di ra ŋɔ lugɔ ii ni siu
ni lalaa bol
ɛɛ nuukpannɛ.
Di hɛhchɔg maa wa chol a nɛra ni,
ka wàá wer
ɛɛ iawaa wiimaa.
Ií dɛlli kara ni nɛdaraa ninɛɛ
alugɔ aabuu
niŋ wer lɛɛ ia.
16Guŋ wia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ,
“Ií ra nuu ɛŋ! N kpa binanii bɛllɛ dau Ziɔn.
N lizuubuu u ɛɛ binanii,
u kpekkoo nɛnnɛ,
ií wer ma hɔŋ u ni.
‘Nɛr la maa n niŋ yarduu,
wiimaa wàá ka tiruu.’
17N daŋ kpa wibii ni wideŋlaa birgi n ŋmɛŋ la
miŋ kpawɛɛ ra mɛgzi kuna,
di mɛgzi koŋlaa la
iin niŋ ma
hɔŋ a bii ni la.”
Iiŋ kpa kara ni nɛdaraa di maa la wia,
dobia daŋ wa huraa ta,
nii ge taali ii suahribɔra.
18Nuukpaŋ la ii ni siu n dɔɔwɛ la daŋ bir pɛɛ,
ii ni lalaa bol
nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la
wàá ka du de.
Di hɛhchɔg haŋ wa chol,
u daŋ wa hurgi ia ha.
19A tɔɔrɔɔ naa daŋ ɔɔ ra ba digiidigii,
chɔɔzii chɔɔzi maa,
hɔpizaa ge ni hamuŋa guŋŋ
di ra ba saŋa la
un niŋ wa gbaari
ii maa kaali la.
Di ii wa nuu a amaniye
di zum u zɛɛ,
ɔnsii werge daŋ lau ia.
20A wia naa n na ba naa daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ kunchɔɔrikuŋ n kpusse, hàá wer chɔɔ u ni tɛrgi i naazi,
di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ
kita ge n waa
war lugɔ ú wer tɔi.
21Kɔraawiizi daŋ izi fɔŋŋa ni gunla uŋ faa izee Bizeŋ Pɛrazim nyuu la,
di yoo u dɔma ni baaŋ,
gunla uŋ faa
ɛɛwɛ Gibiɔn Waluu la.
U wiɛɛlaa daŋ kur,
di ɛɛ nuukpuuri
wia werge maa.
22Awia, ii gilɛɛ ra ɛɛ n wiŋɔzi naa chɛɛtɛ,
ii tɔɔrɔɔ gilɛɛ wa
du kaŋ jaa.
N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ n benii
lugɔ u ɛɛ siryaa
ú chɔgi hɛri naa maa.
23Ií ra nuu n be!
Ií keŋŋi digna
di ra nuu
gunla min niŋ ŋɔ.
24Patti ɔɔ hanna paruu di ra laa?
U ɔɔ hanna vuugi a hɛrii
di ra la ka waa
kuna ra duuwaa?
25Di u haŋ wa kossi u koo tuŋ,
u ɔɔ wa mizi u kundee la
n dɛg mizaarɛ,
di duu huuti ni baali,
bɛl maa ni u bɔr.
26A patti ɔɔ zum gunla maa un niŋ ɛɛu,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi
n tɛu nunzuma wia.
27Waa ɔɔ kpa kapɛrɛ di ra lɔ a dɔzi tiuzaa kuna a bee ra lii,
ka daa la n kukkɛɛrɛ
u ɔɔ kpa ra lɔa,
a bee gilɛɛ chɔgi.
28Huutii ba ɔɔ nam kuari paanuu,
awia, ba waa ɔɔ lɔa
di hanna la.
Haali u torko n ɔɔ vol a ni,
ka u zagra waa ɔɔ namaa.
29Annii maa ge lii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la benii.
U bɛnnɛ zum nɛra liize biraa.
U nunzuma ge
kaa du kaŋ werge maa.

english_text:
Jerusalem Will Suffer
The Lord said:
1Jerusalem, city of David,
the place of my altar,
you are in for trouble!
Celebrate your festivals
year after year.
2I will still make you suffer,
and your people will cry
when I make an altar of you.
3I will surround you and prepare
to attack from all sides.
4From deep in the earth,
you will call out for help
with only a faint whisper.
5Then your cruel enemies
will suddenly be swept away
like dust in a windstorm.
6I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will come to your rescue
with a thundering earthquake
and a fiery whirlwind.
7Every brutal nation
that attacks Jerusalem
and makes it suffer
will disappear like a dream
when night is over.
8Those nations that attack
Mount Zion
will suffer from hunger
and thirst.
They will dream of food and drink
but wake up weary and hungry
and thirsty as ever.
Prophets Who Fool Themselves
9Be shocked and stunned,
you prophets!
Refuse to see.
Get drunk and stagger,
but not from wine.
10 The Lord has made you drowsy;
he put you into a deep sleep
and covered your head.
11Now his message is like a sealed letter to you. Some of you say, “We can't read it, because it's sealed.” 12Others say, “We can't read it, because we don't know how to read.”
13 The Lord has said:
“These people praise me
with their words,
but they never really
think about me.
They worship me by repeating
rules made up by humans.
14 So once again I will do things
that shock and amaze them,
and I will destroy the wisdom
of those who claim to know
and understand.”
15You are in for trouble,
if you try to hide your plans
from the Lord!
Or if you think what you do
in the dark can't be seen.
16 You have it all backwards.
A clay dish doesn't say
to the potter,
“You didn't make me.
You don't even know how.”
Hope for the Future
17Soon the forest of Lebanon
will become a field with crops,
thick as a forest.
18The deaf will be able to hear
whatever is read to them;
the blind will be freed
from a life of darkness.
19The poor and the needy
will celebrate and shout
because of the Lord,
the holy God of Israel.
20All who are cruel and arrogant
will be gone forever.
Those who live by crime
will disappear,
21together with everyone
who tells lies in court
and keeps innocent people
from getting a fair trial.
22The Lord who rescued Abraham
has this to say
about Jacob's descendants:
“They will no longer
be ashamed and disgraced.
23When they see how great
I have made their nation,
they will praise and honor me,
the holy God of Israel.
24Everyone who is confused
will understand,
and all who have complained
will obey my teaching.”
translation_text:
Wiarɛ huuzi Koori Deevid bolzeŋ
1Ee, Jɛrusalɛm, Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la,
bolzeŋ la Koori Deevid
n faa soge la,
wia daŋ huuzii!
Binaa bina maanii nɛra ɔɔ ra lizi mbusukpila i biini,
di ra di ba hɔpizizenaa.
2Ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil hɛhchɔg chol bolzeŋ la banna yir Kɔraawiizi Mbusu Lizibɔr la ni.
Wiraa ni chɛɛhgaa
daŋ du de,
a bolzeŋ maa ɛɛ lugɔ
chal n tɔ mbusu lizibɔr ni.
3Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u dɔma
wa fɔɔu di lɔu.
4A saŋa, u wiŋɔzi daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ koguu n na fir u ŋɔ wia lii hɛrii,
hɛɛhraa biinii a ra lii
lugɔ munnaa.
5Ka i dɔma la n kpillɛ werge la daŋ wa kaali alugɔ nyɔɔ,
nɛkpila la n faa waa
i ni ra suŋ la daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ zɔga
pekpeg n paawɛ kaali.
6Kakpaŋ, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
daŋ huuzi baa
ni nazaa, hɛri ziglaa, kɔɔi werge,
pechuma ani niŋ
n niŋ fuuh baa.
7Denii hɛrkpila laallɔɔra la n na lɔ Jɛrusalɛm laal,
di fɔɔ u diikpeg la
daŋ leu alugɔ deeza
alugɔ kuŋ baŋ nawɛɛ
lugɔ deeza biini hamuŋa ni.
8A daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ lɔzi n na kpu nɛr,
u chɔɔ deezi unna di diwee,
ka wa izi
lɔzi haa ra kpuu la.
Di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ niinyɔgzi n lau nɛr,
u chɔɔ deezi unna nyɔɔ nii,
ka wa izi zɛɛɛ,
a niinyɔgzi haa lawuu la.
Gunnɛ niŋ ɛɛ hɛrkpila nɛra la maa
n na lɔ Jɛrusalɛm laal la.
9Wia naa gil ii nuuzi kpu,
ií birgi nyuŋŋa.
Ií ra dɛɛzi, ka a wàá lii siŋ be,
di kaa ra jiŋli,
ka a wàá lii siŋ be.
10Kɔraawiizi kpa dɔzeŋ bɛllɛ du ii ni,
ii nfɛssi du tɔg werge.
U tɔɔgi u dɔgtɛɛzi siwee
ni ba nyuunii,
ba waa wia ra na
deeza biini.
11Wia naa n lugɔ deeza biini maa iin niŋ vii nuu a zɛɛ naa, jaa ɛɛu lugɔ wiŋɔzi baŋ sɛbɛɛ du hɔŋ baŋ piŋŋee di mari u nua biini. Di i kpau tɛɛ nɛr la n zum karmaa ŋɔ ú karmi, u daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ ba mari u nuarɛ, wàá wer karmuu. 12Di i kaa kpau tɛɛ nɛr la ge n waa zum karmaa ŋɔ ú karmi, u daŋ ŋɔ waa karmaa zummɛ.
13Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Nɛra naa, ba nuuzii ba kpa ra tɔgziŋ,
ka ba bampiree
wan lauwɛ tama maa.
Baŋ ɔɔ ra jaamiŋ la
ɛɛ newea baglaarɛ
baŋ bagli baa ba helli
di ra ŋɔa labuu.
14Dikuu guŋ wia, n daŋ bir ra ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia a nɛra naa be
a tir baa werge maa.
N daŋ gil ba nunzunna nunzuma bir pɛɛ,
bá sichaana ge tuŋ.”
15Wia daŋ huuzi banla n aah siwii
di kpa ba jinazi
di ra suahzi
Kɔraawiizi ni la,
di ra hum ba huma bɔbiri la, ka ra fɛ ba biine,
“Anɛɛ ra na yaai?
Anɛɛ n niŋ zumɛi?”
16Ií bir wiarɛ chig.
Viimaari ni chuuri ɛɛ kpannɛaa?
Vii daŋ wer ŋɔ u maari be
lugɔ waa lɛi mauwaa?
Vii daŋ wer ŋɔ u maari wia
lugɔ waa wiimaa zummɛaa?
17A wàá birgi, ka Lɛbanɔn kɔr birgi koo,
a koo ge ɛɛ lugɔ kɔr.
18A hɔl hiŋ, dignitaŋa hina danna nuu banna karmi lii hɔŋ biini,
nyuŋŋa la ge n ɔɔ ra vol
bɔbiri ge siwee daŋ pilli
bá wer di ra na.
19Banla n waa bahinaa ra tɔgzi la daŋ jaa dɔɔ bɔsɔna Kɔraawiizi be.
Nyaara bɔra daŋ sɔɔni
werge maa dikuu
Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la wia.
20Sikpegii hina wia daŋ tuŋ,
banla ge maa
n na ɛɛ nɛra chɛɛtɛ
wàá ka du de,
banla ge maa
n dɔɔ nfɛrchɔgaa
di ra nyiŋŋi
wichɔgaa ɛɛi la
21ni banla n ɔɔ wer kanni kara chug nɛra,
baabuu ɔɔ gil
sitɔɔra di nɛra la hora
n summɛ seriya ba chol la.
22Guŋ wiarɛ Abraham Lɛɛri Kɔraawiizi bagli Izrɛl hina wia, di ŋɔ,
“Hiihzi wàá ka kpu baa,
ɔnsii wàá ka lau baa.
23Di ba wa na n wiɛɛlaa
gunla miŋ gillɛ
ba biizi du kpil la,
ba danna tɔgzi
n sɔŋ nɛnnɛ.
Ba danna tɔgzi mìŋ́ Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la werge maa,
ba danna ɔm
mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la
banna hum la.
24Banla n faa leuwe daŋ jaa zum wia zɛɛ nɛnnɛ,
banla ge n faa
ɔɔ ra nuumi werge la,
daŋ jaa sɛɛ
di ra nuu baglaa.”

english_text:
Don't Expect Help from Egypt
1This is the Lord's message for his rebellious people:
“You follow your own plans
instead of mine;
you make treaties
without asking me,
and you keep on sinning.
2You trust Egypt for protection.
So you refuse my advice
and send messengers to Egypt
to beg their king for help.
3“You will be disappointed,
completely disgraced
for trusting Egypt.
4The king's power reaches
from the city of Zoan
as far south as Hanes.
5But Egypt can't protect you,
and to trust that nation
is useless and foolish.”
6This is a message
about the animals
of the Southern Desert:
“You people carry treasures
on donkeys and camels.
You travel to a feeble nation
through a troublesome desert
filled with lions
and flying fiery dragons.
7Egypt can't help you!
That's why I call that nation
a helpless monster.”
Israel Refuses To Listen
8The Lord told me to write down his message for his people, so that it would be there forever. 9They have turned against the Lord and can't be trusted. They have refused his teaching 10and have said to his messengers and prophets:
Don't tell us what God has shown you and don't preach the truth. Just say what we want to hear, even if it's false. 11Stop telling us what God has said! We don't want to hear any more about the holy One of Israel.
12Now this is the answer
of the holy One of Israel:
“You rejected my message,
and you trust in violence
and lies.
13This sin is like a crack
that makes a high wall
quickly crumble 14and shatter
like a crushed bowl.
There's not a piece left
big enough to carry hot coals
or to dip out water.”
Trust the Lord
15The holy Lord God of Israel
had told all of you,
“I will keep you safe
if you turn back to me
and calm down.
I will make you strong
if you quietly trust me.”
Then you stubbornly 16said,
“No! We will safely escape
on speedy horses.”
But those who chase you
will be even faster.
17As few as five of them,
or even one, will be enough
to chase a thousand of you.
Finally, all that will be left
will be a few survivors
as lonely as a flag pole
on a barren hill.
The Lord Will Show Mercy
18The Lord God is waiting
to show how kind he is
and to have pity on you.
The Lord always does right;
he blesses those who trust him.
19People of Jerusalem, you don't need to cry anymore. The Lord is kind, and as soon as he hears your cries for help, he will come. 20The Lord has given you trouble and sorrow as your food and drink. But now you will again see the Lord, your teacher, and he will guide you. 21Whether you turn to the right or to the left, you will hear a voice saying, “This is the road! Now follow it.” 22Then you will treat your idols of silver and gold like garbage; you will throw them away like filthy rags.
23The Lord will send rain to water the seeds you have planted—your fields will produce more crops than you need, and your cattle will graze in open pastures. 24Even the oxen and donkeys that plow your fields will be fed the finest grain.
25On that day people will be slaughtered and towers destroyed, but streams of water will flow from high hills and towering mountains. 26Then the Lord will bandage his people's injuries and heal the wounds he has caused. The moon will shine as bright as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter than usual. It will be like the light of seven days all at once.
Assyria Will Be Punished
27The Lord is coming
from far away
with his fiery anger
and thick clouds of smoke.
His angry words flame up
like a destructive fire;
28he breathes out a flood
that comes up to the neck.
He sifts the nations
and destroys them.
Then he puts a bridle
in every foreigner's mouth
and leads them to doom.
29The Lord's people will sing as they do when they celebrate a religious festival at night. The Lord is Israel's mighty rock, and his people will be as happy as they are when they follow the sound of flutes to the mountain where he is worshiped.
30The Lord will get furious. His fearsome voice will be heard, his arm will be seen ready to strike, and his anger will be like a destructive fire, followed by thunderstorms and hailstones. 31When the Assyrians hear the Lord's voice and see him striking with his iron rod, they will be terrified. 32He will attack them in battle, and each time he strikes them, it will be to the music of tambourines and harps.
33Long ago the Lord got a place ready for burning the body of the dead king. The place for the fire is deep and wide, the wood is piled high, and the Lord will start the fire by breathing out flaming sulfur.
translation_text:
Nuukpaŋ la n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Wia daŋ huuzi n biizi la
n du Juda hɛri,
di ɛɛ dignikpega hina
werge la.
Banla n ɔɔ vɔɔ jinazi la
n waa n be liwɛɛrɛ,
ba ni nɛra ɛɛ nuukpaŋ n Duma n waa baa baglɛɛ ŋɔ bá ɛɛ.
Gunnɛ ba ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa
di ra sag dɔŋa ni.
2Ba wan pɛɛzɛɛ wiimaa,
ka ra la Ijip koori be,
di ra nyiŋŋi u lɛɛ baa lii ba tɔɔrɔɔ biini,
di gil u bɔsɔŋ tɔ ba ni.
3Too, baŋ yardi Ijip koori ú guu baa naa,
ba daŋ di hiihzi,
wàá wer guu baa.
4Haali baŋ hum nabɔnzenaa
ba la bolzenaa Zoan
ni Hanɛs gba,
5ka ba maa daŋ wa di hiihzi
dikuu Ijip hina n wàá wer
hiini baa tama maa wia.
Ba wàá dɔɔ tɔna maa tɛɛ baa,
hiihzii ba di.”
6Amaniye la miŋ nuuwɛ lii Kɔraawiizi be, u ra bagli wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma sela wiarɛ keŋ,
“Nabɔnzenaa la baŋ hummɛ Ijip hɛri la
ra voluu di ra la, a ra nuu baa.
Hɛribɔduma labuu ba ga,
bɔr la bunyinzi,
hɛrikunchɔgaa ani
nyugzenzenaa n duwɛɛ.
Ba kauzi ni nyugmazi chi daama kuna werge maa,
bá ga tɛɛ
Ijip hɛri koorizeŋ
ú hiini baa.
Ka pɛɛrɛ, ba wàá na
hiinaa maa u be.
7Ijip hɛri la waa hiinaa maa dɔɔwɛ.
Awia, n na yiruubuu
‘Nyugzenzeŋ la n waa
fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ.’ ”
8Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,
“La ga sɛbi Ijip hɛri wia
naa dau bipɛntɛŋ ni,
di sɛbaa dau hɔŋ ge ni,
á ɛɛ daansɛɛ tɛɛ nɛra la n niŋ haa wa du de,
di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
9N biizi naa ɛɛ dignikpega ni karkannaa.
Biizi la n waa nyiŋŋi
bá nuu
mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baglaa.
10Ba ŋɔ n dɔgtɛɛzi be,
‘Ií gilɛɛ kaa ra na wia
lugɔ deeza biini,
di gilɛɛ kaa bagli wibii ŋmɛnizi
di ra tɛɛ yaa.
Ií ra ŋɔ wia la n na par yaa,
di gilɛɛ di wibii ra tɛɛ yaa.
11Ií gilɛɛ teŋ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ,
di gilɛɛ kaa kpa Izrɛl
Dɔɔrinaniinanii wia
huuzi yaa.’ ”
12Awia, kenne Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la ŋɔ,
“Dikuu iiŋ vɛɛ gunla miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa,
ka kpa ii tamii maa du
nɛsunnaa ni kara ni la wia,
13ii wichɔgii naa daŋ birgi tɔɔrɔɔ tɛɛ ia,
alugɔ koŋlii n la chiŋ,
di peri chi,
di ra nyiŋŋi u chol,
di wa chol kakpaŋ, birim!
14Di u wa chollo, u daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ vii baŋ vigzee,
u ga chol di ŋmuuri la,
u keŋlii gba wàá ka wer buu niŋ
gɛɛ di kaa wer ɛɛ nii gba.”
15Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la, di ɛɛ Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Ií bir ba n be wa heezi.
Anniibuu niŋ gil ii na lɛɛi.
Ií gil ii bampiree sɔɔni
di yardiŋ.
Anniibuu niŋ gil
ii dɔɔ fɔŋŋa.
16Ka ii vɛɛ, di ŋɔ,
‘Akai, yaa daŋ tinni zagra chɔ kaali!’
Wibiire lugɔ ii daŋ chɔ.
Ií ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Yaa daŋ tinni zagra n gbaŋŋɛ di chɔ kaali.’
Awia, banla
n ninna duŋŋi ia la
daŋ du gbaŋ kaali ia.
17Ba laallɔɔra kpaŋkpaŋ daŋ gil ii nɛra kagboŋ chɔ,
banue ge gil ii maa chɔ,
ka ii jaa chɔ ka ka tuuta daajaŋ
a bizeŋ nyuu.”
18Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi haa ra kpaŋ iabuu,
ú ɛɛ winanaa tɛɛ ia,
di ɛɛ sirya
ú na ii sinyɛna.
U ɛɛ wibii hinnɛ saŋa maa.
Banla maa
n na kpaŋuu lugɔ
ú wa hiini baa,
nuu sumaa.
19Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina, ii banla n soge Jɛrusalɛm, ii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka wii. Wibii maa, di ii wiiwo yir Kɔraawiizi, u daŋ hiini ia. Di u haŋ wa nuu ii wiisuŋŋaa, u daŋ ɔɔ sɛɛ kakpaŋ. 20Haali Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ tɔɔrɔɔ birgi ii diwee, biinichɔg ge birgi ii niinyɔɔlii la gba, ka u himmaa daŋ bagli ia, ii wàá ka nyiŋŋi u bɔr. 21Di ii wa leu ŋmɛnɛɛ, ii daŋ nuu loobii bɛl ii harbɔɔ n na ŋɔ, “A ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ keŋ. Ií hiŋuu di ra la!” 22Denii ii chɔgi ii vuga baŋ kuarɛɛ, di kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa tɔa la, di kpaa ha lugɔ haaŋ doŋa wɛjɛ, ka ŋɔ, “Ií kaali de!”
23Denii Kɔraawiizi jaa gil dooŋ ba, saŋa la iin niŋ waa duu kuna, di gil a lii du binanaa, di lɛɛ nɛnnɛ di wazi, ii sela gba na kooriinanaa di ra di a kipar. 24Nabala ni kauzi n na par ii kooni la daŋ na diunanaa baŋ kuarɛɛ nɛnnɛ, di ra di. 25Saŋa la ban niŋ wa kpu ii dɔma werge, ba diikpega la n jaŋŋɛ la chiŋ, chogli la, niiri danna bul bizenaa ni giŋgimee maa nyuuni. 26Baagu daŋ bir chaani alugɔ wiizi, wiizi ge chaanaa la bir ɛɛ u guŋ dɔŋ buniidaanɛɛ. A saŋaa Kɔraawiizi jaa vɔɔzi u nɛra bɔra uŋ gillɛ a kuugi la, di chaa baa.
27Ií na! Kɔraawiizi Sɔŋ lii bɔɔnɛɛrɛ di ra ba.
U baaŋ ra fuuh werge maa,
nyɔɔzi ra lii
di tɔ bɔr maa kulululu.
Baaŋfuuih wiŋɔzii u ra ŋɔ,
u nuuzuŋŋi ɛɛ lugɔ ninlau.
28U heeza dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa lugɔ gɔnzeŋ n suwee,
di hel baŋaa.
U zigli a durnya hɛssi maanii, ú chɔgaa,
di kpa kabargazi du
a hɛssi nɛra nuuzi,
di tɛrgi baa ra la
bá ga leu.
29Denii ii jaa yir yira
lugɔ baŋ ɔɔ ra yir yira
hamuŋa ni,
di ra di hɔpizizenaa la.
Ií bɔra daŋ sɔɔni
lugɔ saŋa la tiitorii huuhra
n du nɛra di ra la Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ la nyuu,
Izrɛl hina Bizeŋ la.
30Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil nɛra nuu
u zenni loobii,
di gil ba na gunla uŋ lalli
u banonii baaŋ ni,
di kpa ninlau n na di kuna werge,
baama n na pogzi,
nazaa ani dobizenaa
di tuu ra ba.
31Kɔraawiizi daŋ ŋɔ wikpaŋ
di gil Asiiria hina
maa ŋmuuri.
U daŋ kpa u kooridaŋkpala
di lɔ baa.
32Too, saŋa maa, di u wa lalli
u daŋkpala yag baa,
di tɛr ba digna la,
u nɛra danna yir yirsuma, di ra lɔ kemzi, di ra yigzi lɔŋgɔma.
Gunnɛ ú ɛɛ di lɔ
Asiiria hina laal,
ni u banonii.
33U teŋ kuari bɔttɛ birgi,
ú fuuh Asiiria koorizeŋ.
Ba kiubuu, u du luŋ di kaa du war jaa,
bá du daazi de werge,
Kɔraawiizi heeza n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ
jilbi ni ninlau gil
a ra lau zagzagzag.

english_text:
Don't Trust the Power of Egypt
1You are in for trouble
if you go to Egypt for help,
or if you depend on
an army of chariots
or a powerful cavalry.
Instead you should depend on
and trust the holy Lord God
of Israel.
2The Lord isn't stupid!
He does what he promises,
and he can bring doom.
If you are cruel yourself,
or help those who are evil,
you will be destroyed.
3The Egyptians are mere humans.
They aren't God.
Their horses are made of flesh;
they can't live forever.
When the Lord shows his power,
he will destroy the Egyptians
and all who depend on them.
Together they will fall.
4The Lord All-Powerful
said to me,
“I will roar and attack
like a fearless lion
not frightened by the shouts
of shepherds trying to protect
their sheep.
That's how I will come down
and fight on Mount Zion.
5I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will protect Jerusalem
like a mother bird circling
over her nest.”
Come Back to the Lord
6People of Israel, come back!
You have completely turned
from the Lord.
7The time is coming
when you will throw away
your idols of silver and gold,
made by your sinful hands.
8The Assyrians will be killed,
but not by the swords
of humans.
Their young men will try
to escape,
but they will be captured
and forced into slavery.
9Their fortress will fall
when terror strikes;
their army officers
will be frightened
and run from the battle.
This is what the Lord has said,
the Lord whose fiery furnace
is built on Mount Zion.
translation_text:
Wiarɛ huuzi banla n dɛlli Ijip hina ni
1Wia daŋ huuzi banla n ɔɔ ra la Ijip hɛri, di gaa nyiŋŋi hiinaa,
banla n dɛlli zagra,
banla n yardi laal torkokpila
ni ba zagtinna la
n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la.
Ba waa hiinaa ra nyiŋŋi Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii be,
gɛɛ di suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi
ú hiini baa.
2Waabuu dɔɔ nunzuma, u daŋ wer gil hɛhchɔg chol,
gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ,
gunnɛ ú ɛɛ.
U daŋ hau biinikpola hina ni,
di hau banla
n na hiini wichɔgɛɛra ni.
3Newea lɛi Ijip hinaa? Ba waa Kɔraawiizi ɛɛwɛ.
Ba zagra ɛɛ ola bɛnnɛ,
a waa dunzi ɛɛwɛ.
Di Kɔraawiizi haŋ wa tɛr u nonii,
unla n na hiini nɛra,
daŋ jiŋli,
unla ge baŋ hiinee,
daŋ chol,
ba maa kpau siu.
4Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Aizaaya be,
“Di bunyiŋ gɛɛ u biipɔl lau peezi,
u baga waa hoo
penɔɔna pogzaa be,
haali di ba kpillɔ gunla maa di ra kɔɔ werge gba,
ka u ɔɔ chɔɔu
di ra di u kuŋ.
Guŋ himmaanii niŋ wa ɛɛ saŋa la Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
n niŋ ba wa naa kalu,
Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu.
5Gunla zumbee n ɔɔ zaah ra bar u daŋ, di ra du u biizi tau la,
gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa
Maa Hiŋ la wa zaah ra bar
Jɛrusalɛm, di ra du u tau,
di lɛɛu u dɔma be.”
6Hoi, Izrɛl hina, haali iiŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la gba, ka ii bir ba u be. 7A saŋa, ii maa daŋ vɛɛ saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa vuga la iiŋ kpa nonee kuari, guŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa la.
8Asiiria hina daŋ tuŋ laal biini, ka a wàá lugɔ neweare niŋ kpu baa.
Akai! Kɔraawiizi tokobii
niŋ kpu baa,
ba daŋ chɔ lii laal biini,
bá lauri ba biipɔllaa,
di gil ba gaa
hum humkpega.
9Ɔnsii werge daŋ lau ba koorizeŋ, ú chɔ,
ɔnsii kaa lau
ba laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ge,
bá gil tuutazi ka chɔ.
Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ,
waabuu ba ra jaami
Jɛrusalɛm la,
u niŋ ra lau de,
mbusuzi lizaa wia.

english_text:
Justice Will Rule
1A king and his leaders
will rule with justice.
2They will be a place of safety
from stormy winds,
a stream in the desert,
and a rock that gives shade
from the heat of the sun.
3Then everyone who has eyes
will open them and see,
and those who have ears
will pay attention.
4All who are impatient
will take time to think;
everyone who stutters
will talk clearly.
5Fools will no longer
be highly respected,
and crooks won't be given
positions of honor.
6Fools talk foolishness.
They always make plans
to do sinful things,
to lie about the Lord,
to let the hungry starve,
and to keep water from those
who are thirsty.
7Cruel people tell lies—
they do evil things,
and make cruel plans
to destroy the poor and needy,
even when they beg
for justice.
8But helpful people
can always be trusted
to make helpful plans.
Punishment for the Women of Jerusalem
9Listen to what I say,
you women who are carefree
and careless!
10You may not have worries now,
but in about a year,
the grape harvest will fail,
and you will tremble.
11Shake and shudder,
you women without a care!
Strip off your clothes—
put on sackcloth.
12Slap your breasts in sorrow
because of what happened
to the fruitful fields
and vineyards,
13and to the happy homes
in Jerusalem.
The land of my people
is covered with thorns.
14The palace will be deserted,
the crowded city empty.
Fortresses and towers
will forever become
playgrounds for wild donkeys
and pastures for sheep.
God's Spirit Makes the Difference
15When the Spirit is given to us
from heaven,
deserts will become orchards
thick as fertile forests.
16Honesty and justice
will prosper there,
17and justice will produce
lasting peace and security.
18You, the Lord's people,
will live in peace,
calm and secure,
19even if hailstones flatten
forests and cities.
20You will have God's blessing,
as you plant your crops
beside streams,
while your donkeys and cattle
roam freely about.
translation_text:
Wideŋlaa kora wia
1Ií ra nuu! Koori bɛl daŋ wa di kora u wia deŋli,
u nabɔnzi la
n niŋ jaa u ni ge
gba wia dɔɔ wibii.
2Bɛl maa daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ lɔɔ di tɛɛ Izrɛl hina,
di pechɔgii maa haŋ wa ta ba ni
ba chɔ ga zuu.
Ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ gɔŋa n na pal hɛribɔduma la dooŋ n waa ba,
gɛɛ bizenzeŋ n na tɔ baa
bɔsɔŋ hɛrhilii biini.
3Denii a nɛra wàá ka tɔɔgi ba siwee. Ba daŋ pilli siwee,
di keŋŋi digna ge nuu wia,
4di dɔɔ kanyitti di ra nuu wia, di zum a zɛɛ.
Banla ge n ɔɔ ra mɛuli
wàá kaa ra mɛuli,
ka jaa ra ŋɔ wia
a ra chaani.
5Nɛra wàá kaa ra tɔgzi gɛnaa,
ba wàá kaa ra tɔgzi
karkanna ge.
6Gɛnii ɔɔ ra ŋɔ gɛnni wiarɛ,
di dɔɔ nfɛrɛchɔgaa werge.
Waa ɔɔ ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnizi,
ka ra bagli nɛra wia la
n waa deŋlee
Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa biini.
Waa ɔɔ sɛɛ tɛɛ banla lɔzi n na kpu diwee, bá di,
waa ɔɔ tɛɛ
banla niinyɔgzi
n na kpu nii, bá nyɔɔ.
7Karkanni ni u kara maa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ.
U ɔɔ suahzuu di ta jina
dí na gunla
un niŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa,
di kanni kara chɔgi nyaara,
haali di ba hor
summɔ gba.
8Ama, girme hiŋwaa ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu gunla un niŋ ɛɛu, a hiini nɛra,
di lau guŋ
wiɛɛlaa nɛnnɛ.
Jɛrusalɛm haana wia
9Haana, ii ra fɛu lugɔ wiimaa wàá huuzi ia,
ií ra nuu n be.
Biihaana, ii ra fɛu lugɔ
wiimaa waa ia titte,
ií ra nuu gunla minna ŋɔ.
10Di bina ni tama wa jaawɔ,
ii banla wiimaa
n waa ia titte la
siwii daŋ jaa aah,
ii bɔra ra sa.
Ií grepuzi daazi daŋ vɛɛ nɔnaa,
ii wàá naa tɔrgi.
11Ií gil ii bɔra ra sa,
haana, ii baga n waa hoo
wiimaa be la,
wiimaa n waa ia titte la.
Ií wir ii wɛjɛzi,
ka kpa gbɔglɔnzi nigni,
di ra bagli ii biinichɔg.
12Ií lɔ ii bampiree ni biinichɔg di ra wii,
dikuu ii koonanaa
ni daazi la
n faa ra nɔŋ werge
13ni n nɛra hɛri la maa n chɔkkɛ,
sɔɔhri ni choŋgolaa lii
u ni la wia.
Ií ra wii dikuu iiŋ faa du ii diini biine di dɔɔ bɔsɔna di ra mam la
ani bolzeŋ la iiŋ ɔɔ
faa ra di iihinaa
u biini la wia.
14Koori diahina maa daŋ chɔ ka ka u diikpeg,
bolzeŋ la nɛra
n faa su u biini la,
ba maa daŋ chɔ ka giluu.
Diikpeg ni diijaŋ la n la chiŋ maa,
daŋ birgi diŋgela
di hanna la.
Bol sela maa jaa ra zuu de di ra di a hinaa,
di ra di kooree.
15Guŋ daŋ wa ɛɛ guŋŋ di ra la
saŋa la Kɔraawiizi
n niŋ jaa wa
gil u Duma tuu yaa ni.
Denii hɛribɔduma la jaa birgi hɛrsum,
hɛrsum la ge
kuna izi nɛnnɛ
di ɛɛ lugɔ kɔr.
16Wibii daŋ du hɛribɔduma biini,
wideŋlaa du hɛrsum la biini.
17A wideŋlaa ɛɛi daŋ gil bɔsɔna du de,
nɛra so bɔɔiih,
wiimaa wàá ka
tir ba saŋaa saŋa maa.
18N nɛra daŋ jaa so ni bɔsɔna,
di du bɔɔiih bɔr la maa
baŋ duwɛɛ,
wichɔgii maa
wàá ka huuzi baa.
19Haali dobizenaa n niŋ wa chɔgi kɔr la,
bolzeŋ la ge
maa puri chol,
20ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ haa kissi u nɛra werge maa.
Ba daŋ ɔɔ duu ba kuna
gɔŋa kɛraa,
ba nauna ni
kauzi ge gaagi
di ra di a kipar.

english_text:
Jerusalem Will Be Safe
1You defeated my people.
Now you're in for trouble!
You've never been destroyed,
but you will be destroyed;
you've never been betrayed,
but you will be betrayed.
When you have finished
destroying and betraying,
you will be destroyed
and betrayed in return.
2Please, Lord, be kind to us!
We depend on you.
Make us strong each morning,
and come to save us
when we are in trouble.
3Nations scatter when you roar
and show your greatness.
4We attack our enemies
like swarms of locusts;
we take everything
that belongs to them.
5You, Lord, are above all others,
and you live in the heavens.
You have brought justice
and fairness to Jerusalem;
6you are the foundation
on which we stand today.
You always save us and give
true wisdom and knowledge.
Nothing means more to us
than obeying you.
The Lord Will Do Something
7Listen! Our bravest soldiers
are running through the streets,
screaming for help.
Our messengers hoped for peace,
but came home crying.
8No one travels anymore;
every road is empty.
Treaties are broken,
and no respect is shown
to any who keep promises.
9Fields are dry and barren;
Mount Lebanon wilts
with shame.
Sharon Valley is a desert;
the forests of Bashan and Carmel
have lost their leaves.
10But the Lord says,
“Now I will do something
and be greatly praised.
11Your deeds are straw
that will be set on fire
by your very own breath.
12You will be burned to ashes
like thorns in a fire.
13Everyone, both far and near,
come look at what I have done.
See my mighty power!”
Punishment and Rewards
14Those terrible sinners
on Mount Zion tremble
as they ask in fear,
“How can we possibly live
where a raging fire
never stops burning?”
15But there will be rewards
for those who live right
and tell the truth,
for those who refuse
to take money by force
or accept bribes,
for all who hate murder
and violent crimes.
16They will live in a fortress
high on a rocky cliff,
where they will have food
and plenty of water.
The Lord Is Our King
17With your own eyes
you will see the glorious King;
you will see his kingdom
reaching far and wide.
18Then you will ask yourself,
“Where are those officials
who terrified us and forced us
to pay such heavy taxes?”
19You will never again have to see
the proud people who spoke
a strange and foreign language
you could not understand.
20Look to Mount Zion
where we celebrate
our religious festivals.
You will see Jerusalem,
secure as a tent with pegs
that cannot be pulled up
and fastened with ropes
that can never be broken.
21Our wonderful Lord
will be with us!
There will be deep rivers
and wide streams
safe from enemy ships.
The Lord Is Our Judge
22The Lord is our judge
and our ruler;
the Lord is our king
and will keep us safe.
23But your nation is a ship
with its rigging loose,
its mast shaky,
and its sail not spread.
Someday even you that are lame
will take everything you want
from your enemies.
24The Lord will forgive your sins,
and none of you will say,
“I feel sick.”
translation_text:
Biinichɔg ni hiinaa wia
1Wia daŋ huuzi hinla n na kpu nɛra,
ka ba waa hiŋwaa kpuwɛɛ!
Wia daŋ huuzi hinla n na ɛɛ sɔsɔgɔ,
ka nɛra haa waa hiŋwaa
ɛɛwɛ sɔsɔgɔ!
Di i haŋ wa gil nɛra kpui,
ba daŋ jaa kpui.
Di i haŋ wa gil sɔsɔgɔ ɛɛi,
ba daŋ jaa ɛɛ i ge sɔsɔgɔ!
2N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, suŋ yaa ni di hiini yaa!
Yaa ra binni i siweere.
Tɛɛ yaa fɔŋŋa hɔpizibii maa,
di ra lɛɛ yaa tɔɔrɔɔ saŋa.
3Di i pozoo, hɛssi nɛra ɔɔ nuu i loobiire di ra chɔ.
Di i wa izoo di ra nyiŋŋi
i lɔ laal,
hɛssi nɛra ɔɔ yaaruu.
4Hɛssi nɛra, nɛra daŋ jaa paagi i kuna maa nyaamm
alugɔ lotorozi n ɔɔ tuŋ
pattikuna gunla.
5Kɔraawiizi zenni kaali kummaa, awia, u duuribɔttɛ chiŋ.
U daŋ gil wibii
ni wideŋlaa su bolzeŋ
Jɛrusalɛm werge maa.
6Waabuu niŋ ɛɛ ii fɔŋŋa a saŋa.
U danna lɛɛ ia werge maa,
di ra tɛɛ ia sichaana
ani nunzuma ge werge.
U ɔmaarɛ niŋ ɛɛ ii wizeŋ.
7Ií na! Ba baala la n dɔɔ bampiree werge ra wiiu, ba bola ŋmɛnizenaa biine.
Nabɔnzi la baŋ hummɛ
lugɔ ba ga kuari wia
ra wiiu werge maa
ni biinichɔg.
8Ŋmɛnizenaa maanii ba gil ta,
nɛr maa waa
kaa ra volaa.
Nɛra ra chɔgi nuukpaŋ la ba ni nɛra n ɛɛwɛ,
di jaa ra gbɛlli
ba jinazi baŋ tawɛɛ,
ba waa kaa ra tɔgzi
nɛr maa.
9A hɛri maanii chɔɔ pɛɛ di birgi diŋgela.
Lɛbanɔn hɛri kɔr daazi
maanii hillɛ,
Sarɔn gba hɛrnanaa la maanii jaa birgi hɛribɔdumazi.
Basan ni Bizeŋ Kamɛl
daakpega maa
paŋhoori wattɔɔ.
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Filaŋkeŋ n daŋ izi
di bagli n zenni la
n kaali kummaa zenni la.
11Wia la iiŋ ta jina ii ɛɛ,
ani anla iinna ɛɛ
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zɔga.
Ii himmaa heeza
daŋ birgi ninlau
di fuuh ia.
12Hɛssi hina daŋ fuuh nyaamm, hɔɔhri bɛŋ ka,
alugɔ sɔɔhri baŋ ŋmɛnnɛɛ
di du niŋ a ra lau
zagzagzag la.
13Ii banla n du bɔɔnɛɛ, ií ra nuu gunla miŋ ɛɛwɛ!
Ii banla ge n duglɛɛ,
ií ra tɔgzi n fɔŋŋa la!”
14Ɔnsii werge lau wichɔgɛɛra la n du Bolzeŋ Ziɔnnɛ,
banla n waa Kɔraawiizi
ŋmɛnizi ra hiŋ la bɔra ra sa,
ba ra pɛɛzi,
“Yaa biini, u bɛliirɛ niŋ wer so bɔr la niŋ la n na chɔgi kuna la n duwɛɛnɛi?
Yaa biini, u bɛliirɛ
niŋ wer du bɔr la
niŋ n na lau,
waa dinzaa dɔɔwɛ la biinei?”
15Nɛr la n niŋ wer du denii unla wia n deŋlee,
u ra di wibii,
waa nɛra ra fini di ra na tɔna,
waa kuna ra lɛɛ nɛra be,
waa sɛɛwɛ ra tɛɛ nɛra la n
ɔɔ ra ta jina
bá ga kpu nɛr,
di ɔɔ tɔ u siwee
ú gilɛɛ wa na wia la
n niŋ lul wichɔgaa.
16Wiimaa wàá wer ɛɛ a hindee u sognibɔr.
De ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
diikpeg bɛl
n du giŋgimii nyuu.
Ba daŋ tɛu diwee ú di,
u niinyɔɔlii gba
wàá tuŋ maa.
17Ii daŋ wa na koori la wessi werge,
di kaa na hɛri ge
n chɔɔwɛ yɛlɛlɛlɛ
kaali.
18A saŋa hiŋ ii daŋ bir liizi saŋa la ɔnsii werge n faa du de la wia, ka ra pɛɛzi iihinaa,
“Lee a huŋhunna
nabɔma la duɛi?
Lee lampolɛɛri la duɛi?
Lee a nabɔma la
n na binni diijaŋra la
n la chiŋ ni la duɛi?”
19Ii wàá ka na a nɛkpoŋlaa la maa.
Ba wàá ka mɔɔ
ba mɔɔri la iiŋ
waa nuu la tɛɛ ia
ii nua huhzi.
20Ii daŋ binni Jɛrusalɛm, bolzeŋ la yaa n na di yaa hɔpizizenaa u biini la,
di na lugɔ u ɛɛ bolzeŋ la
nɛra du u biinii
ni bampirsɔna.
U daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ tanti dia la baŋ baŋŋɛ, waa panzaa dɔɔwɛ,
ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá panzi
u daasiraa gɛɛ di chaahzi
u ŋmɛnni.
21Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Hiŋ la yaa n na hum.
U daŋ du sum lugɔ
hɛri muuwara ni gɔŋa kpila
n na pal u biini la.
U dɔm maa wàá wer kpa muugbera di ga a ni ba a hɛri,
u dɔm muugberzenaa bɛl maa
wàá wer vol a ni ba.
22Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ yaa seriya diirii,
di ɛɛ yaa gbɔgtɛɛri,
di ɛɛ yaa koori,
waabuu niŋ lɛɛ yaa.
23Yaa dɔma muugbessi pergoore, di kuugi,
Daazi la n lauri
ba muugbessi wɛjɛzi,
peu ra ta a ni
a ra vol la kuugoore,
a wɛjɛzi hiŋ sag de yɔgɔyɔgɔ,
a wàá wer yaa.
Kɔraawiizi nɛra daŋ bɔnni ba dɔma daama la.
Haali gbɛraa gba
daŋ na ba hora!
24Nɛra la maa n du Bolzeŋ Ziɔn ŋmɛnɛ wàá ka ŋɔ ba bɔra ra wii baabuu.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil
ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.

english_text:
The Nations Will Be Judged
1Everyone of every nation,
the entire earth,
and all its creatures,
come here and listen!
2The Lord is terribly angry
with the nations;
he has condemned them
to be slaughtered.
3Their dead bodies will be left
to rot and stink;
their blood will flow
down the mountains.
4 Each star will disappear—
the sky will roll up
like a scroll.
Everything in the sky
will dry up and wilt
like leaves on a vine
or fruit on a tree.
Trouble for Edom
5 After the sword of the Lord
has done what it wants
to the skies above,
it will come down on Edom,
the nation that the Lord
has doomed for destruction.
6The sword of the Lord
is covered with blood
from lambs and goats,
together with fat
from kidneys of rams.
This is because the Lord
will slaughter many people
and make a sacrifice of them
in the city of Bozrah
and everywhere else
in Edom.
7Edom's leaders are wild oxen.
They are powerful bulls,
but they will die
with the others.
Their country will be soaked
with their own blood,
and its soil made fertile
with their own fat.
8The Lord has chosen
the year and the day,
when he will take revenge
and come to Zion's defense.
9Edom's streams will turn into tar
and its soil into sulfur—
then the whole country
will go up in flames.
10 It will burn night and day
and never stop smoking.
Edom will be a desert,
generation after generation;
no one will ever travel
through that land.
11Owls, hawks, and wild animals
will make it their home.
God will leave it in ruins,
merely a pile of rocks.
The End of Edom
12Edom will be called
“Kingdom of Nothing.”
Its rulers will also be nothing.
13Its palaces and fortresses
will be covered with thorns;
only wolves and ostriches
will make their home there.
14Wildcats and hyenas
will hunt together,
demons will scream to demons,
and creatures of the night
will live among the ruins.
15Owls will nest there
to raise their young
among its shadows,
while families of vultures
circle around.
16In The Book of the Lord
you can search and find
where it is written,
“The Lord brought together
all of his creatures
by the power of his Spirit.
Not one is missing.”
17The Lord has decided
where they each should live;
they will be there forever,
generation after generation.
translation_text:
Hɛssi hina seriya dii wia
1Hɛssi hina maa, ií ba wa nuu!
Nɛra maa,
ií keŋŋi digna di ra nuu!
Ií gil hɛri ni kuna la maa n du u biini
ni durnya kummaa
nuu n loobii.
2Kɔraawiizi izoore ni baaŋ, ú chɔgi hɛssi hina maa.
U baaŋ hiŋ na fuuh
ba laallɔɔra maa ninɛɛ.
U daŋ chɔgi ba maa nyaamm,
di gil ba kpuuzi ba maa.
3Ba daŋ kpa ba lalaa haazi bɔr maa,
ba sɔɔh tɔ
a hɛri maa puihpuihpuih,
ba challi ra pal
bizenaa la nyuuni.
4Chinchiŋwilaa maa n du chiŋ daŋ ŋmɛɛri,
chiŋ ge piŋŋi
alugɔ baŋ ɔɔ
piŋŋi hɔnsɛbii la.
Chinchiŋwilaa maa daŋ chogli
lugɔ grepu daa paŋhoori
n ɔɔ war gunla.
Lugɔ fig nɔŋhɛɛlaa
n ɔɔ chogli gunla.
5Di n tokobi la wa hum u huma tuŋ chiŋ,
u daŋ jaa tuu
Ɛdɔm hina la
miŋ di ba chɔgaa seriya
tuŋ la ni.
6Kɔraawiizi tokobi la maa ɛɛ challɛ,
nuuri faa u maa.
Peballi, buuna chal
ani pebala siga
nuurii faau la.
Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ mbusu lizaarɛ bolzeŋ Bɔzra.
U daŋ kpu sekpila
Ɛdɔm hɛri.
7A nɛra nɛkpega n lugɔ nabalkpoŋlaa,
naballi ani nabalzenaa
maa daŋ siu.
Chal danna pal ba hɛri maa,
a nuuri ge gil nyɔɔ
wàá ka wer izi de.
8Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi lizi a saŋaa, ú tɛr ba digna,
di turgi wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛ
Jɛrusalɛm hina la kim,
gunna bagli lugɔ
Jɛrusalɛm hor summɔɔ.
9Ɛdɔm hɛri niiri maa daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ kotaal,
u hɛɛhraa maa ge
ɛɛ lugɔ jilbi,
u hɛri maa ra lau niŋ.
10A niŋ daŋ du denii saŋaa saŋa maa,
nyɔɔzi ge tɔ saŋa maa,
a waa kaalaa dɔɔwɛ.
U daŋ chɔɔ diŋgela jiminikpila maa,
nɛr maa wàá kaa ra ga de.
11De daŋ ɛɛ kukuballi
ni duglizi duuribɔr,
Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil
Ɛdɔm hɛri chɔɔ pɛɛ
gunla hɛri n faa
waa duula dɔɔwɛ,
di chɔɔ woo la.
12Koori wàá du de di ra binni a hɛri,
ba sitɔɔra maa tuŋ.
13Sɔɔhri ni paŋhoori la n dɔɔ sɔɔhri
daŋ lii ba diikpega
ni ba bolkpega maa biine,
de jaa birgi hohobiazi
ni kukuballi duuribɔr.
14Hɛribɔduma sela daŋ ɔɔ huuzi munuzi de,
sejigzi ge du de
di chɛɛhgi ra du dɔŋa,
sela la n na di hamuŋa ba de,
di wa chɔɔ.
15Kikiuzi du a daŋa de, di he hala,
di teezaa di yaa
a keeri tɔ a biifulli ni.
Kɔlli ge ɔɔ chaali de,
bɛl maa ni u cheeŋ.
16Binni Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini, di karmi gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ,
A sela ni a zumbizi naa maanii niŋ du de,
bɛl maa ni u cheeŋ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi himmaanii dau guŋ,
u Duma genii niŋ
chaalaa ba dɔŋa be.
17U himmaanii mɛgzi a sela duuribɔr tɛɛa,
de birgi a zuuribɔr
á du de di hanna la,
saŋaa saŋa maa.

english_text:
God's Splendor Will Be Seen
1Thirsty deserts will be glad;
barren lands will celebrate
and blossom with flowers.
2Deserts will bloom everywhere
and sing joyful songs.
They will be as majestic
as Mount Lebanon,
as glorious as Mount Carmel
or Sharon Valley.
Everyone will see
the wonderful splendor
of the Lord our God.
God Changes Everything
* 3 Here is a message for all
who are weak, trembling,
and worried:
4“Cheer up! Don't be afraid.
Your God is coming
to punish your enemies.
God will take revenge on them
and rescue you.”
5 The blind will see,
and the ears of the deaf
will be healed.
6 Those who were lame
will leap around like deer;
tongues once silent
will shout for joy.
Water will rush
through the desert.
7Scorching sand
will turn into a lake,
and thirsty ground
will flow with fountains.
Grass will grow in deserts,
where packs of wild dogs
once made their home.
God's Sacred Highway
8A good road will be there,
and it will be named
“God's Sacred Highway.”
It will be for God's people;
no one unfit to worship God
will walk on that road.
And no fools can travel
on that highway.
9No lions or other wild animals
will come near that road;
only those the Lord has saved
will travel there.
10The people the Lord has rescued
will come back singing
as they enter Zion.
Happiness will be a crown
everyone will always wear.
They will celebrate and shout
because all sorrows and worries
will be gone far away.
translation_text:
Banla n na lɛɛi bɔsɔna wia
1Bɔsɔna daŋ du hɛribɔduma ni hɛri la n hillɛ pergi biine,
á fur kooree,
daazi fii di du wer.
2Hɛribɔduma ra yir yira di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.
U daŋ du wer lugɔ Lɛbanɔn bizenaa,
di du sum alugɔ
Kamɛl ni Sarɔn hɛssi.
Nɛr maa daŋ na Kɔraawiizi girme,
u zenni ni u fɔŋŋa.
3Ií du nɛra la bɔra n huahwɛ, bɔkpega,
bá wer chi nɛnnɛ.
4Ií ŋɔ tɛɛ banla maa bɔra n huahwɛ, ɔnsii lau baa la,
“Ií chiiri zɛɛ,
di gilɛɛ ra ɔm!
Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ ba
di wa tɛr ii dɔma digna
di turgi ba wichɔgaa kim,
ka lɛɛ ia.”
5Denii nyuŋŋa siwee pilli,
dignitaŋa hina ge
jaa ra nuu wia,
6gbɛraa ra zaahzi alugɔ weenzi,
banla ge n waa wette
ra ŋɔ wia
jaa ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.
Niiri daŋ pogzi hɛribɔduma,
gɔŋa ra pal.
7Bɔr la wiizi n lɔwɛɛ u hil, daŋ birgi pol,
hɛssi la n nyaa nii la
maa ge furgi bulli,
bɔra la hohobiazi n faa ra chɔɔ la
fur kooree la
n ɔɔ ra lii nii bɔr.
8Ŋmɛnizeŋ daŋ du de,
ba ra yiruu,
‘Ŋmɛninaniinanii.’
Wichɔgɛɛri maa wàá vol u ni.
Gɛnaa wàá wer dar
banla n na hiŋuu.
9Bunyiŋ maa wàá du de,
sechɔgii bɛl maa ŋmɛnɛ
wàá vol u ni.
Banla Kɔraawiizi n lɛɛwɛ
bɛnnɛ niŋ ga de
kaali bol.
10Ba daŋ zuu Jɛrusalɛm ni bɔsɔna,
di ra yir yira,
di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna la
n waa tuna dɔɔwɛ maa.
Ba bɔra daŋ sɔɔni di hanna la,
biinichɔg ni himaa
wàá ka du de.

english_text:
The Assyrians Surround Jerusalem
(2 Kings 18.13-27; 2 Chronicles 32.1-19)
1Hezekiah had been king of Judah for 14 years when King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city 2except Jerusalem. The Assyrian king ordered his army commander to leave the city of Lachish and to take a large army to Jerusalem.
The commander went there and stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool. 3Three of the king's highest officials came out of Jerusalem to meet him. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
4The Assyrian commander told them:
I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself. 5Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria? 6 Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
7Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord, your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
8The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people! He will give you 2,000 horses, if you have enough troops to ride them. 9How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry? 10Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
11Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
12The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you!”
13Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted out in Hebrew:
Listen to what the great king of Assyria says! 14Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you. 15Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria. 16Stop listening to Hezekiah. Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns 17for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards and raise your own grain.
18Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him. Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria? 19What happened to the gods of Hamath, Arpad, and Sepharvaim? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces? 20None of those gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord, your God, can do any better?
21-22Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_text:
Asiiria Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib n ɔnzi Jɛrusalɛm hina wia
1Koori Hɛzɛkia kora dii binni fidaanaazuhiŋ biinii, Asiiria Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib faa wa fɔɔ Juda bolzeŋkpega maa ni laal, di kpeglaa. 2Denii u hum u laallɔɔra nabɔma ni u laallɔɔrakpila lii bolzeŋ Lakis, ba la Koori Hɛzɛkia be Jɛrusalɛm. A laallɔɔra nabɔma ga chi bɔr la baŋ peree, nii ga de di gaa zuu Chiŋ Pol la, ba ga de di ra la Wɛjɛ Suahra Bɔr ŋmɛnɛɛ la. 3Juda hina bahoro lii bá ga chem u ni. Hilkia biibaal Ɛliakim n na binni kooridia wikpoglaa, seriya diiribɔr karchi Sɛbna ani Asaf biibaal Joa la n na binni ba wikpoglaa hɔna ni la, lii bá ga chem u ni.
4A laallɔɔra nabɔma la ŋɔ ba be,
“Ií ga ŋɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia be, kenne Asiiria koorizeŋ la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la ŋɔ, ‘Bɛɛ ninɛɛ i dɛllɛi?’ 5I ŋɔ i teŋ lau wii bɛllɛ, i laallɔɔra ge du kpeg. Ka wiŋɔpɛɛri bɛnnɛ i ra ŋɔ. Anɛɛ i dɛlli di ra gbɛllinnɛi? 6Na! I dɛlli Ijip koori ninɛɛ. Ka u ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ kɔlii daŋkpala. Di i dɛlli u ni, u daŋ ku di dui pira. Gunnɛ Ijip koori du tɛɛ banla maa n dɛlli u ni. 7Gɛɛ di i ŋɔ n be, ‘Yaa dɛlli Kɔraawiizii la yaa n na hum la ninɛɛ.’ U vuga kuaribɔra ni u mbusu lizibɔra lɛi Koori Hɛzɛkia faa chɔgi, ka ŋɔ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina be, ‘Ií ra jaami Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la n du Jɛrusalɛm bɛŋ laa?’
8Awia, ba filaŋkeŋ, i ni n dɔɔri Asiiria koorizeŋ la na dɔŋa. N daŋ tɛi zagra kagboŋa anɛɛ, di i daŋ wer na a tinna! 9Haa Asiiria laallɔɔra nabɔnjiga gba duglɛɛ, ka ra tami lugɔ Ijip hina tɛi torkozi ani zagtinna! 10Di kaa kpa jaa, n ballɔɔ ń wa lɔ hɛri naa hina laal di chɔguu, di maa wiimaa nuuwɛ lɛi lii Kɔraawiizi bee? U himmaanii ŋɔ ń wa fɔɔ a hɛri naa, di chɔguu.”
11Denii Ɛliakim, Sɛbna ani Joa ŋɔ a laallɔɔra nabɔma be, “Yaa dɔɔri, jaande, a mɔɔ Aram hina mɔɔri di ra tɛɛ yaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa ra nuuabuu, ka gilɛɛ mɔɔ Hibru hina mɔɔri di ra tɛɛ yaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛra la n soge koŋlii ni la ra nuuabuu.”
12Ka a laallɔɔra nabɔma la bir ŋɔ, “Ií fɛwɔɔ lugɔ ii ni ii dɔɔri la bɛŋ benii n dɔɔri humiŋ ŋɔ ń wa ŋɔ a wia naa, ka gil banla waa n soge koŋlii ni laa? Ií ni baa maa lɛi niŋ di ii himmaa bina, di nyɔɔ ii himmaa fiihniiaa?”
13Denii a laallɔɔra nabɔma izi chi, ka pozi Hibru mɔɔri biini, di ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu Asiiria koorizeŋ n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge wiŋɔzi! 14U ra ŋɔu lugɔ ií gilɛɛ gil Koori Hɛzɛkia dar ia! Wàá wer lɛɛ ia. 15Ií gilɛɛ wa gil Koori Hɛzɛkia wàá dar ia, ií yardi Kɔraawiizi, di u wa ŋɔwɔɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ yaa, wibii maa, wàá kpa yaa bolzeŋ naa du Asiiria koorizeŋ nonee biini.’
16Ií gilɛɛ waa nuu Koori Hɛzɛkia be. Asiiria koorizeŋ ra ŋɔu lugɔ ií gil u ni ia dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, ií ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra. Ii bɛl maa daŋ jaa ra di u himmaa grepu ni fig daazi nɔna, di ra nyɔɔ nii u himmaa kɔlɔŋ biini 17guŋŋ u jaa wa kpogli ia kaali hɛri bɛl n duwɛɛ lugɔ ii hɛri naa. Hɛri la n dɔɔ mia ni siŋfalii, di ɛɛ hɛri la n dɔɔ diwee ni grepu daazi.
18Ií gilɛɛ gil Koori Hɛzɛkia dar ia, di u ŋɔwɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ ia! Hɛrbɛlii vugrɛ haa wette lɛɛ u hɛri lii Asiiria koorizeŋ nonee biinei? 19Lee bolzenaa Hamaf ni Aapad vuga la duɛi? Lee Sɛfavam hina vuga la duɛi? A wettoo lɛɛ bolzeŋ Samaria hina lii u nonee biiniaa? 20Hɛssi naa, u bɛlii vugrɛ wette lɛɛ u hɛri lii u nonee biinei? Ka ɛrɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wer lɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm lii u nonee biinei?”
21Ka a nɛra ɛɛ kirkirkir, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba koori faa ŋɔ ba benii lugɔ ba gilɛɛ waa hagzuu.
22Denii Ɛliakim, Sɛbna ani Joa lau ba laala piili, dikuu ba biine n chɔkkɛ wia, ka la ga ŋɔ ba koori be gunla Asiiria hina laallɔɔra nabɔma la n ŋɔwɛɛ.

english_text:
Hezekiah Asks Isaiah for Advice
(2 Kings 19.1-13)
1As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord. 2He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell me:
3Isaiah, these are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born. 4Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
5When these leaders came to me, 6I told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah:
I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria. 7I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
8Meanwhile the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
9About this same time, the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
10Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me. 11You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe? 12The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them? 13The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared.
Hezekiah Prays
(2 Kings 19.14-19)
14After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see. 15Then he prayed:
16 Lord God All-Powerful of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world. 17Just look and see how Sennacherib has insulted you, the living God.
18It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts. 19They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped. 20But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only Lord.
Isaiah Gives the Lord's Answer to Hezekiah
(2 Kings 19.20-34)
21-22I went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said:
Hezekiah, you prayed to me about King Sennacherib of Assyria. Now this is what I say to that king:
The people of Jerusalem
hate and make fun of you;
they laugh behind your back.
23Sennacherib, you cursed,
shouted and sneered at me,
the holy One of Israel.
24You let your officials
insult me, the Lord.
And here is what you
have said about yourself,
“I led my chariots
to the highest heights
of Lebanon's mountains.
I went deep into its forest,
cutting down the best cedar
and cypress trees.
25I dried up every stream
in the land of Egypt,
and I drank water
from wells I had dug.”
26Sennacherib, now listen
to me, the Lord.
I planned all of this long ago.
And you don't even know
that I alone am the one
who decided that you
would do these things.
I let you make ruins
of fortified cities.
27Their people became weak,
terribly confused.
They were like wild flowers
or like tender young grass
growing on a flat roof
or like a field of grain
before it matures.
28I know all about you,
even how fiercely angry
you are with me.
29I have seen your pride
and the tremendous hatred
you have for me.
Now I will put a hook
in your nose,
a bit in your mouth,
then I will send you back
to where you came from.
30Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year, you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest. 31Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit. 32I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
33I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack. 34As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem. 35I will protect it for the sake of my own honor and because of the promise I made to my servant David.
The Death of King Sennacherib
(2 Kings 19.35-37)
36The Lord sent an angel to the camp of the Assyrians, and he killed 185,000 of them all in one night. The next morning, the camp was full of dead bodies. 37After this, King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh. 38One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_text:
Baŋ felee ŋɔ Jɛrusalɛm lɛɛi wia
1Koori Hɛzɛkia n wa nuu guŋ, u tɛr u laala piili ni biinichɔg, ka kpa gbɔglɔŋ laala laali, di zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia. 2Denii u hum kooridia nabɔma Ɛliakim, ba karchi Sɛbna ani Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi, ba maa laali gbɔglɔŋ laala, di la Amɔz biibaal Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya be. 3Baŋ ga hel u be, ba ŋɔ u be, “Kenne Koori Hɛzɛkia ŋɔ, ‘Zinaa ɛɛ biinichɔg, dignitɛraa ani hiihzi dii hɔpiziirɛ. Yaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hilula n lɔ haaŋ ka waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ ú lul. 4Asiiria koorizeŋ la hum u laallɔɔra nabɔmaa, ú wa chagzi Kɔraawiizi himmaa. Kɔ́raawiizi la hinna hum la nuu chagzaa naa, di tɛr banla maa n ŋɔ gunla digna. Awia, suŋŋi wiizi tɛɛ yaa nɛra la n kawɛɛ.’ ”
5Koori Hɛzɛkia nabɔnzi la n ba Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya be la, 6u ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ga ŋɔ ii dɔɔri Hɛzɛkia be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Gilɛɛ ra ɔm dikuu wiŋɔzi la Asiiria koorizeŋ n hum u balaa ba wa ŋɔ di binniŋ pɛɛ la wia. 7A nuu, n daŋ kpa duma bɛl du u ni, di u wa nuu amaniye bɛl, u daŋ bir kaali u himmaa hɛri, denii ń ga gil ba kpuu ni tokobi.’ ”
8A laallɔɔra nabɔma la n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Asiiria koorizeŋ la waa kaa hoo Lakis la, u bir har di ga na a koorizeŋ ni bolzeŋ Libna hina, n na lɔ laal.
9Denii Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib nuu lugɔ Ijip Koori Tirhaka n ɛɛ Itiopia hinuu, vɔɔ laallɛ di ra ba u ni. Uŋ wa nuu guŋ, u hum u balaa Koori Hɛzɛkia be, di ŋɔ, 10“Ŋɔ Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia be, ‘Gilɛɛ gil Kɔraawiizi la hiŋ dɛllɛɛ la darii, dikuu uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛi lugɔ Jɛrusalɛm wàá birgi Asiiria koorizeŋ kundɔɔlii la.’ 11Wibii maa, i nuu gunla Asiiria koorizenaa n ɛɛ hɛrkpila maa hinaa, di chɔg ba hɛssi nyaamm. Hiŋwaa daŋ wer lii a biiniaa? 12N naabaala n faa puri Gɔzan, Haran, Rɛzɛf ani Ɛdɛn hɛssi la n faa du Tɛl Asa la, ba vuga faa wettoo lɛɛ baa? 13Lee bolzenaa Hamaf, Aapad, Sɛfavam, Hɛna ani Iva koora la duɛi?”
Koori Hɛzɛkia wiisuŋŋaa wia
14Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia faa lɛɛ a hɔŋ lii a koorizeŋ balaa la be, di karmuu. Ka jaa kpau ga zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia, di yaau dau Kɔraawiizi see, 15ka suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ, 16“Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum, hinla n soge chɛrubzi baambaaŋ, i bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi la n na di kora durnya kossi maa ni. Hinuu ta chiŋ ni hɛri. 17Kɔraawiizi, n na suŋŋiibuu, keŋŋi digna di ra nuu, pilli i siwee na! A nuu gunla Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib n ŋɔwɛɛ, di ra chagzi hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la.
18Wibii maanii lugɔ Asiiria koorizenaa faa kpegli hɛrkpila maa nɛraa, ba hɛssi birgi diŋgelli, 19di paagi ba vuga fuuh. A faa ɛɛ bia ni daazii di nyaa fɔŋŋa, dikuubɛɛwiai, newea kuŋkuaraarɛ. 20Awia, filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, lɛɛ yaa lii u nonii biini, durnya hɛssi maa nɛra zum lugɔ i bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi.”
Sɛnakɛrib cholaa wia
21Denii Amɔz biibaal Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya faa hum nɛr Koori Hɛzɛkia be, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ u nuu i wiisuŋŋaa labuu dikuu Asiiria Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib wia. 22U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
‘Jɛrusalɛm ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ toloori,
di ra gbɛllii,
di ra ɛɛi chɛɛtɛ.
U ra viigi u nyuurɛ
dikuu hinna chɔ la wia.
23Anɛɛ i ra gbɛlli di ra chagzɛi?
Anɛɛ ninɛɛ i pozei?
Anɛɛ i ra maarei?
Mìŋ́ Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii
labuu i ra ɛɛ gunla!
24I hum i balaarɛ ba wa chagziŋ.
I ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ i
kpa i zagkpila
ni a torkozii
di tinni bizenaa nyuuni,
haali Lɛbanɔn bizenaa la nyuuni,
di teŋri de hɛriŋkpola la n jaŋŋɛ ani daananaa la maa n wesse la.
I zuuwɔɔ la bɔɔnɛɛ,
di ga hel u kɔr bɔra la
n wesse werge.
25I ta barabaraa lugɔ,
i ki kɔlɔnzii
hɛrdumazi biine,
di nyɔɔ a niiri.
Di kaa ŋɔ lugɔ,
i laallɔɔra fɛrgi
Muu Naallɛ, u hil.
26Haa nuuwɛa?
N dau gunnɛ saŋa maa.
Awiarɛ filaŋkeŋ n jaa ɛɛ guŋ la.
N tɛibuu fɔŋŋa
i puri bolzenaa
la baŋ ma koŋlaa bar la.
27Gunnɛ faa gillɛ a bola zuura waa fɔŋŋa maa dɔɔwɛ,
ɔnsii faa lau baa,
ba di hiihzi la.
Ba faa gɛrgɔɔrɛ lugɔ kooriibii,
ba faa waa
fɔŋŋa maa dɔɔwɛ
lugɔ kooree n lii sal,
wiizi lɔ a ni a hil la.
28Ama, n zum i wiimaanii,
i wiɛɛlaa ni bɔr la hinna la.
Di zum gunla,
i baaŋ n na fuuh n ni,
werge maa.
29Dikuu i baaŋ n na fuuh n ni,
n kaa nuu i jigsaa ge wia,
n daŋ kpa n gɔrga gori i miizi,
di kpa n kabarga ge du i nua,
di gil i bir kaali
gunla hiŋ ballɛ la.’ ”
30Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya
faa ŋɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia be,
“Kenne niŋ ɛɛ daansɛɛ wii tɛi,
dɛɛnnaa ni bina,
i daŋ di mitɛɛri.
Ka biŋhorohiŋ waa,
i himmaa daŋ duu mia,
di kumaa
di duu grepu daazi,
di di a nɔna.
31Ii banla n ka Juda,
daŋ nyɛɛli lugɔ
daazi la lunne,
n zuu hɛri nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋ.
32Banla n kawɛɛ la daŋ lii Jɛrusalɛm,
baŋhina ge lii Bizeŋ Ziɔn.
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu
niŋ aah siwii guŋ ɛɛ.”
33Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Asiiria koorizeŋ wia,
“Wàá zuu a bolzeŋ naa biini.
Wàá ta hobikpaŋ maa ɛŋ.
U laallɔɔra wàá dugli bol naa,
gɛɛ di wer baruu,
gɛɛ di ta pee tinni zuu ɛŋ.
34Ŋmɛnɛɛ la uŋ kpawɛɛ ba la,
waabuu ú kaa bir kpa kaali.
Wàá zuu bolzeŋ naa ŋmɛnɛ maa.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
35N daŋ guu bolzeŋ naa di lɛɛu
dikuu n ni n balii
Koori Deevid wia.”
36Denii a hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa ni, Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la ga kpu Asiiria laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfa ni tokkoanaazu ni anue, ba chɔɔribɔr. A nɛra n wa izee chɔɔzi ni, ba na lalaa n chɔɔwɛ bɔr maa. 37Awia, Asiiria Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib faa bir har, di la u bolzeŋ Ninɛvɛ, di ga so de.
38A hɔl bɛl, u du u vug la banna yir Nisrɔk dia, di ra jaamuu. Denii u biibaala Adramɛlɛk ni Sarɛza wa kpuu ni tokobi, ka chɔ gilli Ararat hɛri. Gunnɛ a ɛɛ, u biibaal Ɛsahadɔn kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

english_text:
Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies
(2 Kings 20.1-11; 2 Chronicles 32.24-26)
1About this time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. So I went in and told him, “The Lord says you won't ever get well. You are going to die, and so you had better start doing what needs to be done.”
2Hezekiah turned toward the wall and prayed, 3“Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried hard.
4Then the Lord sent me 5with this message for Hezekiah:
I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will let you live 15 more years, 6while I protect you and your city from the king of Assyria.
7Now I will prove to you that I will keep my promise. 8Do you see the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway built for King Ahaz? I will make the shadow go back ten steps.
Then the shadow went back ten steps.
King Hezekiah's Song of Praise
9This is what Hezekiah wrote after he got well:
10I thought I would die
during my best years
and stay as a prisoner forever
in the world of the dead.
11I thought I would never again
see you, my Lord,
or any of the people
who live on this earth.
12My life was taken from me
like the tent that a shepherd
pulls up and moves.
You cut me off like thread
from a weaver's loom;
you make a wreck of me
day and night.
13Until morning came, I thought
you would crush my bones
just like a hungry lion;
both night and day
you make a wreck of me.
14I cry like a swallow;
I mourn like a dove.
My eyes are red
from looking to you, Lord.
I am in terrible trouble.
Please come and help me.
15There's nothing I can say
in answer to you,
since you are the one
who has done this to me.
My life has turned sour;
I will limp until I die.
16Your words and your deeds
bring life to everyone,
including me.
Please make me healthy
and strong again.
17It was for my own good
that I had such hard times.
But your love protected me
from doom in the deep pit,
and you turned your eyes
away from my sins.
18 No one in the world of the dead
can thank you or praise you;
none of those in the deep pit
can hope for you
to show them
how faithful you are.
19Only the living can thank you,
as I am doing today.
Each generation tells the next
about your faithfulness.
20You, Lord, will save me,
and every day that we live
we will sing in your temple
to the music
of stringed instruments.
Isaiah's Advice to Hezekiah
21I had told King Hezekiah's servants to put some mashed figs on the king's open sore, and he would get well. 22Then Hezekiah asked for proof that he would again worship in the Lord's temple.
translation_text:
Koori Hɛzɛkia wiila wia
1Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, wiila lɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia, u ra nyiŋŋi u siu. Amɔz biibaal, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya faa ba u be di wa ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Kossi i dia nɛnnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, hàá ka nyaagi, i daŋ siu.’ ”
2Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia bir u siwee chaŋ koŋlii, ka suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ, 3“N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, a liizi lugɔ n humiibuu ni wibii ani n biini maa, di ɛɛ wia la maa n deŋlee i be.” Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, u wii werge maa.
4Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya be, 5lugɔ ú bir la Koori Hɛzɛkia be di ga ŋɔ, “Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la i naabaal Koori Deevid n faa ra hum la ŋɔ, ‘N nuu i wiisuŋŋaa labuu, di kaa na i sinii ge. N daŋ chaai. N daŋ gil i kaa di binni fidaanue jaa. 6N daŋ lɛɛ i ni bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm maa lii Asiiria koorizeŋ nonee biini, di guuu.’ ”
7Aizaaya bir ŋɔ u be gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ɛɛ ú zum lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ gunla un ŋɔ nua la. U ŋɔ, 8“Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil chunchugle naa bir la har keeriilɔŋa fi, Ahaz keeraa la ni.” Denii a wiizi n faa ra chol la bir la har keeriilɔŋa fi.
9Kenne Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia faa sɛbi di chɔli Kɔraawiizi u nyaagaa saŋa la,
10“N Dɔɔri, n de dui n jaa chi nɛnnɛ naa,
a dɛkkɔɔ miŋ siuwɛ,
ka n binni la
n kawɛɛ la bir pɛɛa?
11Màá ka na Kɔraawiizi,
nyinee biini.
Màá ka na nɛra,
gɛɛ di kaa du ba be
durnya naa biini.
12Ba faa wil n diarɛ di lɛɛu lii n be,
gunla baŋ ɔɔ wil
penɔɔni lɔɔ ta la.
N miibɔɔ faa tunnɔɔ alugɔ suahri gessi,
u lawiŋ teŋ kɔɔrɛɛ ni.
Di lii hɔpizaa
di ga hel hamuŋa,
u gil n miibɔɔ tuŋ.
13N di kanyittii kpaŋii guŋŋ di ga hel chɔɔzinnua,
ka u purgi n hoga
gunla bunyiŋ
n ɔɔ purgi hoga la.
Di lii hɔpizaa
di ga hel hamuŋa,
u gil n miibɔɔ tuŋ.
14N wiiwoo lugɔ koŋkoroŋbee gɛɛ kagchagii,
N jaa ra nuumi lugɔ
chɔɔziŋkomma n na wii.
N binni chinne guŋŋ n siwee wa dim.
Siaahmu biinii n du.
N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
wa lɛɛŋ!”
15Ka ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔi?
U ŋɔ wiarɛ tɛŋ.
U himmaanii ɛɛ guŋ.
N daŋ sɔɔni siwii di hiŋuu n binni la n kawɛɛ biini maa
dikuu aŋ kpolle tɛŋ wia.
16N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, anniibuu gillɛ newea du de.
N gba ra na miibɔɔrɛ
di lii a biini.
I chaambuu
di gil n dɔɔ miibɔɔ.
17Ajaa n suma dii wiarɛ
n faa ra di a dɔgnya la.
I nɔŋŋaa wiarɛ
i lɛɛŋ lii siu be,
di bir i har
kpu n wichɔgaa.
18Dikuubɛɛwiai, lalaa wàá wer chɔlii.
Di nɛr siuwɔ,
wàá wer yir yira chɔlii.
Banla n du lalaa bol
wàá wer dɔɔ i wibii tamii.
19Nyinee bɛnnɛ niŋ wer chɔlii
alugɔ kennaa minna
ɛɛ zinaa naa.
Mɛɛwaa ra bagli ba biizii
i wibii dɔɔi wia.
20Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛŋ,
ka ya jaa wer kpa
janjalanzi lɔ,
di yir yira chɔluu u Dia biini,
yaa de dui biini,
saŋa maa.
21Denii Aizaaya faa ŋɔ, “Ií lug fig nɔna tɔ u kunsɔŋ la, ú nyaagi.”
22Koori Hɛzɛkia faa pɛɛzi Aizaaya, “Bɛɛ n niŋ bagli lugɔ n daŋ wer la Kɔraawiizi Diai?”

english_text:
Isaiah Speaks the Lord's Message to Hezekiah
(2 Kings 20.12-19)
1Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah was well, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him. 2Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
3I asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?”
“They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
4“What did you show them?” I asked.
Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
5Then I told Hezekiah:
I have a message for you from the Lord All-Powerful. 6One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left. 7 Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
8Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told me, “The message you brought from the Lord is good.”
translation_text:
Nabɔnzi n lii Babilɔn wia
1A saŋa hiŋ, Baladan biibaal Babilɔn Koori Mɛrɔdak Baladan, faa sɛbi hɔna, di kpa sunzaa jaa, di hum u balaa Koori Hɛzɛkia be, dikuu uŋ faa nuu u wiila ni u nyaagaa maa la wia. 2Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia faa lɛɛ a nabɔnzi ni bɔsɔna werge maa. Di faa kpa u daama kuna dauribɔra maa bagli baa, u saliŋhuŋŋa, u saliŋ, u dɔzi tiuzaa kuna, nuunanaa, u laal dɔŋkuna ani kuna la maa n faa jaa u daama ni. Kummaa faa waa kawɛɛ u dia ni u kora biini, di wɔɔ kpawɛɛ bagli baa.
3Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya faa wa pɛɛzi Koori Hɛzɛkia, “Ɛrɛɛ a baala naa wa ŋɔi? Lee genii ba liiyɛi?”
Koori Hɛzɛkia ŋɔ lugɔ hɛhjannɛ ba lii, Babilɔnnɛ ba lii.
4Aizaaya pɛɛzuu, “Beedee ba na i kooridia biinei?”
U ŋɔ, “N dia kummaanii ba na. N daama kummaa waa hoo, di maa kpawɛɛ bagli baa.”
5Denii Aizaaya ŋɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia be, dí Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, 6“Saŋa bɛl ra bau, wibii maa, kunla maa n du i kooridia naa, daama la maa i naabaala n nyiŋŋee dau di wa lii ni zinaa, ba daŋ wa chi a maa kaali Babilɔn hɛri. Kummaa wàá ka ka. 7I naanna la n ɛɛ i himmaa challɛ bá lauri kaali Babilɔn hɛri, di ga vari baa, bá ra hum Babilɔn kooridia.” Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
8Koori Hɛzɛkia ŋɔ Aizaaya be, “Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa hiŋ wa tɛŋ naa wessoo.” U faa fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ bɔsɔna daŋ du de, ú kora chi chigigi u de dui biini.

english_text:
Encourage God's People
1Our God has said:
“Encourage my people!
Give them comfort.
2Speak kindly to Jerusalem
and announce:
Your slavery is past;
