challi fɔg ii laalaa.
Haali iiŋ waa baa lauwɛ
di ba ra ŋmɛɛ kummaa gba.
Ka annii maa biini,
35ii ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
‘Yaa waa wiimaa zummɛ,
Kɔraawiizi baaŋ waa kaa
ra fuuh yaa ni.’
Ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛɛ ia chɔgri,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ii hɔɔwɔɔ lugɔ
ii waa wichɔgaa maa ɛɛwɛ.
36Ii gbɛlli iihinaarɛ,
di gaa kuari hɛrdumazi vuga.
Ka Ijip hina daŋ kpa hiihzi kpu ia
gunla Asiiria hina
n faa kpa hiihzi kpu ia la.
37Ii daŋ willi ii nyuuni ni hiihzi,
Ijip hɛri, dikuubɛɛwiai,
mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi vɛɛ banla iiŋ yardɛɛrɛ.
Ii wàá na hiinaa maa ba be.”

english_text:
Sin and Shame
1The Lord said to the people of Israel:
If a divorced woman marries,
can her first husband
ever marry her again?
No, because this
would pollute the land.
But you have more gods
than a prostitute has lovers.
Why should I take you back?
2Just try to find one hilltop
where you haven't gone
to worship other gods
by having sex.
You sat beside the road
like a robber in ambush,
except you offered yourself
to every passerby.
Your sins of unfaithfulness
have polluted the land.
3So I, the Lord, refused
to let the spring rains fall.
But just like a prostitute,
you still have no shame
for what you have done.
4You call me your father
or your long-lost friend;
5you beg me to stop being angry,
but you won't stop sinning.
The Lord Asks Israel To Come Back to Him
6 When Josiah was king, the Lord said:
Jeremiah, the kingdom of Israel was like an unfaithful wife who became a prostitute on the hilltops and in the shade of large trees. 7-8I knew that the kingdom of Israel had been unfaithful and committed many sins, yet I still hoped she might come back to me. But she didn't, so I divorced her and sent her away.
Her sister, the kingdom of Judah, saw what happened, but she wasn't worried in the least, and I watched her become unfaithful like her sister. 9The kingdom of Judah wasn't sorry for being a prostitute, and she didn't care that she had made both herself and the land unclean by worshiping idols of stone and wood. 10And worst of all, the people of Judah pretended to come back to me. 11Even the people of Israel were honest enough not to pretend.
12Jeremiah, shout toward the north:
Israel, I am your Lord—
come back to me!
You were unfaithful
and made me furious,
but I am merciful,
and so I will forgive you.
13Just admit that you rebelled
and worshiped foreign gods
under large trees everywhere.
14You are unfaithful children,
but you belong to me.
Come home!
I'll take one or two of you
from each town and clan
and bring you to Zion.
15Then I'll appoint wise rulers
who will obey me,
and they will care for you
like shepherds.
16You will increase in numbers,
and there will be no need
to remember the sacred chest
or to make a new one.
17The whole city of Jerusalem
will be my throne.
All nations will come here
to worship me,
and they will no longer follow
their stubborn, evil hearts.
18Then, in countries to the north,
you people of Judah and Israel
will be reunited,
and you will return to the land
I gave your ancestors.
19I have always wanted
to treat you as my children
and give you the best land,
the most beautiful on earth.
I wanted you to call me “Father”
and not turn from me.
20But instead, you are like a wife
who broke her wedding vows.
You have been unfaithful to me.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People Confess Their Sins
The Lord said:
21Listen to the noise
on the hilltops!
It's the people of Israel,
weeping and begging me
to answer their prayers.
They forgot about me
and chose the wrong path.
22I will tell them, “Come back,
and I will cure you
of your unfaithfulness.”
They will answer,
“We will come back, because you
are the Lord our God.
23On hilltops, we worshiped idols
and made loud noises,
but it was all for nothing—
only you can save us.
24Since the days of our ancestors
when our nation was young,
that shameful god Baal has taken
our crops and livestock,
our sons and daughters.
25We have rebelled against you
just like our ancestors,
and we are ashamed of our sins.”
translation_text:
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di baal vɛɛ u haaŋ,
u la ga yuu baduma,
a dɛkkɔ u jaabinii kaa bir la u bee?
Guŋ wàá chɔgi a hɛriaa?
Ka ii duwɔɔrɛ lugɔ sɛnsɛnna,
di dɔɔ sɛnnikpila.
Ii daŋ kaa wer biruu
ba n be naa?
2Ií binni giŋgimee nyuuni na.
Yembɛl du de
ii waa sɛnsɛŋ wia ɛɛwɛaa?
Ii ɔɔ so ŋmɛnikɛraarɛ di ra kpaŋ baala,
di kaa du ŋmɛnikɛraa maa
alugɔ Lɔrbi n du hɛribɔduma.
Ii kpa sɛnsɛŋ ni biinikpolaa,
di chɔgi a hɛri maa.
3A gunnɛ baani dooŋ waa ba,
haali yuuliŋ dooŋ
gba waa ballɛ.
Ka ii haa ɛɛ lugɔ sɛnsɛnni,
hiihzi waa ia lauwɛ gba.
4Di lii ii pɔlaa saŋa,
miŋ lɛi ii ra yir ii mɛɛ
ni ii dammu laa?
5Ii ɔɔ kaa pɛɛzi, ‘Saŋa maanii i baaŋ na fuuh gɛɛ?
I baaŋ danna fuuh yaa ninɛɛ
di hanna la
saŋaa saŋa maa?’
Kenne ii ɔɔ ra ŋɔ saŋa maa,
ka haa vɛɛ ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa
la maa dee iiŋ wette.”
Izrɛl hina wibii nyaai wia
6Koori Jɔsia kora dii saŋa, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia benii, “I na Izrɛl hina wibii nyaairɛ naa? Ba tinni giŋgimee nyuunii, di so daazenaa zɛɛzi, di ra kuari vuga. 7N faa zummɔɔ lugɔ annii naa maa baŋ ɛɛwɛ naa, ka ba daŋ bir ba n be, ka ba vɛɛ. Haali ba lulla Juda hina la wia n waa wibii dɔɔwɛ la gba na gunnɛ. 8N tɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa hahvɛɛri hɔŋ, dikuu ba wibii nyaai wia, di duŋŋi baa lugɔ ba ra la, dikuu ba sɛnsɛŋ wia. Ka n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ ba lulla Juda hina la gba wia n waa wibii dɔɔwɛ la waa ɔm. Ba ge gba haa vɛɛwɔɔ ra sɛm. 9Dikuu Izrɛl hina sɛnsɛŋ la n waa wizeŋ ɛɛwɛ ba be wia, ba chɔgi a hɛrii, di ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ wia, di ra kuari bia ni daazi. 10Annii naa maa har, ka ba lulla Juda hina la wia n waa wibii dɔɔwɛ la, waa sɛɛwɛ bir ba n be, ka ra ɛɛ dawari. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
11Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Haali Izrɛl hina n nyaa wibii la gba, ka ba wiarɛ deŋlee kaali wibiinyaara Juda hina. 12La ga sii wia naa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di ŋɔ,
‘Wibiinyaara Izrɛl hina, ií bir ba n be,
n baaŋ wàá ka fuuh ii ni,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n na suŋ nɛra ninɛɛ.
Màá na baaŋ di hanna la
saŋaa saŋa maa.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
13Iawaa haa sɛɛ lugɔ ii di bilchɔgrɛ,
lugɔ ii vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la
iinna hum la nuarɛ.
Ií sɛɛ chɔgri lugɔ ii nɔŋŋi hɛrdumazi vugaa,
daazenaa zɛɛzi, ka vɛɛ
n widaulaa hiŋaa.’
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
14Wibiinyaara, ií bir ba n be, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ii jaari, ii ɛɛ n horaa. N daŋ lizi nɛkpaŋ lii bol maa biini, di kaa lizi banɛɛ lii domee maa biini, di kpogli ia bir ba Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu. 15N daŋ tɛɛ ia sitɔɔra la n ninna ɛɛ n kipar, bá ra tɔ ii see ni nunzuma ni wia zɛɛ zumaa.” 16Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa la iin niŋ wazi werge maa a hɛri biini la, nɛra wàá ka ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la wia. U wia wàá ka du ba nfɛssi biine gɛɛ bá kaa liizi u wia. Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka nyiŋŋuu gɛɛ bá kaa kuari bɛl. 17A guŋ saŋa, ba daŋ yir Jɛrusalɛm Kɔraawiizi Koorikara. Denii hɛssi hina maa chaali ba Jɛrusalɛm, di waa jaamiŋ, di ra dargiŋ. Ba wàá ka dɔɔ dignikpega, di ra hiŋ ba nfɛrchɔgaa la. 18A saŋa, Juda hina daŋ ba wa jaa Izrɛl hina ni, ba maa kpau izi lii a hɛri wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di la hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ii naabaala, u ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ la.”
Kɔraawiizi nɛra vuga kuaraa wia
19Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Izrɛl hina, n na nyiŋŋuu ń kpogli ia nɛnnɛ alugɔ n biibaala,
di tɛɛ ia hɛri la n summɛ
di du wer kaali hɛssi hina
maa kapɛttɛ kuna.
N na nyiŋŋuu ií ra yiriŋ ii Mɛɛ,
di gilɛɛ kaa bir har kpuŋ.
20Gunla haaŋ bɛl wia n waa ɔɔ dɔɔ wibii u jaari be la,
gunnɛ Izrɛl hina wia waa
wibii dɔɔwɛ n be la.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
21Wile ra lɔu a giŋgimee nyuuni maa,
Izrɛl hinaa ra wii
di ra suŋŋiŋ,
dikuu baŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa,
di suuh mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la
banna hum wia.
22Ii banla maa n vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa la,
ií bir ba u be.
U daŋ chaa ia,
di gil ii wia deŋli,
di dɔɔ wibii.
Ií ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ɛɛh, yaa ra ba Kɔraawiizi benii,
dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu ɛɛ
Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum.
23Yaa waa hiinaa maa nawɛɛ
lii a vuga kuaraa biini, saŋa la
yaa n na kuaraa
giŋgimee nyuuni la.
Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la bɛŋ benii,
Izrɛl hina hiinaa ra lii.
24Di lii yaa pɔlaa saŋa, vuga chɔgi
yaa naabaala huma tɔnaa,
ba sela, ba biibaala
ani biihaana maa.
25Ií gil ya chɔɔ ni hiihzi,
di di ŋmaaba.
Yaa ni yaa mɛɛwaa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ
di zuu Kɔraawiizi la
yaa n na hum la ni.
Di haŋ lii yaa pɔlaa saŋa di wa lii ni zinaa,
yaa waa Kɔraawiizi la yaa
n na hum la nua hiŋŋɛ.”

english_text:
How Israel Can Return to the Lord
1The Lord said:
Israel, if you really want
to come back to me, get rid
of those disgusting idols.
2Make promises only in my name,
and do what you promise!
Then all nations will praise me,
and I will bless them.
3 People of Jerusalem and Judah,
don't be so stubborn!
Your hearts have become hard,
like unplowed ground
where thornbushes grow.
4With all your hearts,
keep the agreement
I made with you.
But if you are stubborn
and keep on sinning,
my anger will burn like a fire
that cannot be put out.
Disaster Is Coming
The Lord said:
* 5“Sound the trumpets, my people.
Warn the people of Judah,
‘Run for your lives!
6Head for Jerusalem
or another walled town!’
“Jeremiah, tell them I'm sending
disaster from the north.
7An army will come out,
like a lion from its den.
It will destroy nations
and leave your towns empty
and in ruins.”
8Then I told the people
of Israel,
“Put on sackcloth!
Mourn and cry out,
‘The Lord is still angry
with us.’ ”
9The Lord said,
“When all this happens,
the king and his officials,
the prophets and the priests
will be shocked and terrified.”
10I said, “You are the Lord God. So why have you fooled everyone, especially the people of Jerusalem? Why did you promise peace, when a knife is at our throats?”
The Coming Disaster
11-12When disaster comes, the Lord will tell you people of Jerusalem,
“I am sending a windstorm
from the desert—
not a welcome breeze.
And it will sweep you away
as punishment for your sins.
13Look! The enemy army
swoops down like an eagle;
their cavalry and chariots
race faster than storm clouds
blown by the wind.”
Then you will answer,
“We are doomed!”
14But Jerusalem, there is still time
for you to be saved.
Wash the evil from your hearts
and stop making sinful plans,
15before a message of disaster
arrives from the hills of Ephraim
and the town of Dan.
16-17The Lord said,
“Tell the nations that my people
have rebelled against me.
And so an army will come
from far away
to surround Jerusalem
and the towns of Judah.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
18“People of Judah,
your hearts will be in pain,
but it's your own fault
that you will be punished.”
Jeremiah's Vision of the Coming Punishment
19I can't stand the pain!
My heart pounds,
as I twist and turn in agony.
I hear the signal trumpet
and the battle cry of the enemy,
and I cannot be silent.
20I see the enemy defeating us
time after time,
leaving everything in ruins.
Even my own home
is destroyed in a moment.
21How long will I see enemy flags
and hear their trumpets?
22I heard the Lord say,
“My people ignore me.
They are foolish children
who do not understand
that they will be punished.
All they know is how to sin.”
23After this, I looked around.
The earth was barren,
with no form of life.
The sun, moon, and stars
had disappeared.
24The mountains were shaking;
25no people could be seen,
and all the birds
had flown away.
26Farmland had become a desert,
and towns were in ruins.
The Lord's fierce anger
had done all of this.
The Death of Jerusalem
27-28The Lord said:
I have made my decision,
and I won't change my mind.
This land will be destroyed,
although not completely.
The sky will turn dark,
and the earth will mourn.
29Enemy cavalry and archers
shout their battle cry.
People run for their lives
and try to find safety
among trees and rocks.
Every town is empty.
30Jerusalem, your land
has been wiped out.
But you act like a prostitute
and try to win back your lovers,
who now hate you.
You can put on a red dress,
gold jewelry, and eye shadow,
but it's no use—
your lovers are out to kill you!
31I heard groaning and crying.
Was it a woman giving birth
to her first child?
No, it was Jerusalem,
gasping for breath
and begging for help.
“I'm dying!” she said.
“They have murdered me.”
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n na yir u nɛra bá gil ba wichɔgaa ta wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Izrɛl hina, di ii daŋ bir, guŋwaa,
ií bir ba n be.
Di ii sɛɛwɔ paa ii vuga la miŋ kiiwe la ha n sibɔɔ,
ii wàá ka leu,
2di ii kpa n sɔŋ hɛɛhzi,
ii wia dɔɔ wibii di deŋli,
guŋwaa, hɛssi hina maanii
niŋ ŋɔ ń kissi baa,
bá ra chɔliŋ.”
3Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina be,
“Ií gil ii bampiree la n lugɔ
hɛri la baŋ
waa buglee la du pɛr,
ii duu wideŋlaa tɛɛ iihinaa,
ka gilɛɛ waa duu kuna
ra du sɔɔhri biini.
4Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina,
ií ra hiŋ n ni ia nuukpaŋ la
di kpa iihinaa du n nonee.
Di guŋ lɛi, n baaŋ daŋ fuuh ii ni,
dikuu wichɔgaa la
iiŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia,
U danna fuuh,
ka nɛr maa
wàá wer sɔɔnuu.”
Hɛhchɔg n lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ra ba wia
5Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Sii ŋɔ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina be.
Huuh bensunoniina
bar a hɛri maa!
Lɔ wile werge di ŋɔ,
‘Ií chaali dɔŋa!
Ií gil ya chɔ la bolzeŋkpega la!’
6Ií lalli tuuta di bagli lugɔ ii chɔ la Jɛrusalɛm manaŋ,
di ga lɛɛ iihinaa!
Dikuubɛɛwiai, n kpa hɛhchɔgrɛ lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di ra ba,
a hɛhchɔg daŋ
chum werge maa.”
7Alugɔ bunyiŋ n lii u suahribɔr,
hɛssi chɔgri liwɔɔrɛ.
U liwɔɔrɛ ra ba,
ú wa chɔgi Juda.
U bolzenaa maanii niŋ purgi chɔɔ burburbur,
nɛr maa wàá ka du a biine.
8Awia, ií kpa gbɔglɔnzi tɔ,
di ra chɛɛhgi werge maa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuihchɔgii la
haa waa yaa ni liwɛɛ.
9Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “A hɔl hiŋ,
koori ni u zɛɛsogna
bɔra daŋ huah,
ɔnsii lau Kɔraawiizi kizeehina,
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi
nua kpu.”
10Denii n ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la, i dar Jɛrusalɛm hinaa werge! I ŋɔ lugɔ ba daŋ dɔɔ bampirsɔna, ka tokobizii baŋzi ba baŋaazi.”
11A saŋa, ba daŋ ŋɔ a nɛra naa ni Jɛrusalɛm hina maa be, “Pewem bɛl lii hɛribɔduma giŋgimee nyuunii, di ta ra ba n nɛra be. Ka waa ba lɛi, bá kpau hɛl kuna. 12A keŋ pekpeg naa lii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi benii. Minuu ra di n nɛra seriya guŋ.”
13Ií na! Yaa dɔm ra bau alugɔ baamazi,
u laal torkozi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ vem,
u zagra ge du gbaŋ
kaali chigni.
Wiarɛ huuzi yaa!
Yaa wia tunnɔɔ!
14Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií lizi ii wichɔgaa maa
lii ii bampiree ha, ka na lɛɛi.
Ɛrɛɛ ii ra nyiŋŋi ii kpa wichɔgaa
du ii biine, di birgi magɛi?
15Loobii bɛl lii bolzeŋ Dan
n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ,
di ra sii hɛhchɔg wia
lii Ɛfram giŋgimee nyuuni,
16di ra ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ hɛssi hina be,
di sii Jɛrusalɛm hina ge be
lugɔ ba dɔma lii
hɛhjaŋaa di ra ba.
Ba dɔma naa daŋ wa lɔ laal wile,
di du Juda bolzenaa ni.
17Ba daŋ wa baruu gunla baala n na kpaŋ koo la,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba vɛɛ n nuarɛ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
18Ii manni ni ii wiɛɛlaarɛ gillɛ
keŋ wa huuzi ia.
Ii digna tɛraarɛ guŋ,
dikuu wichɔgaa la
iiŋ ɛɛwɛ wia.
Tɔɔrɔɔ werge maa
daŋ gil ii biine chɔgi!”
19Denii mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ,
“N biini chɔkkɔɔ werge
di ra tɔɔriŋ.
N bɔra ra waaziŋ werge,
n na miŋŋi.
N banchule ra lɔu werge maa,
màá wer siigi.
N nuu bensunoniina wiraa
ni laal wilee.
20Hɛhchɔgni hiŋzi dɔŋaa,
a hɛri maa birgi diŋgela.
N tanti diini maa chɔgi kakpaŋ,
n duuribɔr gba guŋ.
21Ɛrɛɛ ń na laal tuutazi,
di nuu bensunoniina wiraa,
di birgi magɛi?”
22Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N nɛra gɛnnɔɔ,
ba wan zummɛ.
Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ biizi la n waa nunzuma dɔɔwɛ,
ba waa wia zɛɛ zummɛ.
Wichɔgaa bɛŋ ɛɛirɛ ba zum,
ba waa winanaa
ɛɛi zummɛ.”
23N binni hɛrii,
di u duula dɔɔwɛ,
di chɔɔ woo,
di kaa binni chiŋ ge,
di bɔchaaŋ waa hoo.
24N binni bizenaa,
di a ra zigli,
giŋgimee ge ra ziigi.
25N binni, di nɛra waa hoo,
zumbizi maa ge zaahzi kaali.
26N binni, di hɛrsum la birgi hɛribɔduma,
u bolzenaa maa birgi diŋgelli,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ wia.
27Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“N daŋ chɔgi a hɛri,
ka maa chɔgi u maa nyaamm.
28Awia, a hɛri nɛra daŋ wii,
chiŋ ge maa biri,
dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu ŋɔ guŋ,
màá ka bir n nua,
n teŋ lau gunnɛ kpogli,
màá kaa bir har.”
29Di nɛra wa nuu
zagtinna ni hotaara gbɔga,
ba maa danna chɔ.
Baŋhina chɔ zuu kɔrni,
baŋhina ge chɔ
ga tinni bia nyuuni.
Á bola maa chɔɔ pɛɛ,
nɛr maa wàá kaa ra
zuu a biine.
30Jɛrusalɛm hina, ii hɛri chɔkkɔɔ.
Ka ii ra ɛɛ lugɔ sɛnsɛnna,
n na ɛɛ ania bá bir na
ba sɛnna la n hah baa la.
Ii daŋ wer laali tagta aahma,
di du saliŋ digna ni
baŋaakuna ni nonibisiga,
di du kalu, ka pɛɛrɛ.
Ii sɛnna ra nyiŋŋi ii kpuirɛ.
31N nuu wilee alugɔ haaŋ n na nyiŋŋi lulaa,
di nuu hɛmaa lugɔ
haaŋ n na lul u toloobie.
Jɛrusalɛm hina heezaa ra sig guŋ,
ba yaa ba nonee di ra ŋɔ,
“Yaa wia chɔkkɔɔ!
Ba ra bau
bá wa kpu yaa!”

english_text:
Is Anyone Honest and Faithful?
The Lord said to me:
1“Search Jerusalem
for honest people
who try to be faithful.
If you can find even one,
I'll forgive the whole city.
2Everyone breaks promises
made in my name.”
3I answered, “I know
that you look for truth.
You punished your people
for their lies,
but in spite of the pain,
they became more stubborn
and refused to turn back
to you.”
4Then I thought to myself,
“These common people
act like fools,
and they have never learned
what the Lord their God
demands of them.
5So I'll go and talk to the leaders.
They know what God demands.”
But even they had decided
not to obey the Lord.
6The people have rebelled
and rejected the Lord
too many times.
So enemies will attack
like lions from the forest
or wolves from the desert.
Those enemies will watch
the towns of Judah,
and like leopards
they will tear to pieces
whoever goes outside.
Enemies Will Punish Judah
The Lord said:
7People of Judah,
how can I forgive you?
I gave you everything,
but you abandoned me
and worshiped idols.
You men go to prostitutes
and are unfaithful
to your wives.
8You are no better than animals,
and you always want sex
with someone else's wife.
9Why shouldn't I punish
the people of Judah?
10I will tell their enemies,
“Go through my vineyard.
Don't destroy the vines,
but cut off the branches,
because they are the people
who don't belong to me.”
11In every way, Judah and Israel
have been unfaithful to me.
* 12Their prophets lie and say,
“The Lord won't punish us.
We will have peace
and plenty of food.”
13They tell these lies in my name,
so now they will be killed in war
or starve to death.
14I am the Lord God All-Powerful.
Jeremiah, I will tell you
exactly what to say.
Your words will be a fire;
Israel and Judah
will be the fuel.
15People of Israel,
I have made my decision.
An army from a distant country
will attack you.
I've chosen an ancient nation,
and you won't understand
their language.
16All of them are warriors,
and their arrows bring death.
17This nation will eat your crops
and livestock;
they will leave no fruit
on your vines or fig trees.
And although you feel safe
behind thick walls,
your towns will be destroyed
and your children killed.
Israel Refused To Worship the Lord
18The Lord said:
Jeremiah, the enemy army won't kill everyone in Judah. 19And the people who survive will ask, “Why did the Lord our God do such terrible things to us?” Then tell them:
I am the Lord,
but you abandoned me
and worshiped other gods
in your own land.
Now you will be slaves
in a foreign country.
20Tell these things to each other,
you people of Judah,
you descendants of Jacob.
21 You fools! Why don't you listen
when I speak?
Why can't you understand
22 that you should worship me
with fear and trembling?
I'm the one who made the shore
to hold back the ocean.
Waves may crash on the beach,
but they can come no farther.
23You stubborn people have rebelled
and turned your backs on me.
24You refuse to say,
“Let's worship the Lord!
He's the one who sends rain
in spring and autumn
and gives us a good harvest.”
25That's why I cannot bless you!
* 26A hunter traps birds
and puts them in a cage,
but some of you trap humans
and make them your slaves.
27You are evil, and you lie and cheat
to make yourselves rich.
You are powerful
28and prosperous,
but you refuse to help the poor
get the justice they deserve.
29You need to be punished,
and so I will take revenge.
30Look at the terrible things
going on in this country.
I am shocked!
31Prophets give their messages
in the name of a false god,
my priests don't want
to serve me,
and you—my own people—
like it this way!
But on the day of disaster,
where will you turn for help?
translation_text:
Nɛr maa wia waa deŋlee
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Jɛrɛmia, gaagi Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa maa di pessi na,
di binni u kɛraa
ni u bossibaana maa na.
Di i daŋ wer na nɛkpaŋ la maa wia n deŋlee
di dɔɔ wibii,
guŋwaa, n daŋ gil
a bolzeŋ naa hina
wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.
2Haali baŋ ɔɔ ra ŋɔ,
‘Yaa hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de wibii maa la,’
ka ba hɛɛhzaa
waa wibii ɛɛwɛ.”
3N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, wibii lɛi i ra nyiŋŋia?
I tɛr ba dignaa, ka ba bɔra waa wiiwɛ,
i sunni baa werge,
ka ba waa baglaa nuuwɛ.
Ba dɔɔ sikpegiire alugɔ bii,
ba waa sɛɛwɛ gil
ba biine chɔgi,
dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia,
di gilaa ta.
4N faa fɛwɔɔrɛ, “Nɛra naa ɛɛ nyaara bɛnnɛ,
ba ɛɛ gɛnaarɛ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waa Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la ŋmɛnizi zummɛ,
ba waa kaa zum
u winyiŋŋaa gba.
5Awia, n daŋ la ba sitɔɔra be,
di ga ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa,
wibii maa, ba zum Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ,
Kɔraawiizi la banna
hum la winyiŋŋaa.”
Ka ba maa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ,
di vɛɛ u dɔɔra sɛɛi,
di vɛɛ u nua hiŋaa.
6Awia, bunyiŋ daŋ lii kɔr biini wa pig baa,
munu ge lii hɛribɔduma
wa lauri baa.
Amani daŋ chɔɔ ba bola nuuzi di guu baa,
ú chuuri unla maa
n niŋ ŋɔ ú lii chaaŋ,
dikuu ba dignikpega n nyaŋŋɛɛ,
ba ɔɔ bir har kpuu
saŋa kpila maa wia.
7Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi,
“Juda hina, bɛɛ wiarɛ ń gil tɛɛ iai?
Ii biizi vɛɛ n nua hiŋaarɛ,
ka ra kuari vuga la
n ɛɛ kumpɛɛri.
N tɛɛ n nɛraa kummaa,
ka ba ra ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ wia,
ba ni sɛnsɛnna ra chɔɔ.
8Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zagbala baŋ dɛɛzɛɛ nɛnnɛ,
ba ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu
ba lauri ba dɔŋahina haana,
di ra nyiŋŋi saŋaa saŋa maa.
9Bɛɛ wiarɛ màá tɛr ba digna,
dikuu a keŋ wiai?
Bɛɛ wiarɛ màá turgi
a keŋ hɛri naa hina bá kimɛi?
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
10N daŋ ŋɔ ba dɔma be, ‘Ií ga zuu ba grepu daazi kooni di chɔgaa,
ka ií gilɛɛ
waa chɔgaa nyaamm.
Ií kɛuri a kela waa ha,
dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
n nɛra la n waa n hora ɛɛwɛ.
11Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa wia
waa wibii dɔɔwɛ n be.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”
12Ba kanni karaa, di ŋɔ,
“Kɔraawiizi wàá ɛɛ yaa wiimaa.
Tɔɔrɔɔ maa wàá huuzi yaa,
laal ni lɔchɔgii ge
wàá chol yaa ni maa.
13Ba ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ peu,
u Wiŋɔɔlii waa hoo ba be.
Awia, gil gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ
la laŋŋi ba ni.”
14Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ,
“Dikuu a nɛra naa n ŋɔ kennaa wia,
n daŋ kpa n wiŋɔzi du i nua,
a ɛɛ lugɔ niŋ,
di fuuh baa alugɔ daazi.
15Izrɛl hina, n kpa nɛraa lii hɛhjaŋa,
bá wa lɔ ia.
Hɛri la hina n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa,
di ɛɛ faala hina,
iiŋ waa ba mɔɔri ra nuu.
16Ba hotaara ɛɛ laallɔkpegaa,
ba waa nɛra ni ra suŋ.
17Ba daŋ di ii diwee maa,
di kpu ii biibaala
ni ii biihaana.
Ba daŋ kpu ii sela,
di chɔgi ii fig ni
ii grepu daazi maa.
Ba daŋ kpa laal
di chɔgi ii bolzeŋkpega
la maa iiŋ yardɛɛ la.”
18Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“A guŋ saŋa gba,
màá dim ia.
19Di ba wa pɛɛzɔɔ lugɔ bɛɛ n baani mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ baa kennei? Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ ba bir hattɛ kpuŋ, ka ra kuari hɛrdumazi vuga ba himmaa hɛri. Awia, ba daŋ birgi yoma, di ra hum nɛra hɛrduma biini.”
20Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Sii wia naa tɛɛ Juda hina la
n ɛɛ Jekɔb naanna.
21Gɛnaa ni nfɛrnyaara,
ií keŋŋi digna ra nuu.
Ii dɔɔ siweere, ka ii waa na,
di dɔɔ digna,
ka ii waa wia ra nuu.
22Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
Bɛɛ wiarɛ ii wanna ɔmɛi?
Bɛɛ n baani ii bɔra waa sa
ń seei?
N gillɔɔ hɛri ɛɛ muuzeŋ magbɔɔ,
magbɔɔ la uŋ
wàá wer gilli maa.
A muuzeŋ nii danna lɔ
ka wàá wer gilli u ni.
Haali a nii danna lɔ werge,
ka wàá na bɔr kaali.
23Ka a nɛra naa ɛɛ dignikpega hinaa, di kpoŋ.
Ba bir hattɛ kpuŋ,
di vɛɛ n humaa.
24Ba waa ɔɔ ŋɔ bahinaa be,
‘Ií gil ya ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi.
Waabuu ɔɔ tɛɛ yaa sazau ni yuuliŋ dooŋ,
yaa pattikuna lɛɛ,
yaa na diwee werge
kuna kpai saŋa.’
25Ii wichɔgaarɛ gillɛ
ii waa a keŋ wia naa ra na,
di gil ii waa winanaa
gba ra na la.
26Biinikpola hina du n nɛra biinii,
di ɛɛ lugɔ nɛra
n ɔɔ he ŋmɛmbizi,
bá lauri zumbizi la.
27Gunla baŋ ɔɔ lauri zala su zagbɛrɛ la,
gunnɛ ba ɔɔ foozi kuna
su ba diini,
di birgi dɔɔna,
di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge,
28di ra di nɛnnɛ,
di vuh nɛnnɛ la.
Ba wichɔgaa ɛɛi waa maga dɔɔwɛ,
ba waa lalbiizi ra tɛɛ bilii
gɛɛ di di wibii ra tɛɛ nyaara.
29A waa dɛkkɛ miŋ tɛr ba digna
dikuu a keŋ wiaa?
A waa dɛkkɛ miŋ bittɛ turgi
a keŋ hɛri naa hina,
ba wichɔgaa kimaa?
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
30Wia la n na lɔ banchule,
di dɔɔ ɔnsii werge,
ɛɛ a hɛri biinii.
31N dɔgtɛɛzi waa wibii ra ŋɔ,
n kizeehina ge ra ɛɛ wia
ni ba himmaa fɔŋŋa.
Guŋ ge ɛɛ n nɛra kipar,
ka ɛrɛɛ bá ɛɛ a tunai?”

english_text:
A Warning for the People of Jerusalem
The Lord said:
1Run for your lives,
people of Benjamin.
Get out of Jerusalem.
Sound a trumpet in Tekoa
and light a signal fire
in Beth-Haccherem.
Soon you will be struck
by disaster from the north.
2Jerusalem is a lovely pasture,
3but shepherds will surround it
and divided up,
then let their flocks
eat all the grass.
4Kings will tell their troops,
“If we reach Jerusalem
in the morning,
we'll attack at noon.
But if we arrive later,
5we'll attack after dark
and destroy its fortresses.”
6I am the Lord All-Powerful,
and I will command these armies
to chop down trees
and build a ramp up to the walls
of Jerusalem.
People of Jerusalem,
I must punish you
for your injustice.
7Evil pours from your city
like water from a spring.
Sounds of injustice and violence
echo within your walls;
victims are everywhere,
wounded and dying.
8Listen to me,
you people of Jerusalem
and Judah.
I will abandon you,
and your land will become
an empty desert.
9I will tell your enemies
to leave your nation bare
like a vine stripped of grapes.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have spoken.
Jeremiah's Anger
10I have told the people
that you, Lord,
will punish them,
but they just laugh
and refuse to listen.
11Your anger against Judah
flames up inside me,
and I can't hold it in
much longer.
The Lord's Anger Will Sweep Everyone Away
The Lord answered:
Don't hold back my anger!
Let it sweep away everyone—
the children at play
and all adults,
young and old alike.
12 I'll punish the people of Judah
and give to others
their houses and fields,
as well as their wives.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
13Everyone is greedy and dishonest,
whether poor or rich.
Even the prophets and priests
cannot be trusted.
14 All they ever offer
to my deeply wounded people
are empty hopes for peace.
15They should be ashamed
of their disgusting sins,
but they don't even blush.
And so, when I punish Judah,
they will end up on the ground,
dead like everyone else.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People of Judah Rejected God's Way of Life
16The Lord said:
My people, when you stood
at the crossroads,
I told you, “Follow the road
your ancestors took,
and you will find peace.”
But you refused.
17I also sent prophets
to warn you of danger,
but when they sounded the alarm,
you paid no attention.
18So I tell all nations on earth,
“Watch what I will do!
19My people ignored me
and rejected my laws.
They planned to do evil,
and now the evil they planned
will happen to them.”
20People of Judah,
you bring me incense from Sheba
and spices from distant lands.
You offer sacrifices of all kinds.
But why bother?
I hate these gifts of yours!
21So I will put stumbling blocks
in your path,
and everyone will die,
including parents and children,
neighbors and friends.
An Army from the North
22The Lord said,
“Look toward the north,
where a powerful nation
has prepared for war.
23Its well-armed troops are cruel
and never show mercy.
Their galloping horses sound
like ocean waves
pounding on the shore.
This army will attack you,
lovely Jerusalem.”
24Then the people said,
“Just hearing about them
makes us tremble with fear,
and we twist and turn in pain
like a woman giving birth.”
25The Lord said,
“Don't work in your fields
or walk along the roads.
It's too dangerous.
The enemy is well armed
26and attacks without warning.
So mourn, my people, as though
your only child had died.
Wear clothes made of sackcloth
and roll in the ash pile.”
The Lord's People Must Be Tested
The Lord said:
27Jeremiah, test my people
as though they were metal.
28And you'll find they are hard
like bronze and iron.
They are stubborn rebels,
always spreading lies.
* 29-30Silver can be purified
in a fiery furnace,
but my people are too wicked
to be made pure,
and so I have rejected them.
translation_text:
Dɔma n bar Jɛrusalɛm wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Bɛnjamin dee, ií chɔ ra nyiŋŋi ii miibɔɔni!
Ií chɔ lii Jɛrusalɛm biini!
Ií huuh bensunoniina Tɛkua biini,
di chem niŋ
Bɛf Hakɛrɛm biini,
di ra bagli lugɔ siaahmuu!
Dikuubɛɛwiai, hɛhchɔg lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ di ra ba,
di chum werge maa.
2Bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm wessoo werge,
ka ba daŋ chɔguu.
3Laallɔɔra daŋ ba lugɔ penɔɔna ni ba peeza, di wa lɔ a bolzeŋ,
di baŋzi ba tanti diini
bar u maa.
Bɛl maa daŋ so
bɔr la unna nyiŋŋi.
4Ba daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Ií ɛɛ laal sirya yá ga lɔ baa,
ií izi ya ga yoo
baa wibaŋa ni!’
Ka ba daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Saŋa kaalɔɔrɛ,
wiizi ge zuu tuŋ.
5Awia, yaa daŋ ga yoo baa hahmuŋa ni,
di lɔ baa, di purgi
ba diikpega maa!’ ”
6Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ,
“Ií teŋri daazi ta,
di ta pizenaa
bar Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii maa,
di wer tinni zuu u biini.
N daŋ tɛr a bolzeŋ naa hina digna,
dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛsunnaa su
u biinii werge maa.
7Gunla kɔlɔŋ n ɔɔ ra bul nii la,
gunnɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina
wichɔgaa ɛɛi du.
N nuu naari ni chɔgaarɛ a bolzeŋ biini,
wiila ni dɔŋa pira dui
bɛnnɛ n na na.
8Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií ra nuu n wiŋɔzi naa nɛnnɛ,
di guŋ lɛi, n daŋ kizi ia ha,
di gil ii hɛri naa maa birgi diŋgela,
nɛr maa wàá ka du de.”
9Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ,
“N daŋ gil Izrɛl hina dɔma gbaari baa
gunla baŋ ɔɔ
kaari daanɔna maa
lii u ni la.
Awia, a dɛkkɔ ii lɛɛ nɛr la maa iin niŋ wer lɛɛ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, saŋa
haa du denii.”
10Mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia sɛɛ, di ŋɔ,
“Anɛɛ ń ŋɔ wia tɛɛ,
di karfuuwɛi?
Anɛɛ n niŋ nuu n benei?
Ba ɛɛ dignikpega hinaa,
di vɛɛ i amaniye la nuui.
Ba ra mam gunla hiŋ ŋɔ n be
lugɔ n ŋɔ tɛɛ baa labuu.
11Gunla i baaŋ n na fuuh ba ni la,
gunnɛ n gba
baan na fuuh ba ni,
màá ka wer lau n hiŋ.”
Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,
“Gil n baaŋ fuuh bichalli la n du ŋmɛnizenaa
ni biipɔllaa la maa
n chaalɛɛ ni.
Ba daŋ lauri baala ni ba haana kaali,
haali nabɔnzi la maa
n zɛŋŋɛ werge maa gba.
12Di n waa tɛr banla n du hɛri naa digna,
ba diini daŋ birgi
nɛra baŋhina hora,
haali ba kooni ni ba haana maa gba.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
13Ii nɛdumazi ni ii nɛzenaa maanii
ra fini nɛraa bá nyɛɛli.
Haali n dɔgtɛɛzi ni n kizeehina maa
gba ra dar nɛra.
14Ba ɔɔ na n nɛra ŋmɛraa,
ka ra yiraa bɔforgaa,
Ba ɔɔ ŋɔu, ‘Bampirsɔna du denii,
bampirsɔna du denii,’
ka bampirsɔna waa hoo.
15Hiihzi ɔɔ lau baabuu,
dikuu ba wikuna naa wiaa?
Akai, a guŋ waa baa ra ɛɛ hiihzi,
ba baga lɛi.
Awia, ba daŋ chol gunla baŋhina n cholle la.
Di n wa tɛr ba digna,
ba wia maa daŋ tuŋ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
16Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Ií chi ŋmɛnichechema ka binni na,
di pɛɛzi faala ŋmɛnizi bɔr.
Ií pɛɛzi unla n wesse bɔr, di ra hiŋuu,
ii daŋ na heezaa.
Ka ii ŋɔ, ‘Yaa wàá hiŋuu.’
17N hum n dɔgtɛɛzii lugɔ tauduura,
bá wa karfi ia lugɔ
siaahmu ra bau,
ka ii waa nuuwɛ.
18Awia, hɛssi hina, ií ra nuu!
Ií pessi gunla n niŋ wa
huuzi n nɛra.
19Hɛri, a nuu!
N kpa hɛhchɔgrɛ di ra ba
ń wa ta nɛra naa ni,
dikuu ba jinachɔgaa
ni baŋ vɛɛ n baglaa
ni n wiŋɔzi wia.
20N baga lɛi ii daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la iiŋ kpawɛɛ lii Siiba hɛri ba
gɛɛ dɔzi tiuzaa kuna la
iiŋ kpawɛɛ
lii hɛhjaŋa ba la.
Màá lɛɛ ii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa,
awia wan pattɛ.
21Awia, n daŋ gil nɛra naa
lɔɔzi naazi chogli.
Mɛɛwaa ni maawaa
ani biizi daŋ siuzi.
Gunnɛ bá dammuzi
ni ba dɔŋahina gba siuzi.”
22Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií na, laallɔɔra lii
wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag
hɛrii di ra ba.
Ba du hɛrkpeg hina
n du bɔɔnɛɛrɛ bɔkpega.
23Ba kpogli hozi ni kandaazii,
ba dɔɔ sikpegiire werge,
ba waa nɛra ni ra suŋ.
Ba tinni ba zagraa
a ra gbɔgzi lugɔ
muuzeŋ n na kɔɔ,
ba ra bau alugɔ laallɔɔra n ɛɛ laal sirya,
bá wa lɔ ia.”
24Jɛrusalɛm hina ŋɔ,
“Yaa nuu ba wiarɛ,
yaa bɔra huah.
Biinichɔg werge lau yaa
lugɔ hilula n lɔ haaŋ.
25Ií gilɛɛ wa lii ra la kooni
gɛɛ di waa vol ŋmɛnizi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ii dɔma kpogli dɔŋkunaa,
ɔnsii werge su bɔr maa.”
26Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u nɛra be,
“Ií kpa gbɔglɔnzi laali,
di lii chɔɔ hɔɔhri biini
di ra billi.
Ií ra chɛɛhgi werge, sinii ra lii,
alugɔ iin niŋ wii
biibambikpaŋ siu,
dikuubɛɛwiai, unla n na ba
ú wa kpu ia la,
daŋ wa pirgi ia, di lɔ ia.
27Awia, Jɛrɛmia, ɛɛ baa na
gunla baŋ ɔɔ kpa
lugbii du niŋ di lizi u doŋa la,
di na gunla baŋ duwɛɛ.
28Ba maa ɛɛ nɛkpoŋlaare,
di ra chɔgi nɛra sɔna.
Ba kpekkoo lugɔ danyɛ ni lugbii,
di vol ra fini nɛra.
29N nɛra ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ lugbii
gɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋu la n waa wer,
haali di ba lɔ zugze,
a nine mazi werge gba,
ka a waa ɔɔ ŋmɛɛri.
A kuaraa ɔɔ ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.
Gunnɛ n nɛra biinikpola
wàá wer lii ba ni la.
30Nɛra ra yir baabuu
saliŋhuŋŋa la baŋ vɛɛwɛ tau,
dikuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi
n vɛɛ baa ta wia.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Speaks in the Temple
(Jeremiah 26.1-6)
1-3The Lord told me to stand by the gate of the temple and tell the people who were going in that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
Pay attention, people of Judah! Change your ways and start living right, then I will let you keep on living in your own country. 4Don't fool yourselves! My temple is here in Jerusalem, but that doesn't mean I will protect you. 5I will keep you safe only if you change your ways and are fair and honest with each other. 6Stop taking advantage of foreigners, orphans, and widows. Don't kill innocent people. And stop worshiping other gods. 7Then I will let you enjoy a long life in this land I gave your ancestors.
8But just look at what is happening! You put your trust in worthless lies. 9You steal and murder; you lie in court and are unfaithful in marriage. You worship idols and offer incense to Baal, when these gods have never done anything for you. 10And then you come into my temple and worship me! Do you think I will protect you so that you can go on sinning? 11 You are thieves, and you have made my temple your hideout. But I've seen everything you have done.
12 Go to Shiloh, where my sacred tent once stood. Take a look at what I did there. My people Israel sinned, and so I destroyed Shiloh!
13While you have been sinning, I have been trying to talk to you, but you refuse to listen. 14Don't think this temple will protect you. Long ago I told your ancestors to build it and worship me here, but now I have decided to tear it down, just as I destroyed Shiloh. 15And as for you, people of Judah, I'm going to send you away from my land, just as I sent away the people of Ephraim and the other northern tribes.
Punishment for Worshiping Other Gods
16Jeremiah, don't pray for these people! I, the Lord, would refuse to listen. 17Do you see what the people of Judah are doing in their towns and in the streets of Jerusalem? 18 Children gather firewood, their fathers build fires, and their mothers mix dough to bake bread for the goddess they call the Queen of Heaven. They even offer wine sacrifices to other gods, just to insult me. 19But they are not only insulting me; they are also harming themselves by doing these shameful things.
20And now, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will flood Judah with my fiery anger until nothing is left—no people or animals, no trees or crops.
It Is Useless To Offer Sacrifices
21The Lord told me to say to the people of Judah:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, but I won't accept sacrifices from you. So don't even bother bringing them to me. You might as well just cook the meat for yourselves.
22At the time I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I didn't command them to offer sacrifices to me. 23Instead, I told them, “If you listen to me and do what I tell you, I will be your God, you will be my people, and all will go well for you.” 24But your ancestors refused to listen. They were stubborn, and whenever I wanted them to go one way, they always went the other. 25Ever since your ancestors left Egypt, I have been sending my servants the prophets to speak for me. 26But you have ignored me and become even more stubborn and sinful than your ancestors ever were!
Slaughter Valley
The Lord said:
27Jeremiah, no matter what you do, the people won't listen. 28So you must say to them:
People of Judah, I am the Lord your God, but you have refused to obey me, and you didn't change when I punished you. And now, you no longer even pretend to be faithful to me.
29Shave your head bald
and throw away the hair.
Sing a funeral song
on top of a barren hill.
You people have made me angry,
and I have abandoned you.
30You have disobeyed me by putting your disgusting idols in my temple, and now the temple itself is disgusting to me. 31 At Topheth in Hinnom Valley you have built altars where you kill your children and burn them as sacrifices to other gods. I would never think of telling you to do this. 32So watch out! Someday that place will no longer be called Topheth or Hinnom Valley. It will be called Slaughter Valley, because you will bury your dead there until you run out of room, 33and then bodies will lie scattered on the ground. Birds and wild animals will come and eat, and no one will be around to scare them off. 34 When I am finished with your land, there will be deathly silence in the empty ruins of Jerusalem and the towns of Judah—no happy voices, no sounds of parties or wedding celebrations.
translation_text:
Jɛrɛmia n ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia
1Wia naabuu Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Jɛrɛmia be, 2“Chi n Dia dominuuzeŋ sii amaniye naa.
Ŋɔ Juda hina be lugɔ banla maa n ga dominuuzenaa naa di zuu ra jaamiŋ la ra nuu. 3Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Ií char ii manni ni ii wiɛɛlaa, ka ń gil ii du bɔnnaa. 4Ií gilɛɛ waa yardi daraa wiŋɔzi, di ra ŋɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Diarɛ keŋ, Kɔraawiizi Diarɛ keŋ!’ 5Wibii maa, di ii char ii manni ni ii wiɛɛlaa, di ra di dɔŋa wibii, 6di ii waa hɔɔhra, lalbiizi ani luhaana ra fini, di ii waa kpu nɛra la n waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ, di ii waa kuari vuga la n niŋ chɔg ia, 7guŋwaa, n daŋ gil ii du a hɛri naa miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ii naabaala ni bampirsɔna, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. 8Ií ra nuu, ii yardi kara wiŋɔzi la n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛɛ.
9Ii ra ŋmɛɛu, di ra kpu nɛra, di ra sɛm, di ra hɛɛhzi ka ra kanni kara, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ra tɛɛ vug Baal, di ra kuari vuga la iiŋ faa waa zummɛ. 10Wia la miŋ kiiwee ii ra ɛɛ, ka ɔɔ wa chi n see, n himmaa Dia biini di ra ŋɔ lugɔ wiimaa wàá huuzi ia. 11Ií ra fɛu lugɔ n Dia ɛɛ ŋmɛɛna suahribɔttɛa? Ka n na pessi ii wiɛɛlaarɛ! Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
12Ií la Silo la miŋ faa felee lizi, bá ra jaamiŋ de la, di ga na gunla miŋ chɔguu, dikuu n nɛra Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa wia. 13Iinna ɛɛ annii naa maa la, n faa karfi iabuu digiidigii, ka ii waa nuuwɛ. N yir ia ka ii waa sɛɛwɛ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 14Awia, gunla miŋ ɛɛ Silo la, gunnɛ n kpa ɛɛ n Dia naa iiŋ dɛllɛɛ, n Sɔŋ sag u ni naa, bɔr la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ii ni ii mɛɛwaa la. 15N daŋ duŋŋi ii Juda hina lii n be gunla miŋ duŋŋi ii lulla Izrɛl hina la n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
A nɛra dignikpega wia
16Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Jɛrɛmia, gilɛɛ waa suŋŋi wiizi ra tɛɛ nɛra naa. Gilɛɛ waa wii gɛɛ di chi ba naazi suŋŋi wiizi ra tɛɛ baa. Gilɛɛ waa fɔrgiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, màá nuu. 17Haa gunla banna ɛɛ Juda bolzenaa ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biine nawɛɛa? 18Bichalli paagi daazii, ba mɛɛwaa chem ninzeŋ, haana ŋmir sau di ɔɔzi paanuuzi tɛɛ vug la banna yir Chiŋ Wiche. Ba yiili sinnɛ ta vuga, di chagziŋ. 19Ka n baannɛ ba ra fuuhwaa? Akai! Ba himmaanii ba ra tɔɔri, bá ŋmaabi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
20Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ gil n baaŋ fuuh werge bɔnnaa ni newea, sela, kooni daazi ani a hɛri pattikuna ni alugɔ niŋ. U daŋ fuuh, ba wàá wer sɔɔnuu.
21N nɛra Izrɛl hina, màá lɛɛ ii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa maa. Awia, di ii ɔɔ wa daali a ola, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií ra hee a maa! 22Miŋ faa lizi ii naabaala lii Ijip hɛri di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa la, mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni mbusuzi lizaa bɛŋ wia lɛi, 23ka kenne n ŋɔ tɛɛ baa, ‘Ií ra hiŋiŋ, ń ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iin ninna hum, ii ge ɛɛ n nɛra. Ií ra hiŋ ŋmɛnizi la maa miŋ bagli ia la, ii wiimaa kuari.’ 24Ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá nuu gɛɛ di hiŋ guŋ, ka kpa ŋmɛnɛɛ la n waa dɛkkɛ, di kpoŋ di dɔɔ dignikpega, di ra ɛɛ ba kipar. Di bir la har ka gil see laŋaa. 25Di lii saŋa la ii naabaala n lii Ijip hɛri di wa lii ni zinaa, hɔpizi biimaa, aŋ hum n dɔgtɛɛzii ii be digiidigii. 26Ka n nɛra waa sɛɛwɛ bá nuu tɛŋ, ka dɔɔ dignikpega, di ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge maa kaali ba naabaala.
27Jɛrɛmia, di i haŋ ŋɔ ba be annii naa maa, ka ba wàá nuu. Di i yir baa ge, ba wàá sɛɛ. 28Awia, ŋɔ ba be lugɔ ba hɛri naa hina waa sɛɛwɛ bá hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la nua gɛɛ di nuu baglaa. Wibii tunnɔɔ, ba waa kaa ra ŋɔ u wia gba. 29Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií gbaari ii nyuhuna, di kpaa ta. Ií tinni giŋgimee nyuuni di ra yir lee yira. N vɛɛ n nɛraa, dikuu n baaŋ n na fuuh ba ni wia.
Nɛkpui Werge Waluu wia
30Juda hina ɛɛ wikunaa n sibɔɔ, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. Ba kpa ba vuga la miŋ kiiwe labuu wa chiŋŋi n Dia la n sɔŋ n sag u ni la biinii, di chɔguu. 31Ba ma mbusu lizibɔttɛ Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu biini, di ra yiruu Tɔfɛf, bá kpa ba biibaala ni biihaana di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa u ni. Miŋ lɛi ŋɔ bá ra ɛɛ guŋ. N faa waa gunna fɛ gba. 32Awia, ii zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ saŋa ra bau, nɛra wàá kaa waa yiruu Tɔfɛf gɛɛ Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu, ka ba daŋ jaa ra yiruu Nɛkpui Werge Waluu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daŋ hug nɛra de guŋŋ bɔr wàá kaa wa du de. 33Ba bɔrahɔna daŋ birgi diwee tɛɛ zumbizi ni pir sela. Nɛr maa wàá du de di duŋŋaa. 34A hɛri maa daŋ birgi hɛribɔduma. N daŋ tɔ bɔsɔna ni hindii Juda bolzenaa ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biini. Haŋfalaa diuzenaa dii bɔsɔna kɔɔi wàá ka du de.”

english_text:
1Then the bones of the dead kings of Judah and their officials will be dug up, along with the bones of the priests, the prophets, and everyone else in Jerusalem 2who loved and worshiped the sun, moon, and stars. These bones will be scattered and left lying on the ground like trash, where the sun and moon and stars can shine on them.
3Some of you people of Judah will be left alive, but I will force you to go to foreign countries, and you will wish you were dead. I, the Lord God All-Powerful, have spoken.
The People Took the Wrong Road
4The Lord said:
People of Jerusalem,
when you stumble and fall,
you get back up,
and if you take a wrong road,
you turn around and go back.
5So why do you refuse
to come back to me?
Why do you hold so tightly
to your false gods?
6I listen carefully,
but none of you admit
that you've done wrong.
Without a second thought,
you run down the wrong road
like horses running blindly
into battle.
7Storks, doves, swallows,
and thrushes
all know when it's time
to fly away for the winter
and when to come back.
But you, my people,
don't know what I demand.
8You say, “We are wise
because we have the teachings
and laws of the Lord.”
But I say that your teachers
have turned my words
into lies!
9Your wise men
have rejected what I say,
and so they have no wisdom.
Now they will be trapped
and put to shame;
they won't know what to do.
10 I'll give their wives and fields
to strangers.
Everyone is greedy and dishonest,
whether poor or rich.
Even the prophets and priests
cannot be trusted.
11 All they ever offer
to my deeply wounded people
are empty hopes for peace.
12They should be ashamed
of the way they live,
but they don't even blush.
And so, when I punish Judah,
they will end up on the ground,
dead like everyone else.
13I will wipe them out.
They are vines without grapes;
fig trees without figs or leaves.
They have not done a thing
that I told them!
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People and Their Punishment
14The people of Judah
say to each other,
“What are we waiting for?
Let's run to a town with walls
and die there.
We rebelled against the Lord,
and we were sentenced to die
by drinking poison.
15We had hoped for peace
and a time of healing,
but all we got was terror.
16Our enemies have reached
the town of Dan in the north,
and the snorting of their horses
makes us tremble with fear.
The enemy will destroy Jerusalem
and our entire nation.
No one will survive.”
17“Watch out!” the Lord says.
“I'm sending poisonous snakes
to attack you,
and no one can stop them.”
Jeremiah Mourns for His People
18I'm burdened with sorrow
and feel like giving up.
19In a foreign land
my people are crying.
Listen! You'll hear them say,
“Has the Lord deserted Zion?
Is he no longer its king?”
I hear the Lord reply,
“Why did you make me angry
by worshiping useless idols?”
20The people complain,
“Spring and summer
have come and gone,
but still the Lord
hasn't rescued us.”
21My people are crushed,
and so is my heart.
I am horrified and mourn.
22If medicine and doctors
may be found in Gilead,
why aren't my people healed?
translation_text:
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “A saŋa, ba daŋ wigzi Juda koora, u nabɔnzi, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, u dɔgtɛɛzi ani nɛra la maa n faa du Jɛrusalɛm biini hoga lii ba ŋmama biine. 2Wiizi ra lɔ a ni. Baagu ni chinchiŋwilaa la baŋ faa nɔŋŋɛɛ di ra humaa, di ra hiŋaa, di ra pɛɛzaa, di ra kuaraa la ge ra chaani a ni. Ba wàá chaalaa gɛɛ di hugaa, ka a daŋ chɔɔ lugɔ kpaga di yaari hɛri maa. 3Hɛrchɔgii naa nɛra la n niŋ ka, di du bɔra la maa miŋ duŋŋi baa du la, danna nyiŋŋi lugɔ bá siuzi kaali ba de dui. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.”
Wichɔgaa ni dignitɛraa wia
4Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ tɛɛ u nɛra,
“Di baala chollo, ba waa ɔɔ kaa izaa?
Di baal leuwo,
waa ɔɔ kaa biraa?
5Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ nɛra naa bir har kpunnɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina
ɔɔ ra bir ba hara
di ra kpunnɛi?
Ba dɛlli vugaa,
di vɛɛ lugɔ ba bir ba n be.
6N keŋŋi dignaa di nuu ba be nɛnnɛ,
ka ba waa wibii ra ŋɔ.
Bɛl maa biini waa chɔkkɛ u wichɔgaa wia
ka ra ŋɔ, ‘Bɛɛ n ɛɛi?’
Bɛl maa kpa u kipar ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ,
di ra ɛɛ wia la n paruu alugɔ
zagu n ɔɔ chɔ gaa zuu
laal biini gunla.
7Niilaaraazi gba zum saŋazii,
kommazi, koŋkoroŋbizi
ani kagchagaa zum saŋazi la
an niŋ la bɔfalaa.
Ka n nɛra waa,
waa zum wii la minna nyiŋŋi.
8Ɛrɛɛ ii wer ŋɔ lugɔ ii dɔɔ nunzumaa,
di zum n Gbɔgnɛi?
Ii na, karchizi la wia n waa wibii dɔɔwɛ,
lawaabuu birgi.
9Nunzunna daŋ di hiihzi.
Ba bugmoore, di ɛɛ kinchaŋ,
dikuu baŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii wia.
Bɛɛ nunzumaa ba kaa dɔɔi?
10Awia, n daŋ kpa ba kooni tɛɛ nɛfalaa,
di kpa ba haana ge
tɛɛ badumazi.
Ba nɛzenaa ni nɛdumazi maanii
ra fini nɛra bá na kebee.
Haali n dɔgtɛɛzi ni n kizeehina
maanii ra fini nɛra.
11Ba ɔɔ na n nɛra ŋmɛraa,
ka ra yiraa bɔforgaa,
Ba ɔɔ ŋɔu lugɔ bampirsɔna du denii,
bampirsɔna du denii,
ka bampirsɔna waa hoo.
12Hiihzi ɔɔ lau baabuu dikuu ba wikuna naa wiaa?
Akai, a guŋ waa
baa dɔɔwɛ hiihzi,
ba baga lɛi,
ba waa ɔɔ willi
ba nyuuni gba.
Awia, di n wa tɛr ba digna,
ba daŋ chol
gunla baŋhina
n cholle la,
ba wia maa daŋ tuŋ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
13N daŋ chɔgi ba pattikuna maa,
grepu daazi wàá nɔŋ.
Fig daazi wàá nɔŋ,
a paŋhoori maa ge hil.
Anla miŋ tɛɛ baa la maanii
ń bir lɛɛ ba be.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
14Kɔraawiizi nɛra ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yaa so ɛnnɛi?
Ií chaali,
ya chɔ kaali a bolzeŋkpega,
yaa wia ga tuŋ de!
Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la chɔgi yaa wiimaanii, yá siuzi,
u tɛɛ yaabuu nii la n dɔɔ siri,
yaa nyɔɔ,
dikuu yaa n ɛɛ wichɔgaa
zuu u ni wia.
15Yaa faa dɔɔ bampirsɔna tamiirɛ,
ka winanii maa waa ballɛ,
yaa dɔɔ chaai ge tamii,
ka guŋ saŋaa
ɔnsii werge du de.
16Yaa dɔma la teŋ zuu Dan bolzeŋ la biinii tuŋ,
yaa ra nuu ba zagra
n na lɔ a miizizi.
Ba zagra ra wii,
ɔnsii lau a hɛri nɛra maa.
Yaa dɔma ballɔɔ bá wa chɔgi yaa hɛri
ni bolzenaa ni
a nɛra maa nyaamm.”
17Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ií ra du tau,
n daŋ gil ii dɔma la n ɛɛwɛ
lugɔ hɛrikuna la n dɔɔ siri,
a waa pɛssaa dɔɔwɛ la,
wa lɔ ia.”
Jɛrɛmia biini n chɔkkɛ dikuu u nɛra wia
18N biinichɔg waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ,
n tamii tuŋ, n bɔra huah.
19A nuu n nɛra naa n du hɛhjaŋa
n na chɛɛhgi,
“Kɔraawiizi waa hoo Ziɔnnɛ gɛɛ?
U koori waa kaa
du de gɛɛ?”
Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ ba koori ŋɔ,
“Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ba fuuh n baaŋ ni ba nonee kuŋkuaraa
ni ba vuga la miŋ kiiwe,
baŋ kpawɛɛ lii hɛrdumazi
ba lai?”
20A nɛra wii di ra ŋɔ,
“Kuna kumaa saŋa bɛrɔɔrɛ,
lumaŋa ge tuŋ,
di yaa haa
waa lɛɛi nawɛɛ.”
21Awia, Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ,
“N biini chɔkkɔɔ,
dikuu n nɛra biine
n chɔkkɛ wia.
N na wiiu ni biinichɔg werge.
22Di tagzi ni tagɛɛra du Giliadii,
ka bɛɛ n baani n nɛra
waa chaai nawɛɛi?”

english_text:
1I wish that my eyes
were fountains of tears,
so I could cry day and night
for my people
who were killed.
2I wish I could go into the desert
and find a hiding place
from all who are treacherous
and unfaithful to God.
The Lord Answers Jeremiah
3The Lord replied:
Lies come from the mouths
of my people,
like arrows from a bow.
With each dishonest deed
their power increases,
and not one of them will admit
that I am God.
4Jeremiah, all your friends
and relatives
tell lies about you,
so don't trust them.
5They wear themselves out,
always looking for a new way
to cheat their friends.
6Everyone takes advantage
of everyone else,
and no one will admit
that I am God.
7And so I will purify
the hearts of my people
just as gold is purified
in a furnace.
I have no other choice.
8They say they want peace,
but this lie is deadly,
like an arrow that strikes
when you least expect it.
9Give me one good reason
not to punish them
as they deserve.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have spoken.
Jeremiah Weeps for His People
10I weep for the pastureland
in the hill country.
It's so barren and scorched
that no one travels there.
No cattle can be found there,
and birds and wild animals
have all disappeared.
11I heard the Lord reply,
“When I am finished,
Jerusalem and the towns of Judah
will be piles of ruins
where only jackals live.”
Why the Land Was Destroyed
12I said to the Lord, “None of us can understand why the land has become like an uncrossable desert. Won't you explain why?”
13The Lord said:
I destroyed the land because the people disobeyed me and rejected my laws and teachings. 14They were stubborn and worshiped Baal, just as their ancestors did. 15So I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, promise them poison to eat and drink. 16I'll scatter them in foreign countries that they and their ancestors have never even heard of. Finally, I will send enemy soldiers to kill every last one of them.
The Women Who Are Paid To Weep
17The Lord All-Powerful said,
“Make arrangements now
for the women who are paid
to weep at funerals,
especially the women
who can cry the loudest.”
18The people answered,
“Let them come quickly
and cry for us,
until our own eyes
are flooded with tears.
19Now those of us on Zion cry,
‘We are ruined!
We can't stand the shame.
Our homes have been destroyed,
and we must leave our land.’
20“We ask you women
to pay attention
to what the Lord says.
We will teach you a funeral song
that you can teach
your daughters and friends:
21‘We were in our fortress,
but death sneaked in
through our windows.
It even struck down
children at play
and our strongest young men.’
22“The Lord has told us
the ground will be covered
with dead bodies,
like ungathered stalks of grain
or manure in a field.”
What the Lord Likes Best
23The Lord says:
Don't brag about your wisdom
or strength or wealth.
24 If you feel you must brag,
then have enough sense
to brag about worshiping me,
the Lord.
What I like best
is showing kindness,
justice, and mercy
to everyone on earth.
25-26Someday I will punish the nations of Egypt, Edom, Ammon, and Moab, and the tribes of the desert. The men of these nations are circumcised, but they don't worship me. And it's the same with you people of Judah. Your bodies are circumcised, but your hearts are unchanged.
translation_text:
1Jɛrɛmia bir ŋɔ,
“N nyuu faa ɛɛ lugɔ bule,
n sinii ge ɛɛ lugɔ
nii n na pal!
N daŋ vii wii bɔchaaŋ ni hahmuŋa maa,
dikuu baŋ kpu n nɛra wia.
2N vii wettoo na duuribɔr
hɛribɔduma biini,
n daŋ vii lii n nɛra naa be,
di ga du de.
Ba maa wia waa wibii dɔɔwɛ,
ba ɛɛ vugkuara
ni sɔsɔgɔ hinaa.
3A ba ɛɛ siryaa bá kanni kara,
kara bɛnnɛ su a hɛri maa,
wibii waa hoo.”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N nɛra ɔɔ ra ɛɛ
wichɔgaarɛ digiidigii,
ba waa zummɛ lugɔ
minuu Kɔraawiizi la
ban ninna hum.
4Jɛrɛmia, a du i dammuzi tau,
gilɛɛ waa yardi ii lulla gba.
Ba bɛl maa ɛɛ nɛdattii,
i dammu maa ge
ɛɛ nɛzɔɔzi.
5Nɛr ni u dammu ɔɔ ra dar dɔŋaa,
ba bɛl maa wàá ŋɔ
wibii tɛɛ u dɔŋ.
Ba nuuzi zum karaa werge,
ba ra kuuh bahinaa
ni wichɔgaa ɛɛi.
6I du kara baambaannɛ,
dikuu ba nɛdaraa wia,
ba vɛɛ n tɔgzaarɛ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
7Awia, Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ,
“N daŋ lizi ba doŋa, di ɛɛ baa na,
alugɔ baŋ ɔɔ du lugbii niŋ,
bá lizi u doŋa la.
Di guŋ lɛi, ɛrɛɛ ń kaa ɛɛ n nɛra naa,
dikuu ba wichɔgaa naa wiai?
8Ba nuuzuŋŋa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hobichɔgaa,
ba ɔɔ ra kanni karaa
saŋaa saŋa maa.
Nuusum bɛnnɛ ba dɔɔ tɛɛ dɔŋa,
ka ba wiŋɔzi maa
ɔɔ ɛɛ sidɛɛzii,
ba ra he dɔŋa.
9A waa dɛkkɛ miŋ tɛr ba digna
dikuu keŋ wiaa?
A waa dɛkkɛ miŋ turgi
keŋ hɛri naa
hina a kimaa?”
10Denii Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ, “N daŋ lɔ wile, di wii tɛɛ bizenaa
ni sela diiribɔra maa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, a maanii hillɛ.
Nɛr maa ge waa kaa ra vol a biine,
haa ɔɔ kaa nuu
sel maa gbɔga.
Zumbizi maa zaah kaali,
pir sela ge maa chɔ kaali.”
11Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “N daŋ gil Jɛrusalɛm purgi chɔɔ kulululu,
di birgi hohobiazi duuribɔr,
di gil Juda bolzenaa purgi chɔɔ burburbur,
nɛr maa wàá kaa ra zuua.”
12Denii n pɛɛzi, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ a hɛri chɔgi, di hil lugɔ hɛribɔduma, nɛr maa wàá kaa ra vol u biinei? Anɛɛ n dɔɔ nunzuma ú zum keŋ zɛɛi? Anɛɛ i bagli u zɛɛ tɛɛ, ú bagluu tɛɛ nɛrai?”
13Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Kennaa ɛɛwɔɔ, dikuu n nɛra n vɛɛ n baglaa la miŋ bagli baa la. Ba waa n nua hiŋŋɛ gɛɛ di hiŋ n Gbɔg. 14Ka ba kpoŋŋoo di ra kuari vug Baala, gunla ba mɛɛwaa n bagli baa la. 15Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la daŋ gil a nɛra naa di diukpola, di nyɔɔ nii la n dɔɔ siri. 16N daŋ duŋŋi baa yaari hɛssi la, ba ni ba naabaala n waa zummɛ, di kpa tokobi duŋŋi baa guŋŋ di wa kpu baa.”
Jɛrusalɛm hina n wiiwe ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa wia
17Wia naabuu Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la kaa ŋɔ,
“Lɔ nfɛrɛ na di lii wii naa
n na ɛɛ naa biini!
Yir haana la n zum lee wiraa,
banla n zum wiraa nɛnnɛ.”
18Denii a nɛra ŋɔ,
“Ií ŋɔ ba be bá hahzi
wa yir liyir tɛɛ yaa,
di ra ba saŋa la yaa sinii
n niŋ waa pal.”
19Ií ra nuu Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina wiraa,
“Yaa wia chɔkkɔɔ!
Yaa di hiihzii werge!
A dɛkkɔ yaa n lii yaa hɛri naa biini,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba purgi
yaa diini maanii.”
20Denii n ŋɔ, “Haana, ií keŋŋi digna di ra nuu
Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔzi.
Ií bagli ii biihaana gunla banna wii lee,
di kaa bagli ii
dammuzi liyir.
21Siu ga tokorozii
zuu yaa diikpegaa,
di kpu yaa bichalli la n du ŋmɛnizenaa,
di kaa kpu yaa
biipɔllaa la n du bossibaana.
22Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,
‘Lalaa yaari bɔr maanii, di chɔɔ kulululu
lugɔ baŋ paa
nabina dau koo,
di kaa chɔɔ lugɔ baŋ kuugi sɔgmia yaari,
nɛr maa waa hoo u chaalaa.’ ”
23Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Nunzunna, ií gilɛɛ ra jigsi, dikuu ii nunzuma wia.
Fɔŋŋa hina, ii gilɛɛ ra jigsi,
dikuu ii fɔŋŋa wia.
Dɔɔna, ii gilɛɛ ra jigsi,
dikuu ii daama wia.
24Ka nɛr la maa n na jigsi,
ú ra jigsi dikuu uŋ zum
wia zɛɛ, di zum lugɔ
minuu Kɔraawiizi.
Gunla miŋ nɔŋŋi nɛra,
di ra ɛɛ winanaa,
di ra di wibii,
di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa
hɛri naa biini.
Wia naabuu ra pariŋ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
25Saŋa bɛl ra bau min niŋ tɛr banla waa maa n teŋri ba hɛna bɛŋ digna. 26Ijip, Juda, Ɛdɔm, Ammɔn, Moab hina ani banla maa n du hɛribɔduma, di du hɛhjaŋa. A hɛssi naa hina maa wia waa wibii dɔɔwɛ n be, haali baŋ teŋri ba hɛna, di ra bagli n ni baa nuukpaŋ la, ka ba ni Izrɛl hina maa waa a nuukpaŋ hiŋŋɛ.”

english_text:
The Lord Talks about Idols
1-2The Lord said:
Listen to me,
you people of Israel.
Don't follow the customs
of those nations
who become frightened
when they see something strange
happen in the sky.
3Their religion is worthless!
They chop down a tree,
carve the wood into an idol,
4cover it with silver and gold,
and then nail it down
so it won't fall over.
5An idol is no better
than a scarecrow.
It can't speak,
and it has to be carried,
because it can't walk.
Why worship an idol
that can't help or harm you?
Jeremiah Praises the Lord
6Our Lord, great and powerful,
you alone are God.
7 You are King of the nations.
Everyone should worship you.
No human anywhere on earth
is wiser than you.
8Idols are worthless,
and anyone who worships them
is a fool!
9Idols are made by humans.
A carver shapes the wood.
A metalworker hammers out
a covering of gold from Uphaz
or of silver from Tarshish.
Then the idol is dressed
in blue and purple clothes.
10You, Lord, are the only true
and living God.
You will rule for all time.
When you are angry
the earth shakes,
and nations are destroyed.
11You told me to say
that idols did not create
the heavens and the earth,
and that you, the Lord,
will destroy every idol.
12With your wisdom and power
you created the earth
and spread out the heavens.
13The waters in the heavens roar
at your command.
You make clouds appear—
you send the winds
from your storehouse
and make lightning flash
in the rain.
14People who make idols
are so stupid!
They will be disappointed,
because their false gods
are not alive.
15Idols are merely a joke,
and when the time is right,
they will be destroyed.
16But you, Israel's God,
created all things,
and you chose Israel
to be your very own.
Your name is the Lord
All-Powerful.
Judah Will Be Thrown from Its Land
17I said to the people of Judah,
“Gather your things;
you are surrounded.
18The Lord said these troubles
will lead to your capture,
and he will throw you
from this land
like a rock from a sling.”
19The people answered,
“We are wounded
and doomed to die.
Why did we say
we could stand the pain?
20Our homes are destroyed;
our children are dead.
No one is left
to help us find shelter.”
21But I told them,
“Our leaders were stupid failures,
because they refused
to listen to the Lord.
And so we've been scattered
like sheep.
22“Sounds of destruction
rumble from the north
like distant thunder.
Soon our towns will be ruins
where only jackals live.”
Jeremiah Prays
23I know, Lord, that we humans
are not in control
of our own lives.
24Correct me, as I deserve,
but not in your anger,
or I will be dead.
25Our enemies refuse
to admit that you are God
or to worship you.
They have wiped out our people
and left our nation
lying in ruins.
So get angry
and sweep them away!
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi ni vuga wia
1Jɛrɛmiaa kaa ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n na ŋɔ ii be. 2U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
‘Ií gilɛɛ ra hiŋ a hɛssi hina wiɛɛlaa.
Ií gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra ra sa,
dikuu wizenaa la iinna na chiŋ la wia,
haali a hɛssi hina
bɔra n na sa,
dikuu guŋ wia gba.
3A nɛra naa naana wia waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ.
Ba ɔɔ ga mɔŋ daarɛ
lii kɔr biini, sɛɛhri sɛɛuh.
4Ba ɔɔ kpa saliŋhuŋŋu ni salinnɛ bɔguu,
di kpaahzuu chiŋŋi,
ú gilɛɛ waa chol.
5A keŋ vuga naa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
baŋ kuari kuŋ lugɔ
newee chiŋŋi koo,
u ra ɔnzi kuna.
Ba vuga wàá wer ŋɔ wia,
a wàá wer vol,
see baŋ chigaa.
Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔmaa, dikuubɛɛwiai,
a wàá wer ɛɛ ia wichɔgii
gɛɛ winanii maa.’
6N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, nɛr maa waa lugɔi.
I kpekkoo di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge,
di dɔɔ sɔŋ werge.
7Anɛɛ n wàá tɔgzii wergei,
hɛssi maa Kooria?
I dɛkkɔɔ banna tɔgzii.
Hɛssi maa nunzunna
ni ba koora bɛl maa,
wàá wer kpa u nyuu lɔi.
8Ba maa ɛɛ gɛnaarɛ, ba waa nunzuma maa dɔɔwɛ.
Bɛɛ ba wer helli
lii daazi la
n ɛɛ vuga benei?
9Nɛr la n zum nonee huma ni luuri ge
ɔɔ kpa saliŋhuŋŋaa
lii bolzeŋ Taasis
gɛɛ saliŋ lii Ufaz paga,
di luu margi a ni.
Suahra la ge n zum suahri nɛnnɛ,
suah pɛɛmburgu
ni pɛɛŋ aahmu lugɔ
zagbiiŋ nii, di bɔguu chiŋŋi.
10Ka n Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa,
la n du de saŋa maa,
di ɛɛ koori la n waa
luglaa ni tunaa dɔɔwɛ.
Di i baaŋ wa fuuhwo,
durnya hina bɔra ɔɔ ra sau,
hɛssi hina wàá wer chi.
11Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, ‘Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ vuga naa n waa chiŋ ni hɛri tawɛɛ naa maa wia daŋ chɔgi.’ ”
Kɔraawiizi chɔlaa yir
12Kɔraawiizi ta hɛrii ni u fɔŋŋa,
di ta durnya ni u nunzuma,
di yaa chiŋ ni
u wia zɛɛ zumaa.
13Di u wa pozoo lugɔ nazaa, niiri la n du chiŋ ɔɔ wiiu.
U ɔɔ giluu
baamazi izi bɔr maa.
U ɔɔ giluu dooŋ nyɛgzaa ni dooŋ maa kpau ba,
di gil peu lii
u kuna dauribɔr,
di waa ta.
14Nɛr maa ɛɛ gɛniirɛ, di nyaa nunzuma!
Vugkuari maa daŋ di hiihzi,
dikuu u vuga wia.
U vuga ɛɛ kumpɛɛrii,
a waa heezi.
15A ɛɛ kumpɛɛrii, di ɛɛ chɛɛtɛ kuna.
Di a seriya dii saŋa wa hello,
Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgaa.
16Ka Kɔraawiizi la yaa naabaal Jekɔb naanna n na hum la, waa lugɔ annii.
Waabuu ta kummaa,
di lizi Izrɛl hina, ba ɛɛ u himmaa nɛra.
U sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ.
Hɛhchɔg n na ba wia
17Jɛrusalɛm hina, ba fɔɔ iabuu!
Ií chaali ii kundɔɔlaa
lii a hɛri.
18Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“N daŋ duŋŋi nɛra la
n soge hɛri naa biini ta.
N daŋ gil biinichɔg lau baa,
guŋ gil bá wer lauri baa.”
19Jɛrusalɛm hina lɔ wile werge, di ŋɔ,
“Na gunla yaa n na pira werge maa!
Yaa ŋmɛra wàá wer tuŋ.
Yaa faa zummɔɔ lugɔ u ɛɛ wii la
yaa n niŋ wer di u kanyittii!
20Yaa tanti diini maanii chɔkkɛ,
a ŋmɛnni maa chaazi.
Yaa biizi maa siu.
Nɛr maa waa ka hoo
ú bir baŋaa tɛɛ yaa.
21Yaa sitɔɔra nyaa nfɛrɛɛ,
ba waa ɔɔ pɛɛzi
Kɔraawiizi na.
Awia, ba waa ɔɔ nyɛɛli,
ba sela maa yaari.
22Ií ra nuu! Amaniye ballɔɔ.
Kɔɔi werge lii wiifurii
nomɛɛl wiikakag hɛrii ba.
U laallɔɔra daŋ wa purgi Juda bolzenaa maa, a birgi diŋgelli,
di ɛɛ hohobiazi duuribɔra.”
Jɛrɛmia wiisuŋŋaa wia
23N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, n zummɔ lugɔ newee lɛi dɔɔ u miibɔɔ.
Newee hor lɛi lugɔ
ú ra bagli u kipar.
24N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, kpa i wibii dii la di deŋliŋ,
ka gilɛɛ waa kpa baaŋ,
di ra birgiŋ pɛɛ.
25Gil i baaŋ fuuh hɛssi hina la
n wɛɛ ra hum la ni werge,
banla n waa i sɔŋ na yir la ni.
Ba kpu i nɛraa,
ba dim yaabuu,
di gil yaa hɛri birgi diŋgela.

english_text:
Judah Has Broken the Lord's Agreement
1-3The Lord God told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem:
I, the Lord, am warning you that I will put a curse on anyone who doesn't keep the agreement I made with Israel. So pay attention to what it says. 4My commands haven't changed since I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, a nation that seemed like a blazing furnace where iron ore is melted. I told your ancestors that if they obeyed my commands, I would be their God, and they would be my people. 5Then I did what I had promised and gave them this wonderful land, where you now live.
“Yes, Lord,” I replied, “that's true.”
6Then the Lord told me to say to everyone on the streets of Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah:
Pay attention to the commands in my agreement with you. 7Ever since I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I have been telling your people to obey me. But you and your ancestors 8have always been stubborn. You have refused to listen, and instead you have done whatever your sinful hearts have desired.
You have not kept the agreement we made, so I will make you suffer every curse that goes with it.
9The Lord said to me:
Jeremiah, the people of Judah and Jerusalem are plotting against me. 10They have sinned in the same way their ancestors did, by turning from me and worshiping other gods. The northern kingdom of Israel broke the agreement I made with your ancestors, and now the southern kingdom of Judah has done the same.
11Here is what I've decided to do. I will bring suffering on the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and no one will escape. They will beg me to help, but I won't listen to their prayers. 12-13Then they will offer sacrifices to their other gods and ask them for help. After all, the people of Judah have more gods than towns, and more shameful altars for Baal than there are streets in Jerusalem. But those gods won't be able to rescue the people of Judah from disaster.
14Jeremiah, don't pray for these people or beg me to rescue them. If you do, I won't listen, and I certainly won't listen if they pray!
15Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah:
You are my chosen people,
but you have no right
to be here in my temple,
doing such evil things.
The sacrifices you offer me
won't protect you from disaster,
so stop celebrating.
16Once you were like an olive tree
covered with fruit.
But soon I will send a noisy mob
to break off your branches
and set you on fire.
17I am the Lord All-Powerful. You people of Judah were like a tree that I had planted, but you have made me angry by offering sacrifices to Baal, just as the northern kingdom did. And now I'm going to pull you up by the roots.
The Plot To Kill Jeremiah
* 18Some people plotted to kill me.
And like a lamb
being led to the butcher,
I knew nothing
about their plans.
19But then the Lord told me
that they had planned
to chop me down like a tree—
fruit and all—
so that no one would ever
remember me again.
20 I prayed, “Lord All-Powerful,
you always do what is right,
and you know every thought.
So I trust you to help me
and to take revenge.”
21Then the Lord said:
Jeremiah, some men from Anathoth say they will kill you, if you keep on speaking for me. 22But I will punish them. Their young men will die in battle, and their children will starve to death. 23And when I am finished, no one from their families will be left alive.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi la chɔgaa wia
1Wia naabuu Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Jɛrɛmia be, 2“A nuu n ni n nɛra nuukpaŋ naa widaulaa wia, di ŋɔa tɛɛ Juda hina ni nɛra la maa n du Jɛrusalɛm. 3Ŋɔ ba be, dí kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Núuseei di baal la maa n waa sɛɛwɛ ú hiŋ gunla n ni n nɛra nuukpaŋ naa n na bagli. 4Wia la miŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ ii naabaala, saŋa la miŋ lizi baa lii Ijip hɛri la n faa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ zugzizeŋ niŋ la.’ N faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ií ra hiŋiŋ, di ra ɛɛ wia la maa miŋ ŋɔ ií ra ɛɛ la, denii ii ɛɛ n nɛra, ń ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iin ninna hum. 5Denii nua la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ii naabaala la jaa su u maga lugɔ n daŋ kpa hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la tɛɛ baa, ú ɛɛ ba kundɔɔlii.’ ”
Denii n jaa sɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, Ami.”
6Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Sii wia naa maa Juda bola ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biine, di ŋɔ, ‘Ií ra nuu n ni n nɛra nuukpaŋ dɔɔi widaulaa naa, di ra hiŋaa nɛnnɛ. 7Di lii saŋa la miŋ lizi ii naabaala lii Ijip hɛri di wa lii ni zinaa, n karfi baabuu digiidigii, di ŋɔ lugɔ bá ra hiŋiŋ. 8Ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá nuu tɛŋ gɛɛ di ra du tau, ka dɔɔ dignikpega, di ra hiŋ ba nfɛrchɔgaa wiɛɛlaa. Awia, n faa gil n ni baa nuukpaŋ nuuseezi la miŋ karfi baa ŋɔ bá ra hiŋ, ka ba vɛɛ la di baa.’ ”
9Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina ra ta n jinachɔgaarɛ. 10Ba bittɔɔ ra hiŋ ba naabaala wichɔgaa ŋmɛnizi la baŋ faa ra hiŋ, di vɛɛ n nua hiŋaa la. Ba ra kuari vugaa, di ra sɛɛ a dɔɔra. Izrɛl ni Juda hina maanii chɔgi nuukpaŋ la n ni ba naabaala n ɛɛwɛ la. 11Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ra karfi baabuu lugɔ n daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg la baŋ wàá wer lii u biini, ta ba ni. Haali baŋ wiiwe tɛŋ gba, ka màá ka nuu. 12Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina daŋ lii la ga wii ra du ba vuga la baŋ ɔɔ kpu sela, di fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di ra tɛɛa la, ka a wàá wer lɛɛ baa, di a hɛhchɔg wa ballɔ. 13Hoi, Juda hina, ii dɔɔ vugkpilaa werge gunla iin dɔɔ bolkpila la. Mbusu lizibɔra la iiŋ mawɛɛ, ií ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di ra tɛɛ vug Baal la miŋ kiiwe la, kpillɔɔ werge lugɔ Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa.
14Awia, Jɛrɛmia, gilɛɛ wa suŋŋi wiizi di ra tɛɛ a nɛra naa gɛɛ di wa lɛɛ ba nua di ra sɛɛ chɔgri maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, màá nuu tɛɛ baa bá biinichɔg werge saŋa.
15Nɛra la miŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ ra ɛɛ wikunaa.
Anɛɛ n tɛɛ baa ŋmɛnɛɛ
lugɔ ba du n Dia biinei?
Ba zummɔɔ lugɔ nuuzi la banna lɛɛ,
di ra kpu sela,
di ra lizi mbusuzi labuu
niŋ wer lɛɛ baa
lii a hɛhchɔg naa biiniaa?
Guŋ daŋ wer
tɛɛ baa bɔsɔnaa?
16Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi faa ra yir baabuu ɔlivi daa n lɔɔwɛ
di nɔŋ nɛnnɛɛ.
Ka filaŋkeŋ, n daŋ pozi werge
lugɔ nazaa ni niŋ,
di wa fuuh u paŋhoori,
di kuugi u kela maa.
17Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la n gillɛ ii ɛɛ lugɔ daa la miŋ duuwe labuu kpa a hɛhchɔg ta ii ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, wichɔgaa la Izrɛl ni Juda hina n ɛɛwɛ, di fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di ra tɛɛ vug Baal labuu gillɛ n baaŋ fuuh ii ni la.”
Baŋ ta Jɛrɛmia jinachɔgii wia
18Kɔraawiizi pilli ba jinachɔgaa labuu bagliŋ, wia la banna nyiŋŋi bá ɛɛ. 19N faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ peezi la n pɛssɛɛ, ba tɛrguu di ra la bá ga kɔrgi. Ka maa zummɛ lugɔ ba ta n kpui jinaa, di ra ŋɔ,
“Ií gil ya chɔgi a daa ni u nɔna maa,
ií gil ya teŋuu lii nɛra biini,
ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka
liizi u sɔŋ.”
20Denii n suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ,
“Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa
Maa Hiŋ,
hinuu ra di seriya ni wibii,
di ɛɛ nɛra biine ni nfɛssi
di ra na.
Gil n na kim la hin niŋ turgi baa.
N wiimaanii n kpa
du i nonee.”
21Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Jɛrɛmia, Anatɔf hina ra nyiŋŋi i miibɔɔ lizaarɛ, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini, di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ kpui.’ ” 22Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, “N daŋ tɛr ba digna. Tokobii bá kpa kpu ba biipɔllaa, lɔchɔgii ge kpu ba biizi maa. 23N dau saŋaa min niŋ kpa hɛhchɔg wa ta Anatɔf hina ni. Di a guŋ saŋa wa hello, ba bɛl maa wàá ka ka.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Complains to the Lord
1Whenever I complain
to you, Lord,
you are always fair.
But now I have questions
about your justice.
Why is life easy for sinners?
Why are they successful?
2You plant them like trees;
you let them prosper
and produce fruit.
Yet even when they praise you,
they don't mean it.
3But you know, Lord,
how faithful I've always been,
even in my thoughts.
So drag my enemies away
and butcher them like sheep!
4How long will the ground be dry
and the pasturelands parched?
The birds and animals
are dead and gone.
And all of this happened because
the people are so sinful.
They even brag, “God can't see
the sins we commit.”
The Lord Answers Jeremiah
5Jeremiah, if you get tired
in a race against people,
how can you possibly run
against horses?
If you fall in open fields,
what will happen in the forest
along the Jordan River?
6Even your own family
has turned against you.
They act friendly,
but don't trust them.
They're out to get you,
and so is everyone else.
The Lord Is Furious with His People
7I loved my people and chose them
as my very own.
But now I will reject them
and hand them over
to their enemies.
8My people have turned against me
and roar at me like lions.
That's why I hate them.
9My people are like a hawk
surrounded and attacked
by other hawks.
Tell the wild animals
to come and eat their fill.
10My beautiful land is ruined
like a field or a vineyard
trampled by shepherds
and stripped bare
by their flocks.
11Every field I see lies barren,
and no one cares.
12A destroying army
marches along desert roads
and attacks everywhere.
They are my deadly sword;
no one is safe from them.
13My people, you planted wheat,
but because I was furious,
I let only weeds grow.
You wore yourselves out
and gained only shame!
The Lord Will Have Pity on Other Nations
14The Lord said:
I gave this land to my people Israel, but enemies around it have attacked and robbed it. So I will uproot them from their own countries just as I will uproot Judah from its land. 15But later, I will have pity on these nations and bring them back to their own lands. 16They once taught my people to worship Baal. But if they admit I am the only true God, and if they let my people teach them how to worship me, these nations will also become my people. 17However, if they don't listen to me, I will uproot them from their lands and completely destroy them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jɛrɛmia nuumaa wia
1Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
saŋa maanii i wia maa ɔɔ deŋli,
di n haŋ wa kpa wia
ba i be.
Ka n daŋ ŋɔ i wibii dii wia.
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ biinikpola hina
ra nyɛɛlɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yarda nyaara
du ni bampirsɔnai?
2Hinuu duu baa lugɔ daa,
di gil ba nyɛɛli, di ra nɔŋ.
Ba ɔɔ ra chɔliibuu,
ka ba baga lɛi i wia.
3N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, ka i zumimbuu,
i ra na n wiɛɛlaa
ni gunla miŋ nɔŋŋiibuu.
Tɛrgi wichɔgɛɛra naa kaali alugɔ peeza banna nyiŋŋi bá kpu.
A binni baa guŋŋ
bá kpui saŋa wa hel.
4Ɛrɛɛ yaa hɛri hil,
kooree la n du kooni
siu di birgi magɛi?
Dikuubɛɛwiai, banla maa n du de la ɛɛ biinikpola hinaa,
Sela ni zumbizi maanii siuwɛ.
Haali guŋ gba, a nɛra ra ŋɔu,
‘Kɔraawiizi wàá na wii la
n na ɛɛ yaa.’ ”
Gunla Kɔraawiizi n bittɛ ŋɔ Jɛrɛmia be wia
5Denii Kɔraawiizi bir ŋɔ,
“Jɛrɛmia, di i ni nɛra chɔwɔɔ,
ba gil i kuuh,
ɛrɛɛ i ni zagra wer chɔi?
Hinna jiŋli bɔr la n chaanɛɛ biini,
ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛ vol,
kɔr la n du Jɔɔdan muu
kɛrii la biinei?
6I lulla, haali i diahina gba,
ra chɔgi i sɔnnɛ.
Ba ɛɛ nuukpannɛ bá naai.
Gilɛɛ waa yardi baa,
haali banna ŋɔ
i wia nɛnnɛ gba.”
7Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ,
“N vɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa ta.
N vɛɛ hɛri la nɛra
miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hinnɛ.
N kpa nɛra la miŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ wergee
du ba dɔma nonee biini.
8Nɛra la miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hiŋ la, bittɔɔ chi n ni
alugɔ bunyiŋ n du kɔr biini,
di wii ra duŋ,
awia, n hah baabuu.
9Nɛra la miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hiŋ la,
ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zumbee,
kɔlli n gowee, á lau.
Ií yirgi pir sela,
á ba wa di diuzenaa.
10Hɛrdumazi koorikpila ballɔɔ di wa chɔgi n nɛra alugɔ grepu daazi koo,
di fɛrgi n kooni,
di gil n hɛrsum la
birgi hɛribɔduma.
11U daŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ,
di hil werge n sibɔɔ.
A hɛri maa daŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr maa
wàá dɔɔ u saŋa.
12A hɛribɔduma giŋgimee nyuuni maanii,
chɔgra kpila wa yaari,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa u tokobi,
wa chi a hɛri tuna bɛl,
di chɔguu ga lii bɛl,
nɛr maa wàá na u hiŋ.
13N nɛra daŋ duu mia, ka kum kooree.
Ba daŋ kuuh werge,
ka ba wàá na kummaa.
Awia, ií di ii kuna kumaa hiihzi,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi
baaŋfuuihchɔgii la wia.”
14Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Hɛssi la hina biine n kpolle, ba so bar hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina la chɔguubuu. N daŋ duŋŋi baa lii ba hɛssi, di lizi Juda hina maa lii ba biini. 15Ka di n wa duŋŋi baa de tuŋ, n daŋ kaa na ba sinyɛna, di gil bɛl maa bir ba u himmaa hɛri, di kaa wa dɔɔ u kapɛttɛ kuna. 16Di ba wa helli n nɛra ŋmɛnizi nɛnnɛ, di kpa n sɔŋ hɛɛhzi, di ŋɔ, ‘N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de,’ haali baŋ faa bagli n nɛra, ba kpa vug Baal sɔŋ hɛɛhzi la gba, ka ba daŋ so n nɛra biini. 17Ka di hɛri la maa hina waa haŋ wa nuu tɛŋ, n daŋ lizi baa, di dim baa nyaamm. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
Jeremiah's Linen Shorts
1The Lord told me, “Go and buy a pair of linen shorts. Wear them for a while, but don't wash them.” 2So I bought a pair of shorts and put them on.
3Then the Lord said, 4“Take off the shorts. Go to Parah and hide the shorts in a crack between some large rocks.” 5And that's what I did.
6Some time later the Lord said, “Go back and get the shorts.” 7I went back and dug the shorts out of their hiding place, but the cloth had rotted, and the shorts were ruined.
8Then the Lord said:
9Jeremiah, I will use Babylonia to destroy the pride of the people of Judah and Jerusalem. 10The people of Judah are evil and stubborn. So instead of listening to me, they do whatever they want and even worship other gods. When I am finished with these people, they will be good for nothing, just like this pair of shorts. 11These shorts were tight around your waist, and that's how tightly I held onto the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. I wanted them to be my people. I wanted to make them famous, so that other nations would praise and honor me, but they refused to obey me.
Wine Jars
The Lord said:
12Jeremiah, tell the people of Judah, “The Lord God of Israel orders you to fill your wine jars with wine.”
They will answer, “Of course we fill our wine jars with wine! Why are you telling us something we already know?”
13Then say to them:
I am the Lord, and what I'm going to do will make everyone in Judah and Jerusalem appear to be full of wine. And the worst ones will be the kings of David's family and the priests and the prophets. 14Then I will smash them against each other like jars. I will have no pity on the young or the old, and they will all be destroyed. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People of Judah Will Be Taken Away
15People of Judah,
don't be too proud to listen
to what the Lord has said.
16You hope for light,
but God is sending darkness.
Evening shadows already deepen
in the hills.
So return to God
and confess your sins to him
before you trip and fall.
17If you are too proud to listen,
I will weep alone.
Tears will stream from my eyes
when the Lord's people
are taken away as prisoners.
18The Lord told me to tell you
that your king and his mother
must surrender their thrones
and remove their crowns.
19The cities in the Southern Desert
are surrounded;
no one can get in or out.
Everyone in Judah
will be taken away.
20Jerusalem, you were so proud
of ruling the people of Judah.
But where are they now?
Look north, and you will see
your enemies approaching.
21You once trusted them to help,
but now I'll let them rule you.
What do you say about that?
You will be in pain
like a woman giving birth.
22Do you know why
your clothes were torn off
and you were abused?
It was because
of your terrible sins.
23Can you ever change
and do what's right?
Can people change the color
of their skin,
or can a leopard
remove its spots?
If so, then maybe you can change
and learn to do right.
24I will scatter you,
just as the desert wind
blows husks from grain
tossed in the air.
25I won't change my mind.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
You rejected me
and worshiped false gods.
* 26You were married to me,
but you were unfaithful.
You even became a prostitute
by worshiping disgusting gods
on hilltops and in fields.
27So I'll rip off your clothes
and leave you naked and ashamed
for everyone to see.
You are doomed!
Will you ever be worthy
to worship me again?
translation_text:
Pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii kirsɔɔ wia
1Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, “La ga yau pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii kirsɔɔ di kirsi, ka gilɛɛ wa gil nii ra gbɔgzuu.” 2Awia, n ga yawuu, di kpau kirsi, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ n ɛɛ la.
3Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, 4“Kpa a kirsɔɔ la Muu Yufretis nua, di ga suah bii bɔɔ biini de.” 5Awia, n kpau la Muu Yufretis di ga suah, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ n be la.
6Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “La Muu Yufretis ga kpa kirsɔɔ la miŋ ŋɔ i kpa suah la, di ba.” 7Awia, n la Muu Yufretis, bɔr la miŋ kpau suah. Miŋ ga nau, di u siuwɔ, waa kaa dɔɔ tɔna maa.
8Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, 9“Keŋ himmaanii n chɔgi Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina barabara werge la. 10A biinikpola hina naa vɛɛ n nua hiŋaarɛ, ka dɔɔ dignikpega, di ra ɛɛ ba kipar, di la gaa kuari vuga, di ra sɛɛ a dɔɔra. Awia, ba daŋ ɛɛ alugɔ a kirsɔɔ naa n waa kaa dɔɔ tɔna naa. 11Gunla kirsɔɔ n ɔɔ lau baal chara nɛnnɛ la, gunnɛ n lau Juda ni Izrɛl hina maa nɛnnɛ. N ɛɛ gunnɛ bá ɛɛ n nɛra, ń sɔŋ na chɔlaa ni girme. Ka ba waŋ hiŋŋɛ.”
Siŋ hure wia
12Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Jɛrɛmia, ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ bá fɛɛni siŋ su siŋ hur maa. Ba daŋ ŋɔ i be lugɔ ba zummɔ lugɔ a dɛkkɔɔ siŋ hur maa n niŋ su siŋ. 13Denii í ŋɔ ba be, ‘Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ lugɔ n daŋ gil nɛra la maa n du hɛri naa ɛɛ sinnyɔɔra, koora la n soge Koori Deevid koorikara ni, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi ani banla maa n du Jɛrusalɛm biini. 14N daŋ lau mɛɛwaa ni biibaala maa lɔ dɔŋa alugɔ baŋ purgi viini. Màá na ba sinyɛna, di gil ba kpui. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”
Jɛrɛmia n karfi Izrɛl hina ba jigsi wia
15Denii n ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Ií keŋŋi digna di ra nuu nɛnnɛ.
Ii gilɛɛ kpoŋ di ra jigsi!
Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
16Ií ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la,
mɔɔ ka u gil bɔbiri chol ii ni,
ii ra lɔɔzi naazi
giŋgimee nyuuni,
di ra chogli.
Ii dɔɔ bɔchaaŋ tamiirɛ,
ka u daŋ lauwuu
birgi bɔbiri limpiriŋ,
di birguu biinichɔg werge.
17Ka di ii waa nuuwɛ,
n daŋ suah wii
dikuu ii jigsi wia.
N daŋ wii werge, sinii ra lii,
dikuu ban niŋ lɔ
Kɔraawiizi nɛra laal,
di lauri baa kaali wia.”
18Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,
“Ŋɔ a koori ni u maa be
lugɔ bá izi ba koorikassi ni,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba saliŋ kahuronanaa la
daŋ lii ba nyuuni chogli.”
19Nɛgɛv bolzenaa maanii bá wa fɔɔ,
nɛr maa wàá wer zuu
gɛɛ di lii.
Juda hina maanii bá wa lɔ laal
di lauri kaali hɛrduma.
20Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií na,
ii dɔma lii
wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ
di ra ba!
Lee nɛra la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia ŋɔ ií ra binni la duɛi,
banla iiŋ faa kuu ba wia
di ra jigsi lai?
21Ɛrɛɛ ii ŋɔi,
di nɛra la iinna
yir ii dammuzi
wa lɔ ia di kpegli ia,
di ra di kora ii ninɛi?
A danna wii ii ni werge maa
alugɔ hilula n ɔɔ lɔ
haaŋ la.
22Di ii wa pɛɛzi iihinaa,
“Bɛɛ n baani kennaa
wia huuzi yaai?”
Ii wichɔgaa wiarɛ
tɔɔrɔɔ naa huuzi ia
ii bɔra nyɛgi la.
23Itiopia hinuu daŋ wer chɛr u bɔrahɔŋ duula
gɛɛ amani daŋ wer
dinzi u bɔra chɛssaa?
Gunnɛ ii wàá wer ɛɛ winanaa,
dikuu wichɔgaa ɛɛi
n mani ia wia.
24“N daŋ yaari ia gunla peu
n ɔɔ lɔ zɔga yaari la.
25Ii hotte guŋ,
n lizi dau ia,
dikuu iiŋ suuh n wia,
ka ra kuari vuga wia.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
26Awia, n daŋ wir ii laala maa,
ka ii di hiihzi.
27N na iinna ɛɛ wia la miŋ kiiwee,
gunla iinna sɛm
giŋgimee nyuuni
ni kooni la, di ra hiŋ vuga
alugɔ baal n nyiŋŋi
u dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ
