Next I went to the king of Uz, and then to the four kings of Philistia, who ruled from Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what was left of Ashdod. 21Then I went to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, 22and to the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and their colonies across the sea. 23-24After this, I went to the kings of Dedan, Tema, Buz, the tribes of the Arabian Desert, 25Zimri, Elam, Media, 26and the countries in the north, both near and far.
I went to all the countries on earth, one after another, and finally to Babylonia.
27The Lord had said to tell each king, “The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, commands you to drink from this cup that is full of the wine of his anger. It will make you so drunk that you will vomit. And when the Lord sends war against the nations, you will be completely defeated.”
28The Lord told me that if any of them refused to drink from the cup, I must tell them that he had said, “I, the Lord All-Powerful, command you to drink. 29Starting with my own city of Jerusalem, everyone on earth will suffer from war. So there is no way I will let you escape unharmed.”
30The Lord told me to say:
From my sacred temple
I will roar like thunder,
while I trample my people
and everyone else
as though they were grapes.
31My voice will be heard
everywhere on earth,
accusing nations of their crimes
and sentencing the guilty
to death.
Disaster Is Coming
32The Lord All-Powerful says:
You can see disaster spreading
from far across the earth,
from nation to nation
like a horrible storm.
33When it strikes, I will kill so many people that their bodies will cover the ground like manure. No one will be left to bury them or to mourn.
The Leaders of Judah Will Be Punished
34The Lord's people are his flock,
and you leaders
were the shepherds.
But now it's your turn
to be butchered like sheep.
You'll shatter like fine pottery
dropped on the floor.
So roll on the ground,
crying and mourning.
35You have nowhere to run,
nowhere to hide.
* 36-37Listen to the cries
of the shepherds,
as the Lord's burning anger
turns peaceful meadows
into barren deserts.
38Like a lion leaving its den,
the Lord has abandoned
his people
to the destruction of war.
translation_text:
Dɔma n lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag wia
1Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim n di Juda kora binni anaazuhiŋ biinii, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Juda hina wia tɛɛ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia. A keŋ bina naabuu ɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza lugli bina, uŋ di Babilɔn kora. 2Denii mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ Juda hina ni banla maa n du Jɛrusalɛm be, 3“Binni tokko ni ahoro, di lii binni fidaahorohiŋ la Amɔn biibaal Jɔsia n di Juda kora la, Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ ŋɔ wiarɛ ra tɛŋ, n ge ŋɔa ra tɛɛ ia digiidigii, ka ii waa nuuwɛ.
4Haali Kɔraawiizi n hum u balaa dɔgtɛɛzi ii be saŋa kpila maa, ka ii waa sɛɛwɛ nuu tɛɛ baa. 5Ba ɔɔ ŋɔ ii benii lugɔ ii bɛl maa bir lii u biinikpola wiɛɛlaa ni u wikuna ɛɛi maa biini. Guŋ gil ii wer so hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ii ni ii naabaala, ú ɛɛ ii kundɔɔlii di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa la. 6Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa gɛɛ di waa sɛɛ u dɔɔra. Ií gilɛɛ gil n baaŋ waa fuuh, dikuu ii nonee kuŋkuaraa wia, ń gilɛɛ waa tɔɔri ia.
7Ka ii waa nuuwɛ tɛŋ, ka gil n baaŋ fuuh dikuu kuna la iiŋ kuarɛɛ la wia, di gil wia huuzi ia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
8Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, “Dikuu iiŋ vɛɛ n nua nuui wia, 9n daŋ chaali nɛra la maa n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ni n balii Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza, bá wa lɔ hɛri naa ni anla maa n baruu la hina laal. N daŋ chɔgi a maa nyaamm, di gil ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, nɛra nuuzi kpu, di gil ba bola chɔɔgi diŋgelli di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 10N daŋ lizi bɔsɔna ni hindii kɔɔi, haŋfalaa ni ba janna loobee, nanni gbɔga ani fintinazi chaanaa ba biini. 11A hɛri naa maa daŋ chɔɔ diŋgela, ka hɛssi naa hina maa jaa gaa hum Babilɔn koori di ra la binni tokkoahoro ni fi.
12Di a binni tokkoahoro ni fihiŋ wa su a maga, n daŋ jaa bir tɛr Babilɔn koori ni u hɛri hina maa digna, dikuu ba bilchɔg wia, di gil de chɔɔ diŋgela, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 13N daŋ kpa hɛhchɔgni la maa miŋ ŋɔ a daŋ chol hɛssi hina ni la, di tɛr Babilɔn hina digna, saŋa la miŋ ga Jɛrɛmia be di ŋɔ hɛhchɔgni la maa wia baŋ sɛbɛɛ du hɔnnaa biini la. 14Ba daŋ birgi yoma tɛɛ hɛrkpila hina ni ba koorizenaa maa. N daŋ kaa kpa ba wiɛɛlaa kim turgi baa, gunla n dɛkkɛ.”
Kɔraawiizi n niŋ di hɛssi hina seriya wia
15Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, “Siŋ ni libeere keŋ, lugɔ n baaŋ n suu. Kpau la hɛssi la hina maa be miŋ humii la, di gil ba maa nyɔɔu. 16Di ba wa nyɔɔu, ba danna jiŋli, di birgi chugla hina, dikuu laal la miŋ kpawɛɛ ra ba ba ni wia.”
17Denii n lɛɛ a siŋ ni libee Kɔraawiizi be, di kpau la ga tɛɛ hɛssi la hina be uŋ humiŋ la, ba nyɔɔu. 18Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda bola maa ni ba koora ani ba nabɔnzi maanii ń gil ba nyɔɔu. Guŋ gil bá hɛssi birgi hɛribɔdumazi, ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii ni nuukpui werge. Nɛra kpa ba sɔŋ di ra see dɔŋa nuuzi. Gunnɛ ba haa ra ɛɛ haali ni zinaa. 19Banla maa n niŋ nyɔɔ a sinnɛ keŋ, Ijip koori, u balaa, u nabɔnzi ani Ijip hina maa, 20di kpa hɔɔhra maa, Uz koora maa, Filisti koora maa, banla n lii Askɛlɔn, Gaza, Ɛkrɔn ani banla n ka Asdɔd la, 21di kpa Ɛdɔm, Moab ani Ammɔn hɛssi hina, 22di kpa Taaya ni Saidɔn koora maa ani koora la n du a muuzeŋ baŋgia kɛraa, 23Dɛdan, Tɛma, Buz ani banla n du hɛhjaŋa la maa, 24di kpa Lɔrbizi koora maa ni hɔɔhra la maa n du hɛribɔduma la koora maa, 25di kpa Zimri ani Ɛlam ni Mɛdi hɛssi koora maa, 26di kpa koora la maa n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, n duglɛɛ gɛɛ n du bɔɔnɛɛ, di hiŋzi dɔŋa.
Ba maa har, Sɛsak koori gba daŋ nyɔɔu.
27Awia, ŋɔ ba be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Ií nyɔɔ werge di dɛɛzi, di ra hɛɛhzi, di chogli, ii wàá ka izi maa, dikuu laal la min niŋ kpa ta ii ni la wia.’ 28Ka di ba wa vɛɛwɔ lugɔ ba wàá lɛɛ a siŋ i be di nyɔɔ, ŋɔ ba be, ‘Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ a dɛkkɔ ií nyɔɔu! 29Na, n faarɔɔrɛ kpa hɛhchɔg di ra ta n himmaa bolzeŋ la n sɔŋ n sag u ni la ninɛɛ. Ii fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ màá tɛr ii digna. Akai, màá gil ii digna tɛraa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ gil laal chol durnya nɛra maa ni. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.’
30Awia, ŋɔ wia naa n niŋ wa huuzi baa naa du ba ni.
‘Kɔraawiizi daŋ pozi lii u bol,
u daŋ pozi lii
u duuribɔnaniinanii
lugɔ nazaa,
di pozi u hɛri ni werge.
U danna kɔɔ lugɔ nɛra la n ɔɔ ra fɛrgi ba grepuzi,
di ra pogzi durnya hina
maa ni.
31Denii a pogzaa hel durnya maa.
Kɔraawiizi ni durnya
nɛra maanii dɔɔ wia,
u daŋ di bɛl maa seriya,
di kpu wichɔgɛɛra maa.’ ”
Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
32Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ,
“Ií na! Hɛhchɔg ra yaaruu lugɔ dooŋ pekpeg
di lii hɛri bɛl di ra la bɛl.”
33A saŋa hiŋ, banla Kɔraawiizi n kpuwɛɛ la daŋ yaari bɔr maa. Nɛr maa wàá wii ba lee gɛɛ di chaali baa gɛɛ di hug baa gba, ka ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ nabina n chɔɔ hɛri.
34N nɛra binna n lugɔ penɔɔna, ií ra chɛɛhgi!
N nɛra sitɔɔra,
ií chɔɔ hɛɛhraa biini ra billi.
Dikuubɛɛwiai, ii kɔrgaa saŋa helloo,
ba daŋ ŋmɛnni ia lugɔ pebala.
35N nɛra sitɔɔra n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ penɔɔna,
wàá dɔɔ bɔr la ban niŋ chɔ la.
36A nuu a nɛra sitɔɔra n na wii
alugɔ penɔɔna,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi n na chɔgi
ba sela diiribɔr wia.
37Ii waa bampirsɔna dɔɔwɛ ii hɛri,
dikuu Kɔraawiizi n kpa
u baaŋ chɔgi ii hɛri wia.
38Kɔraawiizi vɛɛ u nɛraa ta alugɔ bunyiŋ n chɔ u bɔzuulii.
Laal nuukpuuri wia
ni Kɔraawiizi baaŋ gillɔɔ
a hɛri birgi hɛribɔduma.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Message in the Temple
(Jeremiah 7.1-15)
1 Soon after Jehoiakim became king of Judah, the Lord said:
2Jeremiah, I have a message for everyone who comes from the towns of Judah to worship in my temple. Go to the temple courtyard and speak every word that I tell you. 3Maybe the people will listen this time. And if they stop doing wrong, I will change my mind and not punish them for their sins. 4Tell them that I have said:
You have refused to listen to me and to obey my laws and teachings. 5Again and again I have sent my servants the prophets to preach to you, but you ignored them as well. Now I am warning you that if you don't start obeying me at once, 6 I will destroy this temple, just as I destroyed the town of Shiloh. Then everyone on earth will use the name “Jerusalem” as a curse word.
Jeremiah on Trial
7The priests, the prophets, and everyone else in the temple heard what I said, 8-9and as soon as I finished, they all crowded around me and started shouting, “Why did you preach that the Lord will destroy this temple, just as he destroyed Shiloh? Why did you say that Jerusalem will be empty and lie in ruins? You ought to be put to death for saying such things in the Lord's name!” Then they had me arrested.
10The royal officers heard what had happened, and they came from the palace to the new gate of the temple to be the judges at my trial. 11While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
12-13Then I told the judges and everyone else:
The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
14You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right. 15But if you put me to death, you and everyone else in Jerusalem will be guilty of murdering an innocent man, because everything I preached came from the Lord.
16The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
17Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that 18 years ago when Hezekiah was king of Judah, a prophet named Micah from the town of Moresheth had said:
“I, the Lord All-Powerful, say
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple
now stands.”
19Then the leaders continued:
No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. Then the Lord decided not to destroy Jerusalem, even though he had already said he would.
People of Judah, if Jeremiah is killed, we will bring a terrible disaster on ourselves.
20-24After these leaders finished speaking, an important man named Ahikam son of Shaphan spoke up for me as well. And so, I wasn't handed over to the crowd to be killed.
Uriah the Prophet
While Jehoiakim was still king of Judah, a man named Uriah son of Shemaiah left his hometown of Kiriath-Jearim and came to Jerusalem. Uriah was one of the Lord's prophets, and he was saying the same things about Judah and Jerusalem that I had been saying. And when Jehoiakim and his officials and military officers heard what Uriah said, they tried to arrest him, but he escaped to Egypt. So Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor and some other men after Uriah, and they brought him back. Then Jehoiakim had Uriah killed and his body dumped in a common burial pit.
translation_text:
Banna nyiŋŋi Jɛrɛmia kpui wia
1Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim n wa di Juda kora, a waa birgee ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 2“Lii chi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋee di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ nɛra la n lii Juda bola maa di ba bá wa jaamiŋ n Dia biini la. Ŋɔ ba be wia la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ í ŋɔ tɛɛ baa la. Gilɛɛ wa mɔŋ a bɛl maa ra ta tama maa. 3Aŋhinabe, baŋhina daŋ nuu, di bir lii ba wichɔgaa la banna ɛɛ biini, guŋ gil màá ka kpa hɛhchɔg la miŋ faa ra ta u jina lugɔ n kpa ta ba ni, dikuu wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛwɛɛ la wia ta ba ni.”
4Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ dí n ŋɔ a nɛra be, “A dɛkkɔ ii ra hiŋ n Gbɔg la miŋ kpawɛɛ dau ii see la. 5Di ii waa sɛɛwɛ ii nuu tɛɛ n balaa dɔgtɛɛzi la, miŋ hum ii be digiidigii la, 6guŋwaa, n daŋ chɔgi n Dia naa gunla miŋ chɔgi Silo la. Bolzeŋ naa ge daŋ ɛɛ nuuseei kuŋ tɛɛ durnya hɛssi hina maa.”
7Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, u dɔgtɛɛzi ani a nɛra maa nuu wia la maa mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ baa, Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la. 8Miŋ haŋ wa ŋɔ a wia naa tɛɛ a nɛra tuŋ, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, u dɔgtɛɛzi ani a nɛra maa lawiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “I dɛg kpuirɛ! 9Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i kpa Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ ŋɔ lugɔ Dia naa daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ Silo, a bolzeŋ naa ge birgi diŋgelai?” Denii a nɛra maa jaa bariŋ, Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini.
10Juda hina nabɔnzi n wa nuu a wia naa, ba izi lii kooridia di kpa la Kɔraawiizi Dia, di ga chi ba chigni bɔra u Dominuuzeŋfalii. 11Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni u dɔgtɛɛzi ŋɔ tɛɛ a nabɔnzi ni a nɛra maa, “Baal naa dɛg kpuirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi bolzeŋ naabuu du u ni. Ii himmaa nuu gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛrɛ!”
12Denii Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ tɛɛ a nabɔnzi ni a nɛra maa, “Kɔraawiizii humiŋ ŋɔ ń wa ŋɔ wia naa iiŋ nuuwɛ naa du a Dia ni a bolzeŋ ni. 13Awia, filaŋkeŋ, ií char ii manni ni ii wiɛɛlaa maa, ka ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua. Di ii ɛɛ guŋ, wàá ka gil hɛhchɔg la uŋ faa ŋɔ u daŋ chol ii ni la, chol ii ni. 14Ama, miŋwaa du ii noneere. Ií ɛɛŋ wii la maa iiŋ nawɛɛ lugɔ u wessoo di deŋli. 15Ka ii zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ di ii kpuŋ, ii daŋ lɛɛ nɛr la n waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ haahkɛ di chug ii ni a bolzeŋ naa ni nɛra la maa n du u biini. Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii humiŋ wibii maa lugɔ ń wa ŋɔ wia naa maa, ií nuu.”
16Denii a nabɔnzi ni a nɛra maa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni u dɔgtɛɛzi be, “Baal naa waa kpui dɛkkɛ! Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la sɔŋ biinii u ŋɔ wia tɛɛ yaa.”
17A hɛri nabɔnzi baŋhina lii chi nɛra la n chaalɛɛ la see, di ŋɔ ba be, 18“Mɔrɛsɛf hinuu Maika faa ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Juda hinaa, saŋa la Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia n faa di kora la. U faa ŋɔ Juda hina maa benii lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ,
‘Ba daŋ par Ziɔn alugɔ koo.
Jɛrusalɛm birgi hembugle,
di chɔɔ kulululu.
Kɔraawiizi Dia giŋgimii
ge birgi kɔr.’
19Koori Hɛzɛkia ni Juda hina faa waa Maika kpuwɛɛ. Awia, Koori Hɛzɛkia wia faa par Kɔraawiizi, waa kaa gil hɛhchɔg la uŋ faa ŋɔ u wia la chol ba ni. Ka yaa himmaa ra nyiŋŋuu hɛhchɔg chuma chol yaa ni.”
20Sɛmaaya biibaal Yuria la n faa lii Kiriaf Jiarim la gba, faa kpa Kɔraawiizi sɔnnɛ di ŋɔ wia du bolzeŋ naa ni a hɛri ni, gunla Jɛrɛmia n ŋɔwɛɛ naa. 21Koori Jɛhɔyakim, u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ani karchizi maa n wa nuu wia naa, a koori faa ra nyiŋŋi ú kpu Yuria. Ka Yuria faa nuu guŋ, ɔnsii werge lawuu, u chɔ kaali Ijip hɛri. 22Denii Koori Jɛhɔyakim faa hum Akbɔ biibaal Ɛlnatan ni baala baŋhina Ijip. 23Ba la ga lau Yuria lii de, di kpogluu ba wa tɛɛ Koori Jɛhɔyakim, u gil ba kpa tokobi kpuu, di huguu nɛdumazi hugribɔr la.
24Ka Safan biibaal Ahikam faa chi Jɛrɛmia har, awia, ba faa wɔɔ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ a nɛra ba kpu.

english_text:
Slaves of Nebuchadnezzar
1-2 Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me:
Jeremiah, make a wooden yoke with leather straps, and place it on your neck. 3Then send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Some officials from these countries are in Jerusalem, meeting with Zedekiah. 4So have them tell their kings that I have said:
I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel, 5and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth, 6-7 and I have chosen my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to rule all nations, including yours. I will even let him rule the wild animals. All nations will be slaves of Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his grandson. Then many nations will join together, and their kings will make slaves of the Babylonians.
8This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease. 9You might have people in your kingdom who claim they can tell the future by magic or by talking with the dead or by dreams or messages from a god. But don't pay attention if any of them tell you not to obey Nebuchadnezzar. 10If you listen to such lies, I will have you dragged far from your country and killed. 11But if you and your nation are willing to obey Nebuchadnezzar, I will let you stay in your country, and your people will continue to live and work on their farms.
12After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said:
Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians. 13But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned. 14Your prophets have told you that you don't need to obey Nebuchadnezzar, but don't listen to their lies. 15Those prophets claim to be speaking for the Lord, but he didn't send them. They are lying! If you do what they say, he will have both you and them dragged off to another country and killed. The Lord has spoken.
16When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said:
Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying! 17If you choose to obey the king of Babylonia, you will live. But if you listen to those prophets, this whole city will be nothing but a pile of rubble.
18If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem. 19-21After all, when Nebuchadnezzar took King Jehoiachin to Babylonia as a prisoner, he didn't take everything of value from Jerusalem. He left the bronze pillars, the huge bronze bowl called the Sea, and the movable bronze stands in the temple, and he left a lot of other valuable things in the palace and in the rest of Jerusalem.
But now I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, say that all these things 22will be taken to Babylonia, where they will remain until I decide to bring them back to Jerusalem. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Juda hina daŋ birgi Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza balaa
1Jɔsia biibaal Zɛdɛkia n wa di Juda kora, a waa birgee ka Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 2“Kpa kurhɔna ni daazi kuari napattaa baŋaa daa, di kpau du i baŋaa. 3Ɛdɔm, Moab ani Ammɔn hɛssi ni Taaya ani Saidɔn bola koora nabɔnzi ba Jɛrusalɛmnɛ bá wa na Koori Zɛdɛkia. Awia, kpa tile naa tɛɛ baa, bá ga tɛɛ ba koora. 4Tili baa ba dɔɔra be, di ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií ga ŋɔ ii dɔɔra be, 5n himmaa fɔŋŋazeŋ ni n banoniire n kpa ta hɛri, newea ani sela la maa n du u ni. Aŋ kpaubuu tɛɛ nɛr la maa wia n pariŋ. 6Awia, n daŋ kpa ii hɛssi maa du n balii Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza nonee biini. Haali n daŋ gil pir sela gba ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra. 7Durnya hɛssi nɛra maa daŋ humuu, di hum u biibaal ni u naana maa guŋŋ di ra ba saŋa la u hɛri n niŋ chol. Denii ú hɛri nɛra birgi hɛrkpila ni koorizenaa balaa.
8Ka di hɛri bɛl nɛra gɛɛ koora maa waa haŋ wa sɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra, n daŋ kpa laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii tɛr ba digna guŋŋ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza wa chɔgi baa nyaamm. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 9Awia, ií gilɛɛ nuu ra tɛɛ ii dɔgtɛɛkara hina, ii vugra, ii nɛra la n ɔɔ ra bagli ii deeza zɛɛzi ani hila la n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ií gilɛɛ waa hum Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza la. 10Wiŋɔzi la baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ra tɛɛ ia la maa ɛɛ karaa, a daŋ wer lizi ia hɛri naa biini, di gil n duŋŋi ia lii u biini, ií siuzi. 11Ka hɛri la maa nɛra n niŋ sɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra, di ra humuu, n daŋ gil a guŋ hɛri naa nɛra haa du ba himmaa hɛri biini, di par a di. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
12A keŋ amaniye naa himmaanii n lizi tɛɛ Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia, di ŋɔ, “Í ni i nɛra maa ra sɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra, di ra humuu, denii ií maa dɔɔ miibɔɔ. 13Bɛɛ n baani í ni i nɛra gil laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ gil a kpu hɛri la maa hina, n niŋ vɛɛ Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra sɛɛi, kpu iai? 14Ií gilɛɛ wa nuu di ra tɛɛ dɔgtɛɛkara hina la n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ii gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra la. Ba ra dar iabuu. 15Kɔraawiizi sɔnnɛ ba kpa di kanni guŋ kara di ra tɛɛ ia la. Waa lɛi hum baa. Awia, u daŋ duŋŋi ia lii bɔnnaa, bá kpu ii ni a keŋ dɔgtɛɛkara hina naa maa. Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
16Denii n jaa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni a nɛra maa be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií gilɛɛ wa nuu ra tɛɛ dɔgtɛɛkara hina la n na ŋɔ dí ba daŋ paagi n Dia kuna, di bir lii Babilɔn ba filaŋkeŋ maa la. Karaa ba ra kanni. 17Ií gilɛɛ ra nuu ba be! Ií ra hum Babilɔn koori, di na iihinaa! Bɛɛwiarɛ bolzeŋ naa purgei? 18Di ba ɛɛ n dɔgtɛɛzii wibii maa, di dɔɔ n wiŋɔɔlii, gil ba suŋŋi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ lugɔ n gilɛɛ gil bá wàá paagi kuna la n kawɛɛ n Dia, Juda kooridia ani Jɛrusalɛm biine di ra kaali Babilɔn. 19Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔ ligee, Kolzeŋ la banna yir Muuzeŋ ani torkozi la maa n kawɛɛ a bolzeŋ biini la wia, 20aabuu Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza waa paawɛ, saŋa la uŋ lau Koori Jɛhɔyakim biibaal Juda Koori Jɛhɔyachin ni u nabɔnzenaa lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali Babilɔn la. 21Ií ra nuu! Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ra ŋɔ kuna la n kawɛɛ n Dia, Juda kooridia ani Jɛrusalɛm biine wia, 22‘Ba daŋ paagaa kaali Babilɔn, a du de guŋŋ di ra ba hɔpizii la min niŋ ba a bɔr. Denii n bir kpaa ba di wa du bɔnnaa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

english_text:
Jeremiah Accuses Hananiah of Being a False Prophet
1 Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening, 2he told me that the Lord had said:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I will smash the yoke that Nebuchadnezzar put on the necks of the nations to make them his slaves. 3And within two years, I will bring back to Jerusalem everything that he took from my temple and carried off to Babylonia. 4King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
5The priests and the others were still standing there, so I said:
6Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home. 7But let me remind you and everyone else 8that long before we were born, prophets were saying powerful kingdoms would be struck by war, disaster, and disease. 9Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
10Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it. 11Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.”
I left the temple, 12and a little while later, the Lord told me 13-14to go back and say to Hananiah:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. I will put iron yokes on all the nations, and they will have to do what King Nebuchadnezzar commands. I will even let him rule the wild animals.
15-16Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
17Two months later, Hananiah died.
translation_text:
Dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ Hanania wia
1A bina himmaa biini, Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia kora dii baaguzi anuehiŋ biinii, Azur biibaal Hanania dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ n lii Gibiɔn ŋɔ wia n be Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni a nɛra maa see, di ŋɔ, 2“Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N daŋ chɔgi Babilɔn koori la fɔŋŋa. 3Binni anɛɛ biini, n daŋ paagi kuna la maa Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n paawɛ lii n Dia kaali Babilɔn la, di bir ba. 4N daŋ kaa kpogli Jɛhɔyakim biibaal Juda Koori Jɛhɔyachin ni banla maa baŋ laurɛɛ lii Juda kaali Babilɔn la, di bir ba, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ chɔgi Babilɔn koori fɔŋŋa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”
5Denii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia bir ŋɔ Hanania be, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni nɛra la maa n chigɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la see, 6“Guŋ wesso! Kɔ́raawiizi ɛɛ guŋ! Kɔ́raawiizi gil i wiŋɔzi naa maa ɛɛ wibii lugɔ u daŋ bir paagi kuna la maa baŋ paagɛɛ lii Kɔraawiizi Dia biini kaali Babilɔn ni banla baŋ laurɛɛ kaali de la, di bir ba. 7Ama, a nuu gunla min niŋ ŋɔ tɛɛ i ni nɛra naa maa n du ɛnnaa. 8Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la n ŋɔ wia saŋa kpila maa n bɛrɛɛ, mɔɔ ka n ge nii saŋa wa hel naa, ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ laal, hɛhchɔg ni wiilchɔgii daŋ chol hɛrkpila ni ba kossi maa ni. 9Ka dɔgtɛɛ la maa n na ŋɔ bampirsɔna wia, di u wiŋɔzi hiŋ haŋ wa ɛɛ wibii, guŋwaa, waabuu Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ himmaa.”
10Denii Hanania lau napattaa baŋaa daa la n du n baŋaa la lizi, di kuuguu ta, 11ka ŋɔ a nɛra maa be, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Keŋ himmaanii ń lizi buntɔga la Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n chug hɛssi hina maa la, binni anɛɛ biini.’ ” A guŋ n wa ɛɛwɛ tuŋ, mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia jaa kaali.
12Hanania n wa lizi a daa n baŋaa la, a waa birgee ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, 13“La ga ŋɔ Hanania be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ nauna baŋaa daarɛ i wer kuugi la, ka n daŋ tɛi lugbii hor. 14Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la daŋ kpa napattaa lugbii hora du hɛssi maa hina baŋaazi, bá ra hum Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza. N daŋ gil pir sela gba ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra.”
15Denii mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ Hanania be, “Hanania, a nuu n be! Kɔraawiizi wɛɛ hummɛ, ka i bir hɛssi hina naa nfɛssii, bá yardi i kara naa. 16Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N na nyiŋŋi n liziibuu durnya naa biini. I daŋ siu bina naa biini, dikuu hiŋ ŋɔ ń nɛra vɛɛŋ wia.’ ”
17A bina hiŋ baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ Hanania siu.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Letter to the People of Judah in Babylonia
1-2 I had been left in Jerusalem when King Nebuchadnezzar took many of the people of Jerusalem and Judah to Babylonia as prisoners, including King Jehoiachin, his mother, his officials, and the metal workers and others in Jerusalem who were skilled in making things. So I wrote a letter to the priests, the prophets, the leaders, and the rest of our people in Babylonia. 3I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote 4that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you 5to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them. 6Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
7Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
8-9Some of your people there in Babylonia are fortunetellers, and you have asked them to tell you what will happen in the future. But they will only lead you astray with their dreams. And don't let the prophets fool you, either. They speak in my name, but they are liars. I have not spoken to them.
10 After Babylonia has been the strongest nation for 70 years, I will be kind and bring you back to Jerusalem, just as I have promised. 11I will bless you with a future filled with hope—a future of success, not of suffering. 12You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers. 13 You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you 14and accept your worship. Then I will gather you from all the nations where I scattered you, and you will return to Jerusalem.
15You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
16-19But I have been sending prophets to the people of Judah for a long time, and the king from David's family and the people who are left in Jerusalem and Judah still don't obey me. So I, the Lord All-Powerful, will keep attacking them with war and hunger and disease, until they are as useless as rotten figs. I will force them to leave the land, and all nations will be disgusted and shocked at what happens to them. The nations will sneer and make fun of them and use the names “Judah” and “Jerusalem” as curse words.
And you have not obeyed me, even though 20I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now. 21-23You think Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah are prophets because they claim to speak for me. But they are lying! I haven't told them anything. They are also committing other horrible sins in your community, such as sleeping with the wives of their friends. So I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will put them to death while the rest of you watch. And in the future, when you want to put a curse on someone, you will say, “I pray that the Lord will kill you in the same way the king of Babylonia burned Zedekiah and Ahab to death!”
A Message for Shemaiah
24-25The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
26After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars. 27Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him? 28He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
29When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me. 30Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter 31to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said:
I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name. 32He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Hɔŋ la Jɛrɛmia n sɛbɛɛ tɛɛ Jus hina la baŋ laurɛɛ kaali Babilɔn wia
1Hɔnnaabuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia faa sɛbi tɛɛ Juda hina sitɔɔra ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la maa, n jaa ba ni, Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza lauri lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali Babilɔn hɛri la. 2Saŋa la Koori Jɛhɔyachin ni u maa n ɛɛ wiche, koori zɛɛsogna ani Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina sitɔɔra, di kpa banla n zum nonee huma, ba lauri lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali la harbɔɔrɛ, a wii naa ɛɛ. 3N kpa hɔnnaabuu tɛɛ Safan biibaal Ɛlasa ni Hilkia biibaal Gɛmaria, banla Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia n hummɛ Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza be la. Kenne a hɔŋ ŋɔ,
4“Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ ra tɛɛ banla maa uŋ gillɛ ba lauri lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali Babilɔn la. 5‘Ií ma diini so, di dau kooni, á lii diwee tɛɛ ia, ií ra di. 6Ií paagi haana di lul biizi, di nyiŋŋi haana tɛɛ ii biibaala, di gil ii biihaana ge yuu, di lul biizi, ii wazi, di gilɛɛ waa ka tama de. 7Ií ra nyiŋŋi bampirsɔna ni nyɛɛlaa ra tɛɛ bolzeŋ la miŋ la ii ni la biini. Ií ra suŋŋi wiizi, ú kissi de, ii ge gba na kissaa, ii wia maa nyɛɛli. 8Wibii maa, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií gilɛɛ wa gil dɔgtɛɛkara hina ni vugra la n du ii be la wàá dar ia. Ií gilɛɛ waa nuu ba deeza la baŋ ɔɔ deezi, di wa bagli ra tɛɛ ia la. 9Ba kpa n sɔnnɛ kanni kara ra tɛɛ ia. Min lɛi hum baa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ii Babilɔn dui naa binni tokkoahoro ni fi haŋ wa hel, di su a maga, n daŋ bir ba ii be, di wa hiŋ nua la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ n daŋ bir ba ii ni Jɛrusalɛm la. 11Dikuubɛɛwiai, n zum jinazi la miŋ tawɛɛ dikuu ii wiarɛ, anla n niŋ gil ii nyɛɛli. Ii tɔɔraa wia lɛi. Jinazi la n niŋ gil ii dɔɔ tamii kɛrɛ bɛl wiarɛ. 12Denii ii yiriŋ, di ba wa suŋŋiŋ, ń nuu tɛɛ ia. 13Ii daŋ nyiŋŋiŋ di naŋ, dikuu iin niŋ nyiŋŋiŋ ni ii biine maa wia. 14Ii daŋ naŋ, ń bir kpogli ia lii bɔr la baŋ lauri ia la la. N daŋ chaali ia lii hɛssi ni bɔra la maa miŋ duŋŋi ia du la. N daŋ bir ba ii ni bɔr la miŋ lizi ia kaali hɛrdumazi la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
15Aŋhinabe, ii daŋ ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ yaabuu dɔgtɛɛzi, Babilɔn.” 16Ka kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ koori la n soge Koori Deevid koorikara ni, ni nɛra la maa n kawɛɛ bolzeŋ naa biini, ii himmaa hɛri nɛra la n waa hɛrdumazi laŋŋɛ la wia. 17Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, “N daŋ kpa laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii ta ba ni. N daŋ gil ba ɛɛ lugɔ fig nɔnchɔgaa la n waa wer dii la. 18N daŋ kpa laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii dau ba luge, ɔnsii werge lau hɛssi hina maa durnya naa biini, bá nuuzi kpu. Nɛra danna ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛ, di ra lɔ baa mɔmɔsia, di kpa ba sɔŋ di ra see dɔŋa nuuzi, bá wia dɔɔ ɔnsii, hɛssi la maa biine miŋ duŋŋi baa, ba ga du la. 19Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ, dikuu baŋ waa n wiŋɔzi nuuwɛ, anla miŋ hum n balaa dɔgtɛɛzi digiidigii, ba ga ŋɔa tɛɛ baa la wia. Ii banla ge baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛrduma la gba waa nuuwɛ tɛŋ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
20Awia, ii banla maa miŋ duŋŋɛɛ lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali Babilɔn la, ií ra nuu n wiŋɔzi. 21Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ Kɔlaaya biibaal Ahab ni Maasɛya biibaal Zɛdɛkia wiarɛ lugɔ banla n kpa n sɔŋ di kanni kara di ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi ia, di ra du ii ni la, n daŋ kpa baa du Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza nonee, ú kpu baa ii himmaa sibɔɔ. 22Dikuu ba wia, banla maa baŋ laurɛɛ lii Juda la Babilɔn la maanii niŋ kpa wia naa di ra see nɛra nuuzi, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi ɛɛi lugɔ Zɛdɛkia ni Ahab la Babilɔn koori n fuuhwe la.’ 23Dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ɛɛ wikunaa Izrɛl hɛri. Ba lauri ba dɔŋahina haanaa nyiŋŋi. Di kpa n sɔŋ kanni kara la miŋ waa ŋɔ bá kanni. N zum gunnɛ, di kaa na guŋ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
Baŋ tili Sɛmaaya wia
24Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia benii lugɔ n ŋɔ Nɛhɛlam hinuu Sɛmaaya be, 25“Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ i kpa i himmaa sɔnnɛ, di sɛbi hɔna tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Maasɛya biibaal Zɛfania ani kizeehina maa. 26A hɔŋ biini, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi liziibuu i lɛɛ Jɛhɔyada bɔr, di ɛɛ u kizeehiŋ, di ra binni u Dia. Lau chuglahiŋ la maa n na yir u hiŋ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ, di duu daa, di du u baŋaa ge yɔlɔzi. 27Bɛɛ n baani haa a kennaa kpawɛɛ dau Jɛrɛmia la n lii Anatɔf, di ra yir u hiŋ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ lai? 28Kenne u tili ŋɔ yaa be Babilɔn. A daŋ birgi. Awia, ií ma diini so, di dau kooni, á lii diwee tɛɛ ia, ii ra di.”
29Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zɛfania n wa na Sɛmaaya hɔŋ la, u karmuu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia. 30Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, 31“La ga ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ nɛra la maa baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛrduma la, ‘Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Nɛhɛlam hinuu Sɛmaaya wia. Dikuu uŋ ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi ia di du ii ni, haali miŋ wɔɔ hummɛ, ka u gil ii yardi kara wia, 32n daŋ tɛr u ni u naanna digna. U nɛr maa wàá ka ka nɛra naa biini, ú na winanaa la min niŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ n nɛra, dikuu uŋ ŋɔ bá vɛɛŋ wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
1-2The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you. 3Someday I will let my people from both Israel and Judah return to the land I gave their ancestors.”
4-5Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah:
Screams of terror are heard,
with no word of peace.
6Can men give birth?
Then why do I see them
looking so pale
and clutching their stomachs
like women in labor?
7My people, soon you will suffer
worse than ever before,
but I will save you.
8Now you are slaves
of other nations,
but I will break the chains
and smash the yokes
that keep you in slavery.
9Then you will be my servants,
and I will choose a king for you
from the family of David.
* 10 Israel, you belong to me,
so don't be afraid.
You deserved to be punished;
that's why I scattered you
in distant nations.
But I am with you,
and someday I will destroy
those nations.
11Then I will bring you
and your descendants
back to your land,
where I will protect you
and give you peace.
Then your fears will be gone.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
12The Lord said:
My people, you are wounded
and near death.
13You are accused of a crime
with no one to defend you,
and you are covered with sores
that no medicine can cure.
* 14Your friends have forgotten you;
they don't care anymore.
Even I have acted like an enemy.
And because your sins
are horrible and countless,
I will be cruel
as I punish you.
15So don't bother to cry out
for relief from your pain.
16But if your enemies try to rob
or destroy you,
I will rob and destroy them,
and they will be led as captives
to foreign lands.
17No one wants you as a friend
or cares what happens to you.
But I will heal your injuries,
and you will get well.
The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
18The Lord said:
Israel, I will be kind to you
and let you come home.
Jerusalem now lies in ruins,
but you will rebuild it,
complete with a new palace.
19Other nations will respect
and honor you.
Your homes will be filled
with children,
and you will celebrate,
singing praises to me.
20It will be just like old times.
Your nation will worship me,
and I will punish anyone
who abuses you.
21One of your own people
will become your ruler.
And when I invite him
to come near me
at the place of worship,
he will do so.
No one would dare to come near
without being invited.
22You will be my people,
and I will be your God.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
23I am furious!
And like a violent storm
I will strike those
who do wrong.
24I won't calm down
until I have finished
what I have decided to do.
Someday, you will understand
what I mean.
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina n bittɛ ba ba hɛri wia
1Wia naabuu Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia, 2“Sɛbi wia naa maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛi naa du hɔŋ biini. 3Saŋa bɛl ra bau, min niŋ bir kpogli n nɛra Izrɛl ni Juda hina lii bɔr la baŋ lauri baa kaali la, di ba hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ba naabaala, ú kaa ɛɛ ba hor. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
4A wia naabuu Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ di ra bagli Izrɛl ni Juda hina wia,
5“N nuu ɔnsii wiraare,
u ɛɛ ɔnsii werge wiraa,
waa bampirsɔna hor ɛɛwɛ.
6Lɔ nfɛrɛ na,
baal daŋ wer lulaa?
Ka bɛɛ n baani n na baal maa n lau u hia alugɔ
hilula n lɔ haannɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ nɛr maa
siwee chogli wogliwoglei?
7Hɔpizichuma ra bau,
hàá wer kpa
hɔpizii maa mɛgzuu.
U daŋ ɛɛ hɔpizichuma tɛɛ n nɛra,
ka n daŋ lɛɛ baa
lii u biini.
8Di a hɔpizii wa hello,
n daŋ lizi baa
lii hɔɔhraa sunnaa ni
ba wichɔgaa la maa
n vɔɔzi baa la biini.
N daŋ lizi baa lii hɛrdumazi la
baŋ duwɛɛ la biine.
Ba wàá ka ɛɛ yoma.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
9Bá jaa ra hum mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum
ni Koori Deevid naana la
min niŋ tɔ kora.
10N nɛra Izrɛl hina, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm,
ií gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra ra sa.
Izrɛl hina, wibii maa, n daŋ lɛɛ ia lii hɛhjaŋa la baŋ lauri ia kaali la biine.
Ii daŋ kaa bir ba bol,
di wa dɔɔ bampirsɔna,
di so pɛrɛtɛ.
Nɛr maa wàá ka ɔnzi ia.
11N daŋ ba ii be,
di wa lɛɛ ia.
N daŋ dim hɛssi hina la maa
miŋ yaari ia
ii ga du ba biine la,
ka màá dim iawaa.
Màá vɛɛ ii digna tɛraa,
ka di n waa tɛr ii digna,
n daŋ ɛɛ guŋ ni wibii.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
12Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ,
“Ii ŋmɛra waa chaai dɔɔwɛ,
a ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá wer tuŋ.
13Nɛr maa waa hoo un ninna binni ia,
ii ŋmɛra naa
waa chaai dɔɔwɛ,
ii waa chaai tamii dɔɔwɛ.
14Banla maa ii ni baa n dɔɔ nuukpaŋ suuh ii wiarɛ,
ba baga lɛi kaa ii wia.
N lɔ iabuu alugɔ ii dɔm,
di tɛr ii digna manaŋ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ii bilchɔg kannɔɔ,
ii dɔɔ biinikpola
ge werge maa.
15Bɛɛwiarɛ ii ra wii dikuu ii ŋmɛra wia,
ii bɔra waazaa
waa chaai dɔɔwɛi?
Dikuu ii bilchɔg werge ni ii wichɔgaa kpila wiarɛ
n ɛɛ ia guŋ.
16Ka banla maa n chɔgi ia, ba dɔma daŋ chɔgi baa.
Ba daŋ lauri
ii dɔma maa
kaali hɛrdumazi.
Banla maa n foozi ii kuna, ba daŋ foozi ba hora.
Banla maa n na sunni ia,
n daŋ sunni baa.
17N daŋ kaa gil ii dɔɔ alaanfia,
di chaa ii ŋmɛra la,
haali ii dɔma n na ŋɔ,
‘Ziɔn hina ɛɛ kuntaalaarɛ,
nɛr maa baga
waa hoo ba be.’
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
18Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N daŋ kuari n nɛra soŋŋi ba himmaa hɛri,
di suŋ dia maa hina ni.
Nɛra daŋ bir ma Jɛrusalɛm maa,
bá kooridia chi
bɔr la n dɛkkɛ.
19Ba daŋ yir yira, di ra chɔliŋ,
di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.
N daŋ kissi baa, bá wazi jaa,
ba wàá ka tama.
N daŋ kissi baa, bá dɔɔ girme,
ba wàá kaa ra gbɛlli baa.
20Ba biizi daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ faala hina,
ń kaa kuari ba bola
maa ma, á chi chigigi.
N daŋ tɛr banla maa
n faa ra sunni baa la digna.
21Ba koori daŋ lii
ba himmaa hɛri,
ba sitɔɔri ge gba lii
ba himmaa nɛra biini.
Di n wa yiruu,
u daŋ ba n be.
Anɛɛ n niŋ sɛɛ ba n be,
di mɔɔ yittɛi?
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
22Awia, ii daŋ ɛɛ n nɛra,
n ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la
iinna hum.”
23Ií na, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ pezeŋ
n tawɛɛ ra ba,
peu n na ba kpegzi ni
di ra kɔɔ,
ú wa lɔ wichɔgɛɛra nyuuni.
24Kɔraawiizi baaŋ la wàá bir har,
di waa u kipar maa nawɛɛ.
Di saŋa bɛl wa hello,
ii daŋ zum a zɛɛ.

english_text:
Israel Will Return to God
1The Lord said:
Israel, I promise
that someday all your tribes
will again be my people,
and I will be your God.
2In the desert I was kind
to those who escaped death.
I gave them peace,
and when the time is right,
I'll do the same for you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
3Some time ago, the Lord appeared to me and told me to say:
Israel, I will always love you;
that's why I've been so patient
and kind.
4You are precious to me,
and so I will rebuild
your nation.
Once again you will dance for joy
and play your tambourines.
5You will plant vineyards
on the hills of Samaria
and enjoy the grapes.
6Someday those who guard
the hill country of Ephraim
will shout, “Let's go to Zion
and worship the Lord our God.”
Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
7The Lord says:
Celebrate and sing for Israel,
the greatest of nations.
Offer praises and shout,
“Come and rescue
your people, Lord!
Save what's left of Israel.”
8I, the Lord, will bring
my people back from Babylonia
and everywhere else on earth.
The blind and the lame
will be there.
Expectant mothers
and women about to give birth
will come and be part
of that great crowd.
9They will weep and pray
as I bring them home.
I will lead them
to streams of water.
They will walk on a level road
and not stumble.
I am a father to Israel,
my favorite children.
10Listen to me, you nations
nearby or across the sea.
I scattered the people of Israel,
but I will gather them again.
I will protect them like a shepherd
guarding a flock;
11I will rescue them from enemies
who could overpower them.
12My people will come
to Mount Zion
and celebrate;
their faces will glow
because of my blessings.
I'll give them grain, grapes,
and olive oil,
as well as sheep and cattle.
Israel will be prosperous
and grow like a garden
with plenty of water.
13Young women and young men,
together with the elderly,
will celebrate and dance,
because I will comfort them
and turn their sorrow
into happiness.
14I will bless my people
with more food
than they need,
and the priests will enjoy
the choice cuts of meat.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Offers Hope
15 In Ramah a voice is heard,
crying and weeping loudly.
Rachel mourns for her children
and refuses to be comforted,
because they are dead.
* 16But I, the Lord, say
to dry your tears.
Someday your children
will come home
from the enemy's land.
Then all you have done for them
will be greatly rewarded.
17So don't lose hope.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
18The people of Israel moan
and say to me,
“We were like wild bulls,
but you, Lord, broke us,
and we learned to obey.
You are our God—
please let us come home.
19When we were young,
we strayed and sinned,
but then we realized
what we had done.
We are ashamed and disgraced
and want to return to you.”
20People of Israel,
you are my own dear children.
Don't I love you best of all?
Though I often make threats,
I want you to be near me,
so I will have mercy on you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
21With rock piles and signposts,
mark the road well,
my dear people.
The road by which you left
by will now lead you home.
22Will you ever decide
to be faithful?
I will make sure that someday
things will be different,
as different as a woman
protecting a man.
The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
23The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said:
I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say,
“We pray that the Lord
will bless his home,
the sacred hill in Jerusalem
where his temple stands.”
24The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds. 25Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy, 26and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
27Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow. 28In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow. 29 No longer will anyone go around saying,
“Sour grapes eaten by parents
leave a sour taste in the mouths
of their children.”
30When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death.
The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
31 The Lord said:
The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah. 32It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
33 Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel:
“I will write my laws
on their hearts and minds.
I will be their God,
and they will be my people.
34 “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
35I am the Lord All-Powerful.
I command the sun
to give light each day,
the moon and stars
to shine at night,
and ocean waves to roar.
36I will never forget
to give those commands,
and I will never let Israel
stop being a nation.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
37Can you measure the heavens?
Can you explore
the depths of the earth?
That's how hard it would be
for me to reject Israel forever,
even though they have sinned.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
38The Lord said:
Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate. 39From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah. 40Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina n bittɛ ba bol wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, ń ɛɛ Izrɛl hina dizi maa Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum, ba ge ɛɛ n nɛra.
2Nɛra la n chɔwɛɛ lii siu biini,
ba wia daŋ pariŋ
hɛribɔduma biini,
n daŋ ba wa tɛɛ
Izrɛl hina heezaa.”
3Kɔraawiizi faa ba yaa benii, saŋa bɛl n bɛrɛɛ, di wa ŋɔ,
“N nɔŋŋi iabuu ni nɔŋŋaa la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ,
di haa vɛɛ ra bagli
ia n nɔŋŋaa.
4Izrɛl hina, n daŋ kaa kuari ia soŋŋi,
ii kaa kpa kuŋyigzaa,
di ra sa ni bɔsɔna.
5Samaria giŋgimee la nyuunii,
ii kaa dau ii kooni,
di duu ii grepu daazi.
Ii banla n niŋ duua,
daŋ di a nɔna.
6Saŋa bɛl ra bau, tauduura lɔ wile
Ɛfram giŋgimee nyuuni,
di ŋɔ,
‘Ií ba ya la Bizeŋ Ziɔn n du Jɛrusalɛm,
Kɔraawiizi la yaa
n na hum la be.’ ”
7Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Ií yir yira ni bɔsɔna, di ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina
n ɛɛ Jekɔb naanna.
Ií chaasi ra tɛɛ
hɛri la n kaali hɛssi maa.
Ií gil bá nuu iinna chɔluu, di ra ŋɔ,
‘N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
lɛɛ i nɛra Izrɛl hina la
n kawɛɛ.’
8N daŋ lizi baa lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag,
di chaali baa lii bɔr maa.
Gbɛraa ni nyuŋŋa maanii
niŋ jaa ba ni.
Haana la n kpogli hizi
ni banla n na nyiŋŋi lulaa.
Ba daŋ du kpil werge,
di bir ba a hɛri.
9Min niŋ kpogli baa di ra ba la,
ba danna wii, di ra suŋŋi wiizi.
N daŋ tɔ ba see, gɔŋa n dɔɔ niiri kɛraa,
ŋmɛnizi la n du kpantalaŋ ni,
ba wàá lɔɔzi naazi di jiŋli.
N ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Izrɛl hina mɛɛ,
Ɛfram ge ɛɛ
n biibambilugli.”
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Durnya hɛssi hina, ií ra nuu n be,
di gil n wiŋɔzi naa yaari
la hɛhjaŋa muuzenaa nuuzi.
N yaari n nɛraa, ka n daŋ bir chaali baa,
di ra binni ba ni alugɔ
penɔɔni n na
binni u peeza la.
11N lɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa ta, ba dɔɔ bahinaa,
di lɛɛ baa lii hɛri la hina
n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa kaali baa be.
12Ba daŋ ba Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu, di waa yir yira ni bɔsɔna,
ba bɔra ra pur,
dikuu kuna la
miŋ tɛɛ baa wia.
Mia, siŋfalii, nuu,
peeza ani nauna la
miŋ tɛɛ baa wia.
Ba daŋ jaa ɛɛ lugɔ kambol n sɔɔnɛɛ nɛnnɛ,
bá dɔɔ kunla maa
banna nyiŋŋi.
13Denii suŋgure jaa ra sa ni bɔsɔna,
biipɔllaa ni nɛzɛŋzi maa jaa.
N daŋ gil ba wiraa birgi bɔsɔna,
di tɛɛ baa bɔsɔna,
ka gil biinichɔg.
14N daŋ tɛɛ n kizeehina diunanaa werge,
di tɛɛ n nɛra kuna la maa
banna nyiŋŋi werge.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
15Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Ba nuu nɛbɛl loobiire Rama,
unna wii werge maa.
Rachɛllɛ ra wii dikuu u biizi wia,
ba laafuu ra huhzi,
dikuu u biizi la
n waa hoo wia.”
16Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Gil wiraa ka lau i hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai,
i daŋ na i huma kinturgaa.
Ba daŋ lii ba dɔma hɛri bir ba.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
17Awia, i dɔɔ tamiirɛ kɛrɛ bɛl,
dikuubɛɛwiai, i biizi hiŋ
daŋ bir ba ba himmaa hɛri.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
18N nuuwɔɔ Izrɛl hina n na ŋɔ ni biinichɔg,
‘Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, yaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ sekpoŋlii,
ka i bagli yaabuu
gunla yaa n ninna
sɛɛ i dɔɔra.
Awia, bir yaa ni ba,
yaa ɛɛ siryaa yá bir ba i be.
19Yaa faa bir hattɛ kpui,
yaa kaa ra nyiŋŋuu
yá bir ba i be filaŋkeŋ.
Hiŋ wa tɛr yaa digna tuŋ la,
yaa willi yaa nyuunii
ni biinichɔg.
Yaa faa di hiihzii, di ŋmaabi,
dikuu yaa n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa
yaa bichalli saŋa maa wia.’ ”
20Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Izrɛl hina,
ii ɛɛ n biinɔŋŋaarɛ,
biizi la miŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ werge.
Di n haŋ wa yir ii sɔna,
anna fɛ ii wiarɛ ni nɔŋŋaa.
N bampirii lau iabuu,
n daŋ suŋ ii ni.
21Ií baŋ kuna ŋmɛnikɛraa,
á ra bagli bɔra.
Á ra bagli ŋmɛnɛɛ la iin niŋ ga.
Izrɛl hina, ií bir ba,
ií bir ba ii bola.
22Ɛrɛɛ ií juuri di birgi magɛi,
biizi la wia
n waa wibii dɔɔwɛi?
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ wifalii bɛl
durnya naa biini,
ú kur werge maa,
alugɔ haaŋ n na guu baal.”
Kɔraawiizi nɛra kɛrɛbɛl nyɛɛlaa wia
23Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, “Di n wa lii ii ni hɛrdumazi la baŋ lauri ia kaali la, di bir ba, ii nɛra la n du Juda hɛri ni u bola daŋ kaa ra ŋɔ wia naa, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi kissi Bizennaniinanii Ziɔn la n ɛɛ u duuribɔr la.’ 24Nɛra daŋ kpau so Juda ni u bola maa, patta ni banla maa n kpogli ba peeza di vol ra gaagi. 25N daŋ tɛɛ banla n kuuhwɛ la fɔŋŋa, di tɛɛ banla maa n huahgɛɛ diwee, bá di.”
26Denii nɛra jaa ŋɔ, “Yaa chɔɔgi dɔzii, di izi fogofogo.”
27Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, min niŋ gil nɛra ni sela su Izrɛl ni Juda hɛssi maa. 28Gunla miŋ haŋ sɔɔni bɔra di kpuzi baa, di taa baa ha, di kpegli baa, di chɔgi baa, di kpa hɛhchɔg ta ba ni la, gunnɛ n sɔɔni bɔra di lau baa bá chi chigigi lugɔ kunduulaa. 29A guŋ saŋa, nɛra wàá ka ŋɔ,
‘Mɛɛwaa di grepu nɔnnyɛgaa,
ka ba biizi nyina
lɛɛ ra nyiiri.’
30Ka bɛl maa daŋ siu, dikuu u himmaa wichɔgaa wia, unla maa n di a grepu nɔnnyɛga, u himmaa nyinaa niŋ nyiiri.”
31Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Saŋa bɛl ra bau,
ń ni Izrɛl ni Juda hina
ɛɛ nuukpaŋfalii.
32Wàá ɛɛ lugɔ nuukpaŋ la
n ni ba naabaala n faa ɛɛwɛ,
saŋa la miŋ kpogli baa
lii Ijip hɛri la.
Haali miŋ faa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ ba jaari gba,
ka ba chɔgi a guŋ nuukpannɛ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
33Nuukpaŋfalii la n ni Izrɛl hina
n niŋ ɛɛu keŋ,
n daŋ kpa n Gbɔg du ba biine,
di sɛbaa du
ba bampiree biine.
N daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum,
bá ge ɛɛ n nɛra.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
34A wàá ka ɛɛ lugɔ nɛr maa n niŋ bagli u niwee
gɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ, di ŋɔ,
‘A wesso hiŋ
zum Kɔraawiizi,’
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba maanii niŋ zumiŋ,
nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa maa.
N daŋ suŋ ba ni, di gil ba wia la n waa deŋlee la tɛɛ baa.
Màá ka liizi
ba wichɔgaa wia maa.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
35Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Minuu ɔɔ gil wiizi ra chaani hɔpizaa,
di gil baagu ni chinchiŋwilaa
ra chaani hamuŋa.
Minuu ɔɔ koozi muuzeŋ u ra lɔ, di ra kɔɔ la.
N sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ.
36Gunla wiizi furaa ni u cholaa
n niŋ du de di hanna la la,
gunnɛ Izrɛl ge du de
di birgi mag.”
37Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Di nɛr maa daŋ wer mɛgzi chiŋ,
di kaa wer pigzi zum
gunla miŋ chiŋŋi hɛri zɛɛ,
guŋwaa, n ge gba daŋ wer vɛɛ Izrɛl naanna maa ta,
dikuu wia la maa
baŋ ɛɛwɛ wia.”
38Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, ban niŋ kuari Jɛrusalɛm ma, ú ɛɛ n bolzeŋ, di chi Hananɛl Diijaŋ di ga hel Sirii Dominuuzeŋ la. 39U magbɔɔ daŋ lii de wiicholii di ga hel Garɛb giŋgimii, di bir ga hel Gɔa. 40Waluu la banna hug nɛra, di kaa ra ta hɔɔhri de la maa ni bɔwillaa la maa, di ga hel Kidrɔn Waluu n du wiifurii, guŋŋ di ga hel Zagu Dominuuzeŋ, daŋ ɛɛ bɔnaninanii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka puri a bolzeŋ gɛɛ di chɔguu.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Buys a Field
1 The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia. 2At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards. 3Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said:
I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem. 4King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face. 5Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
6Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
7Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
8Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.”
The Lord had told me to buy it 9from Hanamel, and so I did. The price was 17 pieces of silver, and I weighed out the full amount on a scale. 10-11I had two copies of the bill of sale written out: an official copy containing the details of our agreement and another copy, without the details. Some witnesses and I signed the official copy, which was folded and tied, before being sealed shut with hot wax. Then I gave Hanamel the silver. 12And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
13-14I told Baruch that the Lord had said:
Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time. 15I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country.
Jeremiah Questions the Lord
16Then I prayed:
17 Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything. 18You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful. 19With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
20You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well. 21You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt. 22Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
23But when our ancestors took over the land, they did not obey you. And now you have punished Israel with disaster. 24Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
25So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians?
The Lord Explains about the Field
26The Lord explained:
27Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
28 It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem. 29The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
30-33The kings and the officials, the priests and the prophets, and everyone else in Israel and Judah have turned from me and made me angry by worshiping idols. Again and again I have tried to teach my people to obey me, but they refuse to be corrected.
I am going to get rid of Jerusalem, because its people have done nothing but evil. 34 They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me. 35 And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
36Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
37I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety. 38They will be my people, and I will be their God. 39-41I will make their thoughts and desires pure. Then they will realize that, for their own good and the good of their children, they must worship only me. They will even be afraid to turn away from me. I will make an agreement with them that will never end, and I won't ever stop doing good things for them. With all my heart I promise that they will be planted in this land once again. 42Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
43Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals. 44But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia n yau hɛri wia
1Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia kora dii binni fi hinnɛ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia tɛŋ. Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ge kora dii binni fidiŋmantannaazi hinnɛ guŋ. 2A saŋa, di Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra ballɔ wa fɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm, di faa tɔŋ du Juda kooridia tauduura diŋŋee.
3Juda Koori Zɛdɛkiaa faa tɔŋ de, di ra nyiŋŋi u na n chollibɔr, di ŋɔ n ɔɔ siiu, di ŋɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ gil Babilɔn koori kpegli a bolzeŋ, 4Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia wàá na bɔr chɔ. Ba daŋ kpau du Babilɔn koori nonee. U daŋ nau siwii ni, ú nuu ŋɔ wia. 5U daŋ lau Koori Zɛdɛkia kaali Babilɔn, denii u ga du ka ń jaa ɛɛu gunla minna nyiŋŋi. Di u hanna yoo Babilɔn hina, ka wàá wer kpegli baa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
6Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be lugɔ 7n naara Salum biibaal Hanamɛl daŋ ba n be di wa ŋɔ, “Yau n koo la n du Anatɔf, dikuubɛɛwiai, hinuu n lulli himmaa, i dɛg lugɔ í yawuu.”
8Gunla himmaa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la, n baal Hanamɛl ba n be a diŋŋee biini, di wa ŋɔ, “Yau n koo la n du Anatɔf, n du Bɛnjamin hɛri la. Dikuubɛɛwiai, a dɛkkɔɔ hiŋ yawuu, ú ɛɛ i hor.”
N jaa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔliirɛ guŋ. 9Awia, n yau a koo Hanamɛl be, di turguu saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau fidaaniidaanɛɛ. 10N jaa jag n nonii daansɛɛ hɔŋ ni, ka gil ba sɛbi gunla maga miŋ turgee la du u ni. 11Denii n kpa a daansɛɛ hɔna, unla baŋ tɔwɛɛ, u ra bagli a koo yawaa wia ni unla baŋ waa tɔwɛɛ la. 12N kpaa tɛɛ Nɛria biibaal Baruk naabaal n ɛɛ Masɛya la. N baal Hanamɛl ni banla n di daansɛɛ di jag ba nonee, Jus hina la n soge a diŋŋee la maa sibɔɔ.
13N ŋɔ Baruk be ba sibɔɔ, 14“Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ í kpa hɔna naa, unla baŋ tɔwɛɛ ni unla n waa tɔwɛɛ la maa, di du tɔg biini, á wer birgi. 15Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ diini, kooni, daazi ani grepu daazi kooni maanii, bá kaa yau hɛri naa biini.”
Jɛrɛmia wiisuŋŋaa wia
16Miŋ wa kpa a daansɛɛ hɔŋ tɛɛ Nɛria biibaal Baruk tuŋ, n jaa suŋŋi wiizi, di ŋɔ,
17“Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, hinuu kpa i fɔŋŋazeŋ ta chiŋ ni hɛri, wiimaa waa kpol i be. 18Hinuu bagli nɔŋŋaa ra tɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa, ka ɔɔ tɛrgi nɛra digna dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia. Hinuu dɔɔ sɔŋ ni kpegzi werge. I sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ. 19I ɔɔ ra ta jinananaarɛ, di ra ɛɛ wizenaa. I zum nɛr maa wiɛɛlaarɛ, di ɔɔ turgi bɛl maa u wiɛɛlaa kim. 20I faa ɛɛ wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wiarɛ Ijip hɛri, haali di haa ra ɛɛa wa lii ni zinaa, Izrɛl hina ni newea maa biini, a guŋ gil i dɔɔ sɔŋ bɔr maa. 21I kpa witittaa ni nuukpuuri wiarɛ du yaa dɔma ɔnsii werge, di kpa i fɔŋŋa ni i banonii lizi i nɛra Izrɛl hina lii Ijip hɛri. 22Hinuu tɛɛ baa hɛrsum naa hiŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ i daŋ tɛɛ ba naabaala la. 23Baŋ wa ballɛ di wa lɛɛ a hɛri dɔɔ, ka ba wɛɛ hiŋŋɛ gɛɛ di hiŋ i Gbɔg. Ba waa gunla hiŋ ŋɔ ba ɛɛ la ɛɛwɛ. Awiarɛ i kpa hɛhchɔg naa ta ba ni la.
24Babilɔn hina wa teŋri daazii teli a bolzeŋ koŋlii ni, di ta pizenaa bar a bolzeŋ maa, bá wer tinni zuu de, di lɔ baa. Laal, lɔzi ani wiilchɔgii daŋ gil bá kpegli a bolzeŋ. I nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ wii la maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la ɛɛ wibiire. 25Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, hinuu ŋɔ di n yau a koo naa, nɛra naa n di u daansɛɛ naa see, haali Babilɔn hina n na ba bá wa foozi a bolzeŋ dɔɔ gba.”
26Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 27“N ɛɛ newea maa Kɔraawiizii, wii bɛl kpolloo tɛŋŋ? 28Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu ń kpa bolzeŋ naa du Babilɔn laallɔɔra ni ba Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza nonee, bá kpegluu. 29Ba daŋ wa pig a bolzeŋ, di fuuh u ni diini la nɛra n na fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma a salli ra tɛɛ vug Baal, di ta siŋ ra tɛɛ vuga aŋhina ge, di ra fuuh n baaŋ la wia.
30Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa waa wiɛɛlii maa dɔɔwɛ bá pɔlaa saŋa maa, di wichɔgaa ɛɛi bɛŋ lɛi, n sibɔɔ. Wibii maa, Izrɛl hina waa wiɛɛlii maa dɔɔwɛ, di n baaŋfuuhri wia bɛŋ lɛi, dikuu kuna la baŋ kuarɛɛ wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 31A hɔl la baŋ ma bolzeŋ naa di wa lii ni zinaa maanii, ba gil n baaŋ fuuh werge, n jaa fɛ lugɔ n chɔguu. 32Izrɛl ni Juda hina gillɔɔ n baaŋ fuuh, dikuu ba ni ba koora, ba nabɔnzi, n kizeehina ani n dɔgtɛɛzi wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛwɛ wia. 33Ba bir ba haraa kpuŋ, haali miŋ haa vɛɛwɛ ra bagli baa digiidigii gba. Ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá nuu n baglaa gɛɛ di hiŋ n nua. 34Haali ba kpa ba vuga la miŋ kiiwee chiŋŋi n Dia biini, di doŋuu. 35Ba ma mbusu lizibɔraa tɛɛ vug Baal, Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu biini, di kpa ba biizi lizi mbusuzi ra tɛɛ vug Mɔlɛk. Maa ba be ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ bá ɛɛ guŋ, maa fɛwɛɛ lugɔ ba daŋ sɛɛ ɛɛ a keŋ wiɛɛlaa naa, di gil Juda hina ɛɛ wichɔgaa.”
36Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ n be, “Jɛrɛmia, a nɛra ra ŋɔu lugɔ laal, lɔzi ani wiilchɔgiirɛ niŋ gil bolzeŋ naa zuu Babilɔn koori nonee biini. A nuu gunla miŋ dɔɔwɛ n ŋɔ. 37N daŋ chaali baa lii bɔra la maa miŋ kpa n baaŋ di yaari baa, ba ga du la, di bir ba ba ni bɔnnaa, bá wa so pɛrɛtɛ. 38Ba daŋ ɛɛ n nɛra, ń ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum. 39N daŋ gil ba nfɛrɛ ni ba wiɛɛlaa maa ɛɛ kpaŋ. Denii bá ra tɔgziŋ saŋa maa, guŋ hiini ba himmaa, ba biizi ani ba naanna. 40N daŋ gil n ni baa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ. Màá gil ba winanaa ɛɛi maa. N daŋ du baa bɔkpega, bá ra ɔmiŋ. Guŋ gil ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka bir har kpuŋ. 41N daŋ kpa bɔsɔna di ra ɛɛ baa winanaa, di soŋŋi baa hɛri naa, bá haŋ du de di hanna la, saŋaa saŋa maa.
42Kennaa miŋ haŋ kpa tɔɔrɔɔ ni dɔgnya ta nɛra naa ni naa, gunnɛ ń gil ba nyɛɛli, gunla miŋ ŋɔ nua la. 43A nɛra ra ŋɔu lugɔ hɛri naa daŋ du lugɔ hɛribɔduma, bɔr la newea gɛɛ sela n waa duwɛɛ, ka bá kpau tɛɛ Babilɔn hina. Ka ba daŋ kaa yau kooni u biini. 44Ka saŋa bɛl daŋ wa hel, nɛra bir kpa ba saliŋhuŋŋu di ba waa yau kooni. Ba daŋ jag nonibee di di daansɛɛ Bɛnjamin hɛri, boljigzi la n bar Jɛrusalɛm, Juda bola ani giŋgimee hɛssi bola la n du wiicholii ni Nɛgɛv la, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ gil ba bir nyɛɛli. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
The Lord Promises To Give the Land Back to His People
1-2I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me:
I am the Lord, and I created the whole world. 3Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
4-5Many of the houses in Jerusalem and some of the buildings at the royal palace have been torn down to be used in repairing the walls to keep out the Babylonian attackers. Now there are empty spaces where the buildings once stood. But I am furious, and these spaces will be filled with the bodies of the people I kill. The people of Jerusalem will cry out to me for help, but they are evil, and I will ignore their prayers.
6Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace. 7I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before. 8They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt. 9When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
10Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear 11 happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say:
“We praise you,
Lord All-Powerful!
You are good to us,
and your love never fails.”
The land will once again be productive. 12-13Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord's Wonderful Promise
14 The Lord said:
I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
15I promise that the time will come
when I will appoint a king
from the family of David,
a king who will be honest
and rule with justice.
16In those days,
Judah will be safe;
Jerusalem will have peace
and will be named,
“The Lord Gives Justice.”
17 The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants, 18 and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
19Then the Lord told me:
20I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them, 21and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel, 22and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
23The Lord also said:
24You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
25Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands. 26In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ bir kuari u nɛra soŋŋi wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, di n haa du tauduura diŋŋee la biini, 2“Minuu unla n ma hɛri, di tau, di chiŋŋuu. N sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi. 3Yiriŋ, n daŋ sɛɛ, di ŋɔ i be wizenaa ni wisuahlaa la hiŋ waa zummɛ. 4Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ di ra bagli a bolzeŋ diini ni Juda kooridia la baŋ puree, bá kpa ma koŋlii di gber Babilɔn, dikuu laallɔɔra wia la. 5Ba ni Babilɔn hina n niŋ waa lɔ dɔŋa la, Jɛrusalɛm diini maanii niŋ su lalaa. Baabuu ń kpa n baaŋ kpu la. N daŋ bir har kpu a bolzeŋ, dikuu Jɛrusalɛm hina biinikpola wia.
6Annii maa har, n daŋ chaa baa, bá dɔɔ alaanfia, di dɔɔ bampirsɔna werge, di so pɛrɛtɛ. 7N daŋ kpogli Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa lii bɔra la baŋ lauri baa kaali la, di bir ba, di wa kuari baa soŋŋi, gunla baŋ faa duwɛɛ la. 8N daŋ lizi ba wichɔgaa la maa baŋ ɛɛŋ ba ni, di gil ba wichɔgaa ni baŋ vɛɛŋ la tɛɛ baa. 9Jɛrusalɛm daŋ gil n dɔɔ sɔŋ, bɔsɔna ani girme, bá ra chɔliŋ durnya hɛssi hina maa n nuu winanaa la miŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛu la sibɔɔ. Denii ɔnsii lau baa bá bɔra ra sa, di ba wa nuu gunla la miŋ gillɛ a bolzeŋ nyɛɛli di dɔɔ bampirsɔna wia.”
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Nɛra ra ŋɔ bɔnnaa wiarɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ diŋgelaa. Nɛra gɛɛ sela waa hoo de. Wibiire ba ŋɔ. Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda bolzenaa maanii chɔɔwɛ woo. Newea ni sela waa hoo de. Ka ii daŋ kaa wa nuu, 11nɛra n ninna chaasi ni bɔsɔna, di ra nuu haŋfalii ni u jaari loobee ni banla n kpa kuna ra ba, bá wa jaamiŋ, n Dia biini. Ba danna ŋɔ,
‘Ií ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la jaaŋ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u wia wessoo,
u nɔŋŋaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.’
N daŋ gil a hɛri naa nyɛɛli werge maa, gunla uŋ faa duwɛɛ la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
12Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “A hɛri naa n chɔɔ diŋgela, newea ni sela waa hoo de naa, ka peeza diiribɔra daŋ kaa wa du u bola maa biine, penɔɔna kpogli ba sela la, a gaa di. 13A hɛri giŋgimee bɔr bola biine, wiicholii giŋgimee zɛɛzi, Nɛgɛv, Bɛnjamin hɛri, Jɛrusalɛm boljigzi la n baruu ani Juda bola biine. Penɔɔna daŋ kaa kur ba peeza. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
14Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, min niŋ gil nua la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl ni Juda hina la, su u maga.
15A saŋa hiŋ,
n daŋ lizi koori la
wia n deŋlee lii
Koori Deevid naanna biini.
Waabuu ninna ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee,
di ra di wibii,
a hɛri maa biini.
16A saŋa hiŋ, Juda hina daŋ na lɛɛi,
Jɛrusalɛm hina ge so pɛrɛtɛ.
Sɔnnaabuu ba wa kpa ra yir a bolzeŋ,
‘Kɔraawiizii Yaa Lɛɛri.’ ”
17Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Koori Deevid ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá nyaa nɛr la n niŋ di Izrɛl kora 18gɛɛ n kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la gba wàá nyaa nɛr la n niŋ ɔɔ wa chi n see, di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, di ra fuuh mbusuzi lizaa mia kuna, di lizi mbusuzi lizaa kuna di ra tɛŋ.”
19Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 20“N ni hɔpizaa ni hamuŋa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ, bɛ́l maa ɔɔ ba saŋa la n dɛg u balaa. A keŋ nuukpaŋ naa wàá wer chɔgi maa. 21Gunnɛ n ni Koori Deevid ni Levi dee la n ɛɛ n kizeehina di ra humiŋ la, nuukpaŋ la wàá wer chɔgi maa la. 22N daŋ gil n balii Koori Deevid naanna ni Levi dee la n na humiŋ la du kpil alugɔ chinchiŋwilaa baŋ wàá wer kur gɛɛ gunla baŋ wàá wer kur hɛɛhriichaa la.”
23Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, 24“I nuu gunla nɛra naa n na ŋɔ lugɔ n vɛɛ Izrɛl ni Juda la miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hinnɛ. Awia, ba ra gbɛlli baabuu. Ba waa kaa ra yir baa hɛri bɛl hina. 25Di n ni hɔpizaa ni hamuŋa faa waa nuukpaŋ ɛɛwɛ, di dau chiŋ ni hɛri gbɔgni, 26guŋwaa, n daŋ faa vɛɛ Jekɔb ni n balii Koori Deevid naanna, di vɛɛ u biibaal bɛl lizaa ú di kora Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb naanna ni. N daŋ bir kpogli baa lii bɔra la baŋ lauri baa kaali la, di ba, di suŋ ba ni, di gil ba nyɛɛli.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Warns Zedekiah
1 King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me 2to say to King Zedekiah:
I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down. 3You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
4Zedekiah, I promise that you won't die in battle. 5You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
6I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said. 7Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured.
The People Break a Promise
8-10King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
11But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
12That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
13I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves. 14 As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service.
Your ancestors did not obey me, 15-16but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
17You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
18You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf. 19-20I will let your enemies take all of you prisoner, including the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the royal officials, the priests, and everyone else who walked between the two parts of the calf. These enemies will kill you and leave your bodies lying on the ground as food for birds and wild animals.
21-22These enemies are King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia and his army. They have stopped attacking Jerusalem, but they want to kill King Zedekiah and his high officials. So I will command them to return and attack again. This time they will conquer the city and burn it down, and they will capture Zedekiah and his officials. I will also let them destroy the towns of Judah, so that no one can live there any longer.
translation_text:
Koori Zɛdɛkia karfaa wia
1Saŋa la Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ni u laallɔɔra, u kossi ani nɛra la maa n du u kora diiribɔr n faa ra naa Jɛrusalɛm hina ni bola la maa n baruu la, 2Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, “La Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia be, di ga ŋɔ u be lugɔ n na nyiŋŋuu ń kpa bolzeŋ naa du Babilɔn koori nonee, ú fuuuh. 3Awia, hàá na bɔr chɔ, ba daŋ lawii wa tɛu. I daŋ na Babilɔn koori ni siwii, í nuu so ŋɔ wia tɛɛ dɔŋa, ka ba kpoglii kaali Babilɔn.
4Ama, Koori Zɛdɛkia, a nuu gunla minna ŋɔ i wia. Ba wàá kpui laal biini. 5I daŋ siu ni bampirsɔna. Gunla baŋ ɔɔ faa fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di hug i naabaala la n di kossi mɔɔ ka tɛi, di tɛɛ baa girme la, guŋ himmaanii bá fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma tɛi. Ba danna wii i lee, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Yaa koori siuwɔɔ!’ Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
6Denii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ wia naa maa tɛɛ Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia, Jɛrusalɛm biini. 7Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra la n haa ra yoo Jɛrusalɛm ni bolzenaa la n kawɛɛ Juda hɛri, ba ra yiraa Lakis ni Azɛka la, a bɛnnɛ faa haa dɔɔ koŋliikpega baraa, Juda hɛri.
Yoma n niŋ na bahinaa wia
8Saŋa la Koori Zɛdɛkia ni Jɛrusalɛm hina maa n ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, bá sii yoma hinnai wia la, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be lugɔ 9nɛr maa gil Hibru hinuu la n ɛɛ u yom, na u hiŋ, di baallɛ gɛɛ haannɛ. Bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa lau u dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu yom. 10Awia, a nɛra maa ni ba sitɔɔra sɛɛ lugɔ ba daŋ gil ba yoma na bahinaa, ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka lau baa ɛɛ yoma. Ba jaa sɛɛ, di ta baa. 11Ka a harbɔɔ, ba bir ba nfɛssi, di kaa lauri baa di wa ɛɛ yoma.
12Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 13“Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ni ii naabaala ɛɛ nuukpannɛ, saŋa la miŋ lizi baa lii Ijip hɛri la, hɛri la baŋ faa ɛɛ yoma la. N faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ 14binni aniidaanɛɛ maa biini, bɛ́l maa ɔɔ ta Hibru hinuu la n kpa u hiŋ yoo tɛu. Di u wa humii binni anumbɛl, tau ŋmɛnɛɛ, ú dɔɔ u hiŋ. Ka ii mɛɛwaa faa waa sɛɛwɛ tɛŋ gɛɛ di hiŋ n nua. 15A hɔpizaa anɛɛ naa biinii, ii bir ii nfɛssi, di ɛɛ wii la n pariŋ. Ii maa sɛɛ lugɔ ii daŋ ta ii dɔŋahina Izrɛl hina, bá dɔɔ bahinaa. Haali ii ɛɛ nuukpaŋ n sibɔɔ, n Dia la iinna jaamiŋ la biini. 16Ka ii kaa bir ii nfɛssi, di gbɛlliŋ. Ii maa kaa bir lau ii yoma la iiŋ tawɛɛ a par baa la, di fir baa, ba kaa ɛɛ yoma.
17Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ii gbɛllimbuu. Ii waa sɛɛwɛ ta ii lulla Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛɛ, bá dɔɔ bahinaa. Awia, miŋwaa daŋ ta ia ŋmɛnɛɛ, ii dɔɔ iihinaa, bá kpu ia laal biini, wiilchɔgii ni lɔchɔgii jaa. N daŋ gil hɛssi hina maa nua kpu ii wia. 18Baala la n chɔgi n nuukpaŋ, ba waa u ŋmɛnizi hiŋŋɛ n sibɔɔ la, n daŋ ɛɛ baa lugɔ nabii la baŋ chauh anɛɛ, di vol a baaŋ. 19Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm sitɔɔra, kooridia nabɔnzi, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani a hɛri nɛra la maa n vol a nabii bɔra anɛɛ la baambaaŋ, 20n daŋ kpa baa du ba dɔma la n na nyiŋŋi ba kpui la nonee biini. Ba bɔra daŋ birgi diwee tɛɛ zaahra ni pir sela.
21N daŋ kpa Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia ni u nabɔnzi maa du ba dɔma la n na nyiŋŋi baa, bá kpu la nonee ni Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra la n faa bir har la nonee biini. 22N daŋ gil ba bir ba a bolzeŋ naa, di wa lɔ baa, di fuuh u maa, ú puri chɔɔ burburbur. N daŋ gil Juda bolzenaa maa birgi diŋgelli. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
Learn a Lesson from the Rechabites
1 When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me, 2“Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
3So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan. 4I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
5I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
6But they answered:
No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine 7or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
8-10Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops.
