And we have lived in tents, 11except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
12-13Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem:
I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson 14from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me! 15You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
16The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me, 17your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
18Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan:
“I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab, 19so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_text:
Rɛkab domee wia
1Saŋa la Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim n wa di Juda kora la, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 2“La ga yir Rɛkab domee hina, bá ba Kɔraawiizi Dia diibizi la bɛl biini, di wa tɛɛ baa siŋ bá nyɔɔ.”
3Denii n la ga yir Habazinia biibaal Jɛrɛmia ge biibaal Jaazania ni u lulla ni u biibaala maa, baabuu Rɛkab domee hina, 4di kpogli baa wa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Igdalia biibaal Hanan biibaala chɔɔribɔr. A dia naa faa hiŋ a nabɔnzi hor la n hɔŋ Salum biibaal Maasɛya la n ɛɛ dominuuguuri hor ninɛɛ. 5Denii n kpa siŋ ni libizi tɛɛ baa, di ŋɔ, “Ií lɛɛ siŋ nyɔɔ!”
6Ka ba bir ŋɔ, “Yaa waa sinna nyɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa naabaal Rɛkab biibaal Jonadab ŋɔ yaa benii, ‘Ií ni ii naanna ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa nyɔɔ siŋ.’ 7U kaa ŋɔ yaa benii lugɔ yá gilɛɛ waa ma diini, di gilɛɛ waa dau kooni gɛɛ di waa duu grepu daazi kooni. Dí ya ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ annii bɛl maa, ka ɔɔ ra zuu tanti diini biine. Denii ya wer dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ, di du hɛri la yaa n ɛɛ famaraa naa biini. 8Yaa ra hiŋ wia la maa yaa naabaal Jonadab n ŋɔ yaa be labuu. Yaa himmaa gɛɛ yaa haana ni biizi bɛl maa ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa siŋ nyɔɔwɛ 9gɛɛ di ma diini ra zuu gɛɛ di dɔɔ grepu daazi kooni, gɛɛ di duu kuna. 10Yaa hiŋ yaa naabaal Jonadab nua labuu di ra zuu tanti diini. 11Ka Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n wa zuu hɛri naa di lɔ yaa, di lɛɛu dɔɔ la, yaa ŋɔ, ‘Ií ba ya chɔ lii Babilɔn ni Siiria laallɔɔra be, di kaali Jɛrusalɛm.’ Awiarɛ yaa ka Jɛrusalɛm biini la.”
12Denii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 13“La ga ŋɔ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina be lugɔ di ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá helli wia, amɔ, ba wàá helli wia, di hiŋ n wiŋɔzia? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 14Jonadab naanna faa hiŋ u nuarɛ, di vɛɛ siŋ nyɔɔi di wa lii ni zinaa. Ka n na ŋɔ wiarɛ di ra tɛɛ ia digiidigii, ka iawaa waa sɛɛwɛ ii nuu tɛŋ, di hiŋ n nua. 15N hum n dɔgtɛɛzii ii be, digiidigii. Ba ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ií bɛl maa gil u biinikpola wiɛɛlaa, di chɛr u manni. Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vuga, di waa sɛɛ a dɔɔra. Denii ii wer du hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ii ni ii naabaala la biini. Ka ii waa sɛɛwɛ nuu n be, di hiŋ n nua. 16Ka Jonadab naanna waa hiŋ u nuarɛ. Ka iawaa, waa sɛɛwɛ ii hiŋ n nua.
17Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií ra nuu! N daŋ kpa hɛhchɔgni la maa miŋ ŋɔ a wia la, di ta Juda hina ni nɛra la maa n du Jɛrusalɛm ni. N ŋɔ wiarɛ tɛɛ baa, ka ba waa nuuwɛ, di yir baa, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ.”
18Denii mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia jaa ŋɔ Rɛkab domee hina la be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ii hiŋ ii naabaal Jonadab nuarɛ, di ɛɛ wia la maa uŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ ia la. 19Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Rɛkab biibaal Jonadab ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá nyaa nɛr la n niŋ ɔɔ lii u domee biini di ra humiŋ.”

english_text:
King Jehoiakim Burns Jeremiah's First Scroll
1 During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah, 2since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you, 3then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
4I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll. 5Then I said,
Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple, 6so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud. 7The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
8-10In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud.
This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials. 11Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said. 12When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah. 13Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people. 14Then the officials sent Jehudi and Shelemiah to tell Baruch, “Bring us that scroll.”
When Baruch arrived with the scroll, 15the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did. 16After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked, 17“Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
18“Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
19The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
20-22The officials put the scroll in Elishama's room and went to see the king, who was in one of the rooms where he lived and worked during the winter. It was the ninth month of the year, so there was a fire burning in the fireplace, and the king was sitting nearby. After the officials told the king about the scroll, he sent Jehudi to get it. Then Jehudi started reading the scroll to the king and his officials. 23-25But every time Jehudi finished reading three or four columns, the king would tell him to cut them off with his penknife and throw them in the fire. Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah begged the king not to burn the scroll, but he ignored them, and soon there was nothing left of it.
The king and his servants listened to what was written on the scroll, but they were not the least bit afraid, and they did not tear their clothes in sorrow.
26The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us.
Jeremiah's Second Scroll
27I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me 28to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one. 29Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim:
Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals. 30So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah. 31You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
32After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_text:
Koori Jɛhɔyakim n fuuh Jɛrɛmia hɔŋ wia
1Juda Koori Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ biinii, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 2“Kpa hɔŋ sɛbi wia la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛi, di ra bagli Izrɛl ni Juda ani hɛssi la maa n kawɛɛ hina wia, di lii saŋa la miŋ faarɛɛ ŋɔ wia ra tɛi, Koori Jɔsia kora dii saŋa, di wa lii ni zinaa la. 3Aŋhinabe, di Juda hina wa nuu gunla minna nyiŋŋi ń kpa hɛhchɔgni ta ba ni, ba bɛl maa daŋ gil biinikpola wiɛɛlaa. Denii ń gil ba biinikpola ni ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.”
4Denii mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia yir Nɛria biibaal Baruk, di ŋɔ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la di ra tɛu, u sɛbaa ra dau hɔŋ ni. 5Awia, n ŋɔ Baruk be, “Ba wan tɛɛwɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ n kaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia biini. 6Awia, la Kɔraawiizi Dia, di ga karmi Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ i sɛbi dau a hɔŋ ni la tɛɛ a nɛra, ba nuuvɔɔi hɔpizii hɔl. Karmuu tɛɛ Juda hɛri nɛra la maa n lii bola di ba de la, bá maa nuu. 7Aŋhinabe, ba daŋ suŋŋi wiizi, di gil ba biinikpola wiɛɛlaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ɔnzi baabuu ni u baaŋfuuihchɔgii.”
8Denii Baruk ɛɛ wia la maa miŋ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la, di ga karmi a hɔŋ Kɔraawiizi Dia biini. 9Koori Jɛhɔyakim, Juda kora dii binni anuehiŋ baaguzi kabɛl biinii, nɛra la maa n du Jɛrusalɛm ni banla maa n lii Juda bola faa vɔɔ nua, bá wia par Kɔraawiizi. 10Karchi Safan biibaal Gɛmaria diibee la n du Kɔraawiizi Dia chiŋ diŋŋee, n du Kɔraawiizi Dia Dominuufalii la biinii, Baruk karmi mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia wiŋɔɔlaa lii a hɔŋ biini tɛɛ a nɛra maa.
Baruk n karmi a hɔŋ tɛɛ nabɔnzi wia
11Gɛmaria biibaal Mikaaya, u naabaal ge ɛɛ Safan, n wa nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlaa la maa Baruk n karmɛɛ lii a hɔŋ biini la, 12u izi la kooridia karchi diibee la n du kooridia biini, bɔr la nabɔnzi la maa n faa chaalɛɛ la. Baabuu karchi Ɛlisama, Sɛmaaya biibaal Dɛlaaya, Akbɔ biibaal Ɛlnatan, Safan biibaal Gɛmaria, Hanania biibaal Zɛdɛkia ani ba nabɔnzi la maa n kawɛɛ. 13Mikaaya n wa ŋɔ wia la maa uŋ nuuwɛ Baruk n karmɛɛ, lii a hɔŋ biini tɛɛ a nɛra wa tuŋ, 14a nabɔnzi maa hum Nɛtania biibaal Jɛhudi, u naabaal n ɛɛ Kusi biibaal Sɛlɛmia, dí u ga ŋɔ Baruk be, “Kpa hɔŋ la hiŋ karmɛɛ tɛɛ a nɛra la ba.”
Awia, Baruk kpa a hɔŋ di la. 15Ba ŋɔ u be, “Gaafura, ka so hɛri di karmuu tɛɛ yaa.” 16Baŋ wa nuu wia la uŋ karmɛɛ tɛɛ baa la, ɔnsii lau baa, ba bir binni dɔŋa, ka ŋɔ Baruk be, “Yaa daŋ ga bagli wia naa tɛɛ koori.” 17Denii ba ŋɔ Baruk be, “Bagli yaa gunla hiŋ ɛɛwɛ sɛbi wia naa maa. Jɛrɛmiaa ŋɔa, i sɛbiaa?”
18Baruk ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, waabuu ŋɔa, n sɛbaa dau hɔnnaa ni.”
19Denii a nabɔnzi ŋɔ Baruk be, “Í ni Jɛrɛmia chɔ ga suah, di gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa ra zum bɔr la iiŋ duwɛɛ.”
20Baŋ wa kpa a hɔŋ dau karchi Ɛlisama dia tuŋ, ba la koori be di ga bagli wiimaa tɛu. 21Denii a koori hum Jɛhudi, dí u la ga kpa a hɔŋ ba. U la ga kpau lii karchi Ɛlisama dia ba. Uŋ wa ba u ni, a koori gil u karmuu tɛɛ u ni nabɔnzi la maa n chigɛ baruu la. 22Baaguzi kabɛlhiŋ biinii, di a koori faa sogo u waari saŋa dia, di ra ŋmaani niŋ. 23Di Jɛhudi haŋ wa karmi a hɔŋ bɔra ahoro gɛɛ anaazu maa tuŋ, a koori ɔɔ kpa kizijigaa di lawaa mɔŋ du a niŋ biini. Gunnɛ u ɛɛ, di fuuh a hɔŋ maa tuŋ. 24Ɔnsii ni biinichɔg faa waa a koori ni u nabɔnzi la maa n nuu wia naa lauwɛ. 25Haali Ɛlnatan, Dɛlaaya ani Gɛmaria n suŋŋi a koori lugɔ u gilɛɛ fuuh a hɔŋ, ka waa nuuwɛ tɛɛ baa, 26ka ŋɔ u biibaal Jɛramiil, Azriɛl biibaal Sɛraaya ani Abdiil biibaal Sɛlɛmia be lugɔ bá ga lau karchi Baruk ni Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia ba. Ka Kɔraawiizi faa kpa baa suah.
27A koori n wa fuuh a hɔŋ tuŋ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 28“Kaa kpa hɔŋ bɛl, di sɛbi wia la maa hiŋ faa felee sɛbi dau unla Koori Jɛhɔyakim n fuuhwe la, di kaa dau u ni. 29Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be lugɔ ń ŋɔ Juda Koori Jɛhɔyakim be, ‘I fuuh a hɔnnɛ ka pɛɛzi Jɛrɛmia lugɔ bɛɛwiarɛ u sɛbi lugɔ Babilɔn koori daŋ ba wa chɔgi hɛri naa, di kpu a newea ni sela maanɛi? 30Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ra ŋɔ hìŋ́ Juda Koori Jɛhɔyakim wia lugɔ i ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá dɔɔ nɛr la n niŋ so Koori Deevid koorikara ni. Di i wa siuwɔ, ba daŋ kpai ha bossee, wiizi kpui bɔchaaŋ, hamuŋa ge, ŋmɛnii chol i ni. 31N daŋ tɔɔri i ni i balaa ni i biizi maa, dikuu ii biinikpola wia. N daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg la maa miŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ chol ii ni banla n du Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina maa la, di ta ii ni, dikuu iiŋ waa nuuwɛ tɛŋ wia.’ ”
32Awia, mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia kaa kpa hɔŋ bɛl tɛɛ Nɛria biibaal karchi Baruk. N kaa kuari ŋɔ wia la himmaa n faa du unla Koori Jɛhɔyakim n fuuhwe la biini, Baruk sɛbaa dau, di faa kpa wiŋɔɔlaa kpila n lia jaa.

english_text:
King Zedekiah Asks Jeremiah To Pray
1 King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead. 2But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
3-5Later, the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem, but they left after learning that the Egyptian army was headed in this direction.
One day, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to talk with me. At that time, I was free to go wherever I wanted, because I had not yet been put in prison. Jehucal and Zephaniah said, “Jeremiah, please pray to the Lord our God for us.”
6-7Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message:
Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt. 8Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire. 9Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before. 10Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire.
Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
11The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us. 12So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land. 13I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
14“I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials. 15-16They were angry and ordered the soldiers to beat me. Then I was taken to the house that belonged to Jonathan, one of the king's officials. It had been turned into a prison, and I was kept in a basement room.
After I had spent a long time there, 17King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?”
“Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
18Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation? 19Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem? 20Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
21King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_text:
Baŋ tɔ Jɛrɛmia dia wia
1Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza faa tɔ Jɔsia biibaal Zɛdɛkiaa Juda kora. Jɛhɔyakim biibaal Koori Jɛhɔyachin bɔttɛ u faa lɛɛ di a kora. 2Ka u ni u balaa gɛɛ u nɛra faa waa sɛɛwɛ bá hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, gunla mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ baa la.
3Ama, Koori Zɛdɛkia faa hum Sɛlɛmia biibaal Jɛhukal ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Maasɛya biibaal Zɛfania, dí ba ba mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia be, di wa ŋɔ, “Jaande maa, suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la tɛɛ yaa.”
4A saŋa naa, di n haa dɔɔ n hiŋ, di vol ra ɛɛ n kipar a nɛra biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, di ba haa wan tɔwɛɛ dia. 5A saŋa, di Babilɔn hina laallɔɔra teŋ ballɔ waa fɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina, ka baŋ wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Ijip koori laallɔɔra gilli ba himmaa hɛri magaa tuŋ, ba bir lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali.
6Denii Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ n be, 7dí n ŋɔ Koori Zɛdɛkia be, “Ijip koori laallɔɔra ra bau bá wa hiinii, ka ba daŋ bir kaali ba hɛri. 8Ka Babilɔn laallɔɔra daŋ bir ba wa pig a bolzeŋ naa, di kpegluu di fuuh u maa.
9Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ra karfi iabuu lugɔ ií gilɛɛ ra dar iihinaa, di ra fɛ lugɔ a Babilɔn hina daŋ gil ia. Wibii maa, ba wàá gil ia ŋmɛnɛ maa! 10Haali di ii faa wettoo kpegli Babilɔn hina laallɔɔra maa gba, ka banla n na pira, di chɔɔgi ba tanti diini biine, daŋ haa lii di fuuh a bolzeŋ naa maa nyaamm.”
11Babilɔn laallɔɔra la n wa kuu Ijip koori laallɔɔra wia di chɔ lii Jɛrusalɛm di wa tuŋ, 12mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia jaa izi a bolzeŋ di ra la Bɛnjamin hɛri, ń ga lɛɛ n kapɛttɛ kuna n nɛra be. 13Ka miŋ ga hel Bɛnjamin dominuuzeŋ, de guure nabɔma Sɛlɛmia biibaal Irija la naabaal n ɛɛ Hanania n wa naŋ, u lawiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “I chɔwɔɔrɛ ra zuu Babilɔn hina!”
14N ŋɔ u be, “Karaa, màá chɔwɛɛ lɛi ra zuu Babilɔn hina.” Ka Irija waa sɛɛwɛ nuu tɛŋ, ka lawiŋ di kpogliŋ ba nabɔnzi be. 15Denii ba baana fuuh n ni werge, ba gil ba lɔɔziŋ, ka kpaŋ ga tɔ kooridia karchi Jonatan dia la baŋ lizɛɛ, u ɛɛ nɛra tɔi dia biini.
16A dia zɛɛ diibee biinii ba faa tɔŋ. N faa du de, di birgi werge maa. 17Denii Koori Zɛdɛkia gil ba ga liziŋ ba u kooridia. Miŋ wa ballɛ, u suahzi pɛɛziŋ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ wiibɛllɛ uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ra tɛɛ yaa gɛɛ?” N ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, ba daŋ kpai du Babilɔn koori nonee biini.”
18Denii n pɛɛzi Koori Zɛdɛkia, “Bɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ n ɛɛ i ni i nabɔnzi ni a nɛra naa maa, i gil ba tɔŋ diai? 19Lee Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la n ŋɔ wia waa huuzii, di ŋɔ lugɔ Babilɔn koori wàá ba di wa lɔ i ni i hɛri hina la duɛi? 20Jara, nuu n suŋŋaa naa, ka gilɛɛ kaa wàá la n ni Jonatan dia, di i ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ ga siu de.”
21Denii Koori Zɛdɛkia gil ba tɔŋ dia u koori diŋŋee la biini, u ra binni n ni. Hɔpizii maa, ɔɔ gil ba tɛŋ paanuu lii paanuu kuara be, guŋŋ a maa wa tuŋ a bolzeŋ biini.

english_text:
Jeremiah Is Held Prisoner in a Dry Well
1One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah 2-3that the Lord had said, “If you stay here in Jerusalem, you will die in battle or from disease or hunger, and the Babylonian army will capture the city anyway. But if you surrender to the Babylonians, they will let you live.”
4So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
5Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
6Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
7-8Ebedmelech from Ethiopia was an official at the palace, and he heard what they had done to me. So he went to speak with King Zedekiah, who was holding court at Benjamin Gate. 9Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
10Zedekiah answered, “Take 30 of my soldiers and pull Jeremiah out before he dies.”
11Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well. 12Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did, 13the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards.
King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
14King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
15“Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
16He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
17Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down. 18But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
19Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
20I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you. 21But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey, 22then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you:
Friends you trusted led you astray.
Now you're trapped in mud,
and those friends you trusted
have all turned away.
23The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
24Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life. 25And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them. 26So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
27The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
28 I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_text:
Baŋ lau Jɛrɛmia ta kɔlɔŋ biini
1Denii Matan biibaal Sɛfatia, Pasur biibaal Gɛdalia, Sɛlɛmia biibaal Jɛhukal ani Malkija biibaal Pasur, nuu wia la maa mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ a nɛra lugɔ 2Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Nɛr la maa n niŋ du a bolzeŋ naa, tokobi, lɔchɔgii gɛɛ wiilchɔgiirɛ niŋ kpuu. Ka unla waa maa n niŋ di kuu Babilɔn hina be, daŋ na u hiŋ.” 3Awia, Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Wibii maa, n daŋ kpa a bolzeŋ naa du Babilɔn hina laallɔɔra nonee biini, bá kpegluu.”
4Denii a nabɔnzi ŋɔ a koori be, “Baal naa dɛg kpuirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ra du a laallɔɔra la n ka a bolzeŋ naa ni a nɛra maanii bɔhuaih, dikuu wia la uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ra tɛɛ baa naa wia. A baal naa waa nɛra naa ni winanaa ra nyiŋŋi, ba chɔgaarɛ u ra nyiŋŋi.”
5Koori Zɛdɛkia ŋɔ, “Too, a du ii be, gunla maa iin niŋ ɛɛu, ii ɛɛu. Màá tɔ ia ŋmɛnɛɛ.”
6Denii ba lau mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia, di kpaŋ du a koori biibaal Malkija kɔlɔŋ la n du guure diŋŋee la biini. Ŋmɛnnii ba faa kpa vɔɔzi n vaampɛrɛzi, ka kpaŋ du a kɔlɔŋ hiŋ biini. Nii faa waa hoo u biini, kpɛchɛgaa bɛnnɛ faa du de, n naazi jaa ra muzi.
7Ka Itiopia hinuu Ɛbɛd Mɛlɛk, n ɛɛ a kooridia nabɔma la, nuu lugɔ ba lawimbuu du a kɔlɔŋ biini. A saŋa, di a koori haa sogo Bɛnjamin Dominuuzeŋ la di ra di nɛra seriya. 8Denii Ɛbɛd Mɛlɛk izi kakpaŋ, di la a koori be di ga ŋɔ u be, 9“Jara, nɛra naa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, dikuu gunla baŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia wia. Ba kpaubuu ta kɔlɔŋ biini, bɔr la lɔzi n niŋ kpuu, ú siu, dikuu diwee n waa kaa hoo bolzeŋ naa biini wia.”
10Denii a koori ŋɔ Ɛbɛd Mɛlɛk be, “Lau baala tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, í ni baa la ga lizi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia manaŋ, di lii a kɔlɔŋ biini, di u haa waa siuwɛ.”
11Awia, Ɛbɛd Mɛlɛk lau a baala, u ni baa la diibee bɛl n du a kooridia daama kuna dauribɔr zɛɛ. Baŋ ga hel de, u kpa yakɔssi ni tagtakɔssi mil dɔŋa lugɔ ŋmɛŋ, di lawuu taŋ a kɔlɔŋ biini. 12Ka ŋɔ n be, “Kpa yakɔssi naa du i lugbɔɔni, ŋmɛnni la gilɛɛ waa dui pira.” N kpaa du gunla uŋ bagliŋ la. 13Ba lau a ŋmɛnni, di tɛrgiŋ lii a kɔlɔŋ biini. N jaa du a kooridia guure diŋŋee la.
Koori Zɛdɛkia n kaa pɛɛzi Jɛrɛmia wia
14Denii Koori Zɛdɛkia hum mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia bɔr. Ba kpogliŋ ga Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuzi ahorohiŋ la, di ba. A koori ŋɔ, “N na nyiŋŋuu ń pɛɛzii wii bɛl. Gilɛɛ wa kpa wiimaa ra suah n ni.”
15N jaa ŋɔ, “Di n dii wibii hàá kpuŋŋ? Haali di n baglii wia gba, ka hàá nuu.”
16Ka Koori Zɛdɛkia suahzi hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua tɛŋ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa, di tɛɛ yaa miibɔɔ la sɔŋ biini lugɔ màá kpui gɛɛ di kpai tɛɛ banla n na nyiŋŋi i kpui la.”
17Denii n ŋɔ Koori Zɛdɛkia be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina la n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di i sɛɛ Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra nabɔnzi dɔɔra, guŋwaa, i daŋ na i hiŋ, bolzeŋ naa ge wàá fuuh, i ni i diahina ge wàá siu. 18Ka di hàá sɛɛ a Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra nabɔnzi dɔɔra, guŋwaa, n daŋ kpa a bolzeŋ naa du ba nonee, bá fuuh u maa. I ge gba himmaa wàá wer chɔ lii ba nonee biini.”
19Koori Zɛdɛkia bir ŋɔ n be, “N na ɔm Jus hina la n chɔwɛɛ ga zuu Babilɔn hina labuu. Aŋhinabe, Babilɔn hina daŋ kpaŋ du ba nonee, bá sunniŋ werge.”
20Denii n ŋɔ u be, “Ba wàá kpai du ba nonee biini. Hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, di ɛɛ wia naa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛi naa. Denii wiimaa kuari tɛi. Hàá siu. 21Ka di i vɛɛ dɔɔra sɛɛi, kenne Kɔraawiizi bagliŋ, 22haana la maa n kawɛɛ Juda kooridia la maanii, bá lauri tɛɛ Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra nabɔnzi. A haana naa daŋ ŋɔ i be,
‘I dammuzi la hiŋ yardɛɛ
dariibuu, di lawii.
I nir fotogozi biini,
i dammuzi vɛɛi ta.’
23I haana ni i biizi maanii bá lauri wa tɛɛ a Babilɔn hina. I himmaa gba wàá na bɔr chɔ. Babilɔn koori daŋ lawii, ka bá fuuh a bolzeŋ naa.”
24Denii Koori Zɛdɛkia ŋɔ n be, “Gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa waa nuu yaa wiŋɔzi naa. Di ba haŋ wa nuua, ba daŋ kpui. 25Di a nabɔnzi wa nuuwɔ lugɔ n nii ŋɔ wiarɛ, ba ba i be wa pɛɛzii, ‘Bɛɛ wiarɛ i ni koori so di ŋɔ lai? Gilɛɛ wa kpa wiimaa di ra suah yaa ni, di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ kpui.’ 26Ŋɔ ba be, ‘N faa ra suŋŋi a koorii lugɔ u gilɛɛ kaa gil ba kpaŋ la Jonatan dia, ń ga siu de.’ ”
27Denii a nabɔnzi maa ba n be, di wa pɛɛziŋ, n ŋɔ ba be gunla maa a koori n ŋɔ n be lugɔ n ŋɔ la. Ba waa kaa ŋɔ wiimaa, dikuu baŋ waa wia la n ni a koori n ŋɔwɛɛ la biini zummɛ wia.
28Denii n du a kooridia guure diŋŋee hiŋ guŋŋ di wa hel a hɔl la baŋ kpegli Jɛrusalɛm hina la.

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Captured by the Babylonians
(Jeremiah 52.4-16; 2 Kings 25.1-12)
1-3In the tenth month of the ninth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian army began their attack on Jerusalem. They kept the city surrounded for a year and a half. Then, on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year that Zedekiah was king, they broke through the city walls.
After Jerusalem was captured, Nebuchadnezzar's highest officials, including Nebo Sarsechim and Nergal Sharezer from Simmagir, took their places at Middle Gate to show they were in control of the city.
4When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley. 5But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty, 6and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families. 7Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
8Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls. 9Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar. 10Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
11Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan: 12“Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
13Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar 14sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah.
The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
15While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say 16to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen. 17-18But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jɛrusalɛm puraa wia
1Kennaabuu ba faa ɛɛ puri Jɛrusalɛm. Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia kora dii binni kabɛlhiŋ, baaguzi fihiŋ biinii, Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ni u laallɔɔra maa faa ba, di wa fɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina. 2U kora dii binni fidikpaŋhiŋ, baaguzi anaazuhiŋ hɔpizaa kabɛl hɔllɛ, ba purgi a bolzeŋ koŋlaa maa, ka zuu de. 3Denii Babilɔn koori nabɔnzi la maa ba a bolzeŋ Baambaaŋ Dominuuzeŋ la, di wa so ba nabɔmbɔra. Nɛra la ge n faa kaa jaa ba ninɛɛ, Samga hinuu Nɛgal Sarɛza, Babilɔn koori nabɔnzi maa nabɔma Nɛbɔ Sasɛkim, u nabɔnzeŋ bɛl Nɛgal Sarɛza ani u nabɔnzi la maa n kawɛɛ. 4Saŋa la Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia ni u laallɔɔra n wa na baa, ba jaa izi hahmuŋa ni, di chɔ lii a bol. A koori kambol biinii ba faa ga di ga lii a dominua la n du a koŋlaa anɛɛ baambaaŋ la, di chɔ ra la Jɔɔdan Waluu paga.
5Ka Babilɔn laallɔɔra dau ba luge guŋŋ di ga lau Koori Zɛdɛkia, Jɛriko lɛl biini. Di kpogluu ba Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza be, bolzeŋ Ribla n du Hamaf hɛri, u di u seriya de, u chol. 6A Riblaa Babilɔn koori faa kpu Koori Zɛdɛkia biibaala u sibɔɔ, di kaa kpu Juda hina nabɔnzenaa maa ge de jaa. 7Uŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ, u foŋzi Koori Zɛdɛkia sibee, ka gil ba kpa danyɛ yɔlɔzi duu, ka ŋɔ bá kpogluu kaali Babilɔn.
8Denii Babilɔn hina jaa fuuh a kooridia ni a nɛra maa diini, ka purgi Jɛrusalɛm koŋlaa maa. 9Nɛbuzaradan n ɛɛ koori guure nabɔma, lauri nɛra la n kawɛɛ a bolzeŋ biini, di kpa banla maa n faa chɔwɛɛ ga zuuu la, di kaali Babilɔn. 10Ka Nɛbuzaradan faa gil banla n ɛɛ nyaara, Juda hɛri biini la waa. Baabuu faa waa kummaa dɔɔwɛ la. U jaa tɛɛ baa kooni ba ra par.
11Denii Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ŋɔ u guure nabɔma Nɛbuzaradan be n wia, di ŋɔ, 12“Ií lawuu di ra binni u ni nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa ɛɛu wichɔgii maa. Di u haŋ wa ŋɔ ii ɛɛ wiimaa tɛu, ií ɛɛ a widee.” 13Awia, Babilɔn koori guure nabɔma Nɛbuzaradan, u nabɔnzi maa nabɔma Nɛbusazban, u nabɔnzeŋ bɛl banna yir Nɛgal Sarɛza ani u nabɔnzi la n kawɛɛ, 14hum ba ga kpogliŋ lii guure diŋŋee hiŋ biini, di kpogliŋ ga tɛɛ Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia, u naabaallɛ faa Safan, ú kpogliŋ bir la n bol. Denii n ga du n himmaa nɛra be.
15Saŋa la miŋ faa haa du a guure diŋŋee la, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, 16“La ga ŋɔ Itiopia hinuu Ɛbɛd Mɛlɛk be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N na nyiŋŋuu ń kpa hɛhchɔg ta bolzeŋ naa hina ni, nyɛɛlaa waa lɛi, guŋ gil ń nua la su u maga. A guŋ saŋa, guŋ daŋ ɛɛ i sibɔɔ. 17Ka n daŋ lɛɛi a keŋ hɔpizii naa biini, ba wàá kpai du nɛra la hinna ɔm la nonee biini. 18N daŋ lɛɛi, màá gil ba kpui, ka í na i hiŋ, dikuu hiŋ yardiŋ wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

english_text:
Jeremiah Is Set Free
1I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free. 2Nebuzaradan said:
Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land. 3But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
4Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish. 5King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose.
Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave. 6I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah.
The Harvest Is Brought In
7-8 Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, together with Johanan and Jonathan, the two sons of Kareah, had been officers in Judah's army. And so had Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah from Maacah. They and their troops had been stationed outside Jerusalem and had not been captured. They heard that Gedaliah had been chosen to rule Judah, and that the poorest men, women, and children had not been taken away to Babylonia. So they went to Mizpah and met with their new ruler.
9Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar. 10I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
11-12Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year.
Gedaliah Is Murdered
13One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah. 14They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!”
Gedaliah refused to believe them, 15so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
16Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_text:
Baŋ lizi Jɛrɛmia nɛra tɔi dia wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, saŋa la koori guure nabɔma Nɛbuzaradan, n faa liziŋ lii nɛra tɔi dia Rama la. A saŋa, di n faa jaa banla baŋ laurɛɛ lii Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda di ba Babilɔn la ni. 2A nabɔma n wa naŋ, u ŋɔ n be, “Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum labuu faa ta jina lugɔ u daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg naa ta bɔnnaa ni. 3Awia, Kɔraawiizii gillɛ guŋ ɛɛ. U ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔ u daŋ ɛɛ labuu. Annii naa maa ɛɛwɔɔ, dikuu iiŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu u ni, di vɛɛ u nua hiŋaa wia. 4Ka n na lizi yɔlɔzi naabuu i nonee zinaa. Ba yá la Babilɔn, di guŋ parii. N daŋ gaa binni i ni. Ka di haa nyiŋŋi laŋaa, í gil. Na, a hɛri maa chɔɔwɔɔ tɛi, a la bɔr la maa n parii.” 5Mɔɔ ka n bir ń kaali, Nɛbuzaradan kaa ŋɔ, “Bir la Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia la naabaal n ɛɛ Safan, koori lizuu u ɛɛ Juda hɛri bola nabɔma la, í nuu ni a nɛra maa kpau du de gɛɛ í ra la bɔr la maa n parii.”
Denii Nɛbuzaradan sunziŋ kuna, di tɛŋ diwee jaa, ka taŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ n kaali. 6Awia, n la Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia be Mizpa, di ga du u ni u nɛra la maa baŋ gillɛ ba ka a hɛri biini la be.
Baŋ kpu Gɛdalia wia
7A laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ni a laallɔɔra maa n du pir la n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Babilɔn koori lizi Ahikam biibaal Gɛdaliaa u ra binni a hɛri maa ni, di kaa ra binni baala, haana, biizi ani banla maa n ɛɛ nyaara du a hɛri, haali ani banla maa baŋ waa lauwɛ kaali Babilɔn hɛri la, 8denii Nɛtania biibaal Ismɛl, Karia biibaala Jɔhanan ni Jonatan, Tanumɛf biibaal Sɛraaya, Nɛtɔfaf hinuu Ɛfai biibaala, Maaka hinuu biibaal Jaazania ani ba baala kpa ba Gɛdalia be, Mizpa.
9Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia, u naabaal ɛɛ Safan chi ba see di hɛɛhzi, di ŋɔ, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm Babilɔn hina humaa. Ií so a hɛri di hum ra tɛɛ Babilɔn koorizeŋ, gunnɛ ii wia kuari. 10Ka miŋwaa himmaa daŋ chi ii naazi di so Mizpa, di Babilɔn hina wa ba yaa be. Ka iawaa la ga tɔrgi ii grepu nɔna, di daali siŋ, di lizi ɔlivi nuu, di kpa nɔŋhilaa du kuna biini chiŋŋi. Ka so bola la iiŋ lɛɛwɛ la biine.”
11Jus hina la maa n du Moab, Ammɔn, Ɛdɔm hɛssi ani hɛssi la n kawɛɛ hina, n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Babilɔn koori gil a nɛra tamaa Juda hɛri, ka lizi Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia, u naabaal n ɛɛ Safan, u ɛɛ ba hɛri nabɔma di ra binni baa la, 12denii ba maa lii bɔra la baŋ yaarɛɛ la, di ba Juda hɛri, Gɛdalia be Mizpa, di wa chaali grepu nɔna ni nɔna aŋhina werge maa.
13Karia biibaal Jɔhanan ni laallɔɔra nabɔnzi la maa lii laŋgarazi la baŋ duwɛɛ la, di ba Gɛdalia be, Mizpa, 14di wa ŋɔ u be, “Haa zummɛ lugɔ Ammɔn hina Koori Baalis hum Nɛtania biibaal Ismɛllɛ lugɔ ú ba wa kpui?” Ka Gɛdalia waa baa yardɛɛ.
15Denii Jɔhanan suahzi ŋɔ Gɛdalia be, Mizpa biini, “Gil ń la ga kpu Ismɛl, di nɛr maa waa zummɛ. Bɛɛ wiarɛ ú lizi i miibɔɔ, guŋ gil Jus hina la n barii naa kaa chɔ yaari, banla ge n kawɛɛ Juda biini siuzɛi?”
16Ka Gɛdalia ŋɔ Jɔhanan be, “Gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ guŋ! Wia naa hiŋ kpawɛɛ ra chug Ismɛl naa, waa wibii ɛɛwɛ.”

english_text:
1 But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah. 2During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia. 3Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
4The next day, the murders had still not been discovered, 5when 80 men came down the road toward Mizpah from the towns of Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They were on their way to the temple to offer gifts of grain and incense to the Lord. They had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes, and cut themselves, because they were mourning.
6Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah. 7But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well. 8He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field. 9The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
10Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
11Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done. 12So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon. 13When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy 14and turned around and ran toward Johanan. 15But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon.
Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
16Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon 17-18toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar.
The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them
On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_text:
1A bina hiŋ, baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, Nɛtania biibaal Ismɛl, u naabaal n ɛɛ Ɛlisama, u faa ɛɛ kooridiiri, di kaa ɛɛ a koori nabɔma bɛl, u ni baala fi, faa ba Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia be, Mizpa. Baŋ faa kpauwɛ ra di, 2Ismɛl ni a nɛra fi la n faa du u be la, maa izi kakpaŋ, di kpa tokobizi yag Gɛdalia kpu. Waabuu Babilɔn koori faa lizi u ɛɛ a hɛri nabɔma. 3Ismɛl faa kaa kpu Jus hina la maa n faa du Gɛdalia be Mizpa, haali Babilɔn hina laallɔɔra la n faa du de la maa.
4Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, mɔɔ ka nɛr maa nuu Gɛdalia kpui wia, 5di baala tokkoanaazu fuŋ ba taŋhuna, di piili ba laala, di mɔnni bahinaa di ra wii Gɛdalia ni nɛra la maa n siuwɛ la lee. Sɛkɛm, Silo ani Samariaa ba faa lii di chi mbusu lizaa mia ani daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di ra ba Kɔraawiizi Dia. 6Denii Nɛtania biibaal Ismɛl lii Mizpa, ú ga chem ba ni, ka ra wii. Uŋ ga huuzi baa, u ŋɔ ba be, “Jaande maa, ií ba wa na Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia.” 7Baŋ kpawɛɛ wa zuu a bolzeŋ biini, Ismɛl ni nɛra la n na hiŋuu la lau baa kpu, di paa baa ha kɔlɔŋ biini. 8Ka ba nɛra fi waa ŋɔ Ismɛl be, “Gilɛɛ waa kpu yaa! Yaa dɔɔ huuti, baali, nuu ani huuhnuu n suah koonii.” Awia, waa sɛɛwɛ ú kpu baawaa. 9A kɔlɔŋ la biini Ismɛl n ta nɛra la uŋ kpuwɛɛ la faa kannɔɔ. Waabuu Koori Asa faa ki di guu u hiŋ, saŋa la Izrɛl Koori Baasa n faa wa fɔɔu ni laal la. Ismɛl faa paa a lalaarɛ su u biini.
10Denii Ismɛl lauri a koori biihaana ni a nɛra la maa n kawɛɛ Mizpa. Baabuu Nɛbuzaradan n faa ɛɛ koori guuri nabɔma, faa kpa du Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia nonee, lugɔ ú ra binni la. U jaa kpogli ba maa lii, di bir u nyuu chaŋ Ammɔn hɛri magbɔɔ barii, di ra kaali.
11Karia biibaal Jɔhanan ni laallɔɔra nabɔnzi la maa n faa du u be la, n wa nuu wichɔgaa la maa Ismɛl n ɛɛwɛ la, 12ba lau ba laallɔɔra maa, ba ni baa la, bá ga lɔ Ismɛl. Banna la la, ba ga huuzuu Gibiɔn pozeŋ. 13A nɛra la maa Ismɛl n laurɛɛ la n wa na Karia biibaal Jɔhanan ni a laallɔɔra nabɔnzi n na ba la, ba bɔra sɔɔni baa. 14Ba maa bir kaali Karia biibaal Jɔhanan be. 15Ka Nɛtania biibaal Ismɛl ni ba nɛra ŋmantannaazi waa faa wer na bɔr chɔ lii Jɔhanan be, di kaali Ammɔn hɛri.
16Denii Jɔhanan ni laallɔɔra nabɔnzi la maa n du u be la kpogli nɛra la uŋ faa lɛɛwɛ lii Nɛtania biibaal Ismɛl be, Mizpa la, di ra kaali. Baabuu faa laallɔɔra, haana ni biizi ani koori zɛɛsogna la uŋ kpoglee lii Gibiɔn, a saŋa, di u jaa kpu Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia la. 17Ba vol guŋŋ di ga chi Gɛruuf Kimham n dugli Bɛtlihɛm, di ra la Ijip hɛri. 18Ɔnsii faa lau baa gunla ban niŋ ɛɛ chɔ lii Babilɔn hina la be, dikuu Ismɛl n faa kpu Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia la wia. Waabuu Babilɔn koori faa lizi u ra binni a hɛri ni la.

english_text:
1Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me 2and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left. 3Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
4“All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
5They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says, 6even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
7Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for 8Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together 9and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said:
You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do. 10I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you. 11Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him, 12and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
13But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God. 14We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
15People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen. 16-17You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
18I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word.
Jeremiah Gives a Warning
19I told the people:
You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt. 20You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake, 21because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him. 22And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_text:
A nɛra n ŋɔ Jɛrɛmia suŋŋi wiizi tɛɛ baa wia
1Denii a laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ni Karia biibaal Jɔhanan, Hɔsaaya biibaal Jɛzania ani a nɛra maa, nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa ba 2mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia be, di wa ŋɔ, “Jaande maa, nuu yaa suŋŋaa naa, ka suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la tɛɛ yaa banla n kawɛɛ. Na, yaa faa kpillɔɔ, ka yaa tama bɛnnɛ kawɛɛ filaŋkeŋ. 3Suŋŋuu, ú bagli yaa bɔr la yaa n niŋ la ni wii la n dɛkkɛ ya ɛɛ.”
4Denii n ŋɔ, “N nuu wii la iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛrɛ. N daŋ suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la tɛɛ ia, gunla iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa. Wii la maa uŋ wa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ n ŋɔ tɛɛ ia, n daŋ ŋɔ a maa tɛɛ ia. Màá kpa wiimaa suah ii ni.”
5Denii ba ŋɔ n be, “Kɔ́raawiizi himmaa ɛɛ yaa daansɛɛ hiŋ ni wibii, di yaa waa sɛɛwɛ hiŋ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n niŋ humii, dí i ŋɔ yaa be. 6Di a ɛɛ yaa kipar gɛɛ a waa yaa kipar ɛɛwɛ gba, ka yaa daŋ hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, di ra humii u be la nua. Guŋ daŋ gil wiimaa kuari tɛɛ yaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa daŋ hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la nua.”
7Hɔpizaa fi n wa bɛrɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ wia tɛŋ. 8Awia, n yir Jɔhanan, laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ani a nɛra maa, nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa maa bɔkpaŋ. 9Denii n jaa ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, ii humiŋ u be la, ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, 10‘Di ii sogo hɛri naa, n daŋ kuari ia chiŋŋi nɛnnɛ, màá kpu ia. N daŋ duu ia, màá kpuzi ia ta alugɔ kunduulaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n biini chɔkkɔɔ, dikuu hɛhchɔg la miŋ kpawɛɛ ta ii ni la wia. 11Ií gilɛɛ kaa ra ɔm Babilɔn koori la iinna ɔm la. Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔmuu. N du ii benii ń lɛɛ ia lii u nonee biini. 12N daŋ suŋ ii ni, guŋ gil Babilɔn koori ge suŋ ii ni, di gil ii bir kaali ii hɛri. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’
13Ka di ii vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua, di ŋɔ lugɔ ii wàá so hɛri naa, 14di ŋɔ, ‘Akai, yaa daŋ la Ijip hɛri di ga so, denii yaa wàá ka na laal gɛɛ di nuu bensunoniina wiraa, haali yaa wàá ka zum lɔzi wia gba.’ 15Hoi, Juda hina, ii banla n kawɛɛ la, ií ra nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la n na ŋɔ, ‘Di ii aah siwiire lugɔ ii la Ijip hɛri di ga so waa, 16guŋwaa, laal la iinna ɔm la ni u nyuu himmaa biinii ii ra la ii ga zuu la, lɔzii niŋ kpu ia de. 17Wibii maa, banla maa n aah siwii lugɔ ba la Ijip ga so la, laal, lɔzi ani wiilchɔgiirɛ niŋ kpuuzi baa de. Ba bɛl maa wàá lii a keŋ hɛhchɔg naa min niŋ kpa ta ba ni la biini.’ 18Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Gunla n baaŋfuuih n du Jɛrusalɛm hina ni la, guŋ himmaanii ń kpau du ii ge ni, di ii haŋ vɛɛ ka la Ijip. N daŋ gil ii birgi nɛkuna, bá kpa ii sɔŋ di ra see dɔŋa nuuzi, ii wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge. Ii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka na bɔnnaa maa.’ ”
19Denii n bir ŋɔ ba be, “Oo, Juda hina la n kawɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ii benii, ‘Ií gilɛɛ waa la Ijip.’ Ií zum gunnɛ, 20n na karfi iabuu zinaa lugɔ ii leuwoo werge maa, iiŋ humiŋ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la be, di ŋɔ, ‘Suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la tɛɛ yaa. Ŋɔ yaa be wii la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, ya ɛɛ.’ 21Awia, n ŋɔ ii benii zinaa wii la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ n ŋɔ tɛɛ ia, ka ii haa waa sɛɛwɛ ii nuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua. 22Awia, ií zum lugɔ laal, lɔzi ani wiilchɔgiirɛ niŋ kpu ia, bɔr la iinna la ii ga so la.”

english_text:
The People Go to Egypt
1I told the people everything the Lord had told me. 2But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt. 3Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
4Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command. 5 So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah. 6Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
7The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes, 8when the Lord told me:
9Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
10Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury. 11He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners. 12-13I will let him set Egypt's temples on fire, and he will either burn or carry off their idols. He will destroy the sacred monuments at the temple of the sun-god. Then Nebuchadnezzar will pick the land clean, just like a shepherd picking the lice off his clothes. And he will return safely home.
translation_text:
Baŋ lau Jɛrɛmia kaali Ijip hɛri wia
1Mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia n wa ŋɔ a nɛra be wia la maa Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ń ŋɔ tɛɛ baa la tuŋ, 2Hɔsaaya biibaal Azaria, Karia biibaal Jɔhanan ani ba nɛkpoŋlaa la maa ŋɔ n be, “I ra kanni karaa! Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la lɛi humii lugɔ i wa ŋɔ yaa be lugɔ yá gilɛɛ waa la Ijip di gaa so. 3Ka Nɛria biibaal Baruk aah siwiire di ra ŋɔ i be lugɔ i kpa yaa du Babilɔn hina nonee biini, bá kpu gɛɛ di lauri yaa kaali Babilɔn.”
4Awia, Jɔhanan, a laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ani a nɛra maa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua lugɔ ba wàá so Juda hɛri. 5Denii Jɔhanan ni a laallɔɔra nabɔnzi la maa kpogli nɛra la maa n kawɛɛ Juda hɛri ani banla maa n faa yaari a hɛssi ka kaa bir ba la maa, di kaali Ijip hɛri. 6Ba kaa kpogli baala, haana, biizi, koori biihaana ani banla maa Nɛbuzaradan n ɛɛ koori guure nabɔma, n gillɛ du Gɛdalia nonee, di kpa Baruk ni mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia gba jaa kaali. 7Awia, ba jaa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua hiŋaa, ka kpogli baa zuu Ijip hɛri, di ga bɛri kaali bolzeŋ Tapanɛs.
8Baŋ du bolzeŋ Tapanɛs hɛssi la, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, 9“Gil Jus hina ra binni, ka i kpa bikuŋŋe di ga hug Ijip kooridia dominua vollibɔr la baŋ paa bia ma la. 10Ka ŋɔ ba be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N daŋ hum n balii Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza, ú ba wa chiŋŋi u koorikara bia naa hiŋ hukke naa ni, di baŋ u koori tanti dia tɔ a ni. 11U daŋ ba wa lɔ Ijip hina, banla wiila n niŋ lɔ, bá siuzi daŋ siuzi, banla ban niŋ lauri kaali, ba daŋ lauri baa kaali, banla ge n niŋ siu laal biini, laal biinii bá siu. 12U daŋ fuuh Ijip hina vuga diizenaa maa, ka paagi ba vuga. Gunla penɔɔni n ɔɔ lauri kariŋgbazi u laala ni la, gunnɛ u wa lauri Ijip hina kaali, di waa pira maa nawɛɛ. 13U daŋ purgi vug wiizi dia bia, di fuuh ba vuga diizenaa la maa n du Ijip hɛri la.’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Will Destroy the People of Judah
1The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
2I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today, 3because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
4Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning, 5but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods. 6Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
7Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies. 8You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word. 9When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens. 10Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
11I, the Lord All-Powerful, have decided to wipe you out with disasters. 12There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word. 13I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you. 14None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back.
The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
15A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
16Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen! 17We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us. 18But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
19Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
20Then I told the crowd:
21Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah? 22And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today. 23This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
24-25Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven. 26Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name. 27Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death. 28Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
29And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt. 30 I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_text:
Hɛhchɔg dikuu vuga kuaraa wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be Izrɛl hina la n du Ijip bolzenaa Migdɔl, Tapanɛs ani Mɛmfis ni a hɛri wiifurii nodig wiikakag wia. 2Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, “Ii na hɛhchɔgzeŋ la miŋ faa kpawɛɛ ta Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina bola la n bar baa labuu. Haali ni zinaa, a maanii haa ɛɛ diŋgelli chɔɔ, 3dikuu wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛwɛ wia. Ba faa fuuh n baannɛ dikuu daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la baŋ fuuhwe, di kaa ra kuari vuga la ba himmaa gɛɛ hiŋ gɛɛ ii naabaala n waa zummɛ wia. 4N hum n huŋhunna n ɛɛ n dɔgtɛɛzii digiidigii, ba wa ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wikuna naa miŋ kiiwe naa. 5Ka ii waa sɛɛwɛ keŋŋi digna nuu tɛŋ. Ii waa sɛɛwɛ gil ii biinikpola wiɛɛlaa gɛɛ di gil daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuih ra tɛɛ ii vuga la. 6Awiarɛ n faa kpa n baaŋ di chɔgi Juda bola ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa, di gil a maa chɔɔ diŋgelli, haali ni zinaa la.”
7Awia, filaŋkeŋ, kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ n baani ii ra ɛɛ keŋ wichɔgaa naa, di ra nyiŋŋi ii kpa hɛhchɔgzeŋ ta baala, haana ani biizi maa ni, ba bɛl maa wàá kaa kai? 8Bɛɛ n baani ii gil n baaŋ fuuh, dikuu daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la iinna fuuh, di ra tɛɛ vuga la n du Ijip hɛri, bɔr la iiŋ ballɛ wa so lai? Ii daŋ chɔgi iihinaa. Durnya hɛssi hina maa danna ɛɛ ia chɛɛtɛ, di kpa ii sɔŋ ra see nɛra nuuzi. 9Ii suuh biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la ii mɛɛwaa, ii koora ani wichezi n ɛɛwɛ Juda bola ni biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la ii ge gba ni ii haana n ɛɛwɛ Juda hɛri ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biine la wiarɛa? 10Haali ni zinaa, ii haa waa sɛɛwɛ sɔɔni siwii gɛɛ di kpaŋ girme gɛɛ di hiŋ n Gbɔgni miŋ tɛɛ ii ni ii mɛɛwaa la gba.
11Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N na nyiŋŋuu ń kpa hɛhchɔg ta ii ni, di kpu Juda hina maa. 12Ka Juda hina la n kawɛɛ di aah siwii lugɔ bá la Ijip ga so la, n daŋ gil ba maa siuzi lɔchɔgii gɛɛ laal biini, ba nɛdumazi ni ba nɛzenaa maa. Ba danna ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛ di kpa ba sɔŋ ra see nɛra nuuzi bɔr maa, ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge maa. 13N daŋ kpa laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii, di tɛr banla n du Ijip hɛri la digna, gunla miŋ faa tɛr Jɛrusalɛm hina digna la. 14Juda hina la n kawɛɛ di la Ijip ga so la, bɛl maa wàá lii gɛɛ di dɔɔ miibɔɔ lugɔ u kaa bir ba Juda, bɔr la banna nyiŋŋi lugɔ ba kaa bir ba wa so la. Ba bɛl maa wàá bir ba, see ba tama la n ɛɛ hɔɔhra hɛrdumazi biine la bɛŋ.’ ”
15Baala la maa n zummɛ lugɔ ba haana fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsumaa ra tɛɛ vuga ni haana la maa n du de la ani Izrɛl hina la maa n du Ijip hɛri wiifurii nomɛɛl ni nodig wiikakagni faa kpillɔɔ werge. Ba faa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, 16“Yaa wàá nuu amaniye naa hiŋ lizɛɛ Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini, di tɛɛ yaa naa. 17Yaa daŋ ɛɛ wia la maa yaa n ŋɔwɛɛ la. Yaa daŋ fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma tɛɛ Chiŋ Wiche, di ta siŋ tɛu gunla himmaa yaa naabaala, koora ani yaa nabɔnzi n faa ɛɛwɛ Juda bola ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biine la. A guŋ saŋa, yaa faa dɔɔ diweere werge maa, di dɔɔ daama, wiimaa faa waa yaa ra tɔɔri. 18Ka di haŋ lii saŋa la yaa n waa kaa ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di lizi siŋ ra tɛɛ Chiŋ Wiche la, yaa waa kaa dɔɔ kummaa, see laal ni lɔchɔgiirɛ ra kpuuzi yaa.”
19A haana kaa ŋɔ, “Yaa n ɔɔ fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ra tɛɛ Chiŋ Wiche, di ta siŋ ra tɛu la, yaa janna waa zummɛ lugɔ yaa ɔɔ ta kaanzaa a ra liu, di ta siŋ ra tɛuwaa?”
20Denii mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ baala ni haana la maa n bittɛ ŋɔ wia ra tɛŋ la be, 21“Mbusuzi la ii ni ii naabaala, koora, nabɔnzi ani a hɛri hina n lizɛɛ Juda bola ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biine la, ii fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi waa a wia zummɛ gɛɛ u suuh a wiarɛaa? 22Kɔraawiizi n waa kaa wa wer ú di ia kanyitti dikuu ii biinikpola wiɛɛlaa ni wikiilaa la iiŋ ɛɛwɛ wia, ii hɛri la birgi nuuseerikunnɛ, di birgi diŋgela. Nɛr maa waa kaa so de di wa lii ni zinaa. 23Dikuu iiŋ fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di ɛɛ wichɔgaa zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di vɛɛ u hiŋaa gɛɛ u Gbɔgni ni u widaulaa wiarɛ, hɛhchɔg naa iin nawɛɛ naa chol ii ni la.”
24Denii n ŋɔ nɛra la ni haana la maa be, “Ií ra nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n na ŋɔ Jus hina la maa n du Ijip hɛri la be, 25Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ií ni ii haana maa wiɛɛlaa teŋ baglɔɔrɛ gunla iiŋ ŋɔ nua, saŋa la iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ii daŋ haŋ hiŋ nuuzi la iiŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ lugɔ ii daŋ fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di ta siŋ tɛɛ Chiŋ Wiche labuu.’
Ií ra ɛɛ guŋ, di ɛɛ gunla iiŋ ŋɔ nua la! 26Jus hina la maa n du Ijip hɛri, ií ra nuu gunla mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ ni n sɔnzeŋ, lugɔ Jus hinuu la maa n du Ijip hɛri yemmaa, ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka yir n sɔŋ gɛɛ di hɛɛhzi, di ŋɔ, ‘N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, di du de saŋa maa la.’ 27Màá ka gil ii nyɛɛli, n daŋ kpu ia. Ii maa daŋ siuzi laal gɛɛ lɔchɔgii biini. Ii bɛl maa wàá ka du de. 28Ka ii nɛtama bɛnnɛ niŋ lii a siu biini, di lii Ijip ba Juda. Denii banla n niŋ na bahinaa la, jaa zum lugɔ n hotte ɛɛ wibii gɛɛ ba hotte ɛɛ wibii.
29Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii zum wibii maa lugɔ n daŋ tɛr ii digna bɔnnaa, guŋ gil nua la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ n daŋ chɔgi ia la su u maga. 30N daŋ kpa Ijip Koori Hɔfra tɛɛ u dɔma la n na nyiŋŋi u kpui la, gunla miŋ faa kpa Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia du Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza nonee, u dɔm la n faa ra nyiŋŋi u kpui la.”

english_text:
The Lord Will Not Let Baruch Be Killed
1 In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him. 2Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
3You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest. 4But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted. 5I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Baruk wia
1Juda Koori Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ biini, di Nɛria biibaal Baruk faa jaa sɛbi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia wiŋɔzi du hɔŋ biini. Denii n ŋɔ u be 2lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Baruk, 3i ra ŋɔu, ‘N lɔgɔ liwɔɔrɛ! Kɔraawiizi kpa biinichɔgrɛ jaa n tɔɔrɔɔ ni. N jaa hɛmuu guŋŋ di wa pɛssi, maa heezaa dɔɔwɛ!’
4Ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘N na purgi kunla miŋ mawɛɛnɛ, di kaa ra kpuzi kuna la maa miŋ duuwee hɛri naa maa biini. 5I ra nyiŋŋi wizenaareaa? Gilɛɛ ra nyiŋŋaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg ta nɛr maa ni. Ka n daŋ gil i chɔ lɛɛ i miibɔɔ, bɔr la maa hin niŋ la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Speaks to Jeremiah about the Nations
1The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world.
What the Lord Says about Egypt
2 In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
3It's time to go into battle!
So grab your shields,
4saddle your horses,
and polish your spears.
Put on your helmets and armor,
then take your positions.
5I can see the battle now—
you are defeated
and running away,
never once looking back.
Terror is all around.
6You are strong and run fast,
but you can't escape.
You fall in battle
near the Euphrates River.
7What nation is this,
that rises like the Nile River
overflowing its banks?
8It is Egypt, rising with a roar
like a raging river
and saying,
“I'll flood the earth,
destroying cities, and killing
everyone in them.”
9Go ahead, Egypt.
Tell your chariots and cavalry
to attack and fight hard.
Order your troops to march out,
with Ethiopians and Libyans
carrying shields,
and the Lydians armed with bows
and arrows.
10But the Lord All-Powerful
will win this battle
and take revenge
on his enemies.
His sword will eat them
and drink their blood
until it is full.
They will be killed in the north
near the Euphrates River,
as a sacrifice to the Lord.
11Egypt, no medicine can heal you,
not even the soothing lotion
from Gilead.
12All nations have heard you weep;
you are disgraced,
and they know it.
Your troops fall to the ground,
stumbling over each other.
A Warning for Egypt
13-14 When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them:
Prepare to defend yourselves!
Everywhere in your nation,
people are dying in war.
15I have struck down
your mighty god Apis
and chased him away.
16Your soldiers stumble
over each other
and say, “Get up!
The enemy will kill us,
unless we can escape
to our own land.”
17Give the king of Egypt
this new name,
“Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
18Egypt, I am the true king,
the Lord All-Powerful,
and as surely as I live,
those enemies who attack
will tower over you
like Mount Tabor among the hills
or Mount Carmel by the sea.
19You will be led away captive,
so pack a few things
to bring with you.
Your capital, Memphis,
will lie empty and in ruins.
20An enemy from the north
will attack you, beautiful Egypt,
like a fly biting a cow.
21The foreign soldiers you hired
will turn and run.
But they are doomed,
like well-fed calves
being led to the butcher.
* 22The enemy army will go forward
like a swarm of locusts.
Your troops will feel helpless,
like a snake in a forest
23when men with axes
start chopping down trees.
It can only hiss
and try to escape.
24Your people will be disgraced
and captured by the enemy
from the north.
25I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power. 26I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Bring Israel Home
The Lord said:
27 Israel, don't be afraid.
Someday I will bring you home
from foreign lands.
You and your descendants
will live in peace and safety,
with nothing to fear.
28So don't be afraid,
even though now
you deserve to be punished
and have been scattered
among other nations.
But when I destroy them,
I will protect you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Ijip hɛri wia
1Gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, di ra bagli hɛssi wiarɛ keŋ,
2Ijip hɛri wia.
Wia naabuu u ŋɔ di ra du Ijip Koori Nɛkɔ ni u laallɔɔra ni. Waabuu Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza faa kpegli bolzeŋ Kakɛmis n du Muu Yufretis nua la. Jɔsia biibaal Juda Koori Jɛhɔyakim kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ biinii guŋ ɛɛ.
3Ijip laallɔɔra nabɔnzi pozi di ŋɔ,
“Ií ɛɛ sirya di kpa
ii laal pɛrɛtuzenaa
ni a jigzi maa
di lii la ga lɔ laal!
4Ií bɔg ii zagra,
di tinnaa!
Ií chi ii chignibɔra
di hi ii laal kahurozi!
Ií sazi ii kandaazi
di kpa ii laal kuna laali.”
5Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi,
“Bɛɛ n nai?
N nawɔɔrɛ ɔnsii n lau baa,
ba bittɔɔ ra chɔ,
ba kpegli ba laallɔɔraa.
Ba ra chɔu manamanaŋ,
ba waa kɛɛwɛ ra binni har,
ɔnsii werge su bɔr maa.
6Banla n gbaŋŋɛ ni banla n kpekke
wàá na bɔr chɔ.
Muu Yufretis wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ
ba lɔɔzi naazi chogli.
7Anɛɛ izee keŋ lugɔ Muu Naal
alugɔ muu n suwee
di yaarɛi?
8Ijip izoore lugɔ Muu Naal,
di ɛɛ lugɔ
muuni n suwee
di ra lɔ werge.
Ijip ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N daŋ izi tɔ hɛri ni,
di chɔgi bolzenaa
ni a nɛra maa.’
9Zagra, ií ra chɔ!
Laal torko zuura,
ií ge ra chɔ ni baaŋ!
Laallɔɔra, ií ge lii ra la!
Banla n lii Itiopia ni Libia,
di kpogli laal pɛrɛtuzi,
banla n lii Lidia
di zum hoo tai!
10Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la,
hɔpiziirɛ zinaa.
Zinaa, u daŋ turgi u dɔma ba kim,
zinaa, u daŋ tɛr
u dɔma digna.
U tokobi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
sechɔgii n diwee guŋŋ
di wa piŋ,
di nyɔɔ chal guŋŋ
di wa dɛɛzi.
Zinaa, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
kpa u dɔmaa lizi mbusu
hɛri la n du wiifurii
nomɛɛl wiikakag
di dugli Muu Yufretis la.
11Ijip hina, ií la Giliad
di ga nyiŋŋi tagzi!
Ii tagzi maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ,
kummaa wàá wer chaa ia.
12Durnya hɛssi hina maa daŋ nuu ii hiihzi dii wia,
di nuu ii wiraa.
Laallɔɔri daŋ jiŋli, di yag u dɔŋhiŋ,
bá maa kpau chol.”
13Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, di ra bagli Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n na ba ú wa lɔ Ijip hina laal wia. U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
14“Sii wia naa Ijip bola ni Migdɔl,
di kaa siia Mɛmfis
ni Tapanɛs biine, di ŋɔ,
‘Ií chi ii chignibɔra di ɛɛ sirya,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba kpa tokobii
di kpu banla
n bar ia labuu.’
15Bɛɛ n niŋ gil ii laallɔɔra maa choglei?
Ba wàá wer chi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi
daŋ taagi baa ha.
16Ba danna jiŋli digiidigii,
di chogli dɔŋa ni,
Ba daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Ií gil yá izi,
di bir kaali yaa himmaa
nɛra be,
yaa himmaa hɛssi biine,
di chɔ lii
yaa dɔma tokobi be.’
17Awia, ba daŋ ŋɔ,
‘Kɔɔi bɛnnɛ Ijip koori
ra kɔɔ, waa bɔr nawɛɛ.’
18Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ɛɛ koorii.
Minuu Kɔraawiizi la
n du de saŋa maa.
Gunla Bizeŋ Tabɔ n saagi bizenaa maa ni la,
Bizeŋ Kamɛl saagi
muuzeŋ ni la,
gunnɛ nɛr la n niŋ wa lɔ
ia la fɔŋŋa du.
19Ijip hina, ií bali ii kuna ɛɛ sirya,
ba daŋ lauri
ia kaali hɛrduma.
Mɛmfis daŋ birgi hɛribɔduma,
nɛr maa wàá ka du de.
20Ijip ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nalor n wesse,
wogogua bɛl lii wiifurii
nomɛɛl wiikakag
di wa dumuu.
21Haali laallɔɔra la uŋ ga kpawɛɛ
gɛrgɔɔrɛ lugɔ nabizi.
Ba waa chigɛ yoo,
ba maanii bittɛ chɔ.
Ba labachɔgii hɔpizii helloo,
ba siu saŋaa guŋ.
22Ijip hina ra fuuri
alugɔ hɛrikuŋ n na chɔ,
dikuu ba dɔm n na ba
fɔŋŋa ni wia.
Ba daŋ kpogli kpaŋfɔzi ba
lugɔ baala n na teŋri daazi.
23Ba daŋ wa teŋri u kɔrzeŋ daazi maa ta,
haali uŋ tɔwɛɛ werge gba.
Ba kpillɔɔ kaali lotorozi,
ba wàá wer kur baa.
24Ijip hina daŋ di hiihzi,
ba kpa baabuu du wiifurii nomɛɛl
wiikakag nɛra nonee.”
25Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N na nyiŋŋuu ń tɛr Tɛbɛs hina vug Amɔn, Ijip koori, Ijip hina ni ba vuga ani banla n dɛlli Ijip koori la digna. 26N daŋ kpa baa tɛɛ nɛra la n na nyiŋŋi ba kpui la. Baabuu Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ni u nabɔnzi. Ka di saŋa bɛl wa hello, nɛra daŋ kaa ba di wa so Ijip hɛri lugɔ saŋa la baŋ faa soge de la.” Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ u nɛra
27“N nɛra Izrɛl hina, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm,
ii bɔra ra sá.
N daŋ lɛɛ ia lii a hɛhjaŋa la biini.
N daŋ lɛɛ ii naanna lii
hɛri la baŋ lauri baa
kaali la.
Ii daŋ bir ba bol di wa du ni bampirsɔna, di so pɛrɛtɛ,
nɛr maa waa kaa ra koozi ia.
28N daŋ ba wa lɛɛ ia.
N daŋ dim hɛssi la hina maa
miŋ yaari ia la biine,
ka màá dim iawaa.
Màá gil ii digna tɛraa,
ka di n wa tɛr ii digna,
n daŋ ɛɛ guŋ ni wibii.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
What the Lord Says about the Philistines
1 Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
2I, the Lord, tell you
that your land will be flooded
with an army from the north.
It will destroy your towns
and sweep you away,
moaning and screaming.
3When you hear the thunder
of horses and chariots,
your courage will vanish,
and parents will even abandon
their own children.
4You refugees from Crete,
your time has now come,
and I will destroy you.
None of you will be left
to help the cities
of Tyre and Sidon.
5The Anakim who survive
in Gaza and Ashkelon
will mourn for you
by shaving their heads
and sitting in silence.
6You ask how long will I continue
to attack you with my sword,
then you tell me to put it away
and leave you alone.
7But how can my sword rest,
when I have commanded it
to attack Ashkelon
and the seacoast?
translation_text:
Filisti hina wia
1Kenne Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ tɛɛ mìŋ́ u dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia, di ra bagli Filisti hina wia, mɔɔ ka Ijip koori faa ba wa lɔ Gaza hina laal la.
2U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Na gunla dɔma n na chaali wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag
alugɔ muu n suwee.
Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ muu n suwee taali di ra ba,
ba daŋ wa tɔ Filisti hɛri
ni kuna la maa n du de.
A nɛra danna lɔɔgi wile,
banla maa n du
a hɛri danna chɛɛhgi.
3Ba daŋ nuu zagra n na chɔ, a naazi ra gbɔgzi,
ba dɔma torkozi
chira ra gbɔgzi.
Mɛɛwaa wàá bir hiini ba biizi,
dikuu ɔnsii werge wia,
ba bɔra daŋ huah.
4Saŋa helloo
ń dim Filisti hina maa,
di kpu banla n kawɛɛ,
banla n niŋ faa hiini Taaya
ni Saidɔn hina la.
Kɔraawiizi ra nyiŋŋuu ú dim Filisti hina,
banla n kawɛɛ di lii
Krit muuzeŋ nua la.
5Gaza hina daŋ gbaari ba nyuuni, di ra wii.
Askɛlɔn hina daŋ siigi.
Ɛrɛɛ Filisti hina la n kawɛɛ la
wii di birgi magɛi?
6A nɛra wiiwoo di ra ŋɔ, ‘Yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi!
Ɛrɛɛ í kpa i tokobi,
di kpuuzi yaa birgi magɛi?
Kpau du u too,
ú du de ra heezi.’
7Ka mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia bir ŋɔ,
‘Ɛrɛɛ ú ɛɛ di heezei,
Kɔraawiizi n tɛu huma
ú hummɛi?
Waabuu ŋɔ u lɔ Askɛlɔn hina
ni nɛra la maa
n du muuzeŋ nua la.’ ”

english_text:
What the Lord Says about Moab
1 The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab:
The town of Nebo is doomed;
Kiriathaim will be captured
and disgraced,
and even its fortress
will be left in ruins.
2No one honors you, Moab.
In Heshbon, enemies make plans
to end your life.
My sword will leave only silence
in your town named “Quiet.”
3The people of Horonaim
will cry for help,
as their town is attacked
and destroyed.
4Moab will be shattered!
Your children will sob
5and cry on their way up
to the town of Luhith;
on the road to Horonaim
they will tell of disasters.
6Run for your lives!
Head into the desert
like a wild donkey.
7You thought you could be saved
by your power and wealth,
but you will be captured
along with your god Chemosh,
his priests, and officials.
8Not one of your towns
will escape destruction.
I have told your enemies,
“Wipe out the valley
and the flatlands of Moab.
9Spread salt on the ground
to kill the crops.
Leave its towns in ruins,
with no one living there.
10I want you to kill the Moabites,
and if you let them escape,
I will put a curse on you.”
11Moab, you are like wine
left to settle undisturbed,
never poured from jar to jar.
And so, your nation continues
to prosper and improve.
12But now, I will send enemies
to pour out the wine
and smash the jars!
13Then you will be ashamed,
because your god Chemosh
cannot save you,
just as Bethel could not help
the Israelites.
14You claim that your soldiers
are strong and brave.
15But I am the Lord,
the all-powerful King,
and I promise that enemies
will overpower your towns.
Even your best warriors
will die in the battle.
16It won't be long now—
disaster will hit Moab!
17I will order the nearby nations
to mourn for you and say,
“Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others,
but now its glorious power
has been shattered.”
18People in the town of Dibon,
you will be honored no more,
so have a seat in the dust.
Your walls will be torn down
when the enemies attack.
19You people of Aroer,
go wait beside the road,
and when refugees run by,
ask them, “What happened?”
20They will answer,
“Moab has been defeated!
Weep with us in shame.
Tell everyone at the Arnon River
that Moab is destroyed.”
21I will punish every town
that belongs to Moab,
but especially Holon,
Jahzah, Mephaath,
22Dibon, Nebo,
Beth-Diblathaim, 23Kiriathaim,
Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
24Kerioth, and Bozrah.
25My decision is final—
your army will be crushed,
and your power broken.
26People of Moab, you claim
to be stronger than I am.
Now I will tell other nations
to make you drunk
and to laugh while you collapse
in your own vomit.
27You made fun of my people
and treated them like criminals
caught in the act.
28Now you must leave your towns
and live like doves
in the shelter of cliffs
and canyons.
29I know about your pride,
and how you strut and boast.
30But I also know bragging
will never save you.
31So I will cry and mourn
for Moab
and its town of Kir-Heres.
32People of Sibmah,
you were like a vineyard
heavy with grapes,
and with branches reaching
north to the town of Jazer
and west to the Dead Sea.
But you have been destroyed,
and so I will weep for you,
as the people of Jazer weep
for the vineyards.
33Harvest celebrations are gone
from the orchards and farms
of Moab.
I have silenced the shouts
of people making wine.
34Weeping from Heshbon
can be heard as far
as Elealeh and Jahaz;
cries from Zoar are heard
in Horonaim
and Eglath-Shelishiyah.
And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
35I will get rid of anyone
who burns incense
to the gods of Moab
or offers sacrifices
at their shrines.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
36In my heart I moan for Moab,
like a funeral song
played on a flute.
I mourn for the people
of the town of Kir-Heres,
because their wealth is gone.
* 37-38The people of Moab
mourn on the rooftops
and in the streets.
Men cut off their beards,
people shave their heads;
they make cuts on their hands
and wear sackcloth.
And it's all because I, the Lord,
have shattered Moab like a jar
that no one wants.
39Moab lies broken!
Listen to its people cry
as they turn away in shame.
Other nations are horrified
at what happened,
but still they mock her.
40Moab, an enemy swoops down
like an eagle spreading its wings
over your land.
41Your cities and fortresses
will be captured,
and your warriors as fearful
as women giving birth.
42You are finished as a nation,
because you dared oppose me,
the Lord.
43Terror, pits, and traps
are waiting for you.
44If you are terrified and run,
you will fall into a pit;
and if you crawl out of the pit,
you'll get caught in a trap.
The time has come
for you to be punished.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
45Near the city of Heshbon,
where Sihon once ruled,
tired refugees stand in shadows
cast by the flames
of their burning city.
Soon, the towns on other hilltops,
where those warlike people live,
will also go up in smoke.
46People of Moab, you worshiped
Chemosh, your god,
but now you are done for,
and your children are prisoners
in a foreign country.
47Yet someday, I will bring
your people back home.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Moab hɛri chɔgaa wia
1Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ Moab hɛri wia,
“Wiarɛ huuzi Nɛbɔ hina, dikuu ban niŋ puri ba bol wia.
Ba lau bolzeŋ Kiriatam hinaa,
di purgi ba diikpeg,
ba ŋmaabi.
2Ba wàá ka chɔli Moab hina,
ba bolzeŋ Hɛsbɔn hina ta
a hɛri chɔgaa jinaa,
Bol la banna yir Madmɛn, ba daŋ chɔgii,
di kpa tokobi
dau i nɛra luge.
3Ií ra nuu Hɔrɔnam hina wile,
banna chɛɛhgi dikuu
chɔgaa werge wia.
4Moab maanii ba purgi,
ií ra nuu bichalli chɛɛhgaa.
5Ií ra nuu ba chɛɛhgaa
ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Luhif.
Biinichɔg werge chɛɛhgaa
ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Hɔrɔnam.
6Ba ra ŋɔu, ‘Ií chɔ lɛɛ iihinaa.
Ií ra chɔ lugɔ
hɛribɔduma kawee!’
7Moab hina, dikuu iiŋ yardi ii wiɛɛlaa ni ii daama wia,
ba daŋ wa lauri ii ge gba
kaali hɛrduma.
Ba daŋ chi ii vug Kɛmɔs kaali,
di lau u kizeehina
ni u nabɔnzi kaali.
8A bola maanii bá chɔgi,
haali walli ni lɛla
maanii bá chɔgi.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
9Ií chi yazi di ga yaari Moab hɛri maa,
dikuu un niŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ wia.
U bola daŋ birgi diŋgelli,
nɛr maa wàá ka du a biine.”
10Kɔ́raawiizi see nɛr la maa n wàá hum Kɔraawiizi huma ni biinihuŋŋu!
U nuuseei di nɛr la maa
n wàá sɛɛ kpa
u tokobi kpu Moab hina!
11Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Moab hina sogoo ni bampirsɔna,
ba ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa
baa laurɛɛ kaali hɛrduma.
Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ siŋ n du golii biini,
ba haa wɔɔ fɛɛnɛɛ maa.
U sunzi ŋmɛnɛ haa waa chɔkkɛ,
u haŋ du sum di hanna la.
12Ka saŋa bɛl ra bau,
min niŋ gil nɛra la
ga fug Moab hina alugɔ
baŋ fug siŋ, tɔga biine.
Kummaa wàá kaa ka,
ba daŋ purgi a tɔga maa.
13Vug Kɛmɔs wia daŋ dɔɔ Moab hina hiihzi,
gunla Izrɛl hina baŋhina
n faa yardi vug Bɛtɛl,
di di hiihzi la.
14Moab baala, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ŋɔ,
‘Yaa ɛɛ laallɔkpegaawɛi?’
15Moab hina dɔma daŋ wa lɔ baa,
di zuu chɔgi ba bola maa,
di kpu ba biipɔlnanaa maa.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ Koora Maa Koori,
di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
