labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
16Moab hina cholaa helloo,
hɛhchɔg daŋ chol
ba ni manaŋ.
17Banla maa n soge bar baa,
ií wii ra tɛɛ baa.
Banla maa n na nuu ba sɔŋ,
ií ŋɔ, ‘Daŋkpalzeŋ la kuugoore,
u girme tunnɔɔ!’
18Dibɔn hina, ií lii ii girme bɔr,
di tuu wa so hɛrhilii.
Moab chɔgri du ɛnnɛ,
di purgi u diikpega.
19Aroa hina, ií chi ŋmɛnikɛrii
di ra du tau.
Ií pɛɛzi banla n chɔwɛɛ ra kaali,
‘Bɛɛ n ɛɛwɛnɛi?’
20Ba daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Moab hina cholloo,
di di hiihzi.
Ií wii di ra lɔɔgi wile!
Ií sii Muu Aanɔn nua
lugɔ Moab maanii purgee!’
21Kɔraawiizi di giŋgimee nyuuni bolzenaare seriya,
aabuu Hɔlɔn, Jaaza, Mɛfaaf,
22Dibɔn, Nɛbɔ, Bɛf Diblatam,
23Kiriatam, Bɛf Gamul, Bɛf Miɔn
24di ga lii Kɛriɔf ani Bɔzra
di kpau guŋŋ
di ga lii Moab bolzenaa
la n nɛɛwɛ ni anla n duglɛɛ.
25Moab hina fɔŋŋazeŋ tunnɔɔ,
n chɔgi u fɔŋŋa maanii.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
26Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ,
“Ií gil Moab hina nyɔɔ siŋ di dɛɛzi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba bir
hattɛ kpuŋ.
Moab hina daŋ chɔɔ
ba himmaa hɛɛhzaa biini,
di ra billi, nɛra ra mam.
27Moab hina, Izrɛl hina lɛi faa ɛɛ ii chɛɛtɛ kuna laa?
Ba faa lau baabuu
ŋmɛɛna biiniaa?
Guŋ gil ii ɔɔ ra viigi ii nyuuni,
di ra gbɛlli baa,
di ii waa ŋɔ ba wia?
28Moab hina, ií lii ii bola
di gaa zuu bizenaa nyuuni.
Ií ɛɛ lugɔ komma la
n du u daŋ bii bɔɔ nua.
29Yaa nuu Moab hina jigsi wiarɛ,
ba kpoŋaa werge wia,
di ra na bahinaa werge,
di ra binni nɛra pɛɛ.
30N zum ba kpoŋaa wiarɛ,
ka a ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ,
ba barabara waa
tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
31Awia, n daŋ wii tɛɛ Moab
ni Kir Harɛsɛf hina maa.
32Sibma hina, n wiiwoo ra tɛɛ ia,
di kaali gunla miŋ wiiwe
tɛɛ Jaza hina la.
Bolzeŋ Sibma ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ grepu daa,
di ta kela ga hel Muuzensiwii,
haali di ga hel
Jaza muuzeŋ.
Ka filaŋkeŋ, nɛchɔgaa ballɔɔ
di wa chɔgi i nɔŋaahma
ni i grepuzi maa.
33N lizi bɔsɔna ni hindiire
lii Moab hɛrsum la biini.
N gillɔɔ siŋ waa kaa ra lii ba siŋ kuaribɔra,
nɛr maa waa kaa ra kuaraa
di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.
Haali banna chaasi gba,
ka bɔsɔna chaasaa lɛi.
34Wiraa lii Hɛsbɔnnɛ
di ga hel Ɛlialɛ ni Jahaz,
Zoa hina gba ra nuu,
di lii Zoa guŋŋ di ga hel
Hɔrɔnam ni Ɛglaf Sɛlisiya,
haali Nimrim niiri maa hil.
35N daŋ tɔ Moab hina ŋmɛnɛɛ,
ba wàá kaa ra lizi
mbusuzi giŋgimee nyuuni,
di fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma
di ra tɛɛ ba vuga.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
36N na wiiu n biini ra tɛɛ Moab
ni Kir Harɛsɛf hina
alugɔ nɛr n na huuh tiitorii di ra wii lee,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daama
maanii tunnɛ.
37Ba maanii gbaari ba nyuuni
ni ba taŋhuna.
Di mɔnni ba nonee,
di tɔɔgi gbɔglɔnzi.
38Wiimaa waa kaa du Moab salli
ni bossibaana,
di wiraa bɛŋ lɛi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n purgi
Moab maanii alugɔ
golii la nɛr maa
n waa kaa ra nyiŋŋi.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
39Ií na, Moab maanii purgee chɔɔ!
Ií nuu gunla banna chɛɛhgi!
Moab hina bir ba haraa ni hiihzi!
Moab hina birgi
chɛɛtɛ kunaa,
ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii
ni nuukpui werge,
banla maa n bar
baa la be.”
40Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Hɛri bɛl hina daŋ ba
di wa gbaari Moab hina kaali,
gunla chig n ɔɔ wa lau kuŋ la.
41Ba daŋ kpegli Kɛriɔf hina,
di foozi ba diikpega.
A hɔl hiŋ, Moab hina laallɔɔra biine daŋ chɔgi
alugɔ hilula n lɔ haaŋ la.
42Ba daŋ dim Moab hɛri hina,
dikuu u nɛra n diŋ mmɔri wia.
43Moab hina, saŋa bɛl ra bau, wia la n niŋ gil ɔnsii werge lau ia,
ii chogli bɔɔni biine,
sidɛɛzi lauri ia.
44Unla maa n niŋ chɔ lii a ɔnsii biini,
u daŋ chol bɔɔ biini,
unla maa n niŋ lii a bɔɔ biini ge,
sidɛɛ daŋ lawuu,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Moab hina
dignitɛraa bina helloo.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
45Banla n chɔwɛɛ lii laal biini
du bolzeŋ Hɛsbɔnnɛ
di ra nyiŋŋi lɛɛi,
bolzeŋ la Koori Sihɔn n faa ra di kora la,
maanii fuuhwe.
A niŋ fuuh Moab hina la
n na nyiŋŋi laal lɔi
hɛri magaa guŋŋ di ga lii
ba bizenaa nyuuni maa.
46Wia daŋ wa huuzi ia, Moab hina!
Nuuseei daŋ di ia,
vug Kɛmɔs kuara
maanii ba chɔgi.
Ba lauri ii biibaala ni biihaana
maanii kaali hɛrduma.
47Ka hɔpizii bɛl ra bau min niŋ kaa gil
Moab hina nyɛɛli.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
Moab hina seriya dii tunaa guŋ.

english_text:
What the Lord Says about Ammon
1 The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon:
The people of Israel
have plenty of children
to inherit their lands.
So why have you worshipers
of the god Milcom
taken over towns and land
belonging to the tribe of Gad?
2Someday I will send an army
to attack you in Rabbah,
your capital city.
It will be left in ruins,
and the surrounding villages
will lie in ashes.
You took some of Israel's land,
but on that day
Israel will take yours!
3Cry, people of Heshbon;
your town will become
a pile of rubble.
You will turn here and there,
but your path will be blocked.
Put on sackcloth and mourn,
you citizens of Rabbah,
because the idol you worship
will be taken
to a foreign country,
along with its priests
and temple officials.
4You rebellious Ammonites
trust your wealth and ask,
“Who could attack us?”
But I warn you not to boast
when your strength is fading.
5I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will send neighboring nations
to strike you with terror.
You will be scattered,
with no one to care
for your refugees.
6Yet someday, I will bring
your people back home.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
What the Lord Says about Edom
7 The Lord All-Powerful says about Edom:
Wisdom and common sense
have vanished from Teman.
8I will send disaster to punish
you descendants of Esau,
so anyone from Dedan
had better turn around
and run back home.
9People who harvest grapes
leave some for the poor.
Thieves who break in at night
take only what they want.
10But I will take everything
that belongs to you,
people of Edom,
and I will uncover every place
where you try to hide.
Then you will die,
and so will your children,
relatives, and neighbors.
11But I can be trusted
to care for your orphans
and widows.
12Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape? 13I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
14I have sent a messenger
to command the nations
to prepare for war
against you people of Edom.
15Your nation will be small,
yet hated by other nations.
16Pride tricks you into thinking
that other nations
look at you with fear.
You live along the cliffs
and high in the mountains
like the eagles,
but I am the Lord,
and I will bring you down.
17People passing by your country
will be shocked and horrified
to see a disaster
18 as bad as the destruction
of Sodom and Gomorrah
and towns nearby.
The towns of Edom will be empty.
19 I, the Lord, will attack you
like a lion from the forest,
attacking sheep in a meadow
along the Jordan.
In a moment the flock runs,
and the land is empty.
Who will I choose to attack you?
I will do it myself!
No one can force me to fight
or chase me away.
20Listen to my plans for you,
people of Edom.
Your children will be dragged off
and your country destroyed.
21The sounds of your destruction
will reach the Red Sea
and cause the earth to shake.
22An enemy will swoop down
to attack you,
like an eagle spreading its wings
and circling over Bozrah.
Your warriors will be as fearful
as women giving birth.
What the Lord Says about Damascus
23 The Lord says about Damascus:
The towns of Hamath and Arpad
have heard your bad news.
They have lost hope,
and worries roll over them
like ocean waves.
24You people of Damascus
have lost your courage,
and in panic you turn to run,
gripped by fear and pain.
25Once I was pleased
with your famous city.
But now I warn you, “Escape
while you still can!”
26Soon, even your best soldiers
will lie dead in your streets.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have spoken.
27I will set fire to your city walls
and burn down the fortresses
King Benhadad built.
Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
28Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia:
Listen, you people of Kedar
and the other tribes
of the eastern desert.
I have told Nebuchadnezzar
to attack and destroy you.
29His fearsome army
will surround you,
taking your tents and possessions,
your sheep and camels.
30Run and hide,
you people of the desert
who live in villages!
Nebuchadnezzar has big plans
for you.
31You have no city walls
and no neighbors to help,
yet you think you're safe—
so I told him to attack.
32Then your camels
and large herds
will be yours no longer.
People of the Arabian Desert,
disaster will strike you
from every side,
and you will be scattered
everywhere on earth.
33Only jackals will live
where your villages once stood.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
What the Lord Says about Elam
34-35Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say:
People of Elam,
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will kill the archers
who make your army strong.
36Enemies will attack
from all directions,
and you will be led captive
to every nation on earth.
37Their armies will crush
and kill you,
and you will face the disaster
that my anger brings.
38Your king and his officials
will die, and I will rule
in their place.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
39But I promise that someday
I will bring your people
back to their land.
translation_text:
Ammɔn hina wia
1Wia la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ di ra bagli Ammɔn hina wiarɛ keŋ,
“Lee Izrɛl hina baala duɛi?
Nɛr maa waa hoo
un niŋ wer yoo lɛɛ ba hɛriaa?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ba gil nɛra la n na kuari vug Mɔlɛk
wa lɛɛ Gad dee hɛri sonei?
2Ka saŋa bɛl ra bau,
min niŋ lɔ laal wile
di du Ammɔn hina
bolzeŋ Raba ni.
Ba daŋ purguu ú chɔɔ kululu,
di fuuh u boljigzi
la maa n baruu.
Denii Izrɛl hina duŋŋi banla
n faa duŋŋi baa la.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
3Hɛsbɔn hina, ií ra chɛɛhgi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba chɔg Airɛ!
Raba hina, ií ra wii!
Ií kpa gbɔglɔŋ tagtaazi di laali ra wii,
ií du a bol koŋlaa biini
di chɔ ra bar,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daŋ kpa vug Mɔlɛk kaali hɛhjaŋ,
u ni u Kizeehina
ni u nabɔnzenaa maa.
4Wibiinyaara, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra ta barabarai?
Ii fɔŋŋa ra tunuu.
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii dɛlli ii fɔŋŋa
di ŋɔ lugɔ nɛr maa
wàá kur lɔ iai?
5N daŋ gil ɔnsii werge lii
banla n bar ia la be
di chol ii ni.
Ba daŋ duŋŋi ii bɛl maa,
nɛr maa wàá wer chaali
banla n chɔwɛɛ la.
6Ka a harbɔɔ, n daŋ bir gil Ammɔn hina kaa nyɛɛli.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
Ɛdɔm hina wia
7Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ di ra bagli Ɛdɔm hina wia,
“Nunzuma waa kaa hoo Tɛman gɛɛ?
Nunzunna baglaa tunnɔɔ gɛɛ?
Ba nunzuma pɔɔhwɔɔ gɛɛ?
8Ií bir chɔ ga suah bia bɔɔluŋe biine,
ii banla maa n du Dɛdan,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ
kpa hɛhchɔg di wa ta
Ɛsau dee ni,
saŋa la min niŋ tɛr
ba digna la.
9Di banla n na tɔrgi grepuzi faa wa tɔrgaa,
ba wàá gil aŋhinaa?
Di ŋmɛɛna faa ballɔ hamuŋa ni,
gunla maga banna nyiŋŋi
lɛi ba ŋmɛɛa?
10N daŋ foozi Ɛsau dee kummaa,
di lizi ba suahribɔra chaaŋ,
guŋ gil ba wàá wer suah.
Ba biizi, lulla ani ba dɔŋahina maa daŋ siu,
ba wia tuŋ nyaamm.
11Ií gil ii lalbiizi tɛŋ, n daŋ guu baa,
ii luhaana gba
daŋ wer yardiŋ.”
12Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Di banla n waa dɛkkɛ lugɔ n tɔɔri baa la ra nyɔɔ tɔɔrɔɔ nii la, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ màá tɛr ii dignai? Wibii maa, ii daŋ haŋ nyɔɔ a tɔɔrɔɔ niirɛ. 13N hɛɛhzi n hinnɛ lugɔ Bɔzra daŋ puri, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, nɛra nuuzi kpu, bá ra ɛɛu chɛɛtɛ, di kpa u sɔŋ ra see dɔŋa nuuzi. U bolzenaa maa ge purgi di birgi diŋgelli, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
14Mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia nuu amaniyee lii Kɔraawiizi be, uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ,
“N hum baliirɛ hɛssi hina
maa be lugɔ bá chaali
di wa lɔ Ɛdɔm hina laal!
15N daŋ gil ii gɛrgi hɛssi hina maa be,
nɛr maa wàá kaa ra
tɔgzi ia.
16Ii barabara dar iabuu.
Nɛr maa waa ia ra ɔm
gunla iinna fɛ lugɔ
bá ra ɛɛ la.
Ii banla n du bia la n jaŋŋɛ la
chiŋ werge nyuuni,
di ra zuu a bɔɔni la.
Haali iiŋ du chiŋ
alugɔ chig gba,
ka n daŋ gil ii lii de
di tuu hɛri.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
17Ɛdɔm wia daŋ dɔɔ ɔnsii werge,
nɛr la maa n niŋ ga
de nua daŋ kpu, ɔnsii lawuu,
dikuu u chɔgaa wia.
18Gunla baŋ faa chɔg Sɔdɔm ni Gɔmɔra
ani bola la maa n baraa la,
gunnɛ bá chɔg Ɛdɔm,
nɛr maa wàá ka du.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
19Alugɔ bunyiŋ n lii Jɔɔdan muu kɔr biini
di ra la sela diiribɔr
la n wesse la,
gunnɛ ń duŋŋi Ɛdɔm hina
lii ba hɛri kakpaŋ.
Anɛɛ ń lizi u ɛɛ kennei?
Anɛɛ n lugɔŋ, ú karsinnɛi?
Sitɔɔri bɛliirɛ
n niŋ wer diŋ mmɔrɛi?
20Awia, ii ra nuu jina la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n tawɛɛ Ɛdɔm hina wia,
gunla minna nyiŋŋi
ń dau Tɛman hina.
N daŋ tuuzi ba biizi kaali,
di chɔgi ba sela diiribɔra maa
dikuu ba wia.
21Di nɛra wa nuu Ɛdɔm hina cholaa wia,
durnya maa daŋ zigli.
Ba wiraa daŋ
hel Muuzeŋaahmu.
22Dɔma daŋ wa pig bolzeŋ Bɔzra hina
alugɔ chig n tuuwe ú lau kuŋ.
A hɔl hiŋ,
ɔnsii daŋ lau Ɛdɔm laallɔɔra
alugɔ hilulaa
n lɔ haaŋ la.”
23Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ bolzeŋ Damaskus wia. U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Bolzenaa Hamaf ni Aapad hina biine chɔkkɔɔ,
dikuu baŋ nuu
amaniyechɔgaa wia.
Kafɔŋ chol ba ni,
alugɔ muuzeŋ n na koozi.
24Damaskus hina bɔra huahwɔɔ,
ba bir chɔ ni bɔsai.
Ba bɔra ra waazi,
biinichɔg lau baa werge maa
alugɔ hilulaa n lɔ haaŋ la.
25Bolzeŋ la n faa dɔɔ sɔŋ werge maa,
di dɔɔ bɔsɔna la
maanii chɔɔ pɛɛ.
26Wibii maa, a hɔl hiŋ,
ba daŋ kpu
ba biipɔllaa maa
di ta ŋmɛnikɛraa,
chɔgi ba laallɔɔra maa.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
27N daŋ du Damaskus koŋlaa maa niŋ,
ú fuuh Koori Bɛn Hadad
kooridia la maa.”
Kɛda Dee ni Bolzeŋ Hazɔr Hina Wia
28Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ di ra bagli Kɛda dee ni Hazɔr kossi la Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n faa lɔ laal la wia.
U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Ií izi di ga lɔ Kɛda dee laal,
di chɔgi nɛra la maa
n soge wiifurii la.
29Ií foozi ba tanti diini,
ba peeza, patiisazi
ani kuna la maa
n du ba tanti diini biine.
Ií foozi ba nyugmazi ka ŋɔ a nɛra be,
‘Ɔnsii werge bar iabuu!’
30Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi karfi iabuu lugɔ
ii chɔ di ga suah bia bɔɔluŋe biine,
ii banla n du bolzeŋ Hazɔr!
Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ta ii jinachɔgiirɛ.”
31Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Ií izi di lɔ hɛri la hina n soge pɛrɛtɛ,
di dɛlli bahinaa la.
Hɛri la hina n waa dominuuzenaa
gɛɛ lugbidaazi dɔɔwɛ,
di so ba bɛŋ la.
32Ií lauri ba nyugmazi
ani ba sela maa.
N daŋ yaari banla n fuŋ ba nyuuni,
di kpa hɛhchɔg ta
ba ni bɔr maa.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
33Bolzeŋ Hazɔr daŋ birgi hohobiazi duuribɔr,
di chɔɔ diŋgela di hanna la.
Nɛr maa ŋmɛnɛ maa
wàá ka so de.”
Ɛlam hɛri wia
34Zɛdɛkia n wa di Juda kora la, a waa birgee, ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be Ɛlam hɛri hina wia.
35Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ n be,
“N daŋ kpu hotaara la maa
n gillɛ Ɛlam hina
du kpeg werge maa la.
36N daŋ gil dɔma lii bɔr maa
di wa lɔ Ɛlam hina.
N daŋ yaari baa bɔr maa,
hɛri maa wàá ka,
di ba wàá du u biini.
37N daŋ gil ba kpu Ɛlam hina,
ba dɔma la n na nyiŋŋi
ba kpui la sibɔɔ.
N daŋ kpa n baaŋfuuihchɔgii
di gil hɛhchɔg chol ba ni.
N daŋ gil laallɔɔra dau ba luge,
di kpuuzi baa.
38N daŋ chiŋŋi n koorikara Ɛlam biini,
ka kpu ba koori
ni ba nabɔnzenaa.
39Ka di saŋa bɛl wa hello,
n daŋ kaa gil
Ɛlam hina nyɛɛli.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
Babylon Will Be Captured
1 The Lord told me to say:
Announce what will happen
and don't leave anything out.
2Raise the signal flags;
shout so all nations can hear—
Babylon will be captured!
Marduk, Babylon's god,
will be ashamed and terrified,
and his idols broken.
3The attack on the Babylonians
will come from the north;
they and their animals will run,
leaving the land empty.
Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
4The Lord said:
People of Israel and Judah,
when these things happen
you will weep, and together
you will return to your land
and worship me,
the Lord your God.
5You will ask the way to Zion
and then come and join with me
in making an agreement
you won't break or forget.
6My people, you are lost sheep
abandoned in the mountains
by their shepherds.
You don't even remember
your resting place.
7I am your true pastureland,
the one who gave hope
to your ancestors.
But you abandoned me,
so when your enemies found you,
they felt no guilt
as they gobbled you up.
8 Escape from Babylonia,
my people.
Get out of that country!
Don't wait for anyone else.
9In the north I am bringing
great nations together.
They will attack Babylon
and capture it.
The arrows they shoot
are like the best soldiers,
always finding their target.
10Babylonia will be conquered,
and its enemies will carry off
everything they want.
Babylon Will Be Disgraced
The Lord said:
11People of Babylonia,
you were glad
to rob my people.
You had a good time,
making more noise
than horses
and jumping around
like calves threshing grain.
12The city of Babylon
was like a mother to you.
But it will be disgraced
and become nothing
but a barren desert.
13My anger will destroy Babylon,
and no one will live there.
Everyone who passes by
will be shocked to see
what has happened.
14Babylon has rebelled against me.
Archers, take your places.
Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
15Attack from every side!
Babylon surrenders!
The enemy tears down
its walls and towers.
I am taking my revenge
by doing to Babylon what it did
to other cities.
16There is no one in Babylonia
to plant or harvest crops.
Even foreigners who lived there
have left for their homelands,
afraid of the enemy armies.
17Israel is a flock of sheep
scattered by hungry lions.
The king of Assyria
first gobbled Israel up.
Then Nebuchadnezzar,
king of Babylonia,
crunched on Israel's bones.
18I, the Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel,
punished the king of Assyria,
and I will also punish
the king of Babylonia.
19But I will bring Israel
back to its own land.
The people will be like sheep
eating their fill
on Mount Carmel
and in Bashan,
in the hill country of Ephraim
and in Gilead.
20I will rescue a few people
from Israel and Judah.
I will forgive them so completely
that their sin and guilt
will disappear,
never to be found.
The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
21The Lord said:
I have told
the enemies of Babylonia,
“Attack the people of Merathaim
and Pekod.
Kill them all!
Destroy their possessions!”
22Sounds of war
and the noise of destruction
can be heard.
23Babylonia was a hammer
pounding every country,
but now it lies broken.
What a shock to the nations
of the world!
24Babylonia challenged me,
the Lord God All-Powerful,
but that nation doesn't know
it is caught in a trap
that I set.
25I've brought out my weapons,
and with them I will put a curse
on Babylonia.
26Come from far away,
you enemies of Babylon!
Pile up the grain
from its storehouses,
and destroy it completely,
along with everything else.
27Kill the soldiers of Babylonia,
because the time has come
for them to be punished.
28The Babylonian army
destroyed my temple,
but soon I will take revenge.
Then refugees from Babylon
will tell about it in Zion.
29 Attack Babylon, enemy archers;
set up camp around the city,
and don't let anyone escape.
It challenged me, the holy God,
so do to it
what it did to other cities.
Proud Babylon Will Fall
30People of Babylon,
I, the Lord, promise
that even your best soldiers
will lie dead in the streets.
31Babylon, you should be named,
“The Proud One.”
But the time has come when I,
the Lord All-Powerful,
will punish you.
32You are proud,
but you will stumble and fall,
and no one will help you up.
I will set your villages on fire,
and everything around you
will go up in flames.
33You Babylonians were cruel
to Israel and Judah.
You took them captive, and now
you refuse to let them go.
34But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will rescue and protect them.
I will bring peace to their land
and trouble to yours.
35I have declared war on you,
your officials, and advisors.
36This war will prove
that your prophets
are liars and fools.
And it will frighten
your warriors.
37Then your chariot horses
and the foreigners in your army
will refuse to go into battle,
and the enemy will carry away
everything you treasure.
38Your rivers and canals
will dry up.
All of this will happen,
because your land
is full of idols,
and they have made fools
of you.
39 Never again will people live
in your land—
only desert animals, jackals,
and unclean birds.
40 I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah
and the nearby towns,
and I will destroy Babylon
just as completely.
No one will live there again.
Babylonia Is Invaded
The Lord said:
41Far to the north,
a nation and its allies
have been awakened.
They are powerful
and ready for war.
42Bows and arrows and swords
are in their hands.
The soldiers are cruel
and show no pity.
The hoofbeats of their horses echo
like ocean waves
crashing against the shore.
The army has lined up for battle
and is coming to attack you,
people of Babylonia!
43Ever since your king heard
about this army,
he has been weak with fear;
he twists and turns in pain
like a woman giving birth.
44Babylonia, I will attack you
like a lion from the forest,
attacking sheep in a meadow
along the Jordan.
In a moment the flock runs,
and the land is empty.
Who will I choose to attack you?
I will do it myself!
No one can force me to fight
or chase me away.
45Listen to my plans for you,
people of Babylonia.
Your children will be dragged off,
and your country destroyed.
46The sounds of your destruction
will be heard among the nations,
and the earth will shake.
translation_text:
Babilɔn hɛri wia
1Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Babilɔn hɛri ani nɛra la maa n du de la wia tɛɛ mìŋ́ u dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia,
2“Sii hɛssi maa biine,
lalli tuuta chiŋ di sii guŋ,
gilɛɛ wa mɔŋ wiimaa ra ta,
ka ŋɔ, ‘Ba daŋ kpegli
Babilɔn hina.
Ba daŋ kpa hiihzi kpu
ba vug Maduk.
Babilɔn vuga maanii niŋ di hiihzi,
ba vuga la miŋ kiiwe
maanii bá purgi.’
3Hɛri bɛl nɛra daŋ lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag,
di ba wa pig baa,
di chɔgi a hɛri, ú chɔɔ pɛɛ.
Nɛr maa wàá kaa du de,
newea ni sela maanii
niŋ chɔ lii de.
4Di a saŋa wa hello,
Izrɛl ani Juda hina maa daŋ kpau,
di wii sinii di ra nyiŋŋi
Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la bɔr.
5Ba daŋ pɛɛzi Bizeŋ Ziɔn ŋmɛnɛɛ bɔr,
di bir ba siwee chaŋuu.
Ba daŋ ba, bá ni mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ nuukpaŋ la
n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ,
nuukpaŋ la baŋ wàá
chɔgi maa.
6N nɛra leuwoo lugɔ peeza,
a nɔɔna gillɔɔ a leu,
di gil a du bizenaa nyuuni
di ra bar.
A du bizenaa ni giŋgimee nyuuni di ra juuri,
a waa kaa zum
a chɔɔribɔr bɔr.
7Nɛr la maa haŋ wa naa,
ɔɔ lɔabuu.
A dɔma ɔɔ ŋɔu,
‘Yaa waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ,
di zuu Kɔraawiizi la
n ɛɛ a diiribɔr himmaa
ani ba naabaala tamii la ninɛɛ.’
8Izrɛl hina, ií chɔ lii Babilɔn hɛri,
ií chɔ lii de!
Ii ɛɛ nɛra la n niŋ feli lii.
9N daŋ du hɛssi aŋhina
n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag
nɛra bɔkpega,
bá ɛɛ nuukpaŋ
di wa pig Babilɔn hina.
Ba daŋ wa chi ba chignibɔra
di kpegli baa.
Ba hobee daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ nɛra la
n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ,
ba waa tawɛɛ ra kir.
10Ba daŋ wa paagi Babilɔn hina kuna kaali,
banla n niŋ paagaa la
daŋ na ba kipar.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
11Babilɔn hina, ii foozi n hɛri kunaa
ii bɔra sɔɔni ia,
ii ra baruu alugɔ nau la n na fɛrgi sɔgmia
gɛɛ zagu la n na wii,
12ka ii bolzeŋkpeg
daŋ di hiihzi, di ŋmaabi.
Babilɔnnɛ niŋ gɛrgi
kaali hɛssi maa.
U daŋ ɛɛ hɛribɔduma,
wàá dɔɔ nii.
13Dikuu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ wia,
nɛr maa wàá ka so de,
ka u maa chɔɔ pɛɛ.
Nɛr la maa n niŋ wa ga Babilɔn,
ɔnsii werge daŋ lawuu,
ú nua kpu.
14Ii banla n ɛɛ hotaara,
ií ga chi ii chignibɔra,
di bar Babilɔn maa.
Ií ta baa hobee,
di gilɛɛ wa gil
hobikpaŋ maa ra ka,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ɛɛ
wichɔgaarɛ di zuu
Kɔraawiizi ni.
15Ií lɔ laal wile di ra bar a bolzeŋ maa!
U di kuurɛ, u diijaŋraa la n la chiŋ
maa purgi chogli,
ba purgi u koŋlaa maanii.
Guŋ n ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi kinturgaa wia,
ií turguu a kim,
di dawuu gunla
ban dau baŋhina la.
16Ií gilɛɛ waa gil bá duu
gɛɛ di kum kuna a hɛri.
Dikuu nɛr la n na sunni nɛra tokobi wia,
gil nɛr maa bir kaali
u himmaa nɛra be,
u himmaa hɛri.”
17Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɔɔ
lugɔ peeza
bunyinzi n duŋŋɛɛ, a yaari.
Asiiria koorizenne felee wa lɔ baa,
ka Babilɔn
Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza
jaa keezi ba di wa
purgi ba hoga.
18Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
‘N daŋ tɛr Babilɔn koori
ani u hɛri hina maa digna,
gunla miŋ tɛr
Asiiria koorizeŋ digna la.
19Ka n daŋ bir gil Izrɛl hina ba
ba himmaa hɛri,
di kaa wa so.
Ba daŋ na diwee
Bizeŋ Kamɛl nyuu
ni Basan hɛri.
Ba daŋ na diwee gunla maga banna nyiŋŋi,
lii Ɛfram ni Giliad
giŋgimee nyuuni, di di piŋ.
20A guŋ saŋa wa hello,
ba daŋ pigzi
di nyiŋŋi Izrɛl hina bilchɔg,
ka ba wàá na bɛl maa,
di nyiŋŋi Juda hina wichɔgaa,
ka ba wàá na bɛl maa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ gil
banla miŋ gillɛ la
wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.’ ”
21Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Ií la ga lɔ
Mɛratam hɛri
ani banla n du Pɛkɔd la.
Ií dau ba luge,
di kpu baa nyaamm.
Ií ɛɛ wia la maa
miŋ ŋɔ ii ɛɛ la.
22Ba nuu laal gbɔgaa a hɛri biini,
chɔgaa werge gbɔga!
23Babilɔn hina faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ silii,
di ra nyiŋŋi ba purgi
durnya naa maa burburbur!
Ka filaŋkeŋ, ba waa kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa,
ba kpegli baabuu!
Na gunla Babilɔn wia n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge,
hɛssi hina maa nuuzi kpu.
24N he iabuu sidɛɛ, Babilɔn hina,
u lau iabuu di ii waa zummɛ.
Ba na iabuu di lau ia,
dikuu iiŋ di
mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi mmɔri wia.
25N pilli n dɔŋkuna diarɛ,
di lizi n baaŋfuuihchɔgii dɔŋkuna,
dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa,
di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la,
dɔɔ humaa ń hum
Babilɔn hɛri.
26Ií lii bɔɔnɛɛ wa lɔ baa,
di purgi ba buugazi,
di chaali kuna la iiŋ paagɛɛ dau
kulululu lugɔ mia.
Ií chɔgi a hɛri maa,
di gilɛɛ wa gil
nɛr maa wàá ka de.
27Ií kpu ba laallɔɔra maa!
Ií kɔrgi baa!
Wiarɛ huuzi Babilɔn hina!
Ba digna tɛraa saŋa helloo.
28Ií ra nuu, nɛra la n lii
Babilɔnnɛ di ba Jɛrusalɛm.
Ba ra bagli gunla Kɔraawiizi
n tɔɔri Babilɔn hinaa,
dikuu baŋ chɔg u Dia wia.
29Chaali hotaara bá ga yoo Babilɔn hina,
banla maa n zum
hoo tai nɛnnɛ.
Ií la ga chɔɔ bar a bolzeŋ maa,
di gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa
wa na bɔr di ra chɔ.
Ií bir turgi baa ba wiɛɛlaa kim,
di dau baa gunla baŋ ɛɛwɛ la.
Dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ta barabaraa
du mìŋ́ Izrɛl
Dɔɔrinaniinanii la.
30Awia, ba biipɔllaa maanii
bá kpu ta ŋmɛnibaana,
di kaa kpu ba
laallɔɔra maa ge a hɔl hiŋ.
31Babilɔn hina, ii kpoŋŋoo werge,
awia, n chigɛ ii ninɛɛ.
Hɔpizii la min niŋ tɛr ii digna la helloo.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.
32Ii kpoŋaa daŋ gil ii jiŋli di chogli,
ka nɛr maa wàá lalli ia chiŋ.
N daŋ du ii bolzenaa maa niŋ,
ú fuuh kuna la maa
n bar ia la nyaamm.”
33Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Ba ra sunni Izrɛl
ni Juda hina maanii.
Nɛra la n lauri baa la ra du ba taurɛ nɛnnɛ,
ba wàá sɛɛ ba na bɔr kaali.
34Ka ba Lɛɛri kpekkoo,
u sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ.
U daŋ aah siwii di lɛɛ ba nua,
di gil bɔsɔna du ba hɛri,
ka kpa tɔɔrɔɔ
ta Babilɔn hina ni.”
35Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Babilɔn hina daŋ siu!
Ba nabɔnzi ni
ba nunzunna daŋ siu!
36Ba dɔgtɛɛkara hina daŋ siu!
Ba daŋ birgi gɛnaa!
Ba laallɔɔra maa daŋ siu!
Ɔnsii lau baabuuu
werge maa!
37Ba zagra ni anla n na tɛrgi torkozi daŋ siu
ani famaraa la maa
n du ba biini la!
Ba daŋ birgi haana!
Ba daama kuna daŋ siu!
Ba daŋ paagaa kaali!
38Hil daŋ chi!
Bá gɔŋa maa hil!
Dikuubɛɛwiai, Babilɔn ɛɛ vuga hɛrii,
vuga la n niŋ gil
ba birgi chuglahina,
dikuu ɔnsii werge wia.
39Awia, hɛribɔduma sela
ni munuzii niŋ du de,
kukuballi ra zuu de.
Nɛr maa ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka so de,
di lii jimini bɛl
di ra la bɛl.
40Gunla baŋ faa chɔg Sɔdɔm ni Gɔmɔra
ani bola la maa n baraa la,
gunnɛ bá chɔg Babilɔn,
nɛr maa wàá ka du.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
41Ií na, laallɔɔra lii wiifuri nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ di ra ba.
Ba du hɛrkpeg hina
ni koorikpila n du
bɔɔnɛɛrɛ bɔkpega.
42Ba kpogli hozi, kandaazi ani ba tokobizii,
di dɔɔ sihilii werge,
ba waa nɛra ni ra suŋ.
Di ba haŋ tinni ba zagra,
ba gbɔga ɔɔ ɛɛu lugɔ
muuzeŋ n ɔɔ ra kɔɔ la.
Ba ɛɛ siryaa bá wa lɔ
Babilɔn hina.
43Babilɔn koori nuu ba wiarɛ,
u nonee maa yɔɔri.
U biini chɔgi werge,
u bɔra ra waazuu
alugɔ hilulaa n lɔ haaŋ la.
44Alugɔ bunyiŋ n lii Jɔɔdan muu kɔr biini
di ra la sela diiribɔr la
n wesse la,
gunnɛ ń duŋŋi Babilɔn hina
lii ba hɛri kakpaŋ.
Anɛɛ ń lizi u ɛɛ kennei?
Anɛɛ n lugɔŋ, ú karsinnɛi?
Sitɔɔri bɛliirɛ niŋ wer
diŋ mmɔrɛi?
45Awia, ii ra nuu jina la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n tawɛɛ
Babilɔn hina wia,
gunla minna nyiŋŋi ń dau
Babilɔn hɛri hina.
N daŋ tuuzi ba biizi kaali,
di chɔgi ba sela diiribɔr maa
dikuu ba wia.
46Di nɛra wa nuu Babilɔn hina cholaa wia,
durnya maa daŋ zigli.
Hɛssi hina maa
daŋ nuu ba wiraa.”

english_text:
Babylon Will Be Destroyed
1I, the Lord, am sending
a wind to destroy
the people of Babylonia
and Babylon, its capital.
2Foreign soldiers will come
from every direction,
and when the disaster is over,
Babylonia will be empty
and worthless.
3I will tell these soldiers,
“Attack quickly,
before the Babylonians
can string their bows
or put on their armor.
Kill their best soldiers
and destroy their army!”
4Their troops will fall wounded
in the streets of Babylon.
5Everyone in Israel and Judah
is guilty.
But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
their holy God,
have not abandoned them.
6Get out of Babylon!
Run for your lives!
If you stay, you will be killed
when I take revenge on the city
and punish it for its sins.
7 Babylon was my golden cup,
filled with the wine
of my anger.
The nations of the world
got drunk on this wine
and went insane.
8But suddenly, Babylon will fall
and be destroyed.
I, the Lord, told the foreigners
who lived there,
“Weep for the city!
Get medicine for its wounds;
maybe they will heal.”
9The foreigners answered,
“We have already tried
to treat Babylon's wounds,
but they would not heal.
Come on, let's all go home
to our own countries.
Nothing is left in Babylonia;
everything is destroyed.”
10The people of Israel said,
“Tell everyone in Zion!
The Lord has taken revenge
for what Babylon did to us.”
The Lord Wants Babylon Destroyed
11I, the Lord,
want Babylon destroyed,
because its army
destroyed my temple.
So, you kings of Media,
sharpen your arrows
and pick up your shields.
12Raise the signal flag
and attack the city walls.
Post more guards.
Have soldiers watch the city
and set up ambushes.
I have made plans
to destroy Babylon,
and nothing will stop me.
13 People of Babylon, you live
along the Euphrates River
and are surrounded by canals.
You are rich,
but now the time has come
for you to die.
14I, the Lord All-Powerful,
swear by my own life
that enemy soldiers
will fill your streets
like a swarm of locusts.
They will shout
and celebrate their victory.
A Hymn of Praise
(Jeremiah 10.12-16)
15God used his wisdom and power
to create the earth
and spread out the heavens.
16The waters in the heavens roar
at his command.
He makes clouds appear;
he sends the wind
from his storehouse
and makes lightning flash
in the rain.
17People who make idols
are stupid!
They will be disappointed,
because their false gods
cannot breathe.
18Idols are merely a joke,
and when the time is right,
they will be destroyed.
19But the Lord, Israel's God,
is all-powerful.
He created everything,
and he chose Israel
to be his very own.
God's Hammer
The Lord said:
20Babylonia, you were my hammer;
I used you to pound nations
and break kingdoms,
21to shatter cavalry and chariots,
22as well as men and women,
young and old,
23shepherds and their flocks,
farmers and their oxen,
and governors and leaders.
24But now, my people will watch,
while I repay you
for what you did to Zion.
25You destroyed the nations
and seem strong as a mountain,
but I am your enemy.
I might even grab you
and roll you off a cliff.
When I am finished,
you'll only be a pile
of scorched bricks.
26Your stone blocks won't be reused
for cornerstones
or foundations,
and I promise that forever
you will be a desert.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Nations Will Attack Babylon
The Lord said:
27Signal the nations
to get ready to attack.
Raise a flag and blow a trumpet.
Send for the armies of Ararat,
Minni, and Ashkenaz.
Choose a commander;
let the cavalry attack
like a swarm of locusts.
28Tell the kings and governors,
the leaders and the people
of the kingdoms of the Medes
to prepare for war!
29The earth twists and turns
in torment,
because I have decided
to make Babylonia a desert
where no one can live,
and I won't change my mind.
30The Babylonian soldiers
have lost their strength
and courage.
They stay in their fortresses,
unable to fight,
while the enemy breaks through
the city gates,
then sets their homes on fire.
31One messenger after another
announces to the king,
“Babylon has been captured!
32The enemy now controls
the river crossings!
The marshes are on fire!
Your army has panicked!”
33I am the Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel,
and I make this promise—
“Soon Babylon will be leveled
and packed down
like a threshing place
at harvest time.”
Babylonia Will Pay!
34The people of Jerusalem say,
“King Nebuchadnezzar
made us panic.
That monster stuffed himself
with us and our treasures,
leaving us empty—
he gobbled up
what he wanted
and spit out the rest.
35The people of Babylonia
harmed some of us
and killed others.
Now, Lord, make them pay!”
The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
36My people, I am on your side,
and I will take revenge
on Babylon.
I will cut off its water supply,
and its stream will dry up.
37Babylon will be a pile of rubble
where only jackals live,
and everyone will be afraid
to walk among the ruins.
38The Babylonians roar and growl
like young lions.
39And since they are hungry,
I will give them a banquet.
They will celebrate, get drunk,
then fall asleep,
never to wake up!
40I will lead them away to die,
like sheep, lambs, and goats
being led to the butcher.
41All nations now praise Babylon,
but when it is captured,
those same nations
will be horrified.
42Babylon's enemies will rise
like ocean waves
and flood the city.
43Horrible destruction will strike
the nearby towns.
The land will become
a barren desert,
where no one can live
or even travel.
44I will punish Marduk,
the god of Babylon,
and make him vomit out
everything he gobbled up.
Then nations will no longer
bring him gifts,
and Babylon's walls will crumble.
The Lord Offers Hope to His People
45Get out of Babylon, my people,
and run for your lives,
before I strike the city
in my anger!
46Don't be afraid or lose hope,
though year after year
there are rumors
of leaders fighting for control
in the city of Babylon.
47The time will come
when I will punish
Babylon's false gods.
Everyone there will die,
and the whole nation
will be disgraced,
48 when an army attacks
from the north
and brings destruction.
Then the earth and the heavens
and everything in them
will celebrate.
49 Babylon must be overthrown,
because it slaughtered
the people of Israel
and of many other nations.
50My people, you escaped death
when Jerusalem fell.
Now you live far from home,
but you should trust me
and think about Jerusalem.
Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
51You feel ashamed and disgraced,
because foreigners have entered
my sacred temple.
52Soon I will send a war
to punish Babylon's idols
and leave its wounded people
moaning everywhere.
53Although Babylon's walls
reach to the sky,
the army I send
will destroy that city.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
Babylon Will Be Destroyed
The Lord said:
54Listen to the cries for help
coming from Babylon.
Everywhere in the country
the sounds of destruction
can be heard.
55The shouts of the enemy,
like crashing ocean waves,
will drown out Babylon's cries
as I level the city.
56An enemy will attack
and destroy Babylon.
Its soldiers will be captured
and their weapons broken,
because I am a God
who takes revenge against nations
for what they do.
57I, the Lord All-Powerful,
the true King, promise
that the officials and advisors,
the governors and leaders,
and the soldiers of Babylon
will get drunk, fall asleep,
and never wake up.
58The thick walls of that city
will be torn down,
and its huge gates burned.
Everything that nation
worked so hard to gain
will go up in smoke.
Jeremiah Gives Seraiah a Scroll
59During Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah, he went to Babylon. And Baruch's brother Seraiah went along as the officer in charge of arranging for places to stay overnight.
60Before they left, I wrote on a scroll all the terrible things that would happen to Babylon. 61I gave the scroll to Seraiah and said:
When you get to Babylon, read this scroll aloud, 62then pray, “Our Lord, you promised to destroy this place and make it into a desert where no people or animals will ever live.”
63 When you finish praying, tie the scroll to a rock and throw it in the Euphrates River. Then say, 64“This is how Babylon will sink when the Lord destroys it. Everyone in the city will die, and it won't have the strength to rise again.”
The End of Jeremiah's Writing
Jeremiah's writing ends here.
translation_text:
Babilɔn hina dignitɛraa jaa wia
1Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“N daŋ du nɛchɔgii bɔkpega,
ú ba wa lɔ Babilɔn hina laal.
2N daŋ gil hɔɔhra la Babilɔn,
di ga chɔgi baa alugɔ
peu n ɔɔ paa kpaga
kaali la.
Di a keŋ hɔpizii naa wa hello,
ba daŋ la ga baruu, di lɔu,
di chɔguu, ú birgi diŋgela.
3Ií gilɛɛ waa tɛɛ ba laallɔɔra bɔr,
ba waa taazi ba hozi
gɛɛ di wa kpa ba laal kuna
di ra laali.
Ií gilɛɛ waa gil ba biipɔllaa!
Ií kpu ba laallɔɔra maa!
4Ba daŋ du baa pira,
bá siuzi chɔɔ
ba bolzenaa ŋmɛnizi.
5Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
waa Izrɛl ni Juda hina
vɛɛwɛ ta.
Haali baŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa
di zuu mìŋ́ Izrɛl
Dɔɔrinaniinanii ni gba.
6Ií chɔ lii Babilɔn!
Ií chɔ ra nyiŋŋi
ii miibɔɔni bɔra!
Ií gilɛɛ gil ba kuu Babilɔn hina
wichɔgaa wia kpu ia.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi jaa ra nyiŋŋuu
ń bir kpa ba wichɔgaa
kim turgi baa,
di tɛr ba digna gunla n dɛkkɛ.
7Babilɔn faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ
saliŋ libee di du n nonii.
N gil durnya hina maa
nyɔɔ u biini siŋ, di ra dɛɛzi.
Hɛssi hina maa ɔɔ nyɔɔ u biini siŋ,
di jaa ra chugli.
8Babilɔn daŋ chol di purgi kakpaŋ.
Ií wii ra tɛu!
Ií nyiŋŋi nuu faa u bɔra wiila,
aŋhinabe, u daŋ nyaagi.
9Famaraa la n du Babilɔn la jaa ŋɔ,
‘Yaa ɛɛ aniaa ya hiini
Babilɔn hina,
ka a teŋ bɛri.
Ií gil ya gil baa filaŋkeŋ,
ka bir kaali yaa bola.
Kɔraawiizi kpa u fɔŋŋazenne
tɛr Babilɔn hina digna,
di chɔg ba
hɛri nyaamm.’ ”
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N nɛra, ií ra chaasi,
Kɔraawiizi baglɔɔrɛ lugɔ yaa hor summɔɔ,
ií ba yá ŋɔ wia la
Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ,
Jɛrusalɛm biini.”
11Denii a laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ŋɔ,
“Ií sazi ii hobee,
di kpa ii laal pɛrɛtuzi!
Kɔraawiizi du Mɛdi hina kooraa bɔkpega,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u dauwɔɔ lugɔ
ú chɔgi Babilɔn hina.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ bir turgi baa ba kim,
dikuu u Dia wia.
12Ií lalli tuuta chaŋ Babilɔn koŋlaa!
Ií nyiŋŋi nɛra jaa
ii tauduura ni bá du kpeg,
di gil ba chi ba chignibɔra,
di gil ba so saga!
Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ wia la maa uŋ dauwɛ,
u ɛɛ Babilɔn hina la.
13Ii banla n soge gɔŋa kɛraa,
di dɔɔ daama werge,
ii saŋa helloo
bá chɔgi ia nyaamm.
14Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
hɛɛhzi u hinnɛ lugɔ
u daŋ gil baala kpila ba,
di wa su ii biini lugɔ lotorozi,
ba daŋ kpegli ia
di chaasi du ii ni.”
Kɔraawiizi chɔlaa yir
15Kɔraawiizi kpa fɔŋŋaa ta hɛri,
di kpa u nunzuma ta durnya,
di kpa u wia zɛɛ zumaa
yaa chiŋ.
16Di u wa pozoo lugɔ nazaa,
niiri la n du chiŋ ɔɔ ra kɔɔu,
ɔɔ giluu baamazi
izi bɔr maa,
di gil dooŋ nyɛgzaa
ni dooŋ maa kpau di ba.
U ɔɔ giluu peu lii
u kuna dauribɔra,
di waa ta.
17Nɛr maa ɛɛ gɛniirɛ Kɔraawiizi be,
di nyaa nunzuma!
Vugkuari maa daŋ di hiihzi,
dikuu u vuga wia.
U vuga ɛɛ kumpɛɛrii,
a waa heezi.
18A ɛɛ kumpɛɛrii,
di ɛɛ chɛɛtɛ kuna.
Di a seriya dii saŋa wa hello,
Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgaa.
19Kɔraawiizi la yaa naabaal Jekɔb naanna n na hum la,
waa lugɔ annii.
Waabuu ta kummaa,
di lizi Izrɛl hina,
ba ɛɛ u himmaa nɛra.
U sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ.
20Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Babilɔn hina, ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ n gulii laal biini.
N ɔɔ faa kpa di ra
chɔgi hɛssi hina,
di kpa ia ra chɔgi kossi,
21di kpa ia ra kpuuzi zagra ni a tinna,
ni banla n soge
laal torkozi biine,
22di ra kpu baala ni haana,
di ra kpu bazɛŋzi ni biipɔllaa,
di ra kpu biibaala
ni biihaana,
23di ra kpu penɔɔna ni ba peeza,
di ra kpu patta ni napattaa,
di ra kpu hɛri nabɔnzi
ni nabɔnzenaa.
24N daŋ bir turgi Babilɔn hina ba wiɛɛlaa kim, ii himmaa siwii na, dikuu wichɔgaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ dau bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm hina la wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
25Babilɔn, i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bizeŋ la n na chɔgi durnya maa,
ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ i dɔmnɛ.
N daŋ fuuih,
í birgi hɔɔhri.
26Nɛr maa ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka kpa i bia di ma dia.
I daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ hɛribɔduma
di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
27Ií lalli tuuta a hɛri biini!
Ií huuh bensunoniina
a hɛssi biine!
Ií ɛɛ hɛssi hina sirya bá ga lɔ baa,
ií yirgi kossi naa,
Ararat, Minni
ani Askɛnaz hina,
bá ga lɔ baa.
Ií lizi laallɔɔra nabɔma ú tɔ ba see,
di gil zagra lii lugɔ
lotorozi miiih.
28Ií ɛɛ hɛssi hina sirya, bá ga lɔ Babilɔn hina.
Ií yir Mɛdi hɛri koora,
ba hɛssi nabɔnzi,
ba nabɔnzenaa ani
hɛssi la maa
banna di kora a ni la.
29Hɛri zigloore, dikuubɛɛwiai,
Kɔraawiizi jina la uŋ tawɛɛ
Babilɔn wia la chigɔɔ.
U daŋ gil Babilɔn hɛri birgi diŋgela,
guŋ gil nɛr maa
wàá ka du de.
30Babilɔn laallɔɔra jaa gil laal lɔirɛ,
ka du ba diikpega biine.
Ba fɔŋŋa tunnɔɔ,
ba jaa ɛɛ lugɔ haana.
Ba diini maanii ba du niŋ,
di kuugi
ba bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa.
31Balaa jaa hiŋzi dɔŋa
di chɔ ra la Babilɔn koori be,
di gaa lizi amaniye
ra tɛu gunla
baŋ purgi u bolzeŋ maa,
di kpegluu.
32Bɔra la baŋ gawɛɛ di ra gi a muu maanii ba teŋri,
di du a muu kɛraa
fotogozi bɔra maa kooree niŋ,
ɔnsii lau a laallɔɔra,
ba bɔra ra sa.”
33Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ,
“A wàá birgi ka ba dɔma kpu baa,
di fɛrgi baa alugɔ
banna lɔ mia pila.”
34Jɛrusalɛm hina ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Babilɔn koori kpu yaabuu,
guŋ gil yaa ɛɛ kinchaŋ,
di gil yaa du lugɔ keuwoo.
U ɛɛ lugɔ hɛrikuŋ n lau yaa lil,
yaa du sum, u hia su,
u bir ug yaa ha.
35Gil Babilɔn hina wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni,
dikuu wii la baŋ kpawɛɛ
dau yaa la wia!
Gil Babilɔn hina wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni,
dikuu baŋ tɔɔri yaa la wia!”
36Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“N daŋ lɛɛ ii nua,
di gil ii dɔma turgi
wia la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ
dau ia la kim.
N daŋ gil u muuzeŋ hil,
di gil u bulli maa hil.
37Babilɔn daŋ purgi chɔɔ kulululu,
di ɛɛ pir sela duuribɔr,
de wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, ú ɛɛ chɛɛtɛkuŋ.
Nɛr la maa n niŋ ɔɔ wa na de,
ɔnsii daŋ lawuu werge maa.
38Babilɔn hina ra wiiu lugɔ bunyimpɔla,
di ra uuhri lugɔ bunyimbizi.
39Ba ɛɛ kpossiiree gɛɛ?
N daŋ daali diuzenaa
tɛɛ baa bá di,
di nyɔɔ siŋ dɛɛzi,
bá bɔra ra pur.
Ba daŋ chɔɔgi dɔzi,
ba wàá ka izi maa.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ guŋ.
40N daŋ gil ba kɔrgi baa
alugɔ pebizi,
pebala ani buuna.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
41Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Babilɔn wia,
“Ba kpegli bolzeŋ la durnya hina maa n na chɔli labuu!
Na gunla Babilɔn wia
n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge
hɛssi hina maa biine!
42Muuzeŋ daŋ su wa tɔ Babilɔn ni,
ú niilɔɔlaa wa tɔ u ni.
43De bolzenaa daŋ birgi diŋgelli,
di ɛɛ hɛribɔduma,
nii wàá du de,
hɛri la nɛr maa n wàá du de,
nɛr maa wàá ra vol de.
44N daŋ tɔɔri Babilɔn hina vug la
banna yir Bɛl la,
di gil u ug kuna la maa
uŋ liglee la.
Hɛssi hina wàá ka chɔ ba u be.
Babilɔn koŋlii daŋ chol.
45N nɛra, ií lii u biini!
Ií chɔ lɛɛ ii miibɔɔni!
Ií chɔ lii Kɔraawiizi
baaŋfuuihchɔgii biini.
46Ií gilɛɛ wa gil ɔnsii waa lau ia, ii bɔra ra huah,
dikuu iiŋ ɔɔ ra
nuu wia hunehune wia.
Bina maa biini,
hunehune ɔɔ du denii
naari wia, koori bɛl
n na lɔ koori bɛl laal.
47Awia, saŋa bɛl ra bau,
min niŋ tɔɔri
Babilɔn hina vuga.
A hɛri hina maa daŋ di hiihzi.
Ba daŋ kpu u nɛra maa
ha u biini.
48Chiŋ ni hɛri ani kuna la maa n du a biine,
daŋ chaasi ni bɔsɔna
di du Babilɔn ni,
dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛra daŋ lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag
di wa lɔu laal.
49Babilɔn daŋ chol, dikuu u nɛra n kpu Izrɛl hina
ani gunla baŋ gillɛ
ba kpu durnya hina
maa la wia.”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ guŋ.
50Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u nɛra benii Babilɔn biini,
“Ii chɔwɔɔrɛ lii siu biini!
Filaŋkeŋ, ií ra la!
Ií gilɛɛ waa kpaŋ!
Haali iiŋ waa bol duglɛɛ gba,
ka ii ra liizi
mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum
ni Jɛrusalɛm wia.
51Ii ra ŋɔu, ‘Yaa di hiihzii,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba
chagzi yaabuu,
hiihzi kpu yaa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, famaraa zuu
Kɔraawiizi Dia
bɔnanaananaa labuu.’
52Awia, n na ŋɔu lugɔ hɔpizaa aŋhina ra bau,
min niŋ chɔgi Babilɔn vuga.
Banla n na pira,
ra hɛm a hɛri maa biini.
53Haali di Babilɔn ga chug chiŋ,
ba ma koŋlii bar
u diikpega gba,
ka n daŋ gil
nɛkpuura wa lɔu laal.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ guŋ.”
54Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ,
“Ií ra nuu gunla wiraa n na lii Babilɔn hina biini,
chɔgaa werge gbɔga,
n du Babilɔn hɛri.
55Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgi Babilɔn nyaamm,
bá chɛɛhgaa la tuŋ.
Ba dɔma daŋ hiihri ba ni alugɔ nii n na lɔ,
ba wiraa wàá tuŋ.
56Nɛkpuuri daŋ ba wa lɔ Babilɔn,
di lauri u laallɔɔra maa,
bá hozi kuugi.
Dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu ra tɛr nɛra digna,
di ra turgi baa
bá wichɔgaa kim,
a ra su a maga.
57N daŋ gil u nabɔnzenaa
ni u nunzunna dɛɛzi,
haali di kpa u hɛri nabɔnzi,
karchizi ani laallɔɔra maa.
Ba daŋ chɔɔ dɔɔ di hanna la,
ba wàá izi,
mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ Koori,
n sɔŋ di Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ
labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”
58Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ,
“Ba daŋ purgi Babilɔn koŋliizeŋ la maa burburbur,
di du u dominuuzenaa
maa niŋ.
A nɛra ra kuuh bahinaarɛ pɛɛ,
durnya hɛssi nɛra
kuuhni maa ɛɛ nindaazii.”
59Amaniye naabuu mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia faa tɛɛ Nɛria biibaal Sɛraaya la naabaal n faa ɛɛ Masɛya la. Waabuu faa ra hiini Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia, saŋa la uŋ la Babilɔn, u kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ biini la. 60N faa sɛbi hɛhchɔgni la maa n niŋ wa chol Babilɔn hina ni ani wia la maa baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ dikuu ba wia labuu dau hɔŋ ni. 61N ŋɔ Sɛraaya benii, “Di i haŋ ga hel Babilɔn, ɛɛ ania ka karmi wia naa maa, á lii chaaŋ nɛr maa nuu. 62Ka ŋɔ, ‘N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ i daŋ chɔgi bɔnnaa, newee gɛɛ sel maa wàá ka du de. U daŋ birgi diŋgela, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.’ 63Di i wa karmi a hɔnnaa tɛɛ baa tuŋ, piŋŋuu di kpau vɔɔ mari bii, di kpau ga ta Muu Yufretis biini, 64ka ŋɔ, ‘Kenne Babilɔn muzi, u ŋmɛnɛ wàá ka lii maa, dikuu hɛhchɔg la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ kpa ta u ni la wia.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia wiŋɔzi tunaa ɛŋ.’ ”

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Captured
(2 Kings 24.18—25.30; 2 Chronicles 36.11-21)
1Zedekiah was 21 years old when he was appointed king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother Hamutal was the daughter of Jeremiah from the town of Libnah. 2Zedekiah disobeyed the Lord, just as Jehoiakim had done, 3and it was Zedekiah who finally rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.
The people of Judah and Jerusalem had made the Lord so angry that he finally turned his back on them. That's why horrible things were happening there.
4 In Zedekiah's ninth year as king, on the tenth day of the tenth month, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia led his entire army to attack Jerusalem. The troops set up camp outside the city and built ramps up to the city walls.
5-6After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month, 7 the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley, 8but the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. The Babylonians arrested Zedekiah, but his soldiers scattered in every direction. 9Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty. 10Zedekiah's sons and the officials of Judah were killed while he watched, 11 then his eyes were poked out. He was put in chains, then dragged off to Babylon and kept in prison until he died.
12Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia.
About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan, 13 and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses. 14Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem. 15He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah. 16Only the very poorest were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
17-20 Nebuzaradan ordered his soldiers to go to the temple and take everything made of gold or silver, including bowls, fire pans, sprinkling bowls, pans, lampstands, dishes for incense, and the cups for wine offerings. The Babylonian soldiers took all the bronze things used for worship at the temple, including the pans for hot ashes, and the shovels, lamp snuffers, sprinkling bowls, and dishes for incense. The soldiers also took everything else made of bronze, including the two columns that stood in front of the temple, the large bowl called the Sea, the twelve bulls that held it up, and the movable stands. The soldiers broke these things into pieces so they could take them to Babylonia. There was so much bronze that it could not be weighed. 21For example, the columns were about 8 meters high and 5.5 meters around. They were hollow, but the bronze was about 75 millimeters thick. 22Each column had a bronze cap over 2 meters high that was decorated with bronze designs. Some of these designs were like chains and others were like pomegranates. 23There were 96 pomegranates evenly spaced around each column, and a total of 100 pomegranates were located above the chains.
24Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials. 25Then he arrested one of the army commanders, seven of King Zedekiah's personal advisors, and the officer in charge of gathering the troops for battle. He also found 60 more soldiers who were still in Jerusalem. 26-27Nebuzaradan led them to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar had them killed.
The people of Judah no longer lived in their own country.
People of Judah Taken Prisoner
28-30Here is a list of the number of the people of Judah that Nebuchadnezzar took to Babylonia as prisoners:
In his seventh year as king, he took 3,023 people.
In his eighteenth year as king, he took 832 from Jerusalem.
In his twenty-third year as king, his officer Nebuzaradan took 745 people.
So, Nebuchadnezzar took a total of 4,600 people from Judah to Babylonia.
Jehoiachin Is Set Free
(2 Kings 25.27-30)
31Jehoiachin was a prisoner in Babylon for 37 years. Then Evil Merodach became king of Babylonia, and in the first year of his rule, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, he let Jehoiachin out of prison. 32Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there. 33Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day. 34As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_text:
Jɛrusalɛm cholaa wia
1Koori Zɛdɛkia binni faa du tokko ni kpaŋ, ka u di a kora, di so Jɛrusalɛm biini, binni fidikpaŋ. U maarɛ faa Jɛrɛmia bɛl biihaaŋ Hamutal n lii bolzeŋ Libna. 2Koori Zɛdɛkia faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ zuu Kɔraawiizi ni alugɔ Koori Jɛhɔyakim. 3Kɔraawiizi baannɛ faa gillɛ a wia naa maa huuzi Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina. A tuna maa, u faa duŋŋi baabuu lii u be. A saŋa, Koori Zɛdɛkia faa waa kaa waa sɛɛ Babilɔn Koori dɔɔra.
4Awia, Koori Zɛdɛkia kora dii binni kabɛlhiŋ biini, baaguzi fihiŋ hɔpizaa fi hɔl, Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ni u laallɔɔra maa faa ba, di wa fɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm ni laal. Ba faa wa chɔɔ a bol nuarɛ, di gil ba ta pizenaa bar a bol koŋliizeŋ maa. 5Ba faa fɔɔubuu guŋŋ di wa hel Koori Zɛdɛkia kora dii binni fidikpaŋhiŋ biini.
6A baaguzi anaazuhiŋ biini, hɔpizaa kabɛl hɔl, lɔchɔgii la n du bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm la jaa nyaŋŋi, a nɛra waa kaa dɔɔ kummaa bá di. 7Haali Babilɔn laallɔɔra n faa bar a bolzeŋ gba, ka a laallɔɔra maa ga dominuuzeŋ la n du a koŋlaa anɛɛ baambaaŋ, di dugli koori kambol la hamuŋa ni, di lii chɔ kaali Jɔɔdan Waluu barii. 8Ka Babilɔn laallɔɔra la faa dau Koori Zɛdɛkia luge guŋŋ di ga lawuu bolzeŋ Jɛriko lɛl biini. A saŋa, di u laallɔɔra maa faa chɔwɔɔ lii u be, di yaari. 9Ba kpogluu ba Babilɔn koorizeŋ be, bolzeŋ Ribla n du Hamaf, u di u seriya de, u chol. 10A Riblaa Babilɔn koori faa kpu Koori Zɛdɛkia biibaala u sibɔɔ, di kaa kpu Juda hina nabɔnzenaa maa ge de jaa. 11Uŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ, u foŋzi Zɛdɛkia sibee, ka gil ba kpa danyɛ yɔlɔzi duu, di kpogluu kaali Babilɔn, di ga tɔu dia, u du de di ra ba a hɔl la uŋ siuwɛ.
12Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza kora dii binni fidikabɛlhiŋ, baaguzi anuehiŋ hɔpizaa fi hɔllɛ, u laallɔɔra nabɔma Nɛbuzaradan la n faa ra binni banla n na guuu la, zuu Jɛrusalɛm, 13di fuuh Kɔraawiizi Dia, kooridia ani nabɔnzenaa maa diini, Jɛrusalɛm biini. 14Babilɔn laallɔɔra la maa koori guure nabɔma n faa ra binni ba ni la, purgi koŋlaa la maa n bar Jɛrusalɛm la. 15Koori guure nabɔma Nɛbuzaradan jaa lauri ba nyaara la baŋhina ni banla n ka a bolzeŋ biini, di kpa banla maa n zum nonee huma nɛnnɛ jaa banla ge n chɔwɛɛ zuu Babilɔn koori ni la, di kaali Babilɔn. 16Ama, Nɛbuzaradan faa gil banla n ɛɛ nyaara werge la baŋhinaa a hɛri, bá ra binni ba grepu daazi kooni ni ba kooni ni.
17Babilɔn hina faa purgi danyɛ ligee ni torkozi la ni danyɛ Kolzeŋ la banna yir Muuzeŋ la n faa du Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la, di chi a maa kaali Babilɔn. 18Ba faa kaa chi a viini, a sɔɔbulzi, fintina yakɔssi mɔnni kuna, kuna mizaa tassazi ani danyɛ kuna la maa, baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra hum a Dia biini la. 19A koori guure nabɔma faa paagi tassazenaa, nimbuurikuna, kuna mizaa tassazi, viini, fintina daazi, tassajigzi ani nii tai tassazi kaali. A maanii ba faa kpa saliŋ himmaa gɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa di kuari.
20Ligee anɛɛ la, torkozi, Kolzeŋ la banna yir Muuzeŋ la nabala fidaanɛɛ du u zɛɛ la ani torkozi la maa Koori Solomɔn n faa kpa danyɛ kuari du Kɔraawiizi Dia la, faa kannɔɔ werge, ba wàá wer mɛgzaa. 21A ligii bɛl maa jaŋzi faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nogumzi fidiŋmantannaazi, kuna la baŋ faa kpawɛɛ hɔŋzi a nyuuni la ge bɛl maa chiŋ laŋaa faa ɛɛ nogumzi fidaanɛɛ bar u maa, bɛl maa gbossi ɛɛ lugɔ nonibee anaazu wassi, bɔɔ du bɛl maa ni. 22Danyɛ la n bɔɔri bɛl maa chiŋ laŋaa ge ɛɛ nogumzi anue, ba kpa yɔlɔzi lugɔ nyagrinyagri ni daa bɛl nɔna n lugɔ pomegranetzi la, di bɔgaa bar. A maanii ba faa kpa danyɛ kuari. 23Pomegranet nɔna tokkoanaazu ni fidaanumbɛllɛ faa du a kɛraa, di du a keŋkerezi hiŋ. A maa kpau n faa du a nyagrinyagrizi chiŋ du kalfa.
24A koori guure nabɔma faa lauri Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Sɛraaya ni u harbɔɔhiŋri Zɛfania ni a Dia dominua tauduura bahoro la maa yoma. 25Banla n faa haa ka a bolzeŋ biini, u faa lauri ba laallɔɔra nabɔma ni koori zɛɛsogna ge baniidaanɛɛ. U kaa lauri ba laallɔɔra nabɔma karchi la n na binni laallɔɔra hɔna ni, ni baala tokkoahoro n du a bolzeŋ biini. 26Denii Babilɔn koori guure nabɔma Nɛbuzaradan faa lauri ba maa, di ba Babilɔn koorizeŋ be, bolzeŋ Ribla 27n du Hamaf hɛri. A koori faa gil ba kpu baa de. Awia, ba faa lauri Juda hinaa kaali hɛrduma, ba waa kaa dugli ba himmaa hɛri. 28Jus hina la Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n faa laurɛɛ kaali u hɛri la magaa keŋ.
U kora dii binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biini, ba faa du nɛra kagboŋa ahoro ni tokko ni ahoro.
29U binni fidiŋmantannaazihiŋ biini,
nɛra kalfa ŋmantannaazi ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni banɛɛrɛ faa lii Jɛrusalɛm.
30U binni tokko ni ahorohiŋ biini,
nɛra kalfaaniidaanɛɛ ni tokkoanɛɛ ni banuere Nɛbuzaradan faa lauri kaali.
Ba maa kpau faa du nɛra kagboŋa anaazu ni kalfaanumbɛl.
Baŋ lizi Koori Jɛhɔyachin lii nɛra tɔi dia wia
31Juda Koori Jɛhɔyachin lawaa binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, baal bɛl banna yir Ɛvil Mɛrɔdak, faa di Babilɔn kora. A baaguzi fidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa tokko ni anue hɔllɛ u gil ba pilli Koori Jɛhɔyachin lii nɛra tɔi dia biini. 32Denii u faa ŋɔ wia ni sisɔna tɛɛ Koori Jɛhɔyachin, ka tɛu nabɔmuu kaali koora la maa n du u be, Babilɔn la. 33Awia, Koori Jɛhɔyachin faa wir u nɛra tɔi dia laala ta, ka kpa u himmaa laala laali. U ni a koori ɔɔ jaa kpau di ra di, u de dui maa biini. 34Hɔpizibii maanii Babilɔn Koori Ɛvil Mɛrɔdak ɔɔ faa ra tɛɛ Koori Jɛhɔyachin kebee, ú wer ra yau u kunnyiŋŋaa, guŋŋ di wa hel u siu hɔpizii.

english_text:
Lonely Jerusalem
The Prophet Speaks:
1 Jerusalem, once so crowded,
lies deserted and lonely.
This city that was known
all over the world
is now like a widow.
This queen of the nations
has been made a slave.
2Each night, bitter tears
flood her cheeks.
None of her former lovers
are there to offer comfort;
her friends have betrayed her
and are now her enemies.
3The people of Judah are slaves,
suffering in a foreign land,
with no rest from sorrow.
Their enemies captured them
and were terribly cruel.
4The roads to Zion mourn
because no one travels there
to celebrate the festivals.
The city gates are deserted;
priests are weeping.
Young women are raped;
Zion is in sorrow!
5Enemies now rule the city
and live as they please.
The Lord has punished Jerusalem
because of her awful sins;
he has let her people
be dragged away.
6Zion's glory has disappeared.
Her leaders are like deer
that cannot find pasture;
they are hunted down
till their strength is gone.
7Her people recall the good life
that once was theirs;
now they suffer
and are scattered.
No one was there to protect them
from their enemies who sneered
when their city was taken.
8Jerusalem's horrible sins
have made the city a joke.
Those who once admired her
now hate her instead—
she has been disgraced;
she groans and turns away.
9Her sins had made her filthy,
but she wasn't worried
about what could happen.
And when Jerusalem fell,
it was so tragic.
No one gave her comfort
when she cried out,
“Help! I'm in trouble, Lord!
The enemy has won.”
10Zion's treasures were stolen.
Jerusalem saw foreigners
enter her place of worship,
though the Lord
had forbidden them
to belong to his people.
11Everyone in the city groans
while searching for food;
they trade their valuables
for barely enough scraps
to stay alive.
Jerusalem Speaks:
Jerusalem shouts to the Lord,
“Please look and see
how miserable I am!”
12No passerby even cares.
Why doesn't someone notice
my terrible sufferings?
You were fiercely angry, Lord,
and you punished me
worst of all.
13From heaven you sent a fire
that burned in my bones;
you set a trap for my feet
and made me turn back.
All day long you leave me
in shock from constant pain.
14You have tied my sins
around my neck,
and they weigh so heavily
that my strength is gone.
You have put me in the power
of enemies too strong for me.
15You, Lord, have turned back
my warriors and crushed
my young heroes.
Judah was a woman untouched,
but you let her be trampled
like grapes in a wine pit.
16Because of this, I mourn,
and tears flood my eyes.
No one is here to comfort
or to encourage me;
we have lost the war—
my people are suffering.
The Prophet Speaks:
17Zion reaches out her hands,
but no one offers comfort.
The Lord has turned
the neighboring nations
against Jacob's descendants.
Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag
to her neighbors.
Jerusalem Speaks:
18The Lord was right,
but I refused to obey him.
Now I ask all of you to look
at my sufferings—
even my young people
have been dragged away.
19I called out to my lovers,
but they betrayed me.
My priests and my leaders died
while searching the city
for scraps of food.
20Won't you look and see
how upset I am, our Lord?
My stomach is in knots,
and my heart is broken
because I betrayed you.
In the streets and at home,
my people are slaughtered.
21Everyone heard my groaning,
but no one offered comfort.
My enemies know of the trouble
that you have brought on me,
and it makes them glad.
Hurry and punish them,
as you have promised.
22Don't let their evil deeds
escape your sight.
Punish them as much
as you have punished me
because of my sins.
I never stop groaning—
I've lost all hope!
translation_text:
1Na gunla bolzeŋ la
n faa dɔɔ nɛra werge
la n jaa chɔɔ woo!
Na, u jaa ɛɛu lugɔ luhaaŋ.
U faa dɔɔ sɔnnɛ
hɛssi hina maa be!
Unla n faa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ wiche
hɛssi la maa biine
la jaa birgi yonne.
2Hamuŋa maa, u ɔɔ ra wiiu werge,
sinii ra pal.
U sɛnni maa waa hoo
ú tig u bampirii.
U dammuzi maa daruubuu,
di jaa birgi u dɔma.
3Juda hina ɛɛ yoma la n waa hiini dɔɔwɛɛ,
ba fir baa, ba ga du
hɛrdumazi biine,
ba waa bol dɔɔwɛ.
Ba dɔma go baa,
ba wàá na bɔr chɔ.
4Nɛr maa waa kaa ra ba
Kɔraawiizi Dia la filaŋkeŋ,
ú wa jaami
hɔpizinanaananaa hɔla la.
Suŋgure la n faa ra yir yira de la
jaa ra di tɔɔrɔɔrɛ,
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina
ra hɛm.
Nɛr maa waa hoo a bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa,
Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina ra
di dɔgnyaa werge.
5Ba dɔma na bɔttɛ,
di dɔɔ ba fɔŋŋa.
Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ ba ra di tɔɔrɔɔ,
dikuu ba wichɔgaa
n kpillɛ werge wia,
ba dɔma lauri ba
biizii kaali.
6Jɛrusalɛm wessi tunnɔɔ,
u sitɔɔra ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ chɛhzi
n waa fɔŋŋa kaa dɔɔ
dikuu lɔzi wia,
di chɔ ra lii
kpaana be ni gɛrga.
7Jɛrusalɛm jaa purguu chɔɔ siriti,
u nɛra jaa ra liizi gunla
uŋ faa wesse la wia.
Nɛr maa faa waa hoo ú hiini baa,
saŋa la ba dɔma
n kpegli baa la.
Banla n kpegli baa la faa ra mam baabuu,
dikuu baŋ cholle wia.
8Jɛrusalɛm ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr la n ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di doŋ,
nɛr maa waa kaa
ra kpau girme la.
U ra hɛm, di kpa u siwee suah,
dikuu hiihzi wia.
Jɛrusalɛm faa kpa wichɔgaa wergee
doŋ u hiŋ.
9U doŋa faa waa suahwɛ,
ka u baga faa waa hoo
u laba ni.
U cholaa faa chummɔɔ werge,
nɛr maa wàá wer tig
u bampirii.
U dɔma kpegluubuu,
u wii ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi
ú suŋ u ni.
10U dɔma faa paagi u daama kuna maanii.
U na banna zuu
Kɔraawiizi Dia la himmaa.
Bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ
banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ
gilɛɛ ra zuu la.
11U nɛra ra hɛm di ra nyiŋŋi diwee bá di,
di kpa ba daama chɛr diwee
bá di, di dɔɔ miibɔɔ.
A bolzeŋ nɛra wii di ra ŋɔ,
“Yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
na gunla
yaa n na di dɔgnya.”
12U wii di ra kali nɛra la maa
n ga u be di waa kaali,
“Ií binniŋ na!
Nɛr maa bɔra wɔɔ ra waazi
kennaa alugɔ n hor.”
Bɔwaazaa la Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ
a chol n ni,
u baaŋfuuih saŋa la.
13“U faa gillɔɔ niŋ lii chiŋ ba,
di waa di n biini.
U he sidɛɛ lawiŋ, n chol hɛri,
denii u giliŋ ta,
n bɔra ra waaziŋ saŋa maa.
14U zum n wichɔgaa maanii,
di chaalaa bɔkpaŋ,
di vɔɔzaa laaliŋ,
a gil n gɛrgi.
Kɔraawiizi faa kpambuu
du n dɔma la
n kpekke kaaliŋ nonee,
n faa waa wette
ń lɛɛ n hiŋ.
15Kɔraawiizi faa ra ɛɛ n laallɔkpegaa chɛɛtɛ.
U faa gillɔɔ laallɔɔra ba
wa kpu n biipɔllaa,
di nam baa alugɔ
banna nam grepu
nɔna siŋ kuaribɔr.
16Awiarɛ n siwee taali sinii di ra pal la.
Nɛr maa wàá wer
tig n bampirii
gɛɛ di duŋ bɔkpega.
N dɔma kpeglimbuu,
n nɛra waa kaa dɔɔ kummaa.
17N yaa noneere,
ka nɛr maa wàá hiiniŋ.
Kɔraawiizi yir dɔmaa lii bɔr maa, bá wa lɔŋ.
Ba ra ɛɛŋ lugɔ kundoŋ.
18Ka Kɔraawiizi wia dɔɔ wibiire,
dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu
vɛɛ u nua.
Nɛra n du yemmaa, ií ra nuu n be,
ií binni na gunla n bɔra
n na waazi.
Ba lauri n biipɔllaa
ni n suŋguree kaali.
19N yir la nɛra la n ni baa n dɔɔ nuukpannɛ,
ka ba vɛɛ n hiinaa.
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni sitɔɔra siuzɔɔrɛ,
bolzeŋ ŋmɛnizenaa biine,
di ba ra nyiŋŋi diwee bá di,
di dɔɔ miibɔɔni.
20N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, binni dɔgnya la minna di!
N biini chɔkkɔɔ,
dikuu n wichɔgaa wia.
Nɛkpui su ŋmɛnizenaa,
haali diini biine maa,
siu du denii.
21A nuu n hɛmaa.
Nɛr maa waa hoo,
ú tig n bampirii.
N dɔma bɔra sɔɔnɔɔrɛ,
dikuu hiŋ gillɛ
hɛhchɔg chol n ni wia.
Gil hɔpizii la hiŋ ŋɔ nua u wia la ba,
di gil n dɔma di tɔɔrɔɔ
naa minna di naa.
22Gil ba di bilchɔg dikuu ba biinikpola wia.
Tɛr ba digna gunla
hiŋ tɛr n digna,
dikuu n wichɔgaa wia la.
N na hɛmuu ni biinichɔg,
n bɔra huah.”

english_text:
The Lord Was Like an Enemy
The Prophet Speaks:
1The Lord was angry!
So he disgraced Zion
though it was Israel's pride
and his own place of rest.
In his anger he threw Zion down
from heaven to earth.
2The Lord had no mercy!
He destroyed the homes
of Jacob's descendants.
In his anger he tore down
every walled city in Judah;
he toppled the nation
together with its leaders,
leaving them in shame.
3The Lord was so furiously angry
that he wiped out
the whole army of Israel
by not supporting them
when the enemy attacked.
He was like a raging fire
that swallowed up
the descendants of Jacob.
4He attacked like an enemy
with a bow and arrows,
killing our loved ones.
He has burned to the ground
the homes on Mount Zion.
5The Lord was like an enemy!
He left Israel in ruins
with its palaces
and fortresses destroyed,
and with everyone in Judah
moaning and weeping.
6He shattered his temple
like a hut in a garden;
he completely wiped out
his meeting place,
and did away with festivals
and Sabbaths
in the city of Zion.
In his fierce anger he rejected
our king and priests.
7The Lord abandoned his altar
and his temple;
he let Zion's enemies
capture her fortresses.
Noisy shouts were heard
from the temple,
as if it were a time
of celebration.
8The Lord had decided
to tear down the walls of Zion
stone by stone.
So he started destroying
and did not stop
until walls and fortresses
mourned and trembled.
9Zion's gates have fallen
facedown on the ground;
the bars that locked the gates
are smashed to pieces.
Her king and royal family
are prisoners
in foreign lands.
Her priests don't teach,
and her prophets don't have
a message from the Lord.
10Zion's leaders are silent.
They just sit on the ground,
tossing dirt on their heads
and wearing sackcloth.
Her young women can do nothing
but stare at the ground.
11My eyes are red from crying,
my stomach is in knots,
and I feel sick all over.
My people are being wiped out,
and children lie helpless
in the streets of the city.
12A child begs its mother
for food and drink,
then blacks out
like a wounded soldier
lying in the street.
The child slowly dies
in its mother's arms.
13Zion, how can I comfort you?
How great is your pain?
Lovely city of Jerusalem,
how can I heal your wounds,
gaping as wide as the sea?
14Your prophets deceived you
with false visions
and lying messages—
they should have warned you
to leave your sins
and be saved from disaster.
15Those who pass by
shake their heads and sneer
as they make fun and shout,
“What a lovely city you were,
the happiest on earth,
but look at you now!”
16Zion, your enemies curse you
and snarl like wild animals,
while shouting,
“This is the day
we've waited for!
At last, we've got you!”
17The Lord has done everything
that he had planned
and threatened long ago.
He destroyed you without mercy
and let your enemies boast
about their powerful forces.
18Zion, deep in your heart
you cried out to the Lord.
Now let your tears overflow
your walls day and night.
Don't ever lose hope
or let your tears stop.
19Get up and pray for help
all through the night.
Pour out your feelings
to the Lord,
as you would pour water
out of a jug.
Beg him to save your people,
who are starving to death
at every street crossing.
Jerusalem Speaks:
20Think about it, Lord!
Have you ever been this cruel
to anyone before?
Is it right for mothers
to eat their children,
or for priests and prophets
to be killed in your temple?
21My people, both young and old,
lie dead in the streets.
Because you were angry,
my young men and women
were brutally slaughtered.
22When you were angry, Lord,
you invited my enemies
like guests for a party.
No one survived that day;
enemies killed my children,
my own little ones.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n tɛr Jɛrusalɛm hina digna wia
1Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih la biini,
u gillɔɔ bɔbiri
tɔ bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm ni,
di gil u daama maa bir pɛɛ.
Haali u baaŋfuuih hɔpizii hiŋ gba,
u vɛɛ u Diarɛ ta.
2Kɔraawiizi faa waa
Juda boljiga maa ni sunne,
ka chɔgaa,
di purgi diikpega la maa,
n na guu a hɛri la.
U faa gillɔɔ hiihzi kpu u kora ni u sitɔɔra.
3U baaŋfuuihchɔgii la biini,
u faa chɔgi Izrɛl hina fɔŋŋaa.
U faa vɛɛ ba hiinaare,
saŋa la ba dɔma n pig baa la.
Ka faa lɔ baa lugɔ ninzeŋ,
di chɔgi ba kummaa.
4U faa ta baabuu u hobee alugɔ u dɔma,
di kpu banla maa
n faa ra tɛɛ baa
bɔsɔna werge la.
U gillɔɔ u baaŋ fuuh ba ni
lugɔ niŋ, Jɛrusalɛm biini.
5Kɔraawiizi kpu Izrɛl hinaa lugɔ ba dɔma,
di purgi ba
diikpega ni kooridiini.
U gillɔɔ biinichɔg la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ
lau Juda hina.
6U faa purgi u Dia la baŋ ɔɔ ra jaamuu u biini labuu,
di gil hɔpizinanaananaa ni
Heezaa Hɔpizaa la tuŋ.
Koori ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina maa faa zummɔ
lugɔ u baaŋ fuuh ba ninɛɛ.
7Kɔraawiizi faa vɛɛ u mbusu lizibɔr
ni u Diinaniinanii labuu ta.
U faa gillɔɔ dɔma purgi u koŋlaa,
di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna,
bɔr la baŋ faa ra jaamuu la.
8Kɔraawiizi siwii faa aahwɔɔ
lugɔ Bolzeŋ Ziɔn koŋlii
la n baruu la chol.
U faa mɛgzaabuu, di zum a maga,
á yemmaa gilɛɛ waa ka wia.
U diijaŋra ni a koŋlii
maanii jaa purgi
kpau dɔŋa chɔɔ.
9A bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa hug hembugle biinii,
a daazi maa kuugi nyaamm.
A koori ni nabɔnzenaa maanii
ba lauri kaali hɛrduma.
Ba waa kaa ra bagli a nɛra
Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg la wia.
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi ge waa kaa ra na wia
lugɔ deeza biini,
di ra lii Kɔraawiizi be.
10Jɛrusalɛm bazɛŋzi sogo hɛrii di ɛɛ surumm,
hɛɛhraa tɔ ba nyuuni,
ba kpa gbɔglɔŋ laala laali.
Suŋgure ge giŋŋi willi ba nyuuni.
11N siwee maanii ɔrgɛɛ dikuu wiraa wia,
n biini chɔgi
di ra tɔɔriŋ werge.
N biini chɔkkɔɔ werge maa,
n bɔra huah dikuu
n nɛra kpui wia.
Bichalli ni biifulli ra huahgi
a bolzeŋ ŋmɛnizenaa biine.
12Lɔzi ni niinyɔgzi n na kpu baa wia,
ba wii ra du ba maawaa.
Di ra chogli a bolzeŋ ŋmɛnizenaa baana lugɔ baŋ na pirazi,
di ɔɔ ra siuzi ba
maawaa nonee biine bɔɔiih.
13N nɔŋŋi Jɛrusalɛm, ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔi?
Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ tig i bampiriiyei?
Nɛr maa haa waa
keŋ tɔɔrɔɔ naa diwee.
I hɛhchɔg kannɔɔ werge
alugɔ muuzeŋ n waa
maga dɔɔwɛ la,
i tamii maa tunnɔɔ.
14Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi faa waa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ
bá ŋɔ tɛi, di kara bɛŋ lɛi.
Ba baglaa faa ra dariibuu,
dikuu baŋ faa waa
i wichɔgaa wia ra ŋɔ la wia.
Ba faa gillɔɔ i ra fɛ lugɔ a waa dɛg hin niŋ
gil i biini chɔgi
i wichɔgaa wia, di gilaa ta.
15Nɛra la maa n ga a bolzeŋ kɛrii
di waa kaali,
ɔɔ ra ɛɛibuu chɛɛtɛ.
Ba ɔɔ ra viigi ba nyuunii,
di ra mam Jɛrusalɛm
chɔgaa wia, di ra ŋɔ,
“Bolzennanii labuu kennaa?
U wiarɛ durnya hina
ra jigsi laa?”
16I dɔma maa ɔɔ ra mamiibuu,
di ra fiilii ni hahzi.
Ba ɔɔ mir ba nuuzii di ra mamii, di ra ŋɔ,
“Yaa chɔguubuu!
A hɔpizii naabuu
yaa ra kpaŋ la!”
17Kɔraawiizi jaa ɛɛ wii la
uŋ ta jina lugɔ
u daŋ ɛɛ labuu.
Waa i ni sunne ka chɔgii,
gunla uŋ karfii faala maa la.
U faa gillɔɔ i dɔma kpeglii,
di tɛɛ baa bɔsɔna,
hiŋ cholle wia.
18Jɛrusalɛm, wii ra du Kɔraawiizi!
Gil i sinii ra pal alugɔ muuni,
hamuŋa ni hɔpizaa maa.
A wii ni biinichɔg, saŋa maa.
19Hamuŋa maa, ɔɔ izi digiidigii,
di wii ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.
Ɔɔ ra suŋŋuu kpegzi ni, ni i biini maa,
di ra tɛɛ i biizi, ú suŋ ba ni.
I biizi la lɔzi n na kpu baa,
ba ra siuzi
ŋmɛnizenaa biine la.
20Yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, binni yaa!
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra tɛrgi
yaa digna gunnɛi?
Haana ra hee
ba biizi la baŋ nɔŋŋɛɛrɛ!
Ba ra kpuuzi i kizeehina ni i dɔgtɛɛzii
i Dia la biini himmaa!
21Bichalli ni nabɔnzi maanii
siuzɛɛ chɔɔ
ŋmɛnizenaa baana!
Biipɔllaa ni haana
ba dɔma n kpuuzɛɛ
ni tokobizi.
I faa waa ba ni sunne,
ka kpuuzi baa werge
i baaŋfuuih hɔpizii la.
22I faa yir n dɔmaa ba wa chaali
alugɔ diuzenaa dii hɔpizii hɔl.
Ba wa bariŋ,
di kpa ɔnsii werge ta n ni.
Nɛr maa faa waa wette ú na bɔr chɔ,
i baaŋfuuih hɔpizii la.
Ba faa kpuuzi n biizi la
miŋ dɛɛzɛɛ
di nɔŋŋi baa labuu.

english_text:
There Is Still Hope
The Prophet Speaks:
1I have suffered much
because God was angry.
2He chased me into a dark place,
where no light could enter.
3I am the only one he punishes
over and over again,
without ever stopping.
4God caused my skin and flesh
to waste away,
and he crushed my bones.
5He attacked and surrounded me
with hardships and trouble;
6he forced me to sit in the dark
like someone long dead.
7God built a fence around me
that I cannot climb over,
and he chained me down.
8Even when I shouted
and prayed for help,
he refused to listen.
9God put big rocks in my way
and made me follow
a crooked path.
10God was like a bear or a lion
waiting in ambush for me;
11he dragged me from the road,
then tore me to shreds.
12God took careful aim
and shot his arrows
13straight through my heart.
14I am a joke to everyone—
no one ever stops
making fun of me.
15God has turned my life sour.
16He made me eat gravel
and rubbed me in the dirt.
17I cannot find peace
or remember happiness.
18I tell myself, “I am finished!
I can't count on the Lord
to do anything for me.”
19Just thinking of my troubles
and my lonely wandering
makes me miserable.
20That's all I ever think about,
and I am depressed.
21Then I remember something
that fills me with hope.
22The Lord's kindness never fails!
If he had not been merciful,
we would have been destroyed.
23The Lord can always be trusted
to show mercy each morning.
24Deep in my heart I say,
“The Lord is all I need;
I can depend on him!”
25The Lord is kind to everyone
who trusts and obeys him.
26It is good to wait patiently
for the Lord to save us.
27When we are young,
it is good to struggle hard
28and to sit silently alone,
if this is what
the Lord intends.
29Being rubbed in the dirt
can teach us a lesson;
30we can also learn from insults
and hard knocks.
31The Lord won't always reject us!
32He causes a lot of suffering,
but he also has pity
because of his great love.
33The Lord doesn't enjoy
sending grief or pain.
34Don't trample prisoners
under your feet
35or cheat anyone out of
what is rightfully theirs.
God Most High sees everything,
36and he knows when you refuse
to give someone a fair trial.
37No one can do anything
without the Lord's approval.
38Good and bad each happen
at the command
of God Most High.
39We're still alive!
We shouldn't complain
when we are being punished
for our sins.
40Instead, we should think
about the way we are living,
and turn back to the Lord.
41When we lift our hands
in prayer to God in heaven,
we should offer him our hearts
and say, 42“We've sinned!
We've rebelled against you,
and you haven't forgiven us!
43Anger is written all over you,
as you pursue and slaughter us
without showing pity.
44You are behind a wall of clouds
that blocks out our prayers.
45You allowed nations
to treat us like garbage;
46our enemies curse us.
47We are terrified and trapped,
caught and crushed.”
48My people are destroyed!
Tears flood my eyes,
49and they won't stop
50until the Lord looks down
from heaven and helps.
51I am horrified when I see
what enemies have done
to the young women of our city.
52No one had reason to hate me,
but I was hunted down
like a bird.
53Then they tried to kill me
by tossing me into a pit
and throwing stones at me.
54Water covered my head—
I thought I was gone.
55From the bottom of the pit,
I prayed to you, Lord.
56I begged you to listen.
“Help!” I shouted. “Save me!”
You answered my prayer
57and came when I was in need.
You told me, “Don't worry!”
58You rescued me
and saved my life.
59You saw them abuse me, Lord,
so make things right.
60You know every plot
they have made against me.
61Yes, you know their insults
and their evil plans.
62All day long they attack
with words and whispers.
63No matter what they are doing,
they keep on mocking me.
64Pay them back for everything
they have done, Lord!
65Put your curse on them
and make them suffer.
66Get angry and go after them
until not a trace is left
under the heavens.
translation_text:
Dignitɛraa, liize biraa ani tamii wia
1Minuu zum gunla
Kɔraawiizi dignitɛraa
n duwɛɛ.
2U faa duŋŋimbuu
du bɔbiri werge biini.
3Di lɔɔziŋ digiidigii,
waa n ni sunne.
4U faa gillɔɔ n zɛŋ,
n bɔrahɔŋ ziimi,
u kuugi n hoga.
5U faa gillɔɔ n du dɔgnya
ni biinichɔg biini
lugɔ baŋ tɔŋ dia.
6U faa firimbuu n du siu bɔbiri la
n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la biini.
7U vɔɔzimbuu yɔlɔzi,
n ɛɛ lugɔ baŋ tɔ nɛr dia,
maa tamii dɔɔwɛ
min niŋ na bɔr chɔ.
8N lɔ wilee di ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa,
ka Kɔraawiizi vɛɛ nuui.
9N na voluu di ra jiŋli,
koŋlaa la baŋ kpa bia ma
ra tɔŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ,
bɔr la maa miŋ bittɛ ń ga.
10U faa guumbuu lugɔ amani,
di jirgiŋ lugɔ bunyiŋ.
11U faa tuuziŋ lii ŋmɛnɛɛ,
di chuuriŋ, ka giliŋ de,
nɛr maa waŋ hiinee.
12U faa kpa u hobee
du u hoo, di taaziŋ.
13U taŋ u hobee
a zuu n bɔra la bɔɔnɛɛ.
14Nɛra ra mamiŋ a hɔl hiŋ
guŋŋ wiizi wa chol,
n birgi mɔmɔsia kuŋ ba be.
15Tɔɔrɔɔkpola bɛnnɛ u tɛŋ,
a ɛɛ lugɔ n diwee ni nii.
16U faa lawimbuu
di kpa n siwee tuuri hɛri,
di kuugi n nyina
nyaŋŋaa biini.
17N suuh gunla alaanfia
bampirsɔna ani bɔsɔna
n duwɛɛnɛ.
18N saŋa waa kaa du kaŋ,
n tamii Kɔraawiizi ni tunnɔɔ.
19Di n wa fɛ n bɔra waazaa
ni n bol nyaai wia,
a ɔɔ ɛɛu lugɔ siri n kpolle.
20N na liizi gunnɛ saŋa maa,
n biini chɔgi werge.
21Ama, aŋ biruu dɔɔ tamii,
di n wa liizi wii naa.
22Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋaa
ni u nɛsunaa dɔɔi la
waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.
23A ɛɛ a falaarɛ alugɔ chɔɔzi,
di ɛɛ lugɔ wiizi furaa
n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la.
24Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ n dɔɔ,
awia, u ninɛɛ n tamii du.
25Kɔraawiizi wia wessoo
nɛr la maa n yarduu be.
26Awia, a wessoo werge maa,
yaa n dɔɔ kanyitti
di ra kpaŋuu, ú lɛɛ yaa.
27Saŋa la n dɛkkɛ yá helli kanyitti diire,
yaa pɔlaa saŋa.
28Di yaa waa di tɔɔrɔɔ,
a dɛkkɔɔ ya so yaa bɛnaa
kirkir ni kanyitti.
29A dɛkkɔɔ ya willi yaa nyuuni,
aŋhinabe, tamii
daŋ haa du de.
30Haali baŋ lɔɔzi yaa di chagzi yaa gba,
ka a dɛkkɔɔ ya sɛɛ a maa.
31Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ nɛsunaare,
wàá vɛɛ yaa ta di hanna la.
32Aŋhinabe, u daŋ gil yaa biine chɔgi,
ka gunla un nɔŋŋi yaa la
ɛɛ wibiire, di du kpeg.
33U kipar lɛi ú gil
ya dɔɔ biinichɔg gɛɛ
bɔra waazaa.
34Wàá sɛɛ sunni
banla maa baŋ tɔ dia.
35U zum saŋa la baŋ ɔɔ kpolli yaa
wia la n dɛg yaa,
ú tɛɛ yaa labuu.
36Di ba wa bir wibii dii seriya diiribɔr,
Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ zumuu.
37Kɔraawiizi kipar bɛnnɛ
ɔɔ wer ɛɛ saŋa maa.
38U wiŋɔzi ɔɔ weruu gil
winanaa ni achɔgaa maa ɛɛ.
39Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yaa ɔɔ ra nuumi,
di ba wa tɛr yaa digna
dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wiai?
40Ií gil ya pessi yaa wiɛɛlaa nɛnnɛ,
ka bir ba Kɔraawiizi be.
41Ií gil ya huuhzi yaa biine
tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la
n du u bol,
ka suŋŋuu, di ŋɔ,
42“Yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
yaa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ
di vɛɛ i nua,
haa gillɛ tɛɛ yaa.
43I dau yaa lugee di kpuuzi yaa.
I baaŋfuuih la faa gillɔɔ
i nɛsunaa la suah.
44Yaa wiisuŋŋaa faa waa wette a helii,
dikuu i baaŋfuuih la n ɛɛwɛ
lugɔ baama n tɔkkɛ,
di tɔ ŋmɛnɛɛ wia.
45I gillɔɔ yaa birgi durnya hul,
hɛssi hina be.
46Yaa dɔma maa ra chagzi yaa,
di ra ɛɛ yaa chɛɛtɛ.
47Hɛhchɔg ni chɔgaa chol yaa ninɛɛ,
yaa du siaahmu ni ɔnsii biini.
48N sinii ra paluu alugɔ muuni,
dikuu n nɛra kpui wia.
49N sinii danna pal
lugɔ gɔŋ nii n waa
teŋaa dɔɔwɛ,
50di ra ba saŋa la
Kɔraawiizi n du u bol
ka na yaa.
51Biinichɔg lawimbuu werge maa,
dikuu wia la miŋ nawɛɛ
baŋ kpawɛɛ dau
a bolzeŋ haana la wia.
52N dɔma la n hahŋ pɛɛpɛɛ la
hembuu sidɛɛ,
di lawiŋ lugɔ zumbee.
53Ba ra nyiŋŋi n kpui,
di kpaŋ ha bɔɔ biini,
di paa bia ra lɔɔziŋ.
54Nii faari di ra nyiŋŋi u tɔ n ni,
n fɛ lugɔ siu duglɔɔrɛ.
55N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
a bɔɔ biinii n du
ka faa wii tɛi.
56Miŋ wa suŋŋii lugɔ
í nuu n wiraa, i nuuwɔɔ.
57I sɛɛ, di ŋɔ ń gilɛɛ ra ɔm.
58N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
i ba wa hiiniŋ, di lɛɛŋ ta.
59Di seriya, di tɛŋ bilii,
i zum wichɔgaa la maa
baŋ ɛɛmbuu.
60I zum gunla n dɔma n hahmbuu,
di ra ta n jinachɔgaa.
61N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi,
i nuuwɔɔ banna chagziŋ,
di zum ba jinachɔgaa la maa
banna ta n wiarɛ.
62Hɔpizii maa, ba ɔɔ ra zɔɔzimbuu,
di ra ta ba jinazi guŋŋ
wiizi wa chol.
63Di lii chɔɔzi di ra la hamuŋa,
ba ɔɔ ra mamimbuu,
di ra ɛɛŋ chɛɛtɛ.
64N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, tɛr ba digna,
dikuu wia la baŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia.
65See baa nua,
di gil ba tamii tuŋ.
66Dau ba luge, di dim baa,
hɛri naa biini nyaamm!”

english_text:
The Punishment of Jerusalem
The Prophet Speaks:
1The purest gold is ruined
and has lost its shine;
jewels from the temple
lie scattered in the streets.
2These are Zion's people,
worth more than purest gold;
yet they are counted worthless
like dishes of clay.
3Even jackals nurse their young,
but my people are like ostriches
that abandon their own.
4Babies are so thirsty
that their tongues are stuck
to the roof of the mouth.
Children go begging for food,
but no one gives them any.
5All who ate expensive foods
lie starving in the streets;
those who grew up in luxury
now sit on trash heaps.
6 My nation was punished worse
than the people of Sodom,
whose city was destroyed
in a flash without the help
of human hands.
7The leaders of Jerusalem
were purer than snow
and whiter than milk;
their bodies were healthy
and glowed like jewels.
8Now they are blacker than tar,
and no one recognizes them;
their skin clings to their bones
and is drier than firewood.
9Being killed with a sword
is better than slowly
starving to death.
10 Life in the city is so bad
that loving mothers have boiled
and eaten their own children.
11The Lord was so fiercely angry
that he burned the city of Zion
to the ground.
12Not a king on this earth
or the people of any nation
believed enemies could break
through her gates.
13Jerusalem was punished because
her prophets and her priests
had sinned and caused the death
of innocent victims.
14Yes, her prophets and priests
were covered with blood;
no one would come near them,
as they wandered
from street to street.
15Instead, everyone shouted,
“Go away! Don't touch us!
You're filthy and unfit
to belong to God's people!”
So they had to leave
and become refugees.
But foreign nations told them,
“You can't stay here!”
16The Lord is the one
who sent them scattering,
and he has forgotten them.
No respect or kindness
will be shown
to the priests or leaders.
