Ba maa faa li Babilɔn hina nabɔnzenaa la n ɔɔ faa zuu torkozi zagra n na tɛrguu. 16Uŋ wa na ba footozi la, u ra nyiŋŋi ba wia, di hum nɛra ba ga yir baa. 17Denii a Babilɔn hina ba wa lawuu ra nyiŋŋi, di chɔguu. Ka ba wia bir wa bazuu, u kaa vɛɛ baa. 18Nɛr maa n faa zum Ɔhɔliba sɛnsɛŋ wia la, n faa vɛɛu gunla miŋ vɛɛ u kpɛɛma Ɔhɔla la. 19U sɛnsɛŋ la faa nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ alugɔ saŋa la uŋ faa ɛɛ toloori, di ra sɛm Ijip hɛri la. 20U faa ra sɛm sɛnsɛnchɔgaa hina la hɛna n kannɛzi alugɔ kauzi gɛɛ zagra hɛnaa. 21Ɔhɔliba, i faa ra nyiŋŋuu i kaa ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ wia la hiŋ faa ɛɛwɛ i toloo saŋa la hiŋ du Ijip hɛri, ba faa ra jagzi i ila werge, di mui laa?
22Awia, Ɔhɔliba, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ i be, ‘N daŋ gil banla n na sɛmii la bir haih. Ba wia baziibuu, awia, n daŋ gil ba bir wa barii ni baaŋfuuih. 23Babilɔn, Pɛkɔd, Soowa, Koowa ani Asiiria hina maa, bunɔɔna la n ɛɛ ba laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ni ba hɛri nabɔnzenaa, torkozi nabɔnzi ani nabɔnzi la maa n tinni ba zagra ba. 24Ba laallɔɔrakpila ge daŋ vɔɔ laal lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag zuu laal torkozi ni ba bunni torkozi ba wa lɔi. Ba daŋ kpa ba laal kuna laali wa barii. Denii ń jaa kpai tɛɛ baa, bá kpa ba gbɔgni dii seriya. 25N baaŋ daŋ fuuh i ni, ń gil ba kpa baaŋfuuih ge tɔɔrii. Ba daŋ mɔnni i digna ni i miizi ta, ka kpu i biizi. Wibii maa, ba daŋ lauri i biibaala ni i biihaana kaali, ka fuuh banla maa n niŋ ka. 26Ba daŋ dilgii, ka paa i saliŋ bɔmbɔga la maa kaali. 27N daŋ gil i sɛnsɛŋ wia nɔŋŋaa la hiŋ faarɛɛ Ijip hɛri la tuŋ. Gunnɛ n ɛɛi, i ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka liizi Ijip hɛri vuga gɛɛ Ijip wia.’ ”
28Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “N daŋ kpai du banla hiŋ hahwɛɛ, ba wia bazii la nonee biini. 29Ba daŋ tɔɔrii dikuu baŋ haih wia, di kaa paa i kundɔɔlaa maa, ka dilgii í ɛɛ chakpal. I daŋ di hiihzi durnya hina maa see. I sɛnsɛŋ wia labuu 30niŋ gil guŋ huuzii, dikuubɛɛwiai, i sɛm hɛssi maa hinaa, di kuari ba vuga di doŋ i hiŋ. 31Hiŋ lɛɛ i kpɛɛma manni la wia, n daŋ tɛr i ge gba digni gunla miŋ faa tɛr i kpɛɛma digni la.”
32Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“A guŋ dignitɛraa himmaanii niŋ huuzi i ge gba.
A dignitɛraa kannɔɔ
werge maa
I daŋ nyaa girme durnya hina maa be,
bá ra ɛɛi chɛɛtɛ di ra mamii.
33I biini daŋ chɔgi,
i ra dɛɛzi,
di di tɔɔrɔɔ,
di birgi diŋgela
alugɔ i kpɛɛma Samaria.
34I daŋ nyɔɔ a tɔɔrɔɔ nii maa kpɛlɛŋŋ,
ka kɔrgi i bɔra.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”
35Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “Ɔhɔliba, hiŋ vɛɛŋ di bir har kpuŋ la wia, i daŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ dikuu i sɛnsɛŋ la wia.”
36Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, i ɛɛ siryaa í di Ɔhɔla ni Ɔhɔliba seriyaa? Gil ba zum ba wiɛɛlaa la miŋ kiiwe la wia, 37dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ wiarɛ werge, di kaa kpuuzi nɛra ge jaa. Ba sɛnsɛŋ wia aŋhinaa vuga la banna kuari ni ba biizi la baŋ lullɛ tɛŋ, ka kpuuzi baa fuuh lizi mbusuzi tɛɛ ba vuga la. 38Guŋ bɛŋ lɛi gba, ka ba ɛɛ a wichɔgaa naa dizii, di chɔgi n Dia ni n Heezaa Hɔpizii la gba kiizi. 39Nau! A hɔl la baŋ kpuuzi ba biizi, di lizi mbusuzi tɛɛ ba vuga la, a hɔl maanii ba wa zuu n Dia la doŋuu.
40Hìŋ́ Ɔhɔliba ni i kpɛɛma Ɔhɔla maa ɔɔ hum nɛraa, ba la hɛrdumazi ga nyiŋŋi baala wa tɛɛ ia. Di ba wa ballɔ ge, ii ɔɔ sɔɔgi niiri du kaluzi, di kaa du saliŋ baŋaa kuna ni dignikuna. 41Di ii wa ɛɛ guŋ, ii ni baa ɔɔ jaa so kardɛllinanaa ni, ka jaa kpa n daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ni nuunanaa la miŋ tɛɛ ia la, di hɔŋzi ii tɛɛbulzi ni.
42Sinnyɔɔra kɔɔi tɔ bɔr maa. Baala la n lii hɛribɔduma ba la, kpa saliŋ gbittizi du haana vaama, di kpa ewiche kahuronanaa hi baa. 43Denii n ŋɔ tɛɛ n hiŋ, ‘Ba ra nyiŋŋuu, bá ni hahsɛnsɛnna naa n chɔgmɛɛ naa nyiŋŋi dɔŋa!’ 44Ba jaa ɛɛ guŋ, di lauri Ɔhɔla ni Ɔhɔliba n ɛɛ hahsɛnsɛnna, di nyaa hiihzi la ra nyiŋŋi. 45Ama, nɛnanaa daŋ gil ba di hahsɛnsɛnna ni nɛkpuura tɔɔrɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ɛɛ hahsɛnsɛnna ni nɛkpuuraa.”
46Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “Gil nɛkpila wa fɔɔ baa, ɔnsii lau baa, ka bá paa ba kuna ge kaali. 47A nɛkpila daŋ lɔɔzi baa ni bia, di kpa tokobizi kpu baa. Ba daŋ kpu ba biibaala ni ba biihaana, ka fuuh ba diini.
48Gunnɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ, sɛnsɛŋ wia ni a dizi maa jaa tuŋ a hɛri. Guŋ daŋ karfi haana la maa n kawɛɛ, bá gilɛɛ kaa wàá chanzi ba wiɛɛlaa la. 49N daŋ turgi baa bá sɛnsɛŋ ni ba vuga kuaraa la maa kim. A maa tɔɔrɔɔrɛ bá di! Denii bá jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa.”

english_text:
A Cooking Pot
1Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem. 3Then tell my rebellious people:
“Pour water in a cooking pot
and set it over a fire.
* 4Throw in the legs and shoulders
of your finest sheep
and put in the juicy bones.
5Pile wood underneath the pot,
and let the meat and bones
boil until they are done.”
6These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it. 7The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground. 8But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
9I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood, 10so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch. 11Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust. 12I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
13Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it. 14That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Ezekiel's Wife Dies
15The Lord said, 16“Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry. 17Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
18One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me, 19and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
20I answered:
The Lord God says 21he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed. 22Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat. 23You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
24I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
25The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well. 26On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened. 27Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Viinyɛɛsii wia
1Binni kabɛlhiŋ, baagu fihiŋ hɔpizaa fi hɔllɛ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, sɛbi zinaa hɔpizii naa dau, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɔpizii naabuu Babilɔn koori ra ba ú wa fɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina ni laal. 3Ta sɛɛlii naa tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm dignikpega hina la, bá nuu. Ŋɔ dí kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ,
‘Kpa vii la hɔŋ niŋ
di ɛɛ nii du u biini.
4Kpa a ol bɔnanaa la du u biini,
u pɔrɔzi, u vaampɛrɛzi
ani u hoga bɔnanaa la, ú su.
5Lau penanii kpu di ɛɛ guŋ.
Hɔŋ a ol ni u hoga maa,
di du daazi a vii zɛɛ,
á ra bɔr.’
6Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ,
‘Tɔɔrɔɔ daŋ huuzi nɛkpuura bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm biini.
U ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ vii n nyɛɛsɛɛ,
ba wàá wer looruu,
ú doŋa lii.
Awia, a laari ola la kpaŋkpaŋa guŋŋ a wa tuŋ.
7Ba kpuuzi nɛraa a bolzeŋ biini,
ba challi chɔɔgi bia nyuuni nɛra ra na,
a waa hɛri chɔɔwɛ
hɛɛhraa tɔ a ni.
8Awia, n gillɔɔ a challi chɔɔ de,
bɔr la aŋ wàá wer suah,
nɛra naa, bá baana fuuh,
ba wa turgi baa
bá wichɔgaa kim.’ ”
9Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ,
“Tɔɔrɔɔ daŋ huuzi nɛkpuura bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm!
N himmaanii niŋ dau a daazi, á du kaŋ.
10Awia, du daazi werge,
a ra lau werge.
Daali a ol ú bii nɛnnɛ,
di du yazi ni kuna,
á du sum,
di gil á hoga fuuh,
11ka jaa kpa a vii
hɔŋ a niŋhɔla ni guŋŋ
ú wa aah,
ú nyɛɛsaa la ge fuuh tuŋ,
ka u bir du wer,
12di i ɛɛ guŋ gba, ka u nyɛɛsaa
la wàá tuŋ.
Haali hiŋ kpa
niŋ fuuuh la maa.
13Jɛrusalɛm hina, ii sɛnsɛŋ wiɛɛlaa doŋ iabuu. Miŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ ń lizi ia ii wichɔgaa biini, ka ii haa du a biini la wia, a wichɔgaa wàá lii ii ni di ra la saŋa la n baaŋ n niŋ wa fuuh ii ni tuŋ. 14Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Saŋa la miŋ baglɛɛ ń tɔɔri ia la helloo, màá ka suŋ ii ni gɛɛ di kaa bir n nfɛrɛ ge gba. N daŋ di ia seriya dikuu ii biinikpola wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”
Ɛzɛkiɛl haaŋ siu wia
15Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, 16“Newee biibaal, n daŋ lɔ i nɛnɔŋŋii kakpaŋ, ú siu. Ama, gilɛɛ waa gil i biini ra chɔgi, í ra him gɛɛ di waa wii gba. 17Di i wàá sigzi gba, a ɛɛ guŋ bɔɔiih. Gilɛɛ waa wii a lee. Gilɛɛ waa pilli i kahuro gɛɛ di waa lizi i gawa gba. Gilɛɛ waa kpa kuŋ di ra tɔ i nua gɛɛ di waa ɛɛ lal wia maa gɛɛ di waa di lee diwee.”
18Denii n faa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ a nɛra chɔɔzi ni, ka bɔr n wa duanɛɛ, n haaŋ siu. Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ ge, n faa ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n bagliŋ la.
19Denii a nɛra pɛɛziŋ, “A wia naa maa hinna ɛɛ naa zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ?”
20Awia, n ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n benii, 21dí n bagli guŋ tɛɛ ia. Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, n daŋ chɔgi n Dia la n ɛɛ ii fɔŋŋa bɔr, ii ra jigsi u wia, di ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi u binnaa ni u biini zuui la. Ba daŋ kpu ii biibaala ni ii biihaana la iiŋ gillɛ Jɛrusalɛm la, laal biini. 22Denii ii jaa ɛɛ gunla mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl n ɛɛwɛ la. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa kuna di ra tɔɔgi ii siwee gɛɛ di waa ɛɛ lal wia maa gɛɛ di waa di lee diwee gba. 23Ií gilɛɛ waa pilli ii kahurozi, di gilɛɛ waa lizi ii gawa gba. Ií gilɛɛ waa wii gɛɛ di waa him gba. Ii daŋ kɔgi dikuu ii wichɔgaa la wia, ii ra sigzi di ra du dɔŋa. 24N ɛɛ gunnɛ bagli ia, ii ge ra hiŋ di ɛɛ gunla maa miŋ ɛɛwɛ la. Di a saŋa wa hello, ii daŋ zum lugɔ waabuu Kɔraawiizii La N Kaali Kummaa.”
25Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Newee biibaal, n daŋ chɔgi n Dia la, n ɛɛ ba fɔŋŋa kuŋ, ba ra jigsi u wia di ra nyiŋŋi u binnaa ni u biini laŋaa la, di lauri ba biibaala ani ba biihaana maa kaali. 26A hɔl hiŋ maanii nɛr chɔ lii a laal biini di wa bagli gunla maa n ɛɛwɛ tɛi. 27Di u wa ballɔ, i nua daŋ kaa bir pilli, í wer ŋɔ wia tɛu. Hinuu a nɛra kpa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

english_text:
Judgment on Ammon
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon 3and tell them:
You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners. 4Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk. 5Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
6You hated Israel so much that you clapped and shouted and celebrated. 7And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
Judgment on Moab
8 The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation. 9So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim. 10The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever, 11Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.”
Judgment on Edom
12 The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah. 13So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan. 14I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.”
Judgment on Philistia
15 The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them. 16Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast. 17In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Ammɔn hina wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, tɛɛ Ammɔn hina chɔgri, di ŋɔ wia la maa n niŋ wa huuzi baa du ba ni. 3Ŋɔ bá keŋŋi digna nuu gunla mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la n na ŋɔ, ‘Ii bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ baŋ chɔg n Dia, di kaa chɔgi Izrɛl hɛri ka lauri Juda hina kaali hɛrduma la. 4Awia, n daŋ gil nɛra lii wiifurii wa lɛɛ ii hɛri dɔɔ. Ba daŋ wa so ii be, di baŋzi tanti diini ii hɛssi. Ba daŋ tɔrgi ii daazi nɔna maa, haali di nyɔɔ ii sela ila niiri gba. 5N daŋ gil ii bolzeŋ Raba la birgi nyugmazi diiribɔr, ka Ammɔn hina hɛri la ge maa birgi peeza chɔɔribɔra. Denii ii zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi. 6Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, dí ii bɔra sɔɔnɔɔrɛ, ii ra lɔ kpaa, di zaahzi ra chiiri, dikuu iinna gbɛlli n nɛra Izrɛl hina la wia, 7n daŋ gil ii di tɔɔrɔɔ. N daŋ kpa ia du ii dɔma nonee, bá kpu ia di paagi ii kuna maa nyaamm. Ii wàá ka dɔɔ dee, ii wàá ka dɔɔ ii himmaa hɛri. Denii ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”
Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Moab hina wia
8Denii Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la kaa ŋɔ, “Dikuu Moab ni Sɛɛ hina n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ Juda hina ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ a hɛssi la maa hina la wia, 9n daŋ gil ba wa fɔɔ Moab hina bolzenaa, di faari Bɛf Jɛsimɔf, Baal Miɔn ani Kiriatam hina la maa n du ba hɛri di ra guu ba hɛri magazi la. 10N daŋ kpa Moab ni Ammɔn hɛssi hina tɛɛ wiifurii hɛribɔduma hina. Nɛr maa wàá ka kur Ammɔn hina jaa hɛssi ni. 11N daŋ tɔɔri Moab hina, denii bá zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi.”
Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Ɛdɔm hina wia
12Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ɛdɔm hina kpa wichɔgaarɛ turgi Juda hina kim, guŋ gil ba dɔɔ bilchɔg werge maa.” 13Awia, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ tɔɔri Ɛdɔm hina, di kpuuzi ba nɛra ni ba sela maa nyaamm, ka gil ba hɛri chɔɔ pɛɛ. N daŋ kpuuzi baa lii Tɛman guŋŋ di ga chug Dɛdan. 14N daŋ kpa guŋ fɔŋŋa du n nɛra Izrɛl hina nonee, bá ɛɛ guŋ. Izrɛl hina ge daŋ bir kpa n baaŋfuuih, turgi Ɛdɔm hina bá wichɔgaa kim. Denii bá zum lugɔ n benii guŋ lii. Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”
Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Filisti hina wia
15Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “Filisti hina ɛɛ wiarɛ, gunna bagli lugɔ ba turgi Juda hinaa ba wichɔgaa kim, di kpu baa dikuu baŋ hah baa saŋa maa la wia. 16Awia, n daŋ tɛrgi Filisti hina la digna, di dim baa. N daŋ kpu Kɛrɛf hina la maa nyaamm, haali banla maa gba n soge muuzeŋ nua la gba. 17N daŋ kpa n baaŋfuuihchɔgii la tɛr ba digna, di turgi gunla baŋ ɛɛwɛ la kim. Di guŋ wa huuzi baa, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

english_text:
Judgment on the City of Tyre
1 Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing,
“Jerusalem has fallen!
It used to be powerful,
a center of trade.
Now the city is shattered,
and we will take its place.”
3Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore. 4They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock, 5where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed 6and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
7King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops. 8First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you. 9He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers. 10He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city. 11His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground. 12The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea. 13 You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps, 14because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
15The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death. 16 The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear 17and sing this funeral song:
“The great city beside the sea
is destroyed!
Its people once ruled the coast
and terrified everyone there.
18But now Tyre is in ruins,
and the people on the coast
stare at it in horror
and tremble in fear.”
19I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you 20and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people. 21 You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Taaya hina wia
1Binni fidikpaŋhiŋ, lugli baagu lugli hɔpizii, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, Taaya hina bɔra sɔɔnɔɔrɛ werge maa, dikuu Jɛrusalɛm n cholle la wia. Ba ra mam ka ra chaasi, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Unla n dɔɔ kɔkɔɔzi ŋmɛnizi fɔŋŋa la cholloo. Jɛrusalɛm n cholle naa wia, yaa daŋ birgi daama hina!’ 3Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘Taaya hina, ii birgi n dɔmaa. N daŋ gil hɛrkpila maa hina hah ia, di ra nyiŋŋi ba chɔgi ia, gunla muuzeŋ nii n ɔɔ ra lɔ ú kɛraa la. 4Ba daŋ wa purgi bolzeŋ Taaya koŋlaa ni ba diijaŋra la n la chiŋ la maa nyaamm, di gbaari u maa maa, ka gil ú ɛɛ lugɔ bital. 5De daŋ birgi bɔr la nyinlaura n ninna nyiŋ ba asauzi muuzeŋ baaŋ. Dikuubɛɛwiai, Taaya daŋ ɛɛ bol la hɛrkpila maa hina n ninna nyiŋŋi bá paagi ba kuna. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La n Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ. 6Laal genii niŋ chɔgi u bola la maa n du a muuzeŋ baŋgia. Denii ba jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”
7Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “N daŋ gil Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza la n ɛɛ Koora Maa Koori la, ni u laallɔɔra, u zagra ni a torkozi ani laallɔɔra la n niŋ tinni zagra maa lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag wa fɔɔ Taaya hina ni laal. 8U daŋ gil ba chɔgi di kpu nɛra la n du Taaya bola la n du a muu baŋgia la. Ii dɔma daŋ ki bɔɔni, di ta pizenaa pɛgli ii koŋlaa, ka kpa ba laal pɛrɛtuzenaa gber ia alugɔ koŋlii. 9U daŋ gil ba kpa dolzenaa ni dɔŋkuna purgi ii koŋlaa ni ii diijaŋra la n la chiŋ la maa. 10U zagkpila daŋ lɔ nyɔɔ tɔ a bolzeŋ maa. A laal zagra torkozi ni a torkozenaa danna kɔɔ, a bolzeŋ la n purgee la koŋlaa ra zigli, di a wa ga u dominuuzenaa ra zuu. 11U laallɔɔra ni ba zagra daŋ su bol biini ni u ŋmɛnizi maa. Ba daŋ kpa tokobizi kpu ii nɛra. Ka jaa purgi a bolzeŋ silminti ligzenaa la maa.
12Ba daŋ paagi ii daama kuna la maa iiŋ dɔɔwɛ la, di chɔgi ii diinanaa la maa, di purgi a koŋlaa. Ba daŋ paagi a daazi ni bia, haali a hembugle maa di ga ta muuzeŋ biini. 13N daŋ gil ii yira la iinna tɔgzi la maa tuŋ. Nɛr maa wàá ka nuu ii nɛra n na lɔ kemzi. 14N daŋ gil a bolzeŋ ɛɛ lugɔ bital, di ɛɛ bɔr la nyinlaura n ninna nyiŋ ba asauzi. Ii wàá ka wer mau maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”
15Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ Taaya hina be, “Ɔnsii daŋ lau ii banla n soge muuzeŋ nua, ii bɔra ra sa, dikuu banla banna kpu ba ra lɔɔgi wilezi wia. 16A muuzeŋ kɛraa bola koora daŋ tuu ba koorikassi ni, di wir ba koori bɔmbɔgnanaa la baŋ tɔɔhzɛɛ nɛnnɛ dau. Ɔnsii daŋ lau baa werge, bá so hɛri ba bɔra ra sa werge maa, dikuu wia la n na ɛɛ i be la wia. 17Ba danna yir lee yira di ra tɛɛ ia, di ra ŋɔ,
‘Ba chɔg bolzeŋ la n faa dɔɔ sɔŋ labuu,
di paagi ba muugbessi la
lii ba be.
A nɛra naa himmaanii,
faa dɔɔ muuzeŋ huma fɔŋŋa.
Ii faa gillɔɔ ɔnsii werge
lau nɛra la maa
n faa soge de la.
18Filaŋkeŋ, muuzeŋ kɛraa hina maa bɔra a sau,
dikuu hìŋ́ Taaya
n cholle la wia.
Ɔnsii werge lau a muuzeŋ baaŋ hɛssi hina,
ba bɔra huah, dikuu
hiŋ cholle wia.’ ”
19Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ gil Taaya birgi diŋgela. Nɛr gɛɛ kummaa gba wàá ka du de. Muuzeŋ vile wa tɔ a bolzeŋ maa ni. 20N daŋ gil i tuu lalaa bol ga jaa faala hina ni. N daŋ gil i tuu hɛri ga zuu chɔgaa la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la biini, í ni lalaa ra zuu. Guŋ gil nɛr maa ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka du i biini durnya naa biini. 21N daŋ gil ii Taaya hina laba chum, ií dim. Ba danna nyiŋŋi ia, ka ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka wer na ia. Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Tyre
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre, 3the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me:
Tyre, you brag about
your perfect beauty,
4and your control of the sea.
You are a ship
built to perfection.
5Builders used cypress trees
from Mount Hermon
to make your planks
and a cedar tree from Lebanon
for your tall mast.
6Oak trees from Bashan
were shaped into oars;
pine trees from Cyprus
were cut for your deck,
which was then decorated
with strips of ivory.
7The builders used fancy linen
from Egypt for your sails,
so everyone could see you.
Blue and purple cloth
from Cyprus was used
to shade your deck.
8Men from Sidon and Arvad
did the rowing,
and your own skilled workers
were the captains.
9Experienced men from Byblos
repaired any damages.
Sailors from all over
shopped at the stores
in your port.
10Brave soldiers from Persia,
Lydia, and Libya
served in your navy,
protecting you with shields
and helmets,
and making you famous.
11Your guards came from
Arvad and Cilicia,
and men from Gamad
stood watch in your towers.
With their weapons
hung on your walls,
your beauty was complete.
12Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products. 13The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze, 14and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules. 15You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods. 16Edom traded emeralds, purple cloth, embroidery, fine linen, coral, and rubies. 17Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise. 18The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar. 19Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices. 20The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets, 21while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats. 22Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products. 23You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad, 24and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope. 25 Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go.
You were like a ship
loaded with heavy cargo
26and sailing across the sea,
but you were wrecked
by strong eastern winds.
27Everything on board was lost—
your valuable cargo,
your sailors and carpenters,
merchants and soldiers.
28The shouts of your drowning crew
were heard on the shore.
29Every ship is deserted;
rowers and sailors and captains
all stand on shore,
30mourning for you.
They show their sorrow
by putting dust on their heads
and rolling in ashes;
31they shave their heads
and dress in sackcloth
as they cry in despair.
32In their grief they sing
a funeral song for you:
“Tyre, you were greater
than all other cities.
But now you lie in silence
at the bottom of the sea.
33“Nations that received
your merchandise
were always pleased;
kings everywhere got rich
from your costly goods.
34But now you are wrecked
in the deep sea,
with your cargo and crew
scattered everywhere.
35People living along the coast
are shocked at the news.
Their rulers are horrified,
and terror is written
across their faces.
36The merchants of the world
can't believe what happened.
Your death was gruesome,
and you are gone forever.”
translation_text:
Lee yir dikuu bolzeŋ Taaya wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, 2“Newee biibaal, yir lee yir naa tɛɛ bolzeŋ Taaya la 3n soge muuzeŋ nua, u ni nɛra la n soge muuzenaa nuuzi durnya maa biini, di ra di kɔɔzi la, dí Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ,
Bolzeŋ Taaya
ŋɔ lugɔ u wessoo werge.
4U sogo muuzeŋ baannɛ,
u maara kuaruubuu u du wer
alugɔ muuzeŋgbernanii.
5Ba kpa daananaarɛ lii
Bizeŋ Hɛmɔn nyuu kuaruu.
Daazi la banna yir hɛriŋkpol lii Lɛbanɔn labuu
ba kpa kuari daajaŋ la
baŋ kpawɛɛ baŋ u baambaaŋ la.
6Haali ba faa kpa Basan hɛri daakpega
sɛɛh daajaŋra la
baŋ ɔɔ kpa ra saa
a muugbera la.
Saiprɔs hɛri daananaarɛ ba kpa pɛ a muugbera biini,
ka jaa kpa bala nyina
kuari de.
7Ijip hɛri pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaarɛ
ba faa kpa kuari
u muugbera wɛjɛ,
peu ra taau,
ú wer ra vol,
u kaa ɛɛ tuuta.
Saiprɔs hɛri pɛɛnnanaa la n ɛɛ burgu ni zagbiiŋ niirɛ,
ba kpa kuari wɛjɛzi,
tɔi chunchugli.
8I muugbersaara la faa lii Saidɔn ni Aavad hɛrzenaare.
Banla ge n faa zum muugbera
huma lii hìŋ́ Taaya biinii,
di faa ɛɛ i muugbersaara.
9Nabɔnzi la n dɔɔ nunzuma
lii Gɛbal, di faa ra kuari
i muugbessi gba.
Nɛra ɔɔ lii hɛrkpilaa zuu muugbessi ba,
i ni baa ra yuu di ra yau kuna.
10Baala faa lii Pɛsia, Lidia ani Libia
hɛssii wa birgi i laallɔɔra.
Ba kpa ba laal pɛrɛtuzenaa ni ba kahurozii
sagzi i koŋlaa ni,
guŋ gil i dɔɔ girme.
11Baala la ge n lii Aavad ni Hɛlɛk hɛssi
ɔɔ tinni a koŋlaa nyuuni
di ra du tau.
Gamad hɛri baala
faa ra binni i diijaŋra la
n la chiŋ la ni.
Ba kpa ba laal pɛrɛtuzenaa sagzi i koŋlaa ni,
gunna bagli i wessi
ni i girme.
12I ni Taasis hina faa ba kpa saliŋhuŋŋa, lugbia, kpana ani a dizi maa, di waa chɛr i daama kuna.
13Kɔkɔɔza ɔɔ faa lii Giris, Tubal ani Mɛsɛk hɛssii, di kpa yoma ni danyɛ, di waa chɛr i kuna.
14Baŋhina ge lii Bɛf Togama, di lauri zagra la n na hum huma, laal zagra ani kauzi di waa chɛr i kuna.
15I ni Roods hɛri hina gba faa ra yuu kuna di tɛɛ dɔŋa. Nɛra ge lii muu kɛraa hɛssi di kpa bala nyina ni pomegranet daazi, di waa chɛr i kunyoolaa.
16Denii Siiria hina gba kɔkɔɔza ɔɔ faa wàá yau kuŋkpila i be. A ba faa kpa binanaa aŋhina banna yir ɛmɛrald, koral, rubizi, pɛɛŋaahma lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaa, pɛɛna baŋ tɔɔhzɛɛ nɛnnɛ ani gonni, di waa chɛr i kuna.
17Juda ni Izrɛl hɛssi hina maanii i ni baa faa ra yau di ra yoo kuna dɔŋa be. A ba kpa mia, huuhnuu, ɔlivi nuu ani nuusɔɔhrinanii bɛl banna fɔgli, di wàá chɛr i kunyoolaa.
18Damaskus hina gba nii faa ra yau di ra yoo kuna, dikuu i daama kuna werge la wia. A ba faa kpa siŋ lii bol bɛl banna yir Hɛlbɔn ni peeza huna ge lii Zahaa ba.
19Dan dee ni Giris hina n lii Uzal, ɔɔ faa kpa lugbia la baŋ gurgee ni tulaale aŋhina banna yir kasia ni kalamusii di waa chɛr i kunyoolaa.
20Dɛdan hina gba ɔɔ faa kpa ba kitazi la baŋ kpawɛɛ ra bɔg zagraa di waa chɛr i kuna.
21Lɔrbizi ni Kɛda sitɔɔra ge ɔɔ lauri pebizi, pebala ani buunaa di waa yoo i be.
22Siiba ni Raama hɛssi kɔkɔɔza ge gba ɔɔ kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ni a irizi, binanaa ani salinnɛ di waa chɛr i kunyoolaa.
23Bolzenaa Haran, Kanɛ ani Ɛdɛn, di kpa Siiba kɔkɔɔza ni bolzenaa Asur ni Kilmad hina maanii ɔɔ faa waa chɛr i kuna. 24A ba faa kpa bɔmbɔgnanaa, wɛjɛ burguzi, kuna baŋ tɔɔhzɛɛ, dia kumpɛɛri kuna, ŋmɛnni ani a dizi baŋ pɛttɛ nɛnnɛɛ di waa chɛr i kuna.
25Taasis hɛri muugbessi labuu
faa ra chi i kunyoolaa.
I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ muugbera la n du muuzeŋ baaŋ,
buntɔga suu werge maa.
26I muugbersaara la
saaibuu di ra zuu
a muuzeŋ baambaaŋ.
Ka wiifurii pezeŋ daŋ chɔgii
a muuzeŋ baambaaŋ.
27I daama, i kunyoolaa,
i muugbersaara,
i muugbersɛɛhra, i kɔkɔɔza,
ani laallɔɔra la maa
n du a muugbera biini,
nii daŋ di baa,
a hɔl la a muugbera
n niŋ pergi la.
28Hɛssi la maa n du a muuzeŋ kɛraa la danna zigli,
di banla maa n du
a muugbera biini la
waa lɔɔgi wilezi.
29Muugbersaara la maanii
niŋ gil ba muugbessi,
muugbersaara nabɔnzi
ni a huŋhunna maa
daŋ chi baŋgia.
30Ba maa ra wii werge di ra tɛi,
di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa
di ra waari ba nyuuni,
di chɔɔ hɔɔhri biini ra billi.
31Ba daŋ fuŋ ba nyuuni,
di tɔ gbɔglɔnzi
dikuu i wia.
Ba daŋ wii werge maa
ni biinichɔg tɛi.
32Ban ninna wii ni biinichɔg werge labuu,
bá yir lee yir naa ra tɛi.
‘Bolzeŋ bɛl faa du denii kaali Taaya naa,
muuzeŋ tɔ u nii?’
33I kunyoolaa la hiŋ faa kpawɛɛ la hɛrdumazi la,
faa kuari hɛrkpila maa hinaa.
I daama werge la faa
gillɔɔ a hɛssi koora
birgi daama hina.
34Filaŋkeŋ, i ɛɛ muugbera la
n pergeere chɔɔ muu zɛɛ,
i ni i kunyoolaa ni
i nɛra maanii a muuzeŋ di.
35Nɛra la maa n soge a muuzeŋ kɛraa la
bɔra faa huahwɔɔ werge maa,
dikuu i cholzeŋ la wia.
Ɔnsii lau ba koorizenaa, ba bɔra ra sa werge maa,
ba hɔrmi.
36Hɛssi kɔkɔɔza ra viigi ba nyuuni,
dikuu hiŋ chol cholchuma,
i ŋmɛnɛ maa n wàá ka
izi wia.”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Tyre
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying:
You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human. 3You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
4Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver. 5You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
6You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God, 7will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get. 8Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
9When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human. 10Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
11The Lord said:
12Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying:
At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking. 13You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born. 14I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
15You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things. 16You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
17It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you. 18You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood, 19and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever.
Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
20 The Lord said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon 22and tell its people:
I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy. 23I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
24When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
A Blessing for Israel
25The Lord God said:
Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob. 26They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_text:
Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Taaya koori wia
1Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, ŋɔ Taaya koori be, dí kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ,
‘Dikuu i barabara werge wia,
i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ i ɛɛ vugrɛ,
di so koorikara ni
muuzeŋ baambaaŋ.
Ka i ɛɛ neweere, haa vug ɛɛwɛ,
haali hinna fɛ lugɔ
i dɔɔ nunzumaa
lugɔ vug la.
3I fɛ lugɔ i dɔɔ nunzumaa kaali Danɛl,
wiimaa waa i ni suahwɛ.
4Dikuu i nunzuma ni i wia zɛɛzi zumaa la wia,
i birgi daama hiŋ werge maa,
di dɔɔ saliŋ ni
saliŋhuŋŋa werge maa.
5Hiŋ zum kɔɔzaa werge la wia,
i daama waazɔɔrɛ werge maa,
guŋ gil i ra jigsi.
6Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ,
Hinna fɛ lugɔ i dɔɔ nunzumaa
lugɔ vug la wia,
7n daŋ gil hɔɔhra la
n dɔɔ sikpegii werge,
wa lɔi laal, di chɔgi
i nunzuma ni i girme la maa.
8Ba daŋ kpui,
í siu siuchuma,
bá kpai ha muuzeŋ biini.
9I daŋ kaa wer ŋɔ i ɛɛ vugrɛ,
nɛra la n niŋ kpui la bee?
Baa waa zummɔɔ lugɔ haa vug ɛɛwɛ,
neweere hiŋ.
10I daŋ siu lugɔ nɛr la n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ
hɔɔhra nonee biini.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”
11Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, 12“Newee biibaal, a wii dikuu Taaya koori wia, di ŋɔ u be, ‘Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ
i faa wessoo kaali nɛra maa,
di dɔɔ nunzuma werge maa.
13I faa du Ɛdɛnnɛ, kambol la
Kɔraawiizi n kuarɛɛ nɛnnɛ,
daazi du de,
di faa laali binanaa naa,
rubi, topaz, ɛmɛrald,
kisolɛt, ɔnigs, jaspa,
safaaya, tɛkɔis
ani bɛril bɔmbɔgaa!
Saliŋ kuna biinii i faa du.
Ba faa kuaraabuu tɛi
a hɔl la miŋ mai la.
14N faa liziibuu, di gil i ɛɛ lugɔ n chɛrub la bɛl,
i ra binni mìŋ́
Kɔraawiizi bizennaniinanii la ni,
di ra vol n binanaa la
n na nyɛgzi biini.
15I faa waa chɔgri maa dɔɔwɛ
lii saŋa la miŋ mai la,
guŋŋ di wa hel a hɔl la
miŋ zummɛ lugɔ i ɛɛ
biinikpola hinnɛ la.
16I soochi dii werge la
faa gillɔɔ i ra nyiŋŋi kalu,
di dɔɔ wichɔgaa.
Awia, n faa duŋŋiibuu,
lii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi
bizennaniinanii la nyuu.
Haali mɛlika la n faa ra guui la gba, duŋŋiibuu lii
n binanaa la
n na nyɛgzi la biini.
17I faa ra jigsuu,
dikuu hiŋ ɛɛ bunɔɔŋ la wia.
I girme werge la
faa chɔgi i nunzumaa.
Awiarɛ n kpai ta hɛri,
í ɛɛ daansɛɛ kuŋ tɛɛ
durnya koora maa.
18I wichɔgaa ni i kɔɔzichɔgaa la
gillɔɔ i chɔgi i jaamibɔra.
Awiarɛ n faa gil niŋ fuuh i bolzeŋ maa nyaamm,
u birgi hɔɔhri
nɛkpila maa see la.
19A hɛssi la maa hina n faa zumii la
bɔra huah werge maa
dikuu i wia.
I wia tunnɔɔ ni biinichɔg werge maa.
I ŋmɛnɛ maa
wàá ka du de.’ ”
Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi bolzeŋ Saidɔn wia
20Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 21“Newee biibaal, hau bolzeŋ Saidɔn hina ni, di ŋɔ wia la maa n niŋ wa huuzi baa du ba ni. 22Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ,
‘Bolzeŋ Saidɔn, n ɛɛ i dɔmnɛ,
i benii ń ga na girme.
Nɛra daŋ zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi,
saŋa la min niŋ wa tɔɔrii,
ka bagli n nanni i biini la.
23N daŋ gil wiilchɔgaa chol i ni,
di gil bá kpu
nɛkpila maa ge i ŋmɛnibaana.
A lalaa daŋ yaari i biini maa,
bá ra lɔi laal bɔr maa.
Denii bá jaa zum lugɔ
Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
24Hɛssi la hina n bar Izrɛl la wàá ka ɛɛ ba dɔma, di ɛɛ lugɔ choŋgolaa ni sɔɔhri n na wii werge. Denii bá zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la.’ ”
25Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “Di n wa chaali n nɛra Izrɛl hina lii hɛssi la baŋ yaarɛɛ la biine, ba bir ga so hɛri la miŋ faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ n balii Jekɔb la, n daŋ bagli n nanni n nɛra Izrɛl hina biini, durnya hina maa na. 26Ba daŋ wa so ba hɛri ni bɔsɔna, di ma diini, di dau grepu daazi kooni ge gba jaa, a nɔŋ di ra tɛɛ baa. Di ba jaa wa na minna tɔɔri hɛssi la hina maa n faa ra tɔɔri baa la, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Egypt
1 Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people 3that I am saying:
King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy! 4I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body. 5I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh. 6 Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord.
You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick. 7When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
8So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock, 9until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things.
You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it. 10Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia. 11No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for 40 years. 12It will be the most barren place on earth. Every city in Egypt will lie in ruins during those 40 years, and I will scatter your people throughout the nations of the world.
13Then after those 40 years have passed, I will bring your people back from the places where I scattered them. 14They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom 15and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past. 16My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
17Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
18King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city. 19So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops. 20Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
21Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Ijip wia
1A binni fi baagu fihiŋ, hɔpizaa fidaanɛɛ hɔl, saŋa la baŋ lauri yaa kaali hɛrduma la, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, hau Ijip koori ni, di ŋɔ wia la maa n niŋ wa huuzi u ni Ijip hɛri maa du ba ni. 3Ŋɔ dí kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ,
‘Ijip koori, n ɛɛ i dɔmnɛ.
I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nyugzeŋ,
di chɔɔ muu biini.
I ra ŋɔu lugɔ Muu Naal la ɛɛ n hotte,
minuu kuaruu.
4N daŋ kpa gɔrgazi
di du i nua lawii.
Nyinni margi i hɔŋ maa ni,
ń tɛrgi i ni nyinni la maa
n margi i bɔrahɔŋ la ni
lii baŋgia.
5N daŋ gil i ni nyinni la maa
n du i muu la
ta hɛribɔduma.
I daŋ chol baŋgia,
nɛr maa wàá hugii.
N daŋ kpai tɛɛ hɛri naa
pir sela ni u zumbizi, á di.
6Denii Ijip hina maa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”
Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ijip hina faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ koori daŋkpala tɛɛ Izrɛl hina. 7Ba faa lawiibuu kpogli, ka i peri lugɔ daapiah di tɔɔh ba kugzi. Ba faa kaa dɛllii, ka i ku, ba chol di guzi ba charazi.
8Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ gil laallɔɔra wa kpu i nɛra ni ba sela maa. 9Ijip hɛri daŋ birgi hɛribɔduma, wàá ka dɔɔ tɔna. Denii bá jaa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi.
Dikuubɛɛwiai, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Muu Naal ɛɛ n hotte, minuu kuaruu.’ 10Awia, n jaa birgi i ni i muu la maa dɔmnɛ. N daŋ chɔgi Ijip hɛri maa ú chɔɔ pɛɛ, di chi bolzeŋ Migdɔl ga hel bolzeŋ Aswan, guŋŋ ga hel i ni Itiopia hɛri magbɔɔ. 11A daŋ di binni tokkoanɛɛ, di nɛr gɛɛ sel gba waa kaa vol a de hɛri hiŋ. De daŋ birgi hɛribɔduma. 12Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil Ijip ni hɛssi la maa n baruu la birgi hɛribɔdumazi. U bolzenaa daŋ chɔɔ diŋgelli binni tokkoanɛɛ di jaa bolzenaa la n purgee ni. Ka n jaa gil Ijip hɛri nɛra maa ge yaari kaali hɛhjaŋa.”
13Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “Di a binni tokkoanɛɛ naa wa su a maga, n daŋ kaa chaali Ijip hina lii a hɛssi la maa baŋ yaarɛɛ la biine, bá kaa wa so ba hɛri. 14N daŋ gil ba kaa bir lii hɛri la baŋ faa lauri baa kaali la ba, di kaa wa so Ijip hɛri wiifurii nodig wiikakag, ba naabaala hɛri. Ba wàá ka dɔɔ fɔŋŋa lugɔ ba saŋa la. 15Waabuu niŋ jaa nyaa girme hɛssi maa biini. U ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka tɔgzi u hiŋ kaalaa. N daŋ gil u gɛrgi werge, guŋ gil u ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka di kora hɛssi hina ni. 16Izrɛl hina wàá ka dɔɔ tamii lugɔ ba yardi Ijip hina lugɔ bá hiini baa. Ijip hɛri cholaa la daŋ gil Izrɛl hina liizi lugɔ ba faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, saŋa la baŋ faa ŋɔ lugɔ Ijip hina hiini baa la. Denii Izrɛl hina jaa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la.”
17Binni tokko ni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ, baagu lugli hiŋ hɔpizikpaŋ hɔl, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 18“Newee biibaal, Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza laallɔɔra faa fɔɔ Taaya hinaa ni laal, ka a du kpol tɛɛ baa. U faa gillɔɔ u laallɔɔra chi buntɔga, ba vaampɛrɛzi ge maa forgi, ka u ni u laallɔɔra la waa tɔna maa nawɛɛ a laal biini. 19Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ n daŋ kpa Ijip hɛri tɛɛ Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza. U daŋ foozi di ŋmɛɛ ba daama ni kuna la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛ, di turgi u laallɔɔra. 20N kpa Ijip hɛrii tɛu, ú birgi u huma tɔna, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ni u laallɔɔra faa chɔg Taayaa tɛŋ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
21Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, n daŋ kaa gil Izrɛl hina dɔɔ fɔŋŋa. Ka gil hìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl ŋɔ wia bɔr la nɛr maa n niŋ nuu i loobii. Gunnɛ ba jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

english_text:
Egypt Will Be a Barren Desert
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying:
Cry out in despair,
3because you will soon
be punished!
That will be a time
of darkness and doom
for all nations.
4Your own nation of Egypt
will be attacked,
and Ethiopia will suffer.
You will be killed in battle,
and your land will be robbed
and left in ruins.
5Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle. 6All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
7Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin. 8I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
9On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
10Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army. 11He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
12I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken.
Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins
The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
13All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land. 14The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed! 15The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
16I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear. 17The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner. 18You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity. 19When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord.
Egypt's King Is Powerless
20Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword. 22So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever, 23and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
24-25I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord. 26I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_text:
Lee yir dikuu Ijip wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, ŋɔ gunla mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ wia ra bau!
Lɔ wile ŋɔ,
‘Ɔnsii werge
hɔpizii ra bau!’
3A hɔpizii duglɔɔrɛ,
a hɔpiziirɛ Kɔraawiizi
hum u huma.
A hɔl, baama daŋ bir biri,
tɔɔrɔɔzeŋ chol hɛssi
hina maa ni.
4Laal daŋ chol Ijip hɛri, bá kpu nɛra ni tokobizi.
Biinichɔg werge lau Itiopia hina.
Di ba wa kpu Ijip hina kpila maa,
ba daŋ chi ba daama kaali,
ka purgi a bola
á birgi diŋgelli.
5Ba daŋ kpuuzi Itiopia, Libia, Lidia ani Lɔrbizi hɛssi hina ni n nɛra baŋhina ani Ijip hina a laal biini.”
6Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Hɛssi la hina ni Ijip hina n dɔɔ nuukpaŋ la daŋ chol laal biini,
Ijip hina laallɔɔra fɔŋŋa la
wia banna jigsi la daŋ tuŋ.
Ba daŋ kpu baa laal biini, di lii
Migdɔl guŋŋ
di ga hel Aswan.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
7A hɛssi daŋ birgi diŋgelli
jaa durnya hɛssi
diŋgelli ni.
A bolzenaa ge purgi
di jaa bolzenaa la
n purgee ge ni.
8Di n wa gillɔ ba fuuh Ijip hɛri,
ka gil banla maa
n na hiinuu, siuzi la,
ba daŋ jaa zum lugɔ
minuu Kɔraawiizi.
9Di a hɔl wa hello Ijip hɛri chɔgi, n daŋ hum n balaa bá kpa muugbessi ga ɔnzi Itiopia hina, dikuu banna fɛ lugɔ wiimaa wàá huuzi baa wia. Bɔsai werge maa daŋ chol ba ni, Ijip tɔɔrɔɔ hɔpizii la n niŋ ba wibii maa la wia.”
10Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ,
“N daŋ gil Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza
kpu Ijip hina kpila maa.
11N daŋ gil u ni u laallɔɔra la n dɔɔ sikpegii werge
kaali hɛssi maa hina la
ba wa chɔgi a hɛri.
Ba daŋ fɔɔ Ijip hina ni laal,
di kpu baa ni tokobizi
yaari bɔr maa.
12N daŋ gil Muu Naal ni u gɔŋa maa hiihzi,
di kpa a hɛri du
nɛchɔgaa nonee biini.
N daŋ gil hɔɔhra wa chɔgi Ijip hɛri
ni kuna la maa n du de la.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
13Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔu,
“N daŋ purgi Ijip hina vuga
ni anla maa baŋ mawɛɛ
lugɔ newea, a du Mɛmfis la.
Sitɔɔri wàá ka du Ijip hɛri maa.
N daŋ gil ɔnsii lau
a hɛri hina maa.
14Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgi Ijip wiifurii nodig wiikakag, ú birgi diŋgela,
di gil niŋ fuuh bolzeŋ Zoan
n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la,
di tɛr bolzeŋ Tɛbɛs hina
digna werge maa.
15Gunnɛ n baaŋ kaa fuuh bolzeŋ Pɛlusiɔm la
n ɛɛ Ijip hina bolkpeg la ni,
di gil ba kpu bolzeŋ Tɛbɛs
hina kpila maa.
16N daŋ fuuh Ijip hɛri,
di gil bolzeŋ Pɛlusiɔm hina
di dɔgnya werge maa,
di purgi bolzeŋ Tɛbɛs koŋlaa la n baruu la nyaamm.
Mɛmfis hina ge daŋ du
siaahmu biini di hanna la.
17Hɛliɔpɔlis ni Bubastis bolzenaa biipɔllaa
maanii niŋ siu laal biini,
ka ba lauri banla
n kawɛɛ kaali.
18A hɔl la min niŋ wa chɔgi
Ijip fɔŋŋa ni u kpegzi la wia
unna jigsi la tuŋ,
Bɔbiri daŋ tɔ Tapanɛs.
A hɔl, baama daŋ tɔ Ijip hɛri,
ka bá lauri u boljigzi la
hina maa kaali.
19Kenne ń tɛr Ijip hina digna werge maa,
bá zum lugɔ
minuu Kɔraawiizi.”
20Binni fidikpaŋhiŋ, baagu lugli hiŋ, hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 21“Newee biibaal, n kpegli Ijip koorii. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ miŋ ku u nonii, ka ba wɔɔ vɔɔwɛ ú choŋŋi, di kaa du kpeg di wer lau tokobi gba. 22Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, dí, n ɛɛ Ijip koori dɔmnɛ. N daŋ kuugi u nonee maa, u kpeg la ni unla n kuwee la gba, di gil a tokobi lii u nonii chol hɛri. 23N daŋ gil Ijip hina yaari durnya hɛssi maa biine. 24N daŋ tɛɛ Babilɔn koori fɔŋŋa werge maa, di kpa n tokobi du ú nonii. Ama, n daŋ kuugi Ijip koori waa nonee, ú chol chɔɔ ra uuri alugɔ baŋ du baal pira, u siu u dɔm see la. 25N daŋ tɛɛ Babilɔn koori la fɔŋŋa werge maa, ka gil Ijip koori waa gɛrgi. Ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi, di n wa kpa n tokobi du Babilɔn koori nonii, ú viiguu Ijip hɛri. 26N daŋ gil Ijip hina yaari durnya hɛssi maa biine. Denii bá zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

english_text:
Egypt's King Will Be Chopped Down like a Cedar Tree
1Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying:
You are more powerful
than anyone on earth.
Now listen to this.
3There was once a cedar tree
in Lebanon
with large, strong branches
reaching to the sky.
4This tree had plenty of water
to help it grow tall,
and nearby streams watered
the other trees
in the forest.
5But this tree towered over
those other trees,
and its branches
grew long and thick.
6Birds built nests
in its branches,
and animals were born
beneath it.
People from all nations
lived in the shade
of this strong tree.
7It had beautiful,
long branches,
and its roots found water
deep in the soil.
8 None of the cedar trees
in my garden of Eden
were as beautiful
as this tree;
no tree of any kind
had such long branches.
9I, the Lord, gave this tree
its beauty,
and I helped the branches
grow strong.
All other trees in Eden
wanted to be just like it.
10King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree:
The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant. 11So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness. 12Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else. 13Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
14Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
15On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither. 16This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble.
The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls. 17Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
18King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Hɛriŋkpol daa n du Lɛbanɔn wia
1Binni fidikpaŋhiŋ baagu ahorohiŋ lugli hɔpizii la, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ míŋ̀ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, ŋɔ Ijip koori ni u nɛra maa be,
‘Anɛɛ n niŋ wer kpa u hiŋ di mɛgzi ii zennei?
3Asiiria faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hɛriŋkpol daa bɛl n du Lɛbanɔn Kɔr,
u kela du wer,
u lɔɔ nɛnnɛ,
u hel saagi u dɔŋahina
maa ni a kɔr biini.
4Nii du de di gil u ra hel,
bulli ge gil u ra hel jaŋzi ni.
A gɔŋa faa pal
ra bar u zɛɛ maa,
di pal ra zuu
a kɔr daazi maa zɛɛzi.
5Awia, u faa helloo
kaali daazi la maa
n du a kɔr biini.
U kela hel nɛnnɛ di du jaŋra,
di yɛl, dikuu nii
n du de nɛnnɛ wia.
6Zumbizi maa
faa du daŋaa u kela ni,
pir sela maa gba
ra lul a biizi u bɔsɔŋ.
Hɛrzenaa maa hina
ge faa ra so u chunchugli
di ra heezi.
7A daa la faa kannɔɔ di du wer nɛnnɛ,
u kela faa yɛl di du jaŋra,
dikuu u lunne n faa zuu hɛri nɛnnɛ
di ra na nii werge wia.
8A daa naa dee faa helloo kaali Kɔraawiizi kambolnanii la
n du Ɛdɛn biini
hɛriŋkpola maa.
Hàá wer kpa daananaa maa
mɛgzi u kela.
Haali daa maa faa waa hoo hin niŋ kpa mɛgzi u kela.
Daa maa ge faa waa hoo
a kambolnanii biini
di du wer heluu.
9N faa gillɔɔ u du wer nɛnnɛ,
di dɔɔ kelkpila werge.
N kambolnanii hiŋ
daazi faa ra nyiŋŋi á du
u duula la.
10Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ ŋɔ ii be gunla n niŋ wa ɛɛ a daa naa n helle di gaa chug baama, di ra tɔgzi u hiŋ naa wia. 11N daŋ kpau du hɛrduma koori nonee biini. U daŋ ɛɛ a daa gunla n dɛkkɛ, dikuu u biinikpola wia. N vɛɛubuu, 12hɛrdumazi hina la n dɔɔ sikpegii kaali hɛssi maa hina la wa teŋuu ta, di giluu. Uŋ cholle la, u kela vuuri bizenaa nyuuni ni walli maa biine. A kuugi chɔɔ a hɛri faalime maa biine. Hɛssi maa hina chɔ lii u chunchugli biini ka kau. 13Zumbizi maa togni a daa la n cholle la ni, ka pir sela maa ge ra vol u kela la ni. 14Awia, daa maa gilɛɛ kaa ra tɔgzi u hiŋ dikuu un na nii bɔr chi di hel, di du jaŋ saagi u dɔŋahina ni wia. Daa maa n na nii nɛnnɛ ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka hel guŋ dɔŋ, a maanii dɛkkɛ an niŋ siuzi zuu hɛri, di ga jaa lalaa ni.’ ”
15Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “A hɔl la baŋ huguu la, n faa gillɔɔ bulli tɔ u ni alugɔ banna wii u lee. N gillɔɔ u muuni ni gɔŋa palaa teŋ, waa kaa ra na nii. Dikuu uŋ siuwɛ wia, n gillɔɔ bɔbiri tɔ Lɛbanɔn bizenaa ni, u kɔr daazi maa siuzi. 16Saŋa la uŋ cholle la, n faa gillɔɔ hɛssi hina la maa bɔra ra sa. Saŋa la miŋ huguu la, daazi la gba maa n faa du a Ɛdɛn kɔr biini, anla n wesse werge lii a Lɛbanɔn hɛri, a lunne zuu hɛri bɔr la n sɔɔnɛɛ la nɛnnɛ la maa, bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ a ŋmam biini. 17Banla maa n faa ra zuu u bɔsɔŋ, ba nuu dɔɔ nuukpaŋ la maa nuubuu zuu a ŋmam biini, di ga jaa banla maa baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi la ni.
18Ɛdɛn kɔr daazi la, ú bɛliirɛ bá kpa i wessi ni i zenni mɛgzi naanɛi? Ka i ge gba ni Ɛdɛn daazi maanii niŋ zuu a ŋmam biini ga chɔɔ banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi, ba waa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la biini.
Ijip koori ni u harbɔɔ hiŋraa guŋ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
A Funeral Song for the King of Egypt
1Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying:
You act like a lion
roaming the earth;
but you are nothing more than
a crocodile in a river,
churning up muddy water
with your feet.
3King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore. 4I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh. 5I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys, 6and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams. 7 I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining. 8The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
9Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you. 10They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
11The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt! 12Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed. 13I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water. 14The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
15Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
16This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
A Sad Ending for Egypt
17On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations. 19Say to them:
You may be more beautiful
than the people
of other nations,
but you will also die
and join the godless
in the world below.
20You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you. 21Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
22-23The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
24-25The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
26The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle. 27They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
28You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
29The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
30The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
31The Lord God says:
When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering. 32I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Lee yir dikuu Ijip koori wia
1Binni fidaanɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi fidaanɛɛ, lugli hɔpizii la baŋ lauri yaa la hɛrdumazi la hɔllɛ, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, yir lee yir tɛɛ Ijip koori, di ŋɔ u be,
‘I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyiŋ hɛssi hina maa biini,
ka i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nyugaa n du
muuzeŋ biini di ra lɔ nii,
di ra koozuu ni i naazi,
di ra puruu.’
3Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ,
‘N daŋ ta asau lawii,
di gil nɛkpila tɛrgii
lii baŋgia.
4N daŋ kpai ta hɛri,
di gil durnya zumbizi
ni pir sela maa wa dii.
5N daŋ gil i ola yaari bizenaa nyuuni,
di gil i hoga ge suugi walli.
6N daŋ gil i chal pal pɔɔh a hɛri
guŋŋ di ga chug bizenaa,
di gil i ola suugi faalime.
7Di mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi wa chɔgi i wia tuŋ kɔrai la,
n daŋ tɔ chiŋ,
di gil chinchiŋwilaa biri.
N daŋ gil baama bɛl tɔ wiizi ni,
baagu ge wàá ka chaani.
8N daŋ gil kuna la maa n du chiŋ
di ra chaani la biri,
di gil i hɛri maa biri.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
9N daŋ gil hɛrkpila hina maa biine chɔgi,
di n wa gillɔ hɛssi la
hiŋ waa zummɛ
la hina nuu i chɔgaa wia.
10N daŋ gil i wia huah hɛrkpila hina bɔra werge,
koora bɔra danna sa,
ɔnsii lau baa dikuu i wia,
di n wa viigi n tokobi ba see.
I cholli hɔpizii la,
ba bɛl maa bɔra
danna sa werge,
dikuu u miibɔɔ wia.’ ”
11A guŋ wia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ,
“Babilɔn koori daŋ kpa
u tokobi wa lɔi laal.
12N daŋ gil laallɔɔra
lii hɛssi la hina n dɔɔ sikpegii werge,
kpa ba tokobizi
wa kpu i nɛra maa.
Ba daŋ kpu i nɛra maa
di chɔgi kuna la maa
hiŋ kuu a wia di ra jigsi la.
13N daŋ kaa kpu i nauna maa
n du niizenaa kɛraa,
nɛra wàá ka koozi a niiri ni ba naazi,
gɛɛ nauna puraa
ni a naazi maa maa.
14Denii ń kaa gil Ijip niiri la maa chol yelemm,
di gil a kaa ra pal
bɔɔiih alugɔ nuu.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
15Di n wa gillɔ Ijip hɛri maa chɔɔ pɛɛ,
di chɔgi kuna la n du u biini,
di kpu nɛra la maa n du de la,
ba daŋ zum lugɔ
minuu Kɔraawiizi.
16Wibii maa, lee yir naabuu bá yir dikuu u wia. Hɛssi hina la maa biihaana daŋ yiruu, di wii ra tɛɛ Ijip hɛri ni u nɛra maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”
17Binni fidaanɛɛhiŋ, lugli baagu hiŋ, hɔpizaa fidaanuehiŋ, baŋ lauri yaa la hɛrdumazi la hɔllɛ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 18“Newee biibaal, wii ra tɛɛ Ijip nɛkpila. Kpa baa ga jaa hɛrkpega nɛra ni, di hug baa, bá ga jaa lalaa ni. 19Awia, ŋɔ ba be, ‘Ii fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ iabuu wesse kaali nɛra maa? Ií tuu la ga chɔɔ banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la be, lalaa bol.’ 20Ijip hina ni banla maa n siuwɛ a laal biini labuu niŋ kpau chol. N pam n tokobii ń kpu ba maa. 21Nabɔnzenaa la n felee du a bɔɔzeŋ la biini, daŋ ŋɔ Ijip hina ni banla maa ni Ijip hina n dɔɔ nuukpaŋ la wia, ‘Ba ballɔɔ wa chɔɔ banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la be, baabuu ba faa kpu ni tokobi la.’
22Asiiria ni u laallɔɔra chɔɔ a ŋmam biinii, u nɛra la baŋ kpuwɛɛ a laal biini la ge ŋmama baruu. 23Ba ŋmama la du a bɔɔluŋ hiŋ biinii, u laallɔɔra ŋmama bar u ŋmam. Banla n faa gillɛ ɔnsii lau nɛra werge a hɛri biini labuu ba kpu ni tokobi la.
24Ɛlam gba chɔɔ denii, u laallɔɔra ŋmama baruu. Ba maanii ba faa kpu laal biini, ba tuu la ga chɔɔ banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la be, lalaa bol. Ba de dui saŋa, ba faa gillɔɔ ɔnsii werge lau nɛra, ka filaŋkeŋ, ba siuzɔɔrɛ chɔɔ ni hiihzi. 25Ɛlam chɔɔwɔɔ jaa banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ laal biini la ni, u laallɔɔra ŋmama baruu. Ba bɛl maa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ, ba kpu ba maa laal biini. Ba de dui saŋa, ba faa gillɔɔ ɔnsii werge lau nɛra, ka filaŋkeŋ, ba siuzɔɔrɛ chɔɔ, ba ni banla maa n siuzɛɛ laal biini la, kpau di hiihzi.
26Mɛsɛk ni Tubal gba maanii ba faa hug de, ba laallɔɔra ŋmama bar baa. Ba bɛl maa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ, ba kpu ba maa laal biini, ka baabuu faa ra ɔnzi nɛra werge ba de dui saŋa la. 27Ba faa waa baa hukke ni girme gunla baŋ faa ra hug nabɔnzenaa saŋa la. Ba ɔɔ faa kpa ba laal kunaa jaa ba ni hugzi, ba nyuuni sil ba tokobizi, ba laal pɛrɛtuzenaa ge tɔ ba bɔra. Nabɔnzenaa naa faa kpekkoo werge, di ɔnzi nɛra ba de dui saŋa la.
28Ijip koori, gunnɛ bá kpu i ge, í ga chɔɔ banla n waa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi zummɛ, ba kpu baa ni tokobi la be.
29Ɛdɔm hina gba, ba koora ani ba sitɔɔra maa faa chɔɔ denii. Haali baŋ faa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la gba, ka ba ni nɛra la maa baŋ faa kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi la maanii chɔɔ de. Ba ni banla n faa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la maanii faa du a lalaa bol.
30Wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag hɛssi sitɔɔra ni Saidɔn hina maanii ba faa hug de. Ba ni banla maa n siuwɛ laal biini la di hiihzi, haali baŋ faa kpa ba kpegzi di ra ɔnzi nɛra werge, ba de dui saŋa la. Ba faa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ, ba ni banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi la chɔɔ de, di ra di hiihzi lalaa bol.
31Ijip koori ni u laallɔɔra maa n niŋ wa na baa, u bampirii daŋ tig werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u laallɔɔra bɛŋ lɛi faa siuwɛ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ra ŋɔ guŋ. 32Haali miŋ faa gillɛ Ijip koori kpa ɔnsii ta nɛra ni werge, u de dui saŋa la, ka n daŋ gil bá kpu u ni u nɛkpila la maa, di hug baa banla n waŋ zummɛ ni banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi la biini. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch
(Ezekiel 3.16-21)
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying:
Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch 3and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming. 4-5If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
6But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
7Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me. 8When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death. 9If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
The Lord Is Always Fair
(Ezekiel 18.21-30)
10The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me. 11Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
12Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
13Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
14Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right. 15For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live. 16Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
17Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair. 18If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned. 19And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 20But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done.
The News of Jerusalem's Fall
21 Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
22The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak.
What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
23Then the Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
25So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying:
How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder 26and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
27As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases. 28I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them. 29I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The People Listen, but Don't Change
The Lord said:
30Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.” 31So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money. 32They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
33Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n lizi Ɛzɛkiɛl ú ɛɛ u nɛra guuri wia
1Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, 2“Newee biibaal, ŋɔ i nɛra be gunla n ɔɔ ɛɛ, di n wa gillɔ laal chol hɛri maa hina ni. Ba ɔɔ lizi ba bɛllɛ u ɛɛ ba guuri. 3Di u wa na ba dɔm n na ba, u ɔɔ huuh bensunoniinaa karfi nɛr maa. 4Ama, unla maa wa nuu a bensunoniina wiraa ka waa hagzɛɛ, a dɔm ba wa kpuu, u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi u hiŋ ni. 5Uŋ nuu a bensunoniina wiraa ka waa hagzɛɛ la, u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi u hiŋ ni. Di u faa hagzɔɔrɛ, u daŋ faa lɛɛ u hiŋ. 6Ama, di a guuri wa na ba dɔm n na ba ka u siigi, waa a bensunoniina huuhwɛ di karfi a nɛra, ka ba wa kpu ba bɛl maa, a hiŋ daŋ siu dikuu u wichɔgaa wia, ka u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi a guuri ni.
7Newee biibaal, n gillɔɔ i ɛɛ Izrɛl hina guuri. Awia, a nuu nɛnnɛ gunla maa min niŋ ŋɔ, di karfi baa tɛŋ. 8Di n wa ŋɔ biinikpola hiŋ daŋ siu, ka hɔɔ karfɛɛ ú gil u biinikpola la, ka lɛɛ u hiŋ, u daŋ siu dikuu u biinikpola la wia, ka u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi i ni. 9Ama, di i karfuu waa, ka u vɛɛ, waa u wichɔgaa gillɛ ta, u daŋ siu dikuu u wichɔgaa hiŋ wia, ka i daŋ lɛɛ i hiŋ.
10Newee biibaal, ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ kenne ba ra ŋɔ, ‘Yaa biinikpola ni wikuna werge siili yaa ninɛɛ. Awiarɛ, yaa maa ra kɔgi! Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ na miibɔɔ naanɛi?’ 11Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ, ‘N bɔra waa ɔɔ sɔɔni biinikpola hina siu wia, ka anna nyiŋŋuu ba gil ba biine chɔgi dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, di gilaa ta, ka na miibɔɔ. Izrɛl hina! Ií gil ii wichɔgaa ta! Ií gilaa ta! Di gil ii biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ií siuzɛi?’
12Newee biibaal, ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ i hɛri hina lugɔ di nɛr la wia n deŋlee ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa ka wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, u wideŋlaa la wàá wer lɛɛu, gunnɛ biinikpola hiŋ ge biinikpola wiɛɛlaa wàá gil ú chol, di u wa bittɔ lii a biini. Di nɛr la wia n deŋlee wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, u daŋ siu. U wideŋlaa la uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ la wàá wer lɛɛu. 13Di n haŋ wa kali nɛr la wia n deŋlee lugɔ u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ, wibii maa, ka u dɛlli u wideŋlaa la ni di ɛɛ wichɔgaa, màá ka liizi u wideŋlaa la bɛl maa uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ la wia. U daŋ siu dikuu wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia. 14Di n haŋ kali biinikpola hiŋ lugɔ u daŋ siu wibii maa, ka u bir lii u wichɔgaa biini, di ra ɛɛ wia la n dɛkkɛ ni wideŋlaa, 15alugɔ di u wa bir talma la uŋ lɛɛwɛ ka kpa kebee kim nɛr la, di bir kpa nɛr la kuna uŋ faa ŋmɛɛwɛ ga tɛu, di ra hiŋ widaulaa la n na tɛɛ miibɔɔ la, di gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi, u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ wibii maa, wàá siu. 16Màá ka liizi u wichɔgaa la uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ la bɛl maa wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, u jaa ɛɛ wia la n dɛkkɛ ni wideŋlaare, u daŋ na miibɔɔ wibii maa.
17Ka i nɛra ra ŋɔu, ‘Kɔraawiizi wia waa wibii dɔɔwɛ.’ Ka ba wiarɛ waa wibii dɔɔwɛ. 18Di nɛr la wia n deŋlee haŋ wa bir lii u wideŋlaa hiŋ biini di ɛɛ wichɔgaa, u daŋ siu dikuu a wia. 19Ama, di biinikpola hiŋ ge wa gil ú wichɔgaa ɛɛi, ka bir ra ɛɛ winanaa, u daŋ na miibɔɔ dikuu guŋ wia. 20Ka Izrɛl hina, ii ra ŋɔu lugɔ n wiɛɛlaa waa deŋlee. N daŋ kpa bɛl maa wiɛɛlaa diu seriya.”
Jɛrusalɛm cholaa wia
21Saŋa la baŋ faa lau yaa kaali hɛrduma la binni fidaanɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi fi hɔpizaa anuehiŋ hɔl, baal bɛl faa chɔ lii bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm, di wa ŋɔ n be, “Jɛrusalɛm cholloo!” 22A duana ni mɔɔ ka a baal ba la, Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa faa iziŋ werge, di pilli n nua ń wer ŋɔ wia di u wa ballɔ chɔɔzi ni. Awia, n nua faa pilli, waa kaa mar.
23Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ n be, 24“Newee biibaal, nɛra la n du Izrɛl hɛri bolzenaa la n purgee la ra ŋɔu, ‘Abraham faa ɛɛ nɛkpannɛ, ka faa wer dɔɔ a hɛri naa maa! Ka yaa kpillɔɔ, awia, a hɛri jaa ɛɛ yaa hotte, wibii maa.’ 25Awia, ŋɔ ba be, ‘Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔu lugɔ ii ra hee ola ni a challii, di ra kuari vuga, haali di ɔɔ ra kpuuzi nɛra. Awia, ii ɛɛ tamii lugɔ a hɛri daŋ wer ɛɛ ii hor, wibii maa? 26Ii dɛlli ii tokobizii, di ra ɛɛ wia la miŋ kiiwe, bɛl ra chɔgi u dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ. A dɛkkɔ a hɛri n ɛɛ ii horaa?’
27Ŋɔ ba be, ‘Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ lugɔ ba daŋ kpa tokobi kpu banla n kawɛɛ bolzenaa la n purgee la biine. N daŋ kpa banla ge n du kooni la tɛɛ pir sela á di. Banla n suahzi bizenaa nyuuni ni bia bɔɔni la, wiilchɔgaarɛ niŋ kpuuzi ba ge. 28N daŋ chɔgi a hɛri ú birgi diŋgela, di chɔɔ pɛɛ, ba fɔŋŋa la baŋ faa ra jigsi u wia la tuŋ. Izrɛl bizenaa la maa daŋ chɔgi, nɛr maa wàá ka wer tinni a nyuuni. 29Di n wa gillɔ ba hɛri birgi diŋgela dikuu ba wiɛɛlaa la miŋ kiiwe, ka ba ra ɛɛa la wia, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”
30Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Newee biibaal, i hɛri hina ɔɔ ra ŋɔ i wiarɛ, di ba wa chem dɔŋa a bolzeŋ koŋlaa kɛraa gɛɛ ba diini dominuuzi. Ba ɔɔ ra ŋɔ dɔŋa benii, ‘Ií ba ya la ga nuu wia la n lii Kɔraawiizi be filaŋkeŋ.’ 31Awia, n nɛra ɔɔ bau wa so i be di ra nuu wia la hinna ŋɔ, ka ba wàá ra hiŋ. Ba nuuzi summɔɔ werge maa, ka ba bampiree nɔŋŋi wichɔgaa ni kebee wia. 32I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr la n na deŋŋi ba siweere alugɔ nɛbɛl loobii n ɔɔ du sum, u ra lɔ gilgo di ra yir nɔŋŋaa yira, di ra deŋŋi nɛra siwee la. Ba ɔɔ nuu gunla maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛnɛ, ka ba wàá ɛɛ guŋ.
33Ama, di annii maa wa huuzi baa, wibii maa, denii bá zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ faa du ba biinii.”

english_text:
Israel's Leaders Are Worthless Shepherds
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them:
I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep. 3You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock! 4You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep. 5 They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals. 6So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
7-8Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep. 9-10So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
11The Lord God then said:
I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself, 12just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them 13and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields. 14They will be safe as they feed on grassy meadows and green hills. 15I promise to take care of them and keep them safe, 16to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right.
Judgment on the Strong Sheep
17The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel:
I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak. 18Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy. 19That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
20So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak. 21You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak, 22but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
23 After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you. 24 He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep
The Lord God said:
25The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace.
