di kaali hɛhjaŋ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ,
ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
Israel Will Be Punished
1Do you rulers in Jerusalem
and in the city of Samaria
feel safe and at ease?
Everyone bows down to you,
and you think you are better
than any other nation.
But you are in for trouble!
2Look what happened
to the cities of Calneh,
powerful Hamath,
and Gath in Philistia.
Are you greater than any
of those kingdoms?
3You are cruel, and you forget
the coming day of judgment.
4You rich people lounge around
on beds with ivory posts,
while dining on the meat
of your lambs and calves.
5You sing foolish songs
to the music of harps,
and you make up new tunes,
just as David used to do.
6You drink all the wine you want
and wear expensive perfume,
but you don't care about
the ruin of your nation.
7So you will be the first
to be dragged off as captives;
your good times will end.
8The Lord God All-Powerful
has sworn by his own name:
“You descendants of Jacob
make me angry by your pride,
and I hate your fortresses.
And so I will surrender your city
and possessions
to your enemies.”
9If only ten of you survive
by hiding in a house
you will still die.
10As you carry out a corpse
to prepare it for burial,
your relative in the house
will ask, “Are there others?”
You will answer, “No!”
Then your relative will reply,
“Be quiet! Don't dare mention
the name of the Lord.”
11At the Lord's command,
houses great and small
will be smashed to pieces.
12Horses can't gallop on rocks;
oceans can't be plowed.
But you have turned justice
and fairness
into bitter poison.
13You celebrate the defeat
of Lo-Debar and Karnaim,
and you boast by saying,
“We did it on our own.”
14But the Lord God All-Powerful
will send a nation to attack
you people of Israel.
They will capture Lebo-Hamath
in the north,
Arabah Creek in the south,
and everything in between.
translation_text:
Izrɛl chɔgaa wia
1Wia daŋ huuzi ii banla n na faazi bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm biini
ni ii banla n du Samaria,
di fɛ lugɔ wiimaa
wàá huuzi ia la.
Ii ɛɛ nɛzenaare, di du Izrɛl naa n dɔɔ sɔŋ,
nɛra ba ii be,
di waa nyiŋŋi hiinaa la!
2Ií la bolzeŋ Kalnɛ ga na,
di lii de la bolzeŋ Hamaf la
n dɔɔ sɔŋ,
di lii de la
Filisti hina bolzeŋ Gaf.
Aabuu faa bɔ Juda ni Izrɛl kossi diiribɔraa?
Ba hɛssii faa kaali ii horaa?
3Ii waa ɔɔ sɛɛ lugɔ
hɛhchɔg hɔpizii ra bau,
ka ii wiɛɛlaa gil u ra dugli.
4Ii ɔɔ so ii karnanaa ninɛɛ,
di dɛlli di ra di iihinaa.
Di ra hee pepɔla
ni napɔla la n vuhwɛɛ nɛnnɛ.
5Ii ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi ii ra yir yirfalaarɛ, gunla Koori Deevid n ɔɔ faa ra ɛɛ la,
di yiraa, di ra lɔ janjalanzi.
6Ii sinlibizi ɔɔ suuguu ii ra nyɔɔ,
ka ra lɔ tulaale nanaa,
ka ii waa ɔɔ ra wii
Izrɛl puraa wia.
7Awia, iabuu bá feli lauri
kaali hɛrdumazi,
ii diuzenaa dii
ni ii chaalizenaa maa tuŋ.
Kɔraawiizi n hah Izrɛl hina jigsi wia
8Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la, hɛɛhzi u hinnɛ. Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N hah Izrɛl hina jigsii,
di kii ba diizennanaa la.
N daŋ kpa ba bolzeŋ la
ni kuna la maa n du u biini,
tɛɛ ba dɔma.
9Di baala fii kawɛɛ du dia, ba maa daŋ siu. 10Di ba lulli bɛl wa ballɔ, ú wa paa baa di ga fuuh, u daŋ pɛɛzi nɛr la maa n haa suah de, ‘I ni nɛbɛllɛ du a dia gɛɛ?’ U daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Akai!’ Denii bá lulli la bir ŋɔ, ‘Siigi! A waa dɛkkɛ yaa n yir Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ.’
11Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ
lugɔ u daŋ purgi diizenaa
ni a jigzi maa burburbur.
12Zagra ra chɔ bia nyuuniiwaa?
Nɛra kpa naunaa
di ra par dee?
Ka ii kpa wibii birgi kɔrtɔ,
di kpa wideŋlaa birgi wikara.
13Ii ta barabaraa lugɔ
ii kpegli Lo Dɛba hinaa,
di ta barabara lugɔ ii fɔŋŋaa,
ii kpa kpegli
Kanam hina.”
14Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Izrɛl hina, n daŋ gil
hɛrduma hina
laallɔɔra wa lɛɛ ii hɛri dɔɔ.
Ba daŋ sunni ia lii Hamaf Ŋmɛnɛɛ
n du wiifurii nomɛɛl
wiikakag guŋŋ
di ga hel Jɔɔdan Waluu
n du wiifurii nodig
wiikakag.”

english_text:
A Vision of Locusts
1The Lord God showed me that he is going to send locusts to attack your crops. It will happen after the king has already been given his share of the grain and before the rest of the grain has been harvested. 2In my vision the locusts ate every crop in the land, and I said to the Lord, “Please forgive your nation. It's so weak. How can it survive?”
3Then the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.”
A Vision of Fire
4The Lord showed me that he is going to send a ball of fire to burn up everything on earth, including the ocean. 5Then I said, “Won't you please stop? How can our weak nation survive?”
6Again the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.”
A Vision of a Measuring Line
7The Lord showed me a vision of himself standing beside a wall and holding a string with a weight tied to the end of it. The string and weight had been used to measure the straightness of the wall. 8Then he asked, “Amos, what do you see?”
“A measuring line,” I answered.
The Lord said, “I'm using this measuring line to show that my people Israel don't measure up, and I won't forgive them any more. 9Their sacred places will be destroyed, and I will send war against the nation of King Jeroboam.”
Amos and Amaziah
10Amaziah the priest at Bethel sent this message to King Jeroboam of Israel, “Amos is plotting against you in the very heart of Israel. Our nation cannot put up with his message for very long. 11Here is what he is saying:
‘Jeroboam will be put to death,
and the people will be taken
to a foreign country.’ ”
12Then Amaziah told me, “Amos, take your visions and get out! Go back to Judah and earn your living there as a prophet. 13Don't do any more preaching at Bethel. The king worships here at our national temple.”
14I answered:
I'm not a prophet! And I wasn't trained to be a prophet. I am a shepherd, and I take care of fig trees. 15But the Lord told me to leave my herds and preach to the people of Israel. 16And here you are, telling me not to preach! 17Now, listen to what the Lord says about you:
Your wife will become
a prostitute in the city,
your sons and daughters
will be killed in war,
and your land will be divided
among others.
You will die in a country
of foreigners,
and the people of Israel
will be dragged
from their homeland.
translation_text:
Lotorozi nai lugɔ deeza biini
1Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la pilli bagliŋ, lugɔ deeza biini. A winaalii biini, n nawɔɔrɛ unna ɛɛ lotorozi sirya, saŋa la baŋ felee kuuri koori kooree, ka a kaa faari furaa la. 2A lotorozi n wa di a hɛri kuna maa tuŋ nyaamm, n wii di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, gil i nɛra wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa. Ɛrɛɛ bá ɛɛ du denei? Ba waa kpil, di ɛɛ gɛrga!”
3Awia, Kɔraawiizi na ba sinyɛna, di ŋɔ,
“Gunla hiŋ nawɛɛ la wàá ɛɛ.”
4Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la kaa pilli wia naa bagliŋ. N na unna ɛɛ sirya ú kpa niŋ, di di u nɛra seriya. A niŋ fuuh muuzeŋ maa, ka kaa faari di ra fuuh hɛri ge. 5Denii n kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, gil guŋ! Ɛrɛɛ i nɛra ɛɛ du denei? Ba waa kpil tama maa, di kaa ɛɛ gɛrga!”
6Kɔraawiizi kaa na ba sinyɛna, di ŋɔ, “Màá gil guŋ ge gba ɛɛ.”
7Kɔraawiizi kaa pilli wia naa di bagliŋ. N na Kɔraawiizi n chigɛ pɛli koŋlii la baŋ kpa ŋmɛŋ mɛgzi, di ma. U faa kpogli a ŋmɛnnɛ. 8Denii u pɛɛziŋ, “Emɔs, beedee i nai?”
N ŋɔ, “Maari ŋmɛŋ baŋ kpawɛɛ ra mɛgzi, di ra ma.” Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “N kpa a kunnaabuu di ra bagli lugɔ n nɛra Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ koŋlii la n waa deŋlee. Awia, màá ka na ba sinyɛna. N daŋ haŋ tɛr ba dignaa.
9Bɔra la maa Aizik naanna n faa ra jaami la maanii niŋ chɔgi,
bɔnanaananaa la maa
banna tɔgzi Izrɛl hɛri la
maanii ń purgi.
N daŋ kpa n tokobi izi
dim Koori Jeroboam diahina.”
Emɔs ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Amazia wia
10Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Amazia la n faa du Bɛtɛl la tili, di ŋɔ Izrɛl Koori Jeroboam be, “Emɔs ni nɛra baŋhina suahzɔɔrɛ ra ta jina, bá ɛɛi wii bɛl hɛri naa biini. U wiŋɔzi hiŋ daŋ chɔgi a hɛri. 11Kennaabuu u ŋɔ,
‘Koori Jeroboam daŋ siu laal biini,
bá lauri Izrɛl hina maa
kaali hɛrduma.’ ”
12Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Amazia bir ŋɔ Emɔs be, “Kaali de, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ! Bir di ra la Juda hɛri, di gaa hum de, di na diwee ra di. La gaa ŋɔ i Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ wiŋɔzi la de. 13Gilɛɛ kaa ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia Bɛtɛl biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ koori jaami bɔttɛ, di ɛɛ a hɛri maa jaami dia.”
14Emɔs ŋɔ Amazia be, “Maa Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ ɛɛwɛ, maa kaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ ge biibaal. N ɛɛ penɔɔnii, di kaa ra binni fig daazi ge ni. 15Ka Kɔraawiizii liziŋ lii a peeza nɔɔnaa biini, di ŋɔ ń la gaa ŋɔ u wia di ra tɛɛ u nɛra Izrɛl hina. 16Awia, a nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii naa,
‘I ŋɔ lugɔ n gilɛɛ kaa ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Izrɛl hina, di ra du ba ni,
di gilɛɛ ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia
di ra du Aizik diahina ni.’
17Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
‘I haaŋ daŋ birgi sɛnsɛnni,
a bolzeŋ biini,
i biibaala ni i biihaana maanii
bá kpu laal biini.
Ba daŋ kpa i hɛri di bɔnni nɛra,
i himmaa ge daŋ siu,
vugkuara hɛri,
ba daŋ haŋ lauri Izrɛl hinaa
kaali hɛrduma.’ ”

english_text:
A Basket of Fruit
1The Lord God showed me a basket of ripe fruit 2and asked, “Amos, what do you see?”
“A basket of ripe fruit,” I replied.
Then he said,
“This is the end
for my people Israel.
I won't forgive them again.
3Instead of singing
in the temple,
they will cry and weep.
Dead bodies will be everywhere.
So keep silent!
I, the Lord, have spoken!”
Israel Is Doomed
The Lord said:
4You people crush those in need
and wipe out the poor.
5You say to yourselves,
“How much longer before the end
of the New Moon Festival?
When will the Sabbath be over?
Our wheat is ready,
and we want to sell it now.
We can't wait to cheat
and charge high prices
for the grain we sell.
We will use dishonest scales
6and mix dust in the grain.
Those who are needy and poor
don't have any money.
We will make them our slaves
for the price
of a pair of sandals.”
7I, the Lord, won't forget
any of this,
though you take great pride
in your ancestor Jacob.
8Your country will tremble,
and you will mourn.
It will be like the Nile River
that rises and overflows,
then sinks back down.
9On that day, I, the Lord God,
will make the sun
go down at noon,
and I will turn daylight
into darkness.
10Your festivals and joyful singing
will turn into sorrow.
You will wear sackcloth
and shave your heads,
as you would at the death
of your only son.
It will be a horrible day.
11I, the Lord, also promise you
a terrible shortage,
but not of food and water.
You will hunger and thirst
to hear my message.
12You will search everywhere—
from north to south,
from east to west.
You will go all over the earth,
seeking a message
from me, the Lord.
But you won't find one.
13Your beautiful young women
and your young men
will faint from thirst.
14You made promises
to the goddess Ashimah
at Samaria;
you made vows to other gods
at the shrines
of Dan and Beersheba.
So now you will fall
and never get up.
translation_text:
Nɔŋaahma n du kɛɛgɔ biini wia
1Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la kaa pilli bagli mìŋ́ Emɔs, n na nɔŋaahma n du kɛɛgɔ biini. 2Kɔraawiizi pɛɛziŋ, “Beedee i nai?”
N ŋɔ, “N na nɔŋaahma n du kɛɛgɔ biinii.”
Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “N nɛra Izrɛl hina saŋa helloo. Màá ka suŋ ba ni.”
3Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di a hɔl wa hello, a jaamaa dia biini yira daŋ birgi wiraa, dikuubɛɛwiai, lalaa daŋ chɔɔgi bɔr maa. Bɔr maa ɛɛ surumm.”
4Ií ra nuu, ii banla n ɔɔ ra fini anuula hina,
di kaa ra kpu nyaara
la n du hɛri naa biini,
5di ra ŋɔ,
“Saŋa bɛliirɛ Baagufalii Hɔpizizeŋ tuŋ,
ka ya yoo yaa miai?
Saŋa bɛliirɛ Heezaa Hɔpizii la bɛri,
ka ya kaa faari
di ra yoo kunai?
Denii ya wer jaa kuna yoola,
di ra mɛgzi kuna fintime ni,
di kpa mɛgzaa kuna la
n waa dɛkkɛ di ra fini nɛra.
6Yaa daŋ kpa saliŋhuŋŋa yau nyaara,
di kpa gawa kebee
yau anuula hina,
di yoo huuti ni a zɔga.”
7Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ di ŋɔ, “Màá suuh ba wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛwɛ wia.
8Awia, a hɛri daŋ zigli,
nɛr la maa n du u biini,
biini chɔgi.
A hɛri maa daŋ zigli di chɔgi,
alugɔ Muu Naal n ɔɔ su tinni,
ka kaa bir wa tuu la.”
9Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Ŋmɛnɛ bɛl, n daŋ gil
wiizi chol wibaŋkanchirii ni,
di gil bɔr biri wibaŋa ni.
10N daŋ gil ii hɔpizizenaa dii,
birgi liizi hɔpizaa,
ii yira maa birgi wiraa.
N daŋ gil ii maa fuŋ ii nyuuni,
ka kpa gbɔglɔŋ laala laali.
Ka ra wii lugɔ
nɛr biibambikpaŋ n siuwɛ la,
a hɔpizii daŋ
ɛɛ hɔpizichuma.”
11Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Saŋa bɛl ra heluu,
min niŋ gil lɔchɔgii
chol a hɛri.
A lɔzi wàá ɛɛ diwee gɛɛ niinyɔgzi lɔzi,
u daŋ ɛɛ n wiŋɔzi nuui
nyiŋŋaa wiarɛ.
12Nɛra daŋ lii muuzeŋ bɛl di wa kaali bɛl,
di lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag,
di wa kaali wiifurii,
di ra nyiŋŋi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii nuui,
ka ba wàá naa nuu.
13A hɔl hiŋ,
suŋgure ni biipɔlkpega daŋ huahgi,
dikuu niinyɔgzi wia.
14Banla n niŋ hɛɛhzi
Samaria, Dan ani bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba vuga,
daŋ chol, ba wàá
ka izi maa.”

english_text:
Judgment on Israel
1I saw a vision of the Lord
standing by the temple altar,
and he said,
“Shake the columns
until the tops fall loose,
and the doorposts crumble.
Then make the pieces fall
on the people below.
I will take a sword and kill
anyone who escapes.
2“If they dig deep into the earth
or climb to the sky,
I'll reach out and get them.
3If they escape to the peaks
of Mount Carmel,
I'll search and find them.
And if they hide from me
at the bottom of the ocean,
I'll command a sea monster
to bite them.
4I'll send a sword to kill them,
wherever their enemies
drag them off as captives.
I'm determined to hurt them,
not to help them.”
His Name Is the Lord
5When the Lord God All-Powerful
touches the earth, it melts,
and its people mourn.
God makes the earth rise
and then fall,
just like the Nile River.
6He built his palace in the heavens
and let its foundations
rest on the earth.
He scoops up the ocean
and empties it on the earth.
His name is the Lord.
The Lord Is God
7Israel, I am the Lord God,
and the Ethiopians
are no less important to me
than you are.
I brought you out of Egypt,
but I also brought
the Philistines from Crete
and the Arameans from Kir.
8My eyes have seen
what a sinful nation you are,
and I'll wipe you out.
But I will leave a few
of Jacob's descendants.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
9At my command, all of you
will be sifted like grain.
Israelites who remain faithful
will be scattered
among the nations.
And the others will be trapped
like trash in a sifter.
10Some of you are evil,
and you deny
that you will ever get caught.
But you will be killed.
The Lord's Promise to Israel
11 In the future, I will rebuild
David's fallen kingdom.
I will build it from its ruins
and set it up again,
just as it used to be.
12Then you will capture Edom
and the other nations
that are mine.
I, the Lord, have spoken,
and my words will come true.
13You will have such a harvest
that you won't be able
to bring in all of your wheat
before plowing time.
You will have grapes left over
from season to season;
your fruitful vineyards
will cover the mountains.
14I'll make Israel prosper again.
You will rebuild your towns
and live in them.
You will drink wine
from your own vineyards
and eat the fruit you grow.
15I'll plant your roots deep
in the land I have given you,
and you won't ever
be uprooted again.
I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi seriyazi dii
1Mìŋ́ Emɔs na Kɔraawiizi n chigɛ mbusu lizibɔr, ka ŋɔ,
“Yag n Dia ligee nyuuni fɔŋŋa ni,
guŋ gil a jaŋgal maa zigli.
Purgaa, a chogli a nɛra nyuuni,
ka n kpu nɛra la
maa n kawɛɛ la, laal biini.
Bɛl maa wàá wer
chɔ lii a biine.
2Haali di ba ki bɔɔ
di ga lii lalaa bol gba,
ka n daŋ lau baa.
Di ba zinnɔɔ kaali chiŋ gba,
ka n daŋ lau baa
tuu hɛri.
3Di ba suah Bizeŋ Kamɛl nyuu gba,
ka n daŋ sɛu di lau baa.
Di ba kaa ga suah muuzeŋ zɛɛ ge,
n daŋ gil muuzeŋ
sechɔgii la dunzi baa.
4Di ba dɔma genii lau baa kaali hɛri bɛl,
n daŋ gil ba kpu baa de.
N siaahmuu lugɔ n chɔgi baa,
maa nyiŋŋi ba hiinaa.”
5Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa,
di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
ɔɔ gbɔgzi hɛrii, u zigli,
banla maa n du u biini ra wii.
Hɛri maa ɔɔ tinni ka bir tuu,
alugɔ Muu Naal n ɔɔ su tinni,
ka bir tuu la.
6Kɔraawiizi ma u bolle chinchiŋ,
di gil u zɛɛ chi hɛri.
U ɔɔ ɛɛ muuzenaa niirii,
di bizaa ta hɛri.
U sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi!
7Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Izrɛl hina, n na fɛ Itiopia hina
wiarɛ werge alugɔ ia.
N lizi Filisti ni Siiria hinaa lii Krit hɛri,
gunla miŋ lizi ia
lii Ijip hɛri la.
8Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la
ra na Izrɛl hina wichɔgaarɛ.
N daŋ kpu baa,
ka màá dim Jekɔb naanna
durnya naa biini.
9N daŋ ŋɔ wia di zigli Izrɛl hina,
alugɔ baŋ kpa jeeraa
di ra je sau la
durnya hɛssi maa biine,
di lizi banla maa
n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ.
10Ba daŋ kpu n nɛra la maa
n ɛɛ wichɔgɛɛra laal biini.
Baabuu banla n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ,
‘Kɔraawiizi wàá gil
wichɔgii maa
huuzi yaa.’ ”
Kɔraawiizi n niŋ bir kuari Izrɛl hina wia soŋŋi wia
11Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Hɔpizii bɛl, n daŋ kaa bir kuari ia soŋŋi,
di wa ma Koori Deevid dia la
n cholle la.
N daŋ bir kuari u koŋlaa ma,
a chi gunla
aŋ faa chigɛ la.
12Awia, Izrɛl hina daŋ lɔ laal,
di foozi Ɛdɔm hɛri la n kawɛɛ
ni hɛssi la maa
n faa ɛɛ n hora la.”
Kɔraawiizi la n niŋ gil
guŋ ɛɛ labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
13Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Hɔpizaa aŋhina ra bau,
sɔgmia daŋ ɔɔ lɛɛ werge,
bá kpɛllaa guŋŋ
paraa saŋa kaa wa hel.
Grepuzi ɔɔ hel di lɛɛ werge,
bá ɔɔ kpaa daali siŋ guŋŋ
a falaa kaa wa lii jaa.
Siŋfalaa daŋ ɔɔ lii bizenaa nyuuni,
di ra toŋzi giŋgimee nyuuni,
di ra pal.
14N daŋ bir kpogli n nɛra la baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛrdumazi la ba.
Ba daŋ bir wa kuari
ba bolzenaa ma,
di du a biine.
Ba daŋ duu grepu daazi kooni, di nyɔɔ a siŋ,
di kuari kambola
duu kuna, di dia.
15N daŋ gil n nɛra na bɔr, di chi a hɛri la miŋ tɛɛ baa la,
nɛr maa wàá ka wer
lizi baa lii de.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
Edom's Pride and Punishment
1 The Lord God gave Obadiah
a message about Edom,
and this is what we heard:
“I, the Lord, have sent
a messenger
with orders for the nations
to attack Edom.”
2The Lord said to Edom:
I will make you the weakest
and most despised nation.
3You live in a mountain fortress,
because your pride
makes you feel safe from attack,
but you are mistaken.
4I will still bring you down,
even if you fly higher
than an eagle
or nest among the stars.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
5If thieves break in at night,
they steal
only what they want.
And people who harvest grapes
always leave some unpicked.
But, Edom, you are doomed!
6Everything you treasure most
will be taken from you.
7Your allies can't be trusted.
They will force you out
of your own country.
And your best friends
will trick and trap you,
even before you know it.
8Edom, when this happens,
I, the Lord, will destroy
all your marvelous wisdom.
9Warriors from the city of Teman
will be terrified,
and you descendants of Esau
will be wiped out.
The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
10You were cruel to your relatives,
the descendants of Jacob.
Now you will be destroyed,
disgraced forever.
11You stood there and watched
as foreigners entered Jerusalem
and took what they wanted.
In fact, you were no better
than those foreigners.
12Why did you celebrate
when such a dreadful disaster
struck your relatives?
Why were you so pleased
when everyone in Judah
was suffering?
13They are my people,
and you were cruel to them.
You went through their towns,
sneering and stealing
whatever was left.
14In their time of torment,
you ambushed refugees
and handed them over
to their attackers.
The Lord Will Judge the Nations
15The day is coming
when I, the Lord,
will judge the nations.
And, Edom, you will pay in full
for what you have done.
16I forced the people of Judah
to drink the wine of my anger
on my sacred mountain.
Soon the neighboring nations
must drink their fill—
then vanish without a trace.
Victory for Israel
17The Lord's people who escape
will go to Mount Zion,
and it will be holy.
Then Jacob's descendants
will capture the land of those
who took their land.
18Israel will be a fire,
and Edom will be straw
going up in flames.
The Lord has spoken!
19The people of Israel
who live in the Southern Desert
will take the land of Edom.
Those who live in the hills
will capture Philistia,
Ephraim, and Samaria.
And the tribe of Benjamin
will conquer Gilead.
20Those who return from captivity
will control Phoenicia
as far as Zarephath.
Captives from Jerusalem
who were taken to Sepharad
will capture the towns
of the Southern Desert.
21Those the Lord has saved
will live on Mount Zion
and rule over Edom.
Then the kingdom will belong
to the Lord.
translation_text:
1Wia la Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la n pillɛɛ bagli Obadia di ra bagli Ɛdɔm wiarɛ keŋ.
Yaa nuu amaniyee lii Kɔraawiizi be.
U faa hum u baliirɛ
ú ba wa ŋɔ hɛssi maa hina be,
“Ií izi ya ga lɔ Ɛdɔm hina laal.”
2Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Ɛdɔm hina benii,
“N daŋ gil ii gɛrgi
hɛssi hina maa be,
ba maa danna gbɛlli
ia werge.
3Ii barabara dar iabuu,
ii banla n du
bia la n jaŋŋɛ
di la chiŋ werge nyuuni,
di ra zuu a fɔɔliizi,
di ra ŋɔ iihinaa be,
‘Anɛɛ n niŋ wer hel yaa
di ba yaa ni hɛrɛi?’
4Haali iiŋ la chiŋ alugɔ chig,
di ma ii diini
chinchiŋwilaa biini gba,
ka n daŋ gil ii lii de
ba hɛri.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
5Di ŋmɛɛna gɛɛ nɛfooza
ba ii be hahmuŋa ni,
hɛhchɔg daŋ chol ii ni.
Ba wàá ŋmɛɛ ia
lɛi ba kiparaa?
Di banla n na tɔrgi grepuzi faa wa tɔrgaa,
ba wàá gil aŋhinaa?
6Ɛsau naanna, ba daŋ wa paagi ii daama kuna maa nyaamm,
haali ii kunnanaananaa la
iiŋ suahwɛ gba.
7Nɛra la ii ni baa n dɔɔ nuukpaŋ la daŋ duŋŋi ia lii ii hɛri,
ii dammuzi daŋ dar ia
di kpegli ia.
Banla ii ni baa n ɔɔ kpau ra di la daŋ he ia sidɛɛ,
ka ii wàá zum.”
8Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N daŋ kpu Ɛdɔm
nunzunna maa,
a keŋ hɔpizii naa,
nɛra la n na nuu wia zɛɛ
daŋ lii Ɛsau bizenaa nyuuni.
9Tɛman hina, ɔnsii ni bɔsai daŋ chol ii laallɔɔra maa ni,
banla maa n du
Ɛsau bizenaa nyuuni la
maanii bá kpu.
10Iiŋ ga foozi ii lulla Jekɔb dee kuna, di kaa kpu baa jaa la wia,
ii maanii bá kpu,
ii wàá ka dɔɔ girme
di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
11Ii chigɔɔ ra binni,
ka ba dɔma wa chɔgi ba
dominuuzi a hɔl hiŋ.
Ii ɛɛ nɛchunzii lugɔ a keŋ nɛra naa n ballɛ
di wa chi Jɛrusalɛm hina
kundɔɔlaa maa kaali,
di ga bɔnni dɔŋa la.
12A faa waa dɛkkɛ ii bɔra n sɔɔnɛɛ
dikuu hɛhchɔg n chol
ii lulla ni wia,
di ra di iihinaa Juda hina ni,
ba anuula saŋa la
gɛɛ di ra ta barabara werge,
ba tɔɔrɔɔ dii hiŋ biini.
13A faa waa dɛkkɛ iiŋ zuu n nɛra bolzeŋ,
di ra di iihinaa ba ni,
ba anuula saŋa
gɛɛ di paagi ba kundɔɔlaa
a hɛhchɔg hɔpizii hiŋ.
14A faa waa dɛkkɛ iiŋ chigɛ ŋmɛnichechema
di ra lauri banla n ga de
chɔ ra kaali la.
A faa waa dɛkkɛ iiŋ kpa baa du ba dɔma nonee biini,
ba biinichɔg hɔpizii hiŋ.
15Hɔpizii la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n niŋ di
durnya hɛssi hina
seriya duglɔɔrɛ.
Ɛdɔm hina, wii la iiŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ ii dɔŋahina la,
guŋ himmaanii bá kpa
ɛɛ ii ge.
Ii wiɛɛlaa la daŋ bir
laŋŋi ii ni.
16N nɛra nyɔɔ n tɔɔrɔɔ niirɛ werge
n giŋgimiinanii la nyuu.
Ka hɛssi la maa n baruu la
daŋ haa nyɔɔ
n tɔɔrɔɔ nii werge maa,
ba daŋ nyɔɔu kpɛlɛŋŋ,
ka siu.
17Ka Jekɔb domee daŋ na lɛɛi Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu,
ú ɛɛ kunnaniinanii,
di ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ
bá ra di.
18Jekɔb ni Joosɛf domeezi maa daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ niŋ.
Ba daŋ chɔgi Ɛsau domee
gunla niŋ n ɔɔ di kɔlaa
bɛl maa wàá ka ka la.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
19Nɛra daŋ lii Nɛgɛv, di wa lɛɛ
Ɛdɔm hɛri bizenaa nyuuni,
di so.
Nɛra kaa lii wiicholii giŋgimee nyuuni di wa lɛɛ
Filisti hɛri maa so.
A Izrɛl hina daŋ wa lɛɛ Ɛfram ni Samaria hina hɛssi maa.
Ka Bɛnjamin domee ge
lɛɛ Giliad hɛri di so.
20Izrɛl hina la baŋ laurɛɛ ba ga so Keenan hɛri la,
daŋ lɛɛ a hɛri haali
di ga lii Zarɛfaf,
banla ge n lii Jɛrusalɛm di wa so Sɛfarad la
daŋ lɛɛ Nɛgɛv bolzenaa waa maa.
21Jɛrusalɛm laallɔɔra la n lɔ laal lii,
daŋ ga lɔ Ɛdɔm hina,
di lɛɛ ba hɛri,
di ra di kora ba ni.
Ka de hɛri kossi maa jaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora.”

english_text:
Jonah Runs from the Lord
1 One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai, 2to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
3Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
4But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces. 5The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter.
All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep. 6The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
7Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
8They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
9Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
10When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
11The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
12Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
13The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute. 14So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.” 15Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down. 16The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
17 The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
translation_text:
Joona n vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua wia
1Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ wiarɛ tɛɛ Amitai biibaal Joona, di ŋɔ, 2“Izi la bolzeŋ Ninɛvɛ, di ga ŋɔ wia du u nɛra ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba wichɔgaa kannɔɔ werge n be.”
3Ka Joona di nyiŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛ ú la Taasis, ú faa wer chɔ lii Kɔraawiizi be. Uŋ ga hel Jɔpa muu nua, u na muugberzeŋ bɛl n na la Taasis. U turgi u chaaji, ka zuu ú la Taasis, di chɔ lii Kɔraawiizi be.
4Uŋ zuuwɛ ba ra la la, Kɔraawiizi gil pezeŋ izi ra ta ba ni fuufuu, a muugberzeŋ ra nyiŋŋi u pergi. 5Ɔnsii jaa lau a muugberzeŋ biini hina maa, bɛl maa ra yir u vug ú wa lɛɛu. Ba jaa ligzi ba bunni di ra ha a nii biini, ka a gberzeŋ wer du fug di kpa baa la.
A saŋa di Joona waa tuuwo ga chɔɔ a muugberzeŋ zɛɛ, di ra chɔɔ dɔɔ werge maa, haali di waa zum wii la n na ɛɛ gba. 6Denii a muugberzeŋ nabɔma tuu la bɔr la uŋ chɔɔwɛ, di ga lalluu di ŋɔ, “Izi! Ɛrɛɛ i ra chɔɔ dɔɔ werge saŋa naa dɔŋɛi? Izi suŋŋi i vug. Aŋhinabe, u daŋ na yaa sinyɛna di lɛɛ yaa, yaa wàá siuzi.”
7Denii a muugberzeŋ biini huŋhunna maa ŋɔ, “Ií gil ya nyiŋŋi nɛr la n gillɛ siaahmu naa huuzi yaa keŋ.” Ba jaa ga ta kuna, bá zum a hiŋ, a chol Joona ni.
8Ba ŋɔ u be, “Bagli yaa wii la n baani wia naa huuzi yaa keŋ. Anɛɛ hinnɛi? Bɛɛ humaa i ra hummɛi? Lee i liiyɛi? Hɛrbɛliirɛ i liiyɛi? Nɛbɛlii deere hinnɛi?”
9Denii u ŋɔ ba be, “Hibru hinuurɛ miŋ, n na jaami Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la. Waabuu du chiŋ, di ta muuzeŋ ni hɛri la.”
10Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa, ba pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛ gunnɛi?” Ba teŋ zummɔ lugɔ u chɔwɔɔrɛ, Kɔraawiizi gilɛɛ wer nau hum, dikuu gunla uŋ teŋ ŋɔ ba be la wia.
11Ka pekpeg haa ra ta werge maa. Ba pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛi, ka a pekpeg siigɛi?”
12U ŋɔ, “Ií kpaŋ ha a muu biini, ka bɔr chaani tɛɛ ia. N zummɔ lugɔ n benii a tɔɔrɔɔ naa lii di ra huuzi ia la.”
13Ka a huŋhunna ɛɛ ania maa bá faa wer saa a muugbera di la a muunua di ga chi. Ka ba waa wette, dikuu a pekpeg n nyaŋŋɛɛ wia. 14Denii ba suŋŋi wiizi, di ŋɔ, “Hoi, Kɔraawiizi, jaande maa, gilɛɛ gil ya siu dikuu baal naa kpui wia. Gilɛɛ gil ya di bilchɔg dikuu biinihuŋŋu hiŋ naa kpui wia. I kipar wiarɛ i ra duu siaahmu naa.” 15Denii a nɛra jaa lau Joona, di kpau ta a nii biini. Baŋ wa tau tuŋ, a nii siigi kakpaŋ! 16Ɔnsii lau baa, ba ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi werge maa, di lizi mbusu lizaa kuna tɛu, di kaa hɛɛhzi lugɔ ba danna jaamuu.
17Denii Kɔraawiizi jaa gil nyinzeŋ bɛl ba, di wa lau Joona lil. U du a nyiŋ hia hɔpizaa ahoro ni hamuŋzi ahoro.

english_text:
Jonah's Prayer
1From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
2When I was in trouble, Lord,
I prayed to you,
and you listened to me.
From deep in the world
of the dead,
I begged for your help,
and you answered my prayer.
3You threw me down
to the bottom of the sea.
The water was churning
all around;
I was completely covered
by your mighty waves.
4I thought I was swept away
from your sight,
never again to see
your holy temple.
5I was almost drowned
by the swirling waters
that surrounded me.
Seaweed had wrapped
around my head.
6I had sunk down deep
below the mountains
beneath the sea.
I knew that forever,
I would be a prisoner there.
But, you, Lord God,
rescued me from that pit.
7When my life was slipping away,
I remembered you—
and in your holy temple
you heard my prayer.
8All who worship worthless idols
turn from the God
who offers them mercy.
9But with shouts of praise,
I will offer a sacrifice
to you, my Lord.
I will keep my promise,
because you are the one
with power to save.
10 The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
translation_text:
Joona wiisuŋŋaa wia
1Joona n du a nyiŋ hia la, u suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la unna hum la, 2di ŋɔ,
“N anuula biinii n yir hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi,
i nuu tɛŋ.
Miŋ du lalaa bol la n luŋŋe werge biini,
n lɔ wilee tɛi,
i nuu n wile hiŋ.
3I faa kpambuu ta niizeŋ biini,
a muuzeŋ zɛɛ himmaa,
bɔr la niiri maa n bariŋ,
nii tɔ n ni di ra lɔŋ
werge maa la.
4Denii n ŋɔ, ‘Hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi
duŋŋimbuu lii i be.
Ka n daŋ haa bir n siwee
chaŋ i Diinaniinanii la.’
5A nii tɔ n ni di ra nyiŋŋi u kpuŋ,
di bariŋ vil biini,
nii biini kooree ge wa tɔ
n nyuu maa ni.
6N tuu la bizenaa zɛɛzi maa,
a ɛɛ lugɔ baŋ tɔŋ dia,
màá ka lii maa.
Ka i lizimbuu a vil biini, n haa dɔɔ miibɔɔ,
Kɔraawiizi la minna hum!
7Miŋ faa waa kaa dɔɔ tamii maa n miibɔɔ wia la,
n liizi i wia.
N wiisuŋŋaa helii,
i nuu n be lii
i Diinaniinanii la biini.
8Banla n na kuari vuga n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ la,
vɛɛ i hiŋaarɛ.
9Ka miŋwaa, n daŋ yir yira
di ra chɔlii,
di kaa ra lizi
mbusuzi kuna ra tɛi.
Wii la maa miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ ɛɛ tɛi, n daŋ ɛɛu.
Lɛɛi lii hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi
bɛŋ benii.”
10Denii Kɔraawiizi gil nyiŋ la ug Joona ha a muuzeŋ baŋgia.

english_text:
Jonah Goes to Nineveh
1Once again the Lord told Jonah 2to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
3Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it. 4 After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
5They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
6When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust. 7-9Then he and his officials sent out an order for everyone in the city to obey. It said:
None of you or your animals may eat or drink a thing. Each of you must wear sackcloth, and you must even put sackcloth on your animals.
You must also pray to the Lord God with all your heart and stop being sinful and cruel. Maybe God will change his mind and have mercy on us, so we won't be destroyed.
10When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_text:
Joona n la Ninɛvɛ wia
1Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ wia Joona be bunɛɛ, di ŋɔ, 2“Izi la bolzeŋ Ninɛvɛ, di ga lizi n amaniye tɛɛ baa.”
3Denii Joona jaa hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, di izi la bolzeŋ Ninɛvɛ. Ninɛvɛ faa kannɔɔ werge, hɔpizaa ahoroo í kpa vol lii u tuna bɛl di ga hel bɛl. 4Joona n ga zuu a bol, u jaa faari di ra ŋɔ wia kpegzi ni, di ŋɔ, “A ka hɔpizaa tokkoanɛɛ, ka Ninɛvɛ maa purgi!” 5Denii Ninɛvɛ hina maa yardi Kɔraawiizi. Ba gil nɛr maa, nabɔnzi ni bichalli maa vɔɔ nua, di tɔ gbɔglɔnzi, guŋ bagli lugɔ ba biine chɔkkɔɔ dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia.
6Ninɛvɛ koori n wa nuu guŋ, u izi u koorikara ni kakpaŋ, di wir u koori tagtazi, ka la ga kpa gbɔglɔŋ tɔ, di ga so hɔɔhri biini, dikuu u biini n chɔkkɛ wia. 7Denii u gil ba sii Ninɛvɛ biini maa di ŋɔ,
“Koori ni u nabɔnzii du gbɔg naa di ŋɔ nɛ́r maa ni sel maa, gilɛɛ waa di diwee gɛɛ kooree, bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa nyɔɔ nii gba. 8Ií gil nɛra ni sela maa laali gbɔglɔnzi, di ra suŋŋi wiizi siaahmu ni, di ra sɛɛ chɔgri ba wichɔgaa ni ba wikuna maa wia, di gilaa ta. 9Aŋhinabe, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ daŋ sɔɔni, ú suŋ yaa ni, wàá ka kpu yaa.”
10Kɔraawiizi n wa na gunla baŋ ɛɛwɛ, di gil ba wichɔgaa ɛɛi la, u suŋ ba ni. Waa kaa tɛr ba digna gunla uŋ faa ŋɔ u daŋ ɛɛ baa la.

english_text:
Jonah Gets Angry with the Lord
1Jonah was really upset and angry. 2 So he prayed:
Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
3 Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
4The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
5Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
6The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine, 7but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up. 8During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
9But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?”
“Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
10But the Lord said:
You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next. 11In that city of Nineveh there are more than 120,000 people who cannot tell right from wrong, and many cattle are also there. Don't you think I should be concerned about that big city?
translation_text:
Joona baaŋfuuih dikuu Kɔraawiizi nɛsunaa dɔɔi wia
1A wia naa n wa ɛɛwɛ, a guŋ waa Joona pattɛ kɔrai, u baaŋ fuuh. 2U suŋŋi wiizi, di ŋɔ, “Hoi, Kɔraawiizi, miŋ faa du bol la, keŋ lɛi n faa ŋɔaa? Awiarɛ n faa hahzi chɔ kaali Taasis la. N zummɔ lugɔ i ɔɔ ra na nɛra sinyɛnaa, di ra suŋ ba ni. I baaŋ waa fuuh manaŋ. I kaa nɔŋŋi nɛra werge maa. I daŋ wer gil nɛra wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa, di gil wii la hiŋ faa dauwɛ lugɔ i ɛɛ di kpu baa. 3Awia, n Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hiŋ gillɛ n siu, gunnɛ bɔ miŋ du de.”
4Denii Kɔraawiizi bir pɛɛzuu, “A dɛkkɔɔ i baan na fuuhwaa?”
5Joona jaa izi lii ga so a bol wiifurii, di du pampanni so u biini, ka ra kpaŋ wii la n niŋ wa ɛɛ a bolzeŋ hina. 6Denii Kɔraawiizi gil laalinla lii tinni wa tɔ a pampanni ni, u chunchugli wa tɔ Joona ni, wiizi waa kaa ra kpuu. Joona bɔra jaa sɔɔni werge maa dikuu guŋ wia. 7Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi gil sandul ba wa di a laalinla, u siu. 8Wiizi n wa baŋŋɛ, Kɔraawiizi gil pewem lii wiifurii di waa ta Joona ni, wiizi ra kpuu werge maa, u ra bɛɛli di ra nyiŋŋi u siu. U ŋɔ, “Amɔ, n siu waa bɔ n de dui naa?”
9Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzuu, “A dɛkkɔ hiŋ na baaŋ dikuu a laalinla naa siu wiaa?”
Joona ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh! A dɛkkɔɔ n na baaŋ di siu gba!”
10Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa pɛɛzuu, “I biini chɔkkɔɔ dikuu a laalinla siu wiaa? Haa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ ka u lii. U liwɔɔrɛ di hel hɔpizikpaŋ biini, di kaa siu hɔpizikpaŋ ge. 11Na, Ninɛvɛ dɔɔ nɛra kagboŋa kalfa ni tokko n waa ba nodige ni ba nomɛɛla zummɛ, di kaa dɔɔ sela ge werge. Awia, a waa dɛkkɛ min niŋ suŋ ba niii?”

english_text:
1 I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah.
Judgment on Samaria
2Listen, all of you!
Earth and everything on it,
pay close attention.
The Lord God accuses you
from his holy temple.
3And he will come down
to crush underfoot
every pagan altar.
4Mountains will melt
beneath his feet
like wax beside a fire.
Valleys will vanish like water
rushing down a ravine.
5This will happen because of
the terrible sins of Israel,
the descendants of Jacob.
Samaria has led Israel to sin,
and pagan altars at Jerusalem
have made Judah sin.
6So the Lord will leave Samaria
in ruins—
merely an empty field
where vineyards are planted.
He will scatter its stones
and destroy its foundations.
7Samaria's idols will be smashed,
and the wages
of temple prostitutes
will be destroyed by fire.
Silver and gold from those idols
will then be used by foreigners
as payment for prostitutes.
Judah Is Doomed
8Because of this tragedy,
I go barefoot and naked.
My crying and weeping
sound like howling wolves
or ostriches.
9The nation is fatally wounded.
Judah is doomed.
Jerusalem will fall.
10Don't tell it in Gath!
Don't even cry.
Instead, roll in the dust
at Beth-Leaphrah.
11Depart naked and ashamed,
you people of Shaphir.
The town of Bethezel mourns
because no one from Zaanan
went out to help.
12Everyone in Maroth
hoped for the best,
but the Lord sent disaster
down on Jerusalem.
13Get the war chariots ready,
you people of Lachish.
You led Jerusalem into sin,
just as Israel did.
14Now you will have to give
a going-away gift
to Moresheth.
Israel's kings will discover
that they cannot trust
the town of Achzib.
15People of Mareshah,
the Lord will send someone
to capture your town.
Then Israel's glorious king
will be forced to hide
in Adullam Cave.
16Judah, shave your head
as bald as a vulture
and start mourning.
Your precious children
will be dragged off
to a foreign country.
translation_text:
1Kɔraawiizi faa pilli Samaria ni Jɛrusalɛm wiarɛ lugɔ deeza biini, di bagli mìŋ́ Maika n lii Mɔrɛsɛf. A saŋaa Jɔtam, Ahaz ani Hɛzɛkia faa di kossi, Juda hɛri la.
2Durnya hɛssi hina maa, ií ra nuu!
Kuna la maa n du hɛri,
ií ra nuu!
Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la
daŋ hau ii ni,
u Diinaniinanii la biini,
3Kɔraawiizi lii u duuribɔttɛ tuu ra ba.
U tuuwoo ra ba,
ú wa vol bizenaa nyuuni.
4Denii bizenaa ŋmɛɛri u naazi zɛɛ,
walli maa pergi
alugɔ kel n dugli niŋ
di ra ŋmɛɛri la
gɛɛ gunla nii n ɔɔ pal
di ra tuu bɔwillii la.
5Annii maa daŋ ɛɛu,
dikuu Izrɛl hina
wichɔgaa wia.
Izrɛl hina wichɔgaarɛ a bɛlaai?
Samaria hina
wichɔgaa lɛiyaa?
Juda hina vuga kuaribɔttɛ lee?
Jɛrusalɛm lɛiyaa?
6Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ
u daŋ gil bolzeŋ
Samaria puri,
di chɔɔ kulululu,
di birgi grepu daazi pattibɔr.
U daŋ chɔgi a bolzeŋ, di paa u bia maa
ga ha waluu biini,
ka gil a bolzeŋ zɛɛ maa chɔɔ.
7Samaria hina vuga maanii
bá purgi burburbur,
di fuuh ba vuga dia
kuna maa
ani ba vuga maa.
Dikuu baŋ naa di lii sɛnsɛnna kinturgaa biinii wia,
gunnɛ bá kaa kpaa
ga turgi sɛnsɛnna yembɛl.
Wiraa ni biinichɔg wia
8Dikuu keŋ wia, mìŋ́ Maika daŋ lɔ wile, di ra wii,
di ra vol ni n naadumazi
ni chakpal, di ra bar.
N danna uuli alugɔ hohobia n na wii,
di kaa ra wii alugɔ kikiu.
9Ba wàá wer chaa
Samaria hina ŋmɛra.
Juda hina gba daŋ wa di
a keŋ tɔɔrɔɔ naa.
Chɔgaa jaa hel
Jɛrusalɛm dominuuzeŋ
himmaanii, bɔr la
n nɛra n duwɛɛ.
10Ií gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ Gaf hina be,
di gilɛɛ waa wii de gba.
Bɛf Ɔfra hina,
ií chɔɔ bumburi biini
di ra billi,
dikuu ii biinichɔg wia.
11Safir hina, ba daŋ wa lauri ia
ni ii chakpalli,
di kaali hɛrduma, ii di hiihzi.
Zaanan hina wàá kur
lii ba bolzeŋ.
Di ii wa nuu Bɛf Ɛzɛl hina n na wii,
ii daŋ zum lugɔ
suahribɔr waa hoo de.
12Marɔf hina chigɔɔ,
ba bɔra ra waazi,
di ra kpaŋ ba na lɛɛi,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ hɛhchɔg chol ba ni,
haali di ga hel
Jɛrusalɛm dominuuzeŋ
la gba.
13Ii banla ge n du Lakis,
ií lauri ii zagra vɔɔzi a laal torkozi ni.
Ii chanzi Izrɛl hina wichɔgaarɛ,
di gil Jɛrusalɛm hina
ɛɛ wichɔgaa.
14Awia, filaŋkeŋ, Juda hina,
ií ta Mɔrɛsɛf Gaf hina ŋmɛnɛɛ.
Izrɛl koora wàá ka na hiinaa,
lii Akzib hina be maa.
15Marɛsa hina,
Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa ia
du ii dɔma nonee,
bá ba wa foozi ii bol dɔɔ.
Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra daŋ la
ga suah Adulam bia bɔɔni.
16Juda hina, ií gbaari ii nyuuni alugɔ duuni,
dikuu ii biine n chɔkkɛ,
ii bichalli la iin nɔŋŋɛɛ wia.
Ba daŋ wa lauri baa yoma,
di kaali hɛrduma.

english_text:
Punishment for Those Who Abuse Their Power
1Doomed! You're doomed!
At night you lie in bed,
making evil plans.
And when morning comes,
you do what you've planned
because you have the power.
2You grab any field or house
that you want;
you cheat families
out of homes and land.
3But here is what the Lord says:
“I am planning trouble for you.
Your necks will be caught
in a noose,
and you will be disgraced
in this time of disaster.”
4When that happens,
this sorrowful song
will be sung about you:
“Ruined! Completely ruined!
The Lord has taken our land
and given it to traitors.”
5And so you will never again
own property
among the Lord's people.
6“Enough of your preaching!”
That's what you tell me.
“We won't be disgraced,
so stop preaching!”
7Descendants of Jacob,
is it right for you to claim
that the Lord did what he did
because he was angry?
Doesn't he always bless
those who do right?
8My people, you have turned against
one another!
You have even stolen
clothes right off the backs
of innocent neighbors
who pass by in peace.
9You take over lovely homes
that belong to the women
of my nation.
Then you cheat their children
out of the inheritance
that comes from the Lord.
10Get out of here, you crooks!
You'll find no rest here.
You're not fit to belong
to the Lord's people,
and you will be destroyed.
11The only prophet you want
is a liar who will say,
“Drink and get drunk!”
A Promise of Hope
12I, the Lord, promise
to bring together
the people of Israel
who have survived.
I will gather them,
just as a shepherd
brings sheep together,
and there will be many.
13I will break down the gate
and lead them out—
then I will be their king.
translation_text:
Banla n na sunni nyaara laba wia
1Wia daŋ wa huuzi banla
n ɔɔ chɔɔ hamuŋa ni,
di ra ta wichɔgaa ɛɛi jina la!
Di hɔɔ wa pizɔɔ, ba ɔɔ na bɔttɛ,
di jaa ra ɛɛ a wichɔgaa la
jina baŋ tawɛɛ la.
2Di koonii ba ra nyiŋŋi, ba ɔɔ foozaabuu.
Di diini genii ba ra nyiŋŋi,
guŋ himmaanii ba ɔɔ ɛɛ.
Nɛr maa waa ɔɔ dɔɔ u diahina
gɛɛ u kundɔɔlaa fɔŋŋa.
3Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N na ta hɛhchɔg jinaa ń wa ta ii ni,
ii bɛl maa wàá wer lii u biini.
Ii wàá ka wer na bɔr di ra vol barabara ni,
dikuubɛɛwiai, a saŋa
daŋ ɛɛ saŋa chuma.
4Di a hɔpizii wa hello, nɛra danna ɛɛ ia chɛɛtɛ,
di ɔɔ yir biinichɔg yir naa,
di ra ɛɛ ia chɛɛtɛ, di ra ŋɔ,
‘Yaa wiimaa chɔkkɔɔ tuŋ!
Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ yaa hɛrii,
tɛɛ nɛra la
n wa lauri yaa
kaali la.’ ”
5Awia, di a saŋa wa hello lugɔ bá kpa a hɛri bir tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra,
iawaa bɛl maa
wàá na u yemmaa.
Dɔgtɛɛkara hina wia
6Ba dɔgtɛɛzi ŋɔ,
“Gilɛɛ ra ŋɔ wia la
n niŋ wa huuzi yaa,
di ra du yaa ni,
hiihzi wàá kpu yaa.
7I fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi see
Izrɛl hinaa nuaa?
Kɔraawiizi kanyitti
dii tunnɔɔwaa?
Wibii maa, wàá sɛɛ ɛɛ
wia naa dɔŋa.
U ɔɔ ra ŋɔ wiarɛ bɔɔiih di ra tɛɛ
banla n na ɛɛ wideŋlaa.”
8Denii Kɔraawiizi bir ŋɔ,
“Ii ballɔɔ wa lɔ
n nɛra alugɔ ba dɔma.
N nɛra ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baala
n lii laal di ra ba, di ra fɛ lugɔ
ba dɔɔ bampirsɔnaa bol,
ka ii du de di ra kpaŋ,
ii foozi ba laala lii ba be.
9Ii duŋŋi n nɛra haanaa
lii ba diinanaa la
baŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ werge maa biine.
Ii tɔ ba biizii ŋmɛnɛɛ
lugɔ ba ŋmɛnɛ maa
wàá na n kissaa.
10Ií izi bɔnnaa kaali,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ii heezi
bɔr lɛi ɛŋ!
De doŋŋoo di puri,
waa kaa dɔɔ kuaraa maa.
11Nɛra naa ra nyiŋŋi dɔgtɛɛ la n na kanni karaa di ra dar nɛra,
di ɔɔ ra ŋɔ, ‘N na ŋɔu lugɔ
siŋ iri maa daŋ pur tɛɛ ia.’
12Wibii maa, n daŋ chaali ii maa, Izrɛl hina.
Wibii maa, n daŋ chaali
Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ.
N daŋ chaali baa alugɔ peeza n du a loŋ,
alugɔ peeza n du a diiribɔr,
nɛkpila werge daŋ su a bɔr.”
13Kɔraawiizi daŋ pilli ŋmɛnɛɛ tɛɛ baa,
di kpogli baa lii hɛrduma.
Ba daŋ kuugi a bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa,
di lii kaali.
Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ ba koori la,
daŋ tɔ ba see.

english_text:
Evil Rulers and Lying Prophets
1Listen to me,
you rulers of Israel!
You know right from wrong,
2but you prefer to do evil
instead of what is right.
You skin my people alive.
You strip off their flesh,
3break their bones,
cook it all in a pot,
and gulp it down.
4Someday you will beg the Lord
to help you,
but he will turn away
because of your sins.
5You lying prophets promise
security for anyone
who gives you food,
but disaster for anyone
who refuses to feed you.
Here is what the Lord says
to you prophets:
6“You will live in the dark,
far from the sight of the sun,
with no message from me.
7You prophets and fortunetellers
will all be disgraced,
with no message from me.”
8But the Lord has filled me
with power and his Spirit.
I have been given the courage
to speak about justice
and to tell you people of Israel
that you have sinned.
9So listen to my message,
you rulers of Israel!
You hate justice
and twist the truth.
10You make cruelty and murder
a way of life in Jerusalem.
11You leaders accept bribes
for dishonest decisions.
You priests and prophets
teach and preach,
but only for money.
Then you say,
“The Lord is on our side.
No harm will come to us.”
12 And so, because of you,
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple now stands.
translation_text:
Maika n hau Izrɛl sitɔɔra ni wia
1Denii mìŋ́ Maika ŋɔ,
“Izrɛl sitɔɔra, ií ra nuu!
A dɛkkɔɔ iinna di wibii,
2ka ii hah winanaarɛ,
ka nɔŋŋi wichɔgaa.
Ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ iiŋ lalli n nɛra bɔrahɔna,
di sih ba ola
lii ba hoga ni
alugɔ sechɔgaa.
3Ii hee n nɛraa,
di sih ba hɔna,
di purgi ba hoga maa.
Di mɔnni baa alugɔ ol,
bá kpa du gbɛɛrɛɛ.”
4Denii bá lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi,
ka wàá hagzi baa.
A saŋa hiŋ, u daŋ bir luŋ kpu baa,
dikuu ba wichɔgaa la
baŋ ɛɛwɛ wia.
5Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Dɔgtɛɛzi la waa,
n ɔɔ ra dar
n nɛra ba ra leu la,
di nɛr haŋ waa tɛɛ baa diwee,
ba ɔɔ ra sii bampirsɔna wiarɛ.
Ka di guŋ waa haŋ wa du de,
ba ɔɔ ra ɔnzuubuu ni laal.
6Awia, dɔgtɛɛzi, hamuŋa daŋ ba, ii wàá ka wer ra na wia lugɔ deeza biini.
Bɔr biri, ii wàá ka wer vug.
Wiizi daŋ chol tɛɛ dɔgtɛɛzi,
hɔpizaa biri tɛɛ baa.
7Hiihzi daŋ kpu sinaara,
vugra ge di hiihzi.
Ba maa daŋ tɔɔgi ba siwee,
dikuu baŋ waa
wiimaa nuuwɛ
lii Kɔraawiizi be wia.”
8Ka miŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ u Duma iziŋ,
di tɛŋ fɔŋŋa, n dɔɔ bɔkpega,
ń di wibii tɛɛ Izrɛl hina,
di bagli baa ba wichɔgaa.
9Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra,
ií ra nuu ɛŋ!
Ii hah wibii diire,
ka kpa kara birgi wibii.
10Ii kpa nɛkpui ni biinikpolaa,
di ma Jɛrusalɛm.
11Ii sitɔɔra ɔɔ lɛɛ kunaa, ka ra di seriya,
kizeehina ɔɔ bagli nɛra,
ka ra lɛɛ kebee.
Dɔgtɛɛzi ge ɔɔ ŋɔ wia
tɛɛ nɛra,
ka ra lɛɛ baa kebee.
Ka ba dɛlli Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ,
“Kɔraawiizi waa yaa be
duwɛɛ lɛiyaa?
Awia, hɛhchɔg maa
wàá chol yaa ni.”
12Dikuu ii wia.
Ba daŋ par Ziɔn alugɔ koo,
Jɛrusalɛm birgi hembugle di chɔɔ kulululu,
Kɔraawiizi Dia giŋgimii ge
birgi kɔr.

english_text:
Peace and Prosperity
1In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills,
and every nation
will rush to it.
2People of many nations
will come and say,
“Let's go up to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
3 He will settle arguments
between distant
and powerful nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never again make war
or attack one another.
4 Everyone will find rest
beneath their own fig trees
or grape vines,
and they will live in peace.
This is a solemn promise
of the Lord All-Powerful.
5Others may follow their gods,
but we will always follow
the Lord our God.
The Lord Will Lead His People Home
6The Lord said:
At that time
I will gather my people—
the lame and the outcasts,
and all others into whose lives
I have brought sorrow.
7Then the lame and the outcasts
will belong to my people
and become a strong nation.
I, the Lord, will rule them
from Mount Zion forever.
8Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
guardian of my people,
you will rule again.
9Jerusalem, why are you crying?
Don't you have a king?
Have your advisors gone?
Are you suffering
like a woman in childbirth?
10Keep on groaning with pain,
you people of Jerusalem!
If you escape from your city
to the countryside,
you will still be taken
as prisoners to Babylonia.
But later I will rescue you
from your enemies.
11Zion, because of your sins
you are surrounded
by many nations who say,
“We can hardly wait
to see you disgraced.”
12But they don't know
that I, the Lord,
have gathered them here
to grind them like grain.
13Smash them to pieces, Zion!
I'll let you be like a bull
with iron horns
and bronze hoofs.
Crush those nations
and bring their wealth to me,
the Lord of the earth.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi kora dii durnya ni daŋ gil bampirsɔna du de
1Saŋa bɛl n na ba,
a bizeŋ la baŋ ma
Kɔraawiizi Dia chiŋŋi
u nyuu la
daŋ la chiŋ kaali
anla maa n baruu la.
Durnya hɛssi nɛra maa waa nyiŋŋi u bɔr.
2Hɛrkpila hina maa daŋ ɔɔ ba de di wa ŋɔ,
“Ií ba ya tinni Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ,
di ga zuu Kɔraawiizi la
Izrɛl hina n na hum
la Dia biini.
Kɔraawiizi daŋ bagli yaa u widaulaa,
guŋ gil ya ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi.”
U Gbɔg daŋ lii Ziɔn,
u wiŋɔzi lii Bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm.
3U daŋ di hɛssi hina maa seriya,
hɛssi la hina n kpekke werge
kaluzii ú laafi.
A hɛssi maa hina daŋ kpa ba tokobizi
luu para,
di kpa ba kandaazi ge
luu daazi kɛuraa kizizi.
Laal maa daŋ tuŋ,
ba wàá kaa ra helli laal lɔi.
4Baal maa daŋ so u himmaa
grepu ni u fig
daa zɛɛ chunchugli,
ka nɛr maa wàá ka ɔnzuu,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.
5Aŋhinabe, hɛssi hina maanii
ninna hiŋ ba vuga,
ka yaawaa danna hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la
yaa n na hum,
di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
Kɔraawiizi jina wia
6Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ chaali gbɛraa,
di chaali banla maa
baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛrdumazi
ani banla miŋ gillɛ
ba biine chɔgi la.
7N daŋ gil banla n ɛɛ gbɛraa ka,
banla baŋ duŋŋɛɛ la ge
birgi hɛrkpeg hina.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii niŋ ɛɛ ba koori,
di lii Bizeŋ Ziɔn,
di lii a hɔl hiŋ,
di hanna la
saŋaa saŋa maa.”
8Ama, hiŋwaa Jɛrusalɛm, bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n duwɛɛ alugɔ penɔɔni,
di ra binni u nɛra ni la,
daŋ kaa ɛɛ kora la
n faa ɛɛ i hor la, bolzeŋ.
9Bɛɛwiarɛ i ra chɛɛhgi gunnɛi?
Haa koori dɔɔwɛ gɛɛ?
I bagli siuwɔɔ,
guŋ gil bɔwiila lawii
alugɔ hilula n lɔ haaŋ laa?
10Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií ra miŋŋi di ra hɛm,
gunla hilula n ɔɔ lɔ haaŋ la,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ii daŋ lii a bolzeŋ naa filaŋkeŋ,
di ga chɔɔ a bol laŋgara.
Ii daŋ la Babilɔn,
ka denii Kɔraawiizi
ga lɛɛ ia lii ii dɔma be.
11Ka filaŋkeŋ, hɛrkpila hina maanii chaalɛɛ,
bá lɔ ia laal.
Ba ra ŋɔu, “Jɛrusalɛm dɛg chɔgaarɛ!
Yaa daŋ na
a bolzeŋ naa puraa!”
12Ka ba waa Kɔraawiizi nfɛrɛ zummɛ,
ba waa kaa zum
u wilauraa ge ŋmɛnizi.
Ba waa zummɛ lugɔ
u chaali baabuu,
ú tɛr ba digna gunla
baŋ ɔɔ chaali mia dau,
bá lɔ la.
13Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Jɛrusalɛm hina,
ií izi di la ga tɛr
ii dɔma digna!
N daŋ tɛɛ ia fɔŋŋa, ii du kpeg
alugɔ nabal n dɔɔ
lugbia nyigzi
ani danyɛ naafiraa.
Ii daŋ kpegli hɛrkpila hina,
di foozi ba daama maa,
baŋ lɔ laal paagi,
di wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la
n na di kora
durnya maa ni la.”

english_text:
A Promised Ruler
1Jerusalem, enemy troops
have surrounded you;
they have struck Israel's ruler
in the face with a stick.
2 Bethlehem Ephrath,
you are one of the smallest towns
in the nation of Judah.
But the Lord will choose
one of your people
to rule the nation—
someone whose family
goes back to ancient times.
3The Lord will abandon Israel
only until this ruler is born,
and the rest of his family
returns to Israel.
4Like a shepherd
taking care of his sheep,
this ruler will lead
and care for his people
by the power and glorious name
of the Lord his God.
His people will live securely,
and the whole earth will know
his true greatness,
5because he will bring peace.
Assyria Will Be Defeated
Let Assyria attack our country
and our palaces.
We will counterattack,
led by a number of rulers
6 whose strong army will defeat
the nation of Assyria.
Yes, our leaders will rescue us,
if those Assyrians
dare to invade our land.
The Survivors Will Be Safe
7A few of Jacob's descendants
survived and are scattered
among the nations.
But the Lord will let them
cover the earth like dew and rain
that refreshes the soil.
8At present they are scattered,
but later they will attack,
as though they were fierce lions
pouncing on sheep.
Their enemies will be torn
to shreds,
with no one to save them;
9they will be helpless,
completely destroyed.
Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
10The Lord said:
At that time I will wipe out
your cavalry and chariots,
11as well as your cities
and your fortresses.
12I will stop you
from telling fortunes
and practicing witchcraft.
13You will no longer worship
the idols or stone images
you have made—
I will destroy them,
14together with the sacred poles
and even your towns.
15I will become furious
and take revenge on the nations
that refuse to obey me.
translation_text:
1Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií chaali ii laallɔɔra!
Ba fɔɔ yaabuu!
Ba daŋ kpa lugbidaa
chɛ Izrɛl koori lia.
Koori daŋ lii Bɛtlihɛm
2Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Juda hɛri bola maa boljiga Bɛtlihɛm naa n du Ɛfrata paga,
haali hiŋ du jiga Juda hina
domeezi maa biini gba,
ka i biinii ń lizi sitɔɔri,
ú ɛɛ Izrɛl koori.
U zɛɛ lii faa maanii.”
3Awia, Kɔraawiizi daŋ vɛɛ Izrɛl hina tɛɛ ba dɔma,
di ra ba saŋa la a haaŋ
n niŋ lul a keŋ biibaal naa.
Denii u lulla la n kawɛɛ,
jaa bir ba,
di wa jaa Izrɛl hina ni.
4Di u wa ballɔ, u daŋ kpa Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa
ni u girme di ra binni
u nɛra ni.
Ba daŋ du ni bampirsɔna, dikuubɛɛwiai,
durnya nɛra maa
daŋ sɛɛ u zenni,
5waabuu niŋ ba
bampirsɔna ni.
Lɛɛi ni dignitɛraa wia
Di Asiiria hina wa zuu yaa hɛri,
di zuu yaa diikpega biine,
yaa daŋ lizi yaa sitɔɔra la
n kpekke werge, bá lɔ baa.
6A sitɔɔra daŋ kpa dɔŋkuna,
di kpegli Asiiria
n ɛɛ Nimrɔd hɛri,
di lɛɛ yaa lii Asiiria hina be,
di ba wa zuu yaa hɛri.
7Izrɛl hina banla n kawɛɛ,
daŋ du nɛra biini
alugɔ ŋmɛnii n lii Kɔraawiizi be,
alugɔ dooŋ n ballɛ
du kooree ni.
Ba daŋ dɛlli Kɔraawiizi ni,
ka gil newea.
8Banla n kawɛɛ a hɛssi biine,
daŋ ɛɛ gunla bunyiŋ
n ɔɔ du kɔr ni
sela diiribɔr biine,
di ra nyiŋŋi diwee la.
U ɔɔ zuu peeza biinii, di ra lauraa, di ra chuuraa,
di gil a waa ɔɔ dɔɔ lɛɛi tamii.
9Guŋ himmaanii Izrɛl hina kpegli
ba dɔma, di kpu
ba maa nyaamm.
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ kpu ii zagra,
di chɔgi ii laal torkozi.
11N daŋ chɔgi ii hɛri bolzenaa,
di kaa purgi
ii diikpega maa.
12N daŋ chɔgi ii hiri,
ii wàá ka wer kpa ii hiri
ra bugmi nɛra.
13N daŋ chɔgi ii vugsɛɛhlaa
ani anla n ɛɛ bia,
ii wàá kaa ra togni kuna la
iiŋ kuarɛɛ.
14N daŋ wigzi ii vughaaŋ Asɛra daazi lii ii hɛri,
di chɔgi ii bolzenaa maa.
15Hɛssi la hina maa n wàá sɛɛ hiŋ n nua,
n daŋ kpa n baaŋfuuih
turgi baa ba wichɔgaa kim
werge maa.”

english_text:
The Lord's Challenge to His People
1The Lord said to his people:
Come and present your case
to the hills and mountains.
2Israel, I am bringing charges
against you—
I call upon the mountains
and the earth's firm foundation
to be my witnesses.
3My people, have I wronged you
in any way at all?
Please tell me.
4 I rescued you from Egypt,
where you were slaves.
I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
to be your leaders.
5 Don't forget the evil plans
of King Balak of Moab
or what Balaam son of Beor
said to him.
Remember how I, the Lord,
saved you many times
on your way from Acacia
to Gilgal.
True Obedience
6What offering should I bring
when I bow down to worship
the Lord God Most High?
Should I try to please him
by sacrificing
calves a year old?
7Will thousands of sheep
or rivers of olive oil
make God satisfied with me?
Should I sacrifice to the Lord
my first-born child as payment
for my terrible sins?
8The Lord God has told us
what is right
and what he demands:
“See that justice is done,
let mercy be your first concern,
and humbly obey your God.”
Cheating and Violence
9I am the Lord,
and you are wise to respect
my power to punish.
So listen to my message
for the city of Jerusalem:
10You store up stolen treasures
and use dishonest scales.
11But I, the Lord, will punish you
for cheating with weights
and with measures.
12You rich people are violent,
and everyone tells lies.
13Because of your sins,
I will wound you and leave you
ruined and defenseless.
14You will eat,
but still be hungry;
you will store up goods,
but lose everything—
I, the Lord, will let it all
be captured in war.
15You won't harvest what you plant
or use the oil
from your olive trees
or drink the wine
from grapes you grow.
16 Jerusalem, this will happen
because you followed
the sinful example
of kings Omri and Ahab.
Now I will destroy you
and your property.
Then the people of every nation
will make fun and insult you.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra n dɔɔ wia
1Ií ra nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n na ŋɔ ra du Izrɛl hina ni,
“Ií izi chi, di bagli ii wia bizenaa
ni giŋgimee maa nuu.
2Bizenaa, ií ra nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n na ŋɔ.
Hɛri zɛɛzi la n waa chɔgaa dɔɔwɛ,
di du de saŋa maa la,
ií ra nuu, dikuubɛɛwiai,
Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra dɔɔ wiarɛ,
u ra nyiŋŋuu
ú di baa seriya.”
3Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ,
“N nɛra, bɛɛ n ɛɛ iai?
Bɛɛ wiarɛ n wia zuu ii nyuunɛi?
Ií ŋɔ n nuu!
4N lizi iabuu lii Ijip hɛri,
di lɛɛ ia, ii waa kaa ɛɛ yoma.
N hum Moosis ni Aarɔn
ani Miriamnɛ, bá tɔ ii see.
5N nɛra, ií liizi gunla
Moab Koori Balak
n faa ta jina ú ɛɛ ia
ani gunla Bɛɔ biibaal Balaam
ge n faa bittɛ ŋɔ u be.
Ií ra liizi saŋa la iiŋ lii Sitim, di ra la Gilgal la.
Guŋ gil ii wer ra liizi
wia la miŋ ɛɛwɛ
di lɛɛ ia la.”
6Bɛɛ ń kpa wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n du u bol chiŋ,
di n wa ballɔ
n wa jaamuuwɛi?
Ń kpa napɔla la n wesse werge
di wa lizi mbusu,
di fuuah tɛu gɛɛ?
7Kɔraawiizi bɔra daŋ sɔɔni, di n kpa pebala kagboŋa di wa tɛu
gɛɛ nuu la n niŋ su
muuni kagboŋa fiaa?
Gɛɛ ń kpa n biinabɔma, di wa lizi mbusu tɛu,
dikuu n wichɔgaa wiaa?
8Akai, Kɔraawiizi bagli yaabuu gunla n wesse.
Wii la unna nyiŋŋi
yaa be maanii lugɔ
ya ra di wibii, di nɔŋŋi nɛra ni sunaa,
di ra hiŋuu ni sisɔna.
Izrɛl hina chɔgri ni ba dignitɛraa wia
9Nunzumaa Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa.
U yir Jɛrusalɛm hinaa
di ŋɔ ba be,
“Ií ra nuu,
ii banla n chaalɛɛ
bolzeŋ naa biini!
10Wichɔgɛɛra diini su daama
la baŋ fini nɛra di nau.
Ba ra mɛgzi kunaa fintime ni,
n hah gunnɛ.
11Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ gil tɛɛ banla
n na mɛgzi kuna
fintime ninɛi?
12Ii daama hina la ɔɔ ra foozi nyaaraa,
ii maa ɛɛ karkannaa.
13Awia, n ɛɛ siryaa ń kpu ia,
ii wia tuŋ,
dikuu ii wichɔgaa hiŋ wia.
14Ii daŋ ɔɔ di, ka ii wàá piŋ,
ii hizi haa woo.
Ii daŋ chaali ii kuna dau,
ka a maa bir pɛɛ.
N daŋ kpa laal,
di wa chɔgi kuna la maa
iiŋ chaalɛɛ dau la.
15Ii daŋ duu kuna,
ka ii wàá naa kum,
ii daŋ ɔɔ lizi ɔlivi nuu,
ka ii wàá naa fɔgli.
Ii daŋ ɔɔ purgi grepu nɔna di lizi a siŋ,
ka ii wàá nyɔɔa.
16Ii hiŋ Koori Ɔmri wichɔgaa widaulaa
ani u biibaal Koori Ahab biinikpola wiɛɛlaarɛ,
di kaa hiŋ ba naana wiɛɛlaa gba.
Awia, n daŋ chɔg ii wia,
dikuu guŋ wia.
Nɛr maa ra gbɛlli ia,
di hah ia.”

english_text:
Israel Is Corrupt
1I feel so empty inside—
like someone starving
for grapes or figs,
after the vines and trees
have all been picked clean.
2No one is loyal to God;
no one does right.
Everyone is brutal
and eager to deceive
everyone else.
3People cooperate to commit crime.
Judges and leaders demand bribes,
and rulers cheat in court.
4The most honest of them
is worse than a thorn patch.
Your doom has come!
Lookouts sound the warning,
and everyone panics.
5Don't trust anyone,
not even your best friend,
and be careful what you say
to the one you love.
6 Sons refuse to respect
their own fathers,
daughters rebel against
their own mothers,
and daughters-in-law despise
their mothers-in-law.
Your family is now your enemy.
7But I trust the Lord God
to save me,
and I will wait for him
to answer my prayer.
The Nation Turns to God
8My enemies, don't be glad
because of my troubles!
I may have fallen,
but I will get up;
I may be sitting in the dark,
but the Lord is my light.
9I have sinned against the Lord.
And so I must endure his anger,
until he comes to my defense.
But I know that I will see him
making things right for me
and leading me to the light.
10You, my enemies, said,
“The Lord God is helpless.”
Now each of you
will be disgraced
and put to shame.
I will see you trampled
like mud in the street.
A Bright Future
11Towns of Judah, the day is coming
when your walls will be rebuilt,
and your boundaries enlarged.
12People will flock to you
from Assyria and Egypt,
from Babylonia
and everywhere else.
13Those nations will suffer disaster
because of what they did.
Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
14Lead your people, Lord!
Come and be our shepherd.
Grasslands surround us,
but we live in a forest.
So lead us to Bashan and Gilead,
and let us find pasture
as we did long ago.
15I, the Lord, will work miracles
just as I did when I led you
out of Egypt.
16Nations will see this
and be ashamed because
of their helpless armies.
They will be in shock,
unable to speak or hear,
17because of their fear of me,
your Lord and God.
Then they will come trembling,
crawling out of their fortresses
like insects or snakes,
lapping up the dust.
No One Is Like God
The people said:
18Our God, no one is like you.
We are all that is left
of your chosen people,
and you freely forgive
our sin and guilt.
You don't stay angry forever;
you're glad to have pity
19and pleased to be merciful.
You will trample on our sins
and throw them in the sea.
20You will keep your word
and be faithful to Jacob
and to Abraham,
as you promised our ancestors
many years ago.
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina dɔgnya dii wia
1N biini chɔkkɔɔ werge maa!
N ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr la n ɔɔ ra tɔrgi daazi nɔna,
á bii saŋa, ka màá naa di.
Grepuzi waa hoo ń di,
haali lugli figzi la
minna kɛlli gba.
2Nɛr maa waa hoo a hɛri naa biini,
u wia dɔɔ wibii.
Nɛr maa ge gba waa hoo,
u wia deŋli.
Bɛl maanii ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi ú na bɔr kpu nɛr.
Bɛl maa ra he u lulli sidɛɛ.
3Ba maanii zum wichɔgaa ɛɛi werge.
Ba nabɔnzi ni sitɔɔra
ɔɔ ra lɛɛ kunaa.
Nɛtɔga ra bagli ba kipar,
awia, ba ni baa
jaa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ,
di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa.
4Haali ba nɛnanaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ sɔɔhri,
banla wia n dɔɔ wibii
ge du guŋ.
Hɔpizii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ tɛr u nɛra digna helloo
gunla uŋ ga
u dɔgtɛɛzi la n ɛɛ
ba guure be, di ŋɔ la.
Filaŋkeŋ, ba jaa bugmuu.
5Gilɛɛ waa yardi i dɔŋhiŋ,
gilɛɛ waa dɛlli i dammu.
Haali i haaŋ gba be,
a du i wiŋɔzi tau.
6Biibaal ra gbɛlli u mɛɛrɛ,
biihaaŋ kpa u maa
birgi u dɔm,
haaŋ kpa u hilahaaŋ birgi u dɔm,
baal ge dɔma ɛɛ
u himmaa diahina.
7Ka miŋwaa, Kɔraawiizii n na binni ni tamii.
N danna kpaŋ Kɔraawiizi la
minna hum n ɛɛ n Lɛɛri labuu.
Kɔraawiizi la minna hum,
daŋ nuu n be.
Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lɛɛ u nɛra wia
8N dɔma, ií gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra sɔɔni!
Haali miŋ cholle naa gba,
ka n daŋ kaa izi.
Haali miŋ soge bɔbiri biini naa gba,
ka Kɔraawiizii niŋ
ɛɛ n bɔchaaŋ.
9Dikuu miŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni wia,
n daŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ dikuu u
baaŋfuuih wia
guŋŋ u wa lɛɛŋ,
di gil n wia deŋli.
U daŋ liziŋ du bɔchaaŋ biini,
ń na u wideŋlaa.
10N dɔm daŋ na guŋ,
hiihzi kpuu.
Unla n ŋɔ n be,
“Lee Kɔraawiizi la
hinna hum la duɛi?”
N daŋ na u cholaa.
Haali filaŋkeŋ gba,
ba daŋ fɛrguu ni naazi
alugɔ kpɛchɛgaa,
ŋmɛnizenaa biine.
11Jɛrusalɛm hina, saŋa la iin niŋ bir kuari ii bolzeŋ koŋlaa ma la daŋ ba.
Hɔpizii la iin niŋ yaa
ii hɛri jaa la.
12A hɔpizii hiŋ, nɛra daŋ lii Asiiria
ni Ijip bolzenaa di ba ii be.
Haali di lii Ijip di ga hel Muu Yufretis,
di lii muuzeŋ bɛl
di ga hel bɛl,
di lii bizeŋ bɛl di ga hel bɛl.
13Ka a hɛri daŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ, nɛr maa wàá ka du de,
dikuu banla n du de la
wichɔgaa wia.
Kɔraawiizi n suŋ Izrɛl hina ni wia
14N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, kpa i daŋkpala alugɔ penɔɔni,
di ra binni i nɛra la
n lugɔ peeza ni.
Ba ɛɛ i kapɛttɛ kunaa, ka du kɔr biini ba bɛŋ,
sela diiribɔr la n summɛ biini.
Gil ba du Basan ni Giliad sela diiribɔra la n summɛ,
di ra di bahinaa
gunla baŋ faa du de,
faala maa la.
15N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, ɛɛ wizenaa tɛɛ yaa gunla hiŋ faa ɛɛwɛ,
saŋa la hiŋ lizi yaa
lii Ijip la.
16Hɛssi hina daŋ na guŋ, hiihzi kpu baa,
ba wàá ka dɔɔ fɔŋŋa.
Ba daŋ kpa ba nonee fɔɔ ba nuuzi,
bá digna ge taŋzi.
17Ba danna lenni hɛɛhraa, alugɔ hɛrikuŋ
gɛɛ kuntuuzaa.
Ba daŋ lii ba chɔɔribɔra ni ɔnsii ani bɔsai,
di bir ba hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la
yaa n na hum la be.
18Nɛr maa waa hoo lugɔ hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.
Hinla n ɔɔ gil
i nɛra la n kawɛɛ
wichɔgaa di ra tɛɛ baa la.
Haa ɔɔ na baaŋ di hanna la,
ka nɔŋŋi nɛra ni sunaa.
19I daŋ kaa suŋ yaa ni,
di fɛrgi yaa
wichɔgaa ni naazi,
di gbaaraa ga ha
muuzeŋ vile biine!
20I daŋ bagli i wibii dɔɔi ni i nɛsunaa dɔɔi,
tɛɛ Jekɔb ni Abraham naanna,
gunla hiŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ yaa naabaala,
di lii faala maa la.

english_text:
1 I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh.
The Fierce Anger of the Lord
2The Lord God demands loyalty.
In his anger, he takes revenge
on his enemies.
3The Lord is powerful,
yet patient;
he makes sure that the guilty
are always punished.
He can be seen in storms
and in whirlwinds;
clouds are the dust from his feet.
4At the Lord's command,
oceans and rivers dry up.
Bashan, Mount Carmel,
and Lebanon wither,
and their flowers fade.
5At the sight of the Lord,
mountains and hills
tremble and melt;
the earth and its people
shudder and shake.
6Who can stand the heat
of his furious anger?
It flashes out like fire
and shatters stones.
The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
7The Lord is good.
He protects those who trust him
in times of trouble.
8But like a roaring flood,
the Lord chases his enemies
into dark places
and destroys them.
9So don't plot against the Lord!
He wipes out his enemies,
and they never revive.
10They are like drunkards
overcome by wine,
or like twisted thornbushes
burning in a fire.
11Assyria, one of your rulers
has made evil plans
against the Lord.
12But the Lord says, “Assyria,
no matter how strong you are,
you will be cut down!
My people Judah,
I have troubled you before,
but I won't do it again.
13I'll snap your chains
and set you free
from the Assyrians.”
14Assyria, this is what else
the Lord says to you:
“Your name will be forgotten.
I will destroy every idol
in your temple,
and I will send you to the grave,
because you are worthless.”
15 Look toward the mountains,
people of Judah!
Here comes a messenger
with good news of peace.
Celebrate your festivals.
Keep your promises to God.
Your evil enemies are destroyed
and will never again
invade your country.
translation_text:
1Bolzeŋ Ninɛvɛ wia la Kɔraawiizi n pillɛɛ bagli Ɛlkɔs hinuu Nahum lugɔ deeza biini, u sɛbi dawuu keŋ.
Kɔraawiizi baaŋ n fuuh Ninɛvɛ hina ni wia
2Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ zoma hinnɛ, di ɔɔ ra turgi u dɔma ba wichɔgaa kim,
di ɔɔ ra tɔɔri banla n na
karsuu ni baaŋfuuih
werge maa.
3Kɔraawiizi baaŋ waa ɔɔ ra fuuh manamanaŋ, ka u ɛɛ fɔŋŋa hinnɛ werge,
waa ɔɔ gil banla
n dɔɔ bilchɔg pɛɛ,
di waa ba digna tɛttɛ.
U vollibɔr maa ɔɔ dɔɔ vem ni dooŋ pekpegre,
baamazi ge ɛɛ u naazi nyɔɔ.
4U ɔɔ ŋɔ wiarɛ fɔŋŋa ni, muuzeŋ hil,
di gil muuni maa hil.
Basan ni Bizeŋ Kamɛl hɛssi kuna maa yɔl,
Lɛbanɔn hɛri ge fiiri maa sizi.
5Bizenaa ɔɔ ra zigluu u see,
giŋgimee ge ŋmɛɛri kaali.
Hɛri ɔɔ ra zigluu kpikpikpi, di u wa ballɔ,
haali durnya ni kuna la
maa n du u biini.
6Di u baaŋ wa fuuhwo werge, anɛɛ n niŋ wer chi u seei?
U ɔɔ ra diu alugɔ niŋ,
bia ɔɔ purguu
burburbur u see.
7Kɔraawiizi wessoo,
di ra guu u nɛra
tɔɔrɔɔ saŋazi.
U ɔɔ ra binni banla n yarduubuu.
8U daŋ chɔgi bolzeŋ Ninɛvɛ nyaamm
alugɔ nii n suwee di ra lɔ werge,
di ɔɔ chɔgi kuna la.
U daŋ duŋŋi u dɔma
du bɔbiri biini.
9Wia la maa baŋ vɔɔwɛ bá ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la,
u daŋ gil a maa tuŋ.
Tɔɔrɔɔ wàá ka ba bunɛɛhiŋ.
10Ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ sɔɔhri n mil baa,
di nyɔɔ siŋ dɛɛzi,
niŋ fuuh baa alugɔ kɔlhilaa.
11Ee, Ninɛvɛ hina, nɛbɛl n dɔɔ biinikpola werge lii ii biinii,
di ra vɔɔ jina ú ɛɛ
Kɔraawiizi wichɔgaa,
di ra bagli nɛra
wichɔgaa ŋmɛnizi.
12Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u nɛra Izrɛl hina be,
“Haali Asiiria hina n dɔɔ nɛra werge di du kpeg,
ka n daŋ kpu baa
bá wia tuŋ.
Hoi, Juda hina, haali miŋ tɔɔri ia la gba,
màá ka ɛɛ ia guŋ maa.
13Filaŋkeŋ, n daŋ chɔgi fɔŋŋa la baŋ dɔɔwɛ ii ni la,
di chaahzi yɔlɔzi la
n vɔɔzi ia la ha.”
14Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wiŋɔkpeg bɛllɛ dikuu ii Ninɛvɛ hina wia,
“Ií wàá dɔɔ naanna
bá ra liizi ii wia.
N daŋ chɔgi ii vugsɛɛhlaa ni a luulaa la
n du ii vuga diini biine la.
N daŋ ki ii bɔɔni dau,
dikuu iiŋ chummɛ
werge wia.”
15Ií binni bizenaa nyuuni na,
nɛbɛllɛ kpogli amaniyesuma
di vol ra ba,
unla n na sii bampirsɔna wia!
Juda hina, ií ra di ii hɔpizizenaa,
di kpa kuna la maa
iiŋ ŋɔ nuuzi
lugɔ ii daŋ tɛɛ
Kɔraawiizi la tɛu.
Biinikpola hina wàá ka zuu ii hɛri
di lɔ ia laal maa,
n daŋ kpu baa nyaamm.

english_text:
Nineveh Will Fall
1Nineveh, someone is coming
to attack and scatter you.
Guard your fortresses!
Watch the road! Be brave!
Prepare for battle!
2Judah and Israel are like trees
with branches broken
by their enemies.
But the Lord is going to restore
their power and glory.
* 3Nineveh, on this day of attack,
your enemies' shields are red;
their uniforms are crimson.
4Their horses prance,
and their armored chariots
dart around like lightning
or flaming torches.
5An officer gives a command.
But his soldiers stumble,
as they hasten to build
a shelter to protect themselves
against rocks thrown down
from the city wall.
6The river gates fly open,
and panic floods the palace.
7Nineveh is disgraced.
The queen is dragged off.
Her servant women mourn;
they moan like doves,
and they beat their breasts
in sorrow.
8Nineveh is like a pond
with leaking water.
Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!”
can be heard everywhere.
But everyone is leaving.
9Enemy soldiers shout,
“The city is full of treasure
and all kinds of wealth.
Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
10Nineveh is doomed! Destroyed!
Her people tremble with fear;
their faces turn pale.
11What happened to this city?
They were safer there
than powerful lions in a den,
with no one to disturb them.
12These are the same lions
that ferociously attacked
their victims,
then dragged away the flesh
to feed their young.
13The Lord All-Powerful
is against you, Nineveh.
God will burn your chariots
and send an army to kill
those young lions of yours.
You will never again
make victims of others
or send messengers to threaten
everyone on this earth.
translation_text:
Bolzeŋ Ninɛvɛ cholaa wia
1Ninɛvɛ hina, nɛbɛl ra bau ú wa lɔ ia laal.
Ií ra guu ii diikpega,
ií ra binni ŋmɛnɛɛ
di ra du tau nɛnnɛ,
ií ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya.
2Kɔraawiizi daŋ kaa gil Izrɛl wessi ni u girme la bir ba,
haali chɔgra n wa chɔgi
u maa, di chɔgi
ba kundɔɔlaa maa
alugɔ baŋ kaari
grepu daa nɔna la gba.
3Ninɛvɛ hina dɔma laallɔɔra pɛrɛtuzenaa aahwɔɔ lugɔ chal.
Ba laala ge aah choihchoih.
Ba laal torkozi lugbia ra nyɛgzuu
a hɔl la baŋ ɛɛ a sirya la.
Ba ra viigi
ba daananaa kandaazii
di ra ɔnzi baa.
4Ba zagra ni laal torkozi ni a tinna du a bol baaŋ ni u ŋmɛnibizii di ra chɔ werge maa,
di yali siwee ra la see,
di ra ba har bɔr maa.
Ba duwɔɔrɛ lugɔ kacheela n na lau niŋ,
di ra chɔ manamanaŋ
alugɔ dooŋ nyɛgzaa.
5Ninɛvɛ hina nabɔma chaali ú laallɔɔra la n kpekke nɛnnɛɛ,
ka ba du ŋmɛnɛɛ
di ra lɔɔzi naazi.
Ba kiiri hel a bolzeŋ koŋliizeŋ,
bá kuari kuŋ
di gber bahinaa.
6Ba pilli muugberzenaa la,
ba kooridia chol
purgi burburbur.
7Hiihzi kpu Ninɛvɛ hinaa,
ba lau ba wichee kaali.
U balaa ra wii lugɔ kommazi,
di ra lɔɔzi ba bampiree
ni biinichɔg.
8Ninɛvɛ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ gbatar,
u nii ra hiihzi.
U nɛra wii di ra ŋɔ, “Ií chi! Ií chi!”
Ka nɛr maa waa har bittɛ.
9Ií paagi ba saliŋhuŋŋa,
di paagi ba salma!
Ba kundɔɔlaa waa maga dɔɔwɛ,
daamaa su a bol maa.
10Ba ŋmɛɛubuu, di foozuu, di wiruu. Ninɛvɛ chɔkkɔɔ, ba paa u kuna maa kpɛlɛŋ!
U nɛra bɔra huah,
ɔnsii lau baa werge,
ba naahiine yɔɔri,
ba bɔra ra sa,
ba siwee maa huuhzi,
di chogli wogliwogli.
11Ninɛvɛ hina faa du ba bolzeŋ biinii alugɔ bunyinzi n du a duuribɔr,
di ra dɛɛzi a biizi.
Denii bunyiŋ bal ni u niina ɔɔ la,
a biizi faa waa
kaa ra ɔm kummaa.
12Ba faa duwɔɔrɛ alugɔ bunyiŋ n ɔɔ kpu sela nɛnnɛ di ra tɛɛ u biizi,
di piili a sela ra tɛɛ u haaŋ,
ola su ú chɔɔribɔr maa.
13Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔ Ninɛvɛ hina benii,
“N chigɔ ii ninɛɛ.
N daŋ fuuh ii laal torkozi, nyɔɔzi tɔ bɔr maa,
bá kpu ii laallɔɔra maa
laal biini.
N daŋ paa kuna la maa
iiŋ faa paawɛ lii nɛra be la.
Ba wàá ka nuu i balaa loobee
á ra du baa ɔnsii.”

english_text:
Punishment for Nineveh
The Lord said:
1Doom to the crime capital!
Nineveh, city of murder
and treachery,
2here is your fate—
cracking whips,
churning wheels;
galloping horses,
roaring chariots;
3cavalry attacking,
swords and spears flashing;
soldiers stumbling
over piles of dead bodies.
4You were nothing more
than a prostitute
using your magical charms
and witchcraft
to attract and trap nations.
5But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am now your enemy.
I will pull up your skirt
and let nations and kingdoms
stare at your nakedness.
6I will cover you with garbage,
treat you like trash,
and rub you in the dirt.
7Everyone who sees you
will turn away and shout,
“Nineveh is done for!
Is anyone willing to mourn
or to give her comfort?”
Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
8Nineveh, do you feel safer
than the city of Thebes?
The Nile River
was its wall of defense.
9Thebes trusted the mighty power
of Ethiopia and Egypt;
the nations of Put and Libya
were her allies.
10But she was captured and taken
to a foreign country.
Her children were murdered
at every street corner.
The members of her royal family
were auctioned off,
and her high officials
were bound in chains.
11Nineveh, now it's your turn!
You will get drunk and try to hide
from your enemy.
12Your fortresses are fig trees
with ripe figs.
Merely shake the trees,
and fruit will fall
into every open mouth.
13Your army is weak.
Fire has destroyed the crossbars
on your city gates;
now they stand wide open
to your enemy.
14Your city is under attack.
Haul in extra water!
Strengthen your defenses!
Start making bricks!
Stir the mortar!
15You will still go up in flames
and be cut down by swords
that will wipe you out like a field
attacked by grasshoppers.
So, go ahead and increase
like a swarm of locusts!
16More merchants are in your city
than there are stars
in the sky—
but they are like locusts
that eat everything,
then fly away.
17Your guards and your officials
are swarms of locusts.
On a chilly day
they settle on a fence,
but when the sun comes out,
they take off
to who-knows-where.
18King of Assyria,
your officials and leaders
are sound asleep,
while your people are scattered
in the mountains.
Yes, your people are sheep
without a shepherd.
19You're fatally wounded.
There's no hope for you.
But everyone claps
when they hear this news,
because your constant cruelty
has caused them pain.
translation_text:
Wiarɛ huuzi Ninɛvɛ hina
1Wiarɛ huuzi kara ni
nɛkpuura bolzeŋ la
daama n suwee,
bá wa ŋmɛɛ di foozi la!
2Ií ra nuu virinzi gbɔgza,
chira kɔɔi,
zagra n na chɔ di zaahzi ra chiiri,
ani laal torkozi gbɔga!
3Zagtinna lii fɔŋŋa ni bá lɔ laal,
ba tokobizi ra nyɛgzi
pilpilpil,
ba kandaazi ra
nyɛgzi pilpilpil!
Nɛra na pira bɔr maa.
Lalaa chɔɔ sagzi dɔŋa ni
kulululu bɔr maa,
ba waa maga dɔɔwɛ,
nɛra ra gargi baa di ra jiŋli!
4Annii maa ɛɛwɔɔ dikuu Ninɛvɛ n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ sɛnsɛnni wia,
di gil vugra kpa kabirɛzi
di ra vɔɔzi nɛra,
di gil u sɛnsɛŋ ni hiri birgi
hɛssi hina yoma.
5Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N chigɛ i ninɛɛ.
N daŋ wirii,
di gil hɛssi hina na i chakpal
ani i hiihzi dii.
6N daŋ kpa doŋa werge ta i ni,
màá ka kpai su siwii,
di gil nɛra ra kɔɔi.
7Banla maa n niŋ nai daŋ chɔ lii i be, ka ŋɔ,
‘Ninɛvɛ puroore,
anɛɛ n niŋ wii tɛuwɛi?’
Anɛɛ ń na u tig
u bampiriiyei?”
8Hinuu bɔ Tɛbɛs la
n chɔɔ Muu Naal nua,
nii baruu laa?
A muurɛ faa gberuu
u nii faa ɛɛ lugɔ koŋlii la.
9Itiopia ni Ijip hinaa faa ɛɛ Tɛbɛs fɔŋŋazeŋ.
Put ni Libia hina faa jaa u ni
banla n ɛɛ nuukpaŋ biinii.
10Ka ba faa wa kpegli Tɛbɛs,
di lau u nɛra kaali hɛrduma.
Ba faa kpu ba biizii ha
ŋmɛnichechemazi maa.
Ba ta kuna lugɔ bee di bɔnni ba nabɔnzenaa,
di kpa yɔlɔzi vɔɔzi
ba nɛzenaa maa.
11Ninɛvɛ hina ge gba daŋ dɛɛzi,
di chɔ ga suah,
di suŋŋi ba dɔma
bá lau baa suah.
12I diikpega la maa n na gberii la ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ fig daazi la
nɔna n luglɛɛ ra aah.
Di ba wa zagaa,
a ɔɔ chogli a diiri nua biinii.
13Binni i laallɔɔra na,
ba maa birgi haanaa!
I hɛri dominuuzenaa
pillɔɔrɛ chɔɔ tɛɛ i dɔma.
Niŋ di a dominuuzi
lugbidaazi maa.
14Ií dɔɔ nii tɛɛ iihinaa, dikuu ii fɔɔi wia,
di kuari ii diikpega
a du kpeg nɛnnɛ!
Ií gbɛr hɛɛhraa,
di fɛrgaa á lau nɛnnɛ,
di ɛɛ birkissi dakkazi sirya,
di mɔnni birkissizi.
15Denii niŋ wa di ia,
ba daŋ kpa tokobi kpu ia,
di di ia alugɔ huuhni.
Ií gil ii nɛra wazi lugɔ huuhni,
di gil ii nɛra wazi lugɔ lotorozi!
16Ii gillɔɔ ii kɔkɔɔza wazi di ra jaa,
di du kpil
kaali chinchinwilaa,
ka ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ lotorozi n di hɛri kuna maa nyaamm,
ka zaah kaali la.
17Ii guure ni ii nabɔnzi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ lotorozi kpila werge maa
n zuu koŋlaa fɔɔliizi
waari hɔpizii,
ka di wiizi wa futtɔ, a ɔɔ zaah kaali,
nɛr maa waa ɔɔ zum
bɔr la aŋ kaalɛɛ.
18Asiiria koorizeŋ, i senɔɔna gɛɛ koora chɔɔ dɔɔrɛ,
i nabɔnzenaa chɔɔ
di ra heezi.
I nɛra yaari bizenaa nyuuni,
ka nɛr maa waa hoo
ú chaali baa.
19Kummaa wàá wer chaa i ŋmɛr,
i pira la daŋ kpui.
Nɛr la maa n niŋ nuu i wia,
daŋ lɔ kpaa dikuu
i cholaa wia.
Nɛr maa di tɔɔrɔɔrɛ
dikuu i sihilii werge wia.

english_text:
1I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me.
Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
2Our Lord, how long must I beg
for your help
before you listen?
How long before you save us
from all this violence?
3Why do you make me watch
such terrible injustice?
Why do you allow violence,
lawlessness, crime, and cruelty
to spread everywhere?
4Laws cannot be enforced;
justice is always the loser;
criminals crowd out honest people
and twist the laws around.
The Lord Answers Habakkuk
5 Look and be amazed
at what's happening
among the nations!
Even if you were told,
you would never believe
what's taking place now.
6 I am sending the Babylonians.
They are fierce and cruel—
marching across the land,
conquering cities and towns.
7How fearsome and frightening.
Their only laws and rules
are the ones they make up.
8Their cavalry troops are faster
than leopards,
more ferocious than wolves
hunting at sunset,
and swifter than hungry eagles
suddenly swooping down.
9They are eager to destroy,
and they gather captives
like handfuls of sand.
10They make fun of rulers
and laugh at fortresses,
while building dirt mounds
so they can capture cities.
11Then suddenly they disappear
like a gust of wind—
those sinful people who worship
their own strength.
Habakkuk Complains Again
12Holy Lord God, mighty rock,
you are eternal,
and we are safe from death.
You are using those Babylonians
to judge and punish others.
13But you can't stand sin or wrong.
So don't sit by in silence
while they gobble up people
who are better than they are.
14The people you put on this earth
are like fish or reptiles
without a leader.
15Then an enemy comes along
and takes them captive
with hooks and nets.
It makes him so happy
16that he offers sacrifices
to his fishing nets,
because they make him rich
and provide choice foods.
17Will he keep hauling in his nets
and destroying nations
without showing mercy?
translation_text:
1Wia la Kɔraawiizi n pillɛɛ bagli u dɔgtɛɛ Habakuk labuu keŋ.
Habakuk nuumaa wia
2N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, ɛrɛɛ ń yirii di birgi mag lugɔ i hiiniŋ,
ka i haa nuuwɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ ń chɛɛhgi dui birgi mag lugɔ í mɔgli yaa lii nɛra la n na sunni yaa werge la be,
ka i haa mɔgli yaai?
3Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i gil n na wibii nyaaiyɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ nɛra ra ɛɛ
wichɔgaa ka haa ra hagzɛi?
Kalu ni naari bariŋ bɔr maa,
di ra chɔgi kuna.
4Awia, gbɔg maa waa kaa ra hum,
wibii dii wàá
ka wer kpegli wichɔgaa.
Biinikpola hina ra tɔ nɛra la wia n deŋleere ŋmɛnɛɛ,
guŋ gil ba waa
kaa ra di wibii.
Kɔraawiizi n bittɛ ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Habakuk wia
5Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u nɛra be,
“Ií binni hɛssi hina,
di pessi baa na,
ii nuuzi daŋ kpu.
N daŋ ɛɛ wii bɛl ii de dui saŋa naa
iiŋ wàá yardi,
haali di ba kali ia gba.
6N na lizi Babilɔn hinaa bá ɛɛ n kipar,
ba ɛɛ sihilii hinaa,
ba waa nɛra
sinyɛna ra na,
ba gbaŋŋɔɔ di ra yoo durnya maa,
bá foozi nɛra
duuribɔra la
n waa ba hora ɛɛwɛ.
7Ba ɛɛ nɛra la wia n dɔɔ ɔnsiirɛ werge maa.
Ba himmaa gbɔgnii
ba ra hiŋ,
di ra tɔgzi bahinaa.
8Ba zagra gbaŋŋɔɔ kaali amanizi,
di du nyɛg kaali munuzi la
lɔzi n na kpu duana ni.
Ba zagra la nɛra n tinnɛɛ lalli a nyuunii, di chɔ zaahzi ra chiiri,
ba zagtinna lii bɔɔnɛɛrɛ di ba.
Ba ra chɔ fɔŋŋa ni
alugɔ duu siwii n ɔɔ aah,
u zaah di ra bar,
ka ú tuu di la.
