9Babilɔn hina ra bau, bá wa chɔgi.
Ba laallɔɔrakpila chɔgi kuna, di ra ba alugɔ hɛribɔduma peu,
di ra chaali nɛra la
baŋ laurɛɛ laal biini,
ba du kpil
alugɔ hɛɛhriichaa.
10Ba ra ɛɛ kooraa chɛɛtɛ,
di ra lɔ hɛssi
nabɔnzi mɔmɔsia.
Ba ra gbɛlli bolkpega la baŋ ma koŋlaa baraa maanii,
di ta pizenaa pɛli a koŋlaa,
di wer tinnaa tuu,
di lauri a bol nɛra.
11Denii ba ɔɔ lii de kaali fɔŋŋa ni alugɔ peu n tawɛɛ ra kaali.
Ba ɛɛ nɛra la n dɔɔ chɔgrii,
di ra tɔgzi bahinaa
alugɔ baŋ ɛɛ vuga.”
Habakuk nuumaa nɛɛhiŋ wia
12Kɔraawiizi, saŋa maa lɛi i du dee?
Kɔraawiizi la minna hum,
i ɛɛ Naniinaniirɛ,
haa luglaa ni tunaa dɔɔwɛ,
hàá gil ya siu.
N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i lizi Babilɔn hinaa, bá wa di yaa seriya.
I ɛɛ Bikpegre tɛɛ yaa.
I lizi baabuu bá wa
tɛr yaa digna.
13I ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ, hàá sɛɛ binni wichɔgaa.
Hàá wichɔgaa wia ra sɛɛ.
Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra sɛɛ biinikpola hina wiai?
Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i siigi
ka biinikpola hina
ra chɔgi nɛra la wia
n deŋlee kaali baai?
14I gillɔɔ nɛra du lugɔ nyinni n du muuzeŋ biini,
lugɔ muuzeŋ biini kunnyinee
n waa binni dɔɔwɛ la.
15Ba dɔma Babilɔn hina kpa gɔrgazii lauri ba maa alugɔ nyinni,
di kpa ba asauzi lauri baa,
di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.
16Awia, ba kpu kunaa lizi mbusu di ra tɛɛ ba asauzi,
di fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma
ra tɛɛa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba asauzii ra tɛɛ baa ba kunnyiŋŋaa maa,
ba ra di ba kipar diusuma.
17I daŋ gil ba hanna kpu nɛra alugɔ nyinni,
di ra kpu hɛssi
hina sikpegii nii?

english_text:
The Lord Answers Habakkuk Again
1While standing guard
on the watchtower,
I waited for the Lord's answer,
before explaining the reason
for my complaint.
2Then the Lord told me:
“I will give you my message
in the form of a vision.
Write it clearly enough
to be read at a glance.
3 At the time I have decided,
my words will come true.
You can trust what I say
about the future.
It may take a long time,
but keep on waiting—
it will happen!
4 “I, the Lord, refuse to accept
anyone who is proud.
Only those who live by faith
are acceptable to me.”
Trouble for Evil People
5Wine is treacherous,
and arrogant people
are never satisfied.
They are no less greedy
than death itself—
they open their mouths as wide
as the world of the dead
and swallow everyone.
6But they will be mocked
with these words:
You're doomed!
You stored up stolen goods
and cheated others
of what belonged to them.
7But without warning,
those you owe
will demand payment.
Then you will become
a frightened victim.
8You robbed cities and nations
everywhere on earth
and murdered their people.
Now those who survived
will be as cruel to you.
9You're doomed!
You made your family rich
at the expense of others.
You even said to yourself,
“I'm above the law.”
10But you will bring shame
on your family
and ruin to yourself
for what you did to others.
11The very stones and wood
in your home
will testify against you.
12You're doomed! You built a city
on crime and violence.
13 But the Lord All-Powerful
sends up in flames
what nations and people
work so hard to gain.
14 Just as water fills the sea,
the land will be filled
with people who know
and honor the Lord.
15You're doomed!
You get your friends drunk,
just to see them naked.
16Now you will be disgraced
instead of praised.
The Lord will make you drunk,
and when others see you naked,
you will lose their respect.
17You destroyed trees and animals
on Mount Lebanon;
you were ruthless to towns
and people everywhere.
Now you will be terrorized.
Idolatry Is Foolish
18What is an idol worth?
It's merely a false god.
Why trust a speechless image
made from wood or metal
by human hands?
19What can you learn from idols
covered with silver or gold?
They can't even breathe.
Pity anyone who says to an idol
of wood or stone,
“Get up and do something!”
20Let all the world be silent—
the Lord is present
in his holy temple.
translation_text:
1N daŋ izi tinni n diijaŋ chi,
di ra du tau,
di ra kpaŋ wii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ŋɔ tɛŋ
ani gunla min niŋ ŋɔ tɛu,
n nuumaa hiŋ wia.
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Habakuk wia
2Denii Kɔraawiizi bir ŋɔ n be,
“Sɛbi wia la min niŋ pilli tɛi
dau bipɛntɛnzi ni,
di gil a chaani nɛnnɛ,
guŋ gil siiri wer karmaa
nɛnnɛ manaŋ.
3A wipillaa hɔpizii daŋ haa ba,
ń bagli wia la n niŋ wa
ɛɛ harbɔɔ ni,
a wàá ɛɛ kara.
Haali aŋ wàá ɛɛ manaŋ gba, ka ií ra kpaŋ,
a guŋ daŋ haŋ bau,
a wàá birgi.
4A wipillaarɛ keŋ, Babilɔn hina ra tɔgzi bahinaarɛ werge,
ba kipar wia waa deŋlee,
ka nɛr la wia n deŋlee,
u yardaa niŋ ɛɛ u miibɔɔ.
5Babilɔn hina daama ra dar baabuu,
ba ra jigsi werge,
ba siwii waa su,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ba dɔɔ kpossiire
alugɔ siu siwii n waa su la,
di chaali hɛssi hina maa ra tɛɛ u hiŋ,
di lauri baa ra ɛɛ yoma.
6Nɛra la maa Babilɔn hina n kpeglee daŋ bir ɛɛ baa mɔmɔsia, di ra ŋɔ,
‘Wia daŋ huuzi ia dikuu iiŋ paagi kuŋŋmɛɛlaa sagzi dɔŋa ni wia,
di paagi kuna
ii wer birgi dɔɔna!
Saŋa bɛliirɛ ii gil
guŋ ɛɛiyɛi?’
7Nɛra la kima iin diwee daŋ izi kakpaŋ,
di du ia siaahmu,
ii bɔra ra sa.
Denii ii bir ɛɛ lugɔ nɛra la kuna
iiŋ faa paagɛɛ la.
8Ii paagi hɛrkpila hina daamaa,
ka filaŋkeŋ, banla
n kawɛɛ la
daŋ paagi ii ge kuna,
dikuu iiŋ kpu hɛssi nɛra werge maa,
di chɔgi hɛssi, bolzenaa ani
a nɛra la maa wia.
9Wia daŋ huuzi ii Babilɔn hina, dikuu iiŋ nyiŋŋi daama gunla n waa deŋlee tɛɛ iihinaa,
di ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ ii du bɔnanaa,
nɛr maa gilɛɛ wer hel
ii be di kpu ia wia!
10Ií vɔɔ nɛkpila kpui jinaa,
guŋ gil chɔgaa ba ii be,
guŋ gil ii himmaa diini hina ge
di hiihzi, di nyaa ii miibɔɔni.
11Bia la iiŋ kpawɛɛ ma koŋlaa la wiraa daŋ lii chaaŋ,
á dolli ge hiini, á wiraa jaa.
12Wia daŋ huuzi nɛr la maa n kpa nɛkpui
gɛɛ wichɔgaa ŋmɛnizi
di ra ma bol!
13Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la dauwɔɔ lugɔ
hɛssi hina kuuhni maa
daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ daazi
baŋ du niŋ biini
a ra fuuh.
U dauwɔɔ lugɔ
ba ra kuuuh pɛɛ.
14Hɛssi hina maa daŋ zum gunla Kɔraawiizi n duwɛɛ, u girme su hɛri
gunla nii n su muuzeŋ la.
15Wia daŋ huuzi nɛr la maa n kpa siŋ di ra tɛɛ u dɔŋahina,
ba nyɔɔ ra dɛɛzi,
guŋ gil ú wer di ra binni
ba chakpalli.
16Girme la hiŋ faa dɔɔwɛ la daŋ birgi hiihzi werge.
I saŋaa filaŋkeŋ!
Nyɔɔ di wir i hiŋ!
Kɔraawiizi kpa libee la n du u fɔŋŋa nonii biinii di ra ba i be, ú wa tɛr i digni,
í girme birgi ŋmaaba.
17Chɔgaa la hiŋ faa chɔg Lɛbanɔn hɛri la daŋ bir dii
ani gunla hiŋ faa kpu sela
werge la daŋ dui
ɔnsii werge.
I faa kpu nɛraa werge,
di faa chɔgi hɛssi, bola
ani nɛra la maa n du a biine.
18Neweere sɛɛh vug, bɛɛ tɔnaa u dɔɔi?
U wia maa ɛɛ karaa.
Nɛr la n sɛɛuh yardi u himmaa kuŋkuariirɛ,
vuga la uŋ sɛɛhwɛ la
wàá wer ŋɔ wia.
19Wia daŋ huuzi nɛr la maa n ŋɔ daa be, ‘Dɔɔ miibɔɔ!’
Gɛɛ bii n waa
miibɔɔ dɔɔwɛ be, ‘Izi!’
U daŋ wer baglii wiaa?
Saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋaa ba
ŋmɛɛri tɔ u maa,
waa heeza dɔɔwɛ kɔrai!
20Ka Kɔraawiizi du u Diinaniinanii biinii.
Gil nɛr la maa n du
durnya naa ba u see
di wa ɛɛ surumm.”

english_text:
Habakkuk's Prayer
1This is my prayer:
2I know your reputation, Lord,
and I am amazed
at what you have done.
Please turn from your anger
and be merciful;
do for us what you did
for our ancestors.
3You are the same Holy God
who came from Teman
and Paran to help us.
The brightness of your glory
covered the heavens,
and your praises were heard
everywhere on earth.
4Your glory shone like the sun,
and light flashed from your hands,
hiding your mighty power.
5Dreadful diseases and plagues
marched in front
and followed behind.
6When you stopped,
the earth shook;
when you stared,
nations trembled;
when you walked
along your ancient paths,
eternal mountains and hills
crumbled and collapsed.
7The tents of desert tribes
in Cushan and Midian
were ripped apart.
8Our Lord, were you angry
with the monsters
of the deep?
You attacked in your chariot
and wiped them out.
9Your arrows were ready
and obeyed your commands.
You split the earth apart
with rivers and streams;
10mountains trembled
at the sight of you;
rain poured from the clouds;
ocean waves roared and rose.
11The sun and moon stood still,
while your arrows and spears
flashed like lightning.
12In your furious anger,
you trampled on nations
13to rescue your people
and save your chosen one.
You crushed a nation's ruler
and stripped his evil kingdom
of its power.
14His troops had come like a storm,
hoping to scatter us
and glad to gobble us up.
To them we were refugees
in hiding—
but you smashed their heads
with their own weapons.
15Then your chariots churned
the waters of the sea.
Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
16When I heard this message,
I felt weak from fear,
and my lips quivered.
My bones seemed to melt,
and I stumbled around.
But I will patiently wait.
Someday those vicious enemies
will be struck by disaster.
Trust in a Time of Trouble
17Fig trees may no longer bloom,
or vineyards produce grapes;
olive trees may be fruitless,
and harvest time a failure;
sheep pens may be empty,
and cattle stalls vacant—
18but I will still celebrate
because the Lord God
is my Savior.
19 The Lord gives me strength.
He makes my feet as sure
as those of a deer,
and he helps me stand
on the mountains.
To the music director:
Use stringed instruments.
translation_text:
Habakuk wiisuŋŋaa wia
1Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Habakuk wiisuŋŋaarɛ keŋ.
2N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, n nuu i nuukpuuri wia la hiŋ ɛɛwɛ labuu.
I wiɛɛlaa hiŋ kpu n nuarɛ.
Bir ɛɛa yaa de dui saŋa naa biini,
gil yaa ge zumaa filaŋkeŋ.
Di yaa wa ɛɛi wichɔgaa
i baaŋ fuuh gba,
ka í na yaa sinyɛna.
3Kɔraawiizi lii Ɛdɔm hɛrii ba,
Paran bizenaa nyuurɛ
Dɔɔrinaniinanii la lii ba.
U girme su chiŋ maanii.
Durnya hina maa ra chɔluu.
4U wessi faa du lugɔ wiizi n na fur,
kuna lii u nonii
di ra nyɛgzi pilpilpil,
di lii bɔr la u kpegzi
n faa suahwɛ la.
5Wiilchɔgaa tɔ u see,
wiilbuulaa ge hiŋ u naajaglaa,
di ra kpuuzi nɛra.
6Di u wa izoo chi, hɛri ɔɔ zigluu,
di u wa binni hɛssi hina,
ba bɔra ɔɔ ra sau.
Bizenaa la n du de faala maa la purgi,
giŋgimee la ge n du de
saŋa maa la chogli.
U wiɛɛlaa ŋmɛnizi
waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.
7Ɔnsii chol Kusan hina la n du tanti diini biinii werge,
Midian hina ge bɔra ra sa.
8Kɔraawiizi, i faa na baannɛ du muuni ni gɛɛ?
I baaŋ faa fuuhwoo
gɔŋa nii?
Muuzeŋ ni lɛi i baaŋfuuihchɔgaa faa du,
hiŋ faa tinnɛɛ chi
baamazi ni alugɔ aŋ faa
ɛɛ laal torkozi, di kpegli
i dɔma tɛɛ i nɛra laa?
9I lizi i hoore chaaŋ,
di ŋɔ ba tɛi hobee kpila.
I kpa muunii peri hɛri,
10bizenaa nai di ra zigli.
Dooŋ ba, nii pal fɔŋŋa ni di waa kaali,
muuzeŋ ra gbɔgzi,
di gil u ra lɔ werge,
di ra izi chiŋ.
11Wiizi ni baagu chi chinchiŋ diindiindiiŋ,
dikuu hiŋ ta hobee,
i kandaa ge ra nyɛgzi
pilpilpil wia.
12I kpa baaŋfuuih wergee di ta naagaliŋgajaŋra hɛri ni di wa kaali,
di kpa baaŋ fɛrgi hɛssi hina.
13I liwɔɔrɛ í wa lɛɛ i nɛra,
di lɛɛ unla hiŋ lizɛɛ
ú ɛɛ koori la ta.
I chɔgi hɛri la hina n dɔɔ biinikpola sitɔɔrii,
di chɔgi u fɔŋŋa maa.
14I faa kpa u himmaa kandaarɛ di yag u nyuu,
di lii saŋa la u laallɔɔra
n faa chɔwɛɛ ba,
bá wa lɔ yaa di yaari la,
di ɛɛ yaa chɛɛtɛ di ra mam lugɔ banna nyiŋŋi ba ligli
gɛrga la n chɔwɛɛ suahzi la.
15I kpa i zagra naazi di fɛrgi muuzeŋ,
di vuugi u niizenaa
a ra izi fufuu.
16N nuu guŋ n banchule ra lɔ,
n nuuhɔna ra lɔ dɔŋa
dikuu gbɔga la wia.
N bɔra huah di zuu n hoga biini,
n naazi ra sa.
Ka n daŋ di kanyitti di ra kpaŋ saŋa la hɔpizichɔgii
n niŋ wa huuzi hɛri la hina
n na yoo yaa la.
17Haali fig daa n wàá fii gba,
grepu daazi ge waa grepuzi nɔnnɛ,
haali ɔlivizi n vɛɛ nɔnaa,
pattikuna vɛɛ gba,
haali peeza n waa hoo lumbol,
nauna ge waa hoo liga gba,
18ka n bɔra danna pur Kɔraawiizi wia,
n bɔra sɔɔni werge
n Lɛɛri Kɔraawiizi la wia.
19Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ɛɛ n fɔŋŋa,
u gillɔɔ n naapezi ɛɛ lugɔ
chaŋkpalŋa naafiraa,
di gil n wer
di ra tinni bizenaa.
N sɛbi wia naabuu di ra tɛɛ yira nabɔma, ú kpa n janjalaŋ lɔa.

english_text:
1 I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah.
When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message.
Judgment on Judah
2I, the Lord, now promise
to destroy everything
on this earth—
3people and animals,
birds and fish.
Everyone who is evil
will crash to the ground,
and I will wipe out
the entire human race.
4I will reach out to punish
Judah and Jerusalem—
nothing will remain
of the god Baal;
nothing will be remembered
of his pagan priests.
5Not a trace will be found
of those who worship stars
from their rooftops,
or bow down to the god Milcom,
while claiming loyalty
to me, the Lord.
6Nothing will remain of anyone
who has turned away
and rejected me.
7Be silent! I am the Lord God,
and the time is near.
I am preparing
to sacrifice my people
and to invite my guests.
8On that day I will punish
national leaders
and sons of the king,
along with all who follow
foreign customs.
9I will punish worshipers
of pagan gods
and cruel palace officials
who abuse their power.
10I, the Lord, promise
that on that day
noisy crying will be heard
from Fish Gate, New Town,
and Upper Hills.
11Everyone in Lower Hollow
will mourn loudly,
because merchants
and money changers
will be wiped out.
12I'll search Jerusalem with lamps
and punish those people
who sit there unworried
while thinking,
“The Lord won't do anything,
good or bad.”
13Their possessions will be taken,
their homes left in ruins.
They won't get to live
in the houses they build,
or drink wine from the grapes
in their own vineyards.
A Terrible Day
14The great day of the Lord
is coming soon, very soon.
On that terrible day,
fearsome shouts of warriors
will be heard everywhere.
15It will be a time of anger—
of trouble and torment,
of disaster and destruction,
of darkness and despair,
of storm clouds and shadows,
16of trumpet calls
and battle cries
against fortified cities
and mighty fortresses.
17The Lord warns everyone
who has sinned against him,
“I'll strike you blind!
Then your blood and your insides
will gush out like vomit.
18Not even your silver or gold
can save you on that day
when I, the Lord, am angry.
My anger will flare up
like a furious fire
scorching the earth
and everyone on it.”
translation_text:
1Wia la Kɔraawiizi n faa kpawɛɛ bagli Zɛfania saŋa la Amɔn biibaal Jɔsia n faa ra di Juda koraa keŋ. Zɛfania mɛɛrɛ faa Kusi, Kusi ge mɛɛ ɛɛ Gɛdalia, Gɛdalia ge mɛɛ ɛɛ Amaria, Amaria ge mɛɛ ɛɛ Hɛzɛkia.
Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii seriya dii wia
2Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N daŋ chɔgi
hɛri naa kummaa.
3N daŋ kpu newea ni sela maa,
di kpu zumbizi
ani muuzeŋ biini nyinni maa.
Biinikpola hina maa wia daŋ tuŋ,
di n wa dim newea maa
hɛri naa biini.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
4N daŋ tɛr Juda hina
ani banla maa n du
bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm biini digna.
N daŋ chɔgi de, di dim Baal wikpoglaa ni u kizeehina maa,
nɛr maa wàá ka liizi ba wia
5ni banla maa n ɔɔ tinni sal
di ra jaami wiizi, baagu
ani chinchiŋwilaa,
banla n ɔɔ ra jaamiŋ di ra hɛɛhziŋ,
ka ɔɔ ra hɛɛhzi
vug Mɔlɛk ge la,
6banla n bir har di vɛɛ n hiŋaa,
ba wàá kaa nyiŋŋi n bɔr gɛɛ
di pɛɛzi n wia gba.”
7Ií ɛɛ surumm Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la see,
dikuu u Hɔpizii la n duglɛɛ wia.
U ɛɛ siryaa ú kpa u nɛra lizi mbusu,
di yir ba dɔma bá
wa paagi ba kuna.
8Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “A hɔl la min niŋ kpu nɛra werge la,
n daŋ tɛrgi koori biibaala,
nabɔnzenaa ani banla maa n na hiŋ
hɔɔhra naana wia la digna.
9A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ tɛr banla maa n na jaami
lugɔ vugkuara digna
ni banla n na ŋmɛɛ, di ra kpu nɛra,
bá vuga diini suugi wia.
10A hɔl hiŋ,
ii daŋ nuu chɛɛhgaa lii
Nyiŋ Dominuuzeŋ la,
chɛɛhgaa su a bolzeŋ bɔfalii la
ani kuna n na chogli,
di ra lɔɔzi dɔŋa gbɔga werge,
giŋgimee nyuuni.
11Ii banla n du yawa barii la, ií ra chɛɛhgi.
Ii kɔkɔɔza maanii niŋ dim,
banla n na yoo saliŋhuŋŋa
maanii niŋ tuŋ.
12A guŋ saŋa, n daŋ kpa fintinazi di pigzi Jɛrusalɛm,
di tɛrgi banla maa
n na faazi digna,
baabuu ra fɛ lugɔ màá ɛɛ wiimaa,
haali di a nanaarɛ gɛɛ
achɔgaarɛ gba la.
13Ba daŋ wa paagi ba daama
di chɔgi ba diini.
Ba daŋ ma diini
ka ba wàá du a biine.
Ba daŋ duu grepu daazi ba kooni,
ka ba wàá nyɔɔ a siŋ.”
Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizizeŋ la wia
14Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizizeŋ la duglɔɔrɛ
di ra ba manamanaŋ.
Ií ra nuu! A Hɔpizii, daŋ ɛɛ hɔpizichuma,
laallɔkpega chaasaa su bɔr maa.
15A Hɔpizii daŋ ɛɛ baaŋfuuih werge hɔpizii,
di ɛɛ biinichɔg ni
lɔgɔ lii werge hɔpizii,
di ɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ ni chɔgaa hɔpizii,
di ɛɛ bɔbiri ni tamii
tunaa hɔpizii
di ɛɛ baamazi ni bɔbiri
limpiriŋ hɔpizii,
16di ɛɛ nyigzi ni laal wiraa hɔpizii
di ra lɔ bolzenaa la
baŋ ma koŋlaa bar
ni a siraa diijaŋra.
17Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ kpa dɔgnya werge di wa ta a nɛra ni,
ba ra vol lugɔ nyuŋŋa,
dikuu baŋ ɛɛŋ wichɔgaa wia.
Ba daŋ fug ba chal lugɔ nii,
bá bɔra chɔɔ hɛri pɔɔh.”
18Ba saliŋhuŋŋa gɛɛ ba saliŋ
wàá wer lɛɛ baa ta
Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuihchɔgii Hɔpizii hiŋ hɔl.
U zoma niŋ
daŋ di durnya maa,
dikuu un niŋ gil nɛra maa
n du durnya naa biini
dim kakpaŋ wia.

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1You disgraceful nation,
gather around,
2before it's too late.
The Lord has set a time
when his fierce anger
will strike like a storm
and sweep you away.
3If you humbly obey the Lord,
then come and worship him.
If you do right and are humble,
perhaps you will be safe
on that day when the Lord
turns loose his anger.
Judgment on Philistia
4 Gaza and Ashkelon
will be deserted
and left in ruins.
Ashdod will be emptied
in broad daylight,
and Ekron uprooted.
5To you people of Philistia
who live along the coast,
the Lord has this to say:
“I am now your enemy,
and I'll wipe you out!”
6Your seacoast will be changed
into pastureland
and sheep pens.
7The Lord God hasn't forgotten
those survivors in Judah,
and he will help them—
his people will take your land
to use for pasture.
And when evening comes,
they will rest
in houses at Ashkelon.
Judgment on Moab and Ammon
* 8 The Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel, said:
I've heard Moab and Ammon
insult my people
and threaten their nation.
9 And so, I swear by my very life
that Moab and Ammon will end up
like Sodom and Gomorrah—
covered with thornbushes
and salt pits forever.
Then my people who survive
will take their land.
10This is how Moab and Ammon
will at last be repaid
for their pride—
and for sneering at the nation
that belongs to me,
the Lord All-Powerful.
11I will fiercely attack.
Then every god on this earth
will shrink to nothing,
and everyone of every nation
will bow down to me,
right where they are.
Judgment on Ethiopia
12 People of Ethiopia,
the sword of the Lord
will slaughter you!
Judgment on Assyria
13 The Lord will reach to the north
to crush Assyria
and overthrow Nineveh.
14Herds of wild animals
will live in its rubble;
all kinds of desert owls
will perch on its stones
and hoot in the windows.
Noisy ravens will be heard
inside its buildings,
stripped bare of cedar.
15This is the glorious city
that felt secure and said,
“I am the only one!”
Now it's merely ruins,
a home for wild animals.
Every passerby simply sneers
and makes vulgar signs.
translation_text:
1Ií chaali dɔŋa be, ií chaali dɔŋa be,
hoi, hiihnyaara.
2Mɔɔ ka Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii la uŋ lizɛɛ la ba,
a hɔpizii daŋ ɛɛ
lugɔ peu n paa nɔɔri,
mɔɔ ka Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuihchɔgii la fuuh ii ni,
mɔɔ ka u baaŋ werge
hɔpizii la chol ii ni.
3A hɛri hina la n sɔɔni siwii, ií nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi bɔr,
ii banla n na ɛɛ gunla
unna ŋɔ la.
Ií ra nyiŋŋi wideŋlaa, di ra nyiŋŋi sisɔna.
Aŋhinabe, ba daŋ tɛɛ
ia duuribɔra
Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii la hɔl.
Filisti hina seriya dii wia
4Nɛr maa wàá du Gaza biini,
Askɛlɔn ge chɔɔ diŋgela.
Ba daŋ tuŋ Asdɔd hina ge wibaŋkanchirii ni,
di dim Ɛkrɔn hina ge.
5Wiarɛ huuzi Filisti hina la
n soge muuzeŋ nua la.
Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii sag ii ninɛɛ,
u daŋ dim ia,
ii bɛl maa wàá ka ka.
6Ii hɛri la n du muuzeŋ nua la,
daŋ birgi senɔɔna duuribɔra
ni peeza lumbola.
7U daŋ ɛɛ Juda hina la n kawɛɛ la hor,
de ɛɛ ba sela diiribɔr.
Duana ni, ba daŋ chɔɔgi
Askɛlɔn hina diini biine.
Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la danna du ba tau.
U daŋ gil ba bir nyɛɛli.
Moab ni Ammɔn hina seriya dii wia
8Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N nuu gunla Moab ni Ammɔn hina n chagzi n nɛra di ra ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛɛ,
di ra ta barabara
lugɔ ba daŋ foozi ba hɛri.
9Awia, miŋ haŋ na du de waa,
Moab daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ
Sɔdɔm wibii maa,
Ammɔn hina ɛɛ lugɔ Gɔmɔra hina.
Di lii kooriichɔgaa,
di ɛɛ yazi bɔɔni,
di chɔɔ pɛɛ di hanna la.
N nɛra la n kawɛɛ la
daŋ paagi ba kuna.
N hɛri hina banla n niŋ di miibɔɔ la daŋ di ba hɛri kapɛttɛ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa
Izrɛl hina ra hum labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”
10Kunla ban niŋ na ú ɛɛ ba barabara kinturgaare guŋ,
dikuu baŋ chagzi
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa nɛra
di ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛ wia.
11Kɔraawiizi wia daŋ dɔɔ ɔnsii
saŋa la un niŋ chɔgi ba
hɛri vuga la.
Hɛssi hina la n du muuni kɛraa daŋ jaamuu,
bá himmaa hɛssi.
Itiopia hina seriya dii wia
12Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpu Itiopia hina gba.
Asiiria hina seriya dii wia
13Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag nonii,
di kpu Asiiria hina,
di gil Ninɛvɛ chɔɔ diŋgela,
di hil lugɔ hɛribɔduma.
14Peeza ni nauna kpilakpila daŋ chɔɔ de,
kunnyinee iri maa dee du de.
Hɛribɔduma kikiu ni kukubalee
daŋ du de hamuŋa ni
di ra wii.
Ba tokorozi daŋ hiini, di gil a wiraa jaa,
hembugle puugi
ba dominuuzi,
bá hɛriŋkpol dolli nyiizi.
15N baga waa hoo hina bolzenne la,
ba faa sogoo,
wiimaa waa baa titte.
Ba ɔɔ ŋɔ bahinaa benii,
“Yaa bolzenne kaali bolzeŋ maa.”
Na gunla ba bolzeŋ n chɔkkɛ,
di birgi pir sela duuribɔr!
Nɛr la maa n ga de kɛrii ɔɔ ra ɛɛubuu chɛɛtɛ,
di zigli noguruŋ
di ra du u ni.

english_text:
Sinful Jerusalem
1Too bad for that disgusting,
corrupt, and lawless city!
2Forever rebellious
and rejecting correction,
Jerusalem refuses to trust
or obey the Lord God.
3Its officials are roaring lions,
its judges are wolves;
in the evening they attack,
by morning nothing is left.
4Jerusalem's prophets are proud
and not to be trusted.
The priests have disgraced
the place of worship
and abused God's Law.
5All who do evil are shameless,
but the Lord does right
and is always fair.
With the dawn of each day,
God brings about justice.
6The Lord wiped out nations
and left fortresses
crumbling in the dirt.
Their streets and towns
were reduced to ruins
and emptied of people.
7God felt certain that Jerusalem
would learn to respect
and obey him.
Then he would hold back
from punishing the city
and not wipe it out.
But everyone there was eager
to start sinning again.
Nations Will Turn to the Lord
8The Lord said:
Just wait for the day
when I accuse you nations.
I have decided on a day,
when I will bring together
every nation and kingdom
and punish them all
in my fiery anger.
I will become furious
and destroy the earth.
9I will purify each language
and make those languages
acceptable for praising me.
Then, with hearts united,
everyone will serve
only me, the Lord.
10From across the rivers
of Ethiopia,
my scattered people,
my true worshipers,
will bring offerings to me.
11When that time comes,
you won't rebel against me
and be put to shame.
I'll do away with those
who are proud and arrogant.
Never will any of them
strut around
on my holy mountain.
12But I, the Lord, won't destroy
any of your people
who are truly humble
and turn to me for safety.
13 The people of Israel who survive
will live right
and refuse to tell lies.
They will eat and rest
with nothing to fear.
A Song of Celebration
14Everyone in Jerusalem and Judah,
celebrate and shout
with all your heart!
15Zion, your punishment is over.
The Lord has forced your enemies
to turn and retreat.
Your Lord is King of Israel
and stands at your side;
you don't have to worry
about any more troubles.
16Jerusalem, the time is coming,
when it will be said to you:
“Don't be discouraged
or grow weak from fear!
17The Lord your God
wins victory after victory
and is always with you.
He celebrates and sings
because of you,
and he will refresh your life
with his love.”
The Lord's Promise to His People
18The Lord has promised:
Your sorrow has ended,
and you can celebrate.
19I will punish those
who mistreat you.
I will bring together the lame
and the outcasts,
then they will be praised,
instead of despised,
in every country on earth.
20I will lead you home,
and with your own eyes
you will see me bless you
with all you once owned.
Then you will be famous
everywhere on this earth.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Jɛrusalɛm kɛrɛbɛl duula wia
1Wiarɛ huuzi bolzeŋ la hina n na fir nɛra,
di dɔɔ dignikpega ra ɛɛ
wia la n doŋŋe la!
2U nɛra waa nɛr maa ra tɔgzi,
ba waa baglaa ra nuu.
Ba waa Kɔraawiizi yardɛɛ,
ba waa tuzɛɛ ra dugli Kɔraawiizi.
3Ba nabɔnzi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyinzi n na wii,
Ba koora ɛɛ munuzi la
lɔzi n na kpu werge,
a waa ɔɔ di kummaa
ka ka u yeŋ ka hɔpizi la.
4A bolzeŋ dɔgtɛɛzi kpoŋŋoo.
Ba ɛɛ nɛchɔgaarɛ.
U kizeehina ɔɔ ra chɔg Kɔraawiizi Diarɛ,
di ɔɔ kpa Gbɔgni la
ra sunni nɛra.
5Kɔraawiizi haa du a bolzeŋ biinii, di ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee,
waa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ ra leu.
Chɔɔzi maa, u ɔɔ ra ɛɛ wibii wiarɛ,
waa wia ɛɛwɛ ra huhzi
hɔpizifalii maa biini,
ka banla wia n waa deŋlee
waa hiihzi.
6Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N chɔgi hɛssi
ni a nɛra maanii.
N gillɔɔ ba diikpega maa purgi,
di gil ba ŋmɛnizi maa
chɔɔ pɛɛ,
nɛr maa waa kaa ra ga u biini.
Ba bolzeŋkpega maa chɔgi,
nɛr maa wàá kaa ka.
7N ŋɔ a bolzeŋ hina benii,
‘Ií danna ɔmiŋ wibii maa,
di ra sɛɛ n baglaa!’
Denii ii duuribɔr wàá chɔgi,
gɛɛ màá tɛrgi ii digna.
Ka ba haa aah siwii
di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa
ba wiɛɛlaa maa biini.”
8Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Awia, ií chi kpaŋiŋ,
dikuu hɔpizii la min niŋ
chi di wibii la wia.
N na nyiŋŋuu ń chaali hɛssi hina maa,
di chaali kossi maa,
di gil n baaŋ fuuh ba ni werge maa,
n baaŋchɔgii la maa.
N zoma baaŋ niŋ
daŋ di durnya maa.
9Denii ń bir kuari nɛra nuuzi á du wer,
bá maa ra yir mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ,
di chaali ra hum n bɛŋ.
10N nɛra la n yaarɛɛ
ga du Itiopia muuni
baŋgizi la
daŋ kpa kuna di wa sunziŋ.
11Ba wàá du ia hiihzi a hɔl hiŋ,
dikuu wichɔgaa la maa
iiŋ faa ɛɛŋ la wia,
dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ lizi banla maa
n faa ra di suma di pɔɔh la,
di lii bol naa biini.
Ií ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka kpoŋ
n giŋgimiinaniinanii la nyuu.
12Ka n daŋ du ii banla
n waa iihinaa ra tɔgzi,
di dɔɔ bunya,
di yardiŋ la biini.
13Izrɛl hina la n niŋ ka la wàá kaa ra ɛɛ wileulaa,
ba wàá kaa ra kanni kara
gɛɛ di kaa ra dar nɛra.
Ba daŋ ɔɔ di, di chɔɔgi,
ka nɛr maa wàá ka ɔnzi baa.”
14Izrɛl hina, ií ra yir yira!
Jɛrusalɛm hina,
ií ra chaasi werge!
Ií gil ii bɔra ni
ii bampiree maa sɔɔni!
15Kɔraawiizi lizi iabuu tɔɔrɔɔ biini,
u bir ii dɔmaa har.
Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ Izrɛl koorizeŋ la du ii benii,
ii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka
ɔm tɔɔrɔɔ maa.
16A hɔl hiŋ ba daŋ ŋɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina be,
“Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina,
ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm.
Ií gilɛɛ gil ii nonee yɔɔri.
17Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la du ii benii,
u kpekkoo di ra lɛɛ.
Ii wia daŋ paruu werge,
u daŋ tɛɛ ia miibɔɔfalii
dikuu uŋ nɔŋŋi ia wia,
u daŋ yir bɔsɔna yir
dikuu ii wia.”
18Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Biinichɔg diuzenaa la baŋ ɛɛ sirya dau la,
n daŋ lizaa ii be,
di lizi hiihzi ii ni.
19A guŋ saŋa, n daŋ tɔɔri
banla maa n faa ra
sunni ia la.
N daŋ lɛɛ banla naazi ni nonee n siuzɛɛ,
di chaali banla maa
n yaarɛɛ la.
N daŋ chɔli baa, di ra tɔgzi baa,
hɛssi la maa baŋ faa kpa
hiihzi kpu baa la biine.
20A guŋ saŋa, n daŋ chaali ia
ba bol.
N danna tɔgzi ia, di ra chɔli ia,
hɛri nɛra maa be,
di n wa bittɔ tɛɛ ia ii kundɔɔlaa
ii sibɔɔ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
Rebuild the Temple
1 On the first day of the sixth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak his message to the governor of Judah and to the high priest.
So Haggai told Governor Zerubbabel and High Priest Joshua 2-5that the Lord All-Powerful had said to them and to the people:
You say this isn't the right time to build a temple for me. But is it right for you to live in expensive houses, while my temple is a pile of ruins? Just look at what's happening. 6You harvest less than you plant, you never have enough to eat or drink, your clothes don't keep you warm, and your wages are stored in bags full of holes.
7Think about what I have said! 8But first, go to the hills and get wood for my temple, so I can take pride in it and be worshiped there. 9You expected much, but received only a little. And when you brought it home, I made that little disappear. Why have I done this? It's because you hurry off to build your own houses, while my temple is still in ruins. 10That's also why the dew doesn't fall and your harvest fails. 11And so, at my command everything will become barren—your farmland and pastures, your vineyards and olive trees, your animals and you yourselves. All your hard work will be for nothing.
12Zerubbabel and Joshua, together with the others who had returned from exile in Babylonia, obeyed the Lord's message spoken by his prophet Haggai, and they started showing proper respect for the Lord. 13Haggai then told them that the Lord had promised to be with them. 14So the Lord God All-Powerful made everyone eager to work on his temple, especially Zerubbabel and Joshua. 15And the work began on the twenty-fourth day of that same month.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ bá kuari ma u Dia wia
1Pɛsia Koorizeŋ Dariɔs kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi anumbɛlhiŋ, lugli hɔpiziirɛ Kɔraawiizi pilli wia naa tɛɛ u dɔgtɛɛ Hagai, di ŋɔ lugɔ u baglaa tɛɛ Sɛɛltiɛl biibaal Zɛrubabɛl, n ɛɛ Juda nabɔma ni Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Jɛhɔzadak biibaal Josua.
2Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, “Nɛra naa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Kɔraawiizi Dia mai saŋa haa waa helle.’ ”
3Denii Kɔraawiizi ga u dɔgtɛɛ Hagai be di ŋɔ, 4“N nɛra, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra zuu diinanaa biine, ka n Dia purgi chɔɔi?”
5Filaŋkeŋ, kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔ, “Ií ra du ii wiɛɛlaa tau nɛnnɛ. 6Ii duu kunaa werge, ka kum tama. Ii ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, ka ii waa kukki, di ra laali kuna, ka waari ra kpu ia. Ii hummɔɔ di ra na kinturgaa, ka a waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ tɛɛ ia. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ii kebee hure n furgɛɛ.”
7Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, “Ií ra du ii wiɛɛlaa tau nɛnnɛ. 8Ií tinni bizenaa nyuuni, di ga tee daazenaa ba, di wa ma n Dia, ń bɔra jaa sɔɔni, bá ra jaamiŋ de, ń na girme. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 9Ii faa ra tami wergee, ka ii na tama. Kuna la iiŋ ɔɔ kpa lii ii kooni maanii aŋ gil a chɔgi. Bɛɛ n baani n na ɛɛ gunnɛi? N na ɛɛ gunnɛ, dikuu n Dia n purgee, ka ii bɛl maa dia wia aah u siwii wia. 10Awiarɛ dooŋ waa ba, kummaa wàá wer hel la. 11N gillɔɔ hil chi. Awiarɛ, mia, siŋfalii, nuu ani kuna la maa n na lii hɛri, nyaa la. Newea ni sela waa kaa ra lul, ii huma maa ɔɔ bir pɛɛ la.”
12Denii Sɛɛltiɛl biibaal Zɛrubabɛl ni Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Jɛhɔzadak biibaal Josua sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔzi la ni u dɔgtɛɛ Hagai amaniye la uŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ baa la, dikuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la, n humuu wia. Kɔraawiizi wia faa jaa dɔɔ a nɛra ɔnsii.
13Denii Hagai faa kpa Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa tɛɛ baa, di ŋɔ, “N du ii benii. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.” 14Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa du Sɛɛltiɛl biibaal Zɛrubabɛl la, n ɛɛ Juda hina nabɔma ni Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Josua ani a nɛra maa bɔkpega. Ba maa faa chaali di ra ma Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la banna hum la Dia. 15Koorizeŋ Dariɔs kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi anumbɛlhiŋ, hɔpizaa tokko ni anaazu hɔllɛ, ba faari a Dia mai.

english_text:
The Glorious New Temple
1-2On the twenty-first day of the next month, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak this message to Governor Zerubbabel, High Priest Joshua, and everyone else:
3 Does anyone remember how glorious this temple used to be? Now it looks like nothing. 4But cheer up! Because I, the Lord All-Powerful, will be here to help you with the work, 5 just as I promised your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt. Don't worry. My Spirit is right here with you.
6 Soon I will again shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land. 7I will shake the nations, and their treasures will be brought here. Then the brightness of my glory will fill this temple. 8All silver and gold belong to me, 9and I promise that this new temple will be more glorious than the first one. I will also bless this city with peace.
The Past and the Future
10On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the Lord God All-Powerful told the prophet Haggai 11to ask the priests for their opinion on the following matters:
12Suppose meat ready to be sacrificed to God is being carried in the folds of someone's clothing, and the clothing rubs against some bread or stew or wine or olive oil or any other food. Would those foods that were touched then become acceptable for sacrifice?
“Of course not,” the priests answered.
13 Then Haggai said, “Suppose someone has touched a dead body and is considered unacceptable to worship God. If that person touches these foods, would they become unclean?”
“Of course they would,” the priests answered.
14So the Lord told Haggai to say:
That's how it is with this entire nation. Everything you do and every sacrifice you offer is unacceptable to me. 15But from now on, things will get better. Before you started laying the foundation for the temple, 16you recalled what life was like in the past. When you wanted 200 kilograms of wheat, there were only 10, and when you wanted 50 jars of wine, there were only 20. 17I made all of your hard work useless by sending mildew, mold, and hail—but you still did not return to me, your Lord.
18Today you have completed the foundation for my temple, so listen to what your future will be like. 19Although you have not yet harvested any grain, grapes, figs, pomegranates, or olives, I will richly bless you in the days ahead.
God's Promise to Zerubbabel
20That same day the Lord spoke to Haggai again and said:
21Tell Governor Zerubbabel of Judah that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth 22and wipe out kings and their kingdoms. I will overturn war chariots, and then cavalry troops will start slaughtering each other. 23But tell my servant Zerubbabel that I, the Lord All-Powerful, have chosen him, and he will rule in my name.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Dia baŋ kuarɛɛ ma girme wia
1Baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ, hɔpizaa tokko ni kpaŋ hɔllɛ, Kɔraawiizi ga u dɔgtɛɛ Hagai be, di ŋɔ, 2“Ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Juda hina nabɔma Sɛɛltiɛl biibaal Zɛrubabɛl ni Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Jɛhɔzadak biibaal Josua ani Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ la, di pɛɛzi baa, 3‘Ii biini, ú bɛliirɛ n du de, di faa na n Dia naa girme la uŋ faa dɔɔwɛ lai? Ɛrɛɛ u du ii be filaŋkennei? Waa ɛɛwɛ lɛi lugɔ kumpɛɛ ii bee? 4Ka filaŋkeŋ, Zɛrubabɛl, Josua ani ii banla maa n du hɛri naa, ií chiiri zɛɛ, di hum a huma, dikuubɛɛwiai, n du ii benii. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu ŋɔ guŋ. 5Nua naabuu n faa ŋɔ tɛɛ ia, saŋa la iinna lii Ijip hɛri la. N Duma du ii benii. Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm.’ ”
6Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “A wàá birgi tama maa, ka ń kaa zigli chiŋ ni hɛri ani muuzenaa maa. 7N daŋ kpegli hɛssi hina maa, di gil n Dia su ni ba daama kuna, di dɔɔ girme werge. 8Saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ la maa n du durnya naa maa ɛɛ n horaa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ. 9Filaŋkeŋ, n Dia naa girme daŋ kaali n Diibinii la girme. Denii ń gil bampirsɔna lii, di ba ii be. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.”
Nɛra la n doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be kissaa wia
10Koorizeŋ Dariɔs kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ biini, baaguzi kabɛlhiŋ, hɔpizaa tokko ni anaazuhiŋ hɔllɛ, Kɔraawiizi kaa pilli wia naa tɛɛ u dɔgtɛɛ Hagai, di ŋɔ, 11“Pɛɛzi n kizeehina bá bagli gunla mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg la n na ŋɔ. 12Di nɛr kpa ol la n waa doŋŋe n be di fɔɔ u wɛjɛ nua, de wa gbɔgzi paanuu gɛɛ dɔzi gɛɛ siŋ gɛɛ nuu gɛɛ diwee waa iri maa, a kundee ge ɔɔ birgi kunnaniinaniirɛ n bee?”
Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la ŋɔ, “Akai.”
13Denii Hagai kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ di nɛr doŋŋo u be, dikuu uŋ gbɔgzi lalii wia, ka gbɔgzi annii bɛl maa, u daŋ doŋaa?” Ba ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, u daŋ doŋ.”
14Hagai kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ gunnɛ a nɛra naa ni ba hɛri naa wia du u be la. Ba wiɛɛlaa ni kuna la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ ra tɛu mbusu lizibɔr ni la doŋŋoo. Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
15Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Awia, ií fɛ wia naa nfɛrɛ nɛnnɛ, di lii zinaa di ra la. Ií pessi nɛnnɛ gunla wia n faa duwɛɛ, ka ii faari n Dia naa mai la. 16Di nɛr ɔɔ la ga na sɔgmia n chɔɔwɛ kululu, di ra fɛ lugɔ a daŋ hel kilozi kalfaanɛɛ, ka kalfa bɛnnɛ ɔɔ na. Di u la siŋ ge bɔr, di ra fɛ lugɔ u daŋ na pirintuani kalfa, ka tokkoanɛɛ bɛnnɛ ɔɔ na. 17N faa gillɔɔ peu la n wenzee werge ni kɔɔla ani dobia chɔgi ii pattikuna maa, ka ii faa haa waa sɛɛwɛ ii biine chɔgi, ii gil ii wichɔgaa ha. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 18Zinaa n ɛɛ baagu kabɛl hɔpizaa tokko ni anaazuhiŋ hɔl, iiŋ chiŋŋi n Dia naa zɛɛ tuŋ naa, ií ra nuu gunla ii kɛrɛbɛl wia n niŋ du. 19Midee maa waa kaa hoo buuga biini. Di filaŋkeŋ lɛi, grepu, fig, pomegranet ani ɔlivi daazi faa waa nɔŋ, ka haŋ lii zinaa di ra la, n daŋ kissi ia.”
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Zɛrubabɛl wia
20Kɔraawiizi kaa pilli wia naa tɛɛ u dɔgtɛɛ Hagai bunɛɛhiŋ, a baagu hɔpizaa tokko ni anaazuhiŋ hɔl, di ra ŋɔ, 21“Ŋɔ Juda hina nabɔma Zɛrubabɛl be lugɔ n daŋ zigli chiŋ ni hɛri. 22N daŋ kpegli hɛrdumazi hina kossi ni ba fɔŋŋazi. N daŋ kaa kpegli laal zagra ni a torkozi ani a zuura. Laal zagra ni a tinna daŋ chogli, dikuu ba lulla n niŋ kpa tokobizi di kpuuzi baa wia.
23A hɔl hiŋ, n balii Zɛrubabɛl, Sɛɛltiɛl biibaal, n daŋ gil i ɛɛ lugɔ n nonibisig la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, n kpa ra jag kuna ni la, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ lizii, í chi n naazi, di ɛɛ n nɛra sitɔɔri. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1 I am the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo.
In the eighth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told me to say:
2-3Israel, I, the Lord All-Powerful, was very angry with your ancestors. But if you people will return to me, I will turn and help you. 4Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. They were warned by the earlier prophets to give up their evil and turn back to me, but they paid no attention.
5Where are your ancestors now? Not even prophets live forever. 6But my warnings and my words spoken by the prophets caught up with your ancestors. So they turned back to me and said, “Lord All-Powerful, you have punished us for our sins, just as you had planned.”
First Vision: Horses and Riders
7-8 On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, which was the eleventh month of that same year, the Lord spoke to me in a vision during the night: In a valley among myrtle trees, I saw someone on a red horse, with riders on red, brown, and white horses behind him. 9An angel was there to explain things to me, and I asked, “Sir, who are these riders?”
“I'll tell you,” the angel answered.
10At once, the man standing among the myrtle trees said, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to find out what's happening on earth.”
11Then the riders spoke to the Lord's angel, who was standing among the myrtle trees, and they said, “We have gone everywhere and have discovered that the whole world is at peace.”
12At this, the angel said, “Lord All-Powerful, for 70 years you have been angry with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. When are you ever going to have mercy on them?”
13The Lord's answer was kind and comforting. 14So the angel told me to announce:
I, the Lord All-Powerful, am very protective of Jerusalem. 15For a while I was angry at the nations, but now I am furious, because they have made things worse for Jerusalem and are not the least bit concerned. 16And so, I will have pity on Jerusalem. The city will be completely rebuilt, and my temple will stand again. 17I also promise that my towns will prosper—Jerusalem will once again be my chosen city, and I will comfort the people of Zion.
Second Vision: Animal Horns
18Next, I saw four animal horns. 19-21The angel who was sent to explain was there, and so I asked, “What do these mean?”
His answer was, “These horns are the nations that scattered the people of Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem, and took away their freedom.”
Then the Lord showed me four blacksmiths, and I asked, “What are they going to do?”
He replied, “They are going to terrify and crush those horns.”
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n na yir u nɛra bá bir ba u be wia
1Pɛsia Koorizeŋ Dariɔs kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ baaguzi ŋmantannaazi biinii, Kɔraawiizi kpa u amaniye tɛɛ Ido biibaal Bɛrɛkia ge biibaal Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Zɛkaria.
2Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔ Zɛkaria benii, “Ŋɔ n nɛra be lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la baaŋ faa fuuh ii naabaala ninɛɛ werge. 3Ka filaŋkeŋ, n na ŋɔ ii benii, ií bir ba mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ be, n ge bir ba ii be. 4Ií gilɛɛ ɛɛ lugɔ ii naabaala. Faala la, n dɔgtɛɛzi faa feloore ŋɔ ba be lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ií bir lii ii wichɔgaa ŋmɛnizi la, di gil ii wichɔgaa wiɛɛlaa la.’ Ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ nuu n be gɛɛ di du n wiŋɔɔlaa tau. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. 5Ii naabaala la du lee filaŋkennei? Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la ge gba waa kaa hoo. 6Ii naabaala faa vɛɛ n widaulaa ni n karfaazi la n dɔgtɛɛzi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ baa labuu. Awiarɛ tɔɔrɔɔ faa chol ba ni.
Denii ba biine chɔgi, ba sɛɛ chɔgri di ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la tɔɔri yaabuu gunla yaa wiɛɛlaa ni ŋmɛnizi la yaa n na hiŋ la n dɛkkɛ, gunla uŋ aah siwii ú ɛɛ yaa la.’ ”
Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ n na zagra lugɔ deeza biini wia
7Baagu fidikpaŋhiŋ la banna yir Siibat la hɔpizaa tokko ni anaazu hɔl, Koorizeŋ Dariɔs kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ biinii, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia tɛɛ mìŋ́ u dɔgtɛɛ Zɛkaria, di pilli wia bagliŋ lugɔ deeza biini.
8N na baal bɛl a hamuŋa ni n tinni zagaahmu, di chi daazi aŋhina banna yir mɛrtil biini, waluu bɛl nua. Zagaahma, a hulahulazi ani a huŋŋa chi u har.
9N pɛɛzi, “Zagtinna bɛlaarɛ kennei, n dɔɔri?”
Mɛlika la n nuu n na ŋɔ wia la ŋɔ n be, “N daŋ baglii nɛra la n ɛɛwɛɛ.”
10Baal la n chigɛ mɛrtil daazi la biini bagli ba wia keŋ, “Baabuu Kɔraawiizi hum bá gaagi durnya hɛssi maa, di na wia la n na ɛɛ a biine.”
11Denii ba ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la n chigɛ mɛrtil daazi biini la be, “Yaa gaagi durnya maanii di na lugɔ koozaa maa waa hoo. Bampirsɔna bɛnnɛ du de.”
12Denii Kɔraawiizi mɛlika ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ, ɛrɛɛ a birgi mag ka i haa suŋ Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda bola la i baaŋ n na fuuh a ni, binni tokkoahoro ni fi maa biini lai?” 13Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ wiŋɔnanaa ni bampirtigaa wiŋɔzi tɛɛ mɛlika la n nuu n na ŋɔ wia la.
14Denii mɛlika la n nuu n na ŋɔ wia la ŋɔ, “Sii wiŋɔɔlii naa, dí kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, ‘N nɔŋŋi Jɛrusalɛm ni Bizeŋ Ziɔnnɛ werge, 15ka n baaŋ na fuuuh werge durnya hɛssi hina la n na fɛ lugɔ wichɔgii maa wàá wer huuzi baa la ni. N baaŋ faa waa fuuh guŋ, ka a hɛssi hina wiɛɛlaarɛ gillɛ n nɛra tɔɔrɔɔ nyaŋŋi.’
16Awia, n bittɔɔ ba bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm n wa suŋ ba ni, ba kaa bir ma n Dia ni a bol maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.”
17Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la kaa ŋɔ n sii ŋɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N bola daŋ kaa su ni daama, ń kaa tig Jɛrusalɛm ni Bizeŋ Ziɔn hina bampiree, di lizi Jɛrusalɛm ú ɛɛ n hor.”
Nyigzi anaazu wia
18Denii n binni di nyigzi anaazuu du n see! 19N pɛɛzi mɛlika la n na ŋɔ wia n be la, “Bɛɛ nyigzii kennei?”
U ŋɔ n be, “Nyigzi naabuu chigɛ tɛɛ durnya fɔŋŋa hina la n gillɛ Juda, Izrɛl ani Jɛrusalɛm hina maa yaari la.”
20Denii Kɔraawiizi bagliŋ luura banaazu n kpogli silaa. 21N pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛ ba ra ba bá wa ɛɛi?”
Denii u ŋɔ, “Ba ballɔɔ bá wa ɔnzi di kpegli durnya hɛssi hina la n chɔgi Juda hɛri, di gil u nɛra yaari la.”

english_text:
Third Vision: A Measuring Line
1This time I saw someone holding a measuring line, 2and I asked, “Where are you going?”
“To measure Jerusalem,” was the answer. “To find out how wide and long it is.”
3The angel who had spoken to me came toward me, when another angel came up to him 4and said, “Hurry! Tell that man with the measuring line that Jerusalem won't have any boundaries. It will be too full of people and animals even to have a wall. 5The Lord himself has promised to be a protective wall of fire surrounding Jerusalem, and he will be its shining glory in the heart of the city.”
A Call to Action
6The Lord says to his people, “Run! Escape from the land in the north, where I scattered you to the four winds. 7Leave Babylonia and hurry back to Zion.”
8Then the glorious Lord All-Powerful ordered me to say to the nations that had raided and robbed Zion:
Zion is as precious to the Lord as are his eyes. Whatever you do to Zion, you do to him. 9And so, he will put you in the power of your slaves, and they will raid and rob you. Then you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful.
10City of Zion, sing and celebrate! The Lord has promised to come and live with you. 11When he does, many nations will turn to him and become his people. At that time you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful. 12Then Judah will be his part of the holy land, and Jerusalem will again be his chosen city.
13Everyone, be silent!
The Lord is present
and moving about
in his holy place.
translation_text:
Ŋmɛŋ baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra mɛgzi kuna wia
1Denii mìŋ́ Zɛkaria binni chiŋ di na baal bɛl n kpogli ŋmɛŋ baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra mɛgzi kuna! 2N pɛɛzuu, “Lee i ra lanɛi?”
U ŋɔ n be, “N na lau ń ga mɛgzi Jɛrusalɛm, di zum u wassi ni u jaŋzi maga.”
3Denii mɛlika la n faa ŋɔ wia ra tɛŋ la bir di ra kaali. Unna kaali la, mɛlika bɛl chem u ni 4di ŋɔ u be, “Chɔ ga ŋɔ a biipɔllii naa be lugɔ Jɛrusalɛm daŋ ɛɛ bolzeŋ la n wàá dɔɔ koŋlaa, dikuu nɛkpila ni sekpila n niŋ su u biini wia. 5N himmaa daŋ birgi ninlau koŋlii baruu. N girme daŋ su u biini maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
6Ií ra ba manamanaŋ! Ií chɔ lii hɛri la n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la, dikuubɛɛwiai, n gillɔɔ ii yaari bɔr maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
7Ziɔn hina, ií chɔ ba. Ii banla n du Babilɔn hɛri la, ií lii chɔ bir ba Jɛrusalɛm! 8Unla maa n niŋ lɔ ia, lɔ n kunla n wessene n be.”
Awia, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la kpa amaniye naabuu humiŋ ń ga tɛɛ hɛssi la hina n foozi u nɛra kuna la. 9Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɔɔri baa, di gil ba yoma wa foozi ba kuna. Denii ii zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu humiŋ.
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií ra kɔɔ, di gil ii bɔra sɔɔni, n na bau ń wa du ii be.”
11Hɛssi kpila maa hina daŋ ba Kɔraawiizi be, di birgi u nɛra a saŋa hiŋ. U daŋ du ii be, ii zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu humiŋ ii be. 12Juda hɛri daŋ birgi Kɔraawiizi kundɔɔlii la uŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ u hɛrnaniinanii la biini. Jɛrusalɛm ɛɛ bolzeŋ la uŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ kaali a maanii. 13Durnya hina maa, ií chi kirkir Kɔraawiizi see, dikuubɛɛwiai, u izi chinne lii u bɔnaniinanii la uŋ duwɛɛ labuu di ra ba.

english_text:
Fourth Vision: Joshua and Satan
1 I was given another vision. This time Joshua the high priest was standing in front of the Lord's angel. And there was Satan, standing at Joshua's right side, ready to accuse him. 2 But the Lord said, “Satan, you are wrong. Jerusalem is my chosen city, and this man was rescued like a stick from a flaming fire.”
3Joshua's clothes were filthy. 4So the angel told some of the people to remove Joshua's filthy clothes. Then he said to Joshua, “This means you are forgiven. Now I will dress you in priestly clothes.”
5I spoke up and said, “Also put a clean priestly turban on his head.” Then they dressed him in priestly clothes and put the turban on him, while the Lord's angel stood there watching.
6After this, the angel encouraged Joshua by telling him that the Lord All-Powerful had promised:
7If you truly obey me, I will put you in charge of my temple, including the courtyard around it, and you will be allowed to speak at any time with the angels standing beside me. 8 Listen carefully, High Priest Joshua and all of you other priests. You are a sign of things to come, because I am going to bring my servant, the Chosen King.
9Joshua, I have placed in front of you a stone with seven sides. I will engrave something on that stone, and in a single day I will forgive this guilty country. 10 Then each of you will live at peace and entertain your friends in your own vineyard and under your own fig trees.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma wia
1Wipillaa aŋhina ge lugɔ deeza biini, Kɔraawiizi kaa bagliŋ u Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Josua, di u chigɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika see, Sitaani ge chi u nodig keŋkere, di ɛɛ sirya ú kpa wia chuguu. 2Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la ŋɔ Sitaani be, “Kɔ́raawiizi hau i ni! Kɔ́raawiizi la n nɔŋŋi Jɛrusalɛm la jugmii! Baal naa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ daa baŋ vɛzɛɛ lii niŋ biini.”
3Tagta la n doŋŋee Josua faa laali chi a mɛlika see. 4Mɛlika la ŋɔ tɛɛ u dɔŋahina la maa n faa chigɛ u see la, “Ií wir u tagtadoŋ naa.”
Denii u ŋɔ Josua ge be, “N lizi i wichɔgaarɛ i ni, ka ń kpa tagtananii laalii.”
5Denii u ŋɔ, “Ií kpa pɛɛnnanii di vɔɔu namu.” Awia, ba kpa a pɛɛŋ di vɔɔu namu, di laaluu laala Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la see.
6Kɔraawiizi mɛlika ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ Josua, di ŋɔ lugɔ 7kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ra ŋɔ, “Di i danna hiŋzi n ŋmɛnizi di ra ɛɛ wia la minna nyiŋŋi, guŋwaa, i daŋ ɛɛ n Dia ni u diŋŋizi maa binni. N danna nuu i wiisuŋŋaa gunla minna nuu mɛlikazi la n du n see la wiisuŋŋaa la.
8Ií ra nuu, Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Josua ani i dɔŋahina la n soge i be naa, ii chigɔɔ tɛɛ wia la n na ba la. N daŋ lii n balii la banna yir Daa Kel la ni bɔchaaŋ. 9Ií na bii la miŋ kpawɛɛ baŋ Josua see! Bɔra aniidaanɛɛrɛ du u ni. N daŋ sɛɛhzi wii bɛl dau u ni. Hɔpizi kpannɛ ń kpa lizi hɛri naa hina wichɔgaa ba ni. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.
10A hɔl hiŋ, ii bɛl maa daŋ yir u dɔŋhiŋ, u nuu so u grepu ni u fig daa zɛɛ ni bampirsɔna.”

english_text:
Fifth Vision: A Lampstand and Olive Trees
1The angel who explained the visions woke me from what seemed like sleep. 2Then he asked, “What do you see?”
“A solid gold lampstand with an oil container above it,” I answered. “On the stand are seven lamps, each with seven flames. 3 One olive tree is on the right side and another on the left of the oil container. 4But, sir, what do these mean?”
5Then he asked, “Don't you know?”
“No sir,” I replied.
6 So the angel explained that it was the following message of the Lord to Zerubbabel:
I am the Lord All-Powerful. So don't depend on your own power or strength, but on my Spirit. 7Zerubbabel, that mountain in front of you will be leveled to the ground. Then you will bring out the temple's most important stone and shout, “God has been very kind.”
8The Lord spoke to me again and said:
9Zerubbabel laid the foundation for the temple, and he will complete it. Then everyone will know that you were sent by me, the Lord All-Powerful. 10 Those who have made fun of this day of small beginnings will celebrate when they see Zerubbabel holding this important stone.
Those seven lamps represent my eyes—the eyes of the Lord—and they see everything on this earth.
11 Then I asked the angel, “What about the olive trees on each side of the lampstand? What do they represent? 12And what is the meaning of the two branches from which golden olive oil flows through the two gold pipes?”
13“Don't you know?” he asked.
“No sir, I don't,” was my answer.
14Then he told me, “These branches are the two chosen leaders who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
translation_text:
Fintina daa wia
1Mɛlika la mìŋ́ Zɛkaria nuu n faa ra ŋɔ wia la bir wa lalliŋ alugɔ nɛr n na chɔɔ dɔɔ la, 2di pɛɛziŋ, “Bɛɛ i na naanɛi?”
N ŋɔ, “Saliŋ fintina daarɛ n na, tassa hɔŋ u ni. U kaa dɔɔ fintinazi aniidaanɛɛ, bɛl maa dɔɔ yakɔssi duuribɔra aniidaanɛɛ. 3Ɔlivi daazi anɛɛ ge du u kɛrii, bɛl du u nodig keŋkere, bɛl ge du u nomɛɛl keŋkere.”
4N pɛɛzi mɛlika la n na ŋɔ wia n be la, “N dɔɔri, bɛɛ a chi tɛɛi?”
5U pɛɛziŋ, “Haa kuna naa zummɛa?”
N ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, akai, màá zummɛ.”
6Denii u ŋɔ n be, “Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔliirɛ keŋ, u ŋɔ n ŋɔ tɛɛ Zɛrubabɛl, ‘I wia daŋ kuari, ka a wàá lii laallɔɔra gɛɛ i himmaa fɔŋŋa biini, ka n Duma benii á lii,’ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu ŋɔ guŋ.
7Kummaa waa hoo di du kaŋ lugɔ bizeŋ, ú teŋ hìŋ́ Zɛrubabɛl see. I daŋ bir ma n Dia la. Di i wa kpa tuna bii la sag, a nɛra daŋ chaasi, di ra ŋɔ, ‘U wesso, u wesso!’ ”
8Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Zɛkaria be, 9“Zɛrubabɛl chiŋŋi n Dia naa zɛɛrɛ, awia, u daŋ mau tuŋ.” Denii n nɛra zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu humiŋ ba be.
10“Anɛɛ n na gbɛlli wijigzi hɔpiziiyɛi? Nɛra bɔra daŋ sɔɔni, di ba wa na maari daa la uŋ kpawɛɛ di ra deŋli u huma la Zɛrubabɛl nonee biini.
Fintinazi aniidaanɛɛ naa chigɔɔ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi siwee aniidaanɛɛ la n na na durnya wiimaa la.”
11Denii n pɛɛzi a mɛlika, “Bɛɛ ɔlivi daazi anɛɛ naa n chigɛ a fintina daa nodig ni u nomɛɛl keŋkerezi naa ra baglɛi?”
12Denii n kaa kuari pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛ kunaa ɔlivi daazi kela naa n chigɛ saliŋ paipuzi anɛɛ naa kɛraa, nuu ra lii di li saliŋ a biine naa ra baglɛi?”
13U pɛɛziŋ, “Haa a zɛɛ zummɛa?”
N ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, akai, maa zum.”
14Awia, u ŋɔ, “Baala banɛɛ naabuu durnya maa Kɔraawiizi lizi, di waari baa nuu, bá ra humuu.”

english_text:
Sixth Vision: A Flying Scroll
1When I looked the next time, I saw a flying scroll, 2and the angel asked, “What do you see?”
“A flying scroll,” I answered. “About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide.”
3Then he told me:
This scroll puts a curse on everyone in the land who steals or tells lies. The writing on one side tells about the destruction of those who steal, while the writing on the other side tells about the destruction of those who lie.
4The Lord All-Powerful has said, “I am sending this scroll into the house of everyone who is a robber or tells lies in my name, and it will remain there until every piece of wood and stone in that house crumbles.”
Seventh Vision: A Woman in a Basket
5Now the angel who was there to explain the visions came over and said, “Look up and tell me what you see coming.”
6“I don't know what it is,” was my reply.
“It's a big basket,” he said. “And it shows what everyone in the land has in mind.”
7The lead cover of the basket was opened, and in the basket was a woman. 8“This woman represents evil,” the angel explained. Then he threw her back into the basket and slammed the heavy cover down tight.
9Right after this I saw two women coming through the sky with wings outstretched like a stork in the wind. Suddenly they lifted the basket into the air, 10and I asked the angel, “Where are they taking the basket?”
11“To Babylonia,” he answered, “where they will build a house for the basket and set it down inside.”
translation_text:
Hɔŋ la n na zaah nai lugɔ deeza biini wia
1Denii mìŋ́ Zɛkaria kaa binni di na hɔŋ n zaahwɛ waa kaali!
2A mɛlika jaa pɛɛziŋ, “Bɛɛ i na naanɛi?”
N ŋɔ, “N na hɔnnɛ n du chiŋ, di zaah waa kaali, u jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi fi.”
3U ŋɔ n be, “Nuuseeire du u biini tɛɛ banla maa n du a hɛri naa biini. Kenne wia la n du u biini ra bagli. U keŋkere bɛl ra bagluu lugɔ bá duŋŋi ŋmɛɛŋ maa lii a hɛri. U keŋkere bɛl ge ra bagli lugɔ bá duŋŋi nɛr la maa n na hɛɛhzi, di ra kanni kara lii a hɛri.” 4Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ gil a nuuseei lii ga zuu ŋmɛɛŋ ani nɛr la maa n kpa n sɔŋ di hɛɛhzi di ra kanni kara dia. U daŋ du a hiŋ dia, di chɔgi u daazi ni u bia maa.”
Haaŋ n du kɛɛgɔ biini wia
5Denii mɛlika la n na ŋɔ wia n be la lii chi n see, di ŋɔ, “Binni chiŋ na kunla dee n na lii naa.”
6N pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛwɛi?”
U bir ŋɔ, “Kɛɛgɔ baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra mɛgzi kunaa.” Di kaa ŋɔ, “U chigɔɔ tɛɛ nɛra la n du a hɛri maa wichɔgaa.”
7Denii ba pilli u kpana nuatua, n na haaŋ n soge u biini! 8A mɛlika kaa ŋɔ, “Biinikpolaa la,” ka taau du a kɛɛgɔ biini, di lau u tua la tɔ.
9Denii n binni chiŋ di na haanaa banɛɛ n zaahwɛ ra ba n be, ba keeri du alugɔ niilaaraa keeri, di wa kpa a kɛɛgɔ zaah ra kaali.
10Denii n pɛɛzi mɛlika la n na ŋɔ wia n be la, “Lee ba kpa a kɛɛgɔ di ra lanɛi?”
11U bir ŋɔ n be, “Ba kpaubuu ra la Babilɔn hɛri, bá ga ma dia duu. Di ba wa mau tuŋ, ba daŋ kpa a kɛɛgɔ chiŋŋi u bɔr a dia biini, di ra jaamuu.”

english_text:
Eighth Vision: Four Chariots
1Finally, I looked up and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains. 2 The first chariot was pulled by red horses, and the second by black horses; 3 the third chariot was pulled by white horses, and the fourth by spotted gray horses.
4“Sir,” I asked the angel. “What do these stand for?”
5 Then he explained, “These are the four winds of heaven, and now they are going out, after presenting themselves to the Lord of all the earth. 6The chariot with black horses goes toward the north, the chariot with white horses goes toward the west, and the one with spotted horses goes toward the south.”
7The horses came out eager to patrol the earth, and the angel told them, “Start patrolling the earth.”
When they had gone on their way, 8he shouted to me, “Those that have gone to the country in the north will do what the Lord's Spirit wants them to do there.”
The Chosen Leader
9The Lord said to me:
10-11Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah have returned from Babylonia. Collect enough silver and gold from them to make a crown. Then go with them to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah and put the crown on the head of the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak. 12-13 Tell him that I, the Lord All-Powerful, say, “Someone will reach out from here like a branch and build a temple for me. I will name him ‘Branch,’ and he will rule with royal honors. A priest will stand beside his throne, and the two of them will be good friends. 14This crown will be kept in my temple as a reminder and will be taken care of by Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah.”
15When people from distant lands come and help build the temple of the Lord All-Powerful, you will know that the Lord is the one who sent me. And this will happen, if you truly obey the Lord your God.
translation_text:
Laal torkozi anaazu nai lugɔ deeza biini wia
1N kaa na a wipillaa bɛl biini, laal torkozi anaazu n na lii danyɛ bizenaa anɛɛ baambaaŋ! 2Zagaahma ra tɛrgi lugli torko la, a biŋŋe ge ra tɛrgi nɛɛhiŋ la, 3horohiŋ la hora huuhzi, anaazuhiŋ la hora du hulahula. A maa faa ɛɛ zagkpega werge. 4N pɛɛzi mɛlika la n faa ra ŋɔ wia n be la, “N dɔɔri, bɛɛ laal torkozi naa ra baglɛi?”
5A mɛlika ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi bol dunzi anaazu labuu. Durnya maa Kɔraawiizi la seere a lii. 6Laal torko la zagbiŋŋe n na tɛrgi la, ra la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag hɛrii. Unla ge hora n huuhzɛɛ la, ra la wiicholii. Unla hora n du hulahula la ge ra la wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere.”
7A zagkpega n wa liiwɛ, a faa aah siwiire, di ra ɛɛ ania á gaagi durnya maa. Denii a mɛlika ŋɔ, “Ií gaagi daani durnya maa.” A faa gaagi daanuu.
8Denii a mɛlika kaa yiriŋ, di ŋɔ, “Na, anla n na la Babilɔn n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la gillɔɔ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ sɔɔni.”
Josua koorikahuro wia
9Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, 10“Lɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ lii Hɛldai, Tobija ani Jɛdaaya la baŋ faa laurɛɛ la Babilɔn hɛri, ka ba bir ba la be. La Zɛfania biibaal Jɔsia dia a hɔl hiŋ maa. 11Kpa a saliŋhuŋŋa ni a saliŋ kuari koorikahuro, di kpau hi Jɛhɔzadak biibaal Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Josua. 12Ŋɔ u be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ra ŋɔ, ‘Baal la sɔŋ n di Daa Kel labuu keŋ. U daŋ hel lii bɔr la un duwɛɛ la, di bir ga ma Kɔraawiizi Dia. 13Waabuu niŋ ma Kɔraawiizi Dia, di na koori girme, di ra di kora u nɛra ni. Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ chi u koorikara kɛrii, bá nɛra banɛɛ dɔɔ bampirsɔna di ra hum ba huma ni nuukpaŋ.’ 14Ba daŋ kpa a koorikahuro tɛɛ Hɛldai, Tobija, Jɛdaaya ani Zɛfania biibaal Hɛn, ú ɛɛ liize kuŋ Kɔraawiizi Dia biini. 15Banla n du bɔɔnɛɛ la daŋ ba wa hiinii di ma Kɔraawiizi Dia la, denii ii zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu humiŋ ii be. A wii naa daŋ ɛɛ, di ii aah siwii di hiŋ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni wibii.”

english_text:
A Question about Going without Eating
1On the fourth day of Chislev, the ninth month of the fourth year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord again spoke to me. 2-3It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
4-5It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests:
For 70 years you have gone without eating during the fifth and seventh months of the year. But did you really do it for me? 6And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment? 7My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
8-9So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another! 10Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
11-12But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry 13and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
14That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
translation_text:
Nuuvɔɔi la n waa Kɔraawiizi siwii ra su wia
1Koorizeŋ Dariɔs koora dii binni anaazuhiŋ la biini, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wiarɛ tɛɛ Zɛkaria baaguzi kabɛlhiŋ Kislɛv la hɔpizaa anaazuhiŋ hɔl. 2Bɛtɛl hina faa hum Sarɛza ani Rɛgɛm Mɛlɛk ni ba dɔŋahina, dí ba la ga pɛɛzi di zum Kɔraawiizi nfɛrɛ, 3lii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ Dia Kizeehina ni u dɔgtɛɛzi be, di ŋɔ, “Ya gil yaa biine chɔgi, yá ra vɔɔ nua baaguzi anuehiŋ la biini, gunla yaa n faa ra ɛɛ biŋkpila maa biini laa?”
4Denii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔ n be, 5“Pɛɛzi a hɛri hina maa ni a kizeehina, dí, baŋ faa vɔɔ nuuzi di wii ni biinichɔg baaguzi anue ni aniidaanɛɛ hina la biine, binni tokkoahoro ni fi naa, n wiarɛ ba faa vɔɔ a nuuzia? 6Baŋ faa ra di di ra nyɔɔ la, bahinaarɛ ba faa ɛɛ guŋ di ra tɛɛ.”
7Wia naabuu Kɔraawiizi faa gil u dɔgtɛɛzi la n tɔ see la sii, saŋa la Jɛrusalɛm ani bola la n baruu la n faa su nɛra, ba so pɛrɛtɛ, daama sua, nɛra faa so wiifurii nodig wiikakag paga ni wiicholii ge giŋgimee zɛɛzi la.
8Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, 9“Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, ‘Ií ra di wibii di ra na dɔŋa sinyɛna di ra suŋ dɔŋa ni. 10Ií gilɛɛ waa fir luhaaŋ gɛɛ lalbiizi gɛɛ hɔɔhri gɛɛ nyaari. Ií gilɛɛ waa fɛ nfɛrchɔgaa ii biine, di ra du dɔŋa ni.’
11Ka n nɛra ɛɛ nɛkpoŋlaa, di vɛɛ ba nuu tɛŋ, di bir ba hara kpuŋ, di fargi ba digna. 12Ba faa dɔɔ dignikpega, di vɛɛ n Gbɔg gɛɛ n wiŋɔɔlaa la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ n ga n Duma be, di hum n dɔgtɛɛzi lugɔ bá ŋɔ la. Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ baaŋ faa fuuh werge maa.
13Miŋ yir baa la, ba vɛɛ nuuirɛ. Awia, di ba yiriŋ, n gba wàá nuu. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ. 14N faa kpa venne di yaari baa durnya hɛssi maa biine, ba faa ga ɛɛ hɔɔhra. Ba hɛri faa chɔɔ diŋgela, nɛr maa faa waa wette ú ba de. Kenne ba ɛɛ, a hɛrsum birgi diŋgela la.”

english_text:
The Lord's Promises to Zion
1The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
2I love Zion so much that her enemies make me angry. 3I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
4Very old people with walking sticks will once again sit around in Jerusalem, 5while boys and girls play in the streets. 6This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful. 7I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west, 8and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
9I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid. 10Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
11My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before. 12Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky. 13People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
14When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back. 15Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness. 16 But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace. 17Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things.
A Time of Celebration
18The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
19People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
20I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere. 21Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
22Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness. 23When this happens, ten people from nations with different languages will grab a Jew by his clothes and say, “Let us go with you. We've heard that God is on your side.” I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kissi Jɛrusalɛm hina wia
1Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Zɛkaria be, 2“N nɔŋŋi Jɛrusalɛm wiarɛ werge. N siwii aahwɔɔ dikuu u wia, di ra zom u wia, guŋ gil n baan na fuuh u dɔma ni werge.
3N daŋ bir la Jɛrusalɛm, n bolzennaniinanii la, di ga du de. Ba danna yiruu Wibii Bolzeŋ, di ra yir mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ bizeŋ la Bizennaniinanii.
4Bazɛŋzi ni hahzɛŋzi daŋ kaa kpogli daŋkpalli, di ra vol dikuu ba zɛŋaa werge wia, di ga so Jɛrusalɛm bossibaana. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ. 5Biibaala ni biihaana daŋ su a bolzeŋ ŋmɛnizenaa maa di ra dua.
6Aŋhinabe, wia naa daŋ ɛɛ witittaa tɛɛ banla n niŋ ka a bolzeŋ a guŋ saŋa, ka a waa ɛɛ witittaa n be.
7N daŋ lɛɛ n nɛra lii hɛssi la n du wiifurii ni wiicholii la biine, 8di bir ba ba ni Jɛrusalɛm, bá wa du de di ɛɛ n nɛra, ń ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum. N daŋ dɔɔ wibii di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa ba be. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.
9Filaŋkeŋ, ii banla n na nuu wiŋɔɔlaa naa n dɔgtɛɛzi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ ka ba chiŋŋi n Dia zɛɛ la, ií aah siwii di chiiri zɛɛ, di ma mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Dia la. 10Mɔɔ ka a saŋa faa hel, ba faa waa newee gɛɛ sel maa ra turgi. Nɛr maa faa waa wette u hum u huma dikuu u dɔm wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, n faa gillɔɔ nɛra hah dɔŋa. 11Ka filaŋkeŋwaa, màá ka ɛɛ n nɛra naa n kawɛɛ naa gunla miŋ faa ra ɛɛ la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.
12Di ba duu kuna, a daŋ lii di lɛɛ nɛnnɛ, grepu daazi ge nɔŋ nɛnnɛ. Dooŋ ba nɛnnɛ, á hɛri lii kuna nɛnnɛ. Annii naa maanii ń kpa tɛɛ banla n kawɛɛ la, a ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuna. 13Juda ni Izrɛl hina, iiŋ faa ɛɛ nɛra la hɛssi hina n faa ra see nuuzi la, n daŋ jaa lɛɛ ia, di kissi ia. Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm, ka chi chigigi.”
14Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, “Saŋa la ii naabaala n faa fuuh n baaŋ, n faa ta jinaa ń tɔɔri baa werge. N faa waa n nfɛrɛ bittɛ ka ɛɛ guŋ. 15Ka filaŋkeŋ, n siwii aahwɔɔ ń ɛɛ winanaa tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina. Awia, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. 16Ií ra ɛɛ annii naa, ií ra ŋɔ wibii bɛŋ di ra tɛɛ dɔŋa, di ra di seriyazi ni wibii. 17Ií gilɛɛ ra ta jinachɔgaa dikuu ii dɔŋahina wia gɛɛ di hɛɛhzi ra kanni kara. N kiichɔgiirɛ annii maa ɛɛi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”
18Denii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ kaa ŋɔ n be, 19“Baagu anaazuhiŋ, anuehiŋ, aniidaanɛɛhiŋ ani fihiŋ la biine iiŋ ɔɔ ra vɔɔ nuuzi la daŋ ɛɛ bɔsɔna ni sideŋŋa saŋazi, di ɛɛ hɔpizizenaa dii la n dɔɔ bɔsɔna tɛɛ Juda hina. Awia, ií nɔŋŋi wibii ni bampirsɔna.”
20Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, “Nɛkpila ni ba dizi daŋ lii bolzenaa di haa ba Jɛrusalɛm, 21denii bolzeŋ bɛl hina la bolzeŋ bɛl hina be, di ga ŋɔ, ‘Ií gil ya la ga jaami Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ, di suŋŋuu ú kissi yaa. Ií ba ya kaali.’ 22Denii nɛkpila ni ba dizi ani hɛssi la n kpekke hina ba Jɛrusalɛm, bá wa nuu wia lii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ be, di jaamuu.”
23Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, “A hɔpizaa hiŋ biini, hɔɔhra fi daŋ lii durnya hɛssi ni mɔɔrizi biine, di ba Jus hinuu be di wa lau u tagta ka ŋɔ, ‘Yaa waa ra nyiŋŋuu yaa nii ɛɛ kpaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa nuuwɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du i benii.’ ”

english_text:
Israel's Enemies Will Be Punished
1 This is a message
from the Lord:
His eyes are on everyone,
especially the tribes
of Israel.
So he pronounces judgment
against the cities
of Hadrach and Damascus.
2Judgment will also fall
on the nearby city
of Hamath,
as well as on Tyre and Sidon,
whose people are clever.
3Tyre has built a fortress
and piled up silver and gold,
as though they were dust
or mud from the streets.
4Now the Lord will punish Tyre
with poverty;
he will sink its ships
and send it up in flames.
5 Both Ashkelon and Gaza
will tremble with fear;
Ekron will lose all hope.
Gaza's king will be killed,
and Ashkelon emptied
of its people.
6A mob of half-breeds
will settle in Ashdod,
and the Lord himself
will rob Philistia of pride.
7No longer will the Philistines
eat meat with blood in it
or any unclean food.
They will become part
of the people of our God
from the tribe of Judah.
And God will accept
the people of Ekron,
as he did the Jebusites.
8God says, “I will stand guard
to protect my temple from those
who come to attack.
I know what's happening,
and no one will mistreat
my people ever again.”
The Lord Tells about the Coming King
9 Everyone in Jerusalem,
celebrate and shout!
Your king has won a victory,
and he is coming to you.
He is humble
and rides on a donkey;
he comes on the colt
of a donkey.
10 I, the Lord, will take away
war chariots and horses
from Israel and Jerusalem.
Bows that were made for battle
will be broken.
I will bring peace to nations,
and your king will rule
from sea to sea.
His kingdom will reach
from the Euphrates River
across the earth.
The Lord Promises To Rescue Captives
11 When I made a sacred agreement
with you, my people,
we sealed it with blood.
Now some of you are captives
in waterless pits,
but I will come to your rescue
12and offer you hope.
Return to your fortress,
because today I will reward you
with twice what you had.
13I will use Judah as my bow
and Israel as my arrow.
I will take the people of Zion
as my sword
and attack the Greeks.
The Lord Will Protect His People
14Like a cloud, the Lord God
will appear over his people,
and his arrows will flash
like lightning.
God will sound his trumpet
and attack in a whirlwind
from the south.
15The Lord All-Powerful
will protect his people,
and they will trample down
the sharpshooters
and their slingshots.
They will drink and get rowdy;
they will be as full as a bowl
at the time of sacrifice.
16The Lord God will save them
on that day,
because they are his people,
and they will shine on his land
like jewels in a crown.
17How lovely they will be.
Young people will grow there
like grain in a field
or grapes in a vineyard.
translation_text:
Izrɛl hina dɔma digna tɛraa wia
1Wia la n lii Kɔraawiizi be di ra ba á wa huuzi Hadrak hɛri
ni bolzeŋ Damaskusii keŋ.
Newea ni Izrɛl dizi maa dɛlli Kɔraawiizii.
2Haali Hamaf ni Hadrak n du magbɔɔ gba,
Taaya ni Saidɔn hina,
n dɔɔ nunzuma werge
gba dɛlluubuu.
3Taaya hina ma diikpegaa tɛɛ bahinaa,
di chaali saliŋhuŋŋa
ni saliŋ lugɔ kpaga,
di su ba bola maa.
4Ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ paagi u kundɔɔlaa maa,
di chɔgi u muuzeŋ gbessi la
n gillɛ u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa la maa.
Ninne niŋ fuuh u maa kpɛlɛŋ.
5Bolzeŋ Askɛlɔn hina daŋ na guŋ, ɔnsii lau baa,
bolzeŋ Gaza hina ra miŋŋi,
dikuu ba biine n chɔkkɛ wia.
Bolzeŋ Ɛkrɔn hina gba
tamii daŋ tuŋ, bá lɔgɔ lii baa.
Gaza hina daŋ nyaa ba koori,
Askɛlɔn hina maa chɔ.
6Hɔɔhraa niŋ wa foozi Asdɔd di so.
N daŋ chɔgi Filisti hina
jigsi la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛ la.
7Ba wàá ka ra hee ola la n dɔɔ chal
gɛɛ di ra di diukiilaa.
Banla maa n kawɛɛ daŋ ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi hora,
di ɛɛ sitɔɔra Juda biini.
Ɛkrɔn hina daŋ birgi
n nɛra lugɔ Jɛbus hina.
8N daŋ guu n Dia,
dikuu laallɔɔra n na ba
bá wa lɔu laal wia.
Màá ka gil biinikpola hiŋ maa wa dɔɔ n nɛra di ra sunni baa.
Filaŋkennaa waa,
n na du ba taurɛ.
Kɛrɛbɛl koori wia
9Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina, ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia werge!
Jɛrusalɛm hina,
ií ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna!
Ií binni na, ii koori ra ba ii benii.
U wia deŋloore,
ú wer lɛɛ ia.
U ɛɛ sisɔna hinnɛ,
di tinni kawee ra ba,
kaupɔl bɛllɛ u tinni
di ra ba.
10Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N daŋ lizi laal torkozi lii Izrɛl,
di lizi laal zagra la
lii Jɛrusalɛm.
Ba daŋ kuugi laal hozi la.
Ii koori daŋ sii bampirsɔna wia
tɛɛ durnya hɛssi hina.
U kora daŋ chi muuzeŋ bɛl di ga hel bɛlhiŋ,
di lii Muu Yufretis
di ga hel hɛri tunazi.”
11Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ,
“Ka iawaa, dikuu nuukpaŋ la n ni ia n kpa mbusu lizaa sela chal ɛɛ la wia,
n daŋ lizi ii nɛra lii
hɛrduma nɛra tɔi dia biini.
12Ií bir la ii diikpega la,
ii banla baŋ laurɛɛ
kaali hɛrdumazi
ka ii jaa dɔɔ tamii la.
Haali filaŋkeŋ gba, n na ŋɔ ii benii lugɔ
n daŋ kaa jaa ia kuna la
iiŋ faa dɔɔwɛ la guŋ bunɛɛ.
13N daŋ kpa Juda birgi lugɔ laallɔɔri hoo,
di kpa Izrɛl birgi lugɔ u hobee.
N daŋ kpa Bolzeŋ Ziɔn baala birgi lugɔ tokobizi,
di yoo Giris baala.”
14Kɔraawiizi daŋ izi di guali u nɛra ni,
ú hobii ra nyɛgzi
alugɔ nazaa.
Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ huuh u bensunoniina,
wiifurii nodig wiikakag dooŋ ni
pekpeg biinii ú ga ba.
15Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ daŋ guu baa.
Ba daŋ kpu ba dɔma.
Ba danna chaasi laal biini lugɔ baŋ nyɔɔ siŋ di ra dɛɛzi la.
Ba daŋ kpu ba dɔma,
bá challi ra pal lugɔ
baŋ kpu sela lizi mbusu,
di fug a chal lii tassa biini
waari mbusu lizibɔr ni la.
16Di a hɔpizii wa hello, Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ u nɛra,
gunla penɔɔni
n ɔɔ lɛɛ u peeza la.
Ba danna nyɛgzi u hɛri biini
alugɔ koorikahuro
binanaa la yoola n kpolle la.
17A hɛri daŋ du wer di dɔɔ kɛlli.
U mia ni siŋ daŋ gil
u suŋgure
ni biipɔllaa hel nɛnnɛ.

english_text:
A Bright Future for Judah and Israel
1I, the Lord, am the one
who sends storm clouds
and showers of rain
to make fields produce.
So when the crops need rain,
you should pray to me.
2 You can't believe idols
and fortunetellers,
or depend on the hope
you receive from witchcraft
and interpreters of dreams.
But you have tried all of these,
and now you are like sheep
without a shepherd.
3I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am fiercely angry
with you leaders,
and I will punish you.
I care for my people,
the nation of Judah,
and I will change
this flock of sheep
into charging war horses.
4From this flock will come leaders
who will be strong
like cornerstones and tent pegs
and weapons of war.
5They will join in the fighting,
and together they will trample
their enemies like mud.
They will fight,
because I, the Lord,
will be on their side.
And they will crush
the enemy cavalry.
6I will strengthen
the kingdoms of Judah
and Israel.
And I will show mercy
because I am the Lord,
their God.
I will answer their prayers
and bring them home.
Then it will seem as though
I had never rejected them.
7Israel will be like
a tribe of warriors
celebrating with wine.
When their children see this,
they will also be happy
because of me, the Lord.
8I will give a signal
for them to come together
because I have rescued them.
And there will be as many
as ever before.
9 Although I scattered my people
in distant countries,
they won't forget me.
Once their children are raised,
they will return—
10I will bring them home
from Egypt and Assyria,
then let them settle
as far as Gilead and Lebanon,
until the land overflows
with them.
11My people will go through
an ocean of troubles,
but I will overcome the waves
and dry up the deepest part
of the Nile.
Assyria's great pride
will be put down,
and the power of Egypt
will disappear.
12I'll strengthen my people
because of who I am,
and they will follow me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi daŋ binni Juda hina ni
1Ií suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ú tɛɛ ia dooŋ, dooŋ balaa saŋa.
Waabuu gillɛ dooŋ a tiŋ,
di ba ra tɛɛ nɛra,
di gil kooni kuna biri,
di ra hel nɛnnɛ.
2Karaa vuga ra kanni,
vugra ra na kara wipillaa,
di ra bagli deeza la n ɛɛ kara zɛɛzi.
Ba nɛra bampirtigaa
waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ.
Awia, a nɛra ra gaaguu lugɔ peeza n leuwe,
ba ra fir baa alugɔ peeza la
n waa nɔɔni dɔɔwɛ.
3Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “N baaŋ fuuhwoo penɔɔna la ni,
n daŋ tɛrgi a guŋ
sitɔɔra la digna.
Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ daŋ binni
Juda domee la n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ
peeza la ni,
di gil bá ɛɛ lugɔ
laal biini zagkpega.
4Juda dee biinii bii la n na faari dia zɛɛ la lii,
ba biinii tanti daasirii lii,
ba biinii laal hoo lii,
ba biinii sitɔɔri maa lii.
5Ba maa daŋ kpau ɛɛ lugɔ laal biini nɛkpega,
di ra fɛrgi bol biini
ŋmɛnizenaa la n dɔɔ
kpɛchɛgaa la.
Dikuu Kɔraawiizi n du ba be wia,
ba daŋ lɔ ba dɔma
di kpegli banla
n tinni zagra la.
6N daŋ gil Juda hina du kpeg,
di lɛɛ Joosɛf diahina.
N daŋ gil ba kaa du ba dubinii la,
dikuu miŋ na ba sinyɛna wia.
Ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ miŋ
faa waa baa vɛɛwɛ ta,
dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.
N daŋ nuu ba wiisuŋŋaa.
7Izrɛl hina daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ fɔŋŋazeŋ hina,
ba bɔra daŋ sɔɔni baa
alugɔ baŋ nyɔɔ siŋ la.
Ba biizi daŋ na guŋ ba bɔra sɔɔni,
bá dɔɔ bampirsɔna dikuu
Kɔraawiizi wia.
8N daŋ yir baa,
di chaali baa.
Wibii maa, n daŋ lɛɛ baa,
bá bir du kpil gunla
baŋ faa duwɛɛ la.
9Haali miŋ gillɛ ba yaari hɛssi biine gba,
ka ba danna liizi n wia
a hɛhjaŋa biine.
Ba ni ba biizi daŋ piri,
di bir ba.
10N daŋ bir ba ba ni, di lii Ijip hɛri,
di chaali baa lii Asiiria hɛri,
di ba ba ni Giliad ni Lɛbanɔn hɛssi biine,
ka bɔr waa du de, di hel baa.
11Tɔɔrɔɔzeŋ daŋ huuzi baa alugɔ muuzeŋ nii n ɔɔ ra lɔ werge la,
ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil a nii sɔɔni.
N daŋ gil Muu Naal
nii maa hiihzi.
Asiiria hina ge jigsi
ni Ijip hina fɔŋŋa
la maa tuŋ.
12N daŋ tɛɛ n nɛra fɔŋŋa,
ba danna jaamiŋ,
di nuu ra tɛŋ.
Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

english_text:
Trouble for Israel's Enemies
1Lebanon, open your gates!
Let the fire come in
to destroy your cedar trees.
2Cry, you cypress trees!
The glorious cedars have fallen
and are rotting.
Cry, you oak trees of Bashan!
The dense forest
has been chopped down.
3Listen! Shepherds are crying.
Their glorious pastures
have been ruined.
Listen! Lions are roaring.
The forests of the Jordan Valley
are no more to be found.
Worthless Shepherds
4The Lord my God said to me:
Tend those sheep doomed for slaughter! 5The people who buy and butcher them go unpunished, while everyone who sells them says, “Praise the Lord! I'm rich.” Not even their shepherds have pity on them.
6Tend those sheep because I, the Lord, will no longer have pity on the people of this earth. I'll turn neighbor against neighbor and make them slaves of a king. They will bring disaster on the earth, and I'll do nothing to rescue any of them.
7So I became a shepherd of those sheep doomed to be slaughtered by the sheep dealers. And I gave names to the two sticks I used for tending the sheep: One of them was named “Mercy” and the other “Unity.” 8In less than a month, I became impatient with three shepherds who didn't like me, and I got rid of them. 9Then I said, “I refuse to be your shepherd. Let the sheep that are going to die, go on and die, and those that are going to be destroyed, go on and be destroyed. Then let the others eat one another alive.”
10On that same day, I broke the stick named “Mercy” to show that the Lord had canceled his agreement with all people. 11The sheep dealers who saw me knew at once that this was a message from the Lord. 12-13 I told them, “Pay me my wages, if you think you should; otherwise, forget it.” So they handed me my wages, a measly 30 pieces of silver.
Then the Lord said, “Throw the money into the treasury.” So I threw the money into the treasury at the Lord's temple. 14Then I broke the stick named “Unity” and canceled the ties between Judah and Israel.
15Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd. 16Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
17You worthless shepherd,
deserting the sheep!
I hope a sword
will cripple your arm
and blind your right eye.
translation_text:
1Lɛbanɔn hina, ií pilli ii dominuuzi,
niŋ zuu di ii
hɛriŋkpol daazi maa!
2Daananaa, ií ra wii di ra lɔɔgi wile werge,
dikuubɛɛwiai, hɛriŋkpol
daazi la chogloore,
daananaa la maa chɔkkɔɔ.
Daazenaa la n du Basan, ií ra wii di ra chɛɛhgi werge,
dikuubɛɛwiai, kɔrzeŋ la
daazi maanii ba ŋmɛnni ha.
3Ií ra nuu penɔɔna n na chɛɛhgi,
