Nau! Ii gillɔɔ Kɔraawiizi widaulii la bir pɛɛ dikuu ii naabaala ŋmɛnɛɛ hiŋaa wia. 7Nɛfugzee ia! Aizaaya faa bagli ii wiarɛ nɛnnɛ, di ŋɔ,
8‘Nɛra naa, ba nuuzii ba kpa ra tɔgziŋ,
ka ba bampiree wan lauwɛ tama maa.
9Newea kiizii ba kpa ra bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ,
ka ŋɔ nɛ́ra ra hiŋ. Awia, pɛɛrɛ ba ra jaamiŋ la.’ ”
Kuna la n ɔɔ gil nɛr doŋ Kɔraawiizi be wia
(Maak 7:14-23)
10Yeesu yir nɛkpila la, ba ba u be, u ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu di gil á ra zuu ii bampiree nɛnnɛ. 11Kuna la unna di la wàá wer gil u doŋ. Ka wia la n na lii nua, aabuu niŋ gil u doŋ.”
12Denii Yeesu hiŋra ba u be di wa ŋɔ, “Wia naa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa, a waa Farisizi la pattɛ. I zum gunnɛ naa?”
13Yeesu ŋɔ, “Kunla maa n Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi n waa duuwe, n daŋ kpuzuu ha. 14Ií gil ba wia de. Ba ɛɛ nyuŋŋaa ka ra bagli nyuŋŋa ge ŋmɛnɛɛ. Di nyuŋŋi ra bagli u dɔŋhiŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ, ba maa daŋ chol bɔɔ biini.”
15Pitta ŋɔ Yeesu be, “Bagli yaa a sɛɛlii zɛɛ.”
16Yeesu pɛɛzi, “Ii ge haa waa nfɛrɛ dɔɔwɛa? 17Ii waa zummɛ lugɔ kuna la maa iinna di, hiarɛ aa zuu ii bir nyɛa ra taa? 18Ka wia la n na lii nuawaa, bampirii biinii a ra lii di ra tɛɛ nɛra doŋa. 19Newee biinii nfɛrchɔgaa, dɔŋkpui, sɛnsɛŋ wia, wikuna, ŋmɛɛri, kara kannaa ani dɔŋgbɛllaa ra lii, 20di gil nɛra ra doŋ. Di haa sammɛ ka ra di, guŋwaa wàá tɛi doŋa.”
Haaŋ bɛl yarda wia
(Maak 7:24-30)
21Yeesu kaa izi de di la Taaya ni Saidɔn barii. 22Denii Keenan hɛri haaŋ bɛl lii de di ba u be, di waa yiruu siaahmu ni, “N Dɔɔri, Deevid Naana, na n sinyɛna. Tinnanchɔgiirɛ ra izi n biihambie werge maa.”
23Yeesu siigi u ni. U hiŋra ba u be di wa suŋŋuu, “Ŋɔ ú bir. U ra hiŋ yaabuu di ra kɔɔ.”
24Yeesu ŋɔ, “Izrɛl peleulaa la bɛŋ benii Kɔraawiizi humiŋ.”
25A haaŋ wa hel di giŋŋi u see di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri, hiiniŋ.”
26U ŋɔ u be, “A waa dɛkkɛ baŋ kpa biizi diwee tɛɛ nuuzihina.”
27U ŋɔ, “Wibiire, n Dɔɔri. Ka nuuzihina ɔɔ na anla a dɔɔra n na di a chogli hɛri labuu di ra di.”
28Awia, Yeesu ŋɔ, “I yardimbuu werge. I daŋ na wii la hinna nyiŋŋi.” U bie hiŋ nyaagi lii a saŋa hiŋ.
Yeesu n tɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa anaazu diwee wia
29Yeesu lii de di la Galilii muuzeŋ la nua di ga tinni giŋgimii bɛl di ga so. 30Nɛkpila ba u be di kpogli naasiwaa ni nosiwaa hina, nyuŋŋa, gberaa ani gɛnaa, u chaa ba maa. 31Nɛkpila la n wa na gɛnaa n na ŋɔ wia, gbɛraa n izee, naasiwaa ni nosiwaa hina n na vol, nyuŋŋa ra na, a tir baa werge maa. Ba ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl na hum la sɔŋ.
32Yeesu yir u hiŋra di ŋɔ ba be, “Nɛra naa wia dɔɔmbuu sinyɛna. Ba hɔpizaa ahoroo keŋ baŋ du n be ɛŋ. Ba waa kaa dɔɔ kummaa bá di. Maa nyiŋŋi n ta baa keŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, baŋ waa diwee naa, ba daŋ waa bɛɛli ŋmɛnɛɛ.”
33U hiŋra ŋɔ u be, “Yaa n du bɔduma naa, a nɛra ge du kaŋ werge naa, lee ya na paanuuzi a hel ba maa, bá wer hee di piŋɛi?”
34Yeesu pɛɛzi baa, “Paanuuzi aŋmɛnɛɛ n du ii benei?”
Ba ŋɔ, “Paanuuzi aniidaanɛɛ ni nyinni tamaa du de.”
35Yeesu gil nɛkpila la maa so hɛri, 36ka u kpa paanuuzi aniidaanɛɛ ani nyinni la di suŋŋi wiizi du a ni, ka lawaa mɔnni mɔnni di kpa tɛɛ u hiŋra, ba ge kpa bɔnni nɛkpila la. 37Ba maa hee di piŋ. U hiŋra paagi anla baŋ heewe ka ka la, a su kɛɛgɔzi aniidaanɛɛ. 38Banla n diwee la, ba baala bɛŋ hel kagboŋa anaazu, ka ba waa haana ni biizi waa kutte jaa. 39Yeesu jaa ta baa ka zuu muugbera di la Magadan barii.

english_text:
A Demand for a Sign from Heaven
(Mark 8.11-13; Luke 12.54-56)
1 The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus and tried to test him by asking for a sign from heaven. 2He told them:
If the sky is red in the evening, you say the weather will be good. 3But if the sky is red and gloomy in the morning, you say it is going to rain. You can tell what the weather will be like by looking at the sky. But you don't understand what is happening now. 4 You want a sign because you are evil and won't believe! But the only sign you will be given is what happened to Jonah.
Then Jesus left.
The Yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees
(Mark 8.14-21)
5The disciples had forgotten to bring any bread when they crossed the lake. 6 Jesus then warned them, “Watch out! Guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
7The disciples talked this over and said to each other, “He must be saying this because we didn't bring along any bread.”
8Jesus knew what they were thinking and said:
You surely don't have much faith! Why are you talking about not having any bread? 9 Don't you understand? Have you forgotten about the 5,000 people and all those baskets of leftovers from just five loaves of bread? 10 And what about the 4,000 people and all those baskets of leftovers from only seven loaves of bread? 11Don't you know by now that I am not talking to you about bread? Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees!
12Finally, the disciples understood that Jesus wasn't talking about the yeast used to make bread, but about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Who Is Jesus?
(Mark 8.27-30; Luke 9.18-21)
13When Jesus and his disciples were near the town of Caesarea Philippi, he asked them, “What do people say about the Son of Man?”
14 The disciples answered, “Some people say you are John the Baptist or maybe Elijah or Jeremiah or some other prophet.”
15Then Jesus asked, “But who do you say I am?”
16 Simon Peter spoke up, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
17Jesus told him:
Simon, son of Jonah, you are blessed! You didn't discover this on your own. It was shown to you by my Father in heaven. 18So I will call you Peter, which means “a rock.” On this rock I will build my church, and death itself will not have any power over it. 19 I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven, and God in heaven will allow whatever you allow on earth. But he will not allow anything you don't allow.
20Jesus told his disciples not to tell anyone he was the Messiah.
Jesus Speaks about His Suffering and Death
(Mark 8.31—9.1; Luke 9.22-27)
21From then on, Jesus began telling his disciples what would happen to him. He said, “I must go to Jerusalem. There the nation's leaders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the Law of Moses will make me suffer terribly. I will be killed, but three days later I will rise to life.”
22Peter took Jesus aside and told him to stop talking like that. He said, “God would never let this happen to you, Lord!”
23Jesus turned to Peter and said, “Satan, get away from me! You're in my way because you think like everyone else and not like God.”
24 Then Jesus said to his disciples:
If any of you want to be my followers, you must forget about yourself. You must take up your cross and follow me. 25 If you want to save your life, you will destroy it. But if you give up your life for me, you will find it. 26What will you gain, if you own the whole world but destroy yourself? What would you give to get back your soul?
27 The Son of Man will soon come in the glory of his Father and with his angels to reward all people for what they have done. 28I promise you some of those standing here will not die before they see the Son of Man coming with his kingdom.
translation_text:
Baŋ suŋŋi Yeesu ŋɔ ú ɛɛ wizeŋ wia
(Maak 8:11-13; Luuk 12:54-56)
1Farisizi ni Sajusizi baŋhina ba Yeesu be di waa nyiŋŋi ba ɛɛu di na. Ba ŋɔ ú ɛɛ wizeŋ bɛl lii chiŋ di bagli baa bá zum u wibii.
2U ŋɔ ba be, “Di bɔr wa duanɔɔ, chiŋ aah, ii ɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Dooŋ waa hoo, dikuubɛɛwiai, chiŋ aahwɔɔ.’ 3Di chɔɔzi genii, ii ɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Dooŋ du de, dikuubɛɛwiai, baama tɔwɔɔrɛ, chiŋ aah.’ Ii wettoo zum chiŋ wia zɛɛ, ka ii waa wette zum wia naa n na ɛɛ filaŋkennaa zɛɛ. 4Banla n dɔɔ wichɔgaa di vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, baabuu ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu ba na wizeŋ bɛl mɔɔ ka haa zum n wibii. Ka màá ɛɛ wiimaa bá na. Ka wii naa bɛnnɛ ií kpa di zum n wibii. Waabuu Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Joona wia la.” Yeesu gil baa ka kaali.
Farisizi ni Sajusizi yiisi wia
(Maak 8:14-21)
5U hiŋra n faa ra nyiŋŋi ba gi muuzeŋ la, ba faa waa ba diwee wia liizee ka gi. 6Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ra du iihinaa tau nɛnnɛ dikuu Farisizi ni Sajusizi yiisi wia.”
7Ba ra bil dɔŋa bá zum u wiŋɔzi la zɛɛ, di ra ŋɔ dɔŋa be, “Yaa n waa paanuuzi kpawɛɛ ba la wiarɛ u nii ŋɔ guŋ.”
8Yeesu zum wii la wia banna bil dɔŋa la, u pɛɛzi baa, “Ɛrɛɛ ii ra bil dɔŋa dikuu iiŋ waa paanuuzi kpawɛɛ ba la wiai? Yarda nyaara! 9Ii nfɛrɛ haa waa ballɛa? Ii waa paanuuzi anue la nɛra kagboŋa anue n heewe ani kɛɛgɔzi anla baŋ heewe ka ka n suwee la wia ra liizia? 10Ii waa kaa liizi paanuuzi aniidaanɛɛ la ge nɛra kagboŋa anaazu n heewe ani kɛɛgɔzi anla baŋ heewe ka ka n suwee la wiaa? 11Ka ɛrɛɛ ii waa wette zum lugɔ paanuu wia lɛi n faa ŋɔ lai? Farisizi ni Sajusizi yiisi wiarɛ n ŋɔ ií ra du tau la.” 12Denii ba jaa zum lugɔ paanuu yiisi lɛi u faa ŋɔ. Farisizi ni Sajusizi baglaarɛ u kpa ra yir yiisi la.
Pitta n bagli nɛr la dee n ɛɛ Yeesu wia
(Maak 8:27-30; Luuk 9:18-21)
13Yeesu kaa izi ra la Siizaria Filipai barii. Unna la, u pɛɛzi u hiŋra, “Anɛɛ nɛra ɔɔ ra yir Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaallɛi?”
14Ba ŋɔ, “Baŋhina ra yiriibuu Jɔɔn Kɔraawiizi Niisɔɔri. Baŋhina ge ra yirii Ɛlija. Baŋhina kaa ra yirii Jɛrɛmia gɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la bɛl.”
15U kaa pɛɛzi baa, “Ka anɛɛ ii ge ra yirinnɛi?”
16Saimɔn Pitta ŋɔ, “Hinuu Kristo, Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la Biibaal.”
17Yeesu ŋɔ u be, “Joona biibaal Saimɔn, i nuu sumaa. Newee lɛi pilli guŋ tɛi i zum. N Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizii pilli guŋ tɛi i zum.
18Gil n kaa ŋɔ i be naa. I sɔnnɛ Pitta. Bii naa nyuurɛ ń ma n hiŋra dia hɔŋ. Siu ni u fɔŋŋa wàá wer kpegluu maa. 19N daŋ tɛi Kɔraawiizi Kora saafiibee. Kunla maa hin niŋ vɔɔ hɛri naa, u vɔɔwɔɔ Kɔraawiizi be. Kunla maa hin niŋ pur hɛri naa, u puttoo Kɔraawiizi gba be.” 20Denii u ŋɔ u hiŋra be dí ba gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ nɛr maa be lugɔ waabuu Kristo la.
Yeesu n ŋɔ u tɔɔrɔɔ dii ni u siu wia
(Maak 8:31—9:1; Luuk 9:22-27)
21A saŋa Yeesu Kristo jaa ra bagli u hiŋra lugɔ a dɛkkɔɔ un niŋ la Jɛrusalɛm, bol nabɔnzi, Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi ani Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna la ga tɔɔruu di kpuu, ka u daŋ izi siu biini hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl.
22Pitta lawuu lii kɛrii, di ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ ra ŋɔ gunnɔu. Kɔ́raawiizi kissii wia naa gilɛɛ waa nai, n Dɔɔri.”
23Yeesu bir u har kpu Pitta, ka ŋɔ u be, “Sitaani, tuzi lii n be! I ra tɔmbuu ŋmɛnɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, annii naa hinna ŋɔ naa, a waa Kɔraawiizi be liwɛɛ. Newea benii a lii.”
24Denii Yeesu ŋɔ u hiŋra be, “Nɛr la maa n niŋ hiŋiŋ, ú gil u kipar ka kpa u daakaŋlii sag u baŋaa di ra hiŋiŋ. 25Nɛr la maa n niŋ gil u miibɔɔ wia aah u siwii, wàá na u hiŋ. Ka hinla maa n niŋ gil i miibɔɔ wia ha, dikuu n wia, hìŋ́ niŋ na i hiŋ. 26Di i wetto di durnya suma maa, ka haa i hiŋ nawɛɛ, bɛɛ tɔnaa i nai? Beedee kunnɛ néwee wer kpa chɛr di na u hinnɛi?
27Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal daŋ bir ba ni n Mɛɛ girme ni u mɛlikazi ni. Di n wa ballɔ, n daŋ jaa turgi nɛr maa gunla uŋ hummɛ. 28Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Ii banla n chigɛ bɔnnaa naa, baŋhina wàá siu mɔɔ ka ií na Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal n niŋ di n kora di ra ba.”

english_text:
The True Glory of Jesus
(Mark 9.2-13; Luke 9.28-36)
1 Six days later Jesus took Peter and the brothers James and John with him. They went up on a very high mountain where they could be alone. 2There in front of the disciples, Jesus was completely changed. His face was shining like the sun, and his clothes became white as light.
3All at once Moses and Elijah were there talking with Jesus. 4So Peter said to him, “Lord, it is good for us to be here! Let us make three shelters, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
5 While Peter was still speaking, the shadow of a bright cloud passed over them. From the cloud a voice said, “This is my own dear Son, and I am pleased with him. Listen to what he says!” 6When the disciples heard the voice, they were so afraid they fell flat on the ground. 7But Jesus came over and touched them. He said, “Get up and don't be afraid!” 8When they opened their eyes, they saw only Jesus.
9On their way down from the mountain, Jesus warned his disciples not to tell anyone what they had seen until after the Son of Man had been raised from death.
10 The disciples asked Jesus, “Don't the teachers of the Law of Moses say Elijah must come before the Messiah does?”
11 Jesus told them, “Elijah certainly will come and get everything ready. 12 In fact, he has already come. But the people did not recognize him and treated him just as they wanted to. They will soon make the Son of Man suffer in the same way.” 13Then the disciples understood Jesus was talking to them about John the Baptist.
Jesus Heals a Boy
(Mark 9.14-29; Luke 9.37-43a)
14Jesus and his disciples returned to the crowd. A man knelt in front of him 15and said, “Lord, have pity on my son! He has a bad case of epilepsy and often falls into a fire or into water. 16I brought him to your disciples, but none of them could heal him.”
17Jesus said, “You people are too stubborn to have any faith! How much longer must I be with you? Why do I have to put up with you? Bring the boy here.” 18Then Jesus spoke sternly to the demon. It went out of the boy, and right then he was healed.
19Later the disciples went to Jesus in private and asked him, “Why couldn't we force out the demon?”
20-21 Jesus replied:
It is because you don't have enough faith! But I can promise you this. If you had faith no larger than a mustard seed, you could tell this mountain to move from here to there. And it would. Everything would be possible for you.
Jesus Again Speaks about His Death
(Mark 9.30-32; Luke 9.43b-45)
22While Jesus and his disciples were going from place to place in Galilee, he told them, “The Son of Man will be handed over to people 23who will kill him. But three days later he will rise to life.” All of this made the disciples very sad.
Paying the Temple Tax
24 When Jesus and the others arrived in Capernaum, the collectors for the temple tax came to Peter and asked, “Does your teacher pay the temple tax?”
25“Yes, he does,” Peter answered.
After they had returned home, Jesus went up to Peter and asked him, “Simon, what do you think? Do the kings of this earth collect taxes and fees from their own people or from foreigners?”
26Peter answered, “From foreigners.”
Jesus replied, “Then their own people don't have to pay. 27But we don't want to cause trouble. So go cast a line into the lake and pull out the first fish you hook. Open its mouth, and you will find a coin. Use it to pay your taxes and mine.”
translation_text:
Yeesu birgaa wia
(Maak 9:2-13; Luuk 9:28-36)
1Hɔpizaa anumbɛl n wa bɛrɛɛ, Yeesu kpogli Pitta, Jems ani u niwee Jɔɔn tinni bizeŋ bɛl nyuu ba bɛŋ. 2Denii u izi birgi ba see. U siwee ra chaani lugɔ wiizi. U laala bir huuhzi werge alugɔ bɔchaaŋ. 3Ba ŋɔ bá binni di Moosis ni Ɛlijaa du ba be, ba ni Yeesu ra ŋɔ wia.
4Pitta ŋɔ Yeesu be, “N Dɔɔri, yaa n du ɛnnaa, guŋ wesso. Di i ra nyiŋŋi, n daŋ du pampannizi ahoro, í dɔɔ bɛl, Moosis dɔɔ bɛl, Ɛlija ge dɔɔ bɛl.”
5Pitta n haa ra ŋɔ a wia, di baama wa tɔ ba ni zuuuu. Ba nuu loobii bɛl n lii baama la biini, di ŋɔ, “N Biinɔŋŋiirɛ keŋ. U wia parimbuu werge. Ií ra nuu u be!”
6U hiŋra n wa nuu loobii la, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa, ba chogli hɛri di tɔɔgi ba siwee. 7Yeesu ba ba be di wa gbɔgzi baa ka ŋɔ, “Ií izi. Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm!” 8Ba lalli ba nyuuni, di nɛr maa waa kaa hoo di Yeesu bɛŋ lɛi. Ba izi di ra tuu.
9Banna tuu la, Yeesu ŋɔ, “Ií gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ wia naa iin nawɛɛ naa mɔɔ. Di Kɔraawiizi wa lalli Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal siu biini la, denii ií jaa wer ŋɔa.”
10Ba pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna ɔɔ ŋɔ lugɔ Ɛlijaa niŋ ba mɔɔnɛi?”
11U ŋɔ, “Wibiire. Ɛlijaa niŋ feli ba di wa ɛɛ wiimaa sirya. 12Ka ií gil n ŋɔ ii be. Ɛlija la teŋ ballɔɔ. Ba zumuu huhzi, ka ɛɛu ba kipar. Gunnɛ bá kaa tɔɔri Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal ge.” 13Denii u hiŋra zum lugɔ Jɔɔn Kɔraawiizi Niisɔɔri wiarɛ u ŋɔ la.
Yeesu n chaa biibambie bɛl n dɔɔ gbuŋgbunzi wia
(Maak 9:14-29; Luuk 9:37-43)
14Baŋ wa hel nɛkpila la be, baal bɛl lii ba biini di ba wa giŋŋi Yeesu see, 15di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri, na n biibaal naa sinyɛna. U ra chogli gbuŋgbunzii. Ŋmɛnɛbɛl ɔɔ chol niŋ biinii, ŋmɛnɛbɛl ge u chol nii biini. A ra nuubuu werge. 16N kpau ba i hiŋra be bá chaau. Ba chaau huhzi.”
17Yeesu ŋɔ, “Ii filaŋkeŋ hina ɛɛ yarda nyaara ni wichɔgɛɛraa! Ɛrɛɛ birgaa dɔnnɛ ń du ii be di birgi mag ka ii haa zuminnɛi? Ɛrɛɛ kanyittii ń haa di iai? Ií kpa a bie ba.” 18Yeesu hau tinnanchɔgii la ni, u lii a bie ni. U na alaanfia a guŋ saŋa.
19Yeesu ni u hiŋra n wa du ba bɛŋ, ba pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yaawaa faa waa wette duŋŋi tinnanchɔgii lai?”
20U ŋɔ, “Iin nyaa yarda wiarɛ ii waa wette duŋŋuu la. Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Di ii dɔɔ yarda haali u mɛg mastad bii n du jigajiga gunla, ka ii daŋ wer ŋɔ bizeŋ naa be, dí u izi kaali yembɛl, u daŋ izi kaali de. 21Ii wàá ɛɛ wiimaa huhzi.”
22Yeesu ni u hiŋra wa hel Galilii hɛri. Denii Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “Ba daŋ kpa Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal du n dɔma nonee biini, 23bá kpuŋ, a hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, n daŋ bir izi lii siu biini.” Yeesu n wa ŋɔ guŋ, ba biine chɔgi baa werge maa.
Kɔraawiizi Dia lampoo wia
24Baŋ wa hel Kapɛniɔm, banla n na lɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia lampoo ba Pitta be, di wa ŋɔ, “I nabɔma waa a lampoo ra turgi gɛɛ?”
25Pitta ŋɔ, “U ra turguu.”
Pitta n wa zuu dia, Yeesu feli ŋɔ a wia di pɛɛzi, “Durnya koora naa, anɛɛ ba ɔɔ lɛɛ lampooi? Ba nɛra gɛɛ hɔɔhrai? Saimɔn, ɛrɛɛ i nai?”
26U ŋɔ, “Hɔɔhraa ba ra lɛɛ.”
Yeesu ŋɔ, “Di gunnɛ, ba nɛra liwɔɔrɛ. 27Ka maa nyiŋŋi n fuuh ba baaŋ. Awia, la muuzeŋ la nua di ga ta gɔrga. Nyiŋ la hin niŋ feli lau, í pilli u nua di na, i daŋ na kebii de. Lizuu di kpa la ga tɛɛ baa di turgi n nii maa hora.”

english_text:
Who Is the Greatest?
(Mark 9.33-37; Luke 9.46-48)
1 About this time the disciples came to Jesus and asked him who would be the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. 2Jesus called for a child to come over and stand near him. 3 Then he said:
I promise you this. If you don't change and become like a child, you will never get into the kingdom of heaven. 4But if you are as humble as this child, you are the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. 5And when you welcome one of these children because of me, you welcome me.
Temptations To Sin
(Mark 9.42-48; Luke 17.1,2)
6It will be terrible for people who cause even one of my little followers to sin. Those people would be better off thrown into the deepest part of the ocean with a heavy stone tied around their necks! 7The world is in for trouble because of the way it causes people to sin. There will always be something to cause people to sin, but anyone who does this will be in for trouble.
8 If your hand or foot causes you to sin, chop it off and throw it away! You would be better off to go into life paralyzed or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the fire that never goes out. 9 If your eye causes you to sin, poke it out and get rid of it. You would be better off to go into life with only one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fires of hell.
The Lost Sheep
(Luke 15.3-7)
10-11 Don't be cruel to any of these little ones! I promise you their angels are always with my Father in heaven. 12Let me ask you this. What would you do if you had 100 sheep and one of them wandered off? Wouldn't you leave the 99 on the hillside and go look for the one that had wandered away? 13I am sure that finding it would make you happier than having the 99 that never wandered off. 14That's how it is with your Father in heaven. He doesn't want any of these little ones to be lost.
When Someone Sins
(Luke 17.3)
15 If one of my followers sins against you, go and point out what was wrong. But do it in private, just between the two of you. If that person listens, you have won back a follower. 16 But if that one refuses to listen, take along one or two others. The Scriptures teach that every complaint must be proven true by two or more witnesses. 17If the follower refuses to listen to them, report the matter to the church. Anyone who refuses to listen to the church must be treated like an unbeliever or a tax collector.
Allowing and Not Allowing
18 I promise you God in heaven will allow whatever you allow on earth, but God will not allow anything you don't allow. 19I promise that when any two of you on earth agree about something you are praying for, my Father in heaven will do it for you. 20Whenever two or three of you come together in my name, I am there with you.
An Official Who Refused To Forgive
21 Peter came up to the Lord and asked, “How many times should I forgive someone who does something wrong to me? Is seven times enough?”
22 Jesus answered:
Not just 7 times, but 77 times! 23This story will show you what the kingdom of heaven is like:
One day a king decided to call in his officials and ask them to give an account of what they owed him. 24As he was doing this, one official was brought in who owed him 50,000,000 silver coins. 25But he didn't have any money to pay what he owed. The king ordered him to be sold, along with his wife and children and all he owned, in order to pay the debt.
26The official got down on his knees and began begging, “Have pity on me, and I will pay you every cent I owe!” 27The king felt sorry for him and let him go free. He even told the official that he did not have to pay back the money.
28But as this official was leaving, he happened to meet another official, who owed him 100 silver coins. So he grabbed the man by the throat. He started choking him and said, “Pay me what you owe!”
29The man got down on his knees and began begging, “Have pity on me, and I will pay you back.” 30But the first official refused to have pity. Instead, he went and had the other official put in jail until he could pay what he owed.
31When some other officials found out what had happened, they felt sorry for the man who had been put in jail. Then they told the king what had happened. 32The king called the first official back in and said, “You're an evil man! When you begged for mercy, I said you did not have to pay back a cent. 33Don't you think you should show pity to someone else, as I did to you?” 34The king was so angry that he ordered the official to be tortured until he could pay back everything he owed. 35That is how my Father in heaven will treat you, if you don't forgive each of my followers with all your heart.
translation_text:
Anɛɛ n ɛɛ nɛzeŋ Kɔraawiizi Kora biinei?
(Maak 9:33-37; Luuk 9:46-48)
1Denii Yeesu hiŋra ba u be di wa pɛɛzuu, “Anɛɛ ɛɛ nɛzeŋ Kɔraawiizi Kora biinei?”
2Yeesu yir bichala bɛl, di gil u chi ba baambaaŋ, 3ka ŋɔ, “Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Di ii waa wette kpa iihinaa birgi bichalli, ii wàá wer zuu Kɔraawiizi Kora biini maa. 4Nɛr la maa n niŋ kpa u hiŋ tama lugɔ bichala naa, u ɛɛ nɛzenne Kɔraawiizi Kora biini.
5Nɛr la maa n niŋ lɛɛ bichala naa dɔŋ di dau dikuu n wia, minuu u lɛɛ dau la.
Nɛr daraa ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa wia
(Maak 9:33-37; Luuk 9:46-48)
6Nɛr la maa n niŋ gil bichala naa dɔŋ n yardiŋ naa leu, di ba kpa namzeŋ vɔɔ sag u baŋaa di kpau ha muuzeŋ biini u siu, u gunnɛ bɔ uŋ haa du de di ra nyiŋ.
7Wiarɛ niŋ huuzi durnya dikuu wia n du de, di gil nɛra ra leu wia. A wia daŋ ɔɔ wa du de, ka wiarɛ niŋ huuzi nɛr la maa n niŋ gil a du de la.
8Di i nonii gɛɛ i naa ɔɔ gil i ra leu, teŋuu ha. Di i dɔɔ nokpaŋ gɛɛ naakpaŋ ka dɔɔ miibɔɔ, u gunnɛ bɔ hiŋ dɔɔ nonee anɛɛ gɛɛ naazi anɛɛ, ka ba kpai ha niŋ la n waa dinzi la biini. 9Di i siwii ge ɔɔ gil i ra leu, foŋuu ha. Di i dɔɔ sikpaŋ ka dɔɔ miibɔɔ, u gunnɛ bɔ hiŋ dɔɔ siwee anɛɛ ka ba kpai ha Sitaani ninzeŋ la biini.
Peleulii sɛɛlii wia
10Ií ra dazi ií gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli bichalli naa dɔŋa. Ií gil n ŋɔ ii be. Ba dɔɔ mɛlikazii Kɔraawiizi be a ra binni ba ni. A mɛlikazi ɔɔ ra hel n Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi benii. 11Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal ballɔɔ ń waa nyiŋŋi kuna la n leuwe.
12Di baal bɛl dɔɔ u peeza kalfa, bɛl gaagi di ga leu, wàá gil peeza tokkoanaazu ni fidikabɛl la giŋgimee nyuu, ka la ga nyiŋŋi kpaŋkpaŋ la guŋŋ ú wa nauwaa? Ɛrɛɛ ii nai? 13Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Di u wa nau, pekpaŋkpaŋ la wia daŋ sɔɔni u bɔra werge maa, di kaali tokkoanaazu ni fidikabɛl la n waa leuwe la. 14Gunnɛ ii Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi waa nyiŋŋi lugɔ bichalli naa bɛl maa wa leu la.
I lulli n ɛɛi wichɔgaa wia
15Di i dɔŋhiŋ bɛl wa ɛɛi wichɔgaa, la ga pɛɛzuu a zɛɛ, i nuu bɛŋ. Di u wa nuuwɔ tɛi, i jaa na dammuu tɛɛ i hiŋ. 16Di waa nuuwɛ tɛi, nyiŋŋi nɛkpaŋ gɛɛ nɛra banɛɛ di jaa i hiŋ ni, bá wer nuu ii maa hora, di ɛɛ i daansɛɛ hina. Nɛra banɛɛ gɛɛ bahoro daansɛɛrɛ niŋ wer gil á ɛɛ wibii. 17Di waa nuuwɛ tɛɛ ba ge, i jaa kpa a wii bagli Yeesu hiŋra la maa. Di waa sɛɛwɛ ú nuu tɛɛ ba ge, gil u ɛɛ lugɔ wichɔgɛɛra la n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la bɛl ii be.
18Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Kunla maa iin niŋ vɔɔ hɛri naa, u vɔɔwɔɔ Kɔraawiizi be. Kunla maa iin niŋ pur hɛri naa, u puttoo Kɔraawiizi gba be.
19Ií gil n kaa ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Di ii nɛra banɛɛ ɛɛ nuukpaŋ hɛri naa ani wii la maa iin niŋ suŋŋi ii Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ka suŋŋuu, u daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa iin suŋŋuu la di tɛɛ ia, 20dikuubɛɛwiai, bɔr la maa nɛra banɛɛ gɛɛ bahoro n chaalɛɛ di ra yir n sɔŋ, n gba du ba benii.”
Balii la n waa nɛsunaa dɔɔi dɔɔwɛ sɛɛlii wia
21Denii Pitta ba u be di wa pɛɛzuu, “N Dɔɔri, di n dɔŋhiŋ bɛl ɛɛŋ wichɔgaa n gil tɛu, buŋmɛnɛɛ ú kaa ɛɛŋ wichɔgaa ka ń haa gil tɛuwɛi? Buniidaanɛɛ maga mɛgzɔɔrɛ gɛɛ?”
22Yeesu ŋɔ, “Gil n ŋɔ i be. Buniidaanɛɛ bɛŋ lɛi í gil tɛu. I daŋ gil tɛu buniidaanɛɛ, di kaa gil tɛu buniidaanɛɛgaa guŋŋ hanna la.
23Awia, Kɔraawiizi Kora wia ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ koori bɛl n izee di dɔɔ u balaa. A hɔl bɛl u ŋɔ ú zum kima la maga baŋ diu. 24Ba kpogli bɛl ba. U faa di u kim saliŋ kilozi kagboŋa ahoro ni tokkoanɛɛrɛ, 25ka waa kebee dɔɔwɛ un niŋ turguu. U dɔɔri ŋɔ bá kpa u ni u haaŋ ni u biizi ni u kuna la maa un dɔɔwɛ, dí ga yoo dí turgi a kim.
26U balii la chol u naazi di ra fɔrguu di ŋɔ, ‘Haa ra di kanyitti. N daŋ haa turgi a maa.’ 27U wia dɔɔ u dɔɔri la sinyɛna, u gil a kim maa tɛu ka giluu.
28U balii la lii di ga na u dɔŋhiŋ bɛl. A baal faa di u ge kinnɛ bɔɔtizi tama. U la ga lawuu di hanzi u baŋaa, di ŋɔ, ‘Turgi n kim la.’ 29A baal chol u naazi di ra fɔrguu di ŋɔ, ‘Haa ra di kanyitti. N daŋ haa turgi a maa.’
30Ka waabuu waa sɛɛwɛ tɛu ka gil ba tɔu dia guŋŋ ú wa turgi a kim maa. 31U dɔŋahina n wa na gunla n ɛɛwɛ la, ba biine chɔgi werge maa. Ba ba wa bagli a wia maa tɛɛ ba dɔɔri.
32U dɔɔri yiruu, u ba. U ŋɔ, ‘Baljagaa hiŋ! N gil kim werge maanii tɛi dikuu hiŋ fɔrgiŋ wia. 33Di gunnɛ, a faa waa dɛkkɛ i ge n vii suŋ i dɔŋhiŋ la ni gunla miŋ n suŋ i ni laa?’ 34U baaŋ fuuh werge maa. U ŋɔ bá kpau ga tɔ dia ka tɔɔruu guŋŋ ú wa turgi kim la maa tuŋ.
35Gunnɛ di ii bɛl maa waa sɛɛwɛ ú gil tɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ ani u biini maa, ii Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ u ge gba guŋ.”

english_text:
Teaching about Divorce
(Mark 10.1-12)
1When Jesus finished teaching, he left Galilee and went to the part of Judea east of the Jordan River. 2Large crowds followed him, and he healed their sick.
3Some Pharisees wanted to test Jesus. They came up to him and asked, “Is it right for a man to divorce his wife for just any reason?”
4 Jesus answered, “Don't you know in the beginning the Creator made a man and a woman? 5 That's why a man leaves his father and mother and gets married. He becomes like one person with his wife. 6Then they are no longer two people, but one. And no one should separate a couple God has joined together.”
7 The Pharisees asked Jesus, “Why did Moses say a man could write out divorce papers and send his wife away?”
8Jesus replied, “You are so heartless! That's why Moses allowed you to divorce your wife. But from the beginning God did not intend it to be that way. 9 I say if your wife has not committed some terrible sexual sin, you must not divorce her to marry someone else. If you do, you are unfaithful.”
10The disciples said, “If that's how it is between a man and a woman, it's better not to get married.”
11Jesus told them, “Only those people who have been given the gift of staying single can accept this teaching. 12Some people are unable to marry because of birth defects or because of what someone has done to their bodies. Others stay single in order to serve God better. Anyone who can accept this teaching should do so.”
Jesus Blesses Little Children
(Mark 10.13-16; Luke 18.15-17)
13Some people brought their children to Jesus, so he could place his hands on them and pray for them. His disciples told the people to stop bothering him. 14But Jesus said, “Let the children come to me, and don't try to stop them! People who are like these children belong to God's kingdom.” 15After Jesus had placed his hands on the children, he left.
A Rich Young Man
(Mark 10.17-31; Luke 18.18-30)
16A man came to Jesus and asked, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?”
17Jesus said to him, “Why do you ask me about what is good? Only God is good. If you want to have eternal life, you must obey his commandments.”
18 “Which ones?” the man asked.
Jesus answered, “Do not murder. Be faithful in marriage. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about others. 19 Respect your father and mother. And love others as much as you love yourself.” 20The young man said, “I have obeyed all of these. What else must I do?”
21Jesus replied, “If you want to be perfect, go sell everything you own! Give the money to the poor, and you will have riches in heaven. Then come and be my follower.” 22When the young man heard this, he went away sad, because he was very rich.
23Jesus said to his disciples, “I tell you, it's terribly hard for rich people to get into the kingdom of heaven! 24In fact, it's easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to get into God's kingdom.”
25When the disciples heard this, they were greatly surprised and asked, “How can anyone ever be saved?”
26Jesus looked straight at them and said, “There are some things people cannot do, but God can do anything.”
27Peter replied, “Remember, we have left everything to be your followers! What will we get?”
28 Jesus answered:
Yes, all of you have become my followers. And so in the future world, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, I promise you will sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel. 29All who have given up home or brothers and sisters or father and mother or children or land for me will be given 100 times as much. They will also have eternal life. 30 But many who are now first will be last, and many who are last will be first.
translation_text:
Baal ni haaŋ dɔŋa vɛɛi wia
(Maak 10:1-12)
1Yeesu n wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, u izi Galilii hɛri di la Juda hɛri la n du Jɔɔdan muu baŋgia bɛl la. 2Nɛkpila hiŋuu. U chaa baa de.
3Farisizi baŋhina ba u be di wa ɛɛu na, di pɛɛzuu, “Di baal vɛɛ u haaŋ dikuu wiimaa wia, a gunna kiiu gɛɛ waa kiiyei?”
4Yeesu bir pɛɛzi baa, “Ii haa waa karmɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini lugɔ Kɔraawiizi n ta newea, baal ni haannɛ u maa? 5U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Awia, a wesso baal n gil u maa ni u mɛɛ ka la u haaŋ be, bá nɛra banɛɛ kpau ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋkpaŋ. 6Ba waa kaa ɛɛ nɛra banɛɛ, ka ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋkpaŋ. Nɛra la Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ ba ɛɛ kpaŋ la, a waa dɛg newee n bargi baa dɔŋa ni.’ ”
7Ba ŋɔ, “Moosis faa ŋɔ báal ɔɔ kpa hahvɛɛri hɔŋ tɛɛ u haaŋ ka vɛɛu. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ u ŋɔ gunnɛi?”
8Yeesu ŋɔ, “Ii digna n kpekke werge wiarɛ Moosis gil ii ra vɛɛ ii haana. Ka guŋ lɛi a faa du lugli la. 9Miŋwaa ra ŋɔ ii benii lugɔ baal la maa n vɛɛ u haaŋ, di waa sɛmmɛ lɛi, ka la ga kpa haaŋ bɛl, u ni a haaŋ maa ra sɛmuu.”
10Yeesu hiŋra ŋɔ u be, “Di baal ni u haaŋ wia du guŋ, amɔ, guŋwaa di u faa waa haaŋ kpawɛɛ, u guŋ bɔ.”
11Yeesu ŋɔ, “Nɛr maa lɛi niŋ wer nuu wiŋɔzi naa. Banla Kɔraawiizi n dauwɛ guŋ, ba bɛnnɛ niŋ wer nuua. 12Baala baŋhina waa wer hahkpai dikuu gunla baŋ lul baa ba du wia. Baŋhina ge ɛɛ nɛvaraa dikuu gunla nɛra n ɛɛ baa la wia. Baŋhina kaa lau bahinaa di birgi lugɔ a nɛvaraa dikuu Kɔraawiizi Kora wia. Nɛr la maa n niŋ sɛɛ baglaa naa, ú sɛɛ.”
Yeesu n kissi bichalli wia
(Maak 10:13-16; Luuk 18:15-17)
13Denii nɛra baŋhina kpa bichalli ba Yeesu be di ra nyiŋŋi ú kpa u nonee sagzi ba ni di suŋŋi wiizi tɛɛ baa. Yeesu hiŋra n wa na guŋ, ba ŋɔ bá gilɛɛ ɛɛ guŋ.
14Ka Yeesu ŋɔ, “Ií gil a bichalli ba n be, di gilɛɛ duŋŋi baa. Nɛra la n du kennaa bichalli n duwɛɛ naa, baabuu dɛg Kɔraawiizi Kora biini dui.” 15U kpa u nonee sagzi ba ni, ka izi de kaali.
Biipɔllii bɛl n ɛɛ daama hiŋ wia
(Maak 10:17-31; Luuk 18:18-30)
16Biipɔllii bɛl ba u be di wa pɛɛzuu, “N Nabɔma, bɛɛ winaniirɛ ń ɛɛ di wer na miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ lai?”
17Yeesu pɛɛzi, “Ɛrɛɛ i ra pɛɛziŋ winanaa wiai? Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ ɛɛ nanii ga tuŋ. Ama, di i ra nyiŋŋi i na miibɔɔ, a hiŋ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa la.”
18U pɛɛzuu, “Aabuu a bɛlaa?” Yeesu ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ wàá kpu nɛr, gilɛɛ wàá sɛm, gilɛɛ wàá ŋmɛɛ, gilɛɛ wàá kanni kara. 19A tɔgzi i mɛɛ ni i maa, di kaa ‘nɔŋŋi i dɔŋhiŋ alugɔ i hiŋ.’ ”
20A biipɔllii ŋɔ, “Annii naa maanii n hiŋ. Bɛɛ n kaa kai?”
21Yeesu ŋɔ u be, “Di i ŋɔ í wia wer deŋli ga tuŋ, amɔ, í la ga kpa i kuna la maa hiŋ dɔɔwɛ yoo, di kpa a kebee sunzi nyaara. I daŋ jaa dɔɔ daama Kɔraawiizi be, ka jaa ba waa hiŋiŋ.”
22Uŋ wa nuu guŋ, u bir kaali. U biini chɔgi, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa dɔɔ kunaa werge.
23Yeesu ŋɔ u hiŋra be, “Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. A daŋ du kpol dɔɔna be, ka bá zuu Kɔraawiizi Kora biini. 24Ií gil n kaa ŋɔ ii be. Nyugma ni nɛɛza bɔɔ zuuirɛ duglɛɛ kaali dɔɔŋ ni Kɔraawiizi Kora biini zuui.”
25U hiŋra n wa nuu guŋ, a tir baa werge maa. Ba pɛɛzuu, “Amɔ, anɛɛ n niŋ wer na lɛɛi naanɛi?”
26Yeesu binni baa ka ŋɔ, “A kpolloo newea be, ka wiimaa waa hoo Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ɛɛu huhzi.”
27Denii Pitta ŋɔ u be, “Yaawaa gil yaa kummaanii ka waa hiŋii. Bɛɛ tɔnaa ya na naanɛi?”
28Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Ii banla n na hiŋiŋ naa, di durnya naa wia wa tunnɔ, ufalii wa lii, Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal wa di n kora di so koorikara la ni ani girme, ii ge daŋ so koorikassi fidaanɛɛ ni, di ra di Izrɛl hina dizi fidaanɛɛ la seriya. 29Nɛr la maa n gil u diini gɛɛ u kpɛɛnzi gɛɛ u niuna gɛɛ u maa gɛɛ u mɛɛ gɛɛ u biizi gɛɛ u kooni dikuu n wia, u daŋ kaa na guŋ werge maa, di kaa dɔɔ miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ. 30Ama, nɛkpila n tɔ see di ra di nabɔmuu filaŋkennaa, ba daŋ bir wa kaali har di gaa di bichaluu, ka bánla n faa ra di bichaluu la bir wa lɛɛ nabɔmuu di ra di ba ni.”

english_text:
Workers in a Vineyard
1As Jesus was telling what the kingdom of heaven would be like, he said:
Early one morning a man went out to hire some workers for his vineyard. 2After he had agreed to pay them the usual amount for a day's work, he sent them off to his vineyard.
3About nine that morning, the man saw some other people standing in the market with nothing to do. 4He promised to pay them what was fair, if they would work in his vineyard. 5So they went.
At noon and again about three in the afternoon he returned to the market. And each time he made the same agreement with others who were loafing around with nothing to do.
6Finally, about five in the afternoon the man went back and found some others standing there. He asked them, “Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?”
7“Because no one has hired us,” they answered. Then he told them to go work in his vineyard.
8 That evening the owner of the vineyard told the man in charge of the workers to call them in and give them their money. He also told the man to begin with the ones who were hired last. 9When the workers arrived, the ones who had been hired at five in the afternoon were given a full day's pay.
10The workers who had been hired first thought they would be given more than the others. But when they were given the same, 11they began complaining to the owner of the vineyard. 12They said, “The ones who were hired last worked for only one hour. But you paid them the same that you did us. And we worked in the hot sun all day long!”
13The owner answered one of them, “Friend, I didn't cheat you. I paid you exactly what we agreed on. 14Take your money now and go! What business is it of yours if I want to pay them the same that I paid you? 15Don't I have the right to do what I want with my own money? Why should you be jealous, if I want to be generous?”
16 Jesus then said, “So it is. Everyone who is now last will be first, and everyone who is first will be last.”
Jesus Again Tells about His Death
(Mark 10.32-34; Luke 18.31-34)
17As Jesus was on his way to Jerusalem, he took his twelve disciples aside and told them in private:
18We are now on our way to Jerusalem, where the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses. They will sentence him to death, 19and then they will hand him over to foreigners who will make fun of him. They will beat him and nail him to a cross. But on the third day he will rise from death.
A Mother's Request
(Mark 10.35-45)
20The mother of James and John came to Jesus with her two sons. She knelt down and started begging him to do something for her. 21Jesus asked her what she wanted, and she said, “When you come into your kingdom, please let one of my sons sit at your right side and the other at your left.”
22Jesus answered, “Not one of you knows what you are asking. Are you able to drink from the cup that I must soon drink from?”
James and John said, “Yes, we are!”
23Jesus replied, “You certainly will drink from my cup! But it isn't for me to say who will sit at my right side and at my left. This is for my Father to say.”
24When the ten other disciples heard this, they were angry with the two brothers. 25 But Jesus called the disciples together and said:
You know foreign rulers like to order their people around. And their great leaders have full power over everyone they rule. 26 But don't act like them. If you want to be great, you must be the servant of all the others. 27And if you want to be first, you must be the slave of the rest. 28The Son of Man did not come to be a slave master, but a slave who will give his life to rescue many people.
Jesus Heals Two Blind Men
(Mark 10.46-52; Luke 18.35-43)
29Jesus was followed by a large crowd as he and his disciples were leaving Jericho. 30Two blind men were sitting beside the road. And when they heard that Jesus was coming their way, they shouted, “Lord and Son of David, have pity on us!”
31The crowd told them to be quiet, but they shouted even louder, “Lord and Son of David, have pity on us!”
32When Jesus heard them, he stopped and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
33They answered, “Lord, we want to see!”
34Jesus felt sorry for them and touched their eyes. At once they could see, and they became his followers.
translation_text:
Paahdiire wia
1Yeesu kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi Kora wia ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baal bɛl n izee chɔɔzin pikke ni, di la ga nyiŋŋi paahdiire bá ga hum u grepu daazi koo. 2U na baŋhina, u ni baa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ lugɔ bá hum a hɔl ka wa lɛɛ kebikpaŋ. U hum baa u koo bá ga hum.
3Denii u kaa lii suuri hei saŋa, di ga na nɛra baŋhina n chigɛ yawa pɛɛpɛɛ. 4U ŋɔ ba be, ‘Ií ge gba la n grepu daazi koo la ga hum ka ń turgi ia gunla maa n dɛkkɛ.’ 5Ba kpa kaali gaa hum.
Denii u kaa lii wibaŋkanchirii di kaa hum baŋhina.
A kaa wa ɛɛ tama u kaa lii di kaa hum baŋhina. 6Duana u kaa lii di baŋhina kaa chi yawa la. U pɛɛzi baa, ‘Ɛrɛɛ ii chi ɛŋ pɛɛpɛɛ wiizi wa chol gunnɛi?’
7Ba ŋɔ, ‘Nɛr maa waa yaa tɛɛwɛ huma ŋɔ ya hum.’ U ŋɔ, ‘Ií ge gba la n koo la ga hum.’
8Ba la gaa hum. Wiizi n wa cholle a koo hiŋ yir u balii di ŋɔ ú yir paahdiire la turgi baa. Dí u yir banla n tɔ har la di turgi baa guŋŋ wa hel banla n tɔ see la.
9Banla n laŋŋɛ duana saŋa la ba. U turgi bɛl maa dinaariɔs kpaŋ. 10Banla n tɔ see la n wa helle, ba zumɔɔ lugɔ ba hor daŋ du kaŋ kaali guŋ. Ka dinaariɔs kpaŋkpaŋaa ba gba na. 11Ba lɛɛ ka nuumi ra du koo hiŋ la, di ŋɔ, 12‘Bannii n tɔ har naa, ba hummɔɔ tama, ka yaawaa hum werge, wiizi ge kpu yaa. Ka i gil yaa maa turgaa ɛɛ kpaŋ. Nau!’
13Ka u ŋɔ bɛl be, ‘N dammu, mɛɛ ɛɛwɛ wichɔgaa. Yaa faa waa nuukpaŋ ɛɛwɛ lugɔ ń turgii dinaariɔs kpaŋaa? 14Kpa i kebee ra la. N na nyiŋŋi n turgi baal naa n tɔ har lugɔ miŋ turgi i ge naabuu. 15Minuu dɔɔ n kebee. Màá kpaa ɛɛ gunla minna nyiŋŋiaa? Di n dɔɔ bunya, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ a ra wii ii ninɛi?’
16Awia, banla n tɔ har di ra di bichaluu la daŋ bir wa lɛɛ see di gaa di nabɔmuu, ka banla n faa ra di nabɔmuu la bir la har di ga lɛɛ bichaluu ra di.”
Yeesu n kaa ŋɔ u siu wia buhorohiŋ wia
(Maak 10:32-34; Luuk 18:31-34)
17Yeesu faa ra nyiŋŋi u la Jɛrusalɛm. U yir u hiŋra fidibanɛɛ bɛŋ. Ba maa ra la. Banna la, u ŋɔ ba be, 18“Yaa ra la Jɛrusalɛmnɛ. Di yaa ga hel de, ba daŋ kpa Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal du Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi ni Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna nonee, bá diŋ seriya, di na n kpui ŋmɛnɛɛ, 19di kpaŋ ga du banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ nonee biini, bá ɛɛŋ mɔmɔsia di viiriŋ di kpuŋ daakaŋlii ni, ka Kɔ́raawiizi wa lalliŋ hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl.”
Haaŋ wiisuŋŋaa wia
(Maak 10:35-45)
20Denii Zɛbɛdi haaŋ kpogli u biibaala Jems ni Jɔɔn di ba Yeesu be, di wa giŋŋi jaamuu, di ŋɔ ú suŋŋuu wii bɛl.
21Yeesu pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋei?” U ŋɔ, “N na nyiŋŋuu í ŋɔ nua tɛŋ lugɔ di i wa di i kora la, ń biibaalaa banɛɛ naa nabɔnzi, bɛl so i nodig keŋkere, bɛl ge so i nomɛɛl keŋkere.”
22Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “Wii naa iin suŋŋɛɛ naa, ii waa zum gunla u har n duwɛɛ. Tɔɔrɔɔ nii la ban niŋ wa tɛŋ ń nyɔɔ la, ii ge daŋ wer nyɔɔuwaa?”
Ba ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ wer.”
23U ŋɔ ba be, “Tɔɔrɔɔ nii la min niŋ nyɔɔ la, ii ge gba daŋ nyɔɔu, wibii maa. Ka n nodig sogni ni n nomɛɛl sogni lawaa, miŋ lɛi niŋ lizi baa. N Mɛɛ teŋ lizi baabuu.”
24Denii Yeesu hiŋra fi la n wa nuu guŋ, ba baana fuuh Jems ni u niwee la ni werge maa. 25Awia, Yeesu yir baa, ba ba u be. U ŋɔ, “Ii zummɔ lugɔ nɛra la n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ nabɔnzi ra di kpegzii ba nɛra ni. Ba nɛzenaa ge ra bagli fɔŋŋa nɛra ni. 26Ka a waa wer iawaa n na ɛɛ guŋ. Ii biini, nɛr la maa n na nyiŋŋi ú ɛɛ nɛzeŋ, u daŋ kpa u hinnɛ bichaluu di ra hum ii maa. 27Hinla maa n na nyiŋŋi i ɛɛ nabɔma, i daŋ kpa i hiŋ birgi ii maa yom. 28Gunnɛ Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal waa ballɛ ń wa nyiŋŋi balaa, bá ra humiŋ la. N ballɔɔ ń wa hum tɛɛ durnya, di siu di turgi nɛkpila kim, di lɛɛ baa ha.”
Nyuŋŋa banɛɛ chaai wia
29Ba ga Jɛriko di ra lii. Banna lii la, nɛkpila hiŋuu lii. 30Denii nyuŋŋa banɛɛ so ŋmɛnikɛrii. Baŋ wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Yeesuu ga ba kɛraa waa kaali, ba yiruu kpegzi ni, “Yaa Dɔɔri, Deevid Naana, na yaa sinyɛna!”
31Nɛkpila la hau ba ni, di ŋɔ bá siigi. Ka ba bir ra yiruu werge maa, “Yaa Dɔɔri, Deevid Naana, na yaa sinyɛna!”
32Yeesu chi ka yir baa di pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛ ii ra nyiŋŋi n ɛɛ tɛɛ iai?”
33Ba ŋɔ, “Yaa Dɔɔri, yaa ra nyiŋŋi i pilli yaa siweere tɛɛ yaa.”
34Ba wia dɔɔ Yeesu sinyɛna. U gbɔgzi ba siwee. Kakpaŋ ba siwee pilli. Ba izi ra hiŋuu.

english_text:
Jesus Enters Jerusalem
(Mark 11.1-11; Luke 19.28-38; John 12.12-19)
1When Jesus and his disciples came near Jerusalem, he went to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives and sent two of them on ahead. 2He told them, “Go into the next village, where you will at once find a donkey and her colt. Untie the two donkeys and bring them to me. 3If anyone asks why you are doing this, just say, ‘The Lord needs them.’ He will at once let you have the donkeys.”
4So God's promise came true, just as the prophet had said,
5 “Announce to the people
of Jerusalem:
‘Your king is coming to you!
He is humble
and rides on a donkey.
He comes on the colt
of a donkey.’ ”
6The disciples left and did what Jesus had told them to do. 7They brought the donkey and its colt and laid some clothes on their backs. Then Jesus got on.
8Many people spread clothes in the road, while others put down branches which they had cut from trees. 9 Some people walked ahead of Jesus and others followed behind. They were all shouting,
“Hooray for the Son of David!
God bless the one who comes
in the name of the Lord.
Hooray for God
in heaven above!”
10When Jesus came to Jerusalem, everyone in the city was excited and asked, “Who can this be?”
11The crowds answered, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.”
Jesus in the Temple
(Mark 11.15-19; Luke 19.45-48; John 2.13-22)
12Jesus went into the temple and chased out everyone who was selling or buying. He turned over the tables of the moneychangers and the benches of the ones who were selling doves. 13 He told them, “The Scriptures say, ‘My house should be called a place of worship.’ But you have turned it into a place where robbers hide.”
14Blind and lame people came to Jesus in the temple, and he healed them. 15But the chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses were angry when they saw his miracles and heard the children shouting praises to the Son of David. 16 The men said to Jesus, “Don't you hear what those children are saying?”
“Yes, I do!” Jesus answered. “Don't you know that the Scriptures say, ‘Children and infants will sing praises’?” 17Then Jesus left the city and went out to the village of Bethany, where he spent the night.
Jesus Puts a Curse on a Fig Tree
(Mark 11.12-14,20-24)
18When Jesus got up the next morning, he was hungry. He started out for the city, 19and along the way he saw a fig tree. But when he came to it, he found only leaves and no figs. So he told the tree, “You will never again grow any fruit!” Right then the fig tree dried up.
20The disciples were shocked when they saw how quickly the tree had dried up. 21 But Jesus said to them, “If you have faith and don't doubt, I promise you can do what I did to this tree. And you will be able to do even more. You can tell this mountain to get up and jump into the sea, and it will. 22If you have faith when you pray, you will be given whatever you ask for.”
A Question about Jesus' Authority
(Mark 11.27-33; Luke 20.1-8)
23Jesus had gone into the temple and was teaching when the chief priests and the leaders of the people came up to him. They asked, “What right do you have to do these things? Who gave you this authority?”
24Jesus answered, “I have just one question to ask you. If you answer it, I will tell you where I got the right to do these things. 25Who gave John the right to baptize? Was it God in heaven or merely some human being?”
They thought it over and said to each other, “We can't say God gave John this right. Jesus will ask us why we didn't believe John. 26On the other hand, these people think John was a prophet, and we are afraid of what they might do to us. That's why we can't say it was merely some human who gave John the right to baptize.” 27So they told Jesus, “We don't know.”
Jesus said, “Then I won't tell you who gave me the right to do what I do.”
A Story about Two Sons
28Jesus said:
I will tell you a story about a man who had two sons. Then you can tell me what you think. The father went to the older son and said, “Go work in the vineyard today!” 29His son told him he would not do it, but later he changed his mind and went. 30The man then told his younger son to go work in the vineyard. The boy said he would, but he didn't go. 31Which one of the sons obeyed his father?
“The older one,” the chief priests and leaders answered.
Then Jesus told them:
You can be sure tax collectors and prostitutes will get into the kingdom of God before you ever will! 32 When John the Baptist showed you how to do right, you would not believe him. But these evil people did believe. And even when you saw what they did, you still would not change your minds and believe.
Renters of a Vineyard
(Mark 12.1-12; Luke 20.9-19)
33 Jesus told the chief priests and leaders to listen to this story:
A land owner once planted a vineyard. He built a wall around it and dug a pit to crush the grapes in. He also built a lookout tower. Then he rented out his vineyard and left the country.
34When it was harvest time, the owner sent some servants to get his share of the grapes. 35But the renters grabbed those servants. They beat up one, killed one, and stoned one of them to death. 36He then sent more servants than he did the first time. But the renters treated them in the same way.
37Finally, the owner sent his own son to the renters, because he thought they would respect him. 38But when they saw the man's son, they said, “Someday he will own the vineyard. Let's kill him! Then we can have it all for ourselves.” 39So they grabbed him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
40Jesus asked, “When the owner of that vineyard comes, what do you suppose he will do to those renters?”
41The chief priests and leaders answered, “He will kill them in some horrible way. Then he will rent out his vineyard to people who will give him his share of grapes at harvest time.”
42 Jesus replied, “You surely know that the Scriptures say,
‘The stone the builders
tossed aside
is now the most important
stone of all.
This is something
the Lord has done,
and it is amazing to us.’
43I tell you God's kingdom will be taken from you and given to people who will do what he demands. 44Anyone who stumbles over this stone will be crushed, and anyone it falls on will be smashed to pieces.”
45When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard these stories, they knew Jesus was talking about them. 46So they looked for a way to arrest Jesus. But they were afraid to, because the people thought he was a prophet.
translation_text:
Yeesu n zuu Jɛrusalɛm ni girme wia
(Maak 11:1-11; Luuk 19:28-40; Jɔɔn 12:12-19)
1Ba jaa ra dugli Jɛrusalɛm di wa hel Bɛtfaji, n du Ɔlivizi Bizeŋ la nyuu. Denii Yeesu hum u hiŋra banɛɛ, 2di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ga zuu boljiga naa n du see naa. Di ii wa zuuwɔ, ii daŋ na kawee ni u bie baŋ vɔɔwɛ chiŋŋi. Ií puraa wa tɛŋ. 3Di nɛr maa wa ŋɔ wiimaa tɛɛ ia, ií ŋɔ, ‘Yaa Dɔɔrii ra nyiŋŋaa.’ U daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Ií kpoglaa ga tɛu.’ ”
4Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ faa ŋɔ wia naa wiarɛ. Awiarɛ guŋ wa ɛɛ la. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
5“Ií ŋɔ Ziɔn hina be,
dí ba na ba koori n na ba ba be.
U dɔɔ sisɔnaa di tinni kawee ra ba,
kaupɔl bɛllɛ u tinni di ra ba.”
6U hiŋra la ga ɛɛ gunla um bagli baa la, 7di kpa kawee ni u bie la ba, di wa kpa ba wɛjɛzi bɔgaa. U tinni so u bie la ni. 8Nɛkpila la ga yaa ba wɛjɛzi di pɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ. Baŋhina ge mɔnni paŋhoozenaa di pɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ, u ra vol a ni. 9Ba maa duu ra la. Baŋhina du u see, baŋhina ge du u har. Ba maa ra ŋɔ kpegzi ni,
“Tibaarikala! Deevid Naana!”
“Unla n kpa Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ
di ra ba la, u nuu sumaa!”
“Ii banla maa ge n du Kɔraawiizi be la,
ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni!”
10Unna zuu Jɛrusalɛm la, a tir a bolzeŋ hina maa werge maa. Ba ra pɛɛzi, “Anɛɛ baal naanɛi?”
11Nɛkpila la ŋɔ, “Waabuu Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Yeesu la n lii Nazarɛf n du Galilii hɛri la.”
Yeesu n du Kɔraawiizi Dia biini wia
(Maak 11:15-19; Luuk 19:45-48; Jɔɔn 2:13-22)
12Denii Yeesu zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia, di duŋŋi kunyoora ni kunyaura maa de, di billi kebichɛtta teebulzi haazi, di kaa billi komma yoora ge kassi haazi, 13ka ŋɔ ba be, “Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ, ‘Ba daŋ yir n Dia wiijaami Dia.’ Ka iawaa kpau birgi ŋmɛɛna dia.”
14Denii nyuŋŋa ni gbɛraa la n du Kɔraawiizi Dia la ba Yeesu be. U chaa baa.
15Ka Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi ni Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna la n wa na wizenaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ di nuu bichalli la n du Kɔraawiizi Dia n na pogzi di ra ŋɔ, “Tibarikala, ií ra kpa Deevid Naana girme!” Ba baana fuuh werge maa.
16Ba pɛɛzuu, “Haa nuu gunla banna ŋɔa?”
Yeesu ŋɔ, “N na nuu. Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini, di ŋɔ,
‘Kɔraawiizi kpa chɔlaarɛ
du bichalli ni biifulli nuuzi,
bá wer ra chɔluu nɛnnɛ.’
Ii waa de karmɛɛa?”
17U gil baa de ka lii a bol di la Bɛtani di ga chɔɔ de.
Yeesu n see fig daa nua wia
(Maak 11:12-14, 20-24)
18Hɔɔŋ pizɛɛ u feli izi di kaa ra la Jɛrusalɛm. Unna la la, lɔzi gaa kpuu. 19U binni di na daa bɛl banna yir fig, n chigɛ ŋmɛnikɛrii. U la u zɛɛ ga nyiŋŋi nɔna huhzi u ni. Lɔɔi bɛnnɛ u lɔɔ. U ŋɔ daa la be, “Hiŋwaa wàá ka wer nɔŋ maa di hanna la.” A daa bir hil kakpaŋ.
20U hiŋra na guŋ. A tir baa. Ba ŋɔ, “Na gunla fig daa la n hillɛ manaŋ guŋ.”
21Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Di ii haŋ dɔɔ yarda, di ii waa aani, ii gba daŋ wer ɛɛ lugɔ miŋ ɛɛ fig daa naa, di kaa wer ŋɔ bizeŋ naa be, dí u izi ga chol muuzeŋ biini, ú izi. 22Wia la maa wia iin niŋ suŋŋi wiizi, di ii suŋŋuu ni yarda, ii daŋ naa.”
Baŋ pɛɛzi Yeesu fɔŋŋa wia
(Maak 11:27-33; Luuk 20:1-8)
23U kaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋee biini di ra bagli nɛra Kɔraawiizi wia. Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi ni bol nabɔnzi ba u be di wa pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ fɔŋŋaa i ge dɔɔ ka vol di ra ɛɛ wia naanɛi? Anɛɛ n tɛi guŋ ŋmɛnɛɛi?”
24Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “N ge gba dɔɔ wii bɛl min niŋ pɛɛzi ia. Di n pɛɛzi ia, ii wer bagliŋ u zɛɛ, n ge daŋ bagli ia fɔŋŋa la dee miŋ ge n dɔɔwɛ, di vol ra ɛɛ wia naa. 25Jɔɔn la n faa ra sɔ nɛra Kɔraawiizi nii la, Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ u faa ra hiŋ di ra ɛɛ guŋ gɛɛ nɛra nuuzii u faa ra hiŋɛi?”
Ba jaa ra bil dɔŋa di ra ŋɔ, “Di yaa ŋɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ u faa ra hiŋ di ra ɛɛ guŋ, u daŋ bir pɛɛzi yaa wii la n baani yaa faa wɔɔ yardɛɛ. 26Ama, di yaa kaa wa ŋɔ lugɔ nɛra nuuzii u faa ra hiŋ, ɔnsii du denii. Nɛkpila naa n na yir a Jɔɔn Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ bɛl naa, ba wàá gil yaa.”
27Awia, ba ŋɔ Yeesu be, “Yaa waa zum.” Denii u ŋɔ, “Mhmm. N ge wàá bagli ia fɔŋŋa la dee miŋ dɔɔwɛ di ra ɛɛ wia naa.
Biibaala banɛɛ sɛɛlii wia
28Ama, ií kaa nuu tɛŋ di bagliŋ gunla iin nawɛɛ n sɛɛlii naa biini. Baal bɛllɛ izee di dɔɔ u biibaala banɛɛ. A hɔl bɛl u la u biinabɔma be di ga ŋɔ, ‘N bie, izi la n koo zinaa di ga par.’
29U bie la ŋɔ, ‘Màá la.’ Denii u biini bir chɔgi u wichɔgaa la wia. U izi la a koo.
30Baal la kaa la nɛɛhiŋ ge be di kaa ga ŋɔ dí u la u koo di ga par. U bie la ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ la.’ Ka waa laŋŋɛ.
31Too. Biizi banɛɛ naa biini, u bɛliirɛ n ɛɛ u mɛɛ kipar lai?”
Ba ŋɔ, “Luglihiŋ labuu ɛɛ u mɛɛ kipar.”
Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Wichɔgɛɛra ni hahsɛnsɛnna feli iabuu ra zuu Kɔraawiizi Kora biini, 32dikuubɛɛwiai, Jɔɔn la n wa ballɛ di waa bagli winanaa ŋmɛnɛɛ la, ii waa sɛɛwɛ tɛu. Ka wichɔgɛɛra la ni hahsɛnsɛnna la, waa sɛɛwɔɔ tɛu. Ii na guŋ, ka haa vɛɛ. Ii waa gillɛ ii biine chɔgi dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia di sɛɛ tɛu.”
Paahdiire sɛɛlii wia
(Maak 12:1-12; Luuk 20:9-19)
33“Ií kaa nuu sɛɛlii bɛl. Baal bɛllɛ izee di par grepu daazi koo, di tɔ de maa lugɔ kambol, di ki bɔr la ban niŋ waa lizi a nɔna nii di ra du, di du jaŋ bɛl de, di kpa paahdiire, bá ra binni a bɔr di ra tɛu. Uŋ wa ɛɛ annii naa maa wa tuŋ, u kpa kaali bol bɛl, 34di ga du de guŋŋ, a nɔna tɔrgaa saŋa n wa helle, u hum u balaa bá la paahdiire la be di ga lɛɛ u hor ba. Ba la.
35Paahdiire la ga lauri baa di lɔɔzi bɛl di kpu bɛl ge, ka kpa bia lɔɔzi horohiŋ la. 36Baal la kaa hum u balaa baŋhina ba du kpil kaali banla uŋ felee hum la. A wikpannɛ paahdiire la kaa ɛɛ ba ge. 37A tuna maa, a baal hum u biibaal ba be, di ŋɔ, ‘Ba daŋ tɔgzi waabuu.’
38Paahdiire la n wa na u biibaal la n na ba, ba ŋɔ dɔŋa be, ‘Yaa dɔɔri kapɛttɛ diirii keŋ. Ií gil yá kpuu ka di u kapɛttɛ.’ 39Ba izi ga lawuu di kpau ha koo la baŋgia di kpuu.
40Too. Di ba dɔɔri wa ballɔ, ɛrɛɛ ú ɛɛ u paahdiire lai?”
41Ba ŋɔ, “U daŋ lauri nɛchɔgaa la di kpu ka jaa nyiŋŋi paahdiire la n niŋ ɔɔ tɛu u hor nɔna tɔrgaa saŋazi la.”
42Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “Ba faa sɛbɔɔrɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini di ŋɔ,
‘Bii la maara n faa vɛɛwɛ ha labuu
jaa ɛɛ bikpeg la baŋ kpawɛɛ
ra faari dia zɛɛ.
Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛliirɛ guŋ.
A tir yaabuu werge.’
Ii waa de karmɛɛa?
43Ií gil n ŋɔ ii be. Kɔraawiizi daŋ duŋŋi ia u Kora biini, ka nyiŋŋi nɛra la n niŋ ɛɛ wia la n dɛg u Kora biini dui, di gil ba du de. 44Nɛr la maa n chol bii naa ni, u daŋ kuugi. Di a bii ge wa chol nɛr maa ni, u daŋ pintuu.”
45Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi ni Farisizi la n wa nuu Yeesu sɛɛliizi la, ba zum lugɔ ba wiarɛ u ra ŋɔ di ra ta sɛɛliizi la. 46Ba ra nyiŋŋi ba lawuu, ka ra ɔm nɛkpila la dikuu baŋ kpau ra yir Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ bɛl wia.

english_text:
The Great Banquet
(Luke 14.15-24)
1Once again Jesus used stories to teach the people:
2The kingdom of heaven is like what happened when a king gave a wedding banquet for his son. 3The king sent some servants to tell the invited guests to come to the banquet, but the guests refused. 4He sent other servants to say to the guests, “The banquet is ready! My cattle and prize calves have all been prepared. Everything is ready. Come to the banquet!”
5But the guests did not pay any attention. Some of them left for their farms, and some went to their places of business. 6Others grabbed the servants, then beat them up and killed them.
7This made the king so furious that he sent an army to kill those murderers and burn down their city. 8Then he said to the servants, “It is time for the wedding banquet, and the invited guests don't deserve to come. 9Go out to the street corners and tell everyone you meet to come to the banquet.” 10They went out on the streets and brought in everyone they could find, good and bad alike. And the banquet room was filled with guests.
11When the king went in to meet the guests, he found that one of them wasn't wearing the right kind of clothes for the wedding. 12The king asked, “Friend, why didn't you wear proper clothes for the wedding?” But the guest had no excuse. 13 So the king gave orders for this person to be tied hand and foot and to be thrown outside into the dark. That's where people will cry and grit their teeth in pain. 14 Many are invited, but only a few are chosen.
Paying Taxes
(Mark 12.13-17; Luke 20.20-26)
15The Pharisees got together and planned how they could trick Jesus into saying something wrong. 16They sent some of their followers and some of Herod's followers to say to him, “Teacher, we know that you are honest. You teach the truth about what God wants people to do. And you treat everyone with the same respect, no matter who they are. 17Tell us what you think! Should we pay taxes to the Emperor or not?”
18Jesus knew their evil thoughts and said, “Why are you trying to test me? You show-offs! 19Let me see one of the coins used for paying taxes.” They brought him a silver coin, 20and he asked, “Whose picture and name are on it?”
21“The Emperor's,” they answered.
Then Jesus told them, “Give the Emperor what belongs to him and give God what belongs to God.” 22His answer surprised them so much that they walked away.
Life in the Future World
(Mark 12.18-27; Luke 20.27-40)
23 The Sadducees did not believe people would rise to life after death. So that same day some of the Sadducees came to Jesus and said:
24 Teacher, Moses wrote that if a married man dies and has no children, his brother should marry the widow. Their first son would then be thought of as the son of the dead brother.
25Once there were seven brothers who lived here. The first one married, but died without having any children. So his wife was left to his brother. 26The same thing happened to the second and third brothers and finally to all seven of them. 27At last the woman died. 28When God raises people from death, whose wife will this woman be? She had been married to all seven brothers.
29Jesus answered:
You are completely wrong! You don't know what the Scriptures teach. And you don't know anything about the power of God. 30 When God raises people to life, they won't marry. They will be like the angels in heaven. 31And as for people being raised to life, God was speaking to you when he said, 32 “I am the God worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” He isn't the God of the dead, but of the living.
33The crowds were surprised to hear what Jesus was teaching.
The Most Important Commandment
(Mark 12.28-34; Luke 10.25-28)
34After Jesus had made the Sadducees look foolish, the Pharisees heard about it and got together. 35 One of them was an expert in the Jewish Law. So he tried to test Jesus by asking, 36“Teacher, what is the most important commandment in the Law?”
37 Jesus answered:
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind. 38This is the first and most important commandment. 39 The second most important commandment is like this one. And it is, “Love others as much as you love yourself.” 40All the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets are based on these two commandments.
About David's Son
(Mark 12.35-37; Luke 20.41-44)
41While the Pharisees were still there, Jesus asked them, 42“What do you think about the Messiah? Whose family will he come from?”
They answered, “He will be a son of King David.”
43Jesus replied, “How then could the Spirit lead David to call the Messiah his Lord? David said,
44 ‘The Lord said to my Lord:
Sit at my right side
until I make your enemies
into a footstool for you.’
45If David called the Messiah his Lord, how can the Messiah be a son of King David?” 46No one was able to give Jesus an answer, and from that day on, no one dared ask him any more questions.
translation_text:
Haŋfalii diuzenaa dii sɛɛlii wia
(Luuk 14:15-24)
1Yeesu kaa ta sɛɛliizi aŋhina di ra bagli nɛra, 2di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi Kora wia ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ koori bɛl n izee di lul u bie, u ra nyiŋŋi ú kpa haaŋ. U ɛɛ haŋfalii diuzenaa sirya tɛɛ u bie hiŋ, 3ka hum u balaa dí ba ga yir banla uŋ yittɛ la, bá ba wa di haŋfalii diuzenaa la. Ba la, ka nɛra la vɛɛ balaa.
4U kaa hum u balaa baŋhina banla uŋ faa yittɛ la be di ŋɔ, ‘N ɛɛ diwee la sirya maanii tuŋ. N kpu n nauna ni napɔla la min dɛɛzɛɛ a pɔl nɛnnɛ labuu, di ɛɛ wiimaa sirya. Awia, ií ba wa di n haŋfalii diuzenaa la tɛŋ.’
5Ka ba waa baa hagzɛɛ ka kaali ba huma bɔrazi. Bɛl kaali u koo, bɛl ge kaali ú ga yoo u kuna. 6Banla n kawɛɛ ge lauri u balaa la di tɔɔri baa ka kpu baa. 7Koori la baaŋ fuuh. U hum u soojazi ba bol di gil ba kpuuzi nɛkpuura la di fuuh ba bolzeŋ. 8Denii u ŋɔ u balaa be, ‘Ba ɛɛ haŋfalii diuzenaare chiŋŋi ka banla miŋ yirgɛɛ bá ba wa di la waa dɛg a dii. 9Awia, ií la ŋmɛnizenaa di ga ŋɔ banla maa iin nawɛɛ de, dí ba ba wa di n haŋfalii diuzenaa tɛŋ.’ 10U balaa la ŋmɛnizenaa la ga lauri banla maa baŋ nawɛɛ de, nɛnanaa ni nɛchɔgaa maa, di ba. Ba haŋfalii dia la maa su.
11Koori la zuu ú binni banla maa n ballɛ ba wa di la, di bɛl du ba biini, ka waa haŋfalii laala la laalɛɛ. 12U pɛɛzuu, ‘N dammu, ɛrɛɛ hiŋwaa waa haŋfalii laala laalɛɛ ka wa zuu ɛnnɛi?’ A baal waa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ un niŋ ŋɔ.
13Koori la ŋɔ u balaa be, ‘Ií vɔɔzi u naazi ni u nonee ka kpau ha bossee bɔbiri biini. Bɔr la wiraa ni nyina heei n duwɛɛ.’
14Banla Kɔraawiizi n yittɛ kpillɔɔ. Ka banla un lizɛɛwaa waa kpil.”
Lampoo turgaa wia
(Maak 12:13-17; Luuk 20:20-26)
15Denii Farisizi la, la ga ta jina gunla ban niŋ ɛɛ di wer he u nua, ú leu bá na u cholli bɔr. 16Ba hum ba hiŋra baŋhina ni Hɛrɔd nɛra baŋhina. Ba ba u be di wa ŋɔ, “Yaa Nabɔma, yaa zummɔ lugɔ i ɛɛ wibii hinnɛ. I baga lɛi gunla nɛra n niŋ ŋɔ i wia. Haa nɛr maa ra ɔm, ka ra bagli gunla maa Kɔraawiizi wibii n na vol. 17Awia, bagli yaa gunla hin nawɛɛ wii naa biini, yá zum. Ya ɔɔ turgi lampoo di ra tɛɛ Koorizeŋ Siiza gɛɛ ya gilɛɛ ra turgei?”
18Ka Yeesu zum ba nfɛrchɔgaa la di ŋɔ, “Nɛfugze! Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ií ŋɔ ií he n nua kennei? Ií kpa kebii bɛl ba ń na. 19Ií kpa a kebii bɛl ba ń na.” Ba kpa a kebii bɛl ba. 20U pɛɛzi baa, “Anɛɛ nyuu ni u sɔnnɛ chɔɔ u ni naanɛi?”
21Ba ŋɔ, “Koorizeŋ Siiza nyuu ni u sɔnnɛ chɔɔ u ni.”
U ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ɔɔ kpa Koorizeŋ Siiza kuna ra tɛu, di kpa Kɔraawiizi ge kuna ra tɛu.”
22Uŋ wette na u ŋmɛnɛɛ tɛɛ baa gunla, a tir baa werge. Ba bir kaali.
Baŋ pɛɛzi siu biini izaa wia
(Maak 12:18-27; Luuk 20:27-40)
23A hɔl hiŋ, Sajusizi ba u be. Baabuu ɔɔ ŋɔ dí di nɛr siuwɔ, wàá ka izi siu biini la. Ba ge gba dɔɔ wii bɛl bá pɛɛzuu, 24di ŋɔ, “Yaa Nabɔma, Moosis faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, dí di baal kpa haaŋ, u ni haaŋ la waa biizi lullɛ ka u siu, u niwee gɛɛ u kpɛɛma daŋ kpa u haaŋ la di lul biizi tɛu, ú sɔŋ gilɛɛ dim. 25Too. Baala baniidaanɛɛrɛ faa du yaa be di ɛɛ bakpaŋ ni hahkpaŋ biizi. Ba nabɔma hiŋ izi di kpa haaŋ. U ni haaŋ la waa bie lullɛ ka u siu. Awia, nɛɛhiŋ ge kpa u haaŋ la. 26U nuu gba waa bie lullɛ ka u siu. Horohiŋ gba gunnɛ, guŋŋ ba maa baniidaanɛɛ la wa siuzi. 27Denii haaŋ la ge gba wa siu. 28Too. Saŋa la nɛra maa n niŋ izi siu biini la, u bɛɛ haannɛ ú ɛɛ a saŋai? Ba nɛra baniidaanɛɛ la maanii faa kpau.”
29Yeesu ŋɔ ba be, “Ii leuwoo. Ii waa Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ wia ni Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa wia zummɛ. Awiarɛ ii leu la. 30Saŋa la nɛra maa n niŋ wa izi siu biini, nɛra wàá ka yuu janna, ba wàá ka kpa haana, ka bá maa ɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlikazi. 31Siu biini izaa naa, di ii faa karmi gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ u Hɔŋ biini, ii daŋ faa zum u wibii. U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, 32‘Minuu Kɔraawiizi la Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb n na hum la.’
Lalaa lɛi ra jaami Kɔraawiizi. Nɛnyineere ra jaamuu.”
33Nɛkpila la n wa nuu u baglaa la, a tir baa werge maa.
Gbɔg la n ɛɛ u zeŋ wia
(Maak 12:28-34; Luuk 10:25-28)
34Denii Farisizi n wa nuu gunla uŋ wette na a wii ŋmɛnɛɛ tɛɛ Sajusizi ba waa kaa dɔɔ nua bá wer pɛɛzuu la, ba ge chaali ba. 35Ba gbɔgzunni bɛl ŋɔ ú ɛɛu na di pɛɛzuu,
36“Yaa Nabɔma, Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni maa biini, u bɛliirɛ ɛɛ uzenei?” 37Yeesu ŋɔ, “Waabuu keŋ. ‘Nɔŋŋi i Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la ani i biini maa, i kpegzi maa, di kpa i nfɛrɛ maa du u ni.’ 38Waabuu ɛɛ u zeŋ di tɔ a maa see Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni la biini. 39Nɛɛhiŋ ge ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔu, ‘Ií nɔŋŋi ii dɔŋahina gunla iin nɔŋŋi iihinaa la.’ 40Di i wetto hiŋ Gbɔgni anɛɛ naa, amɔ, Moosis Gbɔg ni dɔgtɛɛzi la baglaa la maanii i ra hiŋ la.”
Anɛɛ biibaallɛ Kristo lai?
(Maak 12:35-37; Luuk 20:41-44)
41Farisizi la n chaalɛɛ la, Yeesu pɛɛzi baa, 42“Ɛrɛɛ ii na Kristo wia biinei? Anɛɛ naanaawɛi?”
Ba ŋɔ, “Deevid naanaa.”
43U kaa pɛɛzi baa, “Ka Deevid n faa ra ŋɔ u wia Kɔraawiizi Duma fɔŋŋa biini la, u faa yiruubuu u ‘Dɔɔri’. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
44‘N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n Dɔɔri la ge be lugɔ
ú so nabɔmbɔr naa
ka ń gil i dɔma birgi i yoma.’
45Deevid n yiruu u dɔɔri naa, ɛrɛɛ ú kaa ɛɛ di ɛɛ u naanai?” 46Nɛr maa waa wette na wiimaa tɛu. Ba waa kaa dɔɔ bampirii, bá kaa pɛɛzuu wiimaa gba, ka jaa gil guŋ pɛɛzaa di lii a saŋa.

english_text:
Jesus Condemns the Pharisees and the Teachers of the Law of Moses
(Mark 12.38-40; Luke 11.37-52; 20.45-47)
1Jesus said to the crowds and to his disciples:
2The Pharisees and the teachers of the Law are experts in the Law of Moses. 3So obey everything they teach you, but don't do as they do. After all, they say one thing and do something else.
4They pile heavy burdens on people's shoulders and won't lift a finger to help. 5 Everything they do is just to show off in front of others. They even make a big show of wearing Scripture verses on their foreheads and arms, and they wear big tassels for everyone to see. 6They love the best seats at banquets and the front seats in the synagogues. 7And when they are in the market, they like to have people greet them as their teachers.
8But none of you should be called a teacher. You have only one teacher, and all of you are like brothers and sisters. 9Don't call anyone on earth your father. All of you have the same Father in heaven. 10None of you should be called the leader. The Messiah is your only leader. 11 Whoever is the greatest should be the servant of the others. 12 If you put yourself above others, you will be put down. But if you humble yourself, you will be honored.
13-14You Pharisees and teachers of the Law of Moses are in for trouble! You're nothing but show-offs. You lock people out of the kingdom of heaven. You won't go in yourselves, and you keep others from going in.
15You Pharisees and teachers of the Law of Moses are in for trouble! You're nothing but show-offs. You travel over land and sea to win one follower. And when you have done so, you make that person twice as fit for hell as you are.
16You are in for trouble! You are supposed to lead others, but you are blind. You teach that it doesn't matter if a person swears by the temple. But you say it does matter if someone swears by the gold in the temple. 17You blind fools! Which is greater, the gold or the temple that makes the gold sacred?
18You also teach that it doesn't matter if a person swears by the altar. But you say it does matter if someone swears by the gift on the altar. 19Are you blind? Which is more important, the gift or the altar that makes the gift sacred? 20Anyone who swears by the altar also swears by everything on it. 21And anyone who swears by the temple also swears by God, who lives there. 22 To swear by heaven is the same as swearing by God's throne and by the one who sits on that throne.
23 You Pharisees and teachers are show-offs, and you're in for trouble! You give God a tenth of the spices from your garden, such as mint, dill, and cumin. Yet you neglect the more important matters of the Law, such as justice, mercy, and faithfulness. These are the important things you should have done, though you should not have left the others undone either. 24You blind leaders! You strain out a small fly but swallow a camel.
25You Pharisees and teachers are show-offs, and you're in for trouble! You wash the outside of your cups and dishes, while inside there is nothing but greed and selfishness. 26You blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of a cup, and then the outside will also be clean.
27 You Pharisees and teachers are in for trouble! You're nothing but show-offs. You're like tombs that have been whitewashed. On the outside they are beautiful, but inside they are full of bones and filth. 28That's what you are like. Outside you look good, but inside you are evil and only pretend to be good.
29You Pharisees and teachers are nothing but show-offs, and you're in for trouble! You build monuments for the prophets and decorate the tombs of good people. 30And you claim you would not have taken part with your ancestors in killing the prophets. 31But you prove you really are the relatives of the ones who killed the prophets. 32So keep on doing everything they did. 33 You are nothing but snakes and the children of snakes! How can you escape going to hell?
34I will send to you prophets and wise people and experts in the Law of Moses. You will kill them or nail them to a cross or beat them in your synagogues or chase them from town to town. 35 That's why you will be held guilty for the murder of every good person, beginning with the good man Abel. This also includes Barachiah's son Zechariah, the man you murdered between the temple and the altar. 36I can promise that you people living today will be punished for all these things!
Jesus Loves Jerusalem
(Luke 13.34,35)
37Jerusalem, Jerusalem! Your people have killed the prophets and have stoned the messengers who were sent to you. I have often wanted to gather your people, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But you wouldn't let me. 38 And now your temple will be deserted. 39 You won't see me again until you say,
“Blessed is the one who comes
in the name of the Lord.”
translation_text:
Tɔɔrɔɔzi aniidaanɛɛ wia
(Maak 12:38-39; Luuk 11:43, 46; 20:45-46)
1Denii Yeesu ŋɔ nɛkpila la ni u hiŋra la be, 2“Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna ni Farisizi la lɛɛ Moosis bɔttɛ di ra bagli ia Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni. 3Awia, ií ra hiŋ gunla maa ban niŋ ɔɔ bagli ia. Ama, ba wiɛɛlaa lawaa, ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ aawaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, gunla banna bagli, guŋ lɛi ba ra hiŋ. 4Ba ɔɔ vɔɔ buntɔgaa sag nɛra baŋaazi. Ka ba himmaa wàá sɛɛ kpa ba nonibee gba di gbɔgzaa.
5Wia la maa banna ɛɛ ge, ba ɔɔ ra ɛɛabuu nɛ́ra na di ra chɔli baa. Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la nɛra n ɔɔ kpaa kuari sɛbɛzi di vɔɔ ba nyuuni ni ba nonee la, baabuu ɔɔ giluu a du war werge. Yɔɔza la banna vɔɔ ba bɔmbɔga nuuzi la, ba ɔɔ gil a ge du jaŋ. 6Di ba chaalɔɔ di ra di ba hɔpizizenaa diwee, ba ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi nabɔŋkassii bá so. Di ba du jaamaa diini biine ge, ba kaa ra nyiŋŋi nabɔŋkassi bá so. 7Gunla nɛra n ɔɔ ra tɔgzi baa di ra jaami baa yauzi biine la, guŋ ɔɔ ra par baabuu. Ba kaa ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ nɛra maa ra yir baa ‘Bagla.’
8Iawaa, ií gilɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi nɛra ra yir ia bagla guŋ. Nɛkpaŋ bɛnnɛ ɛɛ i bagli. Ka iawaa maa ɛɛ kpaŋ. 9Ií gilɛɛ ra yir nɛr maa hɛri naa, ‘N mɛɛ.’ Ii Mɛɛ ɛɛ kpaŋkpaŋ bɛnnɛ. Waabuu ii Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la. 10Ií gilɛɛ gil ba kaa ra yir ia nabɔnzi. Nɛkpaŋ bɛnnɛ ɛɛ ii Nabɔma. Waabuu Kristo la. 11Nɛr la n niŋ ɛɛ nɛzeŋ ii biini, waabuu niŋ kpa u hiŋ bichaluu di hum ra tɛɛ ii maa. 12Nɛr la maa n na tɔgzi u hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u pɛssi. Nɛr la maa ge n dɔɔ sisɔna, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpau zenni.
13Ka Kɔraawiizi Dia Hɔnzunna ni Farisizi, nɛfugzee ia! Wia daŋ huuzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii tɔ Kɔraawiizi Kora zuui ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ. Ii himmaa waa zuu. Ii wàá ka sɛɛ banla n na nyiŋŋi bá zuu, ge zuu. 14Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna, Farisizi, nɛfugzee ia! Wia daŋ wa huhzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ɔɔ kuttuu jaami Kɔraawiizi di birgi guŋŋ, ka kaa bir ra foozi haŋkia kuna ra di. Awia, Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr ii digna werge.
15Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna, Farisizi, nɛfugzee ia! Wia daŋ wa huuzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ra gaagi muuzenaa ni hɛri maa biinee, ií wer na nɛkpaŋ ú tuubi. Di u wa tuuboo, ii ɔɔ giluu u birgi Sitaani balii alugɔ ia.
16Ii ɛɛ nɛra sitɔɔraa ka ɛɛ nyuŋŋa. Wia daŋ wa huuzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Di nɛr hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi Dia, waa hɛɛhzikpeg ɛɛwɛ. Ka di u hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi Dia saliŋ la, gunla maa uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ u daŋ ɛɛ la, gunnɛ ú ɛɛ.’ 17Gɛnaa ni nyuŋŋaa ia! Saliŋ la Kɔraawiizi Dia n gillɛ a ɛɛ salinnanaa la ani a Kɔraawiizi Dia, u bɛliirɛ ɛɛ kunzenei? 18Ii kaa ŋɔ, ‘Di nɛr hɛɛhzi mbusu lizibɔr la, waa hɛɛhzikpeg ɛɛwɛ. Ka nɛr la n hɛɛhzi kunla n hɔŋ mbusu lizibɔr la, gunla maa uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ u daŋ ɛɛ la, gunnɛ ú ɛɛ.’ 19Nyuŋŋa! Kunla n hɔŋ mbusu lizibɔr ani mbusu lizibɔr la n gillɛ a kundee ɛɛ kunnaniinanii la, u bɛliirɛ ɛɛ kunzenei? 20Awia, di i hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr, mbusu lizibɔr ni kuna la maa n du u ni la maanii i hɛɛhzi la. 21Di i hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi Dia, a Dia ni nɛr la n du u biini la maanii i hɛɛhzi la. 22Di i kaa hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi bol, Kɔraawiizi sognibɔr ni Kɔraawiizi la n soge de la maanii i hɛɛhzi la.
23Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna, Farisizi, nɛfugzee ia! Wia daŋ wa huuzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ɔɔ lizi Kɔraawiizi hotte tɛu lii ii diujigzi maa gba biine, ka gil witɔga la Kɔraawiizi n dauwɛ u Hɔŋ biini la ha. Aabuu wibii dɔɔi ni nɛsunaa dɔɔi ni Kɔraawiizi yarda dɔɔi. Ii vii kpa annii wia su siwii ka kaa ra ɛɛ anla gba ra jaa, u guŋ vii bɔ. 24Sitɔɔra ka ɛɛ nyuŋŋa! Di kunzaahrijiga ni nyugma wa chol ii niinyɔɔlii ni, ii ɔɔ ɛɛ aniaa di lizi kunzaahrijiga lawaa ha ka kpa nyugma lawaa lil gbilam.
25Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna ni Farisizi naa, nɛfugzee ia! Wia daŋ wa huuzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ɔɔ loori libizi ni tassazi haraa, ka gil a biine doŋa. Kuŋfoozaa ni wikuna su a biinee. 26Farisi nyuŋŋi! Loori libee biini mɔɔ, ka ú biini ni u har maa wer du wer.
27Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna, Farisizi, nɛfugzee ia! Wia daŋ wa huuzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ŋmama baŋ kuarɛɛ nɛnnɛ di faaa hɔɔhri a du wer. Ka hoga ni kunchɔgaarɛ du a biini. 28Gunnɛ ii ge gba du. Nɛra daŋ binni ia di yir ia nɛnanaa, ka nɛfugzaa ni wichɔgaarɛ su ii biine.
29Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna, Farisizi, nɛfugzee ia! Wia daŋ wa huuzi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ɔɔ ma Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la ŋmamaa a du wer nɛnnɛ, di ra bɔg nɛnanaa ge ŋmama, 30di ra ŋɔ, ‘Di yaawaa faa du denii yaa naabaala saŋa la, yaa faa wàá hiini baa di ra kpu dɔgtɛɛzi naa.’ 31Awia, ii ɛɛ bá kpui daansɛɛ hinaa, di ra sɛɛ lugɔ ii ɛɛ banla n kpu baa la naannaa. 32Wichɔgaa la ii naabaala n faarɛɛ la, ii gba daŋ keezi ɛɛa á su tuŋ.
33Hɛrikuna, duŋkpola biizi! Ii daŋ wer lɛɛ iihinaa lii Sitaani niŋ la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ du ia dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia biinii naa? 34Ií nuu n be. N daŋ hum n dɔgtɛɛzi ni nunzunna ni Hɔnzunna ii be. Ii daŋ kpuuzi baŋhina, di kaa kpaahzi baŋhina daakaŋlaa ni bá siuzi, di kaa viiri baŋhina ii jaamaa diini biine di duŋŋi baŋhina luge bolle bol maa, di ra tɔɔri baa. 35Awia, nɛnanaa la maa baŋ kpuwɛɛ hɛri naa biini, di haŋ kpa nɛnanii Abɛl guŋŋ ga hel Bɛrɛkia biibaal Zɛkaria la iiŋ kpuwɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia ni u mbusu lizibɔr baambaaŋ la, iabuu dɔɔ ba maa kpui chɔgri ií sɛɛ. 36Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii maa tɛɛ ia. Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa a maa pɛɛzi filaŋkeŋ hina naa.
Yeesu n nɔŋŋi Jɛrusalɛm wia
(Luuk 13:34-35)
37Oo! Jɛrusalɛm hina, Jɛrusalɛm hina, ɛrɛɛ ii ɔɔ ra kpuuzi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi di ra lɔɔzi banla uŋ hummɛ tɛɛ ia la bia gunnɛi? Gunla zaniina n ɔɔ chaali u biizi di ra du u keeri biini la, gunnɛ n ɔɔ faa ra nyiŋŋi n chaali ia n be, ka ii waa sɛɛwɛ ii ba n be. 38Ií na! Ii diini birgi diiwoonii. 39Ií gil n ŋɔ ii be. Ii wàá ka naŋ di haŋ chi zinaa guŋŋ di ga hel a hɔl la iin niŋ kaa naŋ minna ba la, di ŋɔ, ‘Ií kpa sɔŋ ra tɛɛ unla n kpa Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ di ra ba la.’ ”

english_text:
The Temple Will Be Destroyed
(Mark 13.1,2; Luke 21.5,6)
1After Jesus left the temple, his disciples came over and said, “Look at all these buildings!”
2Jesus replied, “Do you see these buildings? They will certainly be torn down! Not one stone will be left in place.”
Warning about Trouble
(Mark 13.3-13; Luke 21.7-19)
3 Later, as Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him in private and asked, “When will this happen? What will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the world?”
4Jesus answered:
Don't let anyone fool you. 5Many will come and claim to be me. They will say they are the Messiah, and they will fool many people.
6You will soon hear about wars and threats of wars, but don't be afraid. These things will have to happen first, but that isn't the end. 7 Nations and kingdoms will go to war against each other. People will starve to death, and in some places there will be earthquakes. 8But this is just the beginning of troubles.
9 You will be arrested, punished, and even killed. Because of me, you will be hated by people of all nations. 10Many will give up and will betray and hate each other. 11Many false prophets will come and fool a lot of people. 12Evil will spread and cause many people to stop loving others. 13 But if you keep on being faithful right to the end, you will be saved. 14When the good news about the kingdom has been preached all over the world and told to all nations, the end will come.
The Horrible Thing
(Mark 13.14-23; Luke 21.20-24)
15 Someday you will see that “Horrible Thing” in the holy place, just as the prophet Daniel said. Everyone who reads this must try to understand! 16If you are living in Judea at that time, run to the mountains. 17 If you are on the roof of your house, don't go inside to get anything. 18If you are out in the field, don't go back for your coat. 19It will be a terrible time for women who are expecting babies or nursing young children. 20And pray that you won't have to escape in winter or on a Sabbath. 21 This will be the worst time of suffering since the beginning of the world, and nothing this terrible will ever happen again. 22If God doesn't make the time shorter, no one will be left alive. But because of God's chosen ones, he will make the time shorter.
23Someone may say, “Here is the Messiah!” or “There he is!” But don't believe it. 24False messiahs and false prophets will come and work great miracles and signs. They will even try to fool God's chosen ones. 25But I have warned you ahead of time. 26 If you are told the Messiah is out in the desert, don't go there! And if you are told he is in some secret place, don't believe it! 27The coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning that can be seen from east to west. 28 Where there is a corpse, there will always be vultures.
When the Son of Man Appears
(Mark 13.24-27; Luke 21.25-28)
29 Right after those days of suffering,
“The sun will become dark,
and the moon
will no longer shine.
The stars will fall,
and the powers in the sky
will be shaken.”
30 Then a sign will appear in the sky. And there will be the Son of Man. All nations on earth will weep when they see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. 31At the sound of a loud trumpet, he will send his angels to bring his chosen ones together from all over the earth.
A Lesson from a Fig Tree
(Mark 13.28-31; Luke 21.29-33)
32Learn a lesson from a fig tree. When its branches sprout and start putting out leaves, you know summer is near. 33So when you see all these things happening, you will know the time has almost come. 34I can promise you that some of the people of this generation will still be alive when all this happens. 35The sky and the earth won't last forever, but my words will.
No One Knows the Day or Time
(Mark 13.32-37; Luke 17.26-30,34-36)
36No one knows the day or hour. The angels in heaven don't know, and the Son himself doesn't know. Only the Father knows. 37 When the Son of Man appears, things will be just as they were when Noah lived. 38People were eating, drinking, and getting married right up to the day the flood came and Noah went into the big boat. 39 They didn't know anything was happening until the flood came and swept them all away. This is how it will be when the Son of Man appears.
40Two men will be in the same field, but only one will be taken. The other will be left. 41Two women will be together grinding grain, but only one will be taken. The other will be left. 42So be on your guard! You don't know when your Lord will come. 43 Homeowners never know when a thief is coming, and they are always on guard to keep one from breaking in. 44Always be ready! You don't know when the Son of Man will come.
Faithful and Unfaithful Servants
(Luke 12.35-48)
45Who are faithful and wise servants?
