15Ka di unla n waa Yeesu hiŋri ɛɛwɛ ra nyiŋŋi u gil u jaari gɛɛ u haaŋ la n ɛɛ Yeesu hiŋri la, a waa chummɛ. Ú tɛu ŋmɛnɛɛ ú ra la. An du kennaa, firaa lɛi. Kɔraawiizi n yir yaa, yaa ba u be la, nuukpannɛ u yir yaa ya wa dɔɔ la. 16Haaŋ, di i jaari daŋ na lɛɛi Kɔraawiizi be dikuu i wia, i zummɔaa? Baal, di i ge haaŋ daŋ na lɛɛi Kɔraawiizi be dikuu i wia, i ge zummɔaa?
17Ií bɛl maa kpogli gunla yaa Dɔɔri n tɛɛ ia la. Gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n yir ia ií ra hiŋ, ií ra hiŋ guŋ. Gunnɛ n na bagli bɔr la maa Yeesu hiŋra n duwɛɛ. 18Di baal ɛɛ nɛr la baŋ teŋ u hɛŋ saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n yiruu la, ú gilɛɛ kaa ɛɛ u bɔra lugɔ baŋ waa u hɛŋ teŋŋe. Di baal ɛɛ nɛr la baŋ waa u hɛŋ teŋŋe ge saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n yiruu la, ú ge gilɛɛ gil ba kaa waa teŋ u hɛŋ. 19Di ba teŋ u hɛŋ, pɛɛrɛ. Di ba waa u hɛŋ teŋŋe ge, pɛɛrɛ. Ka Kɔraawiizi nua hiŋaarɛ ɛɛ wizeŋ. 20Awia, ií haa du gunla iiŋ faa duwɛɛ, saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n yir ia la. 21Di i faa ɛɛ yonne ka Kɔraawiizi yirii, gilɛɛ gil a guŋ zuu i nyuu. Ka di ba kaa ŋɔ bá tɛi ŋmɛnɛɛ, í sɛɛ, 22dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr la n ɛɛ yom ka Kɔraawiizi yiruu la, u ɛɛ nɛr la n dɔɔ u hinnɛ Kɔraawiiziwaa be. Nɛr la n dɔɔ u hiŋ ka Kɔraawiizi yiruu la, u ɛɛ Kristo yonne. 23Waabuu yau ia. Awia, ii gilɛɛ ra binni newea, bá dɔɔ ia. 24Yaabalaa, gunla maa iiŋ faa duwɛɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi yir ia la, ií haa du guŋ. Ii ni Kɔraawiizii du de.
25Kɔraawiizi haa wam baglɛɛ suŋgure la n haa waa yuuwɛzi wia. Ka u suŋ n ninɛɛ di hiiniŋ, n wer di ra hum u huma ani wibii. Awia, n danna ŋɔ gunla miŋwaa n nawɛɛ. 26Filaŋkeŋ, tɔɔrɔɔ du denii di ra nuu yaa. Awia, miŋwaa be, a wesso gunla maa baal n soge, ú so guŋ. 27Di i dɔɔ haaŋ, gilɛɛ waa vɛɛu. Di haa haaŋ dɔɔwɛ ge, gilɛɛ waa nyiŋŋi haaŋ. 28Di i kpa haaŋ, a waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ i ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. Di toloori yuu baal ge, waa wichɔgaa ɛɛwɛ. Ka a daŋ ɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ tɛɛ baa bá de dui naa saŋa. N ŋɔ ń lɛɛ iabuu a tɔɔrɔɔ biini.
29Yaabalaa, yaa wàá ka birgi durnya naa biini. Awia, filaŋkeŋ, a dɛkkɔ lugɔ ii banla n dɔɔ haana la n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ ii waa haana dɔɔwɛ, 30ií banla n na wii ge ɛɛ lugɔ ii biine waa chɔkkɛ, ií banla bɔra n sɔɔnɛɛ ge ɛɛ lugɔ ii bɔra waa sɔɔnɛɛ, ií banla n na yauzi kuna ge ra ɛɛ lugɔ ii waa dɔɔwɛ. 31Wia la maa iinna ɛɛ durnya naa biini, ii gilɛɛ waa ɛɛa ra bɛri, dikuubɛɛwiai, durnya naa ra ba tunaarɛ. Wàá ka birgi.
32Maa nyiŋŋi durnya naa wia zuu ii nyuuni. Baal la n waa haaŋ dɔɔwɛ la ɔɔ aah siwiire dikuu Kɔraawiizi huma wia, di ra nyiŋŋi u wia par Kɔraawiizi. 33Ka baal la n dɔɔ haaŋwaa, ɔɔ aah siwiire dikuu durnya wia, ú wia wer par u haaŋ. 34U du wia anɛɛ biinii. Haaŋ la n waa jaari dɔɔwɛ ni toloori, Kɔraawiizi huma wia ɔɔ aah ba siweere. Haaŋ la n waa jaari dɔɔwɛ ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ u bɔrahɔŋ ni u biini maa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora, di ɛɛ kunnanaa u be. Haaŋ la n yuuwɛ ge ɔɔ aah siwiire dikuu durnya wia, ú wia wer par u jaari. 35N na nyiŋŋi ń hiini iabuu. A bɛŋ wiarɛ n na ŋɔ guŋ. Maa ŋɔ ń tɔ ia bɔr. N na nyiŋŋuu ií ra ɛɛ wia la n dɛkkɛ, di wer aah siwii nɛnnɛ di ra hum yaa Dɔɔri huma, wií maa gilɛɛ waa tɔ ia ŋmɛnɛɛ.
36Di baal bɛl dɔɔ u biihambie u hel haaŋ tuŋ, di ŋɔ lugɔ nɛr maa wàá kpau, ka bir binni lugɔ wɔɔ ɛɛwɛ nɛnnɛ, ú ɛɛ gunla maa unna nyiŋŋi. Wichɔgaa lɛi. Ú gil baal bɛl kpau. 37Ka di baal bɛl pessi a wia ka ŋɔ dí wàá kpa u biihambie tɛɛ baal maa, wiimaa wɔɔ ra fir, di a kaa ɛɛ lugɔ u himmaa bampiriire tɛu guŋ, wɔɔ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ baal, u ɛɛ nɛnnɛɛ. 38Awia, unla n kpa u biihambie tɛɛ baal, u ɛɛ nɛnnɛ. Ka unla n waa u biihambie kpawɛɛ tɛɛ baal la, waabuu ɛɛ nɛnnɛ werge.
39Di haaŋ yuuwɔ, di u jaari haa du de, u jaari hinnɛ dɔɔu. Ka di u jaari siuwɔ, waa kaa dɔɔu. U daŋ jaa wer lii di kaa ga yuu baal la maa unna nyiŋŋi. Ka a waa wer uŋ yuu baal maa, di Yeesu hiŋri lɛi. 40Ka miŋwaa be, di u gil yuui, gunnɛ niŋ ɛɛ bɔsɔna tɛu kaali un niŋ yuu. N himmaa bampirii wiŋɔzii guŋ, ka Kɔraawiizi Duma du n gba benii.

english_text:
Food Offered to Idols
1In your letter you asked me about food offered to idols. All of us know something about this subject. But knowledge makes us proud of ourselves, while love makes us helpful to others. 2In fact, people who think they know so much don't know anything at all. 3But God has no doubts about who loves him.
4Even though food is offered to idols, we know that none of the idols in this world are alive. After all, there is only one God. 5Many things in heaven and on earth are called gods and lords, but none of them really are gods or lords. 6We have only one God, and he is the Father. He created everything, and we live for him. Jesus Christ is our only Lord. Everything was made by him, and by him life was given to us.
7Not everyone knows these things. In fact, many people have grown up with the belief that idols have life in them. So when they eat meat offered to idols, they are bothered by a weak conscience. 8But food doesn't bring us any closer to God. We are no worse off if we don't eat, and we are no better off if we do.
9Don't cause problems for someone with a weak conscience, just because you have the right to eat anything. 10You know all this, and so it doesn't bother you to eat in the temple of an idol. But suppose a person with a weak conscience sees you and decides to eat food that has been offered to idols. 11Then what you know has destroyed someone Christ died for. 12When you sin by hurting a follower with a weak conscience, you sin against Christ. 13So if I hurt one of the Lord's followers by what I eat, I will never eat meat as long as I live.
translation_text:
Vuga diwee wia pɛɛzaa
1Too. A ka vuga kuaraa ola la wia. Yaa zummɔ lugɔ yaa maanii zum wia. Ka newee zumaarɛ ɔɔ gil u ra nyiŋŋi sɔŋ. Nɛnɔŋŋaawaa dɔɔ hiinaare. 2Nɛr la maa n na binni lugɔ u zum wiarɛ, u haa waa wia zummɛ nɛnnɛ alugɔ un niŋ vii zum la. 3Ka nɛr lawaa n nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi, Kɔraawiizi zunnii.
4Awia, yaa n ɔɔ ŋɔ vuga kuaraa ola wia naa, yaa zummɔ lugɔ vug maa waa hoo durnya di ra nyiŋ. Wiizizi gba waa hoo, di kpaŋkpaŋ bɛŋ lɛi. Waabuu Kɔraawiizi. 5Kuna la newea n na yir ba wiizizi ni ba dɔɔra la, a kpillɔɔ werge chiŋ ni hɛri biine. 6Ka yaawaa be, Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ kpaŋkpannɛ. Waabuu yaa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la. U fɔŋŋa wiarɛ yaa maa du de la. Yaa Dɔɔri ge ɛɛ kpaŋkpaŋ. Waabuu Yeesu Kristo la n ta kummaa, di kaa tɛɛ yaa miibɔɔ la.
7Ka nɛr maa lɛi zum guŋ. Nɛra baŋhina faa ra ɛɛ vuga wiarɛ a ra mani baa. Awia, haali ni zinaa, di ba hee ol la nɛra n kpuwɛɛ tɛɛ vuga la, ba ɔɔ haa ra sɛɛu lugɔ vuga la du denii di ra nyiŋ. Awia, ba biine ɔɔ chɔgi di ra tɔɔri baa, dikuu baŋ haa ra aani la wia.
8Yaa kundiwee lɛi niŋ gil yaa wia par Kɔraawiizi. Di yaa vɛɛ a dii, a wàá la yaa ni harbɔɔ. Di yaa haa ra dia, a wàá la yaa ni see.
9Ama, ií ra dazi, ii gilɛɛ gil ii guŋ ɛɛi wer dar banla n haa ra aani la, bá chol, 10dikuubɛɛwiai, di ii zum wia naa zɛɛ, ka la vugkuari bɔr di gaa hee ola la, ii dɔŋhiŋ la n haa ra aani la wa na ia de, u ge daŋ dɔɔ bampirii di kutti zuu de di ge ra heea. Ka uŋ haa ra aani la, u biini daŋ chɔgi di ra tɔɔruu. 11Ii chɔg ii dɔŋhinnɛ la. Kristo siuwɔɔ dikuu u wia, ka ii bir chɔguu dikuu ii zumaa wia. Nau! 12Di ii ra ɛɛ ii dɔŋahina kennaa, ba biine chɔgi di ra tɔɔri baa, dikuu baŋ haa ra aani wia naa, Kristoo ii ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa la. 13Awia, di diwee la min niŋ di, daŋ bir n dɔŋhiŋ harbɔɔ, màá ka di a diwee di hanna la, ń dɔŋhiŋ la gilɛɛ waa bir harbɔɔ.

english_text:
The Rights of an Apostle
1I am free. I am an apostle. I have seen the Lord Jesus and have led you to have faith in him. 2Others may think that I am not an apostle, but you are proof that I am an apostle to you.
3When people question me, I tell them 4that Barnabas and I have the right to our food and drink. 5We each have the right to marry one of the Lord's followers and to take her along with us, just as the other apostles and the Lord's brothers and Peter do. 6Are we the only ones who have to support ourselves by working at another job? 7Do soldiers pay their own salaries? Don't people who raise grapes eat some of what they grow? Don't shepherds get milk from their own goats?
8-9 I am not saying this on my own authority. The Law of Moses tells us not to muzzle an ox when it is grinding grain. But was God concerned only about an ox? 10No, he wasn't! He was talking about us. This was written in the Scriptures so that all who plow and all who grind the grain will look forward to sharing in the harvest.
11 When we told the message to you, it was like planting spiritual seed. So we have the right to accept material things as our harvest from you. 12If others have the right to do this, we have an even greater right. But we haven't used this right of ours. We are willing to put up with anything to keep from causing trouble for the message about Christ.
13 Don't you know that people who work in the temple make their living from what is brought to the temple? Don't you know that a person who serves at the altar is given part of what is offered? 14 In the same way, the Lord wants everyone who preaches the good news to make a living from preaching this message.
15But I have never used these privileges of mine, and I am not writing this because I want to start now. I would rather die than have someone rob me of the right to take pride in this. 16I don't have any reason to brag about preaching the good news. Preaching is something God told me to do, and if I don't do it, I am doomed. 17If I preach because I want to, I will be paid. But even if I don't want to, it is still something God has sent me to do. 18What pay am I given? It is the chance to preach the good news free of charge and not to use the privileges that are mine because I am a preacher.
19I am not anyone's slave. But I have become a slave to everyone, so I can win as many people as possible. 20When I am with the Jews, I live like a Jew to win Jews. They are ruled by the Law of Moses, and I am not. But I live by the Law to win them. 21And when I am with people who are not ruled by the Law, I forget about the Law to win them. Of course, I never really forget about the law of God. In fact, I am ruled by the law of Christ. 22When I am with people whose faith is weak, I live as they do to win them. I do everything I can to win everyone I possibly can. 23I do all this for the good news, because I want to share in its blessings.
A Race and a Fight
24 You know that many runners enter a race, and only one of them wins the prize. So run to win! 25 Athletes work hard to win a crown that cannot last, but we do it for a crown that will last forever. 26I don't run without a goal. And I don't box by beating my fists in the air. 27I keep my body under control and make it my slave, so I won't lose out after telling the good news to others.
translation_text:
Wia la n dɛg Yeesu huŋhunni
1Miŋwaa waa Yeesu Kristo huŋhunni bɛlhiŋ ɛɛwɛa? Maa n hiŋ dɔɔwɛɛ gɛɛ? Kennaa ii gba n sɛɛwɛ di ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi naa, n huma la miŋ hummɛ Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini wiarɛ ii sɛɛ di ra hiŋ gunla. 2Di baŋhina waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ n ɛɛ Kristo huŋhunnii, ka iawaa daŋ sɛɛ. Hiŋaa naa iinna hiŋ naabuu, Kɔraawiizi kpa bagli lugɔ n ɛɛ u huŋhunnii wibii maa.
3Di nɛra ra pɛɛziŋ wia, kennaabuu n ɔɔ ŋɔ n hor. 4Di nɛra ra hiini yaa ani diwee ni kunnyɔɔlaa yaa waa guŋ dɛkkɛa? 5Kristo huŋhunna la, yaa Dɔɔri niuna ani Sifas la maa kpa haanaa, ba ɛɛ Yeesu hiŋra, ba ni baa ra vol. Yaabuu waa guŋ fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛaa? 6Gɛɛ n ni Banabas bɛnnɛ ninna di yaa hinaa kuuhni biinei?
7Di i ɛɛ sooja di ra la laal, i dɔɔra kebee lɛi i ra dia? Di i par koo, hàá di u biini diweea? Di i ra nɔɔni nauna ge, hàá nyɔɔ a nailaa? 8Newea wia bɛŋ lɛi ra bagli guŋ. Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ ge gba bagli gunnɛ. 9Moosis sɛbɔɔrɛ, “Ií gilɛɛ waa vɔɔ navarga la n na fɛrgi mia, a bii ra lii nua.” Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ Moosis sɛbi guŋ dikuu nauna wia, ú wer hiini nauna gɛɛ newea hiinaa wiarɛ u gil u sɛbi gunnɛi? 10Yaa wiarɛ u gil u sɛbi guŋ, wibii maa, ya zum alugɔ nɛr la maa n na par, ú ra par ni tamii, nɛr la maa n na kum ge, ú ra kum ni tamii.
11Yaa n duu yaa kuna naa, amɔ, yaa wàá kumaawaa? Yaa n bagli ia Kɔraawiizi wia di hiini ii dunzi kennaa, amɔ, yaa wàá na kummaa ii be di hiini yaa hinaa? 12Ii ɔɔ ra tɛɛ baŋhinaa guŋ. Di ba dɛg guŋ, amɔ, yaawaa waa guŋ dɛkkɛ werge kaali baa?
Ka yaa faa waa guŋ fɔŋŋa ra bagli ii ni, ka ra di kanyitti wiimaa biini, yá gilɛɛ waa teŋ amaniyesuma wia ŋmɛnɛɛ. 13Ii zummɔ lugɔ banla n na hum Kɔraawiizi Dia huma ra di a huma biinii. Banla n na hum mbusu lizibɔr, na mbusu lizaa yeŋaa ra di. 14Gunnɛ yaa Dɔɔri ge dau tɛɛ banla n ɔɔ ra lizi amaniyesuma la, di ŋɔ bá ra di a huma biini.
15N dɛg guŋ maanii, ka maa gunna lɛɛ ii be. Maa wia naa sɛbɛɛ filaŋkeŋ, di ra nyiŋŋi ŋɔ ii tɛŋ guŋ. N siu bɔ miŋ ɛɛ guŋ, nɛ́ra gilɛɛ wer duŋŋiŋ n hinchɔlaa naa wia biini. 16Màá wer kpa amaniyesuma lizaa naawaa di nyiŋŋi sɔŋ tɛɛ n hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n biini ɔɔ ra firimbuu, n na ŋɔa. Di màá ŋɔwɛɛ, wiarɛ. A daŋ nuuŋ. 17Di n himmaa kipar wiarɛ n na ɛɛ guŋ, a dɛkkɔ minna na kinturgaa. Ka Kɔraawiizi kpa amaniyesuma naabuu tɛŋ ŋɔ ń lizi ra tɛɛ nɛra. Awia, min lɛi tɛɛ n hiŋ guŋ, n na hum. 18Beedee n ɛɛ n huma hiŋ tɔnai? N tɔnaa min niŋ lizi amaniyesuma la tɛɛ nɛra pɛɛpɛɛ, ka maa baa ra bagli fɔŋŋa la min niŋ faa bagli ba ni, dikuu miŋ lizi amaniyesuma tɛɛ baa la wia.
19Nɛr maa lɛi dɔɔ n fɔŋŋa, ka n kpa n hinnɛ di birgi balii, di hum ra tɛɛ ba maa, ń vii wer na baa werge tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 20Di n ni Jus hina kpauwɔ, aŋ kpa n hinnɛ birgi ba bɛl, di ra hiŋ ba Gbɔgni la. A waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ Gbɔgni la hiŋaa dɔɔmbuu, ka n na hiŋaabuu gunla ba ge n na hiŋ la, ń wer na baa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 21Di n ni banla n waa gbɔg la ra hiŋ ge kpauwɔ, aŋ kpa n hinnɛ birgi lugɔ baa, ń wer na ba ge tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ka a waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ maa Kɔraawiizi nua ra hiŋ. N na hiŋuubuu gunla Kristo n bagli yaa, yaa ra hiŋ labuu. 22Di n ni banla ge n na aani Kristo hiŋaa biini la ge kpauwɔ, aŋ kpa n hinnɛ di birgi ba ge bɛl, ń wer na baa. Gunla maa nɛra maa n duwɛɛ, aŋ kpa n hinnɛ birgi guŋ, ń vii wer hiini baŋhina, Kɔ́raawiizi lɛɛ baa. 23Annii maanii n kuu amaniyesuma la wia ra ɛɛ, ń ge vii wer nuu suma a amaniyesuma lizaa biini.
24Ii zummɔ lugɔ di nɛkpila ra chɔ bá di kumbɛl, ba maanii ɔɔ chɔ, ka kpaŋkpannɛ ɔɔ wa diu. Awia, kennaa iinna hiŋ Kɔraawiizi naa, ií aah siwii di ra hiŋ guŋ di wer wa na lɛɛi. 25Nɛr la n na helli chɔi, ú wer chɔ chɔzenaa biini di wer ra di, ɔɔ ra lau u hinnɛ wiimaa biini, ka ú wer chɔ di di, bá kpa kooree kahuro bɛl dee hiu. A kahuro wàá birgi chɔgaa. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ yaa Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa biini naa, yaawaa ra chɔu, yá wer na unla n waa chɔgaa dɔɔwɛ maa la. 26Awiarɛ n ɔɔ deŋli ra chɔ guŋŋ ń ga hel u maga. N kaa ɛɛu lugɔ abuloosi lɔɔri Kɔraawiizi huma biini. Maa ɔɔ ta ra kirgi. 27Anna tɔɔri n bɔrahɔnnɛ di ra lau n hiŋ nɛnnɛ, ń himmaa gilɛɛ wa hiŋ wia naa minna bagli nɛra naa huhzi.

english_text:
Don't Worship Idols
1 Friends, I want to remind you that all our ancestors walked under the cloud and went through the sea. 2This was like being baptized and becoming followers of Moses. 3 All of them also ate the same spiritual food 4 and drank the same spiritual drink, which flowed from the spiritual rock that followed them. That rock was Christ. 5 But most of them did not please God. So they died, and their bodies were scattered all over the desert.
6What happened to them is a warning to keep us from wanting to do the same evil things. 7 They worshiped idols, just as the Scriptures say, “The people sat down to eat and drink. Then they got up to dance around.” So don't worship idols. 8 Some of those people did shameful things, and in a single day about 23,000 died. Don't do shameful things as they did. 9 And don't try to test Christ, as some of them did and were later bitten by poisonous snakes. 10 Don't even grumble, as some of them did and were killed by the destroying angel. 11These things happened to them as a warning to us. All this was written in the Scriptures to teach us who live in these last days.
12Even if you think you can stand up to temptation, be careful not to fall. 13 You are tempted in the same way that everyone else is tempted. But God can be trusted not to let you be tempted too much, and he will show you how to escape from your temptations.
14My friends, you must keep away from idols. 15I am speaking to you as people who have enough sense to know what I am talking about. 16 When we drink from the cup we ask God to bless, isn't that sharing in the blood of Christ? When we eat the bread we break, isn't that sharing in the body of Christ? 17By sharing in the same loaf of bread, we become one body, even though there are many of us.
18 Aren't the people of Israel sharing in the worship when they gather around the altar and eat the sacrifices offered there? 19Am I saying that either the idols or the food sacrificed to them is anything at all? 20 No, I am not! This food is really sacrificed to demons and not to God. I don't want you to have anything to do with demons. 21You cannot drink from the cup of demons and still drink from the Lord's cup. You cannot eat at the table of demons and still eat at the Lord's table. 22 We would make the Lord jealous if we did this. And we are not stronger than the Lord.
Always Honor God
23 Some of you say, “We can do whatever we want to!” But I tell you not everything may be good or helpful. 24We should think about others and not about ourselves. 25However, when you buy meat in the market, go ahead and eat it. Keep your conscience clear by not asking where the meat came from. 26 The Scriptures say, “The earth and everything in it belong to the Lord.”
27If an unbeliever invites you to dinner, and you want to go, then go. Eat whatever you are served. Don't cause a problem for someone's conscience by asking where the food came from. 28-29But if you are told it has been sacrificed to idols, don't cause a problem by eating it. I don't mean a problem for yourself, but for the one who told you. Why should my freedom be limited by someone else's conscience? 30If I give thanks for what I eat, why should anyone accuse me of doing wrong?
31When you eat or drink or do anything else, always do it to honor God. 32Don't cause problems for Jews or Greeks or anyone else who belongs to God's church. 33I always try to please others instead of myself, in the hope that many of them will be saved.
translation_text:
Karfaa dikuu vuga wia
1Yaabalaa, n ŋɔ ń liizi iabuu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi baama la faa tɔ yaa naabaala la maa ninɛɛ. Ba maanii ga muu la biini kaali. 2A ɛɛwɔ lugɔ ba faa sɔ baabuu nii guŋ, baama la ni muu la maa biini, bá ra hiŋ Moosis hiŋaa la. 3Ba maanii faa na diwee Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini di ra di, 4di kaa na nii u fɔŋŋa biini di ra nyɔɔ. Bii ninɛɛ a nii faa lii. Kristoo ɛɛwɛ lugɔ bii la, di ɔɔ faa hiŋ baa ra la, ba na nii u be di ra nyɔɔ. 5Ka ba galga maa wia faa waa Kɔraawiizi pattɛ, ba siuzi bɔkpila maa hɛribɔduma la biini.
6Wia naa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ sɛɛliizi, ya kpa ra mɛgzi di ra chaani nɛra siwee, ya gilɛɛ dɔɔ kunchɔgaa kɛkɛluu gunla baŋ faa dɔɔwɛ la. 7Ya gilɛɛ ra kuari vuga alugɔ baŋhina n faa ra kuari vuga la. Moosis sɛbɔɔrɛ, “Ba so di ra di, di ra nyɔɔ sinni, di sa, di ra ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ wia.” 8Ya gilɛɛ ra sɛm lugɔ baŋhina n faa ra sɛm, Kɔraawiizi kpuuzi ba nɛra kagboŋa tokko ni ahoro hɔpizikpaŋ biini la. 9Ya gilɛɛ ɛɛ Kristo na gunla baŋhina n faa ɛɛu na, u gil hɛrikuna dunzi baa, ba siuzi la. 10Ya gilɛɛ nuumi ra du Kɔraawiizi alugɔ ba baŋhina n faa nuumɛɛ di ra duu, u gil siu mɛlika wa kpuuzi baa la.
11Too. Wia naa maa wa ɛɛ baabuu, á chaani ba siwee. Moosis sɛbi a wiarɛ, á chaani yaa ge bannii n du durnya tunaa hɔpizaa biini naa siwee. 12Awia, nɛr la maa n na fɛ lugɔ u chigɔɔ chigigi, ú ra dazi ú gilɛɛ waa chol. 13Nɛr maanii ra di tɔɔrɔɔ. Awia, di hinla ra di tɔɔrɔɔ guŋ, i bɛŋ lɛi haa faarɛɛ ra di a tɔɔrɔɔ dɔŋ. Ka Kɔraawiizi wia dɔɔ wibiire. Wàá kpa wifittii la n kaali i fɔŋŋa ɛɛi na í chol. U daŋ baglii gunla hin niŋ vɛɛ a wii, di wer lii u biini.
Vuga diwee ni yaa Dɔɔri Diwee wia
14Awia, n biinɔŋŋaa, ií gil vuga kuaraa wia ha, di ra dazi a ni. 15Ii ɛɛ nunzunnaa. Awia, ií pessi n wiŋɔzi naa nɛnnɛ na. 16Kristo siŋ la yaa n suŋŋi wiizi di du u ni ka nyɔɔu, di ra liizi u wia la, yaa maa kpauwɔɔ guŋ, ú chal wia biini. Yaa n ɔɔ mɔnni paanuu la ge la, yaa maa kpauwɔɔ ú bɔrahɔŋ wia biini la. 17Yaa ɔɔ du kpil ninɛɛ ka hee a paanuukpaŋ. Awia, yaa ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋkpannɛ, dikuu paanuukpaŋ la yaa maa n kpauwɛ hee la wia.
18Ií ra binni Jus hina wia la. Banla n na di mbusuzi la, ba waa Kɔraawiizi mbusuzi lizibɔr wia biini duwɛaa? 19Minna ŋɔ kennaa, maa ŋɔ lugɔ vug ɛɛ kummaanii gɛɛ mbusu la baŋ lizɛɛ tɛu la ɛɛ kumbɛllɛ. 20N na ŋɔu lugɔ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ n ɔɔ ra lizi ba mbusuzi la, tinnanchɔgaarɛ ba ɔɔ lizaa ra tɛɛ la. Kɔraawiizi lɛi ba ɔɔ lizaa ra tɛɛ. Maa nyiŋŋi ii ni tinnanchɔgaa waa kpau wikpaŋ biini. 21A waa wer iin nyɔɔ yaa Dɔɔri siŋ la, ka kaa la ga nyɔɔ tinnanchɔgaa hor la. Gunnɛ a waa kaa du wer iiŋ hee yaa Dɔɔri paanuu la, ka kaa la ga hee tinnanchɔgaa ol la. Akai! 22Yaa ŋɔ ya fuuh yaa Dɔɔri baannɛ gɛɛ? Yaabuu kpekke kaaluuwaa?
23Too. Miŋwaa be, “Wiimaa ɛɛi waa kii.” Ka wiimaa ɛɛi ge lɛi wesse. Ka wiimaa ɛɛi ge lɛi dɔɔ hiinaa. 24A waa dɛkkɛ nɛr n gillɛ u bɛmbɛŋ wia tiruu. Ú gil u dɔŋahina gba wia tiruu ra jaa.
25Di ba ra yoo ol, olyoori bɔr, di ii ra nyiŋŋi ol, ií yau ra hee di gilɛɛ ra aani lugɔ a waa wer iin niŋ heea, 26dikuubɛɛwiai, “Kɔraawiizii dɔɔ hɛri ani kunla maa n du u biini.”
27Di banla n waa Kɔraawiizi wia sɛɛwɛ bɛl yir ia, ií ba ií nuu di, di ii ra nyiŋŋi guŋ, ií la. Diwee la maa un niŋ tɛɛ ia la, ií di, di gilɛɛ waa pɛɛzi a wia, di ra aani alugɔ a waa wer iin niŋ dia. 28Ka di nɛbɛl ŋɔ ii be alugɔ vugkuaraa olle, di u wa ŋɔ guŋ, ii gilɛɛ waa heea, dikuu nɛr la n ŋɔ ii be la n na aani wia. 29Ii himmaa biine wia lɛi n ŋɔ ií gil. Ka unla hiŋ biini wiarɛ n ŋɔ ií gil.
Ii daŋ pɛɛzi, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ maa gunna kii, ka ń lau n hiŋ dikuu nɛbɛl n na aani wiai?” 30Di n jaami Kɔraawiizi ka ra dia, bɛɛ wiarɛ ba kaa gbɛlliŋ dikuu diwee la miŋ jaami Kɔraawiizi un tɛŋ la wiai?
31Ka wii la maa iinna ɛɛ, di diire i ra di, di niirɛ ii ra nyɔɔ, ka ií ra kpa Kɔraawiizi girme a maa biini. 32Ií ra dazi, ii gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ nɛr maa wiimaa, u biini waa chɔgi di ra tɔɔruu. Di Jus hinaa gɛɛ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ gɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hiŋraa, ii gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ bɛl maa guŋ. 33N gba ra hiŋ gunnɛ, ń wia wer par nɛr maa. Màá sɛɛ gil n bɛmbɛŋ wia tiriŋ. Nɛr maa wiarɛ ninna tiriŋ, ń wer na baa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

english_text:
1 You must follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ.
Rules for Worship
2I am proud of you, because you always remember me and obey the teachings I gave you. 3Now I want you to know that Christ is the head of all men, and a man is the head of a woman. But God is the head of Christ. 4This means that any man who prays or prophesies with something on his head brings shame to his head.
5But any woman who prays or prophesies without something on her head brings shame to her head. In fact, she may as well shave her head. 6A woman should wear something on her head. It is a disgrace for a woman to shave her head or cut her hair. But if she refuses to wear something on her head, let her cut off her hair.
7 Men were created to be like God and to bring honor to God. This means a man should not wear anything on his head. Women were created to bring honor to men. 8 It was the woman who was made from a man, and not the man who was made from a woman. 9He wasn't created for her. She was created for him. 10And so, because of this, and also because of the angels, a woman ought to wear something on her head, as a sign of her authority.
11As far as the Lord is concerned, men and women need each other. 12It is true that the first woman came from a man, but all other men have been given birth by women. Yet God is the one who created everything. 13Ask yourselves if it is proper for a woman to pray without something on her head. 14Isn't it unnatural and disgraceful for men to have long hair? 15But long hair is a beautiful way for a woman to cover her head. 16This is how things are done in all of God's churches, and this is why none of you should argue about what I have said.
Rules for the Lord's Supper
17Your worship services do you more harm than good. I am certainly not going to praise you for this. 18I am told you can't get along with each other when you worship, and I am sure that some of what I have heard is true. 19You are bound to argue with each other, but it is easy to see which of you have God's approval.
20When you meet together, you don't really celebrate the Lord's Supper. 21You even start eating before everyone gets to the meeting, and some of you go hungry, while others get drunk. 22Don't you have homes where you can eat and drink? Do you hate God's church? Do you want to embarrass people who don't have anything? What can I say to you? I certainly cannot praise you.
The Lord's Supper
(Matthew 26.26-29; Mark 14.22-25; Luke 22.14-20)
23I have already told you what the Lord Jesus did on the night he was betrayed. And it came from the Lord himself.
He took some bread in his hands. 24Then after he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is given for you. Eat this and remember me.”
25 After the meal, Jesus took a cup of wine in his hands and said, “This is my blood, and with it God makes his new agreement with you. Drink this and remember me.”
26The Lord meant that when you eat this bread and drink from this cup, you tell about his death until he comes.
27But if you eat the bread and drink the wine in a way that isn't worthy of the Lord, you sin against his body and blood. 28This is why you must examine the way you eat and drink. 29If you fail to understand that you are the body of the Lord, you will condemn yourselves by the way you eat and drink. 30This is why many of you are sick and weak and why a lot of others have died. 31If we carefully judge ourselves, we won't be punished. 32But when the Lord judges and punishes us, he does it to keep us from being condemned with the rest of the world.
33My dear friends, you should wait until everyone gets there before you start eating. 34If you really are hungry, you can eat at home. Then you won't condemn yourselves when you meet together.
After I arrive, I will instruct you about the other matters.
translation_text:
1Awia, n na nyiŋŋi lugɔ ii ɛɛ n hiŋra, di ra hiŋiŋ gunla miŋ ge n ɛɛ Kristo hiŋri, di ra hiŋuu la.
Haana nyuuni tɔi jaamibɔr wia
2N na chɔli iabuu dikuu iinna liizi n widaulaa la maa miŋ faa bagli ia la, di ra hiŋ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n bagliŋ, n ge kpa bagli ia la.
3N na nyiŋŋi ii zum lugɔ Kristoo ɛɛ baal nabɔma, baal ge ɛɛ haaŋ nabɔma, Kristo ge nabɔmaa Kɔraawiizi. 4Di baal maa ra suŋŋi wiizi gɛɛ u ra ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini, ka kuŋ tɔ u nyuu, Kristoo u ra gbɛlli la. 5Di haaŋ maa ge ra suŋŋi wiizi gɛɛ u ra ŋɔ wia u Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini, ka kummaa waa u nyuu tɔwɛɛ, u jaarii u ra gbɛlli la. U ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nyugbala hiŋ. 6Di wàá sɛɛ kpa kummaa tɔ u nyuu, amɔ, bá fuŋ u nyuu. Di a waa wer baŋ fuŋ u nyuu gɛɛ baŋ gbaari u nyuu ha, amɔ, ú kpa kuŋ tɔ u nyuu hiŋ. 7A waa dɛkkɛ baal ge n kpa kuŋ tɔ u nyuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu du Kɔraawiizi duulaa. Haaŋ genii ra bagli baal girme. 8Baal faa waa haaŋ be liwɛɛ. Haannɛ lii baal be. 9Kɔraawiizi faa waa baal tawɛɛ dikuu haaŋ wia, ka u ta haannɛ dikuu baal wia. 10Awia, a dɛkkɔ haaŋ n na sɛɛ baal dɔɔra, di kpa kuŋ ra tɔ u nyuu. U gunnɛ ra bagli lugɔ baallɛ dɔɔ u fɔŋŋa. Mɛlikazi a binni iabuu. Awia, ií ra ɛɛ guŋ.
11Ama, báal gilɛɛ ra binni haaŋ pɛɛ yaa Dɔɔri hiŋaa naa biini, háaŋ ge gilɛɛ ra binni baal pɛɛ. 12Haaŋ faa lii baal ninɛɛ, ka haannɛ jaa ra lul baal. Kummaa ge lii Kɔraawiizi benii. 13Ií pessi na ka bagliŋ. A wesso haaŋ n na jaami Kɔraawiizi, di waa kuŋ kpawɛɛ tɔ u nyuuwaa? 14Ii duula gba ra bagli iabuu lugɔ di baal nyuhuna hello werge, a guŋ waa wer. A gunna ɛɛubuu hiihzi. 15Ka di haaŋ waa nyuhuna hello werge, a guŋ wessoo. A ɔɔ giluu u du wer. Kɔraawiizii tɛu guŋ, ú ra tɔ u hiŋ. 16Di nɛr la maa ra nyiŋŋi hɔɔzi dii, ka gunnɛ yaa ni Kɔraawiizi hiŋra la maa gba ra hiŋ.
Yaa Dɔɔri diwee dii wia
(Mat 26:26-29; Maak 14:22-25; Luuk 22:14-20)
17Wia la minna nyiŋŋi n jaa ŋɔ tɛɛ ia ií ra hiŋ lawaa, màá chɔli ia aawaa wia. Ii dɔŋa be chaalaa waa ia ra hiini, ka ra nyaŋŋi ia. 18A luglii keŋ. N nuu ii wiarɛ lugɔ iiŋ ɔɔ chaali ií jaami Kɔraawiizi la, ii waa ɔɔ dɔɔ nuukpaŋ. N na binni lugɔ wibiire ba ra ŋɔ. 19Dɔŋbargaa daŋ du ii baaŋ, ií banla Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ na, ii wia paruu la wer lii bɔchaaŋ, ya zum ia. 20Iiŋ ɔɔ chaali dɔŋa ií di yaa Dɔɔri diwee la, a dii lɛi ii ɔɔ ra di guŋ, 21dikuubɛɛwiai, ii bɛl maa ɔɔ hahzuu ra di u bɛŋ diwee. Baŋhina wàá na, baŋhina ge na werge di ra dɛɛzi. 22Bɛɛ ii ra ɛɛ gunnɛi? Ii waa diini dɔɔwɛ iin ninna di de di ra nyɔaa? Ii ra binni Kɔraawiizi hiŋraa pɛɛ gunla, di kaa ra du nyaara la ge hiihzi. Ɛrɛɛ ń kaa ŋɔ ii benei? Ń chɔli ia gɛɛ? Akai! Màá chɔli ia.
23Yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu benii n nuu wia naa, di faa bagli ia gunla uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ hamuŋa la baŋ faa ɛɛu sɔsɔgɔ la. U kpa paanuu bɛllɛ a hamuŋa ni 24di suŋŋi wiizi du u ni, ka lawuu mɔnni mɔnni, ka ŋɔ, “N bɔrahɔnnɛ keŋ n na chɔgi dikuu ii wia. Ií ra heea di ra liizi n wia.” 25Gunnɛ baŋ wa diwee tuŋ, u kpa libee ni siŋ, di ŋɔ, “Siŋ naa ɛɛ n challɛ un niŋ kuu ii wia di lii, di kuari ii ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋfalii dɔɔi. Saŋa la maa iin ninna nyɔɔu, ií ɔɔ ra nyɔɔu di ra liizi n wia.” 26U ŋɔ gunnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, saŋa la maa iin niŋ ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la, di ra nyɔɔ siŋ la, yaa Dɔɔri siu wiarɛ ii ɔɔ ra bagli guŋ, di ra la saŋa la un niŋ kaa bir ba la.
27Awia, nɛr la maa n niŋ hee paanuu naa yaa n ɔɔ ra hee, di ra liizi yaa Dɔɔri wia naa gunla n waa dɛkkɛ, u ra binni yaa Dɔɔri bɔrahɔnnɛ pɛɛ la. Nɛr la maa ge n niŋ nyɔɔ siŋ naa, yaa n ɔɔ ra nyɔɔ di ra liizi yaa Dɔɔri wia naa gunla n waa dɛkkɛ, yaa Dɔɔri challɛ u ra binni pɛɛ. 28Awia, ií bɛl maa ɔɔ fɛ nfɛrɛ nɛnnɛ na mɔɔ, ka haa hee a paanuu di nyɔɔ a siŋ. 29Di guŋ lɛi, ka unla maa ra heea di ra nyɔɔa, u ra ba ú wa zuu Kɔraawiizi seriya dii biinii, dikuu uŋ waa pessee nɛnnɛ lugɔ yaa Dɔɔri bɔrahɔnnɛ, ka ra ɛɛ guŋ wia. 30Awiarɛ ii nɛkpila maa gɛrgi ra wii, baŋhina ge siuzi la. 31Di yaa faa pessi yaa biine wiarɛ mɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi faa wàá di yaa seriya, di ra tɔɔri yaa.
32Ka yaa Dɔɔri n ɔɔ di yaa seriya di ra tɔɔri yaa naa, ɔɔ ɛɛ gunnɛ, ya gilɛɛ waa jaa banla un niŋ di ba seriya, di vɛɛ baa la biini.
33Awia, yaabalaa, di ii ɔɔ wa chaali dɔŋa ií di diwee naa, ii gilɛɛ hahzi ra dia. Ií ɔɔ ra kpaŋ dɔŋa. 34Di lɔzi ra kpu unla maa, ú ɔɔ di u dia mɔɔ ka ra ba. Ií gilɛɛ waa di a diwee gunla n waa dɛkkɛ, Kɔraawiizi wa di ii seriya, ií chol.
Wia la maa n kawɛɛ, di n kaa wa ba, n daŋ bagli ia.

english_text:
Spiritual Gifts
1My friends, you asked me about spiritual gifts. 2I want you to remember that before you became followers of the Lord, you were led in all the wrong ways by idols that cannot even talk. 3Now I want you to know that if you are led by God's Spirit, you will say that Jesus is Lord, and you will never curse Jesus.
4 There are different kinds of spiritual gifts, but they all come from the same Spirit. 5There are different ways to serve the same Lord, 6and we can each do different things. Yet the same God works in all of us and helps us in everything we do.
7The Spirit has given each of us a special way of serving others. 8Some of us can speak with wisdom, while others can speak with knowledge, but these gifts come from the same Spirit. 9To others the Spirit has given great faith or the power to heal the sick 10or the power to work mighty miracles. Some of us are prophets, and some of us recognize when God's Spirit is present. Others can speak different kinds of languages, and still others can tell what these languages mean. 11But it is the Spirit who does all this and decides which gifts to give to each of us.
One Body with Many Parts
12 The body of Christ has many different parts, just as any other body does. 13Some of us are Jews, and others are Gentiles. Some of us are slaves, and others are free. But God's Spirit baptized each of us and made us part of the body of Christ. Now we each drink from that same Spirit.
14Our bodies don't have just one part. They have many parts. 15Suppose a foot says, “I'm not a hand, and so I'm not part of the body.” Wouldn't the foot still belong to the body? 16Or suppose an ear says, “I'm not an eye, and so I'm not part of the body.” Wouldn't the ear still belong to the body? 17If our bodies were only an eye, we couldn't hear a thing. And if they were only an ear, we couldn't smell a thing. 18But God has put all parts of our body together in the way that he decided is best.
19A body isn't really a body, unless there is more than one part. 20It takes many parts to make a single body. 21That's why the eyes cannot say they don't need the hands. That's also why the head cannot say it doesn't need the feet. 22In fact, we cannot get along without the parts of the body that seem to be the weakest. 23We take special care to dress up some parts of our bodies. We are modest about our personal parts, 24but we don't have to be modest about other parts.
God put our bodies together in such a way that even the parts that seem the least important are valuable. 25He did this to make all parts of the body work together smoothly, with each part caring about the others. 26If one part of our body hurts, we hurt all over. If one part of our body is honored, the whole body will be happy.
27Together you are the body of Christ. Each one of you is part of his body. 28 First, God chose some people to be apostles and prophets and teachers for the church. But he also chose some to work miracles or heal the sick or help others or be leaders or speak different kinds of languages. 29Not everyone is an apostle. Not everyone is a prophet. Not everyone is a teacher. Not everyone can work miracles. 30Not everyone can heal the sick. Not everyone can speak different kinds of languages. Not everyone can tell what these languages mean. 31I want you to desire the best gifts. So I will show you a much better way.
translation_text:
Sunzaazi la n lii Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii be wia
1Too. Wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋazi la Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii n sunzi ia la, n na nyiŋŋuu ii zum a wia nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ bambugee a biini. 2Ii zummɔ lugɔ saŋa la iiŋ faa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la, Sitaani faa dar iabuu, ii leuzi di ra hiŋ vuga. A waa wette ra ŋɔ wia, ka ii faa ra hiŋaa. 3Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu ii zum lugɔ nɛr la maa n na ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini, a hiŋ wàá wer gbɛlli Yeesu. Nɛr la maa ge n na ŋɔ lugɔ Yeesu ɛɛ yaa Dɔɔrii la, Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biinii u wer zum guŋ di ra ŋɔ.
4Too. Wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋazi la Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii n sunzi yaa la kurgɔɔrɛ. Ka Kɔraawiizi Dumkpannɛ du yaa maa ni di ra ɛɛa. 5Humazi la yaa Dɔɔri n bɔnni yaa la kurgɔɔrɛ. Ka yaa Dɔɔri ɛɛ kpannɛ, yaa maa ra humuu. 6Fɔŋŋazi la Kɔraawiizi n bɔnni yaa la kurgɔɔrɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi kpannɛ ra hum yaa maa biine, di ra ɛɛ a wiimaa.
7Kɔraawiizii ra tɛɛ bɛl maa ni u wiɛɛlaa, ú ɛɛ u Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini di wer hiini ii maa. 8Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii gillɔɔ baŋhina ra ŋɔ wia, a dɔɔ nunzuma, di kaa gil baŋhina ge dɔɔ sichaana. Kɔraawiizi Dumkpaŋ hinnɛ tɛɛ bɛl maa a guŋ fɔŋŋa, 9di kaa gil baŋhina ge dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi yarda nɛnnɛ u fɔŋŋa biini, baŋhina ge dɔɔ fɔŋŋa bá wer chaa nɛra, 10baŋhina ge dɔɔ fɔŋŋa bá wer ɛɛ wizenaa, baŋhina ge dɔɔ fɔŋŋa bá wer lizi Kɔraawiizi amaniye, báŋhina ge wer zum fɔŋŋa dizi la nɛra n dɔɔwɛ, baŋhina wer mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi, baŋhina ge wer bagli a mɔɔdumazi zɛɛzi ra tɛɛ nɛra. 11Ka annii maa, Kɔraawiizi Dumkpaŋ labuu ra ɛɛ a maa, di ra bɔnni bɛl maa ni u wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋazi gunla n paruu.
Bɔrahɔŋkpaŋ ka dɔɔ bɔkpila wia
12Ií na gunla yaa bɔrahɔŋ n duwɛɛ. U ɛɛ kuŋkpannɛ ka dɔɔ bɔkpila. A bɔkpila choŋŋi dɔŋaa di ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋkpaŋ. Gunnɛ Kristo ge du la. 13Yaa ɛɛ Jus hinaa di kaa ɛɛ Giris hina, yaa baŋhina ge ɛɛ balaa, yaa baŋhina ge dɔɔ yaa hinaa. Ka Kɔraawiizi kpa u Dumnanii du yaa maa ni, yaa maa birgi bɔrahɔŋkpaŋ. Kuŋkpannɛ u gil yaa maa na di du yaa biine. U Dumaa yaa maa na la.
14Newee yeŋa waa kpaŋ ɛɛwɛ. A kpillɔɔ. 15Di i naa ŋɔwɔɔ, “Maa nonii ɛɛwɛ, awia, maa hoo i bɔrahɔŋ ni, u leuwoo.” Waa nonii ɛɛwɛ ka u gba du i bɔrahɔŋ ninɛɛ. 16Di i digni ge ŋɔwɔɔ, “Maa siwii ɛɛwɛ, awia, maa hoo i bɔrahɔŋ ni, u leuwoo.” Waa siwii ɛɛwɛ, ka u gba du i bɔrahɔŋ ninɛɛ. 17Di i bɔrahɔŋ vii ɛɛ siwii bɛnnɛ, ka digni waa hoo, i daŋ wer nuu wiaa? Di i bɔrahɔŋ ge vii kaa ɛɛ digni bɛnnɛ ka miizi waa hoo, i daŋ wer nuu sɔaah? 18Ka guŋ lɛi Kɔraawiizi ta yaa. U tɛɛ yaabuu yaa bɔrahɔna yeŋa maa, di dua gunla unna nyiŋŋi. 19Di a yeŋa maa vii ɛɛ kuŋkpannɛ, u daŋ vii wer ɛɛ bɔrahɔnnaa? Akai! 20Ka a kpillɔɔ. A maa ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋkpaŋ.
21Siwii wàá wer ŋɔ nonii be, “N daŋ wer hum huma n bɛŋ, di haa hoo.” Nyuu ge wàá wer ŋɔ naazi be, “N daŋ wer hum huma n bɛŋ, di ii waa hoo.” 22Akai. Yeŋa la n gɛrgɛɛ la, a wiarɛ kpolle werge. 23Anla n waa girme dɔɔwɛ la, aabuu yaa ra tɔgzi werge, anla n chummɛ la ge, yaa ɔɔ ra binni a ni. 24Ka anla n wesse la, a waa kaa ɛɛ lugɔ ya kaa ra binni aawaa ni. Gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi gil yaa bɔrahɔna yeŋa kpau, yaa ra tɔgzi anla n waa girme dɔɔwɛ la, 25bɛl maa gilɛɛ lau u hiŋ bargi u dɔŋa be, ka a bɔkpila maa nuu ra tɛɛ dɔŋa. 26Di bɔrahɔŋ yembɛl waa alaanfia dɔɔwɛ, amɔ, bɔra maanii waa alaanfia dɔɔwɛ la. Di ba wa chɔli yemmaa, a bɔrahɔŋ maanii ɔɔ sɔɔni.
27Too. Ii maanii ɛɛ Kristo bɔrahɔŋ la. Ii bɛl maa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ u yembɛl. 28Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ ii maanii huma la iin ninna hum, Yeesu hiŋra wia biini. Kɔraawiizi huŋhunna labuu ra tɔ see. Banla n na ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini labuu ra hiŋ u huŋhunna la ni. Kɔraawiizi wibagla ge ra hiŋ ba ge ni. Banla n wette ra ɛɛ wizenaa, ba ge ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi wibagla la ni ani banla n wette ra chaa wiila hina la, ba genii ra hiŋ bannii ni, di kaa kpa banla ge n wette ra hiini nɛra ani banla ge n ɛɛ sitɔɔra ani banla ge n wette ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi la. 29Ii maa lɛi Kɔraawiizi huŋhunna. Ii maa lɛi wette ra ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini. Ii maa lɛi kaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wibagla. Ii maa lɛi kaa wer ra ɛɛ wizenaa. 30Ii maa lɛi kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, ií wer ra chaa wiila hina. Ii maa lɛi wette ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi. Ii maa lɛi kaa wer ra bagli a mɔɔdumazi zɛɛzi. 31Ka ií aah siwii ra nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋazi la n wesse werge a biini.
Ama, ií gil n bagli ia hiŋaa la n wesse werge maa di wa bɛri la.

english_text:
Love
1What if I could speak
all languages of humans
and even of angels?
If I did not love others,
I would be nothing more
than a noisy gong
or a clanging cymbal.
2 What if I could prophesy
and understand all mysteries
and all knowledge?
And what if I had faith
that moved mountains?
I would be nothing,
unless I loved others.
3What if I gave away all
that I owned
and let myself
be burned alive?
I would gain nothing,
unless I loved others.
4Love is patient and kind,
never jealous, boastful,
proud, or 5rude.
Love isn't selfish
or quick tempered.
It doesn't keep a record
of wrongs that others do.
6Love rejoices in the truth,
but not in evil.
7Love is always supportive,
loyal, hopeful,
and trusting.
8Love never fails!
Everyone who prophesies
will stop,
and unknown languages
will no longer
be spoken.
All that we know
will be forgotten.
9We don't know everything,
and our prophecies
are not complete.
10But what is perfect
will someday appear,
and what isn't perfect
will then disappear.
11When we were children,
we thought and reasoned
as children do.
But when we grew up,
we quit our childish ways.
12Now all we can see of God
is like a cloudy picture
in a mirror.
Later we will see him
face to face.
We don't know everything,
but then we will,
just as God completely
understands us.
13For now there are faith,
hope, and love.
But of these three,
the greatest is love.
translation_text:
Nɔŋŋaa wia
1Di n wetto ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi ani mɛlikazi mɔɔri gba, ka maa nɛra nɔŋŋɛɛ, n na kɔɔu alugɔ baŋ ɔɔ ra lɔ lugbii ani bɛɛl, a ra kɔɔ nyɛgɛgɛ gunla. 2Di n wetto ra bagli Kɔraawiizi wia nɛnnɛ u fɔŋŋa biini, di dɔɔ sichaana werge maa, di zum Kɔraawiizi wisuahlaa maa, di kaa dɔɔ yarda u fɔŋŋa biini lugɔ min niŋ wer ŋɔ bizeŋ be lugɔ ú izi kaali yembɛl, u izi kaali, di n wetto di ɛɛ annii maa ka maa nɛra nɔŋŋɛɛ, maa nɛnanii maa ɛɛwɛ. 3Di n wetto kpa n kummaa tɛɛ nyaara bá di, di kaa wer sɛɛ bá kpa niŋ fuuh n maa, ń siu dikuu Kɔraawiizi wia, ka maa nɛra nɔŋŋɛɛ, pɛɛrɛ.
4Di i nɔŋŋi nɛra, i daŋ ɔɔ dɔɔ kanyitti i dɔŋahina ni, di ɔɔ ra suŋ ba ni, di ra ɛɛ baa winanaa. 5Ba wia wàá dɔɔi bɔwii. Hàá ra yir i hiŋ nɛzeŋ di dɔɔ barabara. Hàá aah siwii dikuu i bɛmbɛŋ wia, ka ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi ba maa wia. Hàá na baaŋ manamanaŋ di ra du nɛra ni. Hàá ra fɛ nfɛrchɔgaa nɛra ni. 6Wichɔgaa ɛɛi wàá ra sɔɔni i bɔra. Wibii wiarɛ ninna sɔɔni i bɔra. 7Di i nɔŋŋi nɛra, i daŋ pɛssi ba ni ani wiimaa bɔr, di dɔɔ ba yarda guŋ, di dɔɔ ba tamii ge guŋ, di kaa ra tɛɛ baa kanyitti ge guŋ.
8Nɔŋŋaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ. Wiŋɔzi du denii banna ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini. Ka a daŋ ŋmɛnɛ tuŋ. Mɔɔdumazi gba du denii banna mɔɔ u fɔŋŋa biini. A gba daŋ ŋmɛnɛ tuŋ. Sichaana du denii baŋ dɔɔwɛ u fɔŋŋa biini. Ka annii gba daŋ ŋmɛnɛ tuŋ, 9dikuubɛɛwiai, sichaana la yaa n dɔɔwɛ ani wiŋɔzi la yaa n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini la, a bɔzeŋ haa du harbɔɔ. 10Di a bɔzeŋ la wa ballɔ, annii daŋ tuŋ.
11Miŋ faa ɛɛ bichala, n faa ra ŋɔ bichal wiŋɔzii, di ra ɛɛ bichal wia, di ra fɛ bichal nfɛrɛ. Ka miŋ wa hel baal tuŋ, n gil a bichal wia ha. 12A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ yaa n na binni digii biini, ka waa na nɛnnɛ filaŋkeŋ. Ka di saŋa bɛl wa hello, yaa daŋ na wiimaa nɛnnɛ siwii ni. Zumaa la maa yaa n zummɛ filaŋkennaa, ka a bɔzeŋ haa du harbɔɔ. Ka di a saŋa wa hello, n daŋ jaa zum wiimaa gunla Kɔraawiizi n zumiŋ la.
13Awia, wia ahorobuu du de di ɛɛ wizenaa. Aabuu keŋ, yarda, tamii ani nɔŋŋaa. Ka nɔŋŋaa labuu ɛɛ wizeŋ kaali a maa.

english_text:
Speaking Unknown Languages and Prophesying
1Love should be your guide. Be eager to have the gifts that come from the Holy Spirit, especially the gift of prophecy. 2If you speak languages that others don't know, God will understand what you are saying, though no one else will know what you mean. You will be talking about mysteries that only the Spirit understands. 3But when you prophesy, you will be understood, and others will be helped. They will be encouraged and made to feel better.
4By speaking languages that others don't know, you help only yourself. But by prophesying you help everyone in the church. 5I am glad for you to speak unknown languages, although I prefer that you would prophesy. In fact, prophesying does much more good than speaking unknown languages, unless someone can help the church by explaining what you mean.
6My friends, what good would it do, if I came and spoke unknown languages to you and didn't explain what I meant? How would I help you, unless I told you what God had shown me or gave you some knowledge or prophecy or teaching? 7If all musical instruments sounded alike, how would you know the difference between a flute and a harp? 8If a bugle call isn't clear, how would you know to get ready for battle?
9This is how it is when you speak unknown languages. If no one can understand what you are talking about, you will only be talking to the wind. 10There are many different languages in this world, and all of them make sense. 11But if I don't understand the language that someone is using, we will be like foreigners to each other. 12If you really want spiritual gifts, choose the ones that will be most helpful to the church.
13When we speak languages that others don't know, we should pray for the power to explain what we mean. 14For example, if I use an unknown language in my prayers, my spirit prays but my mind is useless. 15Then what should I do? There are times when I should pray with my spirit, and times when I should pray with my mind. Sometimes I should sing with my spirit, and at other times I should sing with my mind.
16Suppose some strangers are in your worship service, when you are praising God with your spirit. If they don't understand you, how will they know to say, “Amen”? 17You may be worshiping God in a wonderful way, but no one else will be helped. 18I thank God that I speak unknown languages more than any of you. 19But words that make sense can help the church. This is why in church I would rather speak five words that make sense than to speak 10,000 words in a language that others don't know.
20My friends, stop thinking like children. Think like mature people and be as innocent as tiny babies. 21 In the Scriptures the Lord says,
“I will use strangers
who speak unknown languages
to talk to my people.
They will speak to them
in foreign languages,
but still my people
won't listen to me.”
22Languages others don't know may mean something to unbelievers, but not to the Lord's followers. Prophecy, on the other hand, is for followers, not for unbelievers. 23Suppose everyone in your worship service started speaking unknown languages, and some outsiders or some unbelievers come in. Won't they think you are crazy? 24But suppose all of you are prophesying when those unbelievers and outsiders come in. They will realize that they are sinners, and they will want to change their ways because of what you are saying. 25They will tell what is hidden in their hearts. Then they will kneel down and say to God, “We are certain that you are with these people.”
Worship Must Be Orderly
26My friends, when you meet to worship, you must do everything for the good of everyone there. That's how it should be when someone sings or teaches or tells what God has said or speaks an unknown language or explains what the language means. 27No more than two or three of you should speak unknown languages during the meeting. You must take turns, and someone should always be there to explain what you mean. 28If no one can explain, you must keep silent in church and speak only to yourself and to God.
29Two or three persons may prophesy, and everyone else must listen carefully. 30If someone sitting there receives a message from God, the speaker must stop and let the other person speak. 31Let only one person speak at a time, then all of you will learn something and be encouraged. 32A prophet should be willing to stop and let someone else speak. 33God wants everything to be done peacefully and in order.
When God's people meet in church, 34the women must not be allowed to speak. They must keep quiet and listen, as the Law of Moses teaches. 35If there is something they want to know, they can ask their husbands when they get home. It is disgraceful for women to speak in church.
36God's message did not start with you people, and you are not the only ones it has reached.
37If you think of yourself as a prophet or a spiritual person, you will know I am writing only what the Lord has commanded. 38So don't pay attention to anyone who ignores what I am writing. 39My friends, be eager to prophesy and don't stop anyone from speaking languages that others don't know. 40But do everything properly and in order.
translation_text:
Sunzaazi aŋhina n kaa lii Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii be wia
1Awia, ií aah siwii dikuu nɛnɔŋŋaa dɔɔi wia di kaa ra nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋazi la. Ka unla iin ninna nyiŋŋi werge, waabuu lugɔ iin niŋ wer ra ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini, 2dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr la n na mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi la, newea lɛi u mɔɔ ra tɛɛ. Kɔraawiizii u mɔɔ ra tɛɛ. Wisuahlaarɛ u ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini, ka nɛra waa nuu. 3Ka nɛr la n na ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini, neweare u ŋɔ ra tɛɛ, di ra hiini baa, bá wer zum Kɔraawiizi wia di ra du baa bɔkpega, di ra tig ba bampiree. 4Nɛr la n na mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi la, u himmaanii u ra hiini Kɔraawiizi wia biini. Ka nɛr la n na ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini, Yeesu hiŋra maanii u ra hiini bá wer zum Kɔraawiizi wia la. 5Di ii maa wetto ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi, n na nyiŋŋi guŋ. Ka di ii maa wetto ra ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini, gunnɛ n na nyiŋŋi werge, dikuubɛɛwiai, di nɛr ra ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini, a guŋ wesso kaali nɛr n na mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi di waa a zɛɛ baglɛɛ á hiini Yeesu hiŋra Kɔraawiizi wia biini.
6Yaabalaa, di n ba ii be di waa mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi, ɛrɛɛ ń wer hiini iai? Di Kɔraawiizi wam baglɛɛ wii bɛl ń kpa bagli ia gɛɛ di wan tɛɛwɛ sichaana, gɛɛ di maa wiŋɔzi dɔɔwɛ ń ŋɔ tɛɛ ia u Duma fɔŋŋa biini gɛɛ maa u baglaa bɛl dɔɔwɛ ń bagli ia, ɛrɛɛ ń wer hiini iai? 7Kuna la n waa nyiŋ gba ra bagli wia naabuu. Di ba ra huuh tiitorii gɛɛ ba ra lɔ janjalaŋ, ka a waa lii nɛnnɛ, ɛrɛɛ nɛ́ra wer nuu gunla banna lɔuwɛi? 8Di ba ŋɔ bá huuh bɛŋkuna nɛ́ra nuu di ɛɛ sirya la laal, ka di ba wɔɔ ra huuh nɛnnɛ, ɛrɛɛ bá wer zum di ɛɛ siryai? 9Ii ge gba, di ii wiŋɔzi waa wette ra chaani, ɛrɛɛ bá ɛɛ nuuawɛi? A daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ ii ra kɔɔu ii bɛmbɛŋ. 10Durnya mɔɔrizi kpillɔɔ werge. A maa ɛɛ mɔɔnuulaarɛ baŋhina be. 11Ka di maa nɛbɛl mɔɔri ra nuu, n daŋ ɛɛu lugɔ bambuguu a hiŋ be, u ge ɛɛ lugɔ bambuguu n be.
12Awia, iiŋ aah siwii ra nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋazi naa, ií ra nyiŋŋi anla n niŋ wer gil ii wer ra hiini Yeesu hiŋra werge la.
13Awia, nɛr la n na mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi la, ú suŋŋi wiizi ú tɛu fɔŋŋa ú wer di ra bagli nɛra a zɛɛzi. 14Di n na jaami Kɔraawiizi ani mɔɔduma, n dumaa ra jaamuu ka n nfɛrɛwaa waa wiimaa zummɛ la. 15Too. Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛi? N danna jaami ni n duma di kaa ra jaami ni n nfɛrɛ ge. N danna yir yira ani n duma di kaa ra yir yira ni n nfɛrɛ ge. 16Di guŋ lɛi, di i ra jaami Kɔraawiizi ni i duma, nɛ́r la n waa nuu la wàá wer ŋɔ, “Ami,” dikuubɛɛwiai, waa gunla hinna jaami la ra nuu. 17I jaamɔɔrɛ nɛnnɛ, ka waabuu waa hiinaa maa nawɛɛ a biini.
18Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ jaannɛ uŋ gillɛ n ge gba ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi di mɔɔa kaali ii maa gba. 19Ka di n wa du Yeesu hiŋra be di ŋɔ witama n mɔɔri biini di wer hiini baa, gunnɛ bɔ min niŋ ŋɔ wikpila maa mɔɔdumazi biini.
20Yaabalaa, ii gilɛɛ dɔɔ bichal nfɛssi. Ií ra fɛ nfɛrɛ lugɔ nɛra la n dirmɛɛ ba nfɛssi biini. Di wichɔgaa ɛɛi waa biinii, amɔ, ií dɔɔ bichal nfɛssi. 21Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini, u ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“N daŋ gil banla n na mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi ŋɔ n wia
tɛɛ n nɛra naa,
ka ba daŋ haa vɛɛ.
Ba wàá nuu tɛŋ.”
Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.
22Too. Banla n waa Kɔraawiizi wia ra sɛɛ wiarɛ u gil nɛra ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi la bá zum u fɔŋŋa. Banla n sɛɛwɛ wia lɛi. Banla n sɛɛwɛ ge wiarɛ u gil nɛra wer ra ŋɔ u wia u fɔŋŋa biini. Banla n waa sɛɛwɛ wia lɛi. 23Awia, di Yeesu hiŋra maa wa chaali bɔkpaŋ di ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi, di nɛdumazi ni banla n waa Kɔraawiizi wia ra sɛɛ la wa zuuwɔ, ba wàá ŋɔ lugɔ ii ra chugluuwaa? 24Ka di ii maa ra ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini, di unla n waa Kɔraawiizi wia ra sɛɛ gɛɛ nɛduma bɛl wa zuuwɔ, u daŋ nuu di sɛɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ wichɔgɛɛrii. Ii maa wiŋɔzi la daŋ zuu u bampirii a tiruu, 25u biini wolo maa lii, u chol Kɔraawiizi naazi di suŋŋuu, di ra ŋɔ nɛra be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du ii benii, wibii maa.
Yeesu hiŋra jaamaa ŋmɛnizi hiŋaa wia
26Iiŋ ɔɔ chaali dɔŋa la, bɛɛ ii ɔɔ ra ɛɛ denei? Kɔraawiizi yittɛ bɛl ɔɔ yir, bɛl ge ba baglaa bɛl ni, bɛl ge ba wiŋɔzi ni un nuuwɛ Kɔraawiizi be, bɛl ge kpa mɔɔduma di ba wiŋɔzi ni, bɛl ge bagli a wiŋɔzi zɛɛ. Ií gil ii wiimaa ɛɛi la wer ra hiini dɔŋa ii wer zum Kɔraawiizi wia nɛnnɛ. 27Banla n niŋ mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi la, ií gil ba ɛɛ nɛra banɛɛ gɛɛ bahoro bɛŋ di gil ba ra ŋɔ ka ra tɛɛ dɔŋa, di ɔɔ gil bɛl bagli a zɛɛzi. 28Di nɛr waa hoo un niŋ wer bagli mɔɔdumazi la zɛɛzi, amɔ, nɛr la n faa ŋɔ ú ŋɔ wia mɔɔdumazi biini la ú siigi, Yeesu hiŋra la be ka ŋɔ ra tɛɛ u ni Kɔraawiizi bɛŋ u biini.
29Banla n niŋ ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini la, ií gil ba ɛɛ nɛra banɛɛ gɛɛ bahoro bɛŋ ka bá dɔŋahina so di ra nuu ba wiŋɔzi la di ra pessaa nɛnnɛ. 30Di unla maa sogo Kɔraawiizi wa bagluu wii bɛl, ií gil unla n na ŋɔ wia la siigi ka tɛu bɔr. 31Ií maa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia ka ra tɛɛ dɔŋa nɛ́ra maa wer na hiinaa ani bɔkpega a biini. 32Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii waa banla n na ŋɔ u wiŋɔzi la ra fir. Ba daŋ wer ra lau bahinaa. 33Kɔraawiizi waa basabasa ra ɛɛ. U du bɔɔiihrɛ. 34Ii daŋ na guŋ bɔr la maa Kɔraawiizi biinanaa n ɔɔ chaali la.
Di ii ɔɔ wa chaali, ií ɔɔ gil ii haana ra siigi bɔɔiih. A waa ŋmɛnɛɛ dɔɔwɛ banna ŋɔ wia de. Ií ŋɔ bá ra sɛɛ dɔɔra. Gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ gba ra bagli. 35Di haana ra nyiŋŋi ba pɛɛzi wia, bá ɔɔ la diini mɔɔ ka pɛɛzi ba janna. A waa wer haana n na ŋɔ wia de.
36Ii benii Kɔraawiizi wia faaria? Ii bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi bagli u wiaa? 37Di bɛl maa ra ŋɔ lugɔ u wettoo ra ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa biini gɛɛ u dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii labuu, ú zum lugɔ wia naa min sɛbɛɛ tɛɛ ia naa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi widauliirɛ. 38Ka nɛr la maa n waa nyiŋŋi u zum wia, ií giluu.
39Yaabalaa, ií aah siwii ra nyiŋŋi fɔŋŋa Kɔraawiizi be, ií wer ra ŋɔ u wia. Ka ii gilɛɛ ra teŋ banla n na mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi la ŋmɛnɛɛ. 40Ií ra ɛɛ wiimaa gunla n dɛkkɛ di gilɛɛ ra ɛɛa basabasa.

english_text:
Christ Was Raised to Life
1My friends, I want you to remember the message I preached and that you believed and trusted. 2You will be saved by this message, if you hold firmly to it. But if you don't, your faith was all for nothing.
3 I told you the most important part of the message exactly as it was told to me. This part is:
Christ died for our sins,
as the Scriptures say.
4 He was buried,
and three days later
he was raised to life,
as the Scriptures say.
5 Christ appeared to Peter,
then to the twelve.
6After this, he appeared
to more than five hundred
other followers.
Most of them are still alive,
but some have died.
7He also appeared to James,
then to all of the apostles.
8 Finally, he appeared to me, even though I am like someone who was born at the wrong time.
9 I am the least important of all the apostles. In fact, I caused so much trouble for God's church that I don't even deserve to be called an apostle. 10But God treated me with undeserved grace! He made me what I am, and his grace wasn't wasted. I worked much harder than any of the other apostles, although it was really God's grace at work and not me. 11But it doesn't matter if I preached or if they preached. All of you believed the message just the same.
God's People Will Be Raised to Life
12If we preach that Christ was raised from death, how can some of you say the dead will not be raised to life? 13If they won't be raised to life, Christ himself wasn't raised to life. 14And if Christ wasn't raised to life, our message is worthless, and so is your faith. 15If the dead won't be raised to life, we have told lies about God by saying he raised Christ to life, when he really did not.
16So if the dead won't be raised to life, Christ wasn't raised to life. 17Unless Christ was raised to life, your faith is useless, and you are still living in your sins. 18And those people who died after putting their faith in him are completely lost. 19If our hope in Christ is good only for this life, we are worse off than anyone else.
20But Christ has been raised to life! And he makes us certain that others will also be raised to life. 21Just as we will die because of Adam, we will be raised to life because of Christ. 22Adam brought death to all of us, and Christ will bring life to all of us. 23But we must each wait our turn. Christ was the first to be raised to life, and his people will be raised to life when he returns. 24Then after Christ has destroyed all powers and forces, the end will come, and he will give the kingdom to God the Father.
25 Christ will rule until he puts all his enemies under his power, 26and the last enemy he destroys will be death. 27 When the Scriptures say he will put everything under his power, they don't include God. It was God who put everything under the power of Christ. 28After everything is under the power of God's Son, he will put himself under the power of God, who put everything under his Son's power. Then God will mean everything to everyone.
29 If the dead are not going to be raised to life, what will people do who are being baptized for them? Why are they being baptized for those dead people? 30And why do we always risk our lives 31and face death every day? The pride that I have in you because of Christ Jesus our Lord is what makes me say this. 32 What do you think I gained by fighting wild animals in Ephesus? If the dead are not raised to life,
“Let's eat and drink.
Tomorrow we die.”
33Don't fool yourselves. Bad friends will destroy you. 34Be sensible and stop sinning. You should be embarrassed that some people still don't know about God.
What Our Bodies Will Be Like
35Some of you have asked, “How will the dead be raised to life? What kind of bodies will they have?” 36Don't be foolish. A seed must die before it can sprout from the ground. 37Wheat seeds and all other seeds look different from the sprouts that come up. 38This is because God gives everything the kind of body he wants it to have. 39People, animals, birds, and fish are each made of flesh, but none of them are alike. 40Everything in the heavens has a body, and so does everything on earth. But each one is very different from all the others. 41The sun isn't like the moon, the moon isn't like the stars, and each star is different.
42That's how it will be when our bodies are raised to life. These bodies will die, but the bodies that are raised will live forever. 43These ugly and weak bodies will become beautiful and strong. 44As surely as there are physical bodies, there are spiritual bodies. And our physical bodies will be changed into spiritual bodies.
45 The first man was named Adam, and the Scriptures tell us that he was a living person. But Jesus, who may be called the last Adam, is a life-giving spirit. 46We see that the one with a spiritual body did not come first. He came after the one who had a physical body. 47The first man was made from the dust of the earth, but the second man came from heaven. 48Everyone on earth has a body like the body of the one who was made from the dust of the earth. And everyone in heaven has a body like the body of the one who came from heaven. 49Just as we are like the one who was made out of earth, we will be like the one who came from heaven.
50My friends, I want you to know that our bodies of flesh and blood will decay. This means they cannot share in God's kingdom, which lasts forever. 51 I will explain a mystery to you. Not every one of us will die, but we will all be changed. 52It will happen suddenly, quicker than the blink of an eye. At the sound of the last trumpet the dead will be raised. We will all be changed, so we will never die again. 53Our dead and decaying bodies will be changed into bodies that won't die or decay. 54 The bodies we now have are weak and can die. But they will be changed into bodies that are eternal. Then the Scriptures will come true,
“Death has lost the battle!
55 Where is its victory?
Where is its sting?”
56Sin is what gives death its sting, and the Law is the power behind sin. 57But thank God for letting our Lord Jesus Christ give us the victory!
58My dear friends, stand firm and don't be shaken. Always keep busy working for the Lord. You know that everything you do for him is worthwhile.
translation_text:
Yeesu Kristo siu biini izaa wia
1Too. Yaabalaa, ií gil n kaa liizi ia amaniyesuma la miŋ faa lizɛɛ tɛɛ ia ii sɛɛ di haa ra hiŋ, a lɛɛ ia la. 2Di ii sɛɛ amaniyesuma la di yardaa wibii maa, di ra hiŋaa nɛnnɛ lugɔ ii wàá vɛɛ a hiŋaa maa, ka lawaa nɛnnɛ gunla miŋ faa bagli ia la, amɔ, aabuu lɛɛ ia la.
3N faa bagli iabuu wia la Kɔraawiizi n bagli n ge la. Wii la n tɔ see labuu keŋ. Yeesu Kristo siuwɔɔ dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wia gunla Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ n faa bagli u wia la. 4Ba huguubuu, ka Kɔraawiizi lalluu siu biini hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl gunla Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ n faa baglɛɛ la. 5Pittaa felee nau. U hiŋra fidibanɛɛ la ge nau jaa. 6Denii u harbɔɔ hiŋra kpila maa n chaalɛɛ, ba maa nau. Ba faa du nɛra kalfaanue ka ra sag. Ba galga maa haa du de filaŋkeŋ ka baŋhina ge siuzi. 7A saŋa Jems gba faa naubuu. Denii u huŋhunna la maa ge kaa nau. 8Ka n ge jaa wa ɛɛ tuna hiŋ di nau. Maa nɛnanii ɛɛwɛ lugɔ bannii ka ɛɛ lugɔ bie la maa hia n waa helle ka u luluu la.
9N ɛɛ u huŋhunna la maa tuna hinnɛ. Maa dɛg ban niŋ yiriŋ u huŋhunni gba dikuu gunla miŋ faa tɔɔri Yeesu hiŋra la wia. 10Ka Kɔraawiizi nɛsunaa ni u hiinaa du n be. Uŋ hiiniŋ wiarɛ n wer du kennaa min duwɛɛ naa la. Ka u nɛsunaa la uŋ suŋ n ni la, waa tawɛɛ. Akai. N izoore ra hum u huma werge di bir kaali ba maa gba. Ka n himmaa fɔŋŋa biini lɛi n na humaa. Kɔraawiizii ra hiiniŋ n wer ra humaa gunla. 11Awia, di yaabuu gɛɛ baabuu faa bagli ia, kenne yaa maa faa bagli ia ii sɛɛ la.
Lalaa siu biini izaa wia
12Too. Di yaa faa bagli Yeesu Kristo wia lugɔ Kɔraawiizi lalluubuu siu biini, bɛɛ wiarɛ ii baŋhina ra ŋɔ dí nɛra wàá izi siu biinei? 13Di nɛra wàá izi siu biini, amɔ, guŋwaa, Kristo waa siu biini izee. 14Di Kɔraawiizi waa Kristo lallɛɛ siu biini, amɔ, yaa baglaa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ, ii ge sɛɛi ɛɛ pɛɛ. 15Di gunnɛ, yaa ra dar iabuu, yaa n na di Kɔraawiizi daansɛɛ la, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa ɔɔ ra bagli iabuu lugɔ u lalli Kristoo siu biini. Ka di nɛra wàá izi siu biini, amɔ, karaa yaa kanni. Wɔɔ lallɛɛ. 16Di nɛra wàá izi siu biini, amɔ, Kɔraawiizi wɔɔ lallɛɛ siu biini. 17Di Kɔraawiizi wɔɔ lallɛɛ siu biini, ii sɛɛ u wiarɛ pɛɛ. Ii wichɔgaa haa du ii ninɛɛ. 18Banla ge n sɛɛ Kristo wia ka siuzi la tawɔɔrɛ. 19Di yaa miibɔɔ naa bɛŋ biinii yaa dɔɔ Kristo tamii, amɔ, yaa wia dɔɔ sinyɛnaa werge kaali nɛr maa wia.
20Ka guŋ lɛi. Kristo izi siu biinii. Waabuu felee izi lii banla n siuwɛ la biini ka bá ge haa izi. 21Nɛkpannɛ ba siu ni. Nɛkpaŋ genii kaa ba siu biini izaa ni. 22Yaa ni Andama la n ɛɛ kpaŋ wiarɛ yaa ra siuzi la. Gunnɛ yáa banla maa ge ni Kristo n ɛɛ kpaŋ la na miibɔɔ di izi siu biini. 23Ka yaa danna izuu ka ra tɛɛ dɔŋa. Kristoo izee mɔɔ, ka bánla n ɛɛ u hora la ge wa izi a hɔl la un niŋ kaa ba la.
24Denii durnya tunaa saŋa wa hel, Kristo jaa kpegli kossi ni nabɔnzi ni fɔŋŋadɔɔra maa di gil a maa sɛɛ u mɛɛ dɔɔra. 25Kristoo niŋ dɔɔ durnya fɔŋŋa mɔɔ guŋŋ u wa kpegli u dɔma la maa. 26U dɔma tuna hinnɛ siu. 27Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ u ra di kora u kuŋkuaraa maa ni. Ka uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u dɔɔ kummaa fɔŋŋaa naa, waa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi la n kpa kummaa kora maa tɛu la gba fɔŋŋaa. 28Di Kɔraawiizi Biibaal la wa lɛɛ kummaa fɔŋŋa tuŋ la, denii ú sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n kpa kummaa fɔŋŋa tɛu la ge dɔɔra, Kɔraawiizi bɛmbɛŋ jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa maa.
29Nɛra baŋhina ɔɔ lɛɛ lalaa bɔttɛ di gil ba sɔ baa Kɔraawiizi nii. Bɛɛ wiarɛ ba ra ɛɛ gunnɛi? Di lalaa wàá izi siu biini, bɛɛ wiarɛ bá ɛɛ guŋ tɛɛ baai? 30Bɛɛ wiarɛ yaa ge ɔɔ ra zuu siu biini saŋa maanɛi? 31Di karaa n na kanni, di maa ɔɔ zuu siu biini guŋ, amɔ, min lɛi ɔɔ ra jigsi dikuu gunla iinna hiŋ yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo wia la. Wibii maa, n himmaa ɔɔ zuu siu biinii hɔpizibii maa. 32Gunla nɛra n faa ɛɛŋ Ɛfɛsus la ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ n ni sechɔgaa n naawɛ. Di durnya wia bɛŋ wiarɛ n ni baa naa, bɛɛ tɔnaa n na a biinei? Di nɛra wàá izi siu biini, yaa daŋ ŋɔ,
“Ii gil ya ra di, di ra nyɔɔ siŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai,
di kɛrɛ yaa daŋ siuzi, yaa zummɔaa?”
33Ka ii gilɛɛ ra dar iihinaa. “Ii ni nɛchɔgaa kpawaa daŋ chɔgi ii dunanaa.” 34Awia, ií izi di kazi ii bɔra di ra ɛɛ winanaa ka gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi. Ii baŋhina haa waa Kɔraawiizi wia zummɛ nɛnnɛ. A guŋ waa ia ɛɛwɛ hiihzia?
Siu biini izaa bɔrahɔŋ wia
35Ka ii bɛl daŋ pɛɛzi, “Ɛrɛɛ lálaa wer izi siu biinei? Ɛrɛɛ duulaa bá bɔra duɛi?” 36Ii gɛnnɔɔ werge. Kumbii la maa iiŋ ɔɔ kpa duu ɔɔ liiu ka pɔɔh. 37Kunla maa iiŋ ɔɔ kpa duu, di miarɛ gɛɛ di kundee bɛllɛ, a himmaa lɛi ɔɔ lii. Aa birgi paŋhoorii di lii. 38Kɔraawiizii ra birgaa gunla am paruu la di gil a maa ra du a duula.
39Bɔrahɔna maa waa kpaŋ ɛɛwɛ. A maa ni a dizii. Newea hora du de di kur sela hora ni. Nyinni ge hora kur zumbizi hora ni. 40Chiŋ kuna du de, hɛri ge kuna du de, ka a wessi kurgi dɔŋa ni. 41Wiizi wessi kuttɔɔ baagu wessi ni. Chinchiŋwilaa ge chaani kaali dɔŋa.
42Gunnɛ nɛra siu biini izaa gba du. Bɔrahɔnnaa yaa n dɔɔwɛ naa, di yaa wa siuzɔɔ, waabuu daŋ chɔgi. Ka bɔrahɔŋ la yaa n niŋ wa izi siu biini di dɔɔ la, waabuu wàá chɔgi maa. 43Kumpɛɛrɛ ba ɔɔ hug, ka Kɔraawiizi lalluu u ɛɛ kunnanii. Kuŋgɛrgii ba ɔɔ hug, ka Kɔraawiizi lalluu u ɛɛ kuŋkpeg. 44Kunla baŋ hukke la, bɔrahɔŋ himmaanii. Ka kunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lalli la, waabuu duma kuŋ.
Bɔrahɔŋ himmaa du denii. Bɔrahɔŋ la ge n ɛɛ duma kuŋ la, u ge du de. 45Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi faa ta lugli nɛr la banna yir Andama labuu u dɔɔ miibɔɔ.” Ka harbɔɔ Andama la ɛɛ duma kunnɛ di ra tɛɛ nɛra miibɔɔni. Waabuu Kristo. 46Ií zum lugɔ bɔrahɔŋ la n ɛɛ duma kuŋ la lɛi yaa feli dɔɔ. Bɔrahɔŋ himmaanii yaa feli dɔɔ mɔɔ ka haa waa dɔɔ duma ge hor. 47Hɛrii lugli newee la lii di ɛɛ hɛri nɛr. Ka Kɔraawiizi benii nɛɛhiŋ la ge lii. 48Gunla unla n lii hɛri la n faa duwɛɛ la, gunnɛ u nɛra maa du. 49Gunla unla n lii Kɔraawiizi be la ge n duwɛɛ la, gunnɛ u ge nɛra maa du.
50Yaabalaa, ií gil n ŋɔ ii be, “Bɔrahɔnnaa dee wàá wer la Kɔraawiizi be. Kunla n dɔɔ pɔɔih wàá wer du bɔr la kuna la n waa pɔɔih dɔɔwɛ n duwɛɛ la.” 51Ií ra nuu ɛŋ. N daŋ pilli wisuahlii bɛl bagli ia. Yaa maa lɛi niŋ siuzi. Haali di yaa siuzɔɔ gɛɛ yaa waa siuzɛɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ birgi yaa maa bɔrahɔna kakpaŋ 52alugɔ siwee kamzaa saŋa la Kɔraawiizi bensuno n niŋ keezi wa wii la. Di u bensuno hiŋ wa wiiwo, Kɔraawiizi daŋ lalli lalaa bá dɔɔ bɔrahɔna la n waa pɔɔih dɔɔwɛ la di birgi yaa nyinee ge bɔrahɔna, 53dikuubɛɛwiai, a dɛkkɔ bɔrahɔŋ la n dɔɔ pɔɔih lii ka unla n waa pɔɔih dɔɔwɛ ge zuu, bɔrahɔŋ la n dɔɔ siwaa lii, ka unla n waa siwaa dɔɔwɛ ge zuu. 54Awia, di unla n dɔɔ pɔɔih wa liwɔɔ ka unla n waa pɔɔih dɔɔwɛ zuu, di unla ge n dɔɔ siwaa wa liwɔɔ, ka unla n waa siwaa dɔɔwɛ ge zuu, gunla baŋ sɛbɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini la daŋ wa ɛɛ, dí, “U kpa fɔŋŋaa kpegli siu.”
55“Siu, lee i fɔŋŋa kaa duɛi?
Ɛrɛɛ í kaa ɛɛ tɔɔri yaai?”
56Wichɔgaarɛ ɔɔ gil siu wer ra tɔɔri yaa. Gbɔg la ge ɔɔ gil wichɔgaa na fɔŋŋa yaa ni. 57Ka Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ jaannɛ werge un tɛɛ yaa fɔŋŋa di lii yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo be ya kpegli siu.
58Awia, yaabalaa la min nɔŋŋɛɛ werge, ií chi chigigi di ra hiŋ, di gilɛɛ wa gil kummaa waa bir ia har. Ií zum lugɔ wii la maa iin niŋ ɛɛ tɛu la wàá ta pɛɛ. Ií ɔɔ haa vɛɛ ra hum yaa Dɔɔri huma werge maa.

english_text:
A Collection for God's People
1 When you collect money for God's people, I want you to do exactly what I told the churches in Galatia to do. 2That is, each Sunday each of you must put aside part of what you have earned. If you do this, you won't have to take up a collection when I come. 3Choose some followers to take the money to Jerusalem. I will send them on with the money and with letters which show that you approve of them. 4If you think I should go along, they can go with me.
Paul's Travel Plans
5 After I have gone through Macedonia, I hope to see you 6and visit with you for a while. I may even stay all winter, so that you can help me on my way to wherever I will be going next. 7If the Lord lets me, I would rather come later for a longer visit than to stop off now for only a short visit. 8 I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost, 9because there is a wonderful opportunity for me to do some work here. But there are also many people who are against me.
10 When Timothy arrives, give him a friendly welcome. He is doing the Lord's work, just as I am. 11Don't let anyone mistreat him. I am looking for him to return to me together with the other followers. So when he leaves, send him off with your blessings.
12I have tried hard to get our friend Apollos to visit you with the other followers. He doesn't want to come just now, but he will come when he can.
Personal Concerns and Greetings
13Keep alert. Be firm in your faith. Stay brave and strong. 14Show love in everything you do.
15 You know that Stephanas and his family were the first in Achaia to have faith in the Lord. They have done all they can for God's people. My friends, I ask you 16to obey leaders like them and to do the same for all others who work hard with you.
17I was glad to see Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus. Having them here was like having you. 18They made me feel much better, just as they made you feel better. You should appreciate people like them.
19 Greetings from the churches in Asia.
Aquila and Priscilla, together with the church that meets in their house, send greetings in the name of the Lord.
20All the Lord's followers send their greetings.
Give each other a warm greeting.
21I am signing this letter myself: PAUL.
22I pray that God will put a curse on everyone who doesn't love the Lord. And may the Lord come soon.
23I pray the Lord Jesus will be kind to you.
24I love everyone who belongs to Christ Jesus.
translation_text:
Yeesu hiŋra kebee kɛɛi wia
1Too. A ka kebee la yaa n na kɛɛ ya tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi biinanaa la. Ií ra ɛɛ gunla miŋ faa ŋɔ Yeesu hiŋra la n du Galesia hɛri lugɔ bá ra ɛɛ la. 2Alaadi maa ií bɛl maa ɔɔ lizi gunla maa iin niŋ wer, di lii kuna la Kɔraawiizi n hiini ia ii dɔɔ la biini dau. Ií ra ɛɛ guŋ, di n wa ballɔ, ii wàá ka kɛɛ. 3Di n wa ballɔ, n daŋ sɛbi hɔna di kpa tɛɛ nɛra la iiŋ yardɛɛ, di hum baa bá kpa ii sunzaa la di la Jɛrusalɛm. 4Di a wa dɛkkɔ lugɔ ń du baa la, n daŋ la.
Pɔɔl jinazi wia
5N ŋɔ ń la Masɛdɔnia hɛrii, ka di n wa lii de ba, n daŋ ba ii be 6di wa du ii be di birgi tama. Aŋhinabe, n daŋ du ii be, waari saŋa wa tuŋ, ka ií jaa taŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ ń la bɔr la maa min niŋ la. 7Di n ŋɔ ń ba wa na ia filaŋkeŋ, màá wer birgi ii be. Ka di n wa wetto ba saŋa bɛl, di Kɔraawiizi sɛɛwɔ, n daŋ birgi ii be. 8Ka n daŋ haa du Ɛfɛsus mɔɔ ka Pɛntikɔs Hɔpizizeŋ la wa hel, 9dikuubɛɛwiai, n na bɔttɛ ɛŋ ń wer hum Kɔraawiizi huma werge á lii tɔna di tɛu. Ka banla n na nyiŋŋi bá tɔ n huma ŋmɛnɛɛ la su denii werge.
10Di Timoti wa ba ii be, ií sɛɛ u wia nɛnnɛ ú gilɛɛ waa ɔm, dikuubɛɛwiai, u gba ra hum Kɔraawiizi humaa lugɔ miŋ ge n na humaa kennaa. 11Awia, ii gilɛɛ waa binnuu pɛɛ, ka ií wa hiinuu ú wer kpa u ŋmɛnɛɛ ani bampirsɔna di bir ba n be. N na binni u ni yaabalaa ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ.
12Ka yaa dɔŋhiŋ Apɔlɔs waa, n fɔrguubuu ú du yaabalaa la di ba ii be, ka de laŋaa wɔɔ pattɛ filaŋkeŋ. Di u wa na ŋmɛnɛɛ, u daŋ la.
13Too. Ií ɔɔ ra du iihinaa tau nɛnnɛ, di haa lau chigigi, di ra hiŋ. Ií ɔɔ haa dɔɔ bampirii nɛnnɛ di gil ii hiŋaa la dɔɔ fɔŋŋa. 14Ií ra ɛɛ wiimaa ni nɛnɔŋŋaa.
15Yaabalaa, ii zummɔ lugɔ Stɛfanas ni u diahinaa felee sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wia Akaaya di ɔɔ aah siwii di hum ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi biinanaa. 16Awia, n na suŋŋi ia, ií ra sɛɛ ba ni banla maa n na hiini baa di ra hum la dɔɔra. 17Stɛfanas ni Fɔtunatus ni Akayikus balaa sɔɔni n bɔraa werge, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii himmaa waa wette ba ń na ia, ka ba lɛɛ ii balaa ba, 18di wa duŋ bɔkpega werge, di du ii ge gba bɔkpega. Ií ra tɔgzi nɛra naa dɔŋa.
19Yeesu hiŋra la n du Eesia hɛri la ra jaami ia werge. Akuila ni Pirsila ani Yeesu hiŋra la n ɔɔ chaali ba dia la gba ra jaami ia werge ani yaa Dɔɔri sɔŋ. 20Yaabalaa maa ra jaami ia. Ií jaami dɔŋa nɛnnɛ.
21Mìŋ́ Pɔɔl ge sɛbaarɛ keŋ n himmaa n sɛbɛɛ di ra jaami ia.
22Nɛr la n waa yaa Dɔɔri nɔŋŋɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi seeubuu nua. Yaa Dɔɔri ra bau.
23Yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo, u nɛsunaa ani u hiinaa du ii be. 24Ii banla maa ni Yeesu Kristo n kpauwɛ la, n na jaami ia ni nɔŋŋaa. Ami.

english_text:
1 From Paul, chosen by God to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, and from Timothy, who is also a follower.
To God's church in Corinth and to all of God's people in Achaia.
2I pray that God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
Paul Gives Thanks
3Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! The Father is a merciful God, who always gives us comfort. 4He comforts us when we are in trouble, so that we can share this same comfort with others in trouble. 5We share in the terrible sufferings of Christ, but also in the wonderful comfort he gives. 6We suffer in the hope that you will be comforted and saved. And because we are comforted, you will also be comforted, as you patiently endure suffering like ours. 7You never disappoint us. You suffered as much as we did, and we know that you will be comforted as we were.
8 My friends, I want you to know what a hard time we had in Asia. Our sufferings were so horrible and so unbearable that death seemed certain. 9In fact, we felt sure we were going to die. But this made us stop trusting in ourselves and start trusting God, who raises the dead to life. 10God saved us from the threat of death, and we are sure that he will do it again and again. 11Please help us by praying for us. Then many people will give thanks for the blessings we receive in answer to all these prayers.
Paul's Change of Plans
12We can be proud of our clear conscience. We have always lived honestly and sincerely, especially when we were with you. And we were guided by God's gift of undeserved grace instead of by the wisdom of this world. 13I am not writing anything you cannot read and understand. I hope you will understand it completely, 14just as you already partly understand us. Then when our Lord Jesus returns, you can be as proud of us as we are of you.
15I was so sure of your pride in us that I had planned to visit you first of all. In this way you would have the blessing of two visits from me— 16 once on my way to Macedonia and again on my return from there. Then you could send me on to Judea. 17Do you think I couldn't make up my mind about what to do? Or do I seem like someone who says “Yes” or “No” simply to please others? 18God can be trusted, and so can I, when I say our answer to you has always been “Yes” and never “No.” 19 This is because Jesus Christ the Son of God is always “Yes” and never “No.” And he is the one Silas, Timothy, and I told you about.
20Christ says “Yes” to all God's promises. This is why we have Christ to say “Amen” for us to the glory of God. 21And so God makes it possible for you and us to stand firmly together with Christ. God is also the one who chose us 22and put his Spirit in our hearts to show that we belong only to him.
23God is my witness that I stayed away from Corinth, just to keep from being hard on you. 24We are not bosses who tell you what to believe. We are working with you to make you glad, because your faith is strong.
translation_text:
1Mìŋ́ Yeesu Kristo huŋhunni Pɔɔllɛ ra sɛbi hɔnnaa ń tɛɛ ia. A par Kɔraawiizii u tɛŋ a huma.
N ni yaa dɔŋhiŋ Timotii ra jaami ii banla n ɛɛ Yeesu hiŋra du Kɔrint ani Kɔraawiizi biinanaa la maa n du Akaaya la.
2Yáa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo hiini ia di tɛɛ ia bampirsɔna.
Pɔɔl n tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ wia
3Ií ra tɛɛ yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la sɔŋ. U ɛɛ mɛɛ la n na na nɛra sinyɛnaa werge maa di kaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n na tig nɛra bampiree werge. 4Waabuu ra tig yaa bampiree. Saŋa maa, di tɔɔrɔɔ haŋ wa huuzi yaa, ɔɔ ra tig yaa bampiree ka yáa ge wer tig yaa dɔŋahina la n na di tɔɔrɔɔ maa bampiree, gunla un tig yaa ge bampiree la. 5Yaa n na di tɔɔrɔɔ werge lugɔ Kristo n faa diwee la, gunnɛ yaa kaa ra na bampirsɔna werge dikuu u wia. 6Di yaa ra di tɔɔrɔɔ, ii hiinaa wiarɛ yaa ra dia, yá wer tig ii bampiree di lɛɛ ia. Di Kɔraawiizi kaa wa tig yaa bampiree la, ii hiinaa wiarɛ u kaa tig yaa bampiree, ka ya wer hiini ia ií wer dɔɔ kanyitti saŋa la iin niŋ waa di yaa tɔɔrɔɔ la dɔŋ. 7Yaa dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi tamiirɛ werge maa dikuu ii wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa zummɔ lugɔ di yaa ra di tɔɔrɔɔ, yaa ni ii maanii niŋ na bampirsɔna la.
8Yaabalaa, yaa ra nyiŋŋuu ii zum tɔɔrɔɔ la yaa n faa diwee Eesia hɛri la wia. A tɔɔrɔɔ faa siili yaa ninɛɛ werge maa, di lɔ yaa dau. Yaa faa waa tamii ɛɛwɛ lugɔ yaa daŋ lii u biini ani miibɔɔ. 9Yaa faa zumɔɔ lugɔ yaa daŋ faa siu de gba. Ka guŋ ɛɛwɔɔ ya gilɛɛ dɔɔ yaa hinaa tamii, ka dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi la n wette lalli nɛra siu biini la tamii. 10U faa lɛɛ yaabuu siuchɔgii biini, di haa ra lɛɛ yaa. Yaa dɔɔ u tamiirɛ lugɔ u daŋ haa lɛɛ yaa gba. 11A dɛkkɔ ii gba n niŋ hiini yaa di ra suŋŋi wiizi, di Kɔraawiizi wa nuuwɔ, nɛ́kpila wer tɛu jaam dikuu ba suŋŋaa la ba maa n suŋŋɛɛ tɛɛ yaa u nuu di hiini yaa la wia.
Pɔɔl n bir u jinazi wia
12Wii la yaa n niŋ kpa chɔli yaa hinaarɛ keŋ. Yaa zummɔ yaa biine lugɔ yaa wiɛɛlaa maa wessoo wa tuŋ. Yaa ɛɛabuu biinihuŋŋu la Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ yaa la ni. Newea nunzuma lɛi yaa kpa ɛɛa. Kɔraawiizi hiinaa biinii yaa ɛɛ a wia maa durnya maa ani ii be. 13Yaa n sɛbi hɔna ra tɛɛ ia naa, wiimaa waa hoo a biini iiŋ waa wette ii karmi zum a zɛɛ maa nɛnnɛ di wa tuŋ. 14Ii faa zum yaabuu tama. N kaa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ ii wer zum yaa nɛnnɛ, di zum lugɔ yaa danna jigsi dikuu ii wia, ii ge ra jigsi dikuu yaa wia, yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo Hɔpizii la hɔl.
15Miŋ faa dɔɔ ii tamii gunla wiarɛ saŋa la miŋ faa ra la Masɛdɔnia hɛri la n faa ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ n feli ba ii be mɔɔ ií wer na hiinaa bunɛɛ la. 16N faa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ n ga ii be ra la. Denii di n kaa waa nyiŋŋi lugɔ ń bir ba, ń kaa ga ii be di wer du ii be ka ií kaa taŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ ń la Juda hɛri. 17Too. Miŋ faa ra fɛ u guŋ nfɛrɛ la, maa guŋ kpawɛɛ fugzi. Newea daŋ wer ŋɔ nua ka vɛɛ guŋ, ka miŋwaa waa guŋ duwɛɛ.
18Kɔraawiizi la wia n dɔɔ wibii la di yaa daansɛɛrɛ lugɔ yaa wiŋɔzi waa guŋ ɛɛwɛ. Yaa waa ɔɔ ra sɛɛ wia ani nua ka ra vɛɛa. 19Kɔraawiizi Biibaal Yeesu Kristo la n ni Timoti ni Silvanus n bagli u wia tɛɛ ia la dɔɔ wibiire. Waa dɔɔwɛ lugɔ ŋmɛnɛbɛl ú ŋɔ “ɛɛh,” ŋmɛnɛbɛl ú kaa ŋɔ, “Akai.” Di waabuu haŋ ŋɔ wii, u ŋɔwɔɔrɛ. 20Nuuzi la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ yaa la, Yeesu Kristo ninɛɛ yaa chi zum lugɔ a ɛɛ wibiire. U wiarɛ ya wer ŋɔ, “Ami!” Kɔraawiizi wer na sɔŋ. 21Kɔraawiizii gillɛ yaa ni ii maa wer lau Yeesu Kristo nɛnnɛ di ra hiŋ di kpa u Dumnanii du yaa ni, 22u ra bagli lugɔ yaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi horaa, di kaa ra bagli lugɔ u daŋ ŋmɛnɛ lɛɛ yaa di wa tuŋ.
23N na yir Kɔraawiizi la n zum n biini maa la sɔnnɛ ú ɛɛ n daansɛɛ hiŋ ani wiŋɔzi naa biini. Miŋ faa waa Kɔrint ballɛ la, ii tɔɔraarɛ n faa waa nyiŋŋi wiarɛ maa ballɛ. 24A waa lugɔ yaa ra nyiŋŋuu ya bagli fɔŋŋa ii ni ii hiŋaa naa biini. Guŋ lɛi. Ii himmaa lauwɔɔ di ra hiŋ nɛnnɛ. Ka yaa ra nyiŋŋi ya wer hiini ia ií wer dɔɔ bɔsɔna.

english_text:
1I have decided not to make my next visit with you so painful. 2If I make you feel bad, who would be left to cheer me up, except the people I had made to feel bad? 3The reason I want to be happy is to make you happy. I wrote as I did because I didn't want to visit you and be made to feel bad, when you should make me feel happy. 4At the time I wrote, I was suffering terribly. My eyes were full of tears, and my heart was broken. But I didn't want to make you feel bad. I only wanted to let you know how much I cared for you.
Forgiveness
5I don't want to be hard on you. But if one of you has made someone feel bad, I am not really the one who has been made to feel bad. Some of you are the ones. 6Most of you have already pointed out the wrong that person did, and this is punishment enough for what was done.
7When people sin, you should forgive and comfort them, so they won't give up in despair. 8You should make them sure of your love for them.
9I also wrote because I wanted to test you and find out if you would follow my instructions. 10I will forgive anyone you forgive. Yes, for your sake and with Christ as my witness, I have forgiven whatever needed to be forgiven. 11I have done this to keep Satan from getting the better of us. We all know what goes on in his mind.
12 When I went to Troas to preach the good news about Christ, I found that the Lord had already prepared the way. 13But I was worried when I didn't find my friend Titus there. So I left the other followers and went on to Macedonia.
14I am grateful that God always makes it possible for Christ to lead us to victory. God also helps us spread the knowledge about Christ everywhere, and this knowledge is like the smell of perfume. 15-16In fact, God thinks of us as a perfume that brings Christ to everyone. For people who are being saved, this perfume has a sweet smell and leads them to a better life. But for people who are lost, it has a bad smell and leads them to a horrible death.
No one really has what it takes to do this work. 17A lot of people try to get rich from preaching God's message. But we are God's sincere messengers, and by the power of Christ we speak our message with God as our witness.
translation_text:
1Miŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi ii be balaa la, n bir ŋɔ a waa wer min niŋ ba ii be ani biinichɔg di wa chɔg ii biine. 2Di n wa chɔg ii biine, anɛɛwaarɛ du de ban niŋ gil mimbuu bɔra sɔɔni, di ii banla min chɔg ii biine la lɛiyɛi? 3Gunnɛ n faa sɛbi hɔŋ la biini di ŋɔ lugɔ n faa waa nyiŋŋi n ba wa chɔg ii banla n niŋ faa sɔɔni n bɔra la biine. N dɔɔ ii maa tamiirɛ lugɔ n bɔsɔna ɛɛ ii maa bɔsɔnaa. 4Awia, hɔŋ la miŋ faa sɛbɛɛ tɛɛ ia la wia tɔɔrimbuu werge, di tiriŋ werge maa, n na wii gba ka faa ra sɛbuu. N faa waa a hɔŋ sɛbɛɛ ií biine chɔgi. Ka n sɛbuubuu ií faa wer zum gunla min nɔŋŋi ia werge la.
Giltɛɛi tɛɛ wichɔgɛɛri wia
5Nɛr la n ba biinichɔg la ni la, n bɛŋ biini lɛi u chɔgi. Ii maa biinee u chɔgi. Maa nyiŋŋi n tɔɔruu werge.
