You belong to God, and he won't forget the love you have shown his people. 11We wish each of you would always be eager to show how strong and lasting your hope really is. 12Then you would never be lazy. You would be following the example of those who had faith and were patient until God kept his promise to them.
God's Promise Is Sure
13No one is greater than God. So he made a promise in his own name when he said to Abraham, 14 “I, the Lord, will bless you with many descendants!” 15Then after Abraham had been very patient, he was given what God had promised. 16When anyone wants to settle an argument, they make a vow by using the name of someone or something greater than themselves. 17So when God wanted to prove for certain his promise to his people could not be broken, he made a vow. 18God cannot tell lies! And so his promises and vows are two things that can never be changed.
We have run to God for safety. Now his promises should greatly encourage us to take hold of the hope that is right in front of us. 19 This hope is like a firm and steady anchor for our souls. In fact, hope reaches behind the curtain and into the most holy place. 20 Jesus has gone there ahead of us, and he is our high priest forever, just like Melchizedek.
translation_text:
1Awia, yaa n zum Kristo lugli wia la, ya jaa ra la see, di wer ɛɛ nabɔnzi. Ya gilɛɛ kaa faari ra ŋɔ gunla yaa n niŋ gil yaa biine chɔgi, dikuu wipɛɛri la yaa n na ɛɛ la wia ani gunla yaa n niŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi, 2gunla ban niŋ sɔ nɛra Kɔraawiizi nii, gunla ban niŋ kpa nonee sag nɛra ni, gunla lalaa n niŋ izi ani gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ turgi nɛra ba wichɔgaa kim di hanna la saŋa maa la wia. 3Di Kɔraawiizi sɛɛwɔ, yaa daŋ jaa gil wia naa baglaa ka ra la see.
4Kɔraawiizi chaani nɛra siweere ba zum u wia, di na u sunzaa la ni u Dumnanii la, 5di nuu u wiŋɔɔlii, di wer zum gunla uŋ wesse werge, di kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋazi ban niŋ wa dɔɔ saŋa la n du yaa dui naa harbɔɔ, 6di ba zum annii naa maa, ka kaa bir har, ɛrɛɛ bá kaa ɛɛ bá biine kaa chɔgi, bá kaa bir ba naanɛi? Ba wàá wer bir ba Kɔraawiizi be. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ba kaa kpu Kɔraawiizi Biibaallɛ daakaŋlii la ni gunla, di gil u kaa di hiihzi nɛra baaŋ.
7Di hɛri yembɛl du de dooŋ n ɔɔ ra ba, u ra nyɔɔ a nii di ra lii diunanaa di ra tɛɛ banla n na paruu la, u dɔɔ wikuariirɛ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u ɛɛ hɛrnanii. 8Ama, di u ra lii sɔɔhri ni choŋgolli, waa wikuarii maa dɔɔwɛ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ seeu nua. Ba daŋ duu niŋ.
9Ka iawaa, yaa n na ŋɔ wia kennaa, a waa lugɔ yaa ra aani iabuu, n nɛnɔŋŋaa. Yaa dɔɔ ii tamiirɛ lugɔ ii wiɛɛlaa daŋ bɔ, ií wer na lɛɛi. 10Kɔraawiizi wia maa deŋloore. Wàá suuh gunla iiŋ humuu ani gunla iim bagli nɔŋŋaa la iin nɔŋŋuu, di hiini u biinanaa la, di haa ra hiini baa la. 11Yaa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ ii bɛl maa ɔɔ haa aah siwii guŋ di ra la a tuna, ií wer na wia la ni iinna tami la. 12Ií ra dazi, ii gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ bɔhuaih, ka ɔɔ ra hiŋ gunla banla n faa yardi Kɔraawiizi, nɛra ɛɛ baa wiimaa ka ba waa vɛɛwɛ, ka hiŋ di wa na wia la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ baa lugɔ ba daŋ na la.
Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlii ɛɛ wibiire
13Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ nua bɛllɛ tɛɛ Abraham. Uŋ faa ŋɔ nua la, kummaa n waa hoo ɛɛ kunzeŋ kaaluu la wia, u hɛɛhzi u hiŋ, 14di ŋɔ, “N daŋ kissii werge maa di tɛi naanna kpila.” 15Abraham n wette di haa vɛɛ di di kanyitti guŋŋ, u wa na gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua labuu. 16Di newea ra nyiŋŋi ba ŋɔ nua, a ba hɛɛhzi kunla n kaali baabuu. Di ba hɛɛhzɔɔ guŋ, wiŋɔzi maa waa kaa hoo. Ba nua la daŋ chi. 17Awia, Kɔraawiizi n faa ra nyiŋŋi u bagli banla n niŋ na u nuuŋɔɔlii la biini, gunla u nua un niŋ ŋɔ n niŋ waa chi bá zum lugɔ waa biraa dɔɔwɛ la, u jaa hɛɛhzi u himmaa. 18Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua di kaa hɛɛhzi u hiŋ jaa la, a wia anɛɛ hiŋ waa biraa dɔɔwɛ, dikuu uŋ waa kara ra kanni wia. U ŋɔ a maanii ka yáa banla n chɔwɛɛ di ga du u be la wer dɔɔ bɔkpega, dikuu tamii la yaa n dɔɔwɛ u wiŋɔzi la ni wia. 19A tamii daŋ wer gil ya chi nɛnnɛ. A tamii wiarɛ yaa wer zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la patiisazenzeŋ n faa teŋŋe la. 20Yeesu n birgi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma di hanna la alugɔ Mɛlkizɛdɛk la, u teŋ tɔ yaa seere zuu de dikuu yaa wia.

english_text:
The Priestly Family of Melchizedek
1 Melchizedek was both king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He was the one who went out and gave Abraham his blessing, when Abraham returned from killing the kings. 2Then Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he had.
The meaning of the name Melchizedek is “King of Justice.” But since Salem means “peace,” he is also “King of Peace.” 3We are not told he had a father or mother or ancestors or beginning or end. He is like the Son of God and will be a priest forever.
4Notice how great Melchizedek was! Our famous ancestor Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had taken from his enemies. 5 The Law teaches that even Abraham's descendants must give a tenth of what they possess. And they are to give this to their own relatives, who are the descendants of Levi and are priests. 6Although Melchizedek wasn't a descendant of Levi, Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had. Then Melchizedek blessed Abraham, who had been given God's promise. 7Everyone agrees a person who gives a blessing is greater than the one who receives the blessing.
8Priests are given a tenth of what people earn. But all priests die, except Melchizedek, and the Scriptures teach that he is alive. 9Levi's descendants are now the ones who receive a tenth from people. We could even say that when Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth, Levi also gave him a tenth. 10This is because Levi was born later into the family of Abraham, who gave a tenth to Melchizedek.
11Even though the Law of Moses says the priests must be descendants of Levi, those priests cannot make anyone perfect. So there needs to be a priest like Melchizedek, rather than one from the priestly family of Aaron. 12And when the rules for selecting a priest are changed, the Law must also be changed.
13The person we are talking about is our Lord, who came from a tribe that had never had anyone to serve as a priest at the altar. 14Everyone knows he came from the tribe of Judah, and Moses never said priests would come from that tribe.
15All of this becomes clearer, when someone who is like Melchizedek is appointed to be a priest. 16That person wasn't appointed because of his ancestors, but because his life can never end. 17 The Scriptures say about him,
“You are a priest forever,
just like Melchizedek.”
18In this way a weak and useless command was put aside, 19because the Law cannot make anything perfect. At the same time, we are given a much better hope, and it can bring us close to God.
20-21 God himself made a promise when this priest was appointed. But he did not make a promise like this when the other priests were appointed. The promise he made is,
“I, the Lord, promise that you
will be a priest forever!
And I will never
change my mind!”
22This means that Jesus guarantees us a better agreement with God. 23There have been a lot of other priests, and all of them have died. 24But Jesus will never die, and so he will be a priest forever! 25He is forever able to save the people he leads to God, because he always lives to speak to God for them.
26Jesus is the high priest we need. He is holy and innocent and faultless, and not at all like us sinners. Jesus is honored above all beings in heaven, 27 and he is better than any other high priest. Jesus doesn't need to offer sacrifices each day for his own sins and then for the sins of the people. He offered a sacrifice once for all, when he gave himself. 28The Law appoints priests who have weaknesses. But God's promise, which came later than the Law, appoints his Son. And he is the perfect high priest forever.
translation_text:
Kizeehiŋ Mɛlkizɛdɛk wia
1Mɛlkizɛdɛk la faa ɛɛ Salɛm hina koorii, di kaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la kizeehiŋ. Abraham faa la laallɛ ga kpu koora la ka bir ra ba di faa wa chem a Mɛlkizɛdɛk ni, a Mɛlkizɛdɛk suŋŋi wiizi tɛu, ú hiinuu. 2Abraham ge bargi kuna la maa uŋ faa foozee laal la biini la bɔra fi, di kpa a bɔkpaŋ tɛu. Mɛlkizɛdɛk la sɔŋ zɛɛrɛ, “Wideŋlaa Koori.” Uŋ kaa ɛɛ Salɛm koori la, Salɛm ge zɛɛ ɛɛ bampirsɔna la, u sɔŋ kaa di “Bampirsɔna Koori.” 3U faa waa mɛɛ ni maa dɔɔwɛ yaa zum. U faa waa nɛra dɔɔwɛ. Waa lulaa saŋa dɔɔwɛ yaa zum. Waa siu saŋa gba dɔɔwɛ, ka du de ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ di hanna la alugɔ Kɔraawiizi Biibaal la. 4Ií na gunla uŋ faa ɛɛ nɛzeŋ werge, yaa naabaal Abraham faa bargi u kuna la maa un nawɛɛ laal biini bɔra fi, di lizi bɔkpaŋ tɛu la. 5Levi naanna la n ɛɛ kizeehina la faa ra lɛɛ kunaa ba himmaa nɛra be. Di a nɛra bargi ba kuna bɔra fi, a Levi dee ɔɔ lɛɛ a bɔkpannɛ. Ba maanii ɛɛ Abraham naanna, ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Levi deere dɔɔ bɔkpaŋ la. 6Ka Mɛlkizɛdɛk naa, waa Levi dee biini liwɛɛ, ka lɛɛ bɔkpaŋ la lii yaa naabaal Abraham, Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nuuzi tɛɛ la be, ka suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi tɛu. 7Yaa maa zummɔ lugɔ nabɔmaa suŋŋɛɛ ra tɛɛ bichala. 8Yaa Kizeehina n na lɛɛ bɔkpaŋ la, ba daŋ ŋmɛnɛ siuzi. Ka unlawaa, Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ u ra nyinuu. 9Yaa daŋ wer ŋɔ lugɔ Levi la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ú lɛɛ bɔkpaŋ la gba lizi bɔkpannɛ tɛɛ Mɛlkizɛdɛk, dikuu u naabaal mɛɛ Abraham n lizi guŋ tɛu wia. 10Ba faa haa waa Levi lullɛ saŋa la Mɛlkizɛdɛk n faa chem u ni la.
Yeesu ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Mɛlkizɛdɛk
11Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ u nɛra u Gbɔgni la, a saŋaa Levi dee faari ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la. Too. Di nɛra daŋ faa wer birgi nɛnanaa wa tuŋ, di lii mbusuzi la Levi dee n faa lizɛɛ ra tɛɛ baa la biini, amɔ, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ kizeehiŋ bɛl dee n du gunla Mɛlkizɛdɛk la n faa duwɛɛ ka gil Aarɔnwaa dee la wiai? 12Di ba birgi kizeehina wia, amɔ, ba daŋ birgi widaulaa la gba. 13Unla uŋ ŋɔ u wia kennaa ge gba lii dee la n faa waa nɛr maa dɔɔwɛ un niŋ wer kpogli kizee ra hum Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la. 14Yaa Dɔɔri la, yaa zummɔ lugɔ Juda dee biinii u lii. Moosis n faa ŋɔ Juda wia la, u faa waa kizeehina wia ŋɔwɛɛ.
15Kizeehiŋ bɛl n liwɛɛ di ɛɛ lugɔ Mɛlkizɛdɛk la, a wia jaa ra chaani nɛnnɛ di wer chi. 16Newea widaulaa fɔŋŋa biini lɛi u birgi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la. U miibɔɔ la n waa tuŋ la fɔŋŋa biinii u birgi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la, 17dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“I daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ di hanna la saŋa maa
gunla Mɛlkizɛdɛk
n faa ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la.”
18Awia, widaulibinii la n waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ, waa wikuarii dɔɔwɛ la wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi lizuu la. 19Moosis widaulaa la faa waa wette gil nɛr maa birgi nɛnanii wa tuŋ. Wibinaa la n tunnɛ ka wifalaa ge lii la, a wifalaa dɔɔ tamiirɛ werge kaali wibinaa la. A daŋ gil ya wer hel Kɔraawiizi be. 20A wia kaa bɔmbɔ, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n faa hɛɛhzɛɛ a wia la wia. U faa waa hɛɛhzɛɛ lɛi ka baŋhina birgi u kizeehina. 21Ka baŋ wa ŋɔ Yeesu wia, ba ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Kɔraawiizi hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, wàá ka bir ŋɔ,
‘I daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ
di hanna la
saŋa maa.’ ”
22Kɔraawiizi ni nɛra nuukpaŋ dɔɔi naa bɔ ubinii labuu. Yeesu ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi talmaa un dauwɛ ya zum lugɔ u ɛɛ wibiire.
23Levi dee la n ɔɔ ra birgi Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la kpillɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba wàá wer du de ra la. Ba ɔɔ ra siuzuu, baŋhina ge kaa ra di. 24Ka Yeesu n ɔɔ du de saŋa maa la, waabuu ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehinnɛ di hanna la. 25Awia, u wettoo lɛɛ banla maa n ba u be, bá wer hel Kɔraawiizi be la ha werge maa di wa tuŋ, dikuu uŋ ɔɔ du de ra suŋŋi wiizi ra tɛɛ baa wia.
26Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la dee Yeesu n ɛɛwɛ la dɔɔ hiinaare yaa be. U ɛɛ kunnaniirɛ alugɔ Kɔraawiizi n duwɛɛ la. Waa wichɔgaa maa dɔɔwɛ. Doŋa maa waa hoo u ni. U ni wichɔgɛɛra waa kpaŋ ɛɛwɛ. Kɔraawiizi tɛubuu nabɔmuu u kaali kummaa n du chiŋ. 27Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔnzi la ɔɔ ra lizi mbusuzii hɔpizibii maa. A ba feluu lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dikuu ba himmaa wichɔgaa wia mɔɔ, ka jaa lizi ra tɛɛ nɛra la. Ka Yeesu waa guŋ dɔɔwɛ. U lizi mbusuu kakpaŋ bɛŋ. U himmaanii mbusu lizaa sel. 28Banna hiŋ Moosis Hɔŋ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔnzi la, nɛra la n gɛrgɛɛ, ba waa ɔɔ wer bá vɛɛ wichɔgaa labuu ba ra lizi. Ka wiŋɔzi la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ Moosis Hɔŋ harbɔɔ la, di hɛɛhzi u hiŋ la, waabuu gillɛ u Biibaal ɛɛ u Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma di hanna la.

english_text:
A Better Promise
1 What I mean is we have a high priest who sits at the right side of God's great throne in heaven. 2He also serves as the priest in the most holy place inside the real tent there in heaven. This tent of worship was set up by the Lord, not by humans.
3Since all priests must offer gifts and sacrifices, Christ also needed to have something to offer. 4If he were here on earth, he would not be a priest at all, because here the Law appoints other priests to offer sacrifices. 5 But the tent where they serve is just a copy and a shadow of the real one in heaven. Before Moses made the tent, he was told, “Be sure to make it exactly like the pattern you were shown on the mountain!” 6Now Christ has been appointed to serve as a priest in a much better way, and he has given us much assurance of a better agreement.
7If the first agreement with God had been all right, there would not have been any need for another one. 8 But the Lord found fault with it and said,
“I tell you the time will come,
when I will make
a new agreement
with the people of Israel
and the people of Judah.
9It won't be like the agreement
that I made
with their ancestors,
when I took them by the hand
and led them out of Egypt.
They broke their agreement
with me,
and I stopped caring
about them!
10“But now I tell the people
of Israel
this is my new agreement:
‘The time will come
when I, the Lord,
will write my laws
on their minds and hearts.
I will be their God,
and they will be
my people.
11Not one of them
will have to teach another
to know me, their Lord.’
“All of them will know me,
no matter who they are.
12I will treat them with kindness,
even though they are wicked.
I will forget their sins.”
13When the Lord talks about a new agreement, he means that the first one is out of date. And anything that is old and useless will soon disappear.
translation_text:
Nuukpaŋfalii Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma wia
1Wiŋɔzi naa maa biinii keŋ. Yaa dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la n du gunnɛ. U sogo Girme Hiŋ nabɔmbɔttɛ u bol. 2U ra hum Kɔraawiizii u Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la n du u Tanti Dia la n ɛɛ u himmaa la. Yaa Dɔɔri labuu baŋuu. Newee lɛi baŋuu.
3Baŋ ɔɔ lizi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la, mbusuzi ni sela fuuih wiarɛ ba ɔɔ lizuu. Awia, a faa dɛkkɔ unnii naa ge n dɔɔ kuŋ la un niŋ kpa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. 4Di u vii du durnyaa, u vii waa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ ɛɛwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba dɔɔ ba horaa ba ra lizi mbusuzi gunla Moosis Hɔŋ n baglɛɛ la. 5Banna hum guŋ naa, ba ra chanzi gunla banna ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi be labuu. Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii saŋa la uŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi u baŋ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la, “A dazi ka kuari u maa gunla miŋ baglii bizeŋ la nyuu la.” 6Ka Yeesu waa huma wessoo werge kaali guŋ. Nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la uŋ ɛɛ yaa sitɔɔri, u ni Kɔraawiizi kuari la ge bɔ u binii labuu werge. Nuuzi la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ yaa di kuari nuukpaŋ la, a gba wessoo kaali anla. 7Di lugli nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la faa wesso wa tuŋ, ba faa wàá nyiŋŋi bɛl ú lɛɛ u bɔr. 8Ama, Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ u nɛraa chɔgri, di ŋɔ,
“Saŋa bɛl ra bau,
ń ni Izrɛl ni Juda hina
ɛɛ nuukpaŋfalii.
9Wàá ɛɛ lugɔ unla
n ni ba naabaala
n ɛɛwɛ saŋa la
miŋ kpogli baa lii
Ijip hɛri la.
Ba faa waa yaa nuukpaŋ la hiŋŋɛ,
n bir har kpu baa.
10Nuukpaŋ la n ni Izrɛl hina
n niŋ kaa ɛɛ,
a saŋaa keŋ.
N daŋ kpa n Gbɔgni du ba biine,
di sɛbaa du
ba bampiree biine.
N daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum,
bá ge ɛɛ n nɛra.
11A wàá ka ɛɛ lugɔ nɛr maa n niŋ bagli
u niwee gɛɛ
u dɔŋhiŋ, di ŋɔ,
‘A wesso hiŋ zum Kɔraawiizi,’
dikuubɛɛwiai,
ba maanii niŋ zumiŋ,
nɛdumazi ni
nɛzenaa maa.
12N daŋ suŋ ba ni,
di gil ba wia la n waa
deŋlee la tɛɛ baa.
Màá ka liizi ba wichɔgaa wia maa.”
13Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ “nuukpaŋfalii” wia naa, lugli hor la jaa birgi u biniirɛ. Um birgi u binii naa, u fɔŋŋa ra tunuu, u wia ge ra tuŋ.

english_text:
The Tent in Heaven
1The first promise included rules for worship and a tent for worship here on earth. 2 The first part of the tent was called the holy place, and a lampstand, a table, and the sacred loaves of bread were kept there.
3 Behind the curtain was the most holy place. 4 The gold altar for burning incense was in this holy place. The gold-covered sacred chest was also there, and inside it were three things. First, there was a gold jar filled with manna. Then there was Aaron's walking stick that sprouted. Finally, there were the flat stones with the Ten Commandments written on them. 5 On top of the chest were the glorious creatures with wings opened out above the place of mercy.
Now isn't the time to go into detail about these things. 6 But this is how everything was when the priests went each day into the first part of the tent to do their duties. 7 However, only the high priest could go into the second part of the tent, and he went in only once a year. Each time he carried blood to offer for his sins and for any sins that the people had committed without meaning to.
8All of this is the Holy Spirit's way of saying no one could enter the most holy place while the tent was still the place of worship. 9This also has a meaning for today. It shows we cannot make our consciences clear by offering gifts and sacrifices. 10These rules are merely about such things as eating and drinking and ceremonies for washing ourselves. And rules about physical things will last only until the time comes to change them for something better.
11 Christ came as the high priest of the good things that are now here. He also went into a much better tent that wasn't made by humans and that doesn't belong to this world. 12Then Christ went once for all into the most holy place and freed us from sin forever. He did this by offering his own blood instead of the blood of goats and bulls.
13 According to the Law of Moses, those people who become unclean are not fit to worship God. Yet they will be considered clean, if they are sprinkled with the blood of goats and bulls and with the ashes of a sacrificed calf. 14But Christ was sinless, and he offered himself as an eternal and spiritual sacrifice to God. This is why his blood is much more powerful and makes our consciences clear. Now we can serve the living God and no longer do things that lead to death.
15Christ died to rescue those who had sinned and broken the old agreement. Now he brings his chosen ones a new agreement with its guarantee of God's eternal blessings! 16In fact, making an agreement of this kind is like writing a will. This is because the one who makes the will must die before it is of any use. 17In other words, a will doesn't go into effect as long as the one who made it is still alive.
18Blood was also used to put the first agreement into effect. 19 Moses told the people all the Law said they must do. Then he used red wool and a hyssop plant to sprinkle the people and the book of the Law with the blood of bulls and goats and with water. 20He told the people, “With this blood God makes his agreement with you.” 21 Moses also sprinkled blood on the tent and on everything else used in worship. 22 The Law says that almost everything must be sprinkled with blood, and no sins can be forgiven unless blood is offered.
Christ's Great Sacrifice
23These things are only copies of what is in heaven, and so they had to be made holy by these ceremonies. But the real things in heaven must be made holy by something better. 24This is why Christ did not go into a tent made by humans and was only a copy of the real one. Instead, he went into heaven and is now there with God to help us.
25Christ did not have to offer himself many times. He wasn't like a high priest who goes into the most holy place each year to offer the blood of an animal. 26If he had offered himself every year, he would have suffered many times since the creation of the world. But instead, near the end of time he offered himself once and for all, so he could be a sacrifice that does away with sin.
27We die only once, and then we are judged. 28 So Christ died only once to take away the sins of many people. But when he comes again, it will not be to take away sin. He will come to save everyone who is waiting for him.
translation_text:
Hɛri ni chiŋ jaamaa wia
1Lugli nuukpaŋ la Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra n ɛɛwɛ la faa dɔɔ jaamaarɛ ban ninna jaami, di kaa dɔɔ bɔnanii hɛri naa, ban niŋ zuu ra jaami. 2Ba faa baŋ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia bɛllɛ, di kpa patiisa teŋ u biini bɔra anɛɛ, saliŋ fintina daa ni tɛɛbul bɛl ni paanuuzi aŋhina baŋ ɔɔ kpa chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi du bɔr la n du see ba ra yir de Bɔnaniinanii la. 3A Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa ge du patiisa nɛɛhiŋ la harbɔɔ. 4Daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr la baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari ni dakka la baŋ kpa saliŋ tɔ u maa, u ɛɛ ba ni Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la du u biini. Saliŋ vii bɛl baŋ kpa paanuu la dee n lii chiŋ la du u biini ni Aarɔn daŋkpala la n faa fur paŋhoori ani bia anɛɛ la, Kɔraawiizi n sɛbi u ni baa nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la wia a ni la, du Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la biini. 5Ba sɛɛh chɛrubzi chiŋŋi u ni, a willi tɔ bɔr la baŋ faa ɔɔ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih u nɛra ni la. Yaa wàá na bɔr ŋɔ kuna naa wia nɛnnɛ filaŋkeŋ.
6Baŋ wa ɛɛ annii maa sirya guŋ, kizeehina ɔɔ ra zuu lugli dia la hɔpizibii maa, di ra hum ba huma. 7Nɛɛhiŋ lawaa, bina maa, kakpaŋ bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma bɛŋ ɔɔ zuu de. U daŋ kpa chal zuu di mizi de, dikuu u himmaa wichɔgaa ni a nɛra wichɔgaa baŋ waa zummɛ ka ɛɛ la wia. 8Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii ra bagli yaabuu lii wia naa biini lugɔ di u Tanti Dia la haa du de, u Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa zuui haa tɔwɔɔrɛ. 9A wia ra bagli filaŋkeŋ wia naabuu. Ba ra lizi mbusuzii fuuh kuna ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ka a wàá wer gil nɛr la n na ɛɛa la dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu wa tuŋ. 10A ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋ wia bɛnnɛ, lugɔ kuna dii, kuna nyɔɔi ani niisɔi wiarɛ. Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ baabuu guŋ bá ra hiŋ mɔɔ, ka sáŋa la un niŋ wa birgi a maa la wa hel, á ɛɛ a falaa.
Kristo chal wia
11Kristo ballɔɔ di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma, di ra hum winanaa la n liwɛɛ filaŋkeŋ la huma. U ge Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la unna hum u biini la dɔɔ girmee, di du wer kaali unla hiŋ. Newee lɛi baŋuu. Waa hɛri naa kuŋ ɛɛwɛ. 12Kristo zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa labuu. Un zuuwɛ la, buuŋ ni nabii chal lɛi u kpa zuu de. U himmaa challɛ turgi yaa kim, di wer na lɛɛi la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ tɛɛ yaa. Kakpaŋ bɛnnɛ u zuu de. Wàá ka zuu de maa. 13Ba ɔɔ faa kpa buuna, nabala challi ani hɔɔhrii lii bɔr la baŋ fuuh nalor labuu, di mizi banla n doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be la ni, bá doŋa lii. 14Di ba wetto ɛɛ guŋ ba doŋa lii, amɔ, Kristo chal wàá lizi yaa doŋa werge maa kaali guŋŋ? Kɔraawiizi Dumnaniirɛ faa hiinuu u kpa u hiŋ di lizi mbusu la. U faa kpekkoo nɛnnɛ. U chal la daŋ lizi yaa wipɛɛri doŋa yaa ni ha, á gilɛɛ kaa tir yaa, ka ya wer hum unla n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa la.
15Awia, Kɔraawiizi Ni Nɛra Nuukpaŋfaliirɛ u ɛɛ yaa sitɔɔri di kuari la, bánla Kɔraawiizi n yittɛ wer na u kapɛttɛ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ ka haŋ du de di ra la saŋa maa uŋ ŋɔ lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ baa la. U ɛɛ gunnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u siuwɔɔ lɛɛ nɛra lii ba wichɔgaa la baŋ faa ra ɛɛ nuukpambinii la biini.
16Di nɛr sɛbi gunla ban niŋ bargi u kuna saŋa la un niŋ wa siu, ka di waa siuwɛ lɛi, ba wàá wer bɔnnaa. 17Ka di u wa siuwɔ, ba daŋ jaa wer bargi u kuna. Ama, di nɛr la n sɛbi hɔŋ la haa du de, ba wàá wer kpa a hɔŋ fɔŋŋa bɔnni u kuna la. 18Awiarɛ lugli nuukpaŋ la gba, ba faa waa wette ɛɛu tuŋ, di ba faa waa chal fukke mɔɔ. 19Moosis n faa bagli nɛra la maa Kɔraawiizi widaulaa la maa n du u hɔŋ biini la tuŋ, u gillɔɔ ba kpu nabizi di kpa a challi, nii, pehuna la n aahwɛ ani hisɔp daa mizi hɔŋ la ni a nɛra maa ni, 20di ŋɔ, “Chal la n kuari nuukpaŋ la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ii ra hiŋ labuu keŋ.” 21U kaa mizi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni tassazi la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ ra hum de la ni. 22Moosis Hɔnna ra bagluu gunla maa ban ninna ɛɛ ka wer ra lizi doŋa nɛra ni. Challɛ bá kpa ɛɛ a galga maa. Di ba waa kuŋ kpuwɛɛ u chal lii, Kɔraawiizi wàá gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.
23Gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ bá ɔɔ ɛɛ ka wer lizi doŋa Tanti Dia la kuna la ni ha. A kuna ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ anla n du Kɔraawiizi be la, ka anla n du Kɔraawiizi be labuu ɛɛ a himmaa. Mbusu la n wesse werge kaali guŋ la, waabuu ba ɛɛ ka wer lizi a doŋa ha. 24Kristo n zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii la, unla n du dia la newea n mawɛɛ u li u himmaa la n du Kɔraawiizi be la biini lɛi u zuu. Kɔraawiizi bol himmaanii u zuu du de filaŋkeŋ, ú wer kuu yaa hiinaa wia ga chi Kɔraawiizi see. 25Un zuu de la, gunla Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma n ɔɔ kpa chal la n waa u himmaa hor ɛɛwɛ la zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa bina maa la, guŋ lɛi u zuu de ɛɛ. Waa ɔɔ kpa u hiŋ lizi mbusu ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi digiidigii. 26Di u faa ra ɛɛ guŋ, u daŋ faa ra di tɔɔrɔɔ saŋakpila maa durnya faaraa saŋa la guŋŋ wa lii zinaa. Ka u ballɔɔ durnya tuna hɔpizaa naa biini, ú wer kpa u hiŋ lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di duŋŋi wichɔgaa kakpaŋ, á tuŋ. 27Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ neweare lugɔ bá siu kakpaŋ bɛŋ, ka ú jaa di ba seriya. 28Gunnɛ Kristo n kuu nɛkpila wia di kpa u hiŋ lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ú wer lɛɛ nɛra wichɔgaa chi la, kakpannɛ u ɛɛ guŋ. Di u kaa wa ba, wichɔgaa wia lɛi ú ba. U daŋ ba ú wa lɛɛ banla n na binni u ŋmɛnɛɛ ani tamii la.

english_text:
1The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year. 2If there were worshipers who already have their sins washed away and their consciences made clear, there would not be any need to go on offering sacrifices. 3-4But the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. It only reminds people of their sins from one year to the next.
5 When Christ came into the world, he said to God,
“Sacrifices and offerings
are not what you want,
but you have given me
my body.
6No, you are not pleased
with animal sacrifices
and offerings for sin.”
7Then Christ said,
“And so, my God,
I have come to do
what you want,
as the Scriptures say.”
8The Law teaches that offerings and sacrifices must be made because of sin. But why did Christ mention these things and say that God did not want them? 9Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.” 10So we are made holy because Christ obeyed God and offered himself once for all.
11 The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins. 12 But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side, 13and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power. 14By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
15The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
16 “When the time comes,
I will make an agreement
with them.
I will write my laws
on their minds and hearts.
17 Then I will forget
about their sins
and no longer remember
their evil deeds.”
18When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices.
Encouragement and Warning
19My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place 20by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
21We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house. 22 So let's come near God with pure hearts and a confidence that comes from having faith. Let's keep our hearts pure, our consciences free from evil, and our bodies washed with clean water. 23We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us. 24We should keep on encouraging each other to be thoughtful and to do helpful things. 25Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
26No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth. 27 They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire. 28 If two or more witnesses accused someone of breaking the Law of Moses, that person could be put to death. 29 But it is much worse to dishonor God's Son and to disgrace the blood of the promise that made us holy. And it is just as bad to insult the Holy Spirit, who shows us mercy. 30 We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people. 31It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
32Don't forget all the hard times you went through when you first received the light. 33Sometimes you were abused and mistreated in public, and at other times you shared in the sufferings of others. 34You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
35Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards. 36Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised. 37 As the Scriptures say,
“God is coming soon!
It won't be very long.
38The people God accepts
will live because
of their faith.
But he isn't pleased
with anyone
who turns back.”
39We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
translation_text:
Yeesu n kpa u hiŋ lizi mbusu kakpaŋ tɛɛ yaa wia
1Moosis Hɔŋ wia la faa tɔ winanaa la n faa haa du harbɔɔ la seere. A faa waa a himmaa ɛɛwɛ alugɔ nɛr laalii n waa u himmaa ɛɛwɛ la. Awia, mbusuzi la banna lizi binaa bina maa la wàá wer gil banla n kpaa ba la birgi nɛnanaa. 2Di a mbusuzi faa wetto gil ba birgi nɛnanaa guŋ, ba faa wàá gil a lizaa? Di a faa wetto lizi ba doŋa ha, ba faa wàá ka zum wichɔgaa. 3Ka guŋ lɛi a du. Bina maanii ba ra lizi mbusuzi ka ra liizi ba wichɔgaa wia. 4Nabala ni buuna challi wàá wer lizi wichɔgaa nɛra ni ha. 5Awia, Kristo n ba durnya la, u ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Mbusu lizaa ni kuna fuuih lɛi i ra nyiŋŋi.
Bɔrahɔŋ bɛl siryaa
i ɛɛ tɛŋ.
6Baŋ fuuh sela lizi mbusuzi tɛi,
dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia la,
a wɛɛ pattɛ.
7Denii n ŋɔ,
‘Na! N ballɔɔ
gunla baŋ faa sɛbi
n wia i hɔŋ biini la,
ń wa ɛɛ i kipar,
n Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi.’ ”
8Uŋ faa ŋɔ gunla lugɔ mbusuzi lizaa, kuna fuuih ani anla maa banna ɛɛ dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia gunla Moosis Hɔŋ n baglɛɛ la, dí a wɔɔ pattɛ la, 9di kaa ŋɔ, “Na, n ballɔɔ ń wa ɛɛ i kipar la,” uŋ ŋɔ kennaa naa, u lizi lugli hiŋaa labuu ha gunla, ka ú wer dau nɛɛhiŋ la hiŋaa. 10Kɔraawiizi kipar la Yeesu Kristo n ɛɛwɛ la biinii u lizi yaa doŋa yaa ni ha, di gil yaa birgi Kɔraawiizi hora. Uŋ kpa u himmaa bɔrahɔŋ lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kakpaŋ la wiarɛ u wer ɛɛ guŋ.
11Kizeehina la n ɔɔ chi mbusu lizibɔr hɔpizibii maa, di hum ra lizi mbusuzi la dee baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi digiidigii la, a waa wette lizi wichɔgaa maa ra ha. 12Ama, Yeesuwaa, uŋ siuwɛ lizi mbusu dikuu nɛra wichɔgaa wia la, kakpannɛ u ɛɛ guŋ, ú chi saŋa maa ra la, ka jaa ga so Kɔraawiizi nabɔmbɔr. 13U du denii di ra kpaŋ saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ gil u dɔma birgi u yoma la. 14U mbusu lizaa kpaŋkpaŋ la wia banla maa Kɔraawiizi n lizi ba doŋa ba ni ha la, daŋ ɔɔ du wer di ra la saŋa maa. 15Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii gba ra di guŋ daansɛɛrɛ ra tɛɛ yaa, di ŋɔ,
16“Nuukpaŋfalii la n ni baa
n niŋ ɛɛu keŋ,
N daŋ kpa n Gbɔgni
du ba biine,
di sɛbaa du
ba bampiree biine.”
17U kaa ŋɔ jaa,
“Màá ka liizi ba
wichɔgaa wia maa.”
18Too. Di Kɔraawiizi gil wichɔgaa la tɛɛ baa, ba wàá ka lizi mbusuzi dikuu a wia. 19Awia, yaabalaa, yaa daŋ wer dɔɔ bampirii zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la dikuu Yeesu chal wia. 20U pilli ŋmɛnifalii la n dɔɔ miibɔɔrɛ tɛɛ yaa, ya wer zuu de. U bɔrahɔŋ gba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ patiisazenzeŋ la n faa teŋ Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la. Un siuwɛ la, bɔr la jaa pilluu tɛɛ yaa. 21Yaa dɔɔ Kizeehina Nabɔnzenzeŋ bɛl n na binni Kɔraawiizi biizi ninɛɛ. 22Awia, ya la ga zuu de ani biinihuŋŋu, di gilɛɛ waa aani, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi lizi yaa biine doŋaa ha yaa wichɔgaa maa lii. A wàá kaa ra tir yaa. U kaa sɔ yaa niinanii yaa lii. 23Ya lau tamii la yaa n ŋɔ yaa dɔɔwɔ la nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa aani tama maa. Unla n ŋɔ nua la wia dɔɔ wibiire. 24Ya ra binni dɔŋa ni, di zum gunla yaa n niŋ gil yaa maa aah siwii, dikuu dɔnnɔŋŋaa ni winanaa ɛɛi wia. 25Ya gilɛɛ vɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa lugɔ baŋhina n na vɛɛ la. Ya chaali dɔŋa di ra bagli dɔŋa ŋmɛnizi gunla yaa n ninna hiŋ. Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii la ra dugluu. Awia, ya aah siwii werge ra hiini dɔŋa guŋ.
26Di Kɔraawiizi pilli yaa siwee, yaa zum wibii nɛnnɛ, ka kutti ga ɛɛ wichɔgaa, mbusu lizaa maa waa kaa hoo un niŋ wer lizi a wichɔgaa ha, 27ka yaa danna fɔŋ, di ra guu hɔpizii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ di yaa seriya, di du yaa chɔgri niŋ la n na lau siaahmu ni, di ra fuuh u dɔma la biini. 28Di nɛr la maa chɔgi Moosis hɔŋ Gbɔgni la, nɛra banɛɛ gɛɛ bahoro ŋɔ u wia guŋ, ba ra kpuubuu. Ba waa ɔɔ na u sinyɛna. 29Di gunnɛ, ɛrɛɛ bá ɛɛ nɛr la n gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi Biibaal, di binni u chal la n kuari nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la pɛɛ, di kaa gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi Duma nɛsunaa la n na hiinuu, di gil u birgi Kɔraawiizi hor lai? Di Kɔraawiizi waa turgi u ge kim, u hor wàá nyaŋŋi werge maa? 30Yaa zum unla n ŋɔwɛɛ, “Minuu dɔɔ wichɔgaa kinturgaa. Mìń niŋ turgi nɛra ba wichɔgaa kim.” Ba kaa sɛbi yembɛl, di ŋɔ, “Yaa Dɔɔri daŋ di u nɛra seriya.” 31Di i chol unla n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa la nonee biini, ɔnsiirɛ.
32Ií ra liizi saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n felee chaani ii siwee la. Ii faa di tɔɔrɔɔrɛ werge maa, ka faa haa vɛɛ ra hiŋ. 33A saŋa bɛl, ba faa ra chagzi iabuu di ra tɔɔri ia nɛra baaŋ. A saŋa bɛl ge, ii faa ra hiini banla baŋ faa ra tɔɔri la. 34Ii faa suŋ banla baŋ tɔwɛɛ dia la ninɛɛ. Ba foozi ii kunaa, ka ii haa gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii faa zummɔ lugɔ ii dɔɔ kuna la n wesse ninɛɛ kaali durnya kuna naa. A ge daŋ ɔɔ du de di ra la. 35Awia, ii gilɛɛ gil ii yarda la iiŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi Biibaal la ta filaŋkeŋ. U dɔɔ kinturginaniirɛ werge maa. 36A dɛkkɔ iin niŋ haa ra di kanyitti. Di ii wetto di ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi kipar, ii daŋ na nua la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la. 37Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ,
“A ka tamaa, ka unla n niŋ ba la ba.
Wàá ka birgi.
38Nɛr la wia n deŋlee,
yardaa niŋ ɛɛ u miibɔɔ.
Ka di u wa bir har,
u wia wàá ka pariŋ.”
39Ka yaawaa waa banla n niŋ bir har, Kɔraawiizi chɔgi baa la ɛɛwɛ. Yaa daŋ ɔɔ yardi di na lɛɛi.

english_text:
The Great Faith of God's People
1Faith makes us sure of what we hope for and gives us proof of what we cannot see. 2 It was their faith that made our ancestors pleasing to God.
3 Because of our faith, we know that the world was made at God's command. We also know that what can be seen was made out of what cannot be seen.
4 Because Abel had faith, he offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. God was pleased with him and his gift, and even though Abel is now dead, his faith still speaks for him.
5 Enoch had faith and did not die. He pleased God, and God took him up to heaven. This is why his body was never found. 6But without faith no one can please God. We must believe that God is real and rewards everyone who searches for him.
7 Because Noah had faith, he was warned about something that had not yet happened. He obeyed and built a boat that saved him and his family. In this way the people of the world were judged, and Noah was given the blessings that come to everyone who pleases God.
8 Abraham had faith and obeyed God. He was told to go to the land that God had said would be his, and he left for a country he had never seen. 9 Because Abraham had faith, he lived as a stranger in the promised land. He lived there in a tent, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who were later given the same promise. 10Abraham did this, because he was waiting for the eternal city God had planned and built.
11 Even when Sarah was too old to have children, she had faith that God would do what he had promised, and she had a son. 12 Her husband Abraham was almost dead, but he became the ancestor of many people. In fact, there are as many of them as there are stars in the sky or grains of sand along the seashore.
13 Every one of those people died. But they still had faith, even though they had not received what they had been promised. They were glad just to see these things from far away, and they agreed that they were only strangers and foreigners on this earth. 14When people talk this way, it is clear they are looking for a place to call their own. 15If they had been talking about the land where they had once lived, they could have gone back at any time. 16But they were looking forward to a better home in heaven. This is why God wasn't ashamed for them to call him their God. He even built a city for them.
17-18 Abraham had been promised that Isaac, his only son, would continue his family. But when Abraham was tested, he had faith and was willing to sacrifice Isaac, 19because he was sure that God could raise people to life. This was just like getting Isaac back from death.
20 Isaac had faith, and he promised blessings to Jacob and Esau. 21 Later, when Jacob was about to die, he leaned on his walking stick and worshiped. Then because of his faith he blessed each of Joseph's sons. 22 And right before Joseph died, he had faith that God would lead the people of Israel out of Egypt. So he told them to take his bones with them.
23 Because Moses' parents had faith, they kept him hidden until he was three months old. They saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid to disobey the king's orders. 24 Then after Moses grew up, his faith made him refuse to be called the king's grandson. 25 He chose to be mistreated with God's people instead of having the good time that sin could bring for a little while. 26Moses knew that the treasures of Egypt were not as wonderful as what he would receive from suffering for the Messiah, and he looked forward to his reward.
27Because of his faith, Moses left Egypt. Moses had seen the invisible God and wasn't afraid of the king's anger. 28 His faith also made him celebrate Passover. He sprinkled the blood of animals on the doorposts, so that the first-born sons of the people of Israel would not be killed by the destroying angel.
29 Because of their faith, the people walked through the Red Sea on dry land. But when the Egyptians tried to do it, they were drowned.
30 God's people had faith, and when they had walked around the city of Jericho for seven days, its walls fell down.
31 Rahab had been a prostitute, but she had faith and welcomed the spies. So she wasn't killed with the people who disobeyed.
32 What else can I say? There isn't enough time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets. 33 Their faith helped them conquer kingdoms, and because they did right, God made promises to them. They closed the jaws of lions 34 and put out raging fires and escaped from the swords of their enemies. Although they were weak, they were given the strength and power to chase foreign armies away.
35 Some women received their loved ones back from death. Many of these people were tortured, but they refused to be released. They were sure they would get a better reward when the dead are raised to life. 36 Others were made fun of and beaten with whips, and some were chained in jail. 37 Still others were stoned to death or sawed in two or killed with swords. Some had nothing but sheep skins or goat skins to wear. They were poor, mistreated, and tortured. 38The world did not deserve these good people, who had to wander in deserts and on mountains and had to live in caves and holes in the ground.
39All of them pleased God because of their faith! But still they died without being given what had been promised. 40This was because God had something better in store for us. And he did not want them to reach the goal of their faith without us.
translation_text:
Yarda wia
1Bɛɛ yardai? Yardaa hinna tami wia ni, aabuu niŋ bagli lugɔ i daŋ naa. Di i haa waa a wia nawɛɛ ka yardi, a yardaa ɔɔ gil i zum lugɔ i daŋ wa naa.
2Ba Kɔraawiizi yarda hiŋ wiarɛ yaa naabaala la faa na sɔŋ. 3Yaa ge Kɔraawiizi yarda gillɔɔ yaa zum lugɔ chiŋ ni hɛri maa lii Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la fɔŋŋa biinii. Awia, kuna la siwee n na na la lii kuna la siwee n waa na la biinii.
4Abɛl Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ, uŋ faa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, u hor faa du wer kaali u kpɛɛma Keen hor la. Uŋ yarduu wiarɛ u ŋɔ u ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ u be, di bagli lugɔ u mbusu lizaa la paruubuu. A yarda wiarɛ Abɛl siu birgi, ka haa wer ra bagli yaa wia la.
5Ɛnɔk Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi faa kpau kaali u be. Waa siuwɛ. Kɔraawiizi kpaubuu guŋ. Ba nyiŋŋuu huhzi. Ba faa sɛbi u wiarɛ, di ŋɔ lugɔ u wia par Kɔraawiizii. 6Nɛr la n waa Kɔraawiizi yardɛɛ, u wia wàá wer paruu. Di nɛr la maa ŋɔ ú hel Kɔraawiizi be, u daŋ feli yardi lugɔ u du denii, di kaa yardi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ra hiini banla maa n aah siwii ra nyiŋŋi u bɔttɛ.
7Noowa Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ u ge faa kuari muugberzeŋ la. Kɔraawiizi faa karfuubuu wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ la. U ge n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la wia, u kuari muugberzeŋ la di wer lɛɛ u ni u diahina maa. Uŋ wette ɛɛ guŋ ka durnya la n kawɛɛ vɛɛ la, u tɛɛ baabuu chɔgri. Kɔraawiizi di ba seriya ba chol, ka gil Noowa waa ɛɛ nɛnanii u be, dikuu uŋ yarduu wia.
8Abraham Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi n yiruu ŋɔ ú izi u bol la hɛri la un niŋ tɛu la, u wer izi lii. U faa waa zum bɔr la maa un niŋ la, ka izi ra la. 9Yarda wiarɛ u wer ɛɛ hɔɔhri du hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ tɛu la. U faa ra zuu tanti diini biinee alugɔ yaa naabaala Aizik ni Jekɔb maa. U ni ba maanii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ. 10Abraham faa ra nyiŋŋi bol bɛl deere. A bol dee, Kɔraawiizi maubuu u chi nɛnnɛ. Wàá chol maa.
11Saara Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ u wer kpogli hia saŋa la uŋ faa zɛŋŋɛ tuŋ la. Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛu lugɔ u daŋ lul bie la, u faa zummɔ lugɔ u wia dɔɔ wibiire. 12Denii Abraham, saŋa la u fɔŋŋa maa n tunnɛ la, ka u wetto lul biizi, u naanna ge bir wa du kpil alugɔ chinchiŋwilaa gɛɛ muuzeŋ kɛrii hɛɛhriichaa n kpillɛ gunla.
13Bannii maa faa yardi Kɔraawiizii ka siuzi. Ba faa waa wia la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua la nawɛɛ siwii ni ka siuzi. Ka ba faa naabuu alugɔ iinna nɛra bɔɔnɛɛ, di ra jaami baa gunla. Ba faa sɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ba ɛɛ hɔɔhraa durnya naa biini. 14Nɛra n na ŋɔ gunla, ba himmaa hɛrii ba ra nyiŋŋi la. 15Di ba hɛri la baŋ liwɛɛ wiarɛ ba faa ŋɔ guŋ, ba daŋ faa wer bir la de. 16Hɛri la n wesse werge kaaluu labuu ba faa ra nyiŋŋi. Kɔraawiizi be hɛrii ba faa ra nyiŋŋi la. Awia, banna yiruu ba dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la, guŋ wɔɔ ra ɛɛ hiihzi. U ɛɛ bol siryaa tɛɛ baa.
17Abraham Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ, u wer kpa u biibaal Aizik dau mbusu lizibɔr ni, di ŋɔ ú kpuu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ ú ɛɛu na la. A Abraham ɛɛ nɛr la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ labuu, ka u wer kpa u biikpaŋkpaŋ ŋɔ ú lizi mbusu la. 18Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ u benii lugɔ Aizik benii ú ga na biizi ni naanna. 19Ka u faa dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi tamiirɛ lugɔ di u siuwɔ gba, ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ wer lalluu. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ u lalluubuu siu biini la.
20Aizik Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ u wer suŋŋi wiizi ú hiini Jekɔb ni Ɛsau la, di ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ baa la.
21Jekɔb ge Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ unna siu, u suŋŋi wiizi ú hiini Joosɛf biizi banɛɛ la di pi u daŋkpala ni jaami Kɔraawiizi.
22Joosɛf gba Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ u ge n na siu la, u wer ŋɔ lugɔ Izrɛl hina la daŋ ŋmɛnɛ lii a hɛri, di bagli baa lugɔ bá kpa u hoga ra la a saŋa.
23Moosis maa ni u mɛɛ ge Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ baŋ lul Moosis, ba suauh baaguzi ahoro, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ biinaniirɛ. Ba faa waa koori gbɔg la ɔmmɛ.
24Gunnɛ Moosis ge Kɔraawiizi yarda la gil uŋ wa helle, waa sɛɛwɛ ba yiruu koori biihambie la biibaal, 25ka gil ba zum lugɔ u ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra la bɛllɛ, di ra di tɔɔrɔɔ. U ni Kɔraawiizi nɛra la maanii faa ra di a tɔɔrɔɔ. U tɔɔrɔɔ hiŋ dii guŋ faa paruubuu kaali gunla un niŋ faa ra di u hiŋ, di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa la n wàá birgi. 26Gbɛllaa la un niŋ kuu Kristo wia ba gbɛlluu la, aabuu ɛɛ kunnanaa u be werge maa kaali kunnanaa la maa n faa du Ijip hɛri, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra binni hɔpizii la n niŋ ba, Kɔraawiizi wa turgi nɛra maa labuu. 27Uŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ waa Ijip koori la baaŋ ɔmmɛ, ka izi u hɛri la. U wettoo dɔɔ bampirii, dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ u na unla baŋ waa na labuu. 28U yarda hiŋ wiarɛ u dau Gillikaali wia la, di gil ba mizi ba gbessi chal, síu mɛlika la gilɛɛ wa kpu Izrɛl hina biinabɔnzi la.
29Nɛra la Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ Muuzeŋaahmu la wer bargi, hɛrhilii chɔɔ alugɔ u baŋgia, ba wer vol wa lii. Ijip hina n wa ɛɛ guŋ na, nii la di baa.
30Izrɛl hina Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ, baŋ volle bar Jɛriko hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ biini, u koŋlaa la bam mawɛɛ baruu la chogli.
31Hahsɛnsɛnni Rahab la n yardi Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ, ba wɔɔ kpuwɛɛ jaa banla n vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, Izrɛl hina la n faa suahzɛɛ zuu a bol, bá daanuu na di zum gunla un duwɛɛ, ka la ga bagli la, waa baa duŋŋɛɛ ka lɛɛ baa dau.
32Too. Ń haa vɛɛ bagli ra jaaa? Màá wer na bɔr bagli ba maa wia. Gidiɔn, Barak, Samsin, Jɛfta, Deevid, Samuɛl ani Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la maanii du de. 33A nɛra kuu baŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi wia di wer kpegli kossi, di wer gil nɛra ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee, di wer na lii Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlaa la biini, di wer tɔ bunyinzi nuuzi, a waa wette hee baa, 34di wer sɔɔni ninzenaaa nuuzi, a waa wette fuuh baa, di wer lɛɛ bahinaa banla n kpa tokobizi ra nyiŋŋi ba kpu baa la be, di wer na fɔŋŋa saŋa la baŋ gɛrgɛɛ la, di wer yoo laal nɛnnɛ, di wer kpegli hɔɔhra la n ballɛ wa yoo baa la, 35di kaa wer lalli haana baŋhina biizi siu biini. Baŋhina ge, ba dɔma tɔɔri baa di kpuuzi baa. Ba faa waa nyiŋŋi ba lɛɛ bahinaa, ka ra nyiŋŋi bá wer na miibɔɔnanii saŋa la ban niŋ izi siu biini la. 36Ba faa lɔ baŋhina mɔmɔsia di viiri baa, di vɔɔzi baŋhina ge yɔlɔzi di tɔɔgi baa diini. 37Ba faa lɔɔzi baŋhina bia, di ɛɛ baŋhina na, di teŋri baŋhina ge bɔra anɛɛgaa, di kaa kpa tokobi kpuuzi baŋhina. A nɛra baŋhina faa tɔɔgi peeza ni buuna hɔna ra gaagi. Ba faa waa kummaa dɔɔwɛ. Nɛra faa ra tɔɔri baa di ra ɛɛ baa wichɔgaa. 38Durnya faa waa dɛg ba ni baa dui. Ba faa ra gaagi ra du hɛribɔdumazi ni giŋgimee ni bia bɔɔni biine. 39Ba na sɔnnɛ dikuu ba Kɔraawiizi yarda la wia. Ka ba waa Kɔraawiizi nua la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ la nawɛɛ, 40dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa zum yaa saŋa naa hina wiarɛ, di faa dau gunla n wesse, di ŋɔ ba bɛŋ wàá na a maa tuŋ, see yaa maa n niŋ kpau naa.

english_text:
A Large Crowd of Witnesses
1 Such a large crowd of witnesses is all around us! So we must get rid of everything that slows us down, especially the sin that just won't let go. And we must be determined to run the race that is ahead of us. 2 We must keep our eyes on Jesus, who leads us and makes our faith complete. He endured the shame of being nailed to a cross, because he knew later on he would be glad he did. Now he is seated at the right side of God's throne! 3So keep your mind on Jesus, who put up with many insults from sinners. Then you won't get discouraged and give up.
4None of you have yet been hurt in your battle against sin. 5 But you have forgotten that the Scriptures say to God's children,
“When the Lord punishes you,
don't make light of it,
and when he corrects you,
don't be discouraged.
6The Lord corrects the people
he loves
and disciplines those
he calls his own.”
7Be patient when you are being corrected! This is how God treats his children. Don't all parents correct their children? 8God corrects all his children, and if he doesn't correct you, then you don't really belong to him. 9Our earthly fathers correct us, and we still respect them. Isn't it even better to be given true life by letting our spiritual Father correct us?
10Our human fathers correct us for a short time, and they do it as they think best. But God corrects us for our own good, because he wants us to be holy, as he is. 11It is never fun to be corrected. In fact, at the time it is always painful. But if we learn to obey by being corrected, we will do right and live at peace.
12 Now stand up straight! Stop your knees from shaking 13 and walk a straight path. Then lame people will be healed, instead of getting worse.
Warning against Turning from God
14Try to live at peace with everyone! Live a clean life. If you don't, you will never see the Lord. 15 Make sure no one misses out on God's wonderful kindness. Don't let anyone become bitter and cause trouble for the rest of you. 16 Watch out for immoral and ungodly people like Esau, who sold his future blessing for only one meal. 17 You know how he later wanted it back. But there was nothing he could do to change things, even though he begged his father and cried.
18 You have not come to a place like Mount Sinai that can be seen and touched. There is no flaming fire or dark cloud or storm 19or trumpet sound. The people of Israel heard a voice speak. But they begged it to stop, 20 because they could not obey its commands. They were even told to kill any animal that touched the mountain. 21The sight was so frightening that Moses said he shook with fear.
22You have now come to Mount Zion and to the heavenly Jerusalem. This is the city of the living God, where thousands and thousands of angels have come to celebrate. 23Here you will find all of God's dearest children, whose names are written in heaven. And you will find God himself, who judges everyone. Here also are the spirits of those good people who have been made perfect. 24 And Jesus is here! He is the one who makes God's new agreement with us, and his sprinkled blood says much better things than the blood of Abel.
25 Make sure you obey the one who speaks to you. The people did not escape, when they refused to obey the one who spoke to them at Mount Sinai. Do you think you can possibly escape, if you refuse to obey the one who speaks to you from heaven? 26 When God spoke the first time, his voice shook only the earth. This time he has promised to shake the earth once again, and heaven too.
27The words “once again” mean that these created things will someday be shaken and removed. Then what cannot be shaken will last. 28We should be grateful we were given a kingdom that cannot be shaken. And in this kingdom we please God by worshiping him and by showing him great honor and respect. 29 Our God is like a destructive fire!
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizii yaa Mɛɛ
1Awia, nɛkpila naa maa n chigɛ bar yaa, di ra binni yaa kennaa, a dɛkkɔɔ yaa n niŋ ɛɛ lugɔ chɔchɔɔra, di lizi kuntɔga ni wichɔgaa maa yaa ni ha, di kpa kanyitti chɔ ra la maga la Kɔraawiizi n dauwɛ tɛɛ yaa la, 2di ɔɔ ra binni Yeesu la n ɛɛ yaa yarda maa nyuu hiŋ la. Waabuu faa kuu bɔsɔna la un niŋ wa di wia, di di tɔɔrɔɔ daakaŋlii ni la. U faa waa hiihzi wia kuuwɛ vɛɛ, ka jaa so Kɔraawiizi koorikara nabɔmbɔr la. 3Ií ra liizi gunla nɛchɔgaa n faa chagzuu, ka u di baa kanyitti la, ka ii gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra wàá huah, ii wa bir ra laŋŋi harbɔɔ.
4Iinna yoo wichɔgaa naa, ii haa waa yoowe ii challi lii. 5Ii waa bɔr la baŋ yir ia biizi la wia ra liizi. Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ,
“N bie, di Kɔraawiizi tɛr i digni,
gilɛɛ waa binni guŋ pɛɛ.
Gilɛɛ gil guŋ
chɔg i biini,
6dikuubɛɛwiai, banla un nɔŋŋɛɛ dignaa u ra tɛrgi, bá wer zum wia,
di kaa lɔɔzi bie la maa
unna yir
u himmaa bie.”
7Awia, dignitɛraa naa, ií ra di guŋ kanyitti. Kɔraawiizi kpa iabuu birgi u biizi. Mɛɛ waa u bie digni ra tɛraa? 8Di waa ii digna ra tɛrgi gunla unna tɛrgi u biizi maa digna la, amɔ, ii waa u biizi ɛɛwɛ. Ii ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ biizii. 9Yaa dɔɔ banla n ɛɛ yaa mɛɛwaarɛ, dikuu baŋ lul yaa ni yaa bɔrahɔna wia. Ba faa ra tɛrgi yaa dignaa, ka yaa sɛɛ tɛɛ baa. Gunla yaa n faa ra tɔgzi yaa mɛɛwaa la, a dɛkkɔɔ ya ra sɛɛ yaa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n du chiŋ dɔɔra werge maa kaali guŋ, di na miibɔɔ. 10Yaa mɛɛwaa la faa tɛrgi yaa dignaa hɔpizaa tama biini gunla baŋ nawɛɛ la. Kɔraawiiziwaa ra ɛɛ gunnɛ, á wer lii tɔna tɛɛ yaa, ya ɛɛ nɛnanaa la n waa doŋa maa dɔɔwɛ gunla u ge n duwɛɛ la. 11Saŋa la unna tɛrgi yaa digna la, bɔsɔna wia lɛi. Biinichɔgrɛ. Ka di a wa ɛɛ tama, yaa daŋ na, di u gillɔ yaa birgi nɛnanaa dɔɔ bampirsɔna.
12Awia, ií du banla bɔra n huahwɛ bɔkpega, bá wer chi chigigi. 13“Ií ra kuari ŋmɛnizi á ra deŋli, ií wer vol a ni, nɛ́r la n na dugzi kpuŋe gilɛɛ waa lii a bɔɔni, ka á wer nyaagi.”
Kɔraawiizi vɛɛi karfaazi wia
14Ií aah siwii ra nyiŋŋi nuukpaŋ, di aah siwii, ií wer ɛɛ nɛnanaa la n waa doŋa maa dɔɔwɛ la. Nɛr la maa n waa guŋ duwɛɛ, wàá wer na yaa Dɔɔri. 15Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ u nɛsunaa ni hiinaare werge maa, ú wer hiini ia. Awia, ií ra du tau, nɛ́r maa gilɛɛ waa huhzuu. Di guŋ lɛi, wichɔgii bɛl daŋ wa zuu ii biine chɔgi nɛkpila alugɔ kunnyɛg n ɔɔ zuu ii diwee biine, di chɔgaa a nyɛgi la. 16Ií gilɛɛ gil sɛnsɛnni ni nɛr la n vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi du ii biini. Ɛsau la faa du gunnɛ, di kpa u nabɔnzi la un niŋ faa di u niwee ni dikuu uŋ ɛɛ biinabɔma la wia chɛr diwee di. 17Ii zummɔ lugɔ uŋ kaa waa nyiŋŋi ú mɛɛ kissuu, ú bir na gunla maa biinabɔma n niŋ na la, waa kaa na guŋ. U faa aah siwiire ra nyiŋŋi gunla un niŋ na la di ra wii gba. Ka waa kaa wer u bir wia la á kaa du gunla aŋ faa duwɛɛ la.
18Iiŋ ŋɔ ií ba Kɔraawiizi be naa, kunla iin niŋ wer gbɔgzi be lɛi ii ra ba alugɔ Izrɛl hina n faa ba Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ la. A bizeŋ faa ra gbɔgzuu ra lau niŋ guŋ zagzagzag. Baŋ faa ba u zɛɛ la, bɔr la maa biroore di du limpiriŋ, peu ra ta fuufuufuufuu, 19bensunozenzeŋ ra wii, loobii bɛl ra ŋɔ wia. Nɛra la n wa nuu loobii la, ba fɔrguu ú gilɛɛ kaa ŋɔ wia ba be, 20dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di kummaa, haali sel wa gbɔgzi bizeŋ la, bá kpa bia lɔɔzuu kpu ta.” Guŋ faa tir baa werge maa. 21Bizeŋ la wia faa dɔɔ ɔnsiirɛ werge maa. Awiarɛ Moosis ŋɔ, “Ɔnsii lawimbuu, n bɔra ra sa.”
22Ka iawaa, iiŋ ŋɔ ii ba Kɔraawiizi be naa, Bizeŋ Ziɔn ni Jɛrusalɛm la n du u be la benii ii ra ba. Unla n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa la bolle a Jɛrusalɛm. U mɛlikananaa kpila maa du de. 23U biinabɔnzi la n ɛɛ u kapɛttɛ diire, ba sɔna du hɔŋ la n du u be la biini la gba chaalɔɔrɛ de. Ba ni Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ nɛra maa seriya diiri la benii ii ra ba ni lalaa la ŋmɛnizi n faa deŋlee, Kɔraawiizi gil ba birgi nɛnanaa la be, 24ni Yeesu la n kuari yaa ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋfalii dɔɔi la be ani bɔr la u chal n mizɛɛ la be. U chal la dɔɔ hiinaare yaa be werge maa. Waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ Abɛl hor la.
25Ií ra dazi di gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ unla n na ŋɔ wia ii be la. Di saŋa la hina la n faa vɛɛ unla n du hɛri karfi baa la waa wette lɛɛ bahinaa, yaa banla n vɛɛ unla n du chiŋ ra karfi yaa la, ɛrɛɛ ya ge wer ɛɛ lɛɛ yaa hinaanɛi? 26A saŋa u loobii gbɔgzɔɔrɛ, hɛri ra zigli. Ka u ŋɔ nua bɛllɛ filaŋkeŋ di ŋɔ, “N daŋ kaa zigli hɛri kakpaŋ bɛŋ. Ama, hɛri bɛŋ lɛi ń zigli a saŋa. Chiŋ ni hɛri maanii ń zigli.” 27Uŋ ŋɔ, “kakpaŋ bɛŋ” la, u zɛɛrɛ lugɔ di u wa ziglaa, u daŋ lizi kuna la maa un niŋ wer zigli la ha, ka anla n waa ziglaa dɔɔwɛ la wer ka. 28Awia, Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ yaa du u kora la n waa ziglaa dɔɔwɛ biini naa, a wesso yaa n na tɛu jaaŋ saŋa maa, di ra humuu gunla n paruu, di ra tɔgzuu di ra ɔmuu, 29dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niŋ la n wette di ra fuuh kuna werge la.

english_text:
Service That Pleases God
1Keep being concerned about each other as the Lord's followers should.
2 Be sure to welcome strangers into your home. By doing this, some people have welcomed angels as guests, without even knowing it.
3Remember the Lord's people who are in jail and be concerned for them. Don't forget those who are suffering, but imagine you are there with them.
4 Have respect for marriage. Always be faithful to your partner, because God will punish anyone who is immoral or unfaithful in marriage.
5 Don't fall in love with money. Be satisfied with what you have. The Lord has promised that he will not leave us or desert us. 6 This should make you feel like saying,
“The Lord helps me!
Why should I be afraid
of what people
can do to me?”
7Don't forget about your leaders who taught you God's message. Remember what kind of lives they lived and try to have faith like theirs.
8Jesus Christ never changes! He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. 9Don't be fooled by any kind of strange teachings. It is better to receive strength from God's gift of undeserved grace than to depend on certain foods. After all, these foods don't really help the people who eat them. 10But we have an altar where even the priests who serve in the place of worship have no right to eat.
11 After the high priest offers the blood of animals as a sin offering, the bodies of those animals are burned outside the camp. 12Jesus himself suffered outside the city gate, so his blood would make people holy. 13This is why we should go outside the camp to Jesus and share in his disgrace. 14On this earth we don't have a city that lasts forever, but we are waiting for such a city.
15Our sacrifice is to keep offering praise to God in the name of Jesus. 16But don't forget to help others and to share your possessions with them. This too is like offering a sacrifice that pleases God.
17Obey your leaders and do what they say. They are watching over you, and they must answer to God. So don't make them sad as they do their work. Make them happy. Otherwise, they won't be able to help you at all.
18Pray for us. Our consciences are clear, and we always try to live right. 19I especially want you to pray that I can visit you again soon.
Final Prayers and Greetings
20God gives peace, and he raised our Lord Jesus Christ from death. Now Jesus is like a Great Shepherd whose blood was used to make God's eternal agreement with his flock. 21 I pray God will make you ready to obey him and that you will always be eager to do right. May Jesus help you do what pleases God. To Jesus Christ be glory forever and ever! Amen.
22My friends, I have written only a short letter to encourage you, and I beg you to pay close attention to what I have said.
23By now you surely must know that our friend Timothy is out of jail. If he gets here in time, I will bring him with me when I come to visit you.
24Please give my greetings to your leaders and to the rest of the Lord's people.
His followers from Italy send you their greetings.
25I pray that God will be kind to all of you!
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi kipar ɛɛi wia
1Ií haa ra kpa dɔŋa lugɔ maa biizi di nɔŋŋi dɔŋa. 2Ií gilɛɛ ra suuh hɔɔhra wia, ka ɔɔ lɛɛ baa ra dau. Baŋhina faa lɛɛ Kɔraawiizi mɛlikazii dau ka ba waa zummɛ. 3Ií ra liizi banla baŋ tɔwɛɛ dia wia alugɔ ii ni baa maanii ba tɔ dia la, di gil ii bɔra ra nyiiri banla banna tɔɔri la ni dikuu ii gba n dɔɔ bɔrahɔna wia.
4Ií gil nɛr maa ra tɔgzi hahdɔɔi, di gilɛɛ ra chɔɔ nɛdumazi be. Kɔraawiizi daŋ di banla n na ɛɛ wikuna, di ra sɛm la seriya, bá chol. 5Ií gilɛɛ kpa kebee su siwii. Ií gil kunla iin dɔɔwɛ la kukki ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi himmaa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,
“Màá ɛɛ ii wia vɛɛlai maa.
Màá gil ii ta maa.”
6Awia, yaa daŋ wer dɔɔ bɔsɔna, di ŋɔ,
“N Dɔɔri ra hiinimbuu.
Maa ɔm.
Bɛɛ newee
kaa wer ɛɛnnɛi?”
7Ií ra liizi ii nabɔnzi la n bagli ia Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlaa la be. Ií ra binni gunla baŋ hiŋŋɛ ani gunla ba ni Kɔraawiizi yarda dɔɔi ge n duwɛɛ, di ge ra hiŋ guŋ.
8Yeesu Kristo waa birgaa maa dɔɔwɛ. Gunla un dɛɛ duwɛɛ la, gunnɛ u du zinaa gba. U daŋ ɔɔ haa du guŋ saŋa maa ra la. 9Wibaglaa ni a dizi du denii ɛɛ witittaa. Ií gilɛɛ ra sɛɛa di ra leuzi. A wesso yaa n na nyiŋŋi bɔkpega lii Kɔraawiizi hiinaa biini, di gilɛɛ ra nyiŋŋaa diwee aŋhina dee dii biini. Banla n na dia gunla waa hiinaa ra na a be. 10Yaa dɔɔ mbusu lizibɔr bɛllɛ banla n na hum Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la biini n waa dɛkkɛ ban ninna di de.
11Sela la baŋ ɔɔ kpu lizi a challi, Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma kpaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la tɛu, dikuu wichɔgaa wia la, ba ɔɔ kpa a sela hinnɛ lii danzɛɛkɛrii ga fuuah de. 12Awiarɛ Yeesu n faa ra siu, ú himmaa chal wer sɔ nɛra doŋa ba ni ha la, bol danzɛɛ kɛriirɛ u du di faa ra di tɔɔrɔɔ la. 13Awia, ií gil ya ge lii la u be danzɛɛ kɛrii la, yáa maa kpau ra di hiihzi la uŋ faa diwee la, 14dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa waa bol dɔɔwɛ durnya naa biini, yá du ra la. Yaa ra nyiŋŋi bol la n haa du har ra ba la duirɛ.
15Awia, ya ɔɔ ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi saŋa maa, Yeesu fɔŋŋa biini, á ɛɛ lugɔ mbusu u be yaa n lizɛɛ ra tɛu, dikuu yaa n sɛɛ u dɔɔra la wia. 16Ya gilɛɛ suuh winanaa ɛɛi wia, ka ɔɔ bɔnni yaa kuna ra tɛɛ nɛra. Guŋ gba ɛɛ mbusuzii ra par Kɔraawiizi. 17Ií ra hiŋ ii nabɔnzi nuuzi, di ra sɛɛ ba dɔɔra, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ra du ii dunzi taurɛ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ wa pɛɛzi baa ii wia. Awia, ií ra sɛɛ ba dɔɔra, bá wer ra hum ba huma la ni bɔsɔna, di gilɛɛ ra humaa ni biinichɔg. Guŋ wàá hiini ia.
18Ií ɔɔ suŋŋi wiizi ra tɛɛ yaa. Yaa zummɔ lugɔ yaa biine wàá tɔɔri yaa ani wiimaa wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu ya ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee. 19N kaa ra suŋŋi iabuu werge maa, ií suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi, ú gil n wer bir ba ii be manaŋ.
20Kɔ́raawiizi la n ɛɛ bampirsɔna hiŋ, unla n lalli yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu siu biini u ɛɛ Penɔɔnizeŋ, dikuu un siuwɛ u chal kuari nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la n wàá chɔgi maa wia la, 21Kɔraawiizi hiini ia, ií wer dɔɔ bampirsɔna la iin niŋ dɔɔ, di wer ra ɛɛ u kipar. Ú hum u huma yaa maa biine, ya wer du gunla maa n paruu Yeesu Kristo fɔŋŋa biini. Waabuu niŋ dɔɔ girme saŋa maa di ra la. Ami.
22N kaa ra suŋŋi iabuu, yaabalaa, ií nuu ra tɛŋ ani wia naa mim bagli ia naa biini. Maa sɛbɛɛ werge.
23Ba lizi yaa dɔŋhiŋ Timotii nɛra tɔi dia la biini. Di u wa ballɔ manaŋ, n nuu maa daŋ ba wa na ia. 24Ií ra jaami ii nabɔnzi maa ni Kɔraawiizi biinanaa la maa. Banla n ɛɛ Itali hina la ra jaami ia.
25Kɔ́raawiizi nɛsunnaa ni u hiinaa du ii maa be.

english_text:
1 From James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Greetings to the twelve tribes scattered all over the world.
Faith and Wisdom
2 My friends, be glad, even if you have a lot of trouble. 3You know you learn to endure by having your faith tested. 4But you must learn to endure everything, so you will be completely mature and not lacking in anything.
5 If any of you need wisdom, you should ask God, and it will be given to you. God is generous and won't correct you for asking. 6But when you ask for something, you must have faith and not doubt. Anyone who doubts is like an ocean wave tossed around in a storm. 7-8If you are that kind of person, you can't make up your mind, and you surely can't be trusted. So don't expect the Lord to give you anything at all.
Poor People and Rich People
9Any of God's people who are poor should be glad he thinks so highly of them. 10 But any who are rich should be glad when God makes them humble. Rich people will disappear like wild flowers 11scorched by the burning heat of the sun. The flowers lose their blossoms, and their beauty is destroyed. This is how the rich will disappear, as they go about their business.
Trials and Temptations
12 God will bless you, if you don't give up when your faith is being tested. He will reward you with a glorious life, just as he rewards everyone who loves him.
13 Don't blame God when you are tempted! God cannot be tempted by evil, and he doesn't use evil to tempt others. 14We are tempted by our own desires that drag us off and trap us. 15Our desires make us sin, and when sin is finished with us, it leaves us dead.
16Don't be fooled, my dear friends. 17Every good and perfect gift comes down from the Father who created all the lights in the heavens. He is always the same and never makes dark shadows by changing. 18He wanted us to be his own special people, and so he sent the true message to give us new birth.
Hearing and Obeying
19 My dear friends, you should be quick to listen and slow to speak or to get angry. 20If you are angry, you cannot do any of the good things God wants done. 21You must stop doing anything immoral or evil. Instead be humble and accept the message planted in you to save you.
22Obey God's message! Don't fool yourselves by just listening to it. 23If you hear the message and don't obey it, you are like people who stare at themselves in a mirror 24and forget what they look like as soon as they leave. 25But you must never stop looking at the perfect law that sets you free. God will bless you in everything you do, if you listen and obey, and don't just hear and forget.
26If you think you are being religious, but can't control your tongue, you are fooling yourself, and your religion is useless. 27Religion that pleases God the Father must be pure and spotless. You must help needy orphans and widows and not let this world make you evil.
translation_text:
1Mìŋ́ Jems n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo baliirɛ ra sɛbi hɔnnaa, di ra tɛɛ ii banla n ɛɛ Yeesu hiŋra di yaari du yemmaa la. N na jaami ia.
Yarda ni nunzuma wia
2Yaabalaa, di tɔɔrɔɔ kpila wa huuzi ia, ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia werge. 3Ií zum lugɔ di tɔɔrɔɔ maa wa ɛɛ ia di na ka ii haa wer dɔɔ yarda di ra hiŋ, amɔ, gunnɛ niŋ gil ii ɔɔ wer dɔɔ kanyitti. 4Ama, ii gilɛɛ gil ii kanyitti dii waa tuŋ, ka ií haa vɛɛ ra di kanyitti guŋŋ ú wer kuari ia nɛnnɛ di wa tuŋ, ií wer zum wiimaa nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa nyaa mananaa dee maa. 5Di hinla maa ra nyiŋŋi nunzuma, amɔ, í ra suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ú tɛi. Waa ɔɔ ra nyɛg banla n na suŋŋuu guŋ ni, ka u ɔɔ ra tɛɛ baabuu werge maa. Di i suŋŋuu, i daŋ na kunla hiŋ suŋŋɛɛ u be. 6Ka di ii ra suŋŋuu, ií ra suŋŋuu ni yarda, di gilɛɛ ra aani. Nɛr la n na suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ka ra aani lugɔ wàá tɛu la, a hiŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ muuzeŋ la peu n niŋ wer bir u nii di ra la bɔr maa labuu. 7Ú gilɛɛ ra binni lugɔ u daŋ na kunla maa un suŋŋɛɛ Kɔraawiizi be. 8Nfɛssi anɛɛ hinnɛ ra chol. U wiimaa wàá wer kuari.
9Di i ɛɛ Yeesu hiŋri ka ɛɛ nyaari, ka í gil i bɔra sɔɔnii. I ɛɛ nɛzenne Kɔraawiizi be. 10Di i ɛɛ daama hiŋ genii, ka í gil i ni nyaara nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la sɔɔni i bɔra, dikuubɛɛwiai, u daŋ siu lugɔ pir fiiri. 11Gunla wiizi n ɔɔ baŋ di lɔ, koorii hil, u fiiri yɔl, u wessi chɔgi la, gunnɛ daama hiŋ ge ɔɔ ɛɛ u wia ka bir wa siu la.
12Hinla maa n dɔɔ kanyitti di ra di tɔɔrɔɔ, gil i bɔra sɔɔnii. Di a tɔɔrɔɔ ɛɛi guŋŋ di wa huhzi, ka i haa vɛɛ ra hiŋ ani kanyitti, i daŋ na tɔna. Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛi u miibɔɔ la uŋ faa ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ banla maa n nɔŋŋuu la.
13Di kummaa wa darii lugɔ í ɛɛ wichɔgaa, gilɛɛ ŋɔ Kɔraawiizii darii. Kummaa wàá wer dar Kɔraawiizi ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa. U ge gba wàá dar nɛr maa ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa. 14Kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa la n du bɛl maa bampirii labuu ɔɔ ra daruu, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Aabuu ɔɔ ra da u zɛɛ. 15Kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa a lul wichɔgaarɛ. Di wichɔgaa ge wa hello tuŋ, a ge ɔɔ lul siu.
16N nɛnɔŋŋaa, ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa dar u hiŋ. 17Wii la maa n wesse di ɛɛ winanii himmaa, Kɔraawiizi benii u lii, u kpa sunzi yaa. Kuna la maa n na chaani chiŋ, Kɔraawiizii ta a maa. Ka u himmaa waa ɔɔ bir kur gunla aŋ ɔɔ bir kur, di ra tɔ yaa chunchugle la. 18U himmaa kipar wiarɛ yaa wer nuu u wibii wiŋɔzi, di wer birgi u biizi, di ɛɛ u kunnanaa un lizɛɛ tɛɛ u hiŋ, u kuna la maa un tawɛɛ la biini.
Kɔraawiizi wia nuui ni a ɛɛi wia
19Ií ra liizi guŋ, yaabalaa. A dɛkkɔ nɛr maa n hahzee ra nuu nɛra be, ka sɔɔni bɔra ra ŋɔ wia, di gilɛɛ gil u baaŋ na fuuh manamanaŋ. 20Newee baaŋfuuih waa wikuarii maa dɔɔwɛ winanaa hiŋaa la Kɔraawiizi n na nyiŋŋi la biini. 21Awia, ií lizi wichɔgaa maa ii ni di ha ani wijagazi la maa n kannɛ werge ii be la. Ií lizi a maa ha ka dɔɔ sisɔna di nuu ra tɛɛ u wiŋɔzi la uŋ kpawɛɛ du ii bampiree biine la. A wiŋɔzi daŋ wer lɛɛ ii dunzi ha.
22Ama, ii gilɛɛ ra nuu ka ra vɛɛ a hiŋaa. Di ii ra nuu u wiŋɔzi la, ka ii wàá ra hiŋ, ii ra dar iihinaarɛ. 23Ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr la n na binni digii 24di ra na u hiŋ de, ka bir a kaali la. Di u wa kaalɔɔ tuŋ, ɔɔ bir suuh gunla maa un duwɛɛ la. 25Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la n wesse werge di ga tuŋ di lɛɛ yaa, yaa wer dɔɔ yaa hinaa la, u ɛɛ digiire. Nɛr la maa n ninna binni Kɔraawiizi digii la biini di ra pessi wiŋɔɔlaa la nɛnnɛ, waa ra suuh, ka ra hiŋ gunla maa un nawɛɛ de, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u nuu suma u wiɛɛlaa maa biini.
26Di nɛr la maa ra binni lugɔ u ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizii, ka waa u himmaa nua tau ra du, u ra dar u hinnɛ. Himpɛɛrɛ u ra hiŋ la. 27Wii la maa n par yaa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi di du wer u benii keŋ, waabuu lugɔ hinna binni lalbiizi ni luhaana la n na di dɔgnya, di ra hiini baa, di kaa ra binni i hiŋ ni, di gilɛɛ gil durnya wichɔgaa maa waa pɛli i ni.

english_text:
Warning against Having Favorites
1My friends, if you have faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, you won't treat some people better than others. 2Suppose a rich person wearing fancy clothes and a gold ring comes to one of your meetings. And suppose a poor person dressed in worn-out clothes also comes. 3You must not give the best seat to the one in fancy clothes and tell the one who is poor to stand at the side or sit on the floor. 4This is the same as saying that some people are better than others, and you would be acting like a crooked judge.
5My dear friends, pay attention. God has given a lot of faith to the poor people in this world. God has also promised them a share in his kingdom that he will give to everyone who loves him. 6You mistreat the poor. But isn't it the rich who boss you around and drag you off to court? 7Aren't they the ones who make fun of your Lord?
8 You will do all right, if you obey the most important law in the Scriptures. It is the law that commands us to love others as much as we love ourselves. 9But if you treat some people better than others, you have done wrong, and the Scriptures teach that you have sinned.
10 If you obey every law except one, you are still guilty of breaking them all. 11 The same God who told us to be faithful in marriage also told us not to murder. So even if you are faithful in marriage, but murder someone, you still have broken God's Law.
12Speak and act like people who will be judged by the law that sets us free. 13Do this, because on the day of judgment there will be no pity for those who have not had pity on others. But even in judgment, God is merciful!
Faith and Works
14My friends, what good is it to say you have faith, when you don't do anything to show you really do have faith? Can this kind of faith save you? 15If you know someone who doesn't have any clothes or food, 16you shouldn't just say, “I hope all goes well for you. I hope you will be warm and have plenty to eat.” What good is it to say this, unless you do something to help? 17Faith that doesn't lead us to do good deeds is all alone and dead!
18Suppose someone disagrees and says, “It is possible to have faith without doing kind deeds.”
I would answer, “Prove that you have faith without doing kind deeds, and I will prove that I have faith by doing them.” 19You surely believe there is only one God. That's fine. Even demons believe this, and it makes them shake with fear.
20Does some stupid person want proof that faith without deeds is useless? 21 Well, our ancestor Abraham pleased God by putting his son Isaac on the altar to sacrifice him. 22Now you see how Abraham's faith and deeds worked together. He proved his faith was real by what he did. 23 This is what the Scriptures mean by saying, “Abraham had faith in God, and God accepted him.” That's how Abraham became God's friend.
24You can now see that we please God by what we do and not only by what we believe. 25 For example, Rahab had been a prostitute. But she pleased God when she welcomed the spies and sent them home by another way.
26Anyone who doesn't breathe is dead, and faith that doesn't do anything is just as dead!
translation_text:
Nɛtɔgzaa karfaa wia
1Yaabalaa, di ii ra hiŋ yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo la n ɛɛ girme maa dɔɔri la, amɔ, ii gilɛɛ ra tɔgzi baŋhina di kaali baŋhina. 2Di ii maa chaalɔɔ ra jaami Kɔraawiizi, nɛra banɛɛ wa zuu ii be, bɛl du u saliŋ nonibisiga ni u daama laala, bɛl ge laali kuŋkɔssi, 3di ii bagli daama hiŋ la karnanii di ŋɔ ú wa so, ka ŋɔ kuŋkɔssi hiŋ la ge chi gɛɛ ú ba wa so ii naazi zɛɛ, 4amɔ, ii ra tɔgzi baŋhinaa kaali baŋhina la. Ii hiŋaa wàá dɔɔ wibii di wa tuŋ. Ii birgi sitɔɔra la n ɔɔ kpa kuna wia su siwii labuu.
5Yaabalaa, ií ra binni Kɔraawiizi ge wiɛɛlaa. Nyaara lɛi u liziaa? U lizi baabuu bá wer yarduu werge, bá yarda la ɛɛ ba daama, ka bá wer na u kora biini zuu gunla uŋ faa ŋɔ nua lugɔ banla maa n nɔŋŋuu, daŋ zuu u kora biini la. 6Ka iawaa ra gbɛlli nyaara. Daama hina lɛi ɔɔ ra fir ia di ra sami ia, di kpa ia ra la seriya dii bɔra laa? 7Baa lɛi ɔɔ ra gbɛlli Yeesu sɔnnanii la baŋ ɔɔ kpa ra yir ia laa?
8Di ii ra hiŋ yaa koori widaulii la baŋ sɛbɛɛ du u hɔŋ biini lugɔ í nɔŋŋi i dɔŋhiŋ gunla hin nɔŋŋi i hiŋ la, amɔ, ii ra hiŋuu nɛnnɛ la. 9Ka di ii ra tɔgzi baŋhina kaali baŋhina, ii ra ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg lɛi ii ra chɔgiaa? U daŋ di ia seriya ii chol. 10Di i hiŋ Gbɔgni la maa ka wa chɔg kpaŋkpaŋ, ka i chɔg a maanii. Gbɔgni la daŋ tɛi chɔgri, 11dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Gilɛɛ wàá sɛm,” di kaa ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ wàá kpu.” Di haa sɛm, ka kpu nɛr, amɔ, hàá Gbɔgni la chɔkkɛaa?
12Ii gil ii wiŋɔzi ni ii wiɛɛlaa maa du wer, dikuubɛɛwiai, Gbɔgni la n dɔɔ hiinaa, di lɛɛ nɛra bá wer dɔɔ bahinaa labuu, bá wa kpa di di ia seriya. 13Nɛr la maa n waa u dɔŋahina ni ra suŋ, di u seriya dii wa hello, Kɔraawiizi wàá suŋ u ge ni. Ka nɛr la n na suŋ u dɔŋahina ni, wàá ɔm u ge seriya dii.
Yarda ni wiɛɛlaa wia
14Yaabalaa, di nɛbɛl ŋɔ lugɔ u yardi Kɔraawiizii, ka waa winanaa ra ɛɛ, pɛɛrɛ. U yarda hiŋ wàá gil ú na lɛɛi Kɔraawiizi be. 15Di i dɔŋhiŋ bɛl waa kunlaalii dɔɔwɛ ú tɔ u bɔra, waa diwee dɔɔwɛ ú di, ka ba i be, 16i ŋɔ u be, “Kɔ́raawiizi la i ni di ga tɛi kuna la hinna nyiŋŋi í tɔ i bɔra, di kaa tɛi kuna la hin niŋ di.” Ka hiŋwaa waa sɛɛwɛ í tɛu kuna la maa unna nyiŋŋi, yarda naa hiŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi naa, bɛɛ wikuariirɛ u dɔɔ naanɛi? Kumpɛɛrɛ. 17Di i yardi Kɔraawiizi ka haa winanaa ɛɛi maa dɔɔwɛ jaa i yarda la ni, ka dɔɔ yarda la bɛŋ, amɔ, kumpɛɛrɛ i dɔɔ la.
18Aŋhina be, ii bɛl daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ bɛl hotte Kɔraawiizi yarda dɔɔi, bɛl ge horuu winanaa ɛɛi. Ka hàá wer bargaa guŋ. Hinla n ŋɔ i yardi Kɔraawiizii la, ɛrɛɛ í ɛɛ bagli i Kɔraawiizi yarda dɔɔi la, di haa winanaa maa ɛɛwɛi? Ka n ge daŋ ɛɛ winanaa, ń winanaa la ɛɛi baglii lugɔ n yardi Kɔraawiizii. 19I yardɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kpaŋkpaŋ bɛnnɛ du dee? Mhmm. Tinnanchɔgaa gba yardi gunnɛ, a bɔra a sa.
20Gɛniirɛ hiŋ! Gil ń dii wibii, í zum lugɔ nɛr la maa n yardi Kɔraawiizi, ka waa winanii ɛɛi maa dɔɔwɛ jaa u yarda la ni, u yarda hiŋ ɛɛ wipɛɛrii. 21Binni yaa naabaal Abraham wia biini na. Saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ ú ɛɛu na, di ŋɔ ú kpu u bie Aizik lizi mbusu tɛu la, u wiɛɛlaa lɛi Kɔraawiizi faa binni di ŋɔ lugɔ Abraham ra hiŋ ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ, u wia maa deŋlia? 22Haa na gunla u Kɔraawiizi yardaa la n gillɛ u ɛɛ winanaa, u winanaa ɛɛi hiŋ gil u yarda dɔɔi wer du wer di wa tunaa? 23Gunla baŋ faa ŋɔ u wia Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini la ɛɛ wibiire. Ba ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Abraham yardi Kɔraawiizii. Kɔraawiizi gil u wia deŋli u be, ba jaa ra yiruu Kɔraawiizi dammu.” 24Awia, di nɛr yardi Kɔraawiizi ka ra ɛɛ winanaa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u ɛɛ nɛnanii u be. Un yarduu bɛŋ wia lɛi ú ɛɛ guŋ tɛu.
25Ií kaa binni Rahab ge wia biini. A Rahab faa ɛɛ hahsɛnsɛnnii, ka uŋ faa wette lɛɛ huŋhunna la dau, di kaa hiini baa ba wer kpa ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛl di suahzi kaali la wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi faa gil u birgi nɛnanii u be.
26Awia, ií kpa bɔrahɔŋ ani duma di mɛgzi wia naa. Di bɔrahɔŋ waa duma dɔɔwɛ, u ɛɛ kumpɛɛrɛ. Gunnɛ di yarda waa winanaa ɛɛi dɔɔwɛ jaa u ni, u ge gba ɛɛ kumpɛɛ la.

english_text:
The Tongue
1My friends, we should not all try to become teachers. In fact, teachers will be judged more strictly than others. 2 All of us do many wrong things. But if you can control your tongue, you are mature and able to control your whole body.
3By putting a bit into the mouth of a horse, we can turn the horse in different directions. 4It takes strong winds to move a large sailing ship, but the captain uses only a small rudder to make it go in any direction. 5Our tongues are small too, and yet they brag about big things.
It takes only a spark to start a forest fire! 6 The tongue is like a spark. It is an evil power that dirties the rest of the body and sets a person's entire life on fire with flames that come from hell itself. 7All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures can be tamed and have been tamed. 8But our tongues get out of control. They are restless and evil, and always spreading deadly poison.
9-10 My dear friends, with our tongues we speak both praises and curses. We praise our Lord and Father, and we curse people who were created to be like God, and this isn't right. 11Can clean water and dirty water both flow from the same spring? 12Can a fig tree produce olives or a grapevine produce figs? Does fresh water come from a well full of salt water?
Wisdom from Above
13 Are any of you wise or sensible? Then show it by living right and by being humble and wise in everything you do. 14But if your heart is full of bitter jealousy and selfishness, don't brag or lie to cover up the truth. 15This kind of wisdom doesn't come from above. It is earthly and selfish and comes from the devil himself. 16Whenever people are jealous or selfish, they cause trouble and do all sorts of cruel things. 17But the wisdom that comes from above leads us to be pure, friendly, gentle, sensible, kind, helpful, genuine, and sincere. 18When peacemakers plant seeds of peace, they will harvest justice.
translation_text:
Nuuzuŋŋi wia
1Yaabalaa, a waa wer iiŋ kpillɛ di ɛɛ bagla di ra bagli ii dɔŋahina. Ií zum lugɔ yaa banla n ɛɛ bagla, yaa ge seriya dii daŋ du kaŋ kaali baŋhina. 2Nɛr maanii ɛɛ wia ra leu. Nɛr la maa n du de u haa waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ leu, amɔ, a hiŋ ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ. Di u wetto ra lau u nua, amɔ, u daŋ wer lau u himmaa gba.
3Di i ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ zagu ra ɔmii, i daŋ kpa kabarga du u nua, di wer bir u maa ú ra la i kipar bɔr. 4Ií binni muugberzenaa la gba na. A kannɔzii werge. Pekpega ge ɔɔ taa ra kaali. Ka kunjiga bɛl ɔɔ wer deŋlaa a ra la bɔr la maa a muugbersaara nabɔma n na nyiŋŋi. 5Gunnɛ nuuzuŋŋi ge gba du. Waa kaŋ ka wer ra ɛɛ wizenaa. Ii waa nawɛɛ ninjiga n ɔɔ wer fuuh daakpila maa? 6Nuuzuŋŋi ge ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ a niŋ, di wer ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge maa, di wer kpa doŋa ra du yaa ni, di wer ra chɔgi yaa mananaa maa alugɔ niŋ n ɔɔ ra chɔgi kuna gunla. Sitaani ninne choŋŋuu la.
7Pir sela, zumbizi, kunjigzi ani muu biini kuna maa, newee wettoo ra dɛɛzi a maa, a ra pɛssi. 8Ka nuuzuŋŋiwaa, ba ɔɔ lau waabuurɛ di pɛssuu huhzi. U kuttɔɔrɛ dɔɔ wichɔgaa, di kpoŋ werge. U siri ge du kpeg lugɔ ú wer kpui. 9Waabuu yaa ɔɔ kpa ra jaami Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ yaa Mɛɛ. Waabuu yaa ɔɔ kaa kpa ra gbɛlli yaa dɔŋahina la Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ ba du gunla u ge n duwɛɛ la. 10Nuukpaŋ biinii Kɔraawiizi jaamaa ni gbɛllaa la maa ra lii. Nau! U guŋ waa dɛkkɛ, yaabalaa. 11Ii haa na gɔŋ maa n na bul niinanii ni niikpɛlɛkpɛlɛ maa? 12Fig daa waa ɔlivizi ra nɔŋ. Huu ge waa suula ra nɔŋ. Gunnɛ gɔŋ la n na bul niisum wàá wer bul niikpɛlɛkpɛlɛ la.
Nunzuma la n lii chiŋ wia
13Anɛɛ dɔɔ nunzuma ani sichaana ii biinei? Di i dɔɔ nunzuma, i danna kpa i hiŋ fugzi ka ra ɛɛ winanaa, í winanaa ɛɛi la bagli lugɔ i dɔɔ guŋ nunzuma ni sichaanaa. 14Ka di i dɔɔ bɔwii werge di ra nyiŋŋi i bɛŋ sɔŋ, gilɛɛ ra chɔli i hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ra dar i hinnɛ. Haa wibii dɔɔwɛ. 15Kɔraawiizi be nunzuma lɛi. Durnya nunzumaa. Newee ni Sitaani benii u lii. 16Bɔwii ni sɔnnyiŋŋaa haŋ wa zuu nɛra baaŋ, too, ba wiimaa a chɔguu, hunjagazi ni a dee maa ra lii. 17Nɛr la maa n dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi be nunzumawaa u wia maa ɔɔ du wer ninɛɛ parata. U ɔɔ dɔɔ bampirsɔna ani sisɔnaa, di wer sɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ kipar, di wer suŋ u ni di ra ɛɛu winanaa. A hiŋ wia waa ɔɔ dɔɔ aanaa maa, ka dɔɔ wibii. Waa baŋhina ra tɔgzi kaali baŋhina, ka dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu. 18Banla n na nyiŋŋi nuukpaŋ dɔɔi nɛra be, ba kpa nuukpaŋ dɔɔirɛ di ra duu ba kuna, a ra lii winanaa.

english_text:
Friendship with the World
1Why do you fight and argue with each other? Isn't it because you are full of selfish desires that fight to control your body? 2You want something you don't have, and you will do anything to get it. You will even kill! But you still cannot get what you want, and you won't get it by fighting and arguing. You should pray for it. 3Yet even when you do pray, your prayers are not answered, because you pray just for selfish reasons.
4You people aren't faithful to God! Don't you know if you love the world, you are God's enemies? And if you decide to be a friend of the world, you make yourself an enemy of God. 5Do you doubt the Scriptures that say, “God truly cares about the Spirit he has put in us”? 6 In fact, God treats us with even greater kindness, just as the Scriptures say,
“God opposes everyone
who is proud,
but he blesses all who are humble
with undeserved grace.”
7Surrender to God! Resist the devil, and he will run from you. 8Come near to God, and he will come near to you. Clean up your lives, you sinners.
