Denii ba faa kpu ba Dɔɔri daakaŋlii la ni la. 9Nɛra baŋhina n lii nɛdee maa n du hɛri yemmaa biini daŋ na lalaa la de, di ra binni baa hɔpizaa ahoro ni keza biini. Ba wàá sɛɛ bá hug baa. 10Durnya hina bɔra daŋ sɔɔni dikuu ba wia, ba ra di bahinaa di ra sunzi dɔŋa kuna, dikuu Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi banɛɛ la n faa ra tɔɔri baa werge la wia.
11Kenne n kaa na baala la wia. Hɔpizaa ahoro ni keza la n wa bɛrɛɛ, heeza lii Kɔraawiizi be di wa zuu ba ni, ba na miibɔɔ di izi chiŋ. Ɔnsii lau banla n chigɛ di ra binni baa la werge. 12Denii ba nuu loobizeŋ bɛl n lii chiŋ, di ra ŋɔ ba be, “Ií tinni ra ba ɛŋ.” Ba tinni la chiŋ baama biini, ba dɔma ra binni baa. 13Banna binni baa la, hɛri zigli werge maa, a bolzeŋ yeŋ chol. Di i faa bargi bolzeŋ la bɔra fi, u bɔkpannɛ cholle gunla. Nɛra kagboŋa aniidaanɛɛrɛ u kpu. Kafɔŋ lau banla n kawɛɛ la, ba ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la sɔŋ. 14Tɔɔrɔɔzenaa anɛɛhiŋ la bɛrɔɔrɛ kaali, ka horohiŋ la ra ba manamanaŋ.
Bɛnsuno aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la wia
15Mɛlika niidaanɛɛhiŋ la huuh. Uŋ huuhwɛ la, baŋhina n du Kɔraawiizi bol a ŋɔ fɔŋŋa ni,
“Durnya kossi jaa birgi yaa Dɔɔri ni u Kristo la kossii.
U daŋ dɔɔ baa saŋa maa
di ra la.”
16Nabɔnzi tokko ni banaazu n soge ba koorikassi ni Kɔraawiizi be la izi chɔɔ Kɔraawiizi see, di ra jaamuu, 17di ra ŋɔ,
“Yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
hinla n du de filaŋkeŋ,
di du de saŋa maa la,
yaa ra jaamii,
dikuubɛɛwiai, i kpa
fɔŋŋazenne jaa
dɔɔ kummaa.
18Durnya ni u dee maa baana fuuhwoo.
Ka i ge saŋa la i baaŋ n niŋ fuuh ba ni la helloo.
I daŋ jaa di lalaa seriya,
di turgi winanaa la
i balaa dɔgtɛɛzi,
i biinanaa la ani banla
maa n faa ɔmii la,
nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa maa kim,
di kaa chɔgi banla n na chɔgi durnya la.”
19Denii Kɔraawiizi Dia la n du chiŋ la pilli, ba na Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la. Dooŋ a nyɛgzi pilpilpil, loobee ra kɔɔ, nazaa ra pozi pababababa, hɛri ra zigli, dobizenaa ra chogli hɛri katikati.

english_text:
The Woman and the Dragon
1Something important appeared in the sky. It was a woman whose clothes were the sun. The moon was under her feet, and a crown made of twelve stars was on her head. 2She was about to give birth, and she was crying because of the great pain.
3 Something else appeared in the sky. It was a huge red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and a crown on each of its seven heads. 4 With its tail, it dragged a third of the stars from the sky and threw them down to the earth. Then the dragon turned toward the woman, because it wanted to eat her child as soon as it was born.
5 The woman gave birth to a son, who would rule all nations with an iron rod. The boy was snatched away. He was taken to God and placed on his throne. 6The woman ran into the desert to a place that God had prepared for her. There she would be taken care of for 1,260 days.
Michael Fights the Dragon
7 A war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels were fighting against the dragon and its angels. 8But the dragon lost the battle. It and its angels were forced out of their places in heaven 9 and were thrown down to the earth. Yes, that old snake and his angels were thrown out of heaven! That snake, who fools everyone on earth, is known as the devil and Satan. 10 Then I heard a voice from heaven shout,
“Our God has shown
his saving power,
and his kingdom has come!
God's own Chosen One
has shown his authority.
Satan accused our people
in the presence of God
day and night.
Now he has been thrown out!
11“Our people defeated Satan
because of the blood
of the Lamb
and the message of God.
They were willing
to give up their lives.
12“The heavens should rejoice,
together with everyone
who lives there.
But pity the earth
and the sea,
because the devil
was thrown down
to the earth.
He knows his time is short,
and he is very angry.”
13When the dragon realized it had been thrown down to the earth, it tried to make trouble for the woman who had given birth to a son. 14 But the woman was given two wings like those of a huge eagle, so she could fly into the desert. There she would escape from the snake and be taken care of for a time, two times, and half a time.
15The snake then spewed out water like a river to sweep the woman away. 16But the earth helped her and swallowed the water that had come from the dragon's mouth. 17This made the dragon terribly angry with the woman. So it started a war against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God and are faithful to what Jesus did and taught. 18The dragon stood on the beach beside the sea.
translation_text:
Haaŋ bɛl ni sechɔgii bɛl wia
1Denii n na wizenzeŋ bɛl Kɔraawiizi bol. Haaŋ bɛllɛ du de di laali wiizi, ka baagu ge du u naazi zɛɛ. U kpa chinchiŋwilaa fidaanɛɛ di gurgi di hi u nyuu. 2A haaŋ kpogli hiarɛ di jaa ra nyiŋŋi ú lul, a ra ɛɛu tɔɔrɔɔ werge, u ra chɛɛhgi. 3Denii n kaa na wii bɛl Kɔraawiizi bol. Nyugaa bɛl dee lii. U du kaŋ werge maa, di aah di dɔɔ nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ ni nyigzi fi. Koorikahuro hi u nyuuni la bɛl maa ni. 4U diŋ ge gbaari chinchiŋwilaa lugɔ di i bargaa bɔra ahoro, u bɔkpannɛ u gbaari hɛri la. Nyugzenzeŋ la chi haaŋ la n na nyiŋŋi u lul la be, di ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ di u wa lullɔ, ú kpa u bie la hee. 5U lul biibaal. U bie hinnɛ niŋ wa dɔɔ nɛra maa, di kpa lugbii daŋkpala di ra duŋŋi baa lugɔ penɔɔni n na duŋŋi u peeza la. Uŋ wa luluu la, ba toou kaali Kɔraawiizi ni u koorikara la be. 6Haaŋ la ge chɔ zuu hɛribɔduma. Kɔraawiizi faa ɛɛ bɔr siryaa tɛu, bá wer kpogluu hɔpizaa kagboŋ ni kalfaanɛɛ ni tokkoahoro maa biini.
7Denii laal izi Kɔraawiizi bol. Maikil ni u mɛlikazi kpa laal di ra yoo nyugzenzeŋ la ni u ge mɛlikazi, 8ka a waa wette kpegli Maikil ni u hora la. A waa kaa wer á du Kɔraawiizi bol la. 9Kɔraawiizi kpa nyugzenzeŋ la n faa ɛɛ hɛrikuŋ saŋa la, unla n na gbɛlli nɛra, ba ra yiruu Sitaani, u ɔɔ ra dar durnya maa la ni u mɛlikazi maa, di ha hɛri. 10Denii n nuu loobizeŋ bɛl de, n na ŋɔ,
“Filaŋkeŋ, yaa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi durnya lɛɛi helloo.
U fɔŋŋa ni u kora saŋa helloo.
U Kristo daŋ jaa lɛɛ fɔŋŋa di ra di,
dikuubɛɛwiai, unla n faa ɔɔ ra zɔɔzi yaabalaa
saŋa maa yaa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi be la,
Kɔraawiizi kpaubuu ha.
11Ba kpegluubuu dikuu Pebii chal la
ni daansɛɛ la baŋ diwee tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la wia.
Ba waa ba miibɔɔni wia kpawɛɛ su siwii
ka sɛɛ lugɔ bá kpu baa gba.
12Awia, chiŋ ni banla maa n du de la,
ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia.
Ii banla n du hɛri ni muuzeŋ la ge la, wia daŋ wa huuzi ia,
dikuubɛɛwiai, Sitaani tuu ii benii.
U baaŋ na fuuh werge maa,
dikuubɛɛwiai, u zummɔ lugɔ
u saŋa waa kaa du kaŋ.”
13Kɔraawiizi n kpa nyugzenzeŋ la ha hɛri la, a nyugzenzeŋ izi di ra duŋŋi haaŋ la n lul biibaal la. 14Ba tɛu chigzeŋ keeri anɛɛ ú kpa zaah kaali hɛribɔduma, bɔr la baŋ ɛɛ sirya tɛu ú du de bá ra binni u ni binni ahoro ni keza, ú wer na u hiŋ di lii nyugzenzeŋ la be. 15Nyugzenzeŋ la n na duŋŋi haaŋ la luge la, u pilli u nua di ta nii lugɔ muu, ú vii ɛɛ guŋ, á nii kpa haaŋ la kaali. 16Ka hɛri hiini haaŋ la, di pilli u nua di nyɔɔ nii la maa a nyugzenzeŋ n tawɛɛ lii u nua biini la. 17Denii nyugzenzeŋ la baaŋ fuuh werge maa dikuu haaŋ la wia. U kpa kaali ú ga yoo u nɛra la n ɔɔ ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa di sɛɛ Yeesu wia nɛnnɛ la. 18Ka a nyugzenzeŋ chi a muuzeŋ nua.

english_text:
The Two Beasts
1 I looked and saw a beast coming up from the sea. This one had ten horns and seven heads, and a crown was on each of its ten horns. On each of its heads were names that were an insult to God. 2 The beast I saw had the body of a leopard, the feet of a bear, and the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over its own power and throne and great authority to this beast. 3One of its heads seemed to have been fatally wounded, but now it was well. Everyone on earth marveled at this beast, 4and they worshiped the dragon who had given its authority to the beast. They also worshiped the beast and said, “No one is like this beast! No one can fight against it.”
5 The beast was allowed to brag and claim to be God, and for 42 months it was allowed to rule. 6The beast cursed God, and it cursed the name of God. It even cursed the place where God lives, as well as everyone who lives in heaven with God. 7 It was allowed to fight against God's people and defeat them. It was also given authority over the people of every tribe, nation, language, and race. 8 The beast was worshiped by everyone whose name wasn't written before the time of creation in the book of the Lamb who was killed.
9If you have ears,
then listen!
10 If you are doomed
to be captured,
you will be captured.
If you are doomed
to be killed by a sword,
you will be killed
by a sword.
This means God's people must learn to endure and be faithful!
11I now saw another beast. This one came out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon. 12It worked for the beast whose fatal wound had been healed. And it used all its authority to force the earth and its people to worship that beast. 13It worked mighty miracles, and while people watched, it even made fire come down from the sky.
14This second beast fooled people on earth by working miracles for the first one. Then it talked them into making an idol in the form of the beast that did not die after being wounded by a sword. 15It was allowed to put breath into the idol, so it could speak. Everyone who refused to worship the idol of the beast was put to death. 16 All people were forced to put a mark on their right hand or forehead. Whether they were powerful or weak, rich or poor, free people or slaves, 17they all had to have this mark, or else they could not buy or sell anything. This mark stood for the name of the beast and for the number of its name.
18You need wisdom to understand the number of the beast! But if you are smart enough, you can figure this out. Its number is 666, and it stands for a person.
translation_text:
Sechɔgaa anɛɛ la wia
1Denii n na sechɔgii bɛl n na lii muuzeŋ la biini. U dɔɔ nyigzi fi ni nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ. Koorikahuro hi u nyigzi fi la bɛl maa ni, sɔnchɔgaa ge du u nyuuni la maa ni, a bɛl maa ra gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi. 2A sechɔgii li amanii, ka u naaziwaa li sinsiri naazi, u nua ge li bunyiŋ nua. Nyugzenzeŋ la kpa u fɔŋŋa, u kora ani u nabɔmuu la maa un dɔɔwɛ werge la tɛɛ a kuŋ. 3A kuŋ nyuu bɛl ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baŋ faa lɔu di kpu. Ba faa kpuubuu ka u wer izi di nyaagi di ra nyiŋ, u wia tir durnya nɛra maa ba ra hiŋuu, 4di ra tɔgzi nyugzenzeŋ la alugɔ Kɔraawiizi, dikuu un tɛɛ sechɔgii la fɔŋŋa wia, di kaa ra jaami a sechɔgii, di ra ŋɔ, “Sechɔgii naa dɔŋ waa hoo. Anɛɛwaarɛ n niŋ wer lɔu laallɛi?”
5Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ u dɔɔ nua di ra ŋɔ wizenaa di ra gbɛlluu, di gil u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di wer ɛɛ a wia baaguzi tokkoanɛɛ ni anɛɛ biini. 6U pilli u nua di ra gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi ni u sɔŋ, u bɔnanii ani banla n du u be la. 7Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ u yoo u biinanaa di kpegli baa, di gil u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa nɛdee maa n du hɛri naa yemmaa ni. 8Durnya hina la ba sɔna n waa hoo Pebii la baŋ kpuwɛɛ lii durnya luglaa la, miibɔɔ hɔŋ la biini, ba maa danna jaamuu alugɔ Kɔraawiizi.
9Nɛr la maa n dɔɔ digna di ra nuu wia, ú ra nuu.
10Di Kɔraawiizi dau nɛr maa alugɔ bá lawuu,
ba daŋ lawuu.
Di nɛr maa kpa tokobi di kpu nɛr,
tokobii bá kpa kpu u ge.
Denii bá chi zum kanyitti ni yarda la dee Kɔraawiizi biinanaa la n dɔɔwɛ ani gunla un duwɛɛ.
11Denii n kaa na sechɔgii bɛl n na lii hɛri biini. U dɔɔ nyigzi anɛɛ lugɔ pebii nyigzi, di dɔɔ loobii lugɔ nyugzenzeŋ loobii. 12Lugli sechɔgii la kpa u fɔŋŋa la maa di du u ni, u ra ɛɛ wizenaa u sɔŋ biini, di gil banla maa n du durnya ra jaami lugli sechɔgii la baŋ faa lɔwɛɛ di kpu ka u kaa nyaagi la. 13U wettoo ɛɛ wizenaa, haali di gil niŋ lii chiŋ di chol hɛri, nɛra na. 14Uŋ wette ra ɛɛ wizenaa la sechɔgii la fɔŋŋa biini gunla, nɛra sɛɛ u wia, u wer dar baa di ŋɔ bá ma kumbɛl, ú li sechɔgii la baŋ faa kpa tokobi di boŋŋi ka u haa ra nyiŋ la. 15Baŋ wa mau tuŋ, Kɔraawiizi kaa tɛu fɔŋŋa u wer du kunla bam mawɛɛ la heeza, u wer ra ŋɔ wia. A kuŋ ŋɔ, dí banla maa n wàá sɛɛ ra jaami kunla bam mawɛɛ la, bá kpu baa. 16U gillɔɔ ba pii nɛr maa, nɛdumazi, nɛzenaa, dɔɔna, nyaara, banla n dɔɔ bahinaa, yoma, nodige gɛɛ ba hilli. 17Nɛr la maa n waa guŋ piiwɛ wàá wer yau kuna, wàá wer yoo kuna ge, see banla bam piiwɛ la bɛŋ. A sechɔgii sɔŋ gɛɛ u nambaa ba pii la.
18Di i dɔɔ nunzuma, í nuu ɛŋ. Nɛr la n dɔɔ zumaa daŋ wer zum sechɔgii la namba la zɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ newee sɔŋ bɛllɛ. Waabuu keŋ, kalfaanumbɛl ni tokkoahoro ni anumbɛl, 666.

english_text:
The Lamb and His 144,000 Followers
1 I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion! With him were 144,000, who had his name and his Father's name written on their foreheads. 2 Then I heard a sound from heaven that was like a roaring flood or loud thunder or even like the music of harps. 3And a new song was being sung in front of God's throne and in front of the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn that song, except the 144,000 who had been rescued from the earth. 4All of these are pure virgins, and they follow the Lamb wherever he leads. They have been rescued to be presented to God and the Lamb as the most precious people on earth. 5 They never tell lies, and they are innocent.
The Messages of the Three Angels
6I saw another angel. This one was flying across the sky and had the eternal good news to announce to the people of every race, tribe, language, and nation on earth. 7The angel shouted, “Worship and honor God! The time has come for him to judge everyone. Kneel down before the one who created heaven and earth, the oceans, and every stream.”
8 A second angel followed and said, “The great city of Babylon has fallen! This is the city that made all nations drunk and immoral. Now God is angry, and Babylon has fallen.”
9Finally, a third angel came and shouted:
Here is what will happen if you worship the beast and the idol and have the mark of the beast on your hand or forehead. 10 You will have to drink the wine that God gives to everyone who makes him angry. You will feel his mighty anger, and you will be tortured with fire and burning sulfur, while the holy angels and the Lamb look on.
11 If you worship the beast and the idol and accept the mark of its name, you will be tortured day and night. The smoke from your torture will go up forever and ever, and you will never be able to rest.
12God's people must learn to endure. They must also obey his commands and have faith in Jesus.
13Then I heard a voice from heaven say, “Put this in writing. From now on, the Lord will bless everyone who has faith in him when they die.”
The Spirit answered, “Yes, they will rest from their hard work, and they will be rewarded for what they have done.”
The Earth Is Harvested
14 I looked and saw a bright cloud, and someone who seemed to be the Son of Man was sitting on the cloud. He wore a gold crown on his head and held a sharp sickle in his hand. 15 An angel came out of the temple and shouted, “Start cutting with your sickle! Harvest season is here, and all crops on earth are ripe.” 16The one on the cloud swung his sickle and harvested the crops.
17Another angel with a sharp sickle then came out of the temple in heaven. 18After this, an angel with power over fire came from the altar and shouted to the angel who had the sickle. He said, “All grapes on earth are ripe! Harvest them with your sharp sickle.” 19The angel swung his sickle on earth and cut off its grapes. He threw them into a pit where they were trampled on as a sign of God's anger. 20 The pit was outside the city, and when the grapes were mashed, blood flowed out. The blood turned into a river that was about 300 kilometers long and almost deep enough to cover a horse.
translation_text:
Pebii la ni u nɛra wia
1Denii n binni di Pebii la chigɔ Bizeŋ Ziɔn la nyuu. Nɛra kagboŋa kalfa ni tokkoanɛɛ ni banaazu n dɔɔ u ni u mɛɛ sɔna ba hilli ni du u be. 2N nuu kɔɔi bɛl lii Kɔraawiizi bol, u lugɔ muu n na pal werge, di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ nazaa ge n na pogzi werge. A kaa ɛɛ lugɔ janjalaŋ lɔɔra n na lɔ ba janjalanzi. 3Nɛra la chi Kɔraawiizi koorikara la ni kunnyinee anaazu ni nabɔnzi la be di ra yir yirfalii bɛl. Nɛr maa waa wette u zum yir la, di nɛra kagboŋa kalfa ni tokkoanɛɛ ni banaazu la Kɔraawiizi n turgi ba wichɔgaa kim, di lɛɛ baa ha di lii durnya nɛra la maa biini la bɛŋ lɛi. 4Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baala la n waa haana zummɛ, dikuu baŋ faa gil hahwia la wia. Ba ɔɔ ra hiŋ Pebii la bɔr la maa un niŋ la. Baabuu ɛɛ banla baŋ felee yau ha newea biini, di kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni Pebii la. 5Daraa maa waa hoo ba nuuzi. Ba waa wichɔgaa maa dɔɔwɛ.
Mɛlikazi ahoro aŋhina wia
6Denii n kaa na mɛlika bɛl n na zaah chiŋ. U kpogli amaniyesuma la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la, ú lizi tɛɛ nɛdee maa n du hɛri naa yemmaa, 7di ra ŋɔ fɔŋŋa ni, “Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi, di ra tɛu sɔŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, saŋa la un niŋ di nɛra seriya la helloo. Ií ra jaami unla n ta chiŋ, hɛri, muuzeŋ ani bulli maa la.”
8Mɛlika bɛl hiŋ unla ni, di ra ŋɔ, “U cholloo, u cholloo! Babilɔn, bolzenzeŋ la n faa gillɛ durnya nɛra maa ra nyɔɔ u siŋkpega, di kaa gil nɛra ra sɛm werge la cholloo.”
9Mɛlika horohiŋ kaa hiŋ anɛɛ la ni, di ra ŋɔ fɔŋŋa ni, “Di unla maa sɛɛwɔ ra jaami sechɔgii la ni kunla bam mawɛɛ u liu la, di kaa gil ba pii u hile gɛɛ u nonii, 10u daŋ nyɔɔ Kɔraawiizi siŋ. U baaŋ la n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ siŋ la baŋ waa hulle, ka fuguu guŋ di du libee biini labuu, bá tɛu, ú nyɔɔ la. U daŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ werge maa niŋ ni jilbi biini, mɛlikananaa ni Pebii la see. 11Nyɔɔzi daŋ tinni lii bɔr la banna di tɔɔrɔɔ la saŋa maa, di ra la. Banla n jaami sechɔgii la ni kunla bam mawɛɛ ani banla baŋ kpa u sɔŋ pii la, ba wàá lii tɔɔrɔɔ la biini maa, ka ɔɔ ra di a tɔɔrɔɔ hɔpizaa ni hamuŋa maa di hanna la.” 12Denii bá zum kanyitti la dee Kɔraawiizi biinanaa la n na hiŋ u widaulaa di yardi Yeesu la n dɔɔwɛ.
13N nuu loobii bɛl n lii Kɔraawiizi bol n ŋɔwɛɛ, “Sɛbi wia naa ra dau lugɔ banla n yardi yaa Dɔɔri ka siu filaŋkeŋ, di hanna la, nuu sumaa.” U Dumnanii la ŋɔ, “Wibii maa. Ba daŋ gil ba huma ka heezi. Ba winanaa sɔŋ ge daŋ hiŋ baa.”
Durnya kuna kumaa wia
14Denii n binni di na baamahuŋŋu bɛl, nɛbɛl so u ni, di li newee biibaal, di hi saliŋ kahuro, di kpogli kizidiilii ge du u nonii biini. 15Mɛlika bɛl kaa lii Kɔraawiizi Dia di ŋɔ fɔŋŋa ni di ra tɛɛ unla n soge baama ni la, “Kpa i kizee di ra kum. Kuna kumaa saŋa helloo. Durnya pattikuna biiwɔɔ lugɔ í kumaa.” 16Unla n soge baama la ni la kpa u kizee di ra kum durnya pattikuna la.
17Mɛlika bɛl kaa lii Kɔraawiizi Dia la n du u bol biini la. U gba kpogli kizidiilii. 18Bɛl ge lii mbusu lizibɔr la. Unla n dɔɔ niŋ fɔŋŋa ge lii mbusu lizibɔr di pozi di ŋɔ kizidiilii hiŋ la be, “Kpa i kizidiilii la ŋmɛnni grepuzi la di chaalaa. A biiwɔɔ.” 19U lalli u kizee hɛri ni di chaali durnya grepuzi la, di dua kunla baŋ ɔɔ kpa nɔna di du di ra fɛrgi a nii ra lii la biini. Kɔraawiizi baannɛ a kuŋ. 20Ba fɛrgi nɔna la bol baŋgia, bɔr la banna fɛrgi nɔna a nii ra lii la, chal pal lii kunla biini di su di la chiŋ lugɔ nogumzi anɛɛ, di kaa pal guŋŋ lugɔ kilomitazi kalfa ahoro di wa hel zagra kabargazi.

english_text:
The Last of the Terrible Troubles
1After this, I looked at the sky and saw something else that was strange and important. Seven angels were bringing the seven last terrible troubles. When these are ended, God will no longer be angry.
2Then I saw something that looked like a glass sea mixed with fire, and people were standing on it. They were the ones who had defeated the beast and the idol and the number that tells the name of the beast. God had given them harps, 3 and they were singing the song his servant Moses and the Lamb had sung. They were singing,
“Lord God All-Powerful,
you have done great
and marvelous things.
You are the ruler
of all nations,
and you do what is
right and fair.
4 Lord, who doesn't honor
and praise your name?
You alone are holy,
and all nations will come
and worship you,
because you have shown
that you judge
with fairness.”
5 After this, I noticed something else in heaven. The sacred tent used for a temple was open. 6And the seven angels who were bringing the terrible troubles were coming out of it. They were dressed in robes of pure white linen and wore belts made of pure gold. 7One of the four living creatures gave each of the seven angels a bowl made of gold. These bowls were filled with the anger of God who lives forever and ever. 8 The temple quickly filled with smoke from the glory and power of God. No one could enter it until the seven angels had finished pouring out the seven last troubles.
translation_text:
Mɛlikazi la n kpogli tuna wiilchɔgaa wia
1N kaa na witittizeŋ bɛl Kɔraawiizi bol. N na mɛlikazi aniidaanɛɛ n kpogli tuna wiilchɔgaa aniidaanɛɛ. Di annii wa ɛɛwɔ, Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih tunaa guŋ. 2N na yembɛl n chɔɔwɛ lugɔ muuzeŋ di ra chaani lugɔ digii, niŋ koozi u ni. Banla n kpegli sechɔgii ni kunla bam mawɛɛ ni u namba la n ɛɛ u sɔŋ la, ba kpogli Kɔraawiizi janjalanzi di chi nii la n chɔɔwɛ lugɔ digii la kɛrii, 3di ra yir Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis ani Pebii la yir la, di ra ŋɔ,
“Oo, yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ,
i wiɛɛlaa ɛɛ wizenaare
werge maa, di ra tir yaa.
Durnya maa koori,
i ŋmɛnizi maa deŋloore
di ɛɛ wibii.
4Oo, yaa Dɔɔri, anɛɛ n du de wɛɛ ra ɔmɛi?
Anɛɛ n wɛɛ ra tɛɛ sɔnɛi?
I bɛnnɛ ɛɛ nɛnanii di wa tuŋ.
Durnya hɛssi hina maa daŋ ba i be di wa jaamii.
Wia la hiŋ ɛɛwɛ la
deŋloore, nɛr maa na.”
5Denii n binni di na dia bɛl Kɔraawiizi bol, u li Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la baŋ faa baŋŋɛ, u faa ra bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du u nɛra benii la n pillɛɛ. 6Mɛlikazi aniidaanɛɛ la n kpogli wiilchɔgaa tuna aniidaanɛɛ la lii Kɔraawiizi bɔnaniinanii himmaa la biini. A laali pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii laala a du wer werge di ra nyɛgzi. Saliŋ belentizii ba kpa di kirsi a bampiree. 7Kunnyinee anaazu la bɛl kpa saliŋ hɛnni aniidaanɛɛ tɛɛa. Kɔraawiizi la n na nyiŋ saŋa maa la, baannɛ su a hɛnni maa la. 8Nyɔɔzi jaa su Kɔraawiizi Dia la dikuu u girme ni u fɔŋŋa wia. Nɛr maa waa wette zuu de, ka tuna wiilchɔgaa aniidaanɛɛ la mɛlikazi aniidaanɛɛ la n kpoglee la wa tuŋ mɔɔ.

english_text:
The Bowls of God's Anger
1From the temple I heard a voice shout to the seven angels, “Go and empty the seven bowls of God's anger on the earth.”
2 The first angel emptied his bowl on the earth. At once ugly and painful sores broke out on everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol.
3The second angel emptied his bowl on the sea. At once the sea turned into blood like that of a dead person, and every living thing in the sea died.
4 The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and streams. At once they turned to blood. 5Then I heard the angel, who has power over water, say,
“You have always been,
and you always will be
the holy God.
You had the right
to judge in this way.
6They poured out the blood
of your people
and your prophets.
So you gave them blood
to drink as they deserve!”
7After this, I heard
the altar shout,
“Yes, Lord God All-Powerful,
your judgments are honest
and fair.”
8The fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, and it began to scorch people like fire. 9Everyone was scorched by its great heat, and all of them cursed the name of God who had power over these terrible troubles. But no one turned to God and praised him.
10 The fifth angel emptied his bowl on the throne of the beast. At once darkness covered its kingdom, and its people began biting their tongues in pain. 11And because of their painful sores, they cursed the God who rules in heaven. But still they did not stop doing evil things.
12 The sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great Euphrates River, and it completely dried up to make a road for the kings from the east. 13An evil spirit that looked like a frog came out of the mouth of the dragon. One also came out of the mouth of the beast, and another out of the mouth of the false prophet. 14These evil spirits had the power to work miracles. They went to every king on earth, to bring them together for a war against God All-Powerful. But that will be the day of God's great victory.
15 Remember Christ says, “When I come, it will surprise you like a thief! But God will bless you, if you are awake and ready. Then you won't have to walk around naked and be ashamed.”
16 Those armies came together in a place that in Hebrew is called Armagedon.
17As soon as the seventh angel emptied his bowl in the air, a loud voice from the throne in the temple shouted, “It's done!” 18 There were flashes of lightning, roars of thunder, and the worst earthquake in all history. 19 The great city of Babylon split into three parts, and the cities of other nations fell. So God made Babylon drink from the wine cup filled with his anger. 20 Every island ran away, and the mountains disappeared. 21 Hailstones, weighing about 50 kilograms each, fell from the sky on people. Finally, the people cursed God, because the hail was so terrible.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi baaŋ hɛnni wia
1Denii n nuu loobizeŋ bɛl n lii Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini di ŋɔ mɛlikazi aniidaanɛɛ la be, “Ií la ga fugzi Kɔraawiizi baaŋ la n du hɛnni aniidaanɛɛ la biini ha hɛri.” 2Lugli mɛlika la kaali di ga fug u hɛna la ha hɛri. Zallaazi lii banla n dɔɔ sechɔgii pii la di ra jaami kunla bam mawɛɛ la ni.
3Nɛɛhiŋ la kaali ga fug u hor di du muuzeŋ ni. U bir ɛɛ lugɔ lalii chal, kunnyinee la maa n du a muuzeŋ biini siuzi.
4Horohiŋ la kaali ga fug u hor di du gɔŋa ni bulli ni. A birgi chal. 5Denii n nuu mɛlika la n ɛɛ niiri nabɔma la n ŋɔwɛɛ,
“Hinla n du de filaŋkeŋ,
di faa du de saŋa maa
di ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii
di wa tuŋ la,
kennaa seriya hiŋ di
durnya naa,
i hor la deŋloore,
6dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa
kpu i biinanaa ni i
dɔgtɛɛzii, ba chal lii.
I jaa tɛɛ banla n kpu baa la
challi ba nyɔɔ.
Ba dɛg gunnɛ.”
7N kaa nuu mbusu lizibɔr la n na ŋɔ wia,
“Wibiire, Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ.
Gunla seriya hiŋ di baa
la ɛɛ wibiire
di deŋli.”
8Naazuhiŋ la kaali ga fug u hor ha wiizi ni. Wiizi jaa ra baari alugɔ niŋ, 9di ra baari nɛra dikuu uŋ wenzee werge wia. A nɛra ra gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi la n dɔɔ wiilchɔgaa naa fɔŋŋa la. Ba waa sɛɛwɛ ba bir lii ba wichɔgaa biini di tɛu sɔŋ.
10Nuehiŋ la kaali ga fug u hor di ha sechɔgii la koorikara la ni, bɔr biri u kora hina maa ni. Nɛra ra dunzi ba nuuzuŋŋa dikuu ba bɔra n na waazi werge la wia. 11Ba ra see Kɔraawiizi nua dikuu ba bɔra baaraa werge la wia, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ ba bir lii ba wichɔgaa biini.
12Numbɛlhiŋ la kaali ga fug u hor di du Muu Yufretis ni. U nii maa hiihzi. Gunnɛ u ɛɛ ka ú wer dau ŋmɛnɛɛ tɛɛ koora la n niŋ lii wiifurii di ba la. 13Denii n na tinnanchɔgaa ahoro lugɔ sampussi n lii nyugzenzeŋ ni sechɔgii la ani dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ la nuuzi. 14Sampussi naa ɛɛ Sitaani kunaa di wer ra ɛɛ wizenaa. A lii di la durnya maa koora be di ga chaali baa, bá yoo Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la laal, u hɔpizizeŋ la hɔl.
15“Ií ra nuu ɛŋ. N daŋ ba alugɔ ŋmɛɛŋ n ɔɔ ba la. Unla maa n na binni n ŋmɛnɛɛ di laali u tagtazi, ú gilɛɛ wa kpa chakpal di ra vol nɛra nau, á ɛɛu hiihzi nuu sumaa.”
16Sitaani sampussi la chaali koora la bɔr la Hibru hina n na yir Aamagɛdɔn la.
17Niidaanɛɛhiŋ la fug u hor di ha peu ni. N nuu loobii bɛl n na la bɔɔnɛɛ werge, n lii koorikara la ni Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini, di ra ŋɔ, “Wiimaa jaa tunuu!” 18Dooŋ na nyɛgzi, loobee ra kɔɔ, nazaa ra pogzi, hɛri zigli ziglichɔgii bɛl. Kɔraawiizi n haŋ ta newea maa, hɛri ŋmɛnɛ haa waa ziglee guŋ maa. U chummɔɔ werge maa. 19Bolzenzeŋ la bargi bɔra ahoro. Durnya bola maa chogli. Kɔraawiizi liizi Babilɔnzeŋ la wichɔgaa wia, di gil u nyɔɔ u siŋkpeg la n ɛɛ u baaŋ la. 20Hɛssi la n du muu baambaaŋ la izi chɔ. Bizenaa leu, ba nyiŋŋaa huhzi. 21Dobizenaa la n tɔkkɛ lugɔ yabɔɔtizi lii chiŋ di chogli nɛra la ni. Ba ra chagzi Kɔraawiizi dikuu dobee la n ɛɛ wiilchɔgii himmaa wia.

english_text:
The Prostitute and the Beast
1 One of the seven angels who had emptied the bowls came over and said to me, “Come on! I will show you how God will punish that shameless prostitute who sits on many oceans. 2 Every king on earth has slept with her, and her shameless ways are like wine that has made everyone on earth drunk.”
3 With the help of the Spirit, the angel took me into a desert, where I saw a woman sitting on a red beast. The beast was covered with names that were an insult to God, and it had seven heads and ten horns. 4 The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet robes, and she wore jewelry made of gold, precious stones, and pearls. In her hand she held a gold cup filled with the filthy and nasty things she had done. 5On her forehead a mysterious name was written:
I AM THE GREAT CITY OF BABYLON, THE MOTHER OF EVERY IMMORAL AND FILTHY THING ON EARTH.
6I could tell that the woman was drunk on the blood of God's people who had given their lives for Jesus. This surprising sight amazed me, 7and the angel said:
Why are you so amazed? I will explain the mystery about this woman and about the beast she is sitting on, with its seven heads and ten horns. 8 The beast you saw is one that used to be and no longer is. It will come back from the deep pit, but only to be destroyed. Everyone on earth whose names were not written in the book of life before the time of creation will be amazed. They will see this beast that used to be and no longer is, but will be once more.
9Anyone with wisdom can figure this out. The seven heads that the woman is sitting on stand for seven hills. These heads are also seven kings. 10Five of the kings are dead. One is ruling now, and the other one has not yet come. But when he does, he will rule for only a little while.
11You also saw a beast that used to be and no longer is. That beast is one of the seven kings who will return as the eighth king, but only to be destroyed.
12 The ten horns you saw are ten more kings, who have not yet come into power, and they will rule with the beast for only a short time. 13They all think alike and will give their power and authority to the beast. 14 These kings will go to war against the Lamb. But he will defeat them, because he is Lord over all lords and King over all kings. His followers are chosen and special and faithful.
15The oceans you saw the prostitute sitting on are crowds of people from all races and languages. 16The ten horns and the beast will start hating the shameless woman. They will strip off her clothes and leave her naked. Then they will eat her flesh and throw the rest of her body into a fire. 17God is the one who made these kings all think alike and decide to give their power to the beast. And they will do this until what God has said comes true.
18The woman you saw is the great city that rules over all kings on earth.
translation_text:
Hahsɛnsɛnni la n dɔɔ sɔŋ werge wia
1Denii mɛlikazi aniidaanɛɛ la n kpogli hɛnni aniidaanɛɛ la bɛl ŋɔ n be, “A ba ń baglii gunla Kɔraawiizi n tɛr hahsɛnsɛnni la digni. Bolzenzeŋ la n hɔŋ muukpila niiri ni la ɛɛ a hahsɛnsɛnnii. 2Durnya koora sɛmuubuu, durnya nɛra ge nyɔɔ u siŋ di dɛɛzi. U sɛnsɛŋ labuu ɛɛ siŋ la baŋ nyɔɔwɛ dɛɛzi la.”
3Denii Kɔraawiizi Duma izi n ni. Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la kpaŋ kaali hɛribɔduma. N na haaŋ bɛl n soge sechɔgii la ni. A sechɔgii aahwɔɔ, di dɔɔ sɔnchɔgaa u maa ni. U nyuuni ge du aniidaanɛɛ, u nyigzi ge du fi. 4A haaŋ laala aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii. Aŋhina ge aah yorototo. U du saliŋ kuna ni binanaa, di kpogli saliŋ libee, kuŋkiilaa ni sɛnsɛŋ wia suu. 5Ba sɛbi sɔŋ bɛl di du haaŋ la hile. A sɔŋ zɛɛ suahwɔɔ. A sɔnnɛ keŋ,
babilɔnzenzeŋ,
sɛnsɛnna ni hɛri
wikuna maa, maa.
6N na a haaŋ n na dɛɛzi. Kɔraawiizi biinanaa n di Yeesu daansɛɛ la challii u nyɔɔ di ra dɛɛzi.
Miŋ wa nau la, a tiriŋ werge maa. 7Mɛlika la pɛɛziŋ, “Ɛrɛɛ a tirii gunnɛi? N daŋ bagli haaŋ naa ni sechɔgii la n dɔɔ nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ ni nyigzi fi la un tinnɛɛ la zɛɛ tɛi. 8Sechɔgii la hiŋ nawɛɛ la faa ra nyinuu, ka waa kaa ra nyiŋ. Ka u daŋ haa lii Sitaani Bɔɔluŋ la di ra la, Kɔ́raawiizi jaa chɔguu nyaamm. Banla n du durnya, Kɔraawiizi waa ba sɔna sɛbɛɛ du miibɔɔ hɔŋ la biini di lii chiŋ ni hɛri luglaa la, ba daŋ wa na sechɔgii la á tir baa, dikuu uŋ faa du de ka waa kaa hoo, ka ú kaa wa lii la wia.
9Di haa nunzuma dɔɔwɛ, hàá wer zum bɔnnaa. Nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ la ɛɛ bizenaa ge aniidaanɛɛrɛ. Denii ɛɛ haaŋ la sognibɔr. 10A kaa ɛɛ koora baniidaanɛɛ. Ba wir banuere ba kossi biini. Ka bɛl ge haa ra di u kora. Bɛl ge haa waa diwee mɔɔ. Di u wa diwoo, wàá di u kora la birgi. 11Sechɔgii la n faa du de ka waa kaa hoo la, u ge ɛɛ koora ŋmantannaazi hinnɛ, ka du baniidaanɛɛ la biinii. U ra lau Kɔ́raawiizi ga chɔguu.
12Nyigzi fi la ɛɛ koora fii. A koora haa waa ba kossi diwee mɔɔ. Ka ban niŋ wa di a kossi, ba wàá dia birgi. Ba ni sechɔgii la daŋ kpau na fɔŋŋa. 13A koora maa daŋ ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di kpa ba fɔŋŋa maa, di tɛɛ sechɔgii la. 14Denii bá ni Pebii la yoo laal, u kpegli baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ dɔɔra maa Dɔɔrii, di ɛɛ koora maa Koori. U hiŋra ge ɛɛ banla un lizɛɛ tɛɛ u hiŋ, di yir baa ba ba u be, di waa hiŋuu ni wibii labuu.”
15Mɛlika la kaa ŋɔ n be, “Niiri la hiŋ nawɛɛ bɔr la n ɛɛ hahsɛnsɛnni la sognibɔr la, a ɛɛ nɛdee maa n du hɛri naa yemmaanii. 16Nyigzi fi la hiŋ nawɛɛ la, ba ni sechɔgii la daŋ hah hahsɛnsɛnni la di foozi u kummaa, ka giluu ni u chakpalli. Ba daŋ hee u ol ka kpa niŋ fuuuh, 17dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi kpa gunnɛ du ba bampiree, bá ɛɛ u kipar di kaa gil ba ni sechɔgii la dɔɔ nuukpaŋ lugɔ bá kpa ba fɔŋŋa tɛu, ka Kɔraawiizi Wiŋɔɔlii wer ɛɛ wibii. 18Haaŋ la hiŋ nawɛɛ la, u ɛɛ bolzenzeŋ la n dɔɔ durnya maa koora labuu.”

english_text:
The Fall of Babylon
1I saw another angel come from heaven. This one had great power, and the earth was bright because of his glory. 2 The angel shouted,
“Fallen! Powerful Babylon
has fallen
and is now the home
of demons.
It is the den
of every filthy spirit
and of all unclean birds,
and every dirty
and hated animal.
3 Babylon's evil and immoral wine
has made all nations drunk.
Every king on earth
has slept with her,
and every merchant on earth
is rich because of
her evil desires.”
4 Then I heard another voice
from heaven shout,
“My people, you must escape
from Babylon.
Don't take part in her sins
and share her punishment.
5 Her sins are piled
as high as heaven.
God has remembered the evil
she has done.
6 Treat her as she
has treated others.
Make her pay double
for what she has done.
Make her drink twice as much
of what she mixed
for others.
7 That woman honored herself
with a life of luxury.
Reward her now
with suffering and pain.
“Deep in her heart
Babylon said,
‘I am the queen!
Never will I be a widow
or know what it means
to be sad.’
8And so, in a single day
she will suffer the pain
of sorrow, hunger, and death.
Fire will destroy
her dead body,
because her judge
is the powerful Lord God.”
9 Every king on earth who slept with her and shared in her luxury will mourn. They will weep, when they see the smoke from that fire. 10Her sufferings will frighten them, and they will stand at a distance and say,
“Pity that great
and powerful city!
Pity Babylon!
In a single hour
her judgment has come.”
11 Every merchant on earth will mourn, because there is no one to buy their goods. 12 There won't be anyone to buy their gold, silver, jewels, pearls, fine linen, purple cloth, silk, scarlet cloth, sweet-smelling wood, fancy carvings of ivory and wood, as well as things made of bronze, iron, or marble. 13No one will buy their cinnamon, spices, incense, myrrh, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, slaves, and other humans.
14Babylon, the things
your heart desired
have all escaped
from you.
Every luxury
and all your glory
will be lost forever.
You will never
get them back.
15 The merchants had become rich because of her. But when they saw her sufferings, they were terrified. They stood at a distance, crying and mourning. 16Then they shouted,
“Pity the great city
of Babylon!
She dressed in fine linen
and wore purple
and scarlet cloth.
She had jewelry
made of gold
and precious stones
and pearls.
17 Yet in a single hour
her riches disappeared.”
Every ship captain and passenger and sailor stood at a distance, together with everyone who does business by traveling on the sea. 18 When they saw the smoke from her fire, they shouted, “This was the greatest city ever!”
19 They cried loudly, and in their sorrow they threw dust on their heads, as they said,
“Pity the great city
of Babylon!
Everyone who sailed the seas
became rich
from her treasures.
But in a single hour
the city was destroyed.
20 The heavens should be happy
with God's people
and apostles and prophets.
God has punished her
for them.”
21 A powerful angel then picked up a huge stone and threw it into the sea. The angel said,
“This is how the great city
of Babylon
will be thrown down,
never to rise again.
22 The music of harps and singers
and of flutes and trumpets
will no longer be heard.
No workers will ever
set up shop in that city,
and the sound
of grinding grain
will be silenced forever.
23Lamps will no longer shine
anywhere in Babylon,
and couples will never again
say wedding vows there.
Her merchants ruled
the earth,
and by her witchcraft
she fooled all nations.
24 On the streets of Babylon
is found the blood
of God's people
and of his prophets,
and everyone else.”
translation_text:
Babilɔn cholaa wia
1Denii n kaa na mɛlika bɛl n lii Kɔraawiizi bol di ra tuu hɛri. U dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa werge maa. Durnya maa ra chaani dikuu u girme wia. 2U pozi werge, di ŋɔ,
“U cholloo, u cholloo.
Babilɔnzenzeŋ la cholloo
di birgi Sitaani kuna bɔr,
tinnanchɔgaa ni zumbichɔgaa la
maa baŋ hahwɛɛ
la duuribɔr,
3dikuubɛɛwiai, durnya nɛra maa faa nyɔɔ u siŋ
ni u wikuna la uŋ faa
nɔŋŋɛɛ werge labuu.
Durnya koora sɛmuubuu.
Durnya kunyoora
birgi dɔɔna dikuu u fɔŋŋa
ni u kebee wia.”
4N kaa nuu loobii bɛl n lii chiŋ n ŋɔwɛɛ,
“N nɛra, ií lii u be.
Maa nyiŋŋi ii nuu kpau
di ra ɛɛ a wichɔgaa,
di kaa wa kpau
di na wiilchɔgaa la
min niŋ wa kpa tɔɔruu la.
5U wichɔgaa haŋ sagzi dɔŋa ninɛɛ,
guŋŋ di ga hel Kɔraawiizi bol.
Kɔraawiizi ra liizi a wiarɛ.
6Ií ra ɛɛu gunla uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ la.
Ií turguu u hunchɔgaa
la kim bunɛɛ.
Siŋ la uŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ tɛɛ nɛra bá nyɔɔ la,
ií gil u du kpeg bunɛɛ
di kaali guŋ, ú ge nyɔɔ.
7Gunla uŋ faa kpa u hiŋ zenni
di ra di u hiŋ werge la,
ií ra tɛu tɔɔrɔɔ ni biinichɔg ge werge guŋ,
dikuubɛɛwiai, ɔɔ ra fɛ
u biinii, di ra ŋɔ,
‘Minuu wiche. Maa haŋkii ɛɛwɛ.
N biini wàá chɔgi maa.’
8Hɔpizikpaŋ biini, wiilchɔgaa lugɔ siu,
biinichɔg ani lɔzi
daŋ lɔu dau.
Niŋ daŋ fuuuh, dikuubɛɛwiai,
yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la
n di u seriya la
dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa.
9Durnya koora la u ni baa n faa ra sɛm di ra di bahinaa la, di ba wa na unna fuuh, nyɔɔzi ra lii la, ba danna wii di ra lɔɔgi wile. 10Bɔɔnɛɛrɛ bá chi dikuu banna ɔm u tɔɔrɔɔ la unna di la wia, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Wiarɛ, wiarɛ. Bolzeŋ Babilɔn la n faa kpekke werge la, wiarɛ huuzii kakpaŋ,’ 11durnya kunyoora biine chɔgi ba ra wii, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr maa wàá ka yau ba kuna 12lugɔ saliŋ, lugbinanaa, binanaa yoola n kpolle werge, wɛjɛnanaa ni a dizi, daananaa la yoolazi n kpolle werge ge ni a dizi, kuna la baŋ kpa bala nyina ni daananaa kuari, anla baŋ kpa danyɛ ni lugbii luu, anla baŋ kpa binanaa kuari, 13dɔzi tiuzaa kuna lugɔ kokodoro dɔŋ, daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la banna fuuh, nuusɔɔhraa, siŋ, ɔlivi nuu, sananaa, minanaa, nauna, peeza, zagra ni a torkozi ani yoma. Newea dunzii ba yoo la.
14‘Kunnanaa la maa hiŋ faa ra kɛlli a ni la lii i noneere. I daama ni i girme kunnanaa waa kaa hoo. Hàá ka naa maa.’ 15Banla n faa yoo a kuna di na kebee werge a bol biini la, ba chigɔ bɔɔnɛɛrɛ dikuu banna ɔm tɔɔrɔɔ la wia di ra wii ba biine chɔgi, 16ba ra ŋɔ, ‘Wiarɛ, wiarɛ huuzi bolzeŋ la u nɛra n faa kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa wɛjɛ tɔ di faa ra laali tagta lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii ani a aahma yorototo di du saliŋ ni binanaa la, 17dikuubɛɛwiai, u kuna la un dɔɔwɛ werge la, a maa tunnɔɔ kakpaŋ.’ Muugbessi nabɔnzi ni banla n zuu a muugbessi ni a balaa ni banla maa n na hum a muugbessi biine la chi bɔɔnɛɛ 18di na nyɔɔzi n na lii dikuu unna fuuh la di lɔɔgi wile di ra ŋɔ, ‘Bolzeŋ naa faa waa dɔŋ dɔɔwɛ.’ 19Ba ɛɛ nyɔɔ di du ba nyuuni ni di ra lɔɔgi wile, di ra wii, ba biine chɔgi, ba ra ŋɔ,
‘Wiarɛ, wiarɛ huuzi bolzeŋ la
n gillɛ muugbessi hina maa birgi dɔɔna
dikuu a bol kebee dɔɔi werge wia.
Kummaanii u bir nyaa kakpaŋ.
20Ii banla n du chiŋ,
Kɔraawiizi biinanaa ni u huŋhunna ni u dɔgtɛɛzi,
ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni dikuu u wia.
Kɔraawiizi turguubuu wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛ ia la kim.’ ”
21Denii mɛlikakpeg bɛl lalli bikpeg bɛl u lugɔ namzeŋ di kpau ha muuzeŋ la biini ka ŋɔ,
“Gunnɛ bá wa kpa bolzeŋ
Babilɔn la ha kpegzi ni kakpaŋ.
Ba wàá ka nau maa.
22Ba wàá ka nuu nɛra n na lɔ janjalanzi i biini.
Ba wàá ka nuu banla n na huuh tiitoraa
ni bensunozi i biini maa.
Ba wàá ka na banla n na sɛɛh
di ra suah kuna di ra hum a huma dizi i biini.
Ba wàá ka nuu nam ge gbɔga de.
23Fintina maa wàá ka chaani de.
Ba wàá ka nuu baal ni u haŋfalii loobee de maa.
Banla n yoo kuna i biini la faa ɛɛ nɛzenaare
ba dɔŋahina la n du durnya maa be.
I wettoo kpa i biiri di dar durnya nɛra maa.
24Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi ni u biinanaa
ni banla maa baŋ kpuwɛɛ durnya naa biini la,
ba challii bá na a bol biini.”

english_text:
1After this, I heard what sounded like a lot of voices in heaven, and they were shouting,
“Praise the Lord!
To our God belongs
the glorious power to save,
2 because his judgments
are honest and fair.
That filthy prostitute
ruined the earth
with shameful deeds.
But God has judged her
and made her pay
the price for murdering
his servants.”
3 Then the crowd shouted,
“Praise the Lord!
Smoke will never stop rising
from her burning body.”
4After this, the 24 elders and the four living creatures all knelt before the throne of God and worshiped him. They said, “Amen! Praise the Lord!”
The Marriage Supper of the Lamb
5 From the throne a voice said,
“If you worship
and fear our God,
give praise to him,
no matter who you are.”
6 Then I heard what seemed to be a large crowd that sounded like a roaring flood and loud thunder all mixed together. They were saying,
“Praise the Lord!
Our Lord God All-Powerful
now rules as king.
7So we will be glad and happy
and give him praise.
The wedding day of the Lamb
is here,
and his bride is ready.
8She will be given
a wedding dress
made of pure
and shining linen.
This linen stands for
the good things
God's people have done.”
9 Then the angel told me, “Put this in writing. God will bless everyone who is invited to the wedding feast of the Lamb.” The angel also said, “These things God has said are true.”
10I knelt at the feet of the angel and began to worship him. But the angel said, “Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you and everyone else who tells about Jesus. Don't worship anyone but God. Everyone who tells about Jesus does it by the power of the Spirit.”
The Rider on the White Horse
11 I looked and saw heaven was open, and a white horse was there. Its rider was called Faithful and True, and he is always fair when he judges or goes to war. 12 He had eyes like flames of fire, and he was wearing a lot of crowns. His name was written on him, but he was the only one who knew what the name meant.
13 The rider wore a robe that was covered with blood, and he was known as “The Word of God.” 14He was followed by armies from heaven that rode on white horses and were dressed in pure white linen. 15 From his mouth a sharp sword went out to attack the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod and will show the fierce anger of God All-Powerful by trampling the grapes in the pit where wine is made. 16On the part of the robe that covered his thigh was written, “KING OF KINGS AND Lord OF LordS.”
17 I then saw an angel standing on the sun, and he shouted to all the birds flying in the sky, “Come and join in God's great feast! 18You can eat the flesh of kings, rulers, leaders, horses, riders, free people, slaves, important people, and everyone else.”
19I also saw the beast and all kings of the earth come together. They fought against the rider on the white horse and against his army. 20 But the beast was captured and so was the false prophet. This is the same prophet who had worked miracles for the beast, so he could fool everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol. The beast and the false prophet were thrown alive into a lake of burning sulfur. 21But the rest of their army was killed by the sword that came from the mouth of the rider on the horse. Then birds stuffed themselves on the dead bodies.
translation_text:
Kɔraawiizi chɔlaa wia
1Denii n nuu kɔɔi bɛl Kɔraawiizi bol, alugɔ nɛkpila werge maa n na pogzi. Ba ra ŋɔ,
“Tibaarikala! Yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi kpegli u dɔmaa,
di dɔɔ sɔŋ ni fɔŋŋa werge,
2dikuubɛɛwiai, wiazi la seriya
un diwee la ɛɛ wibiire
di deŋli.
U di hahsɛnsɛnnizeŋ la n faa ɛɛ wikuna
di chɔgi durnya
labuu seriya u chol,
di turguu u balaa
kpui la kim.”
3Ba kaa ŋɔ,
“Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi!
U nyɔɔzi ra tinnuu saŋa maa, a waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.”
4Nabɔnzi tokko ni banaazu la ni kunnyinee anaazu la chɔɔ hɛri di ra jaami Kɔraawiizi n soge u koorikara la ni la di ra ŋɔ,
“Ami. Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi!”
5Loobii bɛl lii koorikara la ni di ŋɔ,
“Ii banla n ɛɛ u balaa la,
nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa maa,
di ra ɔmuu la,
ií ra chɔli yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi.”
6N nuu nɛkpila werge maa n ŋɔ wia alugɔ nii n suwee werge di ra pal, nazaa ge ra pogzi werge maa. Kenne ba ŋɔ,
“Ií ra chɔli yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi
Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la
n di kora!
7Ií gil yaa bɔra sɔɔni yaa werge maa.
Yaa daŋ chɔluu, dikuubɛɛwiai,
Pebii la haaŋ kpai helloo.
U haaŋ ge ɛɛ u hiŋ siryaa.
8Ba gillɔɔ u kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa wɛjɛ
n na nyɛgzi di bɔg.”
A wɛjɛnanii ɛɛ winanaa la
Kɔraawiizi biinanaa
n ɛɛwɛ labuu.
9Mɛlika la ŋɔ n be, “Sɛbi wia naa ra dau. ‘Banla baŋ yittɛ bá ba wa di Pebii haŋfalii diuzenaa la nuu sumaa.’ ” U kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔzii guŋ, a ɛɛ wibiire.”
10Denii n chɔɔ u see ń jaamuu. U ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ ɛɛ guŋ. N nii ni i dɔŋahina la maa n na di Yeesu daansɛɛ la ɛɛ u balaarɛ. Kɔraawiizii í jaami. Yeesu wia labuu ɛɛ dɔgtɛɛzi wiŋɔzi la maa zɛɛ.”
Zagtinni la n tinni zaghuŋŋu la wia
11N na Kɔraawiizi bol n pillɛɛ, zaghuŋŋu bɛl lii. Nɛr la n tinnuu la, ba ra yiruu Yarda ni Wibii Hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ra di nɛra seriyazii ni wibii di ra yoo laal ni wibii. 12U siwee ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ninlau. U hi koorikahurozi kpilakpila u nyuu. Sɔŋ bɛl ge chɔɔ u ni. Nɛr maa waa a sɔŋ zummɛ di u himmaa lɛi. 13U sɔŋ bɛllɛ kaa Kɔraawiizi Wiŋɔɔlii. U laali tagtajaŋ bɛl baŋ kpawɛɛ lii chal. 14Kɔraawiizi bol soojazi laali gessihuŋŋa laala, di tinni zaghuŋŋa di hiŋuu kaali. 15Tokobidiilii ra lii u nua, ú ŋmɛnni durnya nɛra. “U daŋ kpogli lugbii daŋkpala, di ra binni baa,” di ra fɛrgi grepu daa nɔna, á nii ra lii, bɔr la banna fɛrgi nɔna a nii ra lii la biini. Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la baannɛ a nii. 16Sɔŋ bɛl chɔɔ u wɛjɛ ni u naapɔg ni,
KOORA MAA KOORI,
DƆƆRA MAA DƆƆRI.
17N kaa na mɛlika bɛl n chigɛ wiizi ni. U ŋɔ zumbizi la maa n na zaah chiŋ be, fɔŋŋa ni, “Ií ra ba. Ií chaali wa di Kɔraawiizi diuzenaa. 18Koora ni soojazi, nabɔnzi, nɛzenaa, zagra ni a tinna, banla n dɔɔ bahinaa, yoma, nɛdumazi ani nɛzenaa maa daŋ siu. Awia, ií chaali wa di baa.”
19Denii n na sechɔgii la ni durnya koora ni ba laallɔɔra n chaalɛɛ bá yoo unla n tinni zagu la ni u ge laallɔɔra. 20Ba lauri sechɔgii la ni dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ la n faa ra ɛɛ wizenaa u be di ra dar banla bam pii sechɔgii pii ba ra jaami kunla bam mawɛɛ la maanii. Ba waa baa kpuwɛɛ ka kpa baa di ha bɔr la niŋ n suwee lugɔ muu di fuuh ra sɔɔhri jilbi la. 21Banla ge n kawɛɛ, tokobi la n na lii unla n tinni zagu la nua la ge kpu baa zumbizi wa di baa, di piŋ.

english_text:
The Thousand Years
1I saw an angel come down from heaven, carrying the key to the deep pit and a big chain. 2 He chained the dragon for 1,000 years. It is that old snake, who is also known as the devil and Satan. 3Then the angel threw the dragon into the pit. He locked and sealed it, so 1,000 years would go by before the dragon could fool the nations again. But after that, it would have to be set free for a little while.
4 I saw thrones, and sitting on those thrones were the ones who had been given the right to judge. I also saw the souls of the people who had their heads cut off because they had told about Jesus and preached God's message. They were the same ones who had not worshiped the beast or the idol, and they had refused to let its mark be put on their foreheads or hands. They will come to life and rule with Christ for 1,000 years.
5-6These people are the first to be raised to life, and they are especially blessed and holy. The second death has no power over them. They will be priests for God and Christ and will rule with them for 1,000 years.
No other dead people were raised to life until 1,000 years later.
Satan Is Defeated
7At the end of the 1,000 years, Satan will be set free. 8 He will fool the countries of Gog and Magog, which are at the far ends of the earth, and their people will follow him into battle. They will have as many followers as there are grains of sand along the beach, 9and they will march all the way across the earth. They will surround the camp of God's people and the city God loves. But fire will come down from heaven and destroy the whole army. 10Then the devil who fooled them will be thrown into the lake of fire and burning sulfur. He will be there with the beast and the false prophet, and they will be in pain day and night forever and ever.
The Judgment at the Great White Throne
11 I saw a great white throne with someone sitting on it. Earth and heaven tried to run away, but there was no place for them to go. 12 I also saw all the dead people standing in front of that throne. Every one of them was there, no matter who they had once been. Several books were opened, and then the book of life was opened. The dead were judged by what those books said they had done.
13The sea gave up the dead people who were in it, and death and its kingdom also gave up their dead. Then everyone was judged by what they had done. 14Afterwards, death and its kingdom were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death. 15Anyone whose name wasn't written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
translation_text:
Binni kagboŋ la wia
1Denii n na mɛlika bɛl n lii Kɔraawiizi bol di ra tuu. Unna tuu la, u kpogli Sitaani Bɔɔluŋ la saafiibii ni yɔlɔzeŋ bɛllɛ u nonii. 2U ga lau nyugzenzeŋ la, unla n ɛɛ faa maa hɛrikuŋ ba ra yiruu Sitaani la, di kpa yɔlɔ la vɔɔzuu, ú du guŋ binni kagboŋ la maa biini, 3ka jaa kpau ga ha Sitaani Bɔɔluŋ la, di tɔ de di kar de kiŋkiŋ, ú gilɛɛ kaa ra dar durnya mɔɔ ka binni kagboŋ la wa bɛri. Di a wa bɛrɔɔ, ba daŋ puruu, ú lii tama.
4N na koorikassi aŋhina nɛra baŋhina n soge a ni. Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ baa fɔŋŋa ba ra di seriyazi. N kaa na baŋhina dunzi, baabuu banla baŋ faa teŋri ba nyuuni, dikuu baŋ faa di Yeesu daansɛɛ, di faa ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la wia, ba faa waa sɛɛwɛ ba jaami sechɔgii la ni kunla bam mawɛɛ la. Ba faa waa kaa sɛɛ ba pii ba hilli gɛɛ ba nonee sechɔgii la pii. Ba izi a nyiŋ. Ba ni Kristo kpau di ra di kora binni kagboŋ la biini. 5Banla n kawɛɛ waa izee mɔɔ ka binni kagboŋ la wa tuŋ. Lalaa siu biini izaa luglii guŋ. 6Unla maa n niŋ izi lalaa lugli izaa la biini, nuu sumaa werge, nɛnaniirɛ a hiŋ. Siu bunɛɛhiŋ wàá dɔɔ fɔŋŋa u ni. Ba daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni u Kristo Kizeehina, di kpau ra di ba kora binni kagboŋ la biini.
Sitaani kpeglaa wia
7Di binni kagboŋ la wa bɛrɔɔ, ba daŋ pur Sitaani di gil u lii bɔr la baŋ tɔu la. 8U daŋ lii di ba ú wa dar nɛra la maa n du hɛri tuna maa, Gɔg ni Magɔg la, di chaali baa bá yoo laal. Ba daŋ du kpil werge maa alugɔ muuzeŋ nua hɛɛhriichaa. 9Kenne n na ba wia. Ba izoore di ba di wa tɔ hɛri maa di bar bol la Kɔraawiizi n nɔŋŋɛɛ u biinanaa chaali de la. Denii niŋ lii chiŋ di chol ba ni di fuuh ba maa nyaamm. 10Ba lau Sitaani la n faa ra dar baa la ge di ha bɔr la niŋ ni jilbi n suwee di chɔɔ lugɔ muu la, bɔr la sechɔgii ni dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ la n duwɛɛ la. Ba maa daŋ haŋ di tɔɔrɔɔrɛ di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.
Tuna seriya dii wia
11N na koorikara bɛl n kannɛ werge di huuhzi. Nɛr la n soge u ni la, chiŋ ni hɛri n wa nau a chɔ kaali. A waa wette na bɔr suah. 12Denii n na lalaa maa, nɛzenaa ni nɛdumazi maa, n chigɛ koorikara la zɛɛ. Ba pilli hɔna aŋhina di kaa pilli unla n ɛɛ miibɔɔ hɔŋ la. Denii Kɔraawiizi di lalaa la ni ba huma la maa n du hɔna biini la maa seriya. 13Nɛra la nii n faa diwee la lii de, banla n du lalaa bol la ge lii. Kɔraawiizi di bɛl maa wiɛɛlaa seriya. 14Denii ba kpa siu ni lalaa bol maa di ha bɔr la niŋ n suwee di chɔɔ alugɔ muu la. Siu bunɛɛ hinnɛ a niŋ. 15Di ba haŋ wa nyiŋŋi nɛr maa sɔŋ huhzi miibɔɔ hɔŋ la biini, amɔ, ba kpaubuu ha a niŋ biini la.

english_text:
The New Heaven and the New Earth
1 I saw a new heaven and a new earth. The first heaven and the first earth had disappeared, and so had the sea. 2 Then I saw New Jerusalem, the holy city, coming down from God in heaven. It was like a bride dressed in her wedding gown and ready to meet her husband.
3 I heard a loud voice shout from the throne:
God's home is now with his people. He will live with them, and they will be his own. Yes, God will make his home among his people. 4 He will wipe all tears from their eyes, and there will be no more death, suffering, crying, or pain. These things of the past are gone forever.
5Then the one sitting on the throne said:
I am making everything new. Write down what I have said. My words are true and can be trusted. 6 Everything is finished! I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will freely give water from the life-giving fountain to everyone who is thirsty. 7 All who win the victory will be given these blessings. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
8But I will tell you what will happen to cowards and to everyone who is unfaithful or dirty-minded or who murders or is sexually immoral or uses witchcraft or worships idols or tells lies. They will be thrown into that lake of fire and burning sulfur. This is the second death.
The New Jerusalem
9I saw one of the seven angels who had the bowls filled with the seven last terrible troubles. The angel came to me and said, “Come on! I will show you the one who will be the bride and wife of the Lamb.” 10 Then with the help of the Spirit, he took me to the top of a very high mountain. There he showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down from God in heaven.
11The glory of God made the city bright. It was dazzling and crystal clear like a precious jasper stone. 12 The city had a high and thick wall with twelve gates, and each one of them was guarded by an angel. On each of the gates was written the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel. 13Three of these gates were on the east, three were on the north, three more were on the south, and the other three were on the west. 14The city was built on twelve foundation stones. On each of the stones was written the name of one of the Lamb's twelve apostles.
15 The angel who spoke to me had a gold measuring stick to measure the city and its gates and its walls. 16The city was shaped like a cube, because it was just as high as it was wide. When the angel measured the city, it was about 2,400 kilometers high and 2,400 kilometers wide. 17Then the angel measured the wall, and by our measurements it was about 60 meters high.
18 The wall was built of jasper, and the city was made of pure gold, clear as crystal. 19Each of the twelve foundations was a precious stone. The first was jasper, the second was sapphire, the third was agate, the fourth was emerald, 20the fifth was onyx, the sixth was carnelian, the seventh was chrysolite, the eighth was beryl, the ninth was topaz, the tenth was chrysoprase, the eleventh was jacinth, and the twelfth was amethyst. 21Each of the twelve gates was a solid pearl. The streets of the city were made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
22I did not see a temple there. The Lord God All-Powerful and the Lamb were its temple. 23 And the city did not need the sun or the moon. The glory of God was shining on it, and the Lamb was its light.
24 Nations will walk by the light of that city, and kings will bring their riches there. 25 Its gates are always open during the day, and night never comes. 26The glorious treasures of nations will be brought into the city. 27 But nothing unworthy will be allowed to enter. No one who is dirty-minded or who tells lies will be there. Only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will be in the city.
translation_text:
Chiŋfalii ni hɛrfalii wia
1Denii n na chiŋfalii ni hɛrfalii. A lugli hora lawaa wia tunnɔɔ. Muuzeŋ maa waa kaa hoo. 2N kaa na Bolzennanii, Jɛrusalɛmfalii n lii Kɔraawiizi be di ra tuu. U bɔguubuu lugɔ haŋfalii n ɔɔ bɔg u hiŋ ú ga yuu u jaari la. 3N nuu loobii bɛl n lii koorikara la be di ra la bɔɔnɛɛ, n na ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu ɛŋ. Kɔraawiizi duuribɔr jaa du newea benii. U ni baa daŋ jaa du de. Ba daŋ birgi u nɛra, ú ge ɛɛ ba Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di du ba be. 4U daŋ fiizi ba sinii maa. Siu ge wàá ka du de. Biinichɔg ni kalu ni bɔwii wàá ka du de. Lugli wia la tunnɔɔ.” 5Unla n soge koorikara la ni la ŋɔ, “Na! N gillɔɔ kuna maa birgi a falaa.” U kaa ŋɔ n be, “Sɛbi a wia dau, dikuubɛɛwiai, n wiŋɔzi naa ɛɛ wibiire. A waa daraa dɔɔwɛ.”
6Denii u ŋɔ, “A tunnɔ! Minuu lugli, minuu kaa tuna. Minuu ra faari wia, minuu kaa ra tunaa. Di nɛr maa ra wii niinyɔgzi, n daŋ gil u la bɔr la miibɔɔ nii n na bul di ga nyɔɔ a nii pɛɛpɛɛ. 7Nɛr la n wette kpegli Sitaani, u daŋ na wia naa maa. N daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la unna hum, ú ge ɛɛ n biibaal. 8Ka banla n na ɔm ani banla n waa yardi, banla n doŋ bahinaa ani banla n ɛɛ nɛkpuura ni sɛnsɛnna ni ziŋgaabo hina ni vugkuara ni banla maa n na dar nɛra, ba hotte bɔr la niŋ n suwee lugɔ muu di fuuh di ra sɔɔhri jilbi la. Siu bunɛɛ hinnɛ guŋ.”
9Denii mɛlikazi aniidaanɛɛ la n faa kpogli hɛnni ni wiilchɔgaa tuna aniidaanɛɛ la bɛl wa ŋɔ n be, “Ba ń baglii Pebii haŋfalii la.” 10Kɔraawiizi Duma izi n ni, u kpaŋ kaali bizenzeŋ bɛl nyuu. A bii faa la chinne werge. Denii u bagliŋ Jɛrusalɛm la n lii Kɔraawiizi be di ra tuu di ɛɛ bolnanii la. 11Kɔraawiizi girme ra chaani u maa u ɛɛ lugɔ binanii la banna yir jaspɛr la n wesse werge maa di du yelemm lugɔ digii la. 12Koŋliizeŋ bɛl n la chiŋ werge baruu. U dominuuzi du fidaanɛɛ. Mɛlikazi fidaanɛɛ ge chi a dominuuzi. Ba sɛbi Izrɛl hina dizi fidaanɛɛ la sɔna dau dominuuzi la ni. 13U wiifurii paga la, dominuuzi ahoroo du de. U wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag paga ge, dominuuzi ahoro du de. U wiicholii paga, dominuuzi ahoroo du de ge. U wiifurii nodig wiikakag ge dominuuzi ahoro du de. 14Bia la baŋ chiŋŋɛɛ di ma a koŋlii hɔŋ a ni la ge du fidaanɛɛ. Pebii la huŋhunna fidibanɛɛ la sɔna ge du a bia ni.
15Mɛlika la n nuu n na ŋɔ wia la kpogli saliŋ daa ú kpa ra mɛgzi bol la ni u dominuuzi ni u koŋlaa la. 16A bol du kɔŋlɔnnɛ. U wassi ni u jaŋzi maa mɛgzi. U kpa saliŋ daa la di ra mɛgzi. U jaŋzi ɛɛ kilomitazi kagboŋa anɛɛ ni kalfaanɛɛ. U jaŋzi ni u wassi ni u chiŋ laŋaa maa ɛɛ kpannɛ. 17U kaa mɛgzi koŋlii la. U chiŋ laŋaa ge ɛɛ nogumzi kalfa ni tokkoanɛɛ ni anaazu. Newee mɛgzaarɛ guŋ. Aabuu u kpa di ra mɛgzi. 18Jaspɛr labuu ba kpa ma u koŋlaa. A bol himmaa ge, saliŋ himmaa n du yelemm alugɔ digiire ba kpa di mau. 19Binanaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ faari a koŋlaa zɛɛ la ge sɔnaa keŋ. Lugli hiŋ ɛɛ jaspaa, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ saafaya, horohiŋ ɛɛ aget, naazuhiŋ ge ɛɛ ɛmɛrald, 20nuehiŋ ɛɛ ɔnigs, numbɛlhiŋ ɛɛ karnɛliɔn, niidaanɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ kuats, ŋmantannaazihiŋ ɛɛ bɛril, kabɛlhiŋ ɛɛ topaz, fihiŋ ɛɛ kalsidoni, fidikpaŋhiŋ ɛɛ turkɔis, fidaanɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ amɛtis. 21Dominuuzi fidaanɛɛ la ge, kunnanaa la banna yir pɛɛl labuu tɔ a maa. A bol ŋmɛnizi ge ɛɛ saliŋ himmaa n du yelemm alugɔ digii.
22Maa Kɔraawiizi jaamidia nawɛɛ de, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ni Pebii la ɛɛ jaamidiarɛ. 23A waa kaa ɛɛ lugɔ wiizi ni baaguu ninna chaani a bol, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi girmee ninna chaani de. Pebii la genii ɛɛ a bol fintina. 24Durnya nɛra danna vol u bɔchaaŋ la biini, durnya koora ni ba girme ge maa wa zuu u biini. 25U dominuuzi ŋmɛnɛ maa waa tɔi dɔɔwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, hamuŋa waa du de. 26Durnya nɛra girme ni ba daama maanii bá kpa zuu de. 27Ka kunla maa n doŋŋe waa wer zuu de maa. Nɛra la maa n na ɛɛ wikuna di dɔɔ daraa maa wàá wer zuu de. Banla baŋ sɛbi ba sɔna di du Pebii miibɔɔ hɔŋ la biini la, bɛnnɛ niŋ zuu de.

english_text:
1 The angel showed me a river that was crystal clear, and its waters gave life. The river came from the throne where God and the Lamb were seated. 2 Then it flowed down the middle of the city's main street. On each side of the river are trees that grow a different kind of fruit each month of the year. The fruit gives life, and the leaves are used as medicine to heal the nations.
3 God's curse will no longer be on the people of that city. He and the Lamb will be seated there on their thrones, and its people will worship God 4 and will see him face to face. God's name will be written on the foreheads of the people. 5 Never again will night appear, and no one who lives there will ever need a lamp or the sun. The Lord God will be their light, and they will rule forever.
The Coming of Christ
6Then I was told:
These words are true and can be trusted. The Lord God controls the spirits of his prophets, and he is the one who sent his angel to show his servants what must happen very soon. 7Remember, I am coming soon! God will bless everyone who pays attention to the message of this book.
8My name is John, and I am the one who heard and saw these things. Then after I had heard and seen all this, I knelt down and began to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown it to me.
9But the angel said,
Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you. I am the same as a follower or a prophet or anyone else who obeys what is written in this book. God is the one you should worship.
10Don't keep the prophecies in this book a secret. These things will happen soon.
11 Evil people will keep on being evil, and everyone who is dirty-minded will still be dirty-minded. But good people will keep on doing right, and God's people will always be holy.
12 Then I was told:
I am coming soon! And when I come, I will reward everyone for what they have done. 13 I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
14 God will bless all who have washed their robes. They will each have the right to eat fruit from the tree that gives life, and they can enter the gates of the city. 15But outside the city will be dogs, witches, immoral people, murderers, idol worshipers, and everyone who loves to tell lies and do wrong.
16 I am Jesus! And I am the one who sent my angel to tell all of you these things for the churches. I am David's Great Descendant, and I am also the bright morning star.
17 The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!”
Everyone who hears this should say, “Come!”
If you are thirsty, come! If you want life-giving water, come and take it. It's free!
18 Here is my warning for everyone who hears the prophecies in this book:
If you add anything to them, God will make you suffer all the terrible troubles written in this book. 19If you take anything away from these prophecies, God will not let you have part in the life-giving tree and in the holy city described in this book.
20The one who has spoken these things says, “I am coming soon!”
So, Lord Jesus, please come soon!
21I pray that the Lord Jesus will be kind to all of you.
translation_text:
Miibɔɔ muu wia
1Denii u bagliŋ muu bɛl n lii Kɔraawiizi ni Pebii la koorikara la be. A nii dɔɔ miibɔɔrɛ di du yelemm, 2di chɔɔ a bol ŋmɛnɛɛ baambaaŋ di ra pal. Miibɔɔ daa bɛl chi u keŋkere bɛl. Bɛl ge chi u keŋkere bɛl hiŋ. A ɔɔ nɔŋ nɔnaa naa bufidaanɛɛ bina maa. Baagu maa a ɔɔ nɔŋ nɔndee kpaŋ. A paŋhoori ge ra chaa durnya. 3Kunla maa Kɔraawiizi n see nua wàá du a bol. Kɔraawiizi ni Pebii koorikara la daŋ du de. U balaa daŋ ɔɔ ra jaamuu. 4Ba daŋ ɔɔ ra binni u siwee, ú sɔŋ ge du ba hilli. 5Hamuŋa wàá du de. Ba wàá kaa ra nyiŋŋi fintina ni wiizi gba, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɔɔ ra chaani ba ni. Ba danna di kora di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.
Yeesu balaa wia
6Denii mɛlika la ŋɔ n be, “Wiŋɔzi naa ɛɛ wibiire. A waa daraa maa dɔɔwɛ. Yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi Duma la n faa izi dɔgtɛɛzi la ni la, waabuu hum u mɛlika u balaa be ú bagli baa wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ filaŋkeŋ.” 7“Ií ra nuu ɛŋ. N daŋ ba manaŋ. Unla n niŋ hiŋ wia naa baŋ sɛbɛɛ hɔnnaa biini nuu sumaa.” 8Mìŋ́ Jɔɔnnɛ nuu wia naa maa di naa. Miŋ wa nuua di naa la, n chɔɔ mɛlika la n bagliŋ a wia see ŋɔ ń jaamuu. 9Ka u ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ ɛɛ guŋ. N gba ɛɛ u balii bɛllɛ alugɔ i ni i dɔŋahina dɔgtɛɛzi la ni banla n na hiŋ wia la n du hɔnnaa biini la. A jaami Kɔraawiizi.” 10U kaa ŋɔ n be, “Gilɛɛ wa kpa wia naa n du hɔnnaa biini naa di ra suah, ka ra bagli wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ la, dikuubɛɛwiai, a wia saŋa ra dugluu. 11Nɛr la n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ú haa ra ɛɛ a wichɔgaa. Nɛr la n na ɛɛ wikuna, ú haa ra ɛɛ a wikuna. Nɛr la n na ɛɛ winanaa, ú haa ra ɛɛ winanaa la. Nɛr la n waa doŋa maa dɔɔwɛ u ni, ú haa du guŋ.”
12“Ií ra nuu ɛŋ. N daŋ ba manaŋ. Kinturgaa la du n benii. N daŋ turgi nɛr maa ani gunla uŋ hummɛ. 13Minuu lugli. Minuu kaa tuna. Minuu tɔ see di kaa tɔ har. Minuu ra lugli wia. Minuu kaa ra tunaa. 14Banla n chag ba tagtajaŋra la ka bá wer di di miibɔɔ daa la nɔna, di ɔɔ wer ra zuu a bol biini ba kipar la, nuu sumaa. 15Nɛkuna, tagɛɛra, sɛnsɛnna, nɛkpuura, vugkuara ni banla maa n na nyiŋŋi nɛdaraa di ra kanni kara la, ba maa du bosseere. 16Mìŋ́ Yeesuu hum n mɛlika la ú wer baglii wiŋɔzi naa í bagli n hiŋra la. Minuu Deevid Dee Faaraa, minuu kaa ɛɛ u Naana Bɛl. Minuu Naanyɔɔ la n na chaani werge la.”
17Kɔraawiizi Duma ni haŋfalii la ŋɔ, “A ba!” Hinla maa n nuuwɛ, í ge ŋɔ, “A ba!” Nɛr la maa n na wii niinyɔgzi, ú ra ba. Nɛr la maa n na nyiŋŋi lugɔ u ba wa nyɔɔ miibɔɔ nii la pɛɛpɛɛ, ú ra ba.
18N ŋɔ ń karfi nɛr la maa n nuu wia naa n du hɔnnaa biini, di ra bagli wia la n niŋ haa wa ɛɛ labuu lugɔ, di bɛl maa wa jaa wiimaa a ni, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil wiilchɔgaa la wia miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ hɔnnaa biini la, chol u ni. 19Di bɛl maa kaa wa mɔŋ wiŋɔzi naa ni ta tama maa, Kɔraawiizi wàá tɛu miibɔɔ daa la nɔna ú di. Wàá tɛu bɔr u bolnanii la biini. Wàá zum anniizi min bagli a wia hɔnnaa biini naa.
20Unla n ɛɛ wia naa maa daansɛɛ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ ba manaŋ.” Ami. N Dɔɔri Yeesu, a ba manaŋ.
21Yáa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo nɛsunaa dɔɔi ni u hiinaa du ii maa be. Ami.
